reviews.comment: He is a very good professor. He is extremely knowledgeable and helpful. He probably provides the best feedback out of any professor on campus. His grading criteria is very clear and fair. Additionally, he always has a willingness to work with students to ensure they're getting what they want from the class, and to make sure they succeed.
Professor Cheon is a man of integrity and a gentleman. He also has a great zeal for teaching.
Prof Cheon is attentive, approachable and knowledgeable. Great course, great prof.
Great Professor

Insanely detailed, logical, and clear feedback on essays. Provides extensive personalized feedback for each and every student, had check-in stages for the assignments that actually made writing research papers fun. I think I learned more about writing good research in this one course than I did throughout all 4 years at Duke/DKU. Highly recommend!!

It really is a shame that everyone has to take Saito-sensei's class to get to the next level. It cuts more than half the students because of how bad the class is. She teaches in a waaaay to traditional way without much help or wiggle room for students. Do not recommend!
currently taking this class. not fun at all. she is a tough grader and doesn't help beyond her old school method of teaching.
At first I really was excited to take prof. Saito's class but omg she is not a good teacher at all. Shocked by how bad she is at explaining grammar while being such a tough grader.
really don't like Saito sensei. She's harsh on students, very old school, and gossips behind students backs.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: So many tests and homework. Not caring at all. She also puts her various homeworks in many different formats so its hard to keep track.
Just horrible honestly. The first day she seemed nice but all she does is make you work and it honestly does nothing but improve busy work.
This class was way too hard and the instructor is too old fashion to be helpful. She lectures and provides a ton of homework and expects you to devote your life to her class.

This class was not fun at all this year. I tried my hardest but even without being graded this teacher made it too difficult. Not just their inability to teach the material but also their harsh grading and lack of empathy towards students learning styles

She just regurgitates the text book and offers little help to students. Spoke to others in the program and was told too late not to continue because of having to take further classes with her…. It's a shame because the Tobira textbook used is otherwise very helpful, in like her old teaching methods

Definitely the worst Japanese teacher at Duke. Everyone I know says to skip her class. She's rude and very cold to students. Her explanations are poor and she's a very tough grader. Also hard to communicate with her as it's her way or the highway. I only got an A through seeking outside help. Some of the class projects were fun though

She seems nice but is very harsh on grades and not understanding at all. She only teaches the old way which isn't helpful and she does not care about this. It was hard to follow her and she wasn't helpful.

She also talks bad about other students in vague manners. Not very professional.

Saito-sensei is very passionate about teaching. 204 is more work than 203 simply because the Tobira textbook is thorough and covers a lot of grammar, but I liked 204 more than 203 since the class size was smaller so it was easier to speak and get closer w/ classmates. Be prepared to spend some time doing HW every day, otherwise, it's not too bad.

The class is flipped so you watch some short lecture videos for homework and most of class is spent on practicing. I've heard that for 203, this semester onward was made easier because few students wanted to take more Japanese. I think difficulty is similar to Kurokawa-sensei's 101/102 if you started learning from zero, but with more creativity.
Good

She's very old school Japanese. Deadlines are a must. Participation is a must. If her class is not taking over your life, then you're not taking it seriously enough. Be very cautious before taking a class with her. She's very friendly on the outside, but she will get inside your head and cause you pain.

The class was more of a seminar than a traditional Japanese class. Still a lot of work though. Saito sensei is very nice and a great professor, but if she can tell you're not putting in any work, that personality will do a total 180. Since the class is pretty small and you get a fair amount of 1-on-1 time with her, I'd try to avoid that.

Saito Sensei is very enthusiastic about teaching, and is ALWAYS available for help outside classes (review interview performance, talk about your writing, grammar, etc.)  Yes, she gives out a lot of work for 4th year classes (JPN 183/184), but everyone has A LOT of fun in her class.  Highly recommended to those who finished 3rd-year Japanese.

Saito Sensei is a very nice, very cute teacher. She smiles all the time and makes the class very enjoyable for you. The class is not that hard if you put in the effort to memorise the kanji (Chinese char).

Easy class, but would not recommend taking a class with him — especially if you're looking for something fun. Incredibly boring and repetitive. Cares more about his own social media presence than his students.

Interesting guy. If you want to take one of his classes, be ready to be featured in the social media content he posts. This class, and most of his classes to my knowledge, are super easy to get an A in, as long as you actually come to class and submit everything on time. Would recommend for an easy A, and if you just want to take a class with him.
he does too much ngl
Very enjoyable class.  Loved it!   Follow him on Facebook/insta too.
Good Professor
Fantastic insta
so funny the tik tok guy strikes again

Honest just appreciate how much this guy tries. Some of his stuff is cringe, but its better than 95% of other professors who want us to sit through their boring lectures and take tests. We need more profs like Dinin in the world teaching classes.
Obviously a prof who is all over social media so understands it. Very down to earth and still makes time for his students.

Pretty straightforward and understanding guy. There were some interesting topics covered but his lectures could get pretty long. I enjoyed the hands-on aspect of the class, but your group really made or broke your experience in class for the day. Overall easy class and I definitely learned a lot about social media.
Very chill professor, you will be bored
Duke in SV is great. Professor Dinin can be a bit overbearing with his videoing and forcing TikTok upon the class, but his lectures are overall engaging and fun. I highly recommend this course.
The TikTok professor!!!!! Yeah he's sometimes a little cringe, but you learn to live with it. At least he's trying to reach students on their level which is more than I can say for most professors.

Sometimes boring, but a very easy class. Little to no homework and class consists of making videos and discussions with others. Learned a lot about marketing and social media, and he gave us fun challenges. Overall good and would take again.

What you see online isn't what you get in class. I mean that in a good way. He looks like he's really self-centered online, but when you take the class you realize it's because he studies social media and understands how to post so his accounts grow. He's super-caring in person and def loves his students. Wish more professors were like him.

Definitely not one of those professors who's going to make your life miserable if you don't do the homework. That's good and bad. It means you get out of it what you put in. If you're interested in social media, take Dinin's class. If you aren't, don't take it. That simple. It's amazing to have a prof with legit experience in what he's teaching.

If you want an easy A and don't want to do anything take the class. If you want to learn about social media marketing take the class. If you don't apply to the first two don't bother wasting your time. Really cool if you're looking to begin a social media career or have a free A basically, otherwise, spend your money and time elsewhere.

Dinin is an engaging professor who cares about connecting with students. His class is discussion-based and hands-on, with helpful assignments. I found unstuck study great for prepping case studies. Worth taking if you're interested in social media.

Just had to comment on someone else's review that was surprised the class had a lot of social media in it. It's called "social marketing". What did he expect? LOL.

Anyway, Dinin is basically the best professor at Duke. A little cringe, but you can tell it comes from a good place. Try to flunch him if you can. Might take him a while to respond.

I personally did not love this class. Dinin is a very cool guy but he was slightly arrogant. Also, 253 is much more social media based than I expected, so don't take this if you aren't super into posting on TikTok. However, I did learn a lot and it was a very interesting experience.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Loved this class!

Really engaging professor. Love that he seems to care so much about trying to understand his students and live in their world instead of just making us do everything his old-fashioned way like a lot of other professors. Makes TikToks in class, lets us have phones and computers, and really seems to care a lot. We need more professors like Dinin.

Great guy. Every class was like a TedTalk. I loved coming into class in the morning and finding out what the topic of that day was going to be. Super valuable info regardless of whether you want to work in Social Media or not.

Dinin is extremely knowledgeable in the world of social media, and will try to give you insights into how to be a "critical reader of social media." The class is graded on case studies, homework (completion grade), and social media experiment which are all hands on, engaging, and relatively easy assignments. Would recommend.

Felt like posting to say he's one of the better professors at Duke. I was thinking of transferring, and his advice was the best. Dinin helped me realize I wasn't happy because I was just following what everyone else was doing and taking the wrong classes. Definitely schedule office hours with him. Worth talking to outside of class.

Lots of little assignments, but an easy and really interesting class. Likes to do group projects which can be a little problematic if you get bad people in your group, but if you talk with him about the problems you're having in your group, Dinin is really good about helping you out. One of the easiest professors to talk to.

reviews.comment: He is a poor professor who advocates for communication but does not actually practice what he preaches. He expects perfection from his students and is the least understanding professor at Duke.

reviews.comment: Dinin is probably the most chill professor I've ever had. But he's able to do that while being really passionate about the subject. Some of his jokes are a little lame, but he bends over backward to help you succeed, and he treats you like an adult rather than a kid, which is really nice for a change.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Aaron is who you want if you're looking for that GPA boost or that chill class in a schedule full of tougher classes.  You're bound to get an A as long as you turn things in for his class.
Dinin is the man! He always wants to help, he will always crack a joke and make the class entertaining. Take his class if you like the subject he is teaching, you will benefit from it!
A gem of a professor. So thoughtful. So caring. I was dealing with a big personal issue this semester, and he reached out multiple times just to check on me and make sure I'm doing OK.

Attendance is mandatory (it affects your grade if you don't go), and there are 2-3 really easy assignments each week. Even though it's easy, I wouldn't recommend the class. He's passionate and a great guy, but the content is dated and oversimplified. Our final project is to get 2000 followers on TikTok, which we've learned to hate.

It's literally a class where the homework is using TikTok. Somehow by doing that Prof. Dinin gets you thinking about TikTok in a way that's totally different than how you used it before. You'll actually start to hate social media by the end of the semester, but in a good way. You'll recognize how manipulative it all is, which is creepy.

I wish more professors taught classes as practical and useful to life beyond college as Dinin. Plus he actually understands what skills students will need when they graduate, as opposed to most of the other classes I've taken. Easily the best professor and class at Duke. No question.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Hands down best class I've had at Duke. Not a hard class at all, but I think that's because a lot of the assignments don't feel like work because you're literally doing things like looking at TikTok, which I'd probably be doing anyway. Some of the readings can be a bit tedious, but there aren't tests on them or anything, so you can skim.

This class is an awesome way to engage with social media and learn more about it. Dinin is growing his own platform, and he brings his input from his experience into the class. Would take this class again in a heartbeat.

Best class I've taken at Duke, it was an amazing class that really made me think about social media's place within our lives and how we can create content that stands out. Professor Dinin's lectures always felt important and engaging. This is also very much so an ENGLISH class, we engaged with literature and how it pertains to social media.

Probably one of the most useful classes at Duke. I came away every class with a new outlook on social media, and also learned about the power of building your personal brand for anyone. Be wary that group projects really depend on your group, so be sure to communicate. Be prepared to participate!
Professor Dinin is a great professor and loves to talk/engage with his students. Do the readings and participate in class and you will do fine.

This class is really engaging and interesting to learn about social media marketing. The workload is not bad and there are a lot of speakers/group projects. Grading criteria is clear from the beginning Professor Dinin is an amazing prof! Would def recommend this class
Class focuses on influencer marketing (not brands), super interesting but only if you want to go into social media, Dr. Dinin is fantastic -- funny, entertaining, accommodating

Most interesting and best class I've had at Duke. Gave me a completely different perspective on social media. Dr. Dinin makes you think about things in ways you wouldn't normally and he's got the background and experience that helps him know what he's talking about.
fascinating + useful

Really entertaining prof. Lots of small assignments, but structures it in a way that makes them easy to earn a good grade on while still learning lots. Really pulls back the curtain on social media and how it works. Can't look at the internet the same way, that's for sure.

Professor Dinin's class was phenomenal. His lectures were interesting, relevant, and he really opened my eyes to the social media world. He never assigns too much work, and there are no tests/quizzes. Classes are seminar style/cool guest speakers.
Great professor. Super interesting material. Loved the class overall would definitely recommend.
def worth taking a class with him at some point during your duke career
I really enjoyed this class! It was very interesting and unique subject material.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: You should honestly take a class with Professor Dinin. He is a dope professor that truly cares about what his students learn and finds great content to talk about. You'll get an A if you put in the effort. Not a ton of work. You will learn a ton!

This class is an unexpectedly quirky romp through the world of social media. Dr. Dinin occasionally comes across as narcissistic (he often uses his own social media accounts and exploits as examples), but while he's not humble, he's certainly entertaining and informed. Consistent assignments but all decently easy. Be prepared to get thoughtful!

As someone who is social media averse, I really enjoyed learning more about it in his class. My favorite part of the class were the connections of historic texts to modern media. Although there are plenty of short homework assignments, they are interesting. Highly recommend taking this course :)
Definitely recommend taking this course if you get the chance. The assignments were interesting and enjoyed the final social media experiment.

Great professor. I took IE253 Social Marketing with him. Lots of reading. Lots of small mini assignments. If you can do them all (which dont take very long) you are going to be fine. Really fun class. Does not teach you how to become an influencer but rather how to become a better marketer and consumer of media.

reviews.comment: Take a class with Dinin if you have the opportunity. Trust me. You'll be sitting in other classes, like I am right now, and wishing you were back in his class.
My third class with Dr. Dinin, and I love how he's never afraid to try something new.

reviews.comment: One of the best professors/classes I've taken at Duke. Wish more classes were like his. The homework never felt like homework because I actually wanted to do it.

Whatever you do, figure out how to take a class with Dr. Dinin. You'll be glad you did.

He attempted something experimental for the I&E Capstone. I'm not sure it went exactly how he planned, but he used our feedback to continue improving throughout the semester, and I ultimately learned a ton.

Best professor I've had at Duke and I think that shows in the class. When I stop and think about, there were a lot of assignments, but I actually enjoyed doing them, so it never really seemed like work. Make sure you stop by Dinin's office hours, too. He's a very caring professor and gives all sorts of good advice.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Really engaging professor. Makes you excited to show up every day. And I felt like I learned a ton.
Great Learning environment

One of the best classes I have taken at Duke. Very caring and has a great way of teaching the material of the class through many different kinds of assignments. Be prepared to have a decent amount of work, but all fun and really interesting to do. Overall, highly recommend taking the class!!

Prof Dinin really makes you think. We critically thought about the social media around us and how they fit into the context in our lives and the world around us. Readings provided really make you think and we have excellent class discussion. You have to make an instagram from scratch and get 1k followers in 2 months, which you MUST start early on.

reviews.comment: The final Instagram experiment is super fun and enjoyable. It seems very challenging at first, but most people put a good amount of work in and do really well. reviews.comment: This was my favorite class that I have taken at Duke - with my now favorite professor that I have had at Duke. Sincerely amazing class - super interesting learning experience about something that was relevant to our lives. The work did not feel like homework but rather something that was actually worth learning. Would HIGHLY recommend.

Heavy on discussion in class about social media use, really makes you question some of the beliefs you hold about social media. Interesting in-class activities and homework where we can apply concepts we learn in class.

reviews.comment: Great class. Professor Dinin puts in lots of effort to make his students understand the core concepts of social marketing. He's very open to questions/comments and an overall understanding person. The final project is fun and you learn a ton. Application/Example based class

Social Marketing is a really fun class to add into your schedule. The assignments and book readings are enjoyable to do and never feel like actual work. Professor Dinin has interesting perspectives and leads a great class on a relevant topic. He can come off a little patronizing at times, but overall really enjoyed.
Interesting class that works a ton with social media platforms. No overwhelmingly large assignments, but you do have to consistently participate and keep up with regular small assignments.

Thoughtful and caring professor. Will make you question your use of social media, but you'll learn more than you expect - through the lens of social media, you'll actually gain knowledge about consumer behavior, building a brand, etc. that can be applied to many more practical situations

reviews.comment: very laid back and engages with students
Professor Dinin is awesome, I've had him for two classes so far and even as a non I&E student I feel like these were some of the most applicable classes that I've taken at Duke.
Great class. Trust the process, you'll get a good grade in the end. Just do your stuff. Can be pretty fun and nice break from brutal Duke classes
Super laid back and caring professor. Not a typical Duke class.

reviews.comment: Went to his office hours thinking he was going to scold me because of some missed assignments, but ended up having the best conversation I've ever had with a professor. He gave all sorts of helpful advice not just about his class, but also about school and career advice. If you take his class, make sure to find some time to talk to him 1-on-1.

Thoughtful, caring and funny. Our class was mostly group work. He helped guide us, but wasn't overbearing. Treated us like adults, allowed us to make our own decisions and set our own goals, which was a unique experience for a college class.

one of the most caring professors ever. i was really struggling in the class and i thought he was going to fail me. instead, he called me to his office he spent the entire time trying to help me get myself back on track. if all professors cared half as much as Dr. Dinin, college would be way better.

funny, relatable professor who is extremely honest clear grading rubric means that there is little room for leeway (even the format for class discussion questions) takes class feedback into account and addresses concerns cool content that provides a different kind of learning the class may seem easy but A's aren't guaranteed

We got to engage with social media platforms a lot which provided a lot of value to the course. Passionate about teaching this course. Provides feedback on everything, so you know exactly what to do to get a better grade.

reviews.comment: Manageable amount of work. Be prepared to make presentations. It is an engaging and a fun class. Professor is funny and chill. Mostly you deal with real life case studies / examples and thus topics are applicable to real word. Really helpful to understand the dynamics behind today's social media and marketing.

The outline for the class was super clear. My one issue wit the class was that most class time was not spent delving into the reading material, or discussing the merits of what we were learning. However, I do think I learned a fair amount by actually engaging in the practice of social media. The final assignment is unique but FRUSTRATING.

One of the best professors and classes I've had at Duke. Dinin takes the concepts we learn in class and applies them to real world opportunities, as in jobs/potential internships. Do yourself a favor and take this class. It's fun and you learn a ton.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This class was very inciteful. You really learn how social media works behind the scenes. This professor really tries to provide real world information. You will learn things you did not expect to learn (in a great way).

Professor Dinin is so great and clearly knows his subject. Social media marketing is so multifaceted, and he does a great job showing students how. Classwork was interesting but not too challenging. You will have to read and write responses. Overall highly recommend.

This class really surpassed my expectations-- Mr. Dinin always finds a way to twist lectures and really make us think. He really changed the way that I view social media and made me want to pursue it further.

Social Media Marketing is a super chill class & very useful if you plan on going into marketing/brand management/sales/or even startups. It is interesting and I really enjoyed how interactive the class was, particularly the final project of making an insta that needs 1K followers and 10% engagement on posts. Some boring reading is assigned though.

I loved everything about this class, and from what I have heard his amazingness applies to his other classes as well.

You spend the entire semester diving into Instagram, Twitter, Youtube, etc. and analyzing how different influencers/brands/etc. find success. Aaron provides a lot of insight and is also just a hilarious and chill dude. Very comfortable and fun classroom environment.
It was a good class. Lots of cool stuff with social media and all of it was engaging and served a purpose. I loved it. This class is his favorite and it shows in the effort he puts in.

Great professor, had him for two courses now, really dives into topics and ideas that are modern, interesting, and will actually help you in the real world
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Easy and fun class! I surprisingly learned a lot about social media marketing. Low workload so highly recommend to take this if you are overloading.

Professor Dinin really just doesn't care about you memorizing abstract facts that you aren't going to use. He cares about enabling you to succeed by applying the underlying principles of entrepreneurship, marketing, and social media. If you want to up your own Insta game, or just want an easy class about social marketing, this is it.

Dinin is a great guy who is witty/funny and knowledgable about the topics that he teaches. He knows how to make a class engaging and I never felt bored/zoned out. Not a ton of work but assignments here and there and group work that is enjoyable. Definitely would take this class again as it provides great social media experience

Building Global Audiences is a fantastic course that takes a hands-on, unorthodox approach to learning the fundamentals of social media and engagement. Would definitely recommend to anybody who is interested in this space! Dr. Dinin was really great at leading us through challenging objectives.
Really chill and accomplished dude. The class is easy but you def learn a ton. This particular class is all hands-on learning with groups, which can be fun.

Professor Dinin is such a kind, down to earth guy. Class was mostly group project based  so beware if you hate that. This was his first time teaching this version of the class, so it was pretty disorganized and experimental, but overall it was fun. Not sure I learned A TON of new information, but definitely got hands-on experience.

reviews.comment: Dr. Dinin clearly prepares all of his classes and really cares about his students and their experiences in his classes. His approach is somewhat unconventional and not very grade-focused. He is definitely approachable and creates a wholesome, light-hearted, friendly environment in his classroom.
Cool class w/ cool professor. Laid back, but fun and interesting work.

TAKE THIS CLASS!! I have never learned more from a class in my life. This class has solidified my passion in marketing and that was all because of Dinin. He is super chill, funny, a great mentor, doesnt care about class structure and if you show you are trying and care about your work, you will get an A. Cant say enough good things about it.
Casual, funny professor who really just wants students to be engaged and excited about the material. Forward-thinking and innovative, his class was a great experience!
It was a very fun class that allowed you to get hands-on experience with social media and brand creation. Dr. Dinin was very enthusiastic and open to feedback. Take a class with him!

Dr. Dinin is AMAZING!!!! Definitely take his class (whether it's 250 or anything else). He cares so much about the success of his students and prioritizes learning over anything else. He is a fair and reasonable grader. If you put in effort, you will definitely be rewarded. By far my favorite professor at Duke.

Dr. Dinin is a funny and very smart guy. He approaches classes with an open mind set, and he is always looking to learn from his students. This is the second class that I've taken with Dr. Dinin, and I can confidently say i would take a third. What you put into Dr. Dinin's classes are what you get out, but he gives you the frame to learn a lot.

reviews.comment: I love this class. I really learned stuff that I felt like could be applied to a real career in the future. You truly learn what it is line to run the social media account of someone else. I would def take this class or any class with him again.
The professor was great. He focuses on learning rather than grades and makes a fun, open class environment.

Dr. Dinin is great. He's the main reason why the class was interesting. He really cares about student feedback and tries to teach the class skills without making it incredibly boring. High learning, low work!

reviews.comment: I enjoyed the course. A lot of work (seemingly feeling like busy work), but in the end it makes sense why you do it all. I'll never look at social media the same. Great class, funny professor. Grading doesn't seem too tough, but the Instagram project is a pain!

reviews.comment: Taking the class and very much enjoyed the semester. The topics were interesting and the prof was really cool.

I took Dinin's Social Media Marketing class and it was probably my favorite class of the semester. The projects are fun and the work load isn't too heavy. The reading are very useful and he brings in really cool guest speakers. Dinin makes the class super interesting and I am so glad I took this course.

Social Marketing for Entrepreneurs is a really interesting class that I recommend to anyone who may want to build an online presence for themselves one day. Dinin is really engaging and cares a lot about the progress of his students.

reviews.comment: The class was good overall, but compared to what people told me beforehand, there were many more assignments and the grading scale was difficult since so many assignments were graded out of so few points. Dinin is funny, but I don't think you want to get on his bad side.

Dinin was incredibly nice and approachable outside of class, and made class an enjoyable experience to come to
He was very enthusiastic and cared about this class!

I took Dinin's class this semester and absolutely loved it. I thought it was so interesting and really different from many of the other classes I have taken at Duke. It made me so much more aware of how I can use social media for good and for bad and how to continue reading the news with lots of caution. Overall great class and work wasn't too hard

reviews.comment: If you are by any means interested in social marketing- this is the class to take. Honestly, Dinin is just a really genuine and nice teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Prof. Dinin's social marketing class was extremely valuable. You learn a lot about social media in ways you've never thought about it. His sarcasm/sense of humor is unique and takes some getting used to, but he's one of the better professors I've had at Duke. He wants you to get good grades and learn, but be ready to participate in class.

Professor Dinin is the man. While many of his classes are a bit quirky and weird, which can be fun or not depending on the type of person/student you are, his social media marketing class is very lecture heavy. His lectures are really interesting and it's a fun, contemporary topic worth learning. Do the work (it's not too tough) and you'll do well.

Very interesting course material that is covered in a hands on, practical manner. Definitely expect to have some amount of work before every class, but the assignments are usually semi-quick and useful. Overall, glad I took the course and Dinin did a great job of teaching it as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I took Dinin's social media marketing class because I thought a class about social media would be cool. It definitely was cool, but not at all how I would expect. Dinin really seems to understand social media in a way I'd never thought of before. It made me much more aware of how people and companies use social media to manipulate others.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Probably one of the most unique classes and professors I've ever had. I wish he gave a bit more feedback on the assignments I turn in. Sometimes it seemed like he wasn't reading everything we submitted. But the classes themselves were awesome.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Definitely one of the best professors on campus. He's actually spent time in the real world building businesses and doing the work he's teaching about, which is a refreshing change of pace.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Dr. D's class changed the way I approach basically everything. I love that he never pretends to have all the answers. He doesn't lecture at students but is more about collaborating with them.
I took Professor Dinin's Learning to Fail class and it completely changed the way I approach everything. It's definitely a must-take class for any student thinking about being an entrepreneur.

Really unusual professor. His expectation is that you can't do what he's asking you to do, which can be frustrating. But, by the end of the semester, you start to understand why class is structured like it is, and you learn to think more critically about your own actions both inside the class and in all your other classes.

Really different class, but in a good way. Spells out things in tons of detail in his syllabus. Almost too much detail. Then people get annoyed at the end of the semester when he does exactly what he says he's going to do. I only mention it because it's fun to watch, so long as you're not one of the ones complaining like some of the reviews here.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Dinin has good ideas and good intentions, I really do believe. The problem is that he lacks the realization that good ideas in theory do not always work in practice. Some of the things that are meant to be productive turn to be almost entirely counterproductive. Good guy at heart. Can be funny. The class is just kind of a bad idea.
great teacher
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Mark was awesome. You learn so much about healthcare, finance, networking, and everything in between. The guest speakers are incredible and the case studies are very cool. Mark is so accessible and easy to talk to. Best SGLE I've taken. Great practice for IB presentations and pitches. Participation matters, but he welcomes any and all questions.
Greatest course I have ever taken.

Hard to sum up how great this course in 350 characters but it is and easily the best I've taken at Duke and probably will ever take. Every lecture was engaging, with outstanding guest speakers from top firms. The projects were insightful and genuinely enjoyable. I can't recommend Professor Augusti's class highly enough.

Despite a class size of ~70, she makes every lecture feel like a seminar by encouraging us to ask questions, asking us questions, and facilitating group discussions. She is a generous and fast grader, willing to help you with anything in her office hours, and overall just a wonderful human being. Workload and exams are very reasonable.

Tori reminded me why I used to love math. Genuinely the best professor I've had at Duke. Kind, accessible, and excited to talk about the content! Like everyone says I wish I could take more math classes with her. Her office hours are amazing and she is a gem. Exams aren't easy but the final project, hw, and presented problems help your grade.

The best teacher I've ever had at Duke. She wants her students to do well, and although the course content was difficult at times she made it 10000x better and explains things very clearly. She is also a very lenient grader. The questions she poses to the class are genuinely interesting, and she fosters such a great class environment.
If I could take every class with her, I would. I would become a Math major if she taught all the courses.

I love Professor Akin! She is like an angel who treats every student with respect, patience, and genuine care. I am excited to go to class every Monday and Wednesday because the classes are so well-designed and engaging (which is rare for math classes). I am very motivated to learn. Her notes are also lovely.

I love Professor Akin. She is like an angel. She treats every student with respect, patience, and genuine care. I am excited to go to class every Monday and Wednesday because the classes are so well-designed and engaging (which is rare for math classes). I am very motivated to learn. Her notes are also lovely.
Best math teacher at duke

Best professor at Duke by far!! Cares about her students. I would definitely recommend taking 242 if you are able to get into the class, the content is hard but she makes it super doable. Tests are hard but projects and other bonuses help bring your grade up. She is a great lecturer, very easy to understand and very easy to ask questions and engage

i love tori so much. she is such an inspiration. discrete math is hard but she makes it doable. her class is very accessible (lectures are posted in a timely manner, there are notes for every lecture on canvas, she responds super fast on Ed). if you can get into this class, do it. the class avgs on her exams were high bc she grades generously.

Tori is by far and above the best professor I have had at Duke. Could not recommend any more. I had an incredibly hard semester but her teaching made this class very doable with minimum time wasted in class. I learned most of the concepts in class, which was really helpful

Tori is hands-down the best professor I have ever had at Duke. If you can get into 242 with her, I would do it. Came into the class very hesitant because I have not had great experience w the math dept. But she really made this class my fav of the semester
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Best Professor I have ever had in my entire Duke career. Gave purpose to my semester. Class is hard if you are not the best at math, like myself, however she gives lots of extra credit opportunities, and very accessible outside of class. Made the class feel like a high school math class. She is literally Ms. Honey from Matilda! No one can compare.

One of the best teachers I've ever had. I read her reviews but thought they were too good to be true, and because this class is mostly taken by math majors. However, she truly deserves the glaze. She explains difficult concepts very clearly and makes anyone, even someone who doesn't feel confident in math, feel like they could be a mathematician.

Great experience taking this class with Professor Akin. Heard good things about them from people I know who took Math 230 with them so I was expecting good things coming in.

Smart enough to explain complex topics in a digestible manner and welcomes (and will at least attempt to answer) all questions.

Learned everyone's name by week 2.

Professor Tori is one of the most down to earth professors at Duke! Even though I've been struggling with math confidence since coming to Duke, she has made me feel competent, capable, and strong about math. She's accessible through her office hours and cares deeply about teaching. A great lecturer. Highly recommend attending lecture!

Tori Akin is the GOAT. She is so incredibly kind and caring, and her lectures are entertaining. Probability is a tough class, but her exams are very fair and she grades extremely leniently. Do whatever you can to take her class.

The best professor I've ever had. If you have to take 230 definitely take it with her! I found the content to be very difficult but there are so many opportunities for help (very responsive on Ed, multiple office hours). A lot of work but is doable if you devote time to the class. Tori sets you up for success! She's the best!!
I was enrolled in a different section with a different prof, but used all of Akins material to learn the course, including stopping by some of her lectures. Tough topic but best math prof at Duke.

The best professor I've had at Duke. May write another review at end of semester, but wanted to submit one now. 

It seems like she teaches and conducts office hours like her life depends on it; I've never seen this level of commitment from a university professor in my life. Hope she teaches more classes in the future if her schedule allows her to.

Tori Akin is one of the most organized, caring, and friendly professors I've ever had. Probability is an incredibly difficult topic, but she always had fantastic and clear explanations for very unintuitive topics. Definitely go to office hours to work through tricky HW problems and clear up questions that you will inevitably have about the content.
Tori Akin is the love of my life. She is the most amazing professor I have ever had. If you have the chance to take a math class with Tori, PLEASE DO.

She is probably the best professor at Duke in the math department. Definetley the most understanding and caring. She even gives partial credit on multiple choice questions on tests. All of the grading is extremely lenient and she really wants her students to succeed.

Professor Akin is hands down the best professor I have had at Duke. Her lectures were amazing, and her lecture pace allowed most students to understand the material. She is also very empathetic to her students, especially about tough material covered in class.

If you have the chance to take a math class with Tori, DO IT! She is the best math professor I have ever had. She makes such intimidating and complex topics very easy to digest, and is a very fair grader. If you need homework help, she will go through any question step by step in office hours. Tests are hard, but manageable if you study.

Tori is EXCEPTIONAL! If I could give her a rating higher than a 5 I would. Super helpful at office hours for the weekly problem sets, and she is VERY generous with partial credit. No math class is a free A, but Tori does everything she can to make it as easy as possible for you. She is so kind and will always answer any question. BEST PROF @ DUKE!

Simply the GOAT PROFESSOR!!! 100% the sweetest person at Duke. Always makes time for her students and stays in OH until everyone's questions have been answered. Reasonable tests. Final exam was a bit rough but she's very generous with grading.

Recorded OH & lectures, fair open-note midterms & final, promotes collaboration on HW, no curve but lets you drop lowest midterm if final is higher, posts annotated notes, always knows how to answer questions. Generally harder for those w/o math background. Great math elective! Tori is a GEM to the department; best and sweetest prof I've ever had!

Tori is an excellent professor. I took the seminar version of this class but whenever she did teach, it was clear and intuitive. She's very caring and understanding. Some of the concepts and test problems in the class were really challenging, but they were open note and untimed which was nice.

One of the best professors at Duke. Always made sure to explain things clearly, provided really good homework help in office hours, and always made sure to answer every question we had. Probability is hard to grasp as a concept, but Dr. Akin goes above and beyond in teaching us and helping us understand.

Professor Akin is so kind and encouraging in this class. She grades everything very leniently. Personally the material was just hard for me to grasp but that is not her fault. She does her best with this course imo.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Tori is the best. I took the seminar version of the course, so most of the teaching was actually done by the students. However, Tori was always there to guide us to the right answers and was available to meet 1 on 1 if needed. She found ways of presenting complicated topics in approachable ways, especially with her skills for proof writing.

Makes complicated math problems seem intuitive. Records office hours in case you can't go. Grades pretty much based on the effort you put in - if you get a wrong answer but have good direction and effort, you will get a lot of the points. Genuinely wish we could clone this woman and have her teach the entire curriculum.
just amazing.
The best professor in the whole word, literally all professors should aspire to be like her. 1000000000/10. Girls run the world!

Akin is one of the best teachers I have had at Duke. She understands the content well, explains the concepts in an understandable way during lectures and office hours (go to OH!), and manages to teach you a lot about probability in a short time. Super sweet, sociable, and understanding- I could not have asked for a better teacher.
Very good lecturer with very clear notes/slides. The workload was very reasonable and really helped to cement the concepts in my head. Overall a very enjoyable class that I learned a lot in.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Deserves the 5/5. Literally amazing and makes me want to major in math. Also check out her fits, they are actually fire.

If I could give Tori more than 5 points in RMP, I would give it. By far the best math professor at Duke. Explains concepts exceptionally well and gives you a lot of practice so you can understand all the material.

Fantastic professor, perhaps the best I have had at Duke. I would genuinely recommend re-arranging your schedule in order to take 230 with Akin. I have no real interest in stats but she made it enjoyable. At the time of writing this, she has a (very rare) perfect 5/5 on this website and I cannot think of a professor that deserves that rating more.
Awesome prof. Super nice

Probably the best profession I've had at Duke or elsewhere. She genuinely cares about her students and seems to always go the extra mile in making sure you understand the material. It's an easy A not because she goes easy on you, but because it's genuinely hard not to learn from her. Just show up to class and watch the office hours for each hw.

I took this in the summer. Probability is a tough class, and moving 3x as fast as a normal semester makes it even tougher. However, Professor Akin was truly amazing and made it a great experience. Probably my favorite professor so far. Great lectures, so caring and incredibly helpful outside class. Take a class with Akin!!! Cant stress it enough!

An amazing professor, quite honestly the most encouraging and helpful math professor I've ever had and I am a math major. She is so sweet. As a girl, this was the only math class at Duke I ever felt comfortable participating in. She stops for questions and will continue to explain until you understand. Take the class with her.

Was extremely understanding of the circumstances this semester having to do a hybrid. Willing to explain topics thoroughly, and is thorough in explaining if you make the effort to ask. Extremely accessible over email, Zoom, and even in-person, all of which I would advantage of. Content is dense, but not impossible, especially if you ask!

The course content itself was pretty confusing especially the lecture format and quality, particularly towards the end. Grading was fair and reasonable on midterms/homework; thought final was a little tough. Tori was unbelievably nice and helpful during in-person lecture and office hours - best professor I've had for a math class. I love her no cap

I was super worried about 230 but taking it with Tori has been the best decision I've ever made, would literally come to Duke JUST to take classes with Tori, makes me want to be a math major, literally just the nicest most helpful person EVER. Tests are fair, if you keep up in class you should be prepared. Easily the best professor I've ever had!!

This is my first ever rating I've given, and I just want to echo what others have said about Prof. Akin. She is literally the sweetest soul ever, SUPER accessible and always willing to help and never makes you feel bad for asking stupid questions. Even tho the content is difficult imo, she is super knowledgeable and explains things really clearly!

The Probability course content was a huge struggle for me, but Professor Akin is a blessing. Makes difficult problems seem simple and always open to questions or offering to explain in other ways. Office hours are beyond helpful! An overall amazing person who really cares about her students' wellbeing and success!

Dr. Akin is by far the best professor I have had at Duke. She is truly a gifted teacher. She is incredibly knowledgeable and does great job of explaining tough concepts. Grading is fair, tests are reasonable, and she wants everyone to be successful. She is always willing to meet with you one-on-one for extra help. Highly recommend.

If God was personified, it would be in Tori. She is LITERALLY the nicest person on the planet. She is caring, accommodating, respectful, just everything you want in a professor. She is so good at making things clear for her students, and she is so accessible outside of class by appointment. GO TO HER OFFICE HOURS! EasilyTHE best professor at Duke

Tori is an amazing professor who is truly skilled and an expert in the classes she teaches. What impressed me most about her was her kindness and commitment to meet with students whenever asked (there were times she met with my group at 9 pm in the library). An amazing person and a great professor! I worked hard but this was a great class

Tori is hands down the best professor in the math department. Math is notoriously hard at Duke and a lot of professors try to make things impossible, but Tori genuinely cares about helping her students learn. If you have to take a math class at Duke and she's teaching it, I would jump on the chance to take it with her over any other professor.

Duke math is notoriously difficult, but Professor Akin is the best math teacher I've come across. She genuinely cares about helping her students do their best, and is always available and willing to help. Graded homework but it is really helpful for exams and learning the material. Go to class or you'll be super lost.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: actually super organized and prepared for class, super helpful and smart, approachable and overall awesome

Best math professor I have had at Duke period. Class: Lectures 3 times per week. Go trust me. You'll be lost if you don't. Grades: Graded homework almost every week, great practice for exams. 3 Midterms + Final. Quizzes in lab material in lab (open notes). Personal: Approachable, great energy. You can tell she is excited to teach us the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Duke math is extremely hard in and of itself, but Tori Akin is one of the few genuinely caring, helpful, amazing math professors who make it bearable. I went to her office hours every week, and she helped me tremendously. Her lectures are amazing; she thoroughly explains every concept. No matter the math course, I highly recommend her!!!

Tori is a fantastic professor. She cares so much about her students and really wants everyone to do well. Make sure you go to class and listen to her lectures. Her tests are difficult so be ready for that, but she's always willing to help if you need it. Probably the best professor you can get for 111.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Honestly she's THE best teacher I've had. Knows all her concepts really well and always gives an outline of what we're gonna learn before we start it. Always goes the extra mile to help us. Has tough tests, but she's an easy grader so it works out in the end. I really wish I'd attended her class more often :(

Math 111L is mandatory and normally taught by graduate students which aren't so great. Tori instead is a professor and really cares about her students and will do everything possible to help you succeed in a class that is designed to fail you. Even though the course is known as hard, Tori makes it much better, is accessible, responsive and helpful.

Hartemink is the best lecturer in the CS department. He limits devices and handwrites lecture notes on the board (no slides). I recommend taking it with a light course load because the homework assignments take a long time, but they are always interesting and help you to deeply understand the material. Most interesting CS class, def take it!!

Alex is the best professor I have at Duke. I feel lucky to be his student. He taught me not only how to be a good student but also how to be a good person. A role model for life.
His class "Human Flourishing in A Digital Age" is especially inspiring. Readings are selected with great taste and push me to think the world differently.
This was my favorite class at Duke. Great professor, unique topic, and very carefully selected interesting readings.
The only course I've ever looked forward to

Absolutely amazing professor, one of the best I've had at Duke. Clearly insanely smart and truly cares about his students and making sure they learn / like his class. Classes are interesting, and he goes the extra mile for his students by bringing food and making class fun in any way he can

Professor Hartemink is highly intelligent and an excellent teacher. His "Intro to Computational Genomics" class will help to make you a better programmer, analyst, and overall interesting person. Out of all my classes at Duke, I would say that I have learned the most in his course. Highly recommend him to the ambitious student.

The grade is mainly from 7 problem sets (no exams). The first 2 are insanely difficult, and after that it becomes quite manageable. This is a compliment, but if I Hartemink wasn't such a great prof, I definitely would've dropped during the first month. He's caring, super clear, INSANELY smart, and just a great guy. Hard class, but very rewarding!

Absolutely brilliant professor who knows how to teach and break down concepts into digestible chunks. Problem sets can be long, but you're given 2 weeks to complete each one. As long as you make good use of office hours and attend lectures, you'll be fine. Probably the best professor I've had at Duke.

He is a great professor and a great person. He is brilliant and has a way of relating everything (even real life stuff) back to bioinformatics/ML. I genuinely enjoyed his class. Beware that he uses a weird "negative" grading scheme, where you start with a 100 and keep getting points taken off for every mistake. Make sure to cover your bases on HW.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Caring

reviews.comment: Not impressed with this professor or the class. The class consists of ten HW assignments that are so harshly graded and subsequently curved that you really don't know your final grade until it's released. I think I would have liked this class more if it wasn't so theoretical, especially since BIO 201 is the only prereq listed for this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This guy is a genius. He triplemajored at Duke and then went to Oxford and MIT. Now he teaches us really interesting algorithms and bio concepts and I have learned so much in this class. I do not like bio at all but from a CS perspective, it is fascinating. 10 problem sets are the whole grade, and TA help is a must. It's a lot of work, but worth it

Professor Hartemink is incredible. Not only is he impressively smart (the guy has like five degrees), but he is a talented teacher as well. Note: While some say his CS260 class is hard, what they really mean is that it is a lot of work. It's actually quite easy to a good grade in (no tests, no midterms, no final, just 7 coding problem sets).

A really incredible professor. His lectures are engaging and he is very passionate about what he teaches. He is amazing at explaining things and I always looked forward to class. Super nice guy and very, very smart. Pretty tough class but I felt like I got a lot out of it, I actually like his philosophy on challenging you and making you think.
Absolutely top quality lecturer. I've gone to a lot of CS lectures in my time, and his is by far the best. Unfortunately, the grading on the assignments can be vague and frustrating.

Hartemink is probably my favorite professor I have ever had. His class is tough, but it's super rewarding if you put in the work and start your assignments early. He is a fantastic lecturer and always explains things so plainly. He also really cares about his students, too, though maybe not necessarily their grades. This is the best class!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: Hartemink is a really smart professor who does a good job of keeping you interested in lectures. Positive grading really isn't as bad as most people here say, you might get docked a few points on a couple assignments because of it. Be prepared to work, the homeworks are extremely long and require a decent amount of bio and CS knowledge
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Smart guy and good at lectures, but assignments were often vaguely worded and usually required 25+ hours in order to finish. His grading system only gives you points for saying specific words, so you end up writing 500+ words per sub question to ensure that you don't lose any potential points. Audit the class if you can just for the lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Best cs professor I've ever had, he makes complicated concepts easy to understand. But despite having no exams, this class is NOT EASY. Analysis portions of bi-weekly homeworks are super open-ended, and he expects you to hit points that aren't explicitly stated in the question. Even going to office hours doesn't guarantee you'll get everything.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Great course, and you learn a lot. Be wary though, it is very difficult to do well on the assignments because of his "positive grading" approach. If you do not hit on every point, even if it is not explicitly asked for in the question, you will lose points.

hartemink is really smart, so his lectures and personality get really pedantic and condescending. the questions on the homework can be open-ended so they only give you points if you write exactly what they want. there's also a participation grade where you basically post on piazza and go to office hours and hope you get full participation credit

One of the best professors I had at Duke. Although he's a compsci professor, I took his Ethics class and he provided pretty interesting insight. He is well-organized and clear about what he expects from his students, but also open and caring to hear and learn new ideas. Highly suggest taking a class of his!

Best professor I've had at Duke. AMAZING lecturer, funny, nice and super distinguished, but genuinely cares about teaching undergrads. Answers every Piazza question win 24 hours. No tests, all Psets. Go to lecture or you're screwed. If you go to class and office hours, Psets are completely doable. Loved this class, it was really rewarding.

This is probably the best class I've taken at Duke. Intellectually engaging, interesting, fun. We got into some pretty difficult material but he makes it so clear that as long as you go to lectures and listen, you will be fine. This class helped me understand my other classes better- couldn't recommend enough!

Possibly the smartest professor at Duke period (Triple Major in Econ CS and Math at Duke, Rhodes scholar, Oxford Masters in Econ and Masters and Ph.D in ECECS from MIT). He's truly excited by his work and takes a genuine interest in teaching, something that few professors at his level do.  He manages to elucidate very difficult concepts.

So chill. Just do prob set and you will be fine. I heard it was hard for some people. If you are a CS major, it will be pretty straightforward (especially if you have taken algorithms or intro to programming). Perl is not too bad, be sure to use EPIC debugger. It will make your life easier.

One of the best professors at Duke. Bioinformatics is a challenging and diverse class that requires a lot of time commitment, especially when biweekly psets are due. However, Alex makes it extremely cogent and clear (if you go to class). Programming isn't necessarily too difficult in this class; however, perl can be hard to pick up.

Alex is the best professor I have had a Duke. He is a great lecturer and the class was extremely interesting. Problem sets are not too bad, especially considering they are the only basis for grading. They usually take about 8-10 hours and are due every 2 weeks. Definitely not as bad as some other classes.

Prof. Hartemink is an excellent lecturer. He is extremely knowledgeable about the subject and can explain everything 5 different ways so that you finally 'get it'. There are no exams so all grade comes from Problem Sets and class participation. The problem sets are difficult and time-consuming, but Alex is always available to help.
the class wasnt fun.
alex rocks

Prof. Hartemink is an excellent professor.  He ties a number of subjects together in his CPS 160 course and does so coherently.  The problem sets are not the easiest things in the world, but since they are the only basis for grading, they are fair.
Excellent Professor; teaches you a lot of interdisciplinary things but teaches them clearly and well.
No Comments

162 is a challenging class and while professor Arce is a really kind and caring person it was sometimes rather hard to follow her lectures. She makes the grading scheme really forgiving however and so it balances out.

Arce is a great person and really cares about everyone's learning. The problem is that she isn't the best of professors. Her slides have lots of typos and they skip over a lot of crucial steps. I would recommend learning from the textbook instead. She is a lenient grader, but you might not understand the material as much as she thinks you do.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Caring

reviews.comment: Arce is a very caring professor and accessible outside office hours, but her lectures are incredible difficult to follow. Typos on the lecture slides and didn't return grades from week 6 until after the final exam.  She wants to encourage her students to succeed, so she was much more lenient with grading, but get the RGB slides if you can.

Arce is friendly and wants students to love learning. However, her lectures spend too long on simple ideas and rush through challenging ones, so heavy reliance on the textbook. In-class Qs not always answered rigorously. Would love a more interactive lecture. 

Grading is generous and there was extra credit, but I wish grades were returned faster!

Professor Arce is easy-going and kind. 162D is difficult because of the large amount of content to cover in 13 weeks, but she grades leniently and is EXTREMELY generous with time on exams. Not complaining but I probably shouldn't have done as well as I did in this class. Stays after class to answer questions. Just a great professor in general

Professor Arce is a great advisor, perfect to discuss a career or major in physics. She's lovely. She cannot teach introductory courses though. She assumes that each student is already proficient in all new material. Even with my reading of the weekly summary and the textbook, I would still struggle during lecture. Wait for another prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She's a very nice and energetic teacher who really likes the material. She brings a lot of demonstration to keep the class interesting and lets the class think about problems before showing the answers. It can be hard to follow her derivations sometimes. The homeworks are well designed, and she is a really easy grader.
Took both CS 201 and 342 with Ola. The goat.

Super awesome and interesting lecturer. While he was great, the course schedule got a little bit messy for certain projects, but honestly didn't matter if you did everything on time (just had weird late submission deadline changes). Could maybe be hard if you have no coding background, but if you took AP CSA you'll be chilling.
w prof w prof w prof
hes the goat
very nice chill funny guy. he was very understanding and used many analogies to explain concepts. some of the projects were overly complicated but overall very good

Course is somewhat disorganized (understandable, he was piloting a few new projects) and Ola goes very fast during lecture. However, there are more than enough resources (lecture recordings, office hours, Ed, etc.) to help you succeed. The grading scheme is very generous, too.

Professor Astrachan has good energy during lectures and is funny, but his slides are disorganized, and his website is difficult to navigate. He struggled to keep up with his course calendar and released projects in an untimely manner. A lot of people who take this class already know the content.
overrated but still pretty good. He is engaging but lectures are useless and the course structure is disorganised. Still, fun at times and is an easy class

ola is very nice and a pretty entertaining character during his lectures. His teaching was decent although I would not say it is as magical as everyone claims. my only issue was i found that the project descriptions and WOTOs were incredibly unorganized and full of errors. there was zero way of knowing your grade or participation points
ola is the goat for a reason. of course, you dont need to read my comment to know he's the goat but yep, he is really good at what he does.
Ola is the definition of aura

Had Ola last semester for 342. While the class content was interesting, he was very disorganized, and I was surprised by the many mishaps as well. He would grade assignments only at the end of the semester, and no one knew their standing in the course. Would not recommend – I'm sure the experience in 201 is better, though.

One of the best professors at Duke. Very interesting class but grading was messy and it was hard to understand what you had to turn in and how were you doing in the class. However, concepts and projects were very fun and engaging. Learned a lot. Would recommend any class he teaches because he is the best.
One of my favorite classes taken at Duke. His class is well structured with clear slideshows and he always livestreams the class.

Honestly such a mess of a class. Syllabus changed multiple times in the last 3 weeks of school. An assignment was migraded which was the difference of a letter grade. Despite numerous desperate attempts to get in contact with ola, i recieved 0 response

Ola is a great professor. His lectures are engaging even if they can be boring sometimes, and it's clear he knows his stuff. The class itself involves a lot of projects and APTs, which are pretty manageable and not that difficult. He has a lot of great resources to help you outside of lecture.

A great class, regardless of whether you plan on majoring in CS or not. There isn't much work, and the tests are generously graded, making the class an easy A. Ola's lectures are accessible and easy to follow, so don't worry if you don't have previous CS experience.

I did the course in 2023 and it was a lot of writing and reading but not more than any other course I ever took. This is the easy elective to take when you have to do other hard core courses. While the large bulk of assignments can be difficult, just stay organized and it's very doable to get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --So many papers

reviews.comment: Ola is the GOAT. He is definitely the best computer science professor. He genuinely cares about his students and is always available to help. He is extremely smart so sometimes he goes over lecture slides a bit quickly, but you can always access them later and are free to ask questions if needed. Definitely take 201 with him.

Lectures good but disorganized. Exam answer keys often had mistakes. I submitted a regrade form, but it was never processed, costing me 10% on my exam grade. I emailed 4 people (including Ola) about this, but no one ever resolved it. I know the class was large, but it's unacceptable for my grade to suffer at a school where I pay $70k to be here.

This class was somewhat difficult at the beginning with no prior Java experience, but definitely doable and got easier throughout the semester. Projects were frustrating at times and some aspects of the class could have been organized better. Lots of resources to help you succeed (practice midterms, TA office hours).

Very structured and relatively easy class if you come in with CS experience. He's a great teacher, but he is stubborn and not the nicest person outside of lectures.
1) he didn't show up to our scheduled flunch
2) grading issue, where I was right but he wouldn't acknowledge it

Ola is knowledgeable and makes class as smooth and forgiving as can be, but I found the lectures a bit scattered; labs aren't bad but can be a bit unclear too; otherwise assignments are really easy. Exams aren't bad, but some of the material wasn't traditional DSA and ended up focusing more on specific Java syntax. Still a great class; def take it.

Grading was confusing but overall the assignments weren't super difficult. The lectures were difficult to follow. It felt very java-specific, and the 1st midterm had a lot of niche syntax questions that even my friend who has been a software engineer for 20+ yrs had no idea what the answers were. It was confusing to figure out how/what to study.

Ola is a great professor. His enthusiasm for the content is evident and infectious—I came in detesting computer science and left loving it. He is very generous and reasonable with his policies so any student should be able to succeed. The course can be a tough transition for someone with no Java experience but other than that is very chill.

Ola is the goat. If you haven't programmed in Java before this class is definitely going to be challenging, but he is very lenient about deadlines and a lot of people completely cheat their way through it. Good lectures, projects are very confusing, but he is very engaging and loves singing happy birthday.

Class is neither easy nor difficult. Ola does a great job with extensions for the whole class when he knows its a busy time. Class policies tend to be geared towards student learning as opposed to punishment.

Amazing professor and teaching style, is consistently available outside of class and is incredibly well-respected and thorough. If you're taking CS201, take it with ola and no one else, he's what makes the course fun & engaging. Lots of "free" points as well, so the class isn't hard either. ola's the goat
Graded an assignment incorrectly which dropped my GPA. Emailed repeatedly about it to no response.

Astrachan's explanation is many at times confusing, his lectures are not easy to follow. The rest of the class teaches you quite a lot, but projects are really useless and take too much time. Take it even if you don't have java experience as long as you've done a bit of programming before.
OLA's class can be a mixed bag - grading is unclear, but the lectures are engaging. unstuck study helped me prep for quizzes and stay on top of the workload.

Grading is done mostly be peers so that's pretty easy. There are a ton of guest speakers: some in person, some by zoom, and they're typically influential and great at talking about their work !! If you do the extra assignments, you're pretty much guaranteed an A-, the A cutoff is pretty high. 

People complaining didn't like the A-, boo-hoo.

The class is graded on too many components. It's annoying having to pay attention to so many things, but the homework isn't hard. Grading is extremely unclear, so you can't keep track of your progress until LWOC. He even tried to change the grading in the middle of the semester. The lectures are good and interesting but not actually necessary.
generational bum this guy gives one morbillion assignments that he cba to grade himself. Then he "grades" your final project (100*np.random.normal(0.5, 0.1)) and calls it a day.

Super easy class - everyone gets an A or A-. However, unclear grading criteria, but this is because OLA does not give af about grades - he just wants students to learn. His lectures are great, and he brings in awesome guest speakers every time. Would recommend this course.

Grading criteria are unclear and can change throughout the semester. 
Graded on too many things and grades are uneasy to track.
Too many tasks with disorganized deadlines.
Unclear exam guidelines (e.g. whether a question is optional or not).

People say it is an easy class but it is really an emotional damage for me.

He's a super fun lecturer and really wants everyone to do well. I had little to no coding experience and am not a comp sci major but was still able to do well. 100% recommend taking the class with friends because the class can get pretty collaborative (ex: partner projects, sharing helper sheets). Love ola he's the best

Although Java can be complicated, Ola makes this class very easy (at least an A-) by giving extra credit as well as allowing AI (GPT and CoPilot) on a lot of the assignments except the actual exams. So you can go through the class without learning anything. Only if you have enough self-discipline will you learn something in this class.
The man is kinda great for cs201. But avoid his 342. Graded on too many stuff. Class super unstructured. He made this class unnecessarily tedious and annoying.

This guy is a decent lecturer. However, he is utterly useless when it comes to class organization. He has this intricate syllabus with 100 different things about grading on it, but he never releases any assignments on time, has unclear instructions, and never responds on ED Discussion.
Compsci201 can at times be conceptually difficult if you don't have much coding experience. That being said, the grading is extremely generous so getting an A is not difficult at all.

ola's the GOAT
'nuff said

Professor Astrachan does a good job teaching and reinforcing the content. I had no Java experience before taking 201, so it took me some time to catch up, but the class is very manageable. A lot of resources to help you with projects/assignments. Lenient with due dates, but don't fall behind on the lectures.

Ola wants you to get an A. Came into the class with 0 coding experience and was able to succeed. Lectures hard to understand, but I'd come back to the recordings later. Lots of assignments but plenty of time, extensions, and lenient grading. Ola is hilarious and always willing to help. Amazing, understanding, dedicated professor! LOVED 201!
I took 102, 201, and 342 with ola. 342 was easy, you get out what you put in. Relevant and current. Amazing speakers

Guest talks every Thursday from alums ranging across a wide spectrum of experiences. Flexible with deadlines. You get out what you put in, but the content is across the board amazingly relevant, topical, interesting, and accessible. Except for the final paper, everything is graded on submitting on time with peer reviews.
Lectures were really interesting. I enjoyed having guest speakers every week. If you do the work you'll get a good grade and the assignments tend to be interesting and enjoyable to do.
Simply the GOAT. Enough said.

Not clear in his explanations, and class time was a complete waste. Didn't seem like he knew what he was doing and relied way too much on his slides. Probably a great 201 professor, but it doesn't seem like he can teach anything else.

By far one of the best (and probably easiest) classes I took. I could have gone by without going to lectures but I didn't want to miss a single one of them. Definitely take a class with him if you can!

For a pass-fail class, Astrachan clearly knows how to make students want to attend every lecture! He organizes speakers a lot and has them talk about their experience in the field and lets students ask questions, and as for course content he's very knowledgeable and his years of experience are very apparent. Take any class you can with Astrachan!

243 is a S/U course where you basically do leetcode problems. Super helpful for SWE internship interviews, and Professor Astrachan brought in guest speakers who work at FAANG-type companies that shared their experiences. I would recommend doing more than the problems he assigns in class if you really want to get good at interview problems.

Very good professor. He was the best professor I've taken so far at Duke, and he gives great lectures. CS201 was not very difficult, especially if you had any java experience. If you are an engineer debating EGR103L or CS201, definitely take this course! I will absolutely take more courses with Owen if possible.
Best professor I've taken during my four years of Duke.

All lectures recorded and he gives many retake options. If you fully understand every lecture and do the exams and apts, definitely will take away something useful from this class. But definitely there is a way to get an A without learning anything. Need to attend discussion sessions.

Compsci 201 was one of the best classes I had last semester. The class was not stressful at all. The TAs are also extremely helpful and the lectures are engaging. (If you've never used Java before, the first 2 weeks might be a little confusing but you'll get the hang of it. You will not need the Zybook)

Don't bother buying zybook. His lectures were good, but often felt long and tiring. The small midterms and the final were easy and low stress. The projects were pretty difficult and confusing, but TAs had a lot of office hours. The APTs and APT quizzes weren't too bad.
