Ola was extremely flexible, but don't procrastinate the projects or the APTs.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Professor Astrachan is amazing. His lectures can be funny and he ties in real-world scenarios. His structure of doing multiple exams as opposed to a couple of midterms greatly reduces the pressure in the class. Don't bother to waste money on the textbook for 201, he explains everything in lecture.
Ola is great. Expectations throughout the course are very clear and there are a million ways to get an A. If you're interested in compsci, this class will teach you all of its foundations.

This class is an easy A but I learned nothing. Ola is a nice guy but he's just not a very organized or understandable lecturer. You won't get to know grade boundaries at the end too so good luck estimating your grade. I actually think it's theoretically possible to not know how to code at all and still pass this class. Discussions were fun tho.

If you have any prior Java experience whatsoever, COMPSCI201 will be incredibly easy for you. Projects/exams are very straightforward, every assignment is open-notes/open-Internet, and there's loads of extra credit (can take every exam twice, lots of make-up problem sets, etc). Ola is a great lecturer - you will get so much out of this class.

Ola is a very outgoing professor and gives many opportunities to boost your grade. Knowing basic Java syntax at the start of the semester is important so you don't fall behind. However, the class does not prepare you enough to answer medium-level SWE questions.

Class is very easy, but my problem is that you do not learn much. Projects are busy work and do not teach anything. Lectures are extremely vague and do not cover content in-depth, leaving students unprepared for intermediate-level interview questions. Does not tell students grade cutoffs, even at the end. Ask to take the skip test if you can.

Fantastic! Ola really knows his stuff and is a giant in the field of computer science. Great lectures! Everyone should take 201 with Ola if possible. Grading system is well laid out from the beginning of the semester, and if you complete every assignment, it is difficult to not get an A. Helps to have some knowledge of Java before but not a must.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Astrachan is hands down the best professor I have ever had. Absolutely amazing lecturer. Made me love computer science. Great person.

Care? ola cares so much. Knowledgeable? Hell yes he knows the stuff cold and he built the APT system we all do a green dance to. Stories? Maybe a few too many, but hes been around and they are generally interesting though sometimes could be shortened. But. ola is the best and if you do everything? Youre ready for SWE interviews for sure.

Astrachan cares about his students and clearly knows what he's talking about, but he needlessly explains things in an overly convoluted way that leaves students confused. He uses excessive tech jargon and then fails to explain the terms, he uses weird analogies rather than just saying it directly. I couldn't stand the lectures after a while.

Funny, relatable prof; really easy elective that teaches you industry/current event/informal things that all CS majors should know about but don't get taught in normal classes; most work gets done in your 3-5 person group made at the beginning, basically if you do everything you get an A. Final group paper 10 pg/person, WOTO's, 2-3 papers

OLA is by far the greatest CS professor at Duke. He is super relatable and you might actually learn something. The class itself might be a bit jumbled in the topics covered, but you go over a lot of things that you wish you had known, but would not have been taught in regular classes. Honestly, ola is someone you'd like to befriend outside of class
Helpful introductory Comp Sci class. Professor is very good.

An amazing professor who really cares about how much you learn. Gives multiple opportunites to re-take tests and chooses your best grade as the grade. He's hilarious and I looked forward to his lectures. The work for this class can be time consuming, but lots of office hours and help. Probably one of the best professors I've had at Duke!
Ola is one of the best professors at Duke. He made the transition to online learning very smooth and was very accommodating to students. You learn so much in this class and never feel stressed out.

CS201 was a great class! Definitely handled the online learning transition really well. Despite the many assignments in the class, I never felt overwhelmed, and the many assignments give you many chances to boost your grade. Very funny and energetic in lectures as well. Come knowing Java, though.
there's a reason why everyone calls ola the goat. come find out for yourself

Really great lecturer, his CS 201 class is fantastic. Knowing Java in advance is definitely an advantage, otherwise you have to learn it quickly at the beginning of the course. Grading is always very clear, and if you work hard to understand the concepts you'll do well.
OLA is absolutely amazing. emphasizes learning to learn, de-emphasizes grades. his caring and funny nature makes lectures quite enjoyable.

I love you ola. Things were a little disorganized at the start of class (since this semester, classes are online), but Astrachan was really understanding about it and gave lots of opportunities for students to show knowledge. Also respect him for helping out during TA hours, he really cares about helping students learn.

Ola is one of the few professors I've encountered who is always thinking about how he can help his students do better in his class. The way he structures CS201 takes a lot of pressure off of his students with flexible deadlines. You can tell he just wants you to learn, not memorize his lectures and restate it on an exam.
Ola is a funny man and his lectures were usually entertaining. The class does have a lot of projects and assignments but nothing super bad.

He is an incredibly interesting professor and makes the class engaging and fun. He truly cares about his students and really focuses on making sure we are learning rather than worrying about grades. This class has great content and is the perfect chance to get to know more about him

CS102 was offered for the first time this semester and it was a bit of a mess. What saved it for me was Professor Astrachan, who is a great lecturer and made me really enjoy computer science. I will be taking CS201 with him next semester.
Professor Astrachan is too good. His lectures are funny and engaging. Best 201 professor by far.
Amazing professor. Best professor I had at Duke so far.

Astrachan has been my favorite professor at Duke so far. He is extremely personable and entertaining during lectures and the class is very project-oriented, which works for a compsci course. I would love to take more classes with him in the future
This class made me enjoy CS even more than I already do, and his lectures are quite entertaining as well. Highly recommend for CS201!
Really entertaining during lectures and cares about the understanding of his students. Would recommend taking his class!
He's super chill

Astrachan is a great lecturer who wants his students to do well in his class. There are a lot of different components (projects, APTs, exams, etc.) that can make this class time-consuming, but there are also plenty of opportunities to earn extra points. This is easily the most fun class I've ever taken at Duke.

Astrachan has been one of my best professors at Duke so far; his lectures are engaging and entertaining (I enjoyed class), and he is incredibly fair with his assignments and tests, and he wants everyone to succeed. When the class performed badly on the midterm, he was generous with the ability to re-do some of the questions for credit back.

compsci 201 with him is the best. very fair and reasonable assessments, relatively organized for such a large class. learned a lot. great preparation for technical interviews. so glad I got to take it with him!

Lectures lack in substance, about 1/3rd of the lecture is actually useful, but by the time he gets there, you're tuned out. The assignments are pretty straightforward but seem kind of pointless. The APTs, however, are extremely useful. This class is very difficult for those without much prior experience in CS, but is v useful and rewarding.

Astrachan's lectures were entertaining and generally helpful. He is sometimes disorganized, but not to the point that it causes major stress or impacts your grade. There's a decent amount of work, but if you get it all done you will likely get at least an A-. Overall, I learned a lot without too much stress - definitely recommend him for CS 201.

Be ready for a gigantic class. The lecture was pretty disorganized but very funny (ola really tries to get the attention of the class). Tests are super easy with an A- median. CS201 is a good intro class to Compsci. It is not super necessary to take CS101 ahead of this even if you haven't had AP CS

Interesting, funny guy. Class is huge (300+) so can be hard to pay attention but he tries to make it interesting and lectures available online. Gives you a solid foundation of Java and made me want to take more compsci. Throws a ton of free points at you and assignments/tests aren't too tough - median grade is an A-. Is pretty disorganized though

Professor Astrachan is a great professor for 201 really cementing these comp sci topics in your head. The class is very project and test based, but the tests and projects are fair. My only critique with this class would be that at times, disorganized.
So many things to do  neverending!! but lectures are great and the UTAs are fantastic. They make all the difference
Great professor! A bit disorganized, but he is a master of the material and really knows how to teach.

Astrachan is a great lecturer and this class was fun! I would often look forward going to class. Work is not too difficult but expect to spend a fair amount of time on the class. One complaint is that we never got feedback on our assignments, but everything ended up working out in the end. Would recommend him as a professor overall though!

Keep up with all the assignments, go to lab, do the WOTOs, and GO TO OFFICE HOURS IF YOU HAVE QUESTIONS! Lectures are streamed online, which is a definite plus. I bombed two of the exams and I suck pretty badly at CS but still somehow managed to walk away with an A-... THERE IS ALWAYS ROOM FOR REDEMPTION IN THIS CLASS. All hail Ola.
Absolutely loved his class! He really makes his lectures fun!

This guy is an unclear lecturer. He is also pretty disorganized. CS201 was one of the worst classes that I've taken at Duke so far. The due dates were always up in the air, you don't really know how you're doing in the class until the end of the semester, and he doesn't really emphasize important points in lectures.

Astrachan is really the best lecturer I have encountered so far. Not only is he super hilarious (at least during lectures), but he is able to explain difficult concepts in an amazingly clear and interesting manner. The quality and depth of his lectures have also improved from previous semesters. You should get an A if you work reasonably hard.

Prof. Astrachan is a great lecturer, but taking a seminar with him was awful. He did very little to help mediate discussion, and sometimes it felt like he hadn't even read the articles he assigned. He only graded two of our many assignments, and he regularly missed meetings scheduled with students. He was also rude to some of the students in class.

It was hard in the beginning to adjust from Python to Java if you came from 101. Projects were confusing and there was a lot of homework, whether it was projects or APTs. Luckily the APT solutions were posted. Tests weren't too bad and they made the higher midterm grade your total midterm grade.

Astrachan is a great lecturer, but can't do seminars. What you need for a good seminar -- communication, feedback, guided discussions -- are Astrachan's weaknesses. He frequently talks over students and seems to prefer refuting things we say rather than helping us actually learn. The upside is, since he's so disorganized, the class is really easy.
Good lecturer but really bad on turning assignments back to students in a timely manner

Astrachan, overall, is a pretty funny and nice guy. However, I don't think he's the best professor, contrary to what people said in previous years. At least my year, grading was quite slow and I felt as if the lectures in the class were disorganized. However, I do think that if you put in effort, you will learn quite a lot in an important CS class!

Had no java experience to start but got full credit on APTs and assignments because of help hours. Can be hard to focus during his lectures, but they're recorded so watching them was very useful. Astrachan was disorganized the whole semester. Got brutalized on the first test and didn't do well on the second but a good final can make up for it.
Best professor ever! Take his class even if you hate compsci. I do, and it was still a great experience :)
He's the man.

Very funny professor who is knowledgeable in the field, and deserves more credit than he gives himself for his programming skills. However some of the lectures cover a variety of unrelated topics and there is little class participation except for Google forms and class activities. Labs were hands-off and included following premade instructions.

Not a very difficult class. Out of all 101 professors, he's definitely the way to go. There were two professors that semester (him and Rogers). It was obvious that Astrachan was the better professor. He was funny and made CS as interesting as possible.
Great Professor. The class was super easy, but he made lectures interesting and funny.

Learning to code is a really useful skill.  I liked the class and APTs were fun but the assignments were so annoying.  Get ahead as much as you can because at the end of the semester the assignments get a lot tougher and take more time. Online textbook is free and interactive

Ola was the only reason I went to lectures; he's hilarious and highlights certain topics I would've glossed over on my own. He's really nice, and helped me with Eclipse on multiple occasions. Lots of assignments and APTs, but most of them are easy(1 or 2 were unclear) and tests were easy and fair. Would definitely recommend. And he got us cupcakes.

Class no longer has extra credit. Assignments are long, sometimes unclear & challenge problems are required. His directions to problems aren't always easy to understand.   Prof. seems nice in class but felt rushed and to the point 1:1. Exams 1&2 are fair but final was difficult and felt like it was there to lessen the  total # of As in the class.

Great professor, entertaining lectures.  Expect weekly APTs, assignments, reading quizzes & APT Quizzes.  Class carries a large work load. Assignments are challenging & very time consuming. Easy to do well, but get the impression the course is more difficult than previous semesters. Would highly recommend Owen. Put in the work & you'll do fine.

Definitely an engaging lecturer, but not the best computer science professor out there. It is just as helpful to self teach the course material. At times it felt as if Astrachan was more concerned with being liked by the students than teaching the course.
Great prof! really engaging in class and brings in cupcakes for the whole lecture if it's your birthday
Great professor stuck teaching an intro-level course.  Really nice guy and always willing to help.
Interesting class, great material. Not too hard, most students get an A-. Professor Astrachan is great at teaching you a little bit about a lot of things, which is perfect for a class like this.
Fabulous, fabulous prof during first two weeks of class. Connects course to world and life. Clear, interesting, motivating.

We Skyped with a guy from Yale who redid their course evals. Labs were easy, but personalized to our interests! Guided by current events and the news, learned skills and how the Internet works. Cybercitizen: I'm in. Astrachan doesn't grade fast enough, but the class is great.
Grades take forever to be reported and assignments are vague/grading is arbitrary...

Professor Astrachan is a really funny and genuinely nice professor. I learned a lot of information that I feel is actually useful and relevant to my life. However, we have received almost no grades or feedback on our work. It's hard to ensure success if you do not know whether or not you are meeting expectations along the way.
10/10 would take class with again

Prof Astrachan is probably the one of the funnest professor at Duke, he's eccentric and hilarious. Assignments not hard in themselves, BUT the assignment instructions are sometimes vague or just confusing. Still he clarifies if you ask him personally! Only real complaint I have is sometimes he is tardy on grading. BUT the class is still worth it!

He is one of those professors that can "teach" but that are not good "teachers". BE CAREFUL with your grades in his classes. He tends to give arbitrary grades with no feedback and if you get docked points, you might have no idea why you got docked points (it might even be an typographical mistake on his part, you just wouldn't know unless you ask)

His teaches really well! Things to warn you about: 1) Extra credit assignments are not "extra" but mandatory if you want to get an A or A+. 2) His grammar is really bad in directions for homework assignment. This gets really annoying as the length of direction increases. 3) The class is not as easy as you might think! Definitely harder than EOS101.
Professor Astrachan is an absolute inspiration. His passion for computer science is infectious and he is arguably the most compassionate teacher I have ever met.

One of the greatest teachers I've ever had.  Extremely engaging, interesting, funny, and passionate about his topic.  His goal really is to get people excited about CS and introduce students to the field.  Very friendly intro course, and he's extremely approachable in office hours.  Definitely take a class with Prof Astrachan if you can.

Owen is fun, engaging, and truly passionate about the field. Often the assignment instructions are somewhat hard to follow. I didn't appreciate when he would say an assignment was easy and wouldn't take very long, but I would end up spending hours on it. It made me feel like I wasn't good enough, but in reality everyone learns at a different speed.

Professor Ola is very passionate about his subject and gives students lots of opportunities to improve their grade. He teaches in such a way that it is hard to get notes of 'this does X', so you end up learning by absorption, a fun change from typical classes. Assignments are long but there is lots of help available, they are how you really learn.

Astrachan is an entertaining professor that makes pretty dry material interesting. In additional the course assignments are pretty good. The class is easy and you can expect an A- if you do the work well; however, Astrachan is pretty reluctant to give out As. Be warned.

Ola is awesome! Very funny and a very good professor! CS 101 is one of the funnest classes you will take here at Duke. No prior knowledge of programming is required! He makes things very very simple to understand, and the assignments he puts up are actually FUN. Because of him I now want to major in CompSci.
Ola is a God. Enough said. (he does ramble a bit though, but it's rather amusing)

Prof Astrachan is a funny and engaging professor/lecturer. The class was too easy in my opinion, and perhaps the powerpoints could be done clearer or more professionally. Also, perhaps following the schedule on the syllabus exactly and using the textbook more often could be extremely helpful.

I took his intro to comp. sci 51 class in 1987 and later an independent study class and graduated with a CS degree in 1991 from Duke. I started Duke to be pre-med and major in biology, but finished with a degree in CS. I'm now a general surgeon in SC, but he's the only professor of CS that I remember bc of his passion for the art of CS.  - Martin

Ola is a fun and quirky prof and he really tries to make this an easy QS (or EI) credit for people who don't understand or care about compsci.  That said, he can go off-topic and get behind on grading, which makes the class a lot less fun.

Take his class.  Prof Astrachan is really nice and his class is easy, just make sure to do each assignment and you will do great.  The reading summaries are the most important part of the course because everything else is pretty much an easy A
He's awesome. Take anything he is teaching.
My favorite class at Duke. Ola is hilarious and the material is extremely interesting and relevant. You have to take this class!
Awesome professor who makes lectures engaging and funny. Very approachable outside of class and extremely helpful. It's not difficult to do well in the class if you're willing to put in the work.

Awesome professor, provides lots of extra credit opportunities. Easy to do well in if you are willing to put in the time. Extremely helpful and approachable outside of class. Makes lectures engaging and funny.
He's really nice and keeps the class engaged. The assignments often take an extremely long time and there are alot of them, though.

Class requirements are difficult to understand and at the end of the year end up being curved which is not what I expected. Lectures are boring and hard to follow. I could not take notes from his slides and most times I did not follow what point he was trying to make. Looking for an easy QS? Look elsewhere.
Compsci 82 is so interesting and it requires minimum amount of effort. Definitely take this class with ola!

He is a good professor who is super engaging, funny, energetic, and passionate about computer science. His lectures weren't entirely useful or helpful in learning how to learn how to program but always entertaining. Class wasn't terribly difficult and the exams were easy. Very lenient and easy going as well. Prepare to watch Youtube videos. A lot.

Astrachan is a very engaging lecturer, funny and easygoing. He really brings the concepts to life. If you are confident in your computer science abilities and are comfortable receiving very limited feedback on your work (read: no projects graded/commented until the final week of classes), you will enjoy this class. If you just want a QS, take CS72.
Best class at Duke. ola is amazing!

I LOVE Professor Astrachan!!!  Favorite professor, hilarious, entertaining lectures. But, I hate his class.  Most people did fine, but I struggled all semester.  You basically write programs to return sought information in different situations.  You'd probably do fine, but if CompSci isn't your thing, don't take it just for the QS (like I did).
Great lecturer, makes you want to come to class. Easy test, straightforward material. Great class to fill requirements
Great professor.  Always entertaining during lectures and tries really heard to make sure everyone understands the material.

This class is great, I'm not sure what the other person was thinking that wrote that ola is a jerk. He's got some idiosyncracies, but lectures are great and the assignments are interesting. Don't expect to get grades back soon though.

Great Professor, he's really nice and funny and tries to mke the classes fun and interesting with guest speakers and crazy youtube vids. You do have to come to class but they're usually not boring. The assignments can be a pain, but they're only every two weeks and he gives mad extra credit

Great class. Below minimal effort can get you an A, and if you have any interest in the subject material the lectures and readings are really interesting. Guest lecturers were very impressive as well. Astrachan is also extremely accessible and funny.

Very humorous and entertaining lector.  Tests were never too hard, they just required thinking (studying doesn't help that much since tests are open-note and open-book).  Projects are fun and interesting, and even though I'm not a comp sci major, I definitely am glad I took this course.  I'm not sure if there's a curve, if so it's quite generous.

i always left class smiling. i didn't find the tests that hard (def. not super easy though). not a hard grader. it's hard to keep up with all of the work. doesn't give feedback on assignments until after final (but gives tests back in a week).
Great professor. His laid back and relaxed attitude makes for great classroom atmosphere that produced some memorable moments. Astrachan is the man.
Easy QS/Writing class. Awesome awesome and is super nice/helpful/fun.
great easy QS class, professor is very laid back and funny, highly recommended

awful. didn't learn a thing. lectures were 85% useless, and projects were tangentially related to class at best. doesn't even look at your code, just grades end result. how are you supposed to learn like that? lots of lecturing personality, but no substance. completely overrated professor.
Hot.

He did a terrible job of teaching this course. 75% of lectures were COMPLETELY useless. It's like he didn't even care. He was very disorganized. TAs were fairly clueless, probably because he didn't tell them much either. After all this, his grading was as harsh as ever.
Excellent Professor!
he is a GREAT professor

Good lecturer, though the lectures are all over the place.  Some explanations are more confusing than helpful.  His lectures make you feel like you completely know the material, but when it comes to the tests, they are definitely harder.  Nice guy, though.

He is a great lecturer.  You don't have to suffer from reading the boring book.  He is sometimes really arrogant in his office hours when you ask some really easy questions.  He is extremely disorganized and he does not care about his students at all when he is not in his office.
Great lecturer, gets the information across without boring you to tears. Cares about his students and about teaching. Funny, nice guy.

Difficult class, but OLA teaches really well and is very entertaining in class. Just sit there, relax, and you'll soak in the knowledge, so forget the dense/hard-to-read text. The mix of assignments, worksheets, APT's, and great lectures will help you learn a lot, although it does take much effort to stay on top of things too.
Funny guy, great guy, but even if you do well on everything and play his games, you aren't guaranteed an A. He is also very busy and doesn't answer emails.

I felt a bit lost some times because he assumed we were all geeks and knew CPS stuff he didn't teach. E.g. all the compiling stuff, all the GUI stuff, UML, etc. If you just want to know how to write the fastest and most efficient algorithms OLA is the man! But don't be surprised if you have to learn some of the other stuff on your own.
A little spacey, but that's cool

Very entertaining lecturer, makes you want to go to class just to hear his lecture.  Almost guaranteed a B- at very least, even if you do very poorly on midterms.  But not easy to get an A.  Downside is his lack of organization.  Dont know your exact grades on anything until well after the final.

Entertaining lecturer. Gives lots of bonus, possible to end class with over 100%. Do all work and guranteed B, do OK on tests and an A. Very disorganized leading to slow grading. This means no real feedback til after final.
Not that good!

The course is easier than peeing in a lake.  Astrachan's a funny guy and makes people laugh a lot.  BUT he also has ADD or something -- never stays on track or on topic, and his explanations tend to be more confusing than helpful.  Takes questions, but makes you feel like an idiot if you ask them.

Really funny guy. His off the wall analogies are helpful and he keeps his lectures entertaining. If you show up to class, do your work, and study just a little, you'll get out with at least a B, guaranteed.
Great Lecturer, but dont expect him to babystep your way through. Not much helpful. But worth taking for the knowledge he imparts.
his class is interesting
Takes questions during class which is very helpful.  Makes class laugh every day.  Also makes bets against the class (never loses tho).
Great Teacher.  He's very funny and exciting and therefore easily keeps your attention.
Wonderful, entertaining, well-versed lecturer.
best lecturer at duke, and very, very knowledgeable when it comes to helping with code
He's a fun teacher, and he's not boring like some other CS teachers ::glares at Ramm::
great entertaining professor, but dont expect him to be very helpful during office hours and stuff. You'll soon know how dumb you are.
No Comments
No Comments
Helpful in class but not good one on one.  Good lecturor
No Comments
Excellent prof.  Very easy to understand.  Makes learning fun!
Lectures are okay

He covers 4 algorithms in 2 classes and manages to explain all of them badly. The lecturing is so unclear that you have to read notes outside of class and do random questions on Prairie learn to supplement the subpar teaching. Abdul Bari is a better resource.
He's a good professor. I came in with no prior Python experience, and I did well in the course. Start the coding assignments early because some of them are pretty difficult or take a lot of time.
DO NOT TAKE A CLASS WITH HIM! If you value your mental health, do not take this class with him. Even the TAs did not know how to do most of it.

Has no idea how to teach. WORST professor in the CS department. PLEASE avoid any class he teaches. He is not only the worst lecturer but actually wants you to fail. Makes it hard to study for tests barely providing material and answer keys. Makes you hate CS even though you might love it.  Absolutely hated this class.

Worst professor Ive ever had. Apart from the fact that he's not good at lecturing, he gave no solutions to practice problems so you had to do everything yourself with no guidance, and were forced to rely on LLMs replies who were wrong 90% of the time,
Holy cow. The answer is no. The answer is no. Do not take this class.

I kinda felt bad for Dr. Steiger as a lot of people complained heavily about things he had little access over, but there were definitely things that could have been improved on. Lots of typos in everything (including midterms and finals) and very disorganized class overall. Grades took forever to be released. Heavy curve applied at the end tho…

Not sure why everyone is so mad about the instruction of this course. Practice materials are given - if you don't know the answers talk to an LLM. Lectures are very clear and thorough (and dry) but teach you everything you need to know. I would love to take another class with as clear of expectations as this one.

Took CS 230 with Prof Steiger and it was incredibly disorganized. 90% of the time we had to ask for lecture notes, discussion notes, and class documents to be posted. Sometimes, homework wouldn't be posted until 2-3 days before it was due. Multiple mistakes and typos on homework. No solutions for exam practice problems.

Provides a bunch of practice question for exams but not actual practice tests. Exams were quite harshly graded, every little detail of the proof had to be spot on. Lectures very dry, but lack of attendance doesn't help. Discussions felt useless. Great response time on Ed. In lecture, just rewrote his own notes/ proofs, which doesn't really help us.

Not sure why everyone is on here complaining. Steiger kept it real the entire semester. Yes Discrete math is not easy and there is a lot of material covered, but that's just the reality of a core computer science course. Offered practice problems for exams. Exams are difficult but keep you honest to understand the class material. Fair grading.

Steiger sets his students up to fail, we had people begging to get solutions for practice questions. Lectures and notes are so confusing and messy. Exams are basically impossible to do good on, given that we have NO PRACTICE! not even a cheat sheet?

Horrible professor. He genuinely does not need to teach again. Lectures are so boring. He doesn't give any test practice materials or previous answers to practice problems. Canceled all of the office hours for the final. Notes are terrible to read (I can get a brain hemorrhage reading them). He sets his students up for failure!!

Terrible communication outside of ED. I understand that discrete is supposed to be a hard class, but the way he teaches it just takes it to another level of unbearable. Won't post practice exam answers, and all his notes are super messy to read/understand. Most of his homeworks are either too hard or directly not applicable to exam materials.
Idk why others complain. This was a chill course in comparison. Perhaps there exists better, but he was fine

Do not take any class with this professor. He sets his students up for failure. Students are so scared to advocate for themselves. He doesn't provide any test examples or solutions to practice problems, and canceled ALL OF OFFICE HOURS DURING FINALS. What kind of professor does this to their students???
(CS230) Does not listen to student feedback. Lectures are extremely boring. The midterms are nearly impossible to score high on with the time given + problem difficulty.
CS 230. Lectures were extremely boring, no slides. Tests and p-sets were very difficult, often problems that we were never taught how to solve. Avoid if possible.
The positive thing about Prof. Steiger is being responsive on Ed. The negatives are essentially everything else (the lectures, the course structure, etc.)
Took CS 230 with Professor Steiger. Horribly managed: it took weeks to receive feedback from exams or homework, given "fodder" questions but with no answer keys to check our work, etc. Avoid.

Genuinely, what is the point of posting practice exam problems if you don't post the answer key? Idk just seems like a lazy professor. If you're not going to have lecture slides, at least have good handwriting. Waffles a lot with no points.

CS230
I can tell Professor Steiger knows the material well himself, but he does not know to articulate his thoughts or teach well at all. Expect to learn all course content on your own.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Do not recommend wasn't fun and I think just kinda misunderstood teaching
Great lecturer for 330.

Steiger gives clear expectations on what will be in exams and is insanely active on Ed (it is really impressive). His lectures are moderately dry but are to the point and easy to follow regardless of experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Steiger took over the second half of the class for Munagala and his lectures/lecture notes were much easier to follow/digest. He's an great lecturer who makes difficult topics simple and wants his students to succeed in what is a tricky class. Also incredibly detailed and fast responses on ED!

Professor Munagala had to travel for the second half of the 330 semester, so Professor Steiger stepped in to teach the course. I found his lectures to be intelligent and intuitive—he's a good computer science professor, especially for advanced topics.

I am taking his computational geometry course right now. It is a small class but Prof. Steiger is very caring and wants all his students to succeed. Low stress because it is a project based course. Definitely worthwhile to have.
Why wouldn't you want to take a class with him!
CS330: great prof, take if possible

Professor Steiger is a great professor that cares about his students and making sure they understand the material. He is more than happy to answer questions and makes sure that expectations on homework or exams are perfectly clear. I would highly recommend taking anything with him.

Class was a disaster. Lectures weren't engaging AT ALL just reads off slides.  Commentary was basically for people who knew a decent amount already. Every lecture we would never get through the material. Textbook was unreasonably long to read before lecture. Take Astrachan, watching his videos saved my grade and hes actually engaging.

I'm unsure of why so many people felt this class was overly difficult (perhaps so in comparison, but really not in practice). We had half a letter grade of raw extra credit, a final that can knock out all three exams, an Ed discussion always answered quickly, lectures that *taught the material* as he would ask it (book not needed). It was solid.

This was his first semester teaching 201 and the midterms were made to be unnecessarily hard. Not a super engaging lecturer. However, was very generous in the end with extra credit and a more fair final exam format. Nice guy but would recommend taking 201 with Astrachan if possible instead. Was a discouraging class and made me lose interest in SWE.
has a good attitude but he reads off his lecture - would definitely recommend another cs lecturer if you get the chance

Worst 201 professor. Lectures were the most boring things and he would literally just read off the slides. He requires participation quizzes for attendance as well. Tests weren't the worst, but his teaching style was awful.

If you have the opportunity to take 201 with Astrachan, do it. Steiger wasn't terrible, but his exams were considerably more difficult and lectures were a drag. Those who took 201 with Astrachan seemed to have a much more positive experience in all departments.
Great!

He reads off the lecture slides and makes you do little participation quizzes. Why do I have to attend in person if you are just going to read the lecture notes? He will put you to sleep in the lecture room.

Course logistics was a total disaster. Right before final exam it was announced that final exam grade can replace midterm grades if you got higher in the part but not vice versa - which was nowhere to find from the syllabus. Why attend midterms then? Only two TAs that could not care less for a course of ~50 people. No regrade for final exam.

DO NOT TAKE HIS COURSE! The equivalent course at Duke is much better than his. His lecture is confusing and his lab report has a really vague grading criteria. Idk how I passed this course but it took my GPA a nose dive
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Amazing person, always ready to help you. Difficult tests, but there are difficult concepts, so it's understandable. He's like my father now.
Floyd is like my mother at this point. If you take him then you can also have two moms.
p cool!!!!
i love this guy if u say he's bad ur lying
floyd beckford my goat!!!!

CHEM110 at DKU is not an intro class. Basics are not taught till later, but labs beforehand require the basics. Overall this class teaches a lot. If you don't have any background in Chem it will be hard to catch up in 7 weeks. Unfortunately, I had overbooked myself for the session I took it and couldn't spend the necessary time on the class.

Dr. Beckford's style of teaching is clear and engaging. He answers every question in a clear and friendly way. However, the workload is VERY heavy (weekly lab report & homework, and lots of exams), and he is really a tough grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Floyd is a good person. However, I don't think his way to manage classes is proper. He uploaded videos instead of giving lectures. His recitation courses are terrible too because they look like a mess. The exams are very difficult and have nothing to do with what he taught. The WORST thing is that he NEVER replies to your emails.

Professor Beckford is generally a good person. His online lecture videos are clear and rather detailed, and I think that they are good enough. He grades on an absolute scale that is based on how well you do on each homework assignment, each reading quiz, each lab report, and each test, so you have to pay attention to everything you do.

He is not a bad person, but his assignments were filled with errors, and every single test had errors. He makes it clear he is a tough grader but by that his standards are absolutely unrealistic. The exams were so long that nobody could even finish reading more than 70% of the exam let alone attempt the exam itself.

SHES SO GOOD. If you can, definitely take egr201 with Bansal. She is super organized, gives you tons of opportunities to raise your grade, and is so accessible outside of class with tons of office hours. She was awesome

Dr. Bansal was an incredible professor for EGR101. Her candid feedback and advice helped propel the success of my team's first year design project, and made my first engineering experience memorable. Dr. Bansal's instruction actively challenged me to think in new ways, challenge my own ideas, and embrace adversity whilst overcoming it.
amaze. Loved this class and prof. Gives great feedback. Sometimes harsh but very clear instructions!
Amazing prof. Helped me a lot throughout the year. Cares a lot about the class and students. Great office hours.

Dr. Bansal is very personable and always willing to provide advice specific to the course or BME curriculum. The examples provided in lecture align well with the quizzes and final exam, so you will always know what to expect. Though the content is rather dry, she does a good job of connecting the topics to real-life applications (usually BME).

She teaches this class like every student is 5 years old, it honestly felt demeaning. She answered questions with reductive, hand-wavey (and often wrong) answers that made me question if she understood even the most basic parts of the material. It's an easy A, but don't take her if you expect to be taught anything. The labs are graded very harshly.
great prof. I love her. but assigns a lot of homework. prepares me well

How did she become a professor? Maybe lost a bet. Lectures feel like watching someone narrate a PDF in slow pain. Assigns 10-page lab reports over holidays like it's a gift. She rewrites the course yearly like she's dropping a mixtape, but it's still trash. Office hours? Only when Jupiter aligns with Mars... Unreal vibes, make sure to be perfect!

Makes attendance mandatory half way through the year because people don't show up to lectures which is just mindlessly copying down slides. Will be passive aggressive when you call her out nicely and be prepared to work on labs which have terrible rubrics over any break because she things it's fair to assign things over then!

She claims to remake the course every year to make it better but doesn't take feedback during the semester politely. Not open outside of class and will claim to do many things but fall short over 80% of the time. She is pretty fake and will act all nice but is genuinely lazy and will “run out of time” to look over things even though it's her job!

Knowledgeable professor who cares about your growth as an engineer. Definitely have to adjust to harsh/sometimes unclear grading at the start but you will learn to succeed in both writing and engineering assignments as the semester goes on. Make use of all your resources as well in EGR 101 (Dr. Bansal, other profs, technical mentor, TA's, etc.)!

Lectures involve mindlessly writing down content on the slides w/ no deeper understanding of content. We learn an incredible amount of useless information. She is not accommodating and failed to make a practice exam because she "didn't have time". She doesn't hold OH outside of 8-5 because she values family time yet assigns lab reports over breaks.
Believed that nobody deserved a 100, but class wasn't inherently difficult. Didn't aid us too much on our project but would get upset when we didn't make a lot of progress??
Dr. Bansal is a great professor. Her class and exams are fair. The labs are graded harshly but it is still more than doable. 10/10 would take again.

Felipe lacks compassion and often leaves the class more confused at the end of lectures than they were beforehand. Very disorganized in his lectures and preparation for the class. If you want to ask him questions outside of class, don't count on it: "I'm too busy with X" will be the response you invariably receive from him.

Incredibly disorganized| his lectures go all over the place| He presents as a knowledgeable expert on the topic, but in reality, he doesn't appear to have a good sense of the material he lectures on. Outside of the class, you'll be lucky if he responds to an email (even if brief) within 15 days: He's always "too busy" with other things

I wish I could take this class all over again. Professor De Brigard's class made me want to take more neuroscience and philosophy classes as soon as I could. Take light notes and focus on what he says, not on the slides. He often goes off-topic, but it's often way more interesting and entertaining!

Very unorganized professor. Very all over the place lecturer - extremely hard to follow. Fails to explain complicated readings clearly and then expects us to write on said readings. Says he doesn't care about grades and wants us just to learn but then proceeds to grade harshly. Nice guy but would never take a class with him again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Felipe de Brigard is an interesting lecturer with a clear, deep understanding of neuroscience and philosophy concepts. However, his explanations can often be more confusing than necessary and I wish he would have shared more of his own opinion. The class is more reading heavy than I primarily expected.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Felipe was truly a funny guy and good lecturer - clearly very passionate. But he was extremely inaccessible outside of class, took up to 3 days to respond to emails (if at all), ended up cancelling exams and and papers previously noted on the syllabus, and changing the grading distribution at the last minute

Dr. De Brigard is a fantastic professor and human being. He is incredibly nice, accessible, friendly and has a wonderful sense of humor, all of which helped me to more easily grasp conceptually challenging concepts at the intersection of philosophy and neuroscience. He's passionate about his class and will push you to question assumptions in neuro.
Waste of time

His class has taught me so much, not just about math, but about how to think more clearly and confidently when solving problems.His passion for teaching and dedication to his students makes his class both challenging and enjoyable, and I've learned more in his class than I ever thought I could.

Caring, humble, and amazing at math. I could glaze him forever, but you probably get the point. Don't take this class if you hate gaining new perspectives on topics you wouldn't have dreamed about before. Highly recommend to literally everyone else.

Professor Bray is easily one of the most knowledgeable profs Ive had. The class is super easy and allows you to practice your presentation skills. Bray loves getting sidetracked and will talk about everything under the sun other than actual math, but I dont mind because I always leave class with a new unique perspective on something. He's a cutie.
Fun stories and energetic class activities. Highly recommend.

Hubert Bray changed my life. I entered as an undecided major, but now I am inspired to puruse mathematics all because of his teachings. He once showed me Oppenheimer and told me to read his book Trevor the Time Travelor. Now, I want to be greatest mathematician in universe like Dr. Bray!

Really made my first semester freshman year the best. The biggest part of this class are the essays, but as long as you actually put effort in your work, you will get an A. He presents very fascinating information information in his lectures, and is a very understandable person.

Easily the best class I have ever taken. Even though Hubert Bray is the head of the math department and probably the smartest person you will ever meet, he is incredibly humble and easy going. We would joke around with him all the time, and it was basically impossible not to get an A. He also presents fascinating concepts. Highly recommend.

This man is awesome and very wise, but he does give a lot of homework so this class will be a big time commitment especially if you're doing it over the summer. He gets sidetracked a lot during lectures but it's always super interesting so I'm cool with it. Tests are exactly like the practice tests and he curves if they're harder than normal
Taken over the summer. Prof Bray believes that students learn through homework, so homework is inordinate. Lectures are engaging but a fair bit of content is left for self study in the textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Inspirational--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Inspiring

Super nice guy who wants you to do well in the class. There are 4 papers that are connected to presentations but nothing too bad. We had a lot of open discussions that we're necessarily on the topics we were learning about but he always tried to keep us engaged and let us debate current topics during the class.
Very knowledgeable about the subject. Takes less than 5 seconds to answer most question. Very caring for his students.

The majority of the class could be summarized Multi2.0. The homeworks are ungodly long and boring. This is an entire class to understand the Gauss-Bonnet Theorem, which could be done in 4-5 lectures. The exam structure incentivizes memorization of practice exams over understanding. I would have rather gotten a worse grade and learned more.
One of the most enjoyable courses Ive taken as a math major.

Dr. Bray is a fantastic person and a great professor. Makes you feel cared for in the class while also pushing you to do your best. Real passion for math that shines in his lectures, overall a lot of fun! Learnt a lot in this class, in a way I will not forget. PS: Start your HW early if you want to get it done at all.

Professor Bray is a very engaging and interesting professor. He aims to make his classes enjoyable and informative, and succeeds in both endeavors. I would highly recommend taking a course with Professor Bray!
Hubert is my favorite professor at Duke, incredibly passionate about Math and Physics, highly highly recommend taking a class with him. Just all-round awesome.

You can tell Bray is passionate, and knows how to answer most questions. But he's judgmental of students' work ethics, and relies on difficult homework for students to prepare for tests. This class felt like a competition. Thankfully, his test grading was very relaxed, but only because he knew us students were VERY stressed out by the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Bray is phenomenal in the classroom. His lectures are great, but sometimes they do get off-topic. The math in the class is very easy and although we have 3 papers that are long, they are very easy. Bray is great though, and gives some really good life advice. When he talks politics, his understanding lacks, still fun though.

Dr. Bray was great. We didn't actually learn too much on the mathematics of the universe, but I think we had a lot of good discussions on the field of science as a whole. If you love to talk about anything science, this is a good class. The class was easy too, just 3 papers of your choice and a final which you can entirely prepare for beforehand.

Very nice man and a great professor to have. Only graded on two papers (yes only 2), which he basically just gave everyone an A on, and a final. You can tell he's very passionate about the subject of game theory, which is very interesting if you pay attention. You'll only get in if you're first registration though, fills up in 2 seconds.

This is a great freshman seminar. It is a little bit theoretical but nothing that people who have an appreciation for math wouldn't enjoy. Sometimes, discussions get a little off-topic but nothing political. Highly recommend if you need a course that doesn't require much work.

This class was structured really strangely.  Basically, we had random discussion every day and had to write three large papers on anything we wanted.  Our grade was based on our peer's ratings of our papers (although I think everyone got As).  Interesting class, but I didn't really learn that much
Great class - we pretty much just talked about whatever we wanted to in class. Final grade was only based on three papers that were on any topic that you wanted to pick.

Textbook was awful, hw was long and tedious, but everything else was great. Lectures were great in class, tests were fair, grading was easy. If you have any interest in relativity, this is a great entry point.

Seriously the coolest guy ever. I want to take him again for diff geo. Only 3 papers in the whole class and all we do is talk for lectures. Do well on your papers and be genuine in your interests and you will surely get an A!

Professor Bray is awesome! Discussions were completely student-guided. The class was on special relativity and math in the universe, but honestly we just talked about whatever we wanted; finance, politics, democracy, etc. No nightly homework, three papers and a final exam, but all graded very easily. Take a class with him!

Professor Bray is a great math professor. Take a class with him if you get a chance. He is brilliant, takes time to not only teach you about math, but also about life. Very easy to relate to him and to understand his lectures. Put in the work, show up to class, do the homework, and complex analysis is not bad at all.

Hubert Bray is an awesome professor! His explanations are clear and insightful. He's very enthusiastic, about math, about teaching - making a what would have been a boring Diff eqs class a pretty good experience. He definitely prepares thoughtfully for the lectures and I got a good grade because working with him was easy!
To put it in his math genius terms: Dr. Bray = THE BEST Professor EVER!!!!! I love him so much; bless him because my first semester would've sucked without him.

This class is only offered in the Fall and is very popular among Freshman trying to fill their first-year seminar requirement. The class is very easy (only 3 papers and a final) and Bray is an awesome teacher. BUT he has no syllabus and decides during class what he wants to talk about. Some days he just talked at you and there was no discussion.
Simply the nicest, most helpful and approachable professor at Duke. Lectures are a bit disorganized, but his tests are very well thought-out. Highly recommended.
INCOMING FRESHMAN: Take this class, you won't regret it! Dr. Bray is super nice, and everything he teaches you is very interesting.

Game Theory & Democracy seminar only offered in the fall. Awesome class, so interesting, & not too much work at all (only 3 papers of your choice length). Everyone was involved and enthusiastic about the class.
Great professor! Super nice and enthusiastic. Very helpful in office hours. Class was interesting.

Awesome professor.  He is the NICEST guy you will ever meet.  He only teaches two classes, but there is no doubt in my mind that they are some of the best classes on campus. He has done a ton of research, published a ton of stuff, and his class is a ton of fun.

Extremely dense course. However, Fain is an incredible lecturer who puts in so much thought into each lecture, homework, and exam (as difficult as they are). He will go above and beyond to clarify concepts for you. Recommend a) not relying on the retake exams and b) using minimal AI for homework, because you'll suffer in the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Good lecturer for a class covering fairly complex topics. Participation fully optional and all lectures were recorded. Not easy, but you can get an A with some effort - class was graded entirely by 4 homework assignments (generous grading) and 4 unit quizzes with optional retakes.
Prof. Fain is a good lecturer and the course was interesting. Definitely harder/more work than i was expecting though.

The best lecturer. States everything so clearly and makes all content and class expectations crystal clear. 330 is tough material and I wouldn't have been able to understand it as deeply as I did without him.
Fain is the BEST. He is clear, precise, and very accessible. Would take any class he teaches a million times over!!!!
He is an amazing professor
I was expecting a 200-level introductory course to be a little easier than this. Only take this if you're actually specifically interested in ML, and not just looking for any interesting elective.

This course is total slop. Brandon is not very knowledgeable and doesn't explain things that well. Lectures are really hard to get through. Exams are not that hard (but your success partially depends on the competence of the graders). Homework problems are mostly doable with the occasional "how would I ever come up with that" problem.

I have now taken CS330 and CS290 with Fain. He is one of the best professors in the CS department. He is a fair grader and gives you multiple opportunities to succeed. His new course on Applied Artificial Intelligence was very well taught and had multiple interesting projects!

Fain is the gem of the CS dept @ Duke - he consistently goes above and beyond. CS290 Applied ML was fantastic. Interesting assignments, very fair tests, and a well structured class. I'd sign up for almost any elective taught by Fain at this point - he is that good.
I LOVE BRANDON FAIN! BOWDOIN PLEASE DON'T HIRE HIM SO HE STAYS AT DUKE!

Professor Fain might be the best professor within the CS department. His lectures are so well-thought out and clear. I always found myself very engaged despite the material being difficult. 330 is a notoriously challenging class, yet Fain made the material far more interesting and enjoyable through fair course policies and grading.
Fain inspired me to pursue CS! he is an amazing professor that cares deeply about his students
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Great professor for a notorious class. If you take 330 take it with him! The tests are the same as the homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: CS330 was made easier under Prof Fain. His tests repeated some homework/lecture problems and people generally did well (however, there's no curve). The grading policy is very forgiving (there's no need to take the final if you ddi well on midterms). His lectures are dry but very very clear. The course provides a lot of support for its students.
Fain's policies make 330 much more accessible and his lectures are super clear and all livestreamed/recorded. Super grateful I took this class with him as the prof.
He is the best lecturer ever!!! He makes this hard algorithm class interesting and easy to understand.

THEE GOATTT! If you need to take 330, you have to take it with Fain. Given what I had heard about the class, I was super nervous, but Fain teaches it in such a fair way. The class isn't curved like previous professors do, but the grading is a lot more manageable which makes a curve not really necessary. Also, Fain cares and wants to see you succeed
Professor Fain always offers amazing lectures!
Very amazing professor !!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Brandon Fain is the GOAT

330 at Duke has a reputation for being needlessly difficult, where exam questions are made for students to pull novel, random answers out of thin air, and if you don't know a hyper-specific algorithm, you're out of luck. Not with Fain, he really cares about making sure what you see on tests is stuff you've seen before. Most reasonable 330 offering.

Taking 330 with Fain was a godsend, clear lectures that were understandable despite some content being challenging. He goes at a good pace and stops for questions people might have. Homeworks and exams graded pretty generously, make sure you understand material and homeworks and you'll be fine. Couldn't ask for a better 330 experience.

I know the class is on algorithms, but Brandon Fain IS an algorithm. Like Professor Fain is such an NPC, perhaps the most advanced GPT we have seen. If you want to learn from GPT, then take a class with Professor Fain!

Every lecture is very well designed and looks at an interesting algorithmic system from cryptography to recommender systems to deep learning, and investigates their TECHNICAL and SOCIAL ISSUES. This class is interesting, not hard but also not easy, get a good group for final project and you will learn a ton from your project as well. Fain the GOAT.

Fain was great! Most of the assignments was a build up towards a final group project, where you create/emulate an algorithmic system and present it to the class. This was graded pretty fairly. Lectures were mostly unrelated to the projects, and with no tests, you did not really have to listen to them. However, they were very interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Brandon Fain was very helpful and understanding!

Everything on the exams he covers in lectures, so the exams are fair, you just have to put in the work to understand the content. Go into the lectures having read some of the textbook on the topic of that day so that you are not struggling to understand what he's talking about in class. Start projects early. Great professor and super nice overall.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Offers no help to students through TAs so assignments are confusing (TAs are not given rubrics or keys so even TAs are confused). Yelled at us after a test one time (?). Incredibly condescending with a fast-paced curriculum that nobody could keep up with (40% average on final exam). Honestly the worst class I have ever taken, wouldn't take again.
The lectures are very well explained and concise. Although sometimes he breezes through some topics he's generally a very great lecturer and teacher.

Fain was fairly helpful in teaching Data Structures and Algorithms. The lectures were somewhat boring, and there's always consistent assignments. A lot of how the course will go for you depends on your previous experience with coding. He's also like 5'3 lol

This class is tedious and difficult. The lectures focus on confusing abstract topics, but the tests are mainly about coding. The class does not teach how to code, but focuses on how to find the runtime complexity and memory of methods or code chunks. Exams are hard, you will need help on projects.

Professor Fain is a very accommodating professor and an amazing lecturer. He tries to explain every concept very clearly and takes time to clear up doubts. He is very generous with extensions and partial credits. He makes sure that you don't have to read the textbook after listening to the lecture and/or going through his slides.
CS201 is interesting enough, but Fain is a monotone and boring lecturer.

Great introduction to Java and data structures and algorithms! It is a tough class, no doubt, especially if you don't have Java background, and there is a learning curve, but you learn many skills. His grading policy affords MANY opportunties to get maintain good grades (participation, discussion, projects, APTs) and your final is optional.

Professor Fain is an engaging and entertaining lecturer who teaches the class in a clear and fun manner. The concepts are all interesting, well as interesting as data structures and algorithms can be. APTs allow for low stress practice, and the exams are all fairly straightforward given you study properly.

Professor Fain is such a nice guy. He is very smart but he makes you feel comfortable when you ask him questions, and his office hours are very helpful. His lectures are very clear and he really tries to make them engaging. Grading criterial is super clear and will drop your lowest grades on everything.

Loved the class. The lectures were super clear and interesting. Projects were pretty hard but fun, and not very time-consuming. If you actually show up to class and do the work, you'll have an amazing experience with Fain.
He's obviously really passionate and cares about CS, but he can be out of touch with students. One of the smartest guys ever though.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prior coding experience especially in Java makes a huge difference. Very different/harder than CS 101. Good lecturer and fair. Nice dude.

This is my second class with Prof Fain and I'm currently taking it. I feel his lectures sound like they have been practiced several times. He speaks undisrupted without pause or even a simple "like" or "um". Also speaks in a very elevated way when it comes to word choice. Kinda hard to focus and listen to imo. Class seems fair, however.
Just have to put in the work. He definitely creates a fair rubric but a couple screw ups can tank your grade

The class is well-structured and has a lot of opportunities to score well. Exam retakes are built into the grading system. Lectures are recorded which is a big advantage but discussion sections aren't productive.

If you've never coded in Java before, I would recomend spending some time before the class starts getting familiar with the basics using literally any online mini course type thing. Fain is very supportive, the grading is generous, and there's a lot of resources if you're struggling.

Don't buy the online zybook, its a waste of money. I never used it once. Be sure to give yourself at least 2-3 days on all projects, even if you are good at CS, as it's possible to get stuck. Otherwise, great teaching makes the class relatively easy.

Prof Fain truly cares about his students and provides many opportunities to boost your grade through projects, APTs, etc. The testing format is 3 midterms, each with a corresponding section on the exam that serves as a make-up or re-do if you do not like your grade on the previous exam. The exams are SUPER similar to the practice exams. Love Fain!

the lectures were somewhat boring but very informational. the grading overall is very fair and it's clear that he's on your side, as there are many remedial opportunities in case you slip up. You should have no problem doing well in this course as long as you engage with the content. I would definitely take CS201 with Dr. Fain.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Not a bad class. Prof. Fain's lectures were sometimes a bit boring, but that's largely just the fault of the content of the class. I also came in w/ background knowledge in ds/a, so that might skew opinion. Participation was "mandatory" in that you only had a small number of unexcused absences but many people skip and just fill the WoTos.

Very well organized course. His lectures were all great. If you just show up to class and pay attention you will learn enough to get an A. The homework isn't light, but pretty easy by Duke standards. Definitely reccomend this class.

COMPSCI201 was great with professor Fain. Nothing really stands out to me about this course, but it was extremely fair and the grading is very clear and lenient. His lecture and discussion absence policy is great for a course with a lot students. Overall, very laid back, not super difficult, accessible TA team.

I can't say enough about Dr. Fain. He made me really enjoy CS and now probably going to add the major. By the end of the semester, I think everyone in the class had a connection with prof. fain. Generous, fair, challenging, and great. Hope to take all my classes with him, and you should too.

Great teacher, good lecturer, funny. Class is graded a bit odd. Tests aren't that hard, almost exactly the same as the example ones he gives out. THIS IS NOT AN INTRO CS CLASS. Really not that hard as long as you have some CS/Java background. People who struggle generally don't and just start behind.  Great class
Fain is god. Close your eyes and just take the course. 100% recommend. There is some work but with Fain it seems like no work.

Fain really is goated for CS 201. Engaging lectures (also posted online), fair workload (just weekly APTs and semi-frequent projects projects), and a very generous test grading policy where you can literally fail every midterm and still get an A if you do well in the final. Also I think his jokes are funny, even if nobody else does >:(

Course has gotten a lot more difficult in recent semesters. Projects every other week. Coding problem sets every week and 2 timed quizzes. Weekly required discussions. 3 midterms are quite difficult but cheat sheet is allowed. Professor Fain is very knowledgeable and a good speaker but lectures are so hard to pay attention to

The best professor you could have for Compsci 201:
Very methodological and clear during lectures. Content can be a little dense, but he posted recordings & he always review the previous lecture during his next one. Tests and assignments are reasonable as well.
Just make sure to utilize office hours since debugging projects can be tough
He was very nice and professional.

Nice guy, but has the most boring lectures ever. Midterms are take-home, online. Doesn't go in-depth at all. Just learn the material on your own. Go to office hours for project/apt answers. If you genuinely are interested in CS or are taking this class for interview prep, it's not that useful.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Professor Fain is the most caring professor I've had so far at Duke. He really understands that as students, we have three other classes, extracurriculars, etc. and he assigns a fair workload. The course was not too hard with test retakes built in. Lectures can get a bit boring, but he's very passionate about the material and an excellent teacher.

Very informative but plain lectures. He occasionally covers difficult concepts too quickly (e.g. some graph algorithms). Put in the effort to understand lectures, do coding PSets and projects, and you'll be fine. He did a multiple choice final exam and had retakes for all three mini-midterms. Don't buy the ZyBoook, his slides are good enough.

Professor Fain is a really good lecturer and most concepts are explained clearly. I really liked how he incorporated so many low-stakes opportunities to get credit and test yourself as you learn the content. Overall, the class was great however I did hear that the other professors have slightly easier finals.
Good prof, but a little confusing at times. Don't be hesitant to take him for CS201.

Professor Fain is very knowledgeable and definitely tries to humanize his students in a lecture of almost 300 people. I found that I purchased the recommended "Zybook", but I never ended up using it and succeeded in the course. Maybe consider saving the money.

Fain is very genuine, and he knows a lot about compsci, but his lectures are very boring and hard to sit through. I learned a lot of the topics through discussions. However, the class is pretty easy, and it is not difficult to get a lot of points on assignments.
dry boring lectures and lots of work. however, he does explain topics clearly if you can muster up the energy to stay focused.

Prof. Fain is really genuine and kind. While teaching a topic he's clearly passionate about, he emphasizes his own humanity and sees his students holistically. He inspires us by being very reassuring and reminding us that grades aren't everything and struggling is important to learning. His lectures are clear and thorough, but hard to focus during.

Very knowledgeable and offers a lot of options for you to demonstrate your understanding. Just beware of the class having at least one assignment active at any given time (projects, APTs, prepping for APT quizzes, mini exams); all very manageable but you don't want to miss deadlines

One of the most competent professors you'll meet, when it comes to running a class with 300 students. It often feels impersonal, but if you pay attention to policies, you can have all the help you need. Lectures can be dry, but they're so huge and accessible outside class that you can learn in whatever environment you need. Medium-high amount of HW

Enjoyable material but Professor Fain is a little boring. He seems really interested and passionate about the material he is teaching, especially the math parts of it, but I almost fell asleep like 5 times. Discussion is also pretty boring.
Super fun class if you enjoy coding and problem solving. Not very hard, but a great challenge to make it all enjoyable and intellectually stimulating. He's also a fantastic lecturer
This man doesn't miss. He was able to explain every concept so clearly that I was basically never confused at any point in this class.

Professor Fain was very sweet and accommodating, just had very dry lectures that were hard to pay attention to. You could probably learn everything from the textbook and the class recordings, but participation matters in class so you'll end up having to go to lectures anyways.

I loved Professor Fain's lectures and I found his explanations to be really understandable as he often uses real world examples to supplement the topics. Sure, rewatching lectures can get boring but he somehow makes it tolerable. Respect
Good teacher in general. He knows what he is talking about and has clear expectations. However, he is very boring and it's impossible to listen to him.
Easy grader and great teacher. The majority of your grade is based off of projects and homeworks.

He's the best professor I have had so far. He explains the material very well. The lectures and presentation slides are clear and organized. He makes very complicated topics seem easy. I want to take all my courses from him.

Fain is the goat, probably the best CS prof I've had at Duke. Lectures are prepared extremely well, he's very articulate/well-spoken, & answers questions really well during class. Very fair grading policy and he's pretty accommodating with deadlines and stuff. Also has a great sense of humor that you can detect if you pay attention during lectures.

A real gem of a professor - material isn't too tough and he provides clear, relevant examples. Really understanding of outside circumstances and a lot of flexibility and creativity allowed in the final project.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I thought this class would be very easy, but the assignments honestly ended up taking a long time - make sure to start them early. Other than that, Fain is a really nice professor, who is clearly really passionate about the subject matter.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Group projects

reviews.comment: Dr. Fain is a great professor. He's a good lecturer, and treats his students with respect. Learned a lot in his class. Homeworks and projects aren't too hard, but they are still interesting to work on. Would definitely recommend taking his classes.
You don't really need to attend class, just watch the lectures and do the work. Professor Fain was really understanding and the class environment is overall welcoming and non-intimidating.
Slow talker, but explains concepts very clearly. Grading is generous, and the APTs are very fun. Fain is a nice guy and he cares. I would take another class of his.

Genuinely a good guy--he did all of the lectures while KSM handled all of the Zoom logistics, and they were fantastic when paired with ola's pre-class lectures. The grading seemed less generous than ola in fall '20, but the course is fairly straightforward and it's not hard to do well. Incredibly helpful if you go to his office hours as well.

ABSOLUTE GOAT, super nice and explains concepts clearly. I don't like that the cutoffs for an A is set at the end; it just leaves you with a bit of stress. Also we don't learn java in the beginning so if your only experience with code is CS101 (Python) you're already behind :( Overall, though, amazing professor and loved this class.
Awesome professor. Even in an online class of 120+ people, he genuinely seems to care about his students. He explains everything clearly and simply. Such a g
Professor Fain is one of the best professors I've had at Duke. Great lectures, thoroughly explained and incredibly fair homework

CS 216 is probably the easiest CS elective. This class was super interesting and the lectures were pretty engaging. The hw and labs were hands-on which I liked. Grades are really only weekly hw, lab completion, attendance, and the final project stuff. I would definitely recommend this class if you're looking for an easy and interesting CS elective!

Graded by final project, HW, and labs/attendance (completion), grading is pretty lenient, one of the easier CS electives. Class material is extremely useful/relevant for use in the real world in data science. Homeworks can sometimes be difficult b/c technical portions aren't really covered in class, but go to OH and you should be fine
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Group projects

reviews.comment: Professor Barnes possesses a unique brand of self-confidence where she assumes that her lectures are even slightly worth listening to. Getting a decent grade is easy as her opinions on the topic are evident, and she is so enthralled by students' agreement with her that she will give out As as long as the "right" opinions are safely regurgitated.

Barnes is egregiously delinquent with grading as marks are only clear very, very late in the semester. Barnes seems to be extremely insecure about both herself and the subject she's supposed to be teaching, frequently complaining about scientific medicine and telling us about her son. Lectures, as a result, are not worth going to.

Dr. Barnes is not only incredibly passionate about her work but an immensely caring person. She takes a genuine interest in her students & their interests, and will truly let you explore what you'd like. We do a lot of reading but it builds nicely and the final is spread out over the semester. She also brings her son to FOCUS dinner-so cute

This was my favorite class at Duke. Take it. She is a fantastic lecturer and an expert, can answer literally any question you have. Genuinely cares about her students, leads guided meditation at beginning of every lecture, gives great feedback on assignments. Also invites some excellent guest speakers! The group project is what you make of it.

Dr. Barnes is so nice and very accommodating as long as you reach out. There's a ton of reading (40 pages minimum) for every class, but you're not graded except for 5 required discussion posts. You're kind of on your own in terms of keeping up with assignments.

I cannot say enough good things about Dr. Barnes. She is truly a gem in her teaching, understanding, and care for her students. She was always nice and accomodating, and really emphasized our health over everything. The class was one of my most favorite classes at Duke so far, and really easy to get an A if you put in the time and effort!
