Professor Camila is really nice and encouraging. She welcomes every question related not only to the course materials but also to the economics major selection in general. I always have many questions to ask her. In the beginning, I was afraid of bringing them to Professor Camila. Thankfully, she encouraged me and explianed everything clearly.

Professor's very nice, always accessible outside of class and accommodating to students' needs. Very inspiring and willing to share her experience. Do find time to talk to her about Econs (if that's your interest) and always be respectful please. You'll do well if you engage in the materials and do the practice exam (strategize accordingly)!!!

Prof. Saez is a great teacher; she is open and willing to help outside of class time. There is a lot of content to cover, which means readings and lectures are heavy, but Prof. Saez manages to explain everything pretty clearly.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Saez is the kindest, most thoughtful professor I've met. She put a lot of effort into helping online students, would meet with us once a week to answer any questions and before the midterms and final. The exams were a bit fast-paced, but professor Saez made lots of resources available for us to prepare.

Prof. Saez is very nice and caring and always says hi to me at school. Her exams are open book so it is easier. Also she gives good grades and is very patient to answer all of my questions! Highly recommended!

Professor Saez was extremely understanding and accomodating for the class. Exams are easy, but time is usually a constraint. Grading is fast and fair. There are some presentations and essays to help you boost your grade, even if you don't do that well in the exams. She also gave us extra credit, so it was easy to get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I end up with an A-, but I still really enjoy the class. I went to office hours a couple of times and Professor is really patient and answer all my questions without problem. I like that the test are open book, and that she provides practice exams in advance. Also, she is the professor that reply my emails the fastest!
I really love Professor Camila, she is super smart and always replies to my emails fast. I will take the econ major only to be able to have more classes with her !!

Professor Camila is super kind. She actually cares about her students and is very engaging. She is always available outside the classroom and is very flexible for international students especially. I highly recommend her, not 1 complaint.

Finally a caring professor who wants students to succeed. He spent a ton of time working with students and holding office hours. Yes, organic is hard and yes he pushes hard, but he does want you to succeed. He puts 100 percent into his courses and while some discussions are confusing, he goes out of his way to help.

COMPREHENSIVE: A great instructor for a difficult class. Lectures cover all key concepts. Use all available resources: the office hours problems, problem sets, and practice exams were great exam prep and usually enough. If you can, also use the OrganoMech textbook. Exams were hard and required deep understanding of topics. Curve at end was useful.

The GOAT. Lectures are a bit slow but gives you all the information. Appreciate the patience and detail he gave. Do the Pset, discussion, sample exams, and lecture notes before the test, and you should be getting a good score. OrganoMech is not necessary. Group exams helped a little bit. He is the best STEM professor I've ever had here at Duke.

i had multiple classes w/ prof cox, and i initially had an F to succeeding in every class. i don't think organic chemistry would be considered a "weed out" if he was teaching at every university. this is to say: he's undoubtedly one of the best and fair professors at duke. attend OHs, lectures, do your psets, and your studying will pay off trust

Usually explains content well, provides a lot of resources and a reasoning grading structure, but exams are hard, go beyond what is covered in the lecture, and he seems indifferent to student difficulties. He may be better than other profs, but still not phenomenal. Study hard and hope for an A. This is organic for majors.

Chem 202 is much harder than 201, which Dr. Parise emphasized as memorization-based. For Cox in 202, you need to understand why and how organic reactions occur. This is NOT easy, but learned organic chemistry extremely well. Cox researches how to teach organic, and his class is truly transformative. It is hard, but very doable with effort!

Everything about how Cox structures 202 is convoluted. This class suffers from overabundance– of information, PSets, etc. Cox tests WAY above the level he lectures, which he said he would never do, but he did it anyways. Grad students shouldn't lead discussions, they are not well–equipped to teach. If they have to, they NEED further training.

The best professor I have had at Duke. Extremely passionate about teaching. He breaks down very difficult topics into an easy to understand way. I walk out of lectures feeling great about the material. He provides more than enough practice materials to prepare for exams. Even if you bomb a midterm, there are opportunities to still succeed.
He is genuinely one of the best teachers I've had at Duke. Made an extremely hard subject enjoyable.
One of the best professors I've had during my time at Duke. Clear, logical lecturer. Truly provides his students with the practice, office hours, and extra resources to master the content.

Highly recommend Prof. Cox, he is very knowledgable about chemistry and is able to explain topics in an interesting and digestible manner. Office hours were very helpful because he cares for his students and walks through every step of the problem. The exams were always aligned with what was covered during lecture and homework. Great Professor.

Easy courze, great lectures, caring guy that made perfectly challenging exams. They seemed ez and we usually finished really early. Class preps u for chem101 well. Def take if you feel uneasy about 101 at all, because that class is hard and this 1 is not, and it preps u well.

I was nervous about taking chemistry because of my lack of experience from high school. I struggled a lot, but Cox truly cares for his students. Everyone had very different experiences, but he really wanted to reach every student. The discussions were great and he provided a ton of resources. Cox is a gem, and I look forward to having him again.

Excellent class, with 55% exams, 45% homework/project, with a solid foundation for different analytical methods and data analysis. Prof. Cox genuinely cares about teaching. I didn't need to use outside references beyond his concise notes. My only complaint is that his exams are a time crunch. Also having him for o-chem would have been helpful.

I did not attend the class, having enrolled only for the easy NS credit. That said, exams were fair, and Charlie came across as a genuinely good and caring person when I'd see him on exam days. Many of my peers share that sentiment. I would recommend any course taught by Charlie, particularly for Chemistry majors.

This is his first semester in 99, and there were quirks, but chemistry is hard. He is caring and wants us to do well. He provides a lot of resources and exams are fair. He normally doesn't teach 99, but he definitely tried to help us get ready for 101. I never took chemistry before, and I feel confident moving into the next course.

Amazing professor. Super caring and genuinely a good lecturer, really makes an effort to explain things. Fair grading policies and most people do pretty well despite Orgo 2 being a very difficult class.

210 is not easy, and having the Parise version of general chemistry made things worse. With that said, Cox was willing to help us succeed by reviewing parts of 101 that should have been covered. I learned a lot of general chemistry, and I found the redox and metal chemistry very interesting. Cox gives a project in lieu of a final, which was nice.

Took Chem 202 with Cox at the Marine Lab. Transformative experience-- took a lot of courses at Duke but I have to say come in ready to dedicate hours of your time to Organic Chemistry every day because this was one of the most challenging courses I'd ever taken. Cox is a lovable guy though and he will give you the motivation to succeed.
CHARLIE COX IS THE BEST! Such a good person and AMAZING professor. 100000/10. Take this class every single time.

Started off with him in Chem 110 freshman year with very limited chemistry knowledge. I had 201 and 202 with him subsequent semesters and he was hands down the best professor I ever had.  I learned so much about general and organic chemistry.  He makes learning engaging and interesting.  Very accessible in office hours and a very fair grader.

Kinda hard to get an A in the class given there is no curve and your grade is basically just exams. Cox is a really great lecturer, the TAs were amazing, and office hours/support is always available at your convenience. Wish Cox had more drip though but overall a solid class

Organic Chemistry II is a challenging course, but Professor Cox makes the course as easy as possible. He is very understanding and wants his student to do well. He is always available outside of class and holds multiple office hours to ensure students have access to help while completing assignments. Class is not solely based on assignments.
Orgo 2 is miserable no matter who you take it with. If you have to take this class, DEFINITELY take it with Cox.

Very knowledgeable and teaches using energetics, which is very different than the approach taken in 201. This approach was initially hard, but it made sense and increased my understanding of mechanisms. Lectures, which are recorded, are key to understanding the content. Exams are very hard, but there is a lot of support. Duke is lucky to have him.

Cox is truly an amazing professors and provides SO many resources for you to excel. Go to office hours, do the organomech practice problems, utilize his lecture summaries, study guides, and "reaction ragers" and you'll be okay. He explains concepts well. The amount of homework (problem sets and discussion) can get overwhelming sometimes though.

Cox is hands down the best prof I've had. Took orgo 2 after an atrocious orgo 1 with qiu wang, yet cox has actually made me enjoy learning about chem. His lectures are super engaging because he goes slowly through the material and ensures everyone understands the content. Super accessible because he dedicates all his time to this class. Love him.

I didn't care for him initially because he has high expectations and is a little snarky and blunt. However, now that I am organic, I realize he went above and beyond. I feel well prepared, and he gave us a ton of time and support. Overall with Cox, you will learn chemistry and be prepared or organic, but he doesn't deal with BS and whining.

In hindsight, he's a really good professor. While you're taking the class, you'll probably be overwhelmed given the course content. However, he truly does want students to succeed and gives you A LOT of resources to do so. Go to/Watch his office hours, then study them-- and you will be set for life. Highly recommend him.

Prof. Cox is extremely caring about his students' success. Students who think otherwise simply haven't tried or didn't want to try. The exams are straightforward. The lectures are engaging with Aktiv problems dispersed throughout and interesting case studies on sustainability. If you go to his lectures, you do well on the exams. No tricks on exams.

Dr. Cox is an excellent lecturer who cares about the success of his students. This could be a tough class with limited chem experience, but regardless, the best way to succeed is to go to his problem solving office hours and do all discussion problems. Labs do take some time but are also very manageable.

Your grade matches your effort. The lecture is MUCH easier than the lab, but you learn a lot. The lecture focuses on what you will NEED to do in your career/lab and is less focused on picky details. Presentations & p-sets make up most of the grade, but these can be challenging. Overall a good way to finish up your senior year. He is very nice.

Prof. Cox is caring & committed to his students doing well. He is clearer than his co-instructor despite his topics being more complex. He lays out the content clearly but needs to review and study it. Chemistry requires practice. Some of my peers think they should walk out knowing everything perfectly, but as Cox says, chemistry takes practice.

Good professor. Analytical had a lot of content but he was clear in what we need to know. Took a more practical approach to emphasize specific instead of everything. Your grade is correlated with effort. In class activities are graded on participation with homework being significant (30%) of the final grade. Exams open note and computer.
Take orgo 2 at the Marine Lab with Cox! Best choice ever. He makes the material so interesting + marine lab is amazing. Made me love orgo.

I was dreading orgo, but Cox made it very straightforward. His exams will challenge you, but the grading format gives you a lot of wiggle room. Overall an extremely gifted educator. He clearly loves chemistry and his students. So receptive to questions and communicative in office hours. A really funny and nice guy overall.

Promotes a cooperative classroom environment. The exams are not easy, but you will be fine if you prepare and pay attention to the lecture. Cox is much more detailed oriented and you have to understand WHY reactions occur. Cox can answer questions with greater depth than Parise but you also need to understand concepts at a deeper level.

Excellent professor who structures his courses for his students to both learn and succeed. His published in organic education and it shows. He is more in depth than my 201 professor but it made the course easier honestly because I made solid connections. Cox's book is outstanding. Exams are hard but doable. You need to understand mot memorize.

He is invested to ensure his students succeed. He is detail oriented with detailed lectures and there is a lot of homework required, but the grading is very fair with homework and lab counting a lot toward the grade. 4 quizzes that were challenging but similar to difficulty of homework. Final was tough. You have to work but he wants you to succeed!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. Cox is truly an amazing professor - patient, kind, and incredibly knowledgeable and passionate about the subject. His lectures are very detailed and he goes deeply into the "why" behind everything, so you learn the content really well. High but reasonable expectations. He explains clearly and was always accessible outside of class.
Good professor but not as easy as I was led to believe. He does a lot for his students and truly does care and goes above and beyond. Exams are not easy but you can excel with effort.
cox is a wonderful professor! he has so many office hours and practice problems. his lecture are clear and he clearly puts a lot of time and effort in helping students.

Organic is hard but Prof. Cox is willing to work hard to ensure his students do well. Students who feel he is a poor professor or goes into too much depth are probably simply not cut out for medical school. He doesn't go on tangents - What he says is important. If you attend lectures, the tests are predictable, but they have challenging problems.
Excellent professor. The grade you get is proportional to the work you put in. He cares and works hard for students. You should be able to pull a B by trying.

Challenging professor who expect you to extend beyond the text. Does not use the common text - he believes the Loudon book is a starting point and goes deeper. He is excellent if you want to learn chemistry. If you want an easy A - take Parise or another professor. Cox is an excellent professor - but challenging.

Very good professor. Orgo 2 is somewhat difficult because of the amount of material, but Dr. Cox does a good job of explaining the underlying theory, which helps with memorizing the amount of reactions. Class is well-structured, and the professor really wants you to succeed. Take it with Dr. Cox if you can!

Prof Cox does research on how to teach 202. He is the only prof in the department to focus on this research and uses different approaches to cover content. He is excellent in office hours and cares. However, his class is hard. Our TAs had Parise who was much easier, but I feel like I learned organic very well. Not easy but you learn organic

Professor Cox is the best chemistry professor at Duke. This is my third semester with him - if you have a chance to take him for any chemistry class, do it. He makes it very possible to succeed if you utilize discussion sets, office hours problems, and in-class problems.
I couldn't imagine a better professor to teach this class than Dr. Cox. If you have a chance to take one of your classes with Cox, absolutely take it.

Very challenging. He only has two mid-terms and a final, but he provides ample information outlining what to study. He is very clear in the lecture about what information is most important. Not easy, but he is very fair with exams. I suggest scheduling a meeting with him to discuss study strategies. Also meet with the TAs.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very challenging professor. Pay attention in the lecture because he doesn't ramble about useful information. Everything he says is useful. Exams represent information covered in the review sessions. His research is in how to teach organic and he focuses on nuanced information that he learns from his research. Not easy but emphasizes key info.

Amazing professor for 202 - lots of resources. My grade improved from 201. Everyone loved his class except those who took the easier route for 201 with the easier 201 profs. Cox is challenging but very detail-oriented, which is excellent for understanding the content. I enjoyed the details. If you want just to learn the minimum, take someone else.

Very challenging professor. Prof Cox is detail-oriented. Prof. Cox focuses on specific trends in organic chemistry instead of all of the reactions we can memorize. You need a solid background in 201. I had him for 110, 201, and 202, which increased my ability in the course. Tests are not easy but possible if you review and understand content.

Orgo II is difficult no matter who you take it with, but Cox makes it much more bearable and not impossible by giving you the resources/extra problems/etc. He is a wonderful lecturer but you really have to be self-motivated in this class.

Professor Cox is understanding beyond what you would expect of university professors. I doubt there is an organic chemistry professor better than him across the world. He teaches students what they need to know in a digestable format and also tests and grades in an extremely fair way. Thank you for an amazing semester Dr. Cox. You will be missed.

As a pre-med student, I feared organic chemistry. However, I excelled because of Prof. Cox. What was a scary class became an outstanding experience with the best professor I have had (out of 4) in the chemistry department. Don't confuse a great and caring instructor with an "easy" instructor-this class was hard, but he helped us to excel.

Outstanding professor for Chem 202. He is much better for 202 than 201, but it could also be the content of the course. His research focuses on how to teach 202, and he has compiled ample resources, including additional practice problems, videos, and several sample exams. A very challenging class, but he works hard to ensure his students succeed.

Cox is the best professor at Duke and really wants you to succeed. He provides so much practice and is really easy to access online and during office hours. The TAs this semester also made additional content but I personally never touched it as it was absolutely useless. Do EVERYTHING Cox provides he tries to help and not overcomplecate.

This class is DIFFICULT by nature but Prof Cox makes it the best experience possible. He provides so much extra practice. Going by just lectures and required HWs is not enough, so take full advantage of all the other help and resources he offers. His grading is also designed so you don't stress too much over one quiz/exam.

Excellent professor for organic. The best for organic in the chem department. He works hard and creates an inclusive environment using collaborative incentives and undergraduate TAs. He cares about students and wants to ensure their success. Premed students love organic with him. More challenging than parise but provides exceptional support.

One of the best if not the best professor/lecturers in the university. Orgo is already a hard topic, but Cox makes the content engaging, intuitive, and interesting for everyone involved...even premeds. Grading is very clear cut, exam content is very clearly explained, and his exams are extremely fair. Lectures at perfect pace, and very organized.

If you could take chemistry with Dr. Cox, do it. As long as you do the work, and there is a lot of work, you will pass. He has amazing TAs and so much good quality practice problems. He cares a lot for his students and wish I took more chemistry classes with him.
Excellent professor. Clear, consist, approachable, and excellent TAs. Take Cox and only Cox for chem courses.

Chem 202 is very challenging, but Cox is very caring and supportive. It is not an easy A - you have to work, but he does his best to help students. Numerous resources, recorded lecture, annotations, group exams, Active, and extra videos reviewing mechanisms. He wants you to understand "why" the reactions occur and gives plenty of bio applications.

He is energetic and caring. Cox himself admits that 201 has a lot of content. He had only taught the course once before, but he put a lot of effort into providing ample resources and office hours. His exams are fair if you study the discussions and office hours problems. Chem 201 was fast. Chem 202 with him has a lot of depth but more patterns.

More challenging Professor than my 201 instructor who skipped content and allowed us to use chest sheets. The learning curve is for real with him. He is caring but his class is not easy. Moves fast in class but lectures are recorded. Lots of resources and he does truly care about his students. You will learn a lot but have to work hard!

Dr. Cox was not amazing at explaining orgo concepts although I had him for gen chem and thought he was great. He is invested in his students, though, and makes it possible to learn from him outside of lecture.
Dr. Cox was so funny and explained concepts really well. He is accessible outside of class and fosters an engaging learning environment. I loved this class.

Professor Cox is extremely knowledgeable and passionate about chemistry. He gives various avenues and a plethora of resources for students to succeed with. His first priority is the success of his students. In the end, this class is still extremely difficult and requires a deep understanding of the mechanisms behind organic chemistry for success.

Great professor. He covers a lot of content very quickly, but is very available to answer questions in office hours and provides a ton of resources. Use his book as the primary resource because much of his lectures are pulled from the textbook. He exams are straightforward and he records his lectures. There is a lot of content- not his fault.

I had prof cox for three classes-101, 202, and 210. You have to work and it is chemistry so it is not easy, but he cares and is willing to help you succeed. Exams are doable but not easy. He is understanding and willing to work with students but there is no curve. He wants students to study together. 210 draws heavily on 101- his 101 prepared me!

Prof Cox cares about his students and puts in a lot of effort. His class is hard, but if you use the resources then it is not too bad. The exams are predictable. Class move quickly but he has a ton of office hours and other resources. He records lectures which helps. You get the grade you earn in his class. No surprises.

Cox is great but not an easy prof. A lot of students signed expecting an easier class. He goes fast in lecture but records everything and lecture follows his book exactly. Study and make connections. Lots of resources and caring. 101 was like high school, but Cox has higher expectations. Take Cox to learn 201 or another prof for an easy premed A

Very good professor. Organized. If you feel that things are not organized, please review content. That is a sign that you don't understand from my opinion. He provides a ton of resources and a lot of his time to ensure students do well. The exams are predictable, but you have to understand the content. No tricks. No surprises. Overall greater prof.

Very caring professor who will go out of his way to support his students.He moves fast in lecture but the lectures are recorded. He tries to stop and engage students but my class didn't participate. His class is harder than the other sections, but I found the extra information very interesting as a pre-med. Exams are the same as discussion problems

Taking organic chemistry for the first time sucks, but Prof. Cox does his absolute best, trying to give students as many resources as possible to succeed. However, his lectures are often disorganized and difficult to understand, although due to the subject, this cannot be entirely his fault. He does give incredible partial credit, though!

Cox is my favorite. Orgo 1 isn't easy so don't hate on him, he literally makes it as easy as possible. He doesn't do any trick questions. To ace the exams, just ace the discussion problems. They are so similar. He is accessible out of class so don't hesitate to reach out.
The GOAT! Class is very hard though so you'll regret not paying attention in class. Otherwise, grading is fair and Cox is somewhat of a funny guy!

This is my second semester with Professor Cox, and he is consistently a great teacher for all chemistry classes. If you're taking orgo at Duke, do it with Cox - the content is obviously hard, but if you go to lecture, review your notes, and take advantage of all of his office hours, his tests are not surprising. He is very fair and cares a lot.

Chem 210 is not bad. He does go into more depth than Canelas, but the topics are interesting. I learned about membranes and fuel cells. He cares and provides a lot of support. Straightforward exams. People who did poorly because of lack of effort. They took Cox to avoid Warren, but are bitter an A isn't gift-wrapped for their pre-med requirements.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Before registration - beware! Chem 210 with Cox is very hard. Much harder than other profs and he isn't flexible. He will not bend on grades. His lectures are clear, provides lots of resources, records lectures and office hours, but this class shouldn't be this hard. Just take another prof and relax. Two exams and a final are 90% of the grade.

It is evident that Dr. Cox was a very respected professor, and his lectures are for the most part clear. Sometimes, it does go a little fast, but if you take some time to review content after lecture you should be fine. tests are fair and the discussion sections helped a lot.

Excellent Prof. Clear grading criteria, caring, accessible, clear lectures, and meaningful discussion activities. I am excited for organic and tempted to take 210- even though he says 110 is harder than 210. The group exams are awesome and the multiple grading options definitely help. If you need help, he will go out of his way to help. We are #1.

Cox is the best. Seriously. Orgo cannot be easy, but he gives you every option to make it manageable and understandable. He lets you learn your way and gives you opportunities to use at your choice. His lectures are great. GO. The tests aren't easy, but everything on them is taught so there are never tricks. Always choose Cox if he's teaching.

He's an absolute work horse for his students, putting in SO many extra hours per week to ensure students' success. Absolutely no surprise he's the DUS. He's clearly a caring guy who wants you to succeed, and if orgo doesn't come naturally to u, go to his office hours. Study A LOT for the tests (it's orgo), and focus on what he emphasizes.

Charlie Cox is an amazing professor. He's great at explaining organic and keeps lectures engaging while providing lots of practice resources for outside of class. He also has built a grading system that is meant to benefit students as much as possible, adjusting weight on exams at the end of the semester so that the highest grade possible is earned

Professor Cox is one of the best professors you can have for chemistry. He gives interesting and clear lectures, abundant supplemental resources (readings, videos, problems), and truly cares about the success of his students. The concepts are not easy, but he makes it feasible to succeed in this class and future courses if you put in the work.

Cox is the prof you want for every single chemistry class you take at Duke. He clearly explains complex concepts and is always willing to provide extra practice problems if you ask. You have to attend all the lectures and stay focused, but if you put in the work, you'll get an A. I suggest you take the lab a semester before you take the lecture.

Lectures are clear and he is always available after class or over email to answer questions. All lectures are recorded with slides, and he provides ample material for exam prep. He also weights your grades in a way that will benefit you the most (ex: if you did worse on the final, it gets weighted less). I highly recommend this class.

Cox is fine, I'm in 110. It's not really Cox, but more the class, but I swear lectures feel sooo dragged out and it's just 75 mins so that's weird but anyway material is VERY tough or at least just kinda weird. I'm sure compared to other profs he's better though so I say take it with him.

Took 202 and 210 with Cox, and while 202 was harder both were great. I learned a lot and he focuses upon predicting/extending concepts. Minimal textbook use-lecture covers all content. He posts recorded lectures. Test heavy with limited fluff points. Harder tests than other profs. If you want to learn take him, if you want to an easy A...not sure.

Professor Cox is an amazing lecturer and made me love Orgo a lil more. He breaks down the conceptual stuff into patterns that are easier to understand. Tests primarily on what's in lecture (textbook was lowkey supplemental) Goated for real, def take any class with him if you can. Super accessible, but does have harder tests. Love this man frr
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: S tier professor that breaks down a very hard class with a vast amount of content into trend-focused chemical concepts that stuck with me long-term. I would delay taking chemistry courses as a premed student just to wait until he teaches it. Orgo 2 is the hardest class most premed students will take at Duke so having the best professor is important

Caring professor who strives to provide resources. Clear explanations were given in lecture. First time teaching 210, but I would recommend his version of 210 and any of his classes. You can do well but you have to work. Very conceptual but fair exams and you can use a crib sheet!

Overall great professor. Very caring and devoted a lot of time to course. He sets up the grading for his students to do well. This was his first time teaching 210 and it had quirks but it was still good and it prepped me for the MCAT. Three exams and homework make up your final grade. If you want an easy A-take another professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Caring professor who works diligently to ensure his students succeed. Exams are heavy on concepts and while it is tempting to focus on calculations, study the concepts. Lots of resources are provided. The material from the middle to end is much hard than the material at the start of the course. Electrochemistry and acid base are major topics.

This course is great prep for the MCAT. He cares about his students and works hard to ensure everyone does well. There are a bunch of pushy students in the course who demonstrate entitlement to the extreme but he focus upon equity and fairness. The exams are like the discussion and office hour problems and there or no shocks or twists.

Class started rocky shifting between online & in person but he is accommodating & understanding. He provides a lot of his time and clearly works hard. Class moves very fast but is recorded. More in depth than 101 and less interesting than organic but does lots of medical applications. Study Office Hour/Discussion Problems. Very fair exams

Explains everything clearly; dedicates a lot of time to helping students understand concepts, no matter how basic. His online office hours consist of him showing how to work through problems, which is a great source of practice for exams. His grading is always beneficial for the student and he uses the best of multiple grading methods
Very caring, approachable, knowledgeable, and creates an environment for students to succeed!
Nice professor.
Professor Cox is awesome! He truly wants his students to succeed.

Don't get me wrong: orgo isn't my thing but Cox is the BEST prof out there. Had a different prof for 201 and the juxtaposition is real. Cox clearly explains otherwise confusing concepts and gives tough but fair exams, obviously with the best interest of his students in mind. I may not have an A+ grade in this class, but I do have an A+ professor.

Had Dr. Cox for CHEM 202. Cox is an amazing and exceptional professor. He is easy to approach with questions and will always try to explain a concept to the class/student as many times as necessary. He has a very trend-focused teaching style (acid-base, electrophilicity, etc.) and this helps understand why certain reactions or selectivity occur.

Very approachable and caring. The exams were not too challenging--the final was significantly more challenging. All exams are cumulative and he does award a lot of partial credit. We covered the same content as other 202 sections. The lectures were done in real - time on zoom and not pre-recorded. There is no curve but it is possible to do well!

Lectures are clear+provide a solid overview of what we need to know for exams. I had him for 101 and 201 and would recommend him strongly for the sequence. He is caring and wants students to do well. Exams are fair but can be hard . Review homework+discussion activities because exams are similar. His orgo lectures focus on kinetics+thermo from 101

Excellent professor. He was my 101& 201 professor, and I am excited to continue with 202 with him in summer II. He is understanding, has empathy for students, and write challenging yet fair exams with avgs in the 80s. The content is vast in 201 and he knows it, but he did a great job teaching it. Spectroscopy first was hard but worked. Recommended
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I took this as a first sem freshman and I gotta say, Professor Cox was so caring--he really empathized with students. Tests were not easy but they were graded fairly. Lectures were pretty good too. Overall, great professor

Dr. Cox is best possible professor for this class. His lectures were synchronous and they weren't just PowerPoints, which made learning the material much more accessible during COVID. He was also very generous with grading for the midterms/final. Orgo 2 isn't easy, but I would take it again with Dr. Cox.

I was really worried about taking Orgo 2, but Dr. Cox actually made me enjoy the class a lot! He was always willing to host review sessions outside of normal lecture times. His lectures were very clear and he provided lots of practice problems. The exams were very fair, and I felt the he wanted everyone to succeed in the course overall.

Orgo 2 will never be easy but Dr. Cox made lecture enjoyable. He moves through the material at a really nice pace and provides a lot of extra help in office hours. It is clear he cares about his students and wants them to succeed. Duke is lucky to have him. One of the best professors I've had.

Dr. Cox is so sweet, and his class is extremely well organized. Although the class is a lot of work (repeat: a lot of work), it is very predictable, and once you learn the structure it's the same assignments almost every week. He has office hours twice a week - go to those because the problems he goes over will sometimes be very similar to the exam

Professor Cox is definitely one of my favorite professors I've had at Duke. He is wicked-smart and a very good speaker. His love for chemistry is apparent in every lecture, it's honestly inspiring (even for us anti-chemistry pre-med folk). He truly dedicates all of his time to his students and is a devoted professor. Duke is lucky to have him.

Professor Cox was fantastic. I wouldn't consider Chemistry my best subject at all, but I ended up succeeding in his class and not actually disliking it, which is an impressive improvement from my other Chem classes. I also had some rough circumstances during the semester and he was incredibly kind and accommodating, and I will always remember that.

The only person in the chem department that hasn't made me regret my chem minor tbh. Professor Cox is the best, tests are fair and he only tests on concepts emphasized in lecture. Office hours are super helpful, definitely go. Grading is very forgiving but I still feel like I learned a lot, and I actually understand orgo now.
orgo is orgo but cox is literally the man. one of the best chemistry professors i have ever had. so accessible, caring and wants students to truly understand orgo + succeed in his class.

Works hard to get and implement student feedback. Switched to more practice material during lecture times due to student feedback (instead of repeating pre-lecture material). Explains concepts well. Worked on additional problems in office hours - and posted all zoom meetings on sakai. Responds fast to emails.

Professor Cox really cares for his students--he holds office hours twice a week to do practice problems and answer questions, allows you to book one-on-one appointments before exams, and emphasizes that his course is not meant to weed anyone out (he never rounds down btw). You can tell that he's passionate about what he teaches. Highly recommend!

Made the best effort he could during his first semester at Duke to teach Chem 101. Makes everything accessible so it was not hard to prepare for midterms and exams. Accessible and quick to respond to concerns. Content same as any Chem 101 class, so content can be difficult at times, but Cox is willing to speak with you and holds Office Hours often.

Great instructor for 101. Everything including lectures and office hours is recorded and posted to Sakai. You do need to watch the lectures, review office hours problems in prep for the exam. The exams are not too bad. Short and can be tricky but very similar to problems worked in lecture. He definitely cares a lot about teaching and chemistry!

I had Prof. Cox during his first semester and first time teaching 101. It was overall a good experience. He is available and he is open to feedback regarding what is working in the course. Exams were hard, but these come directly from lecture. If he spends a lot of time covering it, it will be on the exam. He throws in some jokes and cartoons too.

Great professor, especially for his first semester at Duke. Definitely go to office hours and ask for help outside of class if you feel the need to, he is very approachable. Tests are hard but fair, definitely go to lectures even though they are optional. Prof. Cox is clearly passionate about chemistry and wants his students to do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Great. First semester teaching at Duke. Talks very slowly, but clearly defines and explains the material. Very approachable outside of class. Takes constructive feedback well. Workload same as any other CHEM 101 class. Tests are fair yet tricky. Seems like a very nice person.

Marko gives a generous curve overall, but I found the course structure disconnected: lectures did not align closely with homework, and homework did not prepare me well for exams. The exams often tested material differently than it was presented. He is kind and knowledgeable, but the course could be clearer and better coordinated.
Cetina is a really sweet person but it doesn't translate to his teaching. His lectures, HW, and midterms do not line up and his exams are very different from what we've learned.
He's a very passionate and interesting lecturer, frequent office hours, quite generous grading. 361 will still be hard though

Dr Cetina is a super nice guy, but he genuinely should find a different career. Dr Cetina does not teach anything in this class. Quizzes have nothing to do with homework or lecture, and the textbook he chose makes simple concepts incredibly confusing. He also did not prepare us for Physics 122 in the slightest. Just get a tutor and skip class.

Dr. Cetina cares about students, but is not a good lecturer and does not provide enough resources for success. Weekly quizzes and the final were pretty difficult, although the midterms were somewhat fair. This class requires extensive time outside of the course. The class is doable, but would strongly recommend taking with another professor.
Cetina a generous curve for 361, easily accessible outside of class, but hard final: avg was in the 60s high score was in the 70s. nice guy and loves physics

Honestly, I think people hate on Professor Cetina too much. Yes, I did spend at least 10 hours a week on physics. One thing that helped was that I did a bunch of practice problems from RGBs class and Marko's tests and quizzes were similar to them. Professor Cetina is very accessible outside of class, however his quizzes should be made easier.

Cetina is definitely more suited to upper-level, non-intro classes (lots of tangents, lectures can be unclear). But his teaching did improve over the semester, and he is accessible outside of class. It would be easier to take 121 with another professor, yes, but also, physics is just hard in general, so...

Cetina cares about students learning physics. I think as he continues to teach, he will get better at presenting the material. Midterms were FAIR! Quizzes started off rough but became fair after ~Quiz 5/6. Physics is hard if you don't have prior background. Take your time to learn the intuition and how the equations fit, and you will do well.
He seems to care about his students but this class completely killed my confidence
The final was so unfair and not at all representative of what we've “learned” this semester
IN SOLIDARITY!!! RAHHHH!!!

\While kind, Professor Cetina is not made for intro courses. He fails to explain even the most basic of concepts and routinely waits until the last minute to post review material for the weekly quizzes. This has been a semester of stress and worry, purely due to his class. I do not say this lightly, do NOT take this class with him.
if you aren't religious, pick a religion and pray to pass this class
The mean on our third exam which covered all content was in the mid 70s and there's no class curve. Dont really understand how thats even allowed for an intro physics course

His lectures were terrible. He was unclear about course policies-- changing them constantly and sending out announcements late at night. He would post readings and homework late in the week, making the course preparation extremely difficult. Going to the office hours was unhelpful as he would go off on a tangent about unrelated concepts. No curve.

while Cetina means well and has improved massively since beginning of semester, his lectures lack clarity and are filled with tangents. Weekly quizzes force self-teaching (since you won't get anything from lecture) and mcq/TF qs are generally so obscure that unless you are physics itself, you're better off guessing what he wants you to say
You might as well take 151 or wait for a different professor. Do not take!!

I do think he means well, but his practice exams look nothing like his actual exams. He designs questions that force students into a box by ensuring the problem gets solved 'his way.' If you want to save your GPA (or your wellbeing), wait to take any physics class with a different professor. He was meant for research, not teaching.

Heads up that a lot of reviews around the Fall 2025 semester come from a transition point for the PHYS121 course, so we were essentially the department's second group of lab rats after last year.

Solid professor who has improved throughout the course...just wish he was clearer initially/had things planned out better
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Exam covering all content post-Thanksgiving break! So much to be thankful for!!!

Lol i feel like people have to be trolling on these reviews. Im not going to lie his lectures can be very confusing, but he is extremely accessible and has done a much better job recently at giving materials out beforehand and identifying what we do each week. Not the worst but also could improve by decreasing the amount of abstract ideas he shows.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: SO HARD. the weekly quizzes are super difficult-- we learn a concept and then two days later we're expected to apply it to a spring rotating while someone's juggling the spring (not accurate but its what it feels like). studying is impossible bc there are limited resources that are either super hard or not reflective of the test

He means very well and is obviously very passionate about the subject, however his level of knowledge is not the best fit for an intro course. Being a primarily pre-med class, no one has an issue with a difficult subject or putting in the work- it's literally that the structure of the class makes it near impossible to even know how to do well
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Cetina is the worst lecturer i have had; lectures are totally unrelated to material you need for the weekly homeworks and quizzes. He spends an hour and 15 min talking about abstract concepts and deriving equations. Quizzes are incredibly hard and every week. Completely different to practice quizzes from RGB's course. No clear idea of material.

As bad as taking Orgo with Qiu Wang. Similarly a very smart and kind prof but absolutely horrible at teaching. Hard-to-follow and disorganized lectures make you completely reliant on the textbook, and you spend way more time on this class than you should. Also gives us no time to self-learn advanced concepts before the weekly quizzes. AVOID.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I've never struggled this much with a class. Having to drop more than 1/2 way through the semester, trust me and take physics over the summer

Not to sound like a broken record, but it blows my mind how difficult a single professor can make a course. This is Physics I. The averages on weekly quizzes are low, and the lecture material often makes little to no sense. Decided to take Physics here at Duke. Little did I know.

Terrible professor. Lectures are basically useless, he only talks abstractly about topics, without ever explaining things in a way that actually helps you learn. You're forced to teach yourself everything from the textbook. The quizzes are unpredictable, and he expects you to know more than he's covered. Expect to learn most things on your own.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This professor is by far the worst professor I have ever had. He is so bad, I had to rate (this is my first ever RMP). He makes every other difficult class look like child's play. Ridiculous weekly quizzes that are IRRELEVANT to his lectures. Avoid at all costs. Practice materials are taken from another physics professor whose course was easier.

Do not take physics at Duke. This class was truly the hardest thing that I have ever seen. Even if you study for 20 hours a week you will fail. If I pass this class it will ONLY be by the grace of god. Hopes and prayers for all the premeds, this class will BOMB your GPA.

He is an excellent professor whose deep understanding of physics shines through in every lecture, making complex concepts engaging. Though the coursework is very challenging, the exam questions are often unclear, and the lecture content is unhelpful. He is prepared to discuss at length any topic in office hours.

This class is EXTRAORDINARILY more challenging than it should be. Dr. Cetina is smart, but he does not know how to teach material that is new to most students. He spends the majority of lecture time on confusing demonstrations/history lessons, and assigns readings/practice a day and a half before weekly quizzes. Don't take.
Lecture material does not at all translate to quiz/exam material. I've learned the entire course on my own. Take physics elsewhere if you're a pre-med.
this guy hates premeds and cannot go through a normal physics lecture without trying to act like he personally discovered all of mechanics
Terrible at teaching the material and has really hard exams. 10/10 would struggle through again.

I'll never understand why he's teaching intro physics to nonmajors. Quizzes are much harder than those given by other professors and he often spends most of lecture discussing extra topics that aren't on the syllabus and almost certainly aren't in any other introductory course. He is passionate but simply can't relate to where most of the class is.
Deep understanding of physics, interesting lectures, great at explaining concepts!

Take with another professor at all costs. I would have failed this class if I hadn't had knowledge of some topics. Incomplete solutions to practices were posted a day before tests. Some concepts he introduced were maybe useful but were thrown straight at us without any proper build-up. Marko also showed up late for most exams... absolute disaster

Agree with every comment so far. He's a genius who cannot explain basic concepts without flexing his competence in something grandiose and interesting (enough) to him. If I have to choose between the physics major and this class, retrospectively, I'd switch my major. Absolutely traumatic and drained whatever love I once had for this department.

Absolutely bad. Went on to discuss difficult topics without building proper foundations. Homeworks were weird and unhelpful for the tests. Practice problems were given before exam which were enormously difficult and barely related to the level of ideas discussed in class, and turned out to be utterly irrelevant to the actual test questions.

Notes and homework full of typos in important sections. He does not prepare for lectures in detail and his explanations are disorganized and chaotic. Exam questions are not the hardest but very disconnected from whatever little practice is given and sometimes phrased ambiguously enough to waste much of your time trying to understand them.
Bad, dont take!
Good prof. Easy-going. Recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I took MEDIART209 as a freshman. I personally thought the class wasn't too hard. You focus on using different language and the specific framing in Visual Culture. She's very nice and gives great feedback. I believe she was easier on my class because a majority of us were freshmen. The tests are not hard. Mainly timed writing to a prompt.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: MEDIART109 is so hard and i had no idea about the final project, it's hard to adapt class context in the final. However, Choi is a nice person and so kind in class. Though I got an awful grade in the final she still explained it patiently.
Her style is very lecture heavy, but she gives interesting essay topics.

If you aren't religious, I suggest you pick a god and pray you pass. People did not pass. He abided by the grading policy where there was no wiggle room at all. The grading was in 7 categories you have to get a 70 or above - and the tests were multiple choice so read into that as you will
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: He is an amazing person/lecturer but not the right fit for a giant intro class. He cares way too much about semantics (50% on memo if it's in the wrong file format/has an extra space in the title). Quiz questions are poorly written (only times I got 100 on the quizzes was when I didn't do the readings). Take Intro PubPol with Katz if you can!

Carnes is nice and tries to make lectures engaging. That said, 155 has a heavy memo component with very specific requirements. A LOT of students struggle with them. The good news is it's S/U and you get revision opportunities, but be prepared for a frustrating experience

Don't take 155 with him unless you have time to read. A hard grader and requires you to stay on top of deadlines and read directions VERY carefully. You'll probably be annoyed with him by the end of the semester but he def cares about his students
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Backwards and difficult grading policy. Zealously anti-technology. Petty and earnest like a high-school teacher. His 'sweetness' is irrelevant.

Carnes is a decent person outside of lecture, but represents pubpol badly in 155. Writing coach system is unfair, with feedback feeling like it's justifying a randomly selected grade-- if you get a harsh writing coach, prepare to be ragebaited the whole semester. Entirely too strict on rules. I know 2 people who are dropping the major bc of this
For your mental sanity, don't take this class with him. All he cares about are his rules and is ready to fail you over the tiniest things ever.

Carnes is such a sweetie and he genuinely cares about his students. He makes lectures as engaging as possible, but sometimes the content is just dry. He's very particular about memo formatting and style, but other than that the class is really easy.

Carnes himself is a truly nice and witty guy. Dont listen to everyone hating on him they honestly just didnt want to put in the work. Memos are relatively easy if you spend a couple hours on the first 2 and an hour or so prepping for 3 and 4. Writing coach grading sometimes isnt equitable, but the class is pass-fail. About 1-2 hours reading/week.

Avoid taking this class with Carnes if you can. Very rigid about technical things (if you put an extra space in your memo title he won't accept it), makes easy concepts complicated, and isn't understanding about external situations. This intro class was the bane of my existence. I want to drop public policy as a major.
Strict grading procedures actively detract from the class. Do not take 155 with Carnes if you value sanity.
take this class with any other professor
weird expectations and made the class incredibly boring
Very rigid expectations for participation and technology ban makes it harder to engage in the class.
Great professor
Stickler for weird policies in class and not very flexible for any personal commitments or unique circumstances.

Wow wow wow! In my first semester at Duke, Prof. Carnes stood out as the most intelligent and caring of my teachers. His Neoliberalism and Pop Culture class for FOCUS was amazing. His teaching is intentional and the way he runs the class is interesting and fun. I can only say the best about Dr. Carnes. What a man!

Carnes is a decent lecturer in an unfortunately boring class. He cares about his students and is willing to meet and answer questions. I really only needed to somewhat focus on decent memos and some midterm prep to be successful - he offers memo revisions, cheat sheets, and slides containing pertinent info. Easy to pass - Carnes is a good dude!
Said 99.1 percent of all of his students have passed this class the last 3 years, and I know at least 5 people that failed this semester alone. Take with Katzenstein.

DO NOT TAKE 155 WITH CARNES!! If you have the option, wait a semester and take it with Katzenstein. I finished with an 84 in the course and I didn't "pass" the class because I didn't fulfill all 7 of his grading criteria, where you need a 70% or above in every section. He is the most passive-aggressive and boring lecturer of all time. DO NOT TAKE!
Not the most interesting lectures but considering the class is pass/fail you can't really go wrong.

Easier course in the FOCUS cluster, but it gives you the space to go crazy with the assignments. Carnes is an absolute sweetheart and the course has changed the way I see politics and popular culture. I cannot unsee the concepts we've learnt in the world around us. Discussions are mostly student-led, and he only steps in where necessary.

I took the class S/U and received an S. It is an extremely easy class now that it's S/U. It's a terrible intro to the field of public policy and incredibly boring. Carnes seems cool at first, but he can be a bit too "nice" in a way that seems superficial. He does care about his students' though! 4/10 recommend. Nothing to write home about.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Now that 155 is S/U it is an extremely easy class (only assignments are 3 memos). For an intro class, we did not learn that much content and I found lectures boring. Thought Carnes was really cool at first, but then he scheduled a mandatory memo the week of Thanksgiving. Discussion section is pointless. Class is easy but not engaging.

Take pubpol 155 with Nick! You can tell he really cares about his students and wants us to succeed. It's really easy to ask him questions and get help outside of class. The grading is tough but that's because of the Sanford policies, but he tries his best to help (dropped 5 quizzes!) and is super clear on what's tested. Lectures are helpful.

It is hard to find Professors who care as much about their students as Carnes. The grading is harsh  but that is based on Sanford policies. Carnes does what he can to mitigate the stress about grades (let us drop 5 quizzes!). The reading is heavy but manageable. The memos are tough, but will ultimately help you. Carnes is well-respected and loved.

Prof. Carnes does a great job inspiring his students. He began every class by saying "public policy is life and death serious and the decisions you make matter." The class itself isn't that bad if you know that an A (> 95) is very difficult to receive. The class itself is still quite interesting and valuable but just know that most get an A-.

If you take 155, go with Carnes! Super caring guy. Course content focuses on breadth, not depth, so material isnt always the most engaging. Memos, midterm, and final are weighed heavily, so dont stress over quizzes or TAAs! Try to FLUNCH him early as his spots fill up fast. If you need help, go to office hours! He will refer you for research too!

I loved this class. Carnes really cares about the class and his students. He's a stickler for the rules so don't expect any extensions. You're put into one group for the semester so if they suck you're kind of stuck, but I had a great experience even though I'm not a huge fan of groups. Overall my favorite class even though it was online.

Professor Carnes made a challenging class much more bearable. I couldn't have asked for a better professor. He always emphasized the power behind our decisions/ actions and called us future leaders. In doing so, he empowered us to know that we matter and motivated us that have the power to be influential someday. He really cares about his students

One of those profs that seems like a genuine guy but his class sucks. He acts like he "only cares about the learning, not the grade" but then grades extremely hard. You get a 0 if you name your Memo file incorrectly (even only an extra space!). The class is most definitely a weed out class and doesn't show you what pubpol feels like.

Carnes truly wants all students to do well. We took 13 quizzes, and he is dropping the 5 lowest. Memos are graded pretty aggressively by your Writing Coach, but fairly if you really look at the rubric. Readings weren't bad, but can be long depending on the week. You have an additional group quiz/project every week, so pray you get a good one.

This class is a stressful and extremely abstract introduction to public policy at Duke. Memos are graded harshly and anonymously, and feedback is almost always minimal. The only thing keeping me from abandoning Sanford altogether is the chorus of upperclassmen telling me that 155 is just awful - an anomaly in an otherwise great major.

Carnes is a nice guy who tries to relate to students and be lenient, but that in no way overcomes the fact that the class is graded capriciously, is only loosely related to public policy, and overall will keep you stressed all semester. As far as classes go, this one is easily a textbook weeder that is designed to turn people away - and it shows!

Carnes always made class very enjoyable. Although the class was tough, if youre interested in Public Policy 155D with Carnes is a great class and you have to take it to start. The work was never too much, but was challenging (a good hard).

Prof Carnes is a fantastic guy. 155 is a classic weed out class, and is hampered by a lack of flexibility and Sanford's archaic curriculum. I'm happy to be done with the classthe ridiculous complexity of course policies and having anonymous writing coaches for memos who give unclear feedback were constant sources of frustration and anxiety.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I have never met another professor who cares so much about his students well-being. He adjusted the class multiple times throughout the semester in response to feedback from students, after having already changed from the old 155 grading policy. Accessible through piazza at almost all hours of the day. Memos were graded very harshly.

Nice guy but the course policies are over the top, too strict, and leave no room for error or forgiveness. If you make any mistakes, even with the formatting on your assignments your grade and gpa will suffer.

Sanford has a horrible grading curve, but Dr. Carnes is a fantastic professor. He makes lectures super interesting and is very receptive to student feedback. It is clear he cares about his students and the course.

Everyone should take 155 with Nick. Sanford has a ridiculous grading policy, but the life lessons I learned from Nick's class are 100% worth it. Your GPA doesn't matter as much as permanent life skills and a greater understanding of public policy. Nick is an incredible guy, and I strongly suggest everyone flunch him to get to know him.

Carnes is one of a kind. He is intentional about every single thing that happens in the classroom, is very organized and methodological, cares about his students, and makes class funny and enjoyable. Sanford's grading curve is miserable, but he is open to feedback and adjusts the way he teaches for his students to be as objective as possible.

I am very surprised by the rating given by other students for 155. I really enjoyed the course and found the topics discussed great preparation for other public policy course and can be applied to everyday life. The grading policy is frustrating and the memos don't always have a clear grading format, but you learn a lot. 100% recommend.

Carnes is an amazing professor. Take the time to really get to know him and visit him during his office hours. He is super helpful and always willing to help. This class was very heavily focused on decision making and memo writing. Sanford curves apply (94 for even an A-). I loved this class and the curve was the only thing that I hated.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Grading is completely arbitrary. Cut off to get an A- was a 94% and students below that get curved down. Did not discuss public policy at all. Instead, we only talked about how to make better decisions and then were graded based upon completely subjective standards. If I wanted to take a class based upon decision making, I would have signed up
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: While Carnes is nice, this class is ridiculous. I've never had such bad anxiety in it. The cutoff to get an A- is a 94% right now, and anything below that is a B+. One grade threw me into that range, and it made me angry for trying when I could've just done way less and have gotten the same grade anyways. The curve will make you hate this class.

The lectures are all very engaging and entertaining. He is very clear about course content and has WHAT you have to know slides for all the readings and learning for the day that might come up on the test. Regularly accepts feedback from students and changes accordingly. Very accommodating. Sanford grading scale applies (10-20% A- to A+ only).
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Engaging, genuinely kind prof who tried to be fair. But the class itself sucks. The course material was rudimentary & SO boring, and Sanford's god-awful grading policies mean that your grade is solely decided by things like submitting an assignment in PDF instead of Word doc form (2/3 letter grade deduction). Don't take it unless you really have to

155 is one of the worst classes I have ever taken and Carnes was a large part of that. Nothing you learn gets tested, and memossomething you learn nothing aboutare 50% of your grade. And Carnes counts memos as late for people who upload it as a PDF instead of a Word file. He and the class are extremely unpleasant. Never take it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: NICK CARNES IS THE LOVE OF MY LIFE. Great professor, super helpful and accommodating so don't miss out on office hours. Explains things very clearly and focuses more on practical application. Such a great instructor and one of my favorite courses at Duke so far, learned so much from it. Don't miss out on him.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Dr. Carnes is, hands down, the best professor I have had at Duke. His care for his students and passion for teaching are endless, and he is the first instructor I have ever seen make a flipped classroom work. He made me love my major, and his grading and assessments were beyond fair. You'll learn a lot and earn an amazing mentor all at once.

Prof. Carnes is honestly a rarity in the teaching profession - he genuinely cares about learning and makes it so that students don't have to stress about their grades. Even though I feel like I didn't do much (or really anything) for this class, I still learned a lot. The material is boring but he teaches it super well. TAKE THIS CLASS WITH CARNES.

Carnes is amazing. He's hilarious and actually cares about his students. He understands that students want to learn, but also get good grades, so he gives you several opportunities to boost your grade up if you're not a good quiz-taker. He takes feedback seriously and genuinely wants to make his class enjoyable. Do yourself a favor, take his class.
Nick is one of the best instructors I have ever had. He makes the classroom engaging, and he has a great sense of humor.

I'm glad I didn't take a class with Nick until I was a grad student because he would have raised expectations for Duke professor. Honestly the best professor I've taken in my 5 years here. I hate politics and yet he taught me why I need to care and understand these processes to be an active citizen.

Professor Carnes and this class are ridiculous. The entire class is a theatrical production, and then the final exam (10 questions worth 25% of your grade) erases all the work you did throughout the year. There is no point in taking this class with him.

Great professor. The flipped classroom approach really gets students to learn the material in a non-stressful way. Cares about his students and will go the extra mile to make sure you do well if you are struggling and you reach out.
Carnes is a really funny, interesting professor. He taught the material in a way in which I was confused why I wasn't doing more work, but I still learned a lot. Take 301 with him.
Carnes is the man. So funny and awesome. Class is very manageable.

Carnes is the man. One of the few professors I've ever bonded with on something outside of academics. Some of the weekly readiness assessments are tricky, but if you go to every lecture and understand the slides, you'll slay the midterm and final.
INCREDIBLE. Very easy, but you still learn a lot. He is so passionate about the subject matter, and everything he does is an attempt to make you just as passionate.
Brilliant!
Carnes is the man and so charming!
Awesome professor; approachable, helpful, and manages to make the class incredibly dynamic and interesting. Would highly suggest that you take PubPol 301 with him

Simply put, Carnes is a boss. One of the nicest and funniest teachers I have had at Duke. Makes the subject matter incredibly enjoyable and even runs a march madness bracket every spring. Definitely take PubPol 301 with him.

Carnes is the nicest guy you will ever meet, his lectures are so straightforward and he really cares about his students (always brought us coffee and doughnuts!) he is happy to meet with you out side of class and loves giving popular examples of class topics (memes and jersey shore appeared frequently in lecture slides)

Dr. Carnes is awesome.  During his lectures, he applies all the course material to current events. What was great about his specific 114 course was that for each of the 3 memos, there were 2 drafts.  THe first draft is not graded and the you get great feedback from the TAs.  It really helped my memo writing abilities.

I have no idea how the above review is possible. Dr. Carnes is an excellent professor and a down to earth guy.  His lectures are enjoyable because he is passionate about the subject and he makes the material interesting.  If you attend every lecture and setion, the midterm and final will be a breeze. Howver, the memos can be pretty difficult.
This guy is not helpful and not articulate. stay away.
my goat. he really cares about being a good resource and educator. its so refreshing and wonderful. he sounds like an audiobook and i could listen to him forever

Gooden is a great professor and makes it pretty easy to do well in the class. He is super lenient with grading and really doesn't end up doing a lot of content compared to other profs. Highly recommend if you just need to take Orgo I (like BME or for other reasons), but if you are planning to move forwarding with O chem. Goodluck...

This is a difficult class, no doubt about that. However, Gooden is an incredible teacher who covers all of the content thoroughly, is always available for questions, and is super understanding. All I did was show up & make sure I understood the disc/hw problems & I was able to excel. Anything else is just a skill issue with this goat teacher imo

I had to withdraw after the first exam (50% regraded to 75%) Despite having a 4.9 rating I had an subpar experience. Some people excel in this class which happens to be the vocal minority on RMP and is not representative of the true experience taking this class. I have a strong chem background but this class had me studying 50+ hours for an F.

Dr.Gooden was a great guy but, it didn't work out for me as well as I had hoped. I studied every day, and spent 35+ hours over the weekend studying. The tests did not reflect your knowledge and effort was not translated. My friends at the marine lab had an entirely different experience receiving extra points on their tests. test taking > orgo

LOVE Dr. Gooden. He is one of the most caring and straightforward profs that I've met at my time at Duke that truly understands the students' perspective. Such a nice man and everyone adores him. Gotta say he is really hard on himself and wish he would take care of himself more. Adapts to the needs of each summer cohort!
The GOAT of easy organic chemistry. The GOAT of the whole chem department tbh. Bro was a frickin marine too. Chillest of the chillers.

Although summer orgo was graded on few things, Dr. Gooden is one of, if not the best, profs I've had so far at Duke. Makes efficient use of time and makes sure you know relevant content for exams and real world application. No tricks on exams and a very straightforward and caring person. Can't say enough don't hesitate to take his class!

He's like the real-life version of Organic chemistry tutor - genuinely, I think the best teacher I've had at Duke so far. Explain difficult concepts simply and effectively & really cares about his students. As long as you pay attention, you will do well. If you have the opportunity to take it with him, I'd highly encourage it.

The BEST Orgo 1 professor at Duke. I had a fantastic experience when I took his class last summer and cannot recommend him enough, I wish he taught during the year. He was very very fair and exams were like the practice material. Overall just a great dude, you would be smart to take it with him.

Wow. Just wow. The chem department at Duke isn't the best. But goodness, they truly have a gem in Dr. Gooden. He actually wants his students to do well and cares about their well being. He's a great lecturer, meets with you if you need help, explains things so well and never makes you feel bad if you don't. We truly need more professors like him.

It was extremely stimulating because Dr. Gooden cared about his students and us learning.He was excellent. He is a phenomenal explainer of organic chemistry because he is able to simplify complex concepts so that they are understandable. He is also extremely knowledgable and can explain a single concept in multiple ways. Take his class. period.

Best Chemistry teacher at Duke for sure! Provides note templates to fill in during lecture so attendance is relatively important to do well but not mandatory. Problem sets and practice exams are very similar to the tests. Always willing to take time with students outside of class and is super understanding!

AMAZING. Best organic chemistry teacher ever. He made class interesting and teaches extremely well. Never straight memorization. Gives really good worksheets to prepare for exams. Go to class, ask questions and study hard because it is a difficult class by nature, but he is the best teacher in the Duke Chem department

Super intelligent but was able to explain difficult concepts clearly without being condescending which is rare. Really nice and down to earth. Content is difficult but tests are just like the problem sets.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took Orgo with Dr. Gooden over the summer and loved it! With only six weeks to cover everything, summer courses can be difficult (especially Orgo), but he made it very manageable. He teaches overall topics instead of specifics and tests as such- just practice the problem sets he provides. Definitely one of my favorite professors at Duke!

Best professor at Duke(no cap). Is amazing at taking difficult material and simplifying it. Understands that most of us aren't trying to be organic chemists so don't focus too much on the small details, instead shows us big picture. No quizzes/HW, only 3 exams, but the tests were just like the problem sets, which he makes himself based on old exams
Best Orgo 1 professor at Duke by far. Definitely take this class with Gooden if you can!!!

Best Orgo professor ever. More focused on the big picture and your learning rather than specific details trying to bring your grade down. Extremely accessible and caring. By far, one of the best professors at Duke. Highly reccomend.

Dr. Gooden is an amazing professor who cares about his students. He took the time with me out of class to explain concepts I didnt understand for an hour. His tests are straightforward - as long as you do the practice problems and ask questions when youre confused, the tests are fine. Lectures are succinct, but in a way that ensures understanding

After doing bad on the first exam Dr. Gooden set up a meeting with me and helped me work through all of my mistakes and set up a study plan for the rest of the semester. He knows that most students in the class are not trying to become organic chemists so he focuses on the bigger picture instead of smaller details. Best prof ive had at Duke by far.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Gooden is a real gem. A genius and he's brilliant at simplifying the topics for students to understand. He knows he's not here to make us organic chemists but to teach us the bigger picture. Work hard and you'll be fine. Fair, humble, and way too hard on himself. He makes the STEM department at Duke that much more bearable.

Dr Gooden is the most sincere, fair, caring professor I've had the privilege of taking while at Duke. He has really gone above and beyond in making the transition to online during COVID easier, which shows how much he cares about his students and genuinely wants them to learn. A class where your grade actually indicates your knowledge and effort.

If you have to take orgo at Duke, take it with Gooden. Not only was he extremely accessible outside of class, but his exams were very fair and his expectations were made clear. He does a very good job of taking complex concepts and explaining them in an easily understandable way.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Gooden was an amazing Professor. He was very accessible, very caring, and an amazing lecturer. You can really tell that he enjoys what he does and wants all of his students to do well unlike many other Orgo professors

Gooden tries to make the time for as many students as he can despite being a full-time organic chemist and dad himself. He's caring, and I really suggest going into his office hours if you don't understand the material. I started doing much better when I made the time to see him. Take him if you can, bc he's won't be a professor for long.

If you are taking orgo at duke take it with Gooden!! He truly wants his students to understand the subject. Definitely go to class because he posts lecture notes with blanks so you need to fill in the important info
