I thank my lucky stars every day I got to learn orgo from him. He is very clear and concise, and truly wants to see his students do well! Although orgo isn't an easy subject, he made sure the tests were simple enough to cover the main topics and didn't try to trick students at all! Averages were fairly high and if you study you will do well

The best professor for orgo. Take him you will not regret it. Presents material with clarity and the exams are just like his practice tests. I'm happy to have been in his class as he is one of the best professor that I have taken.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Lectures were straightforward and exams were just like the practice problems. He makes the concepts easy to understand , leaves out complicated stuff we don't need to know, and makes it pretty clear that he won't pull tricks on exams. Organic chemistry is stigmatized to be hard, but if you take it with Gooden, your life will be a lot easier!

Honestly loved learning orgo with this man. He didn't try to trick you, and made sure that you really understood the content. Always willing to help. Really wish he was teaching Orgo 2 because I would take it with him in a heartbeat. He really cares about students actually learning the material and internalizing it. If you take orgo, you want him!

Dr. Gooden is an excellent and clear lecturer. He is extremely knowledgeable, and the biological/drug applications of organic chemistry that he discusses are fascinating. He writes practice problems that give students a good idea of what to expect on the exams. Dr. Gooden made a difficult course enjoyable, and I definitely learned a lot.

yea so the person under says skip class u wont pass but this fake news bc i never went and just used the notes he posted online bc he reads off of them word for word pretty much in class (based on the few times i went). Gooden also uses really big words in class like "nascent" like idk what that means. he makes the last test and the final easy tho

Dr. Gooden is possibly the best professor I have had at Duke. He is an amazing lecturer and really cares about his students. He DOES NOT curve the class, but the tests are reasonable. Dr. Gooden writes his own practice problems that are similar to those on the exam, so there are no surprises.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: You will appreciate this class. This class taught me to appreciate Organic Chemistry and the concepts. You will do well! Study, Study, Study! Practice, practice, practice. Don't be afraid to ask for help either.

Dave was honestly one of the kindest and most supportive professors I have had at Duke! He genuinely wanted everyone in the class to do well and was so willing to go the extra mile to help make sure students felt comfortable with the material.  If you have to take orgo take it with Dave!!!

I was in his first class teaching during summer session 1. He's a very, very smart dude and inserts awesome tidbits relating what we are studying to his research. He's a really nice guy and wants everyone to do well.

Professor Rose was always kind and accommodating for our concerns. Gave hard tests and little feedback on how to do better, but encouraged lots of honest policy discussion. We had an issue with our TA and she was great with taking over the TA tasks and grading our assignments herself, even on a tight timeline at the end of the semester.

Very tough to get an A in this class. Midterms test random content from readings. Grade is almost entirely decided by TA team so make sure to get a good TA. Content is boring and lectures are minimally stimulating. Take with another professor if you can.

I thoroughly enjoyed Professor Rose's Pub Pol 301 class, which offered valuable insights into the politics of public policy. Her engaging discussions made the material memorable, and while the memos were graded rigorously, it pushed us to improve. The midterm and final required solid preparation but were manageable and rewarding.

Professor Rose is a sweetheart and learning Gen Z slang. As other reviews say, assignment guidelines are sometimes unclear, slides aren't posted after class, and Rose is unreachable by email. Course content isn't super interesting, but Rose tries to make it interesting. Grading is completely dependent on your TA. Midterm exam arbitrarily graded.

She stays to answer questions after class, is helpful during office hours, and does her best to find times to meet. Her class is difficult, but I've learned a lot. She's accommodating and wants students to succeed. The TAs are organized although their grading can vary. She's a good lecturer, incredibly smart, and one of the nicest professors here.
Completely agree with the reviewer below. This class is unreasonable. Take 301 with someone else if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Prof Rose is entirely inaccessible outside of class and doesn't respond to emails. The TAs and Prof Rose have ZERO communication, so the class is chaos. Some TAs gave their sections a B- on everything and others gave all As. The exams are on niche facts from readings, not content related to policy analysis. Take 301 with another professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: It seems like no one, including the TAs, knows what 'clear instructions' mean in this class. Resources are poorly organized.

Rose's content is fine and beneficial to the public policy major. The way she does it, though, is unproductive and makes the course much more tedious than necessary. Unfortunate for such a "highly ranked" public policy major.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The professor does not post the slides and the pace is too fast. Readings do not correlate to lecture and is laden with personal agendas. Take 301 with another professor if you can.
SUCH a kind human, but the class itself is boring. I don't really fault Prof Rose for this though; I think the content is just tedious. The guest speakers she brought in were cool though!

Rose is brilliant and inspiring. Although the structure of 301 is frustrating and the material is mundane, Rose brings energy & excitement. She's also incredibly accessible outside of class. However, 301 is primarily graded by TAs with less memo-writing experience than undergrads and seems extremely subjective. That said, lots of EC opportunities.

I don't relate with the perfect reviews of Prof Rose here. We are a class of 100+ people and around 10 actually participate in class, because the material is boring. Her TAs have really high expectation of your memos and grade harshly on memos, especially if you need paragraph or sentence level revision. Exams test on the most trivial things.

Professor Rose is an amazing professor, but the structure of 301 was frustrating. The group projects are very work intensive, so you spend all of your time working on them outside of class and not using any of the material from the lectures until the final exam, which was just an open-ended paper. Overall, a frustrating experience but great prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: Dr. Rose is a true gem among Duke professors. Her enthusiasm and brilliance in the PubPol field shone through in every lecture. Will hope to get her to teach courses at Duke Kunshan for the 2022-23 academic year.

Professor Rose is one of the best professors I've had at Duke. Her lectures are engaging despite occasionally boring material. The readings are maangable, and, more importantly, deeply relevant to modern problems, which is the reason I'm a Pubpol major in the first place. Instructions are clear, assignments are fairly graded. 10/10.

Rose is an amazing person. But her class is insane. The readings are tedious, and her lectures are pointless. The exams are impossible, and she tests you on the most random, specific facts that you would never know to study. She expects you to spend all your time doing projects for this class that end up only being 5% of your grade. Not worth it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Super nice, very knowledgeable, Politics of Inequality is a great class (readings, participation, 10-page paper).  Only complaint is that her quizzes were way too specific and the grade was way too heavily weighted on the midterm and final (70% combined) for a seminar.  Still definitely recommend the class.

Professor Rose is very nice and makes herself available to meet outside of class. Even though Pub Pol 301 is a big class, she really makes an effort to know everyone's name and encourages participation. There are pop quizzes on the reading so you should go to class, but the quizzes are easy and don't count for much of the final grade.
Nice grader and nice professor. Professor Landry's classes are really interesting, and his office hours are really helpful.
Nice professor and nice grader. This course covers a lot of material, but Professor Landry's classes are really interesting.
So bad experience...
Useless class. I didn't learn anything useful. Professor just talk about his research and nothing really important.
I really liked his class and he was very accommodating and easygoing.

reviews.comment:
He is unapproachable and not very nice. He explains concepts very badly and makes it difficult to understand concepts. 

I don't understand why we need to take such useless class.
Class was so boring...I didn't enjoy the class at all, and don't the use of this course in the major. It's a 2 and not a 1 because he was a generous grader....everything else in the class was bad.

You're going to read a lot for this class. If you don't, lectures will feel disjointed. The workload is a bit on the heavy side. The content is insightful and it'll give you more insight into current affairs. He is very kind and provides bonus points. The tests are ridiculously easy, multiple choice and cover the lecture notes and readings.

reviews.comment: A lot of papers as part of the course run by this professor.

reviews.comment: Although ECON201 was not an easy class, and the readings were really long, but professor Landry is very caring and helpful. He's extremely knowledgeable in his field, and although he may be a bit hard to follow at times, I learned a lot from his class. Overall, he's a really impressive professor and I can't wait to take another class with him.

He is not a tough grader nor an easy grader, just equal to the effort one puts in. He is very knowledgeable: gives real-life economic examples to supplement learning. Also gives us opportunity to choose our presentation and essay topic. 10/10 would take again. Also gives great career advice and is very accessible outside class (email)
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Landry is great! He's so knowledgeable about political economy (he's worked extensively in the field so it makes a lot of sense that he knows so much), and he's an expert on tying current events into what we're talking about. The workload for the class is very manageable, which allows you to focus on learning the concepts.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Knowledgeable and gives great feedback. He is also easy to talk to and accessible. The class is great for anyone interested in exploring any of their interests (and have a data analysis take on it)!

There's a lot of reading in this course but if you're interested in Data Analysis, the readings are beyond interesting. The writing assignment give you a lot of freedom to explore any topic you want to focus on and Prof gives detailed feedback as he knows so much about everything lol. Not a harsh grader either so that's nice.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: This professor has his own insight of political economy's development. During the session, multiple perspectives from various factions, institutions and stakeholders are introduced. Anyone interested in fun cases and real life examples should try this class! *His career and education background are also strong for teaching in this field.

Like other fellows have mentioned, Prof. David Landry is quite experienced with his consultant role now and in world bank before. He conducts great researches and is familiar with the situations he lectures. If you read all the materials, you will have a great time, but if you want to cheat or freeride, go somewhere else.

Not much to say. He's just great. He's young, experienced, and very knowledgeable. I think some might get bored in his class but if one can make the most out of him, and once one gets to know him - he's just fantastic!

If you want to major in Political Economy, he's the best professor to take interdisciplinary courses. Not only is he great in teaching, but he is also easily approachable. If you have any questions or concerns, go to his office hours! Highly recommended.

David is simply fantastic. He's young, understands how to teach undergraduates, and is an all-around outstanding professor. He would even give us breaks during out 2.5 hour class time to pick up pastries from the local baker delivering to campus.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr E genuinely is passionate about her area of interest but is hard to reach outside of class. She also would consistently and repeatedly mix up POC students in the class and call them by the wrong name, and then proceed to have really uncomfortable reactions to doing so.
Is a very kind and caring professor, but has very unclear instructions and grading criteria. Grades things very arbitrarily. Pretty interesting content

Dr. E cares for her students, yet curriculum comes up short. Class debates and final paper make up most of the grade, yet grading criteria is arbitrary and biased. Multiple reading responses every week with readings can be tedious. The class concepts are interesting, but lectures tended to be boring, other than her anecdotes. Solid psychology class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Dr. E is incredibly kind and caring, but extremely disorganized. Lecture style & course content are incredibly boring. Class focuses far more on public perspectives of crime than on criminal psychology. No interesting case studies. 2 debates & final paper make up 75% of grade. Grading isn't harsh, but arbitrary with unclear assignment instructions.

medium course load: in-class lectures&seminars w/ readings&responses, group debate presentations, & 5-page brief. 

Very caring prof. who bakes for students, individually checks-in, stays after class, & brings her dog into class. Very intelligent/experienced.

Arbitrary grading w/ unclear criteria. Insufficient feedback. Misses emails. Very liberal

Dr. Ehrensaft is very caring and wants her students to succeed. Her lectures were relatively engaging and she always made sure she was available after class if anybody needed help. Homework was easy, just show up to class and participate. Material was also easy to digest. The final paper was tedious and not explained well yet manageable.
Professor Ehrensaft is a good person but a mediocre professor. She cares about her students, but her lectures tend to be boring, long, and her instructions tend to be very vague.

Dr. Ehrensaft is a decent lecturer, but fairly inaccessible outside of class. She rarely posts assignments in a timely fashion, leading students scrambling to complete assignments and readings. Her grading expectations are unclear, with her rubrics being very broad if any rubric is posted at all. Overall, a nice person but not the best professor.

Dr. Ehrensaft is fairly good overall. Criminal Psych is fascinating but the lectures can get a bit dull. When she didn't finish slides, you had to review them on your own. Discussions were mildly stimulating. Not very timely at posting readings - sometimes you get large chunks in a day's notice. Isn't very accessible outside of class.

One of the easier A's at Duke. Very bureaucratic class with many different assignments but none were particularly difficult. Big assignments are not graded as harshly as people make it seem if you give decent effort. Go to class and your final exam will be optional too. I was never worried I wouldn't get an A in this class.
Michael Jordan of psych profs
She's almost as goated as michael jordan
Of everyone teacher at Duke, Psych midterm coming up, fate of the universe on the line, the Martians have the death beam pointed at Earth, I need to pass... I WANT DR. GRISHAM!
Kind professor with engaging lectures. Class has readings for every lecture, a paper, smaller assignments, and three midterms as well as a test. Enjoyable class overall!

Dr. Grisham is an awesome lecturer. She cares about the subject and her passion is evident. Going to lecturers offers you the opportunity to skip the final exam, which made finals season so much less stressful personally. Definitely read the textbook, study lecture slides, and attend class and A's are doable on the three midterms.
Psych 101 with Dr. Grisham and Dr. Hard was great!

Dr. Grisham was great during lectures, and the information is really presented well. This class is just a lot of work, and if you do not have prior experience with psychology get ready to memorize a ton of terms. Overall, would recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Test heavy

reviews.comment: The lectures for psych 101 were AMAZING. The work is sometimes challenging but manageable, and I absolutely loved this class. If you've taken AP Psychology, you'll do great. Dr. Grisham is super funny and an excellent lecturer.

I love Grisham. Her and Hard make an amazing team. The lectures are so incredibly engaging and I surprisingly loved the tech-free format. This class made me choose to minor in psych. The Canvas organization is so easy to navigate and I enjoyed all of the projects and papers.
Good professor overall. The class itself is lowkey a lot of work so it may not be the easy A you expect, but the lectures are pretty interesting and some of the interactive parts are fun.

Psych 101 with Dr. Grisham was extremely well-run, engaging, and doable. Lectures were very interesting and felt like Ted Talks. Most of the test content is covered in lecture with the remainder coming from the textbook (expect weekly reading and quizzes). Discussion sometimes felt like a waste of time, but overall an amazing class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I LOVED Dr. Grisham! Her and Dr. Hard made learning psychology so enjoyable. Dr. Grisham is so nice and I absolutely recommend chatting with her outside of class about life. The homework is reasonable and you will be just fine on the tests if you study. There is one big project/paper that you need to put considerable effort into though!

Dr. Grisham teaches Psych 101 with Dr. Hard. She is an overall great person and is very kind and caring towards students. However, her lectures are unnecessarily drawn out and slow. Compared to Dr. Hard, Dr. Grisham's lectures take too long to get to the point and can get very boring. The class itself is not too hard but has a lot of busywork.

Dr. Grisham is an amazing teacher for Psych101. Every lecture felt so engaging and gave a wide variety of topics. Expectations for the class are very clear, and the TF's are readily available to provide support and feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Grisham is awesome! She co-teaches PSY101 with Dr. Hard and is relatively new; however, she is a great lecturer and super passionate about psychology. You can tell that she loves what she does, which is inspiring. This class requires reading the textbook in addition to attending lecturers to do well on exams, but the work load is manageable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Co-teaches Psych 101 w/ Dr. Hard. Did amazing for her first year! Super open to helping out students and is excited about the topics she teaches! Her lectures are slightly less continous than Dr. Hard's in terms of explaining concepts but amazing professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Grisham is really cool-- so much more than just someone in Dr. Hard's shadow. Her lectures are kinda dull sometimes (esp compared to Hard) but she is super kind and sweet and will help if you ask. I injured myself during the semester and she remembered to check in on me which was cool given that it is a 300 person class.

Dr. Grisham was brand new to Duke and teaching, but she was amazing. She taught alongside Dr. Hard and made the class incredibly enjoyable. The tests are easy to study for as most of the content in lecture based and only regarding bolded terms in the textbook. This class was one of the reason I decided to pursue psych major, so I highly recommend.

New professor as of Fall 2022. She is really nice and clearly cares about Psych and teaching. She's still working out some kinks as a newbie here like occasional mistakes in lecture, but that's normal. She coteaches with Dr. Hard who gets all the hype (and deserves it), but don't look past Grisham - she's pretty cool too! Very accessible and kind.

Really interesting lectures, and is happy to get to know students outside of class. Also is an easy grader and even bumps up final grades on the edge if you participated in class. Most of the class grades are from memos.

Dr. Albright is truly incredible. I took US Environmental Policy and the class was very fair -- if you take her feedback and participate in class, you will do well. Lectures were engaging and meaningful, with lots of discussion activities that kept class active. Dr. Albright is extremely talented and I learned so much from this class!

I loved having professor Albright! She has a lot of expertise on the topic, and we learned a lot. She was kind and accessible outside of class to discuss assignments or otherwise. Very flexible on due dates, and canceled class a few times. She provides a lot of feedback on writing assignments, and your grades will likely be fine if you use it.

Betsy is one of the best professors I've ever had. I saw some ratings that she "made students feel stupid" and I think that is bs. She is direct, so be prepared to take feedback, but she genuinely wants her students to do well and is extremely helpful. She always answers emails and will make time to help you understand difficult concepts.

She consistently makes students feel unintelligent whenever they ask questions. I genuinely don't understand why she's still teaching at Duke, as she doesn't deserve a position as a professor here. Her behavior also raises concerns about potential racism or bias, as she seems particularly disrespectful toward certain groups of students.
worst professor I've ever met, worst person to get along

Enjoyed taking Prof. Albright's class, she always gave very helpful feedback on assignments and was flexible about due dates. Lecture attendance wasn't mandatory but you'd miss a good bit of information by not going. Not a harsh grader but doesn't hand out As, make sure to read her feedback. Very accessible office hours showing she WANTS to help.

BAD Professor. Expects all of her students to be experts already and makes you feel stupid if you ask her a question. She made me feel stupid that I had a learning disability. I never met a professor so unwilling to help me succeed in a class after trying so hard.

Great professor who really cares about her students' learning. Several memos and papers, but she gives clear feedback and made me much better at writing memos. Content is really interesting and relevant for today. Assigns a decent amount of reading, but doesn't test on it, so you can go at your own pace.

I LOVE BETSY! She is so wonderful and such a great lecturer. Very willing to meet outside class and get you involved in research, ind study, etc. Her Env Policy class was shaped around the current administration and changed everyday. She teaches you how to write a policy memo and gives great feedback on papers and projects. DEF A MUST!

Great professor, 403 covers a lot of content at a pretty fast pace with a decent level of abstraction but his lectures are always engaging and well-motivated. The final project is a great opportunity to dive deeper into whatever pushed you to take the course or some new topic mentioned in lecture

The scoring is pretty unforgiving, and your final mark is heavily tied to just a few tests—so a single off day can tank you. Problem sets take a long time, and you don't get much in the way of comments or guidance back.
Grading is harsh and most of the grade sits on a couple of exams, so one bad day hurts a lot. Homework is long and feedback is limited.
Tough grader is an understatement- it's a terrible class.

Fall2023. Ezra is an incredibly engaging lecturer and sometimes too brilliant for his own good. Material was insanely hard but lectures were so fun I'd take it again in a heartbeat. Our entire class would stay after lectures and he always stayed to help. Office hours were held outside if the weather is nice + the whole class would be there.
I didn't learn anything, and I'm amazed the average is so high.
holy cow linear algebra
Taking this class with this professor is designed to fail you.

Miller's class was genuinely the hardest class I've taken in my life. Expect around 10-15 hours of work per week. If you're interested in a challenge, highly recommend 221, but if you're looking for an easy A, 221 is not the class for you. Be prepared because Miller's test questions are often harder than the other 221 professors.
You will not learn a thing.
I am convinced that the positive reviews are Ezras... not good. Avoid.
Didn't learn a thing and surprised the average is so high
Miller won't care if you pass or fail. DO NOT TAKE HIS LINEAR ALGEBRA.

Truly the worst professor I've ever had in my time at Duke. He promised his students that if they tried and went to office hours he would not fail them and then failed at least 40% of the class. Difficult material and does a very poor job of explaining the material to be understood. Tests are not similar to homework or work done in class.
I had to spend a lot of time on this class, but it's totally worth it!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: grading is unfair and if you don't answer exactly how he wants you to (esp for proofs) he takes off SO many points. he has strong bias toward ppl who go to office hours every week, which DOES COUNT toward boosting grade. also condescending toward ppl he doesn't like. clearly knows subject very well tho and decent explainer
Great teacher but the material is so difficult. Problem sets are tough. Sets difficult exams.
Blatantly does not care. Expects you to know more than him on the topic.
Awful, I have a hunch he judged me on immutable characteristics. Don't risk it; take LinAlg with someone else.

Prof Miller knows his stuff. Linear Algebra in proofs is a conceptual class and he's the right person to teach it. He plans his lectures very carefully to cover all the content in time. However, exams are difficult, proof-based, and heavily test your understanding.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Nice person but makes it known that he does not want to be teaching and does not care if people come to lectures. All lectures consist of him directly copying off the lecture notes and are incredibly fast-paced. Must teach yourself using the textbook. Homework often takes 10+ hours a week and exams are very difficult.

Expects you to know more than he teaches. I learned throughout the course that the secret to doing well in his class is to go to every office hour, and to ask him what he wants to see (which he will generously tell you). AFAIK mid semester grade not curved, but final grade is. Probably to scare you. Lots of homework. Ok lectures. Takes attendance

This class can be exhausted and Ezra can be really fast to somebody but he's trying to cover lots of basic linear algebra concepts in the most understandable manner. He also showed some good intuitions in linear algebra and further concepts that would really helpful for understanding the applications. HW is 100% fair graded. Really accessible.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Miller is very smart and clearly cares a lot about his students. He is very accessible if you email him or go to office hours with questions. Nonetheless, I found his teaching style in lectures very difficult to learn from. Mainly, the lectures went very fast, so it was hard to keep up and understand everything.

Miller cares about his students. You can tell by his short email response times and the effort that he puts in to explain concepts. He is also a fair grader; he will not take off too many points if you simply make calculational mistakes but still demonstrate an understanding of the subject. 5/5 would take again.

The graders kept quitting/get fired, the class was test heavy and the semester was condensed. The textbook in class gives "examples" (does not include the steps for getting the answer), and even people with a proof/linear background did not do well. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS unless you are MAJORING in math- anything else and this class is unnecessary
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I appreciated Prof. Miller a lot, but his teaching style was hard for me to connect to. Concur that the midterms were reasonable but the final was difficult. Can be a harsh grader as well, and only half of our homeworks got graded. That said, he cares a lot about his students, and the COVID-19 transition was done well. Tough class, learned a lot.

Miller is an excellent professor and lecturer. He covers everything in-depth in class and explains well; no need to read textbook. HW took 7-10 hrs/wk but doable with office hours, discussion, and working with others. Midterms were reasonable but the final was hard. This class is difficult if you have no proof-writing or linear algebra experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Only one homework was graded (out of 6) before the first midterm. The final exam was needlessly hard. Professor Miller explains things well if you already understand linear algebra or if you are already familiar with higher-level math, but if you are new to higher-level math, prepare to get burned. Not enough proof writing guidance was given.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Ezra Miller is the GOAT. Although the class was still super challenging, Dr. Miller is still considerate about grading. His lectures are amazing; you can tell he's super smart, but he still makes sure to prove even super obvious things. Take his class if you legitimately want to learn linear; I guarantee you'll know it like the back of your hand.

Prof. Miller isn't a bad person, but I would only take this class if you're certain you want to major in math. Multiple problem sets a week, and very little feedback on them before first exam. Didn't provide nearly enough proof writing resources for students without prior knowledge. Again, don't take unless you're certain you want to major in math.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Miller is amazing!! He is extremely willing to help after class during office hours, and he is just a really nice and funny person in general. He is very prepared for class and the material is very well organized. The class itself was the hardest class I've ever taken but I wouldn't have had any other prof. Make sure you do the homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I like Miller as a person, but his class did not match my learning style. Since he doesn't review/highlight important material I felt constantly lost in proofs during lecture. Not having practice tests or answers for homework/tests after completion severely affected learning ability. Felt like class required previous proof/matrix knowledge.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Honestly, despite the fact that I didn't do so well in the class, I'll gladly say that Professor Miller is one of the fairest graders. His class is pretty difficult, but I genuinely enjoyed it. He's a genuinely caring guy who will listen to your concerns about math and the class in general. I highkey miss him as my professor. Funny dude also
Great guy and truly brilliant. He explains concepts very well. Difficult but fair grader. He teaches well.

great dude. really solidified me wanted to be a math major. however I do think his grading was a little bit vague. he wants you do say specific things that fit a rubric and if you don't do that or explain in a different way he takes off a lot of points. absolutely loved his lectures and his style of teaching and he really does care about teaching
Super awesome and passionate teacher who genuinely loves math and teaching math. However, he is so smart that it can be hard for the average student to sometimes keep up. A overall great guy.

Miller teaches somewhat quickly and expects a lot of his students. Many take a while to adjust to proof-math, too. But he's exceptional at explaining concepts and loves to help in office hours if you've got any issues. He's also a lenient grader, and instead of curving, he bins, so people who are doing well at the end get good grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Miller is definitely the best 221 professor; he tends to be lecture heavy, and there are no practice exams, but if you understand what's going up in the class AND the homework, you're going to get a good grade. Going to office hours and class is good because he will find a way to bump your homework grade to reflect that if your grade is borderline.

Such an incredibly genuine, caring, and hilarious professor. The class is super easy, but is very test heavy (the tests are take home though.) Pretty easy A in my opinion, but lecture is "attendance mandatory." I would definitely take this class if you recruit for finance jobs as it's an easy A, great professor, and is info you learn regardless.

CJ was definitely the highlight of the course. He is super fun, possibly one of the most entertaining you could find at Duke! I would say the material is rather heavy and three exams make up most of the grade. The review videos before each exam are a must-watch. Also, this is an 8:30 class, so be prepared! But overall, great class.
Absolutely hilarious, love him

Professor Skender is super funny and overall just an amazing guy! Intro to Financial Accounting is graded on two exams only, and for anyone without a background or general accounting sense, these exams can feel very dense and difficult. They're take-home, which makes things easier though!
reviews.rating_tags: Hilarious--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Graded by very few things and easy to fall off track if you're not doing the work outside of class. CJ is an amazing professor who cares so much about his students.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: CJ is awesome. He is probably one of the funniest and strange (in a good way) professors I've had at Duke. While I will the material is challenging for an intro to accounting class, and often overwhelming, it's a fun class to take cause of the take home midterms and finals. Not an ”easy A” but would take CJ again.
C.J. Skender is GOAT.
Goes through lectures and class problems extremely fast. Super nice and funny guy. Have to do lot of reading on your own if you really want to understand the material.

Go to class! CJ is one of the funniest professors at Duke but you have to be there for it! The course is challenging and there's not much incentive to keep up with reading/homework BUT you have to force yourself to do it or else you'll be scrambling for the exams (which make up 90% of your grade). Lean heavily on the recorded exam review sessions.
You'll forever remember CJ. He is one of a kind. If we could replicate his style of teaching....all classes would be fun and effective.

Don't take it. Tests are easy, but not a single day of the semester will be enjoyable because simply the thought of having to eventually deal with the material saps away energy. The only reasons to go to lecture are that a) he writes out answers to some questions and b) he takes attendance. Don't buy the textbook.
Very kind and wants us to be engaged. The material was a bit dense for into to accounting but tests were all take home.
He is very flexible and actually wants you to learn.  If you need help then he will help you out and is willing to push you towards a grade that you need by your want to learn.
Very genuine person and willing to help students where they needed it.

Finance in the MEM program with CJ was a great experience.  Very engaging lectures with clear examples, clear expectations, and plenty of funny little quips and amusing anecdotes.  Weekly lecture content was easy to digest and easy to access in Sakai. Highly recommend attending the live session each week if possible.

CJ is really nice, but his teaching style didn't work for me. Lectures were too in-depth and not explanatory enough to help with the exams. He doesn't explain why he does the steps. Thankfully, the exams are take-home, but it took a lot of self-teaching and office hours just to pass. I wouldn't recommend the class if you're looking for an easy QS.
Great class with the GOAT!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: CJ is the goat. He is the nicest guy and makes class fun with movies and songs of the day. It is sometimes hard to keep up with his fast paced problem solving, so reviewing a little outside class would help. Tests are take home and he gives big time slots. Awesome teacher, great class.
Great professor. He's just such a genuinely nice guy and it's hard not to like him. Lectures are pretty heavy so attendance is really important but worth it.

Graded on three take home, open note exams and attendance. The class itself was super engaging and he's an awesome guy. Really excellent lecturer and wants everyone to succeed in his class. Less focused on grading and just wants to teach you something.

He's such a great guy - get to know him if you can! 

Wouldn't recommend for investment banking recruitment at all though - to all the fresh/sophs like myself who thought I would be killer at interviews after this class. This class is too much in depth/ kinda tangential to interview questions.
Really great professor.  Goes over everything in great detail and makes things simple!
Easiest class taken. Exams are open-book and the questions are almost identical to past exams. There is an official textbook but no need to purchase it.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took both econ174 and econ274 with CJ. He is probably my favorite professor at Duke. He is nice & really cares about his students. He wants everyone in his class to do well. Both classes are graded heavily on 3 exams. When I took the class they were all take home exams or open notes. The problems on the tests are exactly what you do in class!

Really passionate teacher who has a lot of experience within the field. As long as you attend the lectures and do all the homework this class is very manageable. His exam reviews are really helpful for preparing for the exams and are in a really similar manner. It's not super fascinating material but valuable nonetheless.

Over Zoom made things more boring than normal, but CJ was great and did all he could to keep the class entertaining. He truly cares about his students. Definitely get to know him outside of class. If you do the practice tests, you will get a good grade.

I loved this professor. One of the best I've ever had at Duke. He is sooo inspirational, his lectures are great (but heavy). I advise you to go over the chapters before class, so you can better understand in class. For the exams, just make sure you understand the older tests and you'll be fine.

CJ is great! His class is relatively easy, but your entire grade comes from just 3 exams. As long as you take thorough notes every class and study the released exams, you'll get a good grade. He's also super understanding and happy to help his students with anything!
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: CJ is so sweet. He is a born teacher and the way he adapted what used to be a huge lecture to the COVID remote learning world was admirable. He wants you to succeed. Content-wise, I wouldn't take this class again because I despise maths and economics and I wouldn't recommend it for people (like me) looking for an easy QS.

Professor Skender was a really engaging and inspirational professor, and his energy and interest in accounting made his students enthusiastic about the material as well. He was accessible outside class with many office hours, and he really cared about his students' understanding of the material. Go to class, do past tests, and you will do well!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational

reviews.comment: CJ is a great professor. He wants to make sure everyone can succeed but he still makes you work for the A. Sometimes he goes through content a little fast but all the lectures are recorded to watch them over, take notes, review past exams, and you'll do well. Would definitely take this class again!

Professor Skender is a sweet and caring man whose compassion shows both in and outside the classroom. He regularly stays after class to help students with questions and hosts helpful review sessions prior to each exam. As long as you complete the practice problems and pay attention during lectures, the class should be fairly straightforward.
Useful and necessary class to take. Prepares you well for banking. You'll need to work for the A.

USE THE PAST PAPERS! The test questions are very similar throughout and careful revision of previous work can help you excel. Regardless, Skender is a good professor who really cares for his students. He wants what is best out of each student, in turn meaning he was very understanding of the conditions some students were placed in bc of COVID.

A very manageable class. CJ never checks HW and prepares you well for exams, since the questions are exactly like those on past exams and practice quizzes. CJ is a great person and more than willing to help, yet his lectures are unclear and often off-topic, so I have to self-learn all contents by reading the textbook, but the material is not hard.

cj is the man. u def need to go to class bc he does all boardwork (doesn't post recording/slides) and is essentially what's on exams. times the lectures perfectly - wants to make make the class worth it. exams are just memorize plug and chug. only reason not a 5.0 is he would get off topic often which is frustrating for someone who woke up for 8:30

Very difficult material. Do not take without extensive Econ/accounting background. Extensive work expected outside of class. Attendance taken as small part of grade. Very kind man. Will help in any way possible. Incredible person.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: C.J. is an amazing professor. Very down to Earth, and serves as a father figure to everyone and anyone who comes to him. Works hard to prepare you for the tests, giving you the exact style questions that will be on them. You won't find a more caring, inspiring professor.

Has a great heart and can be funny, but I really dislike how off-topic he gets during class. Very distracting. Runs through class material too quickly so you will focus on note-taking instead of learning. Better to watch lecture videos than attend class.

One of the best professors I've ever had. Great lectures infused with interesting stories about his experiences. Completely made me forget it was an 8:30. The homework is optional. The tests are easy  he makes sure you know exactly what will be on the test and how to do it. I also took 274 with him, which was just as fun and manageable.

CJ is fun, humorous and acts as an "uncommon" professor in my view. His teaching style is funny. He loves to introduce different songs and movies for us in class and share his stories with us. His records his lecture every time, and his midterm and final are the same as the past ones, which makes it much easier for us to prepare for.
CJ is the best professor I have ever had. Although the lectures are at 8:30am, he manages to keep everyone engaged through his vivid sense of humor and amazing teaching style.

The nicest professor you'll meet at Duke. The 8:30 lectures are worth waking up for. I barely opened the textbook and still passed just from his lectures. I definitely suggest FLUNCHing him as well. 10/10 professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: TAKE THIS CLASS PASS/FAIL, it doesn't fulfill requirements anyways. This way, u can learn accounting without the stress. I found his lectures too fast to learn from. I taught myself by doing his practice questions. He takes attendance, but get old notes from someone and u don't have to pay attention in lecture. I repeat, NOTES ARE IMPORTANT.

He is hilarious and knows how to keep students entertained in a boring business class. He is a great man and he tries to help his students out a lot, even though he has 800 of them. But, the exams come straight from the coursepack!!! You do not need to go to class or pay attention to do good in this class; honestly his lectures just confused me.
Great professor, a real legend. Grade based on attendance, two mid-terms, and a final. Course material and exams become more difficult as the semester progresses.

In general, he is a nice funny guy, but he can say some pretty sexist stuff. Lecture is important (trust me I didn't go because it's at 8 am and I paid for it). Grade is mostly based on the tests, and the concepts can be very difficult. Stay on top of your work because once you get behind, it is really hard to catch up.

CJ is awesome! He's such a funny and charismatic person, especially for 8:30 AM. He's full of wisdom and tries to make a very dry topic entertaining. As long as you pay attention in class, it's an easy A. He goes over everything you need to know in class for the tests but you need to pay attention

CJ is very funny. He makes jokes all the time & tries his best to make an 8:30 AM class entertaining. However, I didn't really find the textbook useful, & CJ moves way too fast in class to grasp concepts. Studying old exams is very helpful b/c our tests are exactly like the old tests, but, in general, accounting principles are difficult to get.
Like everyone else has said, CJ is a great guy, if not the best teacher. Go to recitation and do the homework and you should be fine with the concepts.

The grade is almost entirely dependent on the tests, which you can easily prepare for by taking all of the practice tests he provides, as all of the test questions will be reused. Attending lectures is an easy way to learn the material on the tests, but since it's an 8:30 class, you can still do well in the class by only reading the online textbook

Great professor. Tests are tough and it's really up to you to stay on top of it, but if you make the effort and come to class, you'll be fine. The other day, I emailed him to say I was having some trouble with the material and he spent an hour with me individually going over the problems. Can't say the last time I had a professor do that for me.

**UNC**** CJ is one of my favorite professors that I have had. He really made class fun. The material was very tough, but you just have to put in the time to practice. Rarely took attendance, responded to emails promptly, graded fairly. The midterm and final were difficult but not impossible.

CJ knows his stuff and is incredibly kind and accessible. The course is unfortunately textbook heavy. Instead of supplanting difficult chapters with educational lectures, CJ resorts only to completing examples in class. Examples are helpful, but it's difficult to manage accounting concepts solo. Tests can be managed with lots of practice.

Coolest professor I've ever had. He is very funny and I actually look forward to his class to hear his wisdom and humor. The class is not hard, it just takes a little practice to do well on the tests. There are also plenty of opportunities to practice/ask him questions. Very interesting guy, I admire him a lot.

He's not the best lecturer- he gets very off topic and spends a good amount of class playing music and going on anecdotal tangents, only focusing a short amount of time on the actual material. I ended up having to teach myself a lot of the material but the homework is helpful. There is only a midterm and final, but he curves the final generously.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: This class is sooo easy after Econ174. He helps you out with so many of the take homes and just genuinely wants you to learn. Most of the material is from 174 and the new managerial material is really easy. Plus, it's CJ--the one, the only.

Good professor who cares and wants you to do well, but is tough to understand sometimes. He talks really quickly and uses lots of abbreviations, so sit at the front. Study past tests, do some of the homework problems, and go to the review sessions for an advantage on the tests. If you don't do so well, talk with him and he'll try to help you out.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Attending lectures is not helpful for this class. Attendance was taken sometimes. The examples he works through are not at all similar to the questions that will be on the midterm or the exam. Studying for the midterm is relatively easy; however, the final is too much information. The homework is pointless, but graded, so its just a waste of time.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: BUSI 101 is a pretty tough class at UNC as it is basically two classes worth of material combined into one. CJ is a cool and nice guy, but it's just too much material for him to teach in lectures so most of the learning is done on your own (good luck with that). Tests are pretty tough.

The course had a small portion for class attendance, then the rest of the grade was split up in midterm and final. Not keeping up with the non-graded homework assignments will kill you.  I thought the finance material was difficult and boring, but he made it as fun and interesting as possible.

"A real gem" doesn't describe CJ enough. If every professor was CJ, the world would be a much better place. Tests can be hard if you don't put in the effort, but he genuinely wants everyone to succeed and will boost your grade just by seeing if you've made effort (gone to every class and review session, improved on exams, etc.).

Professor Skender is hands down the best professor I have ever had the pleasure of being taught by. He's extremely dedicated to his students and both of his classes are incredibly interesting (yes, it's accounting). He keeps the students engaged and cracks some of the best jokes I've ever heard. One of the best experiences of my academic career.

Ok so BUSI 101 was one of the most stressful courses I took. DO NOT take this class if you don't want to major in business. The class material is insanely boring so I can't criticize Skender for not making it super interesting. Expect 3-4 hours of your Sundays dedicated to this course. Tests are tough and TA sessions are not helpful at all.

8:30 am every semester with mandatory attendance.  Took the class for job purposes.  Definitely useful in that respect, but dull material.  Cool professor though.  Probably the best-dressed guy I've seen at Duke.

While he kept lectures rather engaging, he really didn't know how to explain major concepts beyond what was given in each practice problem. If you take his class, always go to class and start preparing for the final today.

He is a really boring professor, but he puts all of his lectures online so it is really easy to not ever attend class. The class is also not particularly difficult if you memorize how to do problems rather than actually understand them.

Most incredible teacher at duke. You have to show up to class, though, and you need to make sure that you write down every word he puts on the board, take every in class practice quiz, and take lots of practice tests. That's the only way. Such an inspiring teacher who really "get's it." He knows how to make students care & find what they care about

UNC BUSI 101 Don't take this class if you don't want to major in business. He's really nice and there to help, but the class is difficult. It's managerial and financial accounting, even though I don't think it says that in the class description.

The most unique professor that you can have at Duke! He is a fair grader. He makes the class fun and even when you watch the videos from the sessions, you can't help yourself laughing! The content is really clear and the questions in the final come mostly from what he exercises in the class. He also gives a rough outline for the final exam.
the craziest, most hilarious, most genuine professor i have ever had in my life. he really wants you to get the best grade in the class, and actually learn finance.
best ever
A very cool professor, but not very good at explaining stuff. Read the textbook and do the practice exams

This professor is awesome. Through his hilarity and idiosyncrasy he makes class interesting and entertaining. He genuinely cares about teaching and his students. If you put in minimal effort and attend most classes the material shouldn't be too difficult.

Great teacher! CJ makes accounting enjoyable and fun. The math is not hard, its just a matter of getting used to the terms. Very straight forward tests,  some questions are the exact same as on the practice tests. Do the homework and practice tests and there is no reason you should not get an A.

great, funny professor. very entertaining especially at 8 30 in the morning. material is very dry and tedious. sometimes he goes through lectures really quickly and it's hard to pay attention especially if you hvaen't done the reading. I actually found the textbook to be really useful, although many of my classmates did not.
I had no interest in Financial Accounting but Prof Skender made this course interesting even at 8:30. His love for numbers, basketball, and pop culture is a killer combo and you'll never get bored!

Took CJ for two accounting classes and he made very dry material extremely entertaining.  Inspired me to go on and get an advanced law degree in taxation.  Would have never done that without CJ.  I was his worst student ever - but I am good with that.  He was funny, but frankly I was funnier.  If he ever reads this, he will know who wrote it.
He does his job every day he comes in
great teacher.

If you can keep up with the material and Skender's style of teaching, you'll highly enjoy his class. He makes Accounting interesting. It's challenging and a bit tricky, but Skender's goal is to help you get the best grade possible. Go to him for help if you need it. It's an incredibly difficult class if you wait until the last minute to study.

I like Skender a lot, but I hate this class. I do fine on the tests, but it's way too much material crammed into one semester (other schools split it into 2 semesters). A lot of theory, not enough practical application. Good for a general overview, but difficult to study for unless you just have a passion for it.

The reviews are glowing, and he's a great and fun teacher. However, I'm pretty sure most of the reviews on here are from kids who do well in the class. There's a solid 1/2 of the class who doesn't fare as well too (C's, etc.). Go to class, do your work, study, and you should be fine. Be warned: it's a ton of material.

CJ is amazing. His accounting class is extremely useful and he keeps it interesting. He actually makes an 8:30am class worth going to. The material is not hard at all if you just keep up. HIGHLY recommended.

Makes Accounting class as fun and bearable as he can. There are massive amounts of tedious material, so if you don't mind doing weekly problem sets and multiple practice tests, you can do well in this class if you study well. Not the type of class you want to wait until the last minute to catch up on--that's impossible. Average grades are B's.
Best Professor I have ever had.  I took 5 classes with him at NCSU and loved every class.
god level prof. hillarious and fantastic.
Professor Skender is a great guy, but the material is tedious.   If you get behind by skipping the lectures, it's a lot to catch up on.

Anyone that can make the subject of accounting interesting has got to be an amazing professor.  He gets to know all of his students and the triva/candy time at the beginning of class is always entertaining.  Skender's like a human computer - he knows EVERYTHING!

CJ was one of my favorite professors at Duke.  Loves to get to know the students and is a blast to go visit out of class.  One of the professors that I wish I'd maintained a relationship with.  The class material is so-so, but it's worth taking it to get to experience CJ!
No Comments

really straightforward, gives out candy in class.  funny and a really nice guy.  if you can memorize the lecture material (it's not that much) it's a guaranteed a in the class, he doesn't throw you curveballs or anything like that.
No Comments
No Comments

5 group cases + 1 final individual case. The cases are boring, but they're not too hard. You end up learning a lot of new modeling techniques that don't show up in other core stats classes. There's a lot of technical writing in the reports, but it's a useful skill. Class is dry, but Iversen does care about improving it.

Unusual class with no strict curriculum. Clients (often grad students) come in and ask for stat methods recommendations. You'll see interesting problems that arise in real datasets. Low workload, just writing short reports and giving a few presentations. Iversen is smart and helpful, but discussions are dry and he assumes you know more than you do
So dry. Forced to learn a bunch of concepts by yourself, but overall not a ton of work. Probably one of the easier STAT electives at duke

Not bad, but not great. Iversen's lectures are slow-moving, and very little teaching actually happens. The class is meant to give client recommendations re: statistical methods, but most students don't understand the complex methods themselves, so you end up writing reports on things you've never learned.  Not a lot of work, but also no reward.
Very excellent instructor, good introduction for Python in studies. Nick is very helpful and encouraging when mentoring.

Class was a good introduction to Python for data science. Flipped classroom, so have to do readings outside class and then work on exercises with a partner in class. Some classes have pop quizzes on the readings, so important to stay up to date. Not too much work besides the final project, and have 1 week to do each exercise.
He has a very structured class that is very appreciated

Nick is very, very knowledgeable about subject matter and has curated very important content for data science. Expects you to attend class but makes you do in-class activities that are totally worth it. He does push students for work and deadlines but is a really understanding guy too.
If you can't, don't take it; if you must, this rating is a warning.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Fruh is a very interesting and knowledgeable teacher. In his class, it was mainly discussion based, and there were always intriguing discussions. However, there isn't a lot of feedback on the papers you write, and they are each 25% of your grade, so it can be hard to improve on the next essay.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Fruh was an excellent professor! The class isn't an easy A, but the grading criteria for each assignment were clearly outlined. Every grade I received was reasonably given, so I had no complaints. Professor Fruh was easy to approach and ask for advice, especially with giving feedback. I'd highly recommend taking a class with him!!
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Although the China-mandated common core courses are a bit of a drag, this class was far more manageable than GCHINA and was a pleasure to take in person. Manageable workload, well-maintained Sakai with detailed schedule and resources, straightforward grading.

Kyle is so chill and his classes were not stressful at all. I found the class itself pretty pointless and did not learn much, but the workload was much better than GCHINA. I would definitely recommend his section.

Okay Global Challenges is Global Challenges so while the overall course was terrible, Professor Fruh is extrememly nice and does a good job with what he can. A solid choice for Global Challenges as he is also a fair grader.

GLOCHALL would have been boring if it wasn't for Prof. Fruh. Most of the classes were discussion-based. Unlike other professors, he did not ask direct questions about reading but rather was encouraging us to debate the "application-like" questions. He was easily accessible through email and very understanding when it comes to deadlines.

Prof. Fruh was engaging when we had discussions, and asked thought provoking questions. He is a professor of philosophy and sometimes didn't have answers for questions about the challenges we discussed, but he did give good feedback for our argumentative essays.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Lots of BJT analysis, though I wish there was greater emphasis on MOS. Phenomenal class, arguably the only true circuit fundamentals class at Duke. RB Fair has decades of experience in this area of EE, and his retirement will undoubtedly mark the end of an era for pure analog circuits research at Duke. His impact on Duke ECE will be hard to match.
He's so great!!!!
Brilliant professor with an insane background in analog circuits. Was an honor to learn from him.

Class was weighted mostly towards exams and a final research presentation. Dr. Fair was always willing to stay after class to talk with students and help with class content. He is extremely knowledgeable and has decades of experience in nanoscale IC chip manufacturing (helped to invent many advanced techniques). Highly recommend this course.

The class is a considerable amount of work, almost weekly tough HW, long prelabs that require using simulation tools. However, Fair is a great and very knowledgeable professor, that, despite looking tough, is extremely kind and available to help you. If you pout on the effort, you are going to do well. I highly recommend this class for ECEs into EE
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Was hard but interesting

This man has achieved so much and it seems like so few people ask...flunch him. Anyway he is fairly reserved in lecture and the lectures go very fast so dont bother taking notes just pay attention and ask questions. Very responsive to (aka disappointed in) class grades so just go to more OH than your neighbor and you'll do great. HW is tough.

I dont agree with a lot of these reviews. If you pay attention during lecture and understand what's happening in class then there's not a lot of memorization required. This class is the only true circuit analysis class at Duke and is pretty much required for a career in hardware. Fair is an easy grader and cares about his students. Would recommend.
He's a boring lecturer and just reads off the slides. Go to office hours for the homeworks. To study the exams you just memorize the lecture slides and you'll do fine. Class is curved.

class was basically memorization, which is ridiculous for an electronics class. Talked through slides with no explanation given. If you get this professor and you're not good at memorization, do not take the class. Drop the class and find another course the first week of class if he's teaching this.

Fair is very nice, but not a good teacher. He doesn't make the material interesting or give any motivation behind the solutions. The class felt like memorizing a lot of device behavior and configurations instead of actually understanding circuits.
No Comments
No Comments

COMPREHENSIVE: A lot of work for a 0.25 credit class. Lab reports were intimidating at first ... do not procrastinate. It is essential to learn the general structure of lab reports early, as feedback offers limited help during writing. Labs are pretty interesting, and make you feel like a chemist!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: The grading policy is SUPER SUPER SUPER unfair. He dropped my grade from A to A- because my TA was literally taking off points for the most ridiculous, nitpicky mistakes, and he just refused to do anything about it. He completely DESTROYED my orgo grade. AVOID AT ALL COSTS
Unclear grading rubric for post-labs and passive aggressive when I asked for clarification on grading. Pray you have a good TA and don't have to interact with him.

I took CHEM420L with him several years ago - did not interact with him much but having advanced further into chemistry academia I have respect for him and the challenges associated with organizing so many different lab courses with so many TAs while dealing with premed students and their attitudes. He can be sassy but I respect it.

Without ever having met this man, I don't like him or the way he runs his labs. Lab instructions were often unclear and post-lab grading criteria was unnecessarily harsh. The one time I emailed him to ask a clarifying question (not even to get back the points I lost), he was passive aggressive and generally has a "I'm right, you're wrong" attitude.

Kersey is the lab manager, so we didn't see him much. Labs were taught by TA's, and depending on the TA you could have a good or bad experience. The lab content matched well with the lecture part of the course and the number of lab experiments was manageable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Kersey is great. He isn't student-facing in the lab, more just runs the labs in the background but he is very helpful when you need him. I had a very unhelpful TA in Orgo 1 and he was very understanding about the lab being turned in late and all ended up being well. Know that lab is a heavy bit of work but it becomes more helpful in Orgo 2.

Kersey isn't too involved in the lab itself. I was lucky to have a good TA. However, I have had some frustrations with the class. First, the lab quizzes are consistently sent out late, making for a very inconvenient experience, especially in a Monday lab section. Second, the grading can be harsh at times. However, the workload is what I expected.

Super honest and cool guy to talk to and the post-labs did not take an exorbitant amount of time. He is very responsive if you email him and the lab content sometimes aligns with course material. However, the online labs at the end of the course were entirely busy work and took 7-8 hours for each part. Overall, not a difficult lab manager.

Post labs took hours to complete and were often confusing. The labs were easier than they were in Chem 101. There is a lot of pre-lab assignments and the due-dates were weird. The final four labs which were asynchronous and took a very long time to complete, especially since it was during finals. Sometimes procedures are unclear.

Labs, pre-lab assignments, and post-lab assignments were unnecessarily long, tedious, and time-consuming. (For example, copying the entire procedure into the lab notebook by hand.) They were also almost completely unrelated to lecture content, so they felt irrelevant.

ADORABLE CATS!! Makes labs very fun and communicates with students. Ensures that students are up to date with assignments and is always available to answer questions or discuss any difficulties in lab. Really appreciate Dr. Kersey!! :)

I highly recommend Dr. Kersey. He is an amazing lab instructor. He responds pretty immediately to any and all questions. Additionally, he sends emails about upcoming deadlines to make sure everyone is keeping up and doesn't forget. Very very kind and much better than past experiences with other lab instructors. I really appreciate all of the work

AMAZING LAB DIRECTOR!! Dr. Kersey is so considerate. He always responds to any questions and the fact that he created an ed discussion for any question (and responds within 24 hours) definitely shows that. Very caring and easy to work with. I've had the best lab experience thus far because of Dr. Kersey. Definitely better than other lab instructors

This semester, Cox for lecture and Kersey for laboratory have created a cohesive laboratory experience. This is the first time that lecture and laboratory matched up. Prof Kersey's approaches to the laboratory helped me in the lecture component and vice versa.

Two years ago, I had Orgo 1 lab with Dr. Kersey. I hated it. Labs were long, tedious, and had to be turned in in person. However, he transformed it into an enjoyable and fascinating experience! Labflow can be confusing, but overall it's fair. The generous curve ensures a good grade, but even without it, its easy to get a good grade.

Orgo 2 lab is so much more relevant and useful than Orgo 1 lab. While I have never met Kersey, he is kind with giving whole-class extensions for tests, etc. The grading policy for Orgo 2 lab is also generous. However, copying the whole procedure into the lab notebooks is infinitely dumb, time-consuming, and needs to end.
I am not sure why the ratings are so bad. Prof. Kersey is easily accessible by email for everything. grading criteria can be confusing, but it is TA specific, not Kersey's fault completely.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: His emails can be confusing, but he explains things clearly when you ask for help

Unnecessarily complicated lab policies and documents (many times longer than other natural science labs) Rather than learning anything, most of the time was dedicated to making sure you adhered to every little guideline and trying to figure out answers to questions that are nowhere to be found in the provided course material. Emails ignored as well

This character limit doesn't begin to encompass how TERRIBLE this class is
1.Workload was too much for a 0.25 credit class
2. NMR spectroscopy was arbitrary+blurry
3. labflow was horrific+confusing to navigate
4. had labs that weren't relevant until a month later (aldol)
5. want us to include C-I stretch but didn't provide values on resources given

Terrible. Rude when answering emails. Made us buy lab software for $50 that consistently doesn't work and makes more work for students trying to turn in the lab than just handing in lab pages/reports. Labs themselves aren't that bad but the lab write-ups are unnecessarily complicated and don't help you learn anything.

Really unorganized and incongruent with the lecture part of the class. Tested on concepts we won't learn until orgo 2 and TAs have a weird policy that won't allow them to answer questions. Quizzes were always opened late and TAs were lazy with grading. For how specific they want us to be in assignments, the lab department is lazy and unorganized.

I don't get kersey's bad rep. I never actually saw him in lab, but his handouts were easy enough to follow, and post lab reports were not too difficult compared to 101. The achieve dry labs were kind of annoying and long, but it was hard to get below an A on them. I really only ever lost points on the separation schemes of wet labs.

Labs are taught by TAs instead of Dr. Kersey, but I really enjoyed the labs! Dr. Kersey's lab handouts are quite clear and I thought the labs were more in-depth than gen chem labs (chem 110, at least). The lab reports were a lot easier to write/complete because we could type them up.

Worst class so far at Duke. For a class that is worth 0.25 credits, I had more weekly homework for this class than most of my other classes. Lab reports are tedious and can take hours to complete just for you to receive a mediocre grade from the TA because Kersey tells them to grade harshly. Seriously, someone else needs to take over his labs.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Labs for Chem201 are unnecessarily hard. The TAs are knowledgable but there is a communication barrier as some of them don't speak great English! The labs are graded harshly but it is possible to do well if you put in the work.
So much unnecessary work and very tedious labs. Read the labs carefully so you won't get docked so many points
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: If I could describe this man in one quote, it would be "no offense, but..." because his grading policies are ridiculous but somehow tries to justify them. Emphasis on "tries". Be prepared to spend 10 hours a week on this 0.25 credit class.

I will be honest, this lab isn't for the faint of heart and I was very intimidated at first. That being said, once I finally reached out he helped me tremendously overall. I think he has bad reviews because he can come off as harsh. If you can overlook his dry personality without taking it personally, he is very willing to help.

Most of these bad reviews seem blown out of proportion. Lab was definitely difficult, and I felt as though grading was a bit harsh, but Dr. Kersey is definitely accessible to ask questions and wants to see students succeed. It's definitely possible to do well if you work hard and put in the time!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I learned pretty much nothing in Chem201 lab. The class was unnecessarily difficult, didn't relate to lecture, and I felt like I was wasting my time every time I completed an assignment. I feel horribly prepared for Chem202 lab next semester. You can tell, close to zero effort was put in to modify the labs to fit the virtual/Zoom circumstances.

Yes, pt of reputation comes from how emails r written & how u answer q's (seems condescending, unapproachable). Scary presence b/c students don't see u during a semester unless there r integrity q's so all meeting reports r negative. I've taken 3 classes w/ u but u did show the cats during summer online (good 4 humanizing, connecting, do more!)

Notoriously unforgiving and passive-aggressive as a lab manager. I would recommend contacting your TA unless you really need to speak directly with him. He does have cute cats though, and guidelines/grading aren't that hard to follow if you THOROUGHLY read all details in the syllabus from day 1.

Labs give absolutely no meaning to the course, and are ESPECIALLY useless in an online setting. He gives us the same exact assignment materials as if we were doing in person labs, and doesn't bother to change it to fit an online format. The dry labs are impossible and designed to make you fail, as they have no correlation with the lecture material.

I went into his office once to ask him a question. He rolled his eyes at me and asked me what I wanted. He had his headphones on during our entire 3 minute conversation and I left with a worse understanding of the concept that I was looking to find clarification on.
Dr. Kersey gives out labs that don't help at all for the actual class. The lt abs often take forever and are of no help whatsoever when it comes to lecture material.

He's just the lab guy for Orgo 1 and 2, but his labs are often convoluted and confusing. Better start learning spectroscopy now, because in the last few labs he throws you into it with barely an introduction into spectra analysis and only confuses you. Awful at creating the labs and even worse at interacting with students.

The quizzes were impossible and had nothing to with the lectures. He took off points on the labs for very small details, and never specified what guidelines we should follow. His feedback was always harsh and his emails always came with tons of complicated rules that made my head hurt.

Taking 201 with Kersey was a nightmare.  You must be able to learn the material by only reading the textbook (lecture notes are copies of the textbook projected onto the board). Grading criteria was unclear & changed throughout the term as  50% of each test's questions were thrown out each time because they were found to be incorrectly written.

I really enjoyed the orgo I lab.  Some of the labs were longer than normal, but my TA was always very helpful.  Dr. Kersey is the lab manager, but he doesn't teach the course.  The labs are taught and graded by graduate students.  I'm not sure what the previous person meant by his comments on their work since he didn't grade our lab reports.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Took his class and saw him once. He is the person behind the scenes of Orgo lab that makes you want to cry. He is critical with his comments but it's not constructive. I feel personally victimized. He creates impossible weekly online quizzes. I do not feel like a better student coming out of his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Farid is a great professor who has really clear standards for grading and assignments. Practice tests are super helpful and he makes content very digestible. Definitely recommend taking 212 with him.

Amazing professor. Lectures are engaging and interesting. The slides are posted beforehand (blank notes) and reposted after the lecture (full of notes). The homeworks were pretty doable for the most part. The exams were straightforward, lots of practice exams given. Explains the content in a way easy to digest. OH are fun and useful
