Prof. H. makes simple mistakes during lecture, but because of that is very lenient on simple errors on exams. He grades based on understanding of concepts, not ability to do arithmetic. He makes the class very accessible and homework is harder than the exams so doing it prepares you well. Watch Prof. Leonard on youtube to supplement.

Really like this prof. The lectures were very interactive and we got to see him solve lots of problems which was very helpful. Very chill and forgiving guy in general. Only thing is that there was quite a bit of homework in the weekly problem sets (sometimes it was fair but sometimes it def felt excessive). Overall great class though

A fantastic teacher who always goes out of his way to help students, Dr. Hosseinijafari's lectures were consistently well explained, he was always open to questions both in and outside of class (via ed discussion), and his exams were fair. Grading was lenient (no penalty for minor arithmetic mistakes). Homework could take several hours per week.

Awesome Professor! He teaches well and grades easily. Although he does make tiny mistakes in the notes, he updates them regularly and makes sure that they are always available. You definitely need to lock in with the contents though. The concepts can stack up fast.

confused by these negative ratings, farid is a gem in the duke math dept. he cares so much about his students and is incredibly understanding. he will provide extensions if asked, gives clear explainations and actively answers any questions on email, ed discussion, after class and posts very thorough notes. final is very similar to midterm, 10/10

Farid's a great professor. 1) He can explain concepts well, very open to questions 2) His grading on midterms is based on if you understood the methods taught in class, allows some leeway with mistakes. HOWEVER you also gotta set a few hours per week to do the homework and actually comprehend the topics.. calc 3 in one semester is quick paced.

One of the most caring professors I've had so far. Always asks if anyone has any questions before and throughout the lecture. He even stays after class to answer questions.His lectures are easy to follow, and he breaks down the content really well. Midterms are graded more on your understanding.Seems to have improved from ratings earlier this year

Professor Farid is a good lecturer who takes time outside of class to answer students' questions. He can get distracted at times and occasionally makes minor mistakes, but overall, this doesn't affect the quality of his teaching.
Great professor!

While the content surrounding multi is difficult in general Farid is a super kind teacher that cares about the success of his students. He is always open to answer questions and wants to see students succeed, that said it's helpful to stay on top of work.
Good professor. Will help you out any way possible if you ask him. Extra help is super useful
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This was the best math class I've taken at Duke. Professor Farid is patient and always takes the time to answer everyone's questions in class. The material is definitely challenging, but he offers lots of examples to make it easy to understand. His office hours are really helpful if you need extra help.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Farid really cares about his students and makes sure everyone is on the same page. He always offers clear explanations and answers questions thoroughly. There's a lot of homework and material to cover, but he did a great job and was very fair.

Farid draws a surface, says “visualize,” then skips the steps we actually need.
He defines a limit — somehow we're the ones that vanish.
Partial derivatives? More like partially explained.
In this multivariable maze, he's the gradient pointing the wrong way.

There is an insane amount of material being taught in very little time. Lectures were extremely crammed, and there was little useful feedback on problem sets. Just a very tough class overall. Farid is a nice professor, but the class is difficult.

Incredible professor and lecturer who offers a realistic perspective of how foreign policy is made. Go to office hours; the TAs are super friendly and will clearly delineate tough but fair grading expectations. Prepare to spend your waking hours scrolling NYT, watching lectures, and doing readings.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Feaver is an institution at Duke, and a must take for anyone interested in IR, FP, and a career in government more broadly. The course is reading-intensive, and the grading can be difficult but very rewarding. Regardless, lectures are a blast, constantly filled with anecdotes from his time in government.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Grading is extremely harsh for an intro class. The grading criteria are also loose and are usually left to the TAs to decide. Feaver's lectures are overall intellectually stimulating and engaging, but also usually unstructured, and it is more like Feaver and some students yapping than him actually teaching. The hype for Feaver is exaggerated.

One of the best professors at Duke but also one of the toughest graders. Content is very interesting, he is incredibly knowledgable about everything and has a ton of experience. Class has pop quizzes about current events happening in the world so you need to read the news and very tough grader on papers.  However I would recommend the class 100%.

Given the hype, the lack of depth is disappointing. Covered way too much with little detail. Feaver doesn't provide as much of an insider perspective as I hoped. It's really a touch and go sampler of key FP concepts/case studies. Given the sheer number of readings, you need to take it with light classes to get the most out of it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: While the content of the class is interesting and super applicable, I was underwhelmed by Feaver as a lecturer. The sections (led by TAs) were consistently more engaging and interesting than his lectures, which are basically monologues with a skeleton outline projected on the board. I don't regret this class, but I wouldn't take another with him.

Best professor I've had at Duke. Engaging lectures, insane career in politics, and genuinely cares about his students. The class is challenging, but the work you put in pays off 100x in the knowledge you gain and the effort Feaver puts back in to connecting his students to opportunities in the IR world. Take any class you can with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He's a respected individual in his field. His lectures were interesting and engaging, but he goes at an incredible speed. He definitely expects you to take notes on everything he says verbatim. He is an incredibly hard grader and doesn't believe in giving that many As. Additionally, he shows some level of favor to the students who he knows.

Dr. Feaver is a stellar professor, bringing a wealth of knowledge to discussions and offering a rare right-of-center perspective in academia. He is a skilled facilitator, brings humor to tough topics, and champions his students beyond Duke. His classes will bring the best out of you if you meet his high expectations with your best efforts.

The GOAT, plain and simple. Feaver has an incredible depth of experience, with engaging lectures and assignments that put your knowledge to the test in fun and novel ways. NYT quizzes were no joke, but you pick it up pretty fast if you're paying attention.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Respected

reviews.comment: A must take professor at Duke- he is tough but cares about his students, and is an asset for anyone who hopes to enter the Political Science field or DC space after graduation.

Prof. Feaver is wonderful. The class is very interesting and he is a pleasure to learn from.Very engaging and funny. Super available out of class and is really interested in getting to know his students. Classes are always fun. However, you won't get an A in this class. Whole class has basically come to the consensus that grading is way too strict.

The final is 40% of the final grade and the midterms are both 20%. The class readings are long winded and not as crucial to your grade as Feaver and the TAs make you believe. Be sure to participate and take full advantage of discussion sections. Feaver is a great lecturer and the topics are very interesting but this class is hard and a lot to read.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Really a great intro course- I learned a lot from this professor and thought the class was interesting and engaging. Certainly challenging and some tough grading but if you put in the work (keeping up with the NYT, lectures, and readings) a good grade is doable. Awesome TAs too.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Learned a ton in class, had a really interesting time. Only problem was sometimes the New York Times quizzes detracted from class (ie. most of us spent way more time studying for and stressing about those than actually engaged in the course material.) But great insights, super good TAs.

Great lecturer, lots of reading, weekly NYT quizzes - flipped class (online lecture then in-class discussion). Plan to spend 1 hour per day on the class (readings/online lectures/NYT). My favorite class/professor so far at Duke. Great conversation in class applying IR theory to current events. Have learned so much from this class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Really good guy-great lecturer. Make sure to stay up to date on the videos and the NYT current events(pop quizzes once a week-more likely if the Minnesota Vikings lose). Tests aren't too hard. Readings are alot but you can get by without doing them if desired. Really interesting personal story-cares about his students.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Cool professor. Very interesting to hear about his experiences in the White House. Engaging lecturer. Flipped class which was great because it allows you to rewatch lectures. Lots of assigned reading which is probably useful, but not super necessary for his tests (I didn't do much of the reading). Just take good notes, read all NYT headlines.

Feaver is an amazing lecturer and professor, and he inspires his students to go further in international relations both inside and outside the classroom. He also runs AGS so get to know him and it will definitely add to your experience at Duke.

Professor Feaver is very knowledgable and well-respected and was one of my favorite professors this semester. Be prepared to work hard for your grade, but it's worth it. It's easy to get to know Feaver outside of class -- just make an effort to stop by office hours or get lunch with him. Make sure to go to the AGS events he recommends!

Professor Feaver is one of Duke's best. During the semester I had him, he testified before the Senate about U.S. nuclear policy. Great lecturer, dry wit but a funny guy, and very personable outside of class. Go to lunch with him and get to know him. Prepare to be intimidated - you should be, given this man's resume. Take the class and go to AGS!
Peter Feaver is one of the most amazing and famous professors at Duke. Definitely try to take his class. I have learned so much. This class was only 2 times a week with a discussion section.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Feaver is one of Duke's most renown professors who I hold in the highest esteem. I had him for his quadrennial American Foreign Policy & the 2016 Election class and was thoroughly impressed with the level of preparation and care he devoted to each class. He is, by far, one of the best professors I've encountered at this institution.

One of the best professors I've ever had. I've taken 5 classes with him - Intro to IR, American Foreign Policy, Ethics & IR, Civ-Mil relations, and foreign policy & elections. Hands down phenomenal. Interesting lectures, amazing access to a person who has direct experience in the White House. Helpful outside class. Writes amazing recs. Take him!

Before his class I thought international relations was about logic and theories needed proof. Though an amazing lecturer, Professor Feaver bases his course on personal preferences and opinion. Working hard for it will get you nowhere if you don't see his views as the truth.

flipped class so you spend tons of time preparing for his class. you have to do the readings if you want to participate in section, which is where your participation grade comes from. thought i wanted to be a polisci major until i took this class; just not that interesting

Dr. Feaver is an amazing, charismatic lecturer. His TAs are nice but never responds to emails ever. Quizzes are unfair, grading is unclear, and expectations are vague. All I've learnt at the end of this class is that people who babble on about IR in twisted, illogical ways are rewarded the most.

Intro to IR was an immersive, challenging and stimulating course. Material was heavy on the reading - flipped classroom - but Feaver rocks. Not an easy A, not an easy B either... a real college level course. One of the best Duke Political Science has to offer.

If you can take a class with Professor Feaver, do it. Yes, his class his hard and you absolutely have to do the readings, but you come away actually understanding the material. He makes an effort to get to know the students as well, having lunches before class and throwing a party at the end of the semester. Highly recommend.

One of the best teachers at Duke. Lots of real world and academic experience. Knows IR like no one else. Offers great advice and connections if you ask. Engaging lectures. Did a flipped class well. Very, very hard to get an A. Hard tests, must do readings and watch videos. Immensely worth taking any of his classes--you'll learn a ton.
Very Hard. Interesting class

Has a repetoire of stories that he cycles through. Do not worry about the grade... Real measure of performance in his class: do you become a main character in one of the anecdotes he will share classes to come for the next decade?

1st day of class referenced his ratemyprof comments. Very bright, provides excellent insight due to his NSC experience, and sets fair (but very tough) standards for grading. Expect to work hard and receive an A-. Great lectures, TAs can be a crapshoot, overall very good class. Learned a ton about American Foreign Policy

Has minions (aka TAs) that set up the classroom for him so that he can walk in with a satchel just as class starts, turn on the overhead, and lecture. Says vis-a-vis a lot and makes this little hand-chopping motion as if he is dividing something into sections ALL THE TIME. Just watch for it. On topic, great lectures. Take lots of notes.

TOUGH CLASS. This is the second I've had with Feaver. Very knowledgeable but expects you to spend every waking moment reading for his class. AT LEAST 200-300 pages of reading a week. Final is cumulative. Papers are graded harshly. Tough class but you learn a lot.
Comes off as very pompous and a general show off.  I had to work extremely hard to make a B in the class, pacing of readings (essays, NYT) is integral.

Intro to IR with Feaver was definitely one of my favorite classes at Duke. A lot of work and you have to work for your grade, but you will learn a TON. Feaver is incredibly knowledgeable and lectures are definitely worth going to.

FANTASTIC professor, LOVED the class (introduction to international relations). Really knows his stuff since he was in DC for years  under the Bush administration. His bias really wasn't a problem for me - he is just a great lecturer, very engaging and funny. My favorite class last semester!

Feaver is great- funny, very knowledgeable, and most importantly pompous. GO TO LECTURES. His lectures are really interesting if you can find it within yourself to be open-minded.  There's a good chance he will read this comment in front of the class.  I agree that he looks like the kid from Jerry McGuire from the back of the lecture hall.
Funny guy, but man, he will throw A LOT of jargon at you. Always shows off about his work experience at Washington DC. Great teacher though. A TON of useless readings too.
Pretty interesting lecturer.  Class is fun if you have an interest in the subject.  Lots of reading, but lectures are more important for tests.  Class is difficult unless this stuff comes naturally

GREAT PROFESSOR AND FANTASTIC CLASS.  Feaver has loads of experience in the White House under Clinton and Bush, so he has fascinating perspectives on current issues.  Demanding workload and lots of reading, but you will learn so much and enjoy Feaver's lectures.  Take PoliSci 93 with Feaver!
Knows his stuff but is so blindly by his political views you get a tainted version of the story.

Feaver, it is sad to say, was a very good lecturer. It is rather unfortunate, for his views permeate every scintilla of his classes, from reading choices to exam questions. Although he's quite intelligent, he's a neo-con twit. And quite the narcissist.

He's a great lecturer but also a total narcissist.  Also, he got paranoid about iPods and would start telling stories and quit halfway, which was bizarre. The MANY kids who fawned over him got annoying, as did his conservatism.  However, overall the class was very rewarding.  CHOOSE YOUR TA WISELY!

Worth taking if you're interested in politics, and if you want to see Feaver in action. Lots of reading that's sometimes unnecessary and boring. Tricky tests. Otherwise, Feaver is amusing, interesting, and makes an effort to talk to his students. If you take his class, have lunch with him

From the back row, he looks kinda like the little kid from Jerry Macguire.  Decent speaker, semi-entertaining, although (as you can see from the rave reviews) class if full of annoying kiss-asses who are in love with him.  Class average tends to be a b, b-.  decent amt. of reading, but not too much.
Good lecturer, good jokes in class.  Lots of long readings, which often are not relevant to exams.

Oh how I loved this class.  Took it on a whim and now I'm declaring polisci.  Witty, engaging lectures that meld the loads of dry reading into memorable, comprehensible chunks.  TAs were uniformly helpful.  Makes students overwhelmingly more cognizant of global issues.  DO NOT MISS!!

Feaver is so hot right now.  The guy is a great lecturer, and he knows his stuff.  Certain assignments and grading scales can become frustrating and unclear, but his general hotness more than makes up for what is lacking in grade clarity.  Smart, funny, self-depricating and self-promoting: Da Feave!
smart guy, but turns the class into a self-promotion with stories about how important he is. annoying to listen to and tests are tricky.

What can I say about Professor Feaver? Let's take a temperature of the class to start off with.Sometimes the subject matter can seem to be all over the place, which makes the exams difficult to study for. He also has a penchant for irony, as shown in his exams. Keep the DC out of the man & your set.

Good intro.  Look for Feaver's conserv. bias- actually made me more sensitive to bias in general. Lectures & assign.'s are straightfoward.  BTW, Nietzsche was not a nihilist and "begging the question" means assuming as a premise the very conclusion that the argument is intended to prove.  (He misuse

Excellent lecturer, relates concepts clearly and in an entertaining way.  Tests are tough, but with a little studying you can usually pull off a B.  He seems like such a smart guy I still can't understand why he is conservative, but a good teacher anyway.
terrible teacher

this guy is the man. always has good jokes and awesome stories in lecture that are relevant to topics. tests can be a bit intimidating because theres lots of reading and you dont know what to expect. Bs are def within reach, As are a bit harder to get. if youre interested in ir take it with feaver.

lectures are really enjoyable; i was actually sad when i missed them. he's really engaging, funny. he's conservative but it doesnt come out too often; he jokes a lot about the left/right. he obviously has a good time teaching, very accessable outside of class. definitely take this class.
Wonderful speaker; very engaging lectures, but a tough grader who expects a lot from his students

Brilliant guy and engaging lecturer.Students, even in a large class, show up consistenly. He's never around, but his TA's are helpful. The class is tough. There is a lot of dense reading assigned. Papers and exams are ****y. But most students will find a B easy and some shade of an A within reach.
Keeps class entertaining
Fun, interesting lectures, even with the movie references (which actually are relevant and helpful).  A great guy, and a wonderful professor.
No Comments

Professor Feaver clearly did not understand that the majority of students in his political science class were not interested in his capacity to relate concepts in international relations theory to major motion pictures.
He was very cocky and had the bad habit of using cutesy, complicated terms to label otherwise simple concepts (see: Denzel Washington Paradox of Terrorism).  Known for wearing white pants and shoes.
He's a really good professor.  However, every word that comes out of his mouth is a lie so watch out.  Very nice and easy to talk to after class.
Eh.  He's cool, but the class sucked ass.
Couldn't take my eyes off him!
Tom Ferraro is a professor unlike any other. The books we read and the discussions we had in his class were some of the best in my Duke English experience yet.

You owe it to yourself to take a Ferraro class while at Duke.  You'll read some books you wouldn't choose on your own and end up loving them because his insights and the class discussion make them interesting.  The skill you'll learn of “close reading” will be valuable in whatever you do post-Duke.  Same thing for developing your writing skills.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Not just one of the best professors I've ever had, but one of the best people I've ever met. Ferraro asks that students do something very difficult — think for themselves and be themselves, and to do their best to make those unique selves understandable. Read deeply, with care, and you will have the time of your life. This is the point of college!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Ferraro's classes are extremely engaging because they are discussion based and he is constantly sharing anecdotes to supplement what we are talking about in class. Although he is somewhat of a tough grader, he gives tons of feedback and will meet with you to discuss your essays. Overall a super fun and inspirational professor.

Professor Ferraro is by far the best professor I have ever met. He is very inspirational, provides hilarious anecdotes in classes, and is always very open to listening and helping out his students. There has never been a time where I contacted him to request a meeting and he didn't respond. He makes sure to do everything in his power to be of help!

AMAZING! I am a biology major and had to take a seminar and decided to do this one because of his amazing reviews. I echo what others have said - if you are enrolled at Duke University it is mandatory to take a class with professor Ferraro. I was nervous being in the class with little background and it was tough but so so worth it!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Ferraro genuinely changed the way I read literature. I always looked forward to his classes. He always brought up fantastic points and ideas that I couldn't even hope to imagine. He is extremely knowledgeable and does not hold back in feedback. Admittedly, sometimes his lectures would go above all our heads, but it is what it is. Take his class!

Ferraro was unequivocally the best professor I've had in college so far and I am a junior.  This man is incredibly dedicated to showing students the true ways of english as a discipline.  He makes not only your writing, but also your thinking skills better.  He demands critical engagement, but he ultimately grades on effort over ability.
Ferraro is very nice and an amazing teacher. The wealth of his knowledge astounds me. However, he is a super tough grader. He is very intellectual and asks a great deal of interaction with the text.

Professor Ferraro is unequivocally the best professor Ive had, Duke or otherwise. The real value of his classes dont just come from his fascinating analysis of the texts, but from his knowledge and wisdom of all-things-human. This class is a must for anyone looking to develop a love for reading or just better understand people and situations.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Ferraro is an incredible professor who knows how to manipulate a discussion to produce profound results, and to lead students through a process that allows them to gain confidence and insight in however they choose to think about ideas. He is enjoyable, amiable, intelligent, and extremely helpful. Would love to take a class with him in the future.

Thomas Ferraro is one of the most interesting professors I've had while at Duke, both for his incredible ability to formulate and synthesize ideas and for his eccentricities and humor. Often I went into each class period not really knowing exactly what to expect and left with more questions than answers but certainly learned a great deal overall!

Ferraro is just such an intelligent person. Don't let his crazy vocabulary intimidate you. He's funny, personable, has great stories, and wants to get to know his students. Go to office hours, he is so friendly and just fun to talk to. Class is always interesting and he gives great feedback on papers - good writers will have no problem. The best.

Prof Ferraro is a great lecturer and a fun person to spend time with. He'll push you to challenge what you think, and he's great in office hours, too. He's one of the few professors who still will push back on what you say and challenge you, and that's a great feeling. Would ABSOLUTELY recommend taking any class with him!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Ferraro is weird. What he says sounds intelligent, but rarely seems to make that much sense initially. Usually, it turns out, he's just on a different level than what most students are. Will lead you in circles during discussions trying to get you to understand what he's thinking, but is never condescending or mean. All grading was done by TA's

Professor Ferraro is fantastic. He helped make the classroom conversation and environment dynamic. His pedagogy is polished and his passion is visible and contagious. Honestly, a great man, and an even greater professor. Values both time in & outside of the classroom - learning is more than just a grade.
The best professor I have had at Duke, or ever. While he can be a little harsh with grading, you will learn so much and come out as a much better writer. Take any class with this Prof.

I am returning to Duke this April for my 20th Reunion and while I was there in the late 1980s and early 1990s I took two classes with Tom: contemporary literature and "Readings in Catholic America." Now I am in the interview stage to become an assistant professor of American literature because of Tom's example of passion and commitment!

This man is a genius. I am a hard science major, but Ferraro basically opened my eyes to how, well, how to read (and not in the rudimentary sense...I got an 800 on the writing SATs and 5's on both AP English tests. Ferraro will make you realize that means nothing). He is my favorite professor at Duke, and in fact I consider him my mentor.

Absolutely incredible. His ability to connect english, pop culture, religion and history is overwhelming at first but awe-inspiring once you get used to his pace. Hard to get answers out of, office hours usually turned into discussions about life, not my paper. But seriously, take this professor. He will challenge, frustrate, and inspire you

What is more to say.It's FERRARO. I am an English major and he is the best professor among the ones I have had so far at Duke (and yes I am quite close to graduating). You really need to work hard to earn a good grade, but it's worth it. He is one of a kind, and so are his lectures :)

As you can see from most of the other comments, Tom is one of the best professors and minds at Duke and if you haven't taken him by the time you graduate you've missed out. I don't find him arrogant at all, like some have argues - he's confident, brilliant, and taught me to interact with literature in an entirely new way, bringing it to life.Bravo!

My favorite professor of all time.  Took two classes with him, both were outstanding.  He has inspired me and significantly influenced my career aspirations.  Seems totally insane at first but is actually a genius...and really helpful and nice.  Even takes his class to his house to eat with his family.  TAKE HIM BEFORE YOU LEAVE DUKE!

Best professor I've had at Duke.  Seems like a lunatic for the first month, but once you learn to speak his language you're golden.  Keep up with the reading, be willing to speak- you will be rewarded.  Make an effort to go to office hours, it's like a bonus seminar.  Oh, and maybe watch a couple of episodes of Rome and The Sopranos- you'll see.

He is an amazing professor. He makes class so much fun, I can just sit and listen to him without seeing the time go by. He's the best professor I've had at Duke, he really pushed me to become a better writer. He grades harshly but it's worth it. If you enjoy English, take one of his classes.
Amazing professor, amazing class. Grades papers based on how well he knows you can write, really pushes you to become a better reader/writer. Take a class with him, any class!

Often touted as the most difficult professor in the English department. I was told to stay away from his class, but I took it anyway. Do the reading, really engage yourself with the material, and work harder than you ever thought you could on the essays, and this will be your favorite class--not to mention your favorite prof--at Duke.

Don't be intimidated by his eccentric teaching style; you'll come to appreciate it, and learn more than ever have before in an english class if you put in the effort. He's a genius, yet still accessible and friendly.

Great class began with incredible potential but it slowly declined. Ferraro is a genius, there is no denying that, but he was definitely not a freshman professor and his knowledge and expectations were intimidating. Great, warm man nonetheless, but a genius that demands genius. Given that was his first freshman class, he will bea better frosh prof.

Horrible professor. Impossible to follow, hard grader, and one of the most arrogant and condescending individuals I have ever met. His class had so much potential, but was one of the biggest wastes of time I have experienced at Duke.
Probably one of the more arrogant people you'll meet in your life. Very intelligent. Very heady. But also incredibly conceited. Grading is pretty subjective

He is bound to the Politcal atmosphere that helps to perpetuate his stature within and outside the University. Young girls 'swoon', young guys 'jealous'. Me? Not impressed that he justifies 'praise' above another human. His office rests just one floor ABOVE the University President, again an appropriate location for his SELF opinion. Kind of Greasy
Tom is one of the best teachers I've ever studied with and has profoundly influenced my life.
No Comments

You will probably think he should be locked up in a mental institution when you first meet him but he really is incredible.  Don't try to follow exactly what he is saying (even the Rhodes scholar in my class couldn't), just try to get the gist of it.  I had read books before but never like this.  Take him.

Prof F is pretty much incredible. His teaching style is often oblique, but don't get scared--he knows what he's doing. You'll come to understand and love his theatrics, and the man himself, and your classmates, and you'll learn more than you ever thought you would, or could. Brilliant.
Tom is a great professor and a great man. The classes I've taken with him have had a profound influence on my life choices -- and he speaks in great tangents.

He's absolutely phenomenal.  I can't imagine there being a better prof.  He can be somewhat abrasive, but his teaching style more than makes up for it.  He doesn't grade on a curve, and has no qualms with failing an entire class, so be prepared to work... hard.  You'll learn a lot, though.

Amazing!  I took him twice and in both classes majority of the students thought that he was the best professor they ever had.  Extremely interesting, entertaining and smart.  His energy and passion are contagious
Dr. Gavin was great and so smart. He is a super nice guy and is always willing to help on assignments. No midterms and a take home final was awesome too

Lectures are SO boring and prof Gavin takes an hour to do lengthy derivations just for a formula???? His tests were fairly difficult and extremely unpredictable, and he took AT LEAST a month to grade them. He's a very easy grader and getting an A isn't hard, he's just not engaging or interesting.

Stressful bc we got no grades until the semester's end. Lectures were confusing and hard to know what was important, he would do an hour-long derivation and then tell us we only needed to know the final formula... like why?? HWs are really long and tedious, so start early. Labs are annoying, but HWs, lab, and participation are free points.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Great Professor. Passion for teaching and sharing about the subject. As lenient of a grader as you can get for an EGR class. A little bit slow to grade and not super accessible outside of class/office hours. Very fair with work load and expectations. Take him for EGR201.

Gavin's the man. Most interesting class I've taken so far at Duke.  Super helpful, his projects are epic.  Class is not too challenging as long as you pay attention and put effort into the projects.  Great class, can't say enough about Gavin.  Lucky to have him as my advisor as well
He's the man, super smart

Great professor with a wonderfully amusing sense of humor. Class was difficult and almost completely project-based. Lack of textbook made it more difficult, but if you keep your notes in order and organized, its not too bad to find needed information. In all else fails, he's great at answering questions through email.

Professor Gavin is great. I only wish that we could have had a text book (because sometimes it was quite hard to find what was needed for the homework from the notes and handouts). The projects are interesting, and Professor Gavin is always willing to help.

Gavin is a pretty good guy with an interesting sense of humor. He was relaxed and pretty easy all year but when he says times up on the final, turn yours in immediately because he almost didn't accept mine! True story, haha.

AMAZING lecturer. Exams are very manageable if you read the textbook and go to lecture. Structures slides very simply and posts lecture outlines.

I would recommend her class to anyone that asks me.

Interesting lectures on social psychology and lots of real-world/practical implications. Class graded on 3 exams (no final), textbook/blog completion, and an easy group project. Professor Gaither explains concepts well and the class is fairly easy as long as you study for the exams. Check the syllabus for extra credit.

Professor Gaither is awesome. She makes lectures really interesting and super applicable to the outside world. This class was not difficult, but the group project can be a little tedious. Totally recommend this class to anyone interested in psych.

Dr. Gaither is a wonderful professor! She makes lectures super engaging, interesting, and funny! The material learned in PSY 104 is also really fascinating and applicable to life. Would highly recommend taking this class, whether you are a psych major or not!

This class is so interesting, and the lectures flew by. There are many different things that you are graded on, and the class is one of the easiest I've taken at Duke. As long as you read the textbook, show up to lectures, and do all of the assignments, it should be pretty easy to succeed! I would definitely recommend this class and prof Gaither!

Dr. Gaither is amazing! The class followed the textbook mostly but lectures had a few outside readings. Amazing lectures, really funny, great content for learning about odd stuff we do (sometimes we watch 'what would you do"). Take 104!

Great attitude! It's all about I don't care about what you think of me, I'm gonna keep doing me. Doesn't matter if you like it or not!" Again, very clear, wonderful person, and a pleasure to be around!!

Prof. Gaither is incredible! She's super open, honest, and I feel like she really relates well to her students. This particular course is a writing course but she gives very clear instructions on all her assignments! I recommend going to her office hours and participating as often as you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Gaither made social psychology super accessible. The workload in this class and the simplicity of the content could've been boring but Dr. Gaither managed to keep it interesting and engaging. She uses lots of contemporary and relevant examples, and she really cares about her students.

She is honestly one of the best professors that i've had at Duke. This class is extremely interesting and I 100% recommend it, I learnt so much in her class and she is super friendly so I suggest going to her office hours and getting to know her.

If you are looking to take an interesting class to fulfill your first-year seminar requirement, I would highly recommend taking Dr. Gaither's Diversity in Psychology class! Dr. Gaither cares about her students and wants you to learn as much as you can. In the class, you post weekly discussion questions about readings and have to complete 4 essays.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Would take again

reviews.comment: Dr. Gaither is extremely nice, helpful and flexible. Her seminar class on cultural diversity included two readings per week, three essays and a final presentation + paper. She gives good feedback and helps you outside of class. Her projects are very broad so you can always explore what you like/do best. It's a small class so participation matters.

I initially had no interest in the topic, but the class ended up being my favorite of the semester. Prof. Gellen knows the material well and helps you engage with it - I learned way more than I expected. Graded based on attendance, a few papers and exams, and a final project. Ask questions and use her feedback for an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Gellen was awesome! Really cares for her students and wants those who are engaged to succeed. Very clear grading criteria, and if you put in the time/effort you can get an A, but class is not easy and above average difficulty. Also, she is SUPER smart, and has a fascinating background; she really made this topic and class engaging. Take!

Dr. Gellen is so sweet and genuine. She cares a lot about the material and your learning, and is super receptive to feedback. Her lectures can get a bit boring/tangential at times, but overall the course is very interesting.

Solid. I've had Prof. Gellen for a couple classes, and she's definitely a good one. She's good with the in-class discussion, she picked some solid materials for us to go over in class, and she's not too brutal of a grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Really fun seminar class teacher! Discussions just took off and she took care not to monopolize the discussion, instead gently introducing ideas that we could all tackle. She gave helpful comments on essays, was a pretty easy and flexible grader, and was very accommodating and respectful of all students. Great experience!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Tests? Not many

reviews.comment: Gellen was very sweet and helpful if you sought her outside of class. Seminar based discussion and she was very interested and passionate about what she is teaching, which made the class very interesting. Not a particularly tough grader either.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Professor Gellen was very passionate about the material and fairly open to new ideas. She was also very understanding with assignments and reasonably lenient with the grading.

Dr. Gellen's class was all over the place. She seems genuinely interested in the topic, but isn't open to ideas that don't mirror hers and is pretty unorganized when it comes to leading class and discussion. I don't think I'd take a class with her again.

Dr. Gellen is a good professor who clearly cares about the subject of film. However, the class structure is pretty unorganized, and not much is gained from the discussions besides getting participation points. That being said, she does seem to care, and overall, the class isn't difficult.

German Film is a pretty fun class. Kata is incredibly passionate about the subject and really tries to pull the class into the material. The movies are watched outside of class and if you try to skip it, you will have no idea what is happening in the lecture. As long as you watch the movies, the rest of the class isn't too difficult, but engaging.

Awesome teacher, super cool human being. Take his class without hesitation. Made my life a little better.  Really engaging, patient and well spoken. He makes himself super duper available outside class. Genuinely cares about things he teach and students in his class. I am jealous of you people who get to hang out with him weekly.

Prof. SL is one of the best professors I've had at Duke. He makes stats fun and (relatively) easy. If you have the chance, definitely take a class with him before you leave. A great lecturer and an amazing human being. A gift to Duke psych department.

SL is one of the kindest, most caring, and inspirational people you'll meet at Duke. Truly a gift to have him as a teacher and mentor. Not only are his lectures great, and he's incredibly down to Earth, but he also profoundly cares about each one of his students. Please take the time to meet him outside of class, and you'll find an amazing friend.
super nice and invited cool guest speakers. easy ALP credit esp bc he outlines exactly what you need to do to get an A and it's not a lot of work at all compared to the average class.

Prof. SL is a really cool professor. He understands his students in all ways and thus make the class very engaging. He got creative with the course material, and invited good guests. He somehow knew a lot of students by name despite being a big class. He reads the reflections and acknowledges them. He still says hi when I see him on campus.

Prof SL is an absolute G. Best professor I've had at Duke hands down. He truly cares about his students and makes himself accessible at any point to support their needs. While this class can be daunting, he really breaks it down and will do whatever it takes for you to succeed and feel good about your performance in this class. A great guy.

This class is super easy. You fill out surveys a few times a week, which might take an hour total, max. During lectures, most people do homework for other classes since nobody cares as long as the surveys are done. Attendance is a big part of your grade, so show up! Great for STEM majors needing an easy ALP credit.
he is great. you're lucky to have him.

Prof SL is a great professor who really cares to get to know his students and is very accessible outside of class. His goals are really for you to become more comfortable with the research process and the basic statistical analyses that one might use. The class itself is definitely easier and less stat heavy but grading is clear and you learn a lot

Prof. SL is one of those professors who actually cares about you and helping you learn. Very accessible outside of class and lectures were entertaining. Class is a continuation of PSY204, but I thought it was easier. Same format - weekly assignments, group research project, and optional retake exam.

Professor SL has been my favorite professor I've ever had so far. He makes lectures extremely engaging, fun, and enjoyable. He also cares a lot about each of his students and wants us to actually learn the material and succeed in doing so. Attendance is not mandatory, but I would recommend because his lectures are very helpful and fun to listen to!

Honestly, SL's name should be right up there with Hard when it comes to amazing Duke psych profs. He did a great job balancing the course to serve both the beginner-level "math/stats is scary" humanities majors while also including significant "new statistics" ideas that left me, a Stat minor, an interesting field of applications to chew on.

Prof SL made statistics so easy and accessible. I learned methods that I now apply confidently to my job in a psych lab. Lectures were energizing and Prof SL always seemed to notice when the class was not understanding/ tired/ needing a break. Honestly one of the best professors at Duke.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: I'm taking his class during the pandemic and honestly its one of the few classes that gives me life. Professor Larkins redefines what a psych stats class is and he makes sure his students understand. I honestly hope everyone who has the time takes his class. He is also very cool and easy to talk to. For it to be my first stats class, I'm blessed.

This made statistics so fun! I loved how excited he was to teach and how inspirational as a professor he is. He mentions his journey from high school to college and also highlights many former students and their journeys. Taking statistics with him is one of your college highlights!

Dr. SL made stats so accessible, understandable, and interesting. He tries his hardest so everyone in lecture understands by taking multiple different approaches to explaining things. His class has homework assignments which are very manageable prepare you for the test. He is an inspirational teacher who is a no-(wo)man-left-behind kind of guy.

best prof ever!! so nice and understand and really cares about your learning. my fav quote from him is that "if you don't understand the material then it is my fault" he is always accessible if you need help. also he gives the test questions out 24 hrs in advance w/o the numbers so you can outline everything and just fill in the numbers at the test

It sounds cliche, but Professor S-L actually made statistics fun. He is one of my favorite professors at Duke, and this class helped me with analyzing data for my thesis so much. He is funny, actually cares about students, and wants students to succeed. He gives you all the information you need to do well in the class, and the TAs are amazing.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Prof. SL was amazing. I was nervous about taking Stats but after taking this class, I actually understand how they're helpful in the world and am interested in knowing more. He always has office hours and the TAs were always available. Labs are mandatory attendance but lectures aren't. Go to the lectures though because it's where you learn.

Dr. SL is literally one of the best profs I have ever had, he does his best to make sure that everyone fully understands the material. He and the TAs are accessible outside of class and are always willing to meet with you if you do not understand something and He tries to make homework and class material relatable and interesting. Take his class!

Professor SL was extremely chill but also really knowledgeable about stats and neuroscience. His psych/stats class made statistics super understandable and was very reasonably paced, with weekly homework assignments that were sometimes a little challenging but very fair. He was always accessible outside of class and was a super fun guy overall!
One of my favorite profs. Made me love statistics! Highly recommended.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Prof SL is phenomenal. Makes sure that students understand course material and gives assignments that really help you solidify your understanding of the material. Problem sets (45%) are key to doing well in the class. Cutoff for an A is a 95 but very doable with consistent effort. Highly recommend for any Psych/Neuro majors.

Professor SL is honestly the kind of professor you hope and pray for when signing up for classes. He's super smart but REALLY CARES ABOUT HIS STUDENTS!! This is so important. He makes the material understandable while still keeping the kids engaged. Always making sure everyone is on the same page and wants everyone to SUCCEED! Take his class!
Really nice and caring professor. Lecture isn't mandatory, but lab section is.

I loved Dr. Goodacre. For me, I learned so much and found him interesting and hilarious too. Workload was manageable. I would recommend taking this class if you want a fun, stimulating class taught by an expert.
Mark is such an amazing lecturer, so entertaining. He does a great job of making the topic interesting. He is also a pioneer in the field and incredibly well respected.

I will be taking Goodacre again. Kept content engaging and my God is he the most funny professor I've ever had. He's the perfect amount of self-depricating and famous. Also, Bear Grylls sat in our class. Absolutely sick time.
One of the best professors I've ever had. You will learn so much, his lectures are amazing.

Highly recommend Professor Goodacre, even to those with little background in religious study. He is incredibly accomplished, and his lectures were far and away the most engaging of the three class subdivisions. The real deal, to be sure.
Amazing lectures. He keeps you engaged. Great person and professor overall.

Professor Goodacre is very engaging and his love of the subject is clear to students.  He genuinely enjoys teaching and is understanding of students' needs.  You'll need to do some reading outside of class, but not excessively, and the weekly "quizzes" are a nice way to stay on top of everything.

Goodacre is a great lecturer. He is also hilarious. All of his classes have the same format (online quizzes due every class, 2 7-8 page papers). He is the very best in his field. He's on so many histor channel documentaries. If you are interested in analyzing the Bible then Goodacre is for you.

One of the greats. Made the class super interesting and fun, and I learned a ton. The class met once per week for 2.5 hours, but he makes it feel shorter than a normal class. Reasonable amount of work and reasonable expectations. He really is an amazing professor.

Goodacre is an incredible professor -- made New Testament super interesting and wasn't hard to do well in this class. Work hard on the professors and reach out to TAs, do the daily quizzes and you'll be fine. Sign in sheets during class but you aren't penalized for attendance -- just get to drop two quizzes if your attendance is good.
Goodacre is incredible smart, funny and sweet! Take his classes!!!!!! All of them!

Professor Goodacre is fantastic all the way around - an impressive intellectual, having done all of his education at Oxford, a leader in his field, and charismatic and engaging in lectures.  I learned so much in this class about St. Paul, Scripture, and early Church history, not to mention just reading Scripture for hw is pretty cool. A must take.
Very easy class. skipped most lectures and got an A. Goodacre himself is a very interesting lecturer and made the class enjoyable, I just skipped to prioritize other things
A great guy. Absolutely willing to help. Considerate of student's schedules and stresses. You have to work but you feel good about doing the work because he's such a great guy.
Awesome teacher. Fun class. Would love to have him again. Easy too.

Professor Goodacre is an awesome teacher. Not only is his British accent great to listen to, but he is funny and very supportive of his students. His New Testament class is very straightforward - he gives out lecture notes before every class and you will always know what is going on. I highly recommend him!!

Goodacre's a great lecturer. He presents his views on issues and the opposing views, then allows us the final decision. A note to Christians who don't have a background in scholarly New Testament study: you'll learn things in here that you never did in church. Some may challenge your beliefs! But it's worth it – you'll learn so much in the process!

took non-canonical with him. Great man with a great sense of humor. Loved his class. No that's an understatement. LOVED HIS CLASS. Cap's prolly don't help explain the situation. Put it this way, he's just an amazing professor . The question is, why not take all his classes: Historical Jesus, New Testament, Life and Letters of Paul, and NonCanon?
I love this guy.

Goodacre is the cutest man. Interesting to listen to and truly cares about his students. There are quizzes after every class which are pretty straightforward and three papers. Would definitely recommend this class!!

Professor Goodacre is a fine lecturer and has a knack for creating interesting aspects and bringing them into history which would be otherwise mundane. He is friendly in office hours and very cheerful, and his quizzes are not difficult. Essays in his class may be a bit difficult, so it is best to stick to the sources given and work from there.

This guy is awesome. He's hilarious and spends 30 minutes of the class showing videos, telling interesting stories, and  telling jokes. Students get a 5 minute break halfway through, too. Still, you're guaranteed to learn a ton and have a great time. Very, very little work, but don't forget to take the quizzes after class!

Prof Goodacre had a keen sense of humor so his lectures were very interesting. You don't have to study outside of class at all. However, there were 2 6-paged essays and an online final that will constitute 70% of your grade. Make sure to do WELL on those & you'll be fine.
Extremely knowledgeable about the subject, fair grader, adorable accent. TAKE HIS CLASS.

Easily one of my favorite professors at Duke. I honestly wish I had time before I graduate to take more of his classes. LOVED this class and every thing about him. He's hilarious, charming, and makes the material so exciting to learn. I looked forward to going to this class, which is weird since it was at 10:05. LOVE HIM!

New Testament. very easy, readings aren't necessary for doing well.  Entire grade based on Take Home Midterm and Take Home Final-which are pretty long 10 to 12 pages each. Lecture was somewhat boring.  Goodacre sends out a copy of the lecture before class so you don't need to take notes. Overall class was easy but boring.

I had taken religion classes before, but Goodacre is amazing. He's actually really knowledgeable, and has his own theories, which is pretty cool. He releases Podcasts, which tie in nicely with his lectures. He's a great teacher and makes class interesting.

Mark Goodacre is THE most amazing professor at Duke by far!  I took The Life and Letters of Paul and there is no way to explain how great Goodacre is.  He is hilarious, so entertaining, and makes learning the subject matter which can be rather dry very easy.  He is so useful and really helps you in his assignments, so it's not very hard! TAKE HIM!!
Life and Letters of Paul-- just to add to the praise. Mark Goodacre is amazing. I had no knowledge of biblical scholarship before the class and now I'm considering it as a major. He is amazing!!!

A fantastic teacher with a unique ability to make learning difficult concepts effortless and fun. How many profs can make a 2.5 hour Life and Letters of Paul at 6pm actually entertaining? I wish I had more time at Duke simply to take another class with him. One of the best teachers I had in 6 years of undergrad/grad at Duke-- take his class!

Phenomenal professor - one of the best at Duke!  His Historical Jesus class was fascinating.  Furthermore, he is a master of his discipline, and you can tell from the moment he begins to lecture.  He's funny and never condescending towards any religion.  Goodacre should be an essential part of every Duke student's academic experience.

AMAZING! Highly recommended- down to earth, funny, so smart, basically the authority on New Testament.  He really wants students to learn and asks for their input in class.  Flexible grading if you demonstrate interest and effort in your papers (only a midterm and a final).  Readings not really necessary to do, but interesting to do anyway-TAKE HIM

I LOVE this man, just like every one else.  I am super creepy and even read his online blog, I can't get enough of him!  He is funny, young, energetic, and casual.  You learn so much and don't even realize it.  I would feel so terrible when I would miss class and count down the days until the next one.  Take him.  NOW.

Love, Love, Love Mark Goodacre. He is THE source for the New Testament, Jesus, Peter, Paul, Mary, John, Pontius Pilate, and the like. Take his class. Even if you're not a religion major, or if you are atheist. He's the most engaging professor ever. Its fun if you try to count the number of times he says "when I was at Oxford."

Historical Jesus quickly became one of my favorite classes... ever.  Goodacre is simply the best professor you could have - hilarious, helpful, clear, hilarious, top of his field.  And he's hilarious too. He goes into frequent digressions about American and British culture that are, well, hilarious. Final was tough, but otherwise not too much work.

I absolutely love this man.  He frequently digresses into hilarious tangents about British culture.  Top scholar in his field and completely personable.  I plan to take the other two classes he teaches.

Life and Letters of Paul.  Amazing amazing class, easy to sit through 2.5 hours of his lectures, easy to listen to, but thorough and usually presents all sides of issues.  Top notch in his field, knows his stuff.  Highly recommended class if you have any interest in the subject.
Very engaging and thorough professor, highly recommended for all classes

Zanalda is very sweet. Other than showing up to sign your name on attendance, this class is free time. Note no grades are returned during the semester, but do the assignments (a few presentations, attending outside lectures) and spend class time doing anything.
Professor Zanalda is incredible - class is very chill and his background is super interesting
He is the best. Cares a ton about his students and is incredibly smart. Class is comprised of a presentation, exam, and final project with not many weekly or every class smaller assignments
Professor Zanalda was a super nice professor who was interested in the course's topic. This class was an easy A, but at times felt almost too easy.
Absolute chiller. Definitely take a class with him
The class was not super difficult and it was easy to get engaged as long as you followed the readings. Zanalda himself is a great guy and super fun to talk to outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Zanalda is a cool dude and mega chill professor. However, do not take this class with the intent to learn / be engaged- it's an easy A and tbh has to be the easiest and least time-consuming class I've taken at Duke; a true "gut class". I'd take one of his classes again for that reason, but overall it was super boring and dull, but Zanalda = chiller
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: This was kinda a boring class in an online format, but the concepts discussed are super interesting. Zanalda is unbelievably intelligent and knows so much. He tries to contextualize every students' comment and weave them into a larger narrative, which is cool.

Prof. Zanalda is an incredible person to learn from given his vast array of experiences and storied career. He's also incredibly approachable, kind, and caring. The class can become dry at times though, and there's a bit of a disconnect between the reading assigned and what gets discussed (much more reading assigned than we get through in class).
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Professor Zanalda is such a gem. I can't say that HISTORY201 was the most interesting class I've taken so far, but he cares about his students, what they have to say, and always contributes his own thoughts to each discussion. If this course was more difficult, maybe I would have different thoughts on him, but he's a really down-to-earth, funny guy
Nice and understanding teacher, not the most interesting course but he cares about his students and wants them to enjoy the material
was not the course I was excited to take

Highly recommend taking classes with him. He is highly knowledgeable and easily accessible outside of class. He wants to help out his students and is just such a nice guy. Lectures can sometimes feel long but the workload is manageable and you can tailor final projects to your interests. You do need to attend class and occasionally participate.
Super nice guy and easy class

Great professor and knowledgeable in all aspects of economic history. He's very nice and approachable and very fair in his exams and grading. As long as you show up to class, participate, and turn in work on time you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: One of my favorite professors so far at Duke. He is extremely knowledgable on economics and especially economic history in all aspects. He's also super nice and very approachable and is very lenient about grading and gives very fair exams. As long as you participate in class and do the readings you will be fine. 2 easier exams and short paper.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Class is super laid back but you don't learn a whole lot. Basically you mark down that you're there, he just talks about random things that don't matter for an hour, and then you leave. The only grade you get all semester is the A you get at the end.

Zanalda is just an easy-going economics legend that is probably the smartest guy in almost every room he walks into. His background as a trained economics historian speaks to his vast knowledge in the field on top of his work in the Chief Economist office of the World Bank. Weekly readings and one lengthy research paper at the end of the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Tests? Not many--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Awesome guy - interesting, funny, helpful.  His class was one of the easiest I've taken at Duke. Unfortunately I didn't learn much...
Most approachable and understanding professor. Class material is very interesting and not a lot of work effort required, apart from weekly readings which aren't very taxing.
He's a really nice guy and his classes usually have averages of  b+ or a-. Gives multiple choice tests, doesn't assign a lot of work, and is very friendly.

Even though the lectures were sometimes boring, since professor Zanalda mostly read powerpoint presentations (available online - which was a plus), the content greatly compensated. Professor Zanalda himself was nice, helpful and clear. The midterms require some reading but are easy. The free-topic paper at the end can be interesting too.
No Comments

Very light workload and easy grading. I didn't find that my writing improved significantly through her course, but some of her feedback was valuable. She's very flexible and accommodating, easy to talk to, and eager to slightly adjust coursework to better align with class interests.

Such an amazing professor. It's clear that she loves teaching and genuinely cares about her students. She is very understanding and accommodating when students need flexibility. You can easily do well if you put in the effort. I highly recommend taking a class with her.

Love her downnnn. She's very lenient with work and understanding if anything comes up. Her feedback was amazing and made me a better writer. Her assignments are fun and push the boundaries of what I thought writing was previously. So sweet and amazing, you have to take her
Amazing professor. Lots of resources. Engaging discussions. Valued student perspectives. Organized class. Easy grader. Few assignments. My favorite class of the semester for sure

i rarely write RMPs, but dr. taylor is among the best professors at duke. taylor is one of the rare faculty who genuinely cares for your wellbeing. struggled with my health & she supported me to ensure i could succeed. intellectually challenging content & really enjoyed class discussions! take a class with dr. taylor -- you will NOT regret it!!!!
Professor Taylor is a very caring and sweet person. She always lifts my mood when I go into class. Her classes are interesting and easy to follow.

Professor Taylor is amazing. The best class I've taken so far. Material for WRI120 Reproductive Justice was super interesting. Two papers and a group project make up the bulk of your grade, but they are easy and do not take up a lot of time at all. Attendance is not mandatory, but participation is. Easy grader. Take a class with Prof Taylor!!!

I would say that you only need to take a week out of every month to do your assignments for the class. Only 3 projects and she grades easily. Attendance is graded and after 2 or so absences, your grade will go down.
genuinely one of the best profs i've had at duke, pays attention to each student individually & gives detailed feedback for papers and projects, class was super insightful & fun!

Prof. Taylor's class was probably the highlight of my freshman fall semester. She is the sweetest professor ever, offers so much support in her classes, and is so incredibly understanding. There are a few big projects in class but her grading contract makes everything feel less stressful.

Class was so interesting and facilitated a lot of great conversations. I loved the structure of the grading contract. If you did all the assignments and put in genuine effort you are basically guaranteed an A. Hannah is also such a caring person. I was struggling with mental health during my 1st year and she was so flexible and compassionate.

One of my favorite classes taken. Dr. Taylor's class structure is so easy to work within and the topics you cover in class are all very interesting. Various types of papers and projects, and the workload is light. Super enjoyable overall, highly recommend for Writing 101.

So kind and passionate. The best W101 for those passionate about reproductive rights. Grading is extremely lenient and workload is light. Grading includes 5 reading responses, 2 short papers, participation and a final advocacy project. She is a one of a kind professor!

She is so awesome!! I have never had a professor this nice and who would listen to her students the way that Prof. Taylor does. She is super passionate and engages the class very well. Also, the class is based on a contract where you get an A if you submit something which takes stress off and allows you to grow in writing as best as you can.

Extremely nice, approachable, and understanding. 2 papers and a group project, but assignments are low-stakes due to her grading system which is based on participation/effort. Guaranteed A if you showcase effort on assignments and in class. I would definitely recommend this class.

Professor Taylor accommodated all levels of writing experience with her labor based grading system. So long as you demonstrate proper effort and participation in the class, you are guaranteed an A. She is also very understanding of life circumstances and stress.

Prof. Miller cares about her students a lot and is very flexible with assignments and exams. Lectures can be a bit slow. Two exams that were some MCQ, some short answers, and one long answer. Peer-teaching was an amazing way to understand social inequalities in the context of something you're interested in.

Dr. Miller cares a lot and the material is super interesting. She isn't always the most engaging lecturer which can make some classes a drag, but overall the material is interesting enough and there is enough discussion in class to make up for it.

Professor Miller is super sweet. The content is very straightforward and easy. The slides are hard to study with for exams since she puts questions on there that aren't answered in the slides, but she answers them during lecture. 2 exams. Homework can be done as a group: either essay questions or infographics. 1 semester-long group research paper.

Really kind and caring, and very easily approachable. The class itself isn't the most interesting thing in the world unless you plan to study this topic throughout college, but if you're looking for a class where you can be successful by just putting in the basic amount of effort, this should be fine for you.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Miller is incredibly sweet and cares a lot about her students. The best part about her class is the discussions about the material. She teaches us to be critical in how we learn and gives lots of time for in-depth discussions and debates on topics. The class is super light on work and the classes are super interesting, perfect combo

Take this class for some interesting discussions and a relatively easy A. Almost all assignments were group work and not at all time consuming. We had to lead one lecture per group, and even that was not too time consuming. Genna is really sweet, caring, and passionate about the material. Any of her electives are great and never very challenging!

While I didn't learn that much from the class, she always made it engaging. However, I didn't particularly like that the class was structured around a huge group project that didn't have that much guidance.
Super easy and chill class, take this if you want to make friends and get A. All work are group projects, workload manageable.

Absolutely loved this class! Great professor, lectures easy to follow. It does take a long time to get our grades back. I'm not the biggest fan of economics so I could've done better if I really liked the subject. She does cancel class when she's sick which sucks but she's human so I understand. Would take again for sure.

Easy A & chill class. professor super caring 

Econ 337: the exams(1 midterm 1 final) are all take home, not too difficult
One peer lecture towards the end of the semester, that was the only time comsuming assignment. You can make it in 1-2 days. Everything is group based
There is also volunteer aspect to the class, must have 20 hours tutoring
Overall Loved the class, however does take some time to get grades back

This class is simply poorly run on multiple fronts. Professor Miller runs lecture like she wants a seminar, and as a whole lecture is close to useless and extremely boring. On top of that, her slides are terrible for studying as they don't really contain any explanations at all. 
Professor Miller is nice, but her grading scheme is unclear.

Her Focus class was not the most inspiring; it definitely had potential to be a good class but the lectures and activities really fall short in what should be an interesting subject. There are better Focus classes to take. Aside from that, Professor Miller is a really nice, genuine person who cares about her students. Just not the best lecturer.
So nice, very caring professor who really takes feedback from students to heart. Not difficult to do well if you participate and engage with the material, great econ elective!

I love Genna. Truly such a sweet person who cares a lot about her material. 337 is a great class, exams might be tough but she takes feedback very well. Assignments are longer but again, she is very clear what she wants. She also just really sweet which makes it very fun to learn from her
Professor miller is super sweet and cares about her students. Tests and homework reflect what she teaches in class pretty well.
Interesting subject matter but not very in-depth. The group project takes place over the course of the semester, but as long as you try, you will get a good grade.

A very reasonable and caring professor. Tests are fair and straightforward so long as you study the material. Grading is lenient though ambiguous. Decent work load. Not an "easy A" but comparably an easy and chill class.

caring teacher, but in general the class is pretty disorganized and not that engaging. her grading scheme is also very arbitrary and it takes her a long time to give advice/grades back to students. i wouldn't call this an "easy A" if that's what you're looking for.

Really nice and caring professor, workload is descent, and students like her. Mind that there is a group research and group final paper, and the groups are randomly assigned. Exams are easy. Sometimes marks were deducted just for a wrong word, but usually it's only 4-5 points so that's fine.

Very receptive and nice if you talk to her. She gave me ten points back on a test just by talking to her about an issue. It's not difficult to get a good grade in the class if you read the material and add some creativity to the final project.

Focus class on Game Theory. Genuinely wanted to connect and get participation, but always just missed the mark. Enthusiastic, not particularly clear or interesting. Played games in class, but they were all kinda bs, no real opportunity to think through and strategize.

One of the sweetest women out there. I would give her a 3.5 easiness, not hard to get an A/A- but sometimes her test questions can just be confusing. She tries really hard to make class interesting though.

Professor Miller is one of the sweetest people I've ever met, and is just a genuinely nice person. However, her lectures are very unorganized and she jumps around a lot, making the lectures hard to follow. Tests aren't impossible but sometimes are on obscure topics.

People who are complaining about her probably aren't doing any of the assigned readings and spending class time on facebook. If you read the book and go to class and pay attention everything is clear. Yeah it's boring, but this is an easy class...what do you expect?

Miller cares a lot about her students and sharing the learning experience with them. However, her lectures are disorganized, feedback isn't great, and she often chooses the most obscure material to test. Our class went through 5 revised editions of the syllabus, that tells you something. Still, she's a very nice grader: an A/A- is very doable.

I know I always check ratemyprofessor before taking a class, so I direct this comment people like me. Do not take this class. Take Econ 132. Take 195 (Grace Kim's class). Her grading system is incomprehensible. I got 2x 100s and 2x<70s. I know it sounds easy, but like meth, not even once.

Genna Miller is one of the sweetest professors at Duke. She is genuinely so nice and really cares about her students. Her class could get boring at times, but overall the material was a nice break from the usual econ course and it wasn't that hard. I would recommend taking her class.

She is not good at explaining concepts.  The structure of her lectures is illogical and she shows examples without explaining what she is doing.  Lectures are driven by students asking questions and she often does not understand what is being asked.  She also does not have the heart to tell students when they're wrong.  She is however a nice person

Shes a nice person. Class is easy. Thats it for the good.  Shes an obsessive feminist who is less intelligent than 90% of her students. She posted a reading online and literally changed every word "he", "his", and "him" to "she", "her", and "her" making the paper totally unreadable. Definitely stay away if you want to learn anything from a class.

Very enthusiastic and extremely nice, but not the best teacher. Makes mistakes on the board often, and often responds to questions by praising how good they are rather than by answering them. An A- is easy to get; An A is more annoying. Both are manageable. Wouldn't take this class again.
She's like a bad high school teacher. I have no idea how she works here.

I TA'ed for Prof. Miller 6 yrs ago and found her lectures painful to sit through. In section, students always asked me to elucidate everything that she had discussed in lecture. I'm disheartened to see that there are still complaints about her. Back then, she was a 1st-year teacher. I really thought she would make progress & improve as a lecturer.

She's the motherly type, but her teaching style really didn't work for me. She seemed like she was afraid to correct students when they made comments that were wrong so we always got sidetracked and I left class often feeling like I didn't learn anything new. Plus the 50-minute class always seemed to take forever.
this is probably one of the easiest econ. classes you can take if you want to read/write.  however, it will bore you to tears.  lectures were painful to sit through.
Overall just a bad class, there are much better Econ classes to take than this...

Homework is lengthy, and the tests are incredibly difficult; given that they make up 80% of your grade, you have to do well. There aren't many ways to prepare for the tests, but make sure you do the homework weekly for the other 20% of your grade and to ensure you understand the material. She is kind, but lectures are confusing and hard to follow.
Korean accent

Hahn is so genuinely funny and makes the class a fun low-pressure environment. Super accessible, caring, and never makes you feel embarrassed to ask something in class. Exams were fair and so was grading (final was hard but she curved). Truly an unforgettable Prof. Talks a lot about what's coming up on the exams in lecture so don't skip class

Prof. Hahn's 221 class was definitely interesting. For the midterms, be sure to really read the textbook and homework questions thoroughly. Another tip for the final and midterms: pay attention to the "hints" she gives before exams; they're useful. She's a funny teacher and a very fair exam grader. Just lock in, and you'll be fine.
