As other comments said, it's not an Esay A class (why would it be). Be ready to read the textbook on your own, pay attention to her hints for midterms and finals, and largely you'll be fine.
She is a funny kind soul, but her lectures are just her reading the textbook word for word in a worse way. If you can get another prof, take the other one. Otherwise you better lock in twin.

I had ZERO linear exposure. This course made more sense as we went on, even though content got harder. Hahn is funny and loves the subject so much that she'll make you appreciate the beauty of pure math. 221 is HARD, proofs and all, 85% tests, BUT she's so sweet, gives practice, and a fair grader. Don't let the other reviews scare you!

I came into the class with a high school LA class and still struggled-- but it was worth the learning curve. 
It's difficult, but Hahn is a great professor who's very kind, funny, and accessible. The problem sets and practice questions she gives are also very useful, and she tells you what types of questions will be on the test beforehand.

Legitimately tough for a freshman fall class, but a great way to jump into a challenge. Grading is fine, but get ready to spend a lot of time just thinking, staring, and asking questions. It can get confusing at times, but you can get through it. I particularly enjoyed her funny tangents on random topics.
Hard in comparison, but got furthest of other professors and became more reasonable as you went (first years tend to overreact since this is really par for a college course)

Perhaps a rough introduction to math at Duke for those expecting something easy, but you cover plenty of concepts and more than the other sections. Exams, rough, but fair and doable purely from course material. Funny, significant accent, but get used to it. Take it to learn, perhaps consider another prof if looking for easy class (why are you?)

In the calculus class, Heekyoung Hahn,
With Tofu, fries, and ice cream, a strange domain.
Watermelons roll, curves defined anew,
As partial derivatives dance, students view.

Tangents on fries, integrals of ice,
Limits of melon spheres, so nice.
Hahn's wit and Tofu's silent grace,
Make vectors and gradients, a tasty case.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Tofu, French fries, ice cream, watermelons

Professor Hahn teaches at an extremely fast pace. However, she is kind and her exams are not too hard. Gives clear instructions on question topics.  Exam questions are easy if you have learnt some tricks from physics. Often teaches right off the textbook, poor lecturer.

Hahn is - funny, kind, but most importantly, an awful teacher. You will laugh in class at her jokes and think she is nice, but you will not learn. You will be laughing at the discussion of whether the ice cream on the cone is included in the integral, because she doesn't know. She sits back and learns from students, and leaves the class immediately

Hahn's lectures are not introductory (but they should be). She is unclear, doesn't help develop intuition, only writes proofs on the board, and messes up details. Plus she teaches at a fast pace and is bad at answering questions. Exams are fairly graded but not similar to homework. I self-studied the book with no prior knowledge - not recommended.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Hahn stared strong giving key proofs and intuitions in to differential calculus, but the second half, integral calculus and vector calculus, were covered with much less clarity. Despite glossing over details in lectures and messing them up, Hahn still expected us to have a perfect mastery of the material, frequently testing edge cases on exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Heekyoung Hahn is a nice person, but teaches 222 subpar. Exams were much harder than homeworks, making studying way harder. The exams had more physics applied questions, which 222 is not primarily about. Unless you're a physics major, even lots of studying probably won't earn an A, and math majors beware--222 is computation heavy and proof light.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures disconnected from homework. Way too fast paced and ahead. Boring computations. For MA222

Professor Hahn is simply too smart to teach this class and as a result, lectures are kinda rushed and not as effective. However, she is very accessible and exams seem to be in line with the material we covered so overall it's not too bad. One of the hardest classes at Duke, but the curve comes in clutch big time.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: she brilliant. if only she could teach, she is sweet, will try to get all the math in her brain into yours, but there is just a major disconnect. too smart to teach. goes super fast and she walks in RIGHT when class starts, lectures for the whole time & then leaves AS SOON as class ends. has OH but they arent helpful because her teaching is rough
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: A lovely person who genuinely cares for her students and has a real passion for mathematics. She remembered me years after I took her class and even though math wasn't my thing, I still felt good going in.

The textbook used is terrible and doesn't have an answer key online, the homework isn't properly graded so you can't track your progress, her accent makes it hard to understand lectures, and she assumes we know everything so resorts to writing "duh" on the board instead of explaining concepts. For a potential math major, she is a wrong choice.

Just the worst class I've taken at Duke. It's so poorly structured. Homework is arbitrarily long, exams are unpredictable, no supporting materials or practice exams. I was depressed for most of it; I just hope I haven't failed.

Her lectures are a regurgitation of the textbook. Instead of explaining proofs she writes duh on the board and moves very fast through material. Tests are extremely hard and she encourages people to withdraw. The only way to do well in this class is if you have seen this material before. This is my 4th math class at Duke & by far the worst.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Great person but terrible professor. Just comes to class and writes proofs on the board straight from the book, doesn't really care for developing intuition and big-picture understanding. Very fast-paced: it feels like she only teaches for the top 10% of the class. The class has no TA, no practice exams, no additional resources. Duke Math is evil.

Well, I'll start with the good: Firstly, she's peppy and sometimes makes funny jokes. Yeah, that's about it. She has a pretty thick accent, which isn't her fault, but she speaks so quickly and blasts through so many topics that I always found myself with a dull headache at the end of class. There are NO practice materials and feedback is minimal.

She moves fast in lecture and lectures almost directly from the book. I ended up teaching myself more from the textbook, but that's pretty terrible too. Lots of homework and tests are unpredictable (no practice exams)! If you take this class, be sure to be in a study group from the beginning. You're gonna need it.

A really nice person but not a nice professor. The class is poorly taught and the textbook is useless. Homework problems are often impossible to solve and tests are for creative mathematicians. Almost depressed by taking this class.

Dr. Hahn is a lovely person, but a difficult professor. She is very enthusiastic, but she moves fast and often doesn't explain things thoroughly. You will have to put in a LOT of work and energy outside of class if you want to do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Probably the worst teacher to have instructed this class. Math 221 is already hard enough with a frankly useless book, but to have a teacher essentially reiterate (sometimes verbatim) the book is not helpful. She is extremely fast without being very clear and has trouble solving the homework problems she assigns. Do not take this class with her.

Professor Hahn is the best person to take Math 202 with! She's known for her hard tests, but her classes always understand the material the best out of all the sections. She offers extra office hours outside class just so we can come and ask questions, and she explains concepts many ways to help us understand it better. The textbook is horrible.
She just goes off essentially copying the textbook.  Kinda helpful outside of class.  Not concerned with students understanding the material during class
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Tests are super hard, but if you go to class and she knows your name, she will help you out. She's always willing to meet outside of class and explain things to you. Her accent can be tough to understand, but she is SO EXCITED about teaching multi. Her knowledge of math is like way beyond multi, so sometimes she forgets how to explain things simply
The class isn't the easiest, but she's the best professor to take it with.

Professor Hahn is all around a good teacher. She has a bit of an accent, but after a couple of classes you can understand pretty much every word. She is funny, which makes lectures much more enjoyable. The homework is long but she will push some of it back if the class thinks it's too much. Tests can be tough but aren't bad.

Amazing math professor. She is extremely enthusiastic and is always willing to help. The HW takes a good amount of time, but if actually do the homework and read the textbook, this class isn't too hard.

This class is a nightmare.  She is very bad at explaining abstract concepts or presenting the "big picture." The only thing more useless than the lectures is the textbook.  It will take a LOT of outside work to do well in this class.  She is VERY nice, however.

Professor Hahn is all around very good. She has an accent which can make things difficult to understand at times but she tries very hard/is very enthusiastic. She is hilarious, kind and very personable. Some times she moves a little fast, but that is to be expected with the amount of material.

Professor Hahn is one of the best math professors at Duke. She never tries to be esoteric and is always about helping her students. She is extremely friendly and helpful in her office hours, not to mention she is hilarious. If anyone is interested in Math 221, I recommend taking it with her. I am glad she is teaching Math 401, next fall.
Super easy but generally interesting. Honestly, it's difficult not to get an A.
Very engaging and kind.

Dr. Harrell is such an amazing professor. She is kind, lenient, and cares about her students. Some lectures were a tad bit boring but overall interesting material and she presents it well. If have the opportunity to take a class with her, definitely take it! Grading is super chill as well.

Great professor. Her lectures are straightforward, and the exams require very little review. The course content is extremely interesting, and the TAs and professor are easily accessible. Clear grading criteria. Readings are not necessary. I would definitely take this course with her, many make up assignment opportunities and lenient grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: You can really tell how passionate she is about the material she teaches! Lectures were really engaging. You are assigned into groups at the beginning of the semester but she takes so much time to really assign groups well based on a survey you submit. Quizzes every class but if you read over the slides before you'll be fine. Would take again!

If you have the opportunity to take any class of hers, do it! You can tell she's super passionate about what she teaches, and she genuinely makes an effort to get to know her students. Class is an easy A if you read the slides before quizzes and follow the rubric carefully to all the projects.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Very passionate about the content, which made the lectures interesting. Class is almost entirely based on pre-class readings and quizzes, which get tedious, but the content is interesting. She is a pretty harsh grader, but was super receptive to student feedback and eased off when she realized we were stressed about her class. Overall, recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Super chill class. Cool elementary class about law if you have any legal interests. Daily quizzes are based on readings but all lectures are posted before class so just go through slides and youll ace it. Huge project at end of year. Basically your whole grade, awesome class and great professor. Would recommened this or any of her classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof Hamil is one of the best professors you will have the pleasure of working with at Duke. She is passionate about the material, invested in students' success, and overall amazing. If you complete the readings and prepare for class then it should be no trouble. I found the group based environment to be very enriching. Highly recommend!! :)

Professor Hamil-Luker is an amazing professor who is genuinely interested in what she teaches. The class revolves around group work, but you will also be responsible for individual quizzes and projects. If you cannot finish the readings before class, the notes she uploads give you all of the information you need for the quizzes she gives in class.

Amazing prof. Embodies care for what she teaches not only through class content but also how she interacts with her students. Very open to feedback and extremely personable/accessible. Very clear grading criteria and reasonable workload. She does share a lot about her personal life in class (though for educational purposes). HIGHLY recommend.

Best professor at Duke! I've taken THREE of her classes and absolutely loved them all. She cares so much about the subject matters, is so inspiring, and tries to make class a stress-free environment where learning is the priority (and if you're wondering, I got an A+ in all three classes and did not do the homework 90% of the time).

Prof Hamil-Luker is so cool- I'm a psych major and hadn't considered the systemic issues that contribute to mental health problems until I took her class. So easy and she's very engaging, definitely worth taking. She had a really tough loss in her family halfway through the semester but still showed up and was an awesome prof. Love her!!!

Hamil-Luker's class is great for changing how you think about drugs and drug laws. She challenges stereotypes and encourages you to break your thought patterns. While the group-based nature of the class was frustrating at times, I found the class to be very useful and interesting. Highly recommend.
Jenifer is the best 100% recommend

A real GEM! SOC230 is super engaging, and Dr. Hamil-Luker uses a lot of creative ways to help us learn the content. The course is based on a group policy paper, but she listens to students and makes sure that the work is split fairly. Lenient grader - you will earn good grades if you put in the effort!

This class was extremely interesting and changed my perspective on drugs and addiction in the United States. Professor Hamil-Luker is very passionate and engaging with the class. There are readings for every class, daily quizzes, and an emphasis on group projects, but the work is doable and is done more for understanding and effort.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Hands-down one of the funniest, kindest professors at Duke. She radiates positivity.

A W class, but well structured in guiding you to the final paper. JHL gave very detailed feedback on drafts to help you improve your writing, and she is a lenient grader. SOC332 exposed me to research methods that I do not have much chance to practice in other classes, such as conducting interviews. 25% of grade depends on unlimited-tries quizzes.

Chill class, but not as informative and eye-widening as Drugs in the US. Dr. Hamil-Luker is very understanding of her students and a lenient grader. Reading quizzes (unlimited tries) and in-class writing (graded on completion) composed most of the grade. There's also a group presentation, but Dr. Hamil-Luker ensures a fair split of work.

Learned a lot in this class. JHL debunked many stereotypes about drug use and made me rethink our current legal system. Quiz every class, but open-note and unlimited tries. Lenient grader - put in efforts and you'll get an A. Group projects can be annoying, but I had a great team. Debate outlines can be hard if there're only weak positions left.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--So many papers

reviews.comment: Excellent professor for this course; clear grading criteria, accessible outside class, and engaging/involved with her lectures. Learned a lot taking this course and would recommend anyone interested in the course material to enroll as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Prof Hamil-Luker is a nice person, but I probably wouldn't take the class again. I don't really feel like I learned a lot - just memorizing to do well on the quizzes. Also, she grades very harshly.

Wish more Duke classes were like hers. During every class, I laughed and learned. Material was interesting and relevant to everyday decisions. She debunked many stereotypes about drugs, revealing how powerful lawmakers and companies create addiction--not just bad personal choices.

Definitely the best professor I've had at Duke -- real, down to earth, caring and just a great person. Probably learned the most, real-life relevant things in the class. Easy to get an A, she wants everyone to pass.
She cared about selecting teams, required class participation and was available outside class. Lectures could be fun but the material was poor. Tried too hard to be funny.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Wish more profs were like her! Clear assignment directions. Passionate about material. Realistic work expectations. Cares what students learn and think. Witty jokes & real-life examples make lectures come alive. I had a great team, so liked working on group projects. Must participate in class discussions and activities. Take a class with her!

Wasn't thrilled about taking this required class, but so glad I did! By the end of the semester, I was a much better writer and critic of social science research. I've never had a professor provide such detailed feedback on my drafts! Go to her office hours even if you're doing well. She wants to help you improve, so take advantage of it!

I love her class. She is one of the warmest, nicest and most accesible professors at Duke. If you put in the work, you will certainly do well. Every Duke student should take a class with her. You learn a lot, you have fun, and you feel you came out knowing something valuable. .

Taken several classes with HL b/c of her teaching and grading style. Classes are always different (video, discussion, experiment, case study) so you rarely get bored and want to go to class. Lots of quizzes and short online assignments, but no tests and generous grader. Liberal, but not in your face about it. Wants students to change the world

Dr. Hamil-Luker is hilarious, kind and compassionate.  She cares more about you learning than grading, and you come away with a truly educational experience because of that.  She is down to Earth, a talented lecturer and a great mentor to have!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Wonderful lady. Knows most people are taking her class just to get an A, and doesn't disappoint. Very chill class and she knows her stuff.

Best class I've had at Duke so far! Never bored. Had team projects, which I usually hate, but prof structured assignments to encourage fair distribution of workload.  Creating anti-drug video was much better than writing another paper or taking another exam. Study her online notes and you can ace the quizzes.

One of my favorite professors at Duke! She is incredibly kind, entertaining, hilarious, and good-spirited. She really cares about her students and also understands that her class is not your entire life. I definitely recommend any class with her (I took SOC 265). Quizzes every class are slightly annoying, but you will learn a lot!

Really enjoyed the format of this class with group quizzes, mini-lectures, lots of videos and class participation. Textbook was repetitive and too heavily focused on drugs and crime.  Prof worked with us to decide on grading scheme and assignments. She actually cared what we thought!  Wish there were more profs like her at Duke.

If you are premed, take this class!  HL makes you think about problems in the healthcare system and what the next generation can do to fix them. I'm more aware of social and political reasons for people's health problems, which will be important in my future practice. She's inspired me to consider being a GP in rural areas.

Learned so much in this class, some of it I'll actually use after Duke.  She took too long to return graded papers, but it was because she spent hours giving detailed feedback on our first drafts.  Lots of in-class group work that made time go quickly.  She had us over to her house for dinner--really cool person as well as engaging teacher.

Loved this class. She's so funny, relatable, and well-liked by students. She's really understanding and accommodating and genuinely wants to help her students out. The class was almost always interesting and fun to learn about. Read her powerpoint notes and follow the rubric for papers and you'll be completely fine.
She's an amazing prof. Tests and papers are pretty straightforward, make sure to study her ppt notes.

Super enthusiastic professor, interesting lectures and engaging materials like case studies or videos. Often gave the whole class 100% on quizzes. Good to do your reading, but not essential--her tests are almost identical to the slide sets she posts online.

Amazing professor. great class with manageable workload. Readings interesting. Canvas page is very clear and organized. No exam. 3 analytical essays and final short essay. Grading is fair with good feedback. One of the kindest professors I've had. She really cares about her students. She makes class interactive. Read, go to class, you will do great

Muslim Women throughout the ages was one of my favorite classes I've taken at duke. She really tries to make the readings managable and is understanding that not all readings get done but she selected a great set of readings that are engaging and fun. Easy to work with and not a super hard course if you show up and try

I enjoyed this class so much and it was because of this professor. She was dedicated to making sure every class we were learning not just from her, but from each other. She was helpful in breaking down certain concepts and challenged us to think critically about each readings. She was passionate understanding, kind, and overall great professor
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Had a small class but really enjoyed our conversations, definitely learned a lot and would take again if I could.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This was one of my favorite classes I've taken at Duke. The professor was engaging and genuinely passionate about each topic, and opened my eyes to so many things and perspectives I never would have considered otherwise. I would and have recommended this professor to friends and think that my worldview genuinely changed after taking it.
We would just chat, she told us nothing, then papers with zero feedback. Learned nothing. Highly do not recommend taking this class.

I took 3 classes w/ Prof. Hassan. She is so engaged! She discusses reading material with students like they are respected colleagues, & will stop everything to explain material if that is what even a single student needs. She chooses readings with care so the class is productive for the students. Top tier teaching, I learned so much from her!
She only lectures then has a final paper. We had to turn in summaries of the reading which she never read or responded to. She never replied to emails and I never got feedback on my final paper.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Honestly don't recommend taking a class with her. She's not responsive to emails and unaccessible outside of class. She is also unclear about grading criteria and you are kind of left in the dark about your grade until the end of the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Lectures were extremely boring, doesn't put any grades into the grade book throughout the semester, grades based on others in the class. Not a good class to take in my opinion

Honestly highly disliked this class & Dr.
Hassan.She's extremely lecture heavy which made it really boring. She grades by how much she likes you on a scale of everyone in class. She rarely responds to emails and doesn't like when students ask opposing questions. With the 2 papers every week for the entire semester, it isn't worth it. Pls don't take
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Mona Hassan is a very knowledgable and caring professor. We had discussions once a week, either online or in the gardens. We were expected to write a 2 page reading reflection and a 1 page video reflection every week. There was a lot of material and it was difficult to keep up, but she is very accommodating. Discussions were fun and insightful.
Dr. Hassan is a wonderful professor who is very knowledgeable and passionate about the subject material.
Unclear on expectations sometimes. Expects attendance and shows bias against students who don't show up. However, she is very knowledgeable and a good lecturer, so class time isn't too bad.

Prof Marvian was nice but made the class significantly harder than it should have been. It felt like the tests were much harder than the HWs and the HWs were already big chunks of time. 1 HW before the midterm and 3 after. Participation is an implicit part of your grade and going to lecture is important as it is very easy to fall behind.

Prof. Marvian is knowledgeable and explains the subject clearly. The course is difficult but he is passionate about the material. The grading was fair. Assignment is your chance to improve your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Lecture material is explained poorly and doesn't show up in homework or test problems. Extremely unaccommodating of student availability and rarely offers help outside of class. Never walks through test problems or material in class and doesn't provide helpful practice material. Encourages students to ask questions but can't properly address them.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Shows up late to class. Lectures often did not correspond to homework or test questions. Provided practice exams incomparable to the actual test and was reluctant to give solutions. The actual exam solutions he did give were just copies of a student's test. Not accomodating of student availability out of class. Lab is a nightmare but not his fault.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Professor Marvian tries, he really does. He explains concepts simply and intuitively. Then he works example calculations and everything stops making sense, even though the ideas are still simple. READ THE TEXTBOOK for equations. Still go to lecture, as the class goes from 0-100 in the last third. He doesn't understand what is and isn't easy
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Marvian is very caring and lenient in terms of grading. He cares about understanding more than just doing well in the class. Very great theorist, lectures are very organized and he hand writes everything so that it's easier to follow for note-takers. Definitely learnt a lot in this class!

I like class discussion, so this was perfect for me. Students who don't like coming to class and those who are more quiet found it more challenging. Also, he will cut off students who drone on, which I appreciated.
Amazing class. So glad I took something out of my comfort zone. I wish Prof. Hoffman had more time for individual office hours but his feedback was very helpful.
One of the best professors at Duke. He is in high demand, but if you go to his group office hours you will have a great experience.

Always interrupts students. Does not make the classroom feel like a safe environment. Offers regrade opportunities for certain assignments, but will give you the same grade a lot of the time so its basically a waste of time and effort.

All of the public policy core courses need revision. There was a significant lack of structure in this class, and his busy schedule resulted in many students having to sacrifice their own time to meet his needs.

Loved this class. If you do the extra credit, take advantage of memo rewrites and give your presentation a second time, then it is a lot of work but also very easy to get an A in the class. Students who didn't put in the work early in the semester had a tough time, so be ready to knock out memo rewrites early to leave time for your final project.

Class is a 45+ person discussion, and everyone has to contribute. Four assignments make up your entire grade (each one out of 4.0, but only with 0, 3.0, 3.5, and 4.0, so basically each assignment would round to either an F, B, A-, or A+) with a super unclear rubric. Made me want to drop PubPol tbh

Really great prof. Super engaging and very thought-provoking class. Participation/engagement matters a LOT so do not take this class if you are unprepared to discuss and share to a class of 45+ people.

Hoffman is a great professor that truly cares about his students. The grading criteria in this class is very clear, and you are given multiple opportunities to redo presentations and memos. Participation and attendance are important, but if you actively engage with the class discussions and content, you will be successful.

The grading is not difficult, but this was a very hard class for me. It was hard because it made me question the assumptions about myself as I explored how my personal notions of justice differed from my classmates. Talking about those issues was very challenging for me, but it really paid off. I am glad this is required for public policy majors.

I had a number of difficult things going on last Spring and Prof. Hoffman took great interest in helping me and providing me with flexibility. He even followed up during the Summer to see how I was doing. My favorite Professor at Duke.

Tough but fair and caring was my experience. This was the only class I had at Duke where I had to stand up and give a 15 minute presentation. I hated it, but have now used what it taught me in my job after Duke. You will have to do uncomfortable things for Prof. Hoffman's classes, but they are all focused on helping you think, write and speak well.
Lots of moving pieces in this class to keep track of, but the capstone and the interactive classes are worth it if you are organized.

I appreciated the ability to rewrite the memo twice and the detailed feedback as I am a comp sci major and had never written a public policy document. There were also detailed instructional materials and a fairly useful rubric.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I loved being able to choose my own capstone project and work on climate issues with AI data centers. Attending class is not my favorite thing and we don't have to do that much in compsci but the discussion format made it less boring.

I had a rough semester and really appreciated how flexible Prof. Hoffman was to design different assignments while I was experiencing a significant family issue. He really cares about his students as long as you make an effort.
Cybersecurity and health data policy was a great seminar. I loved how Prof. Hoffman and Prof. Tucker taught together with very different styles. I just wish there were more office hours sessions.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: My favorite class at Duke!!!!!

Professor Hoffman is an incredible professor. He provides really insightful guidance on making life and career decisions and is always eager to serve as a mentor to students. The work that he does at Duke and his past experience is invaluable and fascinating for anyone interested in tech strategy/tech policy.

This class was very stressful to me. Participation matters A LOT no flexibility around and it was difficult for ppl that are introverted to try to speak among the 20 hands raised in a 40 ppl class. Very HIGH expectations of work, the criteria was well laid out but took points off on more extended stuff. Inspiring but traumatizing.
Prof. Hoffman is very clear about what he wants. Follow the rubrics and listen to his feedback and you will get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Hoffman was available to walk around campus with me several times to talk about both my capstone project and give career advice. He has continued to do that after the class ended and been an amazing mentor even though he is very busy.if you take this class defintely take advantage of office hours and getting to know him better.
My favorite class at Duke. Not for everybody, especially if you don't want to put in the work, but I thought it was great.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This class was so much fun. I really enjoyed the way music was integrated into the topic and how we were given time in small groups to get to know the other students in the class. Fantastic experience.

Easy to get an A in this class if you go to office hours and listen to the advice from Prof. Hoffman and the TAs. Prof. Hoffman has a real thing about participating in class, and you can get on his bad side if you don't engage or you don't follow the format for the assignments. But if you do, it is a lot of fun.

This class changed the way I think. It was difficult at times because the class discussions would move fast but the way Prof. Hoffman shaped the material and moderated conversations caused us to truly consider multiple perspectives and question our assumptions while not sliding into moral relativism. Great class!

I was a bit hesitant jumping into class discussions at first because the class environment can be a bit intense with ~35 students participating in a seminar style class. Nonetheless, Prof Hoffman was incredibly caring and accessible outside of class to help with assignments and any career or academic concerns. Definitely recommend 302 with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He clearly has his favorite students. Some students dominate discussions, often with his support. While the course is well-structured, he seems intent on guiding students toward specific answers, making discussions less open. Unlike most professors who value strong arguments, he seems to grade based on whether your answers match his expectations.

This was a tough class for me. It requires students to look at issues like abortion and the genocide in Palestine from multiple perspectives and different ethical frameworks. At first I disliked having to voice positions I did not agree with. However, over time I appreciated how important it was to see the issues from a different ethical framework.
I wish the class had been a bit smaller, but really like the opportunity to explore tough issues from multiple perspectives. The music to start class was fun.
I learned very much in this class but it is hard if English is not your first language as you have to write and speak in English for a top grade. The chance of rewriting memos really helped me.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--So many papers

reviews.comment: Loved this class and really appreciated Prof. Hoffman being supportive of me being a student athlete.

My favorite non-CS class at Duke. Allowed me to apply what I am learning in computer science. I don't think I want to code forever, so it was fun to see all the things I may be able to do later in technology policy. Class was a bit bigger than I had hoped. I hope Prof. Hoffman caps enrollment lower when he teaches it again.

I would have liked clearer rubrics for the presentation and memo. That being said, I really like the substantive content and the discussion format for the class. Prof. Hoffman went out of his way to get to know me and relate what I care about to the class. That is different from most computer science classes and a great way to finish senior year.
What a fun class. Loved the group projects and the meetings in office hours.
TAKE ANY CLASS WITH HIM. He is very knowledgeable and a fair grader. The classes are very worthwhile
Prof. Hoffman really cares about his students. He was very flexible and met with me several times to help me through a difficult period. I loved this class.
Really appreciated how flexible Prof. Hoffman was while I was going through a difficult time. It was clear he genuinely cared about me and my health and made lots of time to talk outside of class.

Prof. Hoffman is a quirky guy who is really into music, Duke basketball and technology. He went to a lot of effort to make everyone feel included in the class and to get to know us, including taking walks across campus, which I really appreciated.Take this class!

Loved the format with lots of different guest speakers and how Prof. Hoffman made himself available for such a large class. Really liked hearing the practical examples that came from real world law practice.

My favorite law school class so far. Profs. Hoffman and Stansbury really went out of their way to try to make a big survey class fun. The guest lectures were amazing (Kashmir Hill and Prof. Dellinger, you are my heroes).

I was surprised when we spent time listening to Guns and Roses, Mozart and Kendrick Lamar in class, but it usually worked. I wish there hadn't been so much focus on having to speak in class, , but all things considered this was a fantastic class and I really liked how much focus there was on building community among the students in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Loved this class. Truly made me think differently and see issues from multiple perspectives. Prof. Hoffman got to know everyone in class and was very flexible. Awesome experience.

I was skeptical at first as we spent too much time on the ethics of grading and reading dead white philosophers, but Prof. Hoffman listened to feedback and adjusted midway to give students more agency. Great class. I learned a lot and really appreciated the amount of time given to creating community.

Really liked this rather odd class. It is an overview of lots of different tech law and policy classes with many professors teaching their discipline. I wish the class had been smaller, but I really appreciated Ptof. Hoffman having group office hours and getting to know me outside of class. If you are interested in tech policy definitely take this.
Really like this survey class with lots of guest speakers and how Prof. Hoffman brought in his professional experience and connections to the class.
Fantastic class. Loved incorporating music as a way to explore important ethical issues. Great use of small group exercises. Really made me think about why I feel the way I do about things.
Really appreciated ability to rewrite my memo for a higher grade and to incorporate feedback. Wish more time had been available in office hours.
Great survey class of cyber law topics. I was able to have a couple office hours appointments and it helped me plan out how to spend the last year of my law school experience.

A cool and relatively easy survey class for grad students with lots of guest lectures by other Tech Law and Policy Professors at Duke. Glad I took this in my first semester as a grad student so I could know what else I wanted to take and to get an overview of privacy and cybersecurity law.
Loved his Cybersecurity and National Security Policy class and he was very helpful in talking with me about what I want to do professionally.
Health Data Policy was my favorite class at Duke and helped me decide what I want to do with my career. I loved that it was team taught and that I got to pick a capstone project that I cared about.
Awesome class!!!! Really appreciated walking office hours and connecting my capstone project to my interests.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: My favorite Duke class. Professor Hoffman focuses on creating community in the class and encouraging diverse perspectives on the material. He encouraged us all to understand practical policy solutions and how those link to our values instead of just teaching academic theory. Working on my capstone project as a group project was a highlight.

I took Cybersecurity and Health Data Policy with Prof. Hoffman and Prof. Campbell Tucker. It was my favorite class I have taken at Duke. The two professors complimented each other well as Prof. Hoffman has lots of experience with technology and Prof. Tucker really understands clinical healthcare delivery. The class was demanding, but really fun!
Fantastic professor who always went out of his way to meet with me and my classmates outside of class. You can get the grade you want if you put in the work.
The busiest professor at Sanford. Not easily accessible outside class. Very inflexible with deadlines. Tough grader. Coursework can get fairly technical.

An interesting class at it combines undergrads, law students and graduate students with lots of break out exercises to allow the class to get to know each other. I really like the focus on discussion instead of lectures.

Not a tough class, but lots of work with quite a bit of material. However, he reduced some of the work in the middle of the semester after taking a poll of the class. The material is interesting and the guest speakers were amazing,

One of my favorite classes at Duke. I loved how Prof. Hoffman took a survey of the class before the semester started to learn more about us and then met with me several times to talk about how the class could help with my career interests. I had to put in lots of time to get an A in the class, especially rewriting my memo, but in the end worth it.

I took Prof. Hoffman's Intro to Cyber Policy class and then he agreed to be my thesis advisor. I also joined his research team and really enjoyed working with the other students on the team. He does everything he can to be available outside of class and to provide input. He has been a huge part of why I have loved going to Duke.

Professor Hoffman has tons of energy for technology policy. I took his cybersecurity and health data policy class and loved the examinations of both how technology can save lives but also how it can negatively impact people. You need to participate in class to do well, so the classes are not for people who just like to sit in the back and be quiet.

I will go against the flow here. I DID NOT enjoy Professor Hoffman's class. The theoretical foundations of his class are weak, at best. Little background is provided on the foundational concepts of Cybersecurity...you feel lost in jargon very soon. He has a liking towards students who kowtow him - take his class only for his industry connections.
Best Professor I've had at Duke! Prof Hoffman's real world experience makes this class extremely rewarding. He cares a lot...take advantage of times to get to know him outside of class!

I scheduled office hours and that made a big difference. This class is taught from a real world perspective on what it takes to influence policy. I enjoyed the discussion and the stories based on practical experience. I am not sure how effective the online discussions were as many students posted high level comments to try to show participation.

Intro to Cyber Policy is a great class if you are interested in engaging in cybersecurity and privacy issues from multiple perspectives. Prof. Hoffman does not lecture and instead guides class discussion. You have to go to class and show up on time. I wish we would have talked about social media more, but the rest of the material was interesting.

I had never written a policy memo before so I liked that we could rewrite it every week based on the feedback given and then count the highest grade. I really feel that that along with meeting with Prof. Hoffman in office hours helped me learn how to write the memo. It was a great semester.

The material is great and Prof. Hoffman's approach is to have students give presentations and then lead class discussion. You need to participate in class and in the online discussion if you want to do well in this class. It was one of my favorite classes at Duke. I really liked being able to pick my own capstone project topic and format.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: You have to work for this class, but grading is straight forward and the material is interesting. I appreciated the transparency on the grading and the ability to pick my own capstone topic. Prof. Hoffman also helped me get an internship.

I took advantage of office hours appointments and that really helped with my writing. I loved the class especially when we would get in discussions about the multiple views on issues. Prof. Hoffman shares lots of stories about his time in the tech industry, which made the material practical.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I took Cybersecurity and National Security Policy. I was worried at first as I do not have any technical knowledge, but Prof. Hoffman made sure that was not an issue. He focuses on giving a ton of feedback on the policy memo assignment with the goal of learning how to write a memo like how it is done in the government and companies. Great class!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Cybersecurity and National Security Law and Policy is my favorite class I have taken at Duke. It was a blend of law, public policy graduate students and undergraduates. I was worried at first that I would not have enough technical knowledge but that did not matter. Prof. Hoffman sees his role in leading students in discussion. Amazing class!
I loved this class especially the focus of the impact on cyber issues on poc. Prof. Hoffman was also really helpful talking with me about my career

Professor Hoffman focuses on creating engagement in discussion in class on interesting issues that are very current. At first I was concerned that I would not have enough technical background for his Cybersecurity and National Security Policy class, but that was not an issue. He also spent lots of time talking with me about potential internships.

Professor Hoffman is my favorite professor yet. He is super caring and makes sure to get to know each student and their aspirations. The class is really interesting because he brings in visitng scholars every week, and the workload isn't too heavy. Mostly structured around a Capstone project of your choosing. LEGEND
He is always able to explain algebra concepts in the way that every student can understand it.
He is always able to explain algebra concepts in the way that every students can understand it.

He is such a great professor. He leads me to understand the beauty in the algebra and he was super caring and kind. I couldn't express how much his advice and his inspirational words mean to me. Sad that he will leave DKU after this semester. Wish all the best for him in the future. Thank you Professor Simonelli.
perfect and kind
extremely fast paced, hard to keep up with during lectures unless you already know the topic at a deep level, barely gives partial credit on exams
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I really like him. He is such a mentor to me. You can always reach him outside class. He is so caring and I like him sooooo much!

He provides very clear explanations and genuinely cares about his students. If you are willing to go to his office hours to learn and master the material, rather than just focusing on grades, he is more than willing to help you. He is kind-hearted and very approachable. I highly recommend him!
would never take this class with him if literally any other professor was offering it
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is an amazing professor. He cares about every individual and always willing to help. He interacts with students very often in class to suit our needs. So patient with every single question. One of my regret is not going to his office hour very often. He provides clear lecture notes during class, and explain every concept in detail.
The professor is real kind and caring. He gives us the proper grade for a reason, but he has difficult exams.

One of the most caring Professors you'll meet, he really gives all his effort in trying to teach you the concepts and will walk you through it step by step. Also is a very understanding and empathetic Professor.

He is friendly and you can find him frequently around the campus. He is one of my favorite professors. Although I did not so well on his MATH 205, I did quite well on MATH 201 that he taught. MATH 205 is a hard and fast-paced course, and it's recommended to take MATH 206 since MATH 206 removed the calculus part and allows you to dig deeper.

Exams are heavily weighted (70%) and he doesn't curve or give extra credit assignments. MATH205 is unreasonably fast-paced but it's not any of the professors' faults. But Simonelli is extremely caring and loves it when students ask questions, so go to his office hours and ask for help whenever possible! Would recommend him but NOT the course.
Great

The class was demanding and hard, professor Simonelli was EXTREMELY CARING with internationals. He organized special meetings and actively sought us. That said, I highly recommend his 200 classes to sophomores, not freshmen. He requires a thorough understanding of the material which is easier if you have more knowledge to integrate.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Math 201 by Prof. Simonelli is one of the toughest things I had to do. Don't expect any extra credit or a curve. Exams are very challenging and limited in time which makes it almost impossible to pass. I never got constructive and helpful feedback both for hw and exams (70% of the grade is exams). He has a really strong accent which makes it reall
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I didn't know what I signed up for before it was already too late. For somebody how's taking MATH205 straight after 101, this class was very challenging. However, Prof. Simonelli is very kind and caring. He always responds promptly to emails and is just generally a nice person to talk to. If I ever have to take math, it would be his class for sure
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: During Covid-19 no professor has been more caring, accessible, and hardworking as Prof Simonelli. Although his lectures are a little disorganized and rushed, he always corrected his flaws with funny examples and very generous grading. I really felt like he wanted his students to succeed and was always kind when responding to emails.

Great guy and means well, accessible outside of class and goes the extra mile to help students. Only downside is that he lectures too slowly and is sometimes overly kind to the point that students could be pushed more than they are. Would still take again though
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Khan is a fine person and relatively fun as a lecturer. However, he simply cannot properly teach the topic. He is very passionate about stats but does not have the teaching chops to convey probability in an easy to understand way. Moreover, exams are quant-like and difficult to study for. Do not take this class if you dislike probability.

Prof. Khan is the best ! He crafts his notes and explains them very clearly. Questions are very well answered in class. If you have additional questions, he also helps during office hours and is very accessible for anything related to the course, or grading. He is great at teaching and very understanding ! Has great humor as well.

This professor would pick on certain students and would treat students differently based on skill level. Did not try to help students, just assigned work and left them on their own. Would not recommend taking his courses.
He is so kind but the class is SO hard. Everyone gets bad grades on all the assessments except a couple people in the class. I don't know how this is an intro level class.
Ian is awesome, he cares about all his students and will go above and beyond to help everyone succeed. If you have the opportunity to take a class with him, don't pass it up.

Hard to judge from this semester - she had family emergencies all throughout the semester which clearly took up a huge chunk of her time. Overall, after the class, I feel like i definitely devloped my scholarly reading and writing skills from the work she gave. Every assignment was given a 100 at the very end of the semester.

Dr. Ishmael is very kind, but her class is a mess. Lectures seemed entirely spontaneous, the class was very poorly paced, and some assignments had nonsensical AI-generated prompts. No grades were given until December, when almost everyone received 100% on everything with no comments. I firmly believe she did not read a word of our writing.

Nice and well-intentioned person, but super disorganized. Frequently late to class, boring rambling lectures (clearly was no lesson plan), often let out late, etc. I learned very little from this class. It's not challenging by any means but also not interesting whatsoever. Writing assignments are relatively simple & grades all returned in December.

Took public speaking with her. She will be very forward with feedback, not in an inherently negative way but instead to just actually help you. DO NOT BE LATE. YOU MUST BE TIMELY. Absolutely loved the class.
easy a but you don't learn anything and the professor has really unclear grading rubric so you lowkey might not even get that easy a...
sat on this class and still learned absolutely nothing. honestly ruined first semester at uni with unclear grading rubric. i didn't pay 90k a year for this quality of teaching...

If you're not one of her favorites, FORGET IT. She kept asking us to write her positive reviews...for what? Here's one: biased, abrasive, unavailable outside of class, unclear grader, and doesn't even follow her own advice. Take a look at her speeches online. She's not good enough to be waxing poetry about herself.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: literally never heard a good thing about her outside of those who want to get an easy a but 90k for an easy a is a hard bargain that i don't think is worth it tbh

Great exposure to public speaking. Dr. Byerly is very personable and funny, but can be a little intimidating at first. Has clear favorites, but doesn't treat anyone badly. You don't always get direct, immediate feedback. Overall chill workload outside of class and fun class to take.

Byerly is a character. Bad: inaccessible out of class, picks favorites, abrasive, unclear grader. Good: knowledgeable, funny, cares about students, provides feedback, unique teaching. She is a tough critic, which is GOOD for a public speaking class! You'll be ok if you can take the heat. Everyone gets an A - student speeches absorb most class time.

Beneficial course to strengthen communication skills, not major specific. Workload is manageable when prepared ahead of time. Confidence with public speaking will make assignment preparation more natural. Expect honest critiques of work than will improve speaking confidence and skill if you consider them with an open mind. Would take again!

In Dr. Byerly's Public Speaking class, you get to present a different piece or kind of speech every single class and receive feedbacks. She builds a very welcoming and intimate environment for her students, and we are truly inspired and learned a lot from each other. Workload is very manageable if you don't procrastinate.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Byerly's class is very engaging and thorough in terms of public speaking. She also manages to make it a 'life skills' class which is useful for professional and personal goals.
Thoroughly enjoyed. Not helpful for basically any major, but a “life skills” class that you'll be glad you took.

I like the context of her class and teachings. Unfortunately, this we discovered that she operates with a degree of unprofessionalism. Couple of instances where students came to her with personal matters and regarding grades, attendance, etc, and she ended up sharing personal info with other students, embarrassing students in class.

Professor Byerly's class was a transformative experience. Her teaching style and feedback pushed me to grow as a speaker and person. While workload is manageable, getting an A requires going the extra mile. Unstuckstudy was a helpful study tool.
Gives easy a's but didn't learn anything at all

Was not accessible outside of class and never responded to emails. Made uncomfortable statements towards POC classmates. Entire course graded on final portfolio with unclear rubric. Feel free to watch her TedTalk. She's not good enough to be waxing poetry about herself.

Dr. Byerly is hilarious and personable, though her tough-love approach can be startling at first. Slightly intimidating at first (especially for inexperienced speakers), but Byerly genuinely cares about students' growth and success. Graded based on effort and class contribution – not speeches. I wish that everyone at Duke had to take this class.

This class is SO OVERHYPED. She's a nice lady who likes to talk a lot about how she's from South Africa. There is no structure—every class has back-to-back speeches that you have to prepare for. You don't know your grade at all until the very end. I can't say I've gained any skills from this class. It's basically a nice fluff class for seniors.

As someone without a public speaking background, I found this class super intimidating esp because your classmates come from varying levels of experience and Dr Byerly doesn't sugarcoat at all. BUT, you will learn A LOT from her, the speaking exercises & from your classmates. She is great- inspirational and funny, and truly cares about her students

Uses a blunt tough-love approach to feedback, incl. mid-speech interruptions. Although there were tears in the 1st week, we all grew exponentially. Once you accept her bizarre method of instruction, she's a hilarious person who cultivates an ideal environment for skill development. Light workload: 3-4 hours of assignments&presentation prep / week.

Byerly's class is very intimidating if you do not have experience in public speaking. I always got anxiety walking into her class because I knew I would have to present a speech, whether I was prepared or not. She is very charismatic and her lectures are soley story-telling. The TedX was very stressful but taught me how to public speak.

I absolutely loved Professor Byerly and wish that I could take her class all over again. I have never learned so much from a course. She is absolutely hilarious and cares a great deal about her students, so lecture is always a joy. Her class was a comfortable space for honest feedback and experimentation, and you will learn so much about yourself.

Do not take this class if you're ONLY interested in improving public speaking. Even though it helps with that, Prof. Byerly gives students valuable tools for their academic life at Duke and beyond. With the fantastic community she fosters in the classroom, this class offers lots of opportunities to grow as a student.

There were moments in the class when I disagreed with Professor Byerly's remarks and methods, but her feedback is thorough, tough, and public, and it helped me develop as a speaker and a person. If you are afraid of that type of environment, you should be the one taking this class. It was easily one of my favorite classes during my time here.

I think this class is overhyped. While it's an opportunity to get speaking experience in a collaborative setting, I didn't learn much/leave with many tangible skills. While workload is easy, it is stated that few students get an A, so be warned. You have to go the extra mile in every aspect of the class to do so. Grading criteria not super clear
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Byerly was a great professor and I was glad to have her be one of my first classes at Duke. In the public speaking course I started out nervous but I learned a lot about myself and my classmates along the way. Make sure to put in the work and show up to class and you should do well.

This was absolutely my favorite class at Duke! Professor Byerly not only teaches us how to speak but creates a community within the class. I learned how to listen to the people around me, got inspired by their stories, and truly made meaningful friendships. Taking this class before graduating is a must!!!

Dr. Byerly gives really clear & tangible advice, whether it's about posture when speaking or how to take notes. The class is not what you might normally expect but she'll walk you through it. She WILL push you out of your comfort zone but you will come out a better and more mature person. I can't exaggerate the growth I experienced with her.

Amazing class. Can't say enough great things about Prof. Byerly. Even over Zoom, the skills learned really enhanced my Public Speaking ability. It's a challenging class, but you get so much out of it. 10/10.

I enjoyed the course, but I will say I do not think I gained that many skills to actually be better at public speaking. It felt like more a storytelling class than anything. There was no grade breakdown in the syllabus, so I wished Prof Byerly included that because it's good teaching pedagogy and it helps students understand their final grade

Professor Byerly is amazing and her class was one of the best I've taken at Duke. If you are a senior looking for a class to end your career at Duke with, you should really consider taking this one with Professor Byerly. You'll learn so much and be inspired

Professor Byerly was wonderful and I learned so much from public speaking. She was always willing to meet offline to practice, which was much appreciated. I loved the open and welcoming environment of the class and I can't wait to implement the skills I learned!

After trying trying for 3 times, I am very grateful that I was able to finally enroll in this class during my final semester at Duke. I learned much more than just specific techniques on public speaking - I discovered interesting things about myself as a person, and I managed to take away invaluable advice on how to approach life after graduation.

If you are looking for a sign to take this class: here it is. Simply the best class I've ever taken at Duke. This class makes the tuition worth it. Totally changed my life. Professor Byerly has a grasp on the world like no one I've ever met.

I took this professor on Semester at Sea. I learned things I did not realize I was unaware of. She was a great teacher and I could tell from how she talked about her teaching at Duke. Definitely would recommend taking this professor.

Dr. Byerly is a Duke legend. While the course is called Public Speaking, that is only the beginning of what you learn. The course forces you out of your comfort zone and gives you moments of deep reflection and introspection. This is the perfect course for seniors about to leave Duke and begin a new phase of life.

This is the best class I've taken at Duke, and its all because of Professor Byerly. She only gives assignments that are applicable to real life (ex: introducing someone at an event, presenting information in a board meeting, ted talks, and even eulogies). The class bonds so well, so you have to be open to sharing personal stories. 10/10.

Ingrid Byerly is the best teacher Ive ever had at Duke University. Im so incredibly grateful that I managed to get off the waitlist for her public speaking course. Shes an amazing soul who makes learning fun again. Pro tip: If you have the chance, take the Spring Breakthrough course with Ingrid as well. Its now one of my favorite memories.

I took this professor on Semester at Sea and she made my voyage incredible. Her lectures are engaging and interesting and are paired with relevant class discussion to enhance the class materials. It also helps that Dr. Byerly is quite hilarious and passionate. I 100% recommend taking her course.

I had professor Byerly for a Music course I took on a study abroad program, Semester at Sea. Professory Byerly is likely to be in the top 5 professors I have ever had. The genuine respect and care she has for her students shines through, and the way she teaches is perfectly enthusiastic for the classroom. 10/10: would take any class of hers.
I took her Music class on semester at sea - such an amazing teacher and I learned so much. I highly recommend taking any of her classes, great teacher and a great person.

As a graduating senior, I was lucky enough to snag the coveted 20th and final spot in Prof. Byerly's Spring 2019 Public Speaking class. Safe to say that I hit the jackpot. Truly one of the rare courses that visibly and tangibly evokes the best in each student in a way that no textbook or exam can. You'll walk out a better speaker, a better person.

Theres a reason that prof Byerlys classes are impossible to get in to. Shes the best professor at Duke and its literally not even close. She is brilliant, and you will walk out of class every week feeling like you accomplished something. Take this class, take this class, take. this. class.
One of the best class I have taken at Duke. Transformative experience. If I only take away one thing from my four years this class would be it. Take it!

Professor Byerly is truly one of a kind. She has a wealth of knowledge from her experiences around the globe that she readily shares. I learned more about life from her than any other professor. She has a passion for teaching, public speaking and music, all of which shine through in her genial personality. I would take her class 100x over. Love her

A fantastic professor who provides a lot of great feedback and insight. She created a wonderful learning environment where students supported each other and where we learned a lot from our classmates. She's encouraging and caring - two qualities that made her public speaking class so enjoyable. Her constructive criticism has improved my confidence!
Easily one of the best professors I've had at Duke. Would strongly recommend. You get what you put into the class and most of your grade is based on the portfolio and your participation in lectures.

Professor Byerly is a true educator. She really cares about her students and expects them to reciprocate her effort with their own. On the last day of class, she handed out a letter detailing why she doesn't give many As so make sure that you really work for it. Overall incredible experience.

Professor Byerly's freshman seminar is the type of course where you get out what you put in. The workload is small, but class discussions are enjoyable if you participate. Byerly really just wants you to show some effort and try to engage with the material. Class is not very structured and sometimes a bit slow, but overall pretty chill.

This is an amazing class. Treat it as a chance to experiment. If you're new to public speaking or aren't very confident in your ability, this will come easy. If you're already a good public speaker, learn from the different styles everyone else brings to the table. Your grade is mostly based on your portfolio, so put some effort into it.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Amazing class if you're a bad public speaker, but if you're already solid you won't improve much. An A is not guaranteed

Professor Byerly is fantastic. Her public speaking class is one of the most practical classes out there, and she assigns very valuable exercises to help you improve. She gives a lot of feedback and is so sweet all the time. I would highly recommend taking any of her classes.
Highly recommend for anyone who loves music and would like a low key class and does not mind little class structure.

Professor Byerly is awesome. She assigns a decent amount of reading but when you do the reading and other assigned homework is up to you - it's very flexible. This class is also good for someone who is terrified of public speaking - most of us (including myself) were to some extent. Great class.

As a second semester senior, I can say that Professor Byerly's public speaking class was easily the best class I have taken at Duke. I LOOKED FORWARD to class every Thursday. I learned about public speaking but I also learned even more about "life advice/lessons." This is a MUST. If you graduate from Duke without taking her class, you'll miss out!

I absolutely loved this class. Professor Byerly is one of the best professors I've ever had at Duke. She makes you want to go to class and as long as you show up and do the work that she expects, you will do well in the class. You'll find that you want to do well in the class just for your own benefit and not for the grade. She is amazing!

Professor Byerly is the most engaging and inspiring professor I've ever had at Duke. She was able to create such a comfortable class environment--which was incredibly necessary in a public speaking class. Her assignments were actually enjoyable and I looked forward going to class every week.
This was the best class I have ever taken, and Ingrid Byerly is the best teacher I have ever had.

You really didn't have to do anything for this class except the final project. It taught me less about the finesse of public speaking and more how to speak on the fly, which is useful I guess. Super easy class.

Dr. Byerly is incredible. Her class will challenge and help you grow, which will be super apparent at the end of the semester.  She truly cares about her students and will share all her wisdom and experience. By far my favorite class and favorite professor at Duke.
Most fun I had have with Professor Byerly's public speaking course. You will leave with confidence and a bunch of amazing stories. Recommend everyone take this class before graduating.

Professor Byerly is one of the best teachers I have ever had. She has had amazing life experiences that make the class so interesting, and we do a wide variety of things in this class that improve your overall skills for college. She is so kind, and also very funny. I highly recommend this course, or any class with her!
She was amazing! This is an awesome class to take. Everybody should take this class. Mrs. Byerly gives great feedback and helps you be the best public speaker you can be.
Participation based class

Professor Byerly was probably the most engaging lecturer I had at Duke. She's not just an amazing professor but an amazing person, giving great feedback, fantastic advice, and amusing thoughts. If you will, imagine weekly lectures as engaging and as invigorating as a TED Talks with as many takeaways and that's this class.
Professor Byerly is one the most enthusiastic, warmest people I have ever met.  She makes lectures endlessly enjoyable and teaches you a lot about public speaking and life.

I took this class to challenge myself in terms of Public Speaking and it was worth the it. Prof. Byerly makes the class such a wonderful experience that every moment in the class in full of fun. I highly recommend this class to everyone.

She was honestly the most incredible professor I had Freshman year. She inspires you to think about certain topics far differently then you ever would. She also allowed me to grown in confidence far more. I can not express how much I loved this class enough.

Took her "Advocacy for Change" as a FOCUS class. She's a great professor. She really cares about your experience in her class. She knows a lot about public speaking and has amazing global experiences.

In the first few classes, you might not think you're learning anything but you definitely are. Prof. Byerly is not only one of the most amazing professors, she's one of the most amazing people I've every had the privilege of knowing. She is so positive and inspirational it would be a shame to go through life not knowing her.

Amazing teacher with great experiences to share! She makes the transition to college level classes a lot smoother due to the fact that she really cares for each one of her students, no matter what kind of learning experience you had before.

I love Ingrid! She makes class entertaining which can be hard in a 2.5 hour class that starts at 6:15pm. She definitely helped with my public speaking skills. If you show up and participate, you'll be fine. Not much out of class work until it comes to the final project. I would definitely take another class with her!

Helped me get through my first semester! Took Music as a Mirror and loved it despite knowing very little about music. Professor Byerly is a sweetheart and is very invested in your success. It was very refreshing compared to other lecture classes where I felt like simply a face in the room. Plus, no tests and no essays. However, very educational.
Her class was intellectually pleasant by making me think outside the box. Also, she was excellent in encouraging students to participate positively.

Took this class while at Semester at Sea and Prof. Byerly was amazing! I was not a big music person, but she taught me so much throughout the semester and made me love the culture of music. She makes her class just difficult enough. Not too hard that you'll be bored, but not impossible or difficult to receive an A at all. Amazing and funny Prof.

Ingrid is one of the most interesting, charismatic, and genuinely down to earth professors I have gotten to know here at Duke. She is willing to help you when you demand it, and  will unilaterally work with you to ensure that you meet your goals. I am immensely grateful to have had the opportunity to work with her and wish her great success.

From her class, public speaking, I have not only learned many empirical knowledge and skills, but also got confidence. I also found that she is so professional in encouraging students to realize their strengths and weaknesses. I am certain that her class makes me to be better than before. I really appreciate her teaching.
I took this course on Semester at Sea and nominated Byerly for best professor, as she had the most significant impact on the ways in which I take in my surroundings, especially aurally.

Professor Byerly was by far the most incredible professor I've ever had in my life. Her class was interesting, hands-on, and truly meaningful. Professor Byerly's passion for her work and her students is evident in every lecture, and this class would benefit any student (regardless of their knowledge of/experience with any type of music).
Prof. Byerly's actual interest in the material made the class worth attending.  Her humor (and not mention accent!) always kept attention in lectures.

Prof Byerly was easily my favorite teacher in college. She was very knowledgable and passionate about her teaching. She made class interesting and fun. Rather than just keeping to a textbook, we explored different ways to interpret class material and be engaged inside the classroom and out. I loved her class and her teaching style!

Professor Byerly was THE best professor on SAS. She makes each class fun & different. She doesn't want students memorizing definitions so there's not much textbook use. She's about listening and interpreting music in your own way. She's enthusiastic and extremely knowledgable about the subject. TAKE HER CLASS! She's the best teacher I'll ever have!

She is an AMAZING professor who is super passionate about her field. You can learn way more than cultural anthropology from her. She is also a very nice and approachable person. It is relatively easy to get a good grade and the workload is totally manageable. I would definitely recommend her taking her class!

By far the best prof I had at Duke. Took her class freshman year. Really teaches students to think for themselves and how to integrate their passions with their studies/career goals. Knows a lot about music, if you take her class you will forever listen differently. She knows Dave Matthews. Take any and every class she teaches.

I took Ingrid's "Breaking Sound Barriers" FOCUS class and it is absolutely the best class I have ever taken. I love music, but her class opened me up to so more much than that. Ingrid is wise above all, and her perspective from living in South Africa is incredible. We have watched incredible films as well. The easiness of the class is a plus.
Professor Byerly was a great professor who truly is passionate about what she teaches. Sometimes she may seem unstructured, but overall her curriculum was engaging and not difficult.

Professor Byerly is extremely passionate about music and culture, and her lectures are never boring. Her classes are always exciting and she allows us to be creative in accomplishing tasks. Our projects were always fun to do because of the independence she gave. One of my favorite classes
Great teacher! She is very knowledgeable on the subject and loves to discuss and answer questions. Very friendly and laid back.
