I've never met a professor more enthusiastic about their course. Ingrid really cared about making this class an enjoyable life experience for us, rather than something to just simply get through with a good grade.

Professor Byerly is amazing. Best professor I have ever had at Duke. She allows you to pursue any topic of your choosing and is fully interested in every person's project. She was also extremely helpful when I met with her outside of class. She pays attention to attendance, but class is so enjoyable that you will want to be there.
Such a great professor! Take her class
This professor is awesome!  Enjoyed her class so much and would take it again if I could.

Ingrid Byerly is by far one of the most fascinating professors I've ever had. The work load isn't overwhelming, and the work she has you do is extremely interesting. She can relate to anything, as she has had so many experiences in her life that are unlike what you have heard before.You honestly need to take a course with her if you have the option

Mrs Byerly is the most amazing professor. Her eyes sparkle with enthusiasm and you learn something unexpected in every class! She has rekindled my love for learning, and I recommend taking one of her classes whenever wherever, they are so worth it!

I audited her Global Music class on Semester at Sea summer 2011. Ingrid fully engages her audience. She encourages independent thinking and self exploration. She made every student feel that their contribution was welcome. We learned the course material joyfully and she imparted much wisdom to all of us about life and joy.
Professor Byerly is an amazing teacher.  Keeps class very interesting and encourages students to broaden their horizons.  Take a class with Her!

Mrs. Byerly is by far one of the best professors I have ever had. I was on the Semester at Sea program with her and took an ethnomusicology course. Learning about the music of each port was super interesting, especially when we applied it in person. Class had great structure, and Byerly is the most engaging, funny, interesting prof you'll ever have
Amazing teacher. The way she structures her class is how every teacher should and her stories are so interesting. Highly recommended!

Professor Byerly is all about excitement. You can see it in her eyes! One can't help but want to learn and be around her. I can't imagine a more perfect individual for the role of facilitating such a challenging task as writing a senior thesis.

This class was well worth the 830 start time. The open discussion provided a great environment for intellectual stimulation and the knowledge I gained goes far behind the title of the class. I highly recommend this class to all freshmen and Professor Byerly as an instructor for any other class.

This class was truly one of the highlights of my freshman year. By creating a classroom environment focused on learning instead of grades, she enables students to be open to adopting new ways of thinking about and listening to music and conceptualizing protest movements, and also endows them with many useful academic skills. Take a class with her!!

Professor Byerly was one of the best professors I've ever had. Beyond the stimulating class structure, she is one of the most fascinating people to listen to and makes class at 8:30 am not only bearable but captivating. Any Duke student should jump at the chance to take a course with her.

I took Professor Byerly's  Fieldwork Methods class and thought that she was a really great professor. As a CulAnth major she was the kind of laid back professor that encourages you to explore what you enjoy that makes me love my choice if major.  I would really encourage taking this class with her:-)

Amazing professor. The class was very much based around discussion and conversation, and Professor Byerly has the rare ability to show students the world  from multiple perspectives. A thoroughly interesting and eye-opening adventure.

Prof Byerly is one of the most fantastic teachers at Duke! She is accommodating to any situation, extremely encouraging, and ALWAYS willing to help. Her syllabus allows you to truly earn the grade you deserve, and though this was difficult to initially get used to, this way of teaching turned out to be super rewarding! I recommend her to everyone!

Ingrid was the perfect prof for a fieldwork methods course. The guidlelines for our semester-long project were broad, leaving us students a bit uneasy about grades. BUT inevitably it allowed us the freedom to do our work freely/without limitations, giving us a real, enriching experience in the field and making us better anthropologists! She rocks!

This class was one of my favorite classes. I learned so much about how music could be used in different ways. I was surprised at what I learned and even more surprised at how well read Prof. Byerly was. She's an easy professor if you are attentive and express interest in the class. Take this class. It is relaxing and stimulating at the same time.

Professor Byerly is one of my favorite professors at Duke. This is one class in which I learned while having a blast. It was awesome! She brings in her own experiences and anecdotes which are soo interesting. This was a very engaging class. She's amazing! Take the class. You'll love it.

LOVED going to this class. Professor Byerly is incredibly captivating, caring, and unconventional. Great class discussions. She gives you the freedom and tools to devise a great fieldwork project of your own choosing! I'm taking another class with her in the fall and can't wait!!

This class was amazing!  Prof. Byerly really cares about her students, and allows them to be free thinkers.  She is really helpful throughout the process of completing the project.  She is ALWAYS there if you need her input or assistance.  I definitely recommend this class. One of the BEST PROFESSORS AT DUKE!!!

Class is fluid, organic & natural and classes are often just an hour of discussion (sitting around & chatting about the most fabulous things). There is no set syllabus, which some students might find hard to wrap their heads around, but I personally loved it. IngyB is easy to talk to; she always has time (and often food) & the best example stories
Great Professor. Really helped with fieldwork, with explaining how to do everything, with advice on improving methods.

Professor Byerly was simply awesome. She is passionate on her subject. And the subject itself is different from rather dry subjects in courses offered in college. She is helpful and encouraging. It is truly a fun class to take!

The purpose of the fieldwork and methods class is not to provide a structured, text-book based atmosphere but rather a very open, student-initiated discussion forum. The variety of projects we discuss are enthralling. This class enriched my senior year, and could have been a kick-start to thesis work as a major had I taken it junior year.

Professor Byerly is fantastic. Her fieldwork methods class is a very do-it-yourself based project where you are given a lot of freedom to create your own project and research what interests you. It really teaches you the methods of the field, and lets you learn through difficulties and successes, always with constructive criticism and great advice.

Dr. Byerly's methods course is so rewarding. While she certainly provides a great deal of guidance in her lessons, she leaves students a lot of room to think and work independently. I learned so much from her,beyond what applies in the classroom. She really opens up a new way of seeing the world. MUST take her course!!!

Byerly is an engaging teacher that challenged students to research a community of their choosing. Quite the opposite from typical seminar professors who seem to be unable to let go of their leash of authority, Byerly fostered classroom methods of self-accountability. This inspired students to take ownership in their academic work. Awesome class!

She is very engaging, very enthusiastic about the course and supportive of the students. She cares about the students and try to accommodate problems. The class was slightly disorganized but workload is manageable and grading is generous. The focus is highly on African music, which startled me at first, but it was overall a good experience.

Professor Byerly is one of the most engaging professors at Duke. I took two of her classes and she always had something new to teach everyday. She made class fun and exciting and made me want to research and learn more. She was always helpful and always had great advice!

Ingrid will go down as one of the highest quality professors, and people,  I met in my time at Duke.  I learned more in this course about life and interacting with others than in any other classroom experience. She is always very respectful of all viewpoints in the class and constantly opens the floor for interactive discussion on all topics.
She is inspiring, definitely suggest you to take her class.
Really really nice. Cares about you and the material. The readings are short and selective. If you work hard and contribute in class, you'll do well.

Great teacher. Really nice and cool.  Easy to relate to. Makes class fun and interesting. Uses lots of different types of media to teach and keep it interesting.  Talks a lot about South Africa. She cares about you and how you're doing. Highly suggest her

Music as a social mediator was really interesting.  Ingrid was very friendly, nice, and helpful in not only the class material but the overall college experience.  She was always willing to meet with students outside of class for papers or assignments.  We only had a group project and a paper so it was pretty easy.  And I think most peopls got As.

Zito is very witty and knowledgeable about what he teaches. His lectures are informative and help prepare you for exams. There really is no curve for the class, but there are ways to improve your grade. Be ready to pay attention, so it helps you do well in lab and on tests. Not an easy A, but it is attainable.
Great and funny lectures with fun material
A really nice professor. Probability is really hard, and Professor Zito really stretched us a little bit on the math part. But he graded the exams generously, and he curved a lot. Highly recommend!

Probability was always going to be rough, but Dr. Zito cares so much about his students. Best stats prof I've had by far. Memorized everyone's names before first day of class. Psets were hard, but OH were always helpful and exams were very reasonable. If he's teaching this class, take it!

Zito is a very funny guy. It is easy to get stuck in the B+ or A- grade during midterm one and two since you  basically need a 90+ in all the categories to get an A. With that said, if you are able to code the problems yourself, you will get an A. Go to office hours! I learned how to code R with no prior coding experience.

JZ is really great. He cares a lot about his students and explains concepts very well. Grade however is dependent on high performance on both midterms (20% each), the project (20%), and the final (20%). You have to go to OH to see your previous tests. Would definitely take again but parts of the grading can be difficult and feel arbitrary

Must take for stats majors. Probability and statistics are weird subjects, but JZ's lectures and notes will show you why they're necessary, useful, and beautiful. The psets can be tricky, but Zito is very helpful during office hours / on Ed and the exams are totally reasonable. 

Median Grades:
Midterm 1: 88.1%
Midterm 2: 80.4%
Final: 88.7%

JZ is my goat🙏🏼. An interesting/kind guy, makes lectures easy to follow. He pauses for questions and knows people's names. That being said, the grading scale is odd. We spend countless hours on labs worth 15% when 2 Midterms and a final make up 60%. As a PubPol major, take Zito if you're a good test taker and can pay attention! Class is lowk hard

JZ is such a funny guy. And he somehow knew so many of the students' names even when there were nearly 200 students crammed in that lecture hall. Loved his lectures and how there were OHs nearly every day. STA199 was singlehandedly the most useful class I took at Duke.
Overall, the class wasn't that difficult, as the concepts are easy to understand. However, the grading for the project is confusing, and the tests are challenging

Very quick-witted, particularly enjoyed delivery of jokes during lecture, "Hey Gang" emails, massage & squinting ifykyk. Tests were reasonable, but beware there's no curve or grade rounding, which is toughhh but such is life and there are other assignments to help you out. Start psets early, don't skip lecture, go to OH. You'll learn a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Zito is a funny guy but this class was frustrating. He knows coding but didn't prepare us well for the exams which were 60% of our grade. I had no issues with coding but underperformed with exams because they were very different from what we were learning and practice questions were not helpful. Most of our grade was all in the last few weeks.

Grading in his class takes a very long time and in class lecture does not really prepare you for the exams well. I would say I learned the most from doing the labs, and I learned the skills on my own, not from in class. The application exercises in class are not really mentioned until the last 10 minutes which was annoying.

BEST TEACHER I'VE HAD AT DUKE. Probability, in general, is a hard and annoying course but he makes it interesting. Love his style of teaching & real world applications in the classroom. Exams are straightforward & as advertised; psets are a little tough, but his office hours help a lot. I love this man and he is the sole reason I'm passing.

The practice questions/kahoots for the midterms didn't really match what the midterms were like. It was hard to gauge how well we were doing in the class because 60% of our grade was left undetermined until the last 2 weeks. The labs were the only thing that felt generally consistent.

He's alright. A little rude, eccentric, and condescending, but I did learn a lot in his class. His class pacing is good but grading structure is weird. The last 60% of your grade is determined in the last 2 weeks of class.

John Zito is a really funny guy and I enjoyed Stat 199. His class was pretty hard though and the labs were incredibly time consuming. Also, the exams didn't really match the questions we had seen prior. If the content is intuitive to you, it's easy to do well, but otherwise not so much. I think he taught computing well, but not inference.

He is a nice professor, however his exam/final review is awful. The practice midterms don't prepare you and he never releases exams. Even if you go to office hours you can't see what you got wrong or the right answers. The midterms and exams also make up 60% of your grade. Additionally, he makes IMPORTANT changes at 3:00am that affect your studies.

Legitimately hilarious guy, knows statistics inside and out and always makes sure to bring in real-world applications to help students engage. Sometimes goes a little fast without explaining his thought process, but is accessible outside of class if you need help.

For whatever reason, Professor Zito refused to release our midterm questions - we had to go to office hours to see them, and still weren't allowed to write down the questions. He also wouldn't release our project grades until after the exam, which made it hard to determine what grade we needed going into the final. This is for STA 199 BTW

I LOVE HIM. He is super funny and makes these witty jokes during class that keep it engaging. There is a lot of material to cover and he does it well. He definitely makes stats and Rstudio interesting and fun. I definitely recommend!
JZ is great! He gives a lot of extra credit opportunities and not too much work. Very funny guy and understanding.

JZ is fantastic. He is genuinely so funny which got me to attend lecture that is pointless for exams. Ask TA's for help on labs to succeed. Coding is very simple and so is overall content. Almost no homework or time outside lab required. Ends with final group project. Please take this class for JZ alone.

Professor Zito is great! He cares a lot about his students and even knew all of our names before coming into the first lecture. He provides many extra credit opportunities and makes it easy to get help if you're not understanding a concept. The course is code-heavy and has a final group project, but he gives you all the resources to succeed!

He is an amazing lecturer. In my opinion, I liked Parise's orgo more than Cox. He explains very well and there was nothing I couldn't understand because of his exceptional teaching skills. I do have to say his exams are not the easiest, not super hard tho, especially because there is 1~2 challenge questions where you acc have to think outside box.

Dr. Parise is a great professor. He has lecture outlines with spaces to fill which makes following along very easy. Attendance isn't taken, but there are no recordings so I would recommend going to lecture. The content of organic chemistry is hard, but Parise lectures well and makes the exams fair if you study and do enough practice problems.

You know there are hard classes that are difficult because of the professor and others that are hard purely because of the content, this class is definitely the latter. Prof. Parise cares and is willing to make time to problem-solve personal strategies to succeed in his class. Would def take the class with him again (even despite the bad grade!)
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Parise is a wonderful professor! I have had him for 3 chem courses. He cares deeply about his students and is determined in figuring out the best ways to teach and support his students in their learning. He definitely expects a lot from his students, but if you put in the time and work, you will learn and do well.

I had Dr. Parise for three courses, and I can say for sure that he's one of the best professors I've had at Duke. Test-based grading can be intimidating at first, but if you stay tapped in and engage with the problem sets, you'll do great. He's also very accessible and cares deeply about your success here, so don't be afraid to ask him for help!

I took chem 101 and 202 with professor Parise, and he was excellent! Makes challenging content feel really accessible with his very clear lectures, and is very accessible in office hours! He is such a kind, lovely person and will make jokes in his lectures and makes a real effort to make a challenging class approachable for everyone!
The lectures were interesting and easy to follow. The exams were definitely challenging, but I do think that if you put in the time and effort to prepare, they are generally fair.

Absolutely amazing. He's committed to helping you in any way you need--extensive office hours & lecture reviews outside of class. He cracks jokes and dresses up for halloween, just is a truly great guy. The class is graded by midterms, lab grade, and final (no drops), so very harsh grading, but an A is certainly feasible. 100% recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great teacher with lectures that are understandable. His tests are extremely difficult, almost to the point where they aren't fair. Put it effort and you won't fail, don't worry. Just get ready to work, but its organic chemistry, what did you expect?

Dr. Parise is an extremely kind professor who makes complicated orgo concepts more comprehensible. He provides so many additional resources (i.e textbook questions and videos) to help you understand the material better. If you put in the work for the class, you will get the grade that you want. Dr. Parise prepared with me a solid orgo foundation.

I thought Parise was ok until I had Cox. Parise tests you at a higher level than he teaches. He refuses to record lectures, post discussion keys, lecture notes, convinces you to buy his $100 textbook. He's so nice but it was a shame he doesn't do these basic things to help his students do better and learn better in his class.

Dr. Parise is a very good professor and strong choice for Orgo 1. Chem 201 isn't an easy class, and I had to study a lot, but he lectures really well and provides tons of practice material to do well in the course.

While Organic Chemistry is a rather difficult class, Dr. Parise is able to make it significantly more bearable. He is a fantastic lecturer and makes every resource available for us to succeed (ample practice, extra videos, etc.). Generally, he breaks down concepts so they are very easy to understand, and with good practice, an A is very achievable.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Parise is a good teacher and probably the best organic chemistry teacher at Duke. Organic 1 is just a hard class, but he does a good job of teaching the core concepts in class. However, some studying outside of class will have to be done. If you put in the time, you will do good.

I am tired of people (freshmen) gaslighting me into thinking Parise is even comparable to Cox. A prof should never set the bar above the level they teach. A prof should never convince us buying his textbook is the only way to succeed. It is his responsibility to provide textbook solutions & questions to prepare us and teach at the level he tests.

Prof. Parise is a phenomenal science professor. Put in the work, and this will be one of your most rewarding classes in college. He is extremely organized, communicates expectations well, and presents the content clearly. He perfectly balances structure and flexibility: clear guidelines and many resources, but a lot of self-study flexibility.

Dr. Parise cares a lot about his students and genuinely tries to help them whenever he can. I thought his lecture reviews were really helpful (even if you can't go, he posts the problem sets) and he shares a lot of great resources (textbook problems are the best in my opinion). Even though the material's hard, his lectures explain it very well!

Parise is a great prof who is obviously very knowledgeable in his field. Great lecturer but you will need to do lots of practice problems to prepare for the difficulty of his tests. If I were to take the class again I would stay up to date with checklist problems and take advantage of lecture reviews. If you do these, you should easily get an A/B.

He is an amazing teacher. Best science teacher I've had in my life. He is so passionate, and if you do all his practice multiple times and checklists throughout the unit. DONT FALL BEHIND. You will be an expert by the time you leave his class. So many people get an A- and definitely wouldn't at any other school knowing this much content.

COMPREHENSIVE: Parise is a kind, well-meaning professor who provides plenty of study materials. His lectures are strong, but to do well on the tests you need to also practice many problems. Midterms are difficult but doable by using all available resources (devote days to prep); final was slightly better. Grading is determined largely by exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Parise genuinely wants all of his students to do well and gives you resources to succeed such as his lecture reviews and unit checklists. However, I felt that his exams were unrepresentative of the preparation materials and were more so based on things not covered in lecture. Reading the textbook and working all the practice problems is crucial
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very nice prof. If you can take his class, take it!

After a horrible gen chem experience, I was afraid going into orgo but Parise is a genuinely a great professor. He provides ample practice and resources that you must take advantage of. The key to succeeding is to constantly do the practice problems. Your grade is basically midterms and a final but an A is possible if you stay on top of it.

Overall a very solid professor. Everything's subjective to each individual, but I think his tests were difficult but he had tons of practices resources and lectured really well. There might be better professors, but I definitely wouldn't hesitate to choose him for orgo.

was scared of parise bc of negative reviews and only professor i could take. BUT i ended up having a great experience. great lecturer, solid textbook + prepares well for exam. 

organic chem is hard, and no doubt you're challenged to apply rather than memorize. just do all the practice problems, attend lecture, and you're solid. parise the goat fr
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Test heavy

reviews.comment: His lectures are extremely basic, his exams are extremely difficult. He's not good enough of a lecturer to justify his exams. My favorite thing about Parise are his resources (not his textbook)

Parise is easily one my favorite professors I've had. While the course is challenging at times with lots a problems, Parise gives good advice on how to succeed in the course and is accessible. He is very funny and genuinely cares about his students. His lectures can sometimes move fast, but he makes the material easy to grasp and enjoyable to learn
Just show up to lectures and you're guaranteed to not bomb the tests.
You should get an A if you show up to lectures and do the work he assigns

He sold us on using his organic book in 101 because he either lazy or didn't want to teach 101. Because of him, 210 has been awful because we had to learn the actually 101 content in addition to the new 210 stuff. He seems good until you take additional courses, then you realize how little effort he puts in.

Swears by textbook questions that aren't actually very representative of the exams, other chem professors are seen as tougher, but they lay out expectations and info in lecture much better in my opinion. Take advantage of problem sets and sample exams the most.

I take back every bad thing I ever said about Canelas, Martinez, and even Dewey if it meant I didn't have to take his class. This class proves to me Orgo is not standardized across professors. How is my C comparable to someone in Dewey having an A but I know more content?

He makes you buy his book and solutions manual, and lectures usually restate examples from the textbook. I sometimes didn't see the point of the lecture. Exams were much easier than Cox's, but Parise down curves and grades harshly to make up for the easier exams. Take Cox or someone else—it may be harder, yet the grading policies should be better.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Not a fan of a mandatory charge for an online textbook, but he was good at teaching.
Lectures are helpful, but textbook reading and questions are much more important for success on exams. Grading is a bit tough when it comes to exams and how letter grades are assigned
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He's a great lecturer, and you'll actually understand orgo if you try
He is a very good professor and is truly caring but at the end of the day, it is orgo... I would def take a class with him again but he only grades by exams and midterms which is a huge negative.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Parise is great as a person, but his class is made to be more difficult than it needs to be. I did not find the textbook problems to be helpful and instead would prefer if we read the textbook but has problems that were more similar to the read to practice from instead. Overall, he is not terrible and his lecture is good. But makes an A, impossible
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Took both orgo 1 and orgo 2 with Parise and found orgo 2 much easier. Exams were very similar to the assigned textbook questions (some exactly from the book). Final had a page of questions exactly from previous midterms. He is very accesible outside of class and exams were fair but they are all that makes up your grade so prepare well
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: W Professor W person. I took Orgo 1, Orgo 1, and Gen Chem with him. All the classes were challenging and required a lot of time outside of class, but he gives you all the resources you need to succeed. There's no reason you can't get an A if you exhaust all his assigned resources. The exams are also very fair.

I took CHEM101, CHEM201 and CHEM202 with Parise. For context I'm not a chemistry person so I found all of the courses to be very difficult, obviously increasing difficultly with the course code. Use the resources that he gives you they're SUPER helpful (practice problems via textbook, lecture reviews, discussion problem sets, practice exams, etc.).
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Lectures aren't mandatory, but not recorded; doesn't share notes from lecture so p much HAVE to attend. Tests are EXTREMELY fair and gives great partial credit/lenient on grading. Sweet person, caring, and tries to teach you orgo conceptually instead of forcing you to memorize mechanisms and reactions. Always willing to help outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Explains chemistry in a clear way in his lectures and the tests aren't that bad if you pay attention in class, lab, etc.

Dr. Parise is a great professor - clear lectures, accessible outside of class, and very organized. I learned a ton in his class. It is SUPER important to keep up with the readings and practice problems/checklists if you want to do well, since the exams draw heavily from the book. Grade comes only from exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Jimmy P. One of the guys, just a super cool Professor. Provides us with great resources like his numerous videos on topics we cover in class and his very helpful practice exams. Pro tip that he also gives: DO THE PROBLEMS IN THE TEXTBOOK. It'll help you tremendously. Midterms are tough, but the final was VERY fair. Gonna miss 8:30s with him…

Definitely a college wake up call. If you want to do well you have know information outside the scope of what he teaches, which is beyond frustrating. Lab is also extremely unrelated to the class and all the reports are beyond confusing.

Parise is great! He sets you up to do well in the course. He provides chapter checklists, and many other resources to make sure you are ready for exams. Go to lecture, do all the practice problems, and you'll be fine. He's also great about giving partial credit on exams.

I thought he was good but after taking 202 with another professor, I realized he wasn't clear and couldn't explain content beyond a surface level. Good for lazy premeds but I want to learn the material. He is popular with students because his is ridiculously easy but that unfortunately didn't translate to a rich understanding of content.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Not to be dramatic but I'm actively avoiding him / will not take another chem class with Parise again... AMAZING guy don't get me wrong, but his teaching style really doesn't work for me and I also think that it's wrong to have tests that are mostly multiple choice where you lose four points per question -- especially in a chemistry class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Hard class. Lectures aren't recorded and notes aren't posted so attendance is important and you need to pay attention to get all the notes down, same with discussion. Exams make up 70% of the grade. Holds lecture reviews twice a week which are helpful if they fit in your schedule. Assigns a lot of textbook problems and readings for practice.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The first test he gives is relatively easy but after that, be prepared to really dedicate your time to this class. The material isn't particularly difficult, it's the sheer amount of it that makes this class so difficult. My entire spring break was spent studying for an exam (8-10h/day) and there was still somehow more to cover. Still adore Parise!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: In this class, your input likely matched your grades. It's easy to underestimate how much you would need to study but trust me, lock yourself away from civilization for a few days for every exam if you want a pretty grade. The final did throw us all for a loop so be prepared for that as well. Overall, fantastic lecturer who cares about you.

Orgo is hard, it takes a lot of effort and time commitment. However, Parise has great and helpful lectures and lecture reviews. It is very important to study everything for the exams. The class grade is nearly completely dependent on how well you do on the exam. Parise assigns a lot of work out of his own textbook.

Parise is a great lecturer and wants to see all of his students succeed. He gives a lot of homework, but it is good practice for the exams. He is accessible outside of class and offered lots of student hours. Exams are difficult and require a lot of studying to succeed. Parise teachs pre-orgo given he teaches out of his own orgo textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Parise has been the best professor I have had at Duke. He is an amazing lecturer and his tests reflect what he teaches in class. Students who do poorly in his class either don't do the assigned practice problems or never seek out help. Dr. Parise hosts lecture reviews outside of class and of the 300 students only 10 showed up every week.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Parise is a great professor. He posts checklists for every chapter. Keeping up with these problems is crucial for success. He doesn't provide many practice exams, but still many prep sources are available (lecture review problems, discussion psets, etc). Solve many problems! Exams are 70% of grade, 25% is lab, and rest is discussion.
parise is a great professor! hes funny and very nice. he got us donuts and likes talking to students. his tests are a little tricky but they are fair. his textbook is really good

Dr. Parise makes chem so enjoyable!! I can't do anything but applaud him for that. There is a lot of reading but as long as you dedicate time to problem solving, you will be successful. He has designed this course in a very fair way. The exams do compose a large percent of your grade, however I feel like you can definitely prepare with his resource

If you have the chance to take any chem course with Dr. Parise, take it!!! I've now had Dr. Parise for two semesters and onto my third semester with him haha but it has been the biggest pleasure. He is an amazing lecturer and although the content is difficult (I mean it is orgo) his jokes and bright personality make lectures engaging. I 100% recomm

YALL when I say you need to take a course with Dr. Parise, I MEAN IT!!! An eye-opening experience for sure loll. He is an amazing prof and I have genuinely learned a lot! I would recommend any course with him
While chem 101 was very organic chemistry heavy, so long as you did the practice problems, you really were fine. He is so positive almost like a proton ;+D

Parise was awul in Chem101. Granted, he is the orgo professor and Duke decided to prepare pre-meds by making the same professor teach genchem, and it definitely showed. As a non pre-med/chem major I don't care about orgo and was penalized for taking a required class. Parise was awful at conveying information and the class was so hard.
Yummy donut holes at the end!!!!
I want other students to know how phenomenal of a professor Dr. Parise is.
My favorite professor at Duke! Gave me a delicious donut hole on LDOC!! It was so worth it :)

Professor seems like a nice lecturer but all the concepts that he explain are so vague. He says one thing in his lectures and his textbook says another. When I go to him for clarification, he never answers the question to the point.

Had Dr. Parise for 101 and 201! He's a lovely professor that is committed to supporting his students. He has made lectures "fun" with his jokes and smiley attitude. He is available on Ed and in person, always willing to meet and discuss topics. I do recommend!

Parise is a great teacher if you have to take organic chemistry. The material is just hard in general, but he does his best to make it bearable. He's available for meetings all of the time and so are the TAs. He's an interesting guy and definitely cares about his students. He has checklists with suggest problems to complete that keep you on pace.

He himself is a great caring guy. The lectures are good but it's hard to absorb the information because you're trying to copy down everything he says. Definitely became humbled and studying a lot doesn't guarantee a good grade. There's basically no homework (other than heinous lab reports) so its just exams...do well on them...or try...

Parise was an engaging lecturer and has a wonderful vibe, but there were definitely lectures I had a hard time following. The homework and readings help you get an understanding of the material as you go. Exams are most of the grades which puts a lot of pressure on each exam. They can be challenging but generally are reflective of the material.

I love Jimmy P. He was a great professor and always showed up to class with a smile on his face. He made an 8:30 worth it, much more enjoyable than expected. Grading was always clear, no surprises on the exam. Lectures were structured well. Make sure you stay on top of the work, because it definitely piles up.

He's a phenomenal lecturer but the class structure is very unforgiving. Three exams and a final are 70% and lab makes up another 25%. You will invest a lot of time into this class. He's pretty good about answering on edstem. You will learn way more orgo than anticipated. Go to lecture or you will struggle so hard. Good luck stem majors

A frustrating class. Praise teaches out of his own organic chemistry textbook, which makes the class infinitely more difficult than comparable classes at other top universities. Not easy to access outside of class, as well as discrepancies between the questions assigned for practice and those on the test.

Dr. Parise is great at what he does. He is super passionate about chemistry, and he puts in a great deal of effort to make sure that students succeed. He supplies tons of practice problems and posts sample exams. As long as you do the readings and problems, exams will not be terrible. Only complaint is not knowing curve until very end of semester.

Great lecturer and gives a very concise group of resources to prepare for the tests. Use the materials he gives you and you will do well on each test. Lots of work and practice problems if you want to succeed but it is rewarding.

Professor seems like a nice lecturer but all the concepts that he explain are so vague. He says one thing in his lectures and his textbook says another. When I go to him for clarification, he never answers the question to the point.

Orgo 2 isn't easy. Other reviews complaining about the curve won't make it as doctors. Curve's reasonable if you study. I lacked time for a higher grade. Dr. Parise emphasizes doing countless book problems for success.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I didn't do amazing on my first exam in the class, and Dr. Parise was very willing to meet one on one with me outside of class to discuss what went wrong and how I can do better in the course. Tests are incredibly fair, and if you go to lectures everything will be doable and something you've seen before.

This will be a tough class no matter who you take it with, but Parise is very clear on his expectations and his lectures are great. If you come to class and do the problems he assigns for practice (not mandatory) the exams aren't overwhelming at all. He is super approachable and helpful outside of class and wants to see students do well.

Parise is a kind guy and a good lecturer. He uses his textbook so get ready to read it and expect it to be overcomplicated. He also wants $ so you have to buy the solutions. If you skim it and focus on the discussion problems (over textbook problems) you should do just fine. But the textbook problems (though being super hard) prep you better.

I had very weak foundation in Chemistry coming from high school, so there was definitely a learning curve for me at the start of this class. He teaches Chem101 out of his Organic Chemistry textbook, so naturally the course is pretty orgo-heavy. Work hard and do problems from his textbook to study-- you will do well on exams.
He is quite good.

James Parise can seem like a good professor, but it is all for show. 
He always has great lectures, but is always late to office hours and never answers questions clearly. He says not to worry if you did poorly on an exam, but there's no way you can get an A if you got a B on the first exams.

Dr. Parise is a great lecturer and a nice guy, but I would definitely avoid Orgo 2 with him. The class is pitted against each other with his grading system, and it makes the class incredibly toxic. He also gives barely any partial credit on exams or other grades to supplement. Wish I waited to take Orgo 2 in the fall.
on god the best professor ever i love him
very fun intro class that includes a lot of organic topics. would highly recommend u take
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Dr. Parise is awesome. He has great lectures that clearly explain often confusing material featured in the textbook. He often includes jokes, songs, or memes in his slides to keep engagement high.
My main recommendations would be to do, as he says, practice problems in the textbook. Those are key to doing well on the tests.

I didn't like the grading system of the class, there's a strange curve for every test and you basically don't know your grade until the end of the semester. The key to doing well is to do the textbook problems, and try not to bomb any tests. Do well on the labs (even though they have no correlation to the class), because it can save your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Parise is a great professor. He cares about his students and is accessible even with the huge class enrollment. For a general chem course, a lot of the content is organic chemistry, which can make it challenging but still doable. To do well on tests, make sure to keep up with textbook readings and practice problems.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Parise/Jimmy P is an awesome professor! His lectures were always thorough and interesting even at 8 in the morning and he's a very nice person. However, only 3 exams + the final make up most of your grade, and the grading was a little confusing (i.e., we didn't know what an A actually "was" till the last week of class).

Live, laugh, love Jimmy P. He's a great professor who made lectures fun and interesting. He was very accessible outside of class and ensured we left feeling confident. One thing I disliked about this class was the way he graded/curved. It's almost impossible to know your grade until after the final and the grades are curved in such a strange way.
Jimmy P is amazing!! He is an amazing professor - always has a great attitude.

Dr. Parise is an AMAZING professor who truly cares about his students! His lectures are great and go over all of the homework readings. Dr. Parise provides practice tests and makes himself available for both in-class exam reviews and reviews during office hours. A LOT of helpful practice problems. Requires a lot of work but is worth it 100%!!!!!
b

Such an amazing teacher. Parise explains everything so clearly that I am never confused after a lecture. Relatively easy course but the bell curve screws up your grade. I fully think it is worth it though! I would love to take another class with Parise.

Dr. Parise is a clear and concise professor, and a great choice if you're planning for Orgo to be your top priority. He wrote the textbook, so the text reflects lecture -- sometimes too well, since almost all the examples in class were straight from the textbook. The textbook is NOT OPTIONAL, and he doesn't release lecture notes/external material.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
He is amazing. He made me love chemistry, and I'm even considering a major related to this subject. His classes require a lot of preparation, but he explains so well that no topic seemed difficult. He is never bored with students' questions and is easily available in his office. The professor also judges very fairly. 
Highly recomended!

Parise is cool. If you really want to do well, you've gotta do extra problems, and Parise emphasizes this. Tests are sometimes tricky, and the practice exams he provides are even trickier. No grade-bumpers like discussion or hw, so try not to fail a midterm. Hard to get an A b/c it depends on your classmates...I had a low 90 and still got an A-
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Orgo was probably the most challenging class I've taken so far at Duke, but Dr. Parise was really helpful throughout the year in ensuring that we all felt comfortable with the content. He wrote the textbook so he knows what he's talking about and is very accessible for office hrs outside of class. If taking 201, definitely try to take it with him!
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Parise has an excellent lecture style. He makes concepts in this course very clear, and he cracks a few jokes here and there as well. His exams can be challenging but are usually pretty fair. He didn't provide a ton of practice exams, but he gives you lists of book problems that can moderately prepare you for the tests.

Absolutely goated professor! Outstanding guy who's also interesting outside of the classroom - loved FLUNCHing him. Put in the work, and you'll see results. Straightforward tests that you can do well on as long as you keep up with the textbook. The 830 was hellish, but Dr. Parise's enthusiasm and dad jokes made it more than worth it.
reviews.rating_tags: Inspirational--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Parise is clear when explaining things and is a really good lecturer. He also helps you when you need it and it understanding as long as you try. However, he does use an Orgo textbook (that he wrote) for what is supposed to be a general chemistry class, and it often did not match the lab content. Regardless, his class is worth taking.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's fantastic. Both smart and personable, lectures are engaging, and class is very regular and structured so you know exactly what to expect. The workload is a lot, but tests are EXTREMELY fair and if you actually do what he says wrt working checklists of problems, going to discussion/lecture, and creating your own resources, you will succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is excellent at explaining organic chemistry (literally wrote the textbook). He has a great lecture style - instead of going through boring powerpoint slides, he used an iPad to write out notes during class so everyone could follow along. Exams are pretty hard, but if you do the assigned problems, you will do well.

Professor Parise is really good at explaining things clearly and efficiently, and he lectures really well. However, you do have to buy his Organic Chemistry textbook for the class even though it does not remotely cover the same material as labs. The course material is also weirdly more Orgo based than Gen Chem based, even though it is a 101 class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Parise is my favorite professor I've ever had. He is such a nice person and really cares about his students. Go to office hours!!! They are so helpful, and he will recognize your effort. Still, the class is hard (I believe it's significantly harder than those who took it with a different professor), so the test grades can be discouraging.

Parise is great, especially during the summer. His lectures are a bit dull, but extremely clear and helpful if you pay close attention. His tests are very straight-forward, so they are easy to do well on, given you study hard for them.

If you are taking orgo 1, take it with Parise. His lectures are clear, organized, and simple. You should try to get to know him outside of the class because he is a fun guy and actually makes an effort to remember you. He made my Orgo 1 experience incredible. His tests are hard but fair and if you work hard for the final, it will pay off.

Dr. Parise provided all I could have asked for in an organic chemistry professor and more. His method of presenting the material highlights what is important and is easy to follow. Highly recommended!
Dr. Parise was approachable and very helpful. He made sure we knew what we needed to know for the test. I didn't really mind going to lecture, and he's pretty funny.

Clear teaching style with logic that follows the textbook. He re-wrote all his notes on the whiteboard with helpful diagrams so it was easy to keep up in class. I was really impressed with his enthusiasm and willingness to help students on a one to one basis.
This guy is awesome. He is enthusiastic and will help you through this difficult subject if you let him.
Terrific prof. Clear, organized, and helpful. Made a huge effort getting to know the students out of class. Absolutely recommend taking orgo with Parise.

I HATE Chemistry but Parise, through his clear and charming lecture style, made orgo less intimidating and actually pretty interesting. Also, he is always available for questions and is very personable. His tests are hard, but fair so if you keep up with reading and problem sets you will do totally fine.

Parise is the best science professor I've had at Duke and probably one of my favorites overall. I really liked his thorough lecture style; he kept us engaged so that I was rarely bored in class. It's difficult not to take good lecture notes, and these, along with the past exams, are the key to doing well on tests.

Dr. Parise could not have been more clear.  Let me repeat that-Dr.Parise could not be more clear.  His lecture style is excellent and definitely the best.  Tests are hard, but honestly how easy can orgo be?  Just know the material really well (make orgo your priority)and you'll be fine.  Plus Parise curves nicely-I got avg on all tests & got a b!

Excellent professor. His lectures are clear, extremely helpful, and pretty funny. He's by far my fav professor at Duke thus far and made orgo enjoyable. I wish he taught my other science courses. He's very helpful and easy to talk to. Definitely make an effort to get to know him outside of class. I recommend him over anyone else.

I've heard horror stories about orgo, but having Parise really made a difference. I still did really poorly on his tests, but it was my own fault; his tests really are straightforward. He doesn't try to trick you and he is extremely clear with his teaching. His old tests are helpful to look at, but his tests now focus a lot more on mechanisms.

First off-orgo is hard at Duke, period.  But Parise does an excellent job.  His tests are hard but you know what to expect (no curveballs). He is straightforward in lecture & very helpful in emails.  Tends to quote the book but is very thorough & a nice guy - I second the comment about the nerdy chem jokes.  Pick Parise over anyone else for orgo.

This is a hard class.  Parise knows what he's talking about and is a very good guy, but the class is really tough.  Test can be tricky, but going through the problems in the book is really essential.  Doing that can help the tests.  Go through his old tests, and beware the final - its kind of ridiculous.

He may write out too much on the board, but he does so to be very clear.  Very available for questions and answers quickly.  Adds some charm to the class with some nerdy jokes, but he teaches the material well.  Orgo is still orgo, but Parise is a solid teacher.
Gives clear straightforward lectures with great notes. Friendly and eager to help. He's great during office hours. Grading was fair. Definitely recommend taking a class he's teaching.

Fantastic professor. Gives excellent notes in class, easy to follow and very clear. I didn't find it necessary to read the textbook, though it was helpful when I did. Very willing to help and answer questions, easy to talk to. Office hours were really helpful.  Exams were tough, but fair. I highly recommend Dr.Parise

Absolutely the best chem teacher I've had thus far in my entire academic career. Notes are succinct, well-organized. and even though I did all of the readings thoroughly they wouldn't have been necessary for the tests. Tests are sufficiently challenging but he takes off a TON of points even for minor, careless errors. I love him nonetheless.
He asks for way too much

By far the kindest professor I've had at Duke. He has a palpable excitement for teaching and is fantastic at lecturing. His grading criteria is sometimes unclear but he's a pretty easy grader so it's not really an issue. He really sticks his neck out to meet and get to know every student, which in a 40-person lecture is very impressive.

Professor Martin is an incredible professor. He made this class genuinely enjoyable and engaging. I had never particularly enjoyed history before taking this course, but his teaching completely changed that for me. I would highly recommend him.

Professor Martin is very kind and deeply cares about his students and his subject. He tries to get to know everyone and has a few out of class meetings that are very relaxed. There are a lot of books and readings, but he does summarize them a bit in class. Half lecture, half discussion. Sign up for this class! It's easy, he just wants you to learn.

Martin was a really passionate professor. Class required a good bit of reading and discussions posts. 3 essays, extracurricular engagement and was definitely work heavy. Overall not too bad but you should definitely stay on top of your work.
The most passionate and intelligent history teacher I have ever had. He will change your perspective on the early modern and contemporary world. Take a class with him. NOW!

I have never learnt so much from one person. He has completely changed how I look at the world. Professor Martin is passionate and cares so much about teaching and learning. It is a reading-heavy class but most history classes are (it was fine for me, even as a freshman). I am genuinely in awe of him. I couldn't rate him more highly.

Professor Martin is great. I took my history gateway seminar with him and even though there was a ton of reading and writing he made the class really interesting. Lots and lots of dull reading that I didn't do but as long as you come to class and talk you're fine. Very interesting guy.
I have never had a more passionate professor.  He truly loves all the material and his enthusiasm really helps what would be an otherwise dry class.  Very reasonable grader.

He is such a great guy, so the conversation were great. The subject matter however, did not interest me at all, and some of the books we read were brutal. Always be prepared because you never know when he will call on you during class.
Great conversations. The subject matter wasn't extremely interesting to me, but I really thought Professor Martin cared about his students, and wanted them to do well.

Professor Martin is a fantastic professor, highly accessible and interested in talking to his students in class and outside of class.  He is passionate about his topic and expects a relatively high level of engagement in his students.  It's a great experience if you're somewhat interested in the topic, though the readings are often difficult.

Prof. Olsavsky is hands down the best CC1 Instructor at DKU. He is very kind, understanding and fun to be around. Do your readings and participate as much as possible in class. He grades really well as well, unlike most CC1 Instructors. Definitely, I would recommend him for a tough and dry course like GCHINA101.
amazing lectures!!! very generous professor !!! if you are interested in history, he is one of the best choice

He is an impressive professor, especially for me. Unfortunately, I'm a Chinese freshman, who has huge professional language problems and knows almost nothing about African history. Since he is so knowledgable and professional, I learn a lot in African history and writing skills. He is always generous if you have a good attitude toward his class!

reviews.comment: Jesse is quite knowledgeable and generous with grade if you work hard. His lectures are well-prepared and really guide you to think comprehensively about the world from a brand-new angle. His feedback on my writing is very helpful. Only thing you have to worry is the workload.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Jesse Olsavsky is clearly knowledgeable about Pan Africanism and it shows. He brings a lot of depth to discussions and is eager to expand on the class material. He sometimes is disrespectful to students that are not following the readings/class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--So many papers--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: More students should know this professor and take his class. As a history professor, he provides inspirational and insightful lectures on the development of American democratic institutions. The knowledge is still quite helpful for me in study. Also, he is approachable and helps his students outside of class--do not agree with the low rate claim.

Prof Jesse seems tough in the beginning but he is a great professor. He gives excellent feedbacks that helps you improve your writing skills. I gained a lot of knowledge and skills. I would recommend his class to everyone
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor olsavsky gives many comments on papers. My writing improved. He met me many times outside class to discuss my questions and give me advise on writing. we read poetry which was hard but the handouts helped.

reviews.comment: It is hard to get in contact with Prof Olsavsky and his lectures are long and unengaging. Won't take his classes again.

reviews.comment: Jesse is one of the greatest professors in history. He is very friendly to his students. He always tries to understand the students' circumstances if they have any issues, for example with deadlines or finding resources. He is also a great storyteller and a master of his subject.
I took American History to 1876 with Prof Olsavsky. He was nice but it was one of his first classes and he had tough grading and talked a lot about himself.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Difficult class, but fulfilling. It's hard bc macro is hard and as a prof exposing you to it for the first time he plays the bad guy. Jurado is extremely smart, cares abt your learning, and makes psets hard (generously graded) so you're prepped for relatively easier exams. Exams: B/A-, Psets: A, ended w/ A, curve built into grade cutoffs.

TAKE THIS CLASS WITH ANOTHER PROFESSOR!!! HEED MY WARNING!! It is lecture heavy, but he always rambles during them. Problem sets take forever, and are graded on accuracy... Curve is nice but the midterms suck. There is also no practice problems or textbooks so you rely on his "midterm reviews", which are vague... Take it in the fall.

To be honest, he is not a very good lecturer...he speeds through every topic he introduces and the problem sets are so difficult... I would avoid taking 210 with him; The curve is nice, but there is no textbook, and the midterms were so bad no matter how much I studied.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Massively underrated. Kyle's class is difficult but extremely fair. Handouts are phenomenally detailed and his lectures are some of the best I've ever attended. There are no shortcuts in this class. You will not do well without 1) going to class, 2) reviewing the handouts on your own time and 3) doing the problem sets without ChatGPT.

Do NOT take this core class with Jurado. Dry lectures where random facts and theories are discussed. The math in this course is frankly egregious. The problem sets take 6-8 hours weekly. They are also graded by accuracy. Not sure what I am learning, not sure why I am relearning quotient and chain rules to apply on long, pointless derivations.
Worst class I have taken at Duke. Unnecessarily difficult and too much material crammed into a semester. Take this class with a different professor.

Kyle is a smart, nice man and explains concepts well. However, the problem sets (8+ hours a week) and exams are way more difficult than what is covered in class. He always stressed "intuition" and expected us to use that on exams instead of adequately preparing us. Do not take this class with him if you want to keep your sanity over the semester.
It would be economically efficient to take this course with another professor.

Problem sets are very difficult and loosely related to class. No textbook to follow. The midterm average was a 66 and is not curved. He does not seem very concerned with the lack of understanding demonstrated by students. Would strongly recommend taking 210 with another professor.

PSETs are extremely time-consuming and barely capture what's learned in class. Also apparently students were doing too well on his PSETs so he decided to make them harder in order to "accurately reflect" the understanding of students. Also Office Hours are basically all after deadline of HW so not really helpful.

Professor Jurado is an extremely clear and engaging lecturer.  Homework can be time-consuming but prepares you well for exams.  This course is more mathematically rigorous than other core classes, and it seems to be adapted from graduate coursework.  However, I highly recommend it for anyone interested in the theoretical side of economics.
Echo 'unnecessarily difficult' and 'needs to read the (class)room.'

An unnecessarily difficult class. The materials seems adapted from his graduate coursework, and there is little support beyond the handouts. The lectures are hard to follow, and, despite the fact that he clearly does care about his students, Professor Jurado isn't able to read the (class)room and figure out when students stop paying attention.
Highly recommended. He'll push your math skills, but you really do feel a deep connection with the concepts.

reviews.comment: No explanation, just vibes. Assumes that reading off a handout equates to explaining concepts.
I have a midterm tomorrow, and you have the opportunity to change this 1 to a 5 Kyle.

He may be brilliant in his field, but it doesn't show in his teaching. The atmosphere felt oppressive, and policies were often enforced in ways that made the course more difficult than necessary. Over time, the experience led to a great deal of self-doubt, and I sought support from the Duke counseling center and my family,......

This professor did a fantastic job in draining me to the bone. I've never felt so worthless, meaningless or helpless at Duke. He has a talent for putting you on the spot and making a lot of my classmates feel uncomfortable. This class pushed me to realize I'm not engineer material in the FASTEST way.
You'll learn to treasure the days this class is not on your schedule. Do yourself a favor and read every other review before you enroll.

Dr. Pastorino is the best prof at Duke! He is incredibly organized and always supports his students. His lectures are highly participated and genuinely loved by everyone. Plus, my Claude skills improved a lot throughout the semester thanks to his class! Highly recommend!

Not sure how this professor is at Duke, but his personality and how he treats students clearly misaligned with the Duke community standards of support and inclusivity. Unless you want to feel like a worthless person at a community college, otherwise don't take his class
WORST professor at Duke. If you currently have him on Dukehub, switch immediately! Don't take any class by this guy

Worst professor I've seen in my 20 years alive. Would rather get cancer than take his class ever again. Such a torture for myself. Stay away from this person. NEVER TAKE HIS CLASS! YOU WILL REGRET IT!!!

The professor have huge character issues, he belittles students and make them feel worthless. You will loss all your interest and confidence in programming. Many of my peers had mental suffering and felt deprived from their passions. I would say take any other professor but him
Take CS201, don't take this class
Very poor lectures, Very unqualified professor
PLEASE PLEASE PLEASE PLEASE PLEASE PLEASE PLEASE PLEASE JUST TAKE CS201. FOR THE SAKE OF YOUR LIFE AND TIME SKIP THIS PROFESSOR AT ALL COSTS!!!!!

I finally got my final grade so now I can speak of the truth. He doesn't know how to teach, like the worst I've seen in my life. You will learn nothing from this class. 99% of the things have to be self taught, you literally don't know what the professor is yapping on stage. For future students, take CS 201, even if you take 105, take another prof.

reviews.comment: Maybe you will get an A, but you will suffer a lot of self doubt, and anxiety. This professor just make you feel you are absolutely nothing and he is everything. In his class, no one understands anything, he just can't teach! It's okay to get a bad grade but it's not okay to feel worthless after a class and it is exactly what this professor does.

This professor ruined all of my confidence and my enthusiasm for engineering. Even ending with an A-, I feel the mental damage on myself is worser than getting an F and dropping out of school. He is a professor that would make you lose all your interest and passions. DO NOT TAKE UNDER ANY CIRCUMSTANCE
The toughest professor on planet earth the exceeds and possible regulations on earth and would absolutely make your time at duke a nightmare, no other word could describe
For ECE juniors and seniors, don't take this professor, chose anyone else. He will make your life 100 times worser
Don't take it, you will regret it, change a track if needed

Hi Friends, this was my first semester at Duke and it was absolutely ruined because of this class and this professor. I would suggest future freshman who have to take this class take it with Lipp or any other professor.
This professor made a 1/10 difficulty class 10000/10, never ever met such a mean professor in my entire life. DO NOT TAKE IT
Don't take it. It will give you PTSD. For the sake of your life and mental health, take CS 201
Worst class ever! Never taking this guys class ever again, worst experience in my entire life!

Very irresponsible and super mental draining. This professor made me question my life many times. I would frame it this way, even if you take this class and get an A, you would be happier with getting a C in another class because you will be hyper depressed. For first years, don't let this be your first experience with duke engineering, take CS 201
