reviews.comment:
Dr.Pastorino is an enthusiastic professor and willing to help students.
But be aware of:
(1) unfixed office hours: u have to make an appointment before meeting.
(2) the homework grading system is not satisfacotry: the readme file do not always tell you every detail of a homework (e.g. whether to raise exceptions in some corner case.)
Not a pleasant experience, had a lot of stress and mental breakdowns, would not recommend this professors for freshman who are trying to adapt and have a relaxed semester.

Dr. Pastorino is a great professor. While I don't agree with the amount of work assigned and attendance being mandatory, I learned something each lecture. As long as you do your homeworks ON TIME (not night of) and ask questions about program requirements, you will be fine. Pastorino thrives on answering questions so just ask if you are confused.

Never in my life have I felt so stressed, helpless, and crushed by a class. It's been an absolute nightmare. I've had breakdowns, felt constantly treated like a criminal just for trying to learn, and I genuinely don't understand why I'm looked at like I'm failing at life. I've never experienced anything this mentally exhausting. I just want to cry!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Genuinely the WORST professor at Duke ever. I took this course along with Linear and Physics, and this class was the WORST out of all my classes. The sheer amount of pain in this class made me want to quit being an engineer. Several classmates reported their mental health declining due to the grading and workload from this class. Take CS 201.

I've seen war vets less traumatized than the students in this class. This professor makes the most mundane tasks look like quantum physics. This professor gaslights you more than the USSR during the Cold War. Getting an A is genuinely impossible. This professor might genuinely be the antichrist. Do NOT take this course unless held at gunpoint!
Highly NOT Recommended
The most outrageous professor I've ever seen. Tons of assignments, the most boring lectures, and they always go overtime. Even during reading week, they still have to teach.
Pretty good. Easy class
He's okay. I mean it's hard to understand him sometimes but it's okay
disorganized prof, doesnt know what he's doing. diff projects are completely diff levels & can't be compared
He was okay. Class was fine but could be more organized. He is very kind and understanding
Great professor
He doesn't know what he's doing when he's assigning work/labs. Hugely disorganized, torturous class. Do NOT TAKE!!! If you don't have to!!!!

Everything I've done in this class is against my will. I would rather be waterboarded for 99 years than be made to take this joke they call a class. The only reason this man is getting a one star from me is because I can't get any lower- but trust me, if I could give 0, I would.

Prof Pastorino is kind, patient, and supportive for his students. When my team failed our AMP project twice, he warmly invited us to his office and gave us another chance to present. Before fall break, when I was late and even overslept a project day, he kindly encouraged me to take better care of myself. After that, I never missed another class.

He is so clueless and disorganized. I wish I could give him 0 stars but the minimum is 1. Horrible experience would not recommend. Take only if there is no other option in the world. I would rather get stage 4 cancer.

As other people mentioned he can be relatively disorganized. However, he truly has a great grasp of the topics he teaches, and is a great resource if you attend office hours. It can be difficult at times to figure out what he is looking for, but once you do, the courses are pretty easy. He is also very nice.

Not the best lecturer but he is so sweet. He is a bit disorganized and I didn't learn so much coding from him but he is good natured and class has good vibes. Helpful is you schedule 1 on 1 office hours with him
Very boring class with poor instruction. He was not very helpful with assignments and inaccesible outside of class.
This professor is wildly unorganized, does not care about time, and I truly do not think he knows what he is doing when he assigns projects or labs. Do not take a course with him if not necessary.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very dogmatic, unclear homework requirements.
Does an awful job at preparing labs and providing instruction for project. Mediocre at best in instruction. Do not take his class if it is not mandatory.
He is very good at torturing students, lecture level is poor

worst, most frustrating professor at Duke. Feedback will be strong, yet the scores will be low bc they don't understand how fractions work. Never met anyone so absent of thoughts yet condescending, it's a Christmas miracle.
Talks down to students. I struggled to find the lectures engaging or valuable.

Very negative experience. The instructor consistently came across as condescending and dismissive, with a clear “better than you” tone toward students. Feedback often felt generic and disconnected from what was actually submitted, as if assignments weren't read. Classes taught nothing. I would not recommend this prof.

I had Professor Zhao for an 8:30 ethics lecture that lasted 2 and 1/2 hours. I thought I was going to hate that class with every fiber of my being as it wasn't 8:30 ethics class yet it was a class I was always excited to go to which is a real testament to his ability.
Arguably one of the best polsci professor I had! Very engaging class activities and good amount of workload.

Personally I think that the way the professor conducts the classes is particularly good, always in dialogue with the class and open to hear perspectives. Even though the readings are many and at times difficult the professor in class goes over them and explains them really well and carefully answering all clarification questions. Great professor!

He is a very kind and supportive professor. He gives good feedback and is easily accessible outside of class and through email. The readings were quite heavy, but the lectures were very engaging and easy to follow. I would take his class again!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: So far, one of the best professors at DKU. Excellent!!!!! The course was well-organized and the grading was excellent. Able to learn a lot.
Would takes his class again. He makes the learning process very interesting
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very enthusiastic to share his library of knowledge with students. Gives good, actionable feedback on writing assignments. Cool teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: He was a very nice and friendly professor. He would bring snacks for us almost every class, there was a lot of reading but the workload itself was overall difficult but manageable. He also gave helpful feedback during optional office hours. He is also very passionate about the subjects he teaches. Would overall take his class again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Heavy workload with not much support from the professor. He's funny and personable, but that doesn't help us learn.

Dr. Kim is an extremely caring and accommodating professor. Homeworks were a bit tedious at the beginning of the semester, but he tapered down as the workload of the semester progressed. Quizzes had clear expectations and were straightforward. Provides lots of opportunities for improving your grade. PBL was a lot of work but a good experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Cares a lot about his students and improving his class/teaching skills. He has a lot of bad reviews in earlier semesters but he clearly shows how much he cares about the class by making necessary changes! Really great guy and knowledgeable!!!

- A lot of work. I spent the most time on this course, more than Wallace's 244 if you've ever heard about it.
- Lectures not easy to follow. A lot of contents in one lecture
- Dr. Kim was accessible outside of lecture and was nice. He just committed to too many responsibilities so he doesn't prioritize lecturing as much as some other profs do.

Dr. Kim really cares about his students and is always looking for feedback to improve his classes and the BME department. He has brought so many amazing changes (like expanding to more biotech/biological engineering). He's very accessible outside of class, and he's been an amazing mentor for many people for deciding careers and post-grad education.

Cameron Kim assigned a problem set and 2 take home quizzes on the last day of classes. Do with that information what you will.

Otherwise, he is a likable person and is relatively accessible outside of class. However, his unorganized lectures and his inability to properly schedule assignments (^^^) mean he has a lot to improve as a professor.

BME260 is a lot of work: psets, PBLs, content quizzes, and mastery problems. Dr. Kim isn't the most organized professor and his lectures are mundane, but he does care about his students. However, he is flexible with the mass amounts of work he assigns. PBLs are group-dependent and will make or break the class. Overall Kim is a caring, funny guy.

It's possible that Dr. Kim has potential, but he's not there yet. His lectures are pretty nonsensical and the group projects are just a ridiculous amount of work. "This is how it's always been," is also a poor excuse for the class structure. But, he is really kind, understanding, flexible, and an easy grader. One day, he may even be great.
Really nice professor. A lot of assignments.
Amazing teacher! Super nice and cares about his students!

I really enjoyed the class, since, while covering challenging topics and the lectures being very equation-heavy at times, Dr. Kim tried his best to make complex topics accessible and engaging. He created a very safe learning atmosphere. Definitely not an easy class, but overall a very interesting class that stands out due to its unique structure.

These other 1-star ratings seem to hyperbolically exacerbate suffering within his class. Kim was an above-average lecturer. He used good humor and tried his best to make content digestible. The slides are dull and the curriculum is overloaded. But, he doesn't deserve to be discredited, especially since he has cut workload from previous semesters.

Kim is very passionate about his teaching, but at times seems like he's got too many fires in the oven. That being said, I don't understand the other reviews complaining about equations or PBLs. You are an engineer, grow up or drop the major if you can't handle it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Don't be fooled by Kim writing his own 5 star reviews. Keeping it real with you, this class is atrocious. Never before has something demotivated me more. The anger is inexpressible, but eventually it eats away at you to where you lose feeling in your soul. Can't blame the creator of PBLs. It's too late. But Kim...this excuse for teaching is on him

Halfway through the semester, I started hating god for giving me the legs to walk to class. Every class is somehow worse than the last. I showed the content to my very successful BME friends and they laughed in my face at the structure, content, and PBLs. The class is saddening, maddening, and a single compliment for Kim is just not happening.

In the world of biomedical engineering, he is a professor who shapes a legacy of innovation. Kim has set the bar for future professors. Never in my life have I had a professor who ensured that I did not learn a single thing. You would think that with the unreasonable amount of work, I would learn something, but there's a first time for everything.

Real talk. Everyone writing a 1-star review is probably lazy af and will drop BME in the future and I would laugh to see them take any 500 level. Kim goes to lengths to make this class easier than it used to be. Quizzes are online open note. Instead of tests, you literally do mastery problems w/ partners. psets are literally right out of lecture.

Awful awful awful. I think the only people who like Kim are those who are genuinely terrible at BME, because only someone like that would not realize how full of it Kim is. Pretending like he's teaching, while it's honestly just a lame excuse for a lecture. I am really sorry for those who have to go through his class and are smart. Just atrocious.

God forbid you take a BME class where you have to.. do BME. 260, specifically the PBLs, is the most directly applicable class to any higher BME level course or BME research you do. The PBLs separate what you'd do as a bio/chem major versus BME. This class is very much so "it is what you make of it", and if people are so negatively rating it then..

Dreams crushed, mornings blue,
Equations hurl, spirits rue.
Humor dry, disappointment brew,
Kim is like a walrus in the zoo.

Learning joy, lost in view,
In BME, a dismal hue.
Lectures dry, confusion grew,
Regret in class, very true.

PBLs pointless, guidance few,
Time sinks deep, benefit accrue.
In this class, understanding flew,
If only I knew...

Dr. Kim is so funny ... if you don't have a sense of humor. I was hopeful, and to be fair Kim is consistent, consistently disappointing. This class makes me depressed and has ruined me entire semester and Duke experience. It's a load of work, for no reason, and if you learn a single thing, you're in the minority. Never take a class with the Kimster

I'm frankly dissapointed every time I have to enter his class. 260 has so much potential, but he manages to make the class a pain to sit through. Could not dissuade you guys from taking him enough. Awful awful professor.

Duke's insult to the BME department. A lackluster performance every class by an unseasoned lecturer. The class is pointless, which may not be Kim's fault, but the terrible class structure is. Psets, mastery problems, PBLs, content quizzes, an unreasonable amount of time for 0 learning. Take it with saterbak if you value your mental health.

I hate this class. I went through a rough patch in my relationship because of this class. On numerous instances, has this class made me not want to get out of bed in the morning. To top it all off, I haven't learned a single useful thing. In some world, Kim may be a nice lecturer, just not this one.

He is genuinely just an awful lecturer. I'm tired of giving him the benefit of the doubt. The lectures have proceeded to get progressively harder to follow, and even if I'm interested in the class, he manages to make the content impossible to digest. Just take this class with Saterbak, its horrible with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: His lectures are extremely dry. He does random derivations without explanations, and his psets are absolutely useless. The PBL project is not fun at all, and he genuinely does not seem to care if what he teaches is useful. Not to mention, it's the most time-sucking BME course I've taken. Would not recommend to my worst enemy.

This class is more work than BME244 some weeks but guaranteed you won't learn a useful thing. You have to go to lecture but lectures are wordy, complex, and convoluted with no actual content. PBLs can be the bane of your existence with a bad group. Kim gives horrible guidance and no rubric (what a surprise)! Easily worst BME class I have ever taken

Dr. Kim probably will be a great professor in a few years, since it's clear he really cares about students and their experience in his class. However, he's not particularly engaging, and there's several very difficult group projects that felt rather unsupported (potentially a side effect of class structure). Overall a quality choice for BME 260.

Dr. Kim is an excellent professor. He's accommodating, caring, and is willing to work with you regardless of the circumstance. He gives great explanations and makes the material clear. The Mastery Problems in this course are also a wonderful alternative to exams. However, Problem Sets and PBLs can be very time-consuming, so prepare for that.

Dr. Kim was really great! His lectures were clear, and homework and exams were very straightforward. He was always so willing to help too. Would definitely take this class with him again. My only complaint was that the group project was a lot of work and difficult to manage as it was a randomly assigned group during COVID.

Dr. Kim is a great Professor. This was his first time teaching at Duke and had to tackle online learning at the same time. Definitely a lot of work to be done between homework assignments and group projects which is typical of BME260, but he is understanding with conflicts in schedules and will work with you. He also really cares about his students
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Group projects

reviews.comment: Great professor, but decent work
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Knust is incredibly knowledgeable and passionate about Religious Studies. I learned so much about the field and multiple different religious communities in her class. Class was really interactive, which I liked a lot. Dr. Knust also really cares about her students as people, and I've enjoyed getting to know her outside of class too.

Overall, the class was super disorganized. The grading criteria was sporadic, chaotic, and random and Knust did not give proper feedback. Also her feedback was somewhat demeaning and passive aggressive. In class, she's a great lecturer and overall very nice but it takes more than being nice to be a good professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Don't take. Only class I've ever withdrawn from. Her grading is erratic and harsh with like 0 feedback. I got Covid and she was insanely passive aggressive and not at all understanding. Tons of reading, material is all over the place. Class is pointless, weird activities and very little lecturing. Feels like preschool or something.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: She cares about the class but her grading on papers is based on criteria that is excessively vague with an erratic grading style that takes off vast numbers of points for minor issues that are completely unrelated to the ideas of a paper. If you are interested in learning about a specific religion I suggest avoiding this class.
One of my favorite professors at Duke, Professor Knust cares a lot about her students and wants you to succeed. If you put in the time and effort, you will get a lot out of this class.

Dr. Knust was an incredibly caring professor, and gave engaging lectures that definitely illuminated her love for her craft. The class isn't really difficult, but that allowed for it to feel less like an item on the to-do list and more like something I looked forward to every Tuesday and Thursday.

Possibly the nicest and most accommodating prof I've had in 4 years. She cares so much about her students and genuinely wants everyone to pass with an A. I took "the end of the world" with her and learned about religious history without it seeming boring. The apocalypse theme turned out to be unfortunately relevant but she stayed super positive.

Jenny really cares for her students! She makes sure to be accessible outside of class, and even began bringing snacks after students unanimously requested them. Amazing women, but sometimes expects slightly more out of us than possible, particularly in the research project conducted throughout the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Kyle's BME 354 was a great class. It was my first BME course where I worked hands-on with circuitry, and throughout the semester I built a lot of confidence in my abilities. Dr. Kyle made himself available through office hours and was always willing to answer questions. He is also a strong lecturer, which made the material easier to understand.

Design class that's a waste of time. The entirety of the first semester is about doing research and writing reports, and most of your time in the 2nd semester is spent on weekly progress reports, progress meetings, and progress videos instead of actual design work. The final for the class involves a poster, a 10 minute video, and a 100+ page report
He is amazing, approachable, and genuinely wants you to succeed to the best of your abilities. I highly recommend coming to his office hours and talking to him!

I loved Dr. Kyle's course because it was centered around the components of a pacemaker. He is a phenomenal lecturer, and he is patient with you when you don't understand something. I am taking his two-semester design course right now because of how much I loved his course and teaching style. It's clear he's passionate about his job!
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Not my advising professor for EGR101, but an amazing lecturer nonetheless, one of the most clear speakers I've had the privilege of learning from. I feel like I learned a lot from him even though I'm Mech E and he's BME, because after sitting in on EGR101 classes with other professors I realized how much better of a speaker Dr. Kyle is.

Very patient and articulate professor. Pushes you to flesh out your ideas as an engineer, which may make him seem overbearing, but it helps you learn. Reasonable with grading, and is generally interesting to talk to. I didn't find him the best at getting me excited about the course materials, though - more good as a person than a teacher.

Dr. Kyle genuinely cared about the class and his students, creating an environment where I felt supported in learning the engineering process. The course provided meaningful feedback and numerous opportunities to practice the engineering process and improve our projects.
He is terrible. He should do better.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Kyle is knowledgeable on the content. While his lectures are tedious, he really teaches you the content. My only issue was his grading. He has unclear rubrics, low tolerances for questions, and has the most ludicrous pre labs assigned on Fridays and due on Fridays. Makes me questions if he has fun in making us struggle. One of those toxic profs

What a joke. Ended up with 90% + on this class, he went against his syllabus and gave me a whole letter grade lower. What a joke. He is rude, condescending, and does not understand digital systems (only analog). His lectures are terrible. Duke should reconsider him. Take it with Nightingale, at least she is respected in the field.

Instrumentation with Dr. Kyle was excellent. I was finally able to understand concepts I'd been taught multiple times before because of how well he explained things. Pretty easy grading and no exams except midterm practical. Very hands-on lab-based course that feels fun and practical. Clear that a lot of intention was put into designing the course.

I was nervous to take her class after seeing this page esp bc this topic isn't my strong area, but it was great. Her lectures were very organized, interesting, and clear. The homework was useful, and tests were fair. She even met w/ students individually who wanted to earn half credit on tests -- you can tell she genuinely cares about her students.
I took 201 with her. I don't know why everyone is complaining; she's an amazing, caring professor
Her slides are giant blocks of text which aren't even her own. Literally did not understand anything in lecture, everything taught was extremely unclear
AVOID AT ALL COSTS. Her class made me want to jump off the chapel.
Negative ratings on here confused me ngl

idk why ppl hatin, not a bad class. it's many ppls first proof-focused math course, hard stuff to grasp no matter who's teaching. Prof's nice and cares abt understanding, makes time outside of lecture, if u put in the effort(esp w/proofs & problem solving), go to OH (which were often empty!), do hw, you'll do fine. Not an ez A but very doable.

Torture. Would rather drop out of Duke than take this class again. She covers a month's worth of material covered in 1 lecture. When she goes on tangents and doesn't finish material, instead of covering next class she expects us to self-teach and then weighs that material EXTRA heavily on exams. Rude and unknowledgeable about almost all topics.

Kate O'Hanlon is a great professor and honestly I was *incredibly* confused after seeing her current RMP score being so low. I've had great interactions, lectures are useful, and homework is not excessive. Genuinely good class and enjoyable, also brought us candies and sweets several times!!! Take classes with Kate O'Hanlon
made me want to end it all tbh 0/10

absolutely atrocious. Slides are completely unreadable and she intentionally takes out anything that might have a sliver of value when she posts them to Canvas. It is impossible to learn anything in this course. She's a nice person but good god she makes this course awful I would rather jump off the chapel than have her as my professor respectfully

Do NOT take CS230 with her. I consider myself a smart person with strong calc/logic foundations, and this class hit me like a truck. Insanely confusing lectures and nearly impossible tests (she says she intentionally includes questions she KNOWS we won't understand). The average on the final was a 67%. You couldn't pay me $1 million to take again.

Lectures are walls of text that fail to explain any of the concepts behind them. It is impossible to learn anything in this course. Tests are completely unreasonable in terms of what we're expected to do in the time alotted. I feel like I could have really enjoyed this class had it been taught by someone else.
Terrible. Just terrible. Avoid at all costs.
Not very knowledgeable on course material, seemed unprepared. Felt like I was in a foreign language class because 90% of the lectures were math vocabulary (and not anything relevant or important)

lectures are blocks of text on the screen she reads off of. exams are way too long for the amount of time we're given and the topics list for exams are literally multiple pages long. she's nice and well-meaning, but the course is run horribly

She's one of the worst professors I've ever had at Duke. Her lecture slides aren't organized well and she somehow manages to explain concepts in the most unintuitive manner possible. She also isn't accessible outside of class.

She cannot explain concepts well or answer questions. The slides are disorganized, content is all over the place. She cannot read the room, or if she does, still does not care to repeat a concept if the class looks confused. Don't take this class with Prof. Kate if you want to learn or at least care about your mental health.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Impossible to understand

Class enrollment rate was so low we did roll call attendance. Exploited TAs to explain anything math-related. Freaked out if previous prof's slides didnt have exact answers to student questions. Projected her own insecurities onto students and TAs. Would NOT post answers to practice tests but they r on the OG prof's course website

Do not EVER take a class with Professor O'Hanlon. I saw her make fun of a TA who was trying to help a student. It left him distraught and nearly in tears, saying "I would never sell you out to a student like that." If she treats her TAs like that, just imagine how she treats students. Rude and treats every question as a personal affront to her ego.
Why does it seem like there is no good 230 professor...

She briefly spoke about buying people on a max weight bipartite matching slide. "Whether it's right to do that, I won't say, it's happened, but I'm not an ethics professor, we'll focus on LP" I think she meant to be funny. She could've said that that's wrong or not have said that. That's one example. She makes the room uncomfortable at times.
Avoid like the plague.

O'Hanlon does a poor job of clarifying and delving into concepts, leaving the students to rely on the TAs and each other to learn the course material. I didn't even mind the in-class daily quizzes; I just wished I could answer them accurately after the lecture instead of going home and searching for YouTube videos that were better than the lecture.

Kate makes this class so convoluted that it's better to go to online sources to learn the material than go to the required lectures. Clarification questions would be waved over, and there's no explanation of the logic behind the curve in this class. A lot of decisions feel arbitrary.

Kate means well but this class was a trainwreck. Unclear lectures with tangents in the material that made knowing what concepts were important for exams very difficult. Each lecture had these quizzes that had strangely scattered focus of comprehension questions.

Kate tries, and she's a good person just a horrible lecturer. I think the professor is not well versed with the material. I found myself more confused with slides + lecturs than just using the internet. Teaching myself discrete to do some crazy hard homeworks is not what I expected to endure. Crazy final for things she could never solve herself.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Unnecessarily harsh grading for homeworks and exams. Even the TAs agreed it didn't need to be that harsh. Also really disliked her participation grade policy: she dropped 25 quiz points for the whole semester but if you enrolled at the end of drop-add, 15 of those would be gone due to the first two weeks. Why not just readjust it??
Do not, at any point, consider taking a course with Kate. Wonderful and energetic person, but she will make your life miserable with work you were not properly prepared to tackle.

Awful professor and lecturer, she is so bad at explaining topics that it seems she doesn't even know what she is talking about. Homework and exams were terrible as well, with grading that made no sense. Never answered a single email the entire semester either. Avoid at all costs
As much as I would love to give O'Hanlong a good rating for her charm, her unabashed dismissal of students in this class overshadows that, by far.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Incredibly disorganized class that had TAs and students alike in anguish. Please for the love of god do NOT take it with Professor O'Hanlon unless you want to flush an entire semester down the drain. Also, the ASTRONOMIC rates of cheating in this class is an open secret. Honestly a joke of a class and the only saving grace is the TAs.

Her lectures are sloppily paced and often spend way more time on a niche example or unnecessary content than the stuff you're actually going to be assessed on. Homeworks are a grind with extremely unclear grading criteria. Her tests are way too long and difficult, and no matter how much you study she'll still find a way to ask a BS quesiton.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The undergrad TAs did a significantly better job at recitation than she ever could during lecture. They weren't even her slides. Definitley would not take again and wish I would have waited a semester to take the course with literally anyone else.

She struggles to explain any concept, so we have to learn from the TAs. As for the tests, the timing is terrible. She figures that, if the TAs can finish the test with 5 minutes left, then every other student should be able to comfortably finish. These tests don't test problem-solving skill, but rather ability to read and write fast.

She gives long rambling lectures, and when asked questions, she gives extremely vague and sometimes incorrect answers. There are quizzes every day of class, often with confusing wording. The only that kept me from completely failing this class was the fact that the TAs know what they are talking about (any of them could teach better than the prof)

Class is hard to understand because the professor clearly hasn't mastered the material. Has difficulty answering questions in lecture and often provides vague or incorrect answers. Very annoying in-class quizzes every lecture and the questions/answers are extremely ambiguous.

Most difficult class of my entire life. She never once answered any of my emails, even when other professors for this class told me to email her, and even when she emailed me first to "offer resources". Clear disregard for if students do well and most students assumed they would fail out due to the 40-50% averages on exams. Do not take this class.

CS 230 is probably one of the easiest classes that I took during the summer. People complain that it's hard but it's probably because they don't listen during the lectures. Class is literally trivial but also very interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Do not take a class with O'Hanlon if you can help it. She is a mediocre teacher at best. Disorganized, she makes big changes to grading and exams last minute, including taking points off for something. In my class of 50 last summer, over 50% signed a petition to the Dean to make the class S/U because of how disorganized and chaotic everything was.

The guidelines of this class were very clear right from the start. A lot of people complained, but honestly, I felt that they weren't really willing to work for it since we were at home. This is a CRUCIAL class for the CS major, and it's not something you should just be able to get by. It's work, but it's interesting, and Kate is really helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Genuinely one of the kindest and most understanding professors I've ever had at Duke. Concepts were broken down well, so tests were not super hard if you paid attention to class. Definitely take micro with Prof Leventoglu if you can!

Good lecturer and breaks down game theory very easily in class with a little more depth on the problem sets. Exams were fairly easy and tested a very basic understanding of the game theory concepts she taught. She's is super super super sweet and cares a lot about her students. The kindest economics professor I've had!
it is very possible to get 100 on all three tests and she also curves even if the median is like a 90. she's awesome.
The best econ professor I've had at Duke. She is the absolute best.

Super super interesting class. Prof Leventoglu is a great lecturer and really knows her subject material. She's a very nice person, extremely smart and knowledgeable, but math 221 is really hard for people who don't have a solid background in writing proofs and linear algebra in advance. Quizzes every other week and lectures go extremely fast. She does try her best to make sure you don't fail and you understand the materials.

Linear Algebra, by itself, is a hard class and proof-based linear algebra is even harder. But I feel Professor Pierce made it even harder as she did not consider that many of the students taking the class were new to proofs. The structure of the class made it good for those who could rely on self-studying and bad otherwise.

Pierce is great if you are genuinely interested in mathematical thinking. She answers every question in class thoroughly. Lectures can be fast if you aren't making sure you understand at every step, but they always are very coherent. She's also very sweet and enthusiastic, she giggles a lot when lecturing. Quizzes and midterms heavily proof-based.

If you don't have much prior experience with proofs then I would consider taking 221 with another professor, especially if you have a heavy courseload. That being said, I absolutely loved professor Pierce. She definetly wants to challenge her students, but she also really wants them to succeed!

She's an incredible person - her research and her life is insane. Learning from such a mind is a privilege and although it can be tough at times, she is extremely understanding and will make a lot of accommodations. Also one of the sweetest professors I've ever met!

Fantastic, knowledgeable professor, very understanding and accommodating. First class where you learn how to learn math. That said, this might be the most difficult class I have ever taken at Duke, and I am done with the CS major.

I have to say that linear algebra is a tough class regardless of who is teaching the course, and the class might be too much for a non-math major student. However, if you are passionate about math, don't hesitate to take this class! Prof Pierce has done a such amazing job explaining concepts and theorems in LA. Would love to take her class again!

This class was alright. It's an extremely difficult course and Dr. Pierce neither helped nor hindered anyone's given ability to do well in the class. Her lectures are good, but I know that many people leave lecture confused, but this could just be due to the difficulty of the material. Tests are extremely difficult, but I wouldn't call them unfair.

Prof. Pierce is a well-respected expert in her field and is definitely caring and accessible outside of class. However, she might have assumed that everybody in her class is passionate to be a math major and already knows hard math. If you are really into math, Prof. Pierce's class would be very inspirational. If not,  the course would be hard.

History of math is a super interesting class. Definitely gives you a perspective you probably wouldn't have had before, and Professor Pierce is passionate and knowledgeable about the subject material. That being said, the workload for this class is insane!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor Pierce is very well-respected in her field and understanding if you reach out to her for help. The problems I had were with the amount of work and the complexity of the content. There were weekly problem sets, 2 oral exams, a large group project, and a large final paper, despite the class being pass/fail this semester.

Pierce may seem a bit cold (partially due to her intimidating intelligence) at first but she is a good person who cares about her students and has a passion for her subject. She understands that not everyone is a math major and avoids using redundant terminology. We somehow managed to get through a #theory class without groups, rings, and fields.
Hardest class I've ever taken. Destroyed my confidence to do a Math major. She is very nice and gives challenging materials, but really doesn't give very easy-to-grasp explainations.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Pierce is insanely smart but she forgets that she's teaching freshmen because she expects you to understand really complicated topics and is too intimidating to ask questions. Her class is designed for upperclassmen and the problem sets take days to do even when you're working in a group. There's a final and a paper due and it consumes your life.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Pierce is difficult, but it's worth it. Problem sets were tough and graded toughly, and tests were even tougher (and grader more toughly). There is a writing component of the course, making it even more challenging. But put in the hard work--it's rewarding! (On another note, she's also an amazing person whose super successful... Just look her up!)

Cryptography and Society was an incredibly difficult class. I was rarely able to meet with her outside class for office hours, and I needed some revision because in class she is so fast paced, it is really challenging to follow.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: This class was one of the hardest class I've taken at Duke. Pierce is super smart and her lectures go super fast. You HAVE to spend time understanding things outside class (in addition to the rigorous weekly homework). While I think she as a teacher is really hard and rigorous, she is one of the nicest people I've met and she is so accommodating.

While her class was the most difficult course at Duke I have ever taken, Professor Pierce makes a great source of help for her failing students.  I've fallen behind in her class numerous times (due to not understanding the material as easily as my other classmates), but she was willing to meet with me to help and I ended up passing the class.

Professor Pierce was an amazing professor. She really wanted you to do well, she was available to help, and she ensured that you understand the material on a very deep level. Not going to lie,the class was very difficult, but I've never learned more in a class at Duke.

Hard class. But she really wants you to succeed and learn the topic. Very accessible and the nicest professor! Class is helpful because she stops to make sure everyone knows what's going on. Also the smartest and most accomplished person I've met thus far at Duke.

Lillian is awesome. She is not an easy professor - in fact, hers was the hardest section among the four 221 Linear Algebra sections thought the semester I took it. However, she is an awesome professor: she is fast paced, but she makes sure that her proofs have proper mathematical rigour. Moreover, she is really friendly and nice.

She's a very nice person who cares about how her students do in the class.  The problem is that her classes are so incredibly fast-paced that I had trouble keeping up with the textbook reading outside of class and was perpetually lost during lectures. That said, she is always willing to help, if you know what to ask.
hard class

Prof. Pierce is very friendly and really cares about her students passing. She is definitely a somewhat quirky person, but her lectures are interesting and not too difficult to follow. There is a lot of homework every week as well as occasional quizzes and exams, but nothing out of the ordinary for a Duke math class. Overall, I would recommend her.

Lectures are unbearably boring, yet you essentially have to go (or read through all the slides thoroughly) because the grading on tests is so nitpicky for phrasing and derivation stuff. The group project is also hard and heavily depends on whether your group is good or not.
Lectures are boring, and grading is strict. Even made all my midterms 90+ still need a 95 on the final to get an A

Lectures were a bit boring, but make sure you attend them since they go over the mathematical derivations and model interpretations exactly as you should know them. You should be proficient in linear algebra, because practically everything in the course is based on matrixes. Also, be proactive with your teammates on the group project.

really loved this class and dr. tackett was an amazing professor tbh. her lectures were very clear and easy to follow along with, and she always posted her notes which i found helpful. tests are really not bad at all if you just memorize interpretations that we go over and know how to do simple derivations. wish she would post answer keys though

Felt like the class was very test-heavy and my understanding of the concepts was not always reflected in my test scores. Need to spend a lot of time studying for the tests. Also the group project really is hard if your teammates are not good
One of the best professors I've had at Duke hands down. Very accessible outside class, clearly cares about students and helping us learn the content well. Ask questions.

Tackett is great and very nice. Like all stats classes, 221 grading is very nitpicky and takes off ridiculous points for small things. You need to go to office hours to get the exact wording for labs and HWs. Don't have both a lab and HW every week. Exams are difficult, make sure to know exact interpretations. Group project is annoying.

The most well-structured class I've taken at Duke, Tackett also explains tough concepts in efficient ways and answers questions in lecture with clarity. Super nice and approachable. Workload is manageable, exams are on the tougher side but line up with lecture material fairly (recommend reviewing lecture slides thoroughly).
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Class took what was great about 210 and ruined it. While intended to be primarily R-based, tests are only

STA 221 is a tough class with heavy grading. It involves weekly labs, 4 homework assignments, a semester-long project, and 2 exams. The material itself isn't too difficult, but memorizing phrasing and wording is time-consuming. Professor Tackett and the TAs are great, but the class structure and grading are unnecessarily harsh.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Tackett was very sweet and an excellent lecturer. She did a great job of conveying the material in an accessible and enjoyable manner. In Fall 2023, the class shifted from online to in-person tests which had minimal partial credit, which led to a drop of grades. Grading overall, like in all duke stat courses, was very nitpicky.
amazing professor

Honestly I feel like Tackett is one of the best professors at Duke. She really cares about teaching and making sure you understand whats going on in the classroom. Her class is graded pretty strictly but thats by nature because Statistics is a field where how you say something matters a lot.
I really like Professor Tackett's teaching style. She is an inspiration, and I feel motivated to actually pay attention in class and take my time doing the homework to fully understand the concepts.

Professor Tackett cares so deeply for her students and makes sure class is as engaging and manageable as possible! Seriously one of the best professors I have had at Duke. She will always make time for you and you can tell teaching is her passion. You will learn a lot in this class without the stress that comes along with many classes at Duke!
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Must take if you are interested in stat/data science. Everything is open book take home and you have tons of time to complete. Professor is nice and accessible outside classroom, and she gives wonderful lecture to make R learnable even for those w/o coding background. Group project is fun, but can depends on team members you are assigned.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Easily one of my favorite courses at Duke. The class structure was clearly organized, and there was a good balance of individual and group assignments. While this course has a decent lot of work, the learning objectives of each assignment were very clear. Some of the TA's weren't so helpful, but it helped that Dr. Tackett replied to emails promptly
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Tackett is great; very knowledgeable, very good at teaching, and very clearly cares about her students. A bunch of people never came to lecture because they're recorded and you only have to come to 80% to get full attendance (I skipped the last 3 completely.) Everything is open note; people who relied on that usually did poorly. A if you try.

STA 199 with Prof. Tackett was great. The class is very valuable, and she did a great job keeping students engaged. Especially if you took AP Statistics in high school, this is a fairly easy and straightforward class that teaches you how to code in R.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Tackett taught STA210 in a flipped classroom setting, where she gave us short videos to watch outside of class and focused on applying these concepts in R during lectures. Her explanations are clear & concise, & she's willing to answer any question you may have. She's approachable & kind & definitely one of my favorite professors at Duke!

Tackett's a pretty good lecturer. Try to do well on the quizzes because she grades pretty hard on the final project. You can either get full credit, half credit, or 0 points on the written report, which is graded pretty harshly. There's a lot of teamwork involved. Overall manageable, but not super easy.

Professor Tackett gives extremely clear lectures and is very willing to answer questions in depth without being condescending. She responds very quickly to emails and piazza posts. Quizzes were extremely difficult and based on material that wasn't covered well in lecture, but the class overall is manageable.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Tackett is one of the best STA professors. She suffers from STA 210 being one of many unfortunate STA classes with the same exact format where you learn basically only about linear regressions and then do a final project in R. Given the format, she's great though -- very thorough slides and always available, clear, answers all your questions, etc
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Tackett is the best!! Take any stats class she teaches, her classes are super well organized, slides and lectures are really clear and she's also a super cool, all-around respected and awesome professor.

I really enjoyed STAT 199. Professor tacket is extremely well versed in R programming and is very informative. She was also easy to get into contact with and responded to emails and Piazza posts quickly. The TAs were all amazing too and extremely helpful. I would highly recommend this class. No programming experience necessary.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Group projects

reviews.comment: Very responsive to student feedback and makes lectures interactive and enjoyable beyond just the course material.

Took both STA 199 and 210 with Dr. Tackett. Both classes had a 4-person lab group that you worked with the entire semester. The workload was nothing crazy, but sometimes due dates for several assignments fell within a couple of days. Dr. Tackett herself was an engaging professor and clearly cares about her students.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Group projects

reviews.comment: Great professor that cares about learning environment and student's success. Office hours were early in the morning so a bit inconvenient, but worth it. R-based class so make sure you can pick it up decently. Group project at end. Hope you get good group. Enthusiastic and topics were fun!
Maria is super accessible outside of class. She has done impressive work and makes lectures super interesting with cool applications of the material

I've had Prof Tackett for two different classes now (199 and 210), and she's truly an amazing teacher. Her slides are really well made, and she's very organized and her expectations are very clear. It's not hard to succeed if you put the work in. You can tell she really cares about her students. Take her class!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Tackett is a reasonable teacher who is very organized and really wants everyone to understand. Her class doesn't go very far into the math or theory behind regression which can be frustrating, but it makes her lectures easy and understandable

Tackett is a very energetic lecturer and always patient when answering questions. Consistent weekly workload, but not overwhelming; HW and labs were generally straightforward, as were the two midterms. Grading was a bit picky sometimes, but it's easy to do well overall. As long as your lab/project group is decent, this class is pretty low-stress.
Great professor who teaches a pretty easy class. Just do well on the HWs and this should be a nice break in the stats core.
Lots of work but loved the class! Would especially recommend for comp sci majors!

Because I took AP Stats before STA199, I loved this class because it focused more on the practical data analysis/coding and didn't waste too much time on basic stat concepts. However, I think that if you don't have much stats experience, STA199 might not be the class for you because it's definitely more coding heavy than stats theory heavy.

Tackett is a nice, smart person, but the class is organized poorly. The work is done in groups, and this random team makes or breaks your semester. Moreover, you mostly teach yourself the material, since the lectures skim through learning R. It's busy, unrewarding work. It's not the worst class, but I wouldn't do it again. Useful material, though.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Group projects

reviews.comment: Clear lectures. Lots of homework and projects, but most of them were pretty intuitive and doable. Tons of opportunities to get extra credits. She did not cover the materials in a theoretical and in-depth way, but in a way that is applicable to future research or jobs. The class was enjoyable and relaxing compared to other rat race courses at Duke.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Prof. Tackett is a great teacher. However, I did not enjoy STA 199 Intro to Data Science as much as I thought I would because the material wasn't as in-depth as I would have liked. The class, however, served as a good introduction to programming in R (although I hate R) and to basic stats concepts, so it's good if you're considering doing stats.

Maria Tackett is a bright and upbeat professor that made me focus in her STAT199 class. I have no coding experience, but her cool attitude and energy made me want to learn and appreciate Data Science overall. I will be taking another course with her next semester. There was a lot of work but I believe it is worth it because you learn a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Very kind person. Very accessible. Highly recommend!

I absolutely loved taking Professor Marcus' class. He explains materials very well and is more than happy to help you with concepts during office hours or even through emails. If you have chance to take mathematics classes with him, use that opportunity! Highly recommended

He is a great teacher and really cares about students. His lectures do get abstract though and as he is very passionate about differential geometry sometimes he is linking material to that even when teaching an intro class, so that a non-math major would be lost a little. He is lenient in grading and very considerate
Great Professor, very enthusiastic about teaching Math. His notes are very helpful and quizzes are rather tricky. Overall, I liked this professor and his passion for teaching.

Good professor, during lectures, you may feel lost, but he gives such good notes that when you look over them, everything will make sense. He sometimes gives alternative proofs to theorems and that is very helpful when the book is confusing. The homework definetely pushes you, but it is definetely worth it.

I liked Prof. Werner as a guy, and from what my advisor told me he was a lot better than anyone else...I would definitely recommend him (took a little while to get used to british accent, but in end very helpful overall)
No helpful and more than often refuse to help.

Great professor, loves mathematics, a little quirky. He gets a while to get used to, but he knows all the work back to front and can teach it to you if you give him a chance. Loved the course, but definitely not easy

Dr. Rizk is very caring and was always invested in EGR101 and his students. I appreciated his enthusiasm. The only downside is that he is a very tough grader compared to other 101 professors which can be frustrating when everyone is submitting the same quality of work but getting different grades.
Great professor, super caring, very interesting and fun class when it gets to prototyping. Dr. Rizk talks so much though

Rizk really cares about his students–makes a conscious effort to stay in touch with them even after the class. His feedback can be a bit vague sometimes and his grading strict, but it's clear he wants you to succeed. Really chill and nice guy. Would take his class again.
Sweetest professor ever, really cares about his students and you can tell - definitely a good resource to stay in touch with after

Dr. Rizk is a great lecturer and is incredibly accessible outside of class, from office hours to weekly garden lunches. It's easy to tell that he's very passionate about the class and the students, since he scales down workload prior to exams and all projects are designed with industry applications in mind.

Dr. Rizk is an amazing professor and mentor. He always provides crucial advice for prototyping and lots of feedback on assignments. While Rizk is not as lenient as other EGR101 professors, he is by no means a strict grader, and you will excel if you stick to the rubric. Rizk is also very accessible outside of class for general Duke advice.

Dr. Rizk is one of the greatest BME teachers out there! Really caring professor who is super knowledgeable about signal processing. Be sure to attend his weekly gardens lunches he is one of the most accessible professors on campus.

Dr. Rizk is a tough grader, but he is one of the most understanding people I know. If you just talk to him and show that you care about your project and put honest effort into it, there's no reason to not end up with an A.
Dr. Rizk is an amazing EGR101 prof and is very caring to his students!

Dr Risk is a caring and nice professor. He helped our group out throughout the entire semester and was also accessible outside of class. He can be a bit of a strict grader so make sure you follow exactly what the rubric and requirements for each assignment are, and ask him to review them before submitting.

Dr. Rizk truly cares about his students and wants to support them in every way. His course is structured perfectly allowing time to learn from him, connect with him, and connect with your peers. Although you don't learn specific content from Dr. Rizk (as is the nature of EGR 101), he is a great support system to gain valuable communication skills.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Rizk was a great teacher, he always gave thorough feedback on assignments and questions during class. I wouldn't say he is a tough grader, but make sure you understand the rubric and exactly what needs to be done. He has his quirks, but he genuinely cares about the success of his students and their projects. Join him for lunch if you can!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Rizk was a great professor, super accommodating during COVID and generally really helpful. "Final" was a final project that was pretty open-ended and informative, overall great class

Dr. Nicholson stopped holding lectures 2/3 through the semester, gave ~5 practice problems total for some exams, and flagrantly lied about curving the final. Absolutely horrendous lecturer and grader whose poor pedagogical abilities have negatively impacted the academic futures of many people I know. A true standout in the Duke physics department.

Dr. Nicholson was great. Organised notes, clear exposition. I like that he taught more elegant approaches (eg Greens). The first midterm caught a lot of people by surprise (which in turn caused undue resentment in some), because many of us had not done PDE in a physics context before. In retrospect, exam 1 was doable. Later exams were easier.
Nope that curve sucked - I take back the things I said.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: 362 with Prof. Nicholson was a blast and wasn't terribly hard either. Very generous grading.
I love Phil. He truly cares about his students and his work. He's always excited to have a conversation with anyone, and will always be engaged in your opinions.
Prof. Napoli is truly fantastic!!!!! Awesome guy with awesome interests.

Content is just a repeat of 155, but definitely take 301 with Napoli. He's chill and fair about exam grading (ex will give points back to everyone for unfair questions). He has a cool perspective on the media and incorporates that into the class, which makes it more interesting. Discussion section is useless. 2 midterms, 2 memos, and a final.

Prof. Napoli is an amazing professor. He's caring and engaging in his lectures. You can tell he genuinely wants to hear from his students during lecture. The material is pretty easy and the class is very do-able work-wise. He also is a nice grader on both memos and tests. Really cool and interesting. Definitely take 301 with him if you can!
Napoli is awesome and very laid back! Really enjoyed his class.

Easy course but not sure what you're supposed to get out of it. He is very knowledgeable -- but only about media and technology policy. He references those two subjects just about every class. No textbook, no exams. Five memos and one group project. Lots of assigned reading but no need to actually read it. Nice guy but lectures very dry.

Professor Napoli is simply amazing, and 361S is equally so. He runs his seminars like dinnertime discussions, which he also hosted one of! The material is fascinating, discussions get deep, and he encourages tangents because they always lead to new revelations. He's so accomplished (we read his upcoming book's manuscript) yet approachable.

He is an excellent professor and extremely passionate about what he teaches... Did a great job re-working the 301 curriculum so that topics are timely after this last election. He makes time for students outside of class and is always happy to go through your memos if you reach out to him. Mostly a PJMS professor but hopefully will teach 301 again

Phil is extremely passionate about the course material (which usually leads to him going off on a few tangents during lecture) but he's also very available and caring towards his students. The class is easy as long as you study a little for the midterm/final. Memo grading can be arbitrary but thats because of the TA's, not the professor.

Phil is really passionate about the course material and has a lot of work experience in the field that he often brings back into lecture. He does tend to go off on tangents a bit but the midterm is incredibly easy. Only negative about the class is that your memo grades depend solely on how chill your TA is.

Professor Nurkin is one of the best professors I've ever had. As a former Duke student, he gets what it's like to be a student and still pushes us to learn. I loved the excursions to cultural events. If you're interested in PubPol or the arts at all, you must take this class! If you're not interested in the subject, you might not like it.

One of my FAV professors. Funny guy who gives students so much respect. Class is a must take with interesting readings and thought provoking discussions. Excursions to performances is a highlight. Readings average about 100 pages per week which is fair for a pubpol class. Community partners do mean (some) extra work outside of class.

One of the BEST professors at Duke. If you are interested in making a difference in the world, Nurkin is the person to talk to. He cares deeply about his work and fostering a good classroom environment. You would be silly not to take a class with him. You have to read and prepare for class, but the workload is similar to other PubPol electives.

Avoid his classes at all costs. Grading is arbitrary with no clear rubric, and he doesn't update grades frequently, so you will be completely in the dark. He gives a crazy amount of reading, so be prepared to have like 200 pages for a two-day span of time.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--So many papers

reviews.comment: Fascinating course topic, but subpar execution. Fair discussions, interesting excursions! Group project with community partner was exciting but sometimes became grunt work. Unfortunately, some excursions canceled/rescheduled from lack of organization? Likewise, agendas of 2.5 hr classes rarely completed for poor pacing. Generous grading, nice prof

Nothing about the class was hard, by itself, but the combined requirements (3 midterms, Axelrod project, video project, hard final exam) meant that the course was challenging.  Still, the lectures were excellent, really different from the usual college class. This course changed the way i think about the world.
Grading on final is a mystery

Super easy class. Three midterms, all multiple choice and very similar to the review material. Final is three essays from ~10–11 provided questions, so it's predictable. Two simple video projects and an Axelrod tournament strategy game. Very chill, low stress, and enjoyable overall.
So engaging and learned so much. Helped me become a polisci major.

Really good class and teacher. Not graded on a lot, but exams are easy if you pay attention during class or read the slides he uploads. Overall made the topics interesting and was a pretty engaging lecturer.

His class on political economy is great for people with little knowledge about it. He sometimes wanders in lectures, but makes lots of dad jokes and teaches good stuff to know for the real world. Exams, though there are several, are easy because they're either open notes take home or he gives you the questions ahead of time.

Munger is an engaging, knowledgable, and passionate professor. If you go to lecture and pay a little bit of attention, you will pass this class. 100+ pages of readings per class, but you don't need to do the readings to pass/they're not on exams. Exams are open note and online, easiest class I've taken at Duke, but you still learn a lot.

Munger was my favorite professor this semester. Wasn't sure about polisci but this class alone led me to make it my minor. He is a great professor and class is really straight forward. Weekly quizzes based on a podcast, 3 open-note tests and essay questions provided before the final. Lectures are engaging but participation is not required.
Professor Munger is super intelligent and passionate about econ. He's truly a great professor that prioritizes learning material rather than just memorizing it for a test.
Clearly has a pro-market perspective, but gives a very fair amount of attention to counter-arguments. And outside speakers add a lot to the class.

Professor Munger's class provided a very engaging format to help understand different perspectives and philosophies of political liberty through the very accessible lens of film. Good class discussions.

Great guy he's hilarious. You watch a movie every week and write a response for homework. Then you talk about it in class and get let out early every time. No midterms and he gives you the questions for the final two weeks in advance. Take it it's the best freshman seminar

He's the absolute man. Love this guy. Everytime i walk into class, I just get happy from seeing him. Love his presentations every wednesday. Can't say enough about this man and this class. Made my semester.

I've learned so much from this class compared to other intro classes. There are a lot of readings but you don't have to read super in depth to do well on his exams; just make sure to pay attention during lectures.

While he has a libertarian bias, Prof Munger is very respected and knowledgeable in his field. He is funny and also an intriguing storyteller so lectures go by fast. I have had 2 classes with Munger and gotten A's pretty easily both times (as do most). If you show up to class most of the time, it should be a relaxed and enjoyable experience.

Witty, humorous, knowledgeable, but a little rambling. Professor Munger is not shy about letting his libertarian ideology shine through in his teaching, but does so tastefully and welcomes discussion. Interesting to talk to outside of class. Flexible grader. Intro to Political Economy is a fantastic intro to the political science major.
Good professor.

You'll learn quite a lot from professor munger. He is a smart guy who is great at explaining difficult concepts. He definitely should not be director of undergraduate studies given how little care he shows for the well being of his students. Definitely take the class to learn, but that is about it.

Prisoner's Dilemma. Can be very bias and narrow-minded, but definitely an interesting professor. Can be a bit intimidating at first, but easy to talk to once you get to know him. Lecture heavy but he keeps lectures intriguing /interesting and he can be funny. Would take a class with Munger again
Planning on swithcing my major after working with Prof. Munger
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Incredibly easy class for seniors. Almost guarantees an A if you put up a good effort. Offers a wide variety of topics across the PPE curriculum over the first few classes, then showcases debates between students for the rest of the semester. I would have preferred more lecture and less debate.

Munger makes it pretty clear that teaching is low on his priority list. He cancels class to attend other events, is rather condescending when moderating discussions (makes good points, but rudely), and prepares little to nothing for class lectures. Usually ends up reverting back to the same phrases/slides every class. Easy but unenjoyable class.

He is very hypocritical and barely teaches the class and instead opts to have other professors come in and do it for him. he is very stringent and this is very annoying. questions on the midterm are few and very specific compared to the amount of content that is given in the class. He also gives no indication of what will be on the midterm.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Super funny and interesting guy, gets you to think about tough issues. Is a libertarian economist so teaches through a big free market lens, but listens to all viewpoints with an open mind and encourages debate. Not much work just weekly quizzes on podcasts, optional readings. Midterms are just 20 ?s MC tho so beware, and final prep was quite a bit

Munger is a hilarious and deeply intelligent lecturer. The content was quite interesting overall, and the examination were 100% fair. The final does take some time to prepare for, but he's a pretty lenient grader. Take this class if you can!

Professor Munger is an amazing professor! There are weekly podcasts/quizzes in his class and the amount of readings are significant, but they are not really that important. I generally did them but I know of a bunch people who didn't do a single one and still got A's. Tends to like people who sit in the front and ask questions after class.

Munger is an incredibly talented professor. However, since he co-teaches the class, only count on him showing up a few times throughout the semester. Lectures are amazing with a strong Libertarian bent. Many of the course readings are authored by him.

Prof Munger's lectures are more energetic and comic than those of his co-professor for this class. The problem is Prof Munger only gave a small percentage of the lectures during the semester. His discussions were interesting, but based on the amount of times he was actually present in class, were rare.
Very unusual structure for the course.  Student debates every class, and you didn't know which side you had until dice roll.  Learned MUCH more that way.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: "Campaigns and Elections" was an academic experience like no other.  We quickly moved away from discussing readings and theory to just spending hours each week talking about the presidential election. I learned a LOT. Also, he brought food to EVERY CLASS. Like giant feasts. He's a super nice dude when you look past his wannabe toughness.

Munger and Salsman are a wonderful pair. Munger especially is a genius and expert in his field. The experience, years of knowledge, and prestige that he brings to the classroom made his Political Economy class worth every penny. Funny, interesting lectures, and real personality. Lots of reading, but tests are manageable. Take any of Munger classes.

A hilarious professor with many interesting (yet somewhat biased) insights, Munger ensures incredible lectures when he is the one speaking and not the numerous guests he invites. Class can sometimes be very confusing and/or dry, but there were many instances where his humor or knowledge kept me interested the entire time.

He's a great professor, knows a lot about the subject he teaches and is passionate. Even though he is a libertarian and very pro-market, he has a very balanced lecturing style that addresses the pros and cons of each side. His course is not easy, but very interesting, and not impossible by any standards. I would definitely recommend this course.
Lectures were very good, sometimes excellent.  Grading was harder than I expected, though I still got an A-.  But it made a big difference in how I think about economics, so it was worth it.

Easy workload but a  pretty hard grader on tests. Didn't really feel like I learned very much. Seems like a cool guy but he expects an unreasonable amount of knowledge and effort on exams. In his word, if you do nothing wrong, you get a B-. You need something "extra." A little ridiculous, in my opinion.
Munger is very engaging and passionate about the topics he teaches. It's easy to get lazy, but if you show up and do what he says, you'll get an A.
One of the most interesting classes that I've taken. Lectures may not necessarily follow the syllabus but very informative. Teaches you how to argue for your idea and how to write clearly.
Class is engaging and helps you understand why people might argue both ways for different economic policies.

Found Munger an interesting lecturer who made concepts entertaining. Learned a lot and definitely easier than Econ 101. Tests and quizzes are easy, reaction papers are graded harshly and arbitrarily by TA's. Most Duke professors are exceedingly liberal so nice to get a libertarian/economic conservative viewpoint on these issues.

Prof. Munger is a great teacher and the class is really easy. He tells you exactly what will be on he midterm/final so all you have to do is study EXACTLY what he tells you. There are weekly virtual quizzes but as long as you listen to the podcast they're extremely easy. I highly recommend this course!

Very interesting class overall. When content got a little boring he would try to liven it up with Youtube videos or other media besides lectures. Easy grader; he told you exactly what questions to expect on the midterm/final and how to go about answering them. I highly recommend this econ class for non-majors.
He is a really great guy.  He is funny and willing to help when it is needed.  He outlined the tests and didn't try to trick anybody.
He is an awesome teacher. He is a great guy and easy to get to know. His tests are fair and he tells you exactly what you need to know for them.

This professor is absolutely awesome. Learned a ton and not incredibly difficult. Makes what's important stand out in lectures. Tests were fair. Great professor and person. Take his classes. Don't read other comments on here.
His Intro to Political Econonomy was was very interesting. He's engaging and intelligent, highly recommended! Be prepare to work hard though, but its worthwhile!
A hard class, but useful, and practical knowledge about STATA
Lots of work, but he was available outside of class.  I learned a lot from the paper about legal research.
Solid class.  Lots of reading, but you learn a lot from the paper.  Met with me twice outside of class for an hour each time to discuss paper.  Grading was tougher than I expected.
A signficantly less-than-effective instructor whose failed political apirations are apprent.  Hypocritical and self-serving.  Not the caliber expected for the expense and prestige of Duke.
Interesting, funny, but too much emphasis on "science," and not enough policy
It wasn't a great class, and perhaps he shouldn't teach Pub Pol.  But the lectures were pretty well organized, and most were on power points that he made available.  TAs were best part of class.

Will put less effort into the teaching the class than you will (Let's hope so because no one can  be that disorganized). He did, in fact, foster great camaraderie amongst such a large lecture - before finals, everyone would stop the other to discuss what he covered in class. Problem was, nobody knew.

do not ever take 114 with munger. he doesn't care about the class. he's extremely vague in lecture and on assignments. he forgets to put up things. he admitted at the end of the semester that he hates to teach this class. i've heard the class being a lot better with other professors.

If Professor Munger is teaching a PPS class, DONT TAKE IT. If Professor Munger is teaching a political science or econ class, take it. Its as simple as that. My only other comment is that he makes funny jokes in class (the only incentive for going...)

Truly one of the best professors at Duke.  This class was so interesting, it literally changed the way I look at the world.  Munger does such a good job relating complex concepts.  Highly recommended.
Great Professor. Extremely accessible given all of his responsibilities.

Has figured out how to teach a class that makes sure you learn everything without making it too hard. At least half the grades were A or A-, and the material was fascinating. Outstanding professor. Top scholar in his field. Libertarianism does not seep into his teaching. Willing to look at papers multiple times. Highly, highly recommend.
No Comments
No Comments

Very disappointing. Sure, he's funny. Sure, he's an easy grader. But he was sooooo unprepared. You could tell he never prepared and just improvised. It's kewl that he's such an easy grader, but please, is this why my parents are shelling out the big bucks at Duke?
Dr. Munger is truly one of the greatest professors at Duke. Anyone who has the chance to take a class with him should definitely do so.
No Comments

This was one of the best classes I've ever taken.  The reading list was daunting - thousands and thousands of pages - but I learned an incredible amount.  I always looked forward to class discussions.  The homework assignments were mind-expanding.  I came to college for classes like this.
Best class i've had. Highly recommend him for anything, especially involving any philosphy. Very smart and funny
Definitely agree with that.  He's really into his image as the conservative darling.  Too bad he can't teach his way out of a paper bag.  Quit blogging and start teaching!
