Amazing Class....Amazing teacher

munger is a great guy, a fun teacher and made pps 55 bearable, even fun. at the end of the semester when my TA messed up my grade, he helped me out quickly and every time i needed to talk to him he was very sincere and receptive.
Unprepared most of the time, the lectures are off the cuff.  Not ever sure he's read the stuff he's lecturing on!  TAs are all that counts in this class.  Skip the lectures.
goes thru the motions but doesn't really deliver
I wish this man taught every class at Duke! What a dream- I mean Professor Munger is hot, smart, funny, and my favorite Duke Prof!!
No Comments
Take it. He is pretty strict on deadlines, which I don't totes love but I suppose I get it. Has a lot of knowledge and you will learn a lot.
You're not going to find a more knowledgeable professor in healthcare systems or healthcare policy for the US context.
Take it. One of the best profs @ Duke and Sanford School of Public Policy

Organizational Ethics: Dr. Boucher is an Excellent prof at Duke's Sanford Sch of Public Policy. Take this course for practical work in org ethics & some emphasis on structural inequities. Attendance counts for crse grade, grading is not cutthroat, just make deadlines. Offers inclusive class & keeps space open to ideas across the political spectrum.

Very insightful class, also pretty easy to get an A in, even though he says it's not. Readings were tough, and you could get away with not doing them. Assignments weren't hard, just have to do it on time or it will destroy your grade. Super interesting guy, definitely take a class with him if you are into medicine!
He is super smart and clearly extremely knowledgeable about what he teaches. Just don't miss any deadlines! It'll cost you the grade.
Professor Boucher is clearly passionate about what he teaches. He's very informed and has lots of experience in his field. The assignments were easy but he is strict on deadlines.

Prof. Boucher covered really insightful material and brought in good speakers. However, the way the material was presented made it hard to stay engaged during a 2.5 hour lecture. Honestly, an easy class if you follow the syllabus and submit everything on time, but he has no tolerance for late work or small errors and each assignment is worth a lot.

Worth taking any course from Dr Boucher. Knowledgeable, understands students have busy/crazy schedules. Come to class prepped with the reading. Turn stuff in on time. Little leeway with late work. No extra credit. Worth your time!
Lost pts on some silly things but I missed knowing some details. Instruction was great; super knowledgeable professor. Accessible. Big focus on struct inequity

If you want a manageable overview of United States health care and health systems, this is THE class to take. There is a good mix of interactive lecture style, breakouts and guest speakers. Instructor is accessible and kind while also a busy researcher with much exp. But always willing to try to improve the course and discuss your career paths.
Great course to take. Knowledgeable professor with tons of experience. Good survey course on healthcare issues in US.

Dr. Boucher is clearly very knowledgeable about the course topics. Sometimes grading criteria can be unclear as the course is graded by only a few assignments, but generally he is very open to clarifying anything through emails and talking to him after class. Doesn't grade that difficult on  assignments and pretty interesting course material.

I was very underwhelmed by this class. It was almost entirely guest lectures and no one really pays any attention (melting in a small classroom for 2.5 hours at 8:30 didn't help matters). Had a very small slip up on a group project and got a A- in the class as a result.

The lectures were pretty boring (nobody really paid attention), but there are no exams and the course work is extremely easy. Your entire grade is based off of 5 assignments which are all easy, but Boucher is not flexible with deadlines so pay attention to dates!! A 95 is an A so if you have 1 late assignment (even a day), you're at an A- overall.

Loved this class! Felt like I was learning about things that actually mattered in real life. 2.5 hr lecture at 8:30 AM is rough, but Boucher makes it engaging. Straightforward grading -- if you follow directions and study slides for exams, you can get an A. Barely any homework, reasonable grading, and you'll learn things that matter. Def recommend!
Hi there - the undergrad course 165 Intro to US healthcare is useful for undergrads. Def take.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Took qualitative methods; super helpful. Best Professor at Duke Sanford School. He is sometimes brutally honest, but I appreciated this. Not all students do. He is honest and real-world. Thankful; glad.
Took graduate qualitative research methods. Super. Learned a great deal! Learn from the expert. Sanford Sch of Public Policy lucky to have Boucher. HJ

Solid course! I learned a great deal about how healthcare delivery works. Students really seem to like this professor. I thought Dr. Boucher was super knowledgeable, cares about his students, well-ensconced in research (and brings that perspective into the course), and clear about expectations. Highly recommend this course, any course he teaches.

Great, funny guy who makes lectures really interesting. Lots of assignments throughout the semester but graded pretty leniently. The midterm and final is MCQ but you gotta really cram for them. A is also at a 95+ but its doable. Def take if going for premed or pubpol because you actually learn a lot.

This class was one of the best I've taken at Duke. Although it's an 8:30, I always look forward to class. He makes up for the early class time by having great lectures, hilarious jokes, and a positive attitude to keep us going. Would highly recommend. Tests and assignments are easy and graded fairly. Must take class

Even though I'm salty that a 95 and up is an A (FYI!!) I still felt that this class was very interesting and definitely manageable. Even though TA was meh and it was an 8:30 class, Boucher made it up with funny jokes and incredible guest speakers to give us all a present context on health care.
I really loved his class even though it was at 8:30 AM. I learned a lot about the healthcare system through his anecdotes. He's one of the best professors I've had. 100% recommend!

Prof Boucher is approachable and creates an environment in which students feel comfortable participating. He has a lot of experience with health care and often includes his own personal stories in the lectures, making them more engaging. Class is very well organized. Not much work at all. Need a 95 to get an A, but it is very doable.

This is one of my favorite classes I have taken at Duke. Professor Boucher is amazing, and the structure of his class really enables students to have a deep, enriching learning experience. He is approachable, and facilitates a comfortable, engaging class environment. I had it 2x a week and was never bored, I always looked forward to this class!

It is very easy to do well in this class, however the lectures are sometimes very boring. I took this class as a once a week, 2.5 hour lecture. It was very hard to understand the complexity of the healthcare system by learning in this fashion. Also, participation is very important in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Tests? Not many--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Good prof, take the class. Worth your time.

Professor Boucher was a great professor. Some of the assignments were tough but he is a fair grader and is always accessible to his students. The class is done in a  discussion based way. I really enjoyed the class and would recommend anyone to take the class
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Solid course if interested in health care/policy. A lot of different topics covered. Tries to be balanced with a topic that can be politicized, but is honest about views; is pretty frank. Style is unique, can take getting used to, but is caring and respectful of his students. Is interested in your insights/interests, incorporates in class.

Wide variety of topics for an Intro course. The readings were sometimes a bit too advanced for a 100 level course, but it did allow me to push myself. There were many smaller assignment that allowed you to "make the grade." Professor Boucher has a variety of ways to teach to several learning styles. Overall? Good course, good professor.

Solid course in US health care systems. Cares about the students - taking extra time to check in, offer interesting readings based on your interests. Runs an active class with some group work and much participation. Has a great breadth of experience in health care. Take the course!

Most assignments received good grades pretty easily. Participation/Attendance was allegedly mandatory but you could get away with skipping a fair amount. Class was decently interesting in terms of getting to know some problems in the U.S. health cares system. Very discussion based.

Probably the most niche and hardest class I've taken at Duke. Don't take this class if you're not well rounded in music and neuroscience. Everyone knows too much in this class. I genuinely didn't know how to study for the exams other than going through the slides and readings (which didn't cover applications). This once a week class was miserable.

Like the other reviews have said, this class is a lot of work. I would not recommend to Neuro majors trying to fulfill the ALP requirement. I felt this class was more the theoretical concept of sounds being produced and it tying in with ear anatomy– not necessarily "Music & The Brain". I wouldn't have taken the class given what I know now.

Professor Overath is a fantastic researcher...He does not teach but merely reads off the slides as if he were presenting research. The slides he uses are very long, and he goes through them quickly, so if you are trying to write all the slides down, you will certainly miss them. Lectures are not recorded. Class was more difficult than should be...
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great guy but horrible lecturer. He lectures like he is reading a textbook and it is really tricky to actually digest the information. Lectures are also really boring. The material is so interesting and he takes all the joy out of learning it.

A knowledgeable and kind professor, and his exams were very manageable and straightforward. Just attend class and review the lecture slides thoroughly, and you'll be set. The grading breakdown is 75% exams, 20% group project, and 5% attendance. If you study well, this class is very enjoyable to learn.

Not sure why his score is so bad, great and knowledgable professor and the exams are insanely easy and straightforward. He's super nice and his lectures are great albeit a little boring. Semester-long group project worth about 20% of the grade but it's not too bad. I'd recommend this course for sure

"Music and the Brain" leaned more towards neuro. So many topics condensed into one class each week, and the midterms tested for really specific stuff. Dr. Overath is clearly an expert on the material, but his presentations tend to be wordy and time-consuming. Lots of fun creative opportunities in the class, but so much work.

Worst professor I've had. Held a mandatory 8:30 online & deducted a percent off your final grade for each lecture you miss. Lectures were painfully boring & slides info just copy and pasted from textbook. Exams only 34 mult choice. I never listened to lecture just reviewed slides but I managed to get an A. Try to take with anybody else.
Was a really enjoyable professor to listen to and was super willing to stay after class to talk to you and answer questions. He obviously loves neuroscience and it shows in his teaching!

Worse professor in the neuro department. Extremely unclear grading criteria, really boring lectures that are mandatory and an absolute waste of timeI didnt learn anything from him in that class. If I could give him a 0/5, I would. AVOID any class taught by him at all costs!
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Music in the Brain is a demanding class, and would not recommend for Neuro majors trying to fill an ALP. Coming from a music background, but a keen interest in the subject, I found the class to be very difficult and time- consuming. Grading was very unclear, and it was hard to do well. Overath is a good professor, but the class was too difficult.

Music and the Brain is the worst classes I've ever taken. You need to know intro neuroscience, even though there are no official pre-reqs. There's also an insane amount of work - 3 papers, midterm, final exam, final group project, 2 individual projects, weekly quizzes, and 100+ pages weekly reading. Lectures are boring and attendance is required.

Professor Overath expects an unreasonable amount of work from his students, and seems oblivious to the fact that they all have many other equally important commitments besides his class which prevent them from devoting their entire lives to the class. Grading criteria were largely unclear, and he set the cutoff for an A to a 94% for no reason.
He's kind of intimidating and this class has a ridiculous amount of work.

Great Professor! Very knowledgable about his field. His class was well structured but he was also very open to feedback from students about what they did and didn't like. His grading was also pretty fair, although not an easy A by any means.

She is a very caring professor especially if you are a freshman. However, I personally felt that some students received more attention than others. I believe she gives amazing feedbacks and I learned a lot from her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Ok, Lit 111 was the only selection for her course, but she teaches other amazing courses, and she does a phenomenal job in getting the material through to students! She's not strict, but don't play in her class. As long as you read the assigned materials, follow her instructions, you're not going to fail! she's a really relatable person too. :-)

I love her. very nice and friendly even outside of class. Make sure to do your readings, participate in class, and submit your assignments on time, and you'll be fine! If you show a genuine interest in her subject, she will help you a lot and appreciate that a lot. Which is very great.

Ms. Odelia is one of the most caring professors you can take as a Freshman. Her classes are full of humor and she makes sure every student gets to speak. That's not to say the workload for the class isn't heavy, but it balances well with the lighthearted lessons. I learned a lot from this class and sincerely miss her feedback!

Very nice, funny professor who is able to simplify very complex material without losing any detail. Extremely helpful, always willing to answer questions and has a great lecture pace. Highly recommend.
Omar is the GOAT, he's really chill and is great at explaining things. 10/10 would recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Omar is probably one of the best professors at Duke. He does not move on to new topics until he makes sure that everyone understands what's going on. He is also very patient so even if it takes you 30 minutes to understand a simple concept, he will stick with you until you do. He's also funny and really nice, makes the class really enjoyable.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Low stress and great overview of NLP! The final project can be hard and come up fast. Highly recommend asking her for project ideas based on what you're interested in. We get to take the content any direction we want. Highly recommend going to class and getting to know her. She's a great resource with so much experience and so kind. Great class!

Professor Osborne is one of my favorites at Duke. Apart from balancing a FT job and family, she never failed to create a positive learning environment. I was able to have a genuine interest in lectures given the low-stress nature of the class. Recommend for any CS major that wants an interesting/easy elective that's relevant to today's tech world!
The GOAT. I've never done a rate my professor before, but had to for this class because Professor Osborne is awesome. So knowledgeable, funny, and understanding! She really cares about her students.

Professor Osborne is amazing! Super understanding and very interesting class. She lets you take the final project in any direction you want which makes working on it a lot more enjoyable :) Would highly recommend taking any of her classes for CS electives.

Very kind professor! Honestly, maybe the most thoughtful and caring professor I've had at Duke, which is incredible because she was also working full-time as a PM and had young kids. Very thorough with her feedback, made it her goal to guide you based on what you were interested in. Would highly recommend taking a class with her.

Actually the goat. Super nice + funny prof, always willing to talk after class, and an interesting perspective as someone without a graduate degree who focuses on industry NLP applications. The class itself is graded pretty easily, but the final project might be a bit of a time crunch. Definitely take if you are even remotely interested in NLP

Mary splits her time working in NLP and teaching in NLP. As a result, she can provide real-world context for the material in the course and does so in an incredibly engaging way. Mary frequently dives into hilarious stories about her family and her work at SAS. Mary also keeps us up to date on the latest in greatest in NLP. Great teacher :)

Worst professor I've had at Sanford. She is often condescending and refuses to take any meaningful feedback. She's expressed unprofessional irritation with students during class time, often acting as if student confusion or requests for clarity are our fault. Course structure is disorganized, and expectations are unclear for a first sem class

Compared to other PUBPOL 803 classes I am severely behind on developing writing skills that I need for future classes and my career. Professor Owen refused to take any constructive feedback for my class and would snap at people who asked valid questions. She also does not have empathy for student's individual circumstances. Don't take her.
If you want to learn, choose another professor. If you want a connection or looking for a friend, maybe take her class.

You can clearly see how passionate Jenni is about the class: she prioritizes students to deeply engage in the real world of politics both intellectually and physically. She is also very caring and gives effective, individualized feedback. However, the classes could have been more organized and could have clarified the takeaways more efficiently.

First and foremost, this is an incredible class that can benefit students from all majors. Jenni cares so much about her students and ensures that they receive quality community partners, as this is a service learning course. She gives incredible feedback and often offers her own experiences from her career in public policy.
Love this guy, loved the class. Reading notes definitely were some work but I learned a lot, his lectures are AMAZING. Tons of super interesting stories and takes, would take any class taught by him.

This class was one of the best I have taken at Duke in terms of changing my mindset. If you come into this class with an open mind and a desire to learn you will get so much out. Be weary that many of the readings are biased, but that is the nature of writing and Dr. Starn was happy when someone brought up these biases in discussion.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This class's grading criteria is based entirely on completion - if you turn in all of the work and go to class, you are guaranteed an A. Professor Starn is very funny, and lectures are engaging. A great intro to CA with low risk.

Professor Starn is so far one of the best professors I have ever had. His seminar consist of lots of reading with weekly reading notes. But he tries to find interesting readings for us. He cares a lot for his students well-being and will be super flexible just to make sure we take care of ourselves first.

Dr. Starn is a well-respected, understanding, & caring prof who loves interacting with his students. He gives us a lot of cool readings that he provides great insight on. This might be the most interesting class I've taken @ Duke. Weekly readings/reflections, 3 essays, and final essay. Trust me, it's a very fair workload. This class is a MUST take!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Love Professor Starn. He really cares about his students and wants you to understand the material. Very easy-going and nice guy to talk to. Occasionally brings in donuts / treats for the class. Def take his classes.

CA101 was a super interesting class. Orin used fascinating personal anecdotes during each lecture and class was rarely boring. However, grading standards were vague and Orin/the TAs provided almost no feedback. This class is worth taking for the content but don't count on getting an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Writing in this class is too subjective, although it is not that difficult and the material is easy
grading is so subjective, not an easy A

Easy class and tests are straight memorization from lecture. Altho he's so disorganized and very late to get back tests/papers. I hate how he does lecture. He legit just talks and says everything out loud, expecting you to scramble to speed write down everything he says. Only key words are given.

Starn is a very interesting lecturer and this class is very interesting. Not a hard grader and the tests are exactly on what he covers in class, so going to lecture and reviewing notes a little are all you need to do to succeed in the class. Good choice for t-reqs.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Class was very simple as long as you showed up to lectures and took notes. Orin usually gave warning before pop quizzes. I found the lectures to be very interesting as the topic of discussion changed each week. Semi-questionable grading done by the TAs but nothing outrageous. Culanth taught me a lot of useful everyday information.

This is a great class if you need to have an easy class. It's both interesting and easy. My class average was an A- if that tells you anything. At first I took it as an easy class, but now I am genuinely interesting in anthropology. Course load is small, you don't have to read much, and you only need someone to get the notes from class that day.
Very arbitrary grading. Points would be taken off for no reason on exams and final paper. Pretty easy class, but I would not take it again.

For some reason, grading seemed to be VERY ARBITRARY this semester. Despite prof saying that TAs marked all exams and papers very carefully, points were randomly taken off without feedback. Even though this is an 'easy' class, seems as though prof wants to make it tougher to get an A. Also, lectures were scattered. Took forever to grade.

Doesn't grade fairly in my opinion. Wrote the same stuff another friend, but got different grades. He is, however, a great lecturer and although his lectures are kind of scattered, you'll be fine as long as you memorize the key terms he gives.
Lectures were pretty interesting, if you just go to class and take notes you will do fine
This class was an easy A. If you're an engineer at Duke looking for a CZ requirement, take this class. You wont regret it.
Orin is awesome and funny. Take this class!

Super easy class and teacher as long as you go to all of the lectures. What he says in lecture is exactly what will be on the exams. He also grades the final paper extremely easily, as long as you sound mildly intelligent, you will get an A.
Easy and unchallenging class. I didn't learn anything new.
Starn is so incredible interesting. He has so many stories from the things that he has been through. Not a hard class, and he is very aware of that. Great class to take.

Orin's lectures are sometimes pretty interesting because he's been all over the place. His TAs grade everything so grades are a little scattered but it's easy to argue points back on tests. Not a hard class by any means. Definitely take if you want to get a CZ credit
Orin gives the most interesting lectures. He's really engaging and teaches in a very lively manner. Also a very interesting guy.

Professor Starn is amazing and the class is interesting and easy. Sometimes the weekly articles to read are long and a little boring but there are only three pop quizzes on them all semester and if you take this class with Starn it is totally worth it.
Orin's the man he just wants people to learn take any class he's teaching.
One of the best professors I've had at Duke so far. Really great lecturer and keeps you engaged the entire time. Pretty easy grader and explains things in very easy to understand terms.
easy class, memorize his lists of key terms and be able to regurgitate his lectures on the exams, TAs handle the grading
The professor explains issues superficially and does not challenge students to think deeply about things. He is probably more interested in getting high ratings than opening minds.
Very interesting course. Professor is a pretty good lecturer. Pretty easy class. I you attend most of the lectures and do most of the readings, you'll get an A.

Starn brings new and interesting insights to ordinary stuff you thought you knew. Lectures are a joy to attend and he's really understanding of his students for someone as renowned as he is. You can tell he loves to TEACH. Ignore the comments about the TAs; they aren't the prof. If you take notes attentively, you'll learn a lot and get a good grade
Amazing professor & amazing class! Culanth 101 is the only class I have never slept in at Duke. You will get an A if you attend every lecture and do majority of the readings.

Lecture is pretty boring but he's a good speaker so he makes extremely boring material a tiny bit more bearable. TAs grade exams completely arbitrarily. He makes the class such a joke that the grading is a joke and he doesn't assess you properly. Lousy class if you care about being graded fairly.

Starn is a great professor who offers great insights and perspectives. The class required a lot of reading and you had to attend lectures.However the way the TA's graded was nonsensical.  If you attend lectures and read you are most likely going to get an A.
LOVED him and Anthropology of Sports. His class helped me become interested in Cultural Anthropology as a major.
TA graders are terrible. They don't know how to grade essays and don't explain their grading.

Of the lowest quality.  Literally had no clue at all how the tests are graded. TAs grade them and arbitrary points are taken off WITHOUT explanation. Really dislikes when students ask about their grades. A "blow off" class that grades like Econ 51--go figure
A lot of reading, serious communication issues, and NO grade feedback until the end...

Wow, this was one of the worst professors I've ever had. He laughed in my face when I told him that I had to miss ONE class for athletics...and this is coming from someone who misses half the classes himself! Lots of boring reading...didn't learn much at all...

Wonderful professor and class. CLear and fascinating lectures. I had never taken a cultural anthropology class before and fell in love with the subject with Prof Starn. He is engaging and loves to take students out to get to know them better. A great class and an even better professor!
he is SO awesome. you will love this class!!!! he is funny and friendly, and he really knows his stuff. he makes everything very interesting.
Great professor. I really enjoyed this class.

amazing professor. crystal clear lecturing. i thought the exams were hard because there was alot of material to memorize, and the exams involved short essay writing which was intimidating. lots of readings too, but most were really interesting.

I love this man, he would just make this class so interesting and easy with a nice balance of lecturing, music, and movies.  the only part that i didn't like was when he let the TAs practice lecturing, no need for that when you have Starn.

Prof Starn is absolutely FANTASTIC! He was engaging, funny, interesting, and a fascinating professor. He made the material come to life with movies, outside sources, and more. Books were great as well. Plus he invited students to lunch to get to know him. Great professor and person!

Professor Starn is THE MAN.  Amazing and interesting lecturer. Nice guy. Plenty of visuals,like movies, music, and pics used with lecture. For the readings, make a study group and have everyone summarize one or two readings.  Tests are easy, just regurgitate notes.

Starn is a great teacher and just a really cool dude.  His lectures are done well for a class of this size.  The only problem I had with the class is the TA's grading the tests and papers because there is no feedback to their grades. However, this shouldn't stop you from taking a class with Starn because he is one of the best prof. at Duke.

His lectures are great, but he doesn't do any grading on the exams himself - they're done by TAs who sometimes completely slack off and just assign random numbers with no reasons. Multiple choice questions on exams ask about useless details of readings, such as "what state did this take place in" and neglect the purpose of the article altogether.
Wonderful teacher.  Makes class enjoyable and is funny.  I wish I could take more classes with him.
The absolute best! His class topics are really interesting, his assignments are clear and fairly easy, and he makes learning fun. Take a class with Orin - you will thank me for it.
Starn is the best!

Prof. Starn is absolutely awesome.  I've had three classes with him and they've been some of the most interesting courses I've taken at Duke. He's the reason that I decided to major in Cultural Anthropology.

CA 180 (Culture and Sports). It was really a fun class. We had a reading every week about some aspect in sports, be it Racial, Gender, or Sexual tensions in sports. Readings were fun and Easy -stress free class. Every week we needed to write one page of notes about the readings - Sign up for it!
Easy class, just keep up with the reading.
hes great
Best class ever!
No Comments
Prof. Starn rocks the house!  He's funny, well-read, modest, and passionate about anthropology.  Tests are fair, class is interesting, and the readings are intriguing.
excellent, excellent professor. very clear and to the point. brings in lots of props to enhance our learning. exams fairly easy. liked his class so much that i decided to take another class with him

The course is centered on a project creating a 10-minute film. Honestly preferred the second half of the course focused on creating the documentary over the discussions in class. Sometimes the discussions in class veered drastically from the topic at hand, and I feel like I know less about what a Minor Utopia is now than before. She's nice though.
She makes the material very engaging but the workload is insane.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Super passionate and excited to teach and learn from students. I learned so much in her class and really respect her. There is a lot of reading but I would highly recommend.
Very scholarly class. Used Social Science as well as historical approach. Intellectually stimulating. Great professor for seminar style classes.
She is weird, assignments and grading are unclear,and lectures and reading can be  boring, boring, boring. She can also be kind of mean...

Dr. Olcott was my advisor on my senior individual seminar, and she was an awesome professor.  We met at fun locations to discuss our papers, and she is both brilliant and witty.  Strongly recommend taking any of her classes...but bear in mind that hard work is a must.
Excellent professor. Extremely intelligent. Accessible to students.
ugh.
don't ever take a class with this professor. classes are extremely boring, grading is arbitrary and assignments are very ambiguous.
Wonderful professor - very interesting and easy to talk to.  Gives great feedback on writing and is helpful with term papers.  I would definitely recommend taking a class of hers.
No Comments

The first half covers outdated frameworks. The second half talked basic finance, repetitive for finance majors, yet too shallow for non majors to grasp. For the assignment and quiz, it feels intentionally designed just to make your life difficult rather than to actually teach you anything.
I am applauding you for your effort and the courage it takes to stand up and present, but you may be surprised with your low score, according to Peggy Matson
The reason why Motorola is only making walkie talkie
The professor might be the very reason that Motorola failed.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Doesn't care about any students and just talks about herself all the time

Appears to do a lot of discussions but doesn't take anyone's input. She thinks she's always right even if the class is arguing against her. Has an ego. Will always mention her experience in WashU, Northwestern and Motorola, to the point where it gets annoying. She writes the case study questions herself and she makes it confusing.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: She doesn't like discussions, she thinks only she's correct. Huge ego.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Matson is smart and passionate but this class needs to be completely redone. The lecture itself is boring, unorganized, and based on outdated capitalist propaganda, and this is reflected in the assignments. The extreme amount of baseless homework leads to memory-based quizzes in every class. I would not recommend this class to anyone.

Professor Matson's whimsical teaching style is unconventional but lacks structure and relies on outdated knowledge, leading to memory-based quizzes. However, she values feedback, showing a commitment to improvement. Her unclear questioning style challenges students and can be frustrating.
The course content is rather interesting. However, the professor makes this an unnecessarily hard businesses course to take due to the sheer amount of HW given.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: very good professor, look strict but cute. His lectures are very logical and well-organized.
Great professor. Simplifies complex concepts and clearly understands the material.

Professor shows amazing lectures, and explain ideas and details of the lecture very clear. No exam for this class. You can learn awesome geometric algorithms, with reasonable workload and comfortable course contents.
Overall, this is a great course.

Most difficult class I have ever had to take. For each topic, you will be given one (1) unclear example before moving on to the next. Lectures are mandatory but confusing and not worth your time. Had to supplement lectures by finding hours worth of online videos to learn anything. Lectures 40-50% average on exams, everyone was beyond stressed.

Pankaj was phenomenal! Accessible to help outside class and on Ed, and made dukes toughest undergrad CS class manageable. The one downside is that his accent can be a bit hard to understand. The class was redesigned to include programming components, which were a fun challenge. Definitely not an easy class regardless of prof, but Pankaj is great.

I like Pankaj's to-the-point lecturing style. He knows clearly what he is talking about. I went to many of his office hours and he often gave abstract remarks, but somehow was those just enough to help me through a question. CS 330 is always hard, but I thought the real midterms were consistently easier than old midterms (with other profs).
He is really nice. Go find him in his office hour. He will give you direction in your homework.

Definitely the hardest class I've taken. Prof Agarwal is organized and clearly knows the material very well, but lectures are still complicated due to difficulty of the material. Lots of supplemental readings. Nearly all homework and exam questions are difficult. Be prepared to work very hard, especially if you don't have a strong math background.

Dude is absolutely brilliant. Doesn't bother using notes for his lectures because he understands the material so well.  Tests are ridiculously hard, but this class is always hard. Hires amazing TAs. You will learn from a master if you take his class.

Agarwal is brilliant. He has such a good understanding of Algorithms that he doesn't use notes for any of his lectures. Gives lots of supplementary readings to help us understand. Very organized lectures. Makes the TAs attend the lectures to ensure recitations are on point. BUT the class content and tests are very difficult. Class is curved.

possibly the most difficult class I have ever taken as CS major. irritatingly unhelpful professor (if you are stuck on a problem, he will give you a hint but usually the hint isn't enough to get you past being stuck). doesn't provide answers to textbook problems, so doing problems is often frustrating and time-consuming.
Class is hard, regardless of the professor teaching it. Do as many problems as possible. Pankaj is nice and helpful but this material is just difficult.
No Comments

Concepts can be hard to grasp if it's your first non-introductory economics course. Doesn't record lectures and posts slides that make minimal sense on their own. Always happy to answer questions though. Definitely feasible to do well if enough time is put in.

Super interesting guy. He does go fast in lecture, but its attendance optional. The test were hard, but partial credit was often given. He was also generous with the end of semester curve for the class. Only downside is that in lecture he sometimes just assumes everything is super easy to understand (claimed to teach us Calc 1 in 5 minutes lol.)

He did not make the class easy, but helped me to understand microeconomics at a deep level and was a great lecturer. The class is test heavy and homework light. There was nothing unreasonable, but be prepared to study when it's time for an exam.

Flipped class teaching style, lectures go way too fast & you need a beefy background in micro (Econ201) to do well. Extremely calculus heavy, he slows down for questions but skip class & you will fall behind. HOWEVER he grades VERY leniently, gives tons of partial credit and grades fairly. But be ready to do lots of self-teaching outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: will not help you out of class. even when i scheduled meetings to discuss things i didnt understand he was dismissive and short. tests are meant to trick you not test knowledge.
Great professor who makes econ 105 also great! very clear and the slides are very helpful. midterms are tricky though. definitely recommend take his econ 105

Lectures are helpful, especially the roadmaps at the end that review for the tests. Reading the book is not. Encourages students to ask questions.  Tests are difficult because questions are tricky and not really straight forward.  However, he's really helpful and you learn quite a bit in his class.  Curve is also fairly generous.
Challenging material, but he gives you everything you need to know.  Tests are hard as hell, but curved.

He covers all the material, but he likes to wait till the end to string it all together.  Tests are only hard because he picks the tricky questions, so you have to know all the little details to everything.  He'll give you the skills you need.
This guy is great. Incredibly clear lecturing. He challenges u, but u will come out of his class having learned a great deal.

Super teacher! He reminds me of Peter Rabbit. The lectures are really good. He's really clear and writes everything on the board. The tests are kind hard, but not as hard as Fullenkamp's or Nechyba's.
Fabulous teacher! Tests are hard, but if you go to every class, it's not bad. Don't buy the book, it's useless.
Very good at explaining difficult concepts.  Great professor.
No Comments
He was cool.
Boring and easy class, seemed to have guests come in / play films when he didn't want to lecture. Take notes in lecture and skim the readings afterwards to prepare for tests.

chill guy who teaches a chill course. lectures are boring, but workload is light and selection of topics/readings is pretty interesting. the 2 exams were reasonable given good lecture attendance and notetaking (readings less important that lectures imo). emphasizes big ideas over details. solid experience overall
TAKE THIS AS AN ECON ELECTIVE! Easy class if you do the readings. Attendance not mandatory but you will be ok on tests as long as you read

Amazing course overall--I went in with no knowledge of the field whatsoever and left wanting to learn more. Lectures are so interesting, and all graded work product is very manageable provided that you come to class and do the reading.
I LOVE PROF PIOT!!!! his stories of anthropological fieldwork made class very interesting and all the readings were well-contextualized. really makes you think outside of the econ framework.

Although the class was very interesting, he is a boring lecturer. Amazing and laid-back person, very understanding and humble. Class is quite easy if you get good notes and keep up with readings. A reading or two per week which are simple to understand. Doesn't force long lectures, if he feels a discussion is done, he'll just end class early.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This was a very nice class! It's composed of 2 four-page essays and 2 exams, and each is worth 25%. So, be ready to read at least 2 readings each week, each being 20 pages. All assignments are based on the readings and lectures, where he breaks down the weekly readings, so make sure to attend class, even if attendance isn't mandatory. Good Luck!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Good material, boring lecturer who doesn't know how to teach and doesn't understand the readings himself. As long as u go to class/take notes from someone else, u will be fine. if he was a better teacher, this class would have been fascinating. random tangents at 8 am are annoying, he will randomly spend entire class periods showing movies.

This wasn't exactly the class I hoped for when thinking about African and African-American culture and history, but it was not bad. This was an easier class compared to my other ones. Take understandable notes (I did using an iPad and/or laptop), listen to Prof. Piot attentively, and read articles closely. Office hours help before tests/exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: - 2 tests and 2 papers. Thats it. The test are on what we read from the first half and then from the second half of the seamster. no cumulative test. As long as you read you will be FINEE. Take this if you want an easy yet informative class seriously.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Easy culanth 101, take this for an easy class
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He ran a nice easy and informative class but had weird grading towards the end because he used letter grades instead of numbers. Also really hyped up in the beginning of the class how he would boost peoples grades that participated, but he did not. Harder class than expected.

Intro to African Studies - A really solid prof if you're looking for a chill ALP. Both an interesting and easy class. Your entire grade is based on 2 papers and 2 midterms. The midterms are 100% based on lectures. Has some interesting research and is really involved in DukeEngage as well. Only delta is that he's very liberal and makes that known.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Piot is a great lecturer and always made his classes interesting. He brought in guest speakers as well as talked about his personal experience with the topics discussed. He makes students think differently about complex ideas.

Great, really chill prof. Really good at communicating. 2 papers, 2 midterms. MUST attend class and take detailed notes to get an A cause exams are mostly based on his lectures more than readings. Paper grading can depend on TA but Piot will lead u in the right direction if u go to OH, so go if u really want to do well. overall enjoyable class
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Graded by 4 things: 2 papers, midterm, and final. The midterm and final are solely based on his lectures so going to class or getting notes is a must. Basically had no work for this class but it is not an easy A. He doesn't curve and he classifies 95 and over as an "A"
Pretty interesting class. Graded by two 4 page papers and two mid-terms (no final was nice). Definitely not as easy as some reviews on here make him seem.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Not the greatest professor, pretty boring in terms of instruction but he doesn't realize it. Well-spoken but likes to lecture, can almost come off as pretentious/pedantic. Can go on tangents, which makes his points hard to understand at times. Class topic by itself seems interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Anthropology of money. Class of about 100 students, which was too bad because not really able to talk with peers in class about readings. Piot mostly talks about his experience in Togo during lecture. Curved class, so not that much of an "easy A", One tough TA. Just 2 essays and two exams. Nice professor, knows a lot. Can definitely get distracted.

Pretty easy class. It was weird though, he clearly didn't want to be there for most of the classes and just showed movies or was extemely lethargic. Would have liked a little more enthusiasm, but all in all its a pretty easy class, and he's a very reasonable grader
Great Professor. Interesting topics. Alternative views to development.

Just attend lecture and memorize lecture notes. He was pretty interesting but sometimes dull. Readings weren't necessary, but he was super helpful outside of class and always responded to emails/questions.

Not a bad professor. Classes could get boring sometimes, but at other times you learned some pretty interesting stuff. The amount of reading was manageable, but the tests did require keeping up with the readings and making sure you understood the material. Overall not a bad class
The readings are tedious and you probably won't keep on schedule by yourself if you aren't interested in the subject. And the tests are reasonable, but not especially easy.

Very easy class that boils down to "white people did it." The tests are 100% based on the notes and are fairly simple, although they do have some tricky items. The two essays are four pages each, which makes it ridiculous that they are worth 25% of the grade each. They are also graded rather arbitrarily. Still, easy A overall
lectures are pretty boring, tests are pretty easy if you read the material (except for tricky MC questions) and his ridiculous shirts make lectures worth attending

Topics are interesting, mostly about how people view African cultures, esp West African cultures. Only two papers and two finals. Prof is a good lecturer, but sometimes it seemed like he didn't really care about the class. It seemed like he just popped in a movie whenever he didn't want to lecture.
Very engaging, made class fun, very down to earth and helpful
Very knowledgeable on the subject of Africa. A dedicated teacher and academic with interesting viewpoints and engaging teaching method.
Professor Piot is really nice and the class wasn't too hard and quite interesting.
He's a fascinating and engaging man. He'll challenge you and is charming. Transformative professor. Everyone should have to take a class with him at least once at Duke!

Professor Philipsen is a breath of fresh air from the usual Duke narratives and ways of thinking. He's inspired me to pursue work that truly impacts people's lives in a positive way. You will be lucky to take his course.

Professor Philipsen is one of the most dedicated and passionate professors I've had. He cares so deeply about his students and courses. He offers new perspectives about topics that feel intimidating at first in a truly inspirational way. I can't recommend him enough.

171 was a by no means enjoyable. It's politically one sided (anti-capitalist), and readings spanned from pros of Marxism to banning private property. Prof. Philipsen can struggle with empathy and student interaction (he harshly criticized me and my background in OH). Tends to dominate discussions and students. Be prepared for overly-harsh feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: You'll be exposed to a LOT of new ideas and it'll forever change your world view. Dirk is extremely knowledgeable and holds some pretty “radical” views, but you'll even learn about the prejudice embedded in that word. A lot of reading, but most of it very interesting. Recommend for those curious about progressive ideas outside the mainstream.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Respected--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dirk loves to hear himself talk. He leverages his intelligence over his students' youth to silence their views and questions. I think I'm politically aligned with him, but he really cannot tolerate any ideas but his own. Participation does not matter, class is repetitive by week three. Worst class of the FOCUS cluster. Sad to see Dirk's demise.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Philipsen pushes you to develop genuine critical thinking in a society that often expects you to accept dominant narratives without question. While his feedback usually circles back to digging deeper into a single underlying diagnosis (capitalism), he nevertheless respectfully engages with differing viewpoints. He's a deeply caring presence.

Dr. Philipsen's class was AMAZING; you will either love the class or hate it, but it will truly make you learn something. His teaching style is different but understandable. As long as you follow the rubrics and closely read the syllabus, your grade will be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The whole class Prof Philipsen has the same argument which is just that capitalism is bad, whatever solution you propose to make our world a better place he just says that capitalism is the root of the issue. Some of the readings were cool but he is stuck in his ways and only wants to believe his ideas

Philipsen's selection of readings are well-thought-out. Chances are, he will change your perspective on politics, public policy and economics. Minor cons include slight disorganization (e.g. forgetting that someone is due to present) and he can be quite interventionist in discussions, but they are outweighed by the interesting perspectives.

I loved this course but I didn't LOVE the way discussions were fostered by Dirk. He is very smart and provided incredibly nuanced reading materials. However, the class environment wasn't very conducive to open conversation. It felt like he was either judging or not listening to students when they spoke and it made it hard to participate.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: There are many readings, but they're nuanced and thought provoking. Most classes were lectures inspired by the readings with space for student participation. There is a strong discussion about capitalism's place in driving current issues (all opinions welcome). More personally, the class made me examine my own ethics, goals, and concept of self.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Philipsen is the greatest professor I've met so far. He truly cares a lot about his students, conversations are always candid and sincere, and he indeed has a lot of inspiring ideas.
determined and inspiring, greatest professor ever

Dirk is the best and most inspiring professor I have ever had. He knows his stuff so well and talks in class with such passion and drive you'd think that the class is a stage and he's the star. His viewpoints might seem odd at first but you'll get to see his reasoning behind it. His class made me grow and augmented my viewpoints. The best class!

Dr. Philipsen's course, though difficult and reading/writing heavy, is extremely thought-provoking and forces you to challenge your preexisting beliefs. He connects with students on a personal level and, though he has a set point of view, is always trying to help strengthen your argumentation skills. He is also very understanding and accessible.

Really changed the way I thought about economics, capitalism, and the role of corporations in advancing and preventing a sustainable future. He's very opinionated but deeply cares about engaging students to challenge their beliefs and think bigger when it comes to structural change.

I feel like the whole point of going to college is to learn things you couldn't learn anywhere else. This is the only class at Duke I have taken where I truly felt that way. This class impacted my worldview more than all other classes I have taken combined. Absolute must-take class, even if you need to take it pass-fail because ur a junk writer.

Not only is an A a 95 (not on syllabus) but he grades everything by letter snd then assigns the lowest grade value to that letter. So A work is given a 95, A- work a 90, etc. This means if you get all As and one A- youll end up with something like a 94.8, which is an A-.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Philipsen is very patient, supportive, and kind. He pushes his students to think outside the box and makes you to rethink questions that we previously ignored. Workload can be heavy. Great class, highly recommend, very intellectually stimulating.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Dirk is awesome. Really forces you to challenge your worldview on a fundamental level. The readings are moderate to heavy but are super important to understand the material. Discussions are great and important. Feel like the entire class got a decent grade but it's hard to get an A.

I LOVED life within capitalism until we went home for covid-19. For someone who talks about inequalities a lot, dirk did very little to help our class during a literal pandemic. He also was extremely rude to a few students toward the end of the semester, including a gendered incident. I just lost so much respect for him and feel disappointed.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Tough grader

reviews.comment: BEST class i have ever taken at Duke. We just had our last official class and I want to cry. Readings are moderate-heavy but ABSOLUTELY ESSENTIAL in getting the most out of this class. You should feel lucky to be in this class. Dirk has pushed me to reconcile my values and become an independent thinker. This class has forever changed my worldview.

Dirk is one of the best and wisest teachers I have ever had. He will both challenge and change your perspective on the economy, climate change, and life. Class is fun, with a good balance of discussion and him speaking.

Dirk has given me a complete new perspective on the world and deeply cares about his students. He challenges you to think in ways you are not usually taught in school and is one of the best teachers I have ever had. Life Within Capitalism will change your life and be one of the most unique classes you take at Duke!

Dirk's class has impacted me more than any other at Duke. I disagree with him often, but that does not make me love him any less. He genuinely cares about his students and is deeply deeply passionate about his area of study.

Prof. Philipsen has really opened my mind up to new ideas and enabled me to think outside the box. Although labeled as a climate change class, this course spanned discipline and ideology. This was by far my favorite class I've taken at Duke.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Challenges his students and genuinely wants them to learn and become better thinkers. Go to office hours-- you will get to know Dirk more personally and he will give you specific feedback. Good prof.

Professor Philipsen's class provides an amazing new way to view climate change, globalization and corporate citizenship. He completely opened my eyes to the different structural issues that exits in our society. He is a really funny guy and discussions are always very entertaining and informative.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dirk is an amazing professor. He completely changed my outlook on political power and climate change. He is always ready to help with projects, and he genuinely cares about what you do in the future. He pushes you to engage with your work instead of being passive. Go in to office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: His class, Denial, Faith, and Reason: Sustainability and Survival was my absolute favorite compared to my past courses at Duke. The material and discussions forced me to reassess my own beliefs as I was confronted with my own biases/assumptions about different economic/social/political systems. The workload isn't light but he's a fair grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Professor Philipsen leads a seminar-style class.

Professor Philipsen is a provocative and passionate teacher, creating consistently interesting lectures. He genuinely cares that his students understand the material and empowers them to be change-makers.

Professor Philipsen is an amazing and inspirational teacher and I would highly recommend you take a class with him. Life Within Capitalism changed my perspective on so many issues, and despite having a lot of reading, the class is not too difficult.

This is the best class I've taken in my four years at Duke. While you're sure to gain plenty of knowledge in most of the courses you take here, I've not found another professor that truly teaches you to THINK, not memorize. My biggest regret of college is that I didn't know about this professor until my last semester. Don't make the same mistake!

Dirk is very well-intended and has an extensive background in ethics, economics, and policy. However, this is a guy who is almost too smart for his own good. He doesn't encourage student participation and the class can easily become a one-sided lecture. His feedback can also be really contradictory so you'll have to rely on your TAs for help
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Professor Philipsen's was a great experience. He really challenges your worldview. While the class itself wasn't an easy A, I felt like I really gained a lot from his class. He gives out a moderate amount of readings and doesn't tend to give out lots of grades (<10) so be sure to be on top of things. I look forward to taking another class with him!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Philipsen is an amazing amazing professor. He has changed the way I see the world, and is also such an amazing person. He is supportive, gives great feedback, and is very available. He wants to have personal relationships with all of his students.

Take a class with Dr. Philipsen! His passion for the environment and business ethics is apparent when he teaches. The class is not too difficult, but you will receive a lot of feedback. It's helpful though as you can build on your skills in a welcoming environment. Everyone should take his focus class as it is so relevant to society today!

The class time is worthwhile:  he is amazing at lecturing in addition to opening up the floor for debate. Heavy reading and reading responses take forever, but it has allowed me to retain taught me to synthesize and produce my own arguments regarding a very interesting subject. He is kind, inspiring and gets to know students. I LOVED this class!!!

This class will change the way you look at the way we all live and interact in American society. Prof. Philipsen doesn't let you BS any assignments and gives detailed (but a bit harsh) feedback, but the work is definitely worth it.
Incredible professor, will change how you view the world.  Grading could be arbitrary, but he curves to help kids get an A- or above.  The Ethics Focus was awesome.

Philipsen is one of the most inspirational professors I've had. He's so passionate about the subject and has so much insight on it. He really likes to engage students with it. There are some really long and intricate assignments over the semester that aren't easy, but they're educational in their own way. I think everyone should take his class.

Awesome professor with great ideas! Dialogues and lectures are always intriguing and not boring, if you do your reading of course. There's a decent amount of work but you should be fine. Nothing comparable to math.

Professor Philipsen is really passionate about this subject and it's clear that he knows his stuff. As long as you are willing to put in some effort, you will get a lot out of this class both academically and in general. I really enjoyed the course and it's made me re-think a lot of preconceptions I had going into it. I would highly recommend it!
This guy is good

Professor Philipsen is an extremely passionate and empathetic teacher who invests himself into his teachings and students, in hopes that they leave his class thinking about life differently. One of the best classes I have taken, I learned a great deal from class and his office hours. There was a ton of reading, but definitely worth taking.
LOVE HIM TAKE ANY  ALL HIS CLASSES!!!

This course confronts the realities of our climate crisis, but also leads students to new solutions. Dr. Philipsen pushes students to interrogate their assumptions and to develop their own arguments, which can be frustrating. But by the end of the semester you'll be glad you've critically examined the issues and defined your own position. Rec'd!

Dr. Philipsen is a good overall guy. I don't think I agreed with everything he said in the class, but I learned a lot. He opened up my thinking about the subject (capitalism and the environment) a ton and I appreciate that, not many professors at Duke do that. The material he assigned challenges all of our previous assumptions.

He really cares about the topic (sustainability), but does not let that get in the way of his students' opinions. Has extremely good clarity of thought and understanding of arguments and reasoning. Take this course if you are willing to consider others' perspectives and ideas. He's also very open to conversation and is always willing to help.

His classes are very challenging in that they require a great deal of reading and effort. However, Dr. Philipsen is always there to help if you do not understand a concept. He also assigns very helpful assignments that are reasonable, but also test your knowledge on the content. Overall, a very effective teacher and good overall guy
I honestly learned a lot in this class both about the topics we were meant to cover, as well as life in general. Dr. phillipsen is a caring proffesor who wants to see his students succeed.
Great teacher, great class
Passionate teacher who certainly does not deserve the criticism that is being put on here. He cares deeply about his students and is always willing to meet with students if more clarity is needed

LITERALLY BEST PROFESSOR IVE HAD AT DUKE. most meaningful class by far, gave me a completely new perspective on life. a significant amount of reading but as a human being going into the adult world, should def take this class. will make you more wordly, knowledge about american society.
A lot of my class mates despised this guy, but I personally felt like that he was cool and very intellectually driven!

Class was Denial, Faith and Reason. He is a really nice person with interesting views. Books in class were interesting but he's not great at generating discussion and didn't really utilize class time that well. Ask for the syllabus and read the books on your own for the interesting ideas but class was kind of a waste of time.

Philipsen is a great professor who is very passionate about his teaching and genuinely cares for his students. He wants to push students to see the big picture and question many of the assumptions we make from day to day. Overall I have enjoyed his class.

well-intentioned, wants you to think, question why. cares for students and wants to help. tries to use socratic method but poor facilitator, unclear. writing assignments also unclear. pushes own ideas, critiques other arguments, but not very receptive to criticism of own views. like him as a person, but not his class. could have just read books.
Loves to monologue, pushes own liberal agenda in class, useless feedback. Killed my interest, though assigned readings were good, didn't manage to facilitate good discussion.

Tests are 100% based on memorization of every single lecture slide and make up 85% of ur grade. Some questions are on a random fact from 1 slide that they mentioned once. Lectures are unengaging and doesnt try to make content applicable at all. The whole class is just memorization of huge charts/facts/dates. if you can't remember well, ur cooked...
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I feel like Dr. Pontzer is a very knowledgeable professor but doesn't really transmit the ideas in lecture in a compelling way. Much of the explanation of certain systems was verbal, without textual support on the slide, making note-taking rigorous. At times, explanations were also unclear, greatly increasing the amount of self-teaching out of lec.

Very memorization heavy on the tests, especially for test 2 and 3. Lectures are interesting but recordings may not be posted. The seats in the room were too comfortable though so I kept falling asleep during lecture

I wish I had taken this class with a discussion. Ultimately you're graded 85% on rote memory of lecture content in the exams and get a free 15% from reports. Dr. Pontzer is a great lecturer and very funny. I have recommended this class to friends.

This class's material is pretty easy so to make it Duke-level prof. Pontzer makes the tests tricky. But, if you memorize literally everything that is written on every slideshow, you will get an A and it will only take like 3 days of memorizing (for each exam) off your life and you will be free to do other stuff.

Favorite class this semester. Very intelligent when it comes to evolution and his research on energetics; talks about it during his lectures. Sweet and caring professor, not a lot of exam prep resources, but as long as you know the stuff on the slides (very memorization heavy), you will be fine. Take this class with Pontzer, you won't regret it!

Tests seemed unfair to me. They were based on really nit-picky facts that he might have stated like once in a lecture. We are responsible for memorizing these humungous charts about the primates and hominin characteristics that are impossible. Class was not engaging or enjoyable.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Pontzer is a great physiology professor. There are lots of facts and details to know but he makes lectures interesting and relevant. You get to learn about all the major body systems and complete a project at the end of the semester.

Dr. Pontzer has very simple and plain lectures/midterms. While very knowledgeable on the topics of anthropology, his tone was sometimes a bit condescending. 3 midterms basically determine your grade in the class, and they are all memorization-based. Exams are very specific on content only found on lecture slides. Mediocre/below average class.

Dr. Pontzer is a great lecturer, and this class is super interesting, especially if you are pre-med. There is lots of content, and tests are based solely on memorized information from class, so be prepared to study hard for exams. However, there is no other work besides studying: no homework, no required readings, etc. All information is taught.

I really enjoyed this class and found the subject engaging while also being approachable for someone with limited actual anatomy and physiology experience. We learned most things at a level higher than MCAT requirement, which is great. Herman was an engaging lecturer who also was clearly invested in student learning. Would take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Pontzer is one of my favorite professors at Duke. His class is very lecture-heavy and requires a ton of memorization, but the content is not difficult. He is very accessible outside of class and really encourages getting involved in EvAnth. He is such a smart guy and, although he can be blunt, he is so nice. (Also highly recommend his book!)

One of the best professors at Duke. So nice and has had a really impressive and interesting career. Course material is quite fascinating and he's an amazing lecturer. 3 blog posts that are easy As and 3 midterms that you can get As on if you study and MEMORIZE. Overall one of my favorite classes. No final which is nice.

Dr. Pontzer is a clear, engaging, and passionate lecturer.  He is also one of the world's top researchers in Human Evolutionary Physiology, which shines through in his lectures. Exams are fairly graded and lecture heavy.  The class is test heavy, but there's not final exam but rather a final project.  Good prep for MCAT physiology as well.

Prof Pontzer is very organized with his lectures. He teaches a lot of content and isnt super clear what will be on his tests. Three midterms basically determine your grade for the class, all based on the content he teaches in class. Lots of memorization, but overall an easy A.
One of the worst professorss ive had in my Duke career. Gives smart a** answers to anyone who has a question, tests on unimportant information you need to memorize from the lectures, stay far away

Originally took this class for the easy A but the material is actually really interesting and Pontzer connects everything really well. Grade was based on three midterms (super easy just go to lecture and write down notes) and three news summary (300 word summary of a scientific article). Really easy A with interesting content, definitely recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The class is very straightforward and does not require much critical thinking, just memorization before the exams. Dr. Pontzer is knowledgeable and tries to make the classes as entertaining as possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He is incredibly knowledgeable and an expert in the field. Tests require a ton of rote memorization of facts and dates which can be more challenging than expected. Pop quizzes do not have a large impact on the final grade.

He knows how to teach. The class is an easy A if you just go to lecture, take notes on everything on the slides (which are not posted) and memorize. You. Must. Memorize. He's an engaging lecturer who is well-versed in EvAnth. I would take another class with him. Even though the class is relatively easy, you still learn a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: If you want to do well, you HAVE to go to lecture because he doesn't post the slides and only tests on lecture content. Get ready to do a lot of memorization, he sometimes tests on very specific content. I would he's a great lecturer, very funny and keeps it interesting. He's a little unapproachable and can make you feel dumb when you talk to him.

Funny dude with cool research. If you treat Ev Anth 101 like a real class and study for the tests you'll get an A. He straight up tells you the class is easy. Pop quizzes are annoying but have little impact on your grade. I would not recommend the discussion sections, but they are VERY easy if you want to lower the stress of this class.
Very interesting and thought provoking class and he is super smart and cool guy. Tests are easy and pure memorization. All test content from lecture, so you do have to show up and take notes.

Pontzer's class isn't difficult if you're fine with memorization. The problem lies in him. He frequently treats students like they're dumb if they ask a question. Get ready to memorize several charts for no apparent reason. Take a different NS class. This one is boring.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Very good lecturer! Attendance is technically optional but he doesn't post slides, so you have to go to get notes. The lectures are worthwhile either way. Dr. Ponzter is very funny and connects material to current issues. Really engaging prof, straight-forward class
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This class is actually so easy that it is extremely boring. It is an easy A to a fault. But Pontzer is extremely nice, smart, and funny. He is also very aware and sensitive to the more hurtful topics of evanth, like eugenics history or conceptions of id/race. I wish we were getting the full use of his brain, tho.

Professor Nechyba was my absolute favorite this semester. He's so nice and caring and truly cares about econ. This class is really easy if you pay attention and do the work. Nechyba is really good at explaining the material and answering any questions. Definitely recommend taking Econ 101 with Nechyba.
He's a funny professor who gave a great intro to economics. I will say, the quizzes were not trivial. You should watch his videos and pay attention in class.

Great professor and great person. A class of 500 people might not sound ideal but Nechyba makes it a good experience. Unfortunate that you can't use AP credit to skip but there's some topics like behavioral economics that Nechyba goes deeper into. Super nice guy and pretty easy to pass, good chance you won't have to take the final.

Like many others have said, Nechyba is the ECON goat. If you pay attention in lectures and outside of class assignments, you have lots to gain from this intro class. It's a pass/fail class, and you'll have to actively try to fail. Very easy course from a special professor.

Such a genuine, caring person. You will get out of this class what you put in. Plenty choose to go the easy route but if you pay attention and try to actively learn the material, it's a strong intro to econ.

Nechyba is the best!! Highly recommend taking Econ 101 - the best class and the most amazing professor. He cares so much about what he is teaching and the class is pass/fail so you can focus more on the material rather than the grade. Class is rather easy to pass (just doing quizzes every night) and lectures are engaging (tech free though).

Genuinely the GOAT of econ at Duke. Nechyba cares about his students a lot and is a really funny guy who makes class engaging. Econ 101 is pass-fail, and everything is just take-home online quizzes, so it's literally impossible to fail the class unless you are lazy. Go to lecture as he sometimes does manual attendance, but he's an amazing lecturer.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
Yo if you get this guy you're set

Funny and great teaching, but most of all genuinely cares about his students

The GOAT of Econ, gets you interested in the field and wants everyone to succeed. Pretty easy class, but requires some time outside of class to watch the videos and do the 3x a week quizzes. Genuinely entertaining.

Super engaging lectures - he's great at getting people of many backgrounds excited about economics. However, the class is so ridiculously easy that anyone who nerds out about the material isn't going to be very stimulated. Class runs on a flipped classroom model with mandatory attendance, but the lectures and homework videos get samey.

I didn't fully appreciate Professor Nechyba's gift for teaching until I had other professors later on. He presents more challenging material in a way that's far easier to grasp. His pre-class modules are unmatched in their quality, and his lectures are incredibly engaging—my only regret is not attending more of them.
Great professor. super engaging.
There is a God. And his name is Thomas Nechyba. Protect him.
The undisputed GOAT.
What a class. What a teacher. What a man. Would recommend to everyone.

Took this as a Duke bucket list thing, but my experience was average. Nechyba gives great lectures, but the content was disorganized so limited takeaways. Topics were too easy and not intellectually stimulating. Grading by 33 Canvas quizzes was annnoying, excruciating. Mandatory attendance, but too many don't pay attention or even game the system.

Professor Nechyba is an amazing person who genuinely cares for his students. Lectures can very easily become extremely boring, but at times highly engaging. He plays ABBA for the class every morning.

It is not hard to pass this class, but SHOW UP TO LECTURE. Do modules assigned after each lecture, as this is the majority of your grade.
Nice professor. Lots of homework outside of class. No one pays attention during class, so it will be hard for you to pay attention as well.

Nechyba is a very sweet, caring guy; just a truly nice person. His lectures at times are really engaging, and at times less so, since it's 75 mins x 3/week. Passing is genuinely easy if you show up to class and give some effort on quizzes (which can be tricky). Pay attention once in a while, because you might get something great out of it.
He was really the best

NECHYBA=GOAT.
