Honestly, he is too nice of a guy, if you put in solid effort, you will pass the class, but he honestly just wants everyone to have a good experience with econ and learn what he teaches. Lectures can be boring and confusing if you do not keep up with the work, and the quizzes can be frustrating but overall, good class.

Professor Nechyba is amazing. Make sure to take Econ 101 in the fall so you get him as your professor. He is extremely caring, knowledgeable, and funny. The class is very easy, you are graded mostly on attendance. Would highly recommend taking Professor Nechyba to FLUNCH!

Mandatory S/U so of course the class will be easy. The mandatory attendance is very annoying and he gets annoyed with the lack of respect as a result of easy ways to get around skipping class. Quizzes with unlimited attempts before every class. Lectures are boring if you have any sort of background with economics coursework in high school.
The sweetest professor ever! His lectures are super engaging, guest speakers are really interesting, and really cares about his students. Not a difficult class at all.
I really like Nechyba as a person and I think his lectures are engaging and interesting at times, especially with guest speakers.

Sitting in a Nechyba lecture is like watching LeBron James play basketball. He is so skilled he makes it look easy. In all seriousness, Nechyba does a great job of making economics accessible from all disciplines. You don't have to be an econ major to take this class or be interested as he applies everything to the real world. A real class act.

Nebycha is the goat of econ, dont taken econ101 with anyone except him. the only problem with the s/u grading system is that you could absolutely study nothing in the class and get through it by having other do your quizzes, you just have to show up to get the Satisfactory, the exam is only compulsory if you don't get 70/75 points(very easy to get)
He's the best! Just bought us 500 donuts 🍩

Nechyba is a fantastic professor who genuinely cares about his students. His lectures are engaging, and he's always willing to provide extra help. Use Unstuck AI along with the textbook to ace this course.
HES THE BEST. TAKE HIS CLASSES

If you put in effort with Nechyba, you will succeed. By far the best professor to take 201 with. If you have the opportunity to Flunch him, do it! He is such an interesting person who genuinely cares about creating an environment for learning and exploration.

Nechyba is the GOAT of the Econ department. Took 101 with him last spring and waited a year just to take 201 with him! Really cares about his students, and gives us all the resources we need to succeed in the class. Exams are fair but require studying, but his flip-classroom approach really helps you prepare and understand the content.
Professor Nechyba is one of my favorite professors I've had at Duke.

My favorite professor at Duke thus far. Super nice and cares so much about his students. He genuinely wants you to succeed and he spends time outside of lectures and homework to help. Do his modules and understand them. Don't stress over the homework problem sets, and 100% go to his bootcamp review sessions in the last month of the class.

Nechyba is a really cool guy. Goes out of his way to answer questions for students and host extra office hours/zooms to provide assistance. This was an extremely challenging class, but I learned a lot and it shaped my way of thinking about the world and economics. Him allowing you to drop one of your midterms is really nice as well!

Such an amazing professor. Honestly cares about his students and sets up the class in a way that it is very possible to come back from a bad grade. Do his modules (and actually understand them) and do the bootcamps for the final. The homework is hard and doesn't matter so don't focus on it.
Absolute GOAT. Take Econ 201 with Nechyba if you have the chance. He presents the material very well and really cares about his students doing well.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: THE GOAT.

Professor Nechyba is by far and away one of the best professors as Duke. Though I have decided not to continue on the econ major path, having taken econ 101 and 201 with him were amazing! He is an incredible teacher - he cares deeply about the subject matter he teaches but also about his students. He is always available and willing to help!

Professor Nechyba is the BEST PROFESSOR EVER! Econ 201 itself is a little boring at times and the homework was always lengthy and complicated, but Professor Nechyba made this core class so much more manageable. He gives extra credit, extends deadlines, and is so accessible outside of class. I also took Econ 101 with him and loved his lectures!!

Make this man the head of the Econ Department. Reasonable and flexible. He helps struggling students, especially towards the finals. Great at explaining econ concepts. Exams are also well-written, and grading criteria is clear. 

Minor con: the homework was vague, unnecessarily hard at times and didn't help with the exams.

Nechyba is the goat. Had him for Econ 101 Fall 23. Class is P/F and has clear grading criteria. If you do all the homework quizzes between classes and attend classes, you won't need to take the final and there are no midterms. Class can get boring due to content, but Nechyba is a funny and personable lecturer. Would 100% reccomend.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: The homework is optional and is extremely lengthy, I suggest you don't do it as long as you are able to do the modules well and understand the material. There is a lot of content so I suggest doing the practice exams before each midterm. Nice guy overall.

I love Nechyba. I did not like the 201 material at all but he made the class tolerable and clearly cares so much about his students. In a giant lecture, it's easy to feel like the professor is being forced to be there, but I never felt like that with him. If I had to take this class with anyone but him, I would've dropped.
Nechyba is great and does a good job at trying to make students care about what is being taught. He's super cool and very knowledgable, so I highly recommend you flunch him.

It's honestly a shame that people graduate from duke without taking at least one class with Nechyba. He is the Econ god and he loves his students very much and does everything to make the content easier for students. I don't think there's anyone that can teach an intro to Econ as good as he did.
Lectures were not interesting and I found his explanations unhelpful. Honestly made me less interested in economics and questioning whether I should take more classes in the subject.

Professor Nechyba is amazing and he makes the class so much easier. It is a great way to be introduced to economics because it shows you everything that it can be used for beyond finance. He brings in a lot of speakers who have great advice about careers in economics. He likes to cancel class on Fridays a lot and usually finishes early.

Great intro to econ. Lectures were engaging, Professor Nechyba is hilarious. He admits when he makes mistakes and is always there to help students. Unlimited attempts on the quizzes so class is easy to pass. Videos he posted aided my learning a lot. A little time consuming, but would take again without hesitation!

Professor Nechyba is fantastic at teaching the information of his course and it was evident that he wanted all students to do well. This was a pass/fail course, and he really did everything he could to ensure that everyone passed. His lectures are engaging and he provided a great baseline for economics without too much stress!
Super easy class. Nechyba is a G.
He's an amazing engaging lecturer and really explains concepts well. The homework is very manageable and discussion sections were great if you had questions. Perfect class for an intro to econ!

Great professor. Econ 101 is a pass-fail class, and the way he does it, there are no tests, just quizzes that you can take online. It's an extremely low-stress class because it's nearly impossible to fail, and the workload is light as well. Great class for those unsure if they want to go into econ.
great professor
Best professor I ever had.
He's him. It;s a good class.

Nechyba is the GOAT. All of us love Nechyba. All praise the man of ECON. The leader, the legend. The second-coming of Arnold. He is a man always with a plan. A man of inspiration and motivation. A man who puts his students first. He is well-rehearsed.
DO NOT SLEEP ON THE EXTRA CREDIT-- IT CAN BE THE DIFFERENCE BETWEEN TAKING THE FINAL OR NOT. Do the extra credit (all of it) even if you think you will pass without it. NOT WORTH THE RISK.

Nechyba is the best it gets in Econ. He structures his class to inspire kids to pursue Econ, and wants everyone to pass the class. The quizzes are tough and can be frustrating, but working through them helps you learn the material. Awesome teacher.

Econ 101 with him is great. It's a lot of content but it's super easy to pass (only available pass/fail) and you don't have to take the final if you just go to class and do the pre-class work. He's just genuinely an awesome teacher and person and you can tell he really wants everyone to do well. Love him, def take his class.

Nechyba is a great professor. He really cares about his students and goes above and beyond to help us. Although the course content was pretty tough and often times unexciting, he helped us get through it.
Looks like the Terminator. Sounds like the Terminator. Excellent Econ teacher.

Nechyba is one of the best teachers I've had in my life. Never before have I laughed so much in a lecture. He's excellent with explaining concepts and making economics fun and interesting. His flipped classroom style is great, with videos and quizzes that help you learn and boost your grade.He is extremely understanding and great with extensions.

Professor Nechyba is truly amazing. It is obvious how passionate he is about the content he teaches and he truly cares about his students, extremely accessible outside of class. 201 is a lot of work, so definitely beware, and the midterms and final are very difficult. But 201 is a hard class by nature, not Nechyba. DO NOT TAKE WITH ANYONE ELSE.

Nechyba has the reputation as the best Econ Professor at Duke and he has earned it. He genuinely cares about all of his students, makes himself available to answer questions, and takes feedback seriously, often changing policies and the schedule when necessary. The content can be hard but he makes an effort to make sure you can succeed.
Econ201 is a difficult class but Prof. Nechyba is great and truly cares about his students

This class was SO good. I learned so much and felt very engaged with the content. Prof. Nechyba breaks the content down in a manageable way, and is incredibly caring and knowledgeable. Grading is very fair. I learned tons about the applications of economics to policy and other disciplines, as well as fundamental theory. 10/10.

ECON 201 is a challenging class with a lot of difficult material covered. Professor Nechyba does an amazing job simplifying the material and using funny and relatable examples in class. He is also really caring and very responsive to emails and questions. I would recommend taking his classes and FLUNCHing him. He wants all his students to succeed.

Econ 201 is a difficult class due to the material alone, but Professor Nechyba made the class way easier. Extremely knowledgeable on the course, very easy to reach out of class, and grades fairly. You'll spend a good amount of time on homework and reviewing around exam time, but he wants you to succeed and you will if you work hard.

Loved him! 
- Lectures in class were ok? They would be engaging if you didn't know the material, but you learn it all through the homework so they serve mostly as review.
- He was accessible outside class and the head TA was always willing to give extensions
- He breaks down complex concepts, giving the intuition behind them.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I love Professor Nechyba with all my heart. He has made my Duke experience really special. Despite this being a huge core class, he somehow managed to feel each and every one of us cared for. He was extremely responsive to any questions, and was even vulnerable at times in class. I really admire and appreciate him and all his efforts for us.

Econ 201 is a hard class, but it's been one of my favorite classes at Duke. Nechyba sets up the class in a way that rewards growth, so you have opportunities to improve throughout the semester. He's an incredible lecturer and prof. This class was challenging but also had stimulating content, and it made me look at the world differently. 10/10!

Take this class if you have the chance. Nechyba is an incredibly caring and inspiring professor who is governed by strong values. Sometimes there is a lot of work outside class, but there is a clear course set for you to succeed. Whether it is through an interesting connection or a funny remark, every lecture I attended added something to my day.
Best Professor Period
Homework graded by completion. Clear and easy to follow lecturer. Passionate. Occasionally funny. Straightforward exams. You'll get out of the class what you put in.

I love this man with all my heart. You could not ask for a better professor. A lot of criticisms are of Econ201 and not Nechyba himself, and that makes sense. Econ 201 is a hard class, but he makes it so much better. He is funny, approachable and genuinely caring. He also wrote the textbook and is a true expert. Power combo!!! LOVE HIM
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Nechyba is a super engaging lecturer and makes lectures interesting. Since ECON 101 is pass/fail, it can be hard to pay attention sometimes, but try your best to listen during lectures and learn something. I would recommend taking ECON 101 with him since his class has a much lighter workload and no exams and is less stressful overall.
Genuine person really cares about the content
Best Professor I have had so far! Very student- centred, and focuses a lot on being of use and help to students.

Econ201 is a difficult course by nature, and while I found the content to be boring/difficult, Nechyba was an AMAZING professor. There is a lot of homework, and I found lectures to not be super useful, but I really appreciated how compassionate Nechyba was. You could tell that he really cares about students and is very passionate about econ.

I didn't go to class or try particularly hard to understand the material, so I'm happy with the grade. The class is tough, but Nechyba goes above and beyond to help your grade. He gave extra credit opportunities and hosted review sessions on Zoom before the midterms and final. If you have to take the class, I can't imagine a better professor.

Professor Nechyba is always willing to make accommodations for students and give them the facilities they need to succeed. The material is difficult however the exams are very similar to what he teaches so there are few surprises, and the curves are generous. The class is definitely, however, in the end, a lot of people do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Take Econ 101 with Nechyba. He is an outstanding professor and person. One of the greatest at Duke.

Genuinely the best, best professor I've had at Duke so far. 201 is by nature a hard class, but Prof. Nechyba is just so caring and kind. As long as you keep up with the work, do the past exams and go to the review sessions, you'll be fine.

Really kind and understanding guy. The class is tough but he does everything he can to make it manageable. Homework can be pretty dense but midterms stick to the basics. Study for the midterms and you'll be fine because they make or break your grade

He's amazing! He's crystal clear at explaining, very patient, and genuinely wants students to learn the course materials well. He uses examples that relate to the real world. The class can be hard, but if you do all homework, do corrections, practice past year papers and attend the final study group sessions, you'll likely ace this class.

Professor Nechyba is an amazing professor and human being who provides tons of help out of class. The textbook homework tends to be extremely difficult, but the modules/quizzes are easy enough if you spend some time on them. I personally had a hard time focusing in lectures, but if you're an Econ major, I can't recommend Prof. Nechyba enough.
Nechyba is the best! Such a great teacher and an amazing person! He really cares about each of his students and gives you all the materials and resources you need to get an A.

Nechyba is the best teacher ever. He is funny, keeps lectures interesting and makes the course very fair. He is also really funny and cares so deeply about all his students. His class has always been my favorite.

Ignore the immature bad reviews... Nechyba is a GOAT! Top-tier Duke professor and ECON professor.

No matter your professor, Econ 201 will be a hard class, so might as take it with one of the most caring and nice professors at Duke (especially considering the class' lecture size). The way he teaches and helps students understand is unparalleled!!

If you watch the videos, show up to class and put in a modicum of effort, you will succeed. The lectures are clear and effective, as well as often including funny bits. He cares about his students but holds them to high ethical standards. He strives to stay aware of student desires and modify his class to help them succeed.

I have no clue how this guy is a 4.9. He's a nice guy and all but he resorts to pre-class videos to deliver most of the content and has quizzes that literally take forever to complete which are riddled with bugs and glitches. Completely put me off the econ department at Duke.
Really frustrating class. If you don't want to waste 10+ hours every week just take the class with another professor.
So nice, very funny. Genuinely wants you to learn and succeed.

Only haters leave bad reviews: this guy is a god and every student should be required to take one of his classes. Legitimately funny, never seen a guy care more about his students, and so chill. Yea it's a hard class: get over it it's not his fault. Lectures are amazing
Love this man and his red pants. People say he gives too much work but it’s not bad if you have a work ethic. Super supportive throughout the semester and actually cares if we learn.

Nechyba is so nice and tries so hard. Provides tons of office hours, old exams, genuinely wants you to succeed and gives you the tools to do so. Yes, the class is hard by nature, but some of the reviews on here are plain unfair. Also, his textbook is genuinely helpful and straightforward if you need it and follows the material nicely.

I really like professor nechyba! econ 201 is hard by nature, but he does his best to prepare you to do well. he actually wants you to succeed and gives you clear ways of doing so. he's really nice and engaging. it's not his fault 201 is hard, and i think he's great at explaining difficult concepts!
I really like Professor Nechyba as a person. But this course is so difficult and confusing. It is like a full time job :(

he sends out a ton of emails everyday which makes it super confusing and also the class in general is so extremely hard. i genuinely think that this is one of the hardest classes at duke. but he is so nice and wholesome
The class is a lot of work but he is so cute and wholesome. If you need to take econ 201 take it with him
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Nechyba is really nice!!! but this course is so hard and confusing with an insane amount of work outside of class.

Incredibly unfair ratings on here. Outstanding lecturer and teacher who describes complex content very clearly. It is a hard class and you will have to work a lot outside of class, but he is a uniquely open available teacher. Outstanding teacher-one of the bet I have had at Duke.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Makes the class much more difficult than it needs to be. Explanations of concepts are simple and easy to understand in the lectures and videos but quizzes and problem sets are extremely difficult and uncessarily time consuming. So much busy work and not a fun or interesting class.
Gives quizzes before each class with many mistakes and questions that he never taught us how to solve. Really frustrating and time consuming.
This man gives us quizzes to do with questions that we have never learned how to solve. It makes no sense.
Clear lectures and nice guy. Over the summer, was lenient on grading. Pretty easy to pass.

Take Econ201 with Nechyba! Econ201 was hard, but Nechyba used plain language to make the material understandable. Go to pre-exam office hours and do the past exams! They are the most helpful to prepare for exams. Nechyba would hold hrs of review sessions before every exam to ensure everyone learned the material. Lenient curve w/ an optional final.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Nechyba is a fantastic professor who excels at what he does. He is incredibly knowledgeable on the topic, and explains it in plain language to make it more understandable. Very accessible outside of class, takes a lot of time out of his busy day to ensure he addresses all questions in office hours. Other professors... take notes.

Dr. Nechyba is the best professor I've had at Duke so far. Going to his lectures is always a joy, and his lectures make the material very accessible. He is always very good at answering questions. Just make sure to go to lecture and keep up with the homework.

Nechyba is a King. THE greatest Econ professor I've ever seen. He's funny, helpful, nice, lenient, and knows the material like the back of his hand; he literally wrote the textbook, is constantly rewriting it and his lectures to better teach students, and can use real world examples and clear language to teach you what you need to know.

Before starting this class I heard a lot of comments from seniors about the difficulty of this class, but with the amount of support Dr Nechyba offers (love those pre-exam office hours) it becomes almost trivial to achieve a good grade. I wouldn't recommend taking ECON 201 with any other professors. He's also a great person outside of class. 11/10.
This guy is incredible. Tests were difficult but Nechyba is one of the best professor's that I have ever had.

Love the dude! Nechyba is so helpful outside of class and you know what to expect on the midterms. The material is hard, but good old persistency does the trick. Heads up that the content begins easy-ish, then spikes in difficulty, and then becomes more manageable. Also, gotta appreciate him giving a fall break when we're on a condensed semester!

Full disclosure, this is part 2 of the last review. I also think he gives really good explanations, and he's really patient with them too. The material is objectively difficult, so being confused isn't necessarily a reflection of his teaching ability. In any case, fantastic prof. I don't think the lower reviews do him justice.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I understand where the 1 star reviews are coming from--Nechyba might seem unapproachable because he's very dead-pan + has a dry sense of humor. However, I personally find him extremely willing to help--the week before every exam, he hosts probably about 10 hours of help sessions. He's also very understanding--he's posted lectures before on request.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Professor Nechyba is hands down the most amazing professor I've had at Duke so far. While the material for this class is not easy, he explains the concepts really well, and not to mention is very entertaining. I really appreciated his office hours before exams. Overall, he makes you work for it but it's 100% worth it!

reviews.comment: Best Professor ever, he is so dedicated and his office hours are so helpful!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This class is difficult, not interesting, and the professor is often condescending when you ask questions. Attendance is mandatory, even though classes are online. Lecture recordings are not posted, which just makes things harder for us. This sucks because it is so hard to pay attention because Nechyba is so boring.

I regret taking this class so much. Nechyba is unapproachable and not very nice. He explains concepts very badly and makes it difficult to understand concepts that should be easy. This class is so stressful for no reason.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I am taking his class during covid, so 2/3 lectures are over Zoom. This dude is so petty he refuses to give us access to the recorded lectures because he wants us to treat the class like "normal." Basically, he refuses to accomodate people in the times of covid and he makes us take exams IN PERSON. 174 students packed in one room. Great idea.

Nechyba wrote the textbook and it shows when he is doing lecture. You can easily fall behind in this class so having a solid study group and participation in discussion sections are very highly recommended. The class is curved to a B+ but the class also has very driven people so make sure you're one of them so you don't end up behind the pack.

Prof Nechyba gives great and personable lectures. He's super smart - he wrote the textbook - and really tries to help his students out with review sessions before midterms. The class is really difficult and material builds fast, so avoid falling behind by going to TA sections. Your grade is essentially only test grades (though curved to a B+).

Nechyba is a very knowledgable professor who loves to teach. Holds extra review sessions even on Sundays before the tests. The class itself is very rigorous and the lectures tend to be very dry at some points. The textbook comes in handy a lot of times. His tests are insanely tough but I'd recommend taking the class with him only.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: great lectuere, probably one of the best. help is really accessible outside of class with TAs, discussions, office hours, etc. doing the homework is really important to do well in the class. attendance definitely helps but isn't mandatory. with that being said, the midterms and final is very hard. taking this course in spring is probably easier

This class was the hardest class I have taken so far. The lectures are very dense and the material is hard to understand. Nechyba is great/well versed on this topic, but his lectures/textbook tend to be unnecessarily wordy. Definitely recommend hitting up office hours (with Chelsea- she taught the class this spring) and spending time on the info

reviews.comment: Great prof do well on your final and you're good
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Caring

reviews.comment: Nechyba is an amazing dude. He's really entertaining in lectures and really cares about teaching his students the material (he did write the textbook). Tests are extremely tough and make up almost all your grade but it's graded on a curve. It's a hard class but as long as you put in hard work it's manageable

Phenomenal professor who is passionate about economics and makes each lecture entertaining. He also wrote the textbook, which is very well written and becomes a valuable resource for mastering the material. The class is fast paced and tests are definitely hard, but there is a fairly lenient grading policy in place.

Great professor who truly cares about the material and student success. I never attended class as the in-class quizzes could be completed from anywhere. The book is a great resource for getting an in-depth understanding of the material. Exams are fairly difficult, but predictable if you review past exams. Material builds quickly.

Smart as hell, nice and funny. Tests are basically the only thing that decide your grade, so make sure you study for those. The class isn't easy and the material builds, but Nechyba is simply great at explaining tough concepts and makes himself very available before exams to help everyone out.

Funny and nice teacher, but lectures can often be a bit confusing, so it's helpful to read the textbook if needed. Exams are really difficult and frustrating, make sure to go see TA's and ask questions.

Nechyba is a great lecturer, explains things clearly and has a good sense of humor. Since he wrote the textbook you don't really need to read it in addition because everything is covered in the lectures. Grading is very fair and he is very transparent about the grading system.

Nechyba is a  brilliant professor and he knows his Economics. Beware though: the material builds up rapidly, and if you are lazy, you will not survive in this class. It's a tough class, but if you put effort into it, you will do  fine. Also, get maximum prepared for every exam, because your whole grade depends on two midterms and a final.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Great Lecturer, turning grades back in a timely manner

Arguably the best Econ professor at Duke, he knows the material better than anyone else (wrote the textbook) so his lectures are very clear and organized. Workload consists of a problem set a week. His tests are difficult, you have to work hard and study a lot to earn a good grade. But in the end, most students usually do well (B/B+ average).

Very tough class and material but Professor Nechyba did a great job of explaining it during lectures. He is always on top of grading and gives plenty of resources for the exams. The midterms and final are all really difficult with the average grade being lower than 65. But the class is curved to a B/B+ and there is a very flexible grading policy.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Nechyba is extremely passionate and actually enjoys teaching. He's department chair so he's not very accessible out of class but the TA office hours and review sessions that he holds are pretty helpful. Mid-semester he hands the class off to an assistant professor but is still there for all the lectures. Generally this prof isn't as good as Nechyba
He is one of the best professors I've ever had.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Best professor I have ever had at Duke!

Very good professor, clear lectures based on book he wrote. Can skip class and get A, as textbook is written by him and extremely useful. Clearly wants to help student. Lectures can be entertaining with jokes, songs (look out for Barney song), and more jokes. Was wrongly criticised on Yikyak for harsh grade distribution (totally untrue!)

Nechyba is just phenomenal. Incredible at explaining concepts and giving relevant examples. His tests will uncover the true extent to which you have understood the material, but the class is curved to a BB+ so most people end up with a decent grade.  He puts great effort into this class so you just want to work hard too. Take 201 with him.
Econ 201 is a hard class in general, but Nechyba's lectures were entertaining and he cares a lot about students doing well. Fair overall, and if you're going to take 201 then take it from Nechyba.

Nechyba is the best. There's no way around it. While the material itself is hard, Nechyba is a great lecturer, and he explains everything well. You're going to have to put work in for this class, but it is definitely not impossible to do well. If you work hard, attend lecture, and do homework, you have a great chance of doing well in this class.

Nechyba is the best Econ teacher I've ever had. His lectures are  very engaging and quite funny. He wrote the Econ 201 textbook, and that speaks volumes about how knowledgeable he is. Tests are tough, but put in effort and let the curve do the rest. If you ever consider taking Econ 201, take it with Nechyba! He is boss.

Could be the best professor I have had at Duke. Professor Nechyba is an AMAZING teacher and person, and I would highly recommend taking a course with him. Class will be pretty difficult, but it is much worth it as you will learn a ton of information. He is willing to help as much as possible outside of class.
Professor Nechyba is brilliant and is an amazing professor. Explains concepts clearly and is very helpful. Class was tough, but if you do the work you will do fine.
Excellent professor, super helpful. Wants the kids to do well. Hard tests!
The modern-day Dr. Seuss of Economics. His lectures are super engaging, but it's a bit difficult to ask questions in class. TA's are great, though.

Extremely intelligent, funny, and really tries to make the material more interesting and relatable to students. Very accessible if you reach out for help and is very personable and knowledgable about the subject and how best to teach it. Fantastic professor.
He's an awesome lecturer, although the course is difficult. If you want to do well, you need to put the work in, plain and simple. But Nechyba is funny, interesting, and absolutely brilliant.
Great professor with obvious experience and knowledge. Connects with students and enjoys teaching.
Tough class no way around it, but Nechyba is tha man.  Great teacher, good at explaining.
Nechyba is a boss. The tests are hard but the curve is massive so you end up doing well. Very funny in class. You do not need to go to class at all.

Cemented my interest in Economics. The man literally wrote the book on Econ 201. Quite literally one of the most amazing professors I've ever known. Any university and student would be lucky to have him.

Nechyba is the absolute best! He's SO friendly and helpful and absolutely hilarious! His class is very entertaining and he makes the subject matter easy to understand - especially since he wrote the textbook. His powerpoints and prelectures are very useful when studying. Midterm averages are low (60s) but the tests aren't too hard. He's wonderful
Nechyba's an amazing professor but his exams are extremely difficult. However, if you pay attention to him in class and put in some effort, it's not that difficult to get a good grade.

Nechyba was an amazing professor. Intermediate microeconomics is generally boring but his class turned me into an econ major. You can screw up big time in the beginning and he will give you chances to come back from it.

Wrote consistently difficult problems, but explained the material so well and provided so much material to help that it was very manageable. I probably learned the most in this course out of all I've taken here. Just keep your head up,; you will never feel like you have mastered the material.

He's amazing! Now that I'm finished with the class, I kind of regret not paying attention to him sometimes in class. If you get behind in class, though, looking at his fantastic powerpoints will be more than enough to catch up. Books are good, but too long; powerpoints will suffice. Tests are hard but previous exams help a lot and the curve is a B+

If you're taking Econ 201D, take it with Nechyba. The tests are very hard but fair. The class is curved to a B.  Nechyba gives engaging lectures, posts tons of study materials online, and is always willing to answer questions in and out of class. He is a teacher of the highest quality. I have no regrets taking the class

Dr. Nechyba is very helpful outside of class and will always answer your emails if you have questions on the material. He is lenient in terms of grading if he knows you're overwhelmed, so talk to him if you have a very bad schedule and can't get through all the work the class gives you. Tests are very hard. Don't cram and do the hw for practice.

This year was a flipped-format class, so prelectures were posted and a quiz was given at the beginning of the class and counted in final grade.You will learn most of the material well, but not quite deep enough to be able to do his problems. Test questions are always never-before-seen, which made me weary toward the end of the course.
Great professor! Funny and made the class really interesting and fun. wrote his own textbook, hilarious!
Incredible teacher. Do whatever you can to take a class with Nechyba. His lectures are fantastic and he's a great role model overall.

Professor Nechyba is a great professor. He clearly explains tough material and makes lectures fun and interesting. He connects everyone with the material instead of simply reading from the powerpoints. Homework is very difficult and so are the tests but if you go to the lectures and sections, do the homeworks, and use the TAs, you will do fine.
If you are an Econ major, try to take 55 with Nechyba.  He explains the material extremely well and you use the textbook that he wrote.

Great prof.  Made lectures interesting and fun.  Had a clever adaptation of the barney theme song reviewing several topics before our exam.  Lectures cover the material at the depth required, and the problem sets work you through the nuances to prepare you for his tests (which are fair) and not that hard.  Best prof i've had at school by far.

Great professor. Extremely smart and funny. He makes big lectures interesting and useful. Tests are hard, but getting a good grade isn't impossible. Answers emails and questions regularly. Very helpful out of class.

Funny professor. Very helpful. He will always stay for a while after class, and it's a good change to ask questions. Homework is impossible, but really helpful on tests. Advice for good grade is attend all classes (awake), look at slides right after classes and do homework.
Funny, smart, and enthusiastic. Makes a large class feel small. Tests are very hard, but you're likely to end up with a decent grade once the curve sets in.

Professor Nechyba is an excellent lecturer and he makes taking this pretty boring core class quite bearable. His textbook is very successful (even though you shouldn't waste time reading it right before the exam) and he is extremely helpful, very responsive to e-mails. He is the way to go if you want to take 55D.

He makes his lectures as interesting as they can be, even though it can be hard to concentrate sometimes in such a huge class. Nechyba is extremely knowledgable, and he can clarify things really well outside of class. His tests, however, are really hard, even with the curve.
the best professor you will ever have at Duke, he makes even a lecture with 250 people feel personable with all the help he provides for everyone.  i mean he wrote the book, he's legit man
Calls himself Econ Boy. Sings Barney in class. Makes Dr.Seuss book about econ lesson.
Great prof.  Really make you understand the materials in depth.  Homeworks and tests are dreadful...  pretty low averages.

He's been the Chair of the dept. for like 5 years, and he still takes time to meet with students outside of class, even though he's super busy. He's a great instructor and judging by my grad TAs he's a great Chair too, looking out for what's best for the department and students, not just professors. HE IS THE MAN!

Hahaha..Dr Nechyba is truly the most awesome professor I've ever had, seriously. He made econs super-interesting and easy, of course!since he knows every single bit of the material!Take his class and prepare to enjoy..I really didn't miss a single class because of HIM.

Nechyba is the only way to enjoy Econ 55. Extremely difficult class, but as the author of the book, he makes it manageable, interesting, and entertaining.  One word of advice: don't be fooled by the high curve (B/B+) or his laid back attitude. The tests are impossible (average on final was 49) and the class is filled with brilliant kids.
suuuch an amazing teacher. hes so knowledgeable! so passionate. hes currently writing his own textbook (which is the "book" we use)...

The most professional teacher i have ever had, made me become an econ major. His Exams are ridiculous but you will really get to know the material. He is funny and entertaining. He was writing the T-book and teaching the class so there were many errors which he admitted later made learning harder, but all in all my favorite professor at duke

Nechyba has been the best prof I've had so far. You learn a lot of interesting economics. He's very funny and talks about his wife a lot. Test averages were, 66,60, and a 55 on final (curved this up to 60). He curves the class to a B avg. Tests are difficult but manageable. He is brilliant and very helpful. Uses the book he wrote.
great professor. class is hard, but he makes it fun.
best prof i have had so far. he is awesome - but it might be find to hard classes he is teaching because he is the head of the department.

All I can say about this guy is that his tests are so effing hard.  I didn't really go to class so I guess it's my fault I didn't do so well.  Also, his book that he was writing as we went along had errors and made things confusing.  He should have finished it before teaching the class.

Fantastic teacher, makes a very difficult class manageable.  you'll wonder why he's making you learn the basics, but you'll appreciate it later on the final, when everything falls into place.  Lectures are really interesting, and he's a generally, all around great guy.  One of the best I've had here
Honestly the reason why I became an econ major...he made economics INTERESTING!!!  I looked forward to every lecture.
Nechyba was a great professor. He really makes the material interesting and easy to understand.
Great professor, funny, good lectures.  Hard exams and long homework assignments.
Great teacher! Very funny guy.

THE BEST CLASS EVER!!! THE BEST TEACHER EVER!!! I'm so glad I got to take his class this semester!! He's not only a great teacher, but really funny and such a terrific person! He holds review sessions before midterms, and that takes real dedication! =)
funny and pretty good lectures

Dr. Nechyba is awesome.  His lectures are fairly interesting, and he makes a really hard class worth taking. He's extremely helpful, but everyone fails the first test. If you go to his office hours he gives hw answers and tells a ton of jokes. generous curve, which is nice; makes fun of his wife

The material was excellently taught, and the guy is hilarious.  He makes fun of his wife practically every lecture, and today he was giving out cash to people.  Generally just an awesome lecturer.  The material in 55 is tough (for me, freshman), but he explains it pretty well.  Take his course!
This is prof is walking aura max-er, her voice, her fit, her gaze, her knowledge. LITERAL LEGEND.
This is prof is walking auramaxxer, her voice, her fit, her gaze, her knowledge. LITERAL LEGEND.

I took gchina course in 2018. Although many years have passed, I still clearly remember how uncomfortable the experience was. Her teaching style was highly dominant, and quieter students were often overlooked, especially in classes with very outspoken or assertive students.

I genuinely love this professor, she's a hidden gem. She's extremely knowledgeable and gives such good lectures so that you can understand the readings. Her feedback on essays, drafts, group presentations are extremely valuable, helpful and detailed! She's also super nice and she values your participation in class discussions a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Looking back, I think she is one of my favorite profs at DKU: she is strict but fair, and also kind and very helpful. She is very demanding (read all texts and speak up!), but it was rewarding. It's obvious that she is an expert in her field and loves the course. So, if you actually want to study the course, I would highly recommend this professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Zhu is a great professor overall and very knowledgeable in what she teaches. She talks a lot and sometimes takes up time that you could use for participation in discussion, which is graded. There are 3 essays throughout the course that she gives good feedback on.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Zhu was very willing to help me with my essays, either over Zoom or over email.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Prof Zhu is kind and caring once she gets to know you. The workload is big yet the course is interesting and engaging. The lectures are quite inspiring.

This course is really rewarding. By watching movies (which I think is very interesting) and doing some reading, you will have a new understanding of Chinese history and culture. Participation matters. Assignments are not so tough. Also, Prof. Zhu is really nice. She is always accessible outside class and gives detailed feedback on your papers.

Visual China in the hybrid format is a LOT of work. Professor Zhu will have require you to watch 2 two and half hour long films each week with forum posts and the lectures are hybrid 2.5 hours twice a week where international students watch the class. I would not recommend taking this class if you are a remote student.

The course content of this professor is substantial, meaningful and not very difficult. The professor has a high demand for language and grammar in essay. She is really strict with your grammar and words.
She's a bit intimidating when you first meet her, but she can be nice and warm once you get to know her more. She has high expectations
Prof. Zhu is a very good professor, and Chinese film history is a part of her speciality, so the class is very well organized. It is a lot of work but it is rewarding.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Tough grader

reviews.comment:
Midterm and final oral exams. One group presentation. Canvas discussion board due prior to each class. Class is discussion based on assigned readings. No electronics allowed.

The grading is unreasonable. Professor Bowman can come as rude, even if that is not his intention. Don't take a class with him unless you have to. Best of luck.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Bowman is condescending and sometimes rude to students. The class is completely useless and not sure how it can be mandatory in the curriculum.

reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Very strict grader, going to his office hours and running essay ideas past him first didn't really help. His feedback was confusing. In class he didn't really appreciate participation much, but still demanded it. Loves to pick apart and challenge the opinions or points students raise. Class is just going through the readings detail by detail.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Bowman is quite knowledgeable and conveys his opinions very clearly. He is also accessible outside of the class. The class is discussion-based and not difficult at all. As long as you do the readings, you will be fine.

Global challenges was MUCH better than I anticipated going in, and I ended up really enjoying the class even if the workload was sometimes a bit intense. Lots of opportunities to discuss (it's a discussion-based class for sure) and chances to learn about pressing real-world issues. Prof Bowman is willing to work with you if you're struggling too!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Prof. Bowman is knowledgeable and conveys his ideas very clearly. He is dedicated to helping students learn, as shown by how meticulous he marks essays and offers advice during office hours. His readings are long but fascinating. Except when we make policy proposals or debate, discussions are dry as they're mostly summaries of readings.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Prof. Bowman is very caring. Students can receive many academic reviews from him via different types of homework. His grading criteria are quite clear and prepare you well for responses. But the readings are a bit difficult and students need to work hard on it to participate in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: ETHLDR 108 is an intro writing course, so of course there's going to be a lot of writing assignments. He encourages engagement with the readings and he places a big emphasis on group discussion. He's understanding of extenuating circumstances, and will work with you to succeed on your assignments. His rubrics for assignments are really helpful!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I personally did not vibe with this class. The readings were super interesting but the discussions and assignments fell short of their full potential (classes were more summary than critical thinking). Also a stickler for grammar/citations etc. so I felt my content/thoughts/learning mattered less. He's a nice guy and tries to reach out out often!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Pop quiz every week but helps u learn things. This class is very useful compared to ones on the theoretical sides if u wanna do swe (cs 590). He loves what he teaches and lectures well. Helpful on ed and during OH. Nice man
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I took CS 590 (Web Dev). This class really does teach you all the stuff the core CS curriculum won't teach you but is crucial for a career as a SWE. I learned so much from this class and the examples he shows are so informative. The final project is time consuming (mostly debugging) but you learn so much from it. Quizzes mostly every week

I took the 590 section, not 290. Dr. Quan was clearly very adept in his field of work and his instruction was concise and packed with information. Honestly pretty easy grading, the course had some decently difficult assignments but it could always be solved within a few days.

*CS590. Dennis is an amazing professor. He is very respected in his industry and knows exactly what students should learn to become a successful full-stack developer from his years of experience in industry. He teaches the fundamentals that every SWE/FEE should know. After taking his course, I am confident that I can apply them in my job post grad

Dennis was a fantastic professor for CS290. He is extremely knowledgable and will always have an answer for you. He's very approachable and will never make you feel stupid by asking questions. He also has insight into how the tech industry works and tries to incorporate that knowledge into class lectures. I learned the most through OH with him.
Dennis is one of the best professors. He's very informative when he teaches and extremely approachable. Whenever you ask him a question, you know that he has a solution for you. He's the best!!

Prof Quan and CS201 were both great. The homework can be tricky and the grading is really slow but he is flexible and its really easy to get help. Towards the end of the class, things start moving really fast but overall I learned a lot and enjoyed the course.
His lectures were very well structured. Regardless of the concept, he explained things with clear explanations and or helpful metaphors.
Dennis was awesome I really enjoyed his lectures and he was super approachable outside class!!Loved the class

Sandra is absolutely incredible! She is so caring, funny, and understanding. She puts so much effort into her classes and cares so much about your performance. French 111 is a lot of work. It's every day at 8:30 am with tons of homework and graded assignments every week. Her grading is very fair, though. An amazing professor! Take French with her.

Sandra is the best professor I've met so far. Lectures and activities are engaging and it's obvious she puts a lot of effort into teaching: every sub-section of your final grade and related feedback will be available ASAP so you know what to work on. 
It's very hard not to love language learning if you're introduced to French by her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Valnes is the most kind, understanding, and considerate professor I have ever had. Her grading criteria are clear and lenient and if you do your light daily workload of homework you are basically guaranteed an A. You will look forward to go to class. She makes you like French, and this says a lot on how good of a professor she is.

SVQ is one of the best language teachers I've had. She is so vibrant and bubbly in class thus creating a comfortable atmosphere for you to try things and slip up. Her tests are fair and while the class overall did move pretty quickly, she was always available to help and was genuinely invested in her students. The kind to really get to know them.
Great teacher.

Madame is the best language lecturer I've ever met in my life. She is caring, and her office hour is always open. If you want to meet professor outside of classroom, just send her an email. Also, she replied my email back really quickly, sometimes less than 10 minutes!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Creates an amazing environment for you to learn in. Very focused on speaking and will make you a better speaker and writer. Good teacher and you can tell she really cares about the material and wants you to learn. Writing-heavy outside of class, but you should still take a course with her!

Madame Quammen was definitely one of my favorite professors at Duke. She really cares about her students and wants us to learn. The class does have a decent amount of homework, but as long as you do the work and participate in class, you will do well. She made this class very engaging and enjoyable.
I absolutely loved Prof. Quammen. Her lessons were engaging and she was great at making students feel comfortable speaking in class discussion. I would definitely recommend her as a language teacher.
Highly recommend for French 204. Lots of grammar, but she is a fair grader and understands each students place in the language level and class as a whole.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof. Quammen was a very approachable and friendly professor who always facilitated organized class discussions. We covered plenty of material in a short semester and it really boosted my confidence in my French speaking skills. Her midterm was disproportionately difficult compared to the rest of the graded work, however.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: She's super nice and always willing to help if you have any questions. That said, she was definitely a slightly tougher grader than other professors teaching the same course. There is a pretty strong focus on grammar in this course, and that can definitely screw you over if you don't have a strong background.

You have to do your work and you can't slack off, but if you put forth the effort it's not a bad class. Her tests, quizzes, etc are all incredibly fair, and you have detailed rubrics for things like writing assignments. She is SUCH a helpful and kind professor; I would definitely recommend taking any course with her!!

She is so enthusiastic! She's very sweet and will always help you out. She is a very good instructor, and I wish I could take her for all of my future French courses. Her tests and quizzes are fair, but you'd need to study to get the grade. Homework can be a bit tedious at times, with some every night. But she would make up for it all.

Loved this class! Hugely recommended for ALL french students. Gives a comprehensive and profound overview of french culture; very engaging and thought-provoking. There is quite a lot of homework, but the grading is VERY fair. Professor Valnes Quammen is sweet, approachable and super helpful.

just look at her raving reviews. she is super sweet and always enthusiastic. definitely take french with her; you'll learn so much. there's 30 min of hw every night, certainly bearable. you have to go to class every day and participate, so do that and you'll get a good grade. i 3 sandra
The absolute best! - Enough said :)

She is everything you could want from a language professor: kind, energetic, passionate, intelligent, and prepared. Do your homework, show up to class, and you will learn more in a semester than you did in a couple of years in High School

She is such a sweet professor! She is always (seemingly) in a good mood and teaches well. Her grading is fair and she teaches well. I felt like I learned more in one semester with her than I did in my two/three years of high school French

I came into this class wanting to learn French. Prof. Sandra solidified my desire. She is easily one of the most dynamic teachers I will ever take, and I highly recommend her. Although it seems like we move at light speed sometimes, she is always available to lend a helping hand and clarify confusing subjects in an instant. Elle est fantastique!
Wonderful Professor, comes to class extremely prepared every day with games and activities incorporating French into everyday circumstances. This is the way French should be taught.

This teacher was fantastic. Everyone that is lucky enough to get this teacher should take her. Grading isn't easy and you have to show up for class, but she makes it very easy to learn and be involved in class.
Great professor. Recommend highly!
Very good teacher, do all of the homework though and participate a lot. Shes very very nice, approachable and grades fairly

the most encouraging instructor out of the department and easily the most approachable. straightforward and articulate. always excited and prepared for class. in my experience, the best french instructor available.

Sandra Valnes is the best French teacher I have ever had.  She comes to class everyday extremely prepared (literally like clockwork) and is extremely upbeat. French at 9AM could have been an awful thing, but she made it the highlight of my semester. The only drawback I would say is that she is an very tough grader.

Valnes's class was the highlight of my semester. She revolutionized both my ability to understand spoken French and my ability to speak it myself. She is extremely engaging, encouraging, and approachable. Don't miss the chance to take Valnes's class.

she's nice but sometimes a little cold.  she's a great teacher but her grading is sometimes harsh and you can be destroyed if you start slacking at any time during the semester.  stay on top of everything and go to class

Possesses great konwledge of subject material and speaks in a clear, articulate french accent. Although the material is straightforward and often times easy, she tends to grade deceptively harder than one would expect. Easily accessible and a great help, but you must have a general idea of what you need help on. An overall good teacher.
She a great person, very helpful and fun.

Sandra is extremely friendly, helpful, and encouraging.  All the French classes are very centalized, but she finds a way of adding a personal touch to them.  Very responsive to email, lots of office hours.  Great person all around.
She is so sweet and she makes class interesting...even at 8:45 am. She is great!

Unclear grading policies which allows seemingly any grade to be justified. Difference between my first paper, which I spent multiple days on, and the second, which I spent an hour on, was 0.25 points. Predatory grading, both my papers were scored just above the retake threshold of 70 (70.5/70.25) despite positive feedback. Destroyed my GPA.
Very caring, organized course structure. Is clearly very passionate, knowledgable, and respectable in the field. Many papers and group debates, but also a decent amount of reading.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--So many papers

reviews.comment: Dr. Quick is a very interesting guy! He has lived all over the world working on health policy and has a lot of first hand knowledge about the things he teaches in class. The class is composed of case studies, debates, papers. The grading on the papers can be tough and erratic but he is willing to give feedback. Good intro to global health policy!
angel sent by heaven

love her! just submit assignments on time and attend class (whilst studying a bit beforehand because she cold calls sometimes to make sure people are studying) and you will have a major buffer for the exams, which is great. super kind and really understanding if you communicate w her, she is happy to make accommodations. great intro course.

A fun and great professor, she gives many extra credits to students as a way to incentivize learning the material more. Also very caring and will work out any situation or problem you have. Grading is alright, you can easily get a good grade but getting perfect or close to it can be difficult. An energetic professor, highly recommend her.

She is nice and fun, I enjoyed her class and have learned a lot. Definitely a lot of work to do but I feel myself making progress all the time. She is fair but she is a tough grader and very serious about class policies. Not easy to get an A.

Laoshi is great. She cares about the students very much, she is always open to help them. Explains Chinese grammar well. She is very fair. These classes require a lot of homework but are very interesting.

She is a fun teacher and to be honest, the class didn't feel like too much work when in it. I say this because things flow like a conversation, and it's all one big conversation. 

You go into zoom breakout rooms before performing contextualized drills, and it's just like how you rehearsed it and nothing changes on the spot.

It's easy to do well.

lots of homework and quizzes, but it made it easier to end up with a good grade as there were many buffers and points to help. really kind teacher who just wants people to pass the class, so reach out if you ever need extra help or are worried - she's super flexible. definitely participate extra in class and prep ahead to make it less stressful.

Chinese 101 is very hard, but A is easy if you follow on the weekly work. Professor Qin, on the other hand, is the kindest instructor I have had the fortune to have. She is the perfect teacher to introduce you to a foreign language. She grades generously too.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Qin Laoshi is super nice! She made learning Chinese very fun. I totally recommend having classes with her.
Best introduction ever to chinese. Great professor.
She is very nice person and generous grader. I had a great experience with her. The best introduction to Chinese

Professor Qin is honestly a gem, she provides feedback on almost all assignments, so if you get points off for something, you'll know why. You have to be on top of your work, sometimes she doesn't assign work until two days before class. Her quizzes are simple and she offers ample opportunity for extra credit. Also, you NEED to do prework.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr. Q is so knowledgeable about disability justice and made the W101 Disability & Democracy course one that I enjoyed. The content learned in this course is very applicable to daily life, and I think this is a class that everyone should take. The final paper is split up so it's not too overwhelming, and lots of low-stakes opportunities for credit.

Dr. Q really made writing 101 such a fascinating class. I really liked how she gave us so many low-stakes opportunities to earn credit. The readings, presentations, and discussions were intriguing and not really a burden at all. The final paper was SUPER organized and never became too much to deal with. Would recommend to any freshmen.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I LOVED Dr. Q! Disabilities & Democracy was fascinating & completely changed how I look at the world around me. You don't HAVE to do the readings, but they're interesting and I enjoyed. She's not a hard grader and the class was discussion-based with a mix of presentations and papers/forums. She really cares and is passionate about what she teaches!

Dr. Q is passionate about disability studies and introduced me to a range of new perspectives. Class discussions are relatively interesting but nothing too special. Workload starts out pretty light but ramps up a lot in the second half of the year.

I took her Writing 101 class and it had an interesting title, but the content of the course had little to do with the title. There's not a ton of work, but there are weekly blog posts. I can't tell if she is a tough grader yet since she has not graded anything, but participation definitely matters a lot. Pretty blunt, course is largely opinion base

I would highly recommend Dr. Q for Writing 101! She is very passionate about disability studies and cares for her students. The discussions we had were very engaging and interesting. I would recommend you to go to her office hours for feedback before you submit an essay. Also, the workload is manageable with weekly reading assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Compared to other writing101 classes, she really makes you work for a good grade. Just take another prof's writing101 class. Most of the discussion is just random crap that's obvious. For example, no one is going to argue against a paper that supports giving disabled people rights.
I had Dr.Q for a disability studies writing course and she is also active with the student disability advocacy group on campus. She is passionate about disability studies and a great person.

Really interesting professor. She definitely is passionate and knowledgeable about disability studies and her class is well organized. Participate in the discussions because they are engaging. There is a good amount of reading but nothing that is not manageable.
I definitely think that my writing improved a lot in Dr. Q's class.  She is extremely organized.  Be prepared to have meaningful discussions.  The workload is manageable, but not light.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Banned Books- Prof Wiegman is a fantastic professor. Engaging, smart, and forces you to be more deliberate and articulate with analysis. Highly recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Very knowledgeable prof. Few assignments, but she allows revisions on papers after submission of first draft and is very accommodating. It is a big workload, but I learned a lot and enjoyed the class overall.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: LIT 89S - Professor Wiegman is amazing. She gives great feedback and is very understanding -- even changed the syllabus a couple times when the work got a bit demanding at points. The seminars were very engaging and thought provoking. If you put in the work, you will get a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: LIT89: Banned Books. Professor Wiegman created an incredibly interesting class that was reading and writing heavy, compared to other seminars. She expected a high level of writing and graded tougher than I expected. I loved class conversations would recommend to students seeking a course that challenges intellectual thinking and writing abilities.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: For ENGLISH89S, Banned Books. I LOVED this class and Dr. Wiegman. She is incredibly knowledgeable on the course content yet she listens to what we have to say about it too. I liked the structure of the class and her teaching style. Most of the time, we just discuss the readings in class, which can get dull sometimes, but overall, was a great class.

I loved taking 201 with Prof. Wiegman. I was debating on a GCS major, and her class absolutely sealed the deal for me. She's also an awesome person and really cares about her students. She appreciates you taking risks and grades accordingly. Awesome course, awesome professor--highly recommend anything she teaches.

This was not taught as an intro course. There was an expectation that you came in with a full understanding of working with theory. Upon struggling and asking for help, I was made to do double the work as my peers with no guidance. I was disappointed that upon asking for help I felt punished. I would not recommend this class for curious non-majors
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Tough grader

reviews.comment: If you do not have prior experience with reading theory or are not a humanities student, do not take this course. It is not designed as an intro. The material itself is super interesting, however, if you disagree with her interpretation of it you will be miserable in this class. She also is not understanding whatsoever of mental health issues.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Wiegman is super understanding/accommodating and very accessible outside of class. This class taught me so much about the world, and it's really given me perspective on the systems of power we operate in on a daily basis. Highly recommend this class and prof. Grading can be a little hard, but it's reasonable.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Robyn is sensational! One of her strengths is her ability to accommodate different intellectual levels in the class - from beginner "non-humanities" ppl to senior Lit majors. She's understanding of students and has pushed deadlines back. Overall, the class is a fair amount of reading and theoretical discussion heavy. Very stimulating
robyn is the best

Professor Wiegman is a great professor. She has interesting lectures, teaches engaging material, and gives amazing feedback on written assignments. Beyond that, there was never a time when she was unresponsive to my requests to meet with her outside of class. The midterm is a lot of writing but the final was a simple, enjoyable essay.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Material is interesting, but the grading makes it harder than it should be. Exams carry almost all the weight. Even when the class did well, it wasn't really reflected positively. Overall, not the most student-friendly setup despite decent content.
Exams and grading feels like AI
Hates giving As. At times he seemed frustrated when the class did well on quizzes, calling them “too easy” and basically promising that next time would be harder.

Feels like he doesn't want people getting A's. Exams graded harshly/inconsistently, people pointed to correct answers and still got no credit. Curve is super strict (people 0.05 from an A didn't get one). Syllabus weight changed late, discussion/attendance stopped mattering and exams became everything.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Don't look at the syllabus because he doesn't follow it. He only curves the top half of the class. Genuinely impossible to read the slides and the most boring lectures ever. At the end of the class he just averaged all of the grades and took no regard for the weighting in the syllabus. Seriously don't take this class.

He is quite knowledgable about this field and contributes a vast amount of information to the neuroscience of memory. However, his teaching style is not well done. His priority is on his research. The lectures are quite dense, the weekly group quiz difficulty is hard to predict, and the exam vary in rigor without any prep. Do not recommend taking.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Classes are based primarily off of tests, which are very straightforward if you read the textbook (multiple choice) and understand the concepts discussed in lectures (essay portion). Overall easy class.

He's an extremely smart professor and it shows, but his lectures are very difficult to pay attention to. His accent isn't difficult to understand, but the whole course is based off of three very difficult mid-terms. Attendance isn't mandatory but you miss material that you'll need to know. I wouldn't recommend this course to freshmen. Killed my GPA

The professor seems like a nice guy but it is definitely easy to zone out during his lectures which he recently has made very important on tests. Tests consisted of multiple choice questions (based off the text book and section readings) and short response questions (based on his lectures). The multiple choice is simple. The Lecture Qs are harder.

Interesting, fairly easy class but not that well-structured. Book is all you need for tests; lecture was somewhat relevant but largely just focused on his own fMRI research which without a conceptual background was incomprehensible. Would have stopped going to class if not for the quizzes. Discussion sections were OK.

Cognitive psych was less exciting than I hoped. The professor seems like a really nice person who is interested in what he teaches, but lectures became repetitive. You cannot learn everything that will be on tests if you do not attend lectures.

Very nice guy, but had a pretty thick accent.  He's much more interested in talking about research in his lectures, but the tests barely touch on it.  Most of the test grade comes from the textbook's test bank.  The TAs make the tests.  You must got to class and you must pay attention if you want the grade.

Professor Cabeza is pretty hard to understand if you don't sit near the front of class. The tests are generated from a random selection of questions, which end up getting harder as the semester wears on. The class is NOT curved despite what is said in class, as I received the exact grade as my points added up to.

Sit near the front of class because there is no way you will see the slides/ understand him any other way. The tests are based off the books and the section readings mostly, but a big question on his lectures might trip you up. Class is curved though.

Amazing class and professor. EASY and relatively interesting. No final paper, no final exam. 4 exams, which are 60% of your grade (you can ace them as long as you read the book and go to class). 8% participation, 32% from these little 4 question quizzes at each lecture's end based on the lecture and reading (easy to ace if you pay attention).
This professor is great!  the quizzes are a super easy way to get an A and the tests aren't bad either.  The average in the class is a B+!

Cabeza is a really nice and interesting professor, although it's really easy to zone out in his class due to his really thick accent. I got below average on all 3 of the exams and still managed to make a B. Make sure you do well on the reading quizzes and the poster project and you should do fine.
cabeza did have a thick accent and was hard to understand however, if you actually put effort into the class and do all the work it's easy to get an A. also, the class is curved to a b+.

Horrid =( Cabeza has a really thick accent and teaches 92 like 91--too much biopsych stuff. Class structure is bad: you end up reading the entire textbook (barely relates to lecture). Tests are too know-it-or-not and they're more on the book (overly specific Q's) than lecture--why attend class? Curve to A-? Lies. Raw --> final grade. (no curve!)

Professor Cabeza is probably the best professor I have had so far. His lectures are very interesting, well-organized, and interactive. The daily quizzes are fine if you do the reading, so you can get close to 100% for 1/3 of your overall class grade. The tests are fair and the professor is very helpful in answering any questions.
Worst prof I ever had at Duke.

TAKE THIS CLASS!!!! if you do the readings, you will get an A in the class and on the daily quizzes. the quizzed will help your grade b/c people won't show to class and just get zeros. the tests are easy and he will learn your name in a huge lecture class. FANTASTIC CLASS AND PROFESSOR!
Most importantly, he can't speak English.  He also gives out quizes at the end of EVERY SINGLE LECTURE.

Wait till he tells you about his curve where the average is an A-. That's awesome. Daily quizzes actually end up helping your grade as long as you stay on top of the reading. His accent is a little difficult, but manageable. Take PSY 92 from him for sure.
Very nice guy, tries to help but can't always. Tries to make class as easy as possible. Daily quizzes help your grade, but make the class a little rough on the nerves.
Really helpful, good professor.  A little bit hard to understand due to his strong accent.  But, a really good guy.
So, there are daily quizzes...not too hard.  The tests can be pretty difficult, since there is a lot of material that is not well-organized.
No Comments
A very nice guy, kind of difficult to understand with his accent sometimes. The lectures are fun and the tests relatively easy.
Very interested in getting to know students, very responsive to student requests
Very dedicated to students
nicest guy ever, great class

she's really nice as a person but terrible as a teacher. It's simply unfair for you as a student to take her massively hard class while other kids who take it in the spring have it so much easier. The tests are full of exceptions and tricks and she teaches too much stuff that doesn't come back in orgo 2 and is just a waste of time.

Her lectures are horrible and not helpful for the tests at all. I had to teach myself everything outside of class and that even was not good enough because her tests are impossible- full of exceptions/tricks. The only redeeming quality was that the curve at the end of the semester is very forgiving.

Worst prof I've ever had. Hands down. Lectures were absolutely useless because she doesn't know how to teach. Tests are impossible and don't reflect what we learned. Had to self study using the textbook. Please don't make the same mistake as me by taking orgo freshman fall. WAIT UNTIL THE SPRING to get a better teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy
