reviews.comment: Dr. Wang likes to emphasize the "why" behind all the concepts in the course, so taking her class is very beneficial for those who would like to have a good chemistry foundation. HOWEVER, if you are looking for an easy A, I would find a different professor. (I highly recommend this course for chemistry majors.)
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Wang is, to be frank, a terrible teacher. Her lectures focus heavily on unimportant topics while skipping past the topics that are on the test, which are considerably difficult. Office hours will be your best friend. However, the curve at the end of the class is VERY generous. She is also a geniuenly nice and caring person.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: oh boy where do i even start. wang is my sunshine. every day i go to class and her lecture makes my day. i dont know where i would be without her. she is the goat.

Dr. Wang is an amazing professor. Her lectures clarify concepts very well and her humor helps the information stick! The textbook isn't always the most helpful so I'd recommend watching videos about the topic if they are available and make sure to go to office hours--they are so, so helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: If you only care about the grade or value your mental health, wait until next semester. If you're there to learn chemistry, I 1000% recommend Wang. She is extremely nice, charismatic, and you will learn so much about chemistry and yourself as a student. With that being said, the class is insanely difficult and the textbook sucks. GO TO OFFICE HOURS

Dr. Wang is unclear and hard to follow. Her tests are incredibly difficult and often based on small exceptions rather than subject knowledge. If you can avoid taking her at all, please, please, please do it. If, by some unholy stroke of luck, you are stuck in that classroom at 8:45 AM with this professor, I am truly sorry.

Dr. Wang say, is an extremely nice/funny person. However, her 8:45 AM MWF lectures aren't very useful as you've gotta read the textbook beforehand so that you're not sitting there clueless. The class is only graded on 4 exams + lab, with the tests being very hard. However, the curve is generous and help is very accessible outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Was about to rate 2, chose 3 as she is nice, but I can't say Prof. Wang is a “great” lecturer. She is clearly a master of ochem and can answer any question, but her 8:45am lectures carry little info due to her subpar oral English. All content is expected to be self-studied prior class. Graded only by 4 exams + lab, no homework—grateful to get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: If you do not excel in chemistry, do NOT take it with this professor. She is a great person, but I would not take another course with her again. Her lectures were very pointless, and she just taught the chapter, which you have to read in advance to understand anything. The only assignments toward your grade are the three exams and the final.

Professor Wang is excellent - funny, personable and extremely accessible over email. She's even better during office hours and forces students to think critically. However, the class is rigorous, with lots of material and tough examinations - be prepared to work hard for this class. Nonetheless, she leaves you with a robust foundation of Orgo 1!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Wang gives you a very deep understanding that is wonderful for building a foundation in orgo. Her lectures are actually very helpful for solidifying and clarifying information gathered in the textbook, but be warned that her tests are very difficult and may require you to logic your way to the answers based on trends that you hopefully learned.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
Wang is such a wonderful and kind person, however everything stated in reviews here could not be more accurate. She cares a lot about her students so its unfortunate that she's not a great lecturer and creates hellish exams (the curve is generous!)

Regardless, I would recommend students who can take the class freshman fall not to wait.

Dr. Wang is clearly very knowledgeable about organic chemistry, and she makes it very clear at the start of the year that most of the learning will be done on our end through reading the textbooks. She is mainly there for clarification. Exams make up the majority of grade but are predictable based on previous years. Great foundation for orgo!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Do not take this class if you want a good impression of chemistry.

Professor Wang is kind, caring, and hilarious. Her lectures are confusing and fast; definitely preview the material before class to get the most out of lecture. GO TO OFFICE HOURS! I learned much more in office hours than in lecture. Exams are difficult but manageable if you study with the provided practice exams; final curve is very generous.

Dr. Wang is an extremely nice person; she stayed after lectures to answer questions, answered emails quickly, and hosted weekly office hours/extra office hours prior to exams. Going to office hours/doing the practice exams will help a lot with the midterms. With that said, don't take this class if you love yourself and just wait until spring.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
Do the problems from the discussion sets, practice exams, and textbook. Also, try to understand the theoretical reasons behind phenomena rather than just memorizing rules. 
If you read the textbook beforehand, the problems she does in class are great supplements and really test your knowledge. With all this prep, the tests are pretty light.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Wang may not be the best lecturer, but she is very accessible outside of class and stays after class to help students. She really cares about her students learning how to learn and her exams definitely reflect that. Though notoriously difficult, I feel prepared for the rigor of any other future course here at Duke.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Wang is a great teacher, despite the extreme rigor of her class. She is understanding and very available to answer questions outside of class. That being said, her teaching in lectures is nowhere near sufficient to learn content. If you do the practice exams and study a lot, this class will be very rewarding, whether you're a freshman or not.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Wang wants her students to come to class prepared so instead of lecturing her students she can let them practice problems on the white board. For me, this worked really well and helped me internalize the material. She cares a lot about her students (she has brought in chocolate for us multiple times) and is helpful during office hours.

Prof. Wang really cares about her students and wants them to do well both intellectually and mentally. She guides students through the process instead of giving direct answers, which was really effective for me. Her exams are hard but predictable with previous tests, and her in-depth content prepares you for future courses.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Wang is a spectacular chemist, and I genuinely enjoyed orgo with her. This class works best if you like studying independently. Tests and labs are very reasonable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Respected

reviews.comment: Prof. Wang is known for putting very hard problems (arguably beyond the scope of our learning) on exams. Lectures are not that helpful for learning new content, but she is always very willing to help outside of class and is clearly very knowledgeable. Attend office hours and grind the hell out of the textbook. The final curve is generous, however.

Professor Wang's class is incredibly time consuming, as she will warn you on the first days of class. She also doesn't teach in lecture, so there is a significant amount of reading. Grades are entirely based on exams and the lab. That being said, Wang herself is an incredible professor who deeply cares about your success if you get to know her.

Dr. Wang's class was challenging yet enjoyable. Content can be heavier than other orgo classes (freshmen only), and exams are difficult yet predictable if you do the practice tests. That said, she is very caring, esp during office hours. Her curves also seem very nice (A-/B+ avg) and she def makes you understand orgo well for future classes.

Lectures did not help at all- if anything they just made me more confused. Taught myself everything from the textbook. Exams often covered really niche topics and were therefore not reflective of your overall understanding of concepts. Freshman section is far too competitive and overall a horrible way to begin your time at Duke. WAIT TIL SPRING

Dr. Wang is very caring and does her best to make sure students understand the concepts. Her content is sometimes more in depth than other professors for some subjects here and there and that makes the class particularly interesting. Her exams include a number of interesting tricks but they're easy to work out by practicing with previous exams

Professor Wang means good, but she really just CANNOT teach. She has a pretty heavy accent and fails to speak in full sentences meaning that you struggle to understand her point and she is unclear about what's relevant and needed. Her lectures are non-mandatory and your grades are based on 3 impossible tests and the final. Do not take orgo with her

Dr. Wang expects you to have in-depth knowledge of organic chemistry, and if you read the textbook as intended and genuinely put in the work, you are rewarded. Ensure you space out your learning and don't try and cram. She is difficult yet predictable and very reasonable. Your grade largely depends on the effort you are willing to put in.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Wang does not lie when she says her class will be challenging and demanding but also fun and rewarding. Make sure youre always 2 weeks ahead in the reading; she goes supersonic, especially during the last 5 minutes of lecture. However, she cares and will make sure you understand orgo WELL. you will be a master of intramolecular rxns at the end

Dr. Wang's class is difficult. Be prepared to study A LOT and still get destroyed by exams. Lectures are fast paced and can be hard to understand, so you need to read the textbook. That being said she is a nice and caring professor. Overall if you are willing to work hard, the freshman orgo section is worth taking with her. Go to office hours!

Qiu Wang is an amazing Chemist who cares about her students. She goes into great depth and covers a lot of stuff you will not learn with other orgo professors. That said, the class is very difficult and will require a LOT of time outside of class. She is also a bit difficult to understand during lectures at times.

Dr. Wang was ok. I didn't actually go to many of the classes and instead only read the textbook and ended up doing fine. The tests were mostly reasonable, and I think if you really put in effort you'll do well. But if you're unsure of first semester orgo, it's better to wait until the spring with Baldwin or Canelas.

Orgo with Qiu is really not that bad. It's tough, yes. But if you do the textbook reading and really keep up with the work then you will do well for sure. She is very knowledgeable and her office hours definitely clarified her at times fast paced lectures. Although the class was difficult, it made 202 with Widenhoefer an absolute breeze.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Don't let anyone here scare you too much. Dr. Wang is an amazing professor. She is super sweet and extremely knowledgeable about chemistry. Her class and her tests are insanely hard, but her curves are extremely reasonable: most people got a B or above. She also prepares you extremely well for orgo 2. No regrets taking this my freshman fall.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: You will definitely learn a lot of chemistry, but I don't think it's worth the trouble freshman fall. The class is already hard enough and Dr. Want makes it even harder with her emphasis on reaction mechanisms and seemingly unlikely products forming. I advise you to save yourself the trouble and take it with an easier professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: This class was really rough honestly. The tests were really hard no matter how much you understood the material. This class literally pushed me to go to CAPS. If you want to spend your 1st semester stressing over this class, be my guest but I regretted my decision frequently throughout the semester. I did well by the skin of my teeth.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Qiu Wang is a nice person, but her class is the worst decision I have made. Please, take orgo next semester with a better teacher. The tests are insanely difficult; she would put in topics 1 or 2 chapters ahead of the current readings. We had 2 extra chapters to read compared to the other classes, and, in general, other classes had it way easier.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Tests? Not many--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed Dr. Wangs class. She gets a bad reputation for being difficult, but if you put the work in youll see good results. Shes also a genuinely nice woman and really cares about her students. Go to office hours!

Worst experience I have ever had in my educational life. You are surrounded by ultra-competitive people on one side while getting shanked by a professor who has a ruthless grading criterion and egregiously difficult exams. Furthermore, to add salt to the wound, you get to witness the sophomores enjoying their exams with their cheat sheets. :(
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Its pretty hard, especially with all the snakes in the class. However, if your last name is Du, you will Du GREAT!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Honestly, not worth taking this course at all. Just wait til spring to have a better professor. Her accent is strong and lectures are very unclear. Writes very difficult tests, usually with at least one or two questions on material that wasn't supposed to be on the test. You can tell she has exceptional chemistry knowledge, just can't teach it well

I have no idea how she is a professor. genuinely it would be better if a random sophomore taught the coarse. you won't be able to understand her speak, so lecture is useless. everyone regrets taking her class. she tries though. AVOID unless you already know orgo well somehow. just wait until next semester. don't put yourself through a nightmare

Im writing this during lecture. She is a terrible professor with unorganized lectures that are hard to follow. This class comes down to how good you are at teaching yourself from the textbook, except her tests are way harder than the textbook material. Ive never hated a class so much. Honestly, just wait until sophomore year to take orgo!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Best professor I've ever had.

Couldn't understand lectures because of accent. Taught myself all material from textbook. Seems nice but unaware.  Will attempt to help students by randomly calling on them during class then make fun of them if wrong.  Tests near identical to practice tests, so memorize those.
Dr. Wang taught the freshman-only section of organic chemistry during the fall. Her accent hinders understandability, but overall she is an excellent teacher. I definitely would take the class again.

If you like chemistry and are ready for a challenge, I recommend taking her class. I should note a few things: GO TO OFFICE HOURS. They were more helpful than lectures (she goes fast and it's easy to get lost), but lectures did makemore sense if you read the book beforehand. She is also very willing to take time out of her day to help her students.
Very hard to understand lectures, and writes terribly hard tests.  She is nice though.

She has an accent and sometimes jumps around topics without giving detailed explanations, so teaching is not very clear. She is a sweet person, though, so if you try to approach her and ask for help, she will be there for you.

Dr. Wang is an exceptional chemist and an atrocious instructor. While she career her students, she simply doesn't have the ability to convey information to a large group. The lectures tend to be disorganized and often don't explain the content expected on the tests. You don't need to take this course first semester; just wait for the better prof.

Professor Wang is really enthusiastic about Orgo, which is great.  She is also willing to help and explain things to you until you get it during office hours, but you have to put in the additional time and effort to seek out that help.  Her tests are very fair but she is a harsh grader and  does not reward too much partial credit.

Dr. Wang is an amazingly knowledgeable chemist. She is also an amazingly ineffective instructor. Her lectures are cursory and generally unhelpful in preparing for exams, and exams expect a depth of knowledge that can hardly be gained without memorizing the textbook. There's no need to take this class first semester. Just wait.

She is the single worst professor I've ever had. She is not clear in lectures, she mispronounces key chemistry terms, her exams are actually impossible, and her office hours consist of people who actually know what is happening and discuss recent studies rather than helping students. This class was the worst decision I've ever made.

Professor wang is a bit rude. she consistently calls out students in class and isn't very kind to them. additional, her lectures are EXTREMELY unclear. i regret taking orgo first semester because she was my only option. the class is essentially entirely teach yourself as the lectures WILL NOT HELP. don't bother going. read your book, cry.

Unlike Chem202, I really disliked Wang's freshman orgo section. She was just extremely unclear and difficult to understand, and really didn't teach the tested concepts that well, or at all in some cases. We pretty much had to learn everything from the book, which is not that unusual for a class like orgo I guess. Overall I would not take again.
Dr. Wang is definitely the best professor for Chem 201. The class wasn't easy, but if you put enough effort in, you'll get a lot out of it.

Tests are very difficult and takes pride in course being very hard. MUST read book to pass, lectures are confusing (esp when coupled with her accent). Flies through material, and lectures usually run late. Overall, I thought she made the course more difficult than it had to be

Prof. Wang is honestly one of the nicest professors at Duke. She cares SO MUCH about her students and wants them all to do well. Yes, the class is hard. You will most definitely have to put in the work, but her door is always open for asking help. She stays after class and extends office hours for her students. Glad I had Freshman Orgo with her.

This class is seriously hard, especially if you take it with all the other first-year students. Lectures are very long, basically a repeat of textbook info. You need to read the textbook and do a bunch of problems for practice if you want to do well in this class.

Takes pride in the difficulty level of the course. Lectures usually run over about 10-15 minutes, are sometimes not clearsomewhat confusing. She repeats the exact same information from the book. Really cares about her students and willing to help, great in person but not very useful in lecture. Must read book to pass. Tests are very difficult.

Prof Wang tries her best to make sure we understand the material. Her lectures correlate with the textbook, so it is essential you read the textbook before lecture to understand what is going on. She posts previous year exams which are VERY useful for the midterms. The class isn't easy, but it's manageable if you put in the effort.

Lectures are useless and she is a terrible teacher. Your better off just reading the textbook instead of going to class. The only thing that saved me in orgo was having a great TA and the practice exams online.

You need to read the book, lectures are basically useless. The tests are very difficult and often cover topics that were barely talking about in class, so make sure to use the practice exams. It is a doable course if you are prepared your first semester.

A very hard class, but it's organic chemistry so the difficulty should be expected. Dr. Wang is very willing to help students outside of class. The office hours are very helpful and when answering questions, she engages students to think. People say students coming out of her class better master orgo.

Professor Wang is a really nice, but her lectures are very disorganized and you don't get much out of it. You MUST read the book in order to pass, Her tests are based completely off the textbook, but there are always curveballs. Her accent also makes it very difficult to understand her. I wish I'd waited to take orgo with someone else.

Challenging but truly cares about her students. A little disorganized during lecture, so read/take notes on textbook chapter before class. To study for tests, review practice exams, recitation sheets, and suggested book problems. If you study hard and get help when needed, you will do just fine. Prepares you very well for Orgo II. Take her class!

Aweful teacher! Absolutely disorganized during lecture. Her accent makes it even harder to understand. Her tests are really hard and cover material that was never covered in class. Basically, you have to learn everything by urself from the book. She did curve class to a B+ though, so at least that was nice of her.

If you take orgo with Dr. Wang, you really have to teach yourself from the book. She's not very clear or organized in her lectures. She's an incredibly sweet person if you talk to her during office hours, but really she makes organic chemistry more difficult than it has to be.

Prof. Wang is honestly one of the best professors I have ever had. Recitation is useless. You must read the textbook to be successful, so read ahead when she tells you to and lecture will actually be useful to you. Go to office hours and do the practice tests and you will do well! Phenomenal prof who cares a great deal and is very helpful!
This is a hard class. No one will hold your hand. You are competing against the best and brightest from the freshman class. The competition is ruthless. Only the strongest survive.

One of the worst professor I have ever had. Her lectures are a not as thorough and more confusing version of the book -- often delving into simply useless stuff. Her lectures are hard to follow, and honestly pointless. If you've ever want a self-taught class, take this. But watch out, even if you know the book... she throws random stuff on the test

She teaches at a very fast rate, so be prepared to keep up. Reading the textbook is a must, and thoroughly reviewing the practice exams is also extremely helpful. Though I've never gone to see her individually, I hear she is very helpful one-on-one and sincerely cares about her students. She can also be sweet and funny.

IF YOU HAVE PROF. WANG, YOU ARE LUCKY. NEVER, AND I stress, Never in my life had I met a teacher/professor who GENUINELY cares about her students as much as Prof. Wang. SHE CARES SO MUCH, and she WILL go all the way to help. SHE'S AWESOME. She's in no way an easy professor, but if you want to learn solid Orgo Chem, you are just SO LUCKY to have her

Her tests are pretty hard, but that only prepares you more for an easier semester in Orgo II. Go to office hours. Read the book and do as many problems as possible. Lots of work but rewarding as she says.

Tough class, but was much more enjoyable with all freshmen. Learned from Loudon's text and Klein's Second Language book more than lecture. Recitation was also very, very, helpful. The problems were beyond the normal scope of the course, but were well written.

Orgo 1 is a difficult class regardless of the professor. Professor Wang was nice and was available outside of class often for extra help, but her lectures weren't always very helpful or clear, and her tests were difficult. The class is manageable, but only if you are willing to put in a lot of time and effort on your own.
Orgo 1 is difficult, it doesn't really matter the professor. She is most helpful during office hours, she'll make a lot of effort to understand and completely answer your question.
She's good

Orgo will be hard no matter the professor. Wang cares a LOT about her students and knew all 200 of us by name. She goes out of her way to help us, but tests are a bit confusing and the accent takes some getting used to. The class will take a lot of time no matter who teaches it, but Wang is fine. Gives a fair amount of partial credit.

Her tests are tricky.  So is understanding her accent sometimes.  But she cares a lot about her students and will go out of her way to help you if you ask.  I found office hours more helpful than lecture.  She faithfully follows the textbook, so studying from the textbook is essential.  Good professor, very tough and frustrating course.

Challenging and expects a lot from her students. Lectures are straight from the textbook, and sometimes difficult to understand because of her accent. Very responsive when you ask her for help. Don't expect a good curve just because it's an all-freshmen section.

This class is extremely hard, especially for one's first semester at Duke. Dr. Wang takes pride in its difficulty. That being said, she is completely dedicated to her students' success. She knows nearly everyone's name and relative grade. She has an accent and grammar trouble but goes to great lengths to get the material across. She is amazing. :)

Dr. Wang is very passionate about teaching, and she is extremely helpful whenever you ask her a question. She wants everyone to succeed and would often stay after class for 15 min to clarify topics from lecture. To do well in her class requires hard work, but if you read the book, do all the problems, and go to office hours, you should do well.

She is very nice and inspiring. Her class is EXTREMELY difficult and time consuming. I found lectures to be a recitation of the book and sometimes useless. She is always available and willing to help and wants her students to do well.

Organic chemistry with Wang is difficult but manageable with dedication. There are many resources available that she talks about at the start of the year, such as the help room, tutoring, and office hours. She is very nice and relatively clear during lectures but also has an accent. Genuine professor that cares a lot about her students.

Ochem is hard, get used to that. She gives a lot of time to her students. As in A LOT of time. You can email her, and she will respond. You can find her in office hours all the time. Ochem is hard, Ochem is hard, ochem requires 2hr/day. Why are you taking ochem? It's hard. But you know what, it is worth it.
Is demanding and has high expectations. She does care about her students and always stays after class to answer questions or past the end of her office hours.

Dr. Wang at first seems intimidating and demanding, but once you go to her office hours, you realize how much she cares about her students. She puts so much effort into preparing for class. I emailed her a question, and she posted a two-page help sheet to Sakai in response. So, she is a good, caring, but challenging professor.
Chemistry, I learn that
Lectures very basic, if you did the reading they're pretty pointless. Learned a lot more from recitation and the textbook than the lectures. Has high expectations and can be demanding.
Pretty demanding

Definitely over-hated, he's very organized and teaches a lot of skills in R that are important for any statistics major to know. That being said, his grading criteria is pretty vague and since it takes forever for him to grade assignments, it's pretty difficult to know what to improve in time.

Colin is a very smart professor and is a solid lecturer but will lose your attention easily. For a mandatory class for the statistics major, the course shows little regard to the differing levels of coding experience among students, and your grades will depend half on your proficiency of a coder, and only half on your ability to recall lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: taken spring 25, never went to lecture.  topics are difficult.  lecture is SO boring and unhelpful.  homeworks were due every two weeks with random groups each time.  challenging but doable take home midterms.  very low effort class, can use chat on entire assignment.  i dont think he looks at our assignments just takes off a few points each time.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is a nice guy, but a really, really bad teacher. You will learn nothing from him and get a bad and confusing grade. BTW, you have to endure his boring lecture since there are pop quizzes for attendance, which test you on obscure details from his lengthy PowerPoint presentation. This course is mandatory and is taught by him every year.
Terrible professor. Grades harshly and on a whim.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
You don't know your grade until its posted on DukeHub; no information given prior. Terrible all-around.
Him and his wife probably make the worst teaching duo in the history of teaching.

I rather take a physics class than this class. That is saying something... I do not understand how he grades the labs and exams??? no one ever has gotten an A on these assingments and in the github issues for these assignments, there's no explanation whatsoever about how and why you lost points. We cant even learn from our mistakes if we dont know
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: what is even going on in this class someone please tell me? came to learn? NO get ready for infinite slides, endlessly long homeworks with random teams each time, no help in office hours, no clear grading rubric, and MULTIPLE RANDOM DISAPPEARING POINTS off every assignment and exam without any explanation! worst class and professor ever at duke boo
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Horrible professor! Grading criteria is the most unclear I have ever seen in any of my classes at Duke so far. Takes off points for things you do not even know because he will not specify. NO matter how much effort you put in to the labs and exams, he grades very arbitrarily and harsh. Do not take this class with him! Lectures are bad!

Both Rundel and the TA came across as dismissive and indifferent. I still remember the TA spending the entire office hour discussing the midterm for a completely different course and even asking those of us not enrolled in that class to leave. It was disappointing, to say the least.

Incredibly disorganized course. Lectures not comprehensive of HW topics, resulting in extensions for almost every HW & only 4 HWs assigned instead of 1 every 2 wks as stated in syllabus. Vague grading criteria & grades released >1mo after due dates (still missing 2 of 4 HW grades during finals week). Useful material, just wish it was taught better

While the material in this class is hard and can get confusing, Professor Rundel is really caring and knows a ton about the subject. He willingly pushed back lots of deadlines based on people's workloads, which I appreciated. Would love to have more knowledge about when midterms were though.
Nobody knows what's going on. Never went to class. I learnt nothing from that class and it's the worst class I have ever taken at Duke
Trust me, if you want a job in the industry, you should take classes with Colin. He knows the in-demand skills such as Hadoop (Map/Reduce) and teaches them!

I can't speak for other courses, but for 323 he was great. Colin's lectures are pretty boring, it's just him reading slides and maybe doing some demonstration with R, but I actually learned a lot about R with all of the group assignments in a low-stress environment. I think at the end if you completed everything adequately, you got an A.
Only class I would actively discourage people from taking. Save your soul and GPA. Lectures are useless and more confusing.

Prof. Rundel's biostatistics class is essentially a repeat of AP Stats (+slightly more in-depth concepts). His lectures are boring/useless but exams are easy (if you have taken AP Stats before, otherwise may be trickier and need to self-teach). Prof. Rundel is accessible outside of class and better at explaining concepts to students 1 on 1.

I know Colin gets a lot of reviews for his BioStat class, but he is perfect for STA 323 Statistical Computing. He really is an absolute expert in this field. And while his lectures are hard to keep up, he posts recordings and they are super helpful to rewatch. Incredibly practical, industry skill class. Group homework every single week.

If you have taken statistics in high school and are looking for a class where you don't have to attend lecture, this is for you! Going to lecture and not going makes no difference at all. He is decent, however, if you go to him during office hours! His class is curved at the end of the semester but no one really knows how he curves the class.

Rundel is an adequate, knowledgeable stats professor who, while lacking enthusiasm, communicates the material clearly. You have to remember that stats is simply not easy and that many students who take it are doing so because it is a requirement for their major. I can't imagine that you would have a much better experience in any other stats class.

Rundel is probably the worst professor at Duke. His lecture slides are riddled with mistakes and full of unnecessary proofs, which he wrote out on the board without ever really explaining what was happening. Even the TA didn't know how to do his homework problems sometimes, and his exams involve info not covered in lecture. Avoid at all costs!

Probably the worst professor I've had at Duke. If I could go back, I would have taken Calc 2 for the bio major instead of this. His apathy is painfully visible, and it's difficult to get through a lecture without stabbing yourself with a pencil to stay up. His tests are not straightforward and filled with mistakes. Do not take a class with him.

His lectures are extremely boring, obtuse, and convoluted. They are rarely without mistakes and even his final had mistakes on it. 10/10 would not recommend. Save you soul, save your GPA, save you chances for med school

Don't take this class. Take a different stats class, or Bio 204. You don't learn much and he  goes way too fast during lectures; the whole experience was long and useless. It wasn't the hardest class I've ever taken but it was hard for no reason.

Without a doubt one of the worst professors at Duke. He makes classes long and hard. His midterms are hard, because you cannot learn from going to class. During finals week, he made a problem set due, a project worth 20% of our grade, a lab, and a final. He is not capable of teaching either.

Makes easy concepts extremely difficult and convoluted. Lectures are very long, powerpoints full of mistakes and formulas you will never use. Homework and labs are repetitive and tedious and don't count much for your grade. Tests are long and very difficult.  He's a good guy, but one of the least rewarding classes I've taken here.
Colin shares extremely helpful material.
Prof. Rundel made statistics seem straightforward and fun. Tests were comprehensive but doable if you always go to class. We used clickers in class.

Rundel is probably a good person. He seems to be a nice guy, but there's more to him than just being a nice guy. Most importantly, he is a terrible teacher. His slides are basically useless, his lecture is confusing, and he makes as many mistakes as Shaq misses his freethrows. (also i suspect the post below is by Rundel himself). AVOID at all cost!

I really did like Prof Rundel, I found his lectures easy to understand, and the slides he publishes makes studying for midterms a breeze. He does tend to make a few mistakes during his lectures but its never really bothered me. He is also extremely helpful during office hours if go and visit him. On top of that he is a great person too

He is a fast, boring lecturer that is very unclear. I have yet to understand any lecture I have attended, and could probably learn far more out of the class. The textbooks are optional but they are the only reason I passed. His slides are pretty useless as he hasn't explained them and includes random formulas without explaining them

The class is super boring and Professor Rundel is never clear during his lectures. The class seemed like it wasn't going to be very tough, but it was unnecessarily difficult in the end because of his vagueness. However, he does try to be there for you, although sometimes he does not respond to emails in a timely fashion.

It would be great if he would actually teach us. He goes into really technical terms without explaining what they mean. He is the type of professor to splurge out all the info without really noticing that no one understands what he is talking about.  The class itself would be easy, but his inability to communicate makes the class much harder.

Great person, terrible teacher. Took AP Stats yet he still manages to confuse me on what he is teaching. His lectures are so boring because he makes mistakes over and over and just chucks proofs on the board (stuff we dont need to know) while glossing over the important things (or writing them wrong). Not sure how he manages to complicate things.

The subject itself isn't too bad and Rundel isn't too demanding of a prof in terms of assignments and grading. Problem is, his lectures are boring and unclear. A lot of concepts make very little sense when he explains them. If you've taken AP Statistics, you should be fine for the most part. Otherwise, this will be a bit of a challenge.

Not an easy class and not an easy subject, but Rundel is very helpful and approachable and a really nice guy! Definitely need to study hard for the exams and work quickly; exams were often more similar to lecture problems than to homework. You won't be fascinated by lectures, but good grades are possible, especially since this class is curved.

He is literally the worst teacher I have ever had. Doesn't know how to do probability, makes mistakes on every single problem, can't do a problem without having done it before class. Do anything you can to avoid taking this class.
Clearly doesn't care about teaching. Puts in no effort.

He's a smart guy, but a horrible instructor. He constantly makes mistakes on his notes, thus it is very hard to get accurate information. He frequently cannot answer questions and does not bother to follow up. Overall, just did not put enough effort into teaching, so the students suffered. Takes off a lot of points for algebraic/small errors.
Absolutely horrible. I hated this semester because of him.

Wow. Rundel is terrible. Absolutely terrible. He is the worst professor I've ever had. Can't communicate his ideas at all. His slides were always wrong and he couldn't explain why. Plus his exams were incredibly difficult. Do not take a class with him.

Rundel regularly provided incorrect formulas in class and confusing examples. There was no continuity between his lectures, the homework, or the exams. Most of your study time will be spent trying to figure out which of his formulas were incorrect and teaching yourself from wikipedia

Clear lectures that are easy to follow. Midterms are challenging, but Rundel is extremely helpful during office hours and really wants his students to succeed. Overall, great professor, he makes the subject very interesting.

The professor is completely disengaged with the course. Grades feel random,  she doesn't respond to emails, and participation grades are not based on how much you talked in class. She is a stickler for late work and tardies while often being late to class. Don't count on office hours and feedback with her to get a good essay score, either. Avoid.

Do not listen to the negative reviews of this teacher (it is one student who did not receive the grade they wanted). Professor Smith was great and made this one of my favorite (and by far my most interesting) courses at Duke. She is very accommodating as long as you submit your work on time (she does not budge on late work, however).
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Smith is an expert in her field. She has published books, which makes her experience very relevant to the course. This class is easy if you do your work and follow her feedback. Make sure to be on time for her classes though.

Writing 120 with Prof. Smith has been great! She is super caring and thoughtful for all her students, and gives a lot of feedback for the writing. She is very enthusiastic about Haiku and that excitement is contagious. Wonderful person and great class! Touse Writing 120.

I think that some of the other comments are ridiculous. I had Professor Smith this semester for Writing 120 and it was a great experience. She is a rather understanding professor, and I think I genuinely gained an appreciation for Haiku as an art! Generally, she gives great feedback on your writing, and it is easy to succeed if you put some effort.
One min late and she acted as if its the end of the world, spent half the class letting students discuss probably she simply doesn't know what to teach
absolutely bad in every sense, torture, makes me hate humanities and writing once again

absolute bouse prof, straight teethinator

good luck, just glaze
Feels like she draws grades randomly out of a hat.
Don't. Do. It.
Don't take her she is really bad and she doesn't even understand what she's saying herself sometimes

One of the worst professors at Duke. DO NOT take this class, or any class with her, for that matter. It's incredibly boring, and she grades based on her own feelings, which makes it completely random. The class is not easy, and she's a terrible professor. Again, DO NOT take her!

Haiku & Zen Buddhism with Professor Smith was completely uninteresting and an absolute waste of time. She gave no feedback/reasoning when she took points off, and for the two major essays we had, the prompts were not well written. The only reason I took this course was because it was required as part of the new Constellations program for freshmen.

Professor Smith is one of roughly 200 American Haiku poets. She is renowned in her field and she shares this passion for Haiku with her students in the Zen Buddhism and Haiku Poetry class. I've enjoyed how discussion-heavy the class is, as it has allowed me to learn about the nature of buddhism and enlightenment through the lens of haiku.

I took Writing 101 with this professor hoping for more insight on political poetry while also being able to improve my writing skills. I felt there weren't many opportunities to do either since grading was arbitrary and lectures were not very structured in terms of the content presented.
Nice and easy-going, significantly lighter workload compared to other Writing 101 sections. Covered some very interesting topics in political poetry too. Great professor.
This class was very easy and a great intro to Global Health. Dr. Ariely is the most caring and kind professor and the TAs were incredibly helpful with group work so make sure to use them!

Dr.Ariely is so caring and lovely; however, the lectures themselves were so boring. I truly am interested in the topic but definitely tuned out everything. As far as the class, it wasn't too hard, but sometimes points were taken off by the TAs for no reason. Group projects were heavy on our grade which I didn't like. Lots of busy homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Pretty solid professor and introductory class. Just keep track of all the details.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: An angel. Take the class. It is so interesting.
lectures were not the most engaging but you will definitely learn and do fine if you put the effort in. lots of group work which makes or breaks your experience with this class

If you are looking for someone who cares about what they teach and how you do in their class, Ariely is the professor you want. Pay attention to the lectures in class, and try to show up for as much as you can. If you are on track with assignments, you should have no issue in this class.

There are two major projects for the semester (one at the beginning, one at the end) and both are group work, so your experience with those heavily depends on your group. Other than that, Ariely seems very kind and understanding. Outside of lectures, you will mostly be dealing with TAs for questions and grading.

Relatively easy to get an A but tedious busywork. Lectures were not engaging and covered the same slide deck we used for HW. Also, HW assignments are graded so that you usually get 95 or 97 (even if you write a lot), and the A cutoff is a 94, so kind of stressful. Group projects/daily group responses can be annoying if you don't have a good group.

Good intro to GH but didn't find the flipped-classroom setting very engaging. I felt like I would spend hours before class researching the material and then sit in class to hear it all repeated to me in lecture. Much of the homework for that reason felt like busy work. Dr. Ariely is a nice person, but graders take off points with no explanation.

Very group heavy, lectures can be a bit repetitive and tedious homework but overall fun light insightful class. Dr. Ariely was caring, tried hard to meet students wishes, accessible outside of class and very knowledgable in global health.

definitely recommend glhlth 101! ariely is super caring and a great lecturer, and the guest lecturers are interesting as well. quizzes are open note but timed so you still need to study, homework can be tedious but is never too difficult to complete. great class!!

I really didn't like GH101 but I don't blame Ariely for it. She was a super sweet professor that was very well-respected in the field. She's super accessible outside of class and accommodating. I didn't like the flip-classroom style and plus this class is entirely based on group work. Avoid class and take electives to see if you like GH first.

Not a cake walk - Learned more in this intro class than any other intro I've had.  Not easy but not hard - you just have to organize time to put in it consistently. If you do the work, not hard to get a good grade.

Dr. Ariely's class was insightful and not an excessive amount of work, but still had to work hard. We did SO many google forms and tons of group discussions, but honestly it wasn't terrible when you got used to your groups and the format. There wasn't always an explanation for random amounts of points taken off, but I learned a lot in the class.

Dr. Airely is super kind and understanding, and her lectures are amazing. There is a lot of work in this class (so many Google forms) and the grading is unnecessarily harsh. There are so many group projects, and groups are random. The tests rely are worded weirdly but if you study her slides and attended lectures, you will be fine. There is also EC

A very disappointing class. Graded harshly on assignments and tests in seemingly random ways , but directions are very vague & her lectures are confusing/arent very helpful for understand material. Doesnt feel like theres a strong theoretical foundation to her class, attendance is necessary & she isnt forgiving if stuff comes up in your life
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: a pretty intense class with lots of critical thinking + assignments graded harshly but prof ariely genuinely cares about her students. she holds plenty of office hours, is accomodating to meet outside of OH and truly pushes her students. while a challenging experience, she is probably one of the best profs ive ever hard.

Dr. Ariely cares about her students and is clearly knowledgeable about global health. However, her exam questions are often worded poorly and grading criteria on assignments and projects seems arbitrary. A large part of your grade in this class is based on group projects, which can either really help or really hurt depending on who is in your group

Dr. Ariely is SO knowledgeable about global health & SO nice. However, the class is disorganized and the assignment instructions are vague. Group projects constitute a large part of your grade (groups are randomly assigned and kept throughout the semester). Also lots of extra credit opportunities. If you attend lecture, it's not hard to do well.

The class is extremely confusing. The TAs and professor is very unclear about the grading. In addition, so much work is given in this class that most students are uncomfortable. I would say stay away from this professor and class. You will be piled up with work, confused about the grading, and this class will take a toll on your mental health.

Dr. Ariely knows her stuff but doesn't have the greatest organizational and planning skills. She cares about her students though, and lectures are interesting. It's easy to get an A, however the required projects and homework were often given with unclear directions and the class always seemed disorganized despite multiple TAs helping.

Dr. Ariely is a knowledgeable prof who cares enough about the success of students to have flexible assignment deadlines, meet frequently outside of class, etc. Methods is a tough class, and I strongly advise taking stats before taking methods, but it is doable. Attendance isn't "mandatory", but your participation grade will suffer if you skip.

Probably the hardest global health class that I've ever taken. You learn a lot in the course, and Dr. Ariely wants you to do well. She's very accessible outside of class. You definitely have to work hard for a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Dr. Ariely really wants you to succeed and will help find time to go over any assignment or question you may have. A genuinely nice professor, although her assignments take a bit of effort and tests start out difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Super nice person, and brilliant. Do seek helpfeedbackclarification and take it into account; you'll never get a perfect score on anything but she'll help tell you what she's looking for. LOTS of group homework. Tests are hard - must know the material backward and forward. Overall interesting and useful course.

good lecturer and genuinely likes her students. lots of assignments, but graded leniently. tests are very, very difficult, you must read the book and know it well to do ok on the exams. participation is part of the grade. lenient with deadlines.

Love her! Superbly brilliant and articulate. Will definitely challenge you, but is very helpful and personable and genuinely believes in her students as long as you demonstrate your interest in the course. Be prepared for lots of work and tough grades, but work hard and you'll be OK, and will most definitely leave her class intellectually enriched.

Prof. Tan Zhang is an amazing option for Chem110. Considering you are willing to put in the hard work, A is achievable. He mostly tests from whats in the slides so make sure you know everything. Exams are quite hard and a T/F Question is like 3 points and MCQs are 4 points each. Do the extra credit assignment, and yeah he curves in the end.

never took a class with him, but when i worked as his lab tech he gave no safety training and i was poisoned by a carcinogen within two weeks. he never apologized for this and seemed unsurprised by my poisoning. other professors in the lab were appalled at the lack of safety in his lab (he was lax about drinks, safety goggles, freshman supervision)
Hilarious guy, but get ready to study on your own. He explains the concepts in class but it is up to you to understand how to apply it as there are not too many practice problems gone over in class.

I really liked the prof, the exams were reasonably composed, were practically fully based on slides and homeworks. We had two midterms and a final. The lectures were clear, the prof is kind and easily approachable, so the communication wasn't stressful. No curve, but I have a feeling that everyone did well. Recommend taking!
Substantial, humorous lecture. Homeworks are assigned every week, but not very much. The grading was clear, but no curve.
The tests are much more difficult and don't cover lecture content, and there was essentially no curve.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Exams are significantly more difficult than the material covered in lectures and assignments (many questions test concepts or problem types that were not clearly explained or practiced in class). Boring lectures.

Professor Tan is one of my favorite professors in the Duke CS department! I'd learned so much from his class, and his lectures and course materials have been very accessible. Thank you for the great course this semeter.

Really interesting class.  Learned a lot of cool tools in connectomics and neuroscience that you don't get in other CS classes. Super interdisciplinary, various topics and guest speakers. Really enjoyed it!

Prof. Song teaches data science in a clear and practical way. The classes are well-organized, and the examples make the concepts easy to understand. I learned a lot and feel more confident applying what we covered. It was a great learning experience.
This is an excellent course, and the professor is super nice!!
This course is perfect for creating a comprehensive mind map for data analysis. I learned ways to approach problems like a data scientist.

Prof. Song's lecture slides are amazing! His speech during the lectures was clear, concise, and aligned well with his slides. It was easy to follow along, even when I was unfamiliar with the topics or hadn't prepared in advance.

In this course, we worked on a team project, where we were encouraged to select our own topic and develop it collaboratively. This process significantly enhanced my critical thinking skills. Professor Song was exceptionally patient and supportive throughout the course. I would love to take a class with him again.

Prof. Song is a nice guy being a new professor to Duke and he can be easily found outside class in OH where he can answer your questions pretty good. However, he basically just reads slides and the exam is 30% with a class average of B-/B and minimally covered concepts. If you really want to take this class, take Pei Jian's. It's gonna be better.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Song only read through slides and not good at giving lecture.

Call people on in lectures, make weird comments on people's midterms, not confident in what she's teaching. The lectures are hard to follow, and the concepts aren't explained clearly. Grading isn't clear, and midterms are tough. AVOID HER AT ALL COSTS. Definitely take 230 with Kip Coonley so at least you don't get mocked
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Course is tough but manageable with effort. I improved significantly and attended office hours, but received comments on my exam that felt dismissive and not constructive. This was discouraging. Grading policies also felt unclear at times. Not a very supportive environment.
Tania Roy is the goat. Trust the process.

This is by far the WORST professor I have had at Duke. She is very passive-aggressive and doesn't explain topics well. Her communication skills are not the greatest and she will call you out in lectures and make weird comments. If you want to learn the course material, and keep your sanity while doing so DO NOT take this class from Tania Roy.

She loves to make fun of her students, and will openly select a student in her lecture and be very disrespectful. During our exam one of the students asked a question and she answered it. When another student asked a question in the same exam she yelled at her and the student sid that she was not being fair by not answering his question. DONT Take

Literally one of the worst professors I've had class with at Duke. She has odd comments towards her students, and it is very uncomfortable to be in her class. She really needs to work on her social and interpersonal skills as well as being confident in what she's teaching.

Really passionate about the topic and takes her time to know all her students' names within the first few weeks of class. Delivers engaging lectures with jokes sprinkled throughout. Course material is definitely a lot but her passion is contagious and will make you want to perform well in the class.

Sometimes hard to understand, but as long as you do practice problems you'll be fine. After not understanding lectures at all and not really paying attention in class I used the lecture slides, ChatGPT, and practice problems to do well on exams. Also pretty funny when I did pay attention.
Charismatic lecturer, show up for lectures/quizzes and pay attention to practice resources

Ignore the bad reviews, Dr. Roy is a great teacher. Unlike some profs, Dr. Roy makes lecture engaging and funny. Her tests are not impossible and graded fairly. The material is fascinating and can be fast but Dr. Roy will walk you through it in office hours. Her jokes and engagement of the class made monotonous lectures fun and interesting.

Dr. Roy is an authentic and hilariously candid professor with a very active teaching style. It is clear she cares very much about her field and that her students genuinely learn the content. Although lectures tend to be fast paced, she is very open to questions and is very available in office hours. I would strongly recommend taking ECE230 with her

Dr. Roy is one of the best professors I have had at Duke. She is very knowledgeable of all material and passionate about semiconductors in a way that is infectious to all the students in the class. More than this, she cares about the students and wanting them to succeed. Highly recommend this course to anyone interested in truly learning.

ECE230 was a ridiculous, hilarious, great time. The material can be difficult, but if you show up consistently, you'll do well.

Yes, she did tease students mid-midterm. Yes, she did pit us against the other section. That's just part of the fun! She is the most unique professor I've ever had. I would certainly take a class with her again.

Very goofy class, had a great time. Very excited about the material and willing to discuss/answer questions outside of class. Not the most approachable/intuitive lectures, but that's mostly a reflection on the content; you have to be okay with not understanding it immediately. If you take yourself or the class too seriously you'll hate her though.

ECE 230 with Dr. Roy was honestly not an enjoyable experience. I had her for the second half of the semester after Dr. Brown had to leave, and honestly it is tough for me to say which made me hate this class the most. None of them know how to teach the material, and both have awful slides and explanations. The class curriculum is also really bad.

Dr. Roy is knowledgeable about the material and a good research and lecturer. The problem with the class is the curriculum, not the professor. She took the time to learn about everyone in the class and was always very friendly. Class is memorization heavy. Pay attention in lecture.

Terrible instructor! She didn't even know half the material she was supposed to teach. She basically wanted us to memorize everything and not learn. Also very socially awkward and patronizing. Her interactions with her students were always weird. She made many students uncomfortable by calling them out.

Worst professor I've had at Duke. Dry lectures. Will go out of her way to learn everyone's names to call out some of her students in front of everyone rudely. She even approached several peers during a midterm and talked with them in a very rude manner, shaming students who didn't come to lecture. Made the section feel like it was us against her.

Great class! honestly was a pretty fun class and a good break from the harder stem classes I was taking. In-depth look at the Beatles and the 1960s, quiz grading is extremely clear and all you really need to do is read his book for it. The essay was also very subjective and gives a lot of freedom, so it was nice! definitely a good ALP to take
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Super chill class, only take if you are interested in the history of the beatles, otherwise very boring

Fascinating course. Top-notch lectures. Middle period on trouveres felt slow and would have liked to spend time on some topics not covered. Great feedback/guidance on essays. Interactive style, complete with many cold calls and in-class chanting, usually appreciated. Listening exams very tedious. Much material learned, research skills improved.

The best class I have taken at Duke. If you like rock in general or the Beatles specifically, just take this class. The lectures are amazing (we literally just listened to songs for half the class). I have zero technical knowledge about music and still enjoyed every lecture. Learned so much from it too!

Dr. Brothers is incredible! He is super passionate about the Beatles, and his classroom environment is very welcoming to people of any musical background. There are a couple brief writing assignments, a midterm exam, and a final term paper, but the workload for the course is very light throughout the semester. Would recommend to literally anyone.
This class was amazing. Never met someone so passionate about the Beatles. Super fun and almost half of every class was listening to music. Only 2 tests and 1-2 short responses.

I took this class as my Freshman seminar, and boy was it a mistake. Not only was the workload in this class borderline insane for such a course (120 pages of reading per week, on top of two papers, a midterm and a final), but the class itself is unbelievably boring. Do yourself a favor; find a better course to take for a seminar.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Directions not clear; lectures out of book and he adds very little personal opinion or insight. You will not want to go to class because he brings very little scholarship to the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: His expectations aren't very clear and I had no idea what the midterm would be like, but overall he is great. He is super knowledgeable and passionate.

Great lecturer - knows SO MUCH about the Beatles. Grading based only on participation, rare small HW assignments, final paper, midterm and final. I was scared for the paper and exams (I know nothing about analyzing rock music), but they ended up fine. Exams are just memorizing notes from class. Zero workload besides that.

Great lecturer, learned a ton about the Beatles. Class based on musical & historical analysis, but not bad even for newcomers. He's a pretty understanding grader, always tries to agree with people's points and tie it back into topic. Need to know dates/names/events/influences. Class was 0 work except for midterm, final, & final paper.

DON'T take this class unless you are a music major!  You can do well, but it's really difficult, and you must be an elegant writer.  Brothers is a terrible teacher, is unclear, hated answering my questions. Worst teacher I've had at Duke. The class content is often interesting, but Brothers find a way to make it dull. TA was the only saving grace.

There is something very special about this man. You can tell that he knows so much more than he reveals. I have a feeling that, if prompted, he would be more than happy to disclose his vast array of musical knowledge. I just started taking this class - but I am very intrigued. I am looking forward to hearing more from Prof Brothers.
Had him for a first year seminar. Not the most interesting lecturer but the nicest guy ever. Super helpful. It you put in the work it is impossible to do badly.

The class is way too long. The seminar is pretty boring and the syllabus is useless because he changes it during the semester... He gives out way too much work and expectations for work and writing-wise are way to high for a seminar. Also, despite what he says he expects you to have a general knowledge of music. I did well but didn't enjoy it.

Intro to Jazz Scholarship, a graduate music course, is in fact as other reviewers have pointed out half taught by the students.  Passive aggressive, as someone else said, and I know for a fact most of the grad students at the time had a low opinion of him, sometimes reaching hate.  The course wasn't terribly difficult, but it was rather lackluster.
A very passive-aggressive teacher who tests absolutely inconsistently and randomly.
This class was horrible.  Its bad enough that material is boring, but Brothers made sure to put us to sleep every class period.  Do not take this class with him.

I took Prof. Brothers's "Intro to Jazz" class to gain an appreciation for jazz music, and that is exactly what I took away from the class.  Prof. Brothers lectures were interesting stories of the lives of the musicians and how each impacted on the evolution of jazz.  I looked forward to every lecture and would take the class again, if I could!

Professor rarely lectures.  He relies on students to “summarize” the readings so you won’t learn much from him.  I found very boring.  Feels like the “read the chapter and answer the questions” style of your high school gym teacher forced to teach history.  Didn't seem to remember what he assigned from week to week.

Prof. Brothers rocks!  I love his tiny glasses and how he "grooves" with the music he plays in class.  He's a fair grader and the work is interesting.  I'd take this class again if I could.  FUN CLASS!  (But beware, the final is pretty random)
It's not that hard of a class but way too long and too specific. also does time manage well.
Jazz and American Culture class is very well taught--a tad boring at times, but his facial expressions "hmm, yessss" make up for it. 2.5 hours IS long, but the nature of the class makes it alright.

Very interesting lecturer, extremely knowledable. Sometimes doesn't comment on class discussions and leaves awkward silences, but otherwise engaging. But...2.5 hour class is very numbing, but he gives a break for us. Lots of work, usually interesting.
Coach Tim is the best golf instructor ever. Fantastic class, planning to take again

great guy, very chill and knows a lot about golf - you get a couple misses but you shouldn't want to use them! class is basically just some short game / putting and range time hitting balls and he'll give you as much help as you want. i will say choosing which level you are doesn't really matter 1 vs 2 vs 3
Miller is a beast.  Really helpful and the class is perfect.  Who wouldn't want to hit balls for an hour 3 days a week?

Tom Miller is a great instructor. He is patient and gives you individual help and tips for improving your swing. I gained insight and  understanding of golf rules and etiquette. Sign up quickly spaces go fast
Mr.Miller is very nice
you gotta love coach miller's intro golf class

Prof. Ubel is so funny, intelligent, and engaging. This class is a must-take for those interested in medicine or medical policy. Just make sure you do well on the essays, which will be graded kinda arbitrarily! You also won't be given a single letter grade until your final grade - so fun!

I learned so much in Intro to US Healthcare Systems! Ubel is such a fantastic lecturer. You can tell he's smart since he explains complicated topics in simple terms (I love reading his papers because they're so easy to understand). He's funny, understanding, and accessible. Only con abt the class is papers are graded by TAs & feedback isn't clear.

One the of the best lecturers at Duke! He's a little awkward but so funny. I loved going to class. He's a tough grader at times - mostly depends on the TAs. Be prepared to dedicate time to his assignments. Taking it P/F is the move
Ubel rocks. Absolutely amazing lecturer. Such a great class. One of the best classes at Duke!

Great lecturer, probably the best I've had at Duke. Classes make people look forward to it even as a Monday 8:30. Hilarious and engaging lectures. Workload isn't too bad for a writing class either. Grading, however, is a bit confusing. Participation most likely is worth a lot more than we expected. Pop quiz also happens so don't be late.

Professor Ubel was awesome and led some great class discussions. Cares about his students and an interesting guy to talk to. Not an easy class, but you can get a good grade as long as you put the work in.

Intro to US Health Care is an awesome class. Definitely take it with Ubel. He has the perfect background to teach this class and does it well. He has a real interest in his students. You only have to write policy briefs, and it's not hard to learn how to do. I had no pubpol experience before this class but still found it pretty easy.

I think he may be the best professor I've ever had. So engaging, always reasonable, cares about deep learning and understanding moreso than grades. Definitely take his class if you can/if you have any interest in health care.

The course was interesting and taught well. It was graded by three midterms with a number of extra credit opportunities. The midterms were fun to take and low stress. Students who did poorly missed lecture and didn't take notes. I enjoyed how the lecture material was structured and thought the mix of theory and real world application was perfect.

Dr. Uyenoyama is horrible. She is the worst professor I have had at Duke, and is the reason some researchers should not be allowed to interact with undergrads. In a class of 15 people she didn't know names, did not engage with students, and acted like she had no desire to be there. Her lectures were confusing and asking questions is useless.

Worst professor I've had at Duke! With a class of about twenty students, she makes no effort to learn names. When you ask questions, she seems frustrated that you don't understand. Get the feeling that she was forced into teaching, but only cares about research. Made me hate genetics. Grade is based on 3 exams which are long and hard! Don't take.

Marcy was very approachable and spends a lot of time preparing her lectures.  They are pretty interesting and she tries to make it moreso by focusing on population genetics that pertains to humans, such as the peopling of the Americas or Migration through polynesia and even forensics. I'd highly recommend her class.

Fabulous teacher. Brings intelligence and humor to what might otherwise be a dry subject. Regarding the snarky comment about her getting her J.D. from a low-ranked school, note that she has a doctorate in law from Yale.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Does not respond well to emails or make herself available for questions. Reads from notes scratched on a legal pad for lectures. Exams are geared toward making her grading easier, not toward who deserves the A. Got her J.D. from one of the lowest ranked law schools in the nation. However she hides her bitterness well. AVOID her classes if you can.
So boring. Should not be teaching. Can barely bring herself to look up at her students as she teaches. A kind old woman, but far better suited to research than instruction.
No Comments
Highly intelligent. Brings a lot of humor into the classroom.

She was great. The class is discussion heavy, but definitely helped improve my verbal skills. Also, there was not too much work outside of class. I HIGHLY recommend taking Fictions of the Body with her.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Prof. Ugarte's class definitely improved my Spanish, without having me worry too much about the grade. The assignments improved my proficiency, and she always made sure that we were not spending too much time outside of class on assignments. Great class atmosphere, which is very different from previous Spanish classes I have taken.

Ana is the best! She's engaging, well-prepared, and selects interesting material, but most importantly she truly cares about her students and wants them to do well. She asks for feedback often and reevaluates the homework load when she finds it too burdensome. Good balance of enough work into improve Spanish proficiency but not overwhelming.

Before this class, I had taken 7 years of Spanish but was still insecure about my speaking abilities. Ana was kind, patient, and gave me confidence. She is well-versed in the material and her syllabus is unique and engaging. Also, she listens to students and respects them as equals. First Spanish class I have ever looked forward to! Thank you, Ana!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Would take again

reviews.comment: Dr. Schott is the boy. Hard class but if you put in the time you'll be alright.
Amazing professor but very hard material. I highly recommend going to office hours and asking for help! Sarah is super nice and will do whatever she can to help you. Good luck!!
I love Sarah! Student teachers are also knowledgeable. Make sure you ask questions and seek help when needed. Don't skip lecture/fall behind in content.

Extremely caring and engaged in student's success. Supportive inside & outside of math and clearly extremely passionate about the well-being of everyone in the classroom. Don't skip lecture although its easy to do so. Utilize all the resources available and you will do pretty well since she also curves leniently and is forgiving for a lot of errors
Lecture is super useful, make sure to go to every one of them.

Great professor and person. Very good at lectures/explaining, but the class is just difficult. You will need to study a lot since there are 3 midterms and 1 final. Recommendation: For exams, redo all Problem Sets and Labs, they are fairly similar to the question types at exams. Also, do the homework each week, even if it is not graded!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very caring professor, but exams are hard

Sarah is an excellent professor and one of the kindest. Tests, however, are extremely difficult unless you are very well prepared. Unless you have significant time to dedicate, class can be very hard.

Sarah is an amazing professor! Very kind and knowledgable. To be honest I did struggle at first (failed first exam) but her curve is generous and the material itself is very challenging. The class is fast paced and you CAN NOT fall behind. Trust me, you won't catch up. Go to the help room and you will be okay. If you put in the time, you'll do well
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Good teacher with good lectures.

Such a great professor - I personally didn't struggle too much with the course but if you do, Sarah makes it so easy to get help - regularly holds office hours before and after lectures and clearly cares so much about her students!

Sarah Schott is a great professor who genuinely wants her students to succeed. Go to office hours for help if you really need it, but If you keep up with lectures, do all problem sets, complete most daily homework, and practice regularly, you'll improve. It's hard to fail, do what's expected, put in effort, and you'll pass and grow in the class.
