reviews.comment: sarah is such an amazing professor - kind, encourages questions, and clear tests! If you do the daily homework and actually make an effort on the problem sets/labs you will have a good understanding of the content, but it's a pretty difficult class regardless
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: One of Duke's harder big classes but she makes the content the best it could possibly be! She's a super sweet person and always available for questions or help. The class expectations are super clear/non-subjective, and there are so many resources to help you succeed. Just a great professor overall!

Hard class but Prof Schott is super good at explaining concepts in an understandable way. If you do the daily hw and problem sets you will be fine and get a good grade. Prof Schott made Calc 2 very manageable.

Great lectures, very clear and also willing to answer any questions from students during the lecture. Will leave room for answering questions, helping students 1-on-1 and doing practice questions. Never a shortage of resources to turn to if you need help. Lectures aren't mandatory as she always posts recordings.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: While the course content is challenging, Professor Schott makes it much more manageable. She's extremely helpful and accessible, always willing to provide extra support. Using Unstuck study alongside the course materials helped me stay on top of the work. Overall, a tough but rewarding class with a great instructor.

This is a really hard class. I would avoid it if you can, or at least take it with a lighter work load but it's definitely not her fault. It's just a hard topic. The midterms can be quite difficult with a lot of content you need to know but she gives good partial credit and they are curved heavily. Super scary class though.

Sarah is the best professor I have ever had at Duke. Calc 2 is hard, but she does her best to make it understandable and is SUUUUUPER accessible outside of class to help explain things to you. She genuinely cares about ALL of her students and wants to do whatever she can to help them succeed! If you need to take Calc 2, take it with Sarah!!!

Sarah is the best professor you could have for Calc 122. She is super approachable and does her best to give partial credit on midterms. Midterms and finals are curved and she gives daily (optional) homework and exam practices to ensure everyone is prepared.

Attendance is optional - try not to miss, but she uploads her notes on Canvas.
This class is going obviously very hard but Sarah is super helpful and genuinely cares about each of her students.

Sarah is probably the best professor to be teaching this course. She tries her best to make sure everyone is able succeed in the course. Very generous with partial credit in exams which helps out a lot. Every midterm is curved and then the final is curved as well which helps out a lot. If you put in the time for this class you will do well.

This class is SO hard but Sarah does everything she can to make you succeed. You have to study a lot to do well but Sarah has so many resources to practice, learn, and get help. She is also SO accommodating. LOVE Sarah, hate math122

This class is hard asf! It's not Schott's fault at all, Duke just has her teaching way too many things. If you can take 122 instead please do that, it'll be just as hard but you'll get two classes of credit. If you do the optional homework everyday you won't be apart of the 40% test average.

SARAH IS THE BEST. I am sort of upset I would have to take another math class to have her as a professor again. Her class was pretty hard though, exams were difficult AND a time crunch so beware. Even with this, she is hands-down my favorite professor at Duke so far.
Professor Schott is amazing. This course SUCKS, so avoid at all costs. If you must take calc 2 at Duke, be glad its with Schott!
Sarah is an awesome professor

Sarah is great! She is very kind, makes herself available to students, and is overall very understanding. If you have to take 112, take it with Sarah! Calc at Duke is hard and 112 is no different (moves fast, lots of material, hard exams) but having a good professor makes it better.

reviews.comment: Professor Schott is absolutely amazing! Calculus II at Duke is very difficult, but having Sarah as my professor made the class so much more manageable and enjoyable. reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Sarah is an extremely kind professor who makes herself accessible both in class and outside of it. There is a discrepancy between the problems done in class and those given in the problem sets (which are graded on accuracy and very difficult), but if you put in the work you really do gain a comprehensive understanding of calculus.

Prof. Schott is one of the best math teachers I've ever had; posts all of her lectures and gives individualized feedback on her check-in's. Incredibly accessible outside of class; go to her office hours with questions and you'll be set for the psets and tests. Make sure to keep up with homework and psets; all q's on tests come from there.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Sarah is extremely caring and intelligent. Office hours are a must for success on problem sets. The course is challenging and moves at a fast pace, but If you spend time reviewing lecture and attending office hours it becomes much easier to grasp concepts! The exams are tough but you eventually adjust.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: As someone who doesn't always like math, Sarah explains concepts so clearly and will stay after class to help her students. She really wants you to succeed and holds lots of office hours. If you have to take 112, take it with Sarah!!

Prof. Schott is the best professor I have had at Duke (and in my life). She is very clear, makes the content straightforward and easy to understand, the course is so organized, there are youtube videos she posts that are exactly like the lectures, and the tests are not unnecessarily difficult. LOVE YOU

Took 112L over the summer with Sarah - could not recommend more! Class was fast-paced during the summer, with 4 quizzes and the final making up 75% of your final grade. However, Sarah and the TAs were extremely accessible and had office hours almost every day. The material is very challenging but it was definitely worth it to take over the summer.

Professor Schott is probably one of the best professors at Duke. She explains the content extremely well, and is always there to answer any of her students' questions, regardless of whatever or whenever. Her tests are fair, but studying for the course is essential. Curves are quite lenient though. Highly recommend FLUNCHing her.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Tests are difficult, but if you study you should be fine. She's really helpful and kind and it's obvious she cares a lot about each student.
Great and passionate teacher, she communicates very clearly. The course itself is pretty difficult but Professor Schott is quite accessible via Ed Discussion or office hours, etc.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Schott is amazing & made this course's dense material much more bearable. I felt very supported - she hosts numerous OH per wk, both in person  & Zoom - where she basically solves the vast majority of the PS questions. Def go to OH a lot! This class will be a grind but if you stay on top of stuff consistently throughout the sem you can get an A.

Professor Schott is amazing. She is a genius who explains complex topics like they are the simplest thing in the world. Lectures are not recorded, so missing too many classes can be rough on your grade. This course is a lot of work, but Professor Schott wants you to succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Schott consistently goes the extra mile to help her students, sending out surveys throughout the semester and, get this: actually acting on the feedback. It's not an easy class, but she makes it so much more bearable. If you must take Calculus 2 here, please take it with her! A gem at Duke.

Sarah does a great job of explaining lecture content and putting up a lot of materials to help students succeed. There are plenty of office hours if help is needed. The homework and overall workload is pretty high and the questions on the exams are often much more difficult and time-consuming than other practice questions in the class.

Schott is phenomenal, and I'm even TAing for 112 this spring because I loved her class so much. Tests can be difficult, but there is an extreme curve. Keep up with the workload and do the extra practice problems to do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Schott was a great professor. She is kind and cares about her students. If you participate and attend office hours you will have a higher chance of doing well in the class. However, the tests and labs are a bit challenging to approach by yourself.

Take her 122 class, seriously. I can't stress how nice and good of a professor she is. 122 is hard but her lectures are so clear and she is always accessible outside of class to help. Go to her office hours religiously and you will understand everything.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Do everything in your power to get Sarah for 112/122. The lectures are very clear with tons of examples, and the homework/tests are EXACTLY like the problems she goes over in class. She encourages collaboration with other students, and will happily explain exactly how to do every single problem on every single HW if you ask her to. Top tier prof.

Sarah is my idol. Show up to lecture and go to her office hours and you'll be fine (it's a lot of work but doable). Her tests are the most reasonable and she really cares about her students. Once she helped me for an hour at an extra OH since I missed her weekly ones. Seriously, sell your soul to take calc 2 with her. Cannot praise her enough!!

Sarah is the absolute love of my life. Her lectures are amazing, she breaks down challenging concepts really well. She made me enjoy math so much that I considered majoring in it. Attend lectures, work through the labs and problem sets and go to her office hours and this class should be an easy A. Duke is lucky to have such a excellent instructor.
Absolute QUEEN of the Math department. Calc 2 at Duke is hard, but she makes her psets and exams very fair and is very willing to give help and answer questions both inside and outside of class.

Sarah taught everything in a very clear and straightforward way and cares a lot about her students.  She's super accessible outside of class, and was always willing to go over psets and labs during office hours. She is brilliant and made a super challenging class seem manageable.

I absolutely loves Sarah - CHOOSE HER if you have to take Math 112/122 (that means if you can skip it please don't ruin your semester taking this one). Super sweet, caring, and gives way better lecture & way more reasonable test papers than other PhD students!! Also super accessible outside classroom & hosts lot of office hour.

Professor Schott is incredible at explaining material and breaking down challenging problems. Her office hours are fantastic and extremely helpful for the problem set. Most students attend at least 1 a week. She clearly cares about all her students and will work with a student to bring them up to speed.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Sarah is the best professor I have ever had! She is so caring and is obviously passionate about what she teaches. She also goes out of her way to help students, often staying beyond the many office hours she holds every week. That being said, the class itself is brutal. The final was the hardest test I've ever taken in my academic career.

Outstanding lecturer. Has online videos if you miss a lecture. Mid-terms are curved to B, but 90%+ guarantees A-. PSets are very representative of the difficulty of mid-terms. Provides some additional practice problems (common homework). She's very kind, but the material is very dense.
Tests are way harder than the assignments on the homework. Schott is ruthless. Avoid if you can.

Do not take this class and if you do make sure to do it Pass/Fail. Professor Schott is one of the most obnoxious professors at Duke in terms of making sure the class average is a B. There is no clear textbook and the test is much harder than any of the homework so she pretty much sets you up to do badly. As a person shes nice at least.

Sarah is a really kind professor. However, I do not recommend taking this class during summer session if she is teaching. The material is overly applicative for the sake of being applicative, tests/quizzes often don't reflect the homework and there is a LOT of work each day. That being said is very nice and gives students the benefit fo the doubt.

Great and caring professor whom delivers good lectures! Not too much work and problem sets are very doable. She teaches in a way that is effectively clear and very understandable for some difficult topics. Sometimes hard to reach her by e-mail but gets back to you as soon as she can. She's a gem in the math department!
She's a queen. No doubt about it. Good amount of homework to do, but nothing thats not manageable. Go to office hours, you'll get an easy A.

I was told at the beginning of the semester by an upperclassmen that Prof Schott was the best prof in the math dept and I was not disappointed. Her lectures were amazingly clear and she was extremely accessible if you had any questions. She also seemed like she genuinely cared about making the class better through the surveys she sent out.

Professor Schott was fantastic. I felt like I learned a lot in her class and that she cared about her students. I went to her office hours every week for help on the weekly problem set and she clearly explained the problems.

Sarah Schott is maybe the best math professor you'll find at Duke. She explains difficult concepts well and makes class welcoming so you'll feel comfortable asking her questions. If she's teaching a class you have to take, try to get in her section, because you really won't regret it.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Great professor. Go to class -- her lectures are incredibly helpful. Make the most of your time by asking Sarah for help with the extra problems or homework. Go to math help room for problem sets. You'll do well if you commit a decent amount of time to this class but you should try your best to stay on top of the work.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Gives awesome lectures that you can interrupt with every question on your mind. Very kind and caring and helpful after/outside of class. The class itself is extremely hard and time-consuming and the tests are NOT easy. That being said, she wants you to succeed and if you put in the time you can!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: This class is a lot of work. Start early on with the homework problems. If you truly review your notes every night and do the practice problems you should be able to receive at least B. But you know what they say. Math 122L at Duke is complete hell.

Math is known to be quite hard at Duke, but Sarah does a fantastic job teaching it. She is very approachable and has office hours at least twice a week. Very helpful lectures and great course structure.

Sarah Schott is the best math teacher I have EVER had! Math is the bane of my existence, but she inspired me to keep working hard at it and was always ready to help one-on-one & explain & reexplain things. She is also just an amazing person who can see the strengths & passions of her students beyond her classroom. Feel blessed to have gotten her!

SARAH IS AMAZING. YOU'RE A VERY LUCKY PERSON IF SARAH IS YOUR PROF FOR MATH. She cares so much about her students, so she always goes out of her way to help you. Though a challenging class, Sarah makes it much more bearable. Her lectures are wonderful & easy to understand. She'll go over anything until you can understand it. Srsly, best prof by far

Sarah is a phenomenal teacher. If you're taking 122 and didn't get her, it would even be worth switching to a section at 6pm if she was teaching it. The intuition she applies during lecture is unparalleled, and you will always leave class with a great grasp on the material. It's a tough course, but hard work and studying will yield good results.

Schott is truly an incredible professor. This class is difficult, but Schott is absolutely the best professor to go through it with. She is one of the most dedicated professors ever and is more than willing to always help online, over email, or during office hours. Take this class with Schott, you will not regret it - she is amazing!!!

best teach i've had at duke. her class is very challenging, but she provides so many resources and is committing to helping you understand. you really learn a lot with her. GO TO OFFICE HOURS. amazing amazing teacher

She's an amazing lecturer and makes sure everyone understand the lecture. She's definitely willing to work with you when you need help. She has hours in the help room, holds office hours, stays before and after class, and holds review sessions before tests. Her weekly problem sets were hard, but they prepare you for the midterms and final.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: objectively and subjectively an extraordinary teacher. SO approachable and helpful on every level. she should win some sort of teaching award honestly
She's by far the best of the 122 teachers, and everyone loves her.
One of the best Math professors at Duke. Go to each class, takes notes, and GO TO HER OFFICE HOURS she is super helpful. Do not buy the textbook you can find it online.
Sarah is the GOAT. Take her class if you can. Literally a goddess among humans.

Sarah is an amazing professor! She is so helpful and her lecture notes are amazing. She really cares for her students and try to be as much help as possible. Would definitely recommend taking this class with her.

Amazing! Class structure & lectures incredibly well thought-out/organized. She is dedicated to helping every student. She recognizes that there are multiple approaches to problems, and tries to get on your page to help you understand. She always answered questions on Piazza & extended office hours. Hard class but she does everything to help

Would definitely recommend taking a math class with Sarah. Lectures are at a good pace and clear. She also has very helpful office hours and will work with you to figure out anything you are struggling with. Extremely nice woman and one of the best professors I have had at Duke. Class itself is somewhat challenging but not too bad with some effort.

Sarah is by far the best teacher I have had in my career as a student.  I've never been particularly great at math or a fan of it, but she was helpful and made the class very doable and actually interesting.  She really cares about her students and is absolutely brilliant and willing to help. 100% recommend taking a class with Sarah.

Absolutely wonderful woman and professor. By far the best math professor I've had here. Can take an extremely difficult concept and explain it in terms you can easily understand. Yeah, her tests may be difficult, but I feel that I've learned so much this semester.

Sarah is one of if not the best teacher I've ever had. Will personally meet with you to talk about anything in addition to being incredibly talented at what she does. Duke math is impossible and without her extra work I wouldn't have passed. Felt like I gained a teacher, mentor, and friend by having her. Simply amazing.
An amazing, helpful professor. Class is very tough though, with lots of work!

She's absolutely brilliant. Because of her, I loved linear algebra. She likes to teach, super clear, and stuck with the book, which I really liked. She just expanded and illuminated the book instead of presenting entirely new material, and she was always willing to answer questions. Don't forget to go to class!

Although this was the hardest class I've ever taken, Sarah is a very helpful teacher. If you have to take Calc 2, Sarah is really the only option. Very willing to meet outside of class. I was struggling the entire semester but I went to her often and I think my final grade was more of a reflection of the work she saw me put in.
Great professor. The  class is tough but if you do all the work  study her notes, which are very helpful, you'll be fine. Really easy to access for help. If you're taking 122 take it with her.

Very hard class, easily took up most of my workload. That being said, Sarah was a great teacher and extremely helpful explaining concepts. Lectures move very fast, so take good notes and expect to have to do some re-teaching on your own.

Awesome teacher! Explains everything clearly and gives out clear notes. What's on the notes are generally what's on the tests. However, her tests are somewhat hard. There are generally no surprising questions, but the questions could be definitely harder than the homework. Best math prof out there.

Sarah is a phenomenal teacher, thoroughly explaining concepts and giving really good explanations in class. Though this class is definitely tough, Sarah is by far the best teacher to take it with. She is willing to stay after class every day to help, and holds lots of office hours to make sure you understand the concepts to your fullest ability.
Hands down the best professor ever.  Made taking Math122 worth it even though I was too naive to use my AP credit to place out of it

The best math professor I've ever had, so nice and makes the material clear in her notes. Tests are hard (its a math class) but she has lots of office hours for you to come by and ask questions. I would only take this course with this professor
Sarah is such a nice professor and is always willing to help. If you do the homeworklabs and understand them, then you will do fine in the class.

Sarah was one of the best professors I have had at Duke so far. Incredibly approachable, possibly a genius, and willing to meet to discuss any concerns or questions outside of class. I actually found myself liking the "most failed class" at Duke. Even though the tests are probably the hardest out of all the teachers, it is well worth for finals.

SARAH SCHOTT IS THE BOMB! SHE IS THE GREATEST PERSON EVER! I say person because Math 122L is actually Hell on earth. I feel bad that Duke's potentially best math teacher has to teach this horrible class. It is so ridiculously hard. You think you know all the material then get a 47 on all the midterms. But Sarah is always willing to help & so smart!

Sarah's a fantastic teacher who will always take the time to meet with you outside of class. The class is terrible (math labs are a terrible invention), but if you need to take it, take it with Sarah!

Professor Schott covers a lot of material very quickly, but only because the syllabus demands it of her. It is strongly recommended to make individual appointments with her and to go to her office hours to slow the pace down and learn concepts better. The tests are very hard and not many people earn the A's and B's they are used to in high school.

Sarah is amazing! She's really good with helping you understand difficult concepts which is vital in a tough class like Math122L. She is a fair grader and gives excellent feedback. She's also really easy-going and enthusiastic. Just great! Probably my best math teacher so far.

She was overall one of the best math teachers I've had.  She was always willing to meet with student's after class, and tried to make everything as clear as possible for her students. While the tests were difficult, I felt much better prepared than a lot of the kids in other sections. More, she was a really awesome person to get to know!

Sarah Schott is about as good as an audio book for the textbook. Over the course of the semester, we have basically transcribed the textbook into our notes. She provides no context in her instruction, merely looping through definitions, theorems, and the occasional (if we're lucky) example. May god have mercy on anyone who takes her lecture.

Puts an incredible amount of effort into teaching. She even went through old tests made by another professor and told us which problems would be the most helpful to us. Possibly the best math teacher I have had in my entire life in terms of clarity and helpfulness
So nice, very approachable, and goes out of her way to help students. Tests are difficult, but she's always willing to answer any questions students may have.
Her tests are hard, but she is incredibly approachable and wants each of her students to succeed.
hard tests but she is VERY approachable and loves to help students.
Easy material but tests are extremely hard and she will explain things at the most basic level so you are not fully prepared by the end. It's a lot of outside work even if you attend every lecture.
One of the better professors I have had at Duke in general. Genuinely interested in her students. Really nice and cool
AMAZING teacher!!!! She is SO NICE and so helpful and really wants you to succeed. The class structure itself is very demanding and challenging, but having her as a teacher makes it so much better.

She was the best Math teacher I have ever had. She is more than willing to help and she can relate to students really well. She presents the material in a clear and understandable way. I went on to TA for one of her classes.
Much easier than other math 41 teachers, eager to help students, really nice. Overall a great class.

Great Teacher! If you're taking math, take it with her. I hate math usually, but sarah made it into a pretty good class. In addition, she is a very fair tester, and goes out of her way to help you. In fact, her tests are harder than the final, which is good, as it prepares you well. Before the tests, she reviews material, and is very accessible

extremely friendly, accessible, personable and sympathetic. patient at explaining concepts, never gets frustrated with people asking the same questions over and over again. really identifies with students. would recommend going to office hours. looks like kate middleton.

Sarah is the best math teacher I have ever had. Definitely take her class if you can. She is always available to answer questions and really wants students to understand the material. For calculus, I used to just memorize formulas without any understanding but after taking Sarah's course, I understand the concepts behind the formulas.

Sarah is an outstanding teacher. She is always very helpful, and it is apparent that she truly cares about each and every one of her students. She is ALWAYS very accessible, and I almost wish I liked Math more so I could have her again--she's great!

Sarah is extremely helpful and understandable, she's one of those teachers who truly wants you to do well and give you the best grade that you deserve. You know what to expect and you go into the final well prepared. Being a grad student herself, shes sympathetic to the stresses of Duke student life.

I have to agree with everyone so far.  Sarah is the best math teacher I've had at Duke as well. She relates to students and answers questions carefully and patiently. She never puts students down or tries to make them feel stupid for asking questions. She really makes the material accessible. Great person, incredible teacher.

Sara is the best math teacher I've had at Duke. She's extremely clear and incredibly helpful. Her grading is fair and unlike a lot of teachers she genuinely cares about her students and is always available if you need her. She is also fun and nice to talk to. I would recommend to take math with her.

Sarah is the best math teacher I have had at Duke. Beautiful and brilliant, she is a compassionate oasis in a desert of callous, cruel math professors. Sarah is fair and generous when it comes to grading and must honestly love teaching undergrads. Amazing. Take her class.

She is definitely the best math teacher ive had here. Really nice. Clear notes. Goes into proofs a lot but examples are really helpful. I heard 108 was going to be really hard but she made it seem easier than 107 and 103.

Take her class. Completely understandable, lectures on what you need to know for the homework and the test, and is a very fair grader. Occasionally will miscopy notes on to the board, but the errors are small and she usually catches them. Rarely gives ridiculous homework or test problems. Easily the best math prof. I've had at Duke
I love Sarah. She is so much better than other Math32L profs out there. Def take her class. Her notes are amazing, and her tests are decent.

she is such a good math teacher. Bookman taught my math31L class, and it was a disaster and he made me hate math. but sarah taught so well, she made me love math again! She gives good notes , good explanations. Shes very available when you need help. Def take her class

Grading criteria is vague. No direction in how forums are to be posted. Does not want student to use materials presented in lecture. Research extra materials. States quizzes are to be focused on one thing and gives a research terms quiz. Poor professor who does not want any type of feedback.
Random group assignment by this professor was not a pleasant experience. I did not like group projects.
Random group assignment by this professor was not a pleasant experience.
Excellent professor.  Very professional and interesting.  Well organized.  She is the best professor in DUSON.  She sets the gold standard for others to follow.

Professor Crespo was evidently knowledgeable about AI systems and was willing to meet with you to discuss anything necessary for the class. There were only 2 major assignments that were each interesting and easy to complete. I would 100% take this writing over others.
TERRBILE CLASS SO HARD READING ABOUT AI
You can tell Crespo really cares about his students. He is really open to feedback in terms of how he grades your work and can be really helpful and accommodating for issues outside of the class.

BEST WRITING 101! Readings can be long, but they are interesting, and you will do much less writing than in other writing 101 sections. Only 2 (easy) essays, one of 1000 words and one of 2000 words. Weekly assignments are 250 words (many dropped). Crespo cares more about the logical structure of your argument than he does about how you write.

Dr. Blum was a good lecturer and was happy to always help outside the classroom. While his lecture notes are dense, being present in class clarifies most of the questions one has about the content. This year he did not have any quizzes in class, but we had weekly homework's and in-class exercises that actually prepared me well for the final project

Prof. Blum is one of the best professors I've had. Computational Materials can be a tough subject especially if you dont have a physics background but his lectures were genuinely engaging. He actually cares about his students and wants them to succeed. Grading was always fair and transparent. Highly recommend taking his class if you get the chance!

Dr. Blum is a fantastic person. He's quite kind, and I find him humorous. Unfortunately, I find the course to be quite boring, at no fault of Dr. Blum. I find it hard to reflect on the course because, respectfully, I struggle to care about steel strengthening. However, I liked Dr. Blum. Homework was easy. Tests also easy. Labs easy.
Nicest guy ever, but lectures are boring and can be confusing. You have to make a good cheat sheet for exams in order to do well
Real Nice and sweet

Blum is one of the most caring and accessible teachers I have had during my Duke career. He was happy to meet with me one on one when I had trouble understanding the material and would answer my email questions in great depth. He genuinely cares about his students, you just need to put in the effort to work outside lectures.

Blum was a thorough lecturer who put an emphasis on making sure students understood the material. If you put in the work and paid attention, he was very invested in the students and couldn't be more helpful. He does not deserve some of the poor reviews left on here. I recommend him highly if you have to take this class.

Dr. Blum was a poor lecturer who wrote quickly and illegibly on the board without taking questions, for the most part. The homework was graded very harshly and was on difficult material that wasn't contained in either the book or the lecture notes. The tests were very difficult. The only reason people did well was due to the massive curve.

Blum is a very nice person but a horrible teacher. In class, he was always writing on the board and talking very fast, non-stop. I had to keep taking notes and often felt like I learned nothing after a lecture. Not much help available either. He really tries to not give you the answer. He only posted 2 homework solutions and no exam sols. Avoid.

His homework assignments were very difficult. I would read through the text and read through notes, but still no examples to solve some problems. Textbook is very old, so can't even verify work online. Overheard that he isn't posting solutions to homework assignments to study for final, very frustrating because many of my hw grades were low.

Dr. Ulett is an amazing person, and I can't imagine freshman year without him. His class is not easy, but if you are willing to put in work, he is willing to help. He always keeps you laughing, and encourages you to do your best. Take his class if you want to actually improve your writing skills. Don't take it if you are not ready to work.
Dr. Ulett is a really nice guy and he really wants you to improve your writing skills. The class wasn't the easiest, but it did make me a better writer and it was very interesting.

I am an international student who wasn't good at writing, but with the help of Prof. Ulett, I made improvements throughout the semester. For this class, you really get out as much as you put in. It is also true for the grade.
He is a very nice professor in class and will answer all the questions you ask him. Don't expect him to be merciful when grading, though.
Awesome guy, really good at editing papers. Very energetic and involved.

One of the most challenging but rewarding Writing 101 classes. You will struggle, but there is plenty of help (you just have to be willing to get help on your own time). Very funny and personable guy, knows what he's talking about.
Great professor. He's smart, eloquent, conversational, and funny.

Professor Ulett was my favorite instructor this semester. He makes the class fun, but I also learned a ton about writing, and greatly improved through the course. It's not an easy class, and the workload is not insignificant, but it was well worth taking, and I would recommend it.
Very willing to help out to make sure your writing skills improve. Cracks hilarious jokes every time. Generally chill and down to earth.
He's a funny dude but the class wasn't a breeze.
He's a really friendly guy, but his Writing101 is reasonably difficult. Overall, great teacher though--the class would probably have been uninteresting with a different professor.
Absolutely fantastic teacher.  Learned so much that semester.

Highly enjoyed the Science of Sherlock Holmes! Ulett is a fantastic professor and person, he's always willing to go the extra mile to help and gives you many opportunities to draft and perfect papers. Would definitely recommend to others if they want to take a fun and fairly easy Writing 101 course.
Prof. Ulett is a fantastic person and he is always willing to help students improve their writing. I really liked his class and I would recommend him to anyone taking Writing 101.

Prof. Ulett is a very good professor. I leaned a lot about academic writing in his class. He was also very available to help me despite my struggle in the class. He is a fair grader - if your paper does not deserve a specific grade, it will not get it.
Great guy, but he will make you work for your grade.  Long papers with extensive research are to be expected.
Very nice professor who genuinely likes working with students and making sure you know the material.
Great guy. Take his course, you'll become a better writer and learn a lot in the process.

Ulett's class was probably the most enjoyable one I had this semester. Just being in the same room with him was a consistent pleasure. He expects a lot from his students, but if you put in the effort you will do well in the class and become a better writer.

Professor Ulett is a fantastic professor and one of my favorites at Duke! He is very enthusiastic about the course topic and really wants you to grow as a writer. While his grading is very tough, you will learn to become a better writer. The workload isn't too bad unless you have a paper due. I would take another class with him if I had the chance!

Professor Ulett is great! Always up for a laugh along with serious class discussion. Very helpful, and he really improved my writing. Would definitely recommend him if you are interested in the topic. Fairly tough grader but I would happily take another class with him!
Ulett is always available and willing to help iron out any issues you may have with your essays. He kept the class interesting throughout the semester.
Ulett was enthusiastic about the material and always available to meet. With some work one could do well and the grading was fair. Though do not try to submit any bs papers.
Best professor I had at Duke, hands down. He cares deeply about his students and every lecture is intentional & clear. Take time to get to know him and his research too, he's fascinating!!

Professor Vanberg was genuinely top 3 professors I've had at Duke. The class itself was difficult, but he is AMAZING. Office hours were extremely helpful and homework was graded on completion. Tests are manageable if you study/do practice problems. 1 pretty simple group project. Vanberg is incredible, would take any class with him.

Professor Vanberg gives very engaging lectures and is great at explaining complicated game theory concepts, steadily building concepts on each other and giving us plenty of practice. The homeworks are straightforward and a good grade buffer, but there are only two tests and one project.

Extremely good professor - would recommend to anyone interesting in Political Science or adjacent fields. Always made class extremely engaging, never a time when I was bored. Readings were always extremely relevant and never too tedious, and he takes feedback on the readings as well. Overall, an amazing professor!

Prof. Vanberg is the best ! You have to take this course since I can't put it into words how good this class was. I can't say for sure if this is the best class at Duke since I'm in freshman year but I know for certain this is going to be one of the best classes I've ever taken in my life. The lectures seem like he is taking you through a journey.

I took Professor Vanberg's class in the Fall of 2024, and he was one of the best professors I have ever had at Duke. Such a kind soul and explains so so well. I already had a background in Game Theory, so it wasn't too hard to keep up with his class, but I still learned a lot. 2 midterms, 1 project, would take again!

Vanberg is a great professor. His class is super organized and well thought out. The lectures are really interactive and fun because he's got a great sense of humor. Even though attendance isn't mandatory, people still show up because his classes are just that good.
Professor Vanberg is probably one of the best teachers I've had at Duke, his class is extremely interesting and each topic builds on the other.

Prof Vanberg is the best prof that I have had this semester. Breaks down complex political economy texts into accessible concepts that are very immediately useful. He tries to not bring his own politics into seminars and will not grade you down for disagreeing with him, but it's pretty clear where he leans from the readings.

Though I took this course in my freshman year, I am confident that Prof. Vanberg and his course will be one of the best courses I will take at Duke. All readings were very informative and Prof. Vanberg's summary and analysis of the pieces in class also made the learning process so much better. Definitely take!

The first half of Game Theory was quite fun and the use of Moblab during lectures was fairly engaging. The second half of the course was less interesting, and more tedious, but the Professor Vanberg really isn't too blame. The grading for the class was unclear at times, but no complaints in the end.

Constitutions in Crisis seems like a miss of a class from Vanberg based on others' reviews. While I liked him as a person and occasionally learned from his lectures, the course was unfocused. The readings were convoluted and not always relevant to the class discussion. As a capstone, it was relatively easy but ultimately unhelpful

Prof V was my favorite this semester and my favorite so far at Duke. His Game Theory class is great. If you attend lectures and keep up with homework assignments you'll be fine. He's very funny and a great guy!
great lecturer good at explaining very patient

Prof V is a great professor. Very accessible outside of class and explains game theory in a way that makes it easy for students to understand. He will keep helping you till you understand the material. Only complaint is that the practice tests he provides are quite easier than the actual midterms/final.

Prof Vanberg (and Atila) did a great job with the discovering game theory course. It is accessible to both Econ and non-Econ students. Not the hardest course, but very interesting. Grading can be a little unclear.
Great professor, great person, makes the class interesting and informative. I'm not very good at econ/game theory but I still did fine and he makes concepts easy to understand. I learned a lot!
Awesome lecturer and very well respected in his field. Class was extremely interesting, and he was a fair grader on all of the assignments. Very reachable outside of class as well.

Amazing professor and amazing person! I really enjoyed his class and it was really cool to learn about constitutional theory. Your grade is divided into 2 midterms, a paper, a group project, and participation. The midterms are graded fairly but you better study. He is harsh on the paper at first but lets you rewrite it for credit.

favorite professor out of the 4 so far. does a great job of explaining the readings carefully while remaining engaging.... pretty lax grader as far as I can tell, the TA grades the papers but everyone does well for the most part. tldr - awesome class, awesome prof, pretty easy grading, made me excited for more polisci classes!

Vanberg is brilliant, an expert in political economy. The best professor I have had (out of the four so far). Take him at some point, even if you aren't in political science. The TA does do most of the grading which is a strange arrangement in such a small class.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Would take again

reviews.comment: He was extremely helpful and a great lecturer. Definitely take a class of his if you can.

TLDR; If you have any interest in political science or decision science, take his class  He is great at breaking down the arguments in our texts, and explaining them step-wise. He doesn't assign much reading, but all of it feels important. He's also got this hilarious deadpan dad sense of humor.
One of the best lecturers I have ever had. He breaks down the material very well and knows exactly what he is talking about. Make sure to do the readings and participate.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Best class I've had at Duke. Amazing lecturer and an all-around great person.
This man is a legend. Highly recommend.

Explains complex and abstract concepts in a clear manner, provides intriguing real-world examples, very approachable and friendly, shows enthusiasm for the subject, very skilled lecturer and always organized. Would recommend to anyone, even those outside the major

This class was so interesting, I was a little intimidating coming in, because the first couple weeks are tough and involve math.  But after the first two weeks, the class becomes infinitely more interesting and I learned so much about strategic voting in the political arena.  He makes this challenging subject matter simple and applicable.

Professor Vanberg is pretty helpful and really nice. He has a fair amount of readings which aren't necessarily mandatory, but you should read them since participation during discussions counts to your grade.
incredibly knowledgable, makes lectures interesting, uses clear examples, loved his class

Victor Strandberg is an iconic staple of Duke. I am sad to have waited until his last semester here to take his class. During lecture he orates, combining his own writings with those assigned. While you have to take extensive notes, his words are rich with insight, knowledge, and jokes. For me, his class was eye opening and a pleasure to take.
Old school thinking.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Super knowledgeable and a privilege to listen to. He grades essays leniently and make sure you write down everything he says in lecture for exams.
Tests require writing down everything he says in class, but if you know your stuff you're good. Cares about his students and sometimes tells interesting stories about his life.

Spends the entire class lecturing in a very monotone voice which can get boring. Tip: record all the lectures on your own using voice memos (he is not good with technology so don't rely on him to record). The exams are purely based on what he says in class so have a thorough understanding of that and you will do well.
Favorite professor at Duke. So insightful and caring. A true fountain of knowledge, not to mention an absolute legend.

Very kind, understanding professor who understands the burden the pandemic has put on students. Take notes on what he says during class so you'll have coherent papers, and follow along with the reading when you can (and go to lectures!) You'll get an A as long as you put in decent effort.

Best professor ever. Truly understands that students have other things going on in life- especially with online learning. Full of knowledge, loves his material, eager to share this joy with students. Manageable workload as long as you take notes and pay attention during classes.

Strandberg is really passionate about the material and spends class lecturing on main themes and takeaways. Reading isn't absolutely necessary, but good notes will help a lot when writing papers. Only 4 total papers, two of which were optional but Strandberg is a relatively easy grader. Understanding and chill but wouldn't necessarily take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Strandberg is extremely knowledgeable and is a good lecturer. He is very sweet and accessible outside of class. Most of his classes depend on taking good notes during his lectures. He does assign quite a lot of readings and has either 3-4 tests or 3-4 essays per semester (depending on class format). He did not change this for covid.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--So many papers

reviews.comment: best of both worlds- very little readings and hw for this class, but can learn so much from an incredible professor. generous about letting people skip class. not much participation required.

All you have to do is memorize everything (EVERYTHING) he says in lecture. Eager to help outside of class, kind man. For 271, has NO papers, only tests with straight route memorization from class. If you are looking for a political/modern class, do not take this one!

Dr. Strandberg is very knowledgeable and experienced (he's over 80 years old!). He's passionate about literature and will make you passionate as well. As for the course itself, the grading was based on tests throughout the semester that drew basically all from his lectures. A lot of rote memorization required.

great professor... love his lectures and just overall a legendary guy. the class itself is super weird. we were only graded on 3 one hour exams which were straight from lecture so TAKE EXTENSIVE NOTES. good class overall.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Inspirational man! Lectures were spent going through the material we read and highlighting his takeaways and themes. His tests were primarily based on what was said in lecture, but my favorite thing about him was meeting after class over a snack to go through the readings for all interpretations. Cares a lot about his students and is very patient.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Professor's lectures are deep and insightful. The books are covered very fast, so it's important to stay on track with readings. Record lectures and make good notes since tests are based on what's discussed. Clear and objective grading. A is achievable if you work hard and manage time well.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Strandberg's lectures are legendary. Detailed analysis of the books, delivered in his trademark voice of God. Class is entirely test based, memorize what he says in lectures and you're guaranteed an A. You don't have to actually read anything. Go to class and take notes, he goes pretty fast.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Lectures were very interesting. Gives a lot of detailed analysis, both on the texts and on the authors and backgrounds. Tests were based entirely on his personal analysis of the text, but were also objectively graded. He goes very quickly, memorize what he says in lecture and you're guaranteed an A. You even don't have to actually read.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Strandberg is incredibly knowledgable on all of the authors he selects and can deliver a very engaging lecture. However be prepared to sit back and listen, take exams, and read. My criticism is that Victor doesn't encourage any critical engagement between students and the texts -- lectures only  -- if you're looking for feedback, I'd pass.

I love Strandberg so much. I'm not an English major, and I was so inspired by his lectures and the information he includes outside of the book. One of my favorite Duke classes, I highly highly recommend it.

There should be no question: take Strandberg's class. Whatever he is teaching, take it. The man is a phenomenal professor and lecturer. Tests are based exactly on what he says in class. Write down exactly what he says and memorize it and you will get an A. If nothing else, the man has a legendary voice.

Strandberg is legendary. Take his class and you won't regret it. Best advice: read as much as you can in advance because he moves super quickly. If you take notes in class you're pretty much guaranteed an A. Plus his wonderful sonorous voice is a treat to listen to.

If you do the reading and go to class, expect an easy A. Class notes are the most important for the tests as most questions are based of that and the books plot. The professor is a legend, 80 years old and going strong.

Professor Strandberg is the best. This is my third class I've taken with him and I am planning to take another. His lectures are super easy, just show up, take notes & look through your notes before tests and you'll do fine. No essays for lectures. The seminars have essays but hes an easy grader so don't worry about it.

Phenomenal Professor- however tests are objective. If you don't have a good memory- not the class for you! You have to remember specifics about the books and his specific analysis. There's only one optional term paper. He goes very fast and you cannot miss a class, however great readings and a passionate professor!

Professor Strandberg is a sweetheart. He's very interesting and knows lots of random facts about everything - which keeps his class entertaining. The workload wasn't too heavy - his tests are VERY specific and related to what he says in class. If you put the effort in, he isn't too harsh a grader on papers. His final was pass/fail!

Strandberg is da man.  His exams are in objective short-answer format, so be sure to bring a laptop and type everything he says to study later.  One of my favorite classes last semester.  Great for pre-meds/science majors.  Read the books in advance--you'll appreciate it later.

Strandberg is the most interesting professor I've had in 4 years at Duke. He's not easy, but if you take notes and pay attention you shouldn't do worse than a B, and you could do better. But his lecture style and breadth of knowledge on his topics are extremely impressive, he cares about his students, and he has the Voice of God. Seriously.
If you take notes during his class you will do fine. Taking one of his classes should be done if you enjoy the material and reading in general.

I also took his early American lit class and will be taking his  20th century American lit class.  Amazing voice, great lecturer with a thorough knowledge of the topic.  Seminar class didn't have much student participation, but it was still an amazing class.  A great teacher if you want to approach a topic you normally find difficult.

His opinions on literature are interested and textually based. A smart and kind old professor, his exams are based solely on facts from the books and his lectures so the course should be an easy A if you have a good memory.

Tests based on lectures and reading.  Basically tested on random facts from in the books and what he says about them in lecture.  Not too hard if you really pay attention during lecture, do the reading and study- but all of these things are necessary for doing well.  Have to meet with him in his office and he videos you saying your name-creepy.

Strandberg has possibly the coolest speaking voice I have ever heard.  I enjoyed going to class just so I could listen to him speak. Classes were the same every day - just listen to him talk.  Tests were pretty useless, quizzing you on random facts from the book.  I highly recommend writing the optional paper. Good class for non-English majors.

The tests can be tricky, but if you read the books, take good notes, and study, you should be fine. Lecture is very important, so don't miss it. He is a great lecturer who will talk about some very interesting ideas. Very good class.

Professor Strandberg is amazing.  I really enjoyed his class, and the tests really aren't too bad if you read the books (which are good) and take good notes.  It's a good idea to compare notes with friends or record the lecture.  You'll definitely gain appreciation for certain authors that you might not have enjoyed previously.  Highly recommended!

Strandberg is a wonderful professor.  He's absolutely riveting in lecture.  His tests aren't bad at all.  I got an A and all I did was review my notes the night before andI actually read the books he assigned (important as at least a few of the test questions aren't covered in lecture) and the books are good anyway.  Tests are all short-answer

Lectures are very engaging.  He is really one of the great Duke professors.  Definitely try to take a course with him before you graduate.  He can move very quickly in lecture, so be sure you always go, and it's helpful to have friends to compare notes with to make sure you got everything down before tests.

Strandberg is one of my fave professors of all time. He ROCKS. The tests aren't easy and draw from both the books and notes, but it's ok. He explains things SO well and the books he chooses are all good. Take a class with Strandberg. He's so cute!! And you can tell he loves getting to know the students!

Strandberg is AMAZING.  He is like your grandfather, but a lot wiser.  As long as you go to lectures (which are great!) and read the books (which aren't bad) you will be fine.  Every single one of his classes is based on 3 1-hour short answer exams.  Also, he makes an effort to get to know everyone in the class.  HIGHLY RECOMMENDED.

Great professor.  You only study HIS (interesting) analyses, which is fine if you're a non-major.  Tests were extremely detail-oriented and came from lecture: you don't really have to read the books, just go to class. He's genuinely interested in his students and class - highly recommended prof.

Tests are very picky and completely based on his lectures...in fact, sometimes he doesn't say things in lecture but still puts them on tests...so sucks for you. Hit or miss tests. Not a hard test if you have an excellent memory and aren't a good writer, but don't expect to improve your writing skills at all (besides grammar).

Strandberg is an incredibly passionate and interesting lecturer. he's extremely literary, which comes out in his every day speech when you get to meet him during office hours-that's right, he makes everyone in his 150 person class go. he's just a really great, caring old guy who wants to see everyone succeed. the tests are fair, but very particular
flash back to high school. most disappointing class of my college career.

Brilliant and passionate guy, but often uses lectures to extend only his interpretation of the piece. Seems willing to listen to alternative readings in class, but on papers quite resistant to iconoclast interpretations. Friendly out of class, but not very helpful. Gives limited to no feedback on content classwork, only conferences on  grammar.

Strandberg is Awesome!  Lectures are entertaining and the books are all quality.  Take notes in class and you'll do fine on the tests.  He also makes sure he gets to meet with everyone in his big lecture classes which is really cool.  Great class.

Strandberg is an AMAZING professor, and the looong classes go by far too fast because his lectures rock. The books are usually decent, but you'll get to love them because he presents them so well. Write down EVERYTHING he says in class, it'll be on those randomly particular tests.

The testing was worthless -- agreed -- but also really easy if you did the reading and have any kind of retention abilities.  A GREAT class and a great prof -- epecially if you aren't the most linguistically-inclined of people.

LOVE him! He is an amazing lecturer who covers so much in so little time. His voice is so soothing and fun to listen to, so appropriate to great literature. Agree a bit that the testing could be improved, but I think he is trying to make sure people are attending lecture, which is most valuable
Books are interesting but the tests are worthless

While he makes an attempt to get to know students in a ridiculously huge lecture, his tests are absolutely worthless.  They test you on minute details that are essentially irrelevant to understanding the books.  His lectures can be interesting and do help you to appreciate the authors' works

Great class if you need an AL or English class and you cant write essays.  Very smart guy who provides great views on some great books.  Lectures are a little boring with a lot of note taking.  Take the class with a girl who can take good notes
Extremely boring lecture style!  Tests that test if you know what he told you about a book - not what you think.  Run if you enjoy discussion!
Amazing English professor
his classes are fantastic and he is a great speaker
Very powerful professor.  I knew he was something special when the lecture started of with,  When I was having lunch with Toni Morrison...
No Comments
goog guy
No Comments
Not accessible outside class time. He does not make his requirements about the exams clearly until he hands out the exams. Personally do not recommend taking his course.

Do not take this class. The course is poorly paced with 1-2 homework in the first half of the semester, then like 7 homeworks on the second half. We were told the final would be fully multiple-choice, then few days before the exam it turns out that's not the case. You should probably go to lectures to understand the material, quite chemistry heavy

Final 60% of total grade & not related to assignments. Open notes, so print out ALL slides.
Personally, the course material is really intriguing and deeply compassionate.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The content itself was interesting, and the lectures were easy to understand. HW problems are worth 40% of the grade, and the exam was worth 60%. Open note exam, just make sure you actually study/prepare for it—print out the slides. Some people underprepared because they were told it would be easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class was pretty much all slideshows that were posted online and problem sets due every other week or so. There were a lot of real-world examples and case studies sprinkled into lectures which made them bit more engaging. Content was interesting, but if you aren't super passionate about water science this might not be the most exciting class.
worst professor, worst class. gives homework that has no relation to what we've talked about in class. horrible ta as well.
Dr. Vengosh is great! Lectures can sometimes be a little confusing because he likes tangents- but class is overall really chill and interesting

HW was 40% of your grade, and a take home final was 60%. Some of the lectures were pretty confusing - I recommend getting help before moving on to new material because some of it builds on each other. Gordon (TA) was awesome. Class really opened my eyes to water issues - Vengosh did a great job making the topics relevant to the global community.

Highly interesting class. Vengosh is super knowledgeable about his field. He's really passionate about the course content and you could tell this class is his bread-and-butter. Would definitely recommend taking for anyone interested in water quality, fracking, or hydrogeology.

Vengosh, while extremely knowledgeable and prominent in his field, is a boring lecturer. He's not good at explaining new concepts and sometimes contradicts himself. Some content was moderately interesting. Attending class is optional; everything you need for hw is in the online powerpoints. If Nathaniel is TAing, go to him for ?s. He's awesome.

First thing Dr. Vengosh tells you is that he doesn't believe in tests, hence the 60%hwk, 40% final essay grad distribution. As a non-major, i thought class was pretty interesting, but you can succeed without going to class b/c hwk assignments are literally manipulations of equations found in lecture slides posted online. easy A.

The lectures were really disorganized. The class was not really introductory, if you have not taken calculus 2 and at least AP Physics 1 and C (Mechanics) you will struggle. No practice exams are given. The homeworks will take you hours to complete as the problems are highly complex. The discussion sessions were a waste of time.
Confusing lectures read straight from the textbook and absurdly hard homeworks. Teaching undergrads does not seem to be a priority for Dr. Vavagiakis at all.

It says this is in an introductory physics class, that's just not true DO NOT TAKE THIS CLAS WITHOUT PHYSICS EXPERIENCE IT WILL ROCK YOUR WORLD. If you're not ready to make this class and have it take up the bulk of your time, also don't take it. Dr Eve is nice but lecture can be unclear at times but this may also be growing pains. Final was awful.

I am a senior, and Dr. Vieth is one of my top 5 worst professors at Duke. Her lectures are very boring and make the tests almost impossible to finish without curving the grade. She also does not give the homework until Thursday night and makes it due Sunday. She seeks student failure and NOT in a good way.

The whole curriculum was redesigned so maybe that is why the class felt a bit unorganized. The tests were also very long. Homeworks were every week. She is a sweet lady overall but really harsh with the regrade requests. I am very grateful I had a great TA. TAs matter in this class. Class wasn't bad but definitely stressful.

Dr. Vieth is an amazing lecturer, truly made a boring topic came to life. She is very clear and funny in class and very easy to reach outside class. Group assignment can be a little annoying if you don't like your teammates, but imo they do their best to let you get to know your teammates before choosing who to group with.
Professor Vieth is really great, but the grading on the homeworks and exams can be very difficult.

No structure in class. One test was okay. The other test was on things we didn't even review. Half of class didn't finish. This should be a wake up call to reassess what is being taught and what is being tested. No practice and if we are given practice, it's at the last moment. No guidelines to follow with hw but then will be graded harshly.

Good intro class to stats, but lack of support. TA's were not the best and we wouldn't get homework until Thursday night, due on Sunday. Some of the grading criteria was not clear, however we did get plenty of extra credit oppor. Midterm is hard, even with preparation, but they give you all the points possible. Overall, decent.
The best! She genuinely cares and the content is fascinating. Worth taking if you are interested in psychology that goes into marketing/buying/ consumerism. Loved it

I feel very fortunate to have had Dr. Vieth as my Statistics professor. Coming into this required course, I initially disliked the subject. But her genuine kindness and caring support got me to stay thru and engage with the material. I highly recommend going to her office hours and staying on top of the weekly groupwork. She is also quite funny.

If you have a good group, you're set. It is a lot of homework and the grading in the beginning is really arbitrary and confusing but you will eventually get the hang of it. The undergraduate TAs are so much better than the graduate ones. Vieth is really funny, it's unfortunate people don't see that. She's very kind and her office hours are fun.

This class is fine. It's not better than fine, but it's also not worse than fine. Vieth makes the methods content extremely clear and accessible, but she lost most of us during the stats content. She definitely tries to be engaging and interesting, but more often than not falls flat. I wouldn't avoid this class, but don't take it unless you have to

Professor Vieth was an incredibly interesting and approachable professor. Her grading criteria and lectures were clear. No outside reading is necessary because she provides so many resources and information in class and discussion. Don't be alarmed if mid-semester you don't like your current grade. I would certainly take this course with her again.

Research methods and statistics isn't a super interesting topic, but Dr. Vieth delivers the content clearly and makes it easy to understand. If you've taken any stats class before, the first half of the class is just review of the basics. Weekly group and individual assignments are straightforward, and there's one midterm and an optional final.
The professor made a class that could seem daunting for a psych major easily digestible and enjoyable.

AAAAAAAAAAA. So much work. Very arbitrary in terms of homework grading (if you write half a word wrong they will take off 5 points). Lectures are okay. She is good. The TAs take forever to get stuff back to us. Assignments open Thursday PM and are due Sunday. Then you get the grade a lifetime after. AAAAAAA.
Lectures cover content which is very fascinating and pertinent to marketing. Lenient grader in that she will often give benefit of the doubt!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: don't take her class
Solid professor. Very clear about expectations. Topics are very cool and applicable to consumer behavior in a marketing sense. Almost all of grade determined by midterm, final, and research paper.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Vieth makes a widely dreaded class as interesting and rewarding as possible. The structure of the final project is really intuitive, as you work on it throughout the semester and get feedback as you go along. She's a great communicator and gives great advice for success in the class, and she keeps lecture as interesting as she can.
Clear and straightforward lectures. Breaks content down in approachable and interesting way. Super funny also
Tests were very rigorous and grading quite harsh. Topic of consumer psych was interesting but expectations may have been too high

She is a great lecturer and incorporates lots of engagement and activities throughout her lectures. Tests are very fair, and you'll do well if you attend class! She is so sweet and cares about all of her students.

She deserves just as must praise for the miracle that was Psy204 this pandemic semester, even if she doesnt proudly announce a grade of F in her first psych stats class, unlike SL (sorry!). She covered the methods section of stats & methods very well and thorough, and always provided great examples. Since tests were open note, it was super easy.

Class material is boring, and two big research papers which you do in groups which you can't choose and end up being unequal. Exams are very straightforward and just have to do with all the lecture slides. No need to read the textbook as it covers the same material as in lecture. Vieth is a pretty good professor, but the class is just not too great

I came out of this class with nothing gained. Her idea of what learning should be is completely arbitrary. She takes off points for the most minute details, including the lack of commas in your papers. Avoid if you can. Probably the most detail-oriented and no offense useless class I have taken at Duke
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Vieth was a nice and generally helpful teacher who just seemed a little too nitpicky at times. Your class grade will largely be determined by research paper assignments--both group projects ugh. She is, however, very good about emails, updates and meeting outside of class and is also always prepared with well-organized lecture slides.
This class was an 8:30 and super boring. Even though it was not that hard, I left the class feeling like I did not get anything out of it.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Go to lecture. Take a few notes. You'll be fine. Do the readings too, but even if you skim should be okay as well. Yes, lectures can be boring sometimes but great info. learned and Vieth is very well informed and if not she takes the time to look up/research and update students. Very fair grader and looking to help, not hurt students!

A solid Psych 101 class. Lectures are pretty much just the textbook in PowerPoint form, with the occasional participation-grade pop quiz to check attendance. Do the textbook readings, take notes, and use the study guides-- exams will be a breeze.

Dr. Vieth has subjective grading criteria, doesnt know how to lecture beyond reading off slides and asking for class feedback, and grades harshly. She holds office hours but why go when she doesnt help in long run.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I love Dr. Vieth! Had her for research methods which is never going to be exciting and she has a great sense of humor and VERY clear grading criteria and lectures. Really the ideal person for this class.

Very clear lecturer with a good sense of humor. Vieth runs a standard lecture class: she flips through a PowerPoint and highlights the assigned textbook reading. Going to class is not a must, but Vieth does throw out the occasional (ungraded) pop quiz to assess attendance. Exams are easy if you read the textbook, and she gives study guides.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: The class is almost taught completely out of the book with only a few surprises on the tests that come from lecture. If you have the time to thoroughly read the textbook from front to back then you will be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Overall, the class was fine. A survey psych class with a good amount of reading. I never did it though. If you pay attention in class and really memorize the powerpoints then you'll be fine. And before the test, read the sections she tells you to do. The tests were overly specific but easy for me since I memorized the information thoroughly.

Dr. Vieth is definitely very knowledgeable on the topic, and the lectures are very helpful in highlighting main points. The class is interesting, but the tests can be frustrating because they ask such specific details. If you read the book and keep up you should be fine though. Overall she's very fair and a good teacher for Psych 101.

Vieth has a peculiar sense of humor, and some lectures were more interesting than others. Pop quizzes count as a 100 if you show up to class. Recommend not reading until she puts out the reading guides before the exam. Then 100% read the sections she tells you to because multiple exam q's are from the textbook. Overall enjoyed the class.

Not a bad class, hardness wise, but kind of just a pain sometimes. There are pop quizzes in class, a lot of long emails with important information, and the tests are strictly memorization. If you are good at memorizing a lot of information you'll get a good grade, otherwise you just have to put in a lot of work.

There is a lot of reading, and the lectures aren't dynamic, but the information is interesting and makes Vieth bearable. She's pretty funny. She does try to engage the lecture by making students tell jokes or talk in small groups. There are pop-quizzes, but they're worth minimal points and you get to drop one, so it's no big deal!

Vieth has been my favorite professor at Duke. She is passionate and really cares about students. Her class is not easy though. I was actually struggling in the class until I went in for help. Very very helpful and sweet lady, and after our meeting, I brought my grade up to an A-. Now I'm considering majoring in psych - all because of her. Take her.

Very smart. Very nice. But like... there's an unnecessary massive amount of work and reading. If you take any other psych classes at Duke you just end up repeating the material so why does it all have to be accounted for in psy 101? Frustrating.

The chapters were ridiculously long. Take years to read. If I ever have trouble sleeping, I will take another Vieth class because she manages to put me right to sleep. Pretty difficult class, do not recommend.
Don't take her class.  All the exams are tricky.
Great professor! Her expectations are very clear about assignments. In class quiz not that difficult but online ones can be tricky.

Super nice lady and very knowledgable. However she reads off the slides and lectures are not dynamic. Tests are hard and focus on obscure details and she does not hand assignments back on time at all.

Vieth mostly just reads off the slides, but her lectures help reinforce the material, and it's necessary to attend them because she hands out pop quizzes.  I thought it would be a walk in the park, but it definitely requires textbook reading and a fair amount of memorization.  You should get an A with some effort.

Decent professor. Lectures are really good and she cares a lot. Definitely read the textbook. Beware that you have to memorize as you read because she gives pop quizzes (about once a week). That's a pain because you have to memorize things every day and then you have to still cram for the exams, but not a bad professor.
Pretty boring but necessary premed requirement. Beware = test averages were a low B. No curve. Most kids did not get As.
Enthusiastic and very helpful professor. Course was definitely a lot of work/not an easy A. However, subject matter was interesting and prof. Vieth gives very clear expectations.
She's awesome
She is very clear! Interesting and answers questions and tests are fair and predictable, mostly MC.
Very interesting class that was very well taught. If you put in the work, which merely consists of textbook reading, you will get an A. Vieth was thorough, very helpful, and very fair.

Interesting subject matter, but tests were based on rote memorization of minutiae and trends that are briefly mentioned in class. Definitely NOT an easy A. However, paper grading is pretty lax and she is willing to give points back on exams if you justify your reasoning. If you just want a painless SS credit like i did, look elsewhere.

I completely disagree that Angie is not enthusiastic. She cracks jokes all the time and tries to engage the class as much as possible during lecture. She even RUNS to the back of the lecture hall if a student has a question during an exam. She made me want to take another class in psychology, especially another class with her. She's just adorable.

Definitely not recommended, if you want an enthusiastic professor, Vieth is not who you are looking for. No need to go to lectures, she just reads her slides. She is making Psych 101 harder on purpose, so that no one gets an A, so the tests are ridiculously hard. I wish I had taken it with another teacher,definitely didn't enjoy her and her classes

She writes down questions if she feels she can't answer them to her satisfaction in class, then sends out emails with the answers later. She also sends out reminders about assignments. Her exams are incredibly straightforward, especially if you utilize the hint sheet. She's very clear in lecture and has a good sense of humor.
Dr. Vieth was an absolutely awesome teacher. I would highly reccomend her Psy 101 class to anyone interested.

I'm sure she's great for higher level classes but it was clear that she was not used to teaching an intro lecture. Dry lectures that sometimes attempted to be funny, hard tests that assumed more dedication than an intro class, but very sweet and helpful outside of class.

The class material was very interesting and her lectures were good, too. But there wasn't much of a need to go to class as long as you read the ppt notes online.
