The tests were rote memorization and did not require any application or comprehensive thinking. It was an easy class if you're willing to study hard for the tests.

Really is a great professor. She gives you study guides for tests. She is extremely fair in grading, class is fairly easy overall. the material is easy and useful. Definitely recommend the class and the professor!

Professor Vieth is great. She is very helpful and you can tell she really cares about her students. However, the class was not well taught at all and even though you may know your stuff, the tests are so nit-picky that it's near impossible to get that "easy A." Material was interesting, but class was just power point slides read verbatim.. boring

I know she got raving reviews, but if you are taking intro psych with her, I would not give her a very high rating.  If you're interested in having a powerpoint read to you for an hour and 15 minutes twice  a week, then by all means, take this class.  If not, you might want to take it from someone else.  The test questions were also too nit-picky.

I can only heartily second ALL these raving reviews. She is amazing. Love her. You would be a fool not to take any class with her. Forget college, she's my favorite teacher of all TIME. 6* Attendance not mandatory, but you'll find it helpful -her tests rely mostly on the lectures, and these are so fun it'll be easier to remember concepts.

one of the best there is @ duke. Vieth is kind, responds to emails, clear, articulate, concerned with her students education. even though i wasn't interested in the content of her class (it was required for my major) i enjoyed her class and learned a lot. highly recommend this in lieu of the other 185s

AWESOME teacher. She cares a lot about the material, and really knows her stuff. The class isn't 'easy', but she is very willing to help. A getting at least a B is definitely doable with a decent amount of effort. I HIGHLY recommend any class with Dr. Vieth

Awesome! Love her... Interesting material..everyone has something to contribute considering the material..she's extremely helpful with the final term paper and a very understanding person. It's also not that difficult to get an A. I'd say take it immediately. Loved it.

Easy class in terms of workload but extremely interesting stuff! She was really nice and helpful and encouraging, too. I took it as an easy A but then realized it was probably one of the more useful classes I've ever taken. Psych. of Gender makes you re-evaluate your views on gender, gender relations, etc. Highly recommended.
really good person and decent lecturer, but what the hell was that 1st quiz... cmon prof volkan u gotta make it more simple than that
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Volkan is kind and clearly wants her students to do well. However, the class is very content heavy, so you will have to review the recorded lectures. There were 6 quizzes that were worth 60% of your grade. The quizzes were long/short answer and kind of hard. Take home final that you create, more like a final project. Overall, it's an okay class.

The class was hard, and you need to memorize many things. The good thing is that you get to do a chapter quiz every week, so what you've learned won't pile up. However, the quiz questions are indeed hard, especially the experiment design. Despite the grading criteria is quite easy to get an A, having a quiz every single week was not fun.

Easy class. Quiz every week with cheat card. Final is a project where you make your own exam and answer it - that was super easy. 1 dropped quiz. Discussion is a waste of time though. Take 223 with her it is pretty easy, but a little annoying at the end because the schedule was overzealous and we had 4 quizzes in the last 10 days of school.
Good lecturer and caring professor.

great professor who really cares about her students and wants them to learn the content. She records lectures you can go back and rewatch, although just go to class and take really good notes and you should be good. Weekly quizzes are very specific so make sure you know your stuff (flashcard allowed). FInal was open-note
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: -Volkan is great : heard 223 was difficult, and while it required hard work, it paid off -compassionate/listens to students needs -weekly in-person quizzes, open-note final -TON of material: make sure to stay on track -didn't take bio @duke before but got an A+ -TA Brooke DArcy was AMAZING and really solidified the main concepts needed for quizzes

Class is much easier now since there are weekly quizzes which are worth 60% of your grade. Just pay attention to lecture slides and figure out what things the TAs look for in quizzes. Overall, not a difficult class to get an A if you put in the work. You don't have to memorize slides too closely cause questions are more experimental design-based.

Dr. Volkan was the kindest most compassionate professor I had this semester. She really understood kids were going through things trying to adjust to online school and really made an effort to listen and accept feedback when students felt stressed. Wonderful professor with a really interesting course!

She's much more organized than her co-lecturer Nina Sherwood, but definitely not the most engaging. This is mostly because it is a mandatory course for the neuroscience major and the information is hardly engaging hearing it a third time around (Biological Bases & Fundamentals of Neuroscience are nearly identical in their content.)
Tests are very very difficult.
Very solid.

Volkan gives great lectures, although she does go pretty quickly. She is always willing to answer questions and clarify things. Her exam questions are more challenging than Sherwood's, but discussion section helps you practice what's important to know. The class has a lot of information, but isn't too bad with consistent studying.

He is so quirky and so unpretentious, and absolutely very intelligent. He gave the best reading recommendations and was very responsive to emails. I did love being in his class and I was worried about his health. So glad he finally took a medical leave. Missing him so much.

he is truly unique. so brilliant yet so unpretentious. i will never forget the deep traces he left in my unconscious. yet, antonio would smile at this comment, challenging me--with his lyrical subtlety--to reconsider the extent to which his traces in my unconscious are visible to me, or the surety with which I declare never to forget him.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: this guy changed my whole perspective on learning, on so many levels. and even better, despite his intelligence and knowledge, he is so unassuming and always approachable, understanding, and genuinely nice.  you have to at least take a class with him once.
He's truly knowledgeable, relatable and gives you more attention and credit for your work than you think you deserve. Amazing guy and life changing class.

I took LSGS101 because I was interested in learning about historical, political, and social issues of Latino immigration in the US, but the class itself was mostly about identity formation. Lots of long readings (which I never did), class discussions predictably about identity fluidity, racism, capitalism, etc. Cool class, but not a lot of new info

Antonio is the quirky professor everyone needs to have at least once in college. He's passionate about what he does and is exceedingly approachable. He's in the Lit department, so expect a good amount of reading & writing, as well as great writing critique, in both his Lit & non-Lit classes. Is a bit anti-establishment at times.

He is amazing. Very smart, makes you question life in a different manner. He is crucial on attendance but there was not one day that I did not feel like going to his class. A Lot of reading but very interesting none the less.

Viego is one of the best professors I have ever had. I didn't expect to enjoy this class as much as I did, and it has changed the way that I think. I definitely recommend it to anyone. It isn't too easy, but it is worth the effort.

Had to take this class because everything else was full, but it turned out to be pretty interesting.  He doesn't get on your case if youre shy and don't want to speak.  I barely ever read more than 4 pages of anything assigned and my final essay was a breeze. He bought our class coffee once.  He's very relatable.
can't get any better than antonio.  he was my advisor and i miss him dearly.  he never failed to put a wrinkle in my brain... every single class.
No Comments
Honest, true to self kind of person. Sexy guy - doesn't look like a professor, sometimes talks about private life...

Quirky and charismatic, he encourages class discussion so long as you can support your claims with relevant information. Lots of reading but his tests come from lectures. Pretty easy on the eyes as well.

Dr. Wallace is a great professor and cares a lot about his students, he tries his best to make himself available to help and always holds office hours before exams for the entire day. It's a really tough class with lots of homework and difficult exam questions, but it is manageable

Despite this being easily the hardest class I've taken (and hopefully will take), Dr. Wallace cares deeply about student success. Exams were graded pretty tough but my growth and engagement over the semester really proved to myself what I was capable of achieving. Focus on learning and engaging with Dr. Wallace and the TAs and the grade will follow

Love a flipped classroom style for this subject because he's right -- it's better to practice problem solving in class than being lost outside of lectures. You get to start the homework in class so there was not a lot of work outside of class besides watching the lectures and some short online quizzes.

The class is a ton of work - I regularly spent around 3-5 hours per week outside of class, and both COMSOL projects took me around 20-30 hours to complete. Don't be fooled by the class not having a lab - it has a similar level of work as one. Tests are super hard, but Wallace is fair with the content. He is super helpful and an amazing teacher.

I cannot say enough good things about Dr. Wallace. Don't get me wrong, this class was difficult and the exams are no joke but it showed me that BME was the major I was meant to be in. He's also as knowledgable as you can get on the given subject, an amazing academic resource and very kind, supportive, and inspirational person.

Extremely caring professor with an amazing understanding of the course (and anything related to BME). The course emphasizes application-based learning opposed to memorization, which is a much better marker of content learned and made the class feel like I was truly in an engineering environment. Dr. Wallace also offers great scheduling advice.

BME 244 is a great indicator of whether the BME major is right for you. The exams primarily consist of application-based problems, making it essential to truly understand the material rather than just memorizing it. Dr. Wallace is an excellent professor, and his extended "mega office hours" before exams were incredibly helpful.

While the class is incredibly difficult, it is an intro class for an incredibly difficult major. Wallace does an amazing job teaching the content in an entertaining manner and setting up proper expectations for what to expect on exams. They are still incredibly difficult, but he works with the students to make it the best experience possible.
Beware the third midterm

BME307 is flipped classroom, where you learn through video lectures outside of class and do your homework in class with an assigned group. Dr. Wallace really cares and challenges his students. He is one of the best lecturers in Duke BME!

This class is a good indicator if you will enjoy the rest of BME. It's a LOT of work but it is the most interesting and rewarding class I've ever taken in terms of content and really knowing what BME feels like. Exams aren't weighted super heavily, and if you do the homework thoroughly and go to office hours before exams you'll be well-prepared.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Id rather fall of a bike twice than take this again. This class mixes every subject into one semester. Its insanely hard. After the first midterm, people dropped Pratt as a whole. This class made me so stressed I almost broke up with my girlfriend. There arent enough words in the English dictionary to express my disdain towards this class.

This is a good class -- quantitatively modeling helps understand physiology with greater depth. I think the workload of the class is exaggerated. There are only five stats modules and lab reports are essentially worksheets with questions (except last one). It's similar to other classes with a lab component. Wallace is available and often helpful.

Idk what these people are saying, but I'm telling you right now: this is the weed out class of BME. I have never studied so hard to end up with such a low grade. He is cramming stats, physiology, ECE, anatomy, and physics all in one class. He's nice, yeah, but many people dropped or withdrew from this class after the first test. Best of luck!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Easily the most intensive class I have ever taken! Physiology, statistics, homework, labs, and exams. I mean just the insanely long name is intimidating. Finishing this class is like conquering a beast, but Wallace gives you the resources to do it. It's an annoying amount of work but lectures are interesting and you really do learn a lot!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: His class definitely gave me a solid introduction to physiology and how to think about it like an engineer. I did well in the class, but the sheer amount of work he gives is completely unnecessary. His smug smile makes me think he enjoys the pain of students. It's okay though. It's not like we have other classes. You'll learn, annoyingly.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Wallace taught an organized and engaging class- great intro to BME! Connections between physiology, statistics, and lab are seamless. Weekly homework is interesting and relevant to tests. OH are frequent and helpful, especially before exams, with reviews and practice problems available. Online BME/stat resources were also useful!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Wallace is the best engineering professor I've had at Duke and is the reason I'm sticking with BME. His lectures are incredibly informative and his homework/practice problems prepare you well for similar questions on tests. His class is hard and he knows it, but he works to make it accessible. I would highly recommend taking his classes.

Get ready to dedicate 110% of your time to this class. This man does not care. Amount of content is ridiculous(physiology, stats, quantitative modeling) and schedule is mind-blowingly crammed(with separate stats lectures, pre/post quizzes, labs, 3hr stats sessions). He expects way too much out of his students. Did learn a lot, but at a high cost.

Professor Wallace actually reminds me of what college professors should be: teaches hard concepts very well to students while giving hard exams that challenge you. If you want an easy class, this definitely is not the class for you. But if you are BME student who is willing to learn, this is one of the best professors out there in Duke BME.

Professor Wallace actually reminds me of what college professors should be: teaches hard concepts very well to students while giving hard exams that challenge you. If you want an easy class, this definitely is not the class for you. But if you are BME student who is willing to learn, this is one of the best professors out there in Duke BME.

Dr. Wallace is without a doubt the best professor I've had at Duke. Granted, his class is very difficult and incredibly time-consuming, but he is an engaging lecture, is great at explaining material, and really prepares us for the exams and takes the time to make sure that we know what is going on. Amazing professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Walace expects and demands a lot, he teaches tough courses at a top school. However, he provides means for some to succeed. He is always available, Skype, IM, and works overtime to prepare students, but regardless, the test is going to always be higher. Hes the type of teacher that not everyone enjoys, he makes you work hard but stick to it!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Hilarious

reviews.comment: One of the best classes I've taken at Duke. This class definitely challenges you, but you learn sooo much. I would highly recommend rewatching his lecture videos. Tests are hard, but usually he's looking for VERY specific concepts and wording in your answers, which he mentions in lecture. Lookout for trick questions on the tests!!

Super nice on the surface, but it's easy to get on his bad side. He stopped liking me near the end of the semester (for various reasons, partly my fault, but regardless) and my grades just dropped dramatically. Kind of petty. Feelings shouldn't affect your grades.

Dr. Wallace reminds me of high school teachers who were good, but didn't teach to the AP exam: they frustrate you while you're taking their class, but are doing the right thing for you in the long run. The class is really hard, but you learn a lot about physiology and engineering. Do practice problems, go to office hours & don't procrastinate labs
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Prof. Wallace puts an insane amount of time making sure that his class runs seamlessly. First time I've seen a partial flipped classroom work so well. Exams are tough, but he prepares you well with homeworks and exam-type practice problems. You will be working very hard in his class, but know that he's probably working harder to help you learn.

To begin, this was a very tough, time-consuming class with a large workload- lab, stats, etc. However, it is very rewarding and you learn a lot. Dr. Wallace really wants his students to understand and apply concepts. He is always happy to answer any questions and is very accessible in the sense that he feels more of like a mentor than a professor.
This class was way too much work (the lab reports are so long) and the tests were hard. If you can take it with someone else I would highly recommend that.
Great class, one of the best professors ever at Duke. If you work, you'll do great. Slackers will be ruined by this class.

His exams are really tough and you'll definitely have to work for that A. However, you can tell just how dedicated he is to teaching and how much effort he puts into preparing his lectures. His course is incredibly organized and truly approaches physiology from an engineer's perspective. He encourages us to have active discussions in class.
Dr. Wallace has been my favorite professor so far! So helpful and makes lectures interesting! Really wants his students to learn and do the best that they can.

The lectures are straight from the textbook. Labs are graded extremely stingy, taking points off for the tiniest formatting error. Tests are not about understanding material, but rather using key words he talked about in lecture. He also rarely answers questions on Piazza and is not very helpful.

Always very prepared for lecture.  Covers topics at a reasonable pace: meaning he presents the new framework slowly and then assigns problems which require you to draw from previous classes pretty quickly to keep up with what's going on the next time.  Homeworks pretty difficult, tests were fairly challenging, but fair material and grading wise.

Very well-organized lecturer and cares about his students. Teaches at the pace that students want. Exams are rather tough and homeworks take a long time, but he was extremely helpful, especially in office hours. Posts helpful youtube tutorials about the homework and in-class problems. One of the better profs in the BME dept.

Avoid if your physics background is weak. Ying's lecture is difficult to follow because he expects you to memorize an equation/concept 5 seconds after he talks about it. Despite putting in significant effort, I stayed confused.

Lectures don't reflect what's on quizzes. Quizzes were meant to ensure you were keeping up, but have now become essentially mini midterms. Doesn't seem to really care about student success and makes this class unnecessarily difficult for what it should be.
please take this class with anyone else I beg of you
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I personally find it a problem when students express having to use his ChatGPT model or extensive online videos to solve even one homework problem because Ying does not explain well enough to tackle his problems, which are almost always outside of the reach of what he "taught" in class
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: chill guy but genuinely don't know what he expects. He teaches the basics of every concept, and the textbook doesn't do much better, and his homework problem sets ask you to apply the basics in almost unimaginable ways. Not good at preparing students conceptually to tackle this class, which is seen in the failing score median of the last quiz

i had wu for phys121 and it was okay. i am no longer okay. he is so unbelievably unclear and it's hard to understand what we're even supposed to know because he spends half the time throwing derivations and extra knowledge at us. the quizzes go outside of the scope of the material taught that week. it's stressful and frustrating. this is atrocious.

Uncaring, conceited professor who tests completely unlike how he teaches. He expects you to understand all of his often confusing, winding lectures and notes, sets no real expectations, and gives no clear guidance, making quizzes and exams far harder than they need to be. AVOID AT ALL COSTS!

Prof. Wu is really nice/funny, but this class ruined my semester. Lectures were often unclear; course content was pulled directly from 141. Weekly quizzes were fairly difficult. Once I cried during office hours. The class is uncurved but has a few extra credit opportunities via attendance/dropped quizzes. The homework is almost impossible w/o help.

If you have the time, take this class. Prof. Wu is funny, caring, forgiving, but not a great lecturer. Skip class, do the assignments, go to office hours, do practice tests, and you will succeed. This class is incredibly time intensive but far from impossible. Wu is disliked for the workload but he is the best you can do for PHY121.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Wu is a nice guy, but he is a really awful lecturer whose tests are not reflective of the course content. We had weekly quizzes and homeworks that took up a lot of time, and you basically had to rely on TAs or online resources to do well in his class, so you needed a lot of free time to access these resources. Take this class with someone else

121 is very doable if you have a physics background (taken physics in high school). Many students expected it to be easier than 141 and were blindsided when this was not the case. Exams and quizzes are fair, but HW takes a lot of time. Dr. Wu provides so much extra credit and drops that most people will easily finish with a good grade.

Not THAT bad, but def not good. Really bad lectures, but I always felt like the tests and quizzes were manageable. Gave a decent amount of extra credit and extra drops to ensure the class wasn't tanked. Not an easier class than 141, rly not different IMHO

No capability in lecturing YouTube videos will help more. When exam averages are low blames it on student attendance/math skills not his own fault. uses old 141 content even though class is 121 and meant for people with no calc background. i took multi and physics in high school but still found this hard. his teaching worse than my hs phys teacher.

exam averages were very low, but with extra credit/lab/hw, the final grade distribution is pretty normal. However, this class is a LOT of work!!! If you, like myself, aren't naturally good at physics, you'll likely spend hrs and hrs outside of class every week to learn material. Learned a lot but was a pretty demoralizing experience for me
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Lectures were very difficult to follow and were not helpful in learning the material. I taught myself this class every Thursday night before our weekly quiz. The concepts were not explained clearly; instead, we were taught to simply memorize formulas without understanding much of their significance.

Dr. Wu is a nice person, but this class is not beginner-friendly even though it is advertised to be. Even the TAs say each lecture is treated as a review rather than teaching concepts. I went to every class and was still confused. The only way to do well is to dedicate several hours to help room + practice problems and teach yourself the content.

I just finished this course and it was very difficult. I spoke with him privately, had my own tutor, and made to all the help rooms I could and that was not enough. There is a lot of work that's for sure, and while physics is a dodduclt course, I found tha

Dr. Wu is an amazing professor who genuinely wants all of his students to succeed. Super caring, friendly, and understands that physics is a difficult course. Extremely responsive to emails, on forums, and is available in helproom. He designs this course so that effort translates into success. If I can get an A, then anyone can!

121 is a class full of premeds who aren't used to intense math or physics classes. Certainly a challenging class, but reasonable, and contrary to what some say, Wu does give quite a bit of extra credit (+5-10% on each quiz, MANY drops, and +3% to the overall grade). Difficult, but doable, especially if you go to helprooms and stay on top of the hw.

Lectures are incredibly confusing and hard to follow to the point where my notes are hardly helpful because there are barely any words and only derivations! Not useful for someone who doesn't think in terms of formulas. Does not communicate big picture ideas well, which was reflected by half of the class failing the "concept-focused" third midterm.

Professor Wu does not care about his student's grades in his course. The test average for this class gets lower with every midterm, and he is unwilling to change anything part of the course structure. He is firmly against providing formula sheets or even a practice final. Honestly good luck if you have to take physics with him.
I took 121, not 141. An unreasonably difficult class with exam averages in the C-D range. I really don't know what advice to give other than to pray and do all the extra credit opportunities.

Prof. Wu is nice and genuinely tries to help but 121 is a lot. 121 was advertised as a class specifically for pre-health students (who only need algebra-based physics anyway) but is basically 141. Quizzes are weekly and nearly always difficult, there are 4 graded assignments each week, lecture is often confusing. It is so overwhelming

I actually took the 121 class that is meant for Trinity/pre-health students and it is the exact same as the 141 class and when the students were giving negative feedback his response was that he refuses to teach high school physics. Every quiz was ridiculously hard. The homeworks are much more difficult than anything he teaches in lecture.

Great professor, very clear grading criteria and well-structured lessons. Weekly quizzes can be slightly stressful but really help you keep up with the course content. Professor Wu is a genuinely caring person and gives lots of extra credit. Overall, he really strikes the perfect balance between achieving educational outcomes and reducing stress.

Dr. Wu is a great professor who's very invested in his students' success. Although the course itself is challenging, his lectures are very organized & digestible. If you have any questions, he is always accessible and happy to help. He's one of the most supportive and kind professors I have had, and I would recommend his physics class to everyone!

Professor Wu is a great teacher - he wants you to succeed and provides the resources to do so. He (and his team) are very accessible outside of class, but be prepared to put in a LOT of time and work. Duke physics is manageable as long as you put lots of time into it - expect this class to be your priority.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He's funny and kind, but his class is not. Hardest class I've taken as a premed. Yes, you learn SO much, but is it worth the time and effort? Idk. Very high workload with weekly quizzes and HW. The HW is also so hard that you can't start without help. Thankfully, quizzes, midterms, and final aren't weighted a lot, so there's lots of grade bumpers

Wu was overall a good professor, he made sure we had all the knowledge we needed to succeed. It is very possible to do well in Wu's class specifically, he gives some extra credit and quiz drops. Expect to dedicate A TON of time to physics outside of class (helproom, homework, studying, etc.), Duke physics is HARD.

Take physics with Wu if possible! Wu's lectures are not always the most clear (aka he sometiems assumes that students have a baseline level of knowledge), but LOTS of help available from Wu and the TAs. Usually need to go to help room to complete HW. Grade is calculated based on a lot of assignments, so tests are lower stress and fair.
Very nice professor who gives good lectures, but sometimes the textbook explained better. So much extra credit and he motivated students to try their best.

Dr. Wu is a nice, charismatic professor, but frankly, he is not a very good lecturer. This class is advertised as an intro course, yet if you have not taken any physics in high school, you are absolutely screwed. If you don't have a strong background in physics, save yourself the suffering and take this class anywhere else but Duke.

Significant extra credit, accessible in helproom, kind and smart man. Dr. Wu genuinely wants you to succeed, which is reflected in the grading policies (drops, final can replace midterm). Do be prepared to spend >3 hours in helproom each week, but don't be scared to take phys at duke if it's with Dr. Wu because it's hard but not a guaranteed C.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Wu is super organized and fair. He teaches concepts well and develops your problem solving skills. The homework is pretty challenging and there's a quiz every week during discussion, but it prepares you well for exams. Please go to help rooms!!! These are basically group hw/study sessions- you'll need these to finish the hw.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Team-based learning class made it much more fun. Approach to teaching is very top-down: weekly quizzes and homeworks to refresh material again and again. Lectures were mostly clear although did not answer questions very well (thankfully, there are office hours). Ultimately very caring and many opportunities to boost your score.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Wu is one of the best in the physics department. Cuz the rest suck. He gave us all extra credit and an extra dropped quiz. The hw and quizzes and tests are HARD and I went to lots of help room sessions but I got an A so you can too. Only issue is that he can be hard to understand and doesn't slow down during lectures.

Wu's class is not that difficult, but best if you put in the time every week to learn the material. I did take AP Physics C in high school and that knowledge was pretty useful and made it easier. Do not freak out when he says the class has "no curve" because there are many free points to balance out your grade (a pseudo curve) and it is very fair.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Wu is not only so smart but he also is great at explaining things for those that are confused. GO TO OFFICE HOURS! The class is a lot of work, but Dr. Wu is there to help you succeed. We got bonus points for doing surveys and attendance. If you put in the time you can get a good grade.

This class challenging because the workload is really high. Between the sunday quiz, the problem set, the friday quiz, and exams, you will probably feel like you're doing physics alllll the time. That being said, Professor Wu is an incredibly kind person. He wants his students to succeed, and there are a lot of safety nets to help your grade.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS IF YOU HAVE NEVER TAKEN PHYSICS BEFORE! I really wish I took "intro physics" at NC central (an easy process: look up Interinstitutional credit). Med schools do not care if it's calc based... An average week includes: 30-60 pages of textbook reading, Sunday quiz, class problems we don't get to, Homework packet, Friday quiz.

course is overkill. every positive review is accurate, but ultimately this course is unnecessarily difficult and time consuming, regardless of how helpful Wu is outside class. This course is a part-time job, and as a premed you are better off taking Phy141 somewhere else and using saved time for ECs. False ad too, this is not a real *intro* class

Wu truly is a good guy. His teaching style can be hard to follow, but only occasionally. He wants his students to succeed, HW is meant to help u do better on quizzes. Weekly quizzes are easier, exams are tough. Many things bring up your grade (bonus points, dropped quizzes, Lab etc). PHYS141 with Wu is a good option at DUke.

Professor Wu genuinely cares about students. He is always there to help, frequently staying late at helprooms to answer our questions, and usually responding to Piazza questions within minutes. This class is difficult, but having friends in the class and knowing that everyone wanted me to succeed helped me stay motivated and keep working hard

I came into this class with no AP Physics background, and Dr. Wu structured it really well. Active learning beats lecture, weekly quizzes prevent procrastination, and helprooms saved me. You have to WORK, but Wu cares for you a lot. 

No curve but can drop your lowest midterm/two quizzes. No calculus on quizzes/tests, which are easier than HW.

Ying my boy fr. This guy really cares about his students learning the topics of mechanical physics, and he is incredibly knowledgeable. Gets unnecessary flack for being difficult, but if you take the time to go to office hours and work with other students on the homework, you'll be just fine.

Despite the rigor of this class, Dr. Wu does truly care about his students. The effort he puts into helping his students outside of class in help room is really admirable. He also provides many opportunities to practice problems in and out of class. Just make sure to really spend time on homeworks and problems.

Dr. Wu truly cares about his students. The rigid class structure helps students master all of the topics efficiently, but it is a lot to complete. The helprooms were very useful. Dr. Wu makes himself very available to help everyone. The drops on assignments were also a lifesaver. Class assignments prepared me well for assessments, which are easier.

Get ready to teach yourself physics because Dr. Wu is incomprehensible. Physics is already a hard subject as is, but to have a professor who is unable to explain concepts and makes critical mistakes that further complicate your understanding makes it even worse. Homework and lab will be your saving grace against the exams, so do at least that much.
Terrible at teaching- avoid at absolutely all costs. Everything I know in this class comes from the textbook and Youtube.

wu tries his best but this class sucks a lot (lots of hard hwk, quizzes every week). be prepared to work hard and teach yourself a lot of the material, especially if you dont have a highschool physics background. the class is uncurved but he does give extra credit which helps a lot!

Prof. Wu is super nice, but he doesnt know how to teach. If you didnt take AP Physics in HS, be prepared to STRUGGLE. Prof. Wu tries his best to ensure every student succeeds. However, you can do the reading and pay attention and study all you want, this class is hard and that does not mean youll do well. Good luck.

Professor Wu is a nice man who cares about his students. His lecture notes are extremely well written and organized so I was able to get away with not attending class. The class is uncurved but with lab and homework grades your grade is only in mild danger. Definitely finish the homework (which is harder than the exams) before the weekly quizzes!

Physics is not easy but Professor Wu makes such an effort to ensure his students understand the class. His teaching style is helpful because he provides many opportunities for graded work, and each one helps the students understand the concepts better. The class is definitely very hard, but Professor Wu helps make learning physics more enjoyable.

Phys141 is def not an easy class, but Prof Wu clearly cares very deeply about his students. He's very accessible via email or Piazza, and organizes extra office hours to help his students. He's not the best lecturer, but his quizzes and tests don't have any surprises. If you need to take this class, Prof Wu is as good a professor as any.

Hands down the hardest class (besides physics 142) I've ever taken. Physics with prof. Wu made Orgo feel EASY. Hard to understand (not his fault I guess). He does provide you with class notes, which are helpful. During office hours, it felt like TAs were looking at material for the first time. Extremely difficult. NO CLUE how I got an A. Luck.

This class is a NIGHTMARE. Weekly quizzes are uncurved and the averages sit from 60-75. TAs are not good, graders are incredibly condescending and disrespectful. Wu teaches basics then expects us to be able to know difficult questions and skips steps in class while explaining questions.

Prof Wu was one of the best professors I've had at Duke. This is not an easy course, but he provides many resources for you to succeed and drops several assignments. He is extremely caring and supportive of all his students. I was not looking forward to this class, but Prof Wu definitely made it enjoyable.

During COVID, Dr Wu was really helpful, considerate, and supportive of his students. He isn't a great lecturer though; he goes very and can't explain to those who don't understand- only repeat what he said. Despite this, there are several office hours with multiple different people every week, so you'll find someone with whom you click. HW is hard.

Dr. Wu has been so supportive of students during this COVID semester. He dropped extra assignments and quizzes and also offered extra credit to make up for the issues people were having with the online platform. His lecturers were slightly overwhelming but the notes he posted afterwards were invaluable and made much more sense than the textbook.

Ying Wu is an amazing lecturer and SO caring. He has a somewhat flipped class -- he expects you to do the textbook readings before lecture. I personally didn't really read the textbook or prepare before lectures, and I was fine. Homework sets + quiz every week, but he allows for 3 quizzes to be dropped. Exams have bonus points that you can earn.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Ying Wu was the worst professor I ever had at duke. I am a strong math student and could not keep up with this class. If you ask a question in class, for example "why did you do ----" he simply responds by repeating himself procedurally, not conceptually. It seems like he has no ability to explain concepts. He moves so fast in his lectures.

I cannot say enough bad things about this course! Dr. Wu seems to prioritize making the class hard just for the sake of making it hard over student's actual learning. He is a poor lecturer and struggles to explain concepts in a logical way. You'll study for hours a week, feel as though you understand the material and still do miserably. Ridiculous

I have never put in more work for a class than I have for Physics 142. Beware it is semi-flipped! Prof Wu really knows his stuff and wants every student to succeed. That being said he is tough and let the class as a whole know when we were doing poorly. Take this class if you do well working in groups.

Dr. Wu expects students to devote 8-10 hours a week on his class, and if you're don't work up to his class, he'll tell you about how bad you are. He doesn't make concepts very clear, but he is devoted to help his students. This is definitely a class you have to clear your schedule for, and where your effort and time put in reflects your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: This class is a lot of work, but your grade will 100% reflect the amount of effort you put into it. Dr. Wu is always there for you, and will go out of his way to help you! He also pays attention to how much effort you put into the class, so just work hard, do all the problem sets, and you'll do fine! (this coming from someone who hates physics)
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Ying Wu was a phenomenal teacher. The requirements to do well in the class are outlined on the first day and if you use help room often you should do well. It also helps if you familiarize yourself with calculus a bit

Dr. Wu is always there for you at literally all times of the day. Any time you have a question on piazza, he will answer it. The class is not easy, but manageable if you stay on top of the readings and pay attention in the class. Dr. Wu also wants every student to succeed so he is always looking for ways to help students bump up their grades.

Dr. Wu is one of the most invested and committed professors I have had. This class was hard, but he and the other instructors were available for ours each week in help room.  The course structure also allowed for many chances to improve your grade. You can succeed in this classjust be sure to work hard each week and really understand assignments.

Dr. Wu is one of the most brilliant people you will meet. Unfortunately, he's also one of the worst lecturers at Duke. His flipped classroom setting just does NOT work with E&M. More than that, the few minutes he does attempt to lecture are mostly confusing derivations that hurt more than they help. Absolutely DO NOT recommend.

Dr. Wu (and Dr. Brown as well) honestly and truly want all of his students to do well. I bombed my first exam, met with Wu right after and he really helped me turn it around and I ended up with a solid B. Homework is long and difficult, but will 100% prepare you for the exams. And they let you drop your lowest quiz, homework, lab grades!

By far the most difficult class I've take so far, but Dr. Wu (and Dr. Brown) held a lot of help rooms and were always willing to stick around and help you learn.  Thick accent but you learn to get past it.

Wu is the sweetest little man. Cares about his students, wants them to do well. Strong asian accent but you can get used to it. Difficulty of the subject matter made this course very hard and time consuming but Wu tried his best to help where he could.
Dr. Welsh is super nice! Gave great feedback and answered any questions thoroughly, even outside of class. Would take again.

I had Dr. Welsh for Preventing Pandemics. She's great! She really cares about her students and helping them learn to write. She is always available for questions or to review your writing. She teaches at a very introductory level, so don't worry if your writing skills aren't great.
Unaccommodating with arbitrary grading.

Class is generally quite boring unless you have a genuine interest in the material. Even if you meet with her, you can still do poorly.  Class grade is based on only 4 total assignments, so success on ALL of them is necessary. Do not take unless you really want to do science/evidence based writing. Very rigid rubrics and not flexible.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Super sweet prof, she's genuinely just a great person and really easy to get along with. Only thing is the class just involves a ton of reading, since she assigns around two papers after each class. The grading criteria for the writing assignments can also be a little harsh sometimes, but overall the class was pretty interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Best professor at Duke!! Dr. Welsh is so nice and other people who complain about her on this page are just on a high horse and doesn't ask for help. She is so accessible outside of class so please, please revise your writing with her and you will do absolutely fine
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Tough grader

Dr. Welsh is a caring professor who makes herself available to students outside of class. Doing well on most papers is critical to earning an A, as there are few graded assignments. Her grading criteria for papers are also unclear, so I highly recommend you have her read over it before the deadline (even if you consider yourself a skilled writer).

Dr. Welsh is amazing! The class content is so interesting and she is always willing to meet with you outside of class to help you edit your paper or answer any questions. It is totally possible to do well in this class if you meet with her and try your best!

Such a sweet and kind professor. However, grading criteria wasn't exactly clear and if you don't do well on every paper your grade is tanked. She is a tough grader! You have to go to office hours and have her edit your paper to do even remotely well. Interesting content matter though... just wish it didn't ruin my GPA.

She's very nice!! I loved her. There are like 3 individual papers that weren't hard to write. She's pretty easy grader and if you're not the best writer just go to her office hours. She's the type to actually help instead of wasting your time. The final was a group project, you'll do well if you write it early and ask her for help in editing.
Dr. Welsh is the nicest most amazing professor I have ever had! She is an absolute angel and just the sweetest professor I have ever had. She is caring and compassionate and cares about her students

she's a cutie. she very nice and the class is chill. she provided great feedback and made everything clear. there were two summary essays about 200-300 words, 1 analysis essay 500-600 words and then the final was a group project in which she assists throughout the whole process. if you put in the work you'll be fine.
She makes Preventing Pandemics one of the best Writing 101s to take. Very chill, class is paced well, and she's always there to help

Preventing Pandemics was an amazing W101! Very light workload compared to other W101s, and is about a somewhat-interesting topic. Dr. Welsh is so sweet, cares about her students, and is accessible outside of class. Only 3 short essays (300 and 600 words) and a final group research paper. You are guided completely through the final paper.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Welsh is very passionate about this class and is very accessible if you take advantage of the materials she provides. She has clear grading criteria and if you meet with her outside of class, she will help your papers immensely. Preventing Pandemics was an interesting class, but very based mainly on readings and not a lot of discussion.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Welsh is super nice and spends a lot of time giving detailed feedback on all of your papers. This class is an easy A and by far one of the easiest writing 101 classes. If you aren't interested in the topic, in-class is pretty boring. This class focuses on learning how to read an write academic papers
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Definitely take this class if you're interested in the subject matter. Compared to a lot of other Writing 101 classes, the workload for this one is very low and Dr. Welsh is a very nice and easy grader. Even though your grade is only based on a few things, you get a lot of time to do your assignments. Do the readings and assignments!
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
She is sweet and wants you to do well. She gives great feedback; if you put in any effort, you should get an A. I did learn a lot about pandemics and stuff even though I don't really care about them. 

Take her if you want to learn how to write but not lose your sense of self and joy.

I love Dr. Welsh. Took Preventing Pandemics w/ her and it was an easy A. Honestly, I sometimes forget that I'm taking her class b/c the workload is so low. Only writing assignments were 3 essays and one big group paper. The group paper is structured so that your grade isn't entirely dependent on your group, so you won't fail if your group sucks.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Preventing Pandemics had extremely clear, fair, and simple rubrics. You will only write the equivalent of 9 pages throughout the entire semester. Two of four total assignments are simply writing a summary of an article. Minimal homework. My only complaint is that class itself is boring and you lose 5% off your final grade for every class you miss.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Took Preventing Pandemics with her this semester. From what I can tell, she's a pretty easy grader and she gives a lot of really good feedback. Also, for every paper there are revision steps to make sure you're turning in the best work. She really cares about our learning and success and made the topic of the class really interesting too.

Took the ecology of disease in spring 2018. It was difficult to engage with the scientific literature at first, and it would've been helpful for her cover strategies to better approach such materials. She had some really fantastic editing and writing advice that I still use today. Reverse outlining is particularly helpful, even now.

Amazing class with a light amount of work. The final paper is teamwork, which makes it a lot easier to write. Just make sure to "show" that you care. You get an A. The topics are kind of boring, but it's an easy writing 101, so make sure you take it.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Welsh is THE writing 101 teacher to have. Three main writing assignments with a generous timeline & multiple revision stages to ensure you turn in a great piece of work. Feedback is insanely detailed & helpful. She also deeply cares for her students by always being available for guidance/resources.

Not a lot of reading or writing for a Writing 101 class, but very interesting topics and she always gives a good selection of papers that are interesting to read. Very clear in how she grades and gives insanely detailed feedback
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Welsh is super nice and very accessible outside the classroom. She will provide much help if you need. The workload of the class is not heavy. Just follow her guidance and you will get an easy A. (If you don't pay efforts, then that's another story.)
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Welsh is a really great choice for Writing 101. She takes the time to give good feedback on all papers and is willing to meet individually if you need extra help. It is also clear that her grading system reflects the amount of effort you put in, so if you make the time to thoroughly work through each assignment, this class should be an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Group projects

reviews.comment: Dr. Welsh is very sweet and fair and great at teaching. For our final project she spent about 3 hours on grading each essay (not because she's a "harsh" grader but because she wants to give helpful feedback) as she truly wants us to become better writers. Gonna miss this class and the classmates I had!! Also the end of semester project was fun!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: I loved this class. Professor Welsh made writing (about disease ecology) so interesting! The grading criteria is very clear. Just make sure to stay on top of the work, and the class should be VERY manageable. If you ever need help, Dr. Welsh is very willing to accommodate you. I HIGHLY recommend this class & Dr. Welsh.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Welsh is a really great professor. Her turn-around for grading is fast and she always offers in-depth feedback. Shes helpful and understandin-- all-around a great writing professor. The exercises may not have always been the most exciting, but one can immediately understand how it functions to make someone a better writer.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Welsh was very clear on everything and had the whole class organized very well. Compared to other Writing 101s, there was not that much work or reading. She really cares about her students. Also, the final paper is due about a week earlier than when the final work for other classes start, which is really nice.

Biji is an unfortunate case where she's a fine professor, but fails to reach the curriculum effectively. This class is completely based on Clark's content, which she barely covers. Her pacing is quite bad, and we skimmed over the two hardest units (line/surface integrals). I would avoid taking her, just take Clark.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very good teacher for those that have a firm grasp in mathematics. I just read through some of the reviews and can attest to the mumbling but a lot of male teachers do the same. Very clear teaching style and test heavy. Not the most talkative but does give you her time if needed.

Biji Wong is genuinely the worst teacher/professor I've ever had. Ever. On the first day of class, she explained middle school-level topics SO BAD that she had students struggling to calculate the slope of a LINEAR LINE (y=mx+b). I wish there was at least some upside to taking MATH 219 with her but there just isn't. STEER CLEAR AT ALL COSTS!!!!!!!!

Dr Biji is a great teacher that is fair as well as goes out of her way to make herself assessable. She great at providing extra assistance when you're struggling with a particular area. Would definitely take any course she is lecturing.
She is a very thorough and is very into the work.  A very good teacher who is patient with those that have a harder time grasping the subject.

She can't get a sentence out without stumbling over her words multiple times, she talks at the board, and she goes so slowly over the simple examples that it really is impossible to pay attention in class. The saving grace of this class was how easy she made the tests. Do not take this class if you want to be taught multivariable calculus.

Biji's lecture doesn't teach the thinking logics and mathematical intuition behind the plain lecturing. Lecture is really boring. She gets irritated as time goes by, and there are times where she has no clue what she's talking about either. Get ready to do your own study by YT.
DO NOT TAKE HER CLASS! I repeat, DO NOT TAKE HER CLASS!

It is not easy to teach a course where the lead instructor has already set a rigid format. Nonetheless, Dr. Wong did a great job keeping pace with the curriculum, was always willing to talk through problems after class, and was genuinely a nice person. Supplementing her lectures with book readings will make you appreciate the wonders of multi.

Don't get me wrong, professor Wong isn't intentionally making the course hard or malicious in any ways, she just simply doesn't know how to teach. Not a great lecturer, but kind and is willing to spend time outside of class to help. Her tests are also slightly easier than the other professors'.
305 is manageable with preparation in advance. Overall quality of the course is great
Nice but hard course to take, you will definitely learn a lot. Go to his office hour.

MATH 305 is very hard in general. But prof. Shixin is a fantastic lecturer on linear transformation, operators, SVD, and related topics. The exams are difficult but the process of learning mathematics feels rewarding and intellectual stimulating.
Very accessible outside the class. Be willing to give chance/extra bonus to students who did not perform well in midterm. But may not curve. Anyway, he is a nice guy. But linear algebra is very hard.
This professor is very good, really kind and friendly. At the same time, he will try his best to give everyone a high score, as long as you carefully write homework and exams.
He is open to help you if you are struggling with math. He also understands your concern about grades and would offer extra credit to the class.

Prof. Xu is very friendly and open for communication. I've stopped by his office with completely random math questions, and we talked for 2 hours straight. He respects your solution if it is correct, even if you do not use his way. Also, he used to bring us candy in every class. Extra credit is for latex submission and attendance.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Well, the class itself is relatively easier than any other 200level math class. However, every two weeks there is a quiz. Forget about partial credit; even if your solution is mostly correct, and u made a little error with the final answer, u will get 0 for this problem. Take it at Duke, save your gpa.
The lectures are okay, but the weekly quizzes suck a lot. Also, no partial point, no grades, and round down policy. The jokes he makes also make zero sense.

His humor is strange and oftentimes uncomfortable as an international student. If you've taken Feng Tian, he isn't any better. His quizzes are graded harshly, making it very difficult to get full marks. Lectures are att. mandatory but reading the textbook is better, and finding class materials on ed is annoying and confusing. Pls take another prof!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He is a stubborn demon. Haven't seen anyone who put "92.99=92=A-" into syllabus. 1 quiz per week and a final which makes students suffer a lot. And, have to come to the lecture and ask/answer questions to get participation points. And he set each question 1 point so that he can deduct all of it if you make a tiny mistake. Please go back to Canada.
Good as a lecturer. Humorous teaching style and funny lecture.

He is definitely a good professor who really want to teach better. I can feel that he has been trying to make all of us understand the lectures. But, really a tough grader. His grade only depends on tons of quizzes(one per week and a final. Completely no curve and even no partial points. If you make one mistake, your final grade will reduce a level
The quizzes were kind of difficult and no curve was offered
His lectures are great, but it is hard to get high scores in quizzes and exams (btw final grade only depend on quizzes and exams). Very caring. King of hell jokes.

One of the best math professors. He tries to make the content as clear as possible so that every single student is able to master the content fully. He allows you to improve in the class by offering multiple opportunities for retakes. His main goal is to make sure that everyone learns and engages in lectures. Highly recommended!

He is a guy who makes jokes even under very serious conditions. For example, if you suffer from fear of getting an F, he will joke that we will randomly pick a student to get an F, and guess who will that student be?
T/F exam and pset format, 3 midterms, no final exam

Dr. Willis is passionate but lectures were a bit too dense and content isn't particularly interesting. The T/F structure was fine and made assignments/exams much more doable. Labs seemed unnecessary and didn't add much to the learning experience. Not a hard class by any means but not an interesting one either

He is really passionate about the material and is pretty funny which is nice. Although his lectures are kind of disorganized and I learned better if I went over the lectures on my own time and did other work during class. Grading is very fair and is made clear at the start of the semester. chill class if you study a bit before midterms

Loved Dr. Willis' lectures! The content itself is not too hard/complex but he connects it to a lot of interesting real-world applications and examples, which was the highlight of the course for me. Super funny, super enthusiastic professor. Everything is in the slides (no textbook), which I liked as it's very clear exactly what you need to know.

All the midterms and quizzes are T/F format which took a while for me to get used to. But overall, Willis is super engaging and makes contents that could be boring to something fun. Just make sure you stay on top of the lecture recordings.

Super enthusiastic lecturer. Almost everything you do in Bio202 will be true/false questions, and I don't remember any questions where the correct answer isn't deducible/clear. If you do well on HWs, you should be getting an A. (Fine to skip lectures here and there; reading through the slides takes less time and was good enough prep for me).
If you did well on the AP Bio exam in highschool, this class will be free. Also feel like I learned a lot of interesting content. Professor Willis is super entertaining.

Great professor - lectures were clear and upbeat. Everything (individual & group problem sets, labs, exams) is true/false and there was no final exam. Showing up to lecture is not super important for learning the content, and lectures could be slow, but overall learned a lot, enjoyed, would take again

Willis is a very upbeat, passionate professor but at times the lectures could be boring and unnecessarily long. The labs and groups psets are team based but not overly difficult. There's minimal work outside of class, which is a huge plus. It's not hard to get an A if you simply study the slides and psets. Overall it's a decently easy intro course.

Great dude, his teaching style just did not do it for me. All exams are true or false and they take no refuting any questions even when there are valid regrades. Not a bad course but I have a fundamental issue with the course formatting. There's a lot of group work -- if you have a good group you are find but if you don't you are a little screwed.

Dr. Willis has a ton of energy in lecture, which is helpful for a subject I don't find particularly energizing. He is super passionate about his field, sometimes to the detriment of the class, since he might go off on a tangent occasionally or move too quickly. I didn't enjoy the class very much, but I definitely enjoyed Dr. Willis lol.

Great intro class, highly recommend for freshman. Willis is energetic and passionate which makes all the difference. Lots of individual/group quizzes force you to keep up but exams are easier. Very forgiving grading criteria includes many drops and opportunities to improve. All q's are true/false so easy to do well.

Great guy, very enthusiastic, real world examples are helpful. You can do well without going to lecture, but his lectures are great. If you were good at AP Bio this will be cash. Just put in effort and dont wait until the last minute to review

Course is very well organized and easy to follow. Slides are so informative that you don't even need to attend lecture, but definitely should. Graded based on many quizzes/assignments/discussions so tests don't determine your grade. Many grades also get dropped. Need to do the work, but overall easy.

Dr. Willis is an awesome professor and human! He's super funny, friendly, and very passionate about his field. The biggest downside of this class was that the TAs treat the students worse than high schoolers and don't allow for freedom in labs.

John Willis is so passionate about what he does, and that's very clear by the way he lectures. However, the teaching team treats students like high schoolers and is often condescending. The entire class is true or false, and assignments and tests are written with the clear intent to trick students. Not a hard class, but an annoying one.

John Willis clearly loves his job, he is very jolly and loves to teach. His class isn't too bad, study for the exams by looking over all of the lectures and redoing practice problems. Student hours are very helpful! Don't go to lecture, you'll get more out of watching them on 2x speed. Sometimes test questions have confusing wording.

John is such a fun little guy. He is clearly enthusiastic about what he teaches, even though lectures are very boring. Midterms are 80 questions all T/F, which is a little weird but as long as you watch all the recorded lectures the week before the test you'll be fine. Content is kinda interesting.

Willis was so great! He is such a funny guy and made lectures so engaging. Good mixture of concrete concepts & fun examples in lecture. He sometimes goes off topic which makes it easy to zone out, but if you dedicate time to reviewing lecture slides after class you'll be able to understand the content. Great class if you like learning about animals

The grade for this class is based solely on your exams. The lectures were boring and you could do well without attending. The exams are made to be hard since the class was fairly easy, but the exams are material you could truly study for.

Willis is an energetic, motivated teacher who clearly is passionate about BIO202 --- this makes lectures more enjoyable (although many are skippable and you can work off the slides). Labs are tedious but relatively straightforward, and grades come from a mix of psets/online labs/tests. Workload is low but tests require decent studying to do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Aggravating class, to say the least. Teaching team genuinely doesn't want you to do well and NEVER answer questions. EVER. Whole class is T/F and wording is horrible. Willis seems excited during lectures, but then you ask a question during pSets and he is dismissive and unhelpful. iPsets due Sat nights/labs 2.5 hrs and they baby you/waste time.

Professor Willis is very humorous and extremely passionate about the course--this made lectures very engaging, personally. Although the content felt very new challenging at first, it got better once I started to go over it. Plus, all graded material (like tests) are only T/F questions, so grades come out better than expected imo.

Willis undeniable/infectious care for content is great. However, this class' teaching team is unsupportive at best, damaging at worst. They do not take requests seriously, nor do they answer questions. They also do not address floating pset answer keys that skew class performance. Frustrating class with clear structural issues, but fun lectures.

Dr Willis is a really nice, but his lecturing style does not work for me or many other students. There were only 3 tests (non-cumulative) and lecture attendance is not required. He records his lectures so just watch all before the tests in 2x speed. He speaks really slow and goes off on tangents which is boring if you are actually in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professors care deeply about this course. They are accessible outside of class and take the time to answer all student questions before/after lecture.

Dr. Willis is an amazing teacher and is very passionate about bio. However, he gets into too much detail during the lecture and the slides are very dense with material that won't be on the exams. The class is 45% exams and no final, and the content is pretty interesting. Just go to lecture/watch the recordings and you should be fine on the tests.

Prof. Willis is hilarious and does his best to make lecture engaging. However, this class has made me question whether I actually like bio/if I should switch majors. The content covered in lecture isn't hard, but the wording on exams/psets is so confusing that it makes the class unnecessarily difficult. No textbook; true/false exams; no curve

Willis is an enthusiastic lecturer, but lectures are tough to follow because he ends up rambling about a slide/topic for 5-10 minutes. The content is relatively intuitive but p-set questions are not. It feels like they are designed to test your reading comprehension -- one word will change your answer or the question will lack specificity.

I disliked this course with a passion. The content was quite interesting however the way it was taught is not conducive to learning. I stopped attending lecture, and did not watch the videos (rather just read the slides) because the way he lectures is confusing. Do all your work and you can succeed just boring class.

This class is easy and interesting if you go to lecture!!! I only missed one or two, and I aced all of the tests. The majority of the grading is from group and individual assignments, as well as labs. Participate in lab, and the class will go smoothly.

Willis was a very engaging and funny lecturer, but it felt like the group and indiv p-sets + tests had no correlation and overcomplicated what we were being taught in class. Definitely work hard to do well on labs since they account for the biggest part of your grade. The tests are deceptive even though they are open note, don't underestimate them.

Willis tries to make the somewhat-boring material as entertaining as possible, but he and the TAs are not accessible outside of class. The weekly individual & group problem sets, and tests, do not often address the material that we cover in lecture. Still, the subject material gets progressively easier, and it is definitely possible to get an A.

Bio 202 was such a fun course. Midterms are a smaller portion of your grade than in other bio classes, which means your performance on weekly individual and group problem sets matters a ton. Lab experiences vary heavily, but lectures are always engaging and relevant.

Willis is a great/enthusiastic professor but super unavailable and the TAs aren't great. Like everyone has said, the content is easy but the exams are ridiculous, super confusing for no reason. Weekly group problem sets, individual problem sets, labs, etc. I stopped going to lecture and it didn't affect anything

Content for this class is very easy. BUT, the psets and exams do not feel like they test your content knowledge, but rather whether you can read. Questions are vague and confusing and TAs do not make them any less confusing. Stopped showing up to lecture and it did not make a difference whatsoever. John is hilarious though and obsessed with bees!!

Wasn't expecting this to be a stressful class, it's just that the exams/problem sets/lab try to trick you w/ wording, and most of the TAs refuse to answer wording questions. The exams are also so long and there's no textbook. John is a really sweet guy though and is really enthusiastic about lecturing. Exams also only make up 45% of the grade.

Dr. Willis is nice and tries to keep the class interesting, but I'd be lying if I said I didn't zone out nearly every class. He's also not accessible outside of class, and the TA's, though friendly, aren't that useful. The material seems really easy to understand, but the tests are hard. They're open note but notes never helped me.

Willis is great. However, TAs know ABSOLUTELY NOTHING about the material. NOTHING. Willis doesn't have OH so you are stuck with a bunch of grad students who study something totally unrelated to genetics. No correlation whatsoever between lectures and exams/problem sets. Seems like they want to make this a pre-med weed-out class (wannabe orgo/phys)

He's a good professor; always behind schedule but very enthusiastic. So don't want to rate too bad. Absolutely AWFUL class tho. Doesn't matter how well you actually know the information/theory because the exams are just reading comprehension and trick questions. The content is super easy, but it's like they're trying to make it a weed-out class

Kind guy who puts some of the childhood wonder aspect that has been grinded out of us by exams/quizzes/labs/problem sets back into biology. The final third of the class is SUPER interesting but the first third is SUPER boring. Course is overall easy + enjoyable, and I never had any moment where I really hated it or didn't want to go to class.

John is fine. The class itself is disorganized, unclear in what is expected, you do not get practice problems before tests. Most of the confusion in this class is due to unclear wording rather than concepts, and the TA's won't answer any questions about wording so you're on your own.

Take Bio202 with Willis! I had half the semester online in 2020 and he still managed to keep us engaged and excited about the material. Amazing, funny, interesting, easy. I listened to the other raters and I full agree, just awesome.

He is the most enthusiastic teacher you will ever meet! What a gem! Even though the material may get a little boring, and he goes off on tangents a lot, he really tries to get people engaged and makes sure they understand. If you have to take bio202 you NEED to take it with Willis!!

Willis is a great professor -- he's very excited about what he teaches. Borderline 4 star prof imo but I'm giving him 5 because he kept me engaged in the course material, and I'm not normally super interested in genetics and evolution (I liked the course material of Bio201 more). Willis is very energetic, which I appreciate.

I liked BIO202L with Dr. Willis - it was graded very fairly. I wouldn't say this class is difficult, but it is definitely a time commitment with three lectures and a lab every week. However, I really enjoyed learning about genetics and felt that Willis did a good job. He definitely cares for his students.

Professor Willis is one of the kindest men I have ever met and he teaches his classes with such great energy. You can tell he honestly cares. Biology 202 was super easy, which is a nice break from other hard stem classes. Genetics is pretty straight forward, and he's always available to help if you're confused.
A pretty engaging lecturer but goes a bit slow. Graded on many assignments and all are pretty fair. As long as you keep up with the material and complete all assignments you will do well!

He is enthusiastic - sometimes a bit over the top. There's some attitude of looking-down-their-noses at people who "don't believe in science" (read: people who question their worldview). There's a lot of work that may make you feel a bit overwhelmed.

Bio 201 was fundamental and microscopic and was taught very systematically. Students might think Bio 202 is the less 'academic' one and might not get invested in the material. but Willis' demeanor and energy, even in the pandemic was almost contagious, and softened the learning curve.
I took this class online, and that made it very difficult to stay engaged and attentive. Other than that, this is a pretty solid class, and Willis is an enthusiastic professor.

TAKE THIS CLASS WITH PROF. WILLIS, HE IS THE BEST YOU CAN GET!!!!! he is enthusiastic, clearly passionate about the material, and genuinely cares about his students' success. lectures are thoroughly enjoyable even when he goes on tangents :)

I really liked him as a teacher. If you listen to lectures then you should do well on any of the homework and exams. He seems to really care about his students and their success in his class and is more in tune with the class (how much they understand and when to adjust) than a lot of other professors.

Willis is the prof you want for BIO202, don't take anyone else. He's super passionate about evolution and it honestly made me more excited to learn. There's a group quiz once a week and three midterms over the course of the semester with no final.

Prof. Willis really cares about his students and is really excited about biology. There is a lot of homework (which can be tedious), but it is definitely still manageable. I was not a fan of the ant lab for this course. Willis can sometimes get off-track but does a good job of presenting the material overall!

He is so all over the place and we are constantly behind. Although he is a chill prof and he makes a lot of jokes, it is honestly annoying that he is so slow. We have to teach ourselves most of the biology concepts when we do the problem sets because he doesn't teach efficiently.

While Willis is extremely enthusiastic about biology, sometimes it can be overwhelming and a little extreme. But, he's a really passionate lecturer so lectures aren't that boring. Bio 202 is restructured to give a lot of unnecessary busy work that makes you strongly dislike the class, so overall Willis is good, but the course is not.

Willis is the best professor for 202. The class is easy as long as you pay some attention in lecture and do the problem sets. Lots of things are dropped so nothing is high stakes. Willis is very enthusiastic and very excited about biology, and tries to make the lectures interesting. The lab section of the class was boring but not due to Willis.

Lectures are pretty useless, but there's no textbook, which means the class pretty useless. He's really enthusiastic but spends half the class talking about how exciting what we are learning is and skims over the actual teaching. It's an INSANE amount of work that's kinda useless.

He's the prof you want for Bio 202. It's not hard at all if you do the work and you get to drop multiple lowest scores on assignments, quizzes, etc. Funny and a bit extra but he cares to teach and only tests you on what he covers in class. The exams are just like the in-class quizzes so there are never any surprises.
