honestly the best professor i've had at duke! willis is so enthusiastic about the subject and carries that enthusiasm through to the class. while he spends a lot of time rehearsing material, he makes a lot of jokes & takes time for questions. one thing to note: he doesn't curve or make the tests tricky, he just wants to make sure his students learn

Prof. Willis is the most outwardly excited professor I've had at Duke and keeps lectures engaging. Lectures can feel slow sometimes as concepts are rehashed, but the quizzes and midterms are largely drawn from questions included in the weekly problem sets.

I love him as a person but as a lecturer-well he's certainly enthusiastic. I've literally never met anyone more excited about their field, but he does get side-tracked easily and lectures can be frustratingly slow sometimes. Overall, would recommend.
I loved Dr. Willis! He's a great guy, and I loved his class. If you do well on his quizzes, you'll have yourself a good time in his class.

One of the loveliest people I've ever met! Such a funny professor, I didn't skip a single class because I loved listening to him. Work load is heavy but not hard. There's a ton of support by TA's. Love him :)

John Willis is so nice and has so much energy and really cares about his students. There is a problem set a week and labs are annoying, but not too much work. There is also an in class quiz every week similar to problem sets that is really annoying, but midterms are very similar to the quizzes. As long as you do the problem sets it's an easy A
Great professor--super enthusiastic and really cares for his students. If you put in a reasonable amount of effort getting an A should not be a problem

Dr. Willis is so enthusiastic and knowledgeable.  He cares about his students understanding the material and provides many opportunities to ask for help.  Though the class could be a bit unorganized in terms of staying on schedule, the deviations from the schedule were mainly to focus on hard topics. Overall great, low stress class!

Honestly, I didn't go to lecture as much as I should have, but when I did, they were pretty informative and engaging. Professor Willis is VERY passionate about his subject matter, most of his emails included at least one "omg." Funny guy, willing to work hard for his students and even made grading easier by dropping a test score

I wasn't a huge fan of Professor Willis's Biology 202 class. While he's extremely energetic, the class felt extremely disorganized and often quite inefficient; I didn't feel like I missed much when I missed a lecture. Fortunately, my TA was very helpful, but based on what I've heard, I'd recommend taking with Noor instead. Content was interesting!

Professor Willis is awesome. He's not very interested in grades and more interested in the material and learning. He is SO enthusiastic about what he is teaching and makes the classroom so much fun. Highly recommend taking bio 202 with him!! You will learn a lot and will NOT be stressed at all.

Professor Willis is a very passionate and dynamic guy. He really does love what he does. His class can seem a bit disorganized at times, and you need to study for the tests -- they count for a lot your overall grade. Definitely go to class; powerpoints are hard to understand without lecture. Overall, a fun and enjoyable class.
He's a great teacher! He is excited about what he teaches. If you go slow on the tests and seek help when you need it you will be okay

Bio 202 is pretty manageable material to begin with and Willis is a bro. The lectures are entertaining and although the class tends to fall behind, WIllis only tests on stuff that's been covered. You have to show up to understand some things (the powerpoints themselves won't explain everything) but this is probably the easiest premed class.

The material is not that bad and TAs are helpful, but the way the tests are weighted makes every question you miss count for so much of your average. Lots of unclear wording on tests/ problem sets does a number on your average even if you're doing well in all other parts of the class

Definitely take this class if flipped classes are not for you. Labs are easy and problem sets are based on the class and the lectures and they can be a bit tricky. If you don't go to class you could probably pull off a decent grade, but don't expect to understand everything through the powerpoints. A good professor overall (and no textbook)

Willis is a great guy and very knowledgeable about plants, but probably shouldn't be teaching this class. Lectures are long, boring, and generally confusing. Spends so much time off topic, often gets flustered in front of a crowd and makes mistakes. Very hard to teach yourself without a textbook. Few tests/questions, but everything counts for a lot

Willis is the man. He's hilarious and would go out of his way to help students/hold review sessions. That said, the class was relatively disorganized and some concepts were not explained very well. Overall, though, it was pretty easy and I'd take another of Willis's classes again.

Professor Willis was super excited about the material during lectures, and he held review sessions for his tests. Class itself was easy with exams being based off of problem sets and lectures. You can also submit the problem sets multiple times. Overall easy class with a very nice professor!

Thought I would do well in this class. No textbook, interested in the subject and a professor that seemed funny and nice. All these things were true, but the class was so unorganized that it didn't matter. Learning was hard without clear info and the professor did not respond to my emails asking for help. Loved my TA though.

John is really enthusiastic about biology. He's really knowledgeable but can go a bit off-topic at times. He really tries to get students excited about learning. The tests weren't cumulative, which was awesome. I just wish we had an actual textbook for reference. Maybe it's just because I didn't take any bio in HS, but some topics were confusing.
Super LOW WORKLOAD.

John is hilarious, kind, and an easy grader. It's hard to imagine how lenient and understanding he can be, and his exuberant positive energy could always light up your day. He lags behind on lecture materials because he jokes too much. That's my only complaint. But apart from that, he is like a father. I love John.
So funny. He my boy. We chill. Material is boring af, but he live af. Had me dying with his jokes. I can tell that he pulled when he was younger. Total bro. Take his class.

I was stoked when Willis told us at the beginning of the semester that we would not use a textbook. However, that idea is much better in theory than in practice. His method of teaching consisted mostly of telling us to google things in place of reading a textbook and his lectures were not helpful in explaining concepts either. Very nice guy though.
Interesting guy, the subject itself is tough to teach but there is a lot of overlap between topics and ideas. Ask for help when you need it and make sure you understand what is happening in lab.

Though I was never really involved in lecture as much as I should have been, Willis is a very enthusiastic professor who cares about what he's teaching. He is clear in his expectations and always wants to make sure that the class understands what he's talking about. Midterms are wholly based on lectures, problem sets, and labs; lecs recorded online

Willis is awesome--he's so excited about teaching and his energy will wake you up. The subject matter towards the end is kinda meh, but the stuff I learned in the first third of the class has been pretty useful. He's not great at teaching technical stuff and calculations, but he's really entertaining when talking about more conceptual stuff.

Very very enthusiastic professor, which is nice to see but sometimes tough at 8:30AM. Not very clear about what we needed to be taking from the lectures, they seemed to talk around the point with lots of COOL EXAMPLES of animals that he was pretty pumped about. Truly nice guy and the material wasn't bad, but not the greatest lecturer around.

Oh Willis, if you only didn't teach with Rausher I would love you forever. Wonderful at explaining concepts, very enthusiastic, so sweet, and cares about his students. But if he is teaching with Rausher, it is not worth it.
Willis is great! Rausher, on the other hand, is pretty awful.

Willis is amazing.  He makes amazing powerpoints, delivers lectures awesome lectures, and makes course expectations extremely clear.  The tests are very fair, too.  He's so enthusiastic at early hours of the morning too.  I don't know how he does it.
Willis is the man

Willis is the man.  Don't let anyone else tell you otherwise.  He is super enthusiastic, excited about biology, and easy to listen to.  Gives example problems in lecture EXACTLY like on the test, so you are completely prepared.  Senior biology major and Willis is one of the best, no..THE best biology prof I've had at Duke.  Cares a lot about studen

The far better lecturer. Wish he had taught more. Enthusiastic, happy to be teaching, willing to take time to make sure everyone understands. Truly loves biology and wants to show you how cool it can be! It isn't easy but he is a great teacher.

taught the evolution portion. not easy as it is, but his lectures make no sense. teaches theoretical approach to problem solving; the only time you will ever solve a problem is on the test. and you wont know how to solve it bc you never were taught how to solve it. and the test is all problems. this prof was terible
No Comments

Genuinely a smart and caring guy. But lectures are so boring, completely monotone and very disengaging. I don't think he deserves all the hate I see on here though. Tests and homework are generally easy, but be prepared to self study a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Worst professor in the econ department. There are a lot of people teaching econ 101, so try to avoid it. His exams are easy (multiple choice) but the lectures are boring and not good.
He can't explain anything, just go in circles. His exams are the same than the exercises of the book, so he can't even make his own questions .Worst professor at DKU

Professor Zhang destroyed my interest in economics :(. Class is so boring, I don't understand the point of any of his activities. Going to class feels a waste of time if I can get the same info from the textbook (also the textbook is too expensive!!)
If you like to read and self-learn everything, take Professor Zhang class. He is really bad explaining, so the only way to learn is from the book.

Professor Zhang class is just based on the textbook. He just reads the ppt, and doesn't provide more explanation, so you will be better off if you just read the textbook and ignore his lectures.

His exams are easy, so that's a plus.
Do yourself a favor, and don't take this class. Professor Zhang is so boring, that 2 and a half hours of his class felt like a torture.
He was super boring, but besides that, it was an ok class. Test and assignments were easy.

He is a nice guy and always accessible for help outside class. Exams were hard but he graded easy. Be sure to read the textbook and go to class. Otherwise you won't know what he will be testing on in the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Highly recommend this entry-level course if you want some exposure to econ. Prof Xiaochen is one of the few professors who really can explain things clearly. Make sure you study hard for the tests though.
This course is required by the curriculum. Readings are mostly survey papers in economics. Work is heavy, but grades are fair.

Professor Zhang is a nice professor, but his lectures were not the most interesting. It was sometimes more useful to use the textbook. Professor Zhang is very approachable, but the overall class was not the best.

Prof Xiaochen is really a nice guy. He's patient and smart. He has a very engaging and interesting class style. After class, you can also talk to him about anything related to economics class or major. He is always so willing to help!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Prof. Xiaochen is excellent at explaining economic concepts. He's clear and easy to understand. The lecture slides, the interactive textbook, YouTube videos, pollev activities and practice exams are effective. He tries to encourage discussion but students hesitate to answer his questions, maybe because he can be a bit intimidating.

Professor Zhang is a nice guy, but the grading system was kinda off. Most of the grade being based on on-the-spot exams that don't really give you anything but binary choices was tough. There were in-class debates and papers on very intriguing topics, and I guess they provided a better opportunity to learn and revise the topics we'd studied.

Getting a C+ for ECON101 taught by Xiaochen Zhang?? That's absolutely hilarious. Many Chinese students never took ECON before college but still got an A for this course. Xiaochen is not to blame for your poor grade.

I literally don't understand the reason why so many students dislike Xiaochen's lectures. And to be honest I think his lectures were well organized and informative, and the class contents were super duper easy to the extent that it was almost impossible to get a grade lower than A- SMH.
Professor Zhangs biggest talent is to literally repeat whatever the textbook says. Nothing more and nothing less! His lectures are the best sleeping pills.

His lectures are usually really long and he sometimes confuses himself. It's kinda cute. He mentions the documentary American Factory over and over again so if you want to impress him, definitely watch that. His class should be easy if you go over his slides thoroughly.

Not really happy with Econ 101 with Professor Zhang, he's a nice guy for sure but his class was somewhat erratic and I had difficulty understanding his lectures. I took AP Econ in high school and thought that was a much more engaging class, Professor Zhang's class is incredibly by-the-book and offers little room for discussion or interaction.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Language learning is supposed to be interactive, engaging, and enjoyable. Unfortunately, she does not accomplish any of those things. I felt judged and completely unmotivated in her class.

I took 300s with both Zhang and Pan. Zhang is really sweet but she's a very soft grader, if you want to learn Chinese take Pan. She's a MUCH harder grader (Got an A- first time I had her) and she will rip you apart but you will actually learn and make progress. It's also very much possible to get an A with her if you put in the effort. She's nice!

Like another review says, if you want to improve your Chinese, Pan Laoshi is the best choice, she gives a lot of feedback, pushes for student discussion, and pushes you to do your best. However, for a 2-credit course, this course may be a bit too much work. I would recommend if you have extra time or good time management and want to LEARN.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: If you just wanna study this course to complete the requirement with a good grade, don't choose her. But if you wanna improve your Chinese (I mean, speak like a native speaker, not just simply improve) and complete the requirement at the same time, then she'll be the best choice.

if you want to consider any review, please consider this one. She is the WORST professor I have had at DKU. She intentionally stresses her students out, and does not give it a second thought. She prides herself on giving students stellar grades conveniently before course evaluations, and then will completely tank your grade.
Highly recommend her! Very accessible both in and out of class, will push you to get the best out of you.

reviews.comment: She is very caring and really wants students to improve. She gives great feedback and her encouragement makes learning Chinese (which is ridiculously hard) much less daunting. She tries to use a lot of Chinese in class for instructions which is beneficial as it improves comprehension skills. The grading is also such that hard work will get you an A

reviews.comment: Pan Laoshi is very strict. Outside of class she is nice and approachable but a lot of her lectures are textbook heavy and most students don't pay attention. She is a harsh grader and often makes you feel demotivated to work. She rarely laughs in class and that makes for a daily hour of no fun. Don't recommend.

reviews.comment: Pan Laoshi is one of the most caring professors Ive had in DKU. She is sweet and understanding. She also tries to make everyone in the class engage. She truly believes in her students and wants whats best for them. Lectures may seem too by-the-book but it works!
Not accommodating at all She is too much by the book person which makes for a hostile environment

reviews.comment: The workload is intense but she is a sweet and caring person that will push you to achieve improvements in your language level.

reviews.comment: Best teacher I've had ever since I came to DKU. She is so nice and fun. Makes the class easy and adjusts it for you and will help if you ask for help.
Xu laoshi was amazing. Best Chinese teacher ever
would take her class again

reviews.comment: One of the best professors I've had at DKU
She is clear about her expectations before and during class, responds to emails quickly, fun class overall. The homework isn't hard and she helps if you ask.
I took her class for whole year, and she is awesome. i would take her class over and over again

reviews.comment: I believe Professor Xu is so nice and cares so much about the well-being of her students, she is very inspiring, and all her classes are useful for your daily life activities. I would definitely recommend you take her class as she is easy to reach outside the classroom

I really like this Chinese professor, she is so sweet and she wants the best for you. Her classes might be a little difficult for those who lack Chinese skills, but she wants us to speak more (no matter the grammar) and be able to use new vocabulary in our daily life.

Prof. Xu is a caring and loving professor. Her feedback is prompt and comprehensive. Her grading is very strict, but because she places significant emphasis on spoken Chinese I decided to stay with her for 102A&B. She would even organize individual speaking practice if a student requested it. If you prefer knowledge over grades, she's great!

Xu Laoshi is a great professor who seems very passionate about teaching, which makes attending her lectures a mere pleasure. She grades fairly and quickly, which helped me keep a constant track of my grades and progress. She also offered to have one-a-one sessions during Chinese holidays and before the finals should we have any questions/struggles.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Xu Laoshi is a great professor and expects a lot from her students. Make sure you are VERY well prepared for each class by finishing the practice drills and understanding them well. She's also big on participation during class and presentations. She gives helpful feedback on the assignments as well. Prepare for the class to be very fast-paced.

She is very nice and quite funny. She is easy to understand and is understanding as well. I had a good time in this class and things made sense, and she tried to explain when they didn't. 

Please know your contextualized drills BEFORE class, don't rely on other students in the class to help you during the breakout rooms to practice.

Xu laoshi might be a demanding professor, but she pushed me to improve my Chinese fast. She gives lots of feedback on the dialogue performances and even takes the time to record an audio correction for each individual student, which I find extremely helpful. She's very encouraging and is always available to discuss learning difficulties.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Xu is very strict on pronunciation and making you pronounce words the Beijing way. She is arbitrary with the way she conducts classes and asks students for their views but does not actually care.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Xu Laoshi is great! She is very caring and gives detailed feedback. She also is willing to help if you ever need it. This class was a very enjoyable experience.

Xu Laoshi is a great professor who really cares about your learning. She uses google classroom instead of Sakai which is something I really like but she gives the option to still use only Sakai. Shes a bit tough on pronunciation grading but gives good feedback and really helps you improve. The workload is very manageable as well.
Xu was very strict on pronunciation when grading our oral presentations. She also did not enjoy using Sakai, the standard Duke/Duke Kunshan education website, and opted for Google Classroom.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Xu Laoshi is very strict with tones when she grades the Dialogue Performances assigned for homework. Otherwise, she is very sweet and caring. She does use Google Classroom over Sakai but gives you the option to stick with Sakai if you prefer.
Professor Xu is amazing! She takes the time to leave detailed comments on every assignment (these really help). She is also very supportive of your learning. I would definitely recommend this class!

Xu Laoshi is incredibly fair in grading. She will ask you what's wrong when anything concerns her and she will actually listen to you and try to solve it together. It could seem she is a tough grader, but it's fair to the point where they start to inspire you to do better. I'd say I love how honest she is.

Xu Li is a very caring Chinese professor. Occasionally she can get upset if you are not prepared for class, but she is excellent at teaching Chinese. I got away with attending less than half of the Chinese classes (be creative with your excuses) and I managed to get a good grade. She is very light hearted and a good choice for taking Chinese.

Xu Laoshi spends most of the class period reviewing the key grammar and vocab points from the homework, and she gives students ample opportunities to participate (which is especially important in a language class). She tends to teach past the end of class (usually 15 mins), but she lets people go if they have another class or other obligations.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: The best language professor I had the fortune to have. If I could, I would rate her with more than 5.

Xu Laoshi is one of my favorite Chinese Professors because she is so caring and encouraging in and outside of class. I think her teaching style is more lecture-like. Sure, she can be tough when it comes to grades, but I would say they are very accurate and her feedbacks are so inspiring to learn more.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Xu Laoshi is a great professor. Although our class was completely online, I learned a lot. She is always upbeat and gets everyone involved and participating during class. She grades quite easily but will take off points for incorrect pronunciation and grammar. Overall a great prof and knows how to get people involved despite cultural background.
Despite time differences, Xu Laoshi basically wants you to attend in-person classes. It is my first semester at DKU and I cannot until junior year when I dont have to take Chinese classes anymore.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Xu Laoshi is the most friendly teacher of Chinese language. I didn't want to learn Chinese in the beginning of my semester, but with Xu Laoshi my attitude to Chinese language changed. She is a real language teacher.
I took Chinese 301 and 302 with Xu Li. She is humorous but can be a tough grader especially with unexpected quizzes occasionally.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--EXTRA CREDIT--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Xu Laoshi is a superb Chinese teacher. Her kind demeanor makes it easy to talk to her and she is alway looking to improve herself as a teacher. Whether you're an advanced student or a beginner, Xu laoshi will adjust to every student's level appropriately. I find this part of her teaching style very admirable.

My Chinese has improved a lot in Xu Laoshi's class. She makes her expectations clear from the beginning and does not assign busy work--every assignment is made to help improve your Chinese. Incredibly open to feedback and cares about her student's well-being and mental health. Tries to be as fair as possible. Gives extra credit. Great teacher!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Xu Laoshi's requires attendance to all her classes and her content is very America centric.
Teacher Xu assigns a lot of homework for a 14 week course and requires attendance to online classes.

reviews.comment: She's super considerate and willing to help inside and outside the classroom. She respects our time and has strong goals to help us learn Chinese. She also provides extra credit opportunities for her students.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Xu Li is one of the best Chinese Professors I've had at DKU. She gives detailed feedback on what you should work on. She takes the success of her students very personally and is very attentive to their needs and progress. I find myself always looking forward to attending her lectures as they are always fun and engaging. Shows slight favoritism tho.
Tough grader who makes optional projects like service learning mandatory. Won't take her course again.

I aint have any background in chinese, but she always let me know what I was laking and where to focus. Her class is tough but I think thats how it should be like... she pays a lot of emphasis in everything from grammar to pronunciation. My biggest issue was with pronunciation and she always told me, but thanks to that it improved a lot.

DKU's Chinese department is overall excellent, you generally can't go wrong with any teacher here. Xu Li is excellent as a teacher not only because I feel like I learned a lot, but my progress was extremely noticeable. She cares for her students and focuses on development. As long as you try your best, you will get an A and you will get better.

Xu Laoshi is a fantastic Chinese professor, she really understands how to engage students from different backgrounds in Chinese. Her grading is incredibly fair, and she will take the time outside of the classroom to check-in and meet with you to address concerns. Chinese is a difficult language and Xu Laoshi is sympathetic and willing to help.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Xu Laoshi is easily one of my favorite professors at DKU. Very supportive and friendly. Also, she was very helpful, explaining grammar and characters. Now I really want to take a 300-level Chinese class, just because she mostly teaches it.

this was the worst math professor imaginable. he was difficult to understand due to his accent and his lectures were scattered and unstructured messes. we were barely graded on anything and our final was worth half our final grade. run far away from this class.

reviews.comment: very fast explanation and assumes a lot of prior knowledge. he gives twice as much hw as all the other math professors here and his midterm and final were so hard the average was so low to the point that when it was curved, we all received at minimum 2.5x what we initially scored, which speaks a lot about him. topics in the final were not taught

reviews.comment: Alot of homework. Other professors only give 60 questions per week but he gives 120. These questions have many parts to them and take a long time.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Xu's classes are enjoyable and have really clear structures. It is engaging to attend his lectures. He's also one of the most caring and nice professors I met. He delivers clear math concepts in class and is always supportive in his office hours. He offers help and answers our questions so patiently.

awful course. exam is too hard. HW are too
heavy
As a professor who attaches importance to concepts as well as principles, he tries to inspire us and pave a correct way for a freshman to learn Mathematics.

The professor's class has a good pace, with assignments that are of moderate difficulty, helping to improve students' learning efficiency. He is patient during office hours, and there are weekly homework, quizzes, and suggested problems. The class is lively and humorous.

The course measure theory is a hard topic, yet Prof. Xu presented it elegantly and explicitly. He is passionate about this topic and the lecture is logically organized. Very comfortable experience as a Math class.

7 weeks isn't enough time to learn calculus. There's a lot of things you need to learn. His teaching (due to 7 weeks) is way too fast for me to fully comprehend. He's approachable and ready to help outside of class but I don't know what I don't know so it was of little help to me. I just watch a lot of online tutorials to learn it myself.

Calculus is hard to teach in 7-weeks. If you haven't learned it before it might be hard but if you haven't its a pretty easy class. Xiaochen isn't the best lecturer and is hard to approach as a foreigner so a lot of the learning is on your own. Oh and his handwriting is incomprehensible.

Dr. Tan was a great Writing 101 professor. Her projects and assignments were interesting for the class topic (AI), and there was lots of group work and collaboration amongst peers within the class. If you show up and do the work, you'll get an A
Her grading is very easy and there isn't a ton of work.

Professor Tan is a very easy grader and the class is easy. If you put some effort in the essays, you will get an A. Lectures can be boring at times. Dr. Tan is nice and is accessible outside of class if you email her. Great class to get Writing 101 out of the way.

Chill professor, long lectures. Went through long math problems in class (also did not post her notes), but the assignments and exams were fair and easy (no math) & prof is super nice. Disregard the other reviews, its not bad and 3 ppl just got pressed bc they thought gender econ would be a joke class & got upset. Really interesting papers though

reviews.comment: maybe one of the worst econ classes i've taken at my time here. Avoid this class

reviews.comment: Do not take this class. Unnecessarily tough and not worth it.

Professor Xiao has put together a masterclass in academic suffering. You know that scene in Good Will Hunting where Will solves the impossible MIT hallway problem on the chalkboard? This class is like that—except the board's on fire, you're not Will, and the problem never ends.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This class was terrible. Not only was it extremely difficult but also uninteresting.
Seeing the other comments, I'm not alone. I should've dropped this class early, and every day I regret not doing it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: I've had a hard time reconciling the fact that I'm even in this class. Lately, the only solace I've found is knowing I can use this awful experience to help someone else avoid it. So here it is: don't take this class. Find something else. You'll be so glad you did.

Stay away from this class at all costs. It assigns more—and harder—work than core econ classes. Problem sets take 10–12 hours, are coding-heavy, and graded harshly. The research project requires endless revisions, and the exams are long and brutal. Electives shouldn't be this rigid or overwhelming. This class is an unmitigated disaster.

Pretty chill class - 4 reading summaries (graded by completion), 3 problem sets, and 1 group presentation. Group presentations are graded by professor and student rating. Prior experience with Stata and econometrics is recommended, as the problem sets are mostly based on them, and nearly all lectures are student presentations.

COMPREHENSIVE: Dr. Jiang is energetic, knowledgeable, and responds to questions quickly. The class has weekly homework, occasional lab assignments, a final project, and three exams (+optional final). HW grading was generally fair but very precise. HW questions were decent prep for exams, but exams always felt harder and required full understanding.

Yue is a super enthusiastic lecturer who's genuinely passionate about statistics. The grade you receive is a roughly 60/40 split between test scores and HW/Labs. His TAs can be very precise in wording when grading homework, so definitely pay close attention to that. Tests are fair, and shouldn't be too difficult if you go to every lecture.

Yue knows his stuff and is the nicest guy. Class is test heavy which made things stressful, and definitely find people to study things with. Tests didn't always match with homework, but were honestly fair if you knew the material. Coding was hard with no prior experience but not too bad and I think friends in stat 199 had it worse.

my goat Yue never let me down. engaging and enthusiastic lecturer, very skilled at teaching in an accessible and fun way. obviously wants every student to succeed. a bit disorganized at times, but lenient grader with deadline grace periods. gave reasonable HW/exams and removed problems everyone had trouble with. great guy overall.

While the content covered in class is quite simple, the exams were full of curveballs and there wasn't a lot of practice material to prepare for them. Though AP Stats isn't a prerequisite for this course, I really think that having a background in statistics is necessary to succeed in this class. The coding/lab aspect is also quite confusing.

Love Yue, great guy and one of my favorite professors. However, this class is pretty hard in the fact that the content is pretty easy, but the midterms throw some pretty confusing curveballs. Also, this class is simply too hard to be a constellation class, and I had to grind to get a solid grade. Take this if you like health, otherwise do Stat 199.
Yue is the best!!!
loved it! learnt a lot and Prof. Jiang is an interesting guy. try talking to him outside of class!

Conveys content well and is accessible, and the material is chill. Grading system is a calamity, with graders looking to take points off for no reason. Think of it this way-- class content not difficult but if you want a good grade/an A the class is very stress inducing. Would recommend taking different class for major req. unless you need STA210.

If you are in ur later college years (upperclassmen) this should be an easy class. He's actually reasonable when grading but the graders are not. I love that he is passionate about stats and do all sorts of amazing things with it. I legit went to lecture once but could just feel that he is a nice person

Colossally dumb grading, but Yue himself was great. Graders would find any excuse to take off points, so get ready to sharpen your regrade skills. Lecture content was engaging, and more than half of the professor's jokes would land, which was a refreshing change from the norm.

Attendance isn't required, but it's extremely worth it to go to class so you fully understand the things you need for homeworks. The actual class material was pretty chill, besides maybe a few confusing concepts. As long as you pay attention to how he words his answers, you won't lose unnecessary points on homeworks and tests. Definitely recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: A very kind professor who wants students to succeed however, there is not enough direction provided for the homework so you end up losing points on small phrasing errors.

Class conveys good information but grading system totally ruins it. Grading system is out to get you with the way all assignments are graded, one slip up in wording can cost you 10 whole points on a homework assignment that is out of a 100. Causes a lot of stress because it makes it very difficult (unless you write an essay per question) to get A.
Interesting lecturer, but grading is horrendous. You can piss a few units and write a couple wrong words and get a 50% on a homework.

Overall friendly professor who really knows what he's talking about, but a ton of work on assignments. Echoing previous comments of nitpicky grading. Go to office hours, or you might have to learn how to do the coding on your own, since not many code examples are provided in class unlike STA199.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Yue is clearly very knowledgeable about regression, but the class was not very engaging. There was no in-lecture coding like in 199, which made lectures boring. Labs were awful and only graded every 2 weeks. Finding a helpful TA and going to their office hours is key, as it is hard to apply concepts from lecture without help.

Hilariously poor grading. Charismatic professor who knows the material inside out and can relay information in lectures well. 

However, the grading (especially on homework) is designed to fail you. Unless you beg for points by writing essays for descriptions, graders will find ways to take full points off for correct answers. Enjoy!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: He teaches well, but the grading is unreasonable. Questions on homework are worth 3 points each, but there are 10+ different ways to get -1. So you can get 7 things right, and miss 3 and get 0 points for the question. If the grading was more reasonable, this class would be great.

It's weird to rate a prof just a month into the semester, but Yue makes learning regression so clear and understandable. Definitely take it with him to learn the concepts! Graders and TAs are tough, though we've only had a few assignments so far. Anyway I'm just so surprised that regression is my favorite class this semester.

Yue was one of the most unfair professors I have ever had a Duke. It was like he wanted everyone to struggle. He grades harshly and what seemed like pretty arbitrary in a lot of cases. He is relentless with work and clearly doesn't expect you to have a life outside of his class. If you can avoid taking a class with him, you should.

Yue is great and incredibly smart, but 440 is a very, very tough class. The grades are brutal and some of the assignments are ridiculous. The final boss of the stats major is a formidable one. This is a class without a safety net and you can do very bad if you do not put in the effort or start things early (many Cs given to good students).

Professor Yue really wants his students to do well. But the lectures do not correspond well to the homework. If you go to office hours/TA hours though, they will help you immensely on the homework. Exams are open book/open note and not difficult if you know how to do the homework.

Yue is an extremely caring professor and wants his students to do well. However, his lectures can be unclear at times, and he often has mistakes on his homework assignments and exams. That being said, he is still very knowledgeable about the course material and beyond, and I definitely recommend taking a class with him for the energy he brings.

I have mixed feelings on this class. Yue is a great professor and clearly cares a lot. That being said, lectures dont directly correspond to homeworks, and homeworks are very lengthy and graded harshly. This class made me a better writer and group project collaborator, but I didnt learn much actual stats.

Yue is very accessible and available to help. That does not change the fact that this course is an absolute meat grinder and will destroy your will to live. If you don't absolutely need this class to graduate, definitely don't take it. You will learn a lot, but the workload/grading difficulty is definitely the highest in the Stats department

Yue was great to have for 440, but the class was tons of work. There is so much too learn and the class moves at a fast pace, which was hard to balance with having three other classes. His grading was tough, but he always provided lots of detailed feedback and gave you the chance to make up lost points.

Yue is a great professor- very accessible and gives good feedback. However, he is a tough grader, and STA440 is definitely the hardest class in the major work-wise. I also wish he was more clear about his grading criteria, as it seemed to change a bit during the semetster.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Group projects

reviews.comment: Yue may be the most accessible professor I have ever had. He quickly responds to emails and is always willing to give his time and help you learn. The class is a decent amount of work with its labs, homework, and exams, (grading criteria not always clear before), but provides a great intro to the subject that's interesting. Great personality too!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Group projects

reviews.comment: AMAZING professor. Extremely helpful and great at explaining concepts. Homework and labs are not too difficult, except for a few problems (TAs come into play here). Tests are manageable if you really review and ace the practice tests. Overall, one of the best professors here. If youre hesitating about taking this class, take ityou wont regret it

Yue is absolutely great. Super nice guy and always open to answering questions. He knows his stuff and also really cares about his students and making sure everyone succeeds. Honestly I wish more professors at Duke were like him.

Yue is one of the best professors I've ever had at Duke. Biostats was my first exposure to coding, and Yue made learning R easy and fast. His lectures were extremely interesting, he quickly responds to emails and Piazza questions, and all of the HW and tests were fair; he also was awesome about regrades. 100% take this class with Yue if you can!

You can tell how much Yue loves teaching. After talking to my friends in other sections, even though most things were the same, we had opportunities that my friends didn't like a career panel. Yue was always patient and caring, but the best part was how freaky fast he is with responding to emails. Taking STAT 199 with Yue made me a stat major.

Dr Jiang is probably the most accessible professor outside of class and clearly cares a lot about his students and wants them to do well. The class is not easy, but keeping up with the homework and attending the lectures makes it very manageable. Lectures are very clear and concepts are always explained well.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: To put it briefly, Yue is the kindest professor I've had at Duke. Everyone knows that statistics sucks, but somehow Yue made it bearable, and dare I say it, useful and interesting? There's a ton of work, but Yue was always there to help us out. It was clear that he just wanted us to learn statistics, and I'm glad I took stats with him.

Yue was an AMAZING professor when it came to responsiveness whether that meant Piazza, email, setting up meetings, you name it. His lectures are very clear but the class is very difficult and I found myself googling concepts and doing lots of outside reading. Felt a little "thrown into the deep end" when it came to the R code.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great Teacher. Took the summer version of Stat199 with him, and he did a phenomenal job with the class. Clear lecturer, super accessible outside of class, and overall a really nice teacher! Isn't too hard if you keep up with the work in the class and watch all lectures.

Super accessible outside of class, quick at responding to emails/Piazza, and extremely pleasant. But there were lots of things that frustrated me. He's extremely unclear about his grading guidelines, put material on the test we didn't really get into, and he didn't explain the basics clearly. Has potential to be a great prof, but need improvement.

Really cares about his students and is extremely accessible to answer questions. Sometimes it felt like he couldn't read that everyone in the class was confused, but as long as you put in effort outside of class you'll be alright for grades. Lots of assignments but not too terrible, all with good feedback and plenty of time to complete.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Group projects

reviews.comment: Yue was always responsive with the course Piazza or email and you can tell he really put a lot of thought into the lectures and cared about his students. His tests are BRUAL (they were fair, honestly...) but you can tell he really cares about students. He was SO much better than my other summer class. START THE HOMEWORK EARLY.

Yue is very personable and will sometimes slip in a few jokes during his lectures. He is very kind and extremely responsive. The a-million-and-one questions I had asked him as well as my classmates were always answered. He is also very understanding and accommodating and will make sure you're really understanding the content in his class.

I LOVE YUE. THE MOST RESPONSIVE, RESPONSIBLE, and on-top-of-things professor I've ever known. He had responded to my MANY emails within 30min and answers every Piazza questions ASAP. He really cares. He held a late-night review session just at the request of a student in another time zone. He's very thorough. Just make sure you're on top of things.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Stat 199 was one of the best classes that I have taken! Prof Yue is a really great lecturer and extremely intelligent. Sometimes, he can come across as a little condescending but that's just because of how smart he is. This class made me want to major in Statistics! But also, very team-heavy. If you end up with a bad team, good luck...

You do have to really work for this class, but you learn a lot (what Duke is all about). This specific semester was COVID so we did not have the final group project. Yue is a brilliant guy, really knows his stuff and wants his students to do well. TA office hours are more helpful than his in my opinion. Going online made things harder for sure.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Didnt realize that someone could like statistics that much but go him, I felt it. TAs graded on bizarre things but that might have just been the course. 100% tidyverse is dumb. I learned a lot and Yue was awesome. He really cared about us and was so helpful in office hours. Take 199 with Yue if you can (talking to friends in other sections here...

Yue was a great Professor! I had him for STA 199, and while things didn't always come easy to me he was so so kind in helping me. He always emailed back within 30 minutes, answered questions very quickly on our class Q+A website (class piazza), and was overall a kind person. I worked hard in here for sure, but a great class. LOTS of group work!!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: There are two assignments due each week which was hard because I'm not a math person AT ALL, but Dr. Jiang was always really patient and helpful in explaining things in office hours. I decided to take STAT 102 because I'm a premed and in the end it was the right choice because I ended up learning a lot. We also had a great course website.

Dr. Jiang is AWFUL and far from understanding. He cares more about creating a distribution of grades in his class than actually imparting knowledge. But, what ruins this class is that it's unfair. Dr. Jiang re-vamped the syllabus halfway through the semester, deviating so much from what he implied at the beginning of the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: It's definitely not an easy class, but so worth it. You learn a great deal since Dr. Jiang let's you work with health datasets, and he is super accessible in and out-of-class. Great professor and course!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Wasn't sure what I'd be getting into taking Stats with Yue as opposed to taking 101, but I'm so glad I made this decision! It certainly required effort, but I feel like I truly got a lot out of this class and Yue was as supportive and understanding as can be, especially in the craziness of COVID-19.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Nice person but the course feels disorganized and unfocused. Slides and structure seem reused w/o revisions, quizzes inconsistent, and he gives misleading information about quiz prep. Homework unclear due to it being mostly AI generated. Attendance is random. Tbh the material can be easily self-taught. Seems to teach better in a more "Mathy" class.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Avoid at all costs. Does not know what he's doing and reads off slides from other people (not even his own) during lectures. Also never credit the original creators of them. Does not know the content he's teaching and has made multiple basic mistakes (does not even understand the basic DCF model).

AVOID!! Does not really know the subject and only reads slides. The grading criteria is so unclear that you have no idea what your grade is until the end of the semester. He said attendance was mandatory but only took attendance in 5 classes, so students got 60-80 on their attendance even if they only missed a 1-2 classes. Didnt learn much.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Vague and versatile grading criteria and schedule. Can be very confusing and do not respect students and their efforts. Most of us didn't understand what we were supposed to do and to learn throughout the course. Do not recommend.

I feel as though her high scores on this site are just because she is a lenient grader. She was quite unclear with her expectations and would get annoyed when students did not understand. She also gave us feedback for our speeches that was clearly AI and would encourage us to use AI instead when we had questions for her on how to improve.

Professor Zhang is a highly effective instructor with a clear and structured teaching style. She explains material in a way that is easy to follow and ensures that students understand key concepts. Her lessons are well-organized and focused on practical communication.
best teacher for A+. highly recommended

She's very encouraging and caring to students. She gives good feedback after each debate. A very interesting class even if you've never debated before. I definitely learn a lot and grew outside my comfort zone. By the end of the class, I'm pretty comfortable debating and conveying ideas using Chinese.

406 does have quite a bit of work (debate + debate script due one week, a writing assignment due the other) but it's a great class to practice your Chinese through debating. Zhang laoshi is also flexible and accessible; she is nice and responsive to our needs
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Chinese 406 is less like a traditional language class (vocab, grammar, etc.) and more of an applied-language class. You debate biweekly, and you have to spend quite a bit of time preparing for the debates beforehand (3+ hours/week). Attendance is mandatory, so I had class at 5 AM. Professor Zhang gives feedback to help you learn how to debate well.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: Zhang Laoshi is really amazing. Seems very strict and harsh at first, which she is lol, but she is also very approachable. Her classes are more challenging than the other sections, but I feel like I have improved a lot too.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She is a very nice and caring professor. Don't be afraid to reach out to her if you need some help.

Dr. Yao is an excellent professor. I took BME 303 and 553 with him, and he made challenging, math-heavy material intuitive through clear explanations and fun analogies (often with pop culture references!). He emphasizes understanding over memorization and is very enthusiastic and passionate about teaching. I highly recommend taking his classes!

Dr. Yao is a very wholesome and funny professor. He will try hard to teach intuitively. You can tell he is very positive, enthusiastic, & extremely approachable.

For Diagnostic Imaging, I recommend attending lectures (rather hard to self-study from slides without it) and to have fun. He wants everyone to succeed as long as they put in the effort.
Not good teacher, teaching is so confusing. The lab is not well organised with silly members.
always loves pop culture references, tests are not very math-heavy, generally gives open-book (and open-laptop if your textbook is an eBook). His homework grader is also very lenient
Very chill prof., I recommend to pair with other hard classes

She extremely kind and caring. Her class was fast paced, and she mainly speaks Chinese, but that forces you to learn. Quite strict with attendance, but the class atmosphere made it all worth it. She needs to work on her grammar teaching cause it is kind of superficial.

Miao Laoshi is very kind, but I don't think she's good as a prof. I took her class twice, once with 3 students in it and then I liked it, but now i'm taking it with 15 ppl in it and it's lowkey awful. I feel like I barely learned anything, since Prof. Miao doesn't explain grammar and just tests on it, and generally can't manage that many ppl.

A lovely individual, but good teaching is lacking. Taking her class was boring, repetitive, and 
intelectually unstimulating. She preaches the value of feedback, however, the moment it's negative, she becomes defensive and takes it personally. The class is focused on unnecessary grammar, writing, and vocabulary, and department isn't taking action.

She's a beautiful human being but not a great teacher. In the class, she makes sure everyone is participating and gives feedback. But her English isn't good and she speaks in Chinese for most of the class. The class pace is really fast and starts to focus more on grammar. The vocabulary we learn seems unreasonable because they are very random...

Prof Miao genuinely cares about her students. She's very encouraging and caring, and always makes sure everyone is comfortable during class. Grading-wise, she's very fair and gives good feedback. I really enjoyed taking Chinese with her - would definitely recommend!

Professor Miao is really caring. She does her best to accommodate all students in her class and makes sure that students are learning as much as possible in her class. Do not be afraid to make mistakes in her class as she will only guide you to improve. Highly recommended!

Professor Miao is really caring and accommodating. She takes time to really get know you outside of classes and will help you to succeed in the course. One thing, Chinese classes are now getting harder from CHIN 202 so make sure you study.

She is very kind and accommodating. Cares deeply about her students performance. Will ask you about your interests to help you with your language learning. Will try to know you personally and help you develop your language skills!

Miao Laoshi is a kind professor who likes to give individualized feedback to all students during her office hours. Though she might be slow in giving written feedback to students, she points out areas in which they can grow and they are helpful! Also note her English skills might be low compared to other professors teaching the same course.
Incredible class. Mela is hilarious, understanding, and a genuinely good guy. Lectures are a bit fast but the he covers the content well and posts recordings after class.
He is a great guy but I found it pretty hard to understand his in person lectures, i much preferred watching the recording. One of the better math classes at Duke i guess?
This class is more than 50% linear even though it is supposed to be Multivariable Calculus for economics. Mela is solid but lectures are a bit fast
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you're looking to *learn* something from the class, do NOT take Mela's class. No discipline, no official solution to "team" worksheet (he only post works from your peers), but workload is light if you're in a *good* team. Hardly a guy knows how to teach maths properly and sometimes give self-conflicting explanations.

Really great guy, funny at times, and has pretty good slides. Homework counts 60% of your grade but it's teamwork so you should definitely take it with some mates! The final was tough, all proofs and derivations, but you should be ok if you reviewed everything in the slides and team worksheets. The course was definitely too theoretical though.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Partial credit is ridiculous and homework is light. Very easy to get a good grade in the class. Mela is also hilarious.

Soooooooo much partial credit. Really easy class if you do the homework with your own merit. Go through the practice tests right before your midterms as their often the same thing. Really hard to get a bad grade even if you don't know the whole unit. Mela is the GOAT. Simple. Only knock on this class is that it was only offered at 8:30,

Took multi in high school but first half of 202 is all linear. Attendance isn't required and he posts 30 min recordings of each lecture after, which was honestly better/easier for me to follow than the in-person lectures. Grading is pretty fair with partial credit, especially on the final, so it's okay if you do bad on one of the three midterms.

Literally the worst math teacher I've had in my life. He gets good ratings because his exams and grading are said to be easier and the homework doesn't make your miserable, but the lectures are horrifically taught. It moves way too fast, and he doesn't stop to explain new terms. The midterm this time was also a lot harder than previous years.

Very good prof in math finance. The workload for the course is light since HW is teamwork, but try to work out all the problems by your own, since they are really helpful for preparing for the final. Likes telling jokes. Nice and accessible outside of class on Zoom. Final is fair, based on theoretical questions from team worksheets and lectures.

Lectures are hard to follow as there is a lot of new content presented extremely quickly. The first half of the semester is entirely linear algebra which threw me off, second half is MVC. There are 3 midterms (55% of grade) and 1 final (30%). They were fairly hard but doable w/ the 6 practice exams + review problems Mela provides for each midterm.

This was my first Duke math course, but based on what I've heard, Mela seems a lot more lenient than the others. Use the old midterms to study throughout the semester and you should be able to do decently on every midterm. I didn't think the final was a good metric; we were tested over some tough questions that were discussed only once in class.

One of my favorite professors in my entire time at Duke.  Definitely cares about his students and always in a cheery mood that will keep you motivated to attend class.  The class material was difficult, but he really helps you understand it.  Final was difficult but manageable with curve.

Overall this was a pretty difficult class because three midterms and a final exam make up 85% of the final grade, but the TAs are told to grade leniently and give a lot of partial credit. Also, since one of your midterm grades can be replaced by your grade on the final, your grade is still salvageable if you mess up on one of the tests.

Mela is a great guy. Class is not an easy A but is very chill (only HWs due every other week) with recorded lectures. Only thing that sucks is that 85% of final grade is from 3 exams and final. Tests are pretty fair and have lots of previous exams to practice with. Would highly recommend for the multi requirement for the stats major.
Mela is a cool guy. His humor makes 8:30 AM lectures less miserable. The only thing I didn't like about this class was that three midterms and the final are 85% of the grade.
Brilliant professor. Funny too. It was one of my best classes at duke

Definitely take this class to fulfill CS linear req. Prof Mela is funny and good at explaining things. His slides are really useful and the homework is beyond manageable. The tests are very fair based off of what we do in class and there are practice tests and review questions to study with.

Although math 202 is inherently not a super fun class unless you really like multivariable calculus, he makes the class as enjoyable as he can. The course material is certainly difficult, but his tests are fair and he gives out practice exams that are very similar to the actual exam.

prof. mela is nice enough but grades are 90 percent exams and the other 10 percent is weekly homeworks. The 3 exams during the semester weren't that bad (you can definitely do good if you prepare) but the final was pretty hard and the average was about an 80 (no curve)

Mela is a funny guy. One of the very few in the Duke math department that make math somehow enjoyable- rather, manageable. 202 with mela is good. Medians on the mid terms were 85, 87, and 92. He posts pages from the book so you don't have to buy.

He is a chill and nice guy, but he is not that great at explaining concepts to people who are not math majors/grad students, as the class is taught in a theorem heavy and terminology dense way. People seem to be claiming that the class is super easy and a guaranteed A, but the midterm averages are consistently in the mid B range with no curve.

Definitely an easy A class. The professor is not very passionate about multi, but at least he's chill. I had him in the early morning, but attendance was not required. Spent almost no time for this class bc the exams were just like expected.

I only did well because I had prior knowledge of multi. Mela is nice and funny, but he struggles explain the concepts. 90% of the class grade is based on exams (3 midterms and 1 final), which are graded pretty leniently. Lectures are not necessary to attend, and he makes recordings available, which is helpful. A necessary burden for the econ major.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great, easy class to overload with. Attendance is never required at any discussion or lecture. Only work is weekly 1-2 hour homeworks and 3 midterms. Midterm content is exactly like past midterms/review problems so never any surprises. Very lenient grading, and very possible to get 100% on every test. Final was slightly harder but not bad.

Insanely long final exam. Slides were pretty surface-level, and prof gave little guidance on how to work through problems similar to the worksheets/the tougher questions on the final. Your grade will mostly depend on if you get a good homework group.

MELA IS GREAT! He has witty jokes that got me through the 8:30 lecture (at least whenever I went, he posts lessons and the slides online thank god). The tests are fairly reflective of old tests and what he teaches. The course is kind of rough overall because some concepts do get skimmed over but it's probably better than 212. Would recommend

The class was manageable overall. I'd definitely recommend taking this over 212 or 218 if you're a comp sci major. While 90% of your grade comes from tests, Mela doesn't try to trick you, and if you watch the lectures, do the homework, and look at past exams, it's a decently easy class. Mela isn't too memorable, but he is still accessible/caring.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: The go-to math class for economics and also COMPUTER SCIENCE majors. Lectures are confusing, but mela gives you all the resources to be successful
very easy tests, definitely the go to math class, mela himself is just objectively a bad teacher
he puts in the minimal work possible

If you are taking this you are probably an econ (or other non-math/hard stem) major who doesn't particularly like math. Class kind of sucks, but it's by far the best multi/linear option Duke has. Mela is funny and tries, but the content is bad anyways, not his fault though. Would def take this over the other options(212,218)

Overall I really appreciate taking Multi with Professor Mela. It is honestly one of the hardest classes content-wise for someone who isn't particularly good at math, but Professor Mela had pretty clear lectures to follow. The final was really brutal and I had a lot of trouble working through it, but I think it comes down to investing a lot of time.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Easy grade distribution-- 60% HW, 30% Final Project (really an exam), 10% participation/attendance. The grader was generous with the grading and deadlines. Open note final project was still really difficult, but I'm pretty sure there's a hard curve. Didn't retain much information, but some content was genuinely interesting. Glad I took the course.

Mela is nice and funny, but he zooms through lectures. The TA's can be pretty hit or miss, but they are always willing to help with homework. Your final grade mostly comes down to your performance on the midterms and final.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Mela is a nice man, but goes way too fast in lectures. Practically your entire grade is dependent on uncurved exams, despite having decently long, mandatory problem sets each week. For the final, he didn't offer any office hours, past exams, comprehensive review, or format (even w/ me sending emails). Could've been much more accomodating.

Xavier Mela is a nice, funny guy but goes way too fast during lectures. The TAs for this class were good people but poor teachers in my opinion. Once you get past these and the insanely test heavy grading criteria, the class is actually very easy. Overall, this class is just a vaguely interesting path of least resistance to fulfil the math req.

Mela is a funny professor who definitely cares about his students. 55% of your grade comes from 3 uncurved midterms and 30% from the final, so make sure you are well-prepared or else your grade will suffer. Mela goes pretty fast during lecture so definitely go to OH if you are confused + the grad TAs are very friendly and helpful!

This is far more basic multi compared to 212, maybe too basic, but good class if you're not planning on taking further math. Mela is great, very helpful and nice. the applications to econ are really interesting. Exams are ok but screwing up even one and your grade takes a huge hit since exams are 80% of your grade. Overall, great professor.

Great professor, super nice. I found the material to be quite interesting, though I wish it was more similar to Math 212. Mela's lecture videos are very concise and he is very accessible. I would say I wish most of our grade wasn't based off of 3 tough exams. Furthermore, cheating was pretty bad this semester since exams are open 24 hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: One of my favorite classes I took this year and Mela is awesome!! Material is interesting and his asynchronous videos are concise and understandable. 80% of your grade is from 3 uncurved exams, so it's hard to do well if you don't nail all 3. Wish it wasn't graded by so little things but you won't do poorly if you work hard in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Mela was one of 3 professors teaching the class but I liked his office hours the best. He's really funny and helpful and his lecture videos were straightforward and clear.
581 with Mela is wonderful. Very helpful & funny guy in and outside of the class, even with Zoom. Learned a lot and the grading is reasonable & lenient. Highly recommend!

A lot of people here says he's a great professor but honestly thought he was really rude and condescending. Cheating was so bad with online class in the summer and this guy literally did not do anything about it and still set the grade boundaries ridiculously high.

Multivariable calculus itself is a tough subject. However, I don't think I would've done half decent if it wasn't for Professor Mela. He was really open to answering questions during lectures, and his lectures were well presented. Tests can be tough, but definitely not unfair. Would highly recommend taking one of his classes before you graduate!
Professor Mela was amazing! He's a great 212 teacher, and is really accessible outside of class for help. He's also really nice, and although it's a hard class, you can for sure do well with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Lectures were great as mentioned, and he's really understanding with HW deadlines and will give extensions if asked for. Homework does take a while each week though. Great 212 prof!

Mela is everything you want in a math professor and more. Multi is a really difficult course, so having a clear, caring, and funny professor makes a world of difference. His lectures are fantastic and thorough so it's a huge mistake to skip them, even though he doesn't take attendance. If you have to take Multi, take it with Xavier Mela.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: Xavier was an amazing professor for 218. He was engaging and hilarious. Grades fairly but challenges you well.
Great, funny professor

Professor Mela is a very laid back teacher, and many classes were spent working in groups on worksheets. Lectures consisted of writing out probability definitions and doing example problems , but the problems for HW and tests required further thinking not really taught in class. Midterms were generally easy, however, with a median of almost 90%
If you have to take multi, take it with him! He's funny and really helpful. My favorite math teacher so far.
Such a nice professor!
Has obvious experience teaching and is always there for the students.
The tests can be challenging, but I sincerely enjoyed Professor Mela's class. He's funny, very laid-back, and will do his best to help you to understand and do well.
Please take a class with Mela before you graduate.
Incredibly clear and good natured professor. The material in mathematical finance was pretty good. Just a few HWs assigned and a very fair final.

Very clear professor. His lectures are filled with productive examples punctuated by very funny jokes. Excellent professor for a pretty difficult subject; office hours are also very helpful. His tests are quite fair and if you do the homework, go to class, and read the textbook, you should be able to get a pretty decent grade. Highly recommended.

Mela is such a cool teacher. He's engaging and funny, and even participates in running class jokes. His lectures are straight off of his notes though, which can usually be found in the textbook. And his tests this year were much more complex than his practice tests from years past. But it was worth it to have him, his personality made up for it.

Definitely lucked out with Mela. If you need to take multivar, take it with Mela! One of the best math teachers I've ever had. Truly cares about his students understanding the material and his tests / curves are reasonable. The lectures' examples are almost exactly like many test questions. Not to mention Mela is one of the funniest ppl on campus.

Mela is the man. 103 is a really hard class, but his lectures are clear, logical, and concise. His tests are very reasonable. He's also a very funny and likable guy and made math one of my favorite classes.

Mela was awesome! He is by far my favorite math professor I've had at Duke. He made everything clear and also made the class entertaining. I would definitely recommend taking him for any math class at Duke you can!
He's a very good teacher and keeps the class interested. He seems to care about making sure the class understands the material, not just how to do the problems.
very helpful recitation professor. makes himself very available to students and is detailed and thorough in explanations one on one and during recitation. makes me wish i had him for 103

Mela was clear and straight forward in class, which was very helpful. He didn't teach by the book for one section, but how he did teach for that section better prepared us for the rest of the course. He may come off as a bit aloof in office hours but he's helpful and wants students to do well. Our class did much better than others on the final.
Great teacher, passionate about math and a funny guy. Extremely helpful one-on-one. Highly recommended.

The tests are pretty straight forward and pretty similar to the final.  The material is difficult, and hence so is the class if you don't have any prior experience with multi/vector calculus.  If you were to take Math 103, definitely try to get Mela b/c he is probably the best one.
Mela is funny, accessible, and a great professor. The subject material is difficult, but he presents it as clearly as possible. Go to office hours!! He is always willing to help.

Professor Mela is hilarious and always makes class entertaining. He definitely knows his stuff and is always helpful during office hours. Straight-forward tests, similar to homework problems. He obviously teaches because he loves math.

Professor Mela is incredibly entertaining, even when he's not trying to be. His silly jokes and awkward mannerisms lighten up an otherwise tough class.  Math 103 is difficult, and it is easy to get lost if you don't keep up with the new material as it comes.  Professor Mela really wants to help you even if he sometimes has a hard tome with it.
I thought mela was a pretty good teacher. The tests are very reasonable but uncurved. hw takes a while every week but test questions are very similar to hw
Standard teaching style, effective if you can pay attention. Takes forever to grade exams.

Math class at Duke is HARD. It is not the teacher's fault. Although his lecture seldom looked unorganized, Mela is overall a great lecturer, funny and straightforward. His tests are reasonable too, unlike those of some graduate students.

I had Xavier for 103 and as a 107 TA. He is funny, good at explaining things, he actually does examples in lecture that help. Went to office hours few times and he explains everything very well and knows the material very well. He is very straight forward about tests, no surprises, he'll let you know what you have to do to get a good grade.

He is a little difficult to understand and not very accessible outside the class. However, he is a nice and funny guy, so class is somewhat enjoyable. Math 103 is going to be hard no matter who you take it with.

Stay away!!! He's a chill, nice guy, but can't teach calculus to save his life. Gets lost when explaining things, forgets to finish writing out the solutions to examples. This is MATH 103, one of the hardest classes at Duke, and this guy just makes it harder. He's like a slacker prof - fun but useless for what you need.

Love. The whole Chinese department is so sweet. Just from the frequency of classes, CHN204 might take up a bit of your time, especially when you have to do a video project or essay, but the material itself is not very challenging as long as you are present in lectures, especially if you have been following the beginners' track since 101.

Zhang Laoshi is the best! She's really funny and always had fire outfits. She was also really nice and understanding. We sometimes did games like Jeopardy that were both fun and helpful for practicing Chinese. She also brought us sweets and mooncakes at times. We did have a lot of homework and quizzes, but that's just the nature of Duke Chinese.
Homework is sometimes quite a lot, but she really wants you to engage and learn the language. Great professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I was very scared of this class because it was going to be my first in-person Chinese lesson in my life. It turned out, however, that my fear was unnecessary. The professor was wonderful. She explained every issue very well. She cared very much for the students (sometimes she even brought us Chinese sweets). The world needs teachers like her!
Nice professor and amazing lectures. He is able to explain most topics clearly, and the exams are not too difficult.
Really good lecturer and helpful outside of the class. Homework and exams might be hard, but the percentage of exams was only 40 or 50 percent, so do not worry too much.
Great lectures, but fell behind pace at times. We did not cover everything set out in the syllabus.
best prof ever, fun classes, cares a lot about our feedbacks, manageable workload

Prof. Dongmian is good. He explains everything clearly and without any water. His approach with the testing is unique if the class did well on midterm he will increase the level of difficulty on final exam (never curves the grade). The workload is manageable. Overall, I think he is the best prof among the math professors who teaches math 105

Professor Zou is the best professor in the Data Science department at Duke Kunshan. Although the material can be hard to grasp at times (actually always), he gives good examples and applications to make it understandable. He also adjusts pace and improves his teaching according to our feedback which is awesome. Of course, we all love his cats lol.

Prof. Zou is very nice and understanding. He always replies to his emails within a day. He is always there if you have any questions or concerns. He gave a lot of extra credit, dropped one hw, and adjusted the final's difficulty depending on how we did on a midterm. The workload is definitely manageable.

Professor Zou has an extremely nice personality and is very open to student comments and feedback. Professor Zou's lectures are always clear, concise, and accessible. Not too much homework and the exam difficulty is just about right. His classes are generally pressure-free and very relaxable. I would definitely recommend taking his class.
Cats lover
