Professor Zou is very nice and approachable. His class was challenging, but the homework amount was reasonable. The lectures were informative but moved too quickly. I had to use the textbook after class to figure out concepts. Overall, it was a good class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Hard class, exams are known to be harder than other PHYS 121 professors, but is passionate about material and good at explaining.

Professor Changcheng gives interesting lectures, which are not tedious. He is very passionate about physics,also He is approachable and will give insights on how to solve things. Phys 101 was just introductory course, but content was hard to grasp, homeworks were hard too.

This professor is kind and you can ask him questions at any time. But he left very many homework, he asked us to complete 20h homework every week, and there are many lab reports to write. Compared with the courses taught by other professors, Professor Changcheng gives far more homework than them.
Very nice professor, but his class--in terms of readings, discussion, and assignments--was extremely boring.

Probably the best writing class you can take as a Duke freshman. He is very caring of his students. Got a lot of valuable experiences, like visiting the Nasher museum, going up the Duke chapel to see the carillon, and listening to the Duke organ. It was a lovely class, and learned about writing without stress. A big thank you.
Absolutely phenomenal professor, very forgiving and cares about his students.
Best writing 101 prof!! Class was very low stress and not many writing assignments.
He's a great teacher and assigns very reasonable work. Make sure to participate in class, though.
As long as your are following assignment instructions, there really isn't any problems with this class.

Dr. Accinno is one of the most composed and clear professors I've ever had. He knows his stuff really well, and he grades very fairly. He doesn't force anything into your beliefs but rather encourage discussions about them, which I enjoyed. His writing projects were really interesting and I definitely became a better writer. Overall very solid.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Just don't take this course or from this professor.
She is a wolf in sheep's clothing. The test is not linked to the lecture. The lecture is not so hard, but the tests are very hard. She gave very low scores!!!
Does not teach well, grading is unclear. Will not tell you how she grades homework. Takes points off on criteria she never mentioned. I'd avoid taking her classes

The teaching quality is poor, and the material is not conveyed effectively, making it difficult to learn.
Grading is unfair, as the criteria were changed at the last minute, which felt unprofessional.
The exams are challenging and not reflective of the instruction provided. I would not recommend taking her course.
Note: Avoid her at all cost.

Professor Jassal is a really awesome person. He has an interesting perspective on Islam and definitely knows what he is talking about. The class is also really easy. He only assigned 2 papers and gives us a lot of time to write them. Pretty easy and interesting class. Highly discussion based so you have to show up every class.

A very good Writing 101 class to take if you have a lot of other difficult classes. The readings are short, and are usually pretty interesting if you choose to read them (you can get away with not doing them towards the end of the semester). He is very engaging in class discussions and supportive of sharing of opinions and open conversation.

This is the easiest class I have taken and probably will take at Duke.   Class is very laid back and mainly discussions.  You have two papers for the semester, and some short readings for the first half of the semester.  He gave everyone in my class an A for the first paper, which is 50% of our grade basically.  Definitely take it!

She is quite a tough grader and at times you don't even understand what she is grading on. Overall, a mid writing course and if you have to take it, it's ok-ish. She has her own agenda and will actively try and change your opinion if you disagree with her.

This class really expanded my repertoire on the history of student activism. Lots of great discussions, and the work was really manageable. The final project was actually a lot of fun to do, and gave the class strong creative license.

She's a good professor and she has a specific agenda for her class so you won't be left floating. She takes things pretty seriously and doesn't have the kind of charisma of some teachers. If you want, you can improve your writing in this class but it is mostly dependent on your own effort. I expected much more work in the class than there was.

She is an awful professor. She always tries to manipulate your thoughts by saying "What I hear you saying is '(insert something that you didn't mean)'" SHe told us that we could call her however we wanted during the course and then got angry when we didn't call her professor or doctor. Never take a class with her, none of my classmates liked her.

She's great! I have really enjoyed being in her class, and if you have any trouble, she's always there to help. Plus, our projects are pretty cool and they really get you to think about real world applications

I am very disappointed because I chose her after reading good comments here and looking at the rankings. Not a good teacher at all... Its hard to talk to her and to suggest ideas. She is very defensive when she talks and classes are extremely boring
She is wonderful

Wonderful professor if you are interested in the material. You get out of this class however much you put into it. If you are interested in the topic, I strongly recommend you take this class with Ahern-Dodson.
i took her writing 20 class 2 years ago. she's an awesome prof. dedicated to helping student's in improve their writing!
Very good teacher, she seems like she really enjoys teaching and is always ready to help.  She gives a lot of work, too much sometimes, but it is usually interesting and she grades pretty fairly.
No Comments
great teacher, get her if you can before she leaves this year
No Comments

A great teacher! Her writing 20 class is a lot of fun, she's very friendly, and there's not much work to be done.  You might be thrown off by the tutoring aspect of her class, but it's worth it.  She's great

Okay so first off, I know this says Duke, but I had him at Michigan State. This man is truly a gem. He is by far one of the kindest and most caring professors I've had. Initially, I didn't think I'd enjoy the class because it wasn't really my thing, but Ahlquist made the class so engaging. He was so supportive and gave great feedback. 10/10.

Professor Ahlquist is a great teacher and person. Very caring and super understanding. He also gives significant and detailed feedback. Fair grader but definitely pushes you to improve. The workload is not easy, but his class is easy to navigate - organized, LENIENT WITH DATES (could have just been for covid tho).

Daniel B. Ahlquist, D.B.A. as he refers to himself, is the most outstanding educator I have had in my career at Michigan State university. He encourages students to be honest with their writing abilities, to work diligently on drafting and editing papers, and to come to his office hours. He is very intelligent but doesn't let it get to his head.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Dr. Ahlquist was, without a doubt, my favorite professor at Duke. It is very clear that  he truly cares for the success of his students.  I can't believe Dr. Ahlquist left Duke for Michigan State - he was a true asset to our university, and am jealous that Michigan got him! I truly wish him all the best- and hope that he returns someday!

Ahlquist is someone who really cares about the success of his students and will do everything he can to ensure you succeed. He gives great feedback on your writing and speaking with him one on one helps immensely. He grades extremely fairly. If you participate and do the readings your writing will improve. He's a pretty reasonable guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Daniel is amazing. One of the best Writing 101 professors at Duke. Not only is he a good professor, but he is also a great all around person. The content was interesting, and there were only 2 major papers, which is a much better workload than most other Writing 101 classes, especially since you had more time to really focus on those two papers.

Daniel is one of the nicest, most down-to-earth professors I've met at Duke. He really cares about his students and wants to get to know them on a personal level. His class made me interested in environmental issues and the workload isn't bad compared to other writing courses. Would highly recommend!

Best teacher I've ever had at Duke. He is brilliant and the nicest person you will probably ever meet. He's also incredibly passionate and knowledgeable about the subject and doesn't impose anything upon you but allows you to challenge and formulate your own opinions

Fantastic professor who is not only passionate about what he teaches but also is truly interested in his students. Reading material can be dense and long, but in class discussions are very helpful. Provides a lot of good feedback on writing assignments and genuinely wants you to succeed. Would highly, highly recommend taking any of his classes.
Best Professor I've had at Duke
He is just awesome!
Incredible teacher, super interesting subject matter, and low workload--it's the holy trinity. You won't find that kind of greatness often in college

I never was that strong at writing, and in high school, I always never liked EnglishWriting courses. However, at college, Dr. Ahlquist literally changed everything -  I can easily say that this class was my favorite by far. And Dr. Ahlquist is the biggest reason why - seriously, he is the man!! TAKE THIS CLASS! You WON'T regret it!!

My absolute favorite professor at Duke. He is such an interesting, and amazing professor. So nice, always willing to help, and made class so much fun. I am genuinely going to miss going to his class. If you ever get the chance, take a class with him!

Daniel was one of the only professors my freshman year who actually was personal and showed interest in his students beyond the classroom. Very engaged with his class, which meant the class was engaged back.

Daniel Ahlquist is really great. He's so understanding and he genuinely cares about all his students. He will try to help you in all ways possible (he makes time for 1-on-1 meetings). Also the class is pretty easy, only 2 writing papers and a couple HW's the whole semester. Need to participate in class though.

Daniel's assignments and discussion were incredibly engaging and intriguing. He is extremely approachable and always willing to help, putting his students as top priority. The class atmosphere was so comfortable and his passion and approach to environmental science led to the course being my favorite thus far. A must take!

Daniel is an incredible teacher.  He is one of the most compassionate and interesting professors I have met at Duke and it was his first year here! Great academic, person, and professor.  Take this class!!!!
Ahlquist is the man and he teaches a sick class topic, it's not over the top on work and he grades generously, take his class if you can

Not the best writing teacher, but he's still pretty solid. His topic--Food, Agriculture, and Society--was incredibly interesting and I loved taking it. Oh yea and this class is low on work and he grades easy. Take this class

Truly one of the best professors I have ever had. If you are at Duke, especially Divinity School, and are not taking Aers, you have not gotten what you could have out of this experience. Read his work.

I honestly hated the subject matter (Milton), though I can't deny that Aers is quite an expert on the topic. It isn't his fault that the material couldn't reach me, and my fellow classmates seemed to enjoy it well enough. The grade was based on the higher of two essays. Class time was a group discussion, so you don't really have to talk.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: I honestly didn't like Aers that much, but I can't deny that he's a solid professor. His knowledge of the subject matter (Milton, in this case) is unparalleled, but he can tend to ramble on about things that nobody in the class understands. Two essays determine your entire grade, though I think he just takes the higher of the two.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Truly amazing.  Makes medieval literature incredibly interesting bc he's so passionate about the subject and interested what students have to say.  Must participate or you waste an amazing opportunity to learn about difficult material and honestly to learn a bit about moral living.  I took Milton and Chaucer and both are in my top 3 classes ever.

Best professor I've ever had.  Amazing knowledge of the material and with great discussions.  Offers incredible insight with historical context and knows everything about Christianity and medieval and ancient thought.  He makes even dense middle English texts come alive and shows how lively and relevant they are.  Took 2 of his classes, both awesom

Prof Aers is one of the top 3 best professors I've ever had. I took a course with him on Milton and was able to learn so much which really enjoying every moment of it. This is probably the only course I've ever taken where I've actually looked forward to every single class. Definitely don't miss a chance to take a class with him.

Aers's Milton class is the first English class I've had at Duke and is definitely one of my favorites. Prof. Aers is hysterical and makes the subject material super interesting. You definitely don't have to have a background in early modern lit or history or poetry to do well in the class. Very highly recommend.

This was his Milton class. Highly recommend taking it if you like Milton. Milton wasn't really my thing, but I still ended up with an A (though it was a little painful). He only assigns two papers, and uses the highest grade as your course grade. He's a really funny guy, loves to argue, so if you have an opinion and defend it he'll like you!

Professor Aers is one of the best professors I've had at Duke. He's brilliant, engaging, and seems genuinely interested in what the students have to say. Grades are based on two longish papers. Also, do the reading if you want to get anything out of the class. I highly recommend taking a class with Professor Aers
Perhaps the best professor I have ever had.

Professor Aers is incredible. Not only is he a foremost expert on what he teaches, but his passion for the subject is contagious. His knowledge of the history and culture of the Middle Ages is amazing. If you're willing to read a lot and participate in class, TAKE A COURSE FROM AERS. You won't regret it and you'll be a better reader/thinker for it.
Combines a wicked wit with penetrating literary insight and great warmth and kindness. Don't miss the chance to take a class with him.
Prof Aers is simply fantastic. he is an engaging teacher and really supportive of his students. I think everyone in my class thought he rocked. He is super intelligent.
this man is a dude. and he's hot. and he knows about medeival literature. no way is he crusty!

Whoever said he is a jaded Marxist is nuts. He's the best professor I've ever had. Absolutely brilliant. Has a great way with students, cares deeply about the texts discussed, has a great sense of humor, and every word he says is worth hearing. The class wasn't too hard, grade came from 2 papers. Do well on the last one and you're fine.
Brilliant, endearingly crusty.  No sugar coating, but also really fair.  Once wore a Winnie the Pooh vest.

Aers is brilliant, insightful, knows more about the middle ages than is healthy. But, from what I remember of his class, he is quite crusty, disdainful of those (especially undergrads) who don't share his appreciation for the good ol' days, whether they be the 15th century or the 1960s. Basically, a jaded Marxist, who won't meet you halfway on anyt

Professor Aers is my favorite professor at Duke.  He's brilliant, funny, and truly interested in getting to know his students.  He has had a profound impact on my academic career and life.  Do yourself a favor and sign up for one of his courses.

Prof. Aers is one of the best teachers I've ever had.  Even at 9am I loved going to his classes.  He seems to know everything there is about Middle English and has a nice way with students too--it's rare to have both qualities. I graduated seven years ago and wish I could remember it all.

Professor Aers is brilliant and at the top of his field.  He could make even the most disagreeable person like Medieval Lit. Plus, he's extremely approachable and very friendly. If you need a pre-1500 course for the English major, definitely take a class with Aers. In fact, take one regardless.
Awesome, awesome professor!! Love for math and students is undeniable, cracks funny jokes once in a while, made a hard course super interesting

Extremely enthusiastic about the course content and it shows in all of his lectures. He widens the scope of the class and the content covered is tough, but it's clear that if you put effort in you will receive the grade you want. Take 401 with him!

Dr. Slipper is a great professor and really cares about his students, both academically and emotionally. His course is difficult, but he strives for everyone to get an A, as long as you put fair work into understanding the content. He also makes the class fun, and is truly very enthusiastic about number theory (which slowly spreads onto everyone).

Such a great prof. So enthusiastic and genuinely passionate about math and teaching. Spent hours with students 1-on-1 in OH to help us understand concepts. The content was very difficult but grading was very lenient so it was not a high pressure environment. You should def take a class with Prof. Slipper if you can. Changed my life frfr
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very smart. Most passionate and knowledgeable math professor at duke. Very funny and cares about making the class interesting. Gives good lectures, sometimes he goes of track and you can get lost. But overall he cares about students actually learning and is super aproachable. Way better than most math prof at duke, would def recommend.

Took discrete math with Prof Slipper and he was extremely encouraging and enthusiastic. He made me excited to come to class. He will put in the effort to explain any questions you have without making you feel stupid for asking. So kind and a wonderful human being and teacher.

Probably one of the smartest professors at duke. Incredible passion and knowledge of math as a whole. He cares more about being able to understand the concept, rather than just getting correct answers. Gives exciting lectures and always the why and how behind each concept. His excitement and passion is contagious. Very hilarious and humble.

I struggled more in Dr. Franklin's class than I've struggled in any other class in my life. This was mostly my fault for falling a little behind with the lectures at the start of the semester due to personal issues, but after some poor midterm results Dr. Franklin helped me make a plan to catch up and it helped tremendously.Super cool material too!

My fav class and prof at Duke. I was struggling a bit with the material at first but Dr Franklin was super kind and helped me a lot. The class was also very helpful when it comes to getting into chip design. 100% recommend taking w/ Dr Franklin
excellent prof.  super friendly guy & learned a ton in his class.  he's very straightforward: prioritize this class to learn, and you'll do well.  fair deal!

Very cool guy and understands the material. Ask him questions if you are lost conceptually and you will get a lot from the class. I wouldn't recommend actually taking notes except for conceptual stuff because the homework is all plug-and-chug. Focus on the big ideas and do the practice tests. He is a very understanding guy and will work with you.
Franklin has engaging lectures and clearly cares about the content. He is also really accessible outside of class through office hours and ed posts. However, his tests are pretty hard.

This course deals with a LOT more content that I expected. There's a lot of equations throughout the course as well. Dr. franklin tries hard to make the course content as understandable as possible, so rewatching the lecture several times help a lot. He answers any questions kindly. He's also funny.

Professor Franklin is both incredibly passionate and effective at conveying ideas in his lectures. The material can be difficult but he provides lots of help through online Ed posts and abundant office hours. Would 100% take this course again.

Usually, a professor being intelligent and being good at teaching are mutually exclusive traits. However, Dr. Franklin is a rare exception. His class is organized and his passion for the subject is contagious. Though I have no intention of doing anything relating to this class in the future, I feel like the knowledge learned has made me a real ee.

The best trait of Dr. Franklin is that he understands the student perspective, which imo is one of the best qualities a professor can have. The content can be tough and seems inapplicable at first, but at the end you can see how everything ties together and can genuinely understand and apply it. Also a super funny guy and very fair grader.

Professor Franklin explains concepts a lot in class but doesn't write the explanations. We rewrote the notes every class, and it's hard to copy and process what he is saying at the same time. Lectures don't give many real applications, and throw diagrams at you without motivation for why they are important. MIT OCW and the textbook will be useful.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: It's clear that Dr. Franklin has taught this course many times, and he's very articulate when communicating the material. Sometimes he gets a little robotic, but that's not necessarily a bad thing, and he's very willing to answer questions and elaborate when prompted. I enjoyed this class.

ECE 230's material is pretty difficult, but Prof. Franklin is a great lecturer and breaks it down really well. The problem sets are long and difficult but are reflective of what you'll see on exams. He also curves the class if the exam averages are low. If you need help he has welcoming office hours.
Franklin is a clear, engaging, and passionate lecturer, gives fair exams, helpful in office hours, etc . One of the best professors at Duke and a great guy.

Incredible lecturer with the most well structured class I have taken in four years at Duke. He is super approachable outside of lecture, and has fair homework assignments that truly prepare you for the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Franklin really knows and loves his stuff, and he really wants you to know and love it too. Attendance is mandatory but it's well worth your time. Lengthy problem sets and reading quizzes each week are annoying in the moment but drive home the material. Tests are weighted fairly, and he's super helpful outside class. Take 230 with him!
He is what a teacher should be.

Dr. Franklin is a top-notch professor. He is enthusiastic, has clear requirements, and provides a carefully structured class experience. At the same time, he is good at adapting to the class needs and adds just enough difficulty to motivate students into cementing course concepts. Homework helps! The exam and group project were both fair.

He structures his class very clearly, and he lets you know what he expects. His homework sets aren't bad/long. He teaches really well, makes tough course material understandable and you can tell he's enthusiastic. Is very fair with respect to quizzes and exams (and sometimes very generous). Would definitely take this class, or any class, with him!

Great class and an excellent professor!  Made very advanced concepts that were previously foreign to me, very easy to understand.  Clear explanations and really great lectures.  Would definitely take a course from him again!

Dr. Hariri is the best neuroscience lecturer. He makes lectures so engaging, and although the attendance wasn't mandatory, everyone showed up because our tests are lecture heavy. He puts up 5-6 fill in the blank questions before each lecture and 90% of them are on our midterms. Final is optional but it's 100% a grade booster.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Loved this class! However-- the book is not enough to use to for exams, so going to lecture is needed. This being said, he is a great lecturer!

The class follows a clear pattern. Watch movies, write reflections, discuss in class. Do all of those things and you'll get an A. Despite how simple the class is, Prof H does a great job of making every discussion engaging and I was never bored despite the classes being 2.5 hours. If you have the chance to take this class, do it.

This is the second class I've taken with Professor Hariri, and he's an amazing, very knowledgeable professor. The class involves watching two movies each week and writing reflections, which is enjoyable . We discuss the movies in-depth, and everyone shares their thoughts. Participation is important but easy, and I highly recommend this class!

Really great lecturer who cares to make it interesting and doesn't just read off of slides. Super charismatic and nice as well. The tests aren't too hard and if you read the textbook and study, it's easy to do well. The class is only tests though, so it can be hard to stay motivated at times and it promotes just focusing on the tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Iconic. Take the class if you get a chance. The class average for each of the tests is 95%+ with even with 100+ students, but not because their easy, cause the material is so interesting and engaging that you actually learn in class, and feel inspired to study. Study the practice questions he puts up in lecture 90% will be on the exam.
GREAT PROFESSOR. HARIRI IS THE BEST. Four exams, not too difficult. Just make sure to read the textbook because... well he wrote it... LOL.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Fav class at Duke & most interesting! Attendance isn't mandatory, but HIGHLY recommend going to lecture because its not recorded, the slides have no text and the exams have content that aren't covered in the txtbook. Exams are 100% of grade. The textbook is a direct copy of the lecture and Dr. Hariri is approachable. Highly recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Amazing class! Attendance not mandatory, but I recommend going to every lecture since it is not recorded, the slides suck to study with, and 100% of the course is graded on exams. Dr. Hariri is an amazing lecturer and makes the material SO interesting/easy to follow - especially w/ his txtbook.

Professor Hariri is an amazing lecturer, he wrote the textbook which makes the classes so interactive. The class is test heavy, but the content is not difficult to learn if studying through the semester instead of cramming the weekend before. Recommend taking for sure!

While there are only 4 things that contribute to your grade in this class, the lectures and content of the class make up for it. The structure of Dr. Hariri's class is extremely easy to follow - each lecture comes straight from his textbook and as well as anecdotal information that he provides. Note taking and lecture going is made very easy!
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Super interesting professor who will leave you with a lasting love of neuroscience and the neuroscience of psychopathology. The lectures are perfect and they always felt short with how much I was engaged. The only problem with the class is how few tests there are (3 + final), and I think I would retain much more if the grading was weekly instead.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: AWESOME CLASS. The content is unbelievably interesting- it's a rare class where you're engrossed the whole lecture. There are only 3 midterms and a final for your whole grade which is daunting, but Hariri's grading criteria is crystal clear and you can tell he wants you to succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Without a doubt, he is the best professor I've had at Duke. Incredibly responsive with respect to email, invests in all of his students as both learners and people, and his grading criteria is very clear. Tests are a very fair reflection of lecture/textbook material, and lectures are fascinating. This course is a must-take.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The content of this class was interesting, but also very very specific. And with the tests being fill in the blank, he really makes you work for the grade. also, your entire grade is based on 4 exams, each weighted 25%. This isn't necessarily bad, but because the exams are tricky, it's difficult to recover after one bad exam
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: 10/10 Professor. Take this class if you get the chance! Not only is the material super interesting, but its broken down in a way thats easy for you to understand. Class grade is based only on exams. Prof Hariri is great and is an extremely engaging lecturer!
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: People like this class b/c it's easy, & the material is interesting. But it just didn't work over Zoom-- lecture recordings were not made available despite quickly glossing over difficult topics once only (bad for non-audio learners), & there were frequent unclear tangents. Exams are fill-in-the-blank from the book. Feel like I didn't learn :/

BEST PROF AT DUKE. Whoever gave him a 1/5 is pathetic...I'm sorry, I don't make the rules. SUCH engaging lectures and always there for the students. I wish he taught more classes, because I'd take all my neuro courses with him if I could. Best prof.
This class wasn't updated for being on Zoom at all. Dr. Hariri didn't even turn on his video.

Dr. Hariri makes neuroscience fun and accessible. Exams were uncomplicated and matched lecture/textbook material. Some topics were covered only in class, so make sure to attend lectures. Even over Zoom, this course was so engaging. Best of all, I understand how major brain circuits work now despite having almost no prior knowledge of neuroscience.
Without a doubt the best professor I have had at Duke - extremely fair, engaging, and truly prioritizes student learning. This class is a must if you have an interest in neuroscience!

Amazing professor, lectures are so engaging and easy to follow. Hariri is very kind and livens class up with jokes. He literally wrote the textbook so you don't have to worry about contradicting material; the textbook is just a helpful resource for you. Graded only by exams but exams were extremely fair, especially if you went to class. Take this!!

Second class I took with Professor Hariri, and it reinforced my opinion that he is one of the best professors I've had. Class is just 2 movies a week and 1 presentation throughout the semester. In-class discussions are intellectually stimulating and Professor Hariri does a great job of adding insight and pushing the conversation along.

Amazing lecturer and brilliant guy. Go to class, keep up with textbook readings (STUDY THE DIAGRAMS!), take notes for both, and you'll do fine. The exams are extremely clear and straightforward-- they hit all the key points of the material without being nitpicky with details. I had a great time in this class, and would 100% recommend.

Dr. Hariri is incredible! If you have even a slight interest in brain disorders, this is the class to take. He is one of the greatest lecturers Ive ever had, and the tests (4 of them) are super fair. As long as you read the book, come to lecture, and take notes... youll do fine. I would take his class again in a heartbeat.

Awesome lecturer and super interesting material. He doesn't post slides online and his tests are based on all lectures so you need to show up to class. He makes the material very accessible and understandable. Very lenient grading policies as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Hands down the best professor I've had at Duke. His tests can be difficult if you don't know the material and don't read the textbook, but he is very willing to meet and talk about how you can improve in the class. The material  has been the most interesting I've learned so far.

Hariri is a great guy. His class is 100% test grade (3 exams, 1 final), so be careful. Tests are heavily neuro based, so memorize the anatomy, all the studies, etc. He let my final count as my entire course grade, which improved my grade a lot. Lectures are interesting. His class is very fair and I highly recommend taking it.
Inside the Disordered Brain is the best class in the Neuroscience major, period. If you have any interest in the neuroscience of mental illness, then take this class!

Everything you want in a professor. Great public speaker, communicates concepts clearly and has a unique sense of humor that comes across in class. Based on intelligence alone, its a gift for Professor Hariri to take time away from his lab to teach undergraduates. Walking proof that great professors are great people..

Dr. Hariri is an amazing lecturer, and the material is really interesting. He is funny, helpful, and very clear in his lectures. The exams are based on lecture material only, and his Powerpoints don't have much detail, so you have to go to class-- but it is definitely worth it! Favourite neuro class so far.
Very engaging class. Challenging if you have no prior neuroscience background (like I did), but still possible if you are willing to find readings to cover the information that you need.
Phenomenal!

THE. BEST. PROFESSOR. AT. DUKE. From the very first lecture, I knew I was hooked. He is incredibly eloquent and very clear/concise in explaining the material. You don't even realize how complex the material is until after you've already learned it. He is super upbeat and energetic, makes class fun, and is more than willing to help any way he can.

Easily the best professor I have had at Duke! The material is fascinating, and Dr. Hariri presents it in a way that is very engaging. He is incredibly knowledgeable, but also very understanding, funny and a great guy. If you have any interest in neuroscience or psychology you must take this class!

He's one of the best professors I've had at Duke. He teaches with enthusiasm and clarity, and  often uses humor to keep the class interested. 3 tests are your whole grade so you need to go to every lecture and take good notes. Highly recommend to anybody interested in biology/neuroscience.

Best professor I've had at Duke, by far.  He's extremely knowledgeable of his material, very interested in his students and their success, and funny/eloquent.  The class itself is great too.  You learn more than you even thought was possible, but it's fun and fascinating material.  If you have the chance, take Dr. Hariri's class!!

Dr. Hariri is the best professor I've had at Duke. He's an expert in his field, and he's incredibly engaging in class. The material is cutting edge and fascinating, which makes it easier and more enjoyable to learn. I loved this class, anybody with a background in neuro/bio bases of behavior should take this course!
Great Professor! Really engaging and the course material is interesting. We did cover a lot of material but it was a enjoyable class!

had him for medicine ethics  & health policy focus cluster---and is my favorite professor ever!!! class was so intriguing because of his personality and his overall enthusiasm. although i admit that most of class was just him lecturing us and going on rants---he tied everything together towards the end. assignments r easy and the class is a free A!

Had him for Race & Language class in Medicine, Ethics, & Health Policy Focus. Very funny guy who made class enjoyable, but I honestly could not tell you a single thing I learned. There was no clear structure to the class, and he would kind of just talk about whatever he wanted and tell random stories. Felt like a waste of time on most days.

He is very knowledgeable about education and clearly cares a lot. He makes the course entertaining and adds very interesting readings. He is very caring and will work with you if you need an extension.
Great professor. Can be very understanding and flexible with deadlines. Good amount of writing throughout the course, but classes are light and entertaining.

Doesn't give much feedback on our work. Delays dates that he originally planned (having not returned some work one month after it was due). Tends to talk whatever pops up in his mind during his explanation of concepts, which is not good because after 15 minutes of explanation you still don't understand what he is talking about.

Professor Vadde is easily one of the best professors I've had at Duke if not the best. 
- Incredible class discussions
- Lots of reading, but she takes you through the entire evolution of fiction!
- Expects real college-level writing (don't expect to get by with high school 5 paragraph essays)
- Creative writing project at end of class

I took Artificial Intelligence in Literature and Film as a CS major. I don't enjoy english classes but I found this class pretty intellectually interesting for the most part. A lot of AI concepts in CS today have actually been pretty well reflected in literature over the past few decades. It was also pretty easy to get an A with very little HW!

Vadde is a great, caring professor, and this class was interesting surrounding lit. and tech. Most important thing is to do the readings which makes classes (discussions and questions around the texts) more enjoyable anyway. Grades outside of class are mainly 3 essays which are toughly graded but she gives good feedback and focuses on improvement.

My class with Professor Vadde was my favorite this semester. She was great at keeping topics interesting and relevant, and the reading was a lot but doable. We read a wide array of stories and had several fun assignments, like playing Minecraft and a creative final project. There were 2 graded papers which were tough but she gave helpful feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Vadde is brilliant. During discussion, she has an extraordinary gift of taking your half-baked idea and turning it into something complex. Fair and kind. Take notes on what she says; makes writing essays later easier. Do your reading! Prof. Vadde can't work her magic, if no one has read the latest chapter.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: This class was super interesting and Professor Vadde gave clear instructions on how to write good thesis statements and essays. My writing skills definitely improved because of this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Absolutely love her. Some people might rate her difficulty higher, but as someone genuinely interested in English the discussions were super engaging and there's only really three graded papers to stress about (the rest of the homework is mostly graded on completion). Come to office hours and get all the encouragement and wisdom in the world.

Professor Vadde is great! She guided our class through one of the toughest novels there is, Ulysses, and challenged us to rise to the occasion. The course was difficult, but it was never overwhelming. She fostered good discussion and really let the class go in the directions we found most interesting. Would highly recommend taking a class with her!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: She does a great job of exploring complex literary trends with grace. I highly recommend taking a class with her.

Vadde is a top professor in the English department. Her intellect and analytical prowess is humbling to see in action. You will be pushed to deeply engage with the course material and use critical thinking and logic to form your argument. Participation is required and she's not an easy grader, but you will leave a better thinker and writer.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: This woman is absolutely brilliant. If you have the chance to take a class with her, don't hesitate. She cares more about mental work than grades, her syllabus was impeccable, and she gives students voice in what they want to read and discuss. Take her class literally just to listen to what she has to say about some great books. Mind blowing.

Having taken both WRIT 101 & 255 with Colton, I can say he's my favorite professor at Duke. Colton is caring about his students, accommodating to their needs, and has a genuine passion for what he teaches. There is a solid amount of work, but the grading is straight forward and re-writes are possible. If you buy in, Colton is a phenomenal teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class wasn't life changing, but I really enjoyed it. He does a good job getting everyone to contribute to the discussion, and he is very reasonable with nightly readings. There were three papers, and the first two he allows you to revise for a regrade. He is super accessible and flexible with deadlines and really cares about his students.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Colton is genuinely really cool. Besides being very knowledgeable about writing center theory and practice, he is very easy to work with and super flexible when it comes to deadlines and attendance if you are having issues outside of class.

Professor Colton is great. He is very passionate about the class and truly cares what his students think of the material. If you have other commitments, he is very understanding and is also always there to chat. He lets students revise each of their papers so if you get a grade you don't like then it's not hard to change that. Take this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Pretty outstanding professor. Understanding, good at facilitating discussion, chooses good readings. Would recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Colton is clearly passionate about what he does. He curated a wonderful set of readings for our W101 class that it didn't really feel like homework. Class was great as well since it was mostly a conversation between everyone. Assignments were unique and interesting and it was obvious he cared about us. Highly recommend him
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Professor Colton is such a caring and kind professor. He really takes the time to get to know his students. His assignments are engaging and will teach students to think critically. I strongly recommend taking his course because of his flexibility, his compassion towards his students, and constant understanding to various circumstances.

Had Dr. Colton for Experiments in the Essay. Fun class with really interesting readings, and Dr. Colton is really good at fostering good class discussions. Cool guy all around, and definitely a pretty easy class (pass/fail for the win)
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: He gives very good lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures--Gives good feedback--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Decent lecturer, class set-up is awful (no incentive to pay attention in class because he doesn't grade papers and you choose your own topics). Very accessible and sometimes entertaining, also slaps himself on the face when he misspeaks.

One of the smartest guys I've ever met. Incredible lecturer--he makes dry material sound interesting and interesting material awesome. Very worldly and culturally knowledgeable (sports, entertainment, society). You determine your own grade based on self-chosen essay topics.
Nice professor.............

Amazingly helpful in office hours.  Go to them.  Pretty engaging lecture given the subject (linear algebra).  Tests aren't too bad.  If you can take linear algebra from Amir, do it.  You will learn linear algebra and it's probably the easiest that such a hard subject can be.

Extremely solid professor, great job at going in to detail and explaining things clearly. Doesn't just stand at the board and write like so many other math people do. Actually cares about his students and is willing to set up additional office hours to help if you need. Tests are quite reasonable for upper level math.
Best recitation teacher ever! Extremely clear, great at explaining complicated problems. Very knowledgeable and intelligent. Very willing to help you out and is an awesome guy to talk to.
TA for Math 107. Easily the only thing I liked about that class. If only linear algebra were as approachable and lucid and he was..

He was by far my favorite recitation professor. Every time I had a question he would answer it completely and perfectly. If he didn't the first time he would explain it a different way and in the end I always left with a full understanding of the subject. Without him I wouldn't have made it through the class. His office hours are a lifesaver!
Amir is AWESOME! He was a very engaging and clear recitation prof. Take advantage of his office hours - they're very helpful!

Dr. Abdulkadiroglu is one of the most caring and dedicated professors I've had at Duke. He loves participation and wants to meet with you outside of class. Very presentation heavy and you create a research proposal over the course of the semester which is difficult, but he is here for you every step of the way. I recommend if you're into education!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Most confusing professor I've ever had. The course had no clear scope, assignments came with zero guidance, and feedback was nonexistent unless you begged for it. He expects extra work without ever explaining the baseline. Often felt like he didn't know what the class was about.

Worst professor I've ever had. 

Tests were impossible and completely unfair based on what we covered in class. Atila is completely incapable of answering questions, yet is confused why his students don't understand the material. Can't understand a word of his lectures either.

Whatever you do, wait to take 201 with Nechyba.

His accent is thick and very difficult to understand very often while reading off the slides, and the class was incredibly math heavy with multivariable calculus concepts, so with the only prerequisite being calculus 111 by all means wait for another professor.

Ugh it was fine actually. I actually liked it because weekly assignments were optional and the whole grade was based off two exams. Didnt really do much work except the week of the exam. But dont expect to actually learn alot from him (his accent is very hard to understand) but he is a good guy
Nice guy but would not have taken this class again. Whatever you do, wait for Nechyba. Lectures are unhelpful and your best bet is to go to TA office hours.

Prof. A is probably one of the worst teachers I have ever had. He has an inability to explain himself during lectures and just reads off of his lecture slides. He NEVER replies to emails, even given how high priority they were (e.g. considering withdrawing from the class). He literally is at Duke for research so doesn't care about his students.

Prof A co-taught this class with Professor Vanberg. I did not enjoy Pro A's lectures at all. It was just hard to understand what he was teaching us. When he was the lecturer for the day (which was not too often) I would usually tune out and go over the material later. He is way better one-on-one, however. Office hours with him were useful.
Scheduled a review session and did not show up; never respond to students' emails

Avoid taking Econ 201 with Atila. While I do think he has good intentions, the grading is not fair. The lectures are not very useful as the only grades come from the highest of two midterms and one final (so 50% highest midterm, 50% your final). Feels impossible and unfair to succeed. Disappointed to have this experience in such a basic class
i wish i was not in this class

How to succeed: read the textbook and take advantage of TA discussion sections. I was super nervous going into this class based on the ratings, but especially with the curve, you should be fine as long as you put the work into understanding the content. The class is a grind, but most people end up doing fine in the end. Lectures not that helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I hate rating Atila so low but his teaching style was boring and hard to follow due to his thick accent. After 1st lecture only 20 out of 170 kids show up, tells you how useful going to lecture is: better spent on your own + asking TAs. If you have to take Econ w/ him, go to TA office hrs and study past midterms, your grade is 2 midterms + 1 final.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Yikes. Never had to work so hard to pass a class. Lectures are not very helpful and most students skip. Even if you understand the textbook, tests are still extremely hard. Your grade only depends on 2 midterms and 1 final, which is stressful since the exam avg. is around 60%. You can tell he cares and tries, but you kinda have to teach yourself.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Atila is a nice Professor who cares his students. He tries his best to let his students succeed. However, he is just bad at lecturing. Be prepared to ask TAs because the lectures are bothersome. Also, the tests seems to be much more difficult that he said, with questions you have never saw before. The final curve is nice, though.

He was an incredibly poor lecturer. They were typically difficult to follow, and he did a horrible job when it came to the more difficult contentglancing over it. The attendance to lecture fell every single time. He also does not care about the students whatsoever. His tests are also very difficult; they are poorly written.

Get ready to be really confused for an entire semester and never really understand what is going on. Atila has a very thick accent which can be difficult to understand on top of his already confusing way of explaining things. Grades are based exclusively on midterms and final but on the bright side, they are curved so you don't need a perfect score

I feel bad rating him poorly because he is a nice guy and is clearly knowledgeable in the field. As a lecturer, however, he moves through the difficult content too fast and many students have trouble understanding him. Lectures aren't very engaging.

This class was pretty awful. There felt like a huge disconnect between what Atila taught and what showed up on exams. The TA's ran the whole operation. Lectures boring and no one ever went. The only way to succeed was relying on TA problems and homework.
Classes are not very engaging but Atila cares and tests are really easy
the lecture is so unclear and the tests are extremely difficult
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Atila is probably best doing research than teaching - he would go in circles and make the simplest concepts more confusing and just read off of lecture slides. Most everyone stopped going to class and instead went Head TA Chelsea's office hours since she wrote the exams - take it with her because she is excellent

Atila is a very respected scholar in his field and an amazing professor. He is very accessible, teaches very systematically making sure concepts are clear in everyone's head. He means extremely well and is a reasonable person. I took two classes with him and they were the best two classes I took at Duke. Duke Econ needs more people like him!

His accent is a bit hard to understand at first, but once you get used to it, not a big deal. Great professor who wants his students to succeed; lectures are clear although somewhat boring; tests are not difficult -- he just wants to see that you understand the main concepts and have learned the material. Take 201 with him if you can.

Atila tries, but doesn't quite pull it off. His lectures are long and dull, and it's definitely more beneficial to skip class and read the textbook then to go to lecture.  His grades are ambiguously graded with major inconsistencies and no corrections.
He has an incredibly thick Turkish accent that makes it very hard to understand. Lectures are also on the boring side.
If you want to learn, take it with Nechyba.
Underrated!

Absolutely loved Atila. You have to pay attention in class to understand his Turkish accent, but past that it's really not bad. The tests are very reasonable and based completely off the homework. He will answer your questions in class, and he will meet with you outside of class if you really want to. You get out of this class what you put into it.
difficult to understand, reads lecture directly off his powerpoint, never seems to cover the more difficult material
he was absolutely terrible

Atila is pretty useless as a teacher. The lecture are really boring and he never seems to cover the most difficult parts of the material. By the end of the year a class of 120 had about twenty people regularly showing up. The only redeeming characteristic is that he moves really slowly so there's not too much material to learn on your own.
Interesting class, learned a lot. If you keep up with the lecture slides and book readings, you should be fine. Easier than Nechyba.

Very difficult class, although easier than 51 since it is curved. Went to the first lectures and all he did was read the slides which are online and which are direct from the book. Read the book, get live graphs, do problems, and go to TA sections and if you stay caught up you should do fine.

It's a pretty standard by-the-book econ class. Prof. A means well and I can't say anything truly bad but he has a pretty thick accent, Griffith is a large auditorium, the class is at 8:30 in the morning, and the lectures go online (as they should) so it is very hard to pay attention. TAs are useful. Problem sets every week but not graded.

Professor Antepli is a very inspirational human being who is full of wisdom. As a person, I like him a lot, and I enjoyed Pubpol 302 for the variety of content we covered, despite it being a little all over the place. His grading criteria are very unclear, and he does not send feedback, so you have to schedule time with him to go over your essays.

Do not take him. Abdullah is not accessible outside of class, no clear grading criteria, zero feedback on midterm or final papers. He starts off inspirational but lectures become repetitive and boring. Guest lectures are great.

Do not take him. If you are even the slightest bit shy, avoid. Grading is extremely arbitrary, with no feedback at all on papers. Seems inspiring at first, but he picks favorites and alienates non-religious students. Class discussions feel performative. You won't have any idea at your grade until it appears in DukeHub, which is so frustrating.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof Antepli is a great lecturer, but unfortunately is inaccessible to the class. He gives no feedback on midterms, journal entries, and seems to arbitrarily assign grades which is frustrating for such a workload intensive class. Seems to choose favorites and goes along with that.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Not my favorite class. Too many guest lectures to make for a coherent semester and no real sense of what we should be taking away to help us with careers in public policy.

He claims to read everyone's notebook entries every week. (~300 pages of writing in less than 24 hours, every week). No feedback on anything throughout the semester. He is a great lecturer, and has incredibly interesting stories and perspectives to share, but like the previous comment said, he is just too busy to teach this class well.

I have to second the last review. It seems this class has gone downhill in quality each iteration he teaches it. He kept getting promoted and it was clear this class was nowhere near his top list of priorities.

Busy course but not rewarding. Weekly writing assignments of ~1000 words and a 20-page final paper. He was impossible to reach outside of class, and left ZERO comments on midterm or final. Office hours got canceled and ignored when we followed up. Our last class, he said he couldn't meet anyone. He ignored emails too, even after finals.

Hands down most influential professor in my life so far. I was excited for lectures every day, and took away more from them on a personal level than I ever could have expected. He values discourse and outside opinions and respects everyone equally. Overall and outstanding human being.

Professor Antepli is the BEST. Hes so caring and eager to get to know you and how he can best support you. Hes understanding, engaging, and has such cool experience he shares with you. Learning about religion/pub pol from someone who has literally worked in the White House on an interfaith council is just incredible. Make sure you FLUNCH him!

Abdullah is awesome! He's funny, wise, and brings the most interesting guest speakers to class. Most ethics classes I've taken were relatively boring, but not this one. A moderate amount of papers required but completely doable. Don't take 302 with any other prof.

An amazing, funny, and friendly person. His class is really enjoyable. Basically a discussion class with weekly readings and short papers every other week. Material is very interesting and class is lively.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: Prof Antepli is INCREDIBLE- one of the most genuinely caring and passionate professors I've had at Duke. He doesn't bog down the class with too many dense readings about moral philosophy. Instead, he shapes class discussions around real-world policy problems with lots of amazing guest speakers. TAKE THIS CLASS!!!

Professor Antepli is INCREDIBLE. Hands down my favorite professor at Duke. He is so kind and caring and is someone who wants to really see you engage in the material rather than worry about your grade. I'm not into ethics discussion, but he made it fascinating and engaging. The class is also doable work-wise. LOVE HIM! TAKE THIS CLASS!

All around terrible experience. Prof is rude and boring. Worst thing is that all the readings are from 10+ years ago (some more like 20) & we are expected to talk about them as if they are current / use them to talk about the current middle east. It seems like he designed the class years ago and never updated it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: Id be cautious of taking his classes. This teacher is the most subjective grader youll come across at Duke. Your midterm and final essays will only pass if you essentially word by word repeat what the textbook says. The professor will take points off if you miss any piece of information. The teacher is an extremely subjective grader.

Do not take this class. While it is easy to get an A, the lectures are extremely boring and the class is organized in the worst way possible. The assigned textbook is equally dry and uninteresting. Shame since the class has so much potential to be engaging, but I struggled to find the motivation to go to class.
Professor Maghraoui is understanding, empathetic, and passionate about his materials. While POLSCI322 was graded by few things, I learned a lot from the readings he assigns.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Genuinely cares for his students and wants them to learn and do well. Teaches an interesting course on a topic most would never think of doing research in. The class is based on discussion rather than a set syllabus. You have to write a 20-25 page final paper but as long you do the research, you will get a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Great guy who really seems to care about the material. Only a few grades throughout the semester and not very clear on the grading criteria. Not much feedback given on assignments, but learned a lot in this class. Pretty average class.

I thought he was going to be an easier grader than he actually was.  He looks for a lot of specifics in the essays, which you obviously don't know beforehand.  You have to kind of guess what he's looking for and squeeze it into the 5 pages you have.  But the class is interesting, and I learned a lot about the Middle East.
If you go to class and do the readings, you'll get an A. He is a fairly interesting lecturer and grades tests and the presentation easily.
Easy course, good professor. Thick accent but not too difficult to understand. Lots of class discussion.

Really knows his stuff, unfortunately class didn't turn out well/like he intended. Dry lecturer but to be fair hardly anyone raised their hands when he opened discussion so failure was 50/50 shared blame, especially after people stopped going a few weeks in. Readings not mandatory except ones on midterm/final. Takehomes weren't difficult. At all.

this class should have been amazing but was a definite disappointment.  maghraoui knows his stuff but doesn't know how to lead a discussion so class was painful-mostly hour long monologues.  though if you're looking for a class with minimal work (though not necessarily an A), this is the class for you.  he assigns readings but no one did them.

Took Chinese Buddhist Art class. Has such a plethora of knowledge as an art historian in this area. Gave us the opportunity to seek out what was interesting to us about Chinese Buddhist art and was extremely helpful for all graded works; a great resource in general. Probably my fav course and prof at Duke so far. Work load is light!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Abe was an okay guy but he had no problem bashing a students work in front of the class.  He would laugh or make fun of students that were nervous or weren't sure what was going on
Enjoyable enough.

Professor Abe was one of the worst professors I've had I Duke. Kids are either on his good side or bad side and if you end up on the bad side, its very hard to save your grade. Overall...just don't take him.
really really nice and helpful guy, not very interesting though (but easy :))

Though the class was boring at times, overall I think it's worth looking into.  Dr. Abe's a pretty nice guy and a relatively straightforward grader.  Bring a pillow for the weekly class discussions, though!

He was by far the worst prof. I have ever had.  He is a prick, very unhelpful and  self centered.  If you don't believe me ask anyone who has had him before.  The grad students told me to avoid him like the plague- no one wants to work with him.  Consider this your warning.

Dr. Abrahamsen lectures in a bored monotone that implies a boredom for the material. The coursera course was easy to use and the quizzes were based on the coursera practice quizzes. Very boring class, but manageable, especially during a summer at the Marine Lab. One of the best, easiest courses at the Marine Lab that allows you to enjoy the campus.

Subject sucks but major requirements usually do. Tavis tries his best and is pretty approachable/nice, but isn't the best at making such dry material accessible or interesting. You NEED to keep up with Coursera bcs if you fall behind its way too hard to catch up. The coding lab is not fun and the TAs aren't super helpful. Try to make a study group.

It's not the prof's fault but the flipped nature of the class is bad design. You are quizzed before the unit starts based on coursera videos that you watch at home, and then lectured on the exact same material a second time in class. Attendance is checked by multiple clicker q's per class. Not difficult at all, but lecture felt pointless.

Tavis has a super boring personality when he lectures, he got fed up with the lack of participation a few times which was kind of crazy because the class is set up so you HAVE to learn almost all of the material yourself from videos. It is impossible to pay attention when you've already learned all the material outside of the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Class is just a repeat of the Coursera videos with some application exercises/clicker questions thrown in. Lectures are a little dry but not too bad. Grading is fair but can vary slightly by TA. Don't leave out any work during exams. Thankfully, the problems are similar to the homework sets (which are more time-consuming than difficult).
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Underrated. His lectures are kind of dry/boring, but they're also very clear and to the point.

STA101 is obnoxiously standardized. I can't fault tavis bc all STA101 profs use the same lectures, tests, etc. He's good with pushing back deadlines, answering Piazza & lecture questions, and that's all you can really ask for bc all STA101 classes are the same. A lot of busy work and quizzes, but you learn a LOT. The group work is hell though.

Tavis himself is fine. One on one with him is rare but helps. Using a flipped class is a poor way of teaching this class. He just repeats the videos and grades attendance on a shaky system of clicker use. I say shaky because if you have problems with your clicker, he is unwilling to help. Grades decided by TA. Takes forever to get grades back.

Unapproachable, unsuccessfully applies flipped class approach (too little time to work through problems), does not listen to mid-semester student input, and doesn't negotiate grades (prob. because he's a new professor and doesn't want to get labeled as lax). Take with another professor if at all possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: The class is flipped, but attendance is still required. Very counterintuitive. He sometimes gets in-class questions wrong or can't explain answers... The class itself is very easy.

Professor Abrahamsen is very helpful, thoughtful, caring, and is also very knowledgable about his subject.  I would disagree with previous students' lower ratings of him. I definitely think he deserves better, considering that STA 101 itself can be a dry subject at times. If there is a lot of work, it's because the STA department standardizes it.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Not a great lecturer but knows his stuff and is helpful at office hours. The class is easy if you watch the online videos and do the psets.  Tests are straightforward and pretty similar to practice tests. So not a hard class but not the most interesting either. Attendance is part of your grade though.

Prof. Abrahamsen made helpful materials really accessible (free online videos and textbook), but his system of making us learn at home and then reteaching everything doesn't make sense to me, and even he seemed bored by his lectures. But tests are fair and if you put in the work it's not hard to do well.
Ben is one of the most respected professors at Duke, I really loved his class. Ya Mama

Great man but generally disorganized. Arabic is tough as it is, and I honestly felt like this class was just a little difficult to follow over course of semester. Tests incredibly difficult in my opinion.
Arabic and humor is a difficult thing to combine, but Ben has done it, He is hilarious. When it comes to explaining grammar no one like him, Brilliant.
Great Prof, helps you with what you need learn, if you don't get it he'll explain it in another way. He entertains his classes, loves to have fun. One of the best professors I've ever had. :)
Great, innovative teaching style. Really knows his stuff. Open to criticism and feedback and has a good balance between a laid-back but hardworking class environment
VERY BEST INDEED!
A great teacher, a great person, a great friend, and a great class. Would defiantly take this class(Arabic 211) again or any class he teach's if I need to in the future. Makes learning fun. Ya Mama.
I took 284 With Ben he is really nice guy, He cares a lot about the students  I really enjoyed his class I would take it again  One of the best professors I ever had

He is a good and clear instructor of the Arabic language and is also pretty funny. He's a super nice guy and wants to give you an A. He rarely checks homework and doesn't punish too harshly if you miss assignments. He does go off the text book a lot so it feels unproductive sometimes, but its just a new set of vocab.

I've hated every math class I've taken since 3rd grade, but Professor Abel was so clear, concise, and responsive to feedback/questions that not only did I understand the course content, but I enjoyed the class. I've never had a better math professor.
Great professor overall, but sometimes goes too quickly in class due to the syllabus
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Great math professor and a really nice, kind guy.

He clearly wants students to learn the material which is evident by his quick and thorough responses to emails regarding questions. Also, he is very willing to answer any questions during class and is very accessible during office hours where he slowly explained anything that was confusing. The material was tough but tests fair and like final.

I took this class my first semester at Duke, and it was really, really hard. It did not help that it was Prof Abel's first time teaching the class, as well. That said, he definitely cares about his students, and he is good at explaining problems if you only ask (which few students do). I expect that over time he'll teach the material better.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Love Abel. He's the man. Multi is an extremely hard class at Duke, but Abel makes it bearable.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Multi sucks but Abel is the best! Had him for multi and linear and found him extremely helpful and encouraging in both. He is always welcome to meet up and hosts office hours several times a week! If you need to take a hard math class definitely try to get Abel.
I really enjoyed Professor Abel's class.  He is always eager to help and really wants everyone to learn.  His office hours are very helpful!
fantastic

To a first approximation, Dr. Grunwald doesn't enjoy teaching and goes out of his way to belittle his students. He expects students to treat his class as if it is their only responsibility yet can't seem to be bothered to take the time to make expectations clear or grade things in a timely manner. Here's the punchline: he needs to actually retire
No comment
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: So as a personal crime a Grindlewald of however that one Harry Potter movie goes, my only crime was wanting to be a Milky Way.
Good guy. Really enjoys lecturing and cares about his students. Definitely learned a lot in Grunwald's class.

Grunwald is a solid professor who is very knowledgable about physiology. You have to put in effort for the class but Grunwald has so much political commentary it's annoying. Feels like im in a political science or sociology class with the amount of political opinion in the class
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: If you're a pre-med, Dr. G's physiology class might be one of the most important classes you have at Duke. Dr. G helps bring together everything else you've learned. There is so much material in this class, but Dr. G is super accessible outside of class. It's hard, but study for quizzes carefully and you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: -Dr. G's a very good lecturer. Makes physiology interesting and interactive. -Lot of details, but definitely not just a memorization class. The biweekly quizzes are application heavy. Dr. G's great about meeting outside of class, and will really help you get the concepts down. -Not an easy class. But definitely possible to do well in.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Great professor that really enjoys teaching the material. The class is hard and sometimes difficult to understand but amazingly helpful when studying for the MCAT. Highly recommend just for the interesting lectures!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Class is easy conceptually. but the quizzes are not possible to understand because they are so poorly written. Makes getting a good grade impossible even when you understand all the material. DO NOT TAKE 329 WIH HIM
Great lecture. Assignments and quizzes hard to understand. Unclear wording. Cares a lot though. good guy

Super nice and cares about all his students. Very interesting material - he takes everything you've learned about living organisms and explains the "why". Really tries to answer everyone's questions or stay after to answer them. No exams, just HW and quizzes. Wording can be confusing but just clarify at office hours and you'll be fine.

Dr. Grunwald is a very underrated professor. He's an excellent lecturer and is very helpful during office hours. Exams were difficult but fair. Take good lecture notes and you will do well in this class. Highly recommended instructor.

Discussion sessions were very helpful in understanding the exam/lecture material. A wonderful lecturer (his humor transcended the students' interest in physiology). His exams are hard but you'll do fine if you understand the lecture material (they do not test rudimentary memorization, but comprehension) and do the problem sets.

Class itself is very intersting, but not the guest lecture except 1. If you study his problem set and review the lecture front and back, it is doable to get an A without touching the book once. Granted, you have to write well in the lab, which I didn't, and it take way too much time. Take this class if u have time and want to challenge yourself.

i agree that the book is useless for 151, his lectures and study questions are the most important. going to class is absolutely necessary, and he's kind of a jerk to you if you miss class. office hours are also very helpful; i think he makes his tests the night before and he'll often include topics that were discussed during his office hours

Very knowledgeable. However, gets sidetracked sometimes. Never really finished a lecture because he'd talk a lot about the material. Focused a lot on the biochem/small detail stuff. Tests were a bit difficult (average around 75) with a mixture of multiple choice and short answer. Do the practice problems! The book is useless.
Fortunately, Grunwald's an excellent lecturer, as class attendance is pretty important if you're going to succeed in BIO 25. The lab section is pretty grueling.

Dr. Grunwald is extremely approachable - go to office hours if you have questions!  Also, be sure to take detailed notes during lecture, because he says a lot of things that are not on the slides.  I thought he was a very engaging lecturer, though.  Tests will go beyond just facts.

Dr. Grunwald is a great professor, very energetic and lively.  But Bio 25 is definitely a hard class.  His lectures assume you've either already had AP bio or knew it beforehand.  I reiterate the comment below about TA office hrs being helpful. Also read the book because Grunwald & Motten talk too fast to understand it from class. Try hard in lab.

I had him for BIO 25 and 151 and I think he is one of the best lecturers at Duke.  Some complain his tests are difficult but I guess that depends on what you are comparing them to.  (as a BME I felt the tests were interesting and fair, really tested understanding not memorization)  Great professor just pay attention in lecture and you will be fine.

BIO 25 IS A VERY VERY HARD CLASS!  That being said, you CAN do well, you just have to work your butt off.  You need to go to TA Office Hours and ask them all your questions, & skipping Lecture is NOT an option with these guys-they don't put e full ppts online.  Dr. G is engaging and a great guy though. TA office hrs are way more helpful than his.

Dr. Grunwald was one of my favorite professors.  He is actually good at teaching, engaging, and available outside of class for help.  Ask questions! Tests are challenging. They test understanding of material and the ability to manipulate information. Ex: understand processes AND how possible mutations can occur.  Studying practice questions helps!

interesting lectures, but tended to digress. very accessible via email. also had a brilliant TA. very hard class generally... lots of content, exams demanded tremendous understanding and application, not curved in the end, which was crazy. but bio25 is probably one big weeder.
He is a good professor in that his lectures are good and his test focus on really understanding and applying the material. However, he curves the class rather unfairly.

Grunwald is TOUGH. His lecture style keeps you engaged, but his tests are absolutely killer. Hardest I've had at Duke. The labs in 151 are actually fun - you are the subjects - but the assignments are NEVER ENDING (lab reports, research papers, etc). I would avoid enrolling in this class unless you have an easy semester otherwise.
