Dr. Grunwald was very enthusiastic about the topic of this seminar (biotechnology and genetics). He didn't really teach it as a seminar, but that is a minor complaint. Very willing to meet with you outside class regarding presentations or papers.
seminar with him was fun.  he's a good guy and knows what he's talking about. he's willing to meet as much as you need to outside of class to help with presentations and papers.

A great professor.  Really interesting lectures, one class that I actually enjoyed getting up early to get to.  Some people had issues with the way tests were set up but I never really had any issues.  As people have mentioned he is extremely helpful and typically holds review sessions before tests that I always found to be a great resource.
His lectures and his tests rarely ever matched up. Read the book. Maybe you'll pass.

He told us that reading the book really wasn't necessary, but I think it is if you want to know enough info to give a full credit answer on a test.  Also really crappy how they don't normalize lab grades- be sure to get a nice TA.

A wonderful, wonderful professor! Lectures are often hard to follow and he goes WAYin depth for material. The exams are super difficult, but if you can figure out the format of his questions, they become much easier.  ASK QUESTIONS before, after class!  He is SUPER helpful, eager to help, and is very, very accessible!One of best professors I've had
Dr. Grunwald is good and knows what he is talking about (he actually knows way too much), but he's tough

Grunwald is an enthusiastic and helpful professor. Exams are quite hard, and require deep understanding of the material and some thinking out of the box. Be prepared for his family anecdotes, to which he draws somewhat questionable parallels to biology.
This class ruined my life. His lecture was not helpful at all in exams. His exams were way too hard for me.

I thought Grunwald was a great professor. His lectures were very enthusiastic and therefore interesting.  Definetely go to class and take notes. The tests only deal with material covered in class, although they are almost exclusively application based. Use practice tests to study. This is very helpful.

Great teacher...rough tests...but you either get it or you don't...it's possible to cram and do well if you're a good test taker. Fun to talk to because he won't stop and is a bit arrogant. The material is still interesting even if your grade is lukewarm.

His tests are quite challenging. Definitely, this class tests you on writing good paragraph not on biology. I will never recommend this class to anyone. His lecture is way too fast although the lectures are not very helpful for tests.

Grunwald loves to teach and he does a good job of it.  He's passionate about biology, if you like bio, you will find this class interesting.  Tests are harder than you would expect, but just practice the technique for answering the questions.  If your having trouble, go talk to him...it WILL help!

Co-taught with Hyman. Very random lecture notes, talks way too fast and goes off on tangents on things you don't need to know in such detail on exams-- but they're very interesting and things you see in later classes in Bio. He is very helpful in test review sessions - GO TO THEM! Tests were hard but fair, just more than simple memorization.
Horrible class, prof, it sucked, studied my ass off for test and continually lost 7+ out of 10 points b/c of small technicality. premed weeder
His lectures put you to sleep and his tests were pretty hard

I can honestly say after taking his class that I will never take a lab class at Duke ever again.  While he can make some lectures interesting, a lot of times he is pompous or insulting.  The tests are really hard as well.

really excited about biology. covered lots of details for an introductory course, but that made it interesting. sure, most of the exam material comes from lectures, so you might have to actually attend a few, but unlike some of the other individuals, that seems like a fair expectation to me. overall a good professor and made the course enjoyable.

Lectures are boring and notes are almost completely worthless when looking back at them.  His tests are way too hard and they expect you to write specific words to get points.  If you go to every single lecture then studying isn't a big deal, though.  Avoid him if you can.
made me lose all interest in biology and research altogether, terrible advisor to anyone (has an attitude problem)
No Comments
Terrible teacher, very arrogant and very boring, unclear in lecture.

He's pretty arrogant. His lectures are interesting and will definitely get you thinking, but his grading policies are also rather arbitrary and if you don't participate, you're doomed. And by participate, I mean lead almost every discussion (at least in the seminar class that I was in). If you HAVE to take him, be careful. If you can avoid it, do.
challenging class, but he is very helpful and will answer any question you have thoroughly

this guy is very arrogant, he can be helpful/straightforward when he's in the mood, but that's seldom. you almost feel like he's out to get you the way that he talks down to you. i just wish he'd lighten up and realize a C really isn't an excellent grade
Great lecturer, very hard tests though, you REALLY have to attend lecture to know what is going on

One of my favorites professors here at duke, although I can understand how he could be preceived as arrogant or unhelpful by many people.  Unless this is your first bio class, I would highly recommend Grunwald (over Alison Hill in the Fall)
arrogant, difficult to reason
Although he is engaging in lecture, when it comes time for the exams you realize he really didn't make ANYTHING clear.  Definitely agree about the arrogance
No Comments

When you meet him, do not be fooled by his "chill" attitude. He liked to achieve a gleeful state off of trying to confuse freshmen and was very successful at discouraging learning by making you feel like a complete idiot!
he is nice ... approachable if you are sincerely interested in his course
Awful. Totally unfair experience for anyone without a background in cellular biology. He's arrogant and lacks the ability to LINEARLY describe very easy AND hard concepts. Just an ass.
Run in the other direction. He might look like Santa, but he's pure evil.
No Comments
interesting and funny lectures, knew his stuff, and always willing to help
No Comments
No Comments

As long as you try, you should be able to get a decent grade in the class. He is a very smart man with a great memory. He knew everyones name by the end of class. Doesn't belive in generic teaching styles, which is a plus! He also makes sure you learn things that will not only better yourself, but those around you as well! Take him!
Ong has moved to HPU this year and I could not have enjoyed his class more. Very helpful and gives great real world examples.

Do the work and you will get a good grade. This course (Business Ethics) may be intimidating  because it throws a lot of financial concepts at you, which you likely aren't familiar with if not an Econ major. But as long as you at least try to understand these concepts, James will be happy with you.

Took this class over the summer. Its cross -listed with Ethics and we spent the whole summer going over Business Ethics.  The subject matter was interesting at times.  No long papers but there was a class presentation but it wasnt hard. You have to do the readings and participate.  Not a hard class at all, but not a really really easy class either.

Ong is a great guy. Don't be discouraged by his class in the first week, it worth sticking around for. He introduces philosophy really well and makes the topic interesting. Willing to help you on any project or any assignment you are confused on. Make sure to take advantage of his helpfulness!

James was a great instructor and very passionate about the subject matter. He has extremely enhanced my academic writing ability and my knowledge of philosophy. Subject matter can be hard, but he goes out of his way to help you under. He was extremely accessible and helpful! Just overall a great person and instructor!

If you have any other options, DO NOT take his class. The materials are very fun, but his lectures are BAD. He tried to go through everything in class but makes everything confusing. The grading system is simply ridiculous. HW takes up a huge amount of final grade. Any small mistake in the HW would cost you a letter grade lower.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I had a 94% and my grade was input as an A-. I thought this was a mistake so I emailed and he said his A range was above 95%. This was not in the syllabus and this range or that the class was on a downward curve was not mentioned in class. I've dealt with bad Econ classes at Duke but being misled to believe I had an A all semester tops the list.

It's impressive to know a professor who makes the easiest material into the worse class ever. The lecture is mid but all the graded assignments are a mess. The instructions are never clear. Good luck guessing what he wants to see on an assignment. The grading criteria is also very vague and the grader doesn't know what score to give. Tough grader.

She's a very clear, helpful, friendly, organized professor. The class required quick quizzes after every class to show that you were in attendance. The homework involved seeing how much improvement you could get over a benchmark, which sometimes this took a very long time.

She was very good, and I would take her class again.
Great lectures - covers everything you'd want to know about NLP and more. Homeworks are time-consuming but not necessarily challenging.

There isn't an RMP page for Monica?! She is a great professor, new to Duke, with valuable lecture delivery, and is accessible after class. Additional notes: Be aware that the homework can be time-consuming, so start working on it as early as possible. Monica offers bonus points, and grades are generally 1-2 points up before applying the bonus.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: There are weekly problem sets that can take a lot of time to complete, but Dr. Agazzi is good about having office hours and helping. He was also very generous with his grading. Before class, he puts all of his notes online, which can be helpful for following along in lecture, but his handwriting can be difficult to read.

He grades quizzes very generously, and I got better grades than what I expected for several times. He is always accessible outside class, whether that's hosting additional office hours or asking for clarification for homework.

He is very nice and proactively asks for feedbacks from students during lectures. His lecturing is quite clear too (although the handwriting is sometimes confusing). Tests are reasonable. The final is a little hard but okay.

Professor Agazzi is definitely a nice guy, and seems very approachable outside of class. But his teaching is pretty average, and lectures tend to get very dry. The class isn't too hard (I would say like your average 200-level math class at Duke), and watching the asynchronous lectures was sufficient to get a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Super super nice person. is willing to work with you in a moment's notice -- he'll extend office hours on zoom by literally 2 hours if it means he can help one student. his midterms were super reasonable (the final wasn't though). and he's just a good person to be around. he knows his stuff and I 10/10 recommend him

Dr. Agazzi is great! Stats isn't really my thing, but he's clear, concise, and open to feedback/questions if you have any. He gets really into the technical details of formulas, and sometimes it gest a bit confusing on how to actually apply those formulas, but when we told him that he went and included more examples, so all was well.
Prof. Agazzi is amazing at explaining theoretical ideas, and he is always well prepared with effective examples. He is also very friendly and responsive if you ask for help and clarification.
She was nice enough. She doesn't teach here anymore though!

HAHA, these comments make me laugh (although they're totally accurate). Only take Spanish with her if you already know the material well and you're enterained by crazy people. I had a good Spanish background in HS so she didn't stress me out, so I enjoyed the freakshow every week. I don't think she teaches here anymore.
No Comments

HORRIBLE TEACHER. a grad student who doesn't want to be in class, is never prepared, is horrible at explaining, and a ridiculously hard and unfair grader. i like jaditza as a person, but DO NOT take spa101 with her. you will want to kill her and eventually yourself. DO NOT TAKE SPANISH 101 with her.
SAVE US FROM HER!!

His passion and immense knowledge of the material shine through in his amazing lectures, and he puts a lot of energy into building topics up step by step and explaining them intuitively. While each homework has a few pretty hard problems, he is very helpful during office hours, and his tests are always reasonable and never harder than the homework.

Prof. Levine deeply cares about his students and wants them to succeed. He talking about the problem sets in groups and going to OH. The course is rather straightforward and partners VERY well as an optional coreq with analysis 431 or 531. Super weird grading scheme that makes the final immensely important, but that means you can always catch up.

Fantastic. Content was hard toward the end of the semester but the grading formula makes it so that if you do well on the final you're set and the final was easy. Great lectures; made me love the subject tbh. He draws out concepts with diagrams and just explains things really well. Funny and happy guy, I always looked forward to his class.

His lectures are really good; he provides clear examples for the concepts and does a great job answering questions. He often reviews definitions from past lectures, which helps with keeping up. He's also helpful during OH and cares about students succeeding in the class. The grading is weird: if you do well on the final, that's all that matters.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Don't listen to person below me, class was very hard and it was difficult for me to even pass the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Tests were very reasonable (especially the final exam) and homework adequately models the difficulty of the exams. Take good notes and review and you'll be solid.

He explains concepts fairly well. His exam were a lot harder than his homework with a mean around 75-80. But somehow he is impressed by a C range mean and he will not curve (gives minimal curve) the final letter grade. According to his grading rubric you will need to at least get a 90%+ on the exams to even think about an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Adam Levine is the worst Math professor at Duke. He can't explain math to his students in a clear way. The midterms are 100 times harder than the homework, which is absolutely misleading, as he gives no preparations for the exams. Honestly, his lectures are useless (the book sufficed). Never had to put so much work into a class as this one.
He is a really good teacher but he usually teaches stuff that's irrelevant to the homework or the exams. Also, exams are much harder than homework, so it's hard to know what to expect from them.
Id take every class with Dr. Levine if I could

As others have noted, this class is really hard, but Levine was a fair grader and always helpful during office hours. Expect homework to take a long time each week. The class was curved generously at the end as well.

Linear algebra is a really difficult course, regardless of who you take it with. Professor Levine is a very smart individual, but he sometimes struggles to break down challenging mathematical concepts and his lectures are somewhat disorganized. That being said, his exams are fair, and he wants all of his students to do well in his course.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Math 221 is one of the most notoriously difficult courses at Duke, no matter who the professor is. Despite this, Professor Levine is great at breaking down complicated concepts and explaining them effectively. There is a lot of time-consuming homework but he is very accessible in office hours and he knows what he's talking about.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I've learned a lot about both proofs and linear algebra from Levine's class. Reading the textbook is crucial and I also recommend 3Blue1Brown and MIT Open Courseware's videos to supplement your learning. The tests aren't too bad if you study and he does curve them a fair amount. Overall, Professor Levine is a solid choice for 221.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Standard math teacher, fairly good at explaining things and cracks jokes in class. Is very open to office hours, holding them multiple times a week. For 411 the tests are fairly difficult, with averages in the 60s, but your success in the class likely depends on how much math background you have.

Easily one of the best classes I've taken at Duke. She explains tough, math heavy topics in a super clear step-by-step way that actually makes things click. Lectures are well-structured, focused on understanding not memorizing and she genuinely cares that students follow the logic. Highly recommend!
I didn't like the flipped classroom approach that much but I found doing problems during class solidified my understanding of the concepts. Also the homework sometimes took my a very long time to do.

Easily among the best profs I've had at Duke. Amazing lecturer and very fair grader. Class is flipped so you watch lecture videos outside of class and spend class discussing and solving problems in groups. There's a lot of assignments between the lecture videos, problem sets, and journal assignments, but the overall workload is not that high.

The best professor I have had at Duke. Dr. Stiff-Roberts is an exceptional lecturer, friendly, and personable. The class material is not difficult for a quantum mechanics course (not because it is too simple; instead, Dr. Stiff-Roberts teaches extremely well). It is a flipped classroom so you get time to ask questions and practice problems.

Does a great job of condensing the material down and conveying it in a way that students can understand. Although tricky, the course follows a clear path and helped me grasp connections between topics. Homework helps to cement understanding of equations, labs are relatively easy, midterms had some tricky questions but followed the course material.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Stiff-Roberts is very clear during lectures and is exceptionally organized even during virtual sessions. The schedule is clear but there is a LOT of work including 3 midterms, a final, weekly quizzes, homework, and lab work. The class itself is a bit dry and not too interesting.

Prof. Stiff-Roberts is an amazing professor. She makes sure that everyone knows the material well by giving simple review quizzes, in-class activities, and by asking students questions. Her lecture slides come from the textbook, but they are greatly abridged and much easier to digest and read through. Wonderful lecturer and prof.

Stiff-Roberts is awesome. She is a fantastic lecturer and structures her class to give you both theoretical insights and knowledge of applications. She has very clear grading criteria, perfect amount of hw (with deadlines posted at the beginning of the sem), very organized (clear lecture notes online), and is fun to learn from. Def recommend!

Class was mandatory. Do the homework and the reading and it'll be an easy class. Asks 2-3 students easy questions about previous topics at the start of class, so you have to be on top of everything. Gives a review sheet before tests which made studying very straightforward.

Had him for Statistics for Science Majors. The class itself was very unclear and hard and his tests are hard too. Except 3 of them were take home tests and 2 were in-class and open-note tests. Assigns WebAssign as part of final grade. Also lets you make test corrections to get points back on exams which helps final grade in the end.
Hard course even for a season graduate student. But surprisingly fair. Probably the best teacher in ISYE - not saying much. I got a B though I did really have to work.
Good guy.
Hard class. Good teacher. I got an A
very hard tests/homework, sloppy handwriting, lecture notes are full of mistakes and are often unclear,  covers a lot of things at a very fast rate

Nice guy; horrible teacher.  Countless times he'll end up with the wrong solution, use the wrong numbers, or just confuse the class. He's a little better on a 1-on-1 level, but still, he needs some work

should stop teaching.(period). Worst teacher ever in my life. Actually, hes not a teacher because he doesn't know how to teach. Didn't learn anything. Do yourself a favor by not wasting a precious semester, let alone your grade or gpa.

Worst teacher in my entire academic career. Constantly confused and confusing. When he makes mistakes (often) he says "They're just numbers" and CONTINUES with the wrong #s. HW is impossible, even other stat profs couldn't do it. His tests have nothing to do with the lessons or text. I took other classes' exams and aced them but was lost on his.

oh my god worst teacher i have ever had. all the does is read off his pdf files. class test average under a 50.  he curses at the class.  always has to get corrected by students and gets upset when we do.  terrible.
he sucks. He should not be teaching. He should go back to elementry school and lose some weight
bad.

Absolutely atrocious professor...did not want to teach and did not know how to teach.  Would cancel lecture arbitrarily and even when he did have class, he was never coherent.  He should not be allowed to teach on the University-level ever again.  Avoid at all costs.

Very good professor. Very hard course. We covered an entire 400 page textbook from cover to cover in one semester. Prof. Abayomi is funny and willing to help after class and in office hours. He doesn't hide displeasure and impatience with lazy students (not me, but much of the class). He was visiting, but way better than stat prof I have this term.

THIS WAS THE WORST PROFESSOR I HAVE EVER HAD. he cannot teach, and should be fired immediately.  He never gets examples right, and his labs and HW are useless. If he actually taught the class  rather than sprinted through the material he might be worthwhile. Avoid him at all costs. All the above posts are completely ridic.

Funny, but not good at lecturing in class. Gone to his office hours before, but found the TAs more helpful. He seems much better at teaching higher level Stats classes, since he tends to rush through the intro material. Could be better if he prepared better before lectures.
Best math teacher I have ever had, though that's not saying much. Good prof though, hard subject, cared if you learned and was (a bit too) displeased when you didn't.
He is funny and a decent to good prof. Much Much better at teaching one on one, than in classroom. His office hours  were amazing, like having the best tutor. The class was too big.

While a hilariously endearing man (with great dreadlocks to match), he still has a long way to go with his teaching skills. He's utterly horrible at explaining concepts and performing practice problems. My natural propensity for math (and the help of my friends who took AP Stats) are the only reason I scored a B+. Most of my friends received Cs.
I agree...examples are usually very funny. In class exercises funny too. Tests are hard - but if you attend review you can do well. Book isn't bad if you read it - but it's very wordy.
He made a boring class funny. The tests are hard - but he does a review before. Make sure you don't miss it. He is a riot.

Very unclear professor. Sometimes, I doubt he even knows what he's talking about. The textbook is horrible and the homework never matches up to the kinds of questions on the test. Tests are arbitrary and unclear. Should be an easy class, but his teaching style is so unclear it makes the class difficult. I learned more in AP Stat in high school

Class was a good introduction to Python for data science. Flipped classroom, so have to do readings outside class and then work on exercises with a partner in class. Some classes have pop quizzes on the readings, so important to stay up to date. Not too much work besides the final project, and have 1 week to do each exercise.
I would avoid this class unless you want a super tough grader lol, there are easier 300-level polisci classes that are more fair
This class was definitely one of my least favorite classes at Duke. I would try to find another 300-level polisci class if you could, the grading itself was just ridiculous

1.) Ton of homework on readings that talk about nothing; mostly fluff pieces that talk about ideas you either already know or sound irrelevant to anything 2.) The grading. You won't know how "well" you're doing in the class until more than half the semester is over 3.) Feedback. Its LONG and mostly unhelpful, she won't give example papers either
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Insane amounts of homework. You will need to prepare extensively before every class period to be able to contribute. I was a student-athlete when I took her course and it was nearly unbearable - this course was by far the most challenging one of that semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Fresh is a great instructor, however be prepared to participate in class about the readings from the homework before. Participation really matters and participating makes the biggest difference. Another factor is she gives great and in-depth feedback about most of your assignments as well!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Fresh is insightful, gives amazing feedback, and really cares about the material and her students. While the class is difficult and readings can be very hard to get through sometimes, Professor Fresh makes sure any questions students have are addressed and resolved. Papers are graded with care and feedbacks are always detailed and helpful
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Adrain is the best (not one of) professor that I've ever seen. His lectures are inspirational. The course has some difficulty, but the homework is just suitable for us to understand everything. The take-home exams are original and innovative. He prepares every lecture carefully on his paper sheets and writes blackboard notes for every course.

A true Renaissance man, Dr. Bejan has been my favorite professor in the ME department. If you go to the lectures for nothing else, go to listen to him speak. He is incredibly quick-witted and surprisingly humorous. He is teaching his own theory but he encourages us to challenge him, which is great. It is obvious why he is so world-renowned.

Bejan is hands-down the best professor that I have had at Duke. He somehow manages to make convective heat transfer fascinating and his lectures are amazing. The problem sets are hard but short and he grades very reasonably. Bejan is world-famous and fascinating to talk to. Other classes taught me concepts, but Bejan taught me how to think.
Best professor in the Pratt Engineering School and one of the best professors at Duke University.
The most excellent professor in the Duke University Pratt Engineering School and at one of the most excellent professors at Duke University.
Best Professor I've had at Duke!
Best professor ever!!!

His jokes & outrageous analogies are the only thing that make this ridiculously dry subject even slightly interesting.  His in-class examples make the material seem pretty straightforward-he is good @ explaining-but tests are impossible (one avg was 11/20).  The curve however is ridiculously helpful.  In all I would def recommend taking w/ Bejan.
Very difficult professor.  He definitely knows his stuff and is a pretty interesting lecturer.  Don't take this class if you're used to getting A's on tests.
This guy is HARD.  But everyone does pretty bad and the curve is VERY helpful.  He's a really good lecturer, but the tests don't really reflect the problem sets.
SOOOOO smart, she's the best. She did assign 1 full book a week which was a little daunting, but its so worth it for what you get out of it.

Prof Smith was a great professor but the 1 novel a week got a little much at times. The class is discussion based so make sure you can make contributions. However, I had a great time and learned a lot as she teaches things you aren't often thinking about regarding US history.

Nice person but an awful professor. Get ready to experience one of the most boring classes ever that is also completely disorganized. Don't expect to get anything graded until near the end of the semester where you have no idea how she grades until the very end. Also don't expect her to be clear about instructions either!

Dr. Lentz-Smith is a nice person who clearly knows what she's talking about, but class frequently felt improvised (even when it wasn't/when was clearly planned around the readings) in a way that made it hard to focus. She also didn't assign assignments until late so the last month of class was really busy. She's accommodating and grades leniently.

Class was mostly discussion  we read a book a week and focused class on that. She definitely goes off topic, but the it was still really interesting and she knows a TON about what she's teaching. Paper grades take a while to come back, but she wasn't a hard grader. Class was 2.5 hours long which was ROUGH at times, but I really enjoyed overall!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She seems like a cool person, but class isn't very interesting or informative. She lectures the whole class and gets off track a lot. It's hard to know what you need to know for tests and she gives an unrealistic level of reading.

Lectures are boring, they are useless. She gets off track a lot and doesn't really get to her point in lectures, dont learn a lot. She doesnt seem prepared for class. Learned mostly from readings and discussion section. Guidelines for essays were unclear, but overall pretty easy class, you just dont learn anything

She's a fun lecturer, but she gets off-track a lot. She's really fun to learn from since she has a pretty easy-going personality. I didn't find the class very difficult at all. It was actually pretty informative, all in all.

Really enjoyed US History 1914-1945 with ALS. Class was not too difficult and the readings were steady, but not overwhelming. She makes class interesting. Her lectures are filled with stories and narratives that make them less mundane. Really enjoyed our class discussions. Take a class with her!
This class is great! Her love for history made me more interested in the topic, The reading assignments are reasonable. Take this class!

I took her class on the American South.  She's extremely knowledgeable.  She absolutely expects you to do the readings and her lectures vary in quality, but if you go talk to her one-on-one she's SO helpful and really interesting.

Great professor. Most lectures are spoken and have a huge amount of information so note-taking is a little frantic, but she keeps it interesting. Easy grader, unbiased lectures and an interesting class. Definitely worth taking if you need an easy A or if you like history.
Though the topic/class seemed interesting, the lectures were hard to follow and mundane. She loves the class though so that kept the class interesting.

I really enjoyed taking a class with him! He is super knowledgable but more importantly very kind and understanding. He wants the best for his students and taking time to get to know him and asking questions will only help you in this class!

His expectations are pretty unclear for assignments, but if you put in an effort and write a good paper you'll get a good grade. He cares about attendance and participation, doing the readings will improve participation, but it's not necessary to read them closely. One 3 page midterm, one 14-16 page paper, and weekly forum posts.

Professor Mestyan is a kind professor who cares a lot about his students. He assigned a lot of readings at times but didn't expect students to read every single one. As long as you put effort into the papers, show up to class, and do well on the presentation he assigns you will do well in the class.

Would have normally been an easy A class, but participation seemingly matters a lot. The essays aren't too harshly graded and overall the class isn't much work, but be prepared to make comments every couple classes. He can randomly assign participation drops that are unexpected and significant.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Mestyan is the kindest professor ever! He is so interested in the topic which makes his lectures incredibly engaging. Highly recommend if you want to walk away having really learned something from the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Poorly adapted to an online format. Lectures were fine but lots of tech problems, followed by 10 mins of rushed Q and A where the same 3 people always talked. Tried to cover way too much material in two 50 minute classes a week, so little incentive to do readings since we didn't have time to discuss them. Mestyan is kind and accommodating though.
Prof Mestyan is very nice and accessible outside of class. Lectures are clear and engaging with interesting content. No exams: just Sakai posts throughout the semester and two papers.
Super interesting and super easy - the ideal duke class.

Mestyan is one of the best professors I've had at Duke. He's funny, knowledgable, engaging, and knows how to teach to college students. There are weekly readings, and while most people didnt do them and were fine, I personally found them really interesting. A fascinating class (History of the Modern Middle East)with very reasonable workload. 10/10.

Professor Mestyan is a gem. Super knowledgable, his grading is very easy, and you can get away with not doing the reading for class. Very accessible outside class, and takes it upon himself to make the class laugh and keeps everyone engaged.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Mestyan is an amazing lecturer! He is very knowledgeable about the subject and also tries to tell lots of jokes during class to keep students engaged. I highly recommend taking his class. Also try to meet with him outside of class because he is just an interesting person to talk to!

Adam is a fantastic lecturer because he is extremely funny and engaging. I loved the first course I took with him so much that I am taking another. He is also very approachable so don't be afraid to take time to talk to him after or outside of class. Workload is not bad but there is a decent amount of reading. He also wants students to get an A.

He's absurdly knowledgeable about everything we covered in Modern Middle East, which makes lectures interesting and papers tough to get right. Gives LOTS of reading that's kind of scattered, but it's interesting and you can skim if you need to. Super chill--I think he owns two pairs of pants and they're both ripped jeans. Glad I took this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: He was not here to teach us, but instead discover and groom the next big journalists. He essentially ignored everyone else. Grading was very unclear and felt like he graded based on how much he liked us. He is a brilliant journalist, but just a terrible professor.

Adair is the worst professor I've ever had. His class structure is very instructor-centric. It enables him to learn and potentially take advantage of his students' ideas and connections, not the other way around. His grading criteria are extremely unclear, leading to constant arbitrary grading. I would not recommend taking any classes with him.
Good class for intro to journalism, he is a tough grader, but he cares about you being a better writer. Easily accessible outside of class and a WIDE network of connections.

Great professor who brings in a lot of guest speakers. You really learn a lot and apply your knowledge to get creative and find solutions. Participation really matters though, so be prepared to talk a lot if you want to get the participation points

I really enjoyed this class. Workload is very manageable, just about 5 short/medium length papers on interesting topics and participation. I'm not even looking to go into journalism but I found the class refreshing and interesting.

One of the most compassionate professors at Duke. Take the time to build a relationship with Adair outside of the classroom. He will bolster your overarching career - help you make connections, etc. Life changer.
His grading was pretty arbitrary, but a course for someone who doesn't know much about newswriting and reporting.

Prof. Adair is a great professor! You will learn a lot from his class, but get ready to work for your grade. The Newswriting course consists of a paper due every 2-3 weeks and you will be doing actual field reporting. Class is fun and interesting. Although he is a tough grader, I highly recommend his class.
Really good professor and well-respected in his field.  Brings in really great guest speakers.  Grading can be tough but he'll make you a better writer/journalist.

Professor Adair is undoubtedly the best professor I had in my time at Duke. I took as many classes with him as I could, yet still wish I could have taken more. As a professor of the practice, and an award-winning journalist, he has a deep knowledge and passion for the subject matter and his enthusiasm comes across clearly in class. Incredible.

Adair is a visiting Professor. He brings a lot of real-world knowledge to the classroom and we had really interesting guest speakers. We had Obama's Communications Director and a former Governor speak to us. He does not assign a lot of work, but grading is kind of random and he will pick at little things in your essay that he may not like.

Adair is awesome! The class isn't super easy, but I highly recommend it. He's a fascinating person with a ton of knowledge and experience in the journalism field. I have learned so much from his "Press and the Presidency" class and would love to take another class with him. He is the current "Knight Chair", for those who don't know.

Bill Adair worked in journalism and helped to found PolitiFact, a fact-checking site that calls out politicians and pundits for lies. He's got a ton of experience and a lot of great stories to share. He's a great person, a great professor, and I highly recommend any class you can take with him!

Biophotonics design with Dr. Wax was very unorganized. He had unclear expectations for the course and provided little to no educational support for semester projects. He often gave a single numerical score as feedback without much constructive criticism on how to improve for future presentations. These scores also didn't match the provided rubrics.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Wax is a magnificent professor. This class was an intensive project-based course, so there wasn't much of traditional lecturing. Although students were largely left to their own devices, where Dr. Wax excelled was in being available for students to consult and get meaningful feedback from. Definitely take a class with him.

The class was not that interesting not because of Dr. Wax but because of the course itself.  Class material is sometimes extremely dull and unorganized.  I heard the other professors who have taught this class are way worse so Dr. Wax could be the way to go.

Very difficult class, but Wax made it seem less illogical from a physics standpoint in his lectures (his research focuses on optics, after all). His lectures largely follows the textbook more than other profs' do, but otherwise the textbook was confusing by itself. HW's not very reflective on what you see on exams.
Super fun 300-level Spanish class. Would recommend. Little unclear at beginning of class, but it all worked out in the end.
Very engaging class discussions, engaging teacher. Minimal work outside of class.

I found the subject matter pretty interesting, but the readings sometimes felt very dense and long. Towards the end of the class it felt a bit repetitive. Dr. Aidoo is a pretty lenient grader though as long as you participate and put effort into the response papers + final paper to be thoughtful it's a chill class.

I took Afro-Latin America w him, probably my favorite class I've taken at Duke. Readings were interesting, relevant, and very manageable, discussions were super engaging and class always seemed to fly by, he's super knowledgeable on the topic and he's hilarious. no unnecessary work, i learned so much from this class and it was never stressful
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Lamonte is lame. Hated his class for so many reasons. Would not recommend. Literally went crazy towards the end of the semester too.

The class was very interesting and Dr. Aidoo is a very intelligent person. However, the class was very reading heavy and sometimes he would assign 60-100 page readings the night before. About 4 weeks in, we stopped using the syllabus, so what was due for each class became unclear. The only grades were a midterm, final paper, and participation
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Dr. Aidoo was awesome. The books he chose for the seminar were all interesting. He was engaging, fun, and made me look forward to coming to class. I would definitely take another class with him.

Dr. Aidoo was an amazing Professor. I entered the class knowing nothing about race and sexuality in Brazil and he completely opened my eyes. The readings and discussions were great and he is such a great guy. Definitely recommend taking his class. Best professor I've had at Duke.

Prof. Aidoo is so funny and passionate about his work. Class was super interesting and even when I didnt know anything about the topic, he took the time to explain everything. He even changed his syllabus to accommodate to the interests of the class, always looking out for us to enjoy the material. Take any and all classes with him.

Best professor Ive taken at Duke. He is truly caring, hilarious, and wants the best for his students. Read the material for class and be prepared to participate, he will know if you didnt read. However, the books are super interesting and he is very passionate about the subject so the class is never boring. Prof. Aidoo is amazing. Take his class.

I would definitely recommend this class and teacher! The class had amazing readings, that were well worth the time. And, he is willing to adapt the syllabus to meet the class's interests and is always available out of class. He is so passionate about the subject. Participation matters, so come to class and talk. One of my favorite classes at Duke!

The professor was very all over the place. Didn't give out a syllabus. Even though I asked for one, he still never gave me one. He always emailed readings the day before. Readings can be a lot and tough to read if you're not into it. I wouldn't recommend this class if you aren't interested in African studies.

Dr. Airall is the best! I had never learned about CRT before but this class was eye-opening and taught me so many things that made me examine my own place in the world. There are articles to read before classes and 2 books throughout the semester. Only 3 papers and 1 final group project. My favorite professor-- couldn't recommend this class more!

Dr. Airall is an amazing professor! I was in her CRT in Education class and learned so much. The classes are heavily discussion-based and participation really matters. Dr. Airall fostered an environment where everyone felt comfortable participating. There are not that many readings (1 book and a few articles) or papers (only 3).

Dr. Airall is the sweetest woman ever. I had her for CRT in Education and learned so much. Each class was a discussion and 45% of your grade is based on participation, so if you aren't comfortable with jumping into group discussions this class might not be for you. Two papers and one presentation throughout the semester.

Best class and professor I've had at Duke! Dr. Airall is an incredible woman who cares deeply about her students, and she shares amazing stories that are both hilarious and thought-provoking. Her class didn't even feel like work-- I legitimately looked forward to going every week. Take Dr. Airall's class if you have the opportunity!!

Dr. Airall is one of the best professors and people you will ever have the pleasure of meeting. Took this class not expecting anything, and it went above and beyond my expectations. She cares so much about her students and is interested in actually getting to know people. She's also hilarious and tells fantastic stories. Take her class!!

A cool person, a cool professor, just amazing. She cares. She knows modern events and ties them into class. She knows lots of people and has done the work to care about communities she's an ally to. She's easy to talk to and also easy to have a brilliant convo with. Please take a class with her if you have the chance.

Professor Kwon is lovely. She is super sweet and nice and knows a ton. However, her lectures can get a little boring because she is so gentle. You will have a lot of reading, weekly responses and responses to your classmates, but you go over the readings in class and you can easily get extra credit. A midterm + final paper to write. Nice professor

Prof. Kwon tends to ramble during lecture. While she would occasionally discuss a fascinating topic, her lectures were for the most part, a bit dull.  The thesis of her course became clear halfway through the semester, at which point I stopped learning new things. Reading heavy and participation (discuss readings) a significant portion of grade.

I loved Prof. Kwon. Her seminar brought up fascinating new ideas and concepts. However, she can be a little monotone and tends to ramble off during class. As long as you listen to her, you're  fine. There was a lot of reading, but if you skim it you'll be ok. She really likes class participation as well.

Dr.Kwon has high expectations for her students and her class has a pretty heavy reading load but she this is because she does not dumb down academic content for undergraduates. I really respect her for not designing her class as a blow off course. The novels we read in this class are all fantastic.
Really, really mean

Everyone at Duke should get the chance to have a class with Dr. Sharma! He's hilarious and really cares about his students. Don't worry if you see other reviews about his comments, such as: "Your writing is stabbing my eyes." It's always in jest and makes the class more enjoyable. Take his class!

The workshops are intense (and may leave you questioning whether to even write anything again). That being said, Akhil cares immensely for his students and for cultivating interesting conversation. You will leave a semi-better writer and a much better commentator on the human experience. One of my favorite classes at Duke.

Professor Sharma is a very good writer with lots of insight. However, the class environment is stressful and he is over-critical to the point of discouraging our writing and creativity. Criticism was very harsh and I felt like no matter how much time I spent or how hard I worked, my writing would never be good.

Prof Sharma is the most interesting person I've ever met. Take this class if you want to improve your writing and want a class that is fun / creative. Don't get discouraged by the critiques. The class makes you a more interesting person and encourages you to be weird and creative. Take it!! Be ready to participate in a low-stakes environment!!

There is no doubt that taking this class will make you a better writer. His criticisms of students' work are often very dramatic, funny, and insulting, but they are productive in helping you understand where you can do better. He is one of the best professors here.

He is one of the best professors I've had at Duke. He is extremely talented, full of wisdom, and a great laugh. He is one of those professors who has a life and understands what it means to have a life. He is so down-to-earth that I can come to him about anything. Amazing feedback on writing, you'll be changed after taking one of his classes.

He makes class very interesting. The workload is reasonable and focuses mainly on critiquing other students' stories. There is work at the end of the semester that helps you reflect on your fears, resentments, and wrongdoings.

Akhil is a thoughtful, caring professor who will tear your writing to shreds in a constructive way. He infuses humor, anecdotes, and words of wisdom into every class. The work load is light and geared more toward reading and editing peer work than writing your own. This course certainly stretched me to be a more intentional and creative writer.
Great class! Super interesting professor and lots of self reflecting get to hear other students work and talk about it so be prepared to share
The smartest person I have interacted with at Duke. My Duke experience would be incomplete without Sharma.

Professor Sharma clearly cares about his students. He cares that we understand ourselves as people, and a lot of the work we do is about understanding our fears, resentments, and regrets. I would definitely take a class with him. It's unlike anything else you'll take at Duke.
He can seem harsh, but he really cares about his students. He mainly focuses on the technical level of writing, but I still learned a lot about structure from this course.

Professor Sharma can come across as rude and condescending, but it is purely meant for entertainment. He is a hilarious professor, and I was definitely engaged during class. He gives excellent feedback and clearly has a breadth of knowledge that he enjoys sharing with students. Don't take yourself too seriously if you take a course with him.

I highly recommend taking a class with Professor Sharma if you want to improve your writing- he gave honest, helpful feedback, and he has a lot of experience and insight into the writing process. He doesn't say something is good if it's not, but if you're looking to improve, you'll appreciate that (probably). Also, he's hilarious!!

Class with Dr. Sharma has been some of the most meaningful time I have spent at Duke. Whether you consider yourself a writer or not I would highly recommend any class with him as a means of better understanding yourself and the human experience at large.

After four years at Duke, my classes with Sharma have been the most transformative for me not just as a writer but also as a person. He will be very blunt, but he is very caring and makes sure there is understanding as to what he is saying and giving as feedback. I wish I could have him for another semester.

He gave no clear guidance on how to improve our work and only provided infrequent, vague feedback. He only focused on the first few paragraphs of our writing, entirely ignoring the rest. His syllabus and in-class instructions were inconsistent, leaving us always ambiguous. He was also mean, unserious, and unprofessional throughout the semester.

Sharma really is fantastic at critiquing your work. He's honest and specific and will improve your writing dramatically. He may also aim criticism at you as a person, and is often unnecessarily mean. 

A quote from him: “I cannot make you do the work. I cannot give you bad grades. I cannot physically beat you. So I will whip you with my words.”

Most 'critics' you meet in life are not honest with you; most honest people aren't honest with you. And it's hard to grow as a writer, or as a person, when these are those who surround you. Fortunately, Dr. Sharma is not one of those people. Although his course was not difficult, it was educational. He is fun, knowledgeable, and will help you grow.

Phenomenal class, one of my all time favorites. One of the best professors at Duke. He cares so much about his students and his feedback is both exceptional and hilarious. Don't get scared by the first week. Just actually do the work (which isn't too much) and go to class and your grade will be fine. I will be taking more of his classes.

The class is easy and there isn't much work. He is very direct and a bit harsh with his criticisms but it didn't bother me much. However, I thought class was often kind of boring as it would be 2.5 hours straight of him critiquing our work at a very slow pace. The lack of structure and formal instruction meant I didn't learn as much as I had hoped.

Dr. Sharma is one of the most interesting people I have ever met. He has so many stories to share, which he somehow weaves into the class content. His criticism is harsh but realistically accurate and very helpful. A lot of the class is pointing out what has gone wrong, and it is up to you to figure out/ try things that can improve it. Please take

Don't be scared by your first class with Sharma, you will grow to understand his style of teaching. He can be a tough critic, but you will undoubtedly improve (and come to understand and love his sense of humor).

Professor Sharma really really really really cares about his students - his classes are fun, entertaining, and you will become a better writer. He can be tough but it is because he cares - and it will make you better. I really enjoyed this class and I would highly recommend to anyone looking for something refreshing, creative, and low stress.

Professor Sharma is so funny. He is genuinely so enjoyable to be around. If you can't take negative feedback then maybe avoid, but he means well. Class with him was great because he has a good personality. Highly highly recommend for a good time and funny written stories.
Caring professor, has a genuine interest in every student. Gives honest feedback on writing in a playful and engaging way.
Dr. Sharma is a wonderful teacher, but get ready for some honest feedback. Definitely makes you a better writer.

Sharma is my favorite prof at Duke. He is blunt yet caring, and his approach yields excellent results: everyone in our class improved as writers. The department stopped him from assigning too much work, so the workload is reasonable, if not light (one story per week). If I could go back, I would have taken all of my writing courses with Dr. Sharma.

Everyone needs to take a class with a Professor Sharma. He is genuinely a pretty crazy guy, but in a way that makes you feel like he's the only normal person in the room. He is definitely intense in his critique, but he genuinely helps you become a better writer. If you want to be praised, don't take this class, but if you want to learn, do it.

If you have thick skin and a willingness to accept feedback, this is an amazing course. Dr. Sharma doesn't hold back with his critiques, but all of his notes are honest, fair, and will genuinely make you a better writer. He's enthusiastic about engaging with students – took us out to lunch and was always willing to meet for office hours.

Everyone should take this class! Akhil gives such harsh feedback but it will make you grow as a writer (and person) in ways you can't imagine. The first time you get read will be DIFFICULT, but you will grow thick skin and learn to write good sentences. He truly cares for his students, has taken us out to lunch, and even invited us to his house!

The workload was not demanding at all, but I did find the practice fun yet a chance to learn what we are discussing in class. Prof Akhil Sharma has high standards when it comes to writing, but doesn't grade harsh at all. He encourages improvement in a very genuine manner and has given me inspiration to be a better writer and human being.

Super sweet guy. I love him. I'm taking his class again, and ideally I'll take classes with him until I graduate. 

The workload is fine. 

The class is for people who are serious about writing. If you're just taking the class for an easy A (he only gives As), I'd recommend another class simply because the work and content won't be interesting.
Taking this class was literally a once in a lifetime experience, you will learn so much about life in general and laugh so much, professor is the most unique person ever and tells the best stories
Truly a one-of-a-kind professor, not just at Duke, but in the entire world. I'm very fortunate and grateful to have been part of this experience.

Truly unique. If you don't actually want to take his class, don't. However, if you want to be there and you put in the work and effort (which isn't even really that much), he will love you and you will get a lot out of his class. Workshop is always helpful, he gives great (but harsh) feedback. The more enthusiasm you have, the better.

There's no one like Professor Sharma at Duke. Feedback can be harsh, but the workshopping is valuable and you develop a great class community. Very little work: reading is 99% Chekhov and 3 short stories over the whole sem. End of semester becomes group therapy-ish. If you're ready to be engaged and openminded, take this class. Attendance MANDATORY

1/2 Hell's Kitchen but for writing; 1/2 intense therapy-slash-life coaching-session Dead Poets Society fever dream

workload isn't bad (weekly 20-30pg readings, ~3 short workshop pieces)

you will get harsh, brutally honest feedback in front of others but it will be the most useful feedback you've ever received 

amazing professor. take this class.

Dr. Sharma is one of the best professors I have had in my time at Duke. Though his criticism can be harsh, he does so with the hopes of making you contribute your best effort and grow as a writer. He goes the extra mile to get to know his students as people and gives extraordinary life advice. Highly recommend.

Since he offers frank writing feedback (no sugarcoating), I recognize that certain students take issue with him. But, he is one-of-a-kind at Duke in the sense that he won't dish out false praise, and instead will be laser-focused on helping his students improve as writers and thinkers. He is thoughtful, precise, and caring.
Never felt more disparaged than when I took this class with Dr. Sharma. Says that he doesn't mean to bully his students, but manages to do so anyways? So the point is moot.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Heavy reading load, daily homework (including weekends), & minimal-to-zero written feedback on students' writing. He made often discouraging comments on students' writing in front of the class and in 1-on-1s. No grading criteria, no guidelines for assignments, no grades whatsoever except for final grade, which is on a harsh curve. Do not recommend.
I love love love Michael! He is super inspirational and very accessible outside class. His course is well structured

A class with Michael is well worth it. He is an amazing lecturer as he can break down complex concepts and make them accessible for everyone. His classes tend to require you to do a lot of work (approximately a constant 15-20 hours a week), but your efforts are compensated. He is a tough grader though, you will have to work very hard for an A or A-
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Michael is amazing! He takes the hardest concepts that I have ever come across and makes them super accessible and intuitive. Definitely the best professor I have ever had.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I had no background in statistics. After taking his class IDS 702, I'm pretty confident in making statistical models. Makes sure everyone understands his material. Very accessible outside class. Overall a great professor.
One of the best classes I've taken so far, amazing lecturer he made sure that every kid understood the material before moving on highly recommend
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Hollowell is an incredible professor! His class consists of many thought-provoking discussions, interesting readings, and deep dives into complex topics. I took so much away from his class. He is extremely knowledgeable about his field and would definitely recommend taking a class with him to everyone! One of the best professors at Duke.

One of the best classes I've ever taken at Duke! This class really pushed me to think deeply about the world and every single class discussion was thought-provoking. Professor Hollowell is a wonderful teacher who truly cares about his students -- would recommend every Duke student to take a class with him and to grab a FLUNCH too!

Hollowell is a very respected teacher which is understandable. His lectures are extremely thought provoking, however often times may leave you in a state of psychological paralysis. The logic may be confusing and disagreeable, but if you are into complex theory and high-level academic and social conversation, Hollowell is a good teacher to try.
Fantastic class (Ethics in an Unjust World) -- probably the best that I took while at Duke, and Adam was great at selecting thought-provoking readings and engaging the class in deep conversation

The class will give you the space to consider an eclectic mix of ethical frameworks, the various ways people engage in service and social impact, and grappling with injustices. Professor Hollowell serves more as a facilitator and lectures minimally, so you'd get more out of this class if you read and speak up in class.

One of the most thought-provoking, inspiring classes at Duke. Readings are not needed to engage in discussion but are still super insightful. Guest-lecture heavy. Take any class you can with this professor!
Best class and professor. He truly cares about his students.
Revolutionary class. 100% recommend this seminar. Hollowell is an amazing professor that changes the way you view education.

TAKE THIS CLASS! Professor Hollowell is a truly great Professor. He cares so much about his students, and he wants to make his class work to teach and inspire as much as possible. The course was easy, but also one of the most meaningful classes Ive taken at Duke.

He made this freshman seminar pretty revolutionary & inspiring. He is open, knowledgeable, fun and not afraid to show his vulnerability. This class changed how I view education and teaching, and it is very accommodating and stress-free in the backdrop of a global pandemic. Highly recommend.
He's a great guy and the discussions in class are always interesting! Really understanding during COVID.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Material would have been radically informative if I was white/didn't know what marginalization was, but neither of those are the case for me. Lectures could be mansplainy and occasionally problematic. That said, he was SO accommodating during the pandemic; he most definitely cares about his students. I would take his class again to pick his brain
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Beware of pop quizzes--Caring

reviews.comment: The conversations I had with him and the topics of this class have greatly inspired me.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Inspirational

reviews.comment: One of the smartest people I've met at Duke. He really knows what he's talking about, and makes sure that students actually learn meaningful material. This class, despite being 2.5 hours long, was never boring. I would absolutely take another one of his classes again.
In Race and Public Policy he was super engaging and communicated the difficult material in an engaging way. However, there were a lot of readings- but if you are going to do Focus I 100% recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Adam was incredibly well-spoken, intelligent, and willing to teach without making students feel ignorant. Would definitely recommend, you will learn so much !

Adam is one of the smartest professors I've ever met. He has a breadth of knowledge and experiences, is really well read, and is eager to share what he thinks with his students. He sets clear classroom expectations. Although the work piles up, the deadlines for major projects are flexible. Highly recommend taking one of his classes while at Duke
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He is a great professor who truly cares about his students. He also provided the class with really interesting readings! I RECOMMEND IT!!!!!

Great class! You'll learn a lot about race and yourself through the discussions. The work is not easy, but if you do whats expected you'll do well. It greatly helps critical thinking and writing skills.

Professor Hollowell is outstanding. He does a phenomenal job stimulating class discussions, challenging our ideas, and making us realize both our responsibilities and limitations. The topics are relevant, the readings are interesting, and the guests speakers are engaging. This is a must take class for anyone at Duke.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Amazing professor-very engaging, works hard to incorporate topics relevant to students, and invites interesting speakers to provide a wide range of perspectives in class. There's lots of reading, but everything is intriguing and relevant to class. DEFINITELY WOULD RECOMMEND!!!!

Race and Public Policy (a Focus class) was by far my favorite class this semester. Adam assigned interesting (albeit involved) readings every class, and pushed students out of our comfort zones in each discussion. He also made sure we had input as to what we read. This class gave me a better idea of what I want to do with my life. Adam is awesome.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--Would take again

reviews.comment: Adam is an all round great professor and I learnt so much from taking his Race and Public Policy FOCUS class. Class discussions are always interesting and engaging, and he's not afraid of making you talk about the hard questions (which I thought was great). This class is very reading-heavy but all the readings are thought-provoking and rewarding.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Would take again

reviews.comment: This class (Race and Public Policy) was taken as part of the American Experience focus, and it was absolutely amazing! It opened my mind to be better able to examine both the outside world and my personal thoughts and perspectives. Adam was a fantastic professor, if a little disorganized at times, and I would definitely recommend taking his class!

A great professor that never ceases to challenge his students. In his class, you will be challenged intellectually like never before. A great listener and discussion leader. He is always readily available to assist in any questions students may have.

Very passionate and interesting professor who really cares about what he teaches. The class field trips were eye-opening, and the class discussions were engaging. There is a significant amount of reading, but it is fairly interesting, and the writing assignments/exams are fair. Would recommend taking a class with him.
Easily the best class I have taken at Duke. No matter your department or major, take this class.

While this class doesn't necessarily seem like a public policy class, it gives you the chance to expand how you think about different policies and institutions and will challenge your conceptions of service in a really productive way. Definitely would recommend.

I love Adam's class, and I'm rating him a 5.0, and I'm not giving him those stars just because he's white, male, and English is his first language. He is genuinely one of the best professors I've had at Duke and his class is amazing. Don't let the readings and grades scare you. I think everyone at Duke should take this class before they graduate.

Engaging, interesting, valuable experience. Adam is the kind of professor who challenges you to think about the ways in which you engage with service work. It questions the savior complex along with cynicism. I highly recommend this course (it's also not too hard, with a few easy quizzes, papers, etc ...

I 0/10 recommend this class.  While the course is taught like a seminar (aka it's discussion-based), I would hesitate to call what goes on in Adam's classroom a discussion.  Adam allows those who share the views he presents in class to speak and reinforces their ideas, while shutting down others. This should be a classroom, not a church.

This class is an awesome opportunity to hear a professor confront and question the many events that happen on Duke's campus and more. He is an exceptional lecturer, but can also be brash. I think this is a must-take for many Duke students.
Amazing teacher, will make you question your existence as a Duke Student. He deserves more than what the university is offering him.

This class will probably be one of the most memorable classes I've taken at Duke thus far. Of course, that's not really saying much considering I'm still a freshman, but I really mean it. Prof. Hollowell is really nice and challenges the way you think in a way that helps everyone learn even more.
Easily the best class I've taken at Duke so far.

Adam Hollowell is just a great guy. I highly suggest that you take this class and the time to talk with him after class and plan to meet one on one. This class will change your views at least in one respect, guaranteed, and you'll also get a really good understanding of basic ethics.

Ethics in an Unjust world with Dr. Hollowell was a great way to cap off my senior year. Out of all the classes I've taken at Duke, this has probably been the best in terms of preparing me in relevant ways for "the real world." It was worth overloading for senior spring.
Take this class! You have never had a class like this before, and it is especially great for someone going to Duke!
One of the best professors in four years and a must-take class for students from any discipline. Cannot recommend highly enough.
This class will make you a more considerate person. Beware that 50% of your grade is the final paper. Not an easy A by any means, but possible. Highly recommend auditing.

Took the class because I heard the professor was great and needed to fulfill prereqs, SO GLAD I DID. Very interesting material, never a dull day of discussion. Adam is engaging and provides thought provoking questions/ideas that make you think. Probably the only class I've taken at Duke that has made me want to really make an impact in the world.

This is definitely a must-take course, but I wonder if I might lack the maturity and the experience to really contribute something valuable to class discussions and reflections. I think the course asks some ESSENTIAL questions about service, but second semester freshman year might be a bit early to be prepared to contribute confidently to class.

Dr. Hollowell is a phenomenal professor and a really kind person. I always enjoyed coming to class-- discussions were engaging and the readings were all super interesting.  I highly recommend any of his classes, regardless of the topic. He is the best professor I've had at Duke and his class was the most meaningful course that I've taken.

Best professor I've had here, and I like think I've had a ton of great professors. Very engaged and genuinely interested in student development throughout the course. Even if you're not a public policy or religion major, taking a class with him is a must.

Professor Hollowell is hands down one of the best at Duke. He selects genuinely interesting readings, and is very clear in his instructions. His feedback is always useful and he grades fairly- and he is always there to help! He gets to know all his students, and really cares about them which is so rare. Take his class!

Hollowell is awesome. His class was super interesting; I always looked forward to it which made the work much more rewarding. There are three papers over the course of the semester he is not an easy grader, but he is fair. Overall great class and really cool guy.

Professor Hollowell is the man! He really connects with each student on a personal level. Had us over to his house for dinner and a movie and made class so interesting (no matter how dense the reading was). Extremely fair grader and instructions are always clear.

Prof. Hollowell is an outstanding teacher and constantly encourages his students.  He is very well spoken, and presents his ideas in a very clear way.  His grading is also very fair, and he provides useful feedback.  He really strives to get to know each student personally, which is so rare.

One of the best classes I've taken. Lectures, class discussions, and paper topics were always thought-provoking. Lots of reading, but most of them are interesting. His office hours and feedback on papers are REALLY helpful. His grading is fair. He really is insightful, and is a great person to talk to about anything. Take one of his classes!

Great professor. Really smart guy. Interesting readings. Challenging, thought provoking essays. Best class I have had at Duke, honestly, and that is saying something. Hopefully I'll be able to take a future class with him.

I have taken two classes and done two informal group book studies with Dr. Hollowell, and I have to say that he is by far one of the best professors I have had at Duke. He chooses excellent readings, guides seminar discussions well, and has helped me become a much better writer. His classes are a must for anyone interested in religion/politics.

This guy's the best professor I've had so far at Duke-invited us over for dinner at his place and took us on a tour of the chapel. He really understood what I, as a freshman, was going through and helped me out after classes. In between the course I somehow strained my back and couldn't come to a few classes, but he let me off. Amazing guy, really!

Prof. Hollowell is one of the best teachers here- he's an amazing guy and really helps students out. Plus he's a duke graduate himself so he knows what students have to go through. I believe our class discussions were quite intriguing and I did learn a lot. Be ready to read a bit though...

Dr. Hollowell was one of the most helpful and encouraging professors I've had at Duke. He met each student where he/she was at and facilitated intellectually stimulating class discussions, as well as gave and encouraged each of us to give constructive feedback. All in all, a wonderful class.

Dr. Hollowell was excellent. Professor thrives on discussions and does well encouraging students with limited experience in the material. All readings were provided online, and Dr. Hollowell provides excellent feedback on papers.

Dr. Hollowell was the most helpful and accessible professor I had at Duke. He assigned interesting readings (never too long) that elicited lively discussion. He was also very helpful in steering discussion without dominating it. And his support and feedback on papers was among the best I received at Duke.

Excellent class. The professor's enthusiasm for the material covered was contagious, and he encouraged students to pursue what they found most interesting. Very helpful on writing papers: would suggest authors and books/chapters to read. Clear feedback on papers/ grading.

Dr. Hollowell was very knowledgeable and prepared for the class, facilitating questions and conversing between the scholars.  His course brought to light too-often ignored presumptions behind the interaction policy ethics and religion.

Really interesting class. Dr. Hollowell was very helpful. The class had a good balance of theory and practice and we were able to interact with many of the scholars we studied. Grading was fair and detailed. All class readings were provided as a pdf.

This class has been my favorite so far at Duke. My perception on poverty, ethics, and service was challenged through small group discussions and out of class trips in the Durham community. Dr. Hollowell was always available to discuss unclear class topics and help with papers. He lead class discussions in an unbiased manner and graded fairly.

The class I had with Dr. Hollowell was undoubtedly the best class I've had at Duke. He's a fair and honest grader who's comments really help. The class was heavily discussion based, and he moderated and lead the discussion with ease. And if you weren't sure about a topic discussed, he always has a book to place your thoughts. Highly recommend him.

Demanding class with a pretty heavy workload, especially the projects, but I learned a lot from it. Prof. MacDonald explains concepts clearly and focuses on applying statistics, not memorizing formulas. Office hours were very helpful, and the extra credit quizzes throughout the semester were a nice boost too. One of the best classes I ever took!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Demanding class with a pretty heavy workload, especially the projects, but I learned a lot from it. Prof. MacDonald explains concepts clearly and focuses on applying statistics, not memorizing formulas. Office hours were very helpful, and the extra credit quizzes throughout the semester were a nice boost too. One of the best classes I ever took!!!
I seriously did not like him at all. Just read the textbook at home.

Prof Macdonald has a very organized and balanced teaching style. His lectures are great and he's very generous with giving extra credits for participation in class! Homework is a bit heavy but should be doable and he gives good feedback.

amazing prof! but please, prepare for the class well and be ready to dedicate 12+ hours for one homework project, it's really a lot of work and self study but he explains well if you didn't understand something
The workload is just too heavy. Think carefully before taking this professor. He sets detailed requirements for almost everything.
