Loved his class! project heavy, but he was super helpful during office hours. Lectures can get boring, but he's nice to look at iykwim (; so I always listened.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. MacDonald is a caring professor who takes care of his students if they decide to get close to him. Students should go to office hours without an essay to talk to him because he is a very engaging professor! GCHINA is generally graded strictly, but I wish prof. Andrew left more comments in the essays. He's easy to talk to if problems arise.
Prepare well before the classes plz! Or you can be completely confused.. And read the course policy and "how to prepare" carefully. They are instructions to survive indeed. take care TAT

The course on social inequality is not a easy course, which contains games theories and models I never know before. The good thing is that he always explains materials clearly and offers interesting extra knowledge. It would be a wonderful experience for you if you want to spend time with political science and intelligent minds.

Prof. Andrew MacDonald is a great professor who offers his own views on course materials. If you don't read the textbook, you will get confused since he would expand on that basis instead of re-read the text for you. However, people will have a good time attending his lectures if required works are finished.

This class is hard but you will never learn more in 7-weeks. MacDonald is fair and although his lectures aren't the best, I learned how to write statistically in his class. Please don't be discouraged by the low ratings it really is worth it.

Prof. MacDonald is a political scientist, not a statistician, so don't know why he's teaching this class. Even so, I think many people psyched themselves when they heard we were programming in R. His instruction guides were always clear and easy to follow. He was a pleasant guy, I would take another course from him that was more in his field.

Stats is hard, and that is not his fault. The homework had lab sections with real practical analysis. He is very accessible and is a good explainer. Moreover, he taught stats and using R very practically. He made sure that we understood the general idea instead of unnecessary hand calculations. If you take him, you will work but it's worth it.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: His lectures were confusing and explanations were unclear. He gave us way too many readings that weren't that helpful. Don't take stats101 with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: His explanations were not very clear. Be ready to do tons of work!

Arguably the best professor I have had at Duke. She is incredibly knowledgeable, genuine, sharp, and generous. She gave me more opportunities to learn and thrive than any other professor I've had. She is deeply inspirational in her ability to speak her truth without compromise. The readings are heavy and not easy, but you will learn so much.
Professor Krylova was excellent and her knowledge or Russian History is insane. There is a fair bit of reading, but the readings are all interesting and as long as you read you will do fine.

Anna Krylova knows so much about Russia it is scary. So you will learn a lot, and what you learn is very interesting. She is a nice person and sharp thinker, but intimidating. Try to meet with her before turning in a paper because she looks for specific things, but is more than willing to work with you on your assignment.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: She is a tough grader and has high expectations, but she appreciates students who are willing to put in the effort and pay attention to details and email her. Always come prepared for class because it is what she expects you to do. However, it is one of the most rewarding classes I've taken at Duke and I definitely learned about Russian history.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I took Professor Krylova for her Russia & WW2 class and this one. I think she's one of the most underrated profs in history dept. She'll challenge you but is fair about it. Her classes are vvv interesting. Do the readings, be on time for class, don't miss class, and you'll learn a LOT. Otherwise, don't bother-- she'll shut you down in a second. :)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I know she has gotten negative reviews, but I do not think she is bad. Mainly, she gets this review because she makes you work for your grade and can often be unclear about what exactly she is looking for. That being said if you demonstrate that you read and you are not afraid to shoot her with a few emails to clarify expectations, you will be ok.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Krylova made Russian history really interesting, great selection of readings and topics. You learn SO much. But she can come across as condescending towards students' comments. Clearly has a "correct" opinion, which shows when she grades papers and responds in discussions. Class is more of a seminar than lecture with lots and lots of discussion
Very interesting readings; fun, discussion based class; Professor Krylova is incredibly knowledgeable about 20th century Russian history.
Professor Krylova is fantastic.  If you have any interest in the Soviet Union or 20th century history in general, The End of Russian Socialism is a must.
One of the best classes I have taken at Duke. She is very enthusiastic about the material and sets clear expectations. I would take anything she teaches.

I do not know why I took this course...  You have to read a lot and write a lot.  She talks too much and it's kind of hard to understand because of her accent.  Unless you are really into Russian history, this course is not recommended.

she is VERY intelligent and knows so much about what she is talking about, but she is native russian and is sometimes hard to understand, talks really fast, which is really hard to take notes. A LOT A LOT of readings!!!
not totally clear about expectations with readings and assignments, gives you the questions that will be on the test so it takes a real effort to fail, but there is a lot of information

I did well in her class, but that doesn't matter.  If you take her course, you will gain absolutely nothing from it intellectually.  She's a terrible lecturer and her comments on essays are unhelpful.  I don't understand how anyone can come away from this course thinking she's a good professor.
Exremely precise and clear. Lots of reading, but she always does a good job of synthesizing the material into manageable ideas.

One of my favorite classes I have taken at Duke. Participation matters and he cold calls. It is important to do readings because they are pop quizzes but makes the class discussion so much more interesting with everyone engaged. Very engaging and passionate lecturer, and you can tell he really cares about his students. 10/10 recommend for Pubpol302
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: One of the best professors I have had at Duke. Participation matters and he will cold call, but everyone is actively engaged. Do the readings, and be prepared for pop quizzes. Very knowledgeable and passionate, and it is obvious he cares about the success of his students a lot. 10/10 recommend for PubPol301!

Krishna is extremely knowledgeable and passionate, even though he took a little time to warm up to. The TAs were fabulous and graded essays kindly. Krishna does like to cold call and give pop quizzes, but as long as you at least skim the readings, you will be totally fine. I found the material surprisingly interesting for a required course.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Krishna was rude and had unclear grading expectations. I dreaded attending his class as he made it a tense environment. Coursework is interesting, but it is not worth taking his class. Other professors will also have interesting material, be respectful, and value your participation. Do not take his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: One of the best professors I've ever had. He loves what he does and you can notice it everyday. Ended class early by almost 30 minutes everyday, once we're done with content we're done. No b.s. He respects you if you respect him. Take him over any other professor offering 301. Don't expect to get an A unless you're doing dumb prep for the class.

Great class and Professor Krishna is hilarious - seriously learned a lot. That being said, I wish I knew how hard it was to get an A. The grading is very subjective and based on TAs who thinks an 80 is a great grade. I can testify it is possible to get an A but if all you care about is the grades, he is probably not the best to take with.

Krishna is incredibly engaging and cares about the material. However, your overall grade is based on three memos that are harshly graded, one midterm, and random pop quizzes. A few Bs on assignments will completely tank your grade in the course. TA bias is real. Getting stuck with a TA that doesn't like you will ruin your grade. Take with caution!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great guy, very intelligent, and I learned a lot. BUT don't take this class if you want an A. Grading system is crazy and is not made for students to get an A, no matter how much work you put into it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: While intelligent, clearly biased towards men. Thinks he is kinder than he is.

This was one of the classes within the PubPol core that reminded me why I chose PubPol to begin with. Krishna really makes you wrestle with the material and why it matters to broader political sphere. Excellent discussion and lectures, and you actually LEARN! Even though he's CLEARLY a research heavy professor, still an excellent lecturer.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: 301 w/ Krishna has hands-down been my favorite & most useful class for a pubpol/government major so far. Effectively teaches so many skills -- writing, analyzing, researching. Super nice & down to earth prof, often tries to be unbiased and calm (especially before & after 2016 election). Would take another class by him again without hesitation.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Great professor and extremely clear when conveying complex ideas through lectures. Memos follow one subject throughout semester which is actually a great idea. The readings can be dull but some are very interesting. Tests are take home case analyses. He learns everyone's name very quickly so you have to go to class. 4 random pop quizzes. Good prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Krishna is one of the best professors I've had at Duke. The lectures are good but the readings are a little boring. Still, he cares a lot about his students and learning to analyze policy is very interesting. The second half of the class is all about analyzing cases, which is great. There are four random pop quizzes which make up 10% of your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Caring

reviews.comment: Krishna is an amazing professor. He is very warm and outgoing, and his lectures are very engaging. Always tried to connect the readings to current events, and always seemed to care about his students' opinions and wellbeing. Readings can sometimes be long/dull, but for the most part are really interesting. Made me extremely passionate about pubpol

Krishna is a low-key amazing professor. Some of the readings are a tad dull but so long as you do them and participate in the class I think it is difficult to do poorly. He makes an effort to learn every students name and really values in class participation. He also finishes the class by fall break which is great if you have a lot of other exams.

Really helpful professor that is passionate about teaching.  He keeps class interesting by going off the books and holding class discussions to get students involved.  Made required subject matter interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Very interesting and very intelligent but also very self-assured.

As a professor, Krishna is fascinating.  It is definitely worth attending his lectures and doing assigned readings.  His classes are not easy and he is very strict.  Outside of class, however, he is often hard to approach and a little intimidating.

Prof. Krishna is awesome.  He is always ready to help or clarify anything that is unclear.  He is also a fair grader.  If you are sick, he will write a personal e-mail to you to hope everything is ok.  The only downside are the readings that he assigns.  Some of them are extremely boring.
Great professor, engaging, funny.
Just not a very good professor at the end of the day. Co taught with Canelas, and Canelas had to play good cop. Pretty sure everyone in this class got a B+ lol
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is kind and approachable, but I found the class hard for an intro course. The tests are challenging and don't align with practice questions you're given. I spent hours studying and still struggled to perform well. She doesn't go into detail on a lot of concepts, and I felt that I learned more from attending tutoring than through her slides.
She accused me of cheating mid final because my notecard was an inch too tall yet empty on the back. A second professor confirmed my test was completely fine. Thanks!

Dr. Martinez is super nice and a reasonably good lecturer. Midterms were very easy and similar to practice tests. Final was a little rough, but they curved it. Homework was an easy 100% in the grade book. Overall, it was pretty easy to finish the course with an A if you kept up with the material

Homework, labs, and exams are fair. Biggest help was practice problems and going to office hours. I didn't really show up to the lecture because I had a solid AP Chem background. Discussions were easy. Gen chem is always tough but I didn't think this class felt impossible.

Dr Martinez is a great professor. My biggest advice would be to do the textbook readings prior to the lectures, go to office hours and do as many questions as possible (discussion questions and the questions on the slideshows are great practice). Lectures are great and engaging, so def do no skip them.

Dr. Martinez is clearly passionate about her work. However, I found her lectures to be very unhelpful apart from the practice problems. The class's exams appeared designed to blatantly confuse you rather than test your acquired knowledge and whether you know how to apply it. Be ready to self study. Do practice exams/problems weeks before tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Very sweet professor and genuinely cares for you to succeed. I wish I put in more effort because she makes it easy to get a good grade. She allows a cheat sheet every exam, and extra 10% in your discussion grade + grades everything to allow the highest possible grade distribution for you. Very sweet overall and helpful

Dr. Martinez is so sweet and honestly I went to most lectures but you don't really need to to do well. I would recommend reviewing things before the lectures or doing khan academy because it makes the lectures make a lot more sense and help put things together. Tests had hard questions but they were definitely fair, & lots of past exams available

Professor Martinez is very sweet and she cares about her students. That being said, you could probably skip most of the lectures and do fine on the exams with a lot of self-studying. She provides past exams as practice - I thought the actual exams were fair but more difficult. Exams not curved.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Martinez is a really sweet professor who clearly cares a lot about her students' success. Her lectures and practice materials are thorough and reflective of exams, so while consistent effort is necessary, getting an A isn't at all an impossible task!

Pr. Martinez is very sweet, but not a great teacher. Going to lecture was not helpful and I learned a majority of the material by self-studying. The course material is not necessarily hard, but you need to practice a lot in order to score well on exams. Final was hard. Tests are not curved. Do the practice exams and re-do the discussion worksheets.
Study practice tests

For a “standardized course”, there were lots of discrepancies this sem. Class wasn't difficult (minus the final) so I'm confused why there aren't more students w A's. Anna isn't a bad prof but she's unwilling to adapt her teaching to her students needs. Last sem she had Cox & Liu to help her, but letting Anna solo Chem 101 this sem was a bad idea.

I can tell that Dr. Martinez cares about her students and I prefer the way she teaches more than Cox. That being said, the class is difficult (regardless of professor). 1st midterm median grade (67) was very low, other midterms were better, final was difficult. Definitely put in work early in the semester/go to office hours to ensure you understand

Exam1 DIFFICULT, average 60 no curve, LOW midterm 1 grade. Exam2+3 a bit better. Final=atrocious, SUPER difficult, Martinez gave students false hope to increase their final grade, things never learned in class tested, no regrades, no discussion of material tested. Average grade=B, no room for higher even with extra credit, overall awful experience.

Dr. Martinez is a really nice person and I preferred how she taught when compared to Cox. She teaches the basics so it is easy to understand the basics, but not what she puts on the tests. There was no curve even one of the mid-terms' test average was a 60. Last semester there was and they got a retake which was very unfair.The final tanked my gpa.

The syllabus states 'everyone can earn an A,' but I think that's inaccurate. Lectures drag on, Aktiv barely helps. That first exam put me at a low starting point. Improving over the next two exams happens, but that final was so difficult and different from the midterms that it crushed my progress, so it didn't matter which grading scale she used.

This was one of the most frustrating experiences. The final was NOT fair by any means. All the work you put into the semester is not reflected because the final will bring your grade down. You MUST end the class with a higher grade going into the final because your final WILL bring your grade down. Want a B+? Must have had an A- before the final.

For her other exams, you can complete the discussions multiple times, do the practice exams, and do very well on each midterm. Our final wasn't fair at all. Questions we've never seen before or tried were on it. And she never even provided an answer key to the provided practice final. She's an average professor but prepare for a hard final.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Her final exam was atrocious and misaligned with the other midterms she has given. The final had problems students were seeing for the first time. Last semester, students were given a retake. Extreme differences in semester difficulty and unfairness by semester hurts students. I should've taken it last semester w the handicap and easier final exam.

One of the better chem101 professors for lecture continuity and answering questions. Course is somewhat misaligned between lecture and lab, but both doable while tedious. Exams are fair and have relatively reduced weight due to many other assignments and discussions.
clear but boring lectures, fair tests, but uses a bunch of different platforms that can be hard to keep track of. Labs are super long, tedious, and time-consuming.

For Chem 101, Martinez is probably the best professor. However, her lectures are a little bit hard to understand. Also, whenever she answered questions she had a bit of a condescending/angry tone? Chem 101 is a big struggle overall but a ton of students have to take it; just prepare yourselves.

Had her for Chem 99 and 101. Excellent lecturer, very clear expectations. Lots of practice tests and homework/discussion problems with keys. Incredibly kind and accessible outside of class. Test problems are similar to problems worked in class/discussion, very doable with some effort. Highly recommend Chem 99 for those with limited chem experience!

Very sweet and caring professor. However, her exams are extremely hard and purposely try to trick you. She always makes a hard question like 20 points. I will say, she does give partial credit which is nice.

Martinez is one of the greatest profs I've had. It's clear from her lectures that she has a very thorough understanding of chemistry and explains topics in the clearest and sweetest way possible. Don't be afraid to ask questions! She provides a lot of study resources; use as many as possible to prepare for exams. Midterms aren't hard but final was.

Dr. Martinez truly cares about her students and wants you to do well! She answers emails quickly, which is impressive considering that she teaches mass lectures, and many test problems are taken directly from the weekly worksheets. She clearly lays out what she wants you to know, and it is easy to do well in this class if you put the work in.

She wants you to do well; plenty of practice problems and textbook problems for before each test. Weekly discussion worksheets (graded for completion), weekly quizzes (group-based and relatively easy), easy homework. Will adjust the weight of your midterms if one is seriously bringing your grade down, listens to student feedback. Take her chem 101
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Rezvani was incredible. A  deeply caring professor, he encourages discussion during lecture, and wants the class to be "a family." Our guest lecturers talked about their own experiences with addiction which changed my perspective of the disease. The final is chill as long as you review the slides. Best class I've taken at Duke - he is so sweet.

The guest lecturers were frequent and phenomenal. It is genuinely not hard to get an A. Yes, you won't know your grade until the end, but as long as you put effort into the two graded assignments we have throughout the semester, you will end with an A. If you know everything on the slides for the final, it is the same + open note at the end incase

you won't know your grade until the end. very unclear grading criteria. two presentations and a final exam. final exam questions are very arbitrary and questions are nearly impossible to solve without the open notes access he gives last 10 min of the exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very random class structure and is unclear on grading policies.
Good teacher

Dr. Rezvani makes it clear how much he cares about his students and always makes classes very entertaining with his humor. The guest speakers he invites are also amazing and solidify the learning we do during the semester.
This class was amazing. Dr. Rezvani is so funny and entertaining. The topics are very interesting and you will learn lots if you focus. It is not a difficult class.

Very caring professor! Emphasizes a "family environment" and facilitates this by making his class a safe space to share experiences/ideas without judgment. No tests except for a book quiz and an open-note final. Would highly recommend taking his FOCUS class!

Dr. Rezvani is super caring and his lecturers are very informational and entertaining. This class allows you to learn about addiction and substance abuse in a stress-free manner, and your grade is determined by projects and participation. The guest speakers, debates, and field trip were the best part. Definitely take this class!

Dr. Rezvani is very casual, and we all love him. The class was memorable for the field trips and group projects, but it's not engaging. The lecture portions seem unstructured and meandering, and there are very few standards for the indiv/group projects. Poor class to learn psych, great class to get immersed in the culture and consequences of drugs.

Dr. Rezvani is very nice and funny. His stories are very interesting. The addiction course is pretty interesting and a super easy A. Only three projects and he is an easy grader. Would highly recommend this course.

Dr. Rezvani's class is the best class that I have taken at Duke. He is passionate about the information that he teaches and is determined to create a stress-free environment. The class has no tests or quizzes and is solely based on gaining valuable information.

Dr. Rezvani is so passionate about this class. He's the kind of professor who really wants to make a difference for students. His class is literally so easy - there are no exams and only four assignments all semester. But, the guest speakers and activities really make you want to pay attention and learn. Overall, one of the best profs I've had.

Class isn't too hard, but it's really interesting material.  Professor Rezvani keeps it interesting and does a variety of lectures, projects, speakers, and discussions in class.  There aren't any tests, grading is based on attendance, participation, two reflection papers, and two projects.
Very enthusiastic and funny. Knew material well and encouraged class discussion. Mandatory field trip was graded but if you went you got all points available.

Genuinely learned nothing. A waste of tuition. Would not recommend. I think there are classes that are easy A's where you can walk away having learned at least one thing. I could not say that about this class. She overcomplicates every topic. Free A, but if you're at duke I would think you would hope to take something out of a class.

This class is possibly one of the easiest offered at Duke. Dr. Hall is incredibly caring and accommodating, but class periods often feel like a waste of time. I didn't walk away from this course feeling like I learned much (if any) new content. Class discussions can be good when everyone buys into them. Almost everyone walks away with an A.

I totally recommend this focus class, it was very light coursework, the material is obscure but interesting. We reviewed an array of writing, movies, tv shows, articles, and art that were all unique. The field trips were: the beach, the art museum, and the archives. Dr. Hall is caring but tends to overexplain or overcomplicate topics of discussion.
Very easy going and caring, you learn a lot.

Dr. Hall made it clear that she was there for you, especially outside of class time. The course itself was almost no work, just a 1-3 page paper about every week. Readings were often just watching Star Trek. The grading scale was unclear, because it seemed that she loved everyone's papers. You get what you put into the class.

Great class for first years. Dr Hall is really caring and wants all of her students to feel welcomed. She gives great feedback and the only assignments are weekly 1-2 page papers. I would recommend to any upcoming first year at Duke. She's great!

Dr. Hall is the BEST professor I have had during my time at Duke. She gives incredible feedback, assigns interesting and approachable texts, and always takes the time to listen to her students. You will not regret taking a class with her. She is a gift to Duke.

Professor Hall is one of the most caring professors I've ever had. She is genuinely concerned for the wellbeing of her students and is very respectful in class. The topics studied in her Global Health focus class are interesting, and she leads discussion well. Only one close reading paper due per week, and she's an easy grader.

Dr. Hall is absolutely one of the best professors I could've asked for my first semester here. She is so genuinely caring, kind, and wants her students to do well. She encourages controversy and individual ideas, and is always so happy to talk to you about her ideas, while encouraging you to share you own. LOVE HER I will be taking any class by her

Duke undergrads, don't let her tenure in the Divinity School scare you: she is not here to preach! Throughout the semester, she fostered thoughtful conversations and a respectful class environment as we discussed a variety of controversial topics in global health. I would take another class of hers no matter what the subject.

LOVE HER. Seriously so, so sweet and caring. Dr. Hall is so thoughtful and genuinely wants everyone to feel comfortable and succeed in her class. I don't think I've ever met someone so nice. PLEASE take a class from her. She has such a unique perspective and helps you see the world from a different lens. Wonderful person and professor.

Dr. Hall is a saint. She goes above and beyond in everything she does. You get the feeling that she actually cares about her students, as in actually living out what it means to be a Christian professor.

Amy Laura Hall is one of the best professors I have EVER had. She cares more about her students engaging with the material rather than have them regurgitate information simply for a grade. There is no such thing as boring in her class because she makes sure students are always involved in the discussion. She's also an amazing person to get to know!
Amazing professor.  Genuinely interested in class/students' progress.  Definitely recommend taking her courses.
Just a bad experience overall

Kathie is one of the most amazing professors at Duke. It is sad to see students grade low on her because they didn't get a good grade in her class. I don't think any professors would grade them lower if they are respectful students. 

I miss her lectures after graduation. Some speech skills are still critical for my work. 100% recommend her.

There is some team project that you are required to purchase halfway through the class, but it is worth it.  The text is free exerpts and case studies.  This is a mandatory course and benefits the students.  Groups meet about once a week.

Professor Amato provided reasonably thorough and interesting lectures to view on Sakai.  Definitely view them at at least 1.5x speed, likely 2x speed.  Assignments are productive but not overkill, not an excessive workload.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: She is very clear at explaining and gives elaborate examples from real businesses. Her lectures are often informative but have little two-way interaction, so students may feel drowsy. The group business case analyses and the HBS articles are the most valuable parts of this class. Prof Kathie gives little feedback on these analyses, though.
The most arbitrary grader!
She is absolutely the worst professor at Duke. Extremely arbitrary grader. She does not treat everyone fairly and equally. Avoid her if you can.
Kathie is great! Super nice, knows her stuff, and truly cares about her students. Class is very straightforward. If you put in the effort, you'll get an A. Would recommend!

I hated this class simply because I feel like I did not learn anything in it, but Kathie Amato is a true gem. She is an amazing lecturer and works incredibly hard to make our class time the best possible. The tests are super fair and straightforward, and the assignments are interesting, real-world case studies.
Super simple concepts made really difficult with proofs and insane stats-based lectures. Exam averages were incredibly low and he blamed us for it.

I was coming to leave a review. But it seems my classmates already took care of it🤣🤣
Nothing left for me to say! Good luck to whoever is next!
Only the top 15% can get an A. Good Luck y'all.
Better not to take this course. Need to be top percent to get an A. Worst worst worst.
The practice was not in the same world as the real tests. The average on midterm 2 was a 40 and the lectures were confusing and unhelpful.
Bad. Take with any other professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Terrible. Such a god awful professor. The content in the class is so so simple, he teaches it to us in complex mathematical proofs that have no significance for the class or the test at all.

Patton's slides are a meandering stream of consciousness, only decipherable through his lectures in which he speaks so quietly that no one can understand him. Zero correlation between lecture and exams. Changed the grading scheme in the last half of class, obviating any hard work done on the two midterms. Do NOT recommend.

Patton's slides were very long and his temper with students was quite short. Anytime someone asked him to post slides or asked about his grading policy he was very defensive. Slides were so hard to get through, my TA carried this course. He made things easy to explain. An A is manageable but it's stressful because you never know w/ Patton's style.

Please never take Prof Patton. He is not very nice and makes backhanded comments. One class a student asked him to put the slides on the board and he refused because of the "lack of students in class that day". If you are going to care about attendance, please make it required instead of punishing the people there. 0/10 would not recommend.
the worst. Absolute worst.
Honestly, one of the hardest classes I've ever taken. Save yourself from stress if you don't need this class. Econ majors- good luck with this professor; you'll learn more on your own.

Worst class ever taken at Duke. Horrible lectures. Couldn't dumb any of the content down for us to comprehend. Never thought I'd withdraw from a class until this. People who've never stepped foot in lecture do FAR better than those who attend consistently. Had to adjust the grading after 2nd midterm, but told the class that most of us were cooked.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: the most evil person . never take. ignorant
Do not take this class with Patton. "Either I made the test horrible or you all didn't understand the material, but either way I'm not changing anything"
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Patton takes simple things and overcomplicates them to the point of nausea. Some students have done better in the course not having attended any of the mandatory lectures than those who have attended all of them. He gave the class practice midterms that are unrecognizable from the midterms he gives. Simply put, he does not care about his students.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Patton has an incredible ability to make the easiest content complex. Lectures barely make sense and I already have to teach myself the material.

"If you do not present, we would assume that you are not interested in studying financial econometrics anymore", "Stop talking about theorem", "This is a terrible presentation." Theses are only tips of the iceberg. Faculty members in your group are very aggressive and nasty. Do not threat a student in this manner.
You can stay calm and do not have to yell at students.
He's fine, no complaints but nothing to praise. If you have a vague background in Statistics, you'll be fine. Just don't procrastinate on problem sets. Sick accent too.

The lectures are a little redundant, but he posts the slides, so you can just find the important info. The homework is very light and usually pretty easy (you can work in groups too). He doesn't give answers to the exams, but the TA's provided them in discussion. Exams weren't ridiculous, but the class is graded on a curve.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Patton is a fine lecturer, sometimes dull sometimes interesting; slides are a little bloated and must be filtered for important info. Class has a light workload, with 1 Pset a week that takes about 2 hrs. Curve is fair with top 25th %tile receiving A and 50-75th %tile receiving A-. Students who took AP Stats have a HUGE advantage due to overlap.

Way overqualified for this class. He made introductory concepts super abstract, especially on exams to get a lower test average. I got an A in 201 and B here, which I think reflects how this class is curved down because you have kids with a stats background who never go to lecture but destroy the curve. 201 is much more of a level playing field.
Clear lectures, everything you need is provided. Problem sets are pretty short and straightforward, very heklpful for exams.

For an intro class, Patton makes things beyond complicated. The things he takes two hours to explain can be summarized in five minutes. Expect to solely depend on self studying off of YouTube videos and your smart friends.

Had Patton for 104 async. Lecture videos were clear, all concepts well-explained and proved when necessary. Sometimes needed to watch a section twice to understand it, but being async that was easy. HW was easy, and exams were pretty much a joke (and would have been even without open note). Great HW policy-bottom two grades dropped.

Very good at overcomplicating the simplest statistics concepts. Would have rather taken any other statistics class for the intro statistics credit. No answers for problem sets or practice tests, which is essential to help us prepare. The only reason students were not overly stressed was because the class is pass/fail. You won't learn anything.

Professor Patton is really smart and there's no doubt he's an expert in his field. But for a 100-level class, not a great professor. He takes very simple stats concepts and makes them very convoluted. Lectures are super long but don't actually provide a lot of information or material to work with. And he never provided answers to psets or exams.
A very condescending professor and does not provide answer keys to the practices and overcomplicates a lot of easy concepts. Could've definitely done better. he's v smart tho

I took Forecasting Financial Markets class with Prof. Patton. He was engaged with the material and made it quite accessible and interesting (despite it being often quite heavy and technical). He closely follows the notes he uploads, which is hepful. The computer assigments were useful as well. Exams, though challenging, are predictable.

Professor Anderson was a really nice professor and the class itself was enlightening and interesting. Work load was mostly nonexistent aside from a couple of assignments but there is a mandatory 20 hour service requirement which is easy to fulfill. Somewhat slow with grading but is much more interested in discussion than being a strict grader.
Dr. Anderson is an extremely caring and kind professor. Her class is pretty easy, and although it can be a bit slow at some points, she creates a very good classroom environment.

I love Dr. Anderson!! She's a little disorganized at times, but during lecture you can tell she genuinely cares about what she's teaching. Classes are mostly discussion-based, and she does a great job about facilitating interesting conversations in class. The assignments themselves are relatively easy but time-consuming—do the work & you'll be ok!

I believe Dr. Anderson is a wonderful person who genuinely cares about her students and what they get out of the course. However, she is extremely disorganized, has yet to grade assignments from September, and many students feel like they did not learn anything substantial about education. As ed minors, this is a troubling example of education.

Super easy class and kind professor, but as someone who genuinely wants to learn about education, I didn't learn much at all, and I was disappointed that this was a class that is required for the education minor. There's no rigor, and class is extremely disorganized. It feels like most people are taking it for an easy A, unfortunately.

Professor Anderson is really kind and cares about every student on an individual level. While she was often scattered and the class was not particularly organized, it was an easy class and Anderson made it known that she was looking out for us. Final project was a lot of work, but not graded harshly. I'd recommend this class

Dr. Anderson is THE best professor at Duke. She genuinely cares about her students, always thanks you for participating, and creates an amazing learning environment for everyone. If you show up to class, participate in lectures, and do the assignments, you will get an A. Highly recommend.
She is very nice and the class is pretty easy. You should get an A  if you do the assignments on time.
Such a kind professor. She can be a little scattered sometimes, and she's not always clear about what her expectations are for assignments, but as long as you do the work you'll likely get an A.

Such a nice and caring professor. Class is not hard but there are a good amount of assignments! Attendance is not taken but class is small enough where she would realize if you never showed up. Don't have to do any of the reading for class.

I really enjoyed this class. It was an easy A and not stressful at all. The material was kinda plain but I enjoyed our assignments and discussions and loved tutoring kids once a week for an hour. Take this class if you want a very easy, stress free time with a very kind, lenient, and caring professor.

I took this class online because of COVID and had no service learning component. Prof. Anderson is super sweet, and the class is an easy A. At times, it could get boring, and it felt like some our topics didnt quite fully interconnect. Its an easy and stress free class, but I didnt get a ton out of it.

In retrospect, I'm not really sure I could name one concrete thing I learned from this class. I don't think we spent enough time talking through the implications of service learning, but I don't really know what we spent time on instead. She covered subjects so topically and quickly that nothing really stuck. Super sweet, but not a great teacher.

Dr. Anderson is very knowledgeable and passionate about education. Her class is easy but also interesting, and readings are not required. Beware, there is a lot of group work and the final project is quite tedious and lengthy although it is very leniently graded. Definitely take Ed 101 if you're interested in education or looking for an easy A.
Awesome teacher. 10/10.
Great professor. Final project is hefty, but other than that not too hard.

Dr. Anderson is a very sweet lady, and her class is a super easy filler. I really enjoyed the service-learning aspect of this class, but the lectures are pointless and, at times, boring. There are quite a few writing assignments, but you don't have to stress over making them exceptional because she grades super easily.
Love Amy. Everyone should take a class with her. She's got a really chill vibe but you come away with so much learning. 100% take classes with her
The class had a lot of work. Essays were pretty common but they werent difficult. Interesting topics and Prof. Anderson is great. Easy A as long as you participate
Prof. Anderson is really nice and makes the class very enjoyable. Not much work. A few papers and reflections due throughout the semester.
Professor Anderson is a wonderful lady who is extremely kind and caring for her students. Make sure you do your service learning and show up and participate in class in a little and you will be fine.

A dedicated educator. She is so caring and sweet, and always says the right thing when discussing important issues. She is a bit scatter-brained... late to class, forgets about her own assignments, and an easy A.

Terrible professor. we didn't go in depth into any topics at all, i found myself falling asleep all the time, didn't show up to the last 3 weeks of class, still an easy A. Definitely the easiest class I've taken at Duke

Dr. Anderson is one of the nicest, most inspirational faculty members I've encountered at Duke. While I can't say I learned all that much from her lectures or assignments, I was motivated by her to continue studying education. Know that there are a few group projects and some long papers and, most importantly, that she takes attendance for a grade.

The class is very easy overall. Professor Anderson is super nice and passionate about the subject. There are no tests, just a lot of readings (that you really don't need to do). Your grade is dependent on participation and a few papers, so if you put in the work, you'll get an A. Plus the material is very interesting

Dr. Anderson is an amazing professor! She's very passionate and knowledgeable about what she does. To top that off, she's incredibly friendly and very easy to talk to -- she clearly cares about her students. Her class is a moderate amount of work, but it's all pretty easy.

Dr. Anderson is really focused on making sure that by the time her students are done with her class, they will have a great knowledge base on the field of Education.  She is very friendly and is always willing to help out in any way possible.

Amy is a great professor that cares a lot about the subject and her students. She is willing to help with anything you need even if it does not pertain to the class. She's always available to speak and help you with any essays or reflections. I would recommend taking this class

This class is a complete nightmare! The material might be interesting, but the way it's taught is unbelievably dull. The professor just throws these super complicated definitions on the board without explaining anything, and then we're stuck doing endless problem sets. Seriously, save yourself the stress and avoid this class at all costs!

too much homework requiring tedious calculation, though the professor looks friendly
DON'T take it

It constantly felt as though there was a large jump in what we learned in class and what we were expected to know for HW (and Exams). It would have been okay if he was willing to help with HW but he outright refused to and the solutions posted afterward were often convoluted or wrong. Just be prepped to do a lot of review/research + go to OH w/ TA

Problem sets are inevitable because of the difficult nature of the course, but hard work pays off. Also, the prof is a really nice guy, trying to make the course as interactive and understandable as possible.
Great intuitive lecturer. Very organized and presents the material in a digestible way. The tests were difficult but not unexpectedly so.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Soft voice, hardly recognizable handwriting, pink marker pen, poor English grammar, plus super super hard exam. Recommended if you feel this world has been in peace for too long, and you want to experience desperation.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Dr. Randles took a course I was stressed about taking due to the precedent established by another professor and made it fantastic. She is approachable and will discuss both the class content and future goals. She teaches quickly but will stop at any point for questions. She cares about her students and doesn't want the class to become a burden.

Randles is that mf. She turns 307 from just a numbers & equations physics class to something where you can actually understand the practical CV effects of the stuff you learn. This is evident in the paper presentations and the computer projects. Textbook examples directly apply to HW/Quizzes/Tests, which she makes an effort to make manageable.

Impossibly disorganized professor. Professor did not host office hours and left help sessions and certain lectures entirely to the discretion of TAs. The TAs were good but the TAs should not be the ones teaching the class (professors should be the ones teaching their own classes). Due dates were never clarified and led to constant anxiety.

Dr. Herring is great. A very sweet professor who really cares about her students & her work. The class itself was very challenging & rigorous as someone without stats or coding experience; I spent a LOT of time on weekly labs & the final project. Exams are difficult, but I steadily improved with each; use all the practice tests/problems she gives!

Prof. Herring is extremely knowledgable and a great professor. However, STA198 can be a harder / higher workload class than expected, especially if you have no prior statistics or R background. She is dedicated to ensuring you succeed and it's possible to do so regardless of background knowledge, but be prepared to do a lot of work for this class.

Sta 198 is a very rigorous class if you have no statistics/R background. The time commitment to this class is much more than I was expecting because you have labs and homework which are coding on R, but then the exams are on probability, so it can be difficult to keep up with both sides of the class throughout the semester.

Professor herring is very kind, helpful, and knowledgeable! However If this is your first exposure to stat and/or using R, it will be somewhat difficult for an intro course and you will have to do a little more work to understand the material.

I think on the long run I am a better Statistician because of Dr. Herring. But as an intro level class it was a) Unbelievably rigorous in time commitment from "deliverables", b) Herring is so smart she often skips the "instructing" part and we have to look up how to write the code ourselves or ask the AMAZING Jackie Du (thank you sm), c) lots of R.

For a new class (debuted Fall 20), this class is really well structured. Herring is super helpful and passionate about the material. The TAs for this class are also great - s/o Jackie. Note however that this class is significantly more work than Sta 199. Youre expected to know more and the exams are in-person + closed book as opposed to take-home.

I would not recommend this class if you don't have any stats or coding experience. Dr. Herring is a great person and very passionate about what she teaches. There's weekly group work for labs where you code in R. The midterms are quite hard. The subject matter is very interesting with its focus on global health.

Herring is a super sweet professor who is eager to help you learn class content. The course is pretty lecture-heavy, but Herring does her best to keep things interesting, drawing on real world examples and anecdotes. She is assessable through office hours which I definitely recommend.

STA 540/440 is always one of the most intensive classes for the major. However, Amy is the real gem; she made all of the work you put in meaningful. She responded to questions very fast and help you get things done. The grading is reasonable if you go to OH and discuss ideas. Typically we cannot choose 440 professors, but I felt lucky to have Amy.

440 will be hard regardless of the prof (very heavy workload), but I feel lucky to have taken it with Amy. She is very nice, gives great project feedback, and will adjust deadlines and project requirements if they are unreasonable. Expectations are not always 100% clear, but that's the nature of 440. Go to OH and get good project groups to do well

This class was ridiculous. Nobody told me that it would be so much work. I was planning on a decent amount of work, but it ended up being about 5x what I expected. There's a group project deliverable due at all times, a huge individual project, and everybody gets slaughtered by the super harsh grading.
Good lecture with a good professor. Suggest taking if you are willing to learn about hierarchical models.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Group projects

reviews.comment: Probability with Dunlap was one of the hardest but most rewarding classes I've taken. His problem sets and exams are insanely difficult, but he curves exams very generously and gives lots of partial credit. His lectures are dense but very clear, and you will learn the material inside and out if you put in the effort.

Nice guy, and knowledgeable. However, he lectures straight from the textbook with no additional content, so don't bother showing up to class. Homeworks assumed knowledge of comp sci, differential equations, real and complex analysis. Tests were little better. Do not expect an A unless you have previously had a rigorous treatment in probability.

Professor Dunlap is brilliant and inspirational. His lectures are clear and engaging, and he makes learning very accessible. His available and happy to help, and is always patient with us. I also love the subject, but with his teaching style it was my favorite class at Duke!

Clearly deep knowledge of the subject; fast-paced lectures but never felt out-of-control-fast. Short homeworks but required several hours each (Questions were hard); reasonable exams (mainly high level "do you understand at all how this works" questions). Banger infinite monkeys on a typewriter casino example to explain applications of martingales

Dr. Dunlap is one of the best math professors I've had, especially given it was his first semester at Duke! He showed incredibly deep understanding of the material yet could explain it on a high level to beginners. Kind-hearted, patient, engaging, and a great lecturer. All the problem sets were conducive to my learning to preparation for exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Dunlap is insanely smart and he knows the material deeply. The homeworks were really hard, but usually had ~4 questions. Tests were fair and curved generously. He responds quickly and is helpful in office hours.

Professor Jordan is incredibly accessible outside class and genuinely cares about her students. Her classes are fun, innovative, and engaging, making learning enjoyable. She fosters an inclusive environment and celebrates diverse festivals, making everyone feel valued. A truly caring and impactful professor.

If you are at Duke and you miss out on taking a class from Prof. Jordan, boy-o-boy, that is going to be a big mistake. She is inspiring, hilarious, easy to go, caring and fun loving. She teaches with real world example and is a phenomenal instructor who is available outside class. Hands down the best Professor during my time at Duke!

Professor Allegra is a truly caring and thoughtful educator who is deeply committed to her students' growth. She genuinely wants her students to succeed, be prepared, and feel confident. Beyond the classroom, she is supportive, approachable, and invested in helping students become not only capable professionals but also happy individuals.

Allegra is an exceptional professor who combines intellectual depth with emotional intelligence, creating a highly engaging and meaningful learning experience. Her classes are practical, forward-looking, and encourage natural participation. I'm grateful to have taken her course and for our meaningful interactions inside and outside the classroom.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Jordan provides inspirational and detailed feedback to both our individual and team assignments. Her feedback helped me grow a lot from her class. She is also very accessible outside of classes. She is always trying her best to help her students get the most out of her classes. She is such an amazing professor! Love all her classes!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I was both a student and TA for Prof. Allegra and looking back on my time at Duke, she will stand out as one of the most transformative and caring professors I've ever had in my academic career. You'll be hard pressed to find another professor that will take the time and effort to believe in you, given you show up with the intention to grow.

Some people leave an impact greater than they can even imagine in your life and Prof. Jordan is one such personality. Each of her slide is based on a book and she takes efforts to keep her presenting content upto date till the morning of each lecture & her content caters all human senses through video, audio, text, humor, body movement and more.

Prof Allegra is an incredible mentor and professor. She truly cares about your growth, values, and well-being. Her course reshapes how you understand management by grounding leadership in purpose and real practice rather than self-help ideas. One of the most valuable classes I've taken at Duke.

I really like Professor Allegra, her method of teaching is very useful. I really love the props she gets to class, makes the class feel more light and good. The only thing I would change about this class is the amount of assignments, it's a tad too much. But apart from that really good teaching style

Prof. Allegra is the most caring and inspiring professor I ever met. She creates a warm and supportive classroom environment where every student feels seen and valued. Her teaching goes beyond leadership and she models kindness, authenticity, and genuine care. Her encouragement has left a lasting impact on me. I'm truly grateful to be her student.

Allegra has been incredibly supportive both when I was a student in her class and when I worked as a TA. She genuinely cares about us beyond just academics — she always shows concern for our well-being and personal growth. It not only shaped the way I think but also provided practical knowledge and mindset that help me as I enter the real world.

Prof. Allegra is the personification of a good parent at your university: tough but fair, challenges you but also helps you, & goes out of their way to help you.

Apart from being an amazing person & having decades of experience, she is a fantastic teacher and her classes are full of long-term insights.

Professor Allegra is one of the few professors who actually cares about students as a human being. I am surprised she would remember every student's life experiences and background, especially since she has to deal with hundreds of students every semester. I feel safe to share anything with her and I know she will always try her best to help.

Some of the material in this class was very interesting and presented in interactive and engaging ways, but some of her lectures either advocated for unethical/illegal business practices or dealt with the subject matter (especially non-binary people) in uncomfortable ways. She also made me uncomfortable in how she addressed me and singled me out.

Prof Jordan is of the most caring & insightful professors I've had. She has a deep, genuine care for her students and works hard to enable us to succeed.

The class itself has provided me with the tools to discover and refine my leadership style and has given me much more confidence in my skills. I cannot say enough good about Prof Jordan and 540

Appears to be in mortal fear of chat GPT despite the usage of chat GPT being not as widespread as she suspects. Incredibly micromanaged classroom. Class is not overly difficult and for some you may not be bothered by the micromanagement but it rubs me the wrong way. Lectures are long but dont cover much material. Feels like a highschool class.

I had doubts taking Bio420 when I read the reviews on RMP, but I was so happy I ultimately took this course with Dr. B! The workload is very manageable, and she takes time to give very caring feedback on the weekly assignment to keep you on track. I felt very supported as she was more than happy to answer questions and provide EC
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Favorite class I've taken at Duke! Dr. B posts her lecture slides w/ speaker notes, so this is a great class to just listen/engage during the lectures. Material is difficult but weekly quizzes provide opportunities to study along the way. So cool to learn the pathways and find yourself understanding complex journal articles related to cancer.

One of the worst professors at Duke. Rude, combative to any questions, and treats students with disrespect when they're just trying to learn. No clue why anyone would go into academia just to be a terrible and negative figure to undergrad students. Do not take her class.

I would not recommend taking cancer genetics with Amy Bejsovec. The subject matter of the course is very interesting, but she makes this class unenjoyable because of the hostile environment she fosters. If you have questions about the subject, expect a sassy and judgmental response back from her. She is not a kind or patient professor.

I don't really like the way she lectures which doesn't help when genetics is already difficult (at least for me). She kind of rambles on but the lecture slides are helpful. I had a different professor for the evolution part of the course and she was way better. Doable class but not the best professor. She answers emails though.

Dr. B was very enthusiastic and knowledgeable about genetics as a topic. With that being said, the material she taught was very difficult. She often lectured as if we have prior knowledge of the material, forgetting that her class is an introductory Bio course. Although a wonderful human being, Dr. Bejsovec is not suited for teaching intro Bio.

I personally thought that Dr. B was a better lecturer than Dr. Yoder, but I have taken AP Bio and was in the genetics focus. She is obviously passionate about her subject, but she definitely isn't great at teaching students, especially ones who have no prior knowledge of the subject. She provides the slideshows with extra notes on every slide.

The lectures lowkey felt like Dr. B was showing off what she knew about genetics, rather than focusing on teaching students who don't know anything. You'll probably do a lot better in this class if you took AP Bio, but if not, you'll need to do a lot of studying outside of class. The good thing is all the exams are open note and there's no final!

Dr. B is a very sweet lady who is passionate about her field of study. However, the content she teaches is very confusing and doesn't understand that most of the students in her class haven't taken biology since high school. She is always quick to jump into the more advanced concepts without throughly covering the basic ones. Avoid this class.

Nice lady but awful teacher. Covers material too quickly and doesn't thoroughly explain topics that are confusing. Ridiculously quick turnaround to learn + complete graded assignments. Assigned questions are poorly written/confusing which only makes hard material further challenging. Sad because I enjoy Bio but this course is ruining it for me.

Let me start by saying that Dr. B is a delightful woman with a contagious passion for biology. That being said, she is one of THE WORST teachers I have had. She speaks a million miles an hour and covers a ton of info every lecture. This is impossible to learn from- she makes an easier subject harder than organic chemistry in my opinion.

Horrible at teaching intro to bio, Anne Yoder is 10000x better at lecturing than she is. Lectures are extremely dense and she will test you on the most minute details that are in the caption of a picture on a slide. Bio 201 is a BREEZE compared to Bio 202. I took this class without Bio 201 first and she assumes you know more than you do.

Earlier I thought she was meh but now that Dr. Yoder is teaching, I realize how horrible Bejsovec was, which would explain why the class was true suffering. Each lecture slide had way too much info on it and there was no time to breathe in lecture. Weekly quizzes on material from the same day. She can't teach. Avoid for your own good. Worst class.

Teaches an intro bio class at a level much higher than it should be at, it feels more like a 400 or graduate level genetics course. No time to synthesize and process information before being tested on it. Avoid taking it with Dr. Bejsovec and take it whenever Dr. Willis is teaching.

The only good thing about this class is that she posts her powerpoints with speaker notes, so I can at least go back and try to comprehend what shes trying to explain. Shes just TERRIBLE at explaining concepts - even after rewatching sections of her lectures countless times and I will still have NO CLUE what shes talking about.

When people say she is demeaning towards questions, it's more like she's offended at people not immediately synthesizing information with something from 4 lectures ago. She's better off in her lab crossing flies than teaching. Dreadful class. 7 weeks of suffering. Fortunately she only teaches the first half. DON'T TAKE THIS CLASS WITH HER.

I don't understand why people are being so hard on her. She's a good professor just trying to relay a lot of information in an introductory class. The turn-around time for quizzes is short but manageable. She is also really responsive to emails and helpful in office hours. Put in the work, and you'll do fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Cannot relay information in a way students actually understand and assumes everything is "common sense". Exam and quiz questions always have ambiguous terms, making answers unclear. I heard bio202 used to be fun and easy, not when online and with this prof. Wait for Willis to teach 202 if you have to take this course.

I truly feel for professors in an online semester. HOWEVER, this woman clearly has not taking a single second to think of what learning is like for students. Expecting them to pay attention to 75 minutes of INTENSE lecture and then immediately testing on it is ridiculous. I would avoid even in an in-person semester because she clearly does not care

Incredible volume of work shoved at you on Monday and Wednesday with a quiz on all of it on Thursday. There is no time to actually process any of the information, which is already complex enough and not explained well in lecture. Quizzes/exams expect large jumps in intuition from the lecture slides. Avoid, avoid, avoid.

she doesn't know how to teach. like others have said, she lectures m/w then gives you a hard quiz the next day. she knows a alot about genetics and flies but cant explain it in a way that anyone understands or cares about. this class and the assessments are actually horrible. Of the 20+ classes Ive taken at Duke, this is hands down the worst by far

Format of the class is not designed to help students. Individual quiz and group quiz every week. Four exams. Even worse in a condensed semester. Way too much info condensed into each lecture with no time to actually learn it before quizzes. Gives lecture Thursday, tests the info Sunday on a midterm. THREE days to learn material. Ridiculous.

Okay I'm mainly writing this just to break up the harsh ratings below. I agree that Dr. B goes extremely fast during lecture, but she posts all of her notes and slides for us to reference whenever. The worst part is definitely the exams and weekly quizzes, which are so terribly worded it often feels like they're trying to trick you.

Words cannot adequately describe my distaste for this class. This class is actually really bad, in basically all respects. Material is sifted through very quickly with inadequate explanation, and then students are quizzed on it. Exams/quizzes are very hard, jumps are made from content taught. Seriously. Not learning anything, just pain & suffering.

Absolutely terrible - the worst class I have taken at Duke. Lectures contain a colossal amount of information, and students are quizzed on Thursday for material covered on Monday and Wednesday. Class format is engineered to frustrate students and to prohibit them from absorbing the material. Just horrifying - take it with a different professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Don't take Bio 202 with her. Seriously. You will regret it. I hear such positive experiences from others who have taken this class with someone else and this has been a terrible experience. She moves over content way too quickly and tests and quizzes are very hard to do well on. Avoid her at ALL COSTS!

Dr. B is the worst. I've seen her laugh at students for asking questions. The way she speaks is demeaning. There's a quiz every Thursday on material we learned that M/W, plus a group quiz every Friday. Literally no time to breathe! And 4 midterms in a short semester- so obnoxious. Students are confused & overwhelmed 24/7. I'd give negative rating.

Dr. B is NOT receptive to student questions and will speak condescendingly if you ask her a "wrong" or "dumb" question. Don't understand why she teaches since she does not seem to like helping students at all.

Horrible. Weekly quiz on Monday and Wednesday's lecture with no time to study and actually understand info. She's not a great lecturer and goes too fast to get anything useful out of class. I have never hated a class (or bio) this much. Ask the wrong question and you'll get grilled. Quizzes and exams are way harder than what is taught in class. 0/5

Lectures consist of a ton of material and are often too complex to fully understand before being quizzed on it (a weekly occurrence). There is very little time to actually spend time processing, and she expects you to make large jumps in thinking from what she lectures on to what is actually asked on assessments. Really makes me dislike bio

teaches way too much in a short time w/o any transient periods to let stuff "soak". I wld take orgo again instead of this w/ her, really. She told us that trying to take notes in class wld be useless; she goes that fast. Do yourself a favor and dont take 202 with her. sophisticated concepts with suboptimal explanation. makes me hate bio - a premed

This teacher expects students to have a lot of prior knowledge especially on material that is not required to have, including in bio 201 which is not a required prereq. She is also quite rude and demeaning to students who ask questions in lecture so be ready for that.
Expects you to know things that she hasn't even taught yet, goes way too quickly, and goes too in depth. Only has lectures and they are very hard to follow. This class is way harder than Ochem.

Everything was open-note, so not too difficult. 75% 3 midterms, 20% group project (vague instructions but most people did well), 5% weekly quizzes. Very info-heavy and in-depth, but if you're like me and sad Duke doesn't have a cell/molec bio major, you'll love the content. Dr. B is a little intimidating; know your stuff before speaking or else

One of the hardest courses Ive ever taken, and the professor did not make it easier I attended most of her office hours for extra help which resulted in her asking if I had undiagnosed dislexia because I wasnt understanding what she was explaining. Made me feel terrible, would not recommend.

She's a good lecturer but covers a lot in one class time, so often doesn't answer questions during class which can be kind of frustrating. But, she's always willing to stay after class and clear up any doubts. She makes an effort to know her students and memorize their names, even in large lectures.

Course was interesting but detailed and required lots of memorization. She lectures quickly, so its important to pay attention in class to do well on tests. She can be judgmental when responding to students questions and speaks condescendingly if she perceives your question as dumb and makes sure to let you know. Know your stuff.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: she is super nice but not the best lecturer, i found her hard to follow. obsessed with drosophilia and dogs. the class is manageable but a ton of work. quizzes every week, problem set, ect.

I know there's some controversy around her but I had her for both Bio 202 and Bio 420 and she was great. 420 was a lot better because she had the opportunity to dive into the details and she's clearly very knowledgable and really excited about the material. Her lectures are really good - easy to follow despite the amount of information. Great prof.
Dr. Bejsovec is very invested in making sure everyone succeeds. Her lectures are interesting and very funny. The class is fast-paced but there are lots of ways to make up your grade.

Dr. Amy is very knowledgable. She has a good grasp of the subject, and can answer doubts well, but is sometimes unable to simplify certain concepts since she conducts research at a high level. The class is very well organized. Overall, would recommend since even the support staff for this class is great.

Dr. B is an amazing professor and person, but she doesn't understand the difference between what an introductory bio class and a higher-level bio class needs to learn. Be prepared to learn a lot, a great deal more than AP Bio. All information you will need to know/be tested on are on her polished lecture slides.

Fall Sem., Bio 202. They upped the difficulty on this class so you have to work for the grade. She goes through a week of material in a single lecture, you walk in 5 mins late or zone out and you'll be completely lost. Class is unnecessarily hard, office hours with Mercer are unhelpful. She seems really cool/nice and passionate, but tough.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. B is the queen of genetics. I would highly recommend taking class with her. She's one of the most passionate professors I've had at Duke. If you love genetics, you will love this class. She keeps lectures interesting and gives clear explanations of difficult topics. You have to understand the material and not memorize it to do well on midterms.

Prof. B is a great professor. Cancer genetics is a tough course with A LOT of info, but Amy does a fantastic job of explaining the content and making sure we understand. I easily learned way more in this course than any other Duke course. Reading the book is useful but not necessary; she only tests from the lectures.

I'm pretty sure that if you looked up the etymology of "intense," it would somehow trickle back to Dr. B. She's nothing if not that, but she's also a great lecturer, who manages to explain concepts that can be quite confusing. This class is not for the faint of heart but you can learn a great deal from Dr. B if you choose to.

Dr. B really is here to teach and help her students learn the material.  Her lectures are interesting and always geared towards why things are relevant.  She's really helpful in office hours and by email for homework and studying.  Her tests are tough but she's generous with partial credit.

Dr.B is great, she is always willing to help her students understand the material. She covers a lot of material every lecture so sometimes it is easy to get lost during class, so go to lectures and stay focused. The homework questions are good studying materials for the exams.

Dr. B was one of the best Biology professors I've had at Duke. Her class was very fast-paced but that's because of how much material there is. She's really passionate about the material and was very helpful both in & out of class. If you want to understand the hallmarks of cancer properly, take this class. Don't be lazy and expect to do well!

Amazing class and professor! Cancer bio covers every corner of cell biology, which can be overwhelming, but Dr. B presents it in an interesting and manageable fashion. There was always at least one hooking example or story each lecture that got me really interested in the material. Dr. B is very accessible and willing to help her students.

Dr. B's class can be intimidating at first, but only because there is so much to learn in each lecture. However, her powerpoints are incredibly clear and concise. If you put the work into the class, you will leave with a rewarding overview of Cancer Genetics. One of the few science classes I've taken that is directly applicable to medical school.

She's one of the most intelligent professors I've met at Duke. This class re-inspired my love for science and for pursuing medicine. It is easily one of the most useful and interesting classes I've ever taken. The Cancer Biology textbook is an incredible resource - use it wisely! Requires a lot of studying but exams were fair. Above an 85 = A-.

Great course and fantastic instruction. She does come off a bit cold sometimes and is unafraid to call people out for being wrong. Word of advice: don't ask questions or make comments simply to get a better participation grade because you will get owned. Think carefully before speaking...
Dr. B is a horrible teacher. I really wonder how she is still a professor at Duke. She is unclear in class and makes her tests way too hard for our level.

bejsovec is tough!  her lectures go very, very fast, so i'd recommend taking a laptop or a recorder.  she goes through so much material, and you really need to understand it all because her tests really are hard.  do all the problems she suggests, and also read the book beforehand.  but she definitely will help and responds to email q's fast

118 is a HARD class - you should know that coming in. I found Dr. B's lectures to be really interesting. Once I asked her a question after class, and by the time I'd walked to the bc she had already sent me an email explanation that she'd accidentally told me the wrong thing. I can think of plenty of professors who would NOT take that effort.
Dr. B was a pretty good teacher, it's just a lot of material and a hard class.  I felt that reading the book was more important than being conscious in class but your own mileage may vary.

I think Dr. B. was just fine.  I emailed all my questions and she answered in a timely manner.  Bio 118 is just a very difficult class to do well in.  I thought the tests were reasonable, but don't be fooled by a good mark.  Again, as someone else has said, +1.5 std not +1 std above = A

Dr. B was fine.  Great lectures and actually seems to enjoy being in class (unlike Dr. Spana).  Anybody that thinks Spana is a better professor is basically overlooking his incompetence during lectures for his extremely easy exams.  Dr. B is much harder but you will learn much more from her.  Also, hosts a helpful Q&A page on blackboard.

Dr. B is so knowledgeable and she has such informative lectures. It is very fast-paced and reading the book is a must. If you take the time to thoroughly understand the material, then the tests aren't too bad. The class itself is hard bc it's a premed class and there are many intense students. Stay on top of it and you'll do okay. 1 sd = A-, not A.

I really enjoyed this class. Many people complain that Dr. B was, in fact, a B. That may be the case when it comes to going over a test you did bad or something but she was a fantastic lecturer. Doing well is very possible if one studies very hard and makes an attempt to understand the material when learning it. Read the book, however.
