The course material is extremely interesting.  The first third of the class was great, but that's because it was taught by Dr. Eric Spana.  The last two thirds, taught by Bejsovec, were shamefully difficult.  She is unclear and puts absurd questions on tests.  Dont take this class unless you are good at memorizing every detail in a textbook
worst class at duke
Really unclear, haphazard lecturer

She is not a great lecturer. For all lectures, she was not really clear for many of really important concepts.  Sometimes she is very helpful, sometimes she is not. Going to lecture is very important for this class.  Her tests are not that bad but the grading for this class is horrible.  You have to get 1SD above average to get an A-(not A).
Her class notes were way to fast.  It was tough to keep up and she was really unhelpful when asked to clarify test questions.  She could have been much better.

A very clear lecturer. Yes, she'll go at 90% light speed sometimes, but that's simply because the course covers so much material. Lecture slides, practice tests, etc. are all helpful and she has them online quite early so there is no excuse for not having study materials. It's a lot of work in terms of memorizing biology, but nothing impossible.
organized lecturer, willing to meet outside class

taking notes is very organized and easy although can be a bit boring at times.  if you realllly understand her notes, you're set. I recommend doing the book reading, cuz it helps clarify and emphasize things. go to class

Dr. B's lectures are decent. Fast-paced and difficult to understand in the grand scheme of things, especially when delving into technicalities of 3-4 letter/number acronyms. Very diff. class. She's not too willing to explain what she considers basics, even though such can be hard to comprehend too.
Like the class, good amount of work, not easy but not impossible.

Rosenberg genuinely wants you to participate, discuss, and learn. Graded ultimately on participation & attendance mainly. Pretty dense readings but incredibly interesting topics. People who claimed his lectures were boring just locked out when things got difficult. Completely reasonable midterm & final. Overall an amazing experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I enjoyed this class more than expected and mainly because of Prof. Rosenberg. He approaches philosophy through a scientific lens, which I found interesting. He encourages questions during lecture however can be often particular about the answers, especially on essays.

Rosenberg's class is one of my required courses for my first semester at Duke, and I'm so thankful I got to experience his lectures. Professor Rosenberg's words and ideas were always inspirational. While he may be set in his beliefs, he will always have thoughts to share with you, and trust, they're enlightening.

This class will get your gears turning, and make you think about political and economic philosophy in a way you never have before. Rosenberg is very knowledgable, and while he usually has a singular expected answer to his questions he is always willing to entertain other viewpoints. He's cynical and harsh, but you will learn and laugh a ton.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. Rosenberg is a brilliant guy! He's such an engaging lecturer, and has enough general knowledge to be able to break down complex topics into understandable examples. Work isn't hard at all, but there is often a right answer to open questions on essays at times. Pick his brain as much as you can!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Rosenberg may literally be the smartest man I've ever met. He is great at methodically breaking down complex topics and thoughtfully responding to questions. There are not many graded assignments, so each essay counts. The only sort of "participation" grade are the weekly writing assignments, which are not a problem, just don't use AI.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Rosenberg is amazing. He is very engaging and often references basic scientific concepts which I really liked. He is very liberal and makes it known, but is also super open to hearing what students have to say. Overall, I loved his class and would highly recommend it.
Lectures are not interesting. Unclear grading criteria.

Took Philo of Econ in my first semester at Duke, and Prof. Rosenberg is amazing. Only graded items are midterm, final (with a greater weight) and weekly responses. PPTs and notes can be random so show up to the lectures and you will be ready for the exams (2-3 essays). Readings are not that heavy, but some previous knowledge of econ is recommended.

Professor Rosenberg is one of the best professors at Duke, and the first half of Prisoner's Dilemma / Distributive Justice was really indicative. The readings were fairly monotonous and also extremely long at some points, but Professor Rosenberg did a good job of recounting them in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Rosenberg is great!! I really enjoyed his class. He seems to know everything about everything. He always lightly referenced basic scientific concepts in his class ranging from quantum to biology which I always really enjoyed. Very open to other opinions and is ready to talk about anything, anytime. Overall, I loved the class.

Rosenberg is a funny guy and solid lecturer. His main thing is the philosophy of science, which should make this class interesting if you're STEM. The class is pretty much all lecturing, so just show up, take notes, and youll do fine. Also on writing assignments, don't try to reinvent the wheel- the main focus should be what was discussed in class.

Prof. Rosenberg is great! Class is highly interesting and not difficult at all (just 4 papers & should be fine if you attend the lectures). Favorite class this semester I highly recommend! Made me interested in a philosophy major

Took this class in my first semester at Duke, an amazing intro to Philosophy and Econ at once 10/10 would recommend. Good at getting discussions going, very willing to hear/consider alternate viewpoints. Readings are all long philosophy papers, but he explains them simply in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is a very knowledgeable person. The lectures are eye opening. He is readily available outside class and gives wonderful assistance.
PHENOMENAL!

Rosenberg is incredibly accomplished and worth taking his class. makes the most of every lecture start to finish. take if you're interested in game/economic theory. readings are tough but he'll explain them very well in class. very little work but your whole grade is essay-based midterm and final and a 250 word essay each week over the readings
Amazing lecturer, has plenty of student interaction, teaches a vast amount of information for a 101 class. Highly recommend.

You have to go to each and every class if you want to pass. Take notes no matter how off topic the discussion goes. Basically, if you listen to the phrases Rosenberg repeats during lecture and spit them on on the writing assignments you'll do well. Assignments are all short essays. Not a hard class, but very interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: He's a cool guy. His lectures are disorganized and hard to take notes on. We had 4 assignments the whole semester that were 2 essays each but they weren't hard at all. Take notes on what you can. Grades the essays super easy. If you do bad, you rewrite.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He is a smart guy, but needs to understand that he doesn't know everything. Was lecturing on inaccurate information at times, and doubled down on his false claims when a student called him out for it. The class itself was pointless. I will never use any of the knowledge I learned in the PPE gateway class ever again.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Good class experience. You can tell he knows a lot about what he is talking about. Lectures are very informative and done without any accompanying slides. You should take ur notes on a laptop with him (easier to keep up). Pay attention in class and at least do some of the reading and you will be fine. Papers are of good length with clear prompts.

One of the worst professors I've ever had.  Very biased, little interested in learning student names, hard to follow lectures because his handwriting is illegible.  He wants very specific answers to his questions and takes points off arbitrarily.  Avoid if possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Great professor. Interesting and very intellectual person. Gives great lectures; you may forget to take notes because you are listening to him speak.  He is a fast speaker, so get ready to write fast.

Definitely a little too keen on showing off his wikipedia-esque knowledge on basically everything. Lectures are fantastic when he has a solid grasp on the material, but are quite painful when he doesn't. Also somewhat dogmatic (tries to deny it), but that comes with the profession I guess. A well designed course; not bad overall.

Brilliant professor, I highly recommend everyone takes a class with him. The long readings (though he doesn't checks if anyone does it) will help you get the most out of lectures. He really requires students to be on their game if they ask questions/participate, and is amazing at getting debates and discussion going. One of the best lecturers here.
He's a very knowledgeable and interesting guy, and the class is really interesting. Just four reasonably short essays throughout the whole semester, along with short readings before most classes.

Professor Rosenberg is one of the brightest minds at Duke, and pushes his students to also be the brightest they can be. I am awestruck by his intellect. He sets high expectations and really challenges you; but you'll come out of the course gaining a skill for critical thinking you may never have had before. HIGHLY recommended.

A wonderful guy with a huge knowledge base. He's pretty personable and makes an effort to get to know the students who speak up in class. He is EXTREMELY liberal and lets everyone know, which isn't really philosophically relevant and can actually be super annoying, but overall he's a pretty great guy.
Even though the rater interest below is mixed, these students MUST really enjoy philosophy classes/talking about nothing. If you don't then you will probably find his class to be extremely annoying.

I don't understand how someone can be so smart! Rosenberg is just so damn smart its unbelievable. He's interesting and fun. You WILL learn so much in his class. What he teaches is amazing. Take this class. Only problem is that his comments on paper can be illegible at times...ask TA for clarification!

Prof's lecture was AWESOME. He was able to explain complicated philosophical terms in a simple, clear way. To my surprise, we didn't get much readings throughout the semester, an average of 5-10 pages per week. Also, Prof and TAs were accessible and really helpful after class. Strongly recommend this class.

One of the best lecturing professors I've had at Duke so far. There's something to be said for a professor's sticking to the chalkboard in an era of endless powerpoint presentations. I also liked the wide variety of readings he collected for each segment of the course. Really didn't get to know him personally though. Highly recommended nonetheless.
The class tries to cover too much ground, so Rosenberg moves fast and does not review. At least you don't get bored. And he is always willing to explain more before or after class.

I have taken three of Rosenberg's classes. The one I liked best was his course in Geneva last sumnmer, in Public Policy. Even though it's a summer class and there was too much work, it covered econ, and poitical science which is what I needed. Studying econ globalization in Geneva makes it real.

Really interesting subjec, but difficult. You need econ 1 or you wont understand. Professor is a philo. uy but knows economics. A different slant on hard subjects. I dont agree with last eval. But I got a good grade on midterm.

He is arrogant and sometimes says incorrect facts. He does not stick to the syllabus and does not offer much help for exams. On the brighter side, the subject is interesting and he is fairly good at clarifying difficult topics. Overall, one of my least favorite classes so far.
Intro to problems in philosophy. It was a small class with lots of discussion. Prof was always available for extra help. Hard problems but really interesting.

Took this summer class on politcal philosophy in Geneva last year. Six weeks of this class covered everything I did the whole next semester in London. Covers the econ, politics and pub policy stuff you really need to know. He talks fast but listens too.
Had to take a science elective and philosophy of biology fit my schedule. But thed first lecture was fasinating and I might even get interested in Darwin!

Rosenberg is a great professor and a nice guy.  He is extremely enthusiastic about the philosophy of science and conducts his lectures in a clear and directed manner.  He can be a bit unclear in his analysis of some ideas, but if you arrange a meeting with him, he will be more than happy to help you see the important points that you are missing.
Great teacher. Always available, reasonable exams, helps with other classes in economics,public policy, political science.
Really gets you interested in the most basic questions in philosophy. Gets people people talking even in the largest classes.
He makes the class interesting. There's a lot of sketchy stuff of course, but that's common in metaphysics.

Professor Rosenberg is extremely interesting.  It's obvious he knows what he's talking about and he will try to teach you as best he can.  He gives lots of examples and is always up for discussion.  However, it's hard to take notes because of his bad handwriting and fast talking.

Inspiring, intense, and surprisingly well-disposed towards his students.  Take his class, or at least sit in through drop/add and see if you click with him.  If you do, you'll love any class you take with him.
Very argumentative, but a rather stereotypical philosophy professor.
No Comments
Would not take this class. It is not a free A. Tests are long testing memorization and not understanding. For example asked about when someone died in an Earth and Climate Science Class

whiny professor who is bitter that people don't care about his class but then makes the most unfair exams where the question difficulty is solely based on obscurity vs critical thinking involved, which, given his lectures, seems to be profoundly absent. trivia ahh class. take anything else for a better use of your time and tuition at this school

Lectures seem rehearsed in the worst way possible and are downright excruciating to sit through, as Prof. Glass is under the impression that repeating something will inspire increasing amounts of wonder. He tries very hard to be "cool" in class but manages to make himself sound like an angsty middle schooler that just discovered the f-bomb.

Horrible professor. Ruined his class with no recordings, and unintelligible, image based slides. Even if you go to class, there are so many unfair questions on the exams, and the assignments are barely weighted. Do not take this course.

Rambles a bit during lecture. Tests not based on understanding of material but rather random facts. For example, asking about the date of someone's death rather than their contributions to continental drift theory. Not super difficult, but not a very useful class. Just tests on memorization.

The course was easy and one that first years should definitely take. Professor Glass is really nice and his lectures are interesting. He does ramble a bit but he has good things to say. There were very few assignments and he had reasonable deadlines.

Easiest class I've ever taken. Lectures have lots of info and are actually interesting, he's a good speaker. Only 3 assignments for entire semester (watch a documentary), review quizzes can be taken multiple times, quiz questions and midterm questions are identical. Attendance not mandatory and review quizzes are a summary of what you need to know.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Extremely easy class. There is basically no homework and only three tests all year. You can take the chapter quizzes he posts online as many times as you like, and the questions on the quizzes are the same as the ones he puts on the test, so you just have to study from those.
Waves for babes was super easy and interesting. I like enviro sci so I liked going to lecture, and Alex clearly cares soooo much about the topic. Would recommend.

Professor Glass is the best. His class is not difficult, and his lectures are very fun and entertaining. His personality is a little zany, but in an endearing way. I have thoroughly enjoyed taking his class, and I have yet to meet one person who does not feel the same.
Hard course, but worth the time. It got me interested in optimization and strengthened my R skills. Always attend lectures so you know what's going on. He's pretty funny too :)

Content of 221 is pretty challenger. Professor Fisher is helpful, but there are not a lot of resources to prepare for the exams. Proofs are tough. Have strong understanding of linear before taking the class and do well on the midterms. No final exam.
Very understanding and kind prof. Class is difficult without having proper background in CS. In class tests were unfair at times.

221 was difficult material, but Dr. Fisher's typeset notes made the content much more digestible. Grading & Syllabus was very clear, just wish the class was a little less end-heavy, as it seemed the last month was more work than the previous 2-3 months in the semester.
Super organized, lectures very simply, and is very approachable. Cares about his students, great sense of humor. Class is definitely not the easiest but he makes the material very digestible.

Amazing math professor. Very kind, accommodating, and has great math jokes. Teaches material in organized, easy to understand manner without overwhelming you with unnecessary notation; he is always happy to answer questions and is available for help. Very fair exams and very well structured course. Highly recommend.

360 is an absolutely miserable class. Fisher is nice and organized, but doesn't make 360 any easier. He believes in putting challenge questions on the exams and that tests shouldn't have an A average, meaning tests are brutal and there's no curve. HWs are incredibly time-intensive (minimum 6-8 hours/week), so you'll be living in office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: While exams are very difficult, the grading seems lenient with lots of partial credit. Knowing this is a hard class, be ready to put in the time on the HW, office hours, and preparing for exams, and you can do well. Fisher is awesome, knowledgeable, and so kind. He always answers questions and is well organized. One of my favorite classes!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Fisher is great. He does his best to encourage students and support them academically. His lectures are clear and he takes pauses for when students have questions. I legitimately can't imagine a better professor for this course.This class is challenging but the content is fascinating - no doubt one of the best classes I've ever taken.
A very difficult course. A lot of homework. Professor does not curve. Spent the most time ever and got the worst grade ever.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Absolutely incredible professor. STA360 is NOT an easy course, but I learned so much thanks to his teaching+organization. He made a beautiful website, recorded and posted every lecture, was super available, and made sure his office hours were very useful. It is rare that you find a teacher who is both a stats genius and down to earth caring person.

360 is just rough no matter who teaches it. Fisher is a nice person, but his tests are brutal and he "curves" final grades, not tests. Grading will depend on if your TA is nice - he doesn't really grade the exams. His psets are also insane, so you'll be living in office hours. Again, not always his fault. 360 is hard, always.

I don't love stats, but 101 was taught in RStudio (coding) and was easy to understand. Exams were just extended assignments that took a decent bit to code. Good teaching allowed me to grasp stat concepts as well as how to code them in R. People say it's harder than 199 but I think it's based on professor. If its Fisher I recommend 101 over 199.

This class was certainly very challenging but Professor Fisher is very welcoming and supportive. He's accessible outside class, is ready to give extra time, and has clear grading criteria. He seems like a good person and is also a great professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: He doesn't curve at all. No idea what will happen...

I have to say Prof. Fisher is a good person and STA 360 itself is extremely tough. BUT THE TA GRADE REALLY HARSH and I will fail this course because although I spent 8hrs on every week's homework I still got a D on the HW. subtract credits if you don't match the page.TA is not helpful with the HW and even gives the wrong guidance. GET READY TO FAIL
The lecture was so well organized and I believe that everyone in the class got abundant respect and attention. Awesome professor.

Nice guy, but not the best teacher. Told us on day 1 that you could get an A without showing up to another lecture, which was true and many people did. Many instances of "you don't need to know how it works, just copy this" - basically a ctrl+c ctrl+v simulator. Average workload, lots in semester-long lab groups. Didn't really learn anything.

Lectures a bit boring: I started sleeping through class which hurt my grade. Rubrics aren't transparent but the  core of assignments wasn't too difficult. Fisher's a good dude, helpful in office hours. Final assignments are group projects, and I got a bad group. Take this class when 1) you have 3 people to take it with 2) you know you can attend

The professor was very accessible and open to questions. His lectures could have been more engaging at times, but its hard when everyone has their computers out to engage the class. He was funny at times and just a kind fella. Grading was fair and not too harsh.

Really amazing teacher who is very passionate and engaging during lectures. Labs can be hard but Professor Fisher and all the TAs are super willing to help. Always willing to reexplain hard concepts or clarify by explaining something a different way. Super nice and I loved taking his class!

Fisher tries to make Stat as interesting as it can be! Funny jokes, veryyy lenient attendance policy, take-home tests, and weekly labs. Labs can be difficult, but the TA team was amazing and very willing to help. However, I will not that I had CS experience before this class; some of my friends who didn't struggled. Still, take Stat101 with Fisher!

STA199 is easy - no final, one final project, and two take-home exams. However, the grading rubric is highly non-transparent; graders deduct points for very minor things that you would not notice. His lectures are slow and disorganized; there were times when he went so slow that we could not write the labs.

Very chill professor who lectures well. The labs and exams weren't hard, but grading is all done by TAs and some of them were more harsh than others. There was also a lot of beef between the professor and TAs near the end of the semester about it. We had two big group projects so it kind of sucks if you get assigned a bad team. Not a hard course.

I took STA101 with Fisher and as someone with no coding experience looking to fill a major requirement, I feel like the class was fair. The exams and labs are difficult, but the TAs help you work through labs and learn from mistakes. There is no homework besides labs and occasional videos. Manageable but be ready to put time into labs and exams.

If you are a humanities major trying to fulfill a QS, avoid this course. This is basically computer science rebranded. Tests are graded very strictly and are heavily weighted. Lectures are not helpful. As far as coding, you can't do well with limited experience, he assumes you can navigate through the errors that will have you stuck for hours.

Fisher made STA199 easy. He's a relatively new teacher, but he definitely knows the material. All lectures are posted online so there is literally no need to go to class. The class is designed for you to get an A if you do all the assignments. Take this class if you want an A, but there may be better options if you really want to learn Data Science

Fisher is a nice person who genuinely cares about his students' success in STA199. He really does his best to get people engaged even when course content isn't all that interesting. His in-class explanations can be confusing and long-winded, but overall I'd say this class is a good way to earn the QS requirement.
Professor Fisher was okay. He is super sweet but lectures weren't particularly helpful at all. If you go to office hours he's a lot more helpful.

As a person who has never coded or done stats, I am super grateful for Fisher. This class is designed for kids to get an A. He wants you to succeed! There are office hours at all times of the day and he posts solutions to every lab/hw/lecture activity. He also makes cheesy funny jokes in class to get you through.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Fisher is an average professor. During lecture, he can get himself confused when explaining some concepts but generally he's okay. If you can take STA199 with a different professor, do that, but if your only option is Fisher, you'll be okay. STA199 is a fairly easy class where you can learn the material yourself if you wanted to.

Lectures were quite repetitive as the semester went on, so if you understand the material, it is not always necessary to go to the lectures (esp when he records). Thus, this class was not very interesting, but Prof is very, very helpful when you struggle and has lots of office hours. He is also a really nice guy, so I recommend talking to him!
Fisher is a great explainer. Class was easy but I actually learned a lot. Group work was OK, could've been worse.
His lecture recordings were very helpful
Professor Fisher is very approachable and always answers my questions!

Fisher is a perfectly nice and well-intentioned person. He is very quick to answer questions and cares about his students. The class is very easy, and often was more copy and pasting than learning. I stopped going to class after the first couple weeks as it was quicker and more efficient to do the work on my own.

Almost no homework, short responses due before class sometimes. Heavy lecturer and lots to memorize but I only spent maybe an hour outside of class per week. Easy ALP credit. Midterms are very fair and the 2 outside reports are easy, but will take some time to do. Need to pay attention to the key images, maps, and names.

Ancient Athletics is one of the most interesting classes I've taken at Duke, and that comes from a senior. Karsten clearly plans carefully for each class and makes them very engaging and interesting. He's also just a fascinating, quirky dude. Very easy to get good grades in the class, as long as you allow yourself to engage with the content.

Should have been an easy and fun class but he made it overly boring and uninspiring. I was hoping for a class to give me a real introduction to ancient greek athletics but he went into depths that were very arbitrary. I felt this class could have been a much more fun course with relations to ancient sports but it was a very boring history class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is a very good and understanding professor. There was just one issue: he would make write about antiquity rather than learn about writing in general. Yes, it was fun. I don't feel I learned that much - but it was fun.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: She is a kind person but truly bad at teaching. You will not learn anything from her lectures as they are so convoluted with her mistakes and you will not remember/understand the material after the course.

Genuinely it couldn't get worse. If you have no prior knowledge of Electrical Engineering then you will be clueless from start to finish so prepare to self study everything. Her exams aren't that hard but you'll also learn nothing.
Lectures are not very good and are boring. If you take this class, be prepared to self study everything. Course is not extremely difficult though.

Seems like a nice woman, but a completely incapable, rambling lecturer and inconsistent test grader. I actually took ECE110 (not listed on rating here), and it was doable if you come in with background knowledge. Those I knew who had no introduction to electrical engineering were totally lost from start to finish in her class

Dr. Brown is kind, and seems to be a good person that cares about her students. But I had never seen anyone be such a bad lecturer. She was clearly making an effort to teach, but she did not know how to approach any of the topics she was covering. She would just go over slides and read one or two sentences without explaining what she was teaching.
Lectures are so disorganized and just reading off of slides. Very boring and you don't really get anything out of it.

Terrible lecturer and very disorganized; she often had trouble answering questions in class. Homework is from the textbook and pretty straightforward. Basically told us what the questions on the exams were gonna be so exams were pretty easy as well. As someone else said, you don't really get anything out of the class, but it's not hard to get an A.

She tried really hard but the lectures are very disorganized. Would cancel class randomly. Tests are not hard because she would go through possible test question during lecture. Didn't really learn anything, but got an A.

Easily one of the most disorganized professors at Duke. She cancelled class at least four or five times throughout the semester and typically cancels her office hours as well. The resources she posts on Sakai are usually very unhelpful. She messed up on grading exams too many times and takes forever to respond to emails.

Fantastic prof. Want her to teach every class. Very methodical, very thorough, super precise language. If you have a question, even if it is beyond the scope of the class, she will definitely be able to answer it. Two exams + final (not cumulative). Very concept-based/straightforward, not a lot of calculation. Weekly HW can get a little tricky.
Great teacher! I suggest taking her class. She's very helpful if you ask questions.

Dr. Henry's amazing! She varies class structure to incorporate lectures, small talk practice, & grammar practice. There's a fair amount of work, but it's actually helpful rather than just busywork. She is also so sweet and understanding, & is super fun in class. I would definitely recommend taking German 101 with her to anyone considering it!
Fun class and paper grading is clear and fair. Class style is good and she is always prepared for class and she even invited us to her house for dinner!
Such an amazing Professor. Cares deeply for all her students. Interesting content. Would take her Seminar again and really recommend!

This teacher was terrific! She works very hard to make the classroom a safe space, and her grades are very clear and fair. She is always open to meeting outside of class hours and will do everything in her power to make sure you are well-prepared. Dr. Henry makes a huge effort to get to know her students, this class will never be stressful!
10/10 would take her freshman seminar again
Awesome class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Really loved April. She is great at leading discussions for the books/movies, and is a very sweet professor. Class flows like a book club, and the work is decently light.

I took The Legend of King Arthur in Literature and Film with Dr. Henry and had a great time! Dr. Henry truly cares about her students, and she's teaching the class because she's genuinely excited about King Arthur. Her excitement comes through in her lectures, although the material does get a bit repetitive towards the end of the course.

If you can take a German class with her, do it! She has clear criteria including participation, but she makes sure everyone gets opportunities to participate in each class, so it never feels like students who are struggling are being drowned out. She's very accessible and genuinely cares about her students.

Dr. Henry is the most incredible language professor. German was enjoyable because of her willingness to make the class extremely interactive, her desire to ALWAYS assist students outside of class hours, and her feedback that allows you to improve. Homework is daily and, admittedly, a lot. At times, you feel like you can't keep up.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Henry is very friendly and fair to all of her students. She cares a lot about each student doing well in the class and will make sure you are well prepared for tests and the final exam. Sometimes, she even walks around and corrects an answer you write while taking a test. I highly recommend this course if you want a great intro to German.
Dr. Henry is a very fair professor. Would highly recommend taking her class if you are at all interesting in learning German. Workload is very fair and tests and quizzes aren't too hard either.
Dr. Henry is great. Makes learning the language really easy. There is homework every night before class, but it is easy and she posts keys. Just show up and you should get an A
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I love Dr. Henry a lot! She and her class are AMAZING. She is incredibly kind and accessible outside class. Her advices are really helpful. Just follow her lead and you will do great in class. I have to say she really makes me become interested in Germany, German and German culture.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Henry is an incredibly kind professor. Very knowledgeable and gives great feedback on papers. If you show up and put forth effort she will do everything she can to make sure you succeed. I took her class for my first-year seminar and it was all good fun and straightforward work. 10/10

Dr. Henry is a wonderful person, who truly cares for her students. This means that (if you are willing to) she will put in a lot of effort to help you. The class is well structured, with many class activities for speaking-practice and participation. Daily homework and occasional assignments. Culture points are required, as well!

Wonderful professor. She is a bright, fun, and passionate which creates such a welcoming classroom to participate in. All you need to do is study the night before the test and write your essays a few days in advance and you'll be golden.
Fairytales from Grimms to Disney - 4 tests, 3 papers, 1 group project, and participation

As a sophomore, Professor Henry is the nicest and easiest professor I have had at Duke thus far. A large amount of the grade is based on homework/participation, so if you show up and do the light daily work, you'll be halfway to an A and have already learned the material, making the tests that much easier. Could not recommend more

Dr. Henry gave me the most enjoyable experience of any professor at Duke in my 3.5 years here. All that she demands is showing up to class and participating but she deserves that as an absolute minimum. Dr. Henry deserves nothing less because she puts her life into her students and is literally the best and most caring professor one could imagine

Dr. Henry is one of the best professors I've had. I took 2 of her classes for FL requirement and would love to have had her for the 3rd. Very thorough in lectures and pays individual attention. Very fair grader- gives clear guidelines of expectations and even what the quiz questions are.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Would take again

reviews.comment: One of the best professors at Duke. She is incredibly caring, accommodating and energetic. It's amazing how she was able to create so much chemistry in our class of 20+ people. Exams are also quite easy and she always gives you an outline on what to expect. She doesn't like it if you skip class so be careful. Homework is frequent but very easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Henry is my favorite and the best professor I've had so far. She teaches so well and cares about her students and their individual learning so much!! Always makes class fun and keeps the class very well prepared for anything! Amazing person and professor

Professor Henry is great! She really cares about making sure her students learn, and tries to make the material as engaging and fun as possible. There's quite a bit of work but she grades fairly and will give good feedback and help if you ask.

Dr. Henry is without a doubt the best Professor I've ever had.   She is incredibly nice, and makes class a lot of fun.  She clearly puts a lot of thought into her lesson plans, and her enthusiasm makes the class incredible.  Even though I had to take her class at 8:30 every morning, she made it lots of fun. 10/10 would recommend!
April is really great. She's super nice, and not a hard grader at all. There's a decent amount of homework and it's pretty consistent, but not difficult. She wants people to do well.

April is by far the best language professor I've ever had. She makes learning German seamlessly easy. Although I have had experience with additional languages in the past, I have never gained such proficiency in vocabulary, grammar, conversational skills, and pronunciation in such a short amount of time. You will love German with her as a professor
If you put in the work, she will too.  She manages to cut down on some of the German Department's sillier policies.

April Henry is such a nice professor that you feel like a breeze attending lectures. Most of the grade comes from homework and attendance. Tests/quizzes are frequent, but they are not hard. Once you've done what she said in class acing is pretty easy. She does give writing homework every day but mostly is writing sentences so not very demanding.

Exemplary professor! Ton of work but totally worth it. Would take again. Go to office hours, she spends hours speaking with you. Genuinely a wonderful person. She is retiring but might come back to teach a course or two, so take her if you get the chance.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Respected--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Apollonio was the best instructor I had at Duke. I took Dostoeveksy with her this semester and really enjoyed it. She is accessible outside of class and is understanding of extenuating circumstances. Provided you do the readings, you will get a good grade. Would recommend to anyone interested in Russian literature.

This class is a lot of work (150+ pgs of reading per week, daily quizzes, many papers) but is so worth it. Prof. Apollonio will make you fall in love with Russian literature. She's very accommodating and provides lots of helpful feedback on writing assignments - you will become a better writer and reader in this class. Would absolutely recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Definitely take one of Prof. A's classes before you graduate. She is funny to listen to and understanding about people's schedules. Easy A as long as you do the homework most days.

Dr. A is one of my favorite professors at Duke, hands down. She's so funny, makes reading incredibly enjoyable. There's reading quizzes at the beginning of every class, but its super chill and you get a 60 just for showing up. Super accommodating overall - I'm definitely going to take more classes with her.

There is a TON of reading in this 89S and there's a reading quiz each class so read carefully. She will make a ton of comments on your papers and there will be a few presentations but overall nothing is too hard. She was super understanding during COVID and made changes in the syllabus to accommodate our workloads. Would take again!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She is an amazing professor who knows how to inspire her students to fall in love with Dostoevsky. (Dostoevsky is great just by himself, of course.) Readings are A LOT, and daily quizzes will make sure that you need to spend a lot of time reading the texts closely. Don't even attempt to overload if you are to take this class for graded.

Prof. Apollonio is a really interesting prof., and she really cares about her students! Beware, her class requires a lot of reading (150+ pages/week), with daily quizzes plus additional writing assignments throughout the semester. But great class, you learn a lot, but be prepared to work!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: She is one of my favorite professors. I took her class on Dostoevsky last semester and was enamored with his writing thanks to her enthusiasm and expertise on the subject. Unlike other professors, she genuinely cares about her students. I wish I could take her class again.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: LOVE HER. Wish I could take more of her classes. Taking her seminar on Tolstoy and Dostoevsky my first semester of freshman year convinced me to minor in Russian. Hilarious, quirky, loving, inspirational. Very important in her field and it shows. Reading quizzes every class but they're not super hard to do well on, just read the book.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Easily one of the best professors I have ever had. Dostoevsky isn't easy to read and she doesn't make it easy, but her grading is fair and clear. Professor Apollonio is a very sweet woman and cares very much about her students as well as the subject matter and I definitely plan to take more of her classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Absolutely LOVE her--she genuinely cares about her students, and goes the extra mile for her students. I would definitely take her classes again. She is the reason that I am now a Russian Lit minor.
Carol is awesome. She's brilliant and loves her Russian Literature. Take this class if you can! Tolstoy is the g.o.a.t and you'll love reading his works even though it is a lotttt of reading.

Terrible.  Not only turned me off from the CCS certificate, but single-handedly turned me away from the Public Policy major and children in general.  Boring, unfair, you learn no practical skills. Awful

Extremely boring.  Tons of "busy work" but nothing remotely interesting and or that you benefit from.  Very particular grader who lists steps to writing a paper as if were fifth graders, and it won't matter if you wrote a great paper; it only matters if you follow her nit-picky criteria.  Lecture= entirely her reading off slides and deathly boring

she's extremely particular, sort of teaches the class like a middle school class. doesn't take attendance everyday, but gives "pop" in class activities that count toward your final grade. not recommended.
Great in Minnesota with one on one teaching sytle.  I learned a lot!!
Having research misconduct (fabricated his data). Was in the Epstein file.

This guy has no redeeming qualities as a professor or human being. He shouldn't be allowed in the same room as students, so don't take his class!

#EpsteinFiles

"Dan Ariely corresponded with Epstein between 2010 and 2016, The Duke Chronicle reported. They appear to have met at least seven times, including a meeting for coffee on Nov. 29, 2010 and for breakfast on Dec. 3, 2014.

On Sept. 20, 2012, Ariely emailed Epstein to ask the name of a “redhead” who was with Epstein....
Great lecturer! #EpsteinFiles

A good lecturer if you do the reading ahead of time. However, Dan Ariely has a prejudice against international students, and those that appear international. He is extremely rude towards Asian students in particular. It turns out, his college girlfriend left him for an Asian man. But he will project his insecurities and hatred on the students.

The best part about taking a class with Dan Ariely is that you're allowed to CHEAT and LIE all you want! Because he is well known to have (allegedly) falsified data on some of his most famous studies, he even encourages it!
Awesome class on Coursera
good guy

I loved this class almost to the end and then realized there was no way to pass the class because it was too heavily weighted towards the Peer Evaluation. Aced the quizzes, did okay on the exams, but the students that rated my paper were totally uneducated in the area I wrote about. That just sunk the results. Course design was poor.
I loved this class. There is a lot of reading (about 30+ required scientific research papers, more suggested). He is very entertaining to listen to and making learning easy.
Took his class on Coursera, I loved it!!!!!! He presents the theories with lots of applicable research, excellent!

I was really lucky to have taken his seminar class (taught with his wife Sumi who is super nice and super smart). He brought a lot of interesting ideas to class . A lot of people said they didn't learn anything, but I feel his class is more about creative thinking, not factual knowledge. Really get inspired by him!
Genius, but not a very good professor. He was very unreachable and understandably completely irrational.

Dan is passionate about teaching and brought a lot of interesting ideas to the class. Take his ideas if you want to get INSPIRED! He doesn't care that much about concepts. He wants creative ideas and critical thinking! I'm so fortunate to have taken his seminar class (also taught by his wife Sumi who's really smart and nice).

Ariely is a very interesting man, but as a professor he is lacking. His accent and subpar English make him difficult to understand, and his lectures are all over the place. Furthermore, he is entirely disengaged from his students. His assistant Aline takes care of all testing and grading, and unfortunately she's largely incompetent
oh my gosh, she needs to retire!

Worst professor Ive ever had. She grades hard but gives unclear prompts. She holds us to very high standards, yet is rarely capable of sending an email without glaring grammatical and spelling errors. Disorganized, patronizing, and unwilling to accept interpretations that dont align with her own, avoid her at all costs!!!
Has a way with words that is just incredible -- can make sense of the insensible; makes ideas usually familiar seem new and exciting.  She's very clear and is very encouraging.

The reading is heavy and boring.  During class, she literally drones on about about nothing for an hour and 15 minutes.  Her expectations for papers are as unclear as rants, and her grading seems arbitrary.  She seems obsessed with the fact that she used to teach at Brown.  Easily one of the worst classes I have ever taken at Duke.

I really enjoyed Glass's class. He clearly cares about his students' wellbeing and wants everyone to succeed without unnecessary stress. Lectures could sometimes be a bit rambly/confusing, but assignments were on the easier side and engaging (often documentary reflections). It's definitely test-heavy, but exams were very manageable with preparation
took this class for the NS credit, but you still have to study for exams, which take up the majority of your grade.
Recycled slides and canvas quizzes. All of class is based on rote memorization. Rambles, poorly planned lectures impede learning.
I think this class is mostly just memory slop. It's easy if you study but don't think you can just come and sleepwalk to an A+, you just might get fried
Unfair exams. Studied for hours and hours and still couldn't get A because he asks insanely specific questions on exams. Wish I hadn't taken this class for credit.
Would not take this class. It is not a free A. Tests are long testing memorization and not understanding. For example asked about when someone died in an Earth and Climate Science Class

Boring lectures with the same reused slides. Most of the students don't attend these lectures since he doesn't take attendance, and there isn't really any reason to go. Graded on very few assignments + a couple multiple-choice exams

Would recommend any class he teaches, amazing lecturer, super passionate about geology, funny, tries to make class entertaining. If you literally just go to every class, pay attention and take notes, studying for the exams will be very easy and doable to get an A.

Lectures seem rehearsed in the worst way possible and are downright excruciating to sit through, as Prof. Glass is under the impression that repeating something will inspire increasing amounts of wonder. He tries very hard to be "cool" in class but manages to make himself sound like an angsty middle schooler that just discovered the f-bomb.

Professor Glass is an amazing lecturer. He's so passionate about geology, and it shows in how clearly he explains everything. I went to every class—even though attendance wasn't required—because he made it so interesting and funny. The tests were fair if you paid attention and read the slides. I'd love to take another class with him in the future.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is a really funny lecturer and is very passionate about the topics. The tests are all multiple choice and exactly what you cover in class. The optional review quizzes have questions that are word for word on the test. If you don't go to class you will not do well because he does not post the lecture recordings.

Professor Glass is really passionate about teaching about the climate and this class is great! As long as you do the review quizzes you'll do well on the midterms. Lectures are interesting and his slides are clear.

Professor Glass brings the material to life with engaging lectures. While not an easy "A" class, the tests are fair if you stay on top of the slides. For study prep, I found unstuckstudy and the optional quizzes very helpful alongside the free textbook.

While the easiest class I've taken at Duke, I would not call it an "easy A." The material and content were straightforward and interesting to learn about, especially with Dr. Glass, but the midterms were sometimes difficult to achieve a raw score of 90 or above. Most people likely end up with A's, but some Pass/Fail the class from what I heard.
Entertaining lectures and super fair tests (just know the slide material).

Glass himself is a character but once you accept that you'll be fine. He loves to joke and teaches really interesting material even if he isn't the best lecturer. Cares about his students and offers flexible Zoom office hours. Assignments and exams are easy if you put in effort, 3 hours memorizing terms on quizlet got me a 98% exam avg across the 3

Glass is a very passionate and inspirational professor. He very clearly cares about the environment and what we as students can do to make an impact in the world, however his lectures can be quite long and verbose and aren't very interactive. Tests are pretty easy as long as you pay attention a little bit you'll likely pass.

Dr. Glass is the best. Took 403, 102, 101, 289A with him and plan to take the rest of his courses before I graduate. Amazing lectures- complicated material at times but all his courses are set up for students to succeed. Hilarious and very knowledgeable- take a field course with him!

While I would say that this class isn't quite as easy as people make it out to be, it is one of the easiest NS credits you can get. Glass is a really nice guy and good lecturer. If you do the optional review quizzes multiple times, you will do well on the exams. Highly recommend for an easy NS.
Really nice guy, super relaxed class. Great NS credit for people for whom science isn't their thing. Learned a ton

All around great person, and it shows. Glass knows how to give engaging and funny lectures; he genuinely wants to hear your questions and always asks if his explanation makes sense. His homework quizzes help you study for the exam. I'm not really inclined to science, but I found his class to be really enjoyable. Consider taking 103 with Glass!

Amazing class!!!! It got me so excited about geology, and Professor Glass is SO passionate about the subject, it's contagious. Now I'm walking around and analyzing rocks everywhere, and dreaming to go to Mount Helena. Take notes during the lectures, do the quizzes and you'll be ready for the exams.

Prof. Glass is a super nice guy, not the most engaging class if you aren't interested in the topic but the workload is very light and the midterms are super easy if you study beforehand (just memorization and most of the exam questions are exactly the same as the practice tests he provides)

Glass is a GREAT professor! Lectures can be a bit dry at times, but he does his best to keep them engaging & you can tell he's super passionate about what he does. He's very accessible outside of class and always willing to clarify something. It was mainly memorization for the tests and homework, but the review quizzes were super helpful! Big fan!

Tests rote memorization, but pretty easy. I found the material interesting but the lack of tangible samples (or a lab/geology component) made it very dry at times. Huge lecture class typically, so there isn't much engagement. Glass is an excellent lecturer, and passionate about what he professes.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Great Professor. Would Definitely take again.
Loved dynamic oceans so much. Great lecturer, super interesting, really cares deeply about the subject. Easy to get an A if you take notes during the lectures and do your homework. Fair grader.

An incredible lecturer! Take good notes and you should be fine. I highly recommend this class, especially if you're passionate about sustainability and conservation because his classes help you understand the science behind very relevant issues.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: By far the best professor in the Nicholas School.

Relatively straightforward class. Came away from it with a very good grasp of how our planet works. I always found lectures to be engaging and interesting, without focusing too much on the small details that are not relevant for a broad understanding. He does a good job of showing why every topic is exciting and impactful

Following lectures can be frustrating. Slides were basically photos, and Alex gave vague definitions (Google gives clearer ones). He often assumed students know all geology terms, so he would mention some terms w/o explaining them. Throughout lectures I kept pausing and googling. Imagine listening in person and testing on tiny info closed-notes.

Alex is hilarious but class is not that interesting, and much harder. The "waves for babes" nickname is so inaccurate if he's the professor. Definitely easy if you are good at memorizing random pointless information, but otherwise not.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Even with an asynchronous class, Glass managed to be the best professor I had this term. Had more office hours than anyone I've ever had, most clear grading criteria at Duke. Can easily work this class into your schedule and get an A without killing yourself.

Passionate and capable lecturer! Handled online classes the best of all my professors, with accessible and high quality lectures. There was clear and empathetic communication throughout the year and deadlines+expectations were extremely transparent. Exams and quizzes can be extremely specific, so taking detailed notes is key.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: you really need to show up to class for his lectures because his powerpoints only have pictures, but if you ask he typically records the lectures and posts them on his website. his tests are deceptively difficult, and some of the questions seemed out of the blue, but if you study you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Glass is incredibly passionate and engaging in class. He's supportive and will always answer questions you have for him about the material. The syllabus is quite carefully outlined so you can track your grades. No daily homework and no textbook is required. Take diligent notes and attend the pre-exam review sessions to do well on exams!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Caring

reviews.comment: He is clearly very passionate but often speaks extremely fast. His tests (which make up like 90% of your grade are all multiple choice. BUT they test on what seems to be unimportant/highly specific information. Attending lectures is a must to do well, and try to write down everything he says. Recording the lectures on your phone is very helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He is one of the most interesting professors in Duke. Knowledgeable about his field and passionate for teaching. If you dig into environmental science, you should not miss his classes. Super
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Hilarious

reviews.comment: I took both EOS101 and EOS102 with Professor Glass for the NS credit. I loved him as a professor. He was hilarious and genuinely tried to make the material somewhat interesting for students who may not enjoy science. It is extremely important to write down nearly everything he says so attending class is pretty important. Almost no homework!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Glass is a good lecturer and seems like a great guy, but the tests are SO hard and worth 90% of your grade. They're based mostly on lectures, which aren't recorded, slides aren't very helpful, and he talks fast so it's hard to write everything down. I thought it'd be an easy NS, but I'm not even going to end up with a B ://
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I wasn't a big fan of his lectures, but Professor Glass was my friend's favorite professor. Easy material, but take the class seriously. Grade based on 3 midterms and a 7-page book report. Other than book report, barely any homework is assigned. Not particularly interesting class, though, so wouldn't recommend taking it just for the NS credit.

he is obviously very passionate about what he is teaching and tries to make boring lectures more interesting, however, this class is extremely difficult. The test questions are all extremely specific and you must write down everything he says during class. Would not recommend taking it if you want an easy A, even a B is hard to attain.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Course structure makes succeeding on exams (the vast majority of your grade) a challenge. There is minimal context on his presentations and he does not record his lectures which makes studying almost solely based on your notes. Questions asked are absurdly random and specific. The exams feel like a guessing game. Good lecturer, awful course.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class is definitely not easy as people say it is. He speaks extremely quickly which does not allow you to write down everything he says. His exams test you on the most insignificant parts of his lectures. I would not recommend taking this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: not necessarily the easy a it used to be. tests almost exclusively assess the most insignificant of facts rather than concepts taught in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Alex Glass has to be one of my favorite professors at Duke. He is very passionate about geology/ bio-geology, and from this, he knows a lot about the relation of these topics to those of human history and interaction. If you allow yourself to see and understand his passions, you will learn a LOT. Take a class with him, and do so with an open mind!

He was a good lecturer and the class had some interesting parts, but some parts were boring because they were too specific. His slides didn't have much information so you have to go to class and pay attention. Average grade was a B. Negatives were him missing some classes and he said he would post grades that night but then posted a week later.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He is a good lecturer. Just pay attention during lectures and take good notes No homework. The final paper is easy because you basically get the entire semester to work on it.

To be successful in his class, all you have to do is show up to lectures and pay close attention. Also, be sure to diligently study for exams. This course is rather straightforward if you take it seriously. Glass is rather interesting about 70% of the time but the other 30% can be hard to stay awake.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Alex is super funny and a GREAT lecturer. He is very unorganized but it didn't really bother me. Everybody takes Rocks as a joke NS class, but is NOT as easy as it is made out to be. I made the mistake of only going to class a couple of times for the first test. Didn't work out and the first test made it impossible for me to get an A. GO TO CLASS!!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Prof Glass is fantastic and I loved his oceans class. I'm premed so I didn't have to take his class for any credit, but I'm glad that I did. That being said, don't go in assuming the course is going to be easy. You definitely have to go to lecture and take great notes, but he makes it a ton of fun and lecture is never boring.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: No work for this class except the tests and one paper. TESTS ARE HARD. Write down everything he says in class!
Amazing lecturer, very funny, slides don't have many words so  you have to process the information and take good notes, exams are the only difficult part but you can do well if you study
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: EOS 101 is definitely not as easy as people make it out to be. Rocks for Jocks? more like Rocks for Geniuses. The material is boring, but Glass does what he can to make it interesting. Funny guy. Tests are multiple choice but are quite difficult, anything he's ever said in lecture, even in passing, is fair game. Don't skip lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Prof. Glass is an awesome professor. Even if you don't find the subject particularly interesting on its own, you will with him. The class wasn't too difficult but don't go in expecting it to be easy. You definitely need to pay attention during lectures and constantly take notes. The exams are pretty tricky even though they're multiple choice.

Glass is the man - he's a funny, friendly guy with amazing Powerpoints and interesting lectures. Dynamic Earth is NOT easy. Not that hard either, but test writing makes things tougher. EOS 101 definitely wasn't the joke I expected. Pulled all-nighters for the midterms, ended up with a 91 and missed an A by two test questions, but heck, my fault...

I heard this class was easy but it really wasn't. There are only a couple of tests and one paper. Tests are pretty difficult and it's not easy to do well in the class if you don't ace everything. Overall, not a bad class but don't underestimate the amount of studying you need to do in order to make an A.

This was an interesting class, and Dr. Glass is a hilarious professor. However, this class is definitely not an easy A. It is possible if you work hard, but the tests are extremely specific making it impossible to do well if you don't really know the material. I recommend this class only if you're ready to do work even when it's not "assigned".

Glass is geeky adorable and a fantastic lecturer - I really learned a lot in his course and he is entertaining and creates spot-on Powerpoints. I went in to this class believing the "Waves for Babes" reputation and expecting an easy A, but I studied really hard to end up with a B. Take the first test very seriously, that's where I went wrong.
Great professor with great lectures. Barely any out of class work but the tests are very difficult. Be prepared to study a lot for them and don't expect an A.

EOS 102 is an interesting class. Alex Glass is a great professor and his powerpoints are the best i've seen in all my life. However, many people drop after the first midterm, only 20% or so get an A and the rest will get Bs and Cs. If you love to memorize information you will not likely use after the class (unless you major in EOS), take this class
Professor Glass is hilarious. Tests are a bit tough so make sure to study the fine details. I would definitely take him again.

Professor Glass is excellent in clarity and conciseness, so long as you attend class. I took this class thinking it would be an easy A and while I got the outcome I wanted, I studied hard for the tests. If you do not show up to class, there will be questions that he only gives information for in person or over audio (and I wouldn't count on audio).

He's a really cool professor who's genuinely interested in what he's talking about. Definitely come to class since thats what tests are based on. He said he would record and post the lectures but he didn't record half of them which made it hard to study for the classes I missed. Even though tests are multiple choice he will find ways to trip u up

He is an amazing lecturer and person. His entire class is graded off of three tests and a field trip to the Marine Lab. This is good as long as you study for the test. When i say study, i mean actually study! This class can be  difficult if you do not memorize his lectures. Also, you must goto class because his notes are spoken with help from ppts.

Glass is hilarious, down-to-earth, and my favorite professor I've ever had. His class is NOT hard if you go to class and take notes well. Study in groups and you'll be fine. He curves tests that are ENTIRELY MULTIPLE CHOICE. I'm not even interested in science or the environment at all but I actually looked forward to class with Glass. Just Awesome!
His lectures are very interesting and engaging.  However, his tests are relatively hard because you have to remember all the details from lectures and slides.

The class is interesting and professor Glass is one of my favorite professors of all time. He is absolutely hilarious. Tests are hard (all multiple choice) because they ask about very specific details, so it is necessary to memorize everything he says in class if you want an A.

Alex Glass is the man! This guy is awesome to listen to. He splits things up nicely between material, some peer interaction, and cool life storiesfield experiences. He really makes class enjoyable. He jokes a lot and keeps the mood light. Pretty hilarious at times. Super knowledgeable. Make sure to show up to class and study for tests.

Professor Glass's Dynamic Oceans class was one of the most interesting I have ever taken at Duke. He is very knowledgeable and enthusiastic about the material, and you can't help but become infected by his excitement. His lectures are always interesting and his powerpoints are AMAZING!!! Definitely would take another class with him.

Professor Glass is the best professor I've had at Duke so far.  He's very engaging and he makes his lectures fun.  I actually looked forward to going to class with him as the professor, and he makes lots of jokes and makes things easy to understand.  His tests are very detail-oriented, so you should go to class and take good notes.
Nice professor in general. Tests tend to be tricky as materials from extra credit assignment have been involved. Recommended for students with perfect attendance.
This guy is a legend. He really loves his powerpoints, for good reason, they're incredible. He's really good though, but you have to go to class and actually study for the test

Fantastic professor. Engaging lectures. Had no interest in geology before taking this course, but looked forward to it every week. Highly recommend it, and not terribly hard. But study!!! I bombed the first midterm because I didn't think studying was necessary and then had to absolutely pull it out at the end.

Great professor! Course material itself could be extremely complicated but Professor Glass manages to explain it in interesting and understandable ways. Lectures are always interesting and keep my attention. One of the best class I have taken!

Professor Glass is an awesome lecturer, but he's also interesting outside of the class. While I have to say he sometimes doesn't have his stuff together, he does a great job regardless. Definitely make use of regrades, because his TA's tend to not speak the best English, but he's great about giving points back. Take his class.

Prof Glass is a boss, enough said! It was fun digressing during class and talking about sci-fi and philosophy and other random stuff, though he made the class content pretty interesting as well. I'd definitely take another class with him!

Professor Glass was great. While some of his test questions were quite difficult, he is an excellent lecturer and his power point presentations are out of this world! I would highly recommend him as a professor.

Grade is based on tests which are drawn solely from the lecture. Show up to class and pay attention, and you'll get a good grade.  Glass is a great professor for non majors because he brings out a childlike wonder about the earth and universe which makes the dry scientific material more engaging. Trees friendly (rocks for jocks, get stoned)

Chill bro. Very interesting lecturer. Makes something that could be impossibly boring interesting. Catch is that tests can be pretty hard in that you really have to know everything he talked about in lecture to do well.
Don't expect an easy A. Tests are very detail oriented & require studying. If you study the lecture slides, though, you will do well.

Must go to class if you want a good grade since a lot of the exam material is based on what he says in lecture. Exams are not comprehensive but are more like trivia. Also beware of study sessions since he tends to mislead you and ends up covering different material on the exam. The trip to the marine lab is a total flop and not worth the time.

This class is super easy. Exams are almost entirely based on the slides with a few questions based on his lecture. Although the lecture can be skipped, if you attend most of the classes and cram the slides, you are ensured a great grade.
Awesome class!

I enjoyed the content of this class, especially the third section which focused on life in the ocean. There is little work to be done for the class but the tests are very hard. Also, there is a mandatory field trip to the Marine Lab for the weekend, which I was not aware of before enrolling, but it was fun. Don't expect an easy A.

He is a interesting professor and always makes the class laugh. But his lecture is pretty unorganized. i feel like he just writes down some random facts that in his mind.(especially the part about marine animals!) the tests aren't that hard but he puts so many details and random facts in them

One of the best lecturers I've ever had. The class isn't easy per se but everything you need to know is in the lectures so the textbook is basically useless. His tests are very detail-oriented but if you study in advance they're fine. I have no interest in the subject whatsoever but his classes are still very engaging
Exams are not fair! He asks random facts.

Prof Glass is enthusiastic, loved his animations and appreciated the analysis of Japan earthquake. Very friendly and helpful, organized fantastic trip to marine lab. Tests are very detailed oriented and have to be memorized to score well

Alex is a fantastic professor and very entertaining. Even if you're not super interested in the subject, he makes class engaging. However, his tests are VERY detail-oriented, which makes them really hard to prepare for.

Although I did not receive the grade I was hoping, I really enjoyed Alex Glass's teaching. He is incredible enthusiastic about geology. I had NO interest in science AT ALL (Humanities, woot woot!), but his class got me hooked on learning more about the Earth. I know, sounds cheesy, but he's great :)

He is a great guy who loves teaching but his tests are horrible. he's questions are tricky for no reason and he will test on thins he will say once in class that is not not slides. if you dont want to memorize a bunch of random facts, dont take this class

This class was horrible. I took earth science in both middle & high school (got A's both times), and I studied for every exam in this class. Yet, it is BY FAR my worst grade of the semester. He tests on random, useless facts he casually mentions, not the important material you would intuitively try to learn. Only take if you have a lot of free time

I have taken EOS 11 and 12 with Glass and he is amazing. Neither are difficult classes and have the potential to be simple lecture-courses, but Glass is so enthusiastic and spends so much time preparing visuals that everything sounds exciting. Definitely take a class with Glass!

Glass is a great teacher, very enthusiastic and accessible.  EOS11 is deemed one of Duke's easy classes.  This is only true IF you attend class.  If you go to class, pay attention, and study some for the test you will get an A. If you don't go to class and study last minute expect closer to a C.  I'd recommend taking him, but go to class or else.

This class is not easy.  I heard this section is the harder of the two.  The tests go over very, very minute details that were sometimes only glossed over in class, and the homework assignments were very unclear.  Still, Professor Glass is a great lecturer.  Extra credit was helpful, but one last warning: It is not easy.
NOT an EASY class

Excellent Professor. Hilarious in class and very enthusiastic. One of the best lecturer I've had,  and I'm a senior. Do not leave Duke without taking his class. Tests cover tiny details, but not hard if you study.  Also offers extra credit, so most people got As.

Glass = Awesome. Though I was not interested in earth science at all before, Glass' lectures were clear, interesting, surprisingly relevant, and often funny. Definitely take this if you need an NS. It's not something you can completely blow off, but it will be interesting, enjoyable, and you'll learn a lot. NOT an easy A, but definitely worth it.

EOS 11 is no longer "Rocks for Jocks"...  You must pay attention in class and study before the exams since the exam questions are often challenging.  Not a difficult course, but don't just blow it off.

One of the bst teachers ive had at Duke. Make sure to take his section, because he makes the material so much more interesting, and it makes the early mornings worth it This class is definitely not an easy class, but if you go to class, and go in for office hours for homework help, you'll be set.
Easy if you go to class, study the sometimes entertaining powerpoints, and listen to what he has to say. He keeps it interesting with current event stories and his own experience.

I am a senior pre-med.  I already got into three medical schools.  I thought this class would be easy to balance out me going to interviews.  And, it turns out that this f(*&*(() class is harder than biochem.  Seriously, I have higher grade in biochem than in this class.  My friends who took this class before either lie to me or it got really hard.
Not easy A.

Everything on the test is covered in class or on the power point slides. All you need to do is come to every class and take notes on everything that is said which is not on the slides. All tests are curved. Glass responds to all e-mails thoroughly. He's also very enthusiastic on the subject which makes his class enjoyable and exciting. Smart guy.

Glass is the greatest teacher that has ever graced that the Duke University community.  Glass is the favorite professor you will ever get at Duke University.  You will regret coming to Duke if you do not take his classes.  I repeat: You will regret coming to Duke or into existence if you fail to take any of his awesome classes.

He's such a good prof that I changed my major to take more EOS classes! Professor Glass imbues his teaching with so much passion that it's difficult to get bored with the potentially mundane material (discussing fossils). EOS141 is a great class--just go to lecture! It's fun, anyway. Glass is the best prof at Duke. He's a total stud, too. ;)

Amazing professor,take a Glass-class during your time at Duke!! Fossil Transitions is an interesting class, especially since Glass is so enthusiastic and knowledgeable. You do need to come to class & pay attention but I actually enjoyed going to this class. (weird, right?) Glass is a fair professor and accessible/ willing to help if needed!

Great Prof-I would def recommend Major Fossil Transitions.  Not much work on a lecture to lecture basis, but when the midterm/final come around you're gonna have a late couple of nights. Attending lecture and taking notes is a must, but to be honest he's an animated guy so it's not that bad. If you put in a decent amount of time you will do well.
