Great guy. Loved his class and his teaching. Very engaging lectures!

I have taken both EOS 11 and 12 from Professor Glass. Both classes were very entertaining and easy to attend. He uses very impressive and entertaining slides and has an energetic lecture style. Some people say that the classes are difficult, but if you try at all and come to class its quite easy. Glass is the man, would take more from him if could

Professor Glass is very fun and entertaining in class, using excellent and very impressive slides and a energetic lecture style to make an otherwise boring topic easy to learn about. He is very fair with grading, has extra credit opportunities, and always curves to a high average if necesary. Good guy to take from.

Take his Major Fossil Transitions class! If you are at all interested in Biology or Paleotology (or if you just want to take another class with him 'cause he's one of the most fun, interesting Profs at Duke), take it and have a blast listening to his engaging lectures. The material isn't hard to understand, but the work is extensive for this class.

Glass is a great prof.  His power points are awesome and he makes the class interesting.  You need to go to class, but the power points are all online and every test question can be answered from the power points.  There is no final, so you only need to learn the material for each test, there are 3 easy HWs and Extra Credit, and the class is curved
NOT AN EASY A, NOT "ROCKS FOR JOCKS," you must put in effort and even then a B is a real possibility, take if you are interested in EOS, do not expect an easy A
"His lecture slides are pretty damn good. Funny guy. But prob not the easiest class." This review said it best, so I'm just going to repeat it.
He is a fun and interesting lecturer and is always willing to help out a student with a question.

Alex is a really nice guy and a very entertaining lecturer. He puts a lot of effort into his powerpoints and he's a very clear teacher. You have to study and go to class to get an A, but otherwise it's pretty easy. He makes studying rocks interesting and entertaining!
Professor Glass is an awesome professor. His lectures are really interesting, concise, and his power points are amazing. I really enjoyed class and would take any others he teaches.

Professor Glass is an extremely animated professor who makes class and slightly mundane material very itneresting to get involved with. His tests were hard but he was extremely fair about grading and very easy to approach. He is generally a cool guy outside of class as well, and very helpful. I liked his teaching style enough to take another class

In case you're curious, "Touching the Void" is on YouTube. It's totally a baller movie. I actually teared up, not even joking. Alex is such a cool guy. If you came to Duke to learn something, take any of Alex's classes. They're not easy, but you definitely come away knowing & understanding things way better than before, and that's a good feelin

Alex is an amazing and very engaging professor. I took this class to fulfill my NS req. and could not have chosen better. While you need to attend lectures to do well, he keeps class interesting and at the end of the semester is a very reasonable grader. Hey, any prof. who reads Dune, watches Firefly and quotes Monty Python is alright with me :)

This class was definitely harder than I expected and not exactly an easy A. You need to attend the lectures to get thorough notes for the exams. However, he is an engaging, interesting, and pretty funny professor who really knows his stuff. Take this class, and you'll learn loads!
Lectures are good. Work involved, but the class was curved at the end. Take it.

Great Lecturer, but recently was forced to make the class way harder than it needed to be. He should have indicated this at the start of the term!!!!!! Has changed from rocks for jocks to impossible tests as he asks needlessly difficult questions just to get a class distribution. If you're going to take this, definitely go with Klein, she's a gem.
Rocks for jocks?  I think not.  More like rocks for rocket scientists...I kid you not.

Alex Glass is a GREAT lecturer. He's interesting, and really knows his stuff. His tests are a little on the difficult side, and his class is in no sense an 'easy A'. Sometimes, his exams tests on some really trivial, exact numbers. But if you go to class and just read over and memorize your notes fairly well, you'll be able to pull off a B easily.
Great lecturer. Lots of stuff to memorize. Don't take unless you're legitimately interested in earth science

In terms of actual workload, the class isn't the most demanding. However, there is a lot of content that must be memorized and there is an opportunity to expand your knowledge with a professor that's enthusiastic about his subject. He also goes out of the way to make himself accessible outside of class. I would definitely recommend this class.
His lecture slides are pretty damn good. Funny guy. But prob not the easiest class.

Prof. Glass is a really great lecturer. He's interesting & funny -- he uses his own pictures in his slides which is nice. He's very knowledgeable and accessible. Also Annie the TA was really helpful as well. It's a great class - I learned a lot and it was fun. Definitely have to go to the lectures though --test material isn't all found in the ppts.
Excellent teacher. Questions on some tests seemed tangential to what was really important, but still worthwhile. If you figure out how the water machine works, please post here.

"On the plus side, his gorgeous eyes, hot accent, and great sense of humor made class fun"   HAHAHAHAHA.   .. But kind of true.  Alex is a great professor - though (as the ratings before have mentioned)not an easy-breezy A.  Go to class - take notes: there are discrepancies btw the book and ppt slides.

Glass is a really cool guy. He makes the class really interesting with his witty anecdotes and interesting powerpoint presentations. As long as you study, the class will be okay. It is interesting, fun and not at all taxing. I always looked forward to his classes.

Alexander Glass is an amazing professor. One of the best i've had at Duke. He is very engaging and makes relatively boring material very interesting. He is funny, witty, and makes a huge effort to make the class fun.I HIGHLY RECOMMEND THIS CLASS.

Glass is a G.  You don't have to go to class, though you should as class is amusing and he's extremely interesting. Tests are pretty easy if you go to *some* of the classes and look over powerpoints. I thought the class would be a bit easier though. Put a bit of effort in and you'll get an A, otherwise you're B-coasting.  Glass is a great guy too.

It's a good class, just not if you're expecting the "easy A."  Go into it expecting it to be like any other class, and it'll be worthwhile.  Glass is pretty funny too.  For as little work as I did and to come out with an OK grade...I'm okay with that.

engaging professor- definitely knows how to make relatively mundane things interesting. on the other hand, i took it for an easy A and it was not. GO to class, and pay attention, and be ready for petty work at teh end of the semester
don't take the class. nice guy , but just not for everyone
Not a good teacher.  Way overrated, does not answer e-mails.  I did not find him very funny, and definitely not an easy A.  This was my hardest class this semester by far.

He's a pretty nice guy, but he definitely is starting to make the class a lot harder than before. Tests are not easy. You need to go to class and take good notes and memorize them. He gives time consuming assignments at the end of the semester. Don't take for easy A.

Class is not just an "easy A," if you're a Bio major looking to boost your GPA like me. You have to work--memorize his lectures, basically. On the plus side, his gorgeous eyes, hot accent, and great sense of humor made class fun!

Taking this class is like putting glass up your ...ss and i mean a bottle so it bleeds and hurts. This is WAY harder than it needs to be. Dont take this if you're looking for an easy A. Homework takes forever... tests are very hard . But the professor is a nice guy, very cool...so to speak,  but once again. not easy.

Glass is an amazing teacher.  He's always willing to help out when you need it.  Hate to break it to you, but there is no easy class at Duke.  However, if you're looking for an awesome teacher and an overall cool dude who knows his stuff, Alexander Glass is your man.

Im taking Dynamic Oceans with Glass and he is AMAZING! The lectures are always very interesting and the slideshows are very entertaining! He always adds fun animations. Overall it is an easy class if you show up to the lectures. 2 Midterms and 1 final. TAKE THIS CLASS
don't take this class unless you are interested in eos. Not a good teacher, not a good class, not an easy A
Tests have become unnecessarily hard (c'mon, it's EOS ELEVEN, not a 100 level course on up).  That said, I'd still take Glass any day.

He was terrible. Made the class harder to the point were you could actually study and go to class and still end up without an A. This class is only a joke bc you don't have to go to class and there is essentially no work other than studying. But he puts questions on tests that he never mentioned before.
His eyes are amazing.

NOT AN EASY A at ALL! DON'T TAKE IF YOU WANT AN EASY A! HE is a WONDERFUL Teacher/Educator, but he has made the class a lot harder! You have to attend all of the lectures and PAY CLOSE ATTENTION! SOMEWHERE IN THE A   range is possible if you dedicate A LOT, Yes I Mean A LOT OF TIME INTO THE CLASS! LOVE THE CLASS AND GLASS THOUGH!

Great, interesting, passionate professor. His lectures are really interesting and hilarious. You don't really have to go to class; tests are all based off of his great powerpoints. Class isn't an easy A, but if you study for tests, you'll be fine. Recommended!
if you go to class and pay attention, you will get an A.... he is an awesome teacher and it's not hard to stay alert in class because he keeps your attention

He is an extraordinary teacher. He is very funny and clever. His tests are based totally off of his discussions during lecture not the PowerPoints he posts. The class is much harder than it has been in the past. If you study a lot and pay attention during class you will do well. TAKE THIS CLASS because it is fascinating! Not an Easy A. WORK HARD :)

Dr. Glass is an amazing professor.  He posts all the powerpoints online, so a lot of people don't go to class...but they are very interesting powerpoints, and all the info you need for the test is on them.  This class isn't THAT easy. Chances are you will still need to study for tests and there is a LOT of info, but it's basically just memorization

Incredible lecturer.  Ties topics in with fun and interesting examples and is genuinely interested in teaching his students about geology.  EOS 11 is more interesting and EASIER than Chem 83 if you take it with Glass.
Class was very easy.  He tells you exactly what you needs to know for the tests, and the homeworks are a joke.  Easy A.

Very easy, but a professor who is truly passionate about his subject.  Clearly, he is trying to spark interest in EOS.  Lectures sometimes got a little boring, but he was wonderful.  Tests and homework extremely easy.

Even though this class is supposed to be easy, Glass really keeps you interested.  I actually looked forward to his lectures by the end of the semester, and I learned way more  about earth sciences than I thought I would in that class.  It has probably been my favorite class at Duke so far.

Glass is a vibrant, hilarious teacher. The info isn't that exciting but he makes class really fun with awesome powerpoints and his great personality. Puts PP online, but go to class because the tests are entirely off of the lectures. Don't read the book--no help.
Alex is an amazing professor.  His lectures are interesting and you'll learn a lot, but his class isn't too hard.  He has a killer personality and an even better sense of humor.

Great professor, really helpful.  The content of the course could be dull, but he really makes it come alive -- highly recommend taking this class, if you're interested in EOS or just want your NS credit.  Class isn't hard either

Dr. Arcila Maya is very caring and works hard to make sure all of her students understand the material. She goes through plenty of examples and work during lectures. The lab questions often did not make sense and the TA's struggled to give helpful feedback without giving the answers. Lots of work for S/U class. At least four assignments each week.

Prof AM is easily the best professor I have ever had in the math dept and is the best professor I have ever had period. She genuinely cares about her students and their feedback and is incredibly helpful and supportive. Her office hours were my saving grace. She breaks down difficult topics in an understandable way and makes this class enjoyable.

She was THE best professor I've ever had! She is so accessible outside of class and cares so much about your well-being, and does everything in her power to make sure you succeed. She posts beautiful lecture notes, and expectations are clear and lectures are engaging. MATH 401 is hard, but she has made it the most enjoyable class of my math degree!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
Do whatever you can to avoid taking 608 with Prof Maurel. The professor just tries to read his slides out loud, assigns useless hw, and gets confused why no one is learning. 
Take ANY of the other econometrics courses to fulfill your credit, you will learn more and get a better grade.
The slides are very organized and clear. The instructor is approachable both after class and during office hours!
Not a good teacher at all, just reads his notes. Not that much work throughout the semester but tests require a ton of studying. Not very helpful outside of class.

tough class, but easier than thomas in fall. 4/8 problem sets are graded, only one midterm, and one final. stuff is really hard so you do need to stay on top of it. he was as good as could be for this class; it's tough anyway you slice it.  exams were very fair and only had things covered in class/section.
Had to teach myself everything through textbooks.

Professor Arya provides well-thought out lectures to cover the tough material covered within the entirety of the course. He makes everything very straightforward for homework and exams. He is super accessible outside of class and is generous in regards to extensions. He genuinely wants everyone to do well in this class!

Professor Arya is a very caring professor who works hard to make sure the content of the class is engaging and interesting to students. He often gives extensions to the class when students ask for them as he understands we are under a lot of academic stress. The class can be difficult at times, but the exams are clear and follow the homework.

Dr. Arya is a brilliant professor who really cares for the students and wants all his students to succeed. He teaches with clarity and his office hours are very useful. The material is pretty tough so it is important to attend classes and do homeworks. The exam has conceptual questions so try to understand the material. He uses a generous curve.

He is a wonderful professor. At the beginning, the material was very hard for me to grasp. However, I learned so much from this class supported by Dr. Arya. He is very caring with his students and is understanding of academic stress. There is a lot of homework, but it is very helpful for learning, and Dr. Arya is lenient with extensions.

Dr. Aryas presentations are clear, concise, and informative, and he genuinely wants everyone to succeed. Grading is rough on algebra mistakes, but its curved at the end and theres a weight redistribution for your worst test (I got a D on one exam, but was able to pull my grade up without too much headache  office hours helped. Hes great.)

Dr. Arya is very wholesome. Like the other reviews said, the beginning to middle of the semester was very rough. However, when the course material actually ramped up and the class transitioned to online due to COVID, his powerpoints and lecture style translated very well and the course quality went up. His tests are fair and match practice exams.

Professor Arya was teaching his first undergraduate course at Duke when I took his class. He was learning the material as we were, and I often felt he did not come prepared to class, increasing the burden on the students. Additionally, I would often asked him questions that he would need days to answer and would then give incoherent responses.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Really nice guy, does some great research in material science, but probably wasn't the best choice for a sophomore/freshman level statics class (he was "learning with us" some of the semester). Wasn't super accommodating during COVID and the final felt a little unfair, but overall not the worst class. Just pay attention and it'll be ok.

Not accommodating for COVID, quite often would not be able to answer a question or clarification, saying he did not know the reason behind it (which seemed like they should be somewhat straightforward). He is very nice in person and wants everyone to learn, just very inexperienced with full classes of undergrads. Also struggled with online lectures

Dr. Arya is the most unaccommodating professor I had during COVID. He weighted the final 40% of the overall grade. His lectures were unengaging and he constantly told the class that this was his first time teaching this materials so he was "learning with us." I learned more from the textbook than I did in his lectures.

Dr. A is very chill and sets all expectations clear from day 1. They are constantly trying to improve the class and make it as relevant as possible. All the reading was really engaging w/ peers and interesting. Compared to other classes I've taken as a freshman, the workload is not that heavy, as others may suggest.

Dr. A's class was a pretty interesting writing 120. I would recommend it to anyone interested in learning about ethical AI use, language, and linguistics. There's a lot of reading and annotations you do as homework, and two big essays you write throughout the year. The classes themselves were boring at times but Dr. A is a very kind and caring prof
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: prof is very nice, BUT her class is definitely one of the most writing- and reading-intensive in the writing120 bunch. If you can avoid, please do. You will be swimming in annotations and writing. pls and thank you.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: Dr. Asmuth is super clear in their expectations. Just do the work and it's an easy A.

This professor came off generally as flat during lectures, bordering passive aggressive (increasingly as the semester progressed). Long and dense readings (around 30-40 pages) but only need to annotate them; some were more interesting than others. Graded off of two papers which I enjoyed because I was really able to explore what I wanted.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Asmuth is a great writing 101 professor: very clear expectations, guides you through the process, and keeps you on track. They breaks down large assignments into smaller deliverables, which was helpful for a procrastinator like me. Their lecturing style isn't super engaging, but I think they still helped me improve my writing.

Will tell you exactly what you need to do to succeed in the class, as long as you are willing to do the work. Very compassionate and fosters safe group environment. Two major projects require effort and time, but very doable and lots of revision opportunities. Relatively easy writing101.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Asmuth is a VERY nice professor. Her writing courses are fantastic. Grading criteria are super clear and specifically listed "Do XXX, and you will earn an A."
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Definitely learned a lot with Dr. Asmuth. She is a kind person and wants you to succeed. Reading exercises are very heavy during the first half of the class. Everything after that was chill.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--So many papers

reviews.comment: Lovely professor - super kind, chill, and very clearly cares about students. If you pay attention and study the vocab a little bit you will be totally fine grade-wise, and she dropped many assignments. Wish I could have her for every Spanish class!

Ashley is one of the kindest and most caring professors at Duke. Spanish 203 with her was sooooo easy - you basically get an A as long as you show up and actually participate! We were supposed to do Boomalangs and other big projects but she just cancelled them so the class was extra easy. Beware: she is NOT responsive to emails at all.
Great professor, cares about her students and generally very lenient with grading. If you put in effort you're basically guaranteed an A.

Amazing professor: funny, caring, gets to know each student. She's very lenient with grading and deadlines, as long as you get the work done and put in effort you'll likely receive an A. My favorite professor for Spanish so far.

If you participate a little bit, you should be fine. Professor Hobson makes the class easy, fun, and relatively enjoyable! Lots of what feels like busy work, but she is probably the best Spanish professor at Duke. Definitely take her class.

Ashley Hobson was an amazing professor, and I would highly recommend taking the course with her. She offers a lot of feedback, both writing and verbal, and I appreciated it for upcoming projects and quizzes. For the quizzes she made sure to review in class with lots of practice. I always felt prepared, and her grading criteria is straight forward.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Ashley cares about her students, is very willing to help with concerns, and is very forgiving and flexible. Only downside is that she does not put grades in until basically the end of the semester, which can make it difficult to figure out how you are actually doing in the class. Also she doesn't respond to emails, but is willing to meet.
She was great. Super chill, straightforward, and knowledgeable.

Prof. Hobson was amazing! She was extremely nice and understanding as she would always push deadlines if students requested. She's not the fastest grader but definitely take any Spanish class with her

Syllabus was unclear about where information could be found and when/if an assignment was due. Professor was consistently 5-10 minutes late to class. Professor did not grade assignments until end of class which made it difficult to improve. Class itself is very front loaded so there are many assignments due each class day through November.
She is super nice and understanding. Sometimes she does not respond to emails, but other than that she is an amazing professor.

Prof. Hobson is the most caring and best Spanish prof I have had at Duke. She is super accessible, understanding, and makes you feel welcome no matter how confident you are in your Spanish skills. Just make sure to actively participate in every class. You will learn a lot in a very welcoming environment!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: She is so nice and friendly, always willing to help. Her classroom environment is super chill and she is not a very tough grader as long as you put in the work on your end. The class structure in general is not bad: mostly quizzes, essays, and group presentations that all feel low-pressure because she is not scary like many otherSpanish professors

Pretty easy class, esp if you have had some higher-level Spanish exposure. Either way, she does a great job explaining things & will switch into English for better comprehension. Ashley is easy-going & very willing to help you. There are group projects & peer-edited essays. Overall great class, & Ashley is a wonderful professor.

I had Ashley Hobson for Spanish 102, and I specifically enrolled in her Spanish 203 class the next semester so I could have her again. She is a great professor and her classroom environment is always super fun and friendly. When we discuss grammar, she will even switch into English to make sure that we fully understand everything.
Favorite professor at Duke so far. Super nice. Always willing to help after class

Aspinwall is a good professor. He lectures well, and you can stop by to ask questions outside of office hours. Weekly homework never exceeds 6 questions. The downside to 603 is the textbook is dry and assumes more background knowledge than you probably have. There are no midterms. The final has hard questions dissimilar to the homework problems.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The pacing of this course was very strange. Either we were computing contour integrals (pretty mindless) or we were reading Ahlfors (not so mindless). We also did a fair amount of physics/applied math for some reason (this wasn't even in the textbook btw). If you're a math major, you'd likely prefer 633.

A good, caring professor who can teach you a lot in lectures, as long as you put in the effort, too. MATH 403 was sometimes very abstract and I often had no intuition for the topics. However, he's very accessible outside class despite being sometimes disorganized. Homework load was average for a math class, and tests were tough but curved heavily.

Aspinwall is probably one of the best math professors I've had at Duke, very good at distilling huge amounts of information into important points. Also a very nice dude, and is pretty nice about grading,

Speaks english, teaches decently well, is willing to help students outside of class.  I still accompanied the class with MIT lecture videos though.  I agree that tests are relatively easier than other professors' tests.
Prof. Aspinwall is really helpful and he always answers questions. Go to his office hours and he will explain even basic concepts to you. He is a great professor to learn calculus from.
He always answers students' questions promptly and his midterms are quite easy (compared to other math212 professors). Very nice person in general.
Aspinwall always made an effort to ensure his students understood the material. He promptly answered emails and made time for private tutoring whenever I asked for it.

Don't know what these reviews below are saying.. Aspinwall is a great lecturer and he always pauses to make sure the class understands. The material is tough, but the tests are very doable if you put in the effort. He never gives you the answer without making sure you think your way towards it.
Not very good at explaining concepts way below his level. Everything is "clear" or "obvious" to him. Don't know how he is at non-intro courses.

He's very willing to help and is a genius but yes, this class is very time consuming and you have to put in a lot of time and effort every week between the quiz and HW especially if you're not a physics person. Go to helproom and ask TAs for help!! It'll take so much stress off of you. He grades exams very leniently though

Mixed feelings about this class. While Kotwal is a good lecturer, a great person, and amazingly helpful in helproom, it's beyond what I'd expect for an intro course. Homework is challenging - go to helproom. Having weekly quizzes was brutal & frustrating, esp. when we hadn't learned the content yet, though the actual weren't bad. Overall recommend.

Weekly quizzes and extreme workload. Get ready for 8 hrs/wk outside lab/class/discussion. Terrible during the fact because you can't slack, but helps you learn and lots of cushion. Tests are fair, do the review problems. Lecture is not that helpful, but Kotwal spends 3+ hours personally answering q's in office hours, more than most profs can say.

While physics is intimidating, I think Kotwal does his best to deliver it in a manner that is logical, especially during his office hours. He's truly down-to-earth and funny. I really enjoyed a science class that was about more than memorization, but about logical concepts. Hard, but glad I took this course at Duke.

This class (122) takes a LOT of work, especially if you're like me and didn't have a strong physics background--Prof. Kotwal is brilliant but I'd advise going to helproom/SAGE/asking your discussion TA/studying with friends as much as possible to get the material in a format an undergrad can more easily digest. He is vv generous with extra credit!

Lectures were unorganized, incomprehensible, and never covered all of the material needed for the weekly quizzes. I learned the entirety of the course content from my discussion group TA and SAGE facilitator. Kotwal is nice enough but is not a good teacher. Don't take physics with him if you can help it.

Probably the worst lectures of any class I have ever taken - Prof. Kotwal is absolutely useless at teaching this material in a coherent way. I passed this class out of sheer will and the help of discussion section leaders.

This was hard for a general physics class, but really interesting. His lectures can be confusing, but he's always willing to answer questions after class and in help room. The exams make you apply concepts in ways you haven't seen before. Pretty much curved- very generous with adjusting grading criteria for exams so no one does too poorly.

Extremely difficult course since he cannot lecture at all. Expected students to understand material immediately and got confused when we didn't know what was going on. I basically learned the entire course with outside resources. Homework extremely hard and not representative of exams (also difficult). He does give a lot of extra credit though.

Yes, this was a pretty hard for a physics course I was expecting at a level for 142. Homeworks take a lot of time and at least one long response on the exam requires you to think hard about the concepts you learned in class. But he gave a LOT of extra credit on exams and the final replaces the lowest midterm if you do better on the final. No curve.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Kotwal is an intelligent professor, but he shouldn't teach intro courses. He teaches at a level that is far above intro. He isn't willing to help students who need different learning styles. I asked him to explain things in a different way in help room & he said no. Explanations for other questions have been 'because it is.' Do not take this class.

Extremely knowledgeable and confident but does not check for student understanding. Explains the content in a variety of ways, which is helpful for students on the ball but unhelpful for those lost. Tough homeworks, many exams (3 midterms + a final).

While I think Prof Kotwal is very knowledgeable and has good notes, the class is beyond challenging and lectures are not a great use of time. From old exams, is seems like the test difficulty was ramped up this year. I recommend to not take Phys142 at Duke if possible since the material is not relevant for a majority of the students (pre-meds).
This man is a legend -- his explanations almost always insightful. His class requires thinking and understanding, not mere regurgitation. Worth your time.

Kotwal is caring/accommodating, but if you want to do well in the class you'll have to attend Help Room AND Office Hours, and just make Physics your entire life for the semester. Homework is a total pain but helps with material on the quizzes/exams. Lab is fun and you just work on homework for the entire discussion period before taking the quiz.

kotwal is great because he explains difficult concepts in a way for non-physics majors to understand. he cares deeply about helping us learn and actually understand the material rather than just memorizing problems and formulas. dude is also a genius and effortlessly hilarious

Tough class, super hard homework, but he'll definitely take the time to explain more than you ever wanted to know about Physics. Also one of the most brilliant people at Duke. He explains all the gory details of derivation well beyond the scope of the course, which is time-consuming but he does it in a way that lets you see the elegance.

physics at duke is quite bad lol but ashutosh is brilliant in general/ prob one of the better physics instructors for this course! he is very helpful in helproom and his tests are fair(also gives lots of extra credit). he doesn't even try to be but he's also quite a funny man.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Kotwal was a strong physics professor, given the rigor of the curriculum at Duke. He can almost always answer your question, even if he may come off as a little condescending at times. He was reasonable about pushing homework assignments back a few days when we needed it (for UNC game day or the end of a break etc). Much better than Wu for Phy141!

Dr. Kotwal was my discussion TA for phy142. This man is a blessing to Duke University. Best professor I've ever had in my life. He can take the most complicated physics topics and explain them to you so clearly that you question why you were ever confused. He can give perfect answers to problems without even writing anything down. Absolute beast.

New appreciation for Kotwal after taking 142 with Edwards. Kotwal's class is organized (1 chapter  1 week, lectures/labs/discussions were coordinated) and he was good about posting answer keys and resources online. I had no physics background so it wasn't an easy A but it was doable with hard work. Bombed a midterm but could replace it with final.

I don't think he was an amazing lecturer and as someone who had literally no high school background in physics I definitely struggled more than most. Find a group of friends and study together. I found this better than searching for a tutor and praying on my knees in my dorm every night, hoping I would absorb any physics. He is a kind man tho.
He is a physics genius! He is also funny without trying. His lectures helped to explain material I did not completely understand. I would take this class to get a solid foundation of mechanics.
I suggest going to office hours and tutoring to get the most out of your learning experience.

Kotwal is a very nice guy and genuinely wants to help you learn physics. He can be hard to follow in lecture because of his accent and handwriting but the essence of it is helpful. His tests arent hard but there is no curve and little mistakes mark you down a lot. He also dissociates himself from grading issues so TAs have a lot of power

Dr. Kotwal is a brilliant guy, really friendly and can give perfect answers to questions on the fly. His lectures were essential for understanding the course material. Skipping lecture or trying to learn it all from the textbook will place you at a disadvantage.

He was very difficult to understand and his notes/handwriting was unclear. I don't think he understood the questions that students would ask in class, so it made it hard to get clarification about the more difficult concepts.

He's a great professor but his lectures are pretty fast-paced and his notes aren't the most organized; however, he's very good about answering questions if you are confused. He's pretty funny in class, but it's hard to make physics interesting. We have quizzes and lots of HW every week. Also, make an equations list b/c knowledge is accumulative.

Dr. Kotwal is clearly a genius but the man cannot teach at the undergrad level to save his life. He is more helpful in office hours but also likes to hear himself talk so prepare to sit there for a while. I had never taken physics before so I taught myself from the textbook + Internet. Work every practice problem and say a prayer; this class sucks.

Professor Kotwal was a poor lecturer and explaining concepts terribly. I would not taking this class unless you like teaching yourself the material. His handwriting is atrocious and at times impossible to decipher.

Kotwal is hard to understand during lectures because his notes are messy and difficult to read. The class is very fast-paced, so if you fall behind at any point you're doomed. Also not very helpful with questions or during office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Tests are tough--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Kotwal is excellent. He teaches physics with true passion, and answers doubts very well. The grading criteria is clear, and the class is well organized. He also throws in some cool movie references! I really enjoyed learning from him!

Dr. Kotwal is a fantastic teacher whose exuberance for the subject really shows in all of his lectures. The man is a legendary physicists but the excitement in his voice when explaining friction in an introductory physics class makes you want to cry sometimes.

Honestly a legend. Google him. This guy has done the most complex things known to man and then has the kindness to come down a billion levels and describe basic physics to struggling students. Always willing to answer your questions, even if it means starting the problem over. He works really hard to make sure you get it. Go to his office hours!

Phenomenal 141 and 142 TA. I have worked my schedule around having him as my TA. He is not only brilliant but able to explain at an understandable level, and will work with you until you get it. Truly makes these classes better, and makes the material really pique your interest!

I had Kotwal for my discussion section and he was honestly amazing. When I saw his rating was so low on here I was shocked. He runs through all the homework problems in discussion and is excellent with questions and explaining. Heavy Indian accent but definitely understandable. Physics is the hardest class I've taken but he really makes it better.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Hard to understand and hard to reach outside of class. Weird way of solving physics problems.

She is super understanding. I would definitely recommend speaking with her before you submit your work and also talk over any graded assignments you get back. Your grade really depends on 3 major assignments but she is very reasonable, especially if she sees that you put in effort.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Professor Giugni is one of the best professor's I've had at Duke. She is extremely knowledgeable, amazing at explaining concepts, and always makes her class engaging (even at 8:30am). Her class does require a fair bit of reading, but its so worth it.

Dr. Giugni is an amazing professor, especially as a first-year. The course comprised of excerpts from books and other resources, which was very manageable. There are very few grades within the course, and participation in class definitely mattered. Papers made up the majority of the course, but overall, an easy class during the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Giugni is such a caring and compassionate professor. She is really engaged with all the books which made the kinda boring discussions much more engaging. There was a lot of reading, but you can get by with Sparknotes (generally). Only 2 big papers and a few blogposts, and all the prompts were manageable. She's an icon!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: I came into the class with low expectations as I tend to dislike humanities courses, but Professor Giugni was able to really help me engage with the material. You can tell that she genuinely cares about her students and the material. Would definitely recommend!
Not an engaging class at all. Barely talked about modern-day and focused way too much on Aristotle and Plato. If you put in a little effort you'll be fine. For sure would not take this class again.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very kind professor, knowledgable on the content. Pretty easy class  a few 350 word reading posts, 1 6pg essay, and group final project. Enjoyed the material.

I absolutely loved Professor Giugni's class! She was super caring to all her students. Definitely go to her office hours because she gives a lot of insightful commentary on the readings. I also loved the selection of readings she had! A lot of in-depth and interesting analysis done during class.

She is a wonderful professor, and helped me significantly improve my writing. She is very knowledgable about what she teaches, and assigns a really interesting mix of readings. She cares a lot about participation; if you don't speak during class she might call on you to answer a question. I'm definitely glad I took this class.

Dr. Giugni is the gem of a person and English professor. She is so sweet and insightful. She gives great feedback and provides incredible guidance to students who take interest in her class. She makes time to be available outside of class as well. She was my favorite professor for first semester of college.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I love Prof. Giugni. She is by far my favorite professor in the department - shes so intelligent, passionate, caring about her students, and really helps you to learn, learn, learn. Took away so much from her class.

Astrid is a real gem. She can be really tough sometimes but she has really good intentions. She wants you to do well but she also wants you to improve as much as possible. Shes interested in hearing your ideas and is good at facilitating class discussion. She will also help if you ask for it. Shell question your ideas but just so you can explore.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Tough. Smart, but a bit unpleasant. A heck of a lot of reading, so get ready for that. overall just a boring seminar

Only two papers, but heavy reading. Readings were carefully selected and class discussion was always interesting! She is a brilliant MIT Mathematics grad who is interested in the humanities. Her analytical skills, open mind, and refusal to judge people for their opinions makes her the best professor I have met. Flunch her!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: She's awesome. If you show up, care a little and skim the readings you'll be fine- very clear expectations. The best thing is that you get graded on a weekly blog post plus a couple not-so-bad papers, so if you don't keep up with the readings it doesn't catch up with you. Spend some time on the papers, plan ahead and she'll give you great feedback.
Nice, but a bit conservative.
reviews.rating_tags: Hilarious--Beware of pop quizzes--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Inspirational as well as motivational

If you are looking for a sign, take this class! I looked forward to every lecture as they were so engaging and interesting. It is evident that Professor Jardina is very passionate about her work and the subject that she is teaching. She also cares about her students . Only graded on 2 midterms & participation.

College during a pandemic is weird. Professor Jardina made it pretty awesome, though. She is brilliant and her lectures are so interesting. She's also really passionate about research and helpful outside of class. I also like the online participation format. I had some of the best, hardest, and most valuable class discussions ever.

Prof Jardina knows how to lead a discussion without getting off track. I took this grad class an an undergrad students and she was definitely accessible and understanding. I also took this class online and she took that added difficulty in mind when constructing the course. All around a great experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Jardina is the best professor I have had at Duke. She is so smart and knowledgeable, and I learned more from this class than any of my other polisci courses. I think her lectures were really interesting, and my favorite part of the class were the really interesting discussions we had.

Such an interesting class, and Jardina is an amazing teacher! She clearly cares about what she teaches, and keeps learning engaging and collaborative through class discussion every day during class. The class was weekly discussion forum posts and two midterms, no final. I would take this class all over again if I could!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Jardina is one of my favorite professors at Duke. Her lectures are really interesting, and she makes class discussion challenging. I also really appreciate that she makes everyone feel like they can contribute, even when we don't always agree on the topics, especially when talking about race in America.

This class was one of the best I've ever taken at Duke. I looked forward to going every week, and I learned a great deal. Dr. Jardina is an outstanding professor who is a total expert in her field. We got to read some of her work for the class, and it's super interesting and important for politics today.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Great course. Actually looked forward to going every week. Jardina really knows her stuff, makes class interesting, and cares about her students.

This was one of the best classes I took at Duke. Professor Jardina is brilliant and the lectures were challenging and always interesting. Talking about race can be hard, but the class was very eye opening.

This was one of my favorite courses at Duke. The lectures were super engaging, and Jardina goes out of her way to make sure students feel like they can participate without judgment or criticism. She is also clearly passionate about what she teaches, and that makes a huge difference.

Shes a mediocre professor at best and our TA was trash. The class wasnt too bad though, one midterm, one final, 4 five page papers, and participation is what we were graded on. Prof Jardina was quite boring, she made really interesting material insufferable. The TA was worst though, he made so many mistakes, and he was awful.
Professor Jardina makes class fun and super interesting. She really knows what she's talking about, and I learned so much for this class.

Dr. Jardina really knows her stuff. As far as workload goes, if you come to class, the readings are pretty optional (but interesting!), and you'll do well on the tests, just take good notes. The response papers are a little burdensome bc of the length, but not too overwhelming, and the grading is fair.

Professor Jardina is incredibly knowledgeable, kind, engaging, and passionate about what she does. I got so much out of this class and hope to take another one with her in the future. She does really cool research so if you take her class you should ask her about it.

Jardina is very smart and definitely knows what she's talking about! Her class is relatively easy as well; we had to write weekly papers that she initially graded, but towards the end of the semester she started just giving everyone perfect scores on them. She gives you a study guide for the midterm and finals which aren't too hard.
Great and engaged professor who really is an expert in what she's teaching. Material is super interesting and makes tests super fair with knowing what to study beforehand.
She's an amazing teacher and the coursework is extremely interesting and eyeopening!
Public. Policy.

Regulation could easily be a dry topic, but Dr. Merck kept this class interesting by discussing many subtopics within the field. She gave very thorough, quick feedback on assignments and was generally generous with grades. Still, this class requires a ton of reading, writing, and class participation, so definitely don't take it for an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Prof. Merck is one of the most organized & thoughtful profs I've ever encountered. She puts A LOT in planning her lectures, providing feedback, and grading our work. She actually reads everything you send her & cares about the wellbeing of her students. She's the kind of prof you would find yourself chatting w/ on the bus. SHE'S ALWAYS DOWN TO HELP

Great teacher - Professor Merck takes the time to get to know us individually outside of class, and regularly ensures that class load is manageable. She is caring, and extremely flexible when it comes to assignments. She also gives great feedback, and encourages everyone to participate.

Prof. Merck is the best professor I ever met at Duke Kunshan. She is really caring for students and ensures each student participates in the class. The student would not feel stress out throughout the semester. I believe everyone in the class is respecting Professor Merck.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Prof. Merck exudes kindness and authenticity. She truly cares about students' wellbeing and learning experience. She delivers as much value as she possibly can to students. PUBPOL101 is heavy on discussion and writing policy memos that get progressively longer over time. The content is practical and applicable to any policy-based career.
Taught as part of the Good Life class. Engaging lecturer and very passionate. Papers assigned were very reasonable.

Coolest class ever. Lectures sometimes were boring but overall my whole outlook on life has changed because of this course. I feel like I understand myself and the world a lot better now. Easy A and you go on a field trip which was one of the highlights of my year. super super cool and interesting course. Jed is great and cares about his students

I really wanted to like Professor Atkins and this course but it fell extremely flat for me. The lectures are not interesting and get boring very fast. He really is passionate about the course and what he teaches but the structure of the class is not designed well. I hope this changes with student input
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Atkins makes it known early on that he'll always be there for his students. He was dealing with familial problems all semester and still remained communicative and open with us. He grades papers fairly and rewards you if you put the effort in on your papers. This class had 6 professors and Atkins did a great job organizing the whole class for us!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Atkins is a good professor who is genuinely excited about the course material which makes lectures enjoyable. He definitely places a larger emphasis on making sure that every student is learning the material then on working everyone to death. He is a good prof :)

Best class in the VOF cluster. He really does want you to succeed and grow. He gives amazing feedback and helps you grow as a writer. The grade is based on a midterm, final, 2 papers, and participation. Engaging lecturer and connects it to modern times and allows the discussion to flow.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Atkins is the best professor I have had during my first semester at Duke. He definitely has the best class in the visions of freedom focus. 80% of your grade in this class comes from 2 tests and 2 papers but it is not stressful because he has clear expectations. He is very passionate about what he teaches and has quite engaging lectures

Professor Atkins was great! Since our classes were on Zoom, it was a little harder to connect with him, but I think in an in-person class you would learn a lot. Clearly LOVES the subject and wants his students to learn. Be prepared to read-- but it's interesting stuff!
Dr. Atkins is a great guy; super kind, interested, and understanding. His lectures are generally pretty interesting and he does a good job of applying content to modern events.
Great professor! Love the class balance the focus between political theory and history!

Attendence is taken through occasional collection of reading questions. Lectures are boring and seem irrelevant sometimes but he can be funny. The material on essays and tests are things covered in class or in readings and there are pretty comprehensive study guides. The breakout sessions are helpful and engaging

Fantastic man and fantastic class. Take anything you can with Jed. Good amount of reading, but the topics are always interesting and relevant. Tests are a fair assessment of the readings and his lectures. This is the only lecture I look forward to attending.

Lectures are really organized with ample room for participation/discussion. Readings can be a bit tedious, especially if you don't have experience reading classical authors. HW is just reflection/discussion questions that takes 15 min. Papers aren't bad either - he even has you schedule an appoint w/ him for consultation... he wants you to do well
Really interesting lectures, fair exams, two essays for a semester. Would take his class again.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Atkins is so great. If you're in Visions of Freedom, get into his class. Classes are centered around individual readings he gives out. It's mostly interesting material, and he really dives deep into the readings, but there's definitely lessons that drag because the material's not that engaging. Go to class, he teaches exactly what he examines.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: Go to class! He literally gives your answers to everything. For midterm and final, study the study guide and you'll get an A. Papers aren't bad either, he's a nice grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures--Would take again

reviews.comment: Prof. Atkins is amazing. Class is always interesting and he is always available and willing to help you. He gives clear directions on assignments and doesn't try to trick you. You can't pass without any work, but if you put the effort in, you will get a good grade out.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Chooses very good readings (dense but highly applicable to many different topics and classes). Readings are tough but he explains them really well. Go to class because he gives you EVERYTHING you need to know for exams.
Fantastic professor and class. Great balance between learning lots of content without being too onerous for the student. Would highly recommend any course with Atkins.

An extremely thoughtful and fair professor. He cares deeply about what he is teaching and that is evident in his lectures. Reading is important in his class, but it's not a big deal to miss one every now and then. Requires students to meet with him to discuss papers- very helpful! Fair grader and very accessible to his students. Great professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: A very intelligent professor who balances lectures and discussion very well. Very knowledgeable about the material. Also, he cares a lot about his students and is very accessible.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Atkins can be regarded as a genius! His lectures are very inspiring, and they bring great insights to the reading. He's very nice as well.
Professor Atkins is a great professor. He is nice, chill, and his grading policy is fair. Classes include quite a bit of translating but the discussions make the material interesting. Great class!

Professor Atkins is wonderful. He is an absolutely brilliant individual who is very enthusiastic about the material he lectures on. I will absolutely be looking for courses that he will be teaching in future semesters, as he truly was one of my favorite professors here thus far.
Atkins keeps class interesting and is just a really great person. Worth going out of your way to take his section.

Great teacher, great guy. He can be affectionately referred to as Haus Baus the III. Unbelievably smart, balances discussion and lecture very well, and the course content is very stimulating. I highly recommend any class he teaches, particularly a Political Science/Classical Studies cross-listed course.
Cool teacher... cool class...

Still very much a work in progress as a professor.  Clearly not completely comfortable in front of a class.  We could get through so much more Latin if he didn't have this bizarre obsession with everyone translating every day.  Definitely knows his stuff, though, and has the potential to be a great professor some day.
Jed's favorite classical text is apparently Aristophanes' Lysistrata because...and I quote, "You ain't gettin' none...'ehkay?"  good teacher
Jed's favorite classical text is apparently Aristophanes' Lysistrata because...and I quote, "You ain't gettin' none...'ehkay?"  Great teacher
Best professor I have had at Duke.

Dr. Caspi is the best professor I have ever had at Duke. The course is structured incredibly well, and he makes sure to cater to the classes interests. Every week you need to submit a reading response, which never took too long, and the material was always relevant and interesting. Seriously such an amazing professor, take this class if you can!
Av is one of the best professors I've had at Duke. He is extremely passionate about what he teaches and truly wants his students to learn! He is also the nicest guy and very funny.
Av is the coolest professor ever. Class is super interesting. He's super passionate about what he teaches!

Av is one of the best professors I've ever had. He is very laid back, but cares deeply about his students and the material he is teaching. He even helped me find a psych lab on campus to get involved in research. Amazing person!

Dr. Caspi is hands down one of, if not the, best professor I've had at Duke. Cares so much about his students and is willing to work with them if they have concerns/difficulties. He's also a high key genius so take this class if you want to learn a lot and genuinely have a good time doing it.

Literally nothing to say about this class except that it was incredible. He is the most lovely man - so passionate, caring, grounded. Incredible researcher and professor - hands down my favorite prof at Duke EVER. I'll miss both him and his class dearly - I'd take it 3 more times if I could!
He's brilliant. The best class I've taken, ever.

Take this class, and you would love African dance forever. She is tough, nice, inspiring, and one of the best dancers ever. I took African dance tech 1 just for fun, but afterwards I was completely drawn to the dance styles. Ava is amazing, with one of the best personalities you can ever find. Her grading is real, and is 100% based on your effort.

If you want to exercise more while in college, take African Tech 1 with her - you will get a crazy good workout.  As for Ava, she's a trip - funny, sassy, and as previously mentioned, an amazing dancer.  She answers questions clearly and is always willing to help and clarify, even outside of class.

She's fun yet real. If you're not doing your best, she will call you out on it. But as long as you're trying and having fun, you won't have any problems. She's an amazing dancer and she takes her dancing seriously so she expects you to as well.

It's difficult to learn anything during lecture. He moves very quickly and writes with some of the worst handwriting I've ever seen. He provides lecture notes for all of his classes, but, again, they are mostly illegible. If you do the homework and read the textbook, though, the class isn't too difficult.

By far the worst professor I have ever had. Lectures consist of solely writing down theorems on a blackboard for an hour and 15 minutes and I do not learn anything. I learn more from doing the homework in the textbook. Midterms are impossible and averages are terribly low. If you have to take Math 353, do NOT take it with this professor.
Very nice guy! Would be a much better professor if his handwriting was legible. Tests are impossible 50% of the time but impossible to finish 100% of the time. Great hair.

Literally the worst class I have ever taken. You cannot understand anything he is saying or writing. He assigns homework he does not understand so it is never worth asking him questions about it. Exams are impossible and I have never finished more than half. Better to just read the textbook than listen to anything he ever says. Do not take this.

The absolute worst. Does nothing except copy verbatim the textbook onto the board, and makes that 10x more confusing and completely illegible. Tests are impossible and do not resemble homework in the slightest. After we all failed the first test we asked for representative practice tests. He refused and told us we just need to try harder.

Professor Said is quite possibly one of the worst professors I have ever had at Duke. Lectures consist of him messily copying the textbook onto the chalkboard. Often times adding more confusion to topics that should be straightforward. A tip for future students is to read along in the textbook as he will often times copy the wrong formulas.

Horrendous. Writing is illegible and accent makes nearly impossible to learn from. He just reads out of the textbook anyways and fails to bring any new insight to lecture, so not a huge loss, but absolutley horrific considering the tests are unfinisheable and impossible compared to any other problems seen in lecture or In the homework .
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Seems like a nice guy, but has a completely uncalibrated understanding of the students. Worst lecturer in the world, legit reads from the textbook, then the tests are several levels of difficulty above anything remotely mentioned in class. Aced the This is a class for engineers, not math majors, but tests are nothing but arcane proofs and oddities
Great proffessor, really appreciate his understanding!
Cults and Conspiracies has been my favorite class at Duke. Hunter's feedback was really helpful and the discussions in class were extremely interesting and thought provoking.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Took cults and conspiracies, cool topic and discussions were disorganized but they were always engaging and interesting. Grade is basically just participation and two projects. Project guidelines are insanely vague and be prepared to be graded super harshly. Overall the class was enjoyable but the grading is frustrating and overly critical
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I took cults and conspiracies, Hunter is an extremely disorganized instructor and is very frustrating to work with. He changed the scope of the final project a month before it was due, and he heavily critiqued the style and structure of my essay without providing any prompts whatsoever. I know he doesn't have experience, but don't be a guinea pig.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: What a guy.

Jeff has been the director of DUMB for ~20 years, and for good reason. He's a caring guy who is talented at organizing drills and music, and I say this as someone who never marched in high school. Go Duke and GTHC!
JEFF IS THE BEST!!! 5 STARs for this wonderful human and great band director.
Jeff is a great marching band director. He can yell at times (only when the band deserves it) but overall he is kind, funny, and passionate about his job.

Jeff is Au-some.   He's super nice and helpful and has a fabulous sense of humor and the band pretty much has a blast picking on him constantly.    I think you have to have a good sense of humor to deal with marching band kids.  He really does put a lot of work into us and is under-appreciated in general... both by us and the administration.
He's making the program a lot better and less of a joke.  I can respect that.  Definitely a worthwhile time commitment, especially w/ added basketball perks.

Marching band -- Jeff is really a great guy, and he's definitely trying to make DUMB a good marching band. He can be a little temperamental, but mostly it's only when we're goofing off. He likes to repeat things 20 times, so rehearsal can get a little tedious, but overall he's a good director. Like others said, he's super-chill during basketball.

Music 102 really helped my 'walking in a straight line' skills and definitely enhanced my standing skills as human.  At times, we were actually expected to play instruments and the course became difficult when we had to walk at the same time.  Emails are long and a take a good amount of time to read them.  If you are a woodwind, do not register.
Jeff is AU-some.
he's a really nice guy and he's trying to make DUMB better. he did really made at use once or twice (but then again...we were goofing off). highly recommend this class.

Jeff's not such a bad guy and practice is usually pretty easy.  Its only a 2hrs twice a week commitment so he tries to get alot done in that time.  Usually hes a pretty decent guy if you're not screwing up or goofing off.  He's much more chill (as is everyone) during basketball season
This guy is a slavedriver, Duke band is supposed to be fun.  NOT a fun man, but we're not letting him take over band.
Very good at engaging the class if you can take this class with her do it!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: One of my favorite classes and professors at Duke thus far. A difficult course for non-fluent speakers but easy to do well. Class consists of a few presentations and essays. Daily vocab quizzes but no exams.

August is a fantastic teacher! She's also really sweet and super understanding in terms of assignments and discussion. I enjoyed the readings she assigned and genuinely look forward to going to class because she makes it fun and thought-provoking.

Great professor to take! Chinese 101 isn't easy, especially for new speakers, but she makes it fun. It's 4 days a week and has daily HW that takes 1-2 hours, so it's a big time commitment. Plus 2 quizzes per week. Fast-paced and lots of material, but you end the semester knowing a lot! Don't talk yourself out of taking it! It's worth it, I promise.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Autry is great. I most appreciate how committed he is to meeting with students outside of class. He really wants you to understand the content of homeworks, so he is flexible on due dates to give time to fully finish assignments. I find his lectures to be a bit dense at times, but the lecture notes he posts are really helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Eric gives really timely response to every question we ask even after class (and sometimes even prepare extra videos for them). He is just wonderful.
Eric is very nice. He holds a lot of office hours and his explanations are very detailed. There are also many chances to gain some extra credits.
Great professor that works hard to make sure everyone has access to resources and information. Would recommend

Lectures are very dense, but they're interesting and generally useful. He has a tendency to go on tangents or spend a long time discussing very minor points (or repeating himself), but it didn't really detract from the class at all. (And the class is really easy lol, although that doesn't mean it isn't interesting!)
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Hes very smart and nice. Absolutely loved his class - great Professor

He is amazing. His explanation in the class is very clear and he makes sure everybody understand the topic before moving. Highly accessible outside of the class as he has office hours a trillion of times a week and is really open to any question. Sometimes I posted questions at 10 pm. online and he still responded lol.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He is the best

Great professor. A bit disorganized, but this was the first offering of Math 290, so I understand why the schedule seemed to change at times. I learned a TON of programming/applied math in this course. I highly recommend taking this class, even if you havent programmed before (like me). Far from an easy A, but not a ridiculously challenging course
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Group projects

reviews.comment: Class is very very hard for most people, but amazing curve! Go to lecture and do homework and you will get a B or above.

Super engaging lecturer! Pretty tough class structure with the two exams and weekly quizzes but manageable at the same time. Personally felt like discussions were not as connected to quizzes and exams as PHY 151 so focus on learning homeworks first. Bombed the first exam and didn't recover well from there, but reflects more on myself than Dr. Roy.

Dr. Roy is a superb lecturer and meticulously makes the class conducive to learning. The content is interesting and is definitely difficult with a learning curve. You must do homeworks, and I recommend the lecture notes when preparing for quizzes&exams. It is easy to have misunderstandings that lead to confusion down the line, so review, review.

Extraordinary and hilarious lecturer. Although lectures are not mandatory I would recommend going as they are fun to attend and he has an uncanny ability to explain complex E&M topics intuitively which helps with learning. The class is extremely difficult however. Recommend doing homework to help with quizzes and pray the curve will do the rest.

Best lecturer I have come across at Duke, even though not mandatory I would highly recommend attending. Homeworks are optional, but are very aligned with quiz content, so taking the time to complete them is worth it. Exams are difficult even with lots of studying, but practice tests are provided that can help.

AMAZING guy, great lecturer, just really fricking tough exams / quizzes. I worked my butt off for my grade and botched the final so ended up a little unhappy but totally not his fault. I would take it with him again in a heartbeat - I would honestly just study differently for the final.
Best professor I've ever had. Fantastic at explaining complex concepts and genuinely wants his students to learn.
My goat, very funny during lectures. More of a life coach really, super respected.

I'm sad I may never hear another lecture from Roy. Not only is he a lovely guy, but he has an awesome physics intuition that he does a great joy transferring to his students. He also does a great job contextualizing and conceptualizing the material. The discussions, quizzes, and tests are challenging but fair. I want him to teach all of my classes.

Literally the goat. Dr. Roy pulls up to every class with only a marker in hand, which is all that he needs to deliver the most remarkable lectures known to man. He is a true genius who is incredible at conceptualizing the world of electromagnetism while offering witty remarks on the side. Easily one of the top 5 professors at Duke.

Your ego will be bruised, but you will learn. I studied the most for this class, but averaged below 60s on tests. Midterms are very time dependent, so you might suffer despite knowing the content. Dont skip out on homework just because its not graded, and try to review Roy's lecture notes. Discussion is meh, textbook is ok, office hours are good.

Prof. Roy will be my best man. I love him more than my own father. His lectures are incredible - they make me want to pay Duke more money. If you are lucky enough to meet this man, let alone be in his class, I recommend you take a moment to realize how lucky you are. I couldn't learn E&M from anyone else. Thats all you need to know.

Roy's lectures are very interesting and easy to follow if you pay close attention. It is easy to get lost because he goes so fast but if you engage with what he's saying it will be a great lecture experience. He is hilarious and tenured, so he says what he wants. I do wish he spent more time on what exactly a Gaussian surface was and why we use it.
Prof Roy makes lectures engaging and explains concepts clearly. The class has a lot of work, but the structure helps stay on track. Unstuck AI was a lifesaver for exam prep.
Nice guy, the class is too hard. He talks about theory in lecture, but we are only ever tested on application.
Incredible clarity of thought -- truly a brilliant & charming man.  Take his class.

I am not a physics person, and I am not great at physics, but this has been my favorite class so far at Duke. Prof Roy is a great lecturer, he encourages to ask questions and clearly explains stuff. He is very funny also which makes lectures even more interesting. He is willing to meet for extra feedback after exams. Overall one of the best profs.

Roy is the best professor I've had at Duke! His lectures are mindblowing and he is so enthusiastic. He is clear, patient, friendly, and stays after class to answer questions. This class is a ton of work since theres homework, discussion, and quiz every week, but the structure helped me not fall behind. The tests are hard but fair. He's the best!

Be on top of the weekly quizzes. This class is relatively assessment-heavy. Partial credit is NOT generous, so stay consistent on midterms and exams. Dr. Roy is an amazing teacher who is dedicated to his students, but he expects and demands a lot of his students- be prepared for a tough grind in his class for a good grade.

This is the most difficult class I have ever taken. I thought 151 was okay, but I was far from prepared for 152. The amount of time necessary to do well in this class is insane if you don't have a significant amount of prior knowledge. I felt like no matter how much I studied, I always failed the weekly quizzes. Professor Roy is excellent, though.

Dr. Roy is an incredible lecturer who has a wealth of knowledge about physics and its many applications to engineering. Attendance and homework are optional but meant to prepare you for the weekly quizzes in discussion. Quizzes can sometimes be difficult but show you what to practice. If you put in the effort this class is very rewarding.

A very difficult freshman class. If you didn't take AP physics in highschool, be prepared for a rough adjustment period. Fantastic professor who lectures clearly and concisely off the dome. Exams are most of the class grade, so take them seriously and do the homework, even though its not mandatory.

Probably one of the best lecturers I have ever had. He makes them super interesting and he is funny enough to keep you entertained. He explains the concepts conceptually rather than just telling you the formulas and how to solve, which really helps you truly learn the material. It is a difficult course however.
I think he is probably the best teacher I have ever had. The lectures were very interesting and motivating although tests are kinda hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Excellent professor.

He's a funny guy and he makes physics interesting. Lectures are boring and redundant so its hard to will yourself to go, but his notes are really good and (if you have some prior knowledge) are honestly sufficient. Practice discussions for exams.

Some of the best and most intriguing lectures I've attended, bit of a tough grader but as long as you show work you'll be fine. All homework is optional but you're screwed for the weekly quizzes if you skip the hw.

This class is graded almost entirely on quizzes and labs which is frustrating but he is a very entertaining lecturer. If you haven't taken E&M in high school however it may be tough to grasp the lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's really good. Lectures are fun and helped me understand the material. The curve is ruined by those who have taken physics in high school, since Roy curves the mean to the boundary between B/B+. We had equation sheets for 152 midterms (but didn't have them for 151) and exam problems are more formulaic than 151.

Arya Roy is the the best teacher I have had in my life. I took his summer class. His lectures were more clear than I have ever seen E&M made. He also gave me great life advice and validated my way of thinking and my questions about Physics. I was never bored. I'm sad that I don't have the opportunity to take more classes with him. I'll miss him.

I had Roy for 151 & 152. This is the only time that having the same professor for a year wouldn't drive me crazy. His lectures are outstanding, I learned ALOT. He has taught me ALL THE PHYSICS I KNOW AND PROBABLY ALL I'LL EVER KNOW. The class is hard though, so WORK HARD! I wish the final weighed less but overral GREAT CLASS, GREAT PROFESSOR.

This class is hard if you don't go to lecture and don't do the homework, which is tempting because neither is required. However, if you mostly understand how to do the discussion quizzes and the homework, you'll do well on the midterms and the final since the questions are very similar. Also, Professor Roy is great during lecture.

I didn't find Roy's lecture particularly useful. I found a lot of resources online so that I could study for his class. I found it easier than 151 and in general very manageable. 10/10 would take again.
Amazing professor with great lectures. Weekly quizzes are rough but they make you learn.

My best professor of the semester. Arya Roy is THE GOAT of physics. He is a great lecturer and his tests and quizzes are nothing but reasonable. His passion is contagious, his class interesting, and the concepts highly applicable in engineering. If you make a genuine effort, you will succeed. Nothing but praise for Dr. Roy.

Roy truly is the goat! Best lectures I have ever attended at Duke. Get ready to understand physics on a whole other level. He really gives you fundamentals and teaches you to question the world around you. Weekly quizzes are annoying but aren't bad if you do the homework and discussion. Exams are definitely doable- Roy really is there to help you!
