Arya Roy is one of the best professors I have had at Duke. Take this class if you want to be taught by someone with a true passion for physics and teaching. He does not prepare for any lecture. He stands up at the board and begins, showing how every formula is derived effortlessly and relating concepts clearly. 100% take this class while at Duke.

Professor Roy is an amazing lecturer! He tries to explain physical phenomenon/derivations intuitively before teaching us how to solve problems. His notes are extremely helpful and contain everything you need to know for the assessments (you do not even have to take notes in class because everything is available on Sakai).

Literally do not go to lecture. His lectures make no sense and he teaches them terribly. He has really good notes posted online so Id just look at those before the quizzes and try to understand them. He also doensnt post complete hw solutions so I lowkey wouldn't recommend doing them and just focusing on the discussion questions/practice exams.
Arya roy grades fairly, gives good lectures, and is fun.
Best Physics professor at Duke. Incredible lectures, very knowledgeable, and fair quizzes and tests

Roy is the most entertaining lecturer I've had so far but I'm not sure how useful the lectures are for learning the content. Most of the grade is tests and weekly quizzes which makes the class challenging and work heavy. Fair warning, everything is curved to a B/B+ average, so the curve will be ruined by people who have physics background.

High school physics. If you've taken IB physics/A-level physics (which don't give AP credit), the class is a breeze (~2hr spent outside class). Arya Roy provides practice exams and the homework are very helpful for exam prep. Grading of weekly quizzes (~10x) and midterms (2x) is prompt and lenient. His lectures are excellent, go and don't sleep.

Good funny professor, lecture is optional. Discussion sections and quizzes every week, the quizzes are hard but doable. The midterms are pretty hard and the final is 40% and impossible. PLEASE DON'T TAKE THIS CLASS IF YOU HAVE CREDIT.

Arya Roy is definitely funny. He is very clearly an intelligent person but I hated the class. The answer keys are constantly messed up, he has terrible handwriting. The notes he gives are sparse and his lectures are just straight off topic tangents. The labs are easy. Your discussion teacher will likely be an idiot. The final (40%) is impossible.

The lectures can be good, but he often goes on tangents not really related to the content. Otherwise, he was pretty good and the midterms were pretty similar to the homework. If you took AP physics 1 and 2, this course will be easy. If you didn't, you will need to work hard, because those that took the same course in HS will wreck your curve.
INCREDIBLE LECTURES.
EXCELLENT.

Professor Roy is a fantastic lecturer and makes the material engaging and approachable. I would HIGHLY recommend going to his office hours as it will really solidify your understanding and make your life a whole lot easier come exam time.

Dr. Roy is a great lecturer, and explains everything really well so you have a good understanding of the content. Discussions and homework were essential to get a good grade on the quizzes, and you need to study a lot to do well on the tests. Make sure you go to class, do the homework, and don't fall behind. 152 was about as difficult as 151.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: 10/10 would take again. Roy teaches the way I wish every professor would teach - concept first, explained as intuitively as possible, on a whiteboard so you can actually follow along. He brings in tons of historical and current examples of ideas being used, and is a massively entertaining lecturer. Exams not too bad if you don't fall behind.

Dr. Roy's lectures are pretty engaging, and they aim to give you more of an intuitive understanding of the content, which I liked. The course grade is almost entirely quizzes and tests, which can be stressful, but I felt like he was always clear with what we could expect.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The lectures were great, they definitely taught you the content well. Weekly quizzes made me hate physics and your grade is determined by basically only quizzes and tests, meaning that you're never gonna catch a break (the final is worth 40% of your grade and no one knows the final grade curve). Homeworks and discussion helped a ton.

Professor Roy is always able to give a great intuitive understanding of the physical concepts at play. There is a lot of information to cover in this class but professor Roy is always able to make it interesting and applicable. Must go to lectures in order to understand the concepts, but lectures are also supplied with notes and homework solutions.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Roy is a fantastic lecturer. However, he uses tests and quizzes to differentiate people in the class, the results of which are shocking to many. He is tough, but very consistent.

The class is graded on a few things, including a final worth 40%. It was absurd, and the statistics showed that. Your grade will not correlate in any way to your actual performance, and he is perfectly willing to admit that.

He's a really cool guy and explained things well during lectures. The class was super hard though (took during fall 20). There was too much video lecture material each week, and exams were brutal. The class was easier than 151, although I could never figure out how to do well. If you're struggling with the class, definitely go and talk to him.

Arya is a great guy and incredibly knowledgeable, but this class is quite challenging. Due to the asynchronous nature of lectures this semester, he assigned upwards of 4 hours of lectures a week. This is not including the required textbook and posted notes reading, plus hw. Midterms and quizzes are challenging, and the final was very difficult.

Dr. Roy is a great lecturer, and although the weekly quizzes and midterms were challenging, they were solvable if you watched the lectures, did the homework, and attended discussions. Very knowledgeable about course materials and gives clear answers to student questions. Easy labs.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Roy is great and cares a lot about his students, but his class was by far the hardest one I've ever taken. Between labs, discussion, lecture, and homework, this class is a huge time commitment. There are weekly quizzes to be prepared for, and the midterms and final are incredibly difficult.

His class was the hardest class I have ever taken in my entire life simply because I can't understand physics. Yet, this man was the most entertaining lecturer I've ever had. He is incredibly smart & engaging & if he taught other classes I would take them. When I was withdrawing he offered to tutor me one on one but I had to withdraw. What a guy

Professor Roy is extremely charismatic, but he was probably the least understanding teacher when it came to COVID. Workload seemed to have increased since PHYS151, with lectures being well over 4hours/week. If you don't stay on top of the homework, the weekly quizzes will eat you alive. Very difficult class, but it's a rite of passage.

He responded to a global pandemic by INCREASING the weekly workload and making the WEEKLY TESTS (on top of over four hours of lecture per week) harder. Seven days before the final, he uploaded hours worth of new material. This teacher does not give breaks, does not want you to get a good grade, and doesn't care what you have to say about that.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Apparently I'm not alone. His lectures were great, but the course over the summer is not designed for making many errors. Graded by few things and the quizzes were each 10% of your grade. The exams were MUCH harder than homework or quizzes but basically much harder versions of the questions you've seen in homework or quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Amazing lectures--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Although I ever met him in person, he is one of the best professors I have ever had. His lectures explain everything, and he clearly states what topics the exams will cover -- no surprises. The only thing is that his exams are SUPER challenging. Even though they were open note, there was barely enough time to complete them, and grading was strict.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Roy is a good professor but intense. Tests/quizzes were very difficult to complete in the allotted time period. He explains problem-solving techniques thoroughly and gives practical applications in his lectures that make you feel in awe of the world around you. To do well, you just have to keep practicing until you have it all down in muscle memory

Dr. Roy is sassy, making lectures entertaining. His class is really really difficult and you need to put in a lot of work. He seems kind of unapproachable, but is always willing to answer questions. His lectures go kind of fast sometimes, so it's important to pay attention.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr Roy is an intelligent professor who has a humorous charisma during his lectures. However, class material was unorganized, grading was unreasonably harsh, and the questions often didn't match up to what was taught. If the whole class did poorly on a test, his first move would be to blame the class' study habits instead of his own teaching system.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Roy is super funny and personable, but this class was very challenging. We had quizzes every week which were usually pretty hard, and the midterms/final were definitely rough.

Dr. Roy is one of the best professors I've had. His lectures are funny and he throws in fun stories that somehow pertain to physics. I highly recommend going to his lectures not only for that but also because they really help you understand the concepts. Do as many practice problems as you can, as that's how you truly learn to work on problems.

My opinion of Dr. Roy is affected by the Covid-19 outbreak, but he really isn't very adaptable. However, he's pretty funny when he's in-person, he's clearly super knowledgeable about physics, and he's decent at articulating difficult concepts understandably. If you like lecture classes and are willing to work on your own, he's the teacher for you.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I feel like he has a cult following. He's interesting to listen to and is charismatic, but the content is difficult and he seems to be willing to let a good portion of the class fail. he can go fast at times which makes it difficult to understand. I think he means well, but the class is difficult and he is often not understanding during COVID-19.
This class went way too fast. It's hard to judge his teaching ability when he's teaching a weed out class.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Best lecturer I ever had. This guy is unbelievably funny, charismatic, and most of all really knows his stuff. Lectures are hilarious and engaging; homeworks are long but soln's are posted. Very approachable, finds ways to connect physics to real life, tells some funny ass stories. The unicorn of the math/physics dept. Will make your day.
Roy is a beast. Definitely take one of his classes if you get the chance.

This class is one of the harder ones at Duke, but I'm honestly glad Roy is the one teaching both 151 and 152. He's a very caring professor and very accessible outside of class, but the material and weekly quizzes can be tough sometimes. Make sure you read ahead and understand the material before the lecture or else it will be very confusing.

Professor Roy is the best introductory physics teacher at Duke; he teaches both mechanics and EM. While the course itself is quite difficult, Roy explains every topic in detail and is amazing at making the lectures actually interesting. Watch out for weekly quizzes though, they can be a pain if you aren't comfortable with the material.

Guy oozes charisma and makes even the most boring physics concepts interesting. Throws in personal anecdotes that are often quite amusing. Very helpful in office hours. Structure of class is a bit chaotic due to lack of consistency across TAs and the prof. Quizzes can be rough. Him and Derek are the Holy Duo.

Roy is a phenomenal professor and very passionate about the topic. He was able to make very complex physics objectives easier to understand (his lecture explanations are arguably better than the textbook). Lectures are easy to follow, and the lecture notes are very reflective of exams.

Arya Roy is a good lecturer (would recommend going if you can sit through a physics lecture) and very accessible outside of class in office hours. He is pretty disorganized and not in good contact with the TAs that do the homework and lead discussions, so prepare for some occasional confusion.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Arya Roy is simply AWESOME! Lectures are dope and really make understanding the material better. The weekly quizzes are pretty difficult . Definitely can't walk in without studying for them unless you are already a master in physics. Usually gives one hard midterm and one easier midterm. Final was very difficult. Overall, great class but not easy!!

Roy is the best lecturer I ever had. He has such a deep understanding of physics and cares a lot about his students. Go to lectures and go to office hours. He has the ability to explain physics like no other professor. Funny guy too
just god

This class was one of the hardest ones I've ever taken, mostly because I failed the first exam, but Roy was always there to help me and really tried to make sure I understood the material. He's one of the smartest people I know, but a bit unorganized. Tests are tough, as he wants you to truly understand things instead of crunching numbers. 10/10

Roys lectures are very well clear and his way of explaining things ensures conceptual understanding rather than memorizing. He usually ties in 1 or 2 interesting practical applications of the theory. Hes very engaging with students and he seems very passionate about the subject. A bit disorganized and tests are tough but manageable.

Arya Roy is an incredible lecturer. Unlike a lot of my other engineering classes at Duke, I actually feel like I learn how to do problems live in lecture. Roy cares that we understand the concepts and that we can do more than crunch numbers. Stay after class to ask questions so that he knows your face.

Only issue I take is with lack of organization in lectures. A typical lecture from him involves a lot of intuition to eventually achieve some kind of result-the problem I have is that I never know what I am supposed to take away. Have we made a definitive statement? Is this result for a specific case? If so, what assumptions have we made?

I love the way Dr. Roy structured his class.  It allows students to engage with the material in the way that's best for them while the weekly quizzes allow you to have consistent feedback about how you're understanding the material.  He was very clear about how he presented material and very patient when helping.

Roy is an absolute godsend - he makes physics so easy to understand and he makes you want to come to class and learn. You'll leave the class learning so much more than just introductory physics, absolutely worth the work and worth the effort.

Professor Roy is truly one of the best professors at Duke, even though I skipped most of the lectures as I already knew the material. He makes you understand the concepts rather than memorize equations, which makes Physics 151DL a very challenging class for those who don't have a background in physics.

A professor who makes the lectures interesting. Roy is super focused on the geometrical meanings of the proofs and problems, and he gives out a good illustration. Lectures and problems are generally not hard, and he gives out notes to help understanding. Super willing to help people.  Textbook is used, but you can survive without it.

Definitely the best teacher I've had so far at Duke.  PHENOMENAL lecturer... please show up to his classes because he's what makes the tuition worth paying.  The class is challenging with those who haven't had a lot of past physics, but it is very possible to do well if you work hard.
He's an amazing dude that connects with his students and makes sure they understand concepts rather than memorize equations. 10/10 would take again.
Arya makes his lectures entertaining and easy to follow, but he also provides notes on sakai (so you don't need to be there to do well). Highly recommend going and FLUNCHing him.

Arya has a great physics mind but leans towards teaching theory rather than practical examples, which can be frustrating for an "engineering" physics class. His homework is much harder than the test or quiz problems, but sometimes he'll throw something weird in there you've never seen before so study carefully.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Every lecture was like getting your mind blown for an hour! The homework was hard, but Arya's awesome explanations as well as overall hilarity was a great combo!
He is amazing in every way and so helpful and humble
He is an amazing lecturer who explains concepts in a very manageable and intuitive way. Very charismatic.

I took the class over a 6 week summer period and moved at a pretty fast pace. However, Dr. Roy offered a lot of support, advice, and help in and out of the classroom. He was very charismatic and almost made me enjoy the material, which helped me complete the enormous workload needed to be successful in the class.
Dr. Roy was my recitation instructor for 151 and 152. He is an absolute legend and manages to make the toughest concepts manageable.
He is a genius and very good at inspiring students.
He somehow made physics make sense to me. The class was challenging but he taught super well!
Dr Roy is the Greatest. I had him for two semesters of physics and am so thankful for his teaching.

He is THE BEST professor I've ever had, he makes everything so clear and actually makes you understand the material! If you follow the path he sets out for you, you will do well in the class. The quizzes and exams are very similar to class work, he is fair.
he is god

Professor Roy is funny, relatable, and cares about his students. He's clearly a brilliant guy but he explains concepts in ways that make it easy for students to understand. His class isn't exactly easy, but he really wants students to do well and his tests aren't all that bad. Probably the best professor I've ever had!

Arya Roy is an amazing physics professor and really tries to break down the idea that physics is just a bunch of math equations and nonsense. Professor Roy is also really fun and always tries to help students out. Although, he is the only professor I can think of who can incorporate Plato's Republic with physics...

Arya is easily the best professor I've had at Duke and debatably the best teacher I have ever had. He is a genius and makes the material so accessible to his students, and is there for you and wants you to succeed. He got me so excited about physics, and I would even take advanced classes in the future just to have him as a teacher again

Roy is the greatest teacher I have ever had in my entire life. Just 2 hours in recitation with Roy will probably teach you more than a month of lectures. He's just that good. His ability to explain and teach difficult concepts is unmatched by anyone I have ever encountered. I've had Roy for 3 semesters now and have gotten A+'s in all his classes.

This man is the reason why I understand physics. He doesn't try to be so pedantic that you cannot understand him. He is a genius and can really connect with his students. He is a stand up guy, and I am so so thankful that he is part of the Duke math department!

Best lectures I've ever had, managed to deviate from the standard teaching of the subject out of consideration for those with less background knowledge, and it worked perfectly. Condensed complex conceptual problems into simple lessons on how to generally approach problems and designed problem sets and tests to be impeccably fair.
Absolute genius. You actually look forward to attending recitations and learning about the subject matter.
The best professor ever! Knows the material and explains the concepts in the clearest way!
Truly amazing professor. Will make sure you understand all concepts perfectly.
Roy is an amazing teacher. Great sense of humor and extremely approachable. Teaches in a very clear manner. The tests he writes are very logical and reasonable.
Wonderful teacher. He has an ability to transmit knowledge. Always in a good mood, and very approachable! Great guy in general.
Want proof that God exists? Attend a Roy recitation and listen to him speak. No man can make physical concepts that clear. No man

Arya is a really good teacher. He makes even something as hard as general relativity understandable and builds up from the basics. He is able to explain the way he thinks about topics instead of just how to apply formulas. Very disorganized though.
Awesome prof!

Perfect combination of brilliance and clarity. Physics wasn't my thing coming in and he completely changed that. Incredibly approachable, cares a LOT about his students. Personally attended every recitation and stayed late every day. Expects a lot but he works just as hard as you do to help you succeed. One of the best professors I've ever had.
Arya Roy is brilliant. He is very clear and urges students to understand material conceptually. He is very funny and very approachable.
Amazing lecturer, will do whatever it takes to make sure each and every student gets the material. Extremely helpful, funny, and handsome. Wish he taught every subject!

Best math professor at Duke. Extremely nice, helpful, and easy to understand. Infinitely better than most other multivariable calc professors. Get him if at all possible. Note: multi is just really hard here in general.

Hands down one of the best professors I have ever had. Roy is very passionate about physics and is phenomenal at breaking down more complicated concepts. He also personally handed back recitation quizzes to every single student and explained exactly what they did wrong. Very interesting to talk to as well.
Best math teacher I've ever had. This guy not only gets math but also REALLY knows how to teach it.

Great teacher. Lazy at times with grading and putting things up online, but extremely lucid in explaining concepts. Wants his students to succeed and will do anything to help them succeed. Go to his lecture - it is invaluable.
This man is magic.
He's full of useful advice, like, expediency comes from practice and knowing techniques are more important than memorization. Also, just take a 1000 integrals and you'll ace this class!
My favorite professor at Duke so far. One you can talk about life with.

Roy is unbelievably brilliant yet relates to his students' confused state of mind as if he were a math103 student. He lectures using his own insights that you can't possibly find elsewhere. He is infinitely patient/sacrifices so much time to make everything make perfect sense. You'll think differently about math and your own mathematical ability.

Arya is the best math professor! He made 212 so enjoyable and really increased my interest in math. He is by far the best 212 professor at Duke and his sections always do the best. He is great at explaining concepts and is very helpful if you seek him out for office hours. He's a really cool, interesting guy, too. Take him for 212!

There is a reason his students do the best on the final (by a lot). Absolutely the best 212 teacher. He is great at explaining difficult concepts and really makes sure that everyone understands. Plus he doesn't collect homework.
Best Multivariable professor by far. Best teacher I've had at Duke so far and an engaging teacher. Always fun to attend lecture and you really will appreciate math after this.

Arya is a great professor. He enjoys the subject and is good at lecturing. I would recommend his class, and if you can't get into his section, it is worth attending his lectures anyway because they are really good.
One of the best professors I have had at Duke; he truly cares about his students and will do everything in his power to make sure they understand the material.
Roy makes everything CRYSTAL clear. Great at summarizing and giving general steps and approaches to the problems.

Dr. Roy is absolutely wonderful! His lectures are very clear and instructive. Also, he truly cares about his students and spends so much time outside of class helping people understand the concepts. He made me understand and appreciate physics even though I considered it to be one of my worst subjects! Take his class if you get the chance!

Arya Roy is an incredible professor. He is literally amazing at explaining concepts and has a vested interest in the students understanding of fundamentals. I would recommend takIng the class for sure!

I think this might've been his first time teaching Physics 5, but he was excellent. He makes the material clear, and he explains it all himself, he doesn't rely on the textbook to teach. His tests can be a little long. Not necessarily difficult, just too long to thoroughly think through problems. In any case, I would highly recommend him!

I know that he teaches both math 103 and physics 53. Both of the classes deal with difficult subject, but Dr. Roy would be willing to help you, and if you try hard enough I think you will end up with a decent grade. He also takes lots of time to write up summary of almost every lecture in front of the homework set, and they are really helpful too!

ARYA IS THE MAN! Take Math 103 with him. He motivates you to work hard and actually enjoy math and see the beauty in it, unlike most teachers, which is why his sections do the best on the final, which is what matters in terms of your grade. I was so scared to take 103 as my first math class at Duke, but I got an A! Plus, he's easy on the eyes ;)

Definitely the best professor I've ever had! Lays out concepts so clearly in lecture, goes out of his way to help his students and really prepares you for the block final--which basically determines your grade in the class. Funny guy who clearly loves what he's doing and cares about his students.

Professor Roy is the man, I took him for math 103 this semester (which is one of the hardest math classes) and scraped an A- without doing anything all semester. He is the best at explaining very complicated ideas and he prepares you far better than any other teacher for the final. Every one of his students left the final saying how easy it was

As aforementioned, Arya is the man. He made the topics as understandable as they could possibly be and actually made them all interesting! He has a part nerdy part dry sense of humor which makes the recitation all the more enjoyable. I HIGHLY recommend him for whatever class he teaches. Definitely the best hard science/math prof I've had here.

He's the best! If you do not have him as a recitation prof. switch!!! You literally don't have to read the book/go to lecture once he's explained it to you (but you should read the book for good measure). Physics is pretty hard but he made it all very understandable. He's also funny which made class fun!

Had Roy for Math 103 and Physics 62, but he's not in the Math department anymore though - only physics. Great teacher - cares a lot about his students. Enthusiastic, hilarious, AWESOME! Duke has gotten it right with this guy!
Dr. Roy is passionate about math, and compassionate to his students. He's the greatest teacher, no greatest man the department has gifted us with. Ladies... He's also pretty hot to boot!
Not too hard.  Great quality!  Take 103 with him.

Math 103 is a tough course, but Arya presents it so that everyone can understand. His midterms are tough, but they prepare you for the final. And he holds extensive review sessions before the final. Also, his sections always do the best on the final, which is the most important part of the grade in Math 103.

Duke has finally gotten it right, when it comes to hiring the right teacher. Whether to commend the university or the math department, I know not; but I can certainly say in Arya we find a professor who connects with his students and teaches with a never before seen passion.Never in a million years did I think I'd end up with an "A" in Math 103!!!

Greatest teacher I've had at Duke.  Cares about his students.  Lays out hard topics and makes sure everyone understands them.  And in the end, his section always ends up with the best grades.  Nuff said.
Quite possibly the best teacher I've ever had.

Roy is one of the best maths teacher ever. Very passionate about the subject and hence lectures with energy. He is one of the few teachers who not only know the content but also know how to teach! His exams might be harder than others but it prepares you for the final. He tries his best and generally gives two 3hrs revision sessions before final!

Arya is a genuinely kind person and a good teacher to boot. He also doesn't sugar coat thing, which I admire.  His recitations were much more clear and helpful than the actual lecture portion of the class. Take a class with him if you can!

Arya is AMAZING. He knows the material and explains it so well. He's also incredibly helpful, and will go out of his way to make sure his students get the help they need to do well. He's one of the few professors who genuinely cares about his/her students.

Arya is great! For the exam (which is by far the most important part of any math 103 student's grade), he is one of the few profs to hold review sessions.  Clear.  Very reasonable guy, and in the rare moments when he gets off-topic, says the funniest things.  It was worth taking 103 at 8:45 to have him as a teacher.

Speeds through lectures but stops frequently to make sure everyone is following along. Teaches with the goal of having the student understand. As stated earlier, sometimes goes through examples and material too quickly. Attendance not required, homework barely counts toward final grade. Study hard for tests. Just an easy guy teaching a hard class.

Aziz is one of the best professors I've had at Duke. I struggle with understanding math but his explanations are always outstanding. Also, one of his best qualities is patience. He takes the time to explain concepts to you when you're confused in the middle of lecture, in office hours, and even through email. Practice midterms/finals help so much.
Difficult Grader

221 is hard + work heavy, but Aziz enables you to succeed IF you put in the work. Multiple office hours each week explaining the tough pset problems. Gives out practice problems before tests that are almost identical to test questions (and explains them during office hours). ppl complaining clearly didn't go to OH + lecture.

Prof. Aziz is a genuinely excellent lecturer, explaining concepts clearly and at a good pace. You really feel as though you're witnessing him invent linear algebra like a 17th-century mathematician. More HW than most other sections but that means less studying necessary. Mid-difficulty exams compared to others, grades somewhat harsh but fair.

Aziz might be the goat. Great lectures and helpful office hours (gives answers). Genuinely nice and approachable person. MATH221 is a heavy class with a heavy workload (8-10hrs/wk) regardless of prof. Aziz assigns a lot of HW, but his tests are very fair and representative of what he covers/assigns. Gives extra credit on final. Highly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Guelen gives an extensive amount of homework. Our class has around two times the homework compared to other MATH221 classes. Nevertheless, the hw only accounts for 20% of the grade. The rest of the grade are composed of 3 tests, which are graded extremely harshly by him (class average for midterm 2 is ~60). Avoid his class if possible.
Worst professor you will ever have.

Incredibly ineffective teaching format. The lecture is entirely example-based and does not go over the fundamentals, meaning that you always need to self-teach everything. I used MIT OCW instead of going to the lecture due to this, and my grades improved. Discussion reviews are a waste of time, and honestly, I only went for quizzes. Disappointed.

Dr. Barbeau is great. He keeps the class consistent and makes his lectures entertaining and compelling. He sometimes moves through the material very quickly in class, making it challenging to comprehend and keep up. Overall, enjoyable class and a solid professor, just be sure to catch up on challenging subjects with the book. Do the homeworks!!!!!

Dr. Barbeau is a super funny and engaging lecturer who also posts notes early which is super helpful. Physics is an inherently difficult class and you need to conceptually understand every homework set and quiz. The curve in the end is fair, so again if you deeply understand every single problem you do, you will do fine in the class.
Doesn't do a great job explaining each topic.

Lectures are very boring and not helpful. The handwriting on the notes is very bad and very hard to read and understand. The grading policy of the course is terrible, and 1 mistake will cost you a lot of points.

I love Professor Iron Man. He's a funny guy and randomly makes his lectures interesting with his devices. Goes over problems in lecture which is very useful. Office hours aren't good because he shows the setup to problems but never the full thing. Duke physics is just hard, but with curves you can definitely do well.

The way Dr. Barbeau lectures is just not very easy to learn from. You feel like you're getting it in the moment but then you try a problem and are lost. He spends so much time on fundamental big-picture stuff that you miss how to actually do the problems. Do the homework and this class will be a breeze.

AMAZING AMAZING AMAZING. So engaging, so funny, so knowledgeable. People are being dramatic if they say anything bad about him or this course. Just do HWs to prep for quizzes, and lecture notes for tests. The final was hard but curves are very very generous in my experience. I am genuinely sad to be done with his class.

Hilarious professor, often goes off topic but that's exactly what makes his class interesting and you get more than what you asked for. I personally enjoy Professor Roy's teaching style more, but Phil is a decent professor regardless. Don't listen to what they say, the practice exams are all way easier than the actual ones.

One of the funniest professors I've had at Duke. Not only will his lectures make you laugh, but his teaching style is very intriguing and the class never seems dull. Tough midterms, quizzes, and final, but the curving was extremely generous at the end and most people end up just fine in the course. The Demos in class are also interesting!

Amazing lecturer with an insane understanding of the topics and incredible depth within the field. Makes the topics come to life through provided notes and visual demonstrations, and often spends time talking about broader applications of the subject and cool theories. The exams are tough but the curve is lenient, so stay on top of the homework.
Good lecturer.  Fair grader and clear what will be tested on.  Problem sets are time consuming but if done thoroughly, they tests will be easy.

Dr. Barbeau is very intelligent and knowledgeable about the subject. Sometimes this made it hard to understand him because he's so smart. Very helpful though, always answered questions and was willing to meet outside class. Goes off on tangents, but he makes real-world connections & it demonstrates his genuine interest. Don't skip discussion

His lectures were average: He would sometimes go off on tangents about random stuff no one cared about but for the most part covered the important points. The fault in this class is not with Barbeau but with the whole organization of the course (and of course the grading procedures)

Great guy in general. Lectures are great even though he tends to get off topic a lot, which just makes it more interesting. Should have gone to more of them. Recitation teaches a lot of concepts anyways. Really passionate and knowledgeable about the subject. Material is difficult but cares that his students do well.

I'm gonna admit that the textbook was maybe a little TOO good at explaining stuff, but Dr. Phil ain't bad either. If you learn better by listening to someone talk to you about it than reading about it, then this guy has you covered. It's not necessary to go to ALL of the lectures, but go to at least a couple; you won't be disappointed.
She is a caring professor, unorganized at times but she makes up for it with genuine passion for the subject.

Prof Baran truly cares about + supports her students, and is so passionate about what she teaches. I love her! Classes are discussion-based so important to do the readings, but they are manageable and she is super intelligent and well-versed in what she teaches. Consistently interesting classes, students encouraged to draw from personal experiences

She's a very knowledgeable academic/enthusiastic about her work. I understand she is busy, but papers were returned more than a month after the due date with minimal feedback, and then you'll have another paper due immediately after, which was a little frustrating.

Readings can be lengthy at times but they are typically explained in lectures and through group work. Grading is based on four papers throughout the semester and weekly discussion posts. Baran is a lenient grader, cares about introducing students to linguistics, and offers great feedback. A robust introduction to sociolinguistics!

It didn't really feel like she was invested into the class. She was clearly passionate about the topics, clearly very accomplished and very smart, and sometimes even funny. However, lectures felt unfocused, especially towards the end. It seems like she prioritizes her research over teaching, but that's academia I suppose.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She was an ok professor and If I'm being honest, I kind of really didn't get much out of the class. Grading is a bit weird because it depends on a midterm/final, an 8pg paper, and hw assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professory Baran is very kind and a very easy professor while still making sure her students learn. If you pay attention in class you will do very well on all of the assignments and she grades easily on the papers as well. Truly enjoyed this class and felt like I learned a lot

Her classes are very interesting. She tells many stories from his life, which makes it very pleasant to listen to them. She evaluates the works honestly. If you show that you work hard and participate in discussions, you have a good chance of an A. Be prepared for many readings (thankfully very interesting). 
I love Flunches with her.

Lectures and course were disorganized. The Professor was an incredibly specific grader and your whole grade concepts of one exam, one paper and a few HW assignments. Although she says attendance isn't mandatory she was easily agitated if you didn't show up and started giving pop attendance quizzes. 

Super frustrating and useless class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class itself was easy, and the TAs were always very available and helpful. However, the lectures themselves were badly delivered and disorganized. I didn't feel like this course was worth the spot it took in my schedule, and it made me question taking more linguistics classes.

Professor Baran is very nice and the course is not hard at all. There are only a few very easy homeworks, 2 open note exams, and a final project. The lectures can be a little boring however. Watching LangFocus on youtube will teach you about the same material too and is more entertaining in my opinion.

I loved this class! Dr. Baran is such an interesting professor, and I highly recommend this class for anyone that is even remotely interested in linguistics. It's not too much of a workload throughout the semester, just keep up with the readings and go to lecture because the homework is mostly taken from lecture. Only 3 big grades so be careful!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is disorganized, uninspiring, and overall, just not great at teaching. It seems like she doesn't put a lot of effort into the class. During the COVID pandemic, despite promising to make online classes a smooth transition, she assigned a final project late in the semester and 50% of our grade was up in the air before the P/F deadline.

Avoid this class. Readings are scattered and extremely disorganized. Concepts are sped through, and if you are not a linguistics major good luck. Huge amounts of reading, but Professor Baran is very vague/unclear what is on the test. Homework is easy, but tests cover content completely unrelated. The tests are take-home though. Boring lecture style

Professor Baran is a terrific professor! Her classes are engaging and interesting. She makes the material relevant to non-linguists. Assignments are designed to make you engage with the material rather than get stressed out. The grading is not to difficult, but you still come out having learned a lot of material. A little disorganized but relatable

Language in Immigrant America is a very interesting class, and, like other people mentioned, she likes to lecture mostly even though its a small seminar class. Final grades are completely uncertain because all of the work in the class ends up in the last week and a half. She takes weeks to respond to emails and is overall disorganized.

Re: Language in Immigrant America: Dominika is a wonderful lecturer. However, her teaching style is not ideal for a seminar. Showing up to class often felt like showing up to a lecture, even though there were only 10 people in the class. Grading (of our 3 essays) was dependent on the TA, such that meeting her outside of class was not very helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Hands down my favorite professor last semester. She's so knowledgeable and open to new ideas, and she really cares about her subject and students. She doesn't grade that harshly, and if you're more proactive she'll look at your drafts as many times as you want before you turn them in. She's super funny and she speaks 6 languages!

Dominika is really great!! She is so knowledgeable and really interesting. Her lectures are engaging and really make you think. She likes participation in class. There were a lot of readings but I never did any of them and I was fine. Although it might have helped me write my essays, it wasn't essential to my grade. Would take it again.

Dominika is a good professor. She has a very interesting background and experience regarding linguistics and teaching. Language in Society class' assignments (3 short midterm papers and 1 longer final paper) have pretty interesting topics and the grading is not too harsh. She is very helpful in office hours and leads a good in-class conversations.

I love Dominika! She is a great linguistics professor and has a really interesting background in the field. With a Polish accent, she has been to places such as Uzbekistan and Taiwan for linguistic research. Her Language and Identity class is great for people without technical linguistic backgrounds. Disorganized at times, and grades honestly.

Dominika is one of my favorite professors. The material is sometimes a little dry, but she tries to make the classes interesting and grades very easily if you put in a little effort. Attendance usually isn't mandatory but you have to keep up on the homework.

Class got a little repetitive by the end, but Dominika generally fueled good conversations. She understands that we don't always do the readings (although she expects you to at least have an idea). In general, I liked her. She is easy to talk to and helpful, if a little boring sometimes.

Pretty good professor, and decently interesting topic. Sociolinguistics does not require a particularly technical linguistics background. Honestly did not think she was the toughest grader, as long as you displayed effort. Very helpful during office hours. Only major downside was that she took forever to return papers and was pretty disorganized.

Dominika is a good professor. She cares about her students and her subject. That said, she sometimes forgets that we don't have the same linguistics background as her and is very quick to point out errors. Grading seems a bit nit-picky, but you can always go talk to her about the grade during her office hours and she'll explain it in detail.

Language and Identity is a great class and I thought she was always thought provoking. However, she is very opinionated and tends to be a somewhat harsh grader. She can seem like she's kind of mean, but she's actually really nice if you go talk to her in her office ours. Overall, I recommend her as a teacher :]

"Language and Identity" is an extremely interesting class. The pace starts out slow and a bit bland, but quickly improves. Dominika is a solid professor and is always willing to offer guidance, but is a tough grader if you don't follow guidelines. The writing projects are fairly open-ended, which makes the class enjoyable.

great prof one of the nicest people you will meet. if you want to learn korean great place ot start there is a lot of hands on experience in the course through discussion and speaking practice. not a hard course at all. prof eun is lowk peak
Although we have to memorize a lot of vocabulary, the class has a very relaxed and comfortable atmosphere, and I genuinely enjoy being in this class.
Phenomenal teacher who teaches you about both the Korean language and culture. Could not recommend this teacher more. Super understanding and kind.
Very caring professor. Class is super chill
Genuinely the best. So caring and flexible. Also dislikes written tests so they're de-emphasized in your grade. So many opportunities to boost your grade to an A.

Barohny cares so much about her students. She's the most understanding professor I've had at Duke by far. She never says no to students asking for an extension as long as they have good reason, and she balances the weight of grades so that your grade is more dependent on effort towards projects, homework and attendance than quiz or test scores

Incredibly nice and caring professor. Course includes a lot of interesting info about Korean history incorporated with language learning. There is daily homework that you must do to understand class, but it's interesting and not too hard. She is very understanding and accommodating. Cares about student's learning and wellbeing. Highly recommend!
Professor Eun is the best! She's very kind and fair and cares a lot about her students. I'd definitely recommend any class with her!
She is the nicest teacher! She is truly understanding and cares about improving your Korean. She is also patient and encouraging.
Professor Eun is literally amazing. Probably one of the nicest and flexible professors here at Duke

Professor Eun really cares about her students and it shows! She's great at explaining, always takes the time to answer questions students might have during class, and is accessible if you need help. Also, with the online format, there are no tests or quizzes.

Attendance and participation are important. The tests aren't easy but she tries to help you do well and in 203 they aren't the majority of your grade -- so work hard on the other stuff! She really cares about her students and will work with you whenever you need help.

Professor Eun is very sweet and a wonderful instructor. She cares a lot about her students, and tries to accommodate everyone. Don't miss too much class and do all homework and journals. Tests get progressively harder, but overall the class was a joy. Would take again.
Not organized. Classes feel spontaneous. Not respectful.

I really hate the way he organizes his slides... very disorganized and hard to understand. He often makes fun of students in lectures, and some of them are inappropriate, although he's just joking yet still makes people feel uncomfortable.

Salman is an awesome professor! He is very direct and treats this class as a 'start-up' environment. However, in order to actually get knowledge from this class, pay attention, participate, and engage in discussion. Salman is also one of the most caring professors I have ever met. While he can be a bit disorganized, it works out well in this class.

Salman is an unbelievable professor. He cares a lot about the material he teaches, and he really cares about getting to know his students as well. He really wants his students to learn the material. He is definitely a professor that I would love to have lunch with.

Azhar is a good guy, but this was his first time teaching cs230 and he clearly didn't put enough time and effort into class preparation. The lecture slides and homework were full of mistakes, and Azhar made simple concepts more confusing. Tests did not reflect what was learned in class/ homework. Challenging for the wrong reasons.

Do not take Azhar for 230. He complicates simple concepts. Tests and homeworks were always disorganized and they would take too long. (Not much respect for students' time). He said he wanted us struggle to help us learn. That doesn't make any sense though because teachers are supposed to teach and make learning easier for students.

Azhar is a great guy, even though his tests may be tough. You'll definitely learn a lot in the course, including random stuff that is unrelated to the course (but still very useful!). He pushes us a lot, and he understands that, so don't worry too much about your final grade. If you put in the effort, you'll get what you want while learning a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This was perhaps the most disorganized class I have taken at Duke. The homework took so much time and yet didn't help you prep for exams. He made people suffer in this class for no particular reason and I would not recommend you take this class with him.

Absolutely terrible class. I've taken CS201 with Azhar before and it wasn't awful, but cs230 was just dismal in every way. The lectures were barely comprehensible, the book was the single worst textbook i've ever seen, and the tests & hw were annoying and poorly constructed; everything was difficult for all the worst, most meaningless reasons. Sad!

Cannot recommend Azhar for CS230. The lectures, recitations, textbook, homework, and exams are over practically mutually exclusive material. The lectures are either too slow or fast, the textbook is miserable, homework takes 10-15 hours yet does not prepare you for exams. Azhar is clearly a nice prof, but this course was unbelievably frustrating.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Unhelpful and disorganized lectures. Class materials don't prepare you for exams at all. Put things that should be taught in lectures into review sessions. Avoid him if you can for CS230.

CS201 is harder than CS101 but in a rewarding way. There is a heavy workload every week but many resources (awesome TA's, Piazza) to make the course doable for those willing to work hard. I started coding in college, so I felt behind the 8 ball with my skills at first. However, Azhar is awesome, and his class prepares you for CS at Duke and beyond.

A professor who you're not afraid to confront and just talk to. He's very knowledgeable on the topics he covers, but sometimes difficult to understand, especially if you sit in the back of the lecture hall.

Dr. Azhar aims to make this class as low stress as possible. Coding is pretty easy up until close to the end of the semester. However, even when it gets tricky, the pseudocode they give is very helpful. Tests are easy and practice exams a very representative. Just a really nice guy with clear expectations.
Have taken his class and TAed for him. He truly cares for his students.

Compsci 201 is a lot more than 101 but there is lots of help to make sure that every student can succeed. A majority of the learning is accomplished by reading off of textbooks and doing assignments from Princeton. Azhar is unclear at times but he does care and has a personality. Not a bad choice to take this class.

Salman Azhar is an amazing professor. I wish students appreciate his humor a bit more, but seriously this guy is really smart and knows the material like the back of his hand. He manages expectations clearly for a 300+ Compsci 201 class, and takes time out of his schedule to help during helper hours/after class. Great professor, and learned a lot.

Professor Azhar really cares for his students. He pushes them, but not beyond their limits and is very accommodating in terms of deadlines. 201 has a lot of homework, but he provided guidance and there were a lot of Helper Hours run by the TAs, so that it was doable. I truly enjoyed the class and learned a lot! Would really recommend!

He is demanding but fair, and will always do whatever he can to help his many struggling students. His class reminds me of Bill Nye trying to explain global warming to the climate change deniers- A smart guy really trying hard not to lose his patience with the idiots around him (us students). Also, he is dreamy like a unicorn and hot like a pepper!

Professor Azhar is a great guy, really tries his best to make sure everyone understands the concepts. Workload is fairly heavy but you're given a lot of help to get through the assignments. Azhar always asks for feedback and is willing to push deadlines back. Put in some effort, and 201 is entirely doable
Dr. Azhar truly cares about his students.

Excellent professor and amazing person. Sometimes lecture can be unclear, but all you have to do is ask him to stop and clarify.  Even though the workload can be heavy, he is very accommodating. The first professor that I have had to continuously ask for feedback on the class through the semester.

He isn't a great lecturer. He doesn't explain things clearly and instead gives vague analogies without giving a real definition of what he's talking about. He doesn't double check his powerpoint notes before lecturing from them so he realizes in the middle of lecture that he wrote the wrong explanation. Lectures need to be more organized.
This guy is a beast. I absolutely love him. He makes CS so interesting and entertaining. He postpones deadlines to accommodate with students too. Really worth taking CS201 with him.

Assignments are often handed out late (sometimes even only a few days before they are due) despite his constant encouragement to "start assignments early." Instructions are unclear, readings are useless, and lecture is unimportant. Does not seem to care about his student's times or the stress that he causes them.

This class isn't hard, it's just a lot of work every week. Quizzes and project assignments were confusing but there are so many available resources (like TAs and office hours) to help you that it wasn't that bad. I liked the class and Azhar was really dedicated to working with students to make it enjoyable.
CompSci201 is not really well-developed at Duke thus disordered. And professor Azhar did not make it much better, though he can be helpful during office hours. Course itself is easy.

Prof Azhar is an incredible teacher who really does care a lot about his students. Compsci is very much something you learn largely through out-of-class work, but Azhar does everything he can to make your experience better. It's visible that he tries hard to make his lectures and class overall interesting. You'll learn a lot if you put in the work.

CS201 itself is a poorly structured and difficult class, especially for those that are not natural programmers, but Professor Azhar does everything he can to help his students and constantly improves the class. Not enough TAs out there to help people who have trouble with assignments. Don't take this class if you have other difficult courses.

The CS201 is a very work intensive class but Azhar wants you to do well. He tries to provide as many resources as possible and is very enthusiastic about teaching. Sometimes the assignments are unclear, but that's what those resources are for.

Professor Azhar really loves his students and puts in the effort to accommodate them. Sometimes lecture gets a bit repetitive but he does his best to make it amusing (and puts in a lot of effort behind the scenes for small references). Class is an assignment/APT set a week, but keep on top of it and tests should be doable.
Great lectures. High workload, but an A is very manageable if you put in the time.
lectures are inspiring, but don't help with assignments. You're left with others to muddle through the theory to get to the practice

Does a really good job of emphasizing the role of failure in success and how it applies to stuff such as computer science. Teaches a lot in a short amount of time and tries to do it in the best way possible. Lectures are dry and boring but he tries to make it as funny as he can. Really cares that his students succeed and is there if you need him.

Professor Azhar is a very helpful and inspirational professor who is always there for you.  His primary objective is to have his students succeed while learning that failure is a real thing from which we can learn and grow.

One of my favorite teachers here, he is really just such a nice guy and finds a way to add humor to his lectures. You can tell he really cares about his students and wants them to do well, he is very understanding regarding extensions and is very clear about material that will be covered on the midterms. Overall amazing guy, highly recommend.

He's SO understanding, like seriously, never met a professor so nice. There for you basically describes him. Really knows his stuff, basically tells you what's going to be on the tests. LECTURES ARE AWESOME, and that's highly unusual for a CS class. 1010  would take again! Not a hard class to get an A in, but you will have to work for it.

One of the NICEST professors I have ever had. It amazes me how understanding he is-with giving extensions, offering extra credit, and telling us EXACTLY what we need to study for the midterms. He is also always willing to help students out with concepts, assignments, etc and devotes many hours outside of lecture on Piazza and review sessions.

One of the NICEST professors I've ever had. It totally surprised me how understanding he was-providing as much help as we needed, including being very clear with what we needed to study for the midterms and giving us extensionsbeing very forgiving for missed assignments and makeup etc. Truly a kind professor that cares for his students.
Great guy, smart guy, funny guy. He recorded the lectures but you will learn more in person.
One of the best people I've ever met. He knows the content knowledge extremely well and did a great job considering it was his first semester teaching. Highly recommend for CS201 at Duke.
Azhar is the man, loves his students.

Salman is the man. His lecture notes are FANTASTIC - he literally must spend hours every single day designing them. Azhar is clear and helpful, and actually really cool. Always looking for a chance to help students out (whether it's modifying the class, extending a deadline etc). I had to work pretty damn hard for this class but got a TON out of it
The legend.
CS at Duke is generally very unorganized and Professor Azhar fits into this generalization. He is a great guy who knows his CS, but sometimes he is unclear and tries to be too funny.

Prof. Azhar is not a bad lecturer. The problem with CS201 lies more with how the course is structured rather than how he teaches it. Important, abstract concepts are glossed over quickly without telling the students how it can be implemented. CS at Duke is more of a self-learning experience anyway so this class isn't too bad.
he's so cool and so funny

LIT333 was my fav. class, changing how I perceive everything! Prof. is amazing- so engaging, inspirational, & funny. The class is structured so that we read (honestly optional, b/c he explains everything so thoroughly in lecture), discuss the broader implications of concepts within our everyday life, & write 2 papers (graded leniently). A must take

LIT314 was definitely a lot of reading, so it is not for those who dislike long texts. Many of the materials that we read were more esoteric philosophers, but Professor Bassiri explains everything so well so that it is easy to understand. His lectures were engaging and made it easy to follow along.

Very inspirational class. Give lots of readings but the lectures are really helpful. He gives not a lot of work in general, and his grading is fair and lenient. Definitely would recommend his first year seminar class.
Really great, really cool.
Honestly a wonderful teacher. I had a great time and learned a tonne. The office hours are also super helpful. Bless him
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Comes off initially as a bit dry and stern, but ultimately an extremely intelligent, engaged and accommodating professor. Discussions were extremely enlightening and informative, and the readings were quite compelling to read as well. Grades largely via class participation and a few essays that were enjoyable to write.
Great professor.

If I weren't graduating I would definitely take more classes with him! He made Derrida and Althusser feel easy and he has a hilarious dry sense of humor. Even from quarantine I looked forward to his lectures.

This professor is very patient with the students' questions and feedbacks towards his teaching. He loves to talk with students before and after class, and holds regular office hours. Be prepared since class content would be a little difficult. However, his curving is very generous.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is a dedicated professor and curves very generously.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: most caring professor at Duke. Prof Banks is willing to go over any question. Curves so generously (10 questions wrong on an exam = still an A) that everyone ends up with A or B by the end. Don't fall behind due to daily quizzes. Easy class + best prof = recommended class.
COLD CALLS
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Amazing teacher, but lectures are so difficult (grad level) & fast. Tough P-Sets and midterms during first half of semester, but levels out into group projects. Don't stress about your grade b/c he curves everyone to an A. Would only recommend if you're unsure about stats; otherwise, take STA199 b/c we learned no R in this class (& 210 requires R).

first half of course has many difficult problem sets BUT he gives answers/explains everything in office hours. lectures are interesting but sometimes loosely related to psets. very inspirational guy (look up his wikipedia) and very wholesome person + good prof to be friendly w/ in stats dept. midterms are just like psets, but he curves everything

Professor Banks is an amazing person. He is extraordinarily smart so the stuff he teaches might fly over your head but he is also caring enough to explain it to you a million times. Nevertheless, the class was very difficult so office hours are pretty much a must.

Honestly overrated. Lectures were somewhat engaging but hard to grasp. Homework started off really hard and got easier over time, while course content started easy but got very hard towards the end. The tests aren't too bad. In the second half the class, we had to give boring presentations on random topics. In the end I think he gives everyone an A

This class is so hard, even if you've taken AP Stats. Go to office hours (!!) and ask questions and you will survive. Come to class prepared bc there is a quiz at the end of every lecture. Grades take forever to come back, but everything is curved. There's a final project and 3 midterms that are noncumulative and you can bring a cheat sheet.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Banks is an interesting person with lots of anecdotes, hence his lectures are entertaining until the maths kicks in. Very difficult content for the first half of the semester, but the second half consists of chilled presentations. Go to his office hours! Outside of class, Banks is one of the nicest people at Duke, and he's always happy to help.

Genuinely one of the most caring professors you could ever have. His lectures are advanced, but he knows this and doesn't expect you to understand everything. He just wants you to and ask questions. Homework can be difficult but he always offers office hours to help with the problems and the exams are never nearly as hard as the homeworks.

Banks is an amazing professor and an incredibly interesting man. He is probably the smartest person I have ever met and taught me not only about Statistics but also just a lot about life in general. 

Course content is pretty hard at first but don't worry about your grade, Banks will help you out.

Professor Banks is the best teacher I've ever had. He is so interested in the content he teaches and cares deeply for his students which really comes through in his lectures and makes you want to learn more. Don't let the difficulty of his courses scare you away - office hours help.

Banks is an absolute legend. He is extremely nice and funny, which makes his lectures interesting. He cares about his students and makes an effort to know everyone. The class is hard and fast-paced, but you get used to it and it gets easier as you go along. You definitely learn a lot and by the end, you will have great grasp on stats concepts.

Professor Banks is super nice and hilarious during lectures. His explanations of topics can be confusing at times, but he's great with clarifying and easy to reach via both email and office hours. STA101 is a decently difficult course with a fast pace at the beginning, but as long as you put in the work, you'll do well. Would highly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Caring

reviews.comment: I really liked STAT110FS with Dr. Banks. The class started out hard. The problem sets and tests were difficult at first. However, it got better. He curved the tests fairly and had office hours for the problem sets. He clearly knows his stuff, and I enjoyed learning upper-level statistics that wouldn't typically be in an introductory class.

worst professor I've had @Duke SUPER nice, SUPER incompetent lectures make NO sense/many mistakes "not given slides much thought in 10 years" unclear grading criteria daily quizzes would offer to meet outside of class but was useless after having taken Orgo I & 2, biochem, cs250, etc, I still withdrew should be easy but was stressful for no reason

Hilarious and has a very distinct way of lecturing--you'll def learn a lot. Quizzes every class on previous lecture + difficult HW that he goes over every week during OH. Lectures/OH are recorded. The way he grades the class, all students get a B/A by the end. Clear grading criteria: curves posted on website + curves quizzes/exams v. generously.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Dr. Banks was a good professor overall! Taught us graduate level material, but tests are curved fairly. Interesting material. You'll like him better throughout the semester.

Banks is the man! Really interesting and quirky guy with no filter. Probably too smart to teach a focus class. For the first half of the semester he taught us random stuff he found interesting, then the second half we just gave presentations. HW/tests are hard so office hours are a MUST! On LDOC he said we were all getting As anyway. (For focus)

Banks is too smart to be teaching a 101 statistics class. He expects that you know things way too often in lectures, quizzes, and exams. He teaches stats in his own unique way that can be challenging if you get behind and don't truly understand a concept. Quizzes every single class and homework basically every week. You need to go to office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Though he was funny, he was assigning wayyyy too much work for a 101 class. it was intense because of a pretty hard quiz EVERY class and impossible problem sets unless you go to office hours and have him tell you what to write
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: David Banks is one of the quirkiest professors out there. He's very smart and has a distinct way of lecturing (you'll see what I mean). His tests are SO HARD but in the end, he's on your side grade-wise because he believes grades don't matter. The only complaint I have is that he's so smart that he often assumes you know more than you actually do.
He makes you work for it but at the end of the day you will learn a lot, be inspired, and do well in class
Banks is a fantastic teacher. I learnt x2 more in this class than any other I have taken at Duke and the content I learnt will serve me the rest of my life.

One of the best professors I've had at Duke. Makes every lecture entertaining, and he's extremely well-known in the stats world. Unless you've been hiding for the entire semester, it's likely Dr. Banks knows your name. It's quite a workload (a quiz each class), but he goes through each homework assignment at his office hours so HW isn't stressful.

Overall Banks is a pretty good professor. You need to stay on top of the material and actually study for the quizzes that are every class. If you don't, your grade will drop. Quizzes were more of a pain than the tests. Definitely go to office hours to get help with the homework otherwise you will lose points there too.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Prof Banks knows pretty much everything there is to know about Statistics. That being said this was by far the most work intensive class I have taken as an Econ major thus far at Duke. With a quiz literally every single class and 4 midterms make sure you are not taking this with a lot of other work heavy classes.
The man is an absolute legend. One of the smartest professors on campus for sure. Tests are pretty tough but pretty reasonable.

Best professor I've had so far at Duke. You have to go to class because of the daily quizzes but they actually help you keep up with material. Go to his office hours! He goes over a lot of the solutions to the homework problems which can otherwise seem impossible.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: D Banks is too smart to be teaching this class. He is an engaging professor and expects too much from his students, but the class is interesting and you will learn a lot. He is a generous grader is general and is not out to give poor grades.
Good.

Dr. Banks is a decent professor-- a genius and cares about his students, but can be confusing and move really fast in lectures. Does a good job of showing students how statistics is relevant to real life. Daily quizzes almost killed me, but did help make sure I knew the material. Office hours are great-- he basically does the problem set for you.

Hate myself for saying this but Prof Banks is a F'ing legend. Yeah he's probably way to smart to be teaching this class and sometimes can be hard to follow in lecture and the daily quizzes are a little ridiculous but if you want a future in stats he is hands down the best professor you could ask for. Test & HW are hard but he curves fairly.

This class had an insane workload-quizzes every lecture and ridiculous homework assignments. The curve both made and killed my grade, since students who had time to study for quizzes on a daily basis did way better. Do not take this class with other difficult classes.

No words to describe how nice and helpful he is! Quizzes everyday are annoying/stressful & the tests are hard; he posts practice versions that are very similar so if you learn those then you'll be good. HW is hard but you can find some of the answers online. An annoying amount of work. He is a fantastic person but don't recommend this class :/

Dr. Banks is great. Almost too smart and moves quickly, but very willing to help. This class is hard but not impossible. Daily quizzes and weekly problem sets can be rough but are actually really helpful for tests, which are not cumulative. If you stay on top of it, put in the work, and go to office hours, you'll be fine.
Absurdly hard class. He's very knowledgable, but he's almost too smart to be teaching this class. Had a very hard time relating the material to his students.

Banks is straightforward, very helpful, and definitely wants to make sure you aren't suffering with his class. The work load is intense but not unbearable. Expect quizzes every class all semester. Midterms are tough but Banks is very invested in making sure his students get help if they need it.

Great professor who takes great strides to make his large lecture class feel more like a small seminar.  Course material is incredibly fast-paced and difficult, but rewarding if you manage to stay on top of your work and keep up.  You do get to drop your lowest HW, Lab, midterm, and 2 quizzes, which is helpful.  No final exam.
Go to class and review each class before quiz. Expect to spend around 10 hours a week outside of class (probably double that when you have a midterm) and you should have at least an A-.

D-Banks is the man. That being said, Stat 111 is rough. It is, by a considerable margin, the most work-intensive course I have ever taken in my entire life. Quizzes every day, 4 midterm exams, and they're all very hard. I had to work very hard to get an A- in this class, and people with tougher schedules than me had it way worse.
He is the best!

Banks is absolutely brilliant and you will learn a lot in the class. The workload is extremely heavy but if you work on the past papers you will do very well. It is not as impossible as people say it is and beware of the daily quizzes.

Learned more from this class than any other class at Duke, but you definitely have to put in the effort. (Hard) quizzes are given every class, and homeworks take a long time. If you prep during homeworkquizzes, tests are straightforward and fair for the most part. He's one of the smartestmost helpful professors I've ever had, and really funny.

While this class is undoubtedly difficult and fast-paced, I can safely say that Banks is the best teacher that I've had at Duke thus far. He is incredibly passionate about the subject matter and  is open to any and all questions. Daily quizzes might be annoying but they make studying for the tests significantly easier.

Banks is brilliant and won't stop explaining something until you understand. He will call on you randomly in class if he knows your name. Four midterms but you can drop one, and although daily quizzes aren't fun they make you keep up with the material and make studying for midterms easier. Study the slides a ton!!
Focus class. Really hard if you haven't taken any stats before.  He's such a great guy and good Professor. I recommend it, even though it will challenge at times it's worth it.  He's brilliant.

111 is hard, but the concepts are very interesting. Daily quizzes suck, but they also mean that you don't have to study as much for the exams, of which there are 4. Banks will mostly read off his slides (which are very comprehensive), and sometimes go on cute little rants. Go to office hours and ASK FOR HELP because you'll need it.
Expect to have a ton of time put into this class- the 111 is a lie. Expect to hit the ground running without understanding why anything works.

Banks is way too smart to be teaching an introduction stats class. Charismatic guy that you won't find elsewhere, but difficult to connect with & lecture is him reads off the slides and sprinkling his quirky humor. Banks is clearly a genius- but that doesn't always bode well for his students who are not.

I took stats 111 with Banks. Banks was the best professor I have had at Duke so far. Not because his class is easy or he gives easy grades but because he is a great teacher. Banks is a brilliant statistician who genuinely cares about his students.

Banks was a good professor, but the way he structured this course was unreasonable at best. There were daily quizzes in class which made attendance mandatory, and these quizzes contained material from just 2 days before. This class is difficult and a gigantic time commitment. If you are an econ major, take stats through the math department.

Professor Banks is a phenomenal professor, one of the best at Duke. He is always willing to help and is the nicest guy you will ever meet. However, the class is very difficult and time consuming but overall you will learn a ton and I would highly recommend this class as the information is useful as well.

I've never cared enough to write a review for a professor I liked before, but Professor Banks is the best. He is astonishingly important in the stat world, but will always have time to personally help you. People say the class is hard, but in a "worth it" way. You will get so much out of this class and if you take it, def get to know Banks.

Banks is a good teacher. His lectures are well done and his slideshows are concise and clear. His HW is very difficult as are the tests. The curve sucks in this class. Also gives quizzes every class. Does not give out partial credit on anything. I enjoyed the class but wished the curve was friendlier.

Prof. Banks is excellent. There is no partial credit, which is irritating, but it worked out for me with the curve. Go to his office hours---he is more relaxed and explains the homework (i.e. the material) perfectly. I recommend him highly. N.B. "Introduction to Probability and Statistics," 4th ed. by Alder and Roessler supplements the course well.
Dr. Banks is a really animated guy with a TON of knowledge which makes his class really interesting. The material of the course is pretty difficult, but he's very willing to help.
