Banks is a really cool guy. He is an awesome professor and loves interesting conversations. I enjoyed his class, although some of the material was going all over our heads. Toward the end, presentations got boring, but Banks himself is pretty great. I'd take another class with him.
Brilliant. Always recommend him. The class is tough but so rewarding.

Banks is one of a kind. He knows literally everything, and he knows all of his 100+ students by name. That being said, his class is not easy.  But it's heavily curved, and as long as you put in enough effort you'll manage a decent grade.

Gets hard right before the first exam and becomes truly difficult until the second one. I learned a lot, but a lot of materials are counterintuitive, and we are just fed with formula. HOMEWORK IS IMPOSSIBLE TO SOLVE. IF YOU CAN'T GO TO HIS OFFICE HOUR, DON'T LISTEN TO THE CLASS.

One of my favorite professors/people at Duke, basically the most approachable, helpful teacher I've ever had. His class material is really hard cuz he's used to teaching grad students, but he will "take care of your grade". Just GO TO OFFICE HOURS and he'll help you with anything. Taking his class convinced me to major in Stat!

Banks is a funny, engaging, helpful prof who truly wants his students to understand and enjoy the materialâ??quite possibly the nicest professor alive. That said, he made Stat 103 the hardest it's been in a long time with DAILY quizzes and no partial credit on exams. He forces you to keep up at a  furious pace, but you get a lot out of the class.

He is a funny and interesting professor who cares a lot about the material and the students. In STA 113, his lectures, however, often did not prepare us well for the homeworks. The problems he comes up with are usually not straightforward and require a deep understanding of the material. On that note, it makes it a more thought provoking class.
Stats 113 is not supposed to be a tough class, but Professor Banks, who taught it for the first time, made it a really hard class. He gives out homework problems that the TAs don't know how to do.
Tough

He's really one of the best professors I met at Duke. Knowledgeable and passionate about teaching! He always told us grades don't matter and wanted us to learn as much as possible. But his class is really fast-paced and sometimes pretty hard!

Professor Banks is a wonderful teacher. He cares about his subject as well as his students. His classes are interesting, his homework relevant, and he answers questions clearly. If you have a problem, he is always more than understanding and ready to accomodate you.
Banks is a really caring professor who really concerned about his students. Classes are full of wisdoms related and unrelated to statistics.

Man oh man, I'm going through the class right now. It is fast paced, and there are a crap-ton of assignments.  The material is easy enough actually but boy can the grading scales suck.  Or rather, the fact that the TA graders don't give partial credit so you end up lower on the scale.  So basically, aim for as perfect as you can be.

He simply doesn't understand people who aren't as well versed in his subject as he is.  That said, I've asked for his input on homework before and he has openly admitted to not knowing how to do it "off the top of his head."

the secret to doing well in this class is the homework. go to office hours and make sure you get As on all the assignements. the book is completely useless except for reading comp questions (i.e. portacaval shunt exp.) - don't try to learn the math thru the book. banks is always willing to help, always. so nice. however, this class is difficult

Such a nice man!  Always willing to help, and keen on learning everyone's name.  Daily quizzes can get tedious, but they force you to really learn the material along the way so that you barely have to study for tests.  The weekly HWs and labs are also dull, but in the end boost your grade.  Pretty OK way to learn stat.

His lectures are really fast paced and confusing but he is always willing to give extra help outside of class. He is really aprocachable and is not the type of teacher that likes to see students fail.
Good teacher. funny. the class is semi hard but if you do the work you will be fine. also, going to the help room helps a lot

Dr. Banks is really a good teacher.  I was not looking forward to stats at all, and he made it much more pleasant than i anticipated. he is quite clear.  its hard to get an A because theres no partial credit and the TAs are on power trips.  Be more wary of the hardcore overachieving students in the class rather than the professor.

Prof Banks is one of the best professors I have had at Duke, loved stat altho I was dreading it for three years.  He is also the spitting image/mannerisms of Mr. Hall from "Clueless" and Vincenzo from "Princess Bride."

Hard class, fast pace and the HW and quizzes are ridiculous but the man does want his students to learn. Also the labs vary from very easy to decently hard and are totally useless in terms of learning material. Very funny in an "am I laughing with him or at him?" kind of way.
Reiter was the best stats teacher, but he has moved on to 103.  Of the current STAT101 profs, Banks is the best.  Not too hard, but not easy... the daily quizes get tiresome.
Not the easiest subject matter, but prof banks is always willing to answer questions and help you out.  He has a genuine interest in having his students understand the material.  Also- he is funny.

Really funny guy who tries hard but does not teach lecture information the same way book presents it so it gets confusing- also quizes after every lecture so you barely get the time to process the information..tests are quite difficult and the labs are usually useless.
No Comments

Flexible, thoughtful, knowledgeable, and wants the best out of his students. While Sandeep could most definitely work on his delivery when he teaches, he is nonetheless extremely helpful to students inside and outside the classroom. Great professor!!!

While Sandeep is a brilliant individual, his teaching abilities are lacking. His lectures are difficult to understand and have little organization. His exams don't allow students to demonstrate what they have learned. He often assigned problem sets that even his TA's cannot not solve. I would recommend taking the course with another professor.

He speaks slowly by nature, but has a very good mastery of his subject matter, especially if you pay attention in his class. Started attending his classes with very low quantitative skills, but after attending his classes and reading his notes, and following up during his office hours, my phobia for figures has disappeared.
Might be the boringest and least engaging professor I've ever had. Makes me want to drop my major just to not sit through this nonsense any longer.

Sandeep is a very kind and caring man, and he grades very fairly. However, his focus is more on his research, and may not be the best lecturer. He does care for his students a lot, and wants his students to do well. The class is much easier than the other PPS 304's I've heard of. For me the material was interesting, but it was not presented well.

Lectures are very important and Dr. Bhandawat covers dense material, but his lectures are straightforward and he's very knowledgeable. I would definitely read ahead in the textbook, especially if you don't have a strong Neuro background. Tests were difficult but fair and Dr. Bhandawat is available to help and cares about his student's success.
His explanations can be convoluted but he's a very smart guy. Give him a chance.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Such an awful class (From Neuron to Brain). The professor is so unclear with his explanations and gave no help when you came to office hours because "if you go to office hours you must not be working hard enough." Terrible textbook and very few resources online. Worst class I've taken at Duke

I think the reasons freshmen don't like 110 is that they are not ready for the pace or intensity of content delivery that will be expected at Duke. Dr Becker has high expectations, the quizzes are brutal and he demands effort. He also cares about students and makes space for learning and questions. This class changed me.

Just finishing up Organic and I am feeling a lot better about Chem 110.  At the end of last fall I was totally exhausted and despite Becker being a good lecturer, engaged and pretty accessible for a Full Professor, I thought his expectations were wildly unreasonable for gen chem.  Well, I was ready for organic and am getting an A.  Was worth it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Respected

reviews.comment: I just took the first organic exam and all the suffering in Chem 110 was worth it.  Chem 110 moves fast and requires hours of work outside class to keep up with homework and problem sets (all ungraded).  Dr. Becker is a good lecturer, provides his notes after class and introduces topics like spectroscopy and MO theory that are not in 110.

This class was rough and required a lot of time outside the lecture to stay on top of the work.  The pace was fast but the lectures were pretty good and Dr. Becker posts his notes after class.  The weekly quizzes were hard, much more so than the exams.  Overall, a pretty good experience despite the volume of work.

Chem 110 has no graded homework, fair exams, and brutal weekly quizzes.  Dr. Becker has very high standards. An A will require you to read the chapters in advance, do the optional problems and attend class where he works through many example problems on the board.  This is not an easy A.  He also is available in office hours for help.

Dr Becker is a global leader in polymer chemistry and biomaterials and his graduate class reflected that status.  While the chalkboard lectures are at times tough to keep up with, his mastery of the subject is clear and what I learned in the class significantly impacted my research.  His reputation in industry is almost unbelievable.

Becker is a solid lecturer and typically provides his notes and example problems. Tests are fair but quizzes are rough and require lots of self study in advance. Now in organic, I appreciate the connections he made with MO theory and spectroscopy. Would highly recommend this class to prepare for orgo.

No graded homework, fair exams, clear expectations and brutal quizzes.  Chem 110 was demanding but after sitting through a few organic lectures this semester, I feel prepared and miss Dr. Becker's lecturing style which was clear with lots of example problems.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Beware of pop quizzes--Respected

reviews.comment: Quizes are brutal but otherwise this course was on par with what I expected at Duke.  Dr. Becker seemed a little bored with the subject matter but I appreciated that a Distinguished Professor was teaching freshman.  Office hours were great, the lecture notes were posted and the exams were reasonable.  Overall a good experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Becker is a good lecturer and provided his notes after class.  Lots of example problems were provided on the board and he was able to answer questions from the class on the fly and in office hours.  He was good with student names even in a large class.  Quizes were difficult but exams and final were fair.  Would recommend this class.

Exams and final were long but reasonable.  Lots of example problems in class.  Attendance not required and there was no graded homework.  Office hours were awesome and alternative times were provided when requested.  Dr. Becker is a no drama, engaged lecturer.  He really cares about students and offered lots of schedule recommendations when asked.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Respected--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very bad at teaching. Super nice guy though and does actually care if you sit down and talk to him. He is incredibly smart, but not a good teacher. The quizzes each week are on niche topics that may or may not have been discussed in lecture. The midterms and final are very fair though.

Dr. Becker is a nice guy, but his lectures are hard to follow and quizzes don't always relate to lecture (though they don't heavily affect your grade). Also, quizzes covered content we'd learn the next day in lecture. Lots of self-studying, the Showme vids he posts are the best resources. However, midterms/final are fair and curve was really good.

This class was fairly difficult and I had to work really hard in order to well. Becker does grade strictly, but he also does want students to succeed. He was a wonderful professor, and I loved being in his class.

This class was a complete nightmare. Quizzes were horrible, lectures were filled with mistakes, and grade percentage range unknown until after final. However, fair midterms/final, chill guy in office hours, and good pre-med advice. Overall, lots of stress and incredibly difficult to succeed. If he's the professor, take CHEM 101 or skip to CHEM 201.

Weekly quizes are rough and require lots of self study outside of class.  Dr. Becker's lectures include lots of example problems and real world connections to medicine.  The class is hard but the exams are fair, there is no graded homework and he has had a ton of extra office hours when I have asked for help.  Would take again for sure.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Respected--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
Pros: mentions relevant research chemistry topics in energy/environment/body. no graded hw. quizzes and exams are not that bad if u study.
Cons: lectures were not helpful, couldve just read the textbook. does NOT answer questions: either says "ill go over that later" and doesnt, or gives you a weird look and asks u to answer ur own question.

Quizzes are difficult but force us to study like Dr Becker clearly states. Exams have been fair and office hours and TA time useful. Class has not been as difficult as advertised. Lecture is a little dry but notes are provided. Dr Becker somehow knew my name which surprised me despite being a large class.

Take 101 unless premed. Good researcher, meh teacher. Wants his class to be renowned as challenging. Lectures = mostly unhelpful, and weekly quizzes based on Cox's videos in the syllabus. He spends most of lecture on easy concepts, skipping over ones that matter. He often ends class early, but questions irritate him. Not the best at partial credit.

Redundant lectures, 90% of what he covers isn't on the weekly quizzes. Be ready to self-study. It's like he made his powerpoints decades ago and hasn't looked at them since. Many mistakes both in lecture and on PowerPoint. TAs/peer tutoring will save you if you have this class. Don't use this class as a refresher, take 101. One pro: exams are fair

I took Chem 110 in the Fall of 2023 and IT WAS HARD.  I wasn't thrilled with the workload at the time but when it was over, I was prepared for organic (and other tough STEM) classes at Duke.  Looking back, it was a reality check that i needed.  Dr. Becker shows up every day, is highly engaged and is able to answer almost any question on the spot.

This class moves fast and it is hard to keep up at times.  The lectures are excellent and include topics that are relevant to current events.  The first exam was ~85 avg but the weekly quizzes are tough.  Dr. Becker lectures are dense but he is always available after class and posts pdfs of the notes. No graded homework is a plus.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Not sure about some of the ratings on this site but I am having a great experience in Chem 110.  The class moves fast, the quizzes are difficult but compared to my other classes, the lectures are clear, the notes are posted after the lecture and Dr. Becker is available at office hours.   This is what I hoped for when I came to Duke.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Respected--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I took this class thinking that I was good at chemistry in high school, and therefore would be fine in honors chem. Would STRONGLY recommend sticking to chem 101. Dr. Becker's entire goal is to humble students. He is a brilliant researcher and his office hours are helpful for pre-med advice, but the class itself is awful. You'll learn more in 101.

I thought the class was difficult due to the pace of instruction and the volume of material that was covered.  His lecture notes were provided, Dr Becker was always available after class and in office hours. His advice for pre-meds is valuable.  I appreciate that a distinguished professor was teaching freshman.  Would take his class again tomorrow.

Pretty good professor. Very kind and explains relatively well in lecture. Definitely prepared me for other classes at Duke. Lectures are much easier to understand if you do the readings prior to them, and the tests are fair for the most part. However the quizzes were not fair at all and often asked about material not in the class/textbook.

At the time, Chem 110 was the most difficult course I had ever taken.  The pace was fast, the homework extensive and the exams were very difficult. In hindsight, Dr. Becker taught me how to study and the structure of the course prepared me for organic and other tough courses at Duke.  He has high expectations but is patient, accessible and kind.

Dr Becker is patient and kind. His exams are very difficult but in line with what I expected at Duke. The pace of the class is fast but I feel more prepared for organic chem than many of my classmates who took 101. He is very approachable and held additional office hours when I needed more help.
I had the worst experience with this professor because he is very redundant and very lecture heavy. He lacks sympathy and simple understanding of personal matters. Overall, very difficult.

Seems like he threw his lectures together years ago and hasn't looked at them since- disjointed & many mistakes. Can't answer questions; babbles about unrelated concepts until students relent. Many mistakes on exams but he refuses to acknowledge them. Standards & grading are very unclear. This class taught me to check this site before registration.

Isn't the worst class imaginable, but there were a good amount of issues. Dr. Becker is a good person but he isn't a good lecturer. The weekly quizzes ranged from easy to impossible difficulty. The exams were fair, but we didn't know the curve until the end (92 was a 4.0 this semester). Save yourself the trouble and take Chem 101 or 201 instead
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Quizzes can be extremely unfair. He likes to "flatten out the curve" by giving us questions in organic chemistry and high level physics (i.e. 3d particle in a box, NMR spectrum). Lectures make you more confused. He spends a lot of time talking about stuff that won't be tested (eg. kidney function) and speeds through the relevant stuff.

Do not take this class. He says nothing important in lecture, and when somebody asks a question, he either stares them down until they pretend like they understand, repeat the same thing he already said before, or talk about a high level chemistry that has no relevance to the class. He also frequently makes mistakes in lecture.
bro really marked everyone's answer to the first question on the midterm wrong because he used the wrong key/table and didn't stop to think it could've been his mistake ???

Taking Chem 110 this semester and was concerned given some of the comments on this site.  Dr. Becker is great!  Very approachable and easy to talk to. The material is presented clearly, the notes are provided after the lecture and examples are provided on the chalk board.  He also take time to answer questions on the fly during lecture.

Prof Becker has so much experience in real world applications of polymers, he can provide context in a way no other professor at Duke has been able to do. The exams are tough but fair and he was accessible all the time. Mostly PhD students but an awesome class.

Becker is a very nice guy but a hard professor. He's not approachable with test corrections and doesn't answer your questions because he's too smart for the basic chemistry level. Chem 110 is just objectively hard class...you are better off in Chem 101 where you are learning the same stuff but the tests and labs are significantly easier.

He is a kind man who made me love chemistry more through his teaching style. However, I didn't figure out how to succeed on his tears until the final -- you have to study enough to be 1000% confident and then be REALLY exacting and careful because almost no partial credit is given; you can "know" everything and then pull a C due to minor errors.

One of the worst classes I've ever taken. Becker doesn't put much effort into this class. Frequently made mistakes on tests and quizzes and partial credit was harsh on tests. The lectures are full of confusing errors and he talks too much about orgo/other stuff that isn't on tests. Ignores criticism on his teaching.

Prof. Becker's lectures could be really confusing and some material seemed to be tangential or not relevant to the test material in general, which could make it hard to sift through when reviewing. He's a very nice man, however, and very much cares about his students. If you put in the work (especially w/ studying), you'll end with a solid grade.
It really isn't that bad if you are willing to study on your own outside of class. Find online problems do work on and you'll end up with an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Becker is lowkey a homie but the class mad hard ��. Fast paced. Not a great teacher. Super boring. Hard to stay awake. Take 101 only perk of 110 is boding with kids over common struggle.

Lectures will never help you with the course because he just talks(often making mistakes) and skips most practice questions. Hard to stay awake even at 10:15. Just take 101 there is no difference in material, overall just worse course. Disorganized. Non-test work makes up half your grade so actually failing is hard, but tests average low at 77.
I took independent study with him, and he was great. He's very caring and invested in his students' success.
Easy class. Smart man. Decent teacher.

Dr. Becker held office hours during the week and on Sunday and was also available during the work weeks prior to the exams. The exams in 110 are punishing but are in line with what I would expect at Duke. Becker is not a hand holder and this class was hard but I thought the lectures were clear and the grading was fair. The research was awesome.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Yeah this class was really badly organized. I'd advise to avoid if possible.
Becker is a sweet person if you have a one on one conversation with him, but in class he just feels rude and disorganized

Tests got more difficult but it was nothing I wouldn't expect from intro chem at a top university (meaning a lot of test questions were inference questions and not formerly learned problems). However, I felt like I struggled in this class because of poor communication from Becker and not because the class itself was that hard. Just take 101 or 201.

Yes the rumors are true about Professor Becker. By far the most disorganized professor I have ever had. I had to read the textbook many times to fully comprehend the material. In addition to bailing on office hours, he spends entire 8:30 AM lectures covering material that is nonexistent on exams (TITRATIONS, BATTERIES, AND HIS COMPLEX RESEARCH).

This definitely isnt an easy A. Dont procrastinate and study for exams in advanced. Hes very accessible outside of class and willing to help. Make use of office hours and pay attention to the sample questions on the slides.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Becker was very disorganized with the course, having errors in nearly every quiz and retaining those errors in the gradebook. He gets very irritable when mistakes are pointed out, and often miscommunicates with students (contradictory information, sarcastic replies to genuine questions, questions unanswered on Sakai)

Becker is very sweet and I think he tries to crack jokes all the time, but most of them come off as uncaring. He wants us to succeed, but is not the most well equip to do so. Lectures have errors in them, nearly every quiz we took did as well. Exams are brutal with the averages being around a 77/78. But we get exempt from taking 210. Grading hazy

Just take 101. The content in 110 is 99% the same as chem101, but the tests are much more difficult. His powerpoints have mistakes that confuse the whole class. He's a nice guy, and he does try to make himself available outside of class, but there is absolutely no benefit to taking chem110.

This is the most demanding course I have ever taken and that is after taking AP chemistry in high school. The 8:30 am time is almost intolerable. I have found Dr. Becker to be available for individual appointments when I have asked and he even holds Sunday office hours for students who needs help. Very tough but fair.

Prof Becker's isn't awful at all, nor is his class anything special. He talks about how the chemistry we're learning relates to his research, and generally covers concepts well as far as gen chem goes. Zoom lectures are pretty low energy, especially 8:30, but I think exams are easier if you attend and take notes. Grading is labs, hw, quiz, exams.
Freshman - just take Chem101 or 201
He can't communicate and is terrible at organization.
Do not take. Avoid at all costs.

Annoying ASFFFFF. You can do all of the work and attend all of the classes and still get a B-. Like, actually, what is the point? The only way you would HAVE A CHANCE of getting an A is if you do 3 extra assignments. The lecture is actually a waste of time; you don't even talk about the readings. IF YOU CAN AVOID THIS PROFESSOR, DO IT!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: If you can avoid this class, please do. You would be doing yourself a huge favor. There's so much busy work for no reason, and you learn absolutely nothing from the class. The only saving grace is that every assignment is for completion. Be prepared to do pointless annotations. However, as long as you do all the work, an A is basically guaranteed.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: If you complete assignments + show up to class, you automatically get a B-. Additional projects are completed to raise your grade to an A, which is not too difficult to achieve. Lots of reading annotations -- not fun but easy to complete. Nice guy but I would recommend another Writing 120 class, b/c my English skills have not improved much.

He's a nice guy but my goodness he sets so many additional things - it doesn't make sense to have the baseline grade be a B- and have to do ' additional labors' outside of class time, nor does it make sense to decide to give the class a final paper with no knowledge on the first day of the last week of classes and make it due 5 days after.
dont ever take his class so many annotations so many unimportant readings and papers that are just not needed, very stupid grading contract. Avoid at all costs if u care abt ur time
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: So boring, take anyone else if you can

He's actually a nice person, and he cares about students and comedy, but the class is just too much. For a writing 101, we have too many readings, homework, and strenuous papers that are not interesting at all. There are so many ways he could've made the class fun, but he simply chose not to. Literally take any other writing 101 class.

Professor Hojem...where do I even begin? One of the greatest professors, top 10. Professor Hojem is one of the most hilarious people I've met. He cares for students. I would not listen to the bad comments, they were written by bad students. Hojem's class is refreshing and I learned to look at life in the Hojem lens...one of the best.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Respected

reviews.comment: I genuinely love this Professor, he's very cool and very helpful and handsome.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Hojem is extremely understanding and it is not difficult to get on his good side. Get ready for the grading contract which can be edited with a class consensus. Attendance is MANDATORY.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dont do it
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Just don't take the class.

My biggest regret since coming to Duke was enrolling in Hojem's class. His style of teaching is very disengaging and he personally adds no nuance to class discussions. He is very unclear with grading expectations and although he seems like a nice person, the class itself was terrible. Definitely would choose another Writing 101 class if I could.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: He's nice but I didn't learn a single thing in this class. The readings are long, boring, and superficial. Dr. Hojem doesn't try to add any nuance into the discussions or provide context for the readings. The essay assignments are not analytical or academic essays, he gives points out of 3, and there's a group essay project for some reason???
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: dr. hojem is my favorite professor ever
So many papers compared to other classes and a lot of homework. Easy to get an A if you follow his rigid grading, but the amount of work isn't worth it. Definitely opt for another Writing 101
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Dr. Hojem is a truly unique soul that you rarely find in the world today. His ability to work humor and joy into the mundane leaves all in his class simultaneously refreshed and cackling with each successive joke. I never thought I'd find a professor so well suited to his class and profession. I'm glad he's starting to get the respect he deserves.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: So amazing. I loved laughing with Hojem. I never stopped smiling in this class. 10/10 FIRST YEARS I RECOMMEND

Wow. Truly life-changing.This course changed my entire life's direction. Deeply inspired by Ben's wit and intellect, I started a charity to assist starving children in underdeveloped countries in his name. I do not exaggerate when I say there aren't enough words in the English language to express how transformative this experience is. 
Much love
MM

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. The amount of work is overwhelming. Lots of boring assignments and it feels like you're not learning nothing at all. The same repetitive assignments every week and you learn nothing from them.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment:
Hojem is a good person but the class he taught (Education is Life) was terrible. He tried. But terrible grading structure and boring assignments where I felt like I didn't learn enough for the number of classes we had in the semester. Unnecessary reflections after each class.

Very easy to game the class/get an A if you're at all smart.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: The workload was relentless, with assignments never-ending. The repetitive nature of the assignments and the harsh/subjective grading created a sense of frustration and ambiguity. A freshman writing class should be enjoyable/motivating, but this class only led to feelings of stress and dread. If given the chance, I would avoid taking this class.

The beginning of the class was a little rough, but once it gets underway Hojem is a great professor. Though his grading system is rigid, if you follow it directly you will get an A. I highly recommend his Rhetoric of Comedy Writing101. Super fun class, and though there are a number of papers, all of the subject matter is interesting.

To put it briefly, Hojem is not a good professor and should not pursue teaching in any form for the remainder of his career. His classes are incredibly uninspiring, and the work he assigns is both repetitive and meaningless. On top of all of that, his grading system is extremely unforgiving and doesn't warrant much room to grow.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Lectures were boring and very unengaging. Grading structure meant that messing up on 1-2 assignments meant no chance of getting an A (everything graded out of 3 points even essays). Essay prompts were really ambiguous and seemed like there was no right answer.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He is a decent guy. However, he is a tough grader(grades out of 3), and his grading is in categories so if you get too many 2's on a category but have 3s in everything else you're automatically at a B. The main issue is the work. Most of time wordcount on assignments>200. His rubrics are also never clear. SAVE YOURSELF!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: The class was extremely unengaging. His grading structure is horrible because he grades things out of 3 points and his grading is in categories. Get too many 2s in category? You have a B even though you get 3s in everything else. So many essays and at least one assignment worked on every day. Most of the time word count > 600. SAVE YOURSELF!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: So much pointless work. 200-word "Reflections" (yapping sessions) after each class. A lot of reading and confusing essay prompts, which he can't clarify, so you have to guess what you should do and see if he likes it. Do not take this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: While it is not necessarily difficult to receive an A in this class, there is A LOT of work--weekly readings, essays, reading responses, etc. I think it has been more work than my Chem class this semester. Major essay guidelines are not clear whatsoever; prompts make no sense and when asked to clarify, he cannot do so. Do not take this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: A LOT of work. Long readings and several assignments. The major assignments are confusing and honestly, I think that even he has no idea what he wants us to write. If I could go back in time, I wouldn't have taken this class.

2.5 hrs of lecture  dude was only physically in the classroom for 30 minutes. The rest? Group discussion while he's out getting a coffee break, the entire class format is basically 2 hours of him getting coffee and the gradings are done by students — peer review.
He doesn't have a clear grading criteria, and his email replies take a long time. However, he's an insightful and dedicated professor in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Inspirational--Beware of pop quizzes--So many papers

reviews.comment: Because of the current world situation, I was online off campus. It was almost impossible to reach him outside of class. Whenever I sent an email, it takes at least 2 days for a response, and a lot of the time his responses were not useful. Also, something felt off when he was teaching the women section of the course.
emm cannot access him outside the class AT ALL!
Professor Beemer kept me engaged and interested in the content of the course. He is very friendly and considerate of students' needs and his feedback on my assessments was timely and helpful.

HOW I LOVE PROFE! She is so sweet and honestly made my Spanish classes at Duke that much better! If you need to take any Spanish class and are worried about your speaking and whatnot, she is the perfect professor for you! The workload-- was just like any other Spanish class, a lot. Also be prepared to participate... even if you do not want to.

Professor Fernandez was incredibly boring and often only focused on her own experiences regarding Latino culture. The course was difficult to enjoy due to the disorganization and the overall lack of utilization of the material's full potential. She also rarely responded to emails, which made it difficult to receive clarification in the class.

AMAZING! She's so welcoming and kind, you can really tell she cares about her students and their progress throughout the language. She makes so many jokes and is accomodating. Participation is important and there's homework every night but nothing too bad

I am not a Spanish major/minor, but I have taken two of Profe's classes. She is the most loving, caring, and compassionate person. She loves her students and they love her! She creates a welcoming environment where students are accepted. She is the definition of a quality Duke Professor. Take any class you can with her!

Profe is one of the most caring people I've met at Duke and is helpful and understanding with the difficult task of language learning. She takes a genuine interest in her students as people and cares infinitely about your well-being. She tries to (and succeeds in) creating a class environment where everyone is comfortable with each other and her

I adore Profe Fernandez and recommend anyone take a class with her. She's so nice and funny and I look forward to going to class. Sometimes the homework is slightly annoying, but never hard. Wish I could take every class with her.
Profe is so amazing and one of the very best professors I have had at Duke. If you are taking Spanish, you need to take it with her!!!

Profe Bethzaida was easily one of the most inspirational professors I've ever had. She makes a genuine effort to get to know you and offers such amazing insights on life. I cannot recommend her enough.

Not much more that I can say about Bethzaida that hasn't already been said. She is a wonderful Spanish professor, and I love her passion and energy for teaching. Highly recommend taking a course with her.

I love professor Fernandez! Her humor and outgoing personality take some time to get used to, but she really makes learning and speaking spanish fun. I never enjoyed classes where participation was mandatory, but this was my favorite class of the semester. She tells you exactly what to expect on assignments and quizzes, but also allows creativity

Profe clearly cares about her students as people, and she's just a great person to be around. Definitely made the 830 worth it. The class itself has a decent amount of busy work, but that's just how languages at Duke are. She's a fairly lax grader, making the busy work not so bad. Show up, participate,and you should get an A and a great experience!

Profe is one of the most kind and caring teachers I have ever had. Despite the Zoom semester, she was enthusiastic and flexible with deadlines (& gave us a break during class). She truly wants her students to succeed and is willing to meet with you whenever to help you out. As long as you put forth a little effort and participate, you will succeed

Professor Fernandez "Profe" is an amazing instructor. She truly cares for her students and is one of the best faculty members in the entire department. She is always so bubbly and loves teaching. She genuinely cares for her students and wants to see them succeed. Take 203 with her! She makes the content easy but also helps you learn so much!

Loved Profe Fernandez!! She is funny, charismatic and cares about her students in and outside of class. The grading scheme is specific and if you come to class, expectations are clear and classtime is enjoyable. The only difficult thing is the 2 papers-the grading can be slightly confusing even if you work hard on them. Would recommend her class!!!

Bethzaida is an absolute GEM! She is the sweetest, funniest professor I could have asked for, and she makes Spanish class so fun and interesting. Participation is extremely important to her, so don't be afraid to answer questions. She is very considerate and her grading criteria is clear. I would choose her for another Spanish class in a heartbeat!

Fernandez is the best professor for Spanish 203. She is very helpful and really cares about her students. She encourages Spanish only in class, but is super helpful and understanding when you're struggling. I wish she taught 204.

A true gem. She's the most enthusiastic professor I've ever had and is super chill and understanding with deadlines and coursework. 306 is not a lot of work at all; participate in class and complete the assignments and you're set. Easily the best spanish professor at Duke and such an interesting class.

If you can do her summer course in Costa Rica, do it--hands down one of the best experiences I've had.  Her classes are engaging, she's incredibly helpful and passionate, and she cares about you on a personal level. I can't recommend her enough--one of the best professors at Duke for sure!

She's the best professor I've ever had at Duke. I had her for Spanish 203 and later did a study abroad in Costa Rica with her. Her lectures are always interesting, and they make you compelled to participate even if you're nervous about your Spanish. Just take her class!!

Prove Fernandez is an AMAZING professor whose enthusiasm for Spanish electrifies the class dynamic! She is very knowledgable about the material and everyday comes in excited to teach. Her PPTs really helped to convey the grammar rules clearly. She was well prepared, gives good feedback, and accessible outside of class.

Professor Fernandez was a great professor. The subject matter was very interesting and this is definitely one of the best Spanish classes offered at Duke. Just be aware that she doesn't know everyone's Spanish background so if you do find yourself struggling more than you expected, talk to her. She is very receptive and understanding.
Best Spanish teacher I've ever had- if you have an opportunity to take a class with her, do it.

Favorite Professor at Duke hands down. She made me discover that I could enjoy Spanish after having a poor experience in high school. I even ended up going on a special trip with her and some other students to Costa Rica to help out an orphanage. She cares so much about her job and brings a fantastic amount of excitement to class.

Her lectures are very helpful and she is a perfect professor for learning language. Her enthusiasm and encouraging nature allowed me to naturally speak out during class and improve both my speaking and listening abilities. If you have the chance, take Spanish with her!

Warm, caring, passionate teacher. Cares a lot about her students as people, and the subjects we talk about as they relate to people. Pretty light grader. Fair number of assignments, but not many difficult ones. Small reading load. One of the nicest+most fun professors around!

Prof. Fernandez was a phenomenal teacher... she is always in a good mood, loves to help, cares about her students, and makes the class fun.  Lots of work, but it's interesting stuff and Prof. Fernandez grades very fairly.  SPAN 106A very very highly recommended!
She is wonderful. Very high energy level. I'm not a big fan of Spanish, especially at Duke, but I loved Bethzaida.

Senora Fernandez Vargas is amazing. She is effervescent and enthusiastic.  She is not intimidating whatsoever which really helps you learn the language.  She gives a little bit more work than most other Spanish professors but the difference is not too significant.  Definitely take Spanish with her if you can!  You will never be bored in class!
extremely enthusiastic, great professor, you learn a lot. take her class :)
Shes is awesome! I hated spanish before her class and now I look forward to it everyday...

She gives lots of extra homework, but she is a great teacher who makes you want to learn spanish. Also, she is very animated, so if you don't know what she is saying in spanish you can usually tell from her body language. Class participation is highly encouraged!

Easily one of the best teachers at duke.  She is very energetic and the class can be a lot of fun which is great because I HATE spanish.  She usually teaches either 63 or 76.  I highly recommend that you take her class
Outstanding Professor!

Energetic, outgoing, and humourous.  Watch her in action and it's like watching some sort of vaudeville routine. Acts out her words= great for those w/ poor listening skills. Spanish 76 has a lot of superflous busy work, but Zaida provides clarity among the confusion of this poorly organized course.
Awesome class and she's really nice and easy.
Fun, energetic teacher, but lots of busy work for the class.
A really nice lady who explains the material very well and isn't too difficult.  She's definitely the one to take for 76
No Comments
No Comments
Worst Economics teacher, I've had, do not take his class
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: A very good course for those who would like to do (theorectical) research, and learn more about modeling as well as academic presentation and writing. The feedback from the instructor/ TAs are also very helpful!

Charlie is a super understanding teacher. He's very knowledgable about spatial economics and regression. The class is primarily focused on research papers so attendance isn't mandatory. In fact, you probably don't even need to go to class. However, get to know Charlie because he does determine final grades and gives great feedback.
Charles Becker is the most understanding, insightful professor I have ever had.  Definitely go to him when you are in need of academic guidance. Definitely the best adviser of all time.

Quirky professor. Did a good job dealing with a senior-heavy class lacking motivation. If you put a decent amount of effort into the assignments, you should do well. Can take away a lot from the class if you want to, but can also coast and get a good grade. Attendance isn't necessary, and since the class is very research heavy, it's not imperative.

Class: African Economic Development.  Prof. Becker is incredibly friendly, smart and helpful.  He loves economics and is easily side-tracked.  Class is interesting.  Reading lists are way too long so students are overwhelmed and don't read anything.  Grading is extremely generous.  You can learn a lot or not much depending on how motivated you are.

A truly exceptional teacher, Dr. Muller did a fantastic job of leading class discussions, assigned consistently interesting readings, and always explained himself very well when lecturing. Participation and homework completion make up half the grade, while the other half is based off of a presentation and a final project (both in groups).
The TA saved my life.

Worst professor at duke - the amount of work put in minimally correlates to success on exams because he provides such limited resources. Would strongly recommend avoiding him, and taking physics elsewhere if pre-med. But if you are taking at Duke, he may unfortunately be your best bet. He also often failed to solve his own problems in lecture.

Note about spring 2021: We were cotaught by Warren and Mueller. For the portions that Mueller taught, I felt like he really cared about his students. His lectures were straightforward and helpful, and while his exams were difficult, he was willing to meet outside of class and help us succeed. Hard class? Yes! Great dude? OMG Yes!

Dr. Mueller struggled with lecturing over Zoom, but he was so kind that you just felt bad for him. He hadn't taught since 2013 and for some weird reason was pulled in to teach intro physics in Spring 2021. He wasn't great at explaining concepts. Still, he cared about students and was willing to adjust the grading criteria to support them.

I actually think Professor Mueller likes his students and wants them to do well, but this class is really hard. The tests were nearly impossible and never about anything we discussed in lecture, and discussion helps way more than lecture does. Don't take if you're looking for an easy A-- or B.

Professor Berndt Mueller is one of the most incompetent professors I've ever had the displeasure of taking a class from. His preparedness for lectures is poor, as is his communication skills. He is truly uncaring for student needs. Try your best to avoid him.

lectures not terribly helpful, but doing homework is really all you need. it's pretty easy to get an A, just because his exams are very very similar to old practice exams. also, this semester he answered anonymous questions about the homework/concepts on piazza, which was actually really helpful.
Lectures were not helpful. Does not give clear notes. Learned most of the material from recitation/book.

Material tested on exams and quizzes have no correlations with the homework. Nonetheless, the exams were predictable based on the old exams released by Muller. Just read the book, familiarize yourself with the old exam questions (i.e. be able to do all of them) and you'll be fine. The final was unexpectedly easy relative to the midterms.
So easy. Idk, didn't go to many lectures...just read the book. The concepts are pretty straightforward. Easy to get an A.
Easy class, very good professor.

Professor Muller was amazing. If you are interested in learning about the universe or have an interest in physics without wanting to commit to the major and the math, I strongly suggest taking this class. Professor Muller is definitely one of the best professors I have had at Duke. He is very clear, helpful, approachable, and interesting.
Probably one of the better recitation teachers, was able to explain all of the material in class very clearly, and was happy to elaborate if I was confused.

I learned most of phy62 material from him; he is incredibly approachable (including holding special review hours before tests). Great for asking good questions but don't fish for answers or risk being disliked. Also has this great smile when you get something right. Recitation is the most important part of this class so you definitely want Muller!

Dr. Mueller was quite a helpful recitation instructor. His concise summaries of the material reinforced the lecture material well, and he explains the homework problems in good detail. He's also helpful at helping you distinguish which concepts are and aren't important. Recommended.
He posts past exams which are really helpful for the midterms!!
Professor Mueller is a great professor.  He's really nice and approachable during office hours.  The TAs are great, as well.  Not too bad for a physics class.

Overall, very good class.  Professor and recitation instructors receptive to students' opinions.  Tests were fair.  Lectures not mandatory, but worthwhile.  Lowest quiz, HW grades dropped.  Mueller is friendly, teaches clearly, and does fun demos.  Highly recommended prof.

Lectures are pretty amusing and helpful and the class itself isn't too tough.  Tests are manageable because you get to pick 2 out of 4 word problems to do, so you can pick the stuff you're good at.  All problems were mandatory for the final, but it wasn't hard. Pretty good for a college physics class.

Low-effort course. Lectures were basically uncredited YouTube videos screenshots passed off as his own. In class he often sounded like he'd just watched the video and repeated it verbatim. Didn't care about the students and was often in a bad mood. Two 50% MCQ exams is a lazy high-stakes grading scheme. Honestly didn't expect this from Duke at all.

Poor lecturer who made a ton of basic mistakes and has no real interest in teaching. Combine that with a massive discrepancy in difficulty between midterms and the heavily weighted final for a very poor course experience.
Horrible lecturer. Should probably just stick to research. If you are pre-med, want to learn for the mcat, and receive a grade equivalent to the work you put in, this professor is not for you.

Wiley was not the most amazing lecturer but the class was fair. I actually never looked at the textbook and studied the content straight from the lecture recordings and found the midterms to be easy and totally fair. He doesn't want you to fail and that shows. The combined final was much much harder than midterms, but he curved it very nicely.

Lecture, if you can even call it that, involved watching him muddle through textbook problems, state objectively incorrect info, and read from disorganized slides that clearly weren't his own. No theory, no depth. Exams were very conceptually easy but barely any partial credit given. Prepare to self-teach, and avoid if you value real instruction.
Far and away the worst course I have ever had the displeasure of taking in high school or at Duke. Absolutely awful professor who constantly makes mistakes and very blatantly does not care about you.

Probably the most discouraging academic experience I have had throughout my time at university. Going to lecture is pointless, and it feels odd considering he acknowledges how he is there for "research," not teaching. If that is the case, give students the resources to succeed, not some random chapters of a textbook. Dreaded every single instance.
I don't know why people won't like him. He is caring, responsive; the exams aren't too hard. I learned a lot from him – he knows his stuff if people actually listen.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Seems like a nice guy but has absolutely no idea how to teach. Thankfully, the content of the course is not difficult, but get ready to teach yourself from the textbook. Going to lecture was actually detrimental to my learning.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Nice, funny guy. Often did not seem prepared for lecture, so many did not attend. Does not have practice tests. Takes all test problems from the textbook, so emphasizes doing daily problems (which is a good idea). States that 1/3 of the class gets an A. Lectures consist mainly of doing practice problems, not the best imo. Practice is key
wiley sincerely could care less about this class and it shows. not prepared to teach at all. reads off the powerpoints. he uses canelas's slides

Wiley is super nice and accessible. He's also got a great sense of humor (particularly when he reminisces about his college days). His tests are straightforward if you do the homework, but he doesn't give much partial credit. Wiley wants his students to succeed though, and I would take another class with him.

Wiley knows his stuff well. And, he uses class period very efficiently.   For presentation, he can come up really a lot questions ( so be prepared!),  people may feel overwhelmed, but the questions are not toward person. His feedback really helps later work. The overall grading was easy, so I recommend to take his course.

Prof. Wiley was able to describe the topics in the text very clearly, and also showed us how the stuff we learned could be used in real life.  Always willing to take the time to answer questions after class or in his office, very helpful in answering questions, really knows his stuff!  Very interesting stories in class.

Wiley doesn't care about the class.  He comes off as condescending, and can't answer the most basic of questions because he doesn't bother looking over the material beforehand.  That said, the class has a decent curve in the end.  Be prepared for annoying multiple choice "conceptual" questions that are unrelated to lecture material.
While this class was not that difficult as long as you do the work, he can be harsh and may run out of patience and kindness with students.

He's a peculiar guy, but he really cares about his students. He wants to make sure you understand the real-world implications of the math he teaches and genuinely cares that you understand the material. His class is pretty easy to pass if you stay on top of all your assignments. The labs get annoying, but overall a pretty chill class.

I did so many worksheets, quizzes, big assignments, and lab reports that it felt overly tedious. The Math Help Room is KEY. Concepts are convoluted, and it gets exhausting to come to class. He gets visibly irritated when people don't answer the questions he poses in class, but the questions don't make sense. I'm glad that it was S/U when I took it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Rann is nice, but we're all scared to ask questions.Class is very hard to pass. If you have calculus experience just take Calc 111. It's MUCH less work. We had 105 assignments (3 hw sheets, 1 lab report, and 1 quiz due EACH week), compared to just 30 assignments in 111. Rann is the best math prof at Duke which I fear says a lot about our Math Dept.

Professor Rann-Bar-On is such a nice guy but I think that he genuinely makes everything up in this class. I've taken Calculus before and the way he teaches concepts that should be easy is so confusing. DO NOT TAKE IF TAKING A SECOND LEVEL CALCULUS. No tests.

The high reviews were promising but 105 is way too theory heavy & not enough actual calc. 3 worksheets/week, only math class to abuse lab sessions. Math 105 is a brutal experience. He's passive aggressive & easily angered. We are confused & instead of using the time to lecture, he takes wastes time waiting for student to answer his theoretical ?'s.
Professor Bar-On is helpful and accommodating. The workload is heavy, but the class is manageable with engagement. Using Unstuck AI and the free textbook helps a lot for study prep.

Rann-Barron often came across as unapproachable, making our class feel inadequate for not being able to answer simple questions. He had a tendency to become easily angered, which created a tense atmosphere. Despite the fairness of his grading, the workload was excessively heavy, demanding a significant amount of time and effort from students.

Probably the nicest Professor I have had at Duke. Super Super accommodating. The classes are definitely homework heavy, but midterms and finals are fair, and he is always willing to help out if you let him know you need it.

He knows his stuff. Work feels heavy at times and the turn around to get first submissions and resubmissions is tight. Whether you pass or fail depends on if you have a lenient or harsh grader. His office hours did not feel helpful to me. They were on zoom and he kinda just asks you exactly what you asked him. Use Help Room. Funny and nice guy tho.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Bar-On is super helpful and kind. Things come at you pretty fast and there is legit absurd amounts of homework but he is the most accommodating professor at this school and will go out of his way to make sure you're learning. If you are terrified of Maths but still need to take it for a major req or TReqs, take Bar-On. You won't regret it.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Rann is an amazing professor. His lectures do go by a bit fast but never hesitate to let him know when you feel like you don't understand something. He's very open with grading and he's super accessible. 10/10 professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Baron is very willing to help students in and outside of classes, and he responds to emails within the hour. There is a lot of homework, but you always get a chance to resubmit your work regardless of if you passed or failed the first time. In my opinion, the class was difficult, but this was also my first time taking a calculus class.
Great professor. Really wants you to succeed and do well. Put in work and stay on top of your assignments, they can really pile up. This class meets 5 days a week!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Really great professor, just so much work probably because it's a S/U course. It's really easy to pass though just make sure you stay on track. Labs are tedious -- do not take an 8:30 lab. Very easy to reach outside of class! Take advantage of office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: There is a lot of homework involved with this class (more so because it is online), however, the professor was easily accesible and very helpful. He works with you until you fully understand the concept. He is also a very good lecturer.

Professor Bar-On was one of my absolute favorite professors at Duke! I never thought of myself as a math person, but he really challenged me and believed in me. I took 105 with him and I made a point to take 218 when he taught it - he's a brilliant lecturer and I wish I had space in my schedule to take another one of his classes :)

Lectures are a bit confusing as he only uses a chalkboard so the process is not clear. The class is only 50 minutes so tests are fair in content, but feel rushed in time. He is accessible outside class, but gets upset when people do not participate in class.
218 lab is an amazing way to improve Python skills and understand linear algebra content more concretely. Rann was very helpful in and out of class and I'm very glad I took this lab!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Group projects

reviews.comment: The lab is newly designed and very applicative. Needs some coding skills but doesn't really matter if you don't have b/c the prof gave very clear instructions. Can learn how to apply linear algebra to data science and machine learning. Graded based on pair homework. The prof will boost up your average homework grade at the end of the semester.
Dr. Baron is a fantastic teacher. He does a great job of explaining the underlying principles of the topics.

Creative labs that are fun and informative. Adding this lab section to linear algebra was a great decision. I feel more confident in my ability to use linear in my programming and to see its applications.
Professor Baron is GREAT! This lab was my favorite class. Really really relevant to life and helps with the regular class too. HIGHLY recommend.

Great lecturer and effective teaching style--very approachable! He does a great job of explaining material so that you get a deep understanding of linear algebra. Not an easy class, but if you do the homework and ask for help, you can definitely do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: In my opinion, Rann is an amazing lecturer (one of the best I've had so far), who makes even tough concepts in Linear Algebra manageable. He always answers students' questions in class patiently and thoroughly, and he is very available outside of class. While his tests are a bit tough, the homework questions prepare you well. Highly recommend!

I highly recommend this class for anyone interested in pursuing a data-related career. This class didn't fulfill any requirements for me, but I'm glad I took it. Rann's presentation of the material balances intuition and rigor well. The lab is a great way to view the lecture material in a practical context and develop data analysis skills.

Dr Rann puts in a good amount of effort in his class preparation. Accessible, considerate and ever-ready to help students outdefinitely take Math 218 with him! (P/S: Definitely check out his lab too!)
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: The class was really hard, but hes a good professor and he curves the tests fairly. Hes helpful and willing to work with you.

I'd really recommend taking this course, especially alongside 218 lecture as it really help reinforce the concept learned in that class. It's definitely a good bit of work for a 0.5 credit class, but the skills you learn are really applicable and the course is definitely one of the most useful ones I've taken in my time here.

At Duke, it's a well-known mantra among students to try to avoid as many math classes as possible due to their sheer difficulty. Rann's class was by no means easy, but his lectures and the way he approaches the material really made linear both quite manageable and honestly enjoyable. Take the class with him if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Clearly puts a lot of work into the class, and everyone respects him. Accessible, too. Honestly is the amount of work of a full class, but I think most (if not every) kid got an A by the end of year bump. I'd take it the course if you're on the edge, at least because it also acts as a study hall of sorts to review what you learn in lecture.

He's put a lot of work into creating this lab course, and it's phenomenal. Math 218 is meant to be application based for cs/econ, and his lab course truly is (the actual courses much less so). It's more work than you would expect for a half-credit course but it's worth every bit. He gives very fair feedback and is genuinely an amazing teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Group projects

reviews.comment: Rann really cares about his students and takes the time to make sure everyone is up to speed before moving onto the next topic. He will come to class early to write explanations for the day's lab on the chalkboard and explains clearly how concepts from the main class (Math 218) can be written into algorithms and applied in the real world.

Professor Baron is very accessible via email and during office hours and goes out of his way to make sure all students are accommodated for. He's very knowledgeable on the topic (linear alg is by no means an easy topic, but he summarizes concepts well) and always leaves time for student questions during and after lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Great professor who makes concepts understandable and is extremely accessible outside of class. Lectures move a bit fast but textbook is a good supplement.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Rann is an amazing linear teacher - couldn't recommend more. If you really don't understand something, go and speak to him (he's always happy to help).

I liked the class. He's a personable guy. He teaches for you to understand concepts more than just solving problems. Use the help room and study groups as well to more fully understand concepts and you'll do well in his class. You don't have to do textbook problems to pass. Make sure to do the handouts he gives in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Class is not easy but Professor Bar-On is not only a great lecturer, but more importantly, a genuinely awesome human being. I should have come to office hour more often!!

Professor Bar-On is easily one of the most caring professors at Duke. He really wants his students to succeed and is very accessible outside of class. The material is difficult, but he will do everything in his power to help you do your best. Take a class with him. It's so inspirational and special to have a professor who cares so much about you!!!

Rann is an amazing professor, the complete anti-stereotype to the typical Duke math professor. This class is obviously difficult, but Rann will make every effort to help you excell and was one of the most accessible teachers Ive had at Duke. Hes just a genuinely amazing guy! PS Take his labs!! You wont find anything like them again at Duke.

Duke should be so happy to have Rann. When you see someone with such passion for a subject you can't help but reciprocate. This has been my favorite class, and I really hope that I will have the privilege to take another math class with Rann before I graduate. The class is obviously difficult, but Rann made it a wonderful experience.
Really great guy in general. Material is tough, but he'll help you through it if you put in the effort.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Caring

reviews.comment: He cares a lot about every student's success and is super reasonable if you talk to him. Really good lecturer and he takes as much time as he needs to answer clarifying questions.

Rann is a great math professor with a deep understanding of the material. Lectures are critical to understanding the material and Rann is always available and eager to help students. One of the most thoughtful and helpful teachers at Duke. Tests were reasonable, as well. This class isnt easy but if you reach out Rann will help you.

Professor Bar-on is fantastic  I wish hed teach other courses so Id have the chance to be his student again. His lectures are well-structured, the labs he designed are super fun (I really found great joy in them), and he is truly a cool and kind person. Helped me feel more confident in and appreciate Math! Not enough words but loved LA this sem!

Rann was one of my favorite professors at Duke so far. He truly cares about all of his students and wants to see us succeed. Math 218 is definitely not an easy class, but I think Rann did a great job with the course.

Rann is one of the most genuinely caring professors on this campus. He puts in a lot of effort to make himself accessible to students outside of class. Probably one of the sweetest and most intelligent people I've met in my life.

Professor Bar-on cares so much about his students. I thought this class was really difficult and math at Duke always will be but he made it a lot better by being funny, making mistakes himself and being an overall incredibly caring teacher

Simply a wonderful human being/genius. Can't think of any other lecturer that has cared so much about his students. Always takes feedback into account, and lectures are very clear. Very accessible outside of class if you have any questions. He also designed an optional lab component to this linear course that I would strongly recommend taking.
Best/toughest professor I've had
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Rann is not only a math genius but also a friendly guy and a solid teacher. Midterms were hard-duh. Final was not as hard-thank the Lord. Most annoying thing about this class were written lab reports: his grading is very abstract. There's no rubric or clear criteria. He either loves or hates the report, which results in low lab grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Looks kinda like white Jesus, and he is a true math genius. If you have to take calc, take it with Rann!
Great Prof, really cares about his students and is there when you need him. Even when he had a baby on the way, he still made sure his students had what they needed to succeed!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests are tough--Would take again

reviews.comment: Hes a tough grader but a really great guy. I was terrible at math and he was understandable. This class was a prerequisite but he knows the information, hes prepared and teaches calc pretty clearly
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Rann is a great teacher. His class structure will not only help prepare you for this class, but other classes you may take as well. Usually accessible outside of class, and there are many chances to prove you know the material. The class is difficult, but if you stay engaged and on top of the coursework, it will make your experience much better.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Don't be deterred by how difficult this site says that Rann is, that is much more representative of how challenging Math at Duke is rather than him as a professor. If you are taking a math at Duke and have the opportunity to take a class with Rann I urge you to do so. He is a great professor and a genuine guy who will help you do well in this class
Difficult tests but good lectures!
Math 112 is hard in itself, by far the best teacher to learn from/better prepare yourself for future classes or exams.

Rann is awesome. There is no subject I like less than math, but calc ended up being my favorite class this semester. He is awesome and has a great sense of humor. The content itself is hard but manageable. Sometimes it is frustrating because Rann makes you understand the math on a fundamental and conceptual level but it helps a lot in the end.
Great professor (who happens to be a genius). Tests were hard but the curve was generous (16 problem final, had ZERO idea for 5 of them)
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Bar-On was very accessible and incredibly willing to help any student understand what they may be missing. His sometime terse demeanor at first can be a little off putting but he truly wants the best for his students and is truly very friendly. Don't be afraid to go to his office hours or ask for extra help!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Rann is a great professor who genuinely cares about each of his students. That being said, the class is not easy and attending lecture & lab is essential to the understanding of the material. It also requires a lot of work outside of class, but office hours and help room are always helpful.
Rann is super laid back and is a great professor who goes out of his way to make sure you really understand what is going on which is why it's really important for you to be at every lecture and lab.

Rann is a character but he has your best interests in mind. The mans a math genius but can also simplify complex topics, unlike the grad teachers. The tests are tough and there are quizzes but you really learn calculus. you can ask questions in class to understand the material and if you need more help, his office hours and help room are good.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Class was definitely challenging but Rann is a great professor who truly cares about his students! All math at duke is hard, so this is a hard class (105, 106, & 112). However, he really makes sure that you understand the concepts you are learning and the reasoning behind them.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: This class was not insanely hard, but he is a ridiculously hard grader.  Very little partial credit, and labs were graded somewhat unfairly--very hard to get above a C on a lab, and graded by specific criteria that you are not aware of.  Homework is never mandatory though, so that was really nice and the workload didn't seem too bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Math 106 is a very hard class, but Rann is a great teacher and really cares for his students.
Rann's great. Take calc with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: As expected from class and teacher, significant tougher if you miss class, and you get a lot more out of it if you participate.

Rann is a great professor and person! His tests are kinda hard,  but that's cause he wants you to understand and think, rather than just reproduce the material. If you are to take 105/106 take it with him cause he's basically its creator. He also wears funny shirts.
Great teacher! I learned so much this semester and he is really understanding.
Rann's class was very tough and he goes through the material very quickly in class. He is available for extra help outside of class and will work with you as long as you show determination.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: Rann is a great teacher, but Math 105L is a difficult class. Be ready to go to several of his office hours and the Math help room.  But really... any math class at Duke is hard:)
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Rann is very meticulous in his grading, but he is also that way in class which helps you get used to the amount of specificity he wants. He is easy to understand and I love talking to him about anything! He knows Duke math is hard and will do basically everything he can to help you succeed.  He really values and puts in effort to know his students.
Rann is challenging but a great professor and person!
He is super awesome. So glad to have him.

After taking math 105 and 106  with Rann, I can definitively say he was a great professor who really helped me understand the Calc 1 material. That being said, he could be overbearing at times in lectures, and the midterms and final count more than they should, given the plethora of other work in the class. If you take 105/106, do it with Rann!

If you want an A then do the homework, even though it's optional. Rann looks like a cross between Gandalf and Dumbledore, but is funnier than both. Go to math help room if you need help, seriously. Do the practice tests. Participating in class makes it go by quicker.

Rann is one of the best professors that I've had at Duke. The materials can be difficult for some, but he taught them in a way that made them really easy to understand. He's super helpful when you need help and the tests are fair.

106 with Rann was one of my hardest classes this semester. Rann is an excellent and brilliant professor and is willing to help out and make time for his students. His tests are very difficult compared to the class material though, so be sure to prepare well and spend plenty of time doing practice.  You'll definitely have to work hard for your grade

It was definitely one of the hardest classes I've taken. I'll be in 106L next semester. Rann is really cool and awesome for sure, but that doesn't change how terrible the tests are. The average on tests are extremely low.   Expect AT LEAST 3-4 hours outside of class for every hour in class if you want to do well.

Professor Bar-On is totally awesome! He looks like Gandalf and has a great sense of humor. He's interested in the subject and teaches extremely clearly, giving equal attention to both practice problems in class and explaining how all the problems work.

Professor Bar-On is an expert when it comes to Math, which means he gets frustrated at times if you don't understand something, but don't take it to the heart. He is willing to meet outside of class for any additional help and will go out of his way if needed. Homework and reviewing notes are key. He genuinely cares about students. Not an easy A

Professor Baron is a great guy, and teaches very well.
