If you attend every class (which he doesn't factor into your grade, but obviously puts you in a much better position to succeed), you shouldn't ever be too confused about the basic material. Tests aren't too bad, however be sure you try in labs. Those actually end up mattering quite a bit.

Professor Bar-on is very knowledgeable of the course work and a good lecturer as well. He was always able to help me understand a topic better when I reached out to him outside of class. The class is deceptively challenging for an intro-level math, and his tests are tough, but I would definitely recommend having Rann as a professor for 105L!

I worked really hard in that class, but my grade definitely doesn't reflect that. I believe I learned a lot of math and grew, but I feel like I could've done better with another professor. He grades harder than he needs to, and the test questions can totally ruin you.  I wanted to drop the class earlier, but I thought hard work would help. It didnt

I'm not gonna lie, this class is going to challenge you (I'm not really a "math person" myself). However, Rann is an amazing teacher and I'm pretty sure he's the most intelligent person I've ever met(prob a genius tbh).He's tough at times but that's because he's seriously passionate about what he teaches and he really wants his students to succeed.

Rann is an excellent professor. His explanations are very clear and if you ask for help it's there. However, be warned - he's a tough grader, and he's very intense. He often gets frustrated with students when they ask for homework help, so if that happens to you don't take it personally, it only means that he cares.

I was nervous taking this class as I'm not a big fan of math but Rann is extremely clear in his explanations and he's very helpful whenever you need clarifications. He made the topics really easy to understand. If you need to take this class for your major, take it with him
Great teaching style that is super easy to comprehend, most importantly he understands what college is like and helps you adapt.  I really enjoyed the class because of Rann
He can be a bit rude when you get questions wrong in class which can be frustrating and discouraging.

Rann is an amazing lecturer and person. He is willing to help you if you need it and is very patient in his teaching style. He is by far the best math teacher I have had. The only complaint I have is the "out-of-the-boxness" of the test questions. Very good teacher though and funny.

Having never taken a Calculus course before attending Duke I was very glad to have Rann to guide me through a difficult course. He makes the lectures entertaining and the amount you'll learn is staggering. Rann may seem tough at first but that's because he truly cares about the performance of his students. One of my favorite classes at Duke so far.

Rann makes calculus as bearable as possible.  He gives clear expectations of grading and work.  The class is tough, but if you complete the assigned homework, go to help room, and attend his office hours, you will do well.  He's always willing to help you if you ask and he explains things really well.  If you have calc, take his class!!

Rann knows what he is doing.  He has been spearheading  105 and 106 for a while and is really great during lectures.  He moves quickly, but offers extra office hours for this reason. He wants you to do well, but it is nearly impossible to make an A.

Rann's an intense guy but you get accustomed to his teaching style and come to appreciate it. His class is well structured and organized. Lessons move quickly so ask questions. Very beneficial class- hard but beneficial.

Rann is the best professor I've had at Duke.  If you have the choice, take his class. That being said, be ready to work. You have to go to class because the key to succeeding is understanding the concepts, not getting the correct answer.  He's a great guy and truly wants to help you succeed in any way he can.  Also, smartest guy you'll ever meet.

I had a bad 105 experience so I took 106 two semesters later. I can say that I walked in not remembering anything but I was able to pass the class. Rann is super helpful and he is willing to answer your questions. If you are willing to put yourself out there you will understand. He can be sassy if you get an answer wrong but he wants you to think.
Great teacher, go to his office hours for more help because the lectures aren't very long. He his really helpful in his office hours and will help you through any math problems you are having.

He is passionate about math and teaching. Thus if you show passion, then he responds well to that. Ways to show passion: do the HW, go to class, show up for office hours. If you're lost, he's always there to help you sort things out. I would also highly recommend going to the Ben Cooke tutorials as you tend to cover the harder topics there.

Rann is willing to help clarify any points that are unclear. He isn't the kind of teacher that is going to give you answers but instead works with you until you understand it for yourself. He pushes his students to comprehend the material and is very supportive of each student. He is the teacher that is a must-have.
It is a very hard class, but he is a good teacher

Rann's classes are really good. He's method for teaching is clear and structured. You do have to practice, do homework and prepare for tests. His midterms are a little harder than other teachers', but it is totally worth it. He might get frustrated with you sometimes, but nothing major. I would undoubtedly recommend him.

You really have to show up to class and stay on top of the homework. As long as you don't get behind its not too hard to do well.  Tests are tough but they are curved so just do better than most.  Rann is really a great guy and super willing to help. He loves math, incredibly smart. If you don't like him, its probably bc you need to study more.
Rann was a great teacher, however, the tests were very hard and he is a tough grader. All Duke math courses will be like that so it is not a bad reflection on his teaching.

Rann  is incredible. His emphasis on conceptual understanding and teaching methods gave me a true appreciation for math, and I can't begin to articulate how much I learned. Rann is not an easy professor, but will push you to reach your full potential. He is extremely approachable and really wants to see every student succeed.

Rann is a really cool guy who's always fun to talk to. That being said, Duke calculus is just plain hard, and he makes it a harder. He's a very hard grader on top of his tests being very difficult. His lectures for this class were difficult to keep up with and he got frustrated often.

Rann is a great professor, however, I found his test to be extremely difficult. He is a hard grader as well and will strip your lab reports apart with comments and deductions (which in some regards is not necessarily bad). He is a cool guy overall.

Rann Bar-On is the man. He always has chocolate chip cookies before his test. He is intimidating at first because of how brilliant he is, but after some time (about 1-2 weeks), you get used to his remarks and his, at times, scary tone! If you do what is asked and all the optional homework problems, which take about 2 hours a week, you'll get an A-
Rann Barron is a homie, hes a great teacher.
This is my second semester with Rann as my math teacher and if I had to take another Math class, and he taught it, I would be his student again. That is all have to say.

Calc in really tough at Duke, no matter what the level. Do all of the HW and go over the labs even after you have finished them. The class was very interesting and Rann is always willing to meet up if you have any questions. Overall, a tough course with a great professor.
Professor Baron a a really good professor, the course is very demanding but professor is always accessible to meet with student if they need help. He is very supportive and helpful.
Rann brings great energy and motivation to class, something wich I still don't understand given that it's Math.
Rann is a great professor! The class isn't easy, but it's totally worth it! Class is not mandatory, but try to attend as much as possible because it gets very confusing very fast.

He is an excellent lecturer. He strives to make sure each student understands the topic.  It was a privilege to him. Actually, it was because of a visit to his class while I was pfrosh that I chose to come to Duke. You will enjoy him. Just take advantage of all the resources he makes available to you and you will do well.
Very clear and easy to understand explanation. Appropriately paced, and, he pays attention t all students. I would HIGHLY recommend.
Learned a lot! Grading was a bit hard but extra work can pay off.
Bar-on's a brilliant, extremely helpful, friendly, nice and caring professor. He's sometimes a little repetitive and slow, and often picky with grading, but the class is definitely well worth taking.

Rann is a professor I won't forget after graduating. He was the most helpful, caring and friendly teacher I have ever had. He genuinely cares about his students understanding the material and is always available for extra help. If you plan to take math at Duke, make a huge effort to get Rann! I promise you will not find another teacher like him!
Rann always makes time to meet with students outside of class.
Rann is really brilliant and is very helpful one on one. His lectures may sometimes be a little complicated but hes always willing to help out if you have any questions

Rann Bar-On was a very good teacher. He has an intense personality that can be intimidating at first, but once I got to know him, I realized I could ask him anything, and that he really wants all of his students to do well on the tests and in the class. He was very understanding and tried his best to meet with students outside of class.
Rann is great! He is personable, clear and very helpful! A great teacher to have!!
Might seem intimidating at first when you see him but he is a really great professor once you get to know him.

The class is very hard and requires a lot of work to do well. However, you learn A LOT, even when you think you aren't. I walked into the final with a C minus and walked out with a B minus in the class. Couldn't have done it without the difficulty and effort Rann demanded of us.
Rann is energetic and dedicated. I would recommend him over taking this class with a grad student. Exams are challenging but studying hard is rewarded.

Rann is by far the best math professor I've had. He is very helpful and makes a lot of time answer questions or explain concepts. His tests can be a little hard, but they definitely prepare you well for the final. He is also very funny, I really enjoyed being in his class for 2 semesters.

Rann is absolutely fantastic. Passionate and energetic in his teaching, and cares a lot about making sure his students understand the material. Extremely helpful and accessible; always happy to answer questions. The class isn't necessarily easy, and the exams can be tricky, but it is definitely worth your while to take it with Rann.

Rann is a brilliant professor and a great guy. His class is difficult, but if you are willing to work he is always there to help. Keep up with your lecture notes they can be very useful for exam preparation.

Rann is very helpful and his lectures are easy to follow. The workload isn't too heavy (no hw due), but expect to do it anyway. The tests are difficult but the practice tests he gave us were great practice. Very easygoing and relatable. I recommend this class to anyone who wants a stronger grasp of basic calculus and is willing to put in the work
Amazing professor! Very helpful, willing to spend time with you to make sure you understand. His midterms are hard but you will definitely be well prepared for the final!

Hard class, harder exams. In class he goes through material way too quickly, but Rann is very interested in every one of his students to fare well in his class, so he is always interested in helping you and will go out of his way to do so. However, he expects the same amount of effort from your part. In the end, you will learn a lot.
I really enjoyed being in Rann's class and plan to take him again next semester. I learned a lot and really feel like he was consistently pushing me to be my best.
Rann is a great professor! He challenges you to think through problems and he makes himself very available if you need more help. I highly recommend him.

He is amaazing!I had him for 24L also. He is a specific grader so don't expect slack. People say his class is tough, but they forget it is college calculus. Go to his office hours because he loves it and you will too. He genuinely wants all his students to succeed.

Rann was an interesting teacher. He would sometimes get frustrated when you did not understand a concept, making it difficult and often embarrassing to ask questions in class. But we was approachable before/after class. His tests weren't that hard. But you definitely need to pay attention in class and to the worksheets!
Rann is a great guy who is willing to help if you're having any trouble. The class is not easy, but if you keep up with the handouts the course is managable.

Rann is a great teacher. His tests were not as difficult as I expected going into the class, but his clarity with the material surprised me. Participation in class is encouraged and he will not move on unless he knows that you understand the material. Great teacher overall. He really helped me understand the difficult concepts.

Rann was very helpful.  Make sure you are clear when you ask questions, though.  Take advantage of office hours and outside help from him; he really wants to help each student.  The tests and quizzes are tough.

Rann is honestly one of the nicest professors you will ever have. He truly cares about each of his students and wants them to do well. However, as others before me have mentioned his tests are hard because they are unlike any of the homework problems in terms of difficulty. Overall he is enthusiastic and a great guy. Participate in class, it helps!

Rann is a great teacher. He is really helpful  and will not move on unless you understand the material. As the others who have reviewed him have said, his tests can be pretty brutal at times, but they make you prepared for the final and a better math student. You may get frustrated with him at times, but his enthusiasm makes the course worth taking

Rann is probably the best math lecturer I've had; he's really clear, enthusiastic in class, and knows his stuff. He is reasonable and approachable outside of class. His only con is that he writes really hard tests. Although you will probably be better prepared for the final, your grade going into it might be low.

Rann is a great professor. He is very hard, his tests are difficult and homework quiz so depressing. However, if you go to class and study everyday in the end the class is extremely rewarding. He is always willing to help and his notes are very useful. If you have to take math 25, take it with him!

Rann is an extremely difficult teacher. Tests are very hard/demoralizing. Worked extremely hard in both his 25L and 26L classes and still got poor grades. Would avoid taking any math with Rann unless you enjoy hating life.

Rann is the man. While the tests are pretty hard, the worksheets Rann uses to teach class everyday are much better than what the other teachers at this level offer, I know this from studying with friends who had different professors. The class is not overly easy but with the right amount of effort (not even that much) it is easy to do well

Very helpful teacher who is glad to help you outside of class. He really wants the students to understand the topic. Tests are pretty difficult though. Need to put in a lot of time to make a good grade.
Great Notes! Should attend class regularly.

Rann is a great guy, really helpful and energetic in class, and great at explaining this.  The class itself is very demanding, and he knows how to write a difficult test, but it was a good experience.  If you need to take 32 I would recommend him.

Test are hard, but Professor Bar-On cares clearly is passionate about the topic and cares a lot about his students.  He's super laid back; also very direct.  Cuts the crap and gets straight to teaching.  Nice guy.  Young too - somewhere in early thirties probably.

really good. very clear. liked him a lot. may be hard, but its better to have a hard teacher that you can learn a lot from than a crappy teacher where you learn nothing and are confused all the time (aka my 31L experience).

Rann has very difficult tests and curves the class average to a C+. However, he is a great teacher who helps his students understand the process of solving an equation rather than just memorizing it. Rann is my favorite professor from Freshman because he has a good heart and he genuinely cares about his students.

Rann is a very cool person and a great teacher. He wants his students to do well and will take the time to help students. He gives you notes which is really nice and are great for studying. One thing is that his tests are super hard, although I found that they prepared me for the pretty well.
I took Rann two semesters in a row and really enjoyed him. he was very knowledgeable and helpful with the material.
Prof very willing to work with you outside of class, to go over material, tests, etc. He moves pretty quickly but explains things clearly. Really nice guy.
Best math teacher I have ever had.
I was too scared to answer questions in class, which led me to fall way behind. He definitely made the class a bazillion times harder than necessary.
He's awesome! Hard tests, but wonderful professor that's more than willing to work with you on problems!

Rann's class is difficult. Easy B- at best. But, he works very hard to be available and assist students when they ask. I took Calculus in high school, but this course was still hard. Rann tries to explain the topic thoroughly (GO TO CLASS), but to really undertand the material, you must really do the homeowrk and take time outside of class.
Rann is a very nice guy. He'll definitely do what he can to help you out. The class was not incredibly easy, but curved. And the final was pretty hard.

Definitely the hardest 25/26 teacher (heard he was tough for 32 too). He doesn't like to answer questions in class though, so don't ask any. Definitely go in to class early though if you're confused, he's really nice and helpful then.

While his tests may not be the easiest, he's fair and is helpful outside of class. He doesn't want you to memorize formulas but rather to understand the concepts. Although not mandatory, attendance and homework are crucial to doing well in his class.

Rann is extremely helpful if you take the time to ask for it. He's quick to respond to his emails and will make time in his schedule for private tutoring if possible (but only if you ask). My only caveat is that his tests are generally pretty tough; however this usually leads to his students doing better on the block final than other classes.

I love the way he teaches. He makes you understand the math instead of just memorize it. Homework is not mandatory, and never collected, so you don't have to do it if you're comfortable with the material. His tests are hard, and even though he grades on a curve, it is not easy to get an A on a test.

Attendance is not "mandatory", but he gives out printouts with blanks you'd like to fill in through the lectures, which are pretty much all the study sources you have for exams. ASK him if you have anything unclear, and he'll give his best to help you. The tests are tricky, but then again, Math 32L tests in general are supposed to be hard.

At the beginning of his class, I was not used to the conceptual style of his teaching and his tests. However, he makes an effort to make sure you understand if you decide to take the initiative to ask him. He can be intimidating if no one speaks up in class, but it's apparent that that's only because he wants his students to engage in math.
Really hard tests. Don't think that if you liked math in high school you will be good in his class
Rann is a good teacher.  He writes difficult tests though.

Rann was an awesome teacher! Always enthusiastic and very willing to help, he'd stay after class to ensure you understood the material. He pushes you to think, not just number crunch, unlike a lot of professors. Don't be deterred by his tough tests/grading because it pays off. You come out of the class feeling like you've accomplished something.
very into conceptual math... very difficult tests and exams
good teaching, enthusiastic, sometimes difficult to understand so make sure you ask questions and he is more than happy to clarify

Everything about him is unconventional, from his appearance to his teaching style, which proves to make class very awesome. He is extremely enthusiastic, helpful, and well-knowledged while not often being disorganized. Tests are freaking hard. He is a super-picky grader. He will cover your paper in marks, guaranteed.

Rann is a very enthusiastic teacher who is VERY willing to help students.  His tests are a little difficult but pretty straightforward in content.  He does tend to get muddled while he teaches, so you have to ask questions so that he'll stop and clarify.  Still, I didn't like math before I took this class, but his enthusiasm made me change my mind!

Rann is a cool guy who is definitely willing to help.    However, his teaching style is very disorganized.  He frequently makes mistakes while lecturing, leading to confusion.  Make sure you're constantly on top of what he's writing so that you don't spend 3 hours trying to decipher a concept and then realize that he made a mistake in the notes.
He's extremely enthusiastic and helpful.  Definitely go to office hours if you have any trouble or aren't sure about certain concepts.

He's a really nice teacher who was very enthusiastic about what he taught. Although he teaches very conceptually, which is sometimes really hard to follow, he is always very accessible for extra help and explanations outside class. You definitely need to come to class and do the worksheets and homework to do well on the tests.

He's a nice guy. He's really helpful, and he tries really hard to be a good teacher. I think he'd be better suited teaching a higher level math though. His teaching style isn't  good for transitioning between high school math and college math.

He was a nice guy but was not good at teaching. The class was more of an independant study to me. When he taught something new he just did an example but didn't explain the steps he was following clearly and didn't do enough repetitions of problems. Class time was not used efficiently and thus I had to spend a ton of time on homework.
He's a really nice guy but he needs to be clearer when he's teaching. Very accessible outside class.

for most of the class, as long as i did the homeworks and went to office hours before the tests i was fine.  he's a really energetic guy and is passionate about teaching math.  has a lot of interesting stuff to say besides math as well.

teaches very conceptually... and you definitely need to go to class to get good grades on his tests (which are not often based off problems like the ones in the book)... very helpful when asked, and flexible about homework...

he is a great guy and is really funny...his tests are considerably harder than the other teachers but our class in general did a lot better on the final exam.  his teaching style takes a little while to get used to but he's readily available during his office hours.  If your willing to put in some work he is a great teacher and you will benefit

I think he's great as a person, but he needs to learn different ways of explaining one idea to different people who have different learning styles.  His handwriting (I know this sounds anal) isat times very difficult to decipher (yes, DECIPHER)and one minor detail in the notes makes a big difference, and any error can throw people off.
No Comments
Unless you have a really strong background in Calculus and you don't need a lot of explanation, don't take this class from him.
No Comments
No Comments
No Comments
Very good professor, very good class

To those who has a bit python background, Luo's class is easy and clear, only a little homework. But to those who has no coding background, there may challenges. So I suggest you to prepare for it before classes. Each Luo's class has a RRH part in the beginning. Two students who were selected a week ago will share some amazing ideas or knowledges.

Good course design, good rhythm arrangement, the course is not very difficult, compared with other professors, his CS101, more suitable for new students to get started with Python. Even if you have no prior experience you still have A chance of getting an A
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: He's not human.

Preparation is needed beforehand if you have no knowledge of CS beforehand. To learn the contents of this class, students are strongly recommended to watch corresponding online courses and Python exercises.

Professor Luo does not explain anything asked during lectures and is very hard to approach with questions. As an online student with no CS experience, this class was ridiculously difficult even with hours of self-study. Unless you have experience, I strongly advise you against taking this class. NOT beginner friendly, as a 101 should be.

Laura is an excellent resource. She is approachable, consistently available, and genuinely enjoys helping students who ask questions. Participation matters, and there is a fair amount of busy work throughout the semester. I opted for S/U because I'm lazy, but for anyone willing to engage, earning an A in this class is quite easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Absolutely LOVE her!!! She is by far the kindest professor I've ever had. The class atmosphere is very fun and low-stress. I genuinely looked forward to her class.

Laura was very sweet and willing to help you succeed. There are assignments nearly every day, but they aren't overly hard if you read the textbook and pay attention in lectures. Getting an A in this class is very feasible if you're willing to study even just 30 minutes a night. Look at her quiz study guides for sure!

Laura is THE BEST - so caring and personable. The only downside is the textbook (Sentieri). We had a lot of homework assignments, but that's to be expected in a 101 language class. We had a new edition last semester and there were a lot of issues with the online automatic homework grading where the prof had to fix it herself.

AMAZING! Laura is kind, caring and so fun. She genuinely wants all of her students to succeed. I took this class with her in the Duke in Bologna program (6 weeks) and it was great. It is a lot of work since you are getting an accelerated italian credit, but she is super understanding and reasonable when you speak with her about workload concerns.

I LOVE Laura! Her teaching methods are super effective. I have learned so much. She assigns a reasonable amount of homework, her tests/quizzes are fair and reflect what she teaches in class. If you pay attention in class there isn't any reason you shouldn't do well. And she is so funny and nice!

Laura is very sweet but do not be fooled- this class is a lot of work. Its easy but still takes work. Grading is pretty arbitrary but you will get an A in the class if you show up and do the work. Easy A
shes awesome. super funny. super chill class and a great way to knock out a language requirement if you have a heavy course load or are an athlete (or both)

Took this class in Fall 2021, I was honestly dreading fulfilling my foreign language reqs but taking 101 w/ Laura was a really good experience, she's super funny and the classes never felt super boring or like a waste of my time. I will say that she does have strong opinions about her students, she will either love you or hate you.

Laura is extremely funny and will make sure you leave Italian 101 knowing a whole lot more than you expected. My only complaint is that if she doesn't like you, she will make that very clear in her grading. What she might correct for you, will be dismissed for someone else. Her comments on assignments can come off as rude.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Laura is the nicest and most caring professor I have had at Duke. She wants you to succeed and is more than willing to help. You will learn a lot, and there is a lot of homework (textbook practice problems, speaking assignments, quizzes, group projects, asynchronous assignments). Expectations are always transparent, and she is a fair grader.

Laura is incredibly nice and caring. This class is just an absolute ton of work. Multiple homework assignments due MWF, with a long asynchronous assignment Wednesday. Never ending assignments and group projects. If you do the work with effort you should get an A. This is probably just the class itself and not a reflection of Laura.

Laura is so sweet but this class is more work and time consuming than 101/102. There is a ton of busy work and she is a stricter grader so don't expect automatic 100s .. but still decently easy to get an A. Lots of participation during class. Asynchronous day takes a lot of time (just a day of more hw). But if you have to take 203, Laura isn't bad!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Laura made me love Italian. She's so sweet, makes class fun, and really cares about us and wants us to succeed. This is an easy A with minimal work, but you'll still learn Italian really well. Tests/quizzes are straightforward, I recommend making quizlets for vocab and grammar to study. The cultural project is kind of dumb but not harshly graded.
Makes Italian fun. Far better than 101 and 102 semesters. Really cares and wants you to do well.
Laura was very sweet and definitely cared about her students. Let us make up homework we missed for full credit, very easy midterms, basically do the work and you'll get an A.
Very charismatic and fun. She really wants to build a community in the class. Great professor and great person
I took "BOOK ART: TYPOGRAPHY AS IMAGE" with Professor Fick, and he's really chill and kind! The class is super interesting, and I always look forward to going and working on my project

Wonderful professor, clearly cares about your motivation for drawing, and guides you in making artistic choices that both enhance your piece and fit the theme/message you are going for w/o compromising your freedom/creativity. Took this as a fifth class in a loaded schedule, put in effort to show that I cared about the class, and ended up w/ an A.
Intermediate Drawing was fun. Good balance between critiques, work time, and watching videos on artists. Professor Fick fostered a good classroom environment despite Covid-19 restrictions.
He was super supportive and gave great feedback. He definitely helped me grow as an artist.
I saw him take out a werewolf with his drawing moves. He makes a mean monster. He keeps an arsenal of drawing materials ready at all times.
Bill is great. A very fun person to be around and really enjoys spending time with his students. I have taken many of Bills courses and will continue to do so in the future.
Projects take as little or as much time on them as you want. I spent an hour on one and almost 30 hours on another. That much time isn't necessary, but you have to meet what standards he gives.

I hadn't taken an art class since 5th grade but Bill helped me feel confident and pleased with my drawing abilities. I was intimidated by how experienced others in the class were but I still felt capable of doing well. Go to every class and do extra sketches in your sketchbook! Class is chill as you can listen to music and sometimes ends early
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: He's a very caring and helpful art teacher- grades everyone on what they are capable of and has clear assignment descriptions. Really enjoyed his drawing class! The homework was really manageable: just one drawing per week usually. Also, showing up to class is a good portion of your grade, so don't skip!

I took intermediate drawing with Fick. Lots of freedom, but minimal guidance. Not for everyone.  Since it takes the exact same period along with drawing199, Fick devotes most of his time in 199 students, and only comes to see you once in a 2-hr period. Don't expect to learn practical stuff. Take only if you are as crazy about drawing as I am. Haha.

Bill is a wonderful person. He's incredibly understanding and always willing to help. The class itself is very basic, but it really builds from the ground up and encourages you to draw from observation. Really chill, and a fun class that only meets once a week.

It was an easy class but it can take up a lot time, with a final drawing due every week with 4 sketch drawings as well. It wasn't what I was expecting, especially looking at Fick's own art. The class is a very traditional drawing class which can get a bit boring if you've taken art before.
Bill is an AMAZING teacher, i loved being in his class. he's incredibly supportive and wants everyone to get a good grade.
The Best Teacher at Duke. BILL IS THE MAN
awesome guy
kinda fun...assignments sorta tedious but not overly stressful

Professor Marsh is great - bad review likely didn't pay attention or didn't study enough. Need to know a fair amount for the exams but the study guide she makes is AMAZING. Study guides help you succeed if you don't just memorize but understand the concept she is getting at. I will admit she is not the greatest lecturer, but everything is clear.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Marsh isn't a bad lecturer, the content is just super boring. She is a very clear teacher and cares about students, it's just hard to pay attention for the duration of the class. Take it for the major/minor but don't expect to be amazed.

Dr. Marsh's Psych 102 class was amazing!! Her lectures were very clear, and often ended early. She provided study guides for all 3 exams and was available to answer questions online. Biweekly reading checks helped us actually read the textbook, and the content (cognition) was super interesting!! Definitely take this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I LOVED this class! Prof. Marsh was engaging, caring, and very knowledgeable. Class had a consistent structure with lectures reviewing and expanding on textbook readings (that weren't dense). She'd make us great study guides for each exam (which weren't not hard) and was very generous with grading - put many policies in place to raise our grades.

Lecture slides and lecture content weren't really clear. No textbook to follow. Content overall kinda all over the place and some just was not high level, useful stuff (we spent a lot of time on memory aids that really could've been summarized in a single slide) Exams were fine and study guide she gives before is really helpful.

Dr. Marsh is a really nice woman but I truly hate her class. Have never hated a class more in my life to be honest. I also do not think her exams are fair, and I think that they are more difficult that necessary.

She was very unclear as a teacher- no textbook no guidelines. Teaches strictly by the most recent research papers about memory, lectures are all over the place and you have no idea what is important and what isn't. I didnt show up to class and got a good grade- just by reading a bunch of research papers- boring, not what i expected.
Very sweet and well-intentioned. Loves her field (myths and mysteries of memory) and doesn't give a lot of work

Past reviewers need to give Dr. Marsh more credit and fewer ad hocs. While her class wasn't a cakewalk, it certainly wasn't impossible to do well. Marsh cares that you learn well, does grade somewhat detail-heavy but carefully, and is big on application-based exams. Ended early when class was tired/confused & sought ample feedback. Has the best TA!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Caring

reviews.comment: Seemed outrageously insecure. Gave bad grades for no reason (there was one essay where like 1 person made an A, no exaggeration).  Thinks super highly of herself. The subject matter was great though.

She is a very boring lecturer.  Give detailed study guides so that you feel confident going into the test but then grades the tests ridiculously hard. Not a fair grader. Also seems like she doesn't care too much about students.

I was interested in this class prior to taking it, but this professor was terrible. She is a terrible grader; just extremely picky. While she will answer e-mails, she also has the "my way is the only right way" kind of attitude. She doesn't care about the effort you put in and don't expect her to be helpful. Her powerpoints are extremely unclear
Marsh teaches every lecture with a powerpoint that puts students to sleep. She is rather picky in grading. The subject of the class was interesting but it did not meet my expectations.

GREAT teacher! I don't know what people are talking about, she responds to emails and encourages you to resend it if she doesn't respond within 24 hours. She is SO HELPFUL and very engaging. She is very fair and a great professor overall. Her class is so interesting!!!

She knows the material very well, and her study guides are helpful. But her exams are way more difficult than the lectures imply and she grades her assignments so meticulously that you'd think she just graduated from school and doesn't have much experience. And she'll let you know at every single lecture that she went to Stanford...just annoying.

do not take this class unless you are really interested in memory and will attend every class. Her tests are difficult because she will take off points if you dont say exactly what she wants you to say. Her lectures are also very boring.

Material is interesting but the tests are very difficult. only 1/3 of what is on the study guide will be on the midterms. The final includes overlapping material even though she says it won't. there will be specific questions from previous exams on the final. She does not respond to emails regarding the study guide or anything else in a timely mann

Very interesting material. a lot of reading and tests can be difficult because she is very picky about how you phrase/express your answers. Not very helpful when it comes to answering questions regarding the study guide. NEVER answers emails in a timely manner.
Class material is really interesting - you'll get an A if you attend class & do the readings.  Beth's lecture style is fairly clear, but she talks very FAST.  So be prepared to pay attention.
really interesting lectures, but a lot of reading and tests were hard.
lectures very clear and interesting, a lot of reading, easy to get a good grade if you study the lecture notes and do the review
interesting lectures, HARD tests
the workload of her classes is quite high, but her research quality is excellent, and she is a good supervisor.
Tons of readings are required. She does not provide clear grading criteria and her class is tedious.
She's very dedicated to her work in the environmental science field, which is admirable. However, exams are pretty difficult.

The best photography professor I've ever had! He's the reason behind my photography practice, and I learned so much from Professor Bamberger both in terms of technique and conceptualization. Highly recommend!

A very good intro course in photography. Bill loves to interact with students and set up appointments. It's definitely not an easy A class - you need to work hard on your 3 photo essays (series of 10 photos) for a really good grade. And he expects you to work on each assignment for at least 4 hours. PS. You can borrow a DSLR if you don't have one.

Super easy freshman seminar. Basically an intro to photography class. Jayson Tatum and Frank Jackson were in the class if that tells you anything. Bill is super accessible and always willing to meet outside of class. He expects you to put a good amount of time into your photos, but it's not too difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: An extremely talented and respected professional photographer who comes to duke just to teach the course because he enjoys working with young people. His photo projects are fantastic and learning from him is amazing. In this class they loan you a DSLR to take photos with, but you need to spend time actually taking photos.

Professor Bamberger was a great professor! He was always willing to discuss my projects and give input after class or outside of class, and was always there for us. It was a great freshman seminar class to take!

Fantastic professor who's very knowledgeable about the subject. He's also extremely helpful and approachable in the lab and outside of class. That being said, it definitely is NOT an "easy A" class, especially for a first year seminar. You have to really work for your grade. Class is interesting and sometimes fun though.

Super interesting class, with fantastically laid out lectures! The structure is somewhat typical of the department: frequent mini assessments, regular lectures, and then a few exams. Make sure to really understand the abstract, intro, and conclusion of the papers for class, but don't stress about minor details since the exams are based on lecture
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Great lectures, clear grading, and fascinating material-- Prof Bilbo does it all! TBL will help you learn if you have a great group. You focus on 2-4 current papers per week which is key since this is such a changing field, and even when the weekly quizzes and graded applications can feel stressful, they challenge you to truly learn the material.
Staci is the best! Class covers the basics of neuroimmunology. Easy grade (she drops the lowest few scores, get to re-take exams in groups, etc.). As a heads-up, it's team-based learning.

Dr. Bilbo is a great professor. The class is incredibly tough (after all, it is the fundamentals of a complex field), but she does a good job highlighting what is important/on the tests (no obscure textbook info!). She may not be the most enthusiastic-sounding, but she actually really cares. You learn A LOT in this course. Take Neuro201 with her!

Dr. Bilbo is a very good professor. Not the most exciting lecturer but very clear and helpful--not out to ruin your day. Exams come only from lectures, and are very fair: they won't cover obscure stuff that even she doesn't fully understand. Textbook is helpful but not necessary. Hard class, but you learn a ton of essential material for the major.

Dr Bilbo is a great professor. No matter what other people say about her, the truth is she is always prepared and is willing to help her students. Her exam is fair, but only if you preview and review the content and keep up the work. She may not be the most dramatic person in the world, she still effectively gets the point across. Very fun class!

She is really boring and says she is interested in the material but sounds like she isn't excited at all. Her tests are based on random parts of the material she covers in class. I advise not taking a class with her.
Professor Bilbo's tests are HARD. Lots of detail.

Fundamentals of Neuroscience is a really cool class with interesting material (too much) and introduces cutting edge research. The problem with the class is the tests are far too specific when 50% is 10 chapters and the other 50% comes from journal articles.  However, it's a fun class and Bilbo is very nice and willing to answer any question.
What is Gravitas..? shout out to Elon.

Very willing to help outside of class. Really wants to be funny and liked by students. Insanely helpful review sessions. As others have said, a fair grader willing to work with you, I got a B despite no math skills.

Funny and a bit silly, he's a lovely guy. If you can get past the jokes he'll do all he can to help you pass the course. Always in his office, for assistance, a chat, advice. Hated physics, loved this class. Just ask questions, he'll answer.

mcnairy is great. he's exceedingly nice 1 on 1 and i felt like he's one of the few professors who cares about students on a personal level. he likes to keep class light by joking around and making fun of people, but not in a malicious way. so don't take mcnairy if you don't have a have of humor

The only reason I can see McNairy having a bad rap is that he can be rudely sarcastic at times but overall he is a great teacher.  He explains the concepts well, his exams are fair, and his grading system is extremely, extremely fair and designed to give you the best shot possible at a good grade.

Am I taking this class with a different professor or something? I was reluctant about signing up for the course with McNairy after reading the horrible reviews here. But in fact, I found him to be one of the most engaging, and engaged, professors I've had at Duke. He brought pie a la mode to those who attend his review sessions. I love him!

Worst teacher I've ever had. He's bitter about his contract being suspended and takes it out on students. His class is unnecessarily difficult, and he makes snide and offensive comments in recitation. His class is one of the few truly awful things at Duke.

I feel as though Dr. McNairy is one of the few excellent lecturers who sincerely cares about his students. When he sees that we are confused, he'll reintroduce concepts with admirable patience. He also conducts recitation, which is helpful since it allows students to see how to work problems for tests. Lectures are engaging and entertaining also.

Took his class this summer and got A. But McNairy sucks! He has very bad tact, makes horribly inappropriate, offensive jokes all the time. Make students purchase useless gadgets. Make "small" mistakes in lectures. Avoid if you can.

Dr. McNairy seems to drop all his commitments to help his students. Many people who complain about the difficulty of this class did not persist in scheduling meetings with him.  If you show him you care and are putting in the effort (attend lecture/recitations, do HW, meet with him), you WILL do well in the class at the end (he makes sure of it).
Hated this class. An interesting guy but this class is hard. Work really hard with very little results. Whole class was completely blindsided by one test. Avoid if you can
No Comments

Dr. McNairy wants all of his students to succeed and learn a lot of physics. When you go to him for help, he likes to guide you through the process of solving the problem rather than just tell you the answer, and I appreciate this a great deal. He's a great guy and you shouldn't take his jokes too personally because he means very well.

If you have no self respect, take him. He's an effective teacher, but very abrasive, and to be honest RUDE, for those with any sense of pride or dignity. Although he is a good prof, he will talk to you like you are bags of crap.
terrible professor
Goes out of his way to simply things and give you the benifit of the doubt.  Great for pre-med physics.

I took this class instead of PHYS 42 bc PHYS 41 was so hard. This class was a lot easier.  McNairy is rude to students, he acts like he's teaching kindergarteners. I think he thinks pre-meds are stupid. The class has virtually no work, & all easy. I didn't crack the book for the final (another test same day) and I still made an A anyway.
I was so frustrated by his lectures I almost cried.. a couple times.

Terrible professor.  Not a good teacher and very rude to students.  I got an A only because I worked like crazy to the detriment of other classes and learned all the physics on my own with the help of TA's. Avoid if at all possible. Honestly.
The worst ever...

Pretty nice guy, a little abrasive, though.  Grading for class is very fair, with regrades, quizzes, etc. to boost your grade.  Only downside is that his lectures are extremely disorganized, and he basically just shows examples and demonstrations without really delving into the concepts.
No Comments

I loved this class, even though I have no interest in physics whatsoever. His lectures are actually fun, because he always does cool demonstrations . He has a great sense of humor, too. He is also helpful if you need it, but you have to make the effort to show him you need it.
Unfortunately... you have to have him if you're taking physics.  So... don't take physics and do yourself a favor!  Get transfer credits!

Amazing professor and one of my favorite classes of the semester. Very understanding of students and will work with you. More concerned with growth than outcomes. Assigned readings/films for every class are absolutely required to follow discussions. Some readings are dense, but overall not overwhelming.

Really passionate about what he teaches and gives a lot of feedback on papers and allows for re-writes. Some of the topics and writings are harder to comprehend than others, but an overall easy class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: This was actually ENGLISH 101. Taylor has been my absolute favorite professor at Duke so far. His class pushed me to think differently and become a better writer and analyze the world more critically (be more gay). The syllabus was not what I expected and I learned so much from him. He is also just a delight to be around and so funny and genuine.

Whatever else you end up doing at Duke, please take at least one class taught by Professor Black. He's an incredible teacher, funny, and flexible with assignments. He does have the tendency to ramble, but nothing he says is filler and there was something interesting going on with every class. His office hours were great too. Amazing guy, 10/10.

Prof Black definitely cares about your development as a writer and pushed me more than any other professor in terms of writing. But the classes were so. boring. He wasn't good at asking thought-provoking questions and discussions were really dry. And he was super sassy. Reading material was very interesting and engaging tho.
Professor Black gives a lot of individual feedback and really helps development as a writer. Legend
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Cool guy, very interested in your development as a writer. Great feedback on drafts. Do the reading and participate and you should be good.
Cool
okay, so the engineer's of the government..? honestly human behavior is the reason the economy will never get better.

Dr. Blount stands out (in a very, very good way I should add) among university professors. I learned immensely in each class. She is kind, wise, and very intelligent. She provides excellent advice, on both academic and life-related matters. She goes beyond her required duties and takes time to meet one-on-one with her students. Excellent professor.

Alma is a warm caring person, yet I always feel profoundly uncomfortable in her class. She encourages class discussion in this backhanded "nudge-y" way, where you're free to voice your opinion only if she deems it right. She offers help, but patronizingly. Sometimes I like her bc she's so kind, but sometimes I'm unsettled by her self-righteousness

Alma is absolutely engaging. She will focus on you and connect with you personally but that does mean you need to be prepared in terms of doing all the readings and be actively thinking about the things we discuss in class. Lots of interesting readings in the beginning (100s of pages per week). Get past that and you are in for a fun semester.

Alma is an amazing teacher. She is very committed to her students and getting them to become better people. SOL is unlike an other course you take at Duke and I guarantee you will be better for taking it. I highly recommend this class. Be warned though, I took it as a freshman and it was EXTREMELY challenging. Take it sophomore or junior year

Great professor; challenged my thinking. I don't agree with everything she says, but I did find this class (and the class materials) compelling. Her feedback is always helpful, and she's great to speak to one-on-one.

Don't take her. Class is abstract. Who cares about border crossing. The mean grade is a B/B+. If you want your gpa to go down the drain, go for it. This class has been one of the worst decisions I have made during my years at Duke. I got an excellent grade but this class won't make you a leader. There are better more interesting classes out there.

Alma is an incredibly good person. She is always willing to help her students out and is compassionate in times of need. She is undoubtedly the best teacher I have ever had. Her class requires that you think outside of the box and write concisely. TAKE THIS CLASS if you can get in.

Get to know her in person, and you will love her.  Her class, however, is hard.  You do a lot of work, but she might not be satisfied with your work.  And, that can really be frustrating.  People say that she doesn't give out grades.  The truth is she grades them and averages them at the end, but she doesn't tell her students about the grades.
Demanding, an excellent approach to facilitating seminars, a committed mentor.  She is thoughtful about feedback and has great insight into a student's strengths and weaknesses.

i love alma, and you might too. her class is touch, grading is arbitrary (though you wont get worse than a B if complete assignments, come to class and are ON TIME). I have loved getting to know Alma as a person and a professor and I would highly recommend her. She will teach you to look at leadership, social issues, and life in a new way.

What a wonderful professor! Her class has allowed me to reassess my approach to leadership and given me a new perspective. Not an easy A, and not knowing your grade is stressful, but one of the best classes I have taken at Duke. If personal growth is your priority, take the class. If you do, I highly recommend that you meet w/ Alma outside class.

Alma really cares about her students and the topic she teachers. She's always willing to talk to you outside of class. LIke other people have said, unfortunately you have no idea how you're doing in the class. Her grading is totally arbitrary and there are no real grades given on assignments. You don't know what you're going to get in the class

Alma is  great professor. If you can take a class with her, I highly recommend it. She really knows her stuff and is super passionate about the material. She really cares about her students and always makes time to meet with you outside of class. Unfortunately, her grading is arbitrary and completely based on how she feels about you as a person.

Blount class is very interesting, however in a class of 15 students one of the most pretigious institutions in America, only 3 recieved A's.  She is unfair in grading. Does not look at improvement, but instead grades arbitrarily based on participation in class and her own personal favoritism.

One of the more interesting and engaging classes I took at Duke. Professor Blount is an engaging and thought lecturer that genuinely cares about her students. Not a particularly hardly graded class, but extremely stimulating. Non PPS majors may disagree.
Always willing to help students, and she genuinely cares about them--not just in class. She asks about social life, family life, etc. Amazing professor.

Alma Blount really cares about her students as people and as adults.  I came to my midterm meeting expecting a discussion about grade status, but was surprised when she launched into a candid discussion about my life and family.

Self-important and thus very arrogant, thinks her class is the only one her students are taking, and thinks that she is the supreme end-all answer to anything. Grades unneccessarily harsh for top students selected into a competitive program, probably because that insecure about her class. Arrogant!

Very structured class. Students give her rave reviews. Grading depends on writing. Not a lot of discussion though. Overall, a really good class that gets you asking questions abt democracy and world issues.
What makes a good journalist..? Perspectives..?

Unhelpful moderator of class discussion and unenthusiastic demeanor makes this class very long to sit through. Minimal feedback and poor guidance, coupled with high expectations on turned-in assignments. If you have to take Magazine Journalism for the certificate, wait until it's taught by another professor.

Awful.  I am currently a senior at Duke. Worst professor I have ever had at this school.  Bliwise is mean-spirited and gives tons of homework.  I gained no factual knowledge from this class. Do not take.
Do not take this class.

I can hardly vent enough frustration - this man is not only awkward but UNbearable.  I loved learning about magazine journalism and he assigned interesting articles to read but assignments were too frequent and too arduous for the thanklessness he gives in return.  YUCK

I'm still in the midst of the course so can't offer any feedback on grading but, although I am very interested in the course material and fascinated with the assigned readings, I've been frustrated at the arduous assignments and minimal feedback.  Bliwise certainly knows his stuff but has a hard time articulating his enthusiasm in a discussion..

Dean Blackshear is probably the most inspirational person I have ever met in my life and the fact that he is willing to share his knowledge and experiences with students to better our lives is so incredible. I am so grateful to have taken his 212 course and learn about forensic psychology from one of the leading experts in the field.

By far the most important and inspiring course I've taken in my academic career. Dean Blackshear is the most charismatic, engaging lecturer; I was actually upset when class ended. He cares about his students and our learning so much, there are weekly reflections and group projects that are really fun. Best class EVER.

Dr. Blackshear is without a doubt the best professor and all-around person you will/can meet at Duke. Class is just lectures and by lectures I mean him telling stories that help you learn. A 1-page reflection due every Sunday and 3 papers (2 are with a group). Best Class at Duke which is why it's so hard to get in. Just show up and he'll let you in

Dr. Blackshear is awesome. He tells stories of his actual cases as a Forensic Psychologist, and is hilarious, extremely intelligent, and accessible. He is so smart and does such incredible work, but is also very relatable. No tests, just 3 essays based on books, movies in class, and in class notes. Super reasonable work load & incredible experience

Dr. Blackshear is an amazing professor. All his lectures are so interesting and he always throws in anecdotes along with the concepts he teaches. He is funny and engaging and the assignments are not too difficult if you review the lectures.

Professor Blackshear is extremely knowledgeable and caring, even though he may be slightly disorganized at some points. You will learn a lot of really useful things about forensic psychology. The material is fascinating and the Proff has experience to put behind the theory. You should attend every lecture but you will get a good grade if you try.

Easiest class I have taken at Duke, but it's not boring by any means! He is an actual forensic psychologist and talks about his past and current cases during class. It's so interesting and there are no tests!

Lectures were extremely interesting. He has a lot of experience in forensic psychology and interesting stories to complement the cases. Entire grade based on three medium-length papers. One of my favorite classes at Duke and wish I could take it again.

Blackshear is awesome. He's a great lecturer, always entertaining. He is very enthusiastic and uses his own, super interesting case studies. I learned a lot and this has been one of my favorite classes at Duke. 100% recommend

Great, engaging professor with interesting material. No tests, just write-ups using outside sources. Very interesting case-study fueled class. The one downside is you don't learn as much about forensic psychology as you do about individual cases. Definitely take this class though.
I ended up choosing my career path because I took his security course. It was also the most fun class I've taken at Duke.
Best prof in the computer engineering department. Radiating with enthusiasm and super knowledgeable about anything hardware related.

Everyone loves Bletsch! He is an amazing lecturer who makes the content as interesting as possible. He is also very helpful outside of class hours and cares about the students. I have now taken several classes with Bletsch and have had a great experience in all of them.

Bletsch is hands-down the best professor I've had at Duke. It was only his second time teaching 350 but you would've never known. His lectures are so engaging. It almost feel more like a high school class both because of his energy and how he's able to make difficult topics so simple. He's the rare professor who got his PhD so that he could teach.

Amazing professor!! Like, one of the best professors I have ever had. Took a graduate CS class with him. The homework is fairly hard (especially if you are trying to actually learn the content not just for the grade), but he is available during OH and will go out of the way to help you. Wish I had a professor like this during my undergrad!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: i love you professor bletsch. bless you and your cardigans and hi-chews
Amazing lectures - incredible at explaining difficult concepts and always has a perfect answer to your questions, plus he has a great sense of humor. Honestly my favorite class I have taken at Duke!

Professor Bletsch is too awesome! Lectures are a little bit fast but there are recordings available. Homework assignments and exams were also not too hard and he explains concepts very clearly. Also is very accessible outside class for questions and homework help. 10/5 stars!

Bletsch tries hard to get students to like him. Very knowledgable in the material and easily accessible outside of class. His presence is watching wet paint dry, but it will at least be the easiest ECE/CS class you will take.

Tyler Bletsch is a really cool and fun professor. He made lectures fun to attend and even threw candy at us. His 350 exams were much easier compared to John Board's exams. I would definitely take his class.

Amazing teacher, so nice and caring. He uses helpful examples to explain complex concepts, and can somehow make even the blandest CS concepts funny and entertaining. Wants to help you if you are confused. Highly recommend. 

As for CS250, start the HW VERY early and go to office hours and you will do well.
He is very knowledgeable, and can explain complex topics very clearly.

I genuinely wanted to go to Prof. Bletsch's lectures every day, because they were just so good. He's such a cool guy and genuinely wants to help and do the best he can for you. Homeworks are long, but everyone knows 250 homeworks are long already and he gives you tons of office hours to help with them. Tests aren't bad at all :D

Bletsch is a very good lecturer who uses analogies to make confusing computer architecture topics simple. As long as you start the HWs early (which are definitely a lot) you'll be okay. He's very reasonable and accomodating.
Truly one of the most respected professors at Duke, and I'm glad I took this class with him. His sense of humor is also awesome. Gem of a professor.

Bletsch really wants you to do well on tests, of which there's only 2. His focus is on the HW, where the real learning happens. If you're on a tight time budget, give it all to the HW. Lectures are kinda fast but he always brings his goofy 2010s-internet humor, including demonstrations with the class. Just a genuine, energetic, well-versed guy.

Lectures are great and really important, but recordings are also available. The homeworks are long, but manageable as long as you start early and go to office hours. The midterm and final were both extremely easy compared to the homework, so if you do well on those you will be fine. Great course if you want to learn about computer architecture.

Genuinely one of my favorite classes I have every taken. He makes the content very interesting and gives very fair exams. The homework can be stressful at times but is still manageable for people with little CS background. Also gives out extra credit and candy, Very funny person.

The best CS professor at Duke by far. Lectures are fun and he is always making sure that the students are engaged by giving them candy. In class he has amazing jokes and the lectures feel like they are a great use of time. The projects are easy if you have a little CS experience and you start early. Also lots of extra credit.

Tyler is a great lecturer. He is passionate, funny, and always willing to answer questions. The home works are reasonable and interesting. The discussions are generally pretty helpful. Nothing is too difficult, but I still learned a lot.

Dr Bletsch's offering has easier hw sets compared to that of Dr Sorin's. He's really approachable and is willing to spend time helping students debug their hw. His tests are really easy, so the hw sets are what you should look out for. He's got lots of fun extra credit opportunities (and the curve may be affected by those).

One of the best lecturers at Duke. Even though I felt like I didn't have to show up to his lectures, I would never miss one. Very clear grading criteria, and felt prepared for every part of this class. I wish every professor were like Dr. Bletsch.

Classes were recorded, so you didn't have to go to class. Exams were pretty easy and were an easy A as long as you watched the recordings. The biggest mistake people make is not starting the homework early which can break your grade because the homework assignments take a LONG time. Overall one of the best professors at Duke.
Tyler's lectures are always interesting and intriguing. The homework covers many topics and I did learn a lot. For the exams, we're only required to master the concepts, which is not difficult.

Prof. Bletsch was an amazing professor. He is very funny and explains concepts in a clear and understandable manner, especially for a challenging subject matter like CS 250. He also consistently holds additional office hours right before projects are due to help out his students, which I think is extremely respectable.

Overall, Bletsch is great at explaining concepts clearly, and I rarely felt confused at the end of class. He is not intimidating, and is overall a great professor to take 250 with. The class is difficult by design, but Bletsch made homeworks reasonable compared to previous semesters.

Bletsch is by far the best CS professor I've had at Duke! He made CS250 not only manageable, but enjoyable and I learned a ton. He is a fantastic lecturer and really cares about making the class accessible for everyone. I'm not an ECE major but I would switch in just to have more classes with him

Best professor I had at Duke! Dr. Bletsch is super smart and engaging on security. The homework assignments were a joy to do, and each one required solving a puzzle to access. He also jokes a lot and his slides are pretty memey so the lectures are fun to attend.

Prof. Bletsch is amazing. Don't know why he doesn't have a perfect 5. I took this class begrudgingly because another one filled up, but it ended up being the highlight of the semester. The class was super interesting (cool hacking stuff), and Prof. Bletsch made it really entertaining and engaging. You have to take this class, you won't regret it.

Bletsch is awesome. This class is crazy hard, but he was super accessible and stayed on office hours with me for like 2 hours one night trying to help me debug. The projects are really difficult, but the exams aren't as bad and I feel like I got a lot out of the class.

Dr. Bletsch is great. You can tell he is really passionate about computers, and will often go on (useful/practical) tangents to demonstrate the concepts that he is covering. He is a bit eccentric in lectures, but you'll almost never have a dry lecture with him. He also holds extended (indefinite length) office hours, which is also a huge plus.

Professor Bletsch is an amazing professor that legitimately cares about his students. Made an extremely challenging class rewarding and made the lectures interesting and engaging. Would definitely recommend taking him.

Professor Bletsch is the best professor at Duke Comp Sci department hands down. I am a senior and I have taken every CS class there and let me tell you his lectures are so well done you won't forget the material for years. It takes so much to teach such a hard class (CS 250) in an understandable way and no other professor can do what he does.

Best professor I have had at Duke, hands down. Prof Bletsch is an incredible lecturer who makes every lecture super interesting and useful, with clear expectations on HW and tests. His course on Computer Security had incredibly challenging HW assignments (5 total), but it is the class I have learned the most at Duke. Average grade was maybe an A-.

Prof Bletsch is one of the most amazing professors I have ever had. I took this class during the summer, and he held ridiculously extended office hours (sometimes for like 6 hours straight) because he cares so much that no student is left behind. He has a gift for teaching and explaining things. Definitely take ANY class with him! He's amazing!
Bletsch is awesome! Just put in the work, and you'll do fine. He makes lectures interesting and clearly loves teaching.
This class was great, and Bletsch is a excellent lecturer. Really reminded me why I signed up for CompSci.

His lectures were simply amazing, and I loved this course despite not getting an A on it  it's hard! He knows the material really well, makes lectures super enjoyable and smooth, and is always willing to meet to clarify any concepts. Probably the best professor I have had at Duke!

I was really apprehensive going into this class, but Tyler made the class go really smooth. The assignments are a lot of work, but that can't be helped. If you make an effort to pay attention in lecture, it will help with assignments a lot. 1 midterm, 1 final, completely doable if you do his practice exam (average for the final was 91%).
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Best lecturer I've come across at Duke. Only downside is that he's kind of unapproachable, as he often makes (kind of hyperbolized/embarrassing) jokes at students' misunderstanding -- this seems unintentional, though, it's just his sense of humor, and he means no real harm. Well-structured course, and Bletsch makes it interesting. Definitely take!
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Tests? Not many--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Tyler is a mean prof. He does not seem to care for how well his students do in his course, and is very willing to spend 20 minutes roasting you for poor decision making skills, even if you can justify all of your decisions. He seems to operate in a world where students have infinite time and wisdom. Nerdy jokes can only get you so far as a prof.

Love Dr. Bletsch. He's a really engaging and knowledgeable teacher-- I know people are intimidated by the workload of CS250, but he's so accessible and there are so many office hours that you'll be fine as long as you pace yourself. Take this class with him!!

Dr. Bletsch is the best CS professor I've had at Duke. CS 250--especially over the summer--is very rough. But Dr. Bletsch is very knowledgeable, funny, organized, and above all-- willing to go above and beyond to help out each student. He made taking a truly difficult class an absolute pleasure, and there's very few Professors who can do that.

The best professor I've ever had. I was frustrated and on the verge of deciding to withdraw from this class, when he remained after class for literally 7 hours until 9pm (yes, skipping lunch and dinner just for the students) and helped out answering questions and walking through everyone's code one by one. I am honored that I got to take his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Interesting material, lectures were engaging and quite helpful. Very knowledgeable guy who has a lot of experience and willing to help you; tests are not difficult and there is extra credit. Assignments take a long time in general so start early. They are difficult but definitely doable if you have enough time. Take 250 with him if you can.

Prof Williams is great in a small seminar setting. She creates a good environment for discussion and makes it easy for everyone to participate. Low, but interesting, workload. Prof Williams is incredibly helpful and is always willing to meet outside of class if you have questions. One of my favorite classes at Duke

I love Blythe Williams. She's really personable in lab section and will really try to relate with you. She is definitely a speed lecturer and has a propensity to rush through slides, but since a lot of the tests are memorization anyway, it's not detrimental to the class.

Dr. Williams is an amazing professor! She highlights important facts in class and is always ready to answer questions. Her tests are detailed, so studying is very much necessary, but it is all understandable and relevant material.

Dr. Williams is my favorite professor at Duke! She is extremely helpful and dedicated. Great class, although some people that are not truly passionate about evanth might find some of the material boring. Just be ready for a LOT of memorization (bones, muscles, attachment points, etc.)

MALS graduate course.  Extremely interesting.  Lifetime influence on thinking.  If you want an easy course, go elsewhere.  If you want a life changing experience, study with this man, he makes you think and think hard!
I took Theorizing Religion with him.

Dated info perhaps- but I would rather think or it as 'timeless' rather than dated. I studied with Prof. Bland in Duke/Israel in 1980, and still remember it like yesterday? the consummate devil's advocate, scholar, provocateur and instiller of passion in the blasé. 30  years gone, still remembered?an inspiration and a joy.

Really nice old guy.  Class was really fascinating and not too difficult - never got a bad grade.  He is humorous and interesting (and a big duke basketball fan) - definitely worth taking a class with him if you are interested in the course work.

I don't know why everyone gave him such harsh grades. Maybe it was just the different class. Religion 40 with him was just fine. He was very easy and the nicest professor I have ever had. He really cares about his students.

Wow. This guy is the worst prof I've ever had. I mean, really bad. DO NOT take this class. Lectures are very boring, discussions are trite and useless. That, along with the fact that he thinks he knows everything make for a bad class. Also, it is impossible to know what he expects on his written assignments, and dissenting opinions are discouraged.
fun professor - excellent moderator for discussions but can be an extremely boring lecturer. readings are largely unnecessary - just read the coupla days before the papers are due.

Some people didn't like his teaching style, but I think he was good.  Very grandfather-like.  Always inviting students to talk outside of class or get lunch or something.  Papers in this class are tough because they're so abstract.  Really makes you think hard, though.  You really have to do all the readings for this class.

Bland is a fun guy, enjoys humor and enjoys teaching the class. Not too hard of a grader and is helpful in that he'll help you think through a problem but he'll also make sure you address the task. Readings aren't as necessary as he says they are.
WORST PROF. AT DUKE.  DO NOT TAKE HIS CLASS. BORING. DISENGAGING. NOT ENOUGH BAD WORDS COULD BE SAID ABOUT THIS CLASS.
I came to Duke to specifically study with Bland. He was so focused on his research that his class lectures were sometimes disorganized. His interest in students is minimal.
Very excited about material, but he will draw the same diagram every day. Sweet man though with some interesting readings. Def worth taking.
His class was kind of boring, but you could tell that he was very enthusiastic about the subject. Always willing to meet with you for extra help. Make sure to show up on time!
He is a little boring, but the sweetest teacher, and genuinely cares about the class. Like an awesome grandpa
the topic could have been made so much more interesting...he's really boring when he lectures, even the ta falls asleep. and he grades hard. i wouldn't recommend the class.
dudes pretty cool...rel 129 was a great class...you have to spend a lot of time on the assignments ...with him a 3 pg paper takes longer to write than a 15 pager for some other prof.

Religion 129 has been the best class i have taken at duke. Allot of personal growth concerning views on religion and science. Bland is an awesome professor. There were 3 4 page papers, which doesn't sound bad, but he grades hard.I HIGHLY RECOMMEND HIM
I agree with previous comments!  He rules!
A very knowledgeable and fun (if somewhat eccentric) Judaism professor.  He's a rabbi, too!  Absent-minded, but only delightfully so.

This prof was awful. 3 weeks into class he decided i was not worth it as a student and blatantly sent me an email saying i show no understanding of the law and that i will fail the class. If you are black and Muslim, expect to be discriminated against. I would not wish this prof for my worst enemy.constantly picked on me and made me feel stupid.

His IP is more like a 1L class. Full Socratic. Everyone will be called on. He's Shakespearean. British/European worldview and sense of humor. Lots of metaphors. He's extremely open-minded & accessible. Ask anything, and he will answer. He advocates for wider access to IP. Co-founded Digital Commons. He gives you his textbook digitally for free.

Prof. Boyle is a very intelligent man but I doubt he's the most intelligent man in the world, which appears to be his opinion. I've never had a prof. who is so in love with his own voice and "wit".  If he would concentrate less on how he comes off and more on actually teaching, both sides would be better off. A smart bore.
No Comments
THE GOAT!!!

Professor Bomze is a really nice professor and person overall. Grades forgivingly and makes sure everyone understands the content of the lab before proceeding. Lab reports can be long but if you do them ahead of time you'll be good.
One of Duke's gems and treasures. I loved every moment of lab with Yuriy.
