Bomze's a great guy who genuinely prioritizes learning and understanding. Comes off as blunt at first, but is really quite chill, approachable and funny. Always accessible via email and ready to clarify instructions. Lab reports are long, but have clear guidelines and are graded leniently. A surprisingly good lecturer too. Learned a lot overall.

this guy is the goat—prelabs aren't graded and he gives individual feedback on every single one, which makes the four labs you do much easier. The labs are a are a good bit of work but Dr. Bomze is always there for feedback/extra help. Very approachable and caring prof

Dr. Bomze's 264 lab made my semester. Four lab reports = lots of work, but pre-labs are accessible. Clear that his top priority is students understanding concepts. Yuriy facilitates great discussion, is an expert in the lab, and goes out of his way to meet outside class time. Practical skills with Python, Overleaf, and lab apparatus learned.

Best remote learning experience during COVID. We need more professors like him at Duke! pretty sad that Dr. Blake is retiring. He was caring and enthusiastic in making the virtual class as comfortable as possible.

Blessed to have Prof. Blake as my professor for MATH 101. He really cares about students and you will understand why he prefers to have small-sized classes. He prefers to teach by writing on boards, no PPTs at all. Be prepared to do homework every single day, but it should be fine. No recitation classes as usual math classes at DKU, instead labs.

Great classes. Brilliant and smart. math 112 is just a bad bad class in general. but he made it better than i expected. not to say i ended up with a good grade in the end. he's caring and lets you retake tests. but get ready to work. theres no reason intro calc should be this bad. but if you ABSOLUTELY NEED IT on your transcript, take him for sure
Professor Blake is a wonderful and kind-hearted professor who makes learning math as tolerable as it can possibly be.

Blake is a great person, very enthusiastic about the course and wants you to learn.  Willing to meet outside of class, and will answer any questions you have.  Doesn't like it if you're late though, if you respect him and do what you're supposed to do, he respects you.  Homework almost every night, but do it if you want an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: You can tell Blake has taught this class many times before because he knows the material extremely well and is great at explaining it. It helps to go to lectures. There is optional homework, but it helps a lot. He puts a few practice problems on each test. If you're willing to put in the time and effort, the class won't be as bad as rumored.
Prof. Blake is very very clear and makes math enjoyable. If I had to take math again, I would definitively take it with him.

Math is notoriously hard at Duke, and I am positive that I would not have passed nor done well in this class if it weren't for Professor Blake. Best Professor I've had at Duke, and probably the best I will ever have. Very knowledgable and excited about teaching, makes you work for your grade but it's such a reward when you do well.

Math classes at Duke will most likely be the hardest classes you ever take. That being said, Professor Blake is extremely knowledgeable, passionate, and will go out of his way to help you. Tough class, great professor.
Definitely one of the best Math professors at Duke. If you have to take Math, take it with him!

Truly one of the best professors I've had the privilege of studying under at Duke. A phenomenal resource, he is always willing to spend extra time covering difficult topics until everyone understands them. He grades hard and collects homework. Lectures are somehow kept interesting, despite it being math. Would highly recommend.
Blake is very organized and his explanations made understanding Calculus 2 topics easy. Make sure you keep up with the work!

Best professor I have had at Duke! He's amazing at explaining tough concepts and he is very helpful when you have questions. He cares about your performance in class too. Go to lectures and do the HW assignments - it really makes a difference on tests.

Blake is an amazing professor. I had him for calc 1 and 2. He's clear and will really help you understand. His tests are really hard though and hes a stickler on time and I couldn't ever fully finish his tests. But hes a great math 111 and 112 professor

He is probably the best professor I've had at Duke so far. Super clear, very helpful, and really makes an attempt to make sure you get the material. Intro calculus is going to be difficult no matter who is teaching it but he makes it absolutely manageable.

Professor Blake is extremely kind and makes calc as bearable as possible. He's always willing to help or re-explain material. I understood concepts I hadn't after sitting through a year of HS calc. The tests are hard, but there's no way around that. I've never liked math, but Prof. Blake is excellent; take calc with him if you can!

Probably failed his course. But wasn't his fault. He didn't even get to write the final. Super nice guy. Amazing professor. Highly recommend taking his class for 112. Definitely tough on the grading. But if you actually put the work in and really study hard for the midterms, you'll be fine. Do the prob sets and don't sleep on those labs either.

Blake is a phenomenal professor.  he is extremely helpful and truly loves teaching. Math111 and 112 are not easy classes, but Blake makes them bearable and doable. Tests aren't awful - on par with any college Calculus course.

Professor Blake is the most awesome math professor you'll ever meet. His ability to explain fundamental concepts into things you can understand is just incredible. He will prepare you very well for the because his tests are very conceptual - which is what the final will be like.  (I took 111 and 112 with him, and wish he taught other math classes)

Blake was an incredible teacher! Incredibly clear and cared about his students. Within the first couple weeks he knew all our names and if someone had any issues he was more than happy to break it down. Tests were hard but if put in effort in class and with homework you should be fine

Blake is definitely the best teacher for Math 111 (old # 31). Willing to help you if you put in the work, and he does a good job in class of explaining how he wants you to answer specific types of problems. Would be very difficult if you had never taken calc, but if you have to take 111, take it with Blake. (He gave out candy during the final!)

I had him for 31L and 32L. He is extremely clear in lectures, and an overall excellent teacher that kept me engaged. This class is brutally hard because of the curve, though I felt like I definitely improved my math skills a lot (C+ in 31L and B+ in 32L) but the fact remains that this class is a GPA killer no matter what teacher you have.

Great professor! This is a really hard class, but Blake makes it infinitely better. If you go to lecture he will clearly explain the topic. Always willing to help a student individually if he/she asks for help.

He explains things really well and are really willing to help the students. He doesn't collect homework, but make sure you do them because it helps you to know the knowledge better. The last year's exam he gave before each exam is VERY useful, make sure you understand every single question. Then you will get good grades.

Extremely nice guy and loves what he does. Explains concepts clearly and is very willing to help out. Tests are ridiculously hard and he tends to focus more on conceptual aspects of Calc. Overall a great teacher.

Best math teacher/professor I've ever had. Presents the material in a way that makes sense. HW assignments after every class are not hard (although time consuming) and really help with understanding. Also very good with extra help

Nice guy but his assessments are ridiculous. He is pretty clear in class if you have taken Calc before. But, his test  purposely throw hard and convoluted questions at you to test your "real understanding." Labs can be confusing and time consuming. Don't take this class unless you are POSITIVE you need it for your major. GPA killer
He's a really nice teacher and he's definitely always there to help. His tests are murder though.

Blake is the nicest guy ever! He makes a real effort to get to know his students. He is extremely patient and clear in his lectures, but they tend to be a bit dull. If you can stay awake, you'll do fine in his class.

Professor Blake is truly an AMAZING professor. His lectures are very clear and he is very willing to help outside of class. Oh, and he pretty much is the nicest guy you'll ever meet. Take Math with Blake if you can; you won't regret it!

Best professor ever! This is a difficult class, but professor Blake makes it way easier! Hard subjects come without pain. His lectures are crystal clear and extremely helpful. You don't need extra work to absorb the material. Just do the homework after class, and you should be fine.
Best teacher ever.  He is patient, clear, and understanding.  If you do the homework (though it is not required) you will do well.
Very nice guy. He is good at explaining math concepts to those who don't necessarily have the most mathematically-oriented minds.

A phenomenal teacher.  He loves math, and he wants to share it with his students.  It's a hard class, but doable because Professor Blake makes it interesting.  And come on, he's the nicest guy in the world!  Take calc with him, it can't get any better than this.

Best teacher I've had in my entire life. I was dreading 8:30am calculus, but, not only did I stay awake during his lectures, I actually looked forward to them. He's crystal clear, eager to help, very approachable and just so nice. He's ALWAYS smiling, clearly loves his job, and he even learned our names. I can't say enough good things about him.
Great professor. Math isn't my favorite, but I was able to get through his class with minimal suffering. He's a really nice guy and a great teacher.

Blake is super nice but his class is impossibly hard (unless you are an ace at math). NOT an easy math credit. Makes material seem easy but makes tests soooo much harder. Otherwise a very nice person, really cares about students and is very willing to help.

After doing poorly on my first quiz and approaching him about it, Professor Blake continually checked up on me to make sure I was continuing successfully, etc. If you put the effort forward, you'll be fine. if you slack, you won't. that simple. It was very difficult, but if you have to take calc 31 at duke, don't do it with anyone but Blake.

One of the best professors I've had at Duke.  I dreaded taking math, but Blake made it about as painless as possible.  If you're going to take 31 or 32, do everything in your power to take it with him.  I can't recommend him highly enough.

Very nice but poor teacher.  Puts so much emphasis on difficult problems that he doesn't teach fundamentals.  Labs focused on material we hadn't covered (we covered it later, but at that point it didn't help on the quiz/reports) and a lab focused on calculator use then had a quiz on which we couldn't use calculators. 2 examples sum up his teaching.

After having him, it makes perfect sense why he's the "Supervisor of First-Year Instruction."  He's been teaching for years, and it shows; he's very good at what he does.  You can tell he loves his job too; he's always smiling.  Encourages participation in lecture.  You really couldn't ask for a better math professor. Great math experience for me!
After two years at Duke, I've found that none of my professors have measured up to Professor Blake. He is undoubtedly one of the best, if not the best professor Duke has to offer.

I never thought math was interesting, but professor Blake changed everything. He made me love math. His lectures are really interesting that you don't want to miss it. He has the ability to take control of students and keep their attention. Exams are not that hard, but is challenging. In one word he's just awesome. Highly recommended.

Professor Blake is very supportive and passionate about his teaching, I don't think I've ever seen him NOT smiling.  His courses (I've taken 31 and 32) are challenging, but the grades you receive are directly related to how much effort you put into the course. He will do all he can to make concepts clear to the students.  really supports athletes

Lewis Blake is a kind and helpful professor. He is willing to make appointments with you to discuss math problems and the tests. We had three tests, some lab reports and a few quizzes. Before each test he gives you a practice test that you can take home to practice. The class requires a lot of understanding. Choose Blake over the other professors.

Professor Blake is such a great teacher!  He explains things clearly and is so enthusiastic that he puts in a lot more effort than most teachers would.  You have to do the homework because it's collected on a random basis, but it helps you stay on top of everything.  I hope I get him for 32L.
Blake is by the far the best guy for intro math classes, class is not easy at all but he's fair and explains everything. Not too boring.
Great instructor, very helpful.  Can relate to students well.  Somewhat difficult class, but bearable.  Should be the first on the list for 31L/32L instructors.
He is very friendly and passionate about teaching. He is easy to access outside of class and is very helpful. Excellent teacher
Good teacher, but this class will kick your ass.
Best teacher ever, I was afraid to take math 32L, and I ended up loving it. tough class, but Blake is definately that best professor, and is really fair, and willing to help.
BEST teacher ever! really helped me understand calculus, and made lectures enjoyable.
Excellent teacher, lays a great calc foundation...tests are a bit hard :)
Very helpful with students...easy to meet with outside of class.
It's worth taking calc just to be in his class

Like everyone else said, a great professor.  Clear, friendly, enthusiastic.  Tests are not easy, but not super hard, either. Do your homework and come to class and you'll do fine.  I've heard this is the most failed course at Duke - if you have Prof Blake and still fail, it's your own fault.

Great professor that loves teaching.  Everything is very clear and he is the most approachable and friendly teacher I've ever had.    Tests are average difficulty.  If you don't learn in this class it's your own fault.
I have never understood math as well as I did when I took this class. He is a great teacher.
best introductory teacher, he really helps you understand hard concept material that you have probably never done before. he is also very approachable and really wants you to do well.
Just a great teacher, nothing more to say

Dr. Blake is a wonderful prof.  I changed to his class from another teacher's class just because of his reputation, and I wasn't let down.  I went from failing miserably to understanding.  I won't take another math class that he doesn't teach.

He is definitely the best calc teacher at Duke if you have to take 31L or 32L but still not wow or anything.  He is very helpful and energetic towards math but sometimes doesn't explain the stuff well.  Class and tests are WAY TOO HARD.
He's a genuinely friendly guy who deserves to become a full professor.
Great teacher, really easy to understand.  His tests really aren't that hard, at least not if you like/understand math.
GREAT teacher, HARD class.  If you have to take calculus, BE SURE to get Blake as your professor.
Great teacher. Helpful. HARD CLASS.
so nice.  fair tests on understanding not memorization.
Great teacher but his tests are just plain HARD
The best introductory Math teacher at Duke.  The tests are challenging but he really explains the material and it all makes sense.
Very, very nice, but he wrote the book.  Trouble understanding his teaching in class=trouble understanding the book=not much of a chance of succeeding in the class!
Very friendly guy, excellent teacher.
No Comments
Really nice guy.
No Comments

Learning from a professor is not just about knowledge. It is far more important to learn things like character, attitude toward teaching, attitude toward students, and values as a leader. In that regard, you score zero.

You significantly contribute to a toxic atmosphere within the Duke Financial Econometrics group. It was no surprise that similarly offensive and aggressive faculty members like JL or BW joined the group, reproducing the nasty atmosphere of the research group.
"MY ANSWER IS NO." This person is twisted.
The TA is much more helpful than him. He does not give you any substantial help when you encounter problems.

You can tell he really puts in the effort in preparing lectures, so listening and participating in class would really help you. Has an interesting policy where you can drop any graded thing (especially the midterm, it was rough) and allocate those weights to your final. Learnt a lot, but overall the material is really dry and not simulating.
A terrible educator. Why do you work in academia if you treat students in an offensive manner?
I didn't have lots of positive experience interacting with him. He may be famous but does not know how to be a good professor.
Do not ascribe your decision to a student to justify yourself. Disgraceful. If one is not enrolled in your course, should he get blamed for not having worked on a problem set? Absurd.
A nasty person creates a vicious cycle in academia. A nasty person gathers nasty colleagues and reproduces other nasty academic descendants in academia.

Lecture heavy, nice guy but not too engaging. The material is similar to econ 372 and isnt that bad if you stay up to date with weekly quizzes etc. If you have an option to take an easier elective do it, but if youre really interested in portfolio management as a career this is a good class
Not a very useful class if you want to work at some famous financial companies. This class is very theory based.

Very clear-cut lectures that make it easy to understand the materials, as long as you pay attention in class or take the time to read the slide notes. Kind and accommodating professor who always tries to help and puts effort into engaging the class. He is also a respectable figure in the academia world and a chill, funny person in real life.

Respectfully, people are being way too harsh. He is a great professor, super funny, and is willing to explain concepts to you if you just ask indivudally. He is very passionate about what he teaches and can simplify very hard concepts. My only caveat is that I took the class in a small group setting, but it is definitely worth your while.

Such an awesome professor -- class is super interesting and applicable if you have an interest in finance. Great at explaining concepts and cares about getting to know students. Very chill and funny guy.

Tim is a really great guy - amazing at explaining and so passionate about what he does. The difficulty of the class is high because of the nature of the content and not Tim. Haven't finished the course yet but should be a good ending !

Tim is a great professor. Not sure why the other reviews are so negative. He's a genuinely great guy who cares about his students and wants them to do well. Really approachable and tries his best to make the material as clear as possible.
Professor Tim is awesome. He is great at explaining concepts(cause he built one of the most widely used models out there). Work hard and this would be an easy class.
Fantastic prof, laughs at basically everything, just show up and put the work in. Really good lecturer and explains concepts very well. Also super cracked dude in the econ world.

He is arrogant in front of students. I asked him questions multiple times, but he answered them impatiently.  I would rather have some more friendly professors teaching this class.  He only knows how to research not how to teach.

A relatively easy 400-level elective and basically an extension of Econ 372. Weekly quizzes (pretty chill), a midterm, 2 HW, and a final that can be used to replace all other grades. Didn't spend time on this course except for one week before exams. The prof/TA doesn't like giving partial credits though, so the grading can be harsh (10 pts or 0).
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Really enjoyed 471. Engaging lectures and  quizzes + p-sets were both useful and interesting. Definitely got a lot out of this class.

He does not care about his students. He acts very above students, and when asked a question, he doesn't even bother to understand what they asked. I hate when professor is involved In research but doesn't know how to teach. He is the perfect example of that.

Professor Bollerslev doesn't care about his students. He is very rigid, and there is no flexibility. I sent him a super friendly email asking for an extension, and what I got back was aggressive and rude. He started off the email with capitalized "NO" and barely read my explanations as to why I missed an assignment. This class is not useful at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Even though he is famous, he is indeed hard to work with. Sometimes you will feel he is quite condescending when answering your questions. Maybe he thinks the class is too easy and not worthwhile for him to put effort into really teaching students. I wish I could take other similar courses in Econ department or Fuqua if I have a chance.
His lecture is interesting overall, but he is not approachable to students after class. He never held office hours and answered questions impatiently.

An enlightening course! One of the most famous financial econometrician in the world. For the tests, if you fully understand most of the problems in the back of textbook and practice exams, you'll be fine. The stuff you learned, which will benefit your personal investment and financial career, is absolutely more important than a letter!

Professor Bollerslev was great -- very comprehensive, went through the material well, and was very accommodating and quick to respond. The final was not bad, assuming that you had read his slides and attempted a problem set or two. Definitely recommend

The class is difficult, yes, but the material is interesting - especially if you're invested in finance. Your grade depends on the final. You have to stay on top of the material as it builds quickly (do the end of chapter questions). The man is a genius though and does a good job of explaining the concepts.
Nice guy but often unclear in expectations  tests hard to prepare for

Terrible lecturer... He gave the hardest test and the final i have ever taken in my 17 years of being a student. If I had studied 10 more days for each of them, i could still not get a good grade on either because they were both irrelevant to what he "taught" in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: I took ECON 471 with Bollerslev. He was a terrible lecturer. Most of what he says is unintelligible, he speaks very silently and repeats the limited info on his slides. All grading is based on one midterm and final - both extremely hard and not related to course material. Worst experience @ Duke. There is a reason why he teaches and not trades.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Was his first time teaching 250 (Fall 23). Lectures were ok, exams were harder than Bletsch's but still very doable if you understood the material. Class content is really interesting (If you are debating between 210 and 250 i'd recommend 250, im CS). Start homeworks early, debugging assembly takes forever.

Would highly recommend, but the final project is the most brutal thing ever. Had to sleep in the lab for 2 days, and I did not procrastinate on it. However, it is super cool when it works and I feel like I know digital systems extremely well now. Even so, if I had to redo, I would take again and would recommend it for sure.

Such a great professor, makes learning very fun. Projects and homework are also super fun and definitely is not a lot of work if you are good with time organization. No final, just a final project you can work on with a partner.

Prof. Board is a super interesting guy. His class may be hard, but he really wants students to succeed. He relates all concepts to real-world scenarios, and only a few main topics are included on exams/final. Projects are definitely tough and at times discouraging, but the TAs in this class actually do God's work and need to be paid more.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: One of the few professors who will make sure you learn. Class will be tough but completely worth it, you will come out of class having a very strong understanding beyond just being able to do midterm style questions. One of the best educators here at Duke, tough but inspiring.
This course is definitely less work than 210, however you should avoid Board if you are a woman or minority. He often says that Duke CS is becoming "too inclusive".
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: A great class with interesting but long homework assignments. The professor is very knowledgeable and passionate about the subject. However, he can tend to skip over some topics assuming students know things they may not.

Very knowledgeable professor. Lectures are interesting but they can go on for really long and are also not very interactive. Overall is a great instructor, but the main piece of advice is to start the homework assignments early, they are assigned about 3-4 weeks ahead of the due date and are very tedious especially to debug.

Dr. Board is great, but this class is an insane amount of work. Weekly labs (that don't give you any credit), written homework, programming homework, then a huge final project and an 8 page report. I learned a lot, but it is way too packed with assignments.

Suffered through that semester; homeworks were very time consuming and difficult to debug. By the end of the semester most people didn't come to his lecture and only watched Bletsch online version. Ended up curving the final a LOT so a large portion of the class either got an A or an A+, but this does not forgive how long the projects took
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: LOVE love this class and Board's effortless humor. Board is a genius and he knows it. His lectures are not super beginner-friendly, since this was his first time teaching 250 and he overestimated how much we already knew. But once you get the concepts with a little googling, his explanations blow your mind. Fav class at Duke, highly recommend.

As an ECE student, I found the C/MIPS projects a lot more difficult then the hardware projects, but overall found all of the assignments interesting when completing them. Lectures covered a lot more specifics then you needed, but if you pay attention, you will get most of the jokes Dr. Board makes. Recitation was extremely useful.

Class itself usually isn't hard when its taught by Bletch but Board made the midterm way harder having to curve both the midterm and final up. But even with this curve, he curved down out homework grades which are worth 55% of our grade so that a 94% would be a B+. Lecture were bad too, everyone I know in the class only watched Bletchs old ones.

I was very disappointed with this class. The lectures are dense and unclear, and he teaches the topics as if they are trivial. The exams and homeworks are extremely hard. He also curved the class down without giving any warning. Overall a cool and chilled guy but maybe he just wasn't meant to teach a beginner architecture course like this.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Worst downwards "linear transformation" (aka curve) I've ever witnessed - an 80% in the HW category translated to a D+. He is a great professor and very respected, but I will NEVER take a course with Prof. Board again because of this.

It's 100% worth it to go to lecture: Dr. Board is a great lecturer and many of the homework problems are from concepts covered in lecture. The processor and final project are a lot of work (so definitely start early), but the midterms end up being pretty easy.

Prof Board is one of the best professors in the ECE department. He is also the head of the IT deparment at Duke and is extremely knowladgable about everything tech at this school. ECE350 is also an amazing class so take it if you can!

Dr. Board is a legend. He's been teaching at Duke for like 40 years and he clearly knows a ton about the subject. This class is challenging but very rewarding if you put in honest effort. Every ECE student should take this class.

This class is a TON of work. Board is an amazing lecturer and provides plenty of resources to help you succeed, but you really need to put in a lot of time to be successful. That being said, every ECE student at Duke should take this course, and the assignments were tough but were definitely a lot of fun.

Dr. Board is awesome! He lectures clearly, and provides slides/recordings outside of class. His tests aren't as bad as he says they are, and there's lots of partial credit. The projects, while challenging, are completely doable (but start early). Start the final project EARLY. Like, before it's assigned. Office hours/Ed posts are very helpful.

The second half of the semester is a lot of work in project form but also very rewarding. You don't really need to go to lectures to do well but Board's lectures are entertaining, enjoyable, and help to prepare for the midterms. Slides and course expectations are very clear; you can get the grade you want if you start early and put in the time.

Dr. Board brings an unparalleled amount of passion to the course: his lectures are all engaging and well-crafted, he assists in every lab section, and he is willing to answer all questions in and out of the classroom. The class has a lot of work, but there is a lot of support and lenient grading. Absolute pleasure to take a class with him!
Board is an amazing prof and a decent lecturer. You'll learn a bunch and have a lot of fun if you don't procrastinate. You can get the grade you want as long as you're willing to spend the time.

Dr. Board is the kind of professor you wish you had for every class. He is very knowledgeable in the field and a very good lecturer. No textbook, slides give you all the info you need and are very clear and easy to understand. This class is by far the hardest ECE classes I've taken, but he really does try his best to make it less painful.

Amazing lecturer. Eccentric, but in a good way. Homeworks and exams tended to have a lot of annoying pencil-and-paper problems, but projects were interesting. He is very busy and has a lot of responsibilities on campus, but he is deliberate about making time for students.

Dr. Board is awesome! He's funny, interesting, knowledgable and everything else you'd like to see in a professor. I especially like how his homework sets are designed to maximize learning what's discussed in lectures. His class ECE550 is a class which touches upon nearly all the fundamentals involved in Computer Systems. Must take!
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Tests? Not many--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Professor Board is the man. Smarter than you will ever be, and is a great lecturer. I recommend taking any class you can get with him.
Great professor, cares a lot about his class and is extremely knowledgeable. The lectures didn't really help with the lab work, but they were still interesting and enjoyable to attend.

Easily one of the best Professors at Duke. Has been around for so long and knows so much about technology its insane. Grad level class, was super easy and interesting. Basically reading for every class that you could not do because we would go over it in class anyway. Theres one presentation and a final project.
Fantastic teacher, really gets to know the students and is always willing to answer questions and help on their projects.  Classes are frequently opened up for discussion.
He was a really good teacher. He's helpful, and the curriculum was well organized. The material in this class is really hard, but having him as a teacher makes it better.

Knows his stuff well, and always willing to help you out if you need it.  Aside from labs, the class is fairly open-ended and Dr. Board expects that you'll be able to pick up a lot of the material yourself.  I enjoy this approach; some people don't.  The best class I've taken at Duke.

The homework will make you want to kill yourself, the labs are unending, and you probably won't sleep for the last month of the semester.  However, Dr. Board does whatever he can to get you through, and you WILL know your stuff after his class.  In fact, maybe even a little too well...
Board is an entertaining, energetic lecturer.  He's no pushover, though.

Assigns projects that enhance the student understanding's of that topic. Very clear on his expectations. It's a hard class, but he makes life easier for you by being available almost all the time when a major proj is due. If you get an A/A-, the final exam is optional.

Super kind and accessible. Great Professor. I really enjoyed taking Math 219 with him.

Some helpful things to know: Classes follow a flipped classroom structure (make sure to watch videos and read textbook) & Dante writes his own midterms, but the final exam is common between all teachers.
Great professor, very chill guy.

Great class format. Since his previous reviews, he's switched up his class format and adapted - adding a flipped classroom with problem-solving during lecture time. I would argue his class was the most-prepared out of all the 219-classes the semester I took it. Great guy.

Dante is friendly professor. He uses a flipped classroom format which is not very helpful though. The videos we need to watch for homework do not have detailed explanations and are very long. The in-class exercises are helpful for exams but his teaching gets confusing sometimes.

Dante was a great professor. He clearly cares about his students and takes time to answer questions and make sure you understand the content. He provides lots of office hours, even going as far has having office hours every day leading up to the final exam. His lectures are engaging and extremely helpful. He really wants everyone to succeed.

Dante is awesome. His lectures are great, he loves to take questions and ensure you understand the topics. I love his humor and he creates a fun classroom environment. I was in a small class, so going to every lecture was super beneficial. Love him!

Amazing lecturer- really took the time to get us to understand the material! Always ready to meet outside lectures when I needed it! 

Love the accent!

Dante was far from a good professor. He needs to learn how to teach. His accent is quite thick, and his jokes are...
He tried to be caring for all students, but he clearly has favorites. I would tell you to run as fast as possible from Dante!! Do not take any class with him at all costs! I got the grade in this class by pure luck!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class isn't the hardest. The lectures aren't really a value-add, so nobody pays attention. Marta is kind.

Marta simply has no idea what she is doing. Her lectures are not comprehensive, engaging, or coherent. Her criteria is very vague and sometimes she just gets upset (ex. confiscated computers in lecture). She claimed her final would be just like midterms but failed to mention she wouldn't curve it at all, like midterms. Do not take with her
Pretty bad. Did not curve the final. She was dropped on us like a bomb. Take 201 with literally anyone else

I enjoyed taking Econ 201 with Marta. She is always accessible to ask questions after class. Her style of exam is very different from that of previous Econ 201 teachers, but in many ways her exams are actually better. Her lectures are fun, but attendance is mandatory (qwickly twice each class).
I actually love her idk what everyone's on about
Good course content, but could be better on delivery of the content. Finished semester having self studied the entire course, so did not really see the point of attending classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: One of the worst, if not the worst professor I have ever had. Completely incompetent at teaching, disingenuous in course policies, no sympathy, no compassion whatsoever. Should be terminated from the university without a second glance. Also, TAs should also be fired, worst I have ever seen, you'd think they were sent from prison to guard exams.

Really easy class, people just hate on her because she wasn't Nechyba. She still uses Nechyba's grade rounding system so the class gets the exact same grades they got with him. 55% of the grade is participation and the other 45% is very generously rounded. She wasn't the best lecturer ever, but she got better as she went along.
Anyone else just straight up not have a grade in Econ 201 rn …

Marta doesn't understand how to run a lecture. She's inflexible and unrealistic about grades, assignments, and especially exams. Marta chose to use the preceding professor's modules, his notes, his textbook, and his homework, but then she writes her own tests which are nothing like anything we cover in class. Doesn't allow laptops in class.

Terrible professor. Had to self-study for everything and Nechyba's videos were infinitely more useful than class. Has a victim mentality about her incompetence and it affects the way she responds to anything that can in some way be regarded as criticism (extensions, regrade requests even). Running grade is an A DESPITE her, not bc of her
Don't love the class or the way she teaches it, but not nearly as bad as some ppl think. econ 201 is notorious for having low exam grades and people are making a big deal

At first, admittedly, I was very critical but then I realized that she's actually not as bad as everyone makes her out to seem. She's a very sweet lady who I believe cares about her students. 55% of the class is whether you put in any effort, and even though the midterms are tough, they are only 11% of your grade each. It ain't so bad.
Jesus. Give the lady a break. She's bad, but these reviews are just mean.
midterm 1 was horrendous, but till midterm 2 she made things much better. her dog aint bad either

When you pay 92 thousand dollars a year for an education, you expect to be taught the material you will be tested on. No, Marta says, you "will not be handheld." So I am paying this school 92 THOUSAND DOLLARS PER YEAR to be told by my professor that she doesn't really need to teach us and that we essentially need to learn the material ourselves.
She is improving as a teacher hugely, and didn't deserve all this exaggerated criticism

Much of the criticism she is getting is unwarranted. The midterm was tough but not impossible. All the material was either covered on the homework, lecture, or assigned textbook readings. The curve was generous and the material isn't that difficult if you put effort into understanding it by reading the textbook and doing practice problems.
people are overreacting
I owe everything I know in this class to Gavin Burns. Marta is clueless, but Gavin is the second coming of Nechyba.

The midterm was hard, but it was not nearly as bad as everyone is saying. Honestly, she's curving it by too much. There's no reason that someone who got a 50% should get an A. She's not great and her lectures are confusing, but everyone is overreacting. You should be thanking her if you failed the test and are still getting an A or a B.

Marta is...
A comedian, joking through examples with kinder bueno vs kinder joys.
A pioneer, inventing exams that perplex even geniuses.
A storyteller, crafting cliffhangers with unsolved questions.
A historian, dwelling on problems from 25 years ago.
A statistician, citing normal midterm scores (mean: 45, sd: 20) to justify our grasp of material.
She leaked everyones grades, how is this legal

While she is a terrible teacher, one of her TAs have really helped me reach a good grade on the first midterm. Reach out to Gavin Burns, he personally helped me before the exam and clarified concepts much better than Marta could dream of.
Marta is a nice person and people overreact but her midterms and lectures are genuinely confusing... like our collective understanding is clearly not the problem
While I'm sure she's a nice person, she just does not know how to teach and Nechyba's modules and textbook do all the teaching for her. Nechyba, please come back.

Just silly at this point. I'm all for hard content but when you get an email saying the exams should be nothing like what you've studied you just stare into an eternal abyss and wonder if you're insane. This is the second econ class for the major, not a phd quantum mechanics problem set. GIVE ME A BREAK!

I'm sorry but if the class average is failing then the professor failed. Then she had the audacity to blame us for expecting to be handheld through life? No, I expect to actually learn the material that will be on the exam. She confuses herself during lectures and often tells us to disregard 30 min worth of lecture time because she made a mistake.
I'm a TA for this class and I feel great fear for these kiddos. It's bad. The TA's have still yet to even have a meeting with her.

Super unreasonable tests which are very difficult as well as completely unrelated to the resources provided. 201 is supposed to be a core class but is made to be not only a weeder but the lectures are very unclear and often times confusing. She is unwilling to consider student inputs and very stressful experince. Take with Nechyba if possible

Her teaching in lecture makes zero sense and just makes the videos we did for homework even more confusing. The first midterm she made for us was literally impossible and the median score was a 45%. She then tried to say that the next test will be even harder. This is the most absurd teaching/difficulty of exams in the History OF DUKE.

Professor Boczon's class has been, by far, my worst experience at Duke thus far. Her lectures are rambling and incomprehensible, her exams are impossible, her homeworks take hours, and, perhaps most importantly, she seems to have a clear disdain for her students. She isn't receptive to constructive feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: content covered in class and on homework is NOT representative of the content on the midterm. i think i could've had her dog taken the exam for me and gotten the same grade. NECHYBA PLEASE COME BACK I'M SO SORRY
Brutally hard and with no remorse
Midterm was lwk light

Just not a good teacher. People say she's a nice person, but any criticism is met with condescending responses to defend herself, as apparently she is incapable of doing any wrong, ever. Poor watson probably has to deal with this cognitive dissonance every day. Be ready to trauma bond with your classmates over this.
Just ridiculous. The first midterm was significantly harder than the old exams and the lectures don't help whatsoever. Avoid at all costs
STUDENTS BEWARE: DO NOT TAKE ECON 201 WITH HER.
Don't take it for your own good

genuinely the worst professor i've ever had. this woman should never teach a class ever again. i have no idea who let her teach this course but someone needs to do something about this because i am not paying 95k for a professor who lied about her exams format/structure/questions, cannot answer questions, and confuses herself with her own lectures
VERY sweet lady but terrible teacher. If the whole class constantly has no idea what's going on, something needs to change.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. The lectures are so hard to understand, and she does not know how to teach in a lecture hall setting. The home works take 4 hours to complete and is nothing like that midterm. Midterm was genuinely the hardest test I have ever taken in my life. The only thing I was sure of was writing my name correctly on the sheet.

Professor Boczon is very kind, and I do think that she means well and is quite smart. That said, her teaching is absolutely awful and there is a massive disparity between the content she assigns (lectures, homework, textbooks written and taught by Nechyba) versus her lectures and, of course, her exams.
Truly listen to every word she said, and didn't understand one
Worst ever?

Firstly, her lessons aren't always correct. She will pause mid-lecture, have a student re-correct some of her work, or simply promise to review the content next class and never review it. Next, to prepare for a midterm, she released a practice midterm with incorrect answers and illegible handwriting. Actual midterm was nothing like it.
Worst class
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Nechyba, if you happen to see this, we sincerely apologize for our behavior in Econ 101. If you choose to return and teach Econ 201, I promise to never miss another lecture again.
Nechyba please come back.
This class is a DISASTER. It literally feel like prison. Lectures make no sense and she messes up in class so much. AV
Econ department should not have made her teach this class. Everything is nechyba except for the exams. Couldn't understand most of the problems.

Awful professor. The videos are made by Nechyba for Nechyba's lectures and tests. She uses all his content but her lectures do not flow the same way and the tests are nothing like the practice tests or videos. Her midterm was unlike anything even related to the content we'd practiced throughout the semester.
I can't do it anymore

She is a horrible teacher. She tries to be sweet but she doesn't know how to teach. Everyone failed the first midterm and she blamed us for not studying enough and told us we need to work harder. The material on the test was 100x harder than what we did in class and so different from all the practice she told us to do like so different not fair

i know this class is not supposed to be easy but the way prof boczon runs it is terrible. our pre-class videos to teach us content is by prof nechyba, the textbook is written by prof nechyba. the homework's are designed by nechyba. and the midterm is made by prof boczon which is 10x harder than any exam nechyba has released in the past 10 years.
So far worst professor at duke. Spent class time explaining problems and getting the answer wrong herself.
didn't explain economic concepts well in class, very hard to learn from and not many office hours before the tests.

The reviews on Marta are only in the wake of a difficult midterm. Give her grace. it's her first time teaching this class. Its a big jump from 101 which was the easiest class at duke. Its not easy but its not her fault, most of this is new content.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Terrible professor. messed up in class all the time.
Terrible, horrible, no good, very bad
Terrible prof

Boczon, not Bokzon—but she's so atrocious, I couldn't care less. Nechyba ran this class like a well-oiled machine. Then she took over and promptly set it on fire. Her lectures are rambling black holes of confusion, she freezes mid-problem like a crashed Windows 98, and her exams might as well be written in hieroglyphics. Avoid at all costs.

Marta just tries to make the tests as hard as possible and she makes minimal effort in making sure the content is conveyed to the class coherently. The test are not at all representative of the class content and as a result many students end up losing interest in microeconomics

Does not know how to teach properly and makes tests hard as hell, doesn't give proper study materials either. The test didn't even match the same format as the previous practice tests. Lectures are super confusing and barely understand anything.

You'll probably never take a class from her since she is a temporary professor, but my god the midterm was something from hell. Probably got like a 10% on that thing. Do not, I repeat DO NOT take a class with her. Seems like a nice enough person I guess though.
DON'T TAKE THIS CLASS FROM THIS PROFESSOR!!!

Professor Boczon is extremely unorganized and impossible to follow. Their teaching is unclear, and lectures feel like a waste of time. No effort to engage students or explain concepts properly. Frustrating and disappointing. One of the worst I've ever seen.

Quintessential example of a class where you get out what you put in. Can get away with doing nothing at all and getting a fine grade, or you can actively participate, read the material, and think about the questions he asks. He lets you thoroughly examine the economics of wealth both broadly and in an area you are interested in. Amazing class.

pretty dry lectures with boring slides, attendance wasn't required and not many people went to class because of that / you really didn't need to, discussion sections were same way so you'd only go if you needed help, class was basically all the exams that weren't crazy hard, this is def one of the easier econ classes

Prof. Brent is a very engaging and charismatic lecturer and it was clear 311 (class on wealth and inequality) is his passion. I learned a lot from the reading assignments and the in-class presentations were fun and interesting too. Would definitely recommend one of his 300-level electives.

This has been my favorite class I've ever taken at Duke. I feel like I have such a good handle on economic thought / ideas now, and a better handle on how to reflect on the behaviors of the ultra-wealthy. The reading and writing assignments in this class were fascinating and always worth engaging with. I grew as a writer and a person in this class.
Overall, I feel like the structure of his class wasn't all that clear and his lectures weren't that helpful, but he was readily available outside the class to help you with anything.

Loved having Professor Brent. A genuine professor who cares deeply about the topic and his students. He is always accessible to talk more or provide feedback. Although there is a lot of reading, he covers content carefully in lectures if you pay close attention.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Super interesting, and I'm glad I took this class. I have nothing bad to say about Prof. Brent, since if you put in the work, you'll end up with the grade you want. He's very responsive to requests for feedback or input on any assignment.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Very interesting class topics, and assignments were not too difficult, but at times it seemed like grading was a little arbitrary. As long as you put in genuine effort into papers and midterms (both the midterm and final were take home), then it shouldn't be too difficult to get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Great class overall. Prof. Brent has really interesting lectures, and you can tell that he really loves the topic; this makes for entertaining discussions. His grading's super clear, and his feedback's always reasonable. He's willing to help out with assignments and generally go the extra mile for you.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I absolutely loved the history of economic thought. He is such a passionate and caring professor and you can tell that he really loves the subject. The readings were interesting and appropriate in length and he was very accessible leading up to the due dates of essays!

This class is basically AP Stats, so if you took that in high school 104 is super easy. Brent's slides are filled with typos and there's no recordings so if you don't know much about stats you should go to class. The tests also varied in difficulty a lot, but the final (which was basically just a third midterm) was pretty easy.

Terrible lecturer, makes me fall asleep 95% of the time. He made numerous errors on the midterms, and had to correct himself while we were writing. Content is not too difficult though, especially if you have a good group working on the problem sets together. Lecture notes also posted online which were kind of helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: TERRIBLE CLASS AND TEACHING SKILLS. his lectures make sense only about half of the time, and he mumbles so hardly anyone can hear him. never sit in the back, especially during the stata lectures, because you cannot see anything. his tests are literally so hard and he makes so many mistakes that half the blackboard is covered in corrections.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Not nearly as bad as what other reviews suggest. Attend class, take notes, do the Psets, and you'll be okay. Lectures and psets were mistake-ridden but mistakes were always corrected and weren't as big of a hurdle as other comments suggest. 

Don't avoid 104 just bc Prof Brent is teaching! Very possible and he is far from the worst prof at Duke.

Worst Professor of my life. Had to stop both our midterm and our final exam multiple times to correct the exams because he made mistakes in them. During class he constantly needs to be corrected on the material he is teaching. Genuinely do not think he knows what he's teaching. Strongly advise to never take a class with him.

Easy A as long as you pay attention during class. Not a lot of work besides the semester modeling project and the model essays, but as long as you have structure in your writing (roadmap in the intro + line of reasoning) and check in w/ him regularly for your project, you'll breeze by. Very supportive and accessible outside of class.

Took Econ104 with him in Fall 2023. Got a 50% on the first midterm when I was consistently going to class, and an 85% on the (harder) midterm where I skipped every single class and learned the content by myself. Feel like that says enough about him as a teacher. The actual content isn't terribly hard but he's just an awful teacher.

Lacks the attention to detail required to teach a kindergarten math class, yet is teaching statistics at Duke University. Lecture slides, homework, practice exams, practice exam solutions, and the EXAMS themselves have multiple (6+ individual errors on exam 2 corrected as people noticed them). 

Save yourself the pain.

If you are a Focus student, ignore all of the reviews for his other class. This class is AMAZING and Jason is truly a fantastic professor. He gives very good, personal feedback and really just wants you to learn. I was nervous coming into his class because of his RMP but I am SO glad that I took this class with him. You will not regret it.

nothing against him personally. HOWEVER- DONOTAKETHISCLASSWITHHIM. cannotlecture without making 10 mistakes on own content, tests constant mistakes in them. how class goes: he goes here's an interesting concept, spends 30 minutes explaining it you get even more confused going out of class then coming into class. fun guy though if you talk to him.

Do not take. Brent cannot teach. Might be the worst class I've taken at Duke spare yourself. The lectures just make me more confused. Counting down the days until I am done with this class. Midterms are too hard and don't reflect what we cover in class. Brent also makes so many errors it is maddening.

This class was a super interesting look into how economists have analyzed the wealthy over time. Jason's lectures were always intriguing, and there was a lot of good class discussion. Many of the sources we read for class gave unique perspectives into the lives of the wealthy. I would recommend this elective to anyone interested in economics!

LOVE HIM!! He creates an exciting discussion based atmosphere about all sorts of interesting concepts. Always happy to meet and help. The courses readings are mostly modern and fun reads. He is amazing at seminar style classes.. Take if you're even remotely interested about the super wealthy. Changed my perspective and had a lot of fun!!!

This contributed to my regret of partaking in the FOCUS program. The class was extremely boring, with the occasional engaging activities. Few essays/writings compose most of the grade. Barely learned anything lol

P sets were easy to get good grades on bc you could work in groups of up to 3 + there were help sessions. Tests were pretty easy bc we got 3 cheat sheets + he gave us very similar practice problems but I would've rather had a better teacher with harder tests bc he constantly made mistakes + the easy tests made the avgs too high for a curved class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Jason Brent was single-handedly my worst professor in my entire Duke career. He does not even understand econometrics himself, much less how to explain it to other people! He literally does not care at all and makes typos everywhere, including in exams. Said he was busy when we asked for help. He is "nice" - that's bare minimum!!

Literally, this class is so easy, but Brent made the class completely unenjoyable and difficult. First of all, the class is graded on 3 things: 30% homework, 30% Midterm, 40% final. 2 tests and homework. Again the class itself is not bad but he is a bad professor. He also made a 95 an A. Do not take this class with Brent take it with anyone else

I LOVE ECON 104!!!!! It is my favorite class at Duke. Don't listen to the haters; I wake up thinking about 104 and I go to bed thinking about 104. Engaging content, incredible lectures, highlight of every single week. Take this class if you have the opportunity. If you miss it, that sucks for you. Jason is amazing and I would do anything for him.

Brent is a very boring lecturer and manages to not know what he is teaching 90% of the time. Worst lecturer I have ever had. Had to teach most of the information to myself before tests as did friends.

While Professor Brent is a nice guy, his class is very difficult to (1) pay attention in, and (2) understand anything. He is an incredibly boring lecturerand can be quite confusing at times. Moreover, unless you have a foundation in statistics going into the class, it can be difficult to get a grasp of the content.
Gives test questions that are harder than homework problems, deductions are ambiguous and unforgiving.

I had Brent for 311 in the fall. Class included a lot of readings and discussions but they are extremely rewarding for an Econ student like me who has never taken a history class at Duke. Prof. Brent is one of the most personable and caring teachers I have had at Duke. If you put in enough effort, the grade will come. Take his class!!

One of the most engaging lecturers I've ever had at duke. The class consisted of 3 papers/presentations which weren't too hard at all as well as a weekly blog post. There are a lot of readings, and I recommend doing them to get the most out of the class, but you can get away without doing them.

I really enjoyed ECON190FS with Dr. Brent and would recommend it to anyone! This class is the reason why I am considering being an economics major, and I found the lectures to be highly interesting. The grading also was not super harsh, and everything we learned is applicable to real life. If you're in MESS, take this class!

Probably one of my favorite professors at Duke because of how engaging he made his lectures in a very niche subject. He genuinely wanted every student to do well. However, as previously stated, I think there were problems with organizing the scheduling of assignments. 60% of our grade was based on the last two weeks of the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Prof Brent is a very kind person. Lectures tend to be slow & repetitive. Material in 104 is quite basic, but the midterm averages are really low because the TA grading is very all-or-nothing. Hardly any homeworkmaybe 1 hour/2 weeks. Not a hard class but be carefulthere are only 2 exams (which make 70% of the grade).

Professor Brent is a good lecturer and tries to keep his students engaged. He goes over some topics quickly, but he reviews them the next class to clarify any questions. He is accessible outside of class and always takes the time to answer questions. Just be aware that this course only has three grades: problem sets, midterm, and final.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Top notch professor. Good lecturer, interesting content. All exams are extremely easy time and difficulty-wise and unlimited open notes and calculator. Tells you exact topics on exams. No work outside class barring a 1 hour problem set every two weeks. Drops lowest 2 of 6 problem sets. Should be an easy A unless you are an athlete and don't try.

Professor Brent is clearly new to teaching Econ 104, his explanations of many of the concepts fail to truly explain them. The midterm was way more difficult than any problem set or example problems given. Gets lost and stumbles on his words during class on many occasions.

Professor Brent is an amazing lecturer and is somehow able to make Economic concepts that come off as dry in other courses interesting and relevant to our lives. He's always available outside of class to talk about paper topics and support you in brainstorming the strongest argument. 100% recommend!

I am a last-semester senior, and this is by far the most engaging class I've taken at Duke. Brent is funny, kind, and has an amazing ability to convert dry readings into practical and relatable lectures. This will probably be the only notebook I save from college, so I can engage in educated conversations about economic issues in the real world.
Hilariously cynical. Really makes you think about what the economics department is teaching you. Highly recommended

Grade is made up of participation, attendance, weekly blog posts, one 750 word essay, and a final 15 page essay. There will also be reading to do for each class, but it's up to you to do. Really great subject for learning how to think critically about economic models and learning the arguments of past, important thinkers.

Took History of Economic Thought. Amazing class, amazing lecturer, I learned a ton from him. He made dry readings interesting and he made people actually want to come to class discussions and lectures. 6 papers total, including 20 page term paper (which is made up of 3 5-page papers written throughout the semester). Highly recommend.

Fair class, lectures are dense so if you can find time to review it's really helpful. Exams are similar to past ones and only cover what you learn in lecture (not as demanding as exams in some other subjects), but again takes some time to memorize.

Fair class, lectures are dense so finding time to review them at least once really helps in building understanding. Exams are similar to previous ones but sometimes picks niche things to ask about bc he just feels like it. If you study you can do well

Broad framing for test questions, but wants a specific response for full credit; hard to get through a lecture (online esp.), as you can easily doze off; new exam policy on assigned seating given minutes before the final exam, but OK. Interesting subject, but discussed in a dull manner. Pretty strict, I think.
Interesting topics, hard to stay focused watching lectures as they are boring. I fall asleep. extra credit can easily boost grade by 3-3.5% if it's just done
so so boring

The class is pretty fair, exams are similar to the problem sets and past midterms (which he releases all old tests). Gave a lot of extra credit at the end, giving a generous grade boost. Class is recorded and not too much work outside of exams. Further, the class content is pretty interesting and Coggins is clearly passionate about the subject.
Mid and boring. class wasn't too hard, but pmo

Questionable dude, and lectures can be dense, but still a very interesting class. Extra credit is very generous and a 2-3% grade boost is easily possible. Very low workload outside of midterms. Its very doable to do well if you stay on top of things just study hard since theres tons of content and exams can be tough but are fair.

If he cares so much about attendance that he's ok with sabotaging the entire class by giving exams that aren't representative of the material covered, then he should just make attendance a mandatory part of the grade. Not to mention he showed up late to the final and gave exams that were missing half the pages. Truly a miserable class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you're in biochem you prob don't have a choice. last third of the class is the most interesting. Coggins is NOT a great lecturer + slides are v dense. Content for the second exam is A LOT of info. But, there's to 3.5 extra credit points added to your final grade! I struggled in orgo but did well in biochem bc of the million practice exams

Coggins is incredibly knowledgeable and gets you inspired, because he genuinely believes in the importance of biochem in our lives. Material was interesting, but lectures sometimes got dull (just 3x a week, repetitiveness). He is petty and tests on material he spent little time on, but explicitly mentions what he doesn't test. 1000 past exams help.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Coggins was solid. He gave up to 3.5% in EC added to your final course grade, which I think is very generous of him. His tests are straightforward, just a lot of memorization. Never went to lecture and he faithfully posts recordings so just watch those. Good prof!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I wouldn't listen to the Coggins hate. He teaches you everything you need to know, no more and no less. The tests are very fair with predictable questions and lots of available practice. An A in an uncurved class can be difficult but he is very generous with extra credit. Opt into SAGE and go to lecture!

Petty, unforgiving, bends the rubric against you, and will test on extremely low-yield material if a lot of people skipped the class. Exams are weighed very heavily, so a bad test day can make it exponentially harder to get a good grade. I stopped looking both ways when crossing my street on my way to lecture. Would not take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lecture slides were updated so they were better than in previous years. Tests are graded pretty harshly and they look for things that aren't explicitly asked for in the question. But do regrade requests and he's pretty fair. Some extra credit opportunities although less than previous semesters. Do all the previous tests he gives and you'll be fine

Un-curved class can be difficult not impossible. Attendance is not mandatory but keep up with class and weekly quizzes or else you'll be overwhelmed quickly. Very stingy with extra credit. Provides lots of good resources--practice tests, Ed, problem sets, etc. Every detail from lecture matters. The heaviest memorization class I've taken
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: BRUH BEC did not teach us the material that is on his exams!! Very hard to learn when you are being taught material up until the week of the exams. it was so annoying.
Does not care about his students and you can tell.
What a careless prof... Did not stay true to his word about problem sets, exams, or anything really.

I would not listen to these other 5/5 reviews. He's recently changed up his course structure and its a lot worse now. He canceled our last extra credit project with barely notice because he 'didn't have time.' He's grouping the topics a bit differently, making the course worse as opposed to better, and doesn't even have office hours. Terrible prof.
BRUH BEC did not teach us the material that is on his exams!! Very hard to learn when you are being taught material up until the week of the exam..

While the semester hasn't finished yet, I wanted to say that Coggins has been an awesome professor. He's a chill dude, willing to answer questions before/after classes, and does a great job of explaining things in lecture. His slides are great, he gives Xtra Cred opportunities, and his tests are quite fair. he makes a difficult subject fun to learn

Coggins is a straightforward lecturer, but this class is a lot of memorization. Go to every lecture and annotate slides by copying down everything he says. Tests are fair, he won't ask a question on something he hasn't taught. But, he can be petty and will test on lectures that were the least attended. Extra credit gives a good boost to your grade.

Dr. Coggins teaches you all the biochem information you need to know and the class is very informational & tests are fair, but the class is taught in a boring manner & there is lots of content to memorize. Try your best to stay on top of the material.

Dr. Coggins teaches biochemistry well in the most objective sense. While the lectures themselves could've been more interesting, everything was very fair. The tests are formatted with some open-ended questions which require you to demonstrate a strong understanding of the content. He gave out some extra credit opportunities which were cool.

impatient when we ask questions after lecture and tells us to rewatch the lecture or says he doesnt know how to answer our question. rude and makes students feel discouraged. no office hours either. he is longwinded, disorganized, confusing. his lectures are boring i always fell asleep. tests are tricky. clearly no passion for teaching. worst ever

He is a terrible professor; he shows no leniency in his grading and is very particular about the terms you use when answering questions on the exam. He doesn't provide office hours, so the best way to prepare for exams is to do the practice exams and focus on how he answers the questions. I would not wish this class on my worst enemy
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Studying his lectures and material will get you a good grade. Practice exams are the best study material. Unfortunately, a lot of his questions are very vague while he asks for a specific answer. This would be fine, but tests are 25% of the grade making one big mess up detrimental to your grade.

A lot of work but you will definitely have some applicable and clinical takeaways, which I found interesting (also mcat content). Sign up for Sage (facilitators are amazing)!! Use the heck out of Ed discussion. Lots of practice is a must (psets and practice tests), bc he wants u to answer things a very specific way sometimes.

Really really well-organized class, super interesting content, and clearly passionate about biochemistry. Make sure you truly understand the material and pathways, and keep up with the content. Dr. Coggins is the best premed prof I've had at Duke. His lectures are very clear and the exams are fair.
I would rather take the whole of the MCAT twice in one sitting than look at Coggins again. This says something.

Awful instructor. As someone who got an A, I must admit it was a lot of useless work. Dr. Coggins says that this class prepares for the MCAT. WRONG! 50% of this class never appears and he never mention stuff that appears (what about teaching us what's anomeric carbons). He says some steps are trivial and never explains them, proceeds to test them.

As a chem mjr, he made me lose all the love I had for chem. He is disorganized, his exams are not clear, the weekly quizzes are nonsensical, and he is condescending. I aced every single assignment, exams 1 and 2, and somehow ended with a B because he takes the answer key and twists it against you. He is THE WORST prof @ Duke. He should retire asap.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Coggins' class is easy, but his grading criteria are, beyond doubt, the worst I've ever seen. There is a lack of words for how terrible he is as a prof/person. He tailors the class for people who have the time to join SAGE, as he can't host OH. After taking every premed/eng class at Duke I know he is the worst prof to ever step foot on campus!!

This class is pretty much a second weed-out class for premeds but I wouldn't say it's as bad as orgo in terms of difficulty. Coggins teaches it pretty well so as long as you pay attention in lectures and use good study strategies, you'll do fine.

Dr. Coggins does an amazing job at catering this class to premeds and ties in many medical applications of the material into his lectures and exams.  He likes to throw some obscure questions on each exam, so make sure you review random and fun (almost tangent) topics that he talks about in class, as it will probably show up on an exam.

He is excellent at teaching and is clearly passionate about biochem. The content itself is very interesting but taught in a well thought out and intentional way. He does speak slowly and record lectures, so you could skip class and watch at 2x speed on your own if you keep up with recordings. Love the ties to current research and events

Best lecturer I've ever had. Makes biochem as easy to understand as it can be. Super nice guy and genuinely knows everything about this subject... you can tell he's been teaching this class for forever because the organization is perfect.

Dr. Coggins makes sure you actually understand what you're learning so you leave with a good foundation and not just a memorized/forgotten set of pathways. Need to make significant effort to understand thermo, mechanisms, regulation but he explains concepts well and if you go to lecture/SAGE and do the psets the class is honestly not super hard.

Nice guy, talks too much about the MCAT, doesn't realize there may be students taking biochem that won't become doctors in the future. Tests are easy if you regurgitate what he says in lecture, so take good notes.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: As someone really interested in biochemistry, this course was a letdown. It felt more like an MCAT prep course than a biochemistry course. We covered mainly physiology and metabolism while glazing over key concepts like protein synthesis. That being said, Coggins does really care about students and has amazing resources to help students learn.

I was dreading biochemistry, but Coggins has perfected the right way to teach this course. He'll mention current research and medical applications concerning a specific topic, and you learn a lot about disease, beer brewing, nutrition, etc. You'll definitely gain a newfound appreciation for all the little cells and proteins that make up your body.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I was dreading this course because I am trash at chemistry, but he makes biochemistry into an engaging class where everything clicks together. The end of the course is especially interesting because he makes it about the  human body and diseases.

Love Dr Coggins. He is a really smart guy and connects so many of the lectures to outside applications. He's pretty funny and can sometimes rush lectures when there is a time stamp he wants to reach. He always answers emails and I recommend going to SAGE for this class. Also, generally an interesting class.

Test heavy class, but Dr. Coggins cares about his students and is open to questions and provides good feedback. The material is challenging at times, but if you have to take Biochem at Duke, definitely take it with Coggins.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: One of the best professors at Duke. Coggins really cares about his students learning and is willing to help outside of class and he made the material easy to understand. Definitely take biochemistry with him!!

Dr. Coggins knew his stuff - he always knew the most recent research findings surrounding a particular topic. He was also a great lecturer; he explained things very thoroughly. His slides are a bit annoying because on their own they don't help too much, but overall a great professor.

Took this over summer session I which is extremely fast paced but Dr. Coggins still made sure students were able to understand everything clearly. Go to lecture or you won't understand his PPTs. Test heavy, 3 exams worth 85% of grade, but very easy if you go to lecture and understand the concepts. Overall, very enjoyable class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Coggins' lectures are very dense but very informative. He explains clearly, and his class prepared me extremely well for the MCAT. But he doesn't respond well to questions and often makes you feel stupid for asking them.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He is the best Biochem 301 professor. There's just no competition at all. .

Goes super in-depth into the material to make sure students are grasping it. Easy to tune out when he goes on tangents and frequently rushes through the important parts of lectures, but otherwise good at teaching. Comes off as condescending quite often. Tests are writing-heavy. The last part of the course is definitely interesting, though.

This was my first biochemistry class and Dr. Coggins made me discover a passion for biochemistry that I didn't know I had. His lectures tie in a lot of concepts to everyday life and I found it very engaging and interesting. Tests count for most of the grade in the class but the content is presented clearly so if you study, you will do well.

Exceptionally rushed, and constantly says, "Rewatch the lectures if you didn't understand something." This essentially gives him an excuse to be a poor professor, pushing the burden on us to catch the ridiculous nuances he likes to test. The tests and quizzes are worded so poorly that it's not even ambiguous; it's clearly asking for something else.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: You can tell that he's extremely passionate & knowledgeable on the subject. Tests are clear & straightforward. Weekly graded quizzes on Sakai. Definitely rewatch the recorded lectures because he goes through the material fairly quickly but if you put in the time and effort, you will do well. Lecture is needed to understand his ppt slides.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: His lecture slides are not very detailed so you have to go to lecture. I recommend recording his lectures since he talks kind of fast.
