He definitely knows his stuff and is a great teacher. But he is kind of condescending esp. when you ask questions outside of lecture. I remember him telling me once: "oh, you just don't get it." Interesting class!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Coggins is an excellent professor. He is a clear lecturer and extremely intelligent. All of the material he covers is so relevant. He is always available to answer questions outside of class, which is very helpful. He wants us all to do well not only in his course, but in our future careers. Overall, course is challenging but intriguing!

He has a magical way of lulling you to sleep with his voice. Explains things very well and slowly but he cares about teaching and the material. It's not hard if you prepare smart for the 3 exams. The "final" is a 3rd midterm. Just do a whole bunch of his practice problems and the past exams and you should get an A. Lots of memorizing though.

Coggins is the mom to Baldwin's dad. (Gooden's the crazy uncle I guess) Great prof, very measured and easy-to-follow pace. Material is interesting and it's clear Coggins knows it inside and out. He cares about students and their performance, but won't make special exceptions or anything. Easy course if you don't push it all to the night before.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Excellent professor. His lectures are very clear (although if you don't attend lecture, the powerpoints can be kinda confusing), he provides several practice exams to test your knowledge, and his exams are very fair. Course is structured for you to do well provided you put the work in.

Professor Coggins gives very informative lectures, but he tends to be monotone which makes it easy to tune out during lectures. He provides plenty of practice test materials for exams and his tests are definitely fair; the TAs are also flexible with their grading. Coggins overall is a great biochemistry teacher, and I learned a lot!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This class was tough for me, but it's objectively an easy class. Go to lecture and don't cram. He doesn't use a textbook and his powerpoints by themselves are kinda vague, so go to lecture. He makes the tests very reasonable if you put in the work for it. Overall a very fair and intelligent teacher and course.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Very clear and straightforward lecturer. Tests are super fair, and he's so accessible outside of class. Lectures got a bit dry at times, but the material was interesting, especially the last third of the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: this man honestly just knows how to teach. he makes fantastic, direct powerpoints. his lectures are extremely well organized. he tells you exactly what he wants from you, in terms of what to memorize, what will be on tests. he provides tons of practice tests and practice problems. literally finally someone who wants me to do well

Legendary man through and through. Took us on a chemical journey from day one. No textbook necessary, his lectures provide the information needed on the exam, so try to not miss class. There is a good chunk of this course that is memorization-heavy but Coggins presents it well. Would recommend

Dr. Coggin's passion for biochem makes his lectures clear and enjoyable. Lecture slides are very streamlined; I recommend recording his lectures for reference. Exams are straightforward, and Dr. Coggins posts all prior exams the week before for practice. While this is an "easier" premed class, be prepared to work hard -- lots of memorization.

I came into this class expecting it to be no work because other premeds said it was 'super easy'. It is easier than orgo/physics and you can do well by straight memorization, but don't slack off on the first test because unlike orgo, you can't replace the lowest test with the final. Make sure you put time in and don't underestimate the class
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Coggins is a fair teacher. No textbook necessary, and his instructions are clear. If you pay attention to his lectures and do all his practice exams, you'll do well. Find the TA that works for you and let them help you better understand (I rec Steve).
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests? Not many--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Coggins is truly a great professor. He gives super clear and articulate lectures with easy to understand slides if you go to class. Textbook not necessary - all the material from lectures. Hard in that there is a ton of memorization. But he gives you lots of past exams that help studying immensely. Psets and recitation helpful, not required.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Sweet adorable caring man. he's a teddy bear. made biochem bearable... but it was still hard, because it was biochem. pretty easy to get away with a B or so. great problem sets. posts lecture slides. really eager to help out and loves his subject so much. great guy. would recommend.

Coggins is a great professor! Solid lectures, although they can be a bit confusing at times. He is happy to clarify concepts after class and during office hours. Tests are challenging but fair and based on lectures and problem sets. Definitely would take again!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Prof Coggins is knowledgeable & connects the material to real life, discussing medical implications of the info (which is great,  since most of the students are premed). He makes it clear what you need to do to succeed and the tests are super straightforward. You need to memorize a lot but conceptually the class is not too hard. Highly recommend!!!

Prof. Coggins is an extremely clear, albeit uninteresting, lecturer. Focus during his lectures and take notes, you will have excellent resource, which you need because exams (85% of grade) are entirely based on his lectures. Study thoroughly with the practice exams he gives, and you should do well. A bit of a victory lap class after orgo I/II.

Dr. Coggins is the man. I did badly on the first test, and he was willing to meet with me outside of class to help raise my grade. I eventually understood and really give him a lot of credit for his encouragement. That said, I did NOT like the grading format - the tests were worth 25% of the grade each and undroppable. Would take him again though!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: I enjoyed his class and the material was really interesting. The exams are fair, but you need to keep up with the material and make sure to attend lectures because his tests are based on them (no need for the textbook). Do the problem sets and the previous exams and you'll be ok.

Clear lecturer w/ all test material taken from lectures (don't buy textbook). 3 exams (25/25/35% of grade) + weekly online/open-note quizzes (15% of grade) + weekly homework (ungraded). Many practice exams are posted, which are very helpful. Lots of content & it's very cumulative, so lectures can become hard to follow if you don't study regularly.

Coggins is an eloquent speaker and writer but extremely boring lectures. Course is generally very easy (haven't taken a premed class in a while as an engineer) and just proves my point that most premeds tend to complain for no reason. 100% memorization. No skill.

Coggins is one of the best lecturers out there. Indeed, the subject matter is a little dry, but he does an excellent job of teaching it. You have to go to class to do well, but the tests are pretty fair in general. The class also gets more interesting towards the end, and Coggins does a great job tying together themes from the entire semester.

Lectures are super dry and boring, but I think that's probably because of the subject itself. You can tell he's passionate about it but just doesn't do a very good job about getting anyone else excited about it. Students don't really respect him, either. His tests are almost exclusively on his lecture so you need to attend class (Fridays optional)

This is underratingly one of the easier pre-med classes. Its a lot of memorization, but the material isn't terribly complex and the tests are pretty straightforward. No lab component and optional friday discussions also makes this class very nice

Go to class - all materials from notes in class, don't open textbook. Coggins gets a lot of hate on yikyak, but he grew on me. Clear lecturer, not the most interesting subject, but not terrible. Very fair exams, writing assignment is no longer required. exams are multiple choice and not cumulative. likes beer - will test on in biochem context
Pay close attention to his lectures and just know biochem, only way to do well.

Prof. Coggins is a phenomenal lecturer. His lectures are well-paced and clear, he is very well-spoken (I have literally never heard him use a filler word), and there is occasional use of humortrivia. The class is extremely difficult, with a huge amount of material thrown at you, but the exams are fair and all the topics are integrated flawlessly.

Dr. Coggins is not a bad lecturer. He gets the job done and is helpful during office hours. The tests are very fair and are based on his lectures. However, the paper assignemnt doesn't help develop our writing skills at all. Huge waste of time for the students and the TAs. I strongly recommend taking biochem over the summer.

He does not know how to run a large class. Exams were straightforward, but the arbitrary TA grading screws you. The figures he draws during lecture are convoluted and confusing, just look at the ones in the book. I recommend taking this over the summer when he is less overwhelmed, or senior fall so it doesn't go on your AMCAS.

The material for this class was easy enough, but you practically have to read Dr. Coggins' mind to succeed on his tests! The regrade policy is absolutely ridiculous and highly unfavorable for students. Students are required to visit multiple TAs who can decide to grant permission to appeal to the professor (or not, in most cases). Avoid this class!

This is the most subjectively graded science class you will ever take. TA's will mark you off on tests if your answers aren't word for word what's on the key, even if what you say isn't wrong. TA's will also refuse regrade requests for no reason. Basically, the material is easy but the testing is WAY too specific and arbitrary, and so is the paper.

Not a very nice guy. Tests were easy, but he expects specific answers, and will not go against TA grading (even if he admits they are incorrect) for the sake of "consistency". Regrade requests are ridiculous and it's nearly impossible to get points back. He seems to get confused easily during lectures. Doesn't really care about students.

He's an awesome professor; he is very clear during lectures, interesting, and if he makes a mistake, he will be sure to correct it and clarify. You can tell that he really enjoys talking about the subject and he knows his stuff well. The paper is a little annoying, but admittedly not a bad exercise -- the guidelines were clear. I recommend.

my advice is to review the stuff after each lecture; if you keep up, then you'll find he's actually good at what he does; if you don't keep up, it's easy to find yourself lost in class. tests were very similar to practice, though the writing assignment is bs.

His lectures are good, but that doesn't translate to his tests.  They're very nitpicky and unfortunately focuses a lot on minor details that he glossed over in class.  This wasn't the worst class I've taken, but it's definitely one of the more annoying ones I've taken.  Would only recommend him as a last resort.
EX. EMP. LA. RY. spent over a decade at duke, including as an undegrad.

This class was not that bad. He's a thorough lecturer and easy to understand. His lectures occasisionally have errors, but he tries to fix them either during class or through email, unlike professors that just keep teaching you the wrong thing. The class needs adjusting for large size, but is otherwise very interesting. I enjoyed it a lot!

SUCH a scrub. his lectures are full of mistakes, and he gets confused figuring them out when he gets called out and ends up having to send out emails w/ corrections. annoying paper assignment w/ barely any guidance that isn't handed back. TWO problem sets on test weeks (one is "optional" but is tested over and isn't put up until really late).

Coggins normally teaches this class in the summer. The paper he assigned was an interesting idea but there's just too many students in the class for him to grade it timely. The lectures are really what you would expect for a science class. I thought he did a fine job in them and drove home important ideas.

I was really disappointed by this class. Lectures were boring, poorly organized, unclear, and often contained errors. Coggins seemed uninterested in teaching the class, and it was clearly his lowest priority. We got back 2/12 homeworks, and will not be getting our essays (an obnoxious and highly weighted assignment). Don't take this class with him!
He was a good professor that was very approachable. Class covers a lot, but if you keep up, you will find it is very interesting.

Was a good professor, although expectations for the course were not clear. He is a boring lecturer, and he graded the exams himself, so grading was very subjective. He knows his stuff, but could definitely improve as an instructor.
I really enjoyed this class. It was definitely challenging, but very engaging and interesting.
Ok professor. Well-established in the field, but does not teach the best, and does not know how to communicate in a concise manner. Took nearly 2 hours to answer a single question from someone.

Not difficult per se to get an A/B, but homeworks and projects take a lot of time. 3 exams are 65% of your grade - not super hard but rely on your ability to reason. Not enough practice given for exams; homeworks, lectures, projects, and exams are often unrelated. TAs are helpful but don't always know the answers. Bruce rambles and loves to talk.

Don't understand the negative reviews. This class was challenging but fair. Extra credit on projects, regrade requests, and office hours made this course manageable. Some lectures were unnecessarily complicated, but the review sessions, ed posts, recitation, prepared me for the content of exams. I would have liked lecture to line up more w exams.

Attending OH (and finding a good partner) is a must for Problem Sets (even though some TAs don't know the answer). Bruce is a giant in his field, but lectures often go over your head and differ from exams. Lots of learning done through recitation/hw. Class is curved so that everyone who participates/does hw gets an A or B, and the mean is a B+/A-

Material is interesting and TAs were wonderful, but Donald's in-person lectures are unintelligible - the only way I learned anything was his recorded Zoom lectures on YouTube - and I left feeling unprepared in terms of proof-writing and algorithm analysis for 330. Insane midterms, easy final, huge end-of-semester curve. Get a good PSET partner.

OH are a must if you want to do well on the short assignments and problem sets. There were a handful of great (and not so great) TAs. Bruce was very unhelpful and often taught material irrelevant to the exams.

Material is not the worst but is taught in the most inaccessible fashion with lectures above the needed level. TAs do not understand the content, office hours do not help, and Professor Donald is rather condescending. He is so afraid of cheating that any questions to him are never answered and invoke a sarcastic rudeness.

Very knowledgeable and lectures on great topics, though they can be hard to understand. This does not pair well with his superior attitude, often mocking students in his replies. Manageable assignments if you start early enough, though it will be difficult to get help if you are stuck. Decent course with an unempathetic and narcissistic professor.
Awful class and awful professor. So many homework assignments. If you're stuck on an assignment, you're in trouble, since the Office Hours are packed and you have a limited time to receive help.

I hated the flipped classroom. The lectures were just Zoom recordings from last year, and quality was terrible. The in-person lecture was a Q&A session, but it was useless. Students asked either basic understanding questions that others already understood, or very abstract and irrelevant things. Large number of assignments; the grind never stops.

Incredibly lazy and arrogant professor who uses past recorded lectures instead of lecturing in person. Believes flipped classroom is superior, going to class in person is worthless. Hid final exam grades and deleted course website after final grades were released. Tough grading with no partial credit. Take the substitution courses instead of CS230.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This class was a nightmare. The flipped classroom approach was terrible, with him requiring us to watch recorded lectures on content that never came up on assignments or exams, and no one coming to class in person which made in-person lectures terrible and unhelpful. Go to office hours, some of the TAs (Matt <3) are great and actually care.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: By far the worst class Ive ever taken and hopefully will ever take. I wont bother to reiterate what everyone else is saying, but I wanted to provide my opinion as someone who did very well in the class. Do not take cs 230 with Bruce Donald. This professor and class are an embarrassment to Dukes CS department.

Had very unclear expectationsgrades were set up such that you had no idea what youd get until the end. The flipped classroom technique and haphazard website made it extremely difficult and frustrating to actually learn the material. Tests and homework were designed to exceed the expected level of comprehension, which felt very disheartening.

2 things to add. #1 "Short assignments" are not short at all and often test concepts above what is needed or even learned in class (some TAs don't even know how to do them). #2 He is so out of touch. Acts so smug thinking his silly math/statistics brain teasers could be asked in our interviews. And is so proud of knowing the answers when we don't??

Doesn't teach anymore and delegated grading to an awful head UTA. Extremely harsh grading, complete lack of transparency, and overall just an enjoyable class. Take this class in the spring if possible, or get the Substitution. Maybe with a better head UTA this class will improve, but don't count on it. Very shady, non-responsive, and unhelpful.

350 characters isnt enough to describe how awful this class is. Useless material. Lazy flipped lecture format. ZERO clarity in grading (literally refused to answer questions about it). Hes absurdly arrogant. Wants students to fail. Obscene amounts of work. Zero practice for tests, which he designs with a mean of 50. If u wanna hate CS, take this.

Not a single concept is useful. Horrible teacher. Consistently assesses you on content BEFORE it is formally taught. Practically 0 partial credit given if even one minor detail is off. Head TA is even more demonic than professor and enjoys watching students suffer. Attempted to conceal students' grades on final exam and forbade regrade requests.

This class is absolutely terrible. Grading for exams is harsh, give no partial points if part of your answer is correct. Some TAs are really unhelpful and mean. You learn nothing useful, feels like a complete waste of time. Exam prep tips are always unclear. The teaching team is just uncaring in general and only wants everyone to have poor scores.

Echoing others' frustrations, the absolute worst aspect of this class was the flipped classroom. Most lazy thing ever, in-person lectures were useless. That leads into problem 2: lectures and recitations quickly devolve into getting too specific into theory and neglecting to teach what you actually need to know for tests. Tests are the hardest ever

Why in the world would you choose to reuse your ultra boring, hour-long recorded quarantine lectures instead of actually teaching us in class?? This added an additional 2+ hours of mind numbing lecture outside of class time every week on top of the already frenetic pace of assignments. This class was a true nightmare.

IF I COULD GIVE THIS CLASS A LETTER GRADE I'D GIVE IT AN A + . . . . FOR AWFUL PLUS TERRIBLE. this class evokes the 2019 hit song No Guidance by Chris Brown featuring Drake flipped lessons waste your time, it's hard to keep track of deadlines because there are so many assignments, bruce is unclear at all times, no partial credit ever

Easily the worst class I've taken at Duke. If you want to take CS230, wait another semester because Donald will make you do way too much unnecessary work and make you code in useless/obscure language that overcomplicates problems and makes finding out how the syntax works impossible.

Way too many things going on at once, and even though he's smart, he is terrible at explaining things. flipped classroom makes the workload a nightmare. doesn't listen to any feedback, is arrogant, doesn't answer questions in a straightforward way, goes so far into theory that you don't even know what exactly you're supposed to be learning.
This class is terrible, very poorrly taught, I hate the stupid useless lecture and the annoying assignments and TAs

If you have undiagnosed ADHD, you will find out in this class. This is a super not neurotypical friendly course. BD has multiple assignments due every week each time on separate days, with zero-exception late policy that is murder. Getting accommodations is next to impossible. if you even think you have ADHD wait for another professor to teach 230

He's one of the smartest, most passionate people I've ever met. He knows an immense amount about computer science, math, and computational biology, and is very accessible and willing to talk about it. The problem sets are tough and quite time consuming, but essential in solidifying and applying the material. The high workload really is worth it.

One of the best CS professors at Duke. Very knowledgeable in the field, and is very approachable if you ever have questions able about the class or just computer science/AI/Biology in general. His lectures are paced well, and if you ask questions and go to office hours you will do well. The workload though is quite intense.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: This man is one of the worst professors at Duke. His lectures are horrible. He writes illegibly with CHALK. The recorded lectures are impossible to follow for this reason. If you ask a question he responds with more questions. He is very arrogant. TAs are not helpful either. He's difficult to reach and isn't willing to help you.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: BRD is the goat, and by far the best prof for CS230 at Duke. Sure, he goes a bit theoretical in lecture and it can get confusing, but his TAs are always spectacular and everything seemed to make sense after they boiled it down in recitation. Genuinely cares about his students and lectures sometimes have participation in a goofy way. Overall awesome

Bruce is an amazing human being and puts an immense amount of thought into his lectures/materials. He will go out of his way to answer your questions in class. CS230 is definitely not an easy class, so if you don't go in with the right mindset you will inevitably be disappointed. If you put in honest work, it will be a very rewarding experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Smartest guy at Duke hands down. His class is super interesting, and his passion for the material is clear in lecture. However, he has a tendency to overcomplicate, and the assignments often are not directly do-able based off lecture, so go to TA office hours when possible!
Horrible teacher with so much work and very little guidance. If you really enjoy doing extra work for no reason, then sure go for it. Otherwise, avoid at all cost.

Bruce is a good professor with high expectations (but not too high). Although the workload was stressful for me at times and I really had to make an effort to grasp the material, Bruce and his TAs were extremely helpful and encouraging throughout the semester. A very rewarding experience if youre willing to work hard.

Bruce Donald is a wonderful lecturer and a brilliant computer scientist. His knack to apply the mathematical concepts we learned to computer science kept the course intriguing and relevant. I wouldnt say the class is hard, but it certainly requires some work to be put in. Be prepared to work and think. Its a rewarding class.

Bruce Donald is the smartest teacher Ive ever had. We went over lots of different interesting topics that are core to the field of Computer Science. Problem sets arent too hard, especially if you go to TAs for help. There was lots of homework in the beginning of the year but it eased off in the final third.

A great class, but very difficult. He's really enthusiastic about the subject matter and enjoys talking to students. However, we're using Scheme, a functional programming language - takes a lot of time to get used to it. Midterms were also difficult and graded toughly. Sometimes we had short assignments due every class (lecture and recitation).
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--EXTRA CREDIT--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Regardless of your major, if you are taking this class with Bruce, it will be one of the hardest classes you will take at Duke. I really appreciate the material, but sometimes he deliberately makes life difficult by not giving you much to study for his tests. It also doesn't help that the material is pretty tough to grasp. Make friends with the TAs

He's clearly very passionate about the subject he teaches and genuinely hopes that he can engage his students' interests. However, the TA's have mentioned that he can be a bit overly ambitious, which makes the class fast-paced and the material a bit difficult to thoroughly grasp.

Discrete Math with Bruce was very interesting. On one hand, I really enjoyed his lectures and we went over a lot of random, interesting topics. On the other hand, the course seemed to lack focus and I forgot a lot since then because we jumped around so much. The class is fast paced and the concepts can be tough for some, but overall, I enjoyed it.

I should be writing this review for ChatGPT who taught me the entirety of this course, yet here I am. Just read the textbook and tune out the lecture and you'll do fine in the class. The midterms are much easier than the homework and his slides are negligible
Literally so bad at teaching. Dense incomprehensible slides. avoid at all costs.

To be honest, he's a nice guy but he does not know how to lecture. The grade distribution is set up really good, but he always brings up the most irrelevant stuff in class that does not pertain at all to the midterms. I will say he is probably better than the Fall semester professor who teaches 104, from what I heard.
Burnside does not do a good job of lecturing big classes. Also, he spends 90% of the time going over complicated proofs that are irrelevant to the class's content.

210 was no joke, but Burnside made it great. Lectures were extremely important to understand material and he did a great job explaining. I found exams to be very hard, but getting average grades and taking the time to work through his pretty tedious homework sets will give you a fine grade. Best 210 prof at Duke, and my favorite econ prof here.

Professor Burnside is the kindest Econ professor I have had at Duke. This was the last core class that I took and I can safely say that he was my favorite professor by a lot. Go to his office hours because he is very good at explaining concepts 1 on 1. Also study the practice problems, the exams are not as scary as the problem sets.

Professor Burnside really made an impression on me. He made me feel welcomed and understood in the classroom and he was there outside of class whenever I had a question for him. Although he can sometimes be a little tough, he actually very willing to talk to you, so don't be afraid to go to him! Overall, I loved his class so much.

Amazing professor! I loved his lectures and his teaching style. He's also very funny and cares about his students a lot. He really brought out a new side of me as a student and now economics is my favorite thing ever! 100% would recommend this professor!

Dry lectures and boring professor. He is really smart and knowledgable, but seems like the kind of professor who prefers to do research but is being forced to teach. But take his class for the macro requirement bc there is no calc on his exams and they were open note too (at least in Fall 2021).
Dry class but he was very nice

Prof Burnside responds to emails very fast and is patient with questions. But I didn't learn much rigorous and clear in Econ210; it was more like an overview of diff macro theories. Weekly graded PS and 3 exams. PS and take-home part of exams can take days of thinking, and often the wording of questions is confusing (like what it wants you to do).

Professor Burnside can seem a little stern when you first meet him, but inside he's just a big softy. He's funny and you can easily crack him up. His class is challenging, but he is always pushing his students to do their best and helping them learn. His class is the best I've taken so far! I thoroughly enjoyed his class and he is a great teacher!

This was Professor Burnside's first time teaching Time Series. Craig's philosophy for the class seemed to be to dump loads of theory and statistical derivations, with little to no motivation for the actual economics being done. Tests were easy as they followed directly from the notes; but I am certain most students left learning virtually nothing.

Craig is very caring towards his students and is always helpful and available to meet outside of class. While the lectures arent the most engaging, his tests are predictable if you do old tests and his grading policy helps everyone out in the end. He might not seem like the warmest at first but he has a soft heart and wants everyone to do well!

Best Professor I have ever had. The classes are difficult but you can learn so much out of it. His assignments are a lot of work, but they are extremely helpful to learn the contents, and the tests are not super hard. He focuses solely on student learning, and if you work hard you will be able to have a good grade and to finally learn economics.

Classes are mandatory with random quizzes. Grading is slightly arbitrary on tests. HW assignments are nothing too bad. Is a pretty dry lecturer but his notes are good and clear. Class ended up curved to a B+. Bottom line - he's not bad but he is no Nechyba.

Lectures can be boring at times, I'll admit I fell asleep multiple times. He was very helpful outside of class through email though. Attendance is kinda mandatory with quizzes, homework is graded pretty randomly, but most people end up getting full credit at the end.  Average grade ended up being a B+ and 38/81 got As while 31/81 got Bs.

He's not mean or rude. He just doesn't have patience for slackers who waste his time. Here's how you get an A: 1. Read notes and understand why religiously. Understand what causes the "shock" mathematically. 2. Do the practice exams. 3. (optional) Memorize the two tables in ch 4 and understand why they happen and the temp/perm graphs 4 all ch.

One of the worst professors I have ever had. Honestly, I have had middle school teachers who are much better than this guy. His notes involve extremely complicated equations which make it impossible to understand certain concepts. Also, he is very grumpy, sends out rude emails, and is unhelpful when asked questions. Grading is also arbitrary.
Unclear notes and lectures.

I found Burnside to actually be really good if you came to lecture, read his notes and powerpoints, and if you talked to him outside of class. actually very clear if ask questions. super knowledgeable. macro is definitely tough and dry at times, but burnside makes the best of it and tries to draw parallels to the real world. great class.

If possible, try to take 110 with Michelle Connelly. Some friends of mine took it with her and got A-s, but most of my friends in Burnside got B-s/Bs. His grading policy is confusing and the tests are difficult. The problem sets (aside from being graded arbitrarily) had nothing to do with the material and did not help in preparation for the exams.

The material wouldn't be so hard, except he makes it so by adding in tons of useless / irrelevant information that confuses people and. No longer sticks to a textbook so and no longer posts classnotes online, so if you're confused by the material you're out of luck - and that happens often. Monotonous lectures. Too math-fucused for economics class.

Witty professor who does his best to make the boring material sound interesting.  Tests are pretty straightforward, and he made some adjustments to grades in our favor.  Tons of old assignments and tests posted online that are really helpful.
REALLY BORING. I only went to half the classes. He reads off his powerpoints. He puts everything online, though. The tests are fair, and a lot of people got A's.
very fair teacher who incorporated stories from his outside research to make an otherwise boring class somewhat bearable.  He's very clear in his requirements and is always willing to help
very fair teacher. lectures are not too exciting, but he post lecture notes online, so you don't even have to go to class. no surprises on the exams. good class

Lectures are a bit boring, but Burnside was always really willing to help outside of classtime.  He puts mp3's of the lectures online which is HUGE when studying for the final.  I'd recommend Econ110 with him.
he is monotone. nuff said

I wouldn't necessarily say Burnside is awful. He's very knowledgeable, but he has to be, by far, one of the most boring people alive. He took a boring subject (macroeconomics), and made it even more boring. It's a problem when you have a 100 person class and 30 show up consistently.

Prof. Burnside is caring and extremely willing to help. His online lecture notes and MP3's are clear and concise, and he is conscientious about answering questions and providing straightforward lectures. Homework/tests require thought. His main problem is that he rarely shows his dry sense of humor.
Horrible teacher.  Problem sets and tests are not related to what he teaches in class.  Very boring and doesn't teach just summarizes his notes which summarize the textbook.  AWFUL.
Got angry and made people try to participate even though we don't want to.

Gavin's strategy of bribing his students with candy is undefeated, much better than his coTA who would constantly miss class and cold call the same people every time. Gavin is the reason why I was able to succeed in ECON 204
I am in love with Gavin Burns
Didn't really know what he was doing at times and he would try to make the class answer the discussion questions. Other TA had to step in to help a lot. Overall pretty chill and easy though
I like the guy but he's not good at teaching. It was very hard to understand and he rarely replied to emails.
Gavin's the best econ 201 TA. Wouldn't have gotten thru that class without his help! Always made me laugh and was truly inspirational. Most influential person I've met in my life so far.

Gavin is an excellent educator; while I struggled with the material, Gavin was there every step of the way, committed to my pursuit of knowledge. He also makes himself extremely accessible outside of class; this unprecedented availability has given me the opportunity to learn from an economics whiz. I am truly grateful for my learning with Gavin.
Stand up guy. High motor, lots of grit, sneaky athletic. He makes economics feel simple, and I attribute all my success to this man. Gavin Burns is a true American hero.
He is the best economics teacher there is. He brings foreign concepts into reach with ease and persuasiveness.
Best Econ 201 TA!
this guy made calc 111 way too difficult and was not a nice teacher. Take this class with any other professor
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Floyd Bullard was a very poor lecturer, and we basically had to teach ourselves the material. His 3rd midterm was insanely difficult, and he did not curve at all. He made my Calc 1 experience much harder than it needed to be.

Professor Bullard was very kind, and passionate during lecture. He is always eager to answer whatever questions the class had.
However, lectures were sometimes unorganized as he would at times lose his train of thought and run out of time.
Overall very kind professor. If you pay attention in lecture and do the work outside of class you'll be fine.

Exams are graded harshly (one midterm had a class average of a failing grade - for a non-curved class), lectures are unclear and unorganized, we were tested on material not covered in lecture, fixing grading mistakes is an unreasonably lengthy process (I gave up eventually).
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Take this class with any other professor
Very nice, caring, and approachable. Writes very reasonable and predictable tests, and will addresses weak spots in lectures.

I had to give Dr. Bullard a good rating because it's bizarre to me how he's getting unfairly nuked by students who got As in his class. This was his first semester at Duke and he did his best. The TAs and labs are most helpful. If you took Calc AB/BC, you will be perfectly fine. I wish I had more time for this class as CHEM101 took all of it away.

Professor Bullard was a kind teacher, but even after taking Calculus BC in high school, I still found the class challenging, and his lectures weren't helpful for understanding the material. The lectures and labs didn't overlap, and we were tested in lab on topics we hadn't been taught or covered beforehand. I wouldn't recommend.

Dr. Bullard is clearly a kind man who genuinely tried in his first semester at Duke, but his horrendous teaching and frequent disorganization has real life implications for students, and I can't look past that. Things to keep in mind: graders are tough (rarely give partial credit), he didn't want to release final exam scores, takes months to grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: You could tell Dr. Bullard cared about his students, but often made things much harder than necessary. It took a long time to get grades back and lecture was not all that helpful. Exams were okay, and it was nice to have corrections for the first two. However, I think that previous calc experience was really the only way to be very successful.

His lectures were wildly unorganized, I stopped showing up after 2 weeks of class. TAs and lab sections are very helpful, but having previous calc experience is the only way to succeed in this class. The tests were fine as long as you study, the final was very easy. Homework is graded pretty strictly, just work with other people and check answers.

I feel bad bc it's his first semester at a uni EVER, but he gets flustered in lecture very easy which makes it hard to focus in lecture because he can get derailed fast. He's very sweet and responds to emails as best he can, but he's not the best at teaching + the super late grading. If you're not good at math, this class won't help :(

After the second week of class I never showed up to a lecture ever again. His way of teaching and organization skills are subpar at best. The tests were pretty easy in my opinion (previous calc experience), so it wasn't a super time consuming course on a weekly basis. The HW was graded fairly strictly, but just show your work and you will be fine.

He made the class more stressful than it needed to be. Annotated lectures were almost never posted (even after he promised they would be), assignments took AGES to grade (we would move on to the next unit and take exams without knowing what we did wrong on the previous one), and he always skipped the more challenging material during lectures.

His lectures were unhelpful. ~70% of the class stopped showing bc he skipped around half the slides. I'm trying to be fair since it's his first term at Duke, but we weren't told he'd teach it. I enrolled for Shira, originally. Grading is very weird. You'll never know their expectations. Even with the correct process/answers, you still lose points.

Yes, he is nice. However, that doesn't justify the unorganized teaching, and grading he provides. Grades took WEEKS to arrive, making reviewing for material difficult when you already pretty much have to teach for yourself. Really utilize the slides, as problems mainly deviate from them.
Nice guy, sucks as a teacher. Don't take his classes, he really sucks and is slow in grading and teaching concepts. Get ready to learn everything by yourself in order to succeed.

Professor Bullard seems like a great guy, however throughout the lectures he constantly just gets ‘flustered' and is unable to continue teaching a lecture that makes sense. The homework and tests are near impossible to get an 100 on because they take off for pretty much anything and seemingly want you to write a whole paragraph for an explanation.

The reviews portrait him as the worst professor possible, which is not the case. He tries to get things to work, just feels like he doesn't know how to do so. Given its his first semester at uni, I can cut him some slack. That being said, material wasn't exciting, tests were made for you to lose points (even if you know calculus). Grades took month

Professor Bullard is a super nice individual, but some of his lessons were slightly confusing. I found that we focused a lot on easier topics but flew by the more complex ones. Homework and tests were solid, not too bad as long as you put work into it. Class was good if you took calculus before, but definitely took effort to get good grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Avoid this professor, while he is sweet as a person he simply can't teach, duke threw him in while having another professor on registration then said he was taking over, this is his first year as a professor and taught at hs, couldn't navigate tech for a while, egrades basically all tests and final, if you didn't take calc before you'll struggle.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: AVOID THIS PROFESSOR AT ALL COSTS. He is not accessible at all (doesn't respond to email/ed discussion, and his once a week office hours are during a lab period for his own class!). He has no grasp of time during lecture and can't get through material. He takes >1 month to grade assignments. Also, he tried to get rid of test corrections.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Do not take math with this professor. He is so bad at teaching!! He is a horrible lecturer and gets distracted very easily. He never gets through all the material he is supposed to teach which forced us to learn it during our labs. He may seem kind but he truly doesn't want us to succeed. It takes him over a moth to grade an assignment. AVOID HIM!
very boring, bad, and unorganized prof. It feels like we are just waiting half the time for him to figure out what to teach.

Pretty bad lecturer. I will give him some slack as its first semester teaching at Duke; however, I have friends at the old school he used to teach, and it's sad to say that he was also not a great teacher there, and people had to resort to self-studying. Nice guy, just not the best teacher for Calc 1. Would avoid if you want a good teacher.
bad lecturer and super boring. you will learn everything in lab and he is not accessible.

Her best quality is that it seems like she genuinely cares about her students' well being outside of class. Unfortunately, my experience in her class was that she was unclear about project requirements, regularly said she wanted things done one way and then took points off when it was done that way, and was frequently in bad moods.

People say "BME303 is one of the easiest cores", it isn't. They should say "Dr. Libby makes BME303 the best core". She takes a very hard class and makes it enjoyable and a great learning experience. If you want to take this class, take it with her.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Libby is a great professor who teaches you everything you need to know and incorporates lots of applications which is really fun. Class is engaging with groupwork. The class can be a lot sometimes, but she's very fair/reasonable. You'll put in the work, but you get out as much as you put in. Truly one of my favorite BME classes and professors.

Dr. Bucholz is an amazing professor. She teaches the content very clearly and makes sure that there are plenty of OH. However, this class is very homework-intensive, and the TAs often don't know the answers to the homework. When I ask them for help during office hours, they sometimes gave the wrong answers. Besides that, the class is great.

Dr. Libby is the mom of Duke BME! She truly cares about her students and continuously wants to make her courses and the Duke BME curriculum better. Even after classes ended, she remembers many of her students and checks in on them. She is always willing to lend a listening ear and give students support in and out of the classroom.

Dr. Libby is charismatic and cares about students. Class is formatted to be table-based problem solving instead of strict lecture based, which I didn't like but lots of people loved. The large amount of material covered means that the class is not very flexible, with some deadlines being pushed tightly together and material being rushed at the end.

While Libby is caring and excited about her subject, she is also very disorganized. This was a graduate level course and we didn't get to fourier transform until 2/3 through the semester. All in all, it was more a class on how to build the tools you already have at your disposal in MATLAB or any other language, rather than how to use them.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Libby is truly a gem in the BME dept. Her energy is infectious & she genuinely cares about everyone doing well. She's so accessible out of class & puts all other lackluster professors to shame. Content is dry & tough but she does her best to make it as digestible as possible. You're not Duke BME if you haven't taken a class with Dr. Libby.

Dr. Bucholz is the best professor I have ever had. If you do not take imaging systems with her as a BME, you are horribly missing out. She is so enthusiastic, and so obviously loves her job and her students. I would take any class she offered. Not only is she a great person, she is so smart and good at explaining things. You learn a LOT in 303.
Pretty good professor. I only wish COVID-19 allowed for a full in-person semester with her.

IF YOU ARE A BME STUDENT AT DUKE, YOU ARE MISSING OUT WHEN YOU ARE NOT TAKING HER COURSE. She is a gem. She is the most caring professor I have seen in my life and she will make sure NO ONE IN HER CLASS is dissatisfied with where they are in the course. Very sad that we couldn't take her course in person because of COVID but she made our lives easy

Very nice professor who puts in the effort to help you in class and tries to help her students do well. She is very understanding and helped my group get in touch with a lot of other professors we needed for our project. Very helpful and a charismatic person.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I've taken 303 and 271 with Dr. Bucholz and she is my favorite professor at Duke. She does an amazing job of making any concept interesting by coming up with creative interactive demos for the class. She has reasonable expectations and pushes students without making impossible assignments. Need more people like her in the BME Faculty at Duke!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: One of the best teachers I have ever had and possibly the best BME teacher at Duke. Professor Bucholz goes out of her way to ensure you understand the material. I would highly recommend this class to anyone.

By far the best professor I've ever had! She is enthusiastic, really cares about and makes an effort to get to know every single student. The classes fly by since lectures are so engaging and interactive. Her office hours are super helpful too! The material can be challenging, but definitely doable as long as you stay on top of the assignments.

Bucholz helps you remember things by repeating the key points throughout the semester, and engages people by requiring a lot of student output in class (i.e. assigning each row to calculate things/ make graphs, trivia-style contest for extra credit, in-class MATLAB simulation, etc.). It's easy to focus even if it's 8:30 am and you are sleepy.

I've taken 271 and 303 with Bucholz, and she is easily the most engaging and clear lecturer I have ever had. The homeworks were demanding but really helped us prepare for the challenging exams. In the end, you learn a LOT, and if she's teaching something that you are interested in, I would absolutely suggest you go for it.
Best professor in the BME department confirmed. Bucholz is amazing

Bucholz is an AMAZING professor, probably one of the best I've had at Duke. You will need to work your ass off to get an A, but she is WORTH it. Trust me. Problem sets are long (prepare to spend days on them) but they really help your understanding and her office hours are a great resource. She speaks fast so be prepared to write quickly.
Very Helpful during lecture and office hours. Work hard and you will succeed!
Prof Buck is a brilliant teacher who truly cares about her students' understanding.  It is important to attend lectures.  Do go to office hours if you need help.

Professor Buck knows her trade, but not how to teach it to others. Her lectures are terrible, they consist of her reading examples pulled from the textbook with no extra information. She publicly shames students for not attending class, and brags about knowing more math than her students on occasion.

I would give Professor Buck a 5 for her teaching but am giving 4 because she was pretty unresponsive to emails/Ed and often scattered with grading. In lectures he follows the textbook to a T but in a good way and I thought she did a nice job of teaching. Very reasonable amount of work and very reasonable test difficulty.

Buck is a very good teacher and cares a lot about students. She explains very well, the problem is just that a lot of people either don't show up to lecture or don't do the homework. At least doing the homework is very important to doing well in this class. You won't do well in Duke Math if you don't do the homework! She's a great teacher

Extremely sweet and caring person, but not the best professor. She treats students as children but expects college-level work. She is often very frazzled during lectures and spends more time picking colors to color-code her notes than actually explaining. She has great intentions, but her execution comes across as patronizing and disorganized.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Buck is truly a wonderful teacher as she is a person. She cares about you and is always ready to teach with a smile. Changed my entire outlook on math in general. The Duke math department glo'd up with her on their staff board. I would take any math class with her!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Buck is a truly caring and cheerful individual and her positive energy is contagious. Classes are well-organized so work and content are pretty manageable, especially if you have done calculus before. Labs can be messy and uninteresting at times.

Amazing professor with the cheeriest attitude. Super helpful in and out of class. Professor Buck is a true gem: second to none. Even in introductory calculus she talks about how the concepts are applicable and where: showing us that what we are doing matters.
N/A

Dr. Bursac definitely knows the content and cares for his students. However, the TAs did not know nor care about anything. This class is extremely hard and I would not suggest taking it. The other reviews are completely right, despite not being about 301, they are still true.
Great Prof , has the best lectures but makes you work for the class.

One of the worst prof I ever had. He knows a lot about this field but fails to teach what he knows effectively. He does not understand how useless his HWs are in preparing students for his tests, which consisted of even more useless but hard topics. OHs are not helpful at all, he expects you to know the math concepts and doesn't clarify anything

Not a great professor.  Sometimes unclear in lecture and tests felt like they could have been written better.  The class material was very interesting (tissue engineering) but I feel that they class would benefit from a different professor or at least some more development. (as it is the topics covered feel a little... scattered)
This guy kinda blows
Lectures unintelligible.  He makes the subject a lot harder than it could be.  Take it with Barr instead.
So the average on one of the exams was a 33% this semester.  Expects a lot of students but will work with you to try and help you get it.

Absolutely loved his class. Very knowledgable. Had lunch with him outside of class to discuss a paper, genuinely interested in helping out. More than grades, he cares about students understanding, thinking, and even questioning what he says.  Highly recommended. Best class I have taken at Duke so far.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This guy was great. He's really interested in the subject, and it shows. Expect to participate, but the atmosphere he fosters makes it easy to. Doesn't give very much work, and if you do the (many) readings he gives, you'll get a good grade without too much trouble. He's just a great dude. Really thoughtful and addresses student needs well.

Probably the best class I have taken so far at Duke.  Really great professor, very helpful outside of class and easy-going.  A fair amount of reading, but as long as you can contribute something to the class discussion you;re good.

Took his Intro to War, Military and Society course. Very interesting topics, only two papers which were easy to write, fair grader. Readings are long (30-40 pgs) but as long as you understand them well enough to contribute to discussion you're fine. Byers is great and his class is very relaxed and easy to contribute to.

I'm actually obsessed with Byers. He's SO helpful and always willing to meet up with you. He's funny, too! He baked our class homemade treats for every holiday. The work can be difficult, but meet with him and he will talk you through it. Readings can be dry, so you should definitely be interested in the class topic. DO THE READINGS.Thatll help you
Interesting professor and class.  Some of the readings can be dry, plus there is probably too much of it though.  But very good class and Byers has a good sense of humor and is helpful.
Great teacher, extremely enthusiastic about the course, very helpful.  One of the best teachers I've had at Duke!

Relative to other classes I've taken, one of the easier A's at Duke. Personally enjoyed Dr. Hard lectures more than Dr. Grisham. Class is quite bureaucratic with many different assignments but none were particularly difficult. R&W project & final essay were a bit annoying but not graded as harshly as people make it seem if you give decent effort.

Impossible to get an A+ despite scoring an average of 97 on all three tests. Put in so much work, and it's not worth it for all the meaningless tasks and assignments that were graded harshly for no reason. The course design is actually bad.

Lectures almost always run longer than necessary and focus heavily on fine details that later appear on exams, even though they say there are no “gotcha” questions. Toward the end of the semester, there is a noticeable increase in assignments, and grading on these is strict, so hard to boost your grade. Need to be reminded they are teaching 101.
dont take lol
AMAZING class. Coming from a non-psych major.

What's the similarity between Bridgette Hard and Benjamin Netanyahu? Both profit off the suffering of others. In this case, Hard makes commissions of the textbook just to introduce a slew of new terms not taught in class. Beyond this, the class is unnecessarily bureaucratic, though both are objectively very engaging lecturers and knowledgeable

YES, THE MOST BUREAUCRATIC CLASS I've EVER had at Duke. Psych is a easy major and they made it so much more difficult, and the difficult part is not the content but the bureaucracy. I wanted to drop this class every second I was in it.

Fantastic professor. 10/10 - discussions and lectures are always interesting and fun. Attendance policy allows you to skip the final if you don't have too many absences. Extra credit is generous as long as you complete bonus surveys. Class is mostly memorization-based except for a research proposal. Unfortunately textbook has to be bought.

Great lecturer and clearly a caring, thoughtful person who makes an effort for class to be interesting, engaging, and relevant for students. A lot of material covered, and the class is harder than it really should be. No individual thing is challenging, but there are a million minor concepts you need to know and plenty of busy work.

Hard + Grisham have managed to end off an engaging class with a sludge of unnecessary, filler work, all while sending condescending emails. A midterm after thanksgiving, a useless 6 page reflection, and a project where no one gets full points are clearly attempts to make an intro class seem more important than what it actually is. Avoid.
Let me be the 100th 'awesome' rating. Because Prof. Hard's psyc101 is simply the best introduction to psyc one can have. She is absolutely incredible, bar none

This class is the most bureaucratic and unnecessarily structured class I have ever taken at Duke. Useless research requirements and summary essays of the class provide zero value to anyone. This class is just an attempt at making freshman girls feel like being a psych major is a rigorous and respectable route.
Dr. Hard is AMAZING! I would highly recommend this class to anyone - even non-psych majors!

reviews.comment: The lectures are great! Though a lot of busy work.

Must attend her lectures - it's true what they say about every lecture being a TED talk + lectures are super important for this course! Take even if not in psych

WHAT A GOAT! Take this class

Lectures are very interesting. There is a reading for every class, along with a reading quiz. You can do the reading quiz until you get all the points. There is also a paper and other assignments and three midterms as well as a final. Definitely work, but worth it.

PSY101 is the best with Hard. Every lecture/assignment is so well-curated. Skim the textbook readings for bold only, don't waste your time. Only study those for exams. All other grades are easily achievable, but attendance and attention during lecture is mandatory. Hard makes everyone want to be a psych major, so don't miss out.

Dr. Hard does lecture like a Ted Talk. She is clearly passionate about the subject and works to engage the class even in a large lecture hall. She makes the topics very personable. reviews.comment: This was such an interesting class!

Dr. Hard is the best. Take this class if you have the opportunity, material is not only relevant but extremely interesting, and Dr. Hard does an amazing job presenting it. The class is not overly difficult, just put in the effort and you will be rewarded.

Hard is an EXCELLENT lecturer who clearly loves what she does. She expects a lot from students, so there is a lot of reading, projects are graded harshly, and tests weigh a lot.

I LOVED Dr. Hard. Her lectures were like Ted Talks every class, and she and Dr. Grisham made an excellent team. The class was sometimes a lot of work, but it was manageable and she did an excellent job preparing us for anything. I'm so happy I took the class, and I looked forward to class every single day.

Great lecturer. No tech in class. Very interesting content, but way more work than I anticipated for a 101 class. Listening to Professor Hard was like attending a Ted Talk every other day. She was so knowledgeable and passionate about the topic, and she made lectures super fun and engaging.  There's a lot of reading to do outside of class, but the content is interesting.

reviews.comment:
Dr. Hard is such a great lecturer. She presented information in such a well-organized, engaging manner that I really liked going to lectures. It was my fave class this yr.

There is quite a bit of overlap w. AP psych, but there def is a lot of new content, so tests require some good studying. However, if you study, the tests will be super easy.
Exceptional professors who make every lecture intriguing

Professors Hard and Grisham are insane lecturers. I would say it's a little bit harder than the typical 101 class should be. It was lighter for me because I took AP Psych in high school. The discussion seems dreadful but it's actually the best part of the class.
Interesting lectures and good professor. Just too much work & the annoying tech-free policy.

TAKE THIS CLASS AS S/U, or you will regret it. Too much work and too many grading criteria. You have both final exams and papers, horrible experience. But Dr. Hard is indeed a GREAT lecturer and could go to a TED talk.

reviews.comment: I absolutely loved Psych101 and professor Hard. She is so incredibly inspirational and every class is like a TedTalk. That being said, the class is a lot of notes and vocabulary, but if you do the readings, you should do fine.

Dr. Hard is a fantastic lecturer. This is one of those classes that everyone at Duke should take because the content is so valuable in itself to just know. If you aren't planning on being a Psych major/pre-med/ this class isn't required for any specific track you plan on taking - take it pass/fail so you don't worry so much about the exam grades.

reviews.comment: Loved Psych101. A little more work than i expected but not bad at all, and lectures are really fascinating.

Dr. Hard is by far the best lecturer I've had. Her lectures are eye-opening, engaging, and have helped me see the world in new ways. On a daily basis, I find myself using the knowledge from this class to be a better person in this world. I truly believe this is the one must-take class at Duke.

Great lecturer, and the tests are a complete joke so that's good! However, extreme busywork: it tries to be a actual science class, but forgets it's a 101. The work is also useless, and god knows why discussions exist. However, if you try even a little bit, it's kind of difficult to not do well. Overall, cut the BS, and keep the lectures.

Dr. Hard is hands down one of the best professors at Duke! Her lectures are informative and entertaining; it sometimes feels like you're watching a TedTalk. reviews.comment: The exams are easy, but there is too much busy work in the class, and the discussions are so silly. Lectures are pretty good, but Hard teaches with a very liberal bias.

Dr. Hard is incredible. Single-handedly made me want to continue with psych as someone who took the class to fulfill the NS requirement. Her lectures are like award-winning documentaries in real-time. Genuinely cares about teaching and her students. This review does not encapsulate how amazing she is. Take the class to see for yourself.
Lots of reading and tests are very memorization heavy, but Dr. Hard is an incredible lecturer and very effective teacher.
Dr. Hard is amazing, her lectures are such a pleasure to attend and she's by far the best professor I've ever had at Duke.

Psychology 101 is an absolutely legendary class simply due to Dr. Hard. She manages the entire course so well. Even though attendance is mandatory, the entertaining lectures make it very worth going. I highly recommend taking PSY101!

I really liked Dr. Hard. She's an amazing lecturer. However, I will caution you to beware the structure of Psych 101 in general...the class is easy if you put in the work, but I sometimes felt like there was useless busywork involved in the class. The class gets better throughout the semester; Hard herself was incredible.

Amazing lecturer, always engaging and made learning interesting. Exams are straight memorization and get easier as the semester goes on. Big emphasis on discussion section. Not a difficult course, and you'll learn a lot of interesting psych concepts that can help you think about the world differently.

Her lectures are like TED talks. It is good that there is no tech allowed because people are actually engaged. Stop complaining about the attendance requirement, tech, etc just do what you're supposed to do and it's basically a free high grade AND you learn a lot.

Amazing lecturer! Has been teaching this class for 16 yrs and her lectures sound like Ted-Talks! reviews.comment: Professor Hard is an amazing lecturer! You may be upset at first with the mandatory attendance and the "no electronics" policy, but she will truly make you forget about all of that! She has the ability to keep over 100 students engaged for the whole class time. Class expectations are clear and you will do well if you keep up with the schedule!

Great lectures. As someone who'd never taken a psych class before, I took a ton of notes so there was a fair share of work. Your grade is cushioned by attendance and discussion. Attendance was a pain in the ass though bc they actually track it. She's fun and makes the content engaging.

Prof. Hard is the best lecturer I've had in my life. She makes the entire content engaging, fun, and easy to understand. However, this class is A LOT OF WORK. It's not hard, but a big part of the tests is only covered in the textbook so you have to read it all. Grading criteria and course structure are clear from the beginning.

Professor Hard is a great lecturer and ensures that the course is as organized as possible considering it tends to have around 300+ students. There is a decent workload but after the 1st exam it lightens if you can optimize

Dr. Hard is one of the most amazing professors that I've had at Duke. She is kind and truly cares about the well-being of her students. reviews.comment: The most interesting and engaging lecturer at Duke. She has a no technology in class rule but it makes sense. Both compassionate and fair. Absolutely love her!

This woman is awesome. Every class is like a TED talk and genuinely so engaging -- she gets the whole class laughing and entertained on the daily. Her class is very organized and clearly lays out the expectations and grading policies. Really great overview of all Psych topics. Beware, it is a lot of work + required attendance + tech free lecture.

Prof. Hard is a really enthusiastic teacher but the psych content is quite tough. There are lectures, weekly quizzes (you can take multiple times until you get 100%) and a reading & writing essay on a study you would like to conduct. I would highly recommend this class if you like psychology, if not don't take it.

Dr. Hard puts an incredible amount of work into making this class a great experience. Lots of textbook reading and studying for midterms requires tons of memorization. Discussions were not the best experience, but the lectures are what made this class great.

Professor Hard is the best lecturer I've had. Her lectures are very engaging and she is extremely well prepared. Be prepared to memorize a lot of terms for the exams.
I don't get the hype surrounding this class ... It's straight up tedious busywork. Unless you're a PSYCH major and have to take it, there are much better alternatives. Be warned.

I took this class because everyone said it would be easy A. It was not true, I had to spend more time on my psychology exams than on chemistry or Chinese, and I got a C from the first test anyway.
Still, I think it was worth the trouble and the professor is great. She gives lectures like a Ted Talk. She is also super helpful and inspiring.

Dr. Hard is probably the best lecturer at Duke. Every single lecture is so engaging and the 75 minute class period doesn't feel long at all because of how good she is at lecturing. Dr. Hard has clear grading criteria and the TAs are very accessible. Every student at Duke should have the opportunity take this class! Take it when you get the chance!

Not an easy class or that enjoyable. Test questions are not hard but there is A LOT of material on each exam which can easily be overwhelming. Loved Dr. Hard. Truly one of the best professors at the university.

This class was truly amazing. I was in awe of Professor Hard's ability to completely captivate a room of 300 people. Never have I had the privilege of experiencing such engaging lectures. I was interested in psych before taking 101 with Dr. Hard, but her class convinced me to major in it. Shes an incredibly gifted lecturer and gives opportunities for extra credit. Loved PSY101 and cannot recommend it enough! Lectures are incredible (they're essentially TED Talks) and make you not care about the mandatory attendance requirement. reviews.comment: Cannot say enough good things about this class and Dr. Hard. Every aspect of her class was designed to make learning welcoming and easy for students. Dr Hard is great! The class is amazing as well. However, it is A TON of work. I repeat A TON. If psych does not interest you or you are looking for an easy elective, I would NOT recommend this class. Great professor, interesting class, lots of readings, and a ton of assignments.

This was by far the hardest class of the semester. If you are hard-working, getting an A is easy. If not, RIP. The lectures themselves are amazing though, every single lecture is like a Tedtalk, and Professor Hard is perfect as a Psych 101 instructor.

reviews.comment: Psych 101 is probably the best class at Duke. Professor Hards lectures are truly amazing. There is a decent amount of work but it is very manageable to do and get an A.

Dr. Hard is one of the must-take professors. She knows the material from inside out. Most of class time is spent with TA but you'll learn a lot from lecture.

There are a lot of readings/ quizzes, and you can't get an A on tests without studying. Don't fall behind! However, Prof Hard is awesome. Psy 101 was online only w her but I still looked forward to pre-recorded lecture because they felt more like TED talks than lectures. SUPER digestible and interesting content! I would def recommend 101 w Hard.

Dr. Hard is one of my favorite professors at Duke. She clearly cares about her students and their learning. She's very accessible outside of class and office hours. Best teacher I've had at Duke, if not ever. The lectures are amazing and her passion for the content is infectious. Class is super well organized. reviews.comment: Despite being asynchronous, every one of Dr Hard's lectures was incredibly engaging and well made. this class is entirely taught by TAs who know nothing about the subject matter. barely saw the professor once.

Sent an extremely rude response to an email requesting a regrade (I ended up being right and got points back). She so desperately wants this class to not be something that people just take for an easy A by adding tedious and unnecessary discussion sections and busywork, but the class is still easy

Amazing lecturer - engaging and material is interesting. Exams make up 60% of the class grade so it helps if you're a decent test taker. Papers aren't so bad but my teaching fellow was a really hard grader.

Professor Hard is a brilliant lecturer! I took AP Psych in high school but had to take this course for a minor and still found it engaging. I liked the semester long project that had you design your own experiment too.

PSY101 is a class that caters to all levels of interest in Psychology and offers real-life experience by making you design your own Psychology study and participating in Psychology studies. Lectures are engaging, very interesting, and extremely well-delivered. Discussion sections could be improved.

Professor Hard is the best lecturer I have ever had. She is extremely engaging, makes the material super accessible and interesting, and is also quite funny and personable. This class does require a lot of work though, like textbook readings, studying, and a writing project.

Professor Hard is an incredible lecturer at Duke, who made my start in Psychology cause me to change my major to pursue it! She is interesting and engaging, and the lectures are very well structured. Exams don't generally contain difficult content, but you need to memorize a lot. Read the textbook, do the Inquisitives and go to lecture to get an A!
Dr. Hard is GOAT. Everyone should take her Psych 101 class.
Dr. Hard is awesome! Her lectures are so interesting, but the course is definitely a good amount of work/reading/studying.

Every one of Dr. Hard's lectures is a TedTalk. Class was fairly simple and plenty of resources to help get the grade you want. She does her best to give everyone a fair chance to succeed and seems to value genuine student interest in the topic. TF's were the only problem but Dr. Hard is available to mediate. Several bonus point opportunities.

Dr. Hard is seriously such an amazing lecturer and she made Psych 101 so so interesting. Even if Psych isn't your major take this class, you will really enjoy it! Dr. Hard is an okay professor, but the curriculum design bothers me. The exams are not tricky, but they require a LOT of memorizations. reviews.comment: This class is a must, even if you are not a psych major. It is a great NS (if that is what you are looking for) but overall so interesting and engaging! She makes the environment of a 200+ person class feel engaging and intimate.

Dr. Hard is the best lecturer I've ever had and even though it's only my first semester at Duke, I'm certain she'll remain at the top for the next 4 years. Another commenter said her lectures feel like TED Talks and I couldn't agree more. Every lecture leaves you blown away and I was genuinely excited for class every day. 10/10 would take again.
SHES A BEAST! best prof at duke and shes hot too

Lets just say that Dr. Hard is not only one of the best professors Ive ever seen, she is also one of the most perfect human I know. When people say every one of her lecture is like a TED Talk, they are not joking. So many people were converted to psych majors after her 101

Dr. Hard is the best professor I've had at Duke so far. Every lecture is literally a TED talk and she makes even the harder topics super easy to understand. Her research also involves students and learning so she sometimes even collects data from us in class to help us learn later on. The tests weren't hard but definitely read the textbook:)

Dr. Hard is the best professor I have ever had. Her lectures are engaging and interesting, and she motivated me to want to learn and ask questions. I would highly recommend this class and any other opportunity to work with her.

Dr. Hard is amazing! She is one of my favorite professors that I've ever had. I took her class my first semester at Duke and could not have asked for a better experience. She is engaging, funny, and makes the material interesting. Tests will require you to study but are definitely not overly difficult, you WILL do well if you work hard.

I'm not a psych major and just took this class as a pre-med requirement but Psych 101 became one of my favorite classes I have ever taken. If you put in the effort, an A is almost guaranteed. Dr. Hard is the best lecturer I have ever had and I actually looked forward to the days I got to hear her teach! She is an all-around amazing professor.

Dr. Hard's class was by far the most logistically sound, efficient class I have ever taken. Lectures were amazing with several cool guest speakers, grading was broken down line by line, and covered great concepts. Amazing professor, amazing class!

I was excited everyday to go to Dr. Hard's lectures. They were extremely engaging and applicable, even though I am not a psych major. Tests are easy if you go to lecture, study, and learn the studies. Very thorough course (and you get an NS) and a good break from hard classes, but you learn a ton of useful information. Definitely recommend

Dr. Hard made this class interesting, as she is a great lecturer. However, she made the class mostly based on the textbook. Tests we heavily based on the readings and barely any about the lectures. The grading is also very harsh as many of her writing prompts are unclear. Not a good class

reviews.comment: Bridgette is one of the best lecturers at Duke. It feels like you're attending a Ted Talk and she mixes things up with videos and studies so you don't feel like she's reciting material. Additionally, all of the logistics of the class are incredibly clear and fair and there's a lot of buffers to your grade so it's easy to do well.

This class helped me to really invest time into lectures. She made the class interesting. The tests were not terrible although they do require a substantial amount of studying. You will learn a lot in this class.

Cannot recommend Dr. Hard enough. She is unbelievable: every lecture is like watching a TED Talk. She made me want to major in Psych. Midterms require a lot of memorization, but once you study enough the exams themselves are not too difficult.

her lectures are freakin amazing. she's hilarious but also actually teaches in a way that gets you to remember everything. midterms are easy, just read the textbook bc sometimes there are specific details from the text. final is so easy bc she tells u exactly how to study. for the R&W, just make sure u revise it a lot so ur TF knows u tried.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Hard couldn't have been nicer or more caring. She genuinely cares about teaching students and is always available after class for questions or concerns.
