The class is very general and requires a lot of memorization but there are enough assessments to boost your grade if needed.

Dr. Hard is a phenomenal teacher, researcher and advisor on so many levels. She confirmed my love for psychology, knows how to teach, and is incredibly knowledgeable. Although her class involved a lot of reading and memorization, I learned an invaluable amount across such a wide range of topics. She's a natural teacher and a fantastic human being.
Absolutely amazing professor. Every lecture is like a Ted Talk. Great class for everyone, not only psychology majors

Psy101 is one of the best classes to take at Duke. Professor Hard is a phenomenal lecturer and makes each class feel like a TED Talk. The material is extremely interesting, and if you stay on top of readings and review your notes for the weekly take home quizzes you won't have to cram for the tests. I would 100% recommend this class .

Doctor Hard is definitely one of the best professors I have had at Duke. She has her own unique way of delivering the content during lectures, all in a very interesting and engaging way. I wish I could take more classes with her! 100% recommendation for anyone thinking about taking her class.

Dr. Hard is one of the best professors I have had at Duke. Her engaging lectures and caring attitude are nearly unparalleled. I could not recommend taking a class with her more. The class itself is not incredibly difficult, and you will be fine if you read the textbook and pay attention to the lectures.

Dr. Hard really does a great job with the lectures. Always engaging and interesting. This class is not a walk in the park, but if you put in some effort you will be fine. In addition, it is really interesting.

Hard is a phenomenal lecturer. She's extremely well prepared and I feel like I'm in a Ted talk every class. The tests are heavily based on what's said in lecture, so pay attention, but there are several questions every test based on the readings. The writing project is quite manageable as you work on it slowly over the whole semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: The best professor I have ever had... she cares so much about her students and genuinely wants students to do well. Lectures are so interesting and the class is structured in a very fair, organized way.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: By far the best class I've ever taken and definitely one of the best professors I've ever had. The lectures were so inspiring and interesting in so many ways and made me really excited to study for the class which is something I've never felt before. I could tell she really cared about the students and what they learned during class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: good and caring prof. he just talks very fast in his lectures and goes off on tangents sometimes. No practice exams, but the exams aren't that hard. lecture attendance not required so just self study

calvin checks all the boxes a math prof should check. good lecturer, speaks fast but you get used to it. decent notes (still better to take your own). HWs and wkly quizzes were light. he does give hard exams that require understanding beyond HW probs, but everything needed is covered in lecture. learned a lot without a massive time commitment

The guy was too smart to be teaching this class. I know this is supposed to be the most challenging multivariable calculus offered, but he assumed that we knew a lot more than we did. He acted like the content was easy to understand, which was not true. His lectures were unclear, and the tests were hard.

Actually one of the worst classes I have ever taken. The professor was too smart to teach the class and lectures were hard to follow. When I went to office hours to get help he would often get frustrated at me. The homework and quizzes did not prepare you for the exams. Honestly just take 212 you'll most likely learn more
Okay class, last third of the class is significantly harder than the rest. Calvin is decent at lecturing but is barely accessible outside of class. Final is significantly harder than midterms.

Clear and concise lectures. Homework is relatively straightforward, and weekly quizzes give good self-evaluations. Tests are very comprehensive and occasionally tricky. The final was rough. Make sure you actually go over what you learn while doing problem sets.

Took this class because he was teaching it. Lectures are well-paced with clear explanations. The book isn't needed since he shares notes. Homework is completion-based, and he answers questions well (in person and on Ed). There's a short weekly quiz with correction opportunities. Exams mirror homework, and grading is generous (if you do the work).

a pretty solid teacher who posts lecture slides and makes it so you don't have to read the textbook. homework/quizzes are essentially based on completion. midterms, while challenging, are curved pretty leniently, and the final can replace *both* your midterm grades. chill class overall and mcphail-snyder is a decent lecturer

Snyder was a good lecturer but generally the lectures didn't really match what was on the homework or tests. Tests are worth 80% but later tests can replace earlier ones if you score better. Homework wasn't too bad but didn't really prepare you for the tests.
Not a great lecturer, kind of all over the place and the notes aren't very helpful. He is very understanding and kind, especially in office hours. This is for math 222

THIS IS FOR MATH 222
He talks very quickly but you get used to it within 2 classes. The lectures are pretty straightforward though some lessons can be a bit unclear. Tests are fair and the grading policy in this course is very very easy as homework and take-home quizzes make up a large portion, and the quizzes can be corrected for full credit.

He's a good guy, but not a good professor as in he explains things at a very high level that's hard to follow. Our class average was also 30 points below other Math221 classes taught by other professors. The tests are hard and weigh 90% of our grade. Would recommend taking Math221 with another professor.

Caring professor who is clearly very passionate about math. He's always willing to discuss topics more in depth and obviously care that his students do well and understand the material. His exams are extremely fair (from lecture/HW) and his completion-based homework emphasizes understanding. Great prof, would take again!!
Great guy.

Really nice guy, makes a conscious effort to explain his thought process in his explanations, although he tends to make some mistakes along the way and pause, which might disrupt your train of thought. Very flexible with homework deadlines. Exams were slightly harder compared to the other section, but he is a significantly more lenient grader
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Calvin is friendly and personable. His grading curves are (almost too?) generous. The exams were reasonable and reflected a fair breadth of content from the homework and lectures. Sometimes, he errs, backtracks, or lays out definitions and examples strangely in his lectures: a little unsteady and hard to follow at times. Readily answers questions.

Professor Calvin's grading scheme made it very easy to do well in the class. Midterms were easier than all other sections, especially when considering the generous curve. Lectures were overall, not the best, but it is hard to argue with stress-free homework grading and exams.

Prof. Calvin is a great guy. He is super accessible during office hours and walks through his thought process while solving HW questions. 3 midterms accounted for 90% of the grade, but he has a test knockout policy. He is a relatively lenient grader, and does not take much (sometimes no) points off for computational errors and focuses on thinking.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great professor. The class was very hard. The homework was graded for completion with feedback given on select problems. Prof Calvin was also very accessible during office hours and encouraged asking questions during class. The lectures were hard to follow sometimes. I found the tests impossible though, and they were the majority of the grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He takes time to explain things and takes questions during lectures, which is helpful, but his lectures get confusing and hard to follow. Have the videos from an old professor and they are much easier to follow. Grade based on three midterms and no final, and later midterms can replace earlier ones. Confusing curve. Nice guy though!

Calvin has a very lenient grading scheme, which makes the difficulty of 221 a bit easier to bear. His lectures are fine, but definitely not the best that I have had. The homework is doable. My class had no final exam and three midterms, although it is not clear if that is what he will plan for in the future.
Almost no Assignment. It won't be matter if you're late or even absent for several times. BTW, he also teaches BIO110, and this review is just based on this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Took Bio 110. Nice person, but goes off on tangents that aren't relevant to the subject. The midterm was open note and relatively easy. He often skipped through slides when lecturing, and did not spend much time on each slide making it hard to follow his lectures and material in class.
Cscscscscs scscscscs big cs
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Took Bio110, Prof Huansheng will teach you everything but the course. He's enthusiastic and caring about the subject, but cannot instill the knowledge of the course into students at all. His classes can become extremely boring, and you learn barely anything. However, the course is easy. It's up to self-study, and the exams are easy too. 5/10.

The Professor was not specialised at all in the course that he was teaching. Most of the time, it was up to self-studying to really learn the material necessary for class. He usually goes off on tangents and never really discusses relevant course information unless it's from his own personal opinion (which is usually unrealistic or pompous).

Some comments about him demanding a specific writing style are just wrong; he simply expects you to write with precision and logic. Helpful for students who want to understand how to read and interpret research publications, improve scientific writing skills, or become better communicators. Class is graded on 3 essays, primarily analyzing research.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Genuinely a condescending professor who obviously won't give you a satisfactory grade unless you write exactly how he wants. The writing required isn't hard, but his grading system is unnecessarily harsh for students adjusting to college.

Professor Moskovitz is genuinely a really good professor. Learned a lot about how to write better, and he was an overall really helpful teacher. I will say that for some of our essays, he would mandate that we meet with him, where he would read parts of our essay aloud and provide real-time feedback, something I found to be incredibly helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He wants you to write in a very specific manner, but as long as you are adaptable in your writing style and put in effort, you should be just fine.
The class wasn't particularly fun, but you do learn some skills necessary for literature research and how to read research papers.

Do not take his Writing 101 class. Extremely harder than the other writing classes. Grades extremely tough and specifically. Don't take this class, makes it harder to get an A than major requirements.

honestly, I feel like as long as you participate in class and engage on a regular basis, this class is not difficult to ace. as long as you show up prepared and are willing to participate, the course ends up being worth it. homework is light and on topic, prepares you for class, and usually doesn't take long.

I enjoyed Writing 101 w/ Professor Moskovitz a lot more than I thought I would. He's super nice and great at giving helpful feedback. I was quite worried as the syllabus stated that "You have to work hard for a B" but as long as you think hard about your writing and really use his feedback you'll do well in the course.

Professor Moskovitz is a great teacher and really improves your writing and make you really work to get better, but grades extremely hard and really difficult to get an A. 4 real grades with random pop quizzes that are about random things in the readings. Papers usually are in the B range and some Cs.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: He is a very nice man but his class was extremely boring and unproductive.  He was also not very clear on how he wanted assignments to be completed so that led to a lot of confusion outside of class.  He can also can be a bit condescending at times which is extremely annoying. I wouldn't recommend this class.

He was strict about attendance and not messing around during class, but his class was unbelievably easy. There was only 4 assignments the entire semester. The final paper (which we had a month to work on) was only 3 pages

I enjoyed his class on the science of sleep. He was very straight forward and was always willing to clarify questions and give helpful feedback. However, the guidelines for the final commentary were unclear. Additionally, he was a hard grader on the final paper.

Not one of the worst writing 20s in regards to work. You have three or four big projects that you work on all semester. However, he definitely lets his opinion of people affect his judgment. Loves men. Loves engineers. If you're not one of those two (or both), it's really hard to get a good grade.

this class is an easier writing 20. i think i only had like 3 maybe 4 papers all semester. compared to a lot of other writing20 classes, that is really really good. also this class is really all about editing and peer editing. i recommend meeting with him outside of class, he likes that. this class is not creative and is somewhat dry but its easy
Really easy WRITING 20 class-- that is if you can put up with the pointless use of class time. Cool professor though, and did learn a lot.
i would say his grading is extremely biased, and his class useless and boring.
pretty good professor. only thing is that he made us buy this Cite Right book that was completely useless... wasted like 35 bucks. other than that pretty good.
Great professor- after I graduated, was one of the most helpful real-world courses I took. Thanks Dr. M!

Make sure to schedule appointments with him to go over your writing--he'll tell you exciting how to fix your paper, it's extremely helpful. He's a harsh grader, and he picks at every single word, so basically strive for perfection. Class is boring and useless-you'll spend the entire class going over one useless detail-most boring classes in my life
Hated writing before his class.  Loved it afterwards.  It is infectious.

This was probably one of the easiest writing 20 classes. Most of the work is done in groups and there weren't that many assignments. Revision was emphasized over the amount of writing, so it was mostly short papers written in multiple drafts. The professor was helpful at times, but lectures weren't so interesting. Grading was relatively generous.

Dr. M was one of the first profs i had at duke- i thought he was amazing. I'm not just saying that for kicks...he was incredibly knowledgable and as long as you aren't retarded and can follow directions, you can pull an A.  you just have to be able to take his teachings and incorporate them in to your writing.

class is boring and prof. is anal and makes you go over drafts way too many times for the bad grades he gives.  did the most pointless research and writing for this class...thought it would be easier than it turned out to be.

Class is harder than I expected.  He is meticulous about little details and makes you beat your writing drafts to death.  It is a boring class, and he is very anal, but compared to a lot of other writing classes, it isn't that much work.
The class is just boring and bland- as is the prof.
Don't take his classes at all costs.

He's totally hot.  We do random and boring class activities but everyone can get through it becasue he's so beautiful.  Seriously, you don't have to be interested in the class because you will be interested in him.
The class was ok. He's a good prof but the material just isn't that great. His voice gets annoying after a while.
No Comments
Dude sometimes goes on and on... class is easy though.  Two papers and a group project.
I now have a deep hatred for Berry, Postman, Zey, and the Tofflers
No Comments
Class poorly thought-out, limited help available, sometimes cruel

History of Latinxs in the US was a really enjoyable class. I learned a lot and the class was really collaborative. It's a great class and not hard at all, it is really easy to get help and you are really never feel alone. Great history class.

I really enjoyed Professor Marquez's History of Latinxs in the US class. The readings are somewhat intimidating at first but they do a great job at humanizing history. Make sure to start your research project early, and feel free to talk to her with any questions or concerns you have, she is very accessible!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Loved History of Latinxs in the U.S. She covers an impressive amount of history in the span of this course. She wants her students to succeed and provides good feedback. The reading material she assigns humanizes history, I came to class excited for discussion every time. Will miss this class a lot!

She is really funny and engaging. However, I like her co-lead Professor Chappel even more. The class is a great foundational course and it's imperative that you go to lecture. You will have to hand in your notebook twice for notebook grades so make sure that you pay attention and date your notes on attended lectures and homework.
Great professor and class.

Celia is an amazing professor who is passionate about teaching Spanish. I learned so much in Spanish 204, but I never felt overwhelmed by the work load or difficulty. If you have the option, take a class with Celia!

100% recommend taking Celia!! she is so kind and understanding and will go out of her way to make sure her students succeed. she isn't a harsh grader and the assignments aren't very difficult. she can be a little unorganized but if you email her she'll clarify and try to support you.

Celia is the best! 302 is the perfect class for the FL requirement - no tests, minimal speaking, and minimal HW/assignments. I am not very good at Spanish, but Celia made me feel comfortable in the class. Celia is hilarious and one of the most caring professors I've had - she asks about our weekends and has gotten to know us well. Take 302!

Celia is an amazing professor. She's super kind given that language classes can be intimidating. The class structure takes time getting used to but becomes routine. You know what she expects each day, and she calls on everyone according to the order of attendance. Writing assignments and quizzes are easy, and I've enjoyed her as a professor.

Not very accessible nor understanding for higher-level courses despite what students report for lower-level courses. She is well-intentioned but too frazzled and unorganized. If you are a student who is passionate about learning the language, do not choose this professor.

TAKE A CLASS WITH HER!! She is the most caring and hilarious prof you will have. She is there to help you succeed. Class is very easy. I have never laughed so hard in a class. Take a class with her if you have the chance! You will not regret it.

Celia is by far the best professor to have for any level of spanish. She is hilarious, caring, and excited to have students learn spanish. The structure of her lectures revolves around conversational spanish while learning the course - giving students a better feel for the language. If Celia is available for a class, you take that class.
She really cares about the students and wants everyone to get a good grade. If you are taking Spanish 204, I highly recommend taking it with Profe Celia!

Prof. Perez-Ventura is one of the best professors at the university. If you can get past a pretty intimidating first week, you'll find the class fine, as she's an easy grader and hilarious. Be prepared for a decent amount of assignments, none of which are super hard.

Celia is the best Spanish professor at Duke! The topics we covered in this class were sometimes difficult, but Celia made sure to explain everything thoroughly and help us when needed. She is super caring and genuinely passionate about teaching Spanish. If you want to take Spanish at Duke, I would highly recommend taking a class with Celia.

I love Celia! If you need a 300-level Spanish class, 302 with her is the way to go. I learned a lot about grammar, and she is such a caring teacher. Challenged me appropriately while making sure the workload was never too much. She's also so funny and loves her students. Would definitely take another Spanish class with her.
Celia was my most favorite professor I've had throughout my time at Duke. She really cares about her students and wants them to succeed.

Celia is such a great Spanish professor. She always tries to help her students succeed. She is a fair grader and provides a lot of feedback on assignments. She is also a very funny and kind person, and I always looked forward to her class even though it was early in the morning. I would highly recommend taking a Spanish class with her!
Best Spanish professor at Duke by a long shot. Sweetest, most caring professor I've had. Outstanding teacher and person. Grades very fairly.

Celia is so kind and really cares about her students understanding AND enjoying the material. She was really caring during the semester when we had some COVID related issues. Shes hilarious and easy to talk to, and I felt like the quality of my Spanish improved but also my confidence in the language. Online wasnt ideal but shes worth it!!!!

I loved class with Celia! She is the sweetest person ever and she really loves her students. The class is also super easy, with not a lot of work needed at all. She does call on students often to read or answer questions, but she goes in alphabetical order so you know when you're next. I would take every class with her if I could.
She is the sweetest woman on the planet. She cares about all of her students and just wants to see them enjoy the Spanish language and culture. I would take every Spanish class with her if I could.

So the bad part is that it's pretty hard to understand what she says. But the good part is that she's really sweet and her quizzes are easy. She's the kind of professor who will basically give you the answer on a quiz if you ask.

Professor Cederbaum is the ABSOLUTE BEST!!! she is a fantastic lecture. However, she has very high expectations for her students. You must, I repeat, must prepare for lectures. If you go in cold turkey, you'll be lost. She goes above and beyond to make the learning experience amazing for everyone.

Her tests are super-super hard and long (about 20 pages), which I feel extremely unfair when I got my midterm grade and compared it to that of the students from other classes. She does a lot of proofs during classes but I don't think they are really useful. But in general, she's nice and willing to help and clear about what she's saying.
Hard Course.Professor is nice and helpful.
She made me switch from literature to math. Need I say more?

She was a great teacher. tests were very hard but the final was extremely easy compared to her tests. she gives a lot of partial credit on her tests and will fight for points that other teacher took off on your final exam. she really cars about her students and wants them to succeed!
She was very good at explaining the material. her tests were hard but gave a lot of partial credit. the final was much easier compared to her tests throughout the year. great teacher!!

Good professor, although can be dreadfully boring. Super nice, super approachable. Oh and she solved some math problem people had been working on for a century in her dissertation or something. She is legit. Tests are rough (averages were a 61, 67, and 56), but gives a ton of partial credit. Does make you write a few essays which is a bit annoying.

She's one of my favorite professors at Duke! I love her! She is super nice and wants students to learn. Instead of repeating the proofs in the book, she always proves theorems with different methods. A lot of people say math professors cannot teach. She's an exception!
Her tests are super tough (averages in the 50's) but she is also generous with partial credit. She's also really big on conceptual stuff and makes you write essays.
The most open and helpful teacher. His lectures are interesting and the exams are easy and graded very generously.

Loved having Tom! He brought so much excitement to History of Energy every day. ~30 pages of reading and required 3 pages of notes before each class but the grading is not harsh at all. The exams are just brain dumping what you remember about the keywords, nothing to stress about. The experiential demonstrations about coal and fire were also neat.
Great dude, amazing lectures.
Genuinely one of the most genuine people out there and really loves what he teaches. Easy class while learning a good amount about energy history. Would recommend anyone to take this class.

Take a class with Tom! He enjoys the content and teaching it as well. It's easy and engaging to follow through the seminars. You need to do the readings tho, so that you are ready to engage in class. He gives good feedback on the essays, and grades gracefully. Was not interested in energy at first but he made it worth it and awesome!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Respected

reviews.comment: Professor Cinq-Mars is an awesome professor. The in-class experience is always enjoyable, even if we veer off course in the discussions often. Only complaint I have is about the amount of reading, but that's to be expected of a seminar course. Not a tough grader, but you just have to get the work done. Sometimes takes a while to release grades.

Professor Cinq-Mars class was really good and he cares more about open discussion than particulars about work. Readings were heavy sometimes but the only homework is taking notes on the readings and tests were basically vocab tests. Very passionate and friendly professor would highly recommend this class or any class with him.
Awesome class. Super easy if you participate and turn in HW. No surprises. There is a good amount of reading.
Great professor
Love his lectures and how he organizes the class. It was easy for freshmen to follow along and the test was not hard as long as you pay attention in class.

One of my favorite teachers at Duke, I connected with him on multiple occasions for guidance through internships in the energy sector. In terms of 197S, he was great. A lot of readings and a lot of writing (essays for exams) but if you pay attention it is very easy to get an A. Energy can be boring, but his history background made the class great.

Tom's an absolute sweetheart and a terrific lecturer. Brings a seemingly boring topic to life. He is incredibly available and adjusts course requirements flexibly in response to feedback. However, be prepared to read 200+ pages per week (though most of the work is front-loaded) and some degree of disorganization. Still amazing overall though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Group projects

reviews.comment: Incredibly engaging professor and recommend taking any class you can with him while at Duke.

Tom was my favorite teacher this semester (Modern Regulatory State-PUBPOL219). He is very dynamic and passionate and encourages everyone to engage. He worked hard to create an intellectual + low-stakes environment. Uses fun, pop-culture references to start class + read lots of primary sources as case studies (including from the 1800s!).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This guy is the GOAT. Everyone needs to take his class
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: This man would literally do anything for his students. He is interested in our lives outside his classroom and most of all, cares about our mental wellbeing. His love for teaching is evident in the effort he puts into organizing the course and class periods. He is incredibly knowledgable and clearly passionate about the topics he teaches.

Tom is amazing! He is passionate, engaging, and empathetic. As a seminar class, it was tiny, but Tom facilitated interesting discussions and somehow got everyone to contribute. His syllabus is organized and clear; the assignments were actually fun to complete... some group, some individual. Definitely take a course with him if you can!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Professor Ciocanel is the nicest professor I have ever come across at Duke. She is the only reason I was able to survive the class. Super accomodative, a great teacher, and cares greatly for her students. Take anything offered by her, and you would be fine.

ABSOLUTELY AMAZING!!! Dr. Ciocanel made 221 a very manageable class. She was always accessible during her twice-weekly office hours. Definitely really cares about her students' success, that much is very obvious. Exams are very fair, mimic homework problems for the most part. Homework assignments are HEAVY, but that's just the nature of 221.

The class itself is very challenging in terms of content, but Dr. Ciocanel is so nice and actually doesnt want us to fail - so the exams are much more doable than homework assignments. Shes very understanding and you can see she cares a lot for her students

Professor Ciocanel did an amazing job with this hybrid course. The content in the course is necessary and valuable for future math classes. Ciocanel lectures well and has a sweet personality. She is helpful in office hours, and her classroom is a very inclusive and welcoming space. I would recommend anybody take a math course with her.

Linear Algebra is a pretty difficult course, but Professor Ciocanel does her best to explain the material (her lectures are from the book, but it's useful to be able to ask questions) , holds pretty regular office hours, and tries her best to make the tests fair and similar to the HW and lectures. Do the HW and read the book- join a study group.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I just really love Dr. Ciocanel. She obviously really cares about both math and her students. I slept through the very first class and she gave me access to the lecture recording. Linear algebra is a super tough subject, so I struggled a lot especially in the first half of the semester; it's best to have a strong math background in this class.
DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. You will regret it. Unbearable amount of work. His art taste is  — only obsessed with his own art. Only accepts his own opinions, never listens to students.

I took one of Kaley's courses to complete my social science requirement at DKU. His grading style and syllabus are confusing and I found him to be quite rude to his students. While his critiques can be valid, i wish he was more nice. If you are planning to take his class, I really hope that you have a good time, but I wouldn't recommend it.

He taught Street Photography Miniterm class. The class was easy, and the non-graded format worked really well. We went out to shoot photos daily, and Prof. gave detailed feedback to students who presented their work before the final projects.
Not very recommended for anyone without any film industry experience.

professors with bad grades. There were no clear criteria, and many of the students in MA212 got bad grades. Although the class was OK, the score was painful. I put in a lot of effort and the professor didn't see it. The class is in the form of group discussion, the actual teaching is relatively small
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I love him!
He's really nice.

Prof. Kaley was really fun to take a class from. He taught us the basics of film editing, which weren't hard to grasp, and then gave us video projects to reinforce them. These were creative projects in which we had little to no restriction and it was super fun. He also accommodated us entering films in school film festivals.

Course is graded off of 2 essays, a 10min presentation & participation. I learned so much in this class. The readings were interesting & lectures helped clarify what we read. There was also opportunity to discuss the articles we read before having to write our papers which was also nice. Dr. Clements is the best-- I'd take every class she teaches!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I took this last semester/my freshman spring. Dr. Clements is easily my favorite professor at Duke. She is so caring, funny, very knowledgeable, and open to talking after class. The course is graded off of 3 tests and homework. Do the readings and go to lecture-- you'll learn a lot and do well!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Class isn't too difficult, though lectures can be dry sometimes. Prof is very helpful and caring, and is accessible outside of class.
I really liked this class. My first language is not Eng, and Dr. Clements always met with me and answered all my questions. Classes/lectures were organized. Tests were tough but fair.

Dr. Clements did not run a good class. Yes, she has interesting anecdotes, but they derail the lecture. There is little organization and, even as an intro class, the depth is only superficial. She is knowledgeable but a poor instructor. Exams were written with errors -- contest the points off! 

Students point out her mistakes and she denies them.

Prof. Clements is not only extremely knowledgeable and is the top in her field, but she is also extremely sweet and kind. As long as you put some effort into the assignments, you'll get a good grade. Lectures are interesting and sometimes funny, though the class isn't super structured which I didn't mind.
the tests are too highly weighted, and the lecture format makes things oftentimes confusing and uninteresting. significant time required outside of class to do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This class is grades 25% homework and 25% for each of three exams. She will say in lecture what is on the test and it will be on the test so if you miss lecture you miss a question or so on the test. I'd say the tests are 60% lecture 40% textbook. Homework is an easy A. I missed too much lecture but if you go and listen you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class is very interesting and should be fairly easy for native English speakers. Dr. Clements is super knowledgeable about all things language, and if you prompt her with a question you will inevitably get back fascinating little tidbits about the topic. She gives you every opportunity for extra credit and is a very generous grader, too.
Very caring prof who can sometimes get off topic (but it's fun/funny). Passionate about what she teaches and a bit unorganized, but super nice and easygoing.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Clements cares about her students and makes herself available outside of class. The class is mostly graded on papers and a few other assignments; however, is it a writing class. She encourages group work when reviewing papers and sharing ideas. She is a fair and fast grader. The workload was not overwhelming and the class was enjoyable.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Good book used. She adds in articles (some older and some newer) to get extra info to discuss. Great lectures with examples. She likes it when you participate, makes for good class conversations. Felt included and not judged for my language differences. Before COVID this is a prof I would have wanted to flunch with.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Helpful class that goes with my language study courses. Phono, morphology, and sociolinguistics I liked. I found out I hate drawing syntax trees (another review mentions that too), but I made it through. I did not like historical linguistics, but it's not a lot. Tests are difficult but fair. She gives partial credit on short answer questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Clements is great. Had prof before, & she wrote a recommendation for me, and I got it. Lecture heavy; intros usually are. Book is ok. She goes over most and gives lots of HW in many languages for phonology, morphology. Syntax is mostly English HW. Tests are online since some people are online and some in class (fair for all). Easy to talk to.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: OK, so a def. lecture heavy. It's been harder to participate in the online sections (i feel weird speaking up on camera). Good subjects covered in the course. Textbook is all Amer English, but she adds in Welsh, Scottish, and Irish Eng. We looked at a Nigerian Eng corpus. And she has a few examples from other dialects. Couple of HWs, mid & final.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Definitely not a mind blowing class, but a good intro to sociolinguistics and that way of thinking. Dr. Clements is in any case a kind fun professor, but if you're looking for super structured classes with specific points to write down, maybe look elsewhere.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Canceled class often. HW and reading unnecessary. Graded easily on small amount of projects at midterm and finals time. Participation is not counted, only attendance for some days. Absolute queen. Easiest class I have taken at Duke.

3 tests (one was open book!) Tests have some memorized vocab and application of ling analysis. Gives little study guides before a test. Lots of ppts. The book can be a bit confusing (syntax), but she answered all my questions. Gives a bit more time than some profs. Still don't like syntax, but I would take another course with Dr. Clements.

My accent has been made fun of before, but not in this class. This entire class is Language and Society. We have looked at things like gender and race & specific examples too of Hebrew, Arabic, English, and French. Textbook is pretty easy to read. Lecture and interesting class discussions, a presentation, &2 tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed this class. OK, maybe not drawing the tree diagrams in Syntax, but she even made that kind of fun. She loves this class and that comes through in her teaching. She is excited about language study, which is a bit infectious. Definitely recommend this and her Language and Society course.

Dr. Clements is awesome in this Intro course. She stays after or meets with you and answers all questions. Her examples are interesting, and she creates a discussion type environment for the class, which I did not expect in an intro course. I would definitely take another course from her!

1) What we (students) should expect from her and what she expects from us are not clear. 2) she cancels classes very often (3 times) , sometimes 15 minutes before the class start. 3) She talks about her son, you know... 4) Honestly, she doesn't have much to say other than what the textbook has already said, which is available online, FOR FREE.

Last Lin course I took at Duke: Language and Society. Great material, ppts covered most material as well. Interesting examples (especially comedy bits and commercials) and discussion was usually fun. We chose our own paper/project topics which I prefer.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Lecture most days, but it's an intro, and many in the class had not had a linguistics class before, so understandable. Some homework in phonology, morphology, and syntax. Does not agree with everything in the book, but not all profs agree, so that's okay. Willing to meet outside of class. Answers all questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Prof Clements was an okay professor and gave a standard enough intro to linguistics that didn't make me want to cancel my double major in it. However, she often contradicted the assigned textbook which made studying troublesome. Other than that, she was lenient on grading and posted class ppts on Sakai so going to lecture wasn't necessary

Professor Clements is cool and accommodating with students, but I can't say I got much out of her class. We just read through the book and she gave powerpoints on the material. Not a hard class though, but overall, I really didn't learn much and could have just read the book on my own. She is really nice and very willing to talk after/outside class
Not a hard class overall. Be sure to read the textbook, powerpoint, and memorize all the materials. Lectures could be dry if you are not interested in the topic.

The semester is not over yet, but so far interesting and loaded with material. Mid-term study guide (not all teachers do). Partial credit on text. She is willing to stay after class or discuss things before class (I'm busy during her office hours). The first few lectures were long; ppts were too much, but most of us did not have the book yet.
She always doubts your answers, even when she doesn't know the facts herself.
Subjective, tough grader. Give points deduction for no reason. Bad lecture quality. Avoid this person if you have other choice.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Nisa is a horrible professor who insists her opinion about behavioral science is the only correct opinion. She has stereotypes for Chinese students and acknowledged use of ChatGPT during a quiz but did not do anything about it due to her reasoning of “Chinese students are not used to thinking in English” and says to “cut them some slack.”
This professor made me want to switch majors and never step in the field of Behavioral Science ever again - not in the courses she teaches.
Funny, hilarious, entertaining and really likes to get to know his students
CONGRATULATIONS ON RETIREMENT, PROFESSOR! BEST PROFESSOR OF ALL TIME.

Had him for my ethics 89S seminar on Natural History of Civilization. Really cares about students on an individual basis. He has awesome stories to tell and a lot of wild lore. We were only required to read the chapter before class and meet with the other presenter whenever it was our turn to present the chapter. Very nice and laid back!

unreasonably difficult. they say you don't need to memorize but MEMORIZE EVERYTHING. no curve even tho avgs are low. u will b tested on random details. also stopped recording the lectures bc they realized ppl wouldn't show up otherwise. content is boring, cunningham is all over the place as a lecturer. take diff/easier class for org div if u can

Genuinely confused why everyone rates him so high. One of the worst profs I've had at Duke. Lectures are rambling & unorganized, and he gets terms mixed up frequently. Tests are clearly recycled and don't match course content in the slightest. Unapproachable and condescending. Him and his research seem interesting, but just not a good teacher

Very funny and very engaging. Some of the material on his tests are a little confusing but he is very supportive and tries to meet all his students on a one-on-one basis. Really passionate about what he teaches and is happy to discuss his life and experiences.

Easily one of my favorite professors at Duke. He has a real knack for making lectures interesting and for connecting his own life experiences to what he teaches about. I am very inspired by Dr. C, and I could not recommend his classes more.
Although its a challenging class, definitely take it! Prof. Cunningham cares about his students and wants them to do well. Definitely recommend!

This is an incredibly easy probably the easiest freshman seminar at Duke. However, actually do the readings. It doesn't take that long and Cunningham is so passionate about his students and the material. He meets everyone outside of class to get to know them. He is the kind of professor who will email people for you if he thinks it will help you.

If you have an opportunity to take a class with Dr. Cunningham, definitely do it! He is a great teacher and loves to tell interesting stories during class. Bio 89S is a great class to take because it is not a lot of work at all. It is a bit of reading, but it is super manageable and the books were read were pretty interesting.

He is the BEST! super laid back and true,y loves his job! He has lots of great stories he loves to share and really has so much experience in the world. He is just straight up amazing. As long as you showed up to the class and spoke once during it you got an A.

Professor Cunningham is the most amazing professor his class seminar is like book club. Do the readings and participate. You will be able to get away not reading but I'm not sure you will be able to cope with the moral sadness of disappointing him by not sharing your thoughts. Awesome class great guy and easy A.

Cliff is an absolute gem. You will not find a better all around guy at Duke. He's absurdly accomplished in his field, but still respects his students and their ideas. He cares about you as a person more than anything, and his only goal is to create a fun class that kids look forward to. #MVP #GOAT #Legend

Prof. Cunningham is my hero. He was the bright spot in my semester of darkness, and for that I am forever grateful. The class was one of few things I actually looked forward to, and I give him immense credit for that. He's GOATed in his academic field and has lived an incredible life. He's also genuinely so caring for his freshmen in his seminar.

Dr. Cunningham's class was one of the most interesting courses I've ever taken at Duke. His lectures might seem very detail oriented at first, but if you understand the bigger picture, you will be amazed by how much interesting knowledge you'll take away from this class. He also includes lots of his past stories that are super fun to listen to.

Dr. Cunningham is scatter-brained, but his love of science and his students shines through that. The course grade depends mostly on the exams, which have very specific questions. This semester, the exams were open note and book though, so it was easy to read through the presentation notes and understand the answers he was looking for.

Dr. Cunningham is a GEM of a professor. He's the sweetest man and he genuinely cares about his students. He even set up individual Zoom calls to meet us all. Most of your grade is the exams, but they're not too difficult and most answers come directly from notes/lecture guides. I will definitely be taking another class with him if I get the chance.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Scatterbrained and gives tests that have mistakes on them. One of the worst Ive had.
Amazing freshman seminar
Dr. Cunningham is a very nice man, but he can be a little scatterbrained in terms of class organization. Content on the quizzes doesn't always match up to lectures.

He seems to have no idea of what he's teaching or how to teach it. His material is outdated and he incorrectly creates his own exams. He's nice and friendly, but could definitely benefit from some teaching courses. Got a xx.98 in the class and he wouldn't round up.

He's not the most organized lecturer, but make lectures engaging and likes to crack jokes/tell stories. He clearly highlights things he considers important in lectures (hinting heavily that they might be tested). His powerpoints have minimal notes on them, so it is really essential to attend lecture and take notes on EVERYTHING. Study in groups!!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Extremely nice and tries very hard. However, just not a great professor and has extremely confusing lectures and tests. Material is interesting but the class definitely needs more structure. Manos  good professor with boring material Cunningham  mediocre professor with interesting material
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Really nice guy.  Enthusiastic lecturer, always willing to talk to students.  Answered questions for hours on Sakai before the final. Tests are different than Manos's, less emphasis on Top 20.  Memorize all the lectures before the test.  The final is really hard because of the amount of info - focus on comparisons and make tables from your notes

He's hilarious. Treats every lecture like a Broadway show... get ready to be entertained. Class itself is straight memorization, but you gotta give it up to Cunningham and Manos for making it interesting and keeping everyone awake. Also you can't skip class if you expect to pass tests.
BIO 207 IS THE WORST its straight memorisation and the tests make no sense

Professor Cunningham is a genuinely nice guy that clearly cares about his students.  His lecture style is very different from Professor Manos', but he is very clear about what points you should focus on for the exams.

I didn't expect to like this class, but thanks to Dr. Cunningham (and Dr. Manos earlier on in the semester) it was really interesting. Cunningham is funny and a nice guy. He's not trying to screw you over on the tests; he even tells you particular things during the lectures that you should pay close attention to. Great professors and a great class.
Cliff's really specific about what he wants you to know for the exam.  His lectures are pretty interesting and his exams are easier than that of Mano.

Hated this class, but I really looked forward to Cunningham's lectures. He's funny and tells some good stories. His tests aren't too bad if you memorize his lectures. Just put in the hours, and you'll come out with a decent grade.

Professor Cunningham is awesome! I'm looking to take another class with him if he's teaching any. Just GO TO LECTURES and memorize/understand what he says. He's an entertaining, engaging lecturer, and willing to help you outside of class. The course sucks, but Cunningham is great.
Unless you like learning about worms and jellyfish, I recommend watching the weather channel instead of taking this class.

in response to the post below, i asked a few detailed questions at one of his review sessions and received satisfactory responses. dr cunningham is overall a great guy. what i appreciate most and find most comment-worthy about him is his atypical sense of humor and perceptible love of his job.

So this guy went to Yale. He wants you to know that. My best tip is to memorize what he says in lecture and don't read the book. Another good tip is to go to the review session and ask him a detailed/coherent/relevant question because he won't know the answer and get flustered and stutter and it's hilarious. And he can't spell.
he's awesome! i'd take a class with him again easily!

Professor Cunningham is a character.  For one lecture he got down on all fours and demonstrated movement without joints.  His tests aren't too difficult so long as you pay attention to the lectures and pretty much memorize most of the stuff.  But lectures were entertaining.

My favorite prof at Duke so far! He's entertaining, extremely intelligent, a great teacher, and you will definitely learn stuff. I suggest bringing a laptop so you can type fast enough to get down everything with his explanations. He is very clear with what is important and if you take good notes and go to class you will do great in the class!
No Comments
No Comments
Take! my fav class
A bit too disorganized.

Organic chemistry is hard regardless of who teaches it. She knows this and tries to make the class doable. Midterms are really easy, which made the final seem harder than it actually was. She is very clear with what you need to know and it's all in the text book so class isn't necessary. Do the textbook problems and you will get an A.

I enjoyed taking this class so much more than Organic Chem 1. The midterms were all very doable and were based on topics covered in class. The final was hard but it was also curved. Prof Canelas as a person is very funny and kind. Would def recommend!

Won't hold your hand, but she's very fair and cares about your success. Don't expect lectures to carry your understanding, but she outlined what we needed to know and made difficult concepts easily graspable. Easy midterms; aced by doing concentrated recall for three days before each exam. Difficult final though it is curved. Way easier than Orgo 1

Professor Canelas is ok. She made many jokes and went on a bunch of tangents, but it was fine. Her lectures were an intro into what you need to learn on your own, but her tests weren't too difficult. However, the final is disproportionately harder than the rest of the tests, with confirmed material that Canelas js skipped. Hopefully a good curve...
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Canelas is one of the most entertaining big lecture-r's and very caring + enthusiastic for students and topics. take any class with her and you'll do great if you go to lecture. while exams are basically the only grades you will receive, she makes a big effort for practicing concepts in class

I LOVE DORIAN CANELAS. She's amazing. She's tough and lectures can get wild sometimes, so a lot of work has to be done outside of class. However, I feel like her exams are fair and she really does care about her students.

Canelas is goated. Lectures are mostly intro to what you should be learning, so a lot of it is outside. However, the materials she gives to review for the tests are very helpful and align alot with the difficulty of the tests. Also, tests are 80% of the overall grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Chem 202 with Professor Canelas was challenging for sure, but I learned so much!

She Is well organized in Canvas and the lectures are clear and concise, covering the materials in an easy to understand way, which is good, because I needed the help.
Good at teaching the rudimentary knowledge of each topic but that was it. Never left class feeling like I learned much. Office hours were at 2pm on weekdays so it was hard to get help.

I took organic with Canelas at the Marine Lab, from what I've heard, it was a bit easier than organic at Duke, mostly because of a few course policy changes. Tests could be a bit pressed for time. Very personable, tells great stories during class. Slides can be a bit bare, learned a lot on my own- but mostly because of my own learning style.

I thought the entire class was very fair, but her final was beyond difficult for me. The average was  lower than any of our midterms. She still curved the class  and is the professor I have learned the best with. You will need to teach some of it to yourself, but that is orgo and will happen with all professors.  I will be taking orgo 2 with her.

It felt like her priority was the organic class before us. Her gen chem class was very disorganized, and she often lost track of what material she taught us. She is a very tangential lecturer, which, although funny, is difficult to follow. Her exams were fair but a time crunch. I had to teach myself most all of the content to adequately prepare.

I enjoyed Professor Canelas's fair grading and her exams were very similar to the past ones which made it easy to predict what I needed to know/the structure of exams. I will say, she doesn't go very in depth during lecture so you do need to do a lot of practice questions outside of class but that's expected for organic chemistry.

Canelas is funny. She helped fill gaps within my knowledge and I learned new things. She did mini experiments which was fun. You need to pick the right group for graded group discussions. My one complaint is Chem 99 class time should be an 30 min longer for questions & practice.

Canelas' orgo class is tough, but her engaging teaching style and helpful nature make it manageable. The exams can be tricky, but studying with tools like unstuckstudy alongside the textbook will prep you well. Take this class - Canelas is a gem!
Canelas is amazing at explaining some hard topics like redox and buffers in a way I can understand and remember. It was clutch for the MCAT.
Really easy to understand her teaching and she is so funny. Loved this class.

She did a great job setting clear expectations. Lecture slides & notes were accessible online, and she provided many practice tests with keys & many practice problems. Didn't love the group-based learning, but her lectures were decent. Highly recommend for those with no prior chem experience - read the book, do the problems, and you'll be fine.

Not the best for 210, had her for other chem classes and thought she did a better job then. Went on so many tangents that we were always behind and scrambling to get through info. But she's still a solidly good prof, sets reasonable (but difficult) expectations

Dr. Canelas gives pretty much everything you need to do well on her exams which comes in very useful when studying. Do ALL the problems she gives in discussion/book problems bc sometimes exams are exactly the same questions. Her tangents get in the way of teaching at some points but overall keep the class interesting and enjoyable. Solid prof

Prof Canelas is actually such a sweet person but not so great of a professor. She constantly goes on tangents during class and doesn't explain anything very well. The whole discussion section of class is based on group worksheets, which gets annoying quickly. Just take Chem 101! Chem 99 counts for nothing and doesn't prepare you that much.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dory's lectures are a hybrid of gen chem and stand-up comedy. Her exams are pretty fair. Going to discussions, doing Achieve, and the textbook problems are incredibly important to do well in her class. Love this woman so much, I wish I went to more of her lectures when i had the chance

CHEM 99 with Canelas was amazing. She provides numerous practice exams that are very true to the actual exams given in class. Lecture was not mandatory, but I went to every lecture. Very light course load and you know what to expect. Sometimes, the questions were taken directly from our recitation worksheets and placed on the exams.

Very disorganized lecturer which is tough to overcome when learning such a complex topic. Discussions are virtually useless. However, Dr. Canelas is super nice and great at answering questions. Very accessible outside of class and really helpful  but if you struggle a lot with orgo shes probably not the best prof

Lectures were lowkey all over the place, but Prof. Canelas was super entertaining! The exams aren't too hard and don't have any surprises; the final was very tricky though. Prof. Canelas is down to earth and understands that school is hard. We even convinced her to not include certain topics on the final. Definetely take orgo with her!!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She's fantastic! Canelas is a very good lecturer and keeps things at a good pace. Goes on tangents pretty often, but it's a nice funny break in class. Super difficult class but you know exactly what you're going to get -- what she says to expect on the test is what to expect. Really cares about students, offers lots of life tips ;)

Dr. Canelas is a gem. I have never liked chemistry, but she made orgo manageable and honestly fun to learn. Has a great sense of humor and loves to tell stories mid-lecture. Her exams are extremely fair if you study hard. Taking a class with her again next semester because she is just that good. If you have to take orgo, take it with her.

Her midterms were super reasonable. Her final was so so hard, but the curve was nice! I loved how she would tell us stories in the middle of lecture, it felt like a brain break for me. Take orgo with Canelas! Makes a terrible class into something almost manageable.
Live, laugh, love Canelas

Had her for 202, tests are easy and she's funny. Sometimes gets disorganized and it's unclear what you actually need to know vs don't need to know. It's orgo, so you obviously need to do a lot of work outside of class.

I loved her. I had her for 201 and 202. Some people don't like how she lectures and find her kinda all over the place, but I never felt this way. She is genuinely so funny which makes class more enjoyable. It's evident that she cares about her students. You can tell that she wants you to do well.Tests were fair, but still a hard class bc it's orgo.

Canelas is a funny, involved professor who made orgo bearable. The exams weren't easy, but she provided practice through drill sets, practice exams, and homework assignments. Her lectures were a little all over the place, but she made 8:30 lectures enjoyable and even gave us real world applications for the concepts we learned. Take it with her!

The professor is amazing. She has a very sane approach. During the classes, she took great care of our mental health, she said not to worry about the grades. She explains difficult concepts in chemistry very well and judges fairly.

Really good lecturer, seems to truly enjoy teaching and made Orgo a good experience. Chaotic in a good way (drinks Bang at 8:30am) Ton of info to get through but she organizes the class well. Still lots of work and extremely difficult, but highly recommend!

Professor Canelas was awesome!! She made class fun by adding in small jokes and advice, which were helpful for an 8:30 am. She was accessible outside of class and was caring about her students. Doing past midterms and reviewing discussion problems helps you prepare for 3 tests, which I thought were reasonable. The final was more difficult, however.

Dr. Canelas' orgo exams are definitely easier than the tests made by other professors. She has an amazing personality and is accessible outside of class. However, her lecturing style is very messy, and I honestly did not learn much from attending lectures. She gives lots of practice problems and resources, which is very helpful. Take orgo with her!
Best orgo professor at Duke. Great class, great slides, great explanations. Plenty of practice problems. Accessible OH. Take orgo with her

I took Orgo, chem, and physics at the same time, and out of the three, Orgo was the easiest thanks to professor Canelas! She honestly does a good job at teaching, gives you a lot of resources to work on, and is super fun to talk to! She knows what she is doing and understands where the students come from. All you have to do is practice!

201 is a notoriously difficult course, but Professor Canelas brought a lot of energy and was extremely helpful, which helped a lot. You need to do a lot of recitation and practice to do well on the tests (which account for a lot of the grade), but you'll be fine if you can get into a rhythm.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The tests were easier than other orgo professors. A lot of work outside of class, but no too bad. Lectures are fast and confusing at times but overall not too bad.
Her tests were fairly easy, but her teaching style is not the best, strictly PowerPoints which are sporadic. If you self study you will be fine.
She teaches off of PowerPoints and goes to fast. Especially for an 8:30 class, her lectures were not the best. Tests are graded fairly.

Worst professor, her lectures are not structured, she just reads off powerpoints She goes quick through her powerpoints and assumes that you understand.On our third midterm she downcurved the exam half the class for a mistake that she made. She made a question too hard on half the tests and penalized the other half by an instant 10 point deduction.

Lectures are chaotic (esp at 8:30am when I had her) & slides are probably the worst in EXISTENCE. Tests are fair; she gives a lot of resources that prepare you (easier tests than Parise). Make sure you review old prac. exams, & she is a stickler for notation. Passive aggressive ab Qs & hardly gives you an answer. Not horrible, but not the best.
Solid class for NS and STS credits. Tests are multiple choice and easy if you go to class. Generous on grading papers and group presentation.

Canelas is a great professor. She goes off on tangents in lectures, but that just makes the class fun & the lectures more interesting. An A is attainable for everyone if you work for it. There is no reason you shouldn't succeed as past tests, practice exams, & E.C. opportunities are made available. Do problems from the book and you will be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Hilarious

reviews.comment: She's a cool person and very funny, but there is material for the exams (which are worth most of the grade) that she does not cover in class that you need to learn from the textbook. As long as you complete the in-class activities and work on plenty of practice problems, you should hopefully be all right.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Canelas will go on tangents ALOT during lectures but I found that this made the lectures more interesting lol. You also really don't need to go to lecture days as long as you read the chapters and do the problems in the back of the book. For me personally, the lectures made the content way more confusing than it needed to be.

The material in this course is not too difficult. If you have a good work ethic, there is zero reason you shouldnt succeed in this course. Canelas is a great lecturer and gives you more than enough resources to succeed (past tests, slides, extra problems). Dont take if you have any chem background, you wont need it. If youre new to chem, take!

She lectures a bit quickly, but presents material in a straightforward manner (& she's funny). Some work, but not at all excessive (one to three p-sets + discussion hw a week). Definitely manageable class. Read the txtbook, and do every prac test, you'll get an A. Decent experience overall. Only take if NO chem background at all (esp for pre med!!)

Professor Canelas knows a lot about chemistry, but her lectures aren't the best as she tends to go off on tangents about random things. If you want to do well in the class, read the textbook and use the old exams she gives you on SAKAI to study.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I had taken Orgo1 during the Spring semester and the professor (Baldwin) was horrific. I withdrew and decided to take the class during Summer Term 1 with Prof. Canelas. I went from withdrawing from the class with absolutely no understanding of the content to a B. She teaches with intent assuming we have little to no understanding. Fantastic!

Canelas has a great sense of humor and is high-energy, which helps with this class & makes learning more engaging. I took this class in Spring 2020 when the pandemic hit, so the tests were actually easier when we transitioned online. Overall she's a straightforward teacher & tests are fair; do as many practice problems as possible & you'll be good!

Dr. Canelas is a real gem of a professor. I feel like I learned so much from her class that will be useful for the MCAT later. Her lectures and grading are extremely clear. She is caring and makes going to class fun. Best prof you can take for Chem210. Also , the class is not unfairly curved (if anything the curve is in your favor usually).

I had Dr. Canelas for Chem 99. For a course designed for students with little to no chemistry experience, her lectures are extremely fast and often more confusing than they are helpful. The only way to actually understand what is going on is to read the textbook closely. She is a nice person but tends to get distracted and go on tangents easily.

Dr. Canelas can go on tangents pretty easily in lecture. Sometimes it's hard to gauge what you need to know for exams especially since she is using Sapling now for her assessments. I really hate Sapling for tests but I quickly realized it's really important to understand the sapling homework problems in order to do well on the exams.

Took CHEM 210 with her in Spring 2020. We used clickers daily in-person, so attendance was basically mandatory. Overall, solid course. She's very clear on her expectations, her tests are representative of the material & she goes on tangents sometimes but they're often quite funny. Optional final that replaces your lowest midterm. Would recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Canelas made the class very interesting and engaging. Tests were intense but fair. In summer there was a quiz or test every week. Class was online but I still think she knew who I was by the end of the term. She made helpful short organic videos on Sakai; these were better than Kahn Academy and others I found on Youtube.
The best professor for Chem 210.

Dr. Canelas is one of the best chemistry profs for pre-med students. I actually enjoyed the content of 210 and she does a good job of identifying misconceptions with her clicker questions. She tries to be fair and her tests will actually be representative of the stuff you learn in class and discussion.
Might seem mediocre during lectures but she is a very interesting and helpful professor if you go to her office hours.

Chem courses are always tough/work heavy/hard tests, but for the first time (this is my 5th Chemistry class at Duke), I've actually enjoyed class. Canelas very obviously cares, goes on really short funny tangents and actually makes the chemistry make sense. She relates the material to real life things so that concepts stick/are interesting!

Canelas is probably the nicest person you can meet at Duke. She is always helpful when I come to office hours and advises me clearly on how to do well in class. But the crux of my rating is her lectures, which consists of tangents and unclear instruction. She says Yes, y'all know this" even if we don't, and BEWARE about half of 110 is Organic Chem

Her lectures are often plagued with tangents that leave the teaching to students. While these tangents are funny, one wonders why they even woke up for the lecture. The tests are thankfully based on the previous years' tests and discussion questions. Don't take this class unless you have an allergic reaction to CHEM 210 and need to skip it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Prof Canelas is a great teacher. I had heard bad things before taking her class, but she is really good at explaining hard concepts. She also really cares about her students and how they feel about her class and tests. She's great

Very fair exams. I taught myself most of the material because even though she went over it in class, it's not explained very clearly. However, her powerpoints are very helpful, and she gave lots of practice with discussion question and previous midterms. Do well on all three midterms because the final is pretty hard.

She is a good professor, sometimes goes off on a t agent during her lectures. She is super funny and approachable outside class. Midterms are similar to discussion and previous test question. Study the discussion and past midterms. She adds orgo into many units which is slightly hard. Manageable class and kind of self-study.

She's hilarious and even though lecture is sometimes confusing because she adds some orgo to the units, it's a pretty doable class. Do well on the midterms (use discussions and old tests to prepare for FRQs) because they're 20% of your grade each and because the final is much harder than the midterms. Overall, you'll be alright as long as you study

Prof. Canelas explains all things chemistry related very well. Overall, really nice person and funny! She can be a bit scattered at times, but if you ask her a question, she'll explain it in a way that's easy to understand. Class is flipped, so you have to make sure you know the material in the textbook and go through the powerpoints on your own.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She is a pretty awesome person and made lectures enjoyable with her humor. However, she isn't the best at actually teaching the topics and the only real way to do well is to self-teach and make sure you do practice problems. Most of my learning came from discussion and the Sapling. You have to do clicker questions for participation every class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: canelas is a really entertaining lecturer, but with the actual material she's kinda confusing in class. also go to discussion the FR on the midterms are based off discussion problems and the MC are off sapling. dropping the lowest midterm and replacing it with the final is great but the final is super hard so try to do well on all 3 midterms

I have a hard time writing thisbecause I really do like Dr. Canalas. Shes fun and cares about her students. She just cant lecture. I learned very little from class, and unfortunately my discussion TA was often unhelpful. There was little corellation between the tests and lecture/hw. Take my adviceif you can take orgo do it. If not, take 101.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Great professor, horrible class. Honestly the flipped classroom was terrible. You're expected to know random information that the TA's and the professor do not teach and they provide no textbook for supplemental help. When Dr. Canelas did lecture, which was rare, she was very personal and funny. If you have AP chem credit, just got to organic.

The flipped structure tended to be a polarizing subject- I loved it, others hated it. I think independent students with a strong chemistry background who enjoy working out problems will really enjoy the class. Due to the class structure, Canelas only lectures once a week. When she does lecture though, it's quite enjoyable- she's really hilarious!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Although I heard she's a great orgo prof, her chem 110 class was the worst. Flipped classroom sucked. She was pretty lazy too, providing little help and letting TAs make ridiculously hard quizzes and midterms. Midterms are worth a lot, so don't mess up. 90% of your time in this class won't be learning; it will be doing stupid applications.

Her Chem110 class is technically flipped but every Monday lecture she did notes (which are always posted) and covered the material of the week. Had a quiz every week and did team based applications. Monday is optional but you must go Wednesday and Friday because you work in groups on problems. Shes a great prof and a funny, kind lady.

Great team-based course. Otherwise, it is a great course that applies previous knowledge about chemistry to a variety of scenarios. Additionally, Monday discussion lectures are always optional, but they are always helpful and entertaining. Canelas makes a point of making sure students have a good time. She tells great stories.

I have taken Canelas for both 201 and 210. She is the best chemistry teacher I have had at Duke. Chem210 was difficult for me and I had to spend many hours working problems, but Canelas was always helpful after class and during office hours. Her lectures went fast but were clear and examples work were hard.

Professor Canelas is a phenomenal lecturer.  She is very funny and explains the concepts extremely well.  Sometimes she'll waste too much time making jokes, but it does keep the class engaged.  Her tests are very fair and a lot of the questions come from topics she talks about specifically in class, so I would strongly recommend going to lecture.
Funny but WAYYYYY too easy. Wasn't prepared for orgo2. If this is your last orgo class, take her. If not, opt for someone harder.

Definitely the easiest orgo professor at Duke. We played Jeopardy. Relatively little theory in lectures compared to the number of examples. Test questions were slight variants of lecture problems. TAKE HER IF YOU CARE ABOUT YOUR GPA! She's pretty funny too.

Was not very helpful outside of class and would redirect me to different resources rather than attempt to explain the material. A lot of the important concepts on the tests were not covered in lectures, and the class required a lot of self-studying. Also, be prepared for two required 8:30 discussions each week (which are group work).

I loved Canelas! She was pretty funny in class and she taught pretty well. Her exams aren't too difficult and they were fair. She does give partial credit so put an answer for each question. She loves it when people participate in her class and she had us do clicker questions to gauge our understanding of the material.
Organic Chemistry is a tough subject, but Dr. Canelas' instructions make the course bearable. The class was definitely difficult but not impossible. You just have to be prepared to do a lot of work.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: One of Duke's best professors; goes at a very, very fast pace but is kind, hilarious, and a great teacher. If you put in the work, you'll succeed.

Prof. Canelas is a pretty straightforward lecturer and grader. Her grading procedures are fair but the tests can be difficult. It's essential to do the reading and practice problems in a timely fashion if you want to succeed on the tests and final. She's not much of a help if you reach out outside of class though.

Dr. Canelas is a funny, engaging lecturer who makes concepts super easy to understand.
