That being said, it's still necessary to read the textbook and work tons of practice problems every day to fully grasp and master the material for exams. She gives you everything you need to succeed in the class -- oh, and lots of partial credit on exams, too.
While her lectures are good and informative, you won't do very well if you don't do a lot of self teaching. This class requires a LOT of work.

Dr. Canelas is an amazing professor who is really enthusiastic about course material and always cares about how her students are doing in the class. She is very approachable and lectures are very enjoyable. The class definitely requires work, but she makes the class enjoyable and the material interesting! Had her for two semesters and loved her!

She is so nice, and really cares about her students. She gives funny anecdotes and explains topics so well that I barely used the book in a class where the book is typically considered essential. Very approachable and willing to help. Definitely need to study, and participation is a sliver of your grade, but AMAZING teacher.

Dr. Canelas is a great professor. She really does care about her students. Participation was considered in the final grade, but it didn't impact it greatly. She explains everything very well and it was a fairly easy class.

Flipped classroom structure, so success depends heavily on other people in your assigned group. A good team will help you learn a lot and succeed in the class. (A lot of test material is based off of in-class work.) Don't worry too much. Dr. Canelas lets you switch groups at the beginning of the semester if you feel necessary.

Wasn't a fan of how the class was structured (this was the first time she's taught this class because the former teacher was on sabbatical so maybe that's why). Basically had to memorize how to do problems to do well on tests. She's pretty generous with the grading, seemed easier to get an A in 110 than 101. Pretty easy to get help too.

This class is flipped and focuses on applications, so you need to know most of the topics really well before hand.  Definitely go to office hours when you can. Julia's are great if she is still a TA.  Professor Canelas's lectures when she does lecture are great though and she is clearly passionate about her teaching.

This class is flipped, so it will be hard to excel if you don't already know the material pretty well. Applications in class are challenging, but doable. Try to come to lecture even though they aren't mandatory because Prof Canelas gives engaging and clear lectures and tells hilarious stories.

Prof. Canelas is very funny and engaging, but the format of Chem 110 (flipped classroom, application-based) is difficult to work with. She does not explain the applications well in lectures, and they inevitably show up on the test. You must go to office hours to pass the midterms well. IRAT/TRAT are easy, midterm applications difficult.

Professor Canelas is probably one of the best Orgo 1 professors you can get at Duke. She's very clear and her grading policy is fair and doable. She made me really enjoy a subject that so many people dread.

Prof. Canelas is a clear and funny lecturer. She has a lot of anecdotes. Going to lecture will give you examples that are not in the slides, and will help your understanding 10x. Don't skip lecture or recitation, do most of the hw problems, and you'll do well. Definitely get a solutions manual. Tests are reasonable, watch out for trick questions.

I really liked Professor Canales and admire her dedication to the teaching of chemistry.  It can't be easy to teach Chemistry as a MOOC.  I would love to know whether the Coursera course was considered a course for people who are not science majors.  I hope not, as it was relatively rigorous.

Dr. Canelas is really great. She's funny and very dynamic, always thinking of better ways to explain the material. The tests are difficult, but the class is manageable if you keep up with the readings and pay attention in lecture and recitation.

Dr. Canelas is a great professor and her tests are fairly straightforward. Go to lecture to get a couple extra points (very helpful in the end). I strongly recommend reading the textbook before class to better understand the material. Makes you work hard, but the class could be so much worse.

Canelas is a very fair professor and clear lecturer. While she might not be inspirational she understands students' difficulty when it comes to learning orgo and is willing to help you if you want. Orgo is not easy and very time-consuming but if you really understand the rationale behind mechanisms you will do great.

I loved Canelas, she made class genuinely fun and interesting and during a few classes this semester I think I laughed more than I took notes! :) One place of improvement- I'll agree with a few other commentors that in person she can come as a bit rude, perhaps not rude but disinterested. Other than that I loved her class and highly recommend!

She was one of the best professors I've ever had at Duke. Her tests are difficult, but her lectures are very clear and she keeps her students engaged through funny anecdotes here and there. There is opportunity for extra points if you show up to lectures so be sure to make it - trust me, you will need them for your final grade boost!

Dr. Canelas was a good professor. Her lectures were entertaining and she knew the material. There are plenty of resources for help in orgo but it is going to be a challenge. You definitely have to put the effort in to get an A but it's not as bad as it could be.

Good professor. The exams will be tough, as they contain questions that are "variations" on concepts that you learn. Lectures are helpful, but the textbook and practice problems (and practice exams) will be your best friends in this class. Also, she will call you out if you fall asleep, are talking, or are using your phone in class.

Dr. Canelas is a great professor! She is funny, engaging, and helpful in class - especially in the flipped classroom setting. If you find any way to take a class where she's teaching along - NOT with Hargove - highly recommended.
I had her for Chem 99D (intro to chemistry for those that didn't take it in high school). The class was pretty easy and she was very nice.
Awesome

Easiest class at Duke! Prof Canelas is very very eccentric but hilarious none the less. Two exams both multiple choice ad a final group presentation. Easier that rocks for jocks. Take to kill STS and NS requirements

Organic chem is taught flipped classroom style. I took orgo in high school lecture style and the flipped classroom way is a much more efficient way to learn Organic. Intelligent people fail organic because you MUST do practice problems. She designed worksheets that simplify the material and she is extremely fair
All around good teacher. She makes complex topics very easy to understand

Canelas was a pretty easy professor compared to other professors, in my opinion. This year she had a flipped classroom setting in which we worked on worksheets in groups each class, which I originally didn't like because we didn't have any lectures. Overall though, her tests are straightforward and predictable.
Canelas was a great teacher. She kept lectures exciting and fun. The flipped classroom did work well for organic chemistry...just don't fall behind on reading the textbook and you'll get an A.

I have to disagree with the other comment left for Dr C this semester. I've HATED the group work-- its fostered a lot of mis-education IMO, I wanted to learn from our prof, NOT my peers. I found myself trying to relearn concepts frequently. Did appreciate all the materials though. I bet she would be a great teach if SHE taught us.

She gives you a lot of resources to help you with, and really wants you to do well in the class. Her class has a pre-set curve, and so she encourages you to work together with the other students in the class. I would highly recommend her for organic chemistry~she has a flipped classroom model, but it actually really works well.

Canelas is a decent professor. She's funny and her lectures are interesting, but I found her rude/unhelpful outside of class. That being said, she gives resources and her tests/homework follow the material. Recitation is mandatory and helpful; lecture is beneficial. Book, her  notes, and problems will help you on the exams, which are mostly math.

Pay attention to what she actually teaches in lecture and do all her practice exams and you should be fine. She was a really fair teacher, and if you keep up with her, then you can definitely do well. I would highly recommend Dr. Canelas!

Canelas is a good lecturer, but she does go very fast, and tends to write down mechanisms that you don't need to know.  Her tests can be tricky, but are straight forward.  She is funny and easy to talk to.

Canelas is the best possible professor for Orgo you could have. Incredibly clear, funny and witty, and is really interested in the subject. Her TA's grade kinda harshly, but she herself is wonderful. A+ 10/10 would recommend.
Canelas is a very clear lecturer. She writes really quickly but will pause for people to copy reactions down, etc. She moves quickly sometimes.

She is so understanding and will help when you ask. Also, she is very responsive to email. She will provide you will tons of resources, which leaves her students personally responsible for their grade.

Dr. Canelas is fantastic. Her lectures are clear (and worth attending!), she's helpful and very approachable, and her tests are relatively straightforward (i.e. over material covered in lecture.) I recommend her highly for Orgo 1!

Canelas is funny in her own way and always available through email and outside class. She cares about you, although Chem 99 it is a 100+ student lecture. She gives lots of extra resources to study and understand the topic. Also,  try to go to lecture (it really does help!)
Great teacher! Funny, helpful, and approachable! Loved her class!
She is humorous and approachable.

Dr. Canelas is a good teacher on the whole. It is clear she enjoys teaching chemistry and her tests correspond to her lectures. She does well in pointing out what she will be requiring of each student before the test. Organic chemistry is generally time consuming but Dr. Canelas does well in highlighting the important ideas for the next semester.

Canelas does everything that you would expect an orgo prof to do, and she does it well. She will not be one of those professors who will blow your mind away and absolutely inspire you. However, she will try her best to ensure that you comprehend the material. She seems like a really nice person and is welcoming and approachable.

I love Dr. Canelas. She does powerpoint lectures, is terrific at explaining concepts and really, really cares about her students. She's approachable and really funny. Taking Chem 20D is wonderful choice for someone who doesn't have a lot of chem background; taking this class will make chem 31 so much easier. Be aware this class will challenge you!

Wonderful teacher!!!! Made Orgo fun! Very fair/clear tests/amount of material expected to know. Harsh grading, but this is done mainly by T.A's. Doesn't try to trick you on tests. She is a great teacher, some people complain about her using powerpoints, but they are very helpful and she uses the blackboard to complement her powerpoints. She's great

Dr. Canelas is really nice. Her lectures are effective and she is always making jokes to keep the room alive. She is also available outside of class. Read the chapters, look over recitation materials (post included), and put in the hours and you will get an A.
Canelas is a great orgo teacher. She does a good job of explaining difficult concepts and she keeps class interesting with her lively personality. She made orgo enjoyable and painless to learn.

Very enthusiastic about the subject matter.  Although very tangential, she genuinely wants you to succeed in the class.  Relies on powerpoints during lectures, which can be annoying and unhelpful.  But her recitation worksheets are great and often show up on exams.

Dr. Canelas is a nice PERSON but not a great teacher. She goes on tangents about drug chemistry during class, which some would find funny, but it's actually annoying to listen to and very unhelpful in the scheme of things. Orgo1 was easy b/c I actually learned something in class. Taught myself 100% from the book in Orgo2..going to class didn't help

Dr. Canelas was great for Orgo II! She's a funny, engaging lecturer, and was obviously enthusiastic about the topic.  Tests are hard, but that's expected for this class, and grading and curve were fair.

GREAT lecturer. Orgo is a hard subject but she definitely makes it fun to learn. So, energetic in class. Her tests are on the hard side but reasonable since the class is curved anyways. Strongly Recommend for orgo!

Strongly recommend taking Chem 20D if you did not take AP chem, chem 31L is very difficult. While the material is pretty basic it is very helpful before chem 31. Also, her tests can be difficult, so don't assume it will be an easy A; although an A is very manageable.

Dr. Canelas is adorable! Even in her 8:45 classes, she's extremely high-energy and chatty. She makes an effort to keep your grades up and while a lot of the work is pretty mundane, it's still a great review for those who haven't had much chemistry in HS.

This class was pretty basic chemistry concepts to prepare you for Chem 31. I would definitely recommend taking it if you're rusty on high school chem as 31 is pretty tough. Dr. Canelas is super nice. Her lectures aren't the best, but she will definitely put the effort into helping you. The recitations, while tedious, boost your grade alot.
Class is hard. She is a nice person but doesn't explain hard concepts well. She tried though. The ta was definitely mOre helpful.
Really easy/basically a review of high school chemistry. Still, she's a really good teacher and although she's pretty corny, at least she was always in a good mood.
She can be cheesy at times, but she wants her students to succeed. She is helpful if you come to her with questions.
I liked her class and would definitely recommend taking her.  Her examples were clear, and the in-class problems helped me practice.  I had to think a lot in class, which is a good thing I guess.
Homeworks and tests were hard but I feel like I learned a lot in class.
I really appreciate her.  She helped me through a rough patch and was supportive when I asked for help on homework and such.  Very kind teacher that genuinely cares.

Since the grading on your presentations and reading notes is entirely subjective, if she doesn't like you, you're cooked. I've seen her randomly give bad grades to folks she doesn't like, probably to keep her grade distribution decent. She's not a good enough professor to justify taking the chance. And I got an A, so I'm not being salty.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Great class. Not very difficult but there is a lot of work - reading and "reading notes." not sure the latter help that much if you're already at an advanced level, but can be fun. Reading is pretty fun. Prof Tufts has some oddball specialties like French comics, which is awesome. You can learn a lot from her you won't learn anywhere else.

Phonetics is pretty pointless and doesn't really improve your overall French. Workload isn't bad and Tufts will reach out to you and help you, but she is a very tough and nit-picky grader. I get the feeling she plays favorites, and though she cares about her students, you're stuck if she happens to not like you.
This class was taught at a highschool level.  Intellectual stimulation nearly zero and work level astronomical.

This class is a great find.  Counts toward major/minor & is much different than other French classes.  Phonetics is really cool, she's a fair grader, a bit of work to keep up with (recording for every class) but overall, your French improves so much & the class is not hard. Tufts is enthusiastic, brings food to class and music, really wants to help

She was a really good teacher, although some of her grammer lessons were not that stellar and her textbook is kinda awful.  Still a very good teacher, she tought me a lot.  You can't get anything by her, she'll make you work.  She also plays favorites... she made fun of me the entire semester.

Prof. Tufts is hard, and wonderful.  She has integrity, and she cares about helping her students as much as she possibly can.  You'll have to work in her class, but it'll be worth it.  I learned twice as much French with her in one semester than I did in 4 years of high-school classes.
Wonderful professor -- she's clearly interested in helping her students and in doing everything she can to improve their French. The class was a lot of work, but it was all very useful.

Very arrogant and does not care about her students. She always mentions she has a PhD and will not allow you to discuss if she does not agree with your ideas. Do not recommend taking any classes with her.

Her Undocumented America in Literature class was one of the most impactful classes I've taken at Duke! It brought such an important perspective on immigration that I could not find a single other class focusing on. She really cared about incorporating feedback to make the class the best it could be, and the course material was really interesting.

Professor Milian is probably one of the most passionate Duke professors I had. She is extremely brilliant and has a way of encouraging students to think outside of the box. She truly cares about the work she does and the student's success in her class. Definitely one of my favorite professors!!!
Very nice professor, content was a bit repetitive and filled with non-substantive humanities jargon, class taught in english and the readings were entertaining.
She was the kind of professor who really liked to make it obvious that she was a doctor and that you were not.

I've had a few classes with her, and she's not at all unfair. In her own words: "Anyone should be able to get an A in my class." She has strict rules for papers, which some people ignore the first time so they do poorly. Even so, she still let me rewrite a paper when I made that mistake. I've done well in every class with her. Good, nice professor.
Professor Milian is an excellent professor that engages with her students.  She is very intelligent, quite the character in class, and a professor that I would highly recommend to take a class with.
Syllabus is badly organized and isn't followed. Grading policies subject to change without notice. By far one of the worst professors I've had at Duke.
BORING class. Arrogant, self-righteous professor. God help you if you accidentally call call her "Sra." instead of "Dra."
This is the professor that utterly destroyed any interest whatsoever that I had in the Spanish language.
No Comments

God bless this man. He loves his students dearly, is a very understanding grader, he came to see me in a musical and literally gave me a bottle of champagne about it. An absolute dream to have your senior year

This year we worked with innovators for our senior capstones. Dr. Clements was super cool for making this happen. Hes pretty hands off but likes to chat with us during the first 15 mins of class. There were only two real check ins otherwise he trusted us for the most part. Really enjoyed his class - hes a good guy & cares about his students.

This is a capstone class, so the whole grade is decided by 1 final group project split up into its components. Dr. Clements made it a lot more manageable. He was funny, and very helpful, and a great resource. Definitely one of my favorite professors at Duke. He's not a tough grader, so as long as you're on top of deadlines, you'll do fine.

The class itself wasn't fun - literally one giant group project - but Dr. Clements made it the best it could be. Friendly, generous, and accommodating of special needs/requests. Loves telling his story and giving career/life advice, which is both interesting and helpful.
As long as you show up(on time) and do your best you'll be fine. Kristin is really sweet and open-minded about the interpretations of movements in class.

Spends a lot of time on meditation-like exercises at the beginning of the class. Never left class feeling like I got a workout OR that I learned any dance technique. Gives surprise low grades at the end of the class. Would not recommend.
This was a great class. I had no experience with ballet, and I genuinely enjoyed this class. Have fun and enjoy yourself!

Poor course design exacerbated by poor lectures. Half the class stopped bothering to show up by the end because lectures would frequently turn into alphabet soup without much explanation beyond math. Hard to get help, as the course was disjointed in the topics it covered, and no notes or textbook for some units. Tests were hard and graded harshly.
Not a fan of the course content or layout, though as a professor she did a good job. Super smart physicist, makes it apparent that she is enthusiastic about the field.
Really bad. May god have mercy on your soul
Dr. Salvador is really awesome. Her lectures are very good and the class was very straightforward and easy.

Dr. Salvador was clearly invested in teachings and made the course very applicable to everyday life. Readings could be heavy, but weekly assignments were easy and the group project was fun. Exams were vocab heavy, but there was definitely room to do very well if you knew definitions and managed your time well. Highly recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Salvador was awesome and will help push you to be better.

Professor Salvador was great in social psychology! Lectures were very engaging and she was always extremely helpful for answering questions. Exams were slightly confusing sometimes but otherwise the class was great!
Dr. Salvador is a good professor. She knows her stuff, lectures well, and her class is relatively interesting (depending on how much you're into psych). Psy 104 with her was pretty easy.

Dr. Salvador is obviously very informed and interested in what she teaches, and her enthusiasm is infectious.  Cultural Psychology class was unlike any other  class I've taken, and I learned a lot about myself through it. It is very lecture-heavy, with the occasional discussion in the form of answering questions. You need the textbook for homework!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Had her for cultural psych. Super interesting content and class material. She is great at what she does, has done amazing research and you can tell she genuinely cares. She listens to the needs of the students too. I highly recommend her! Loved the discussion section too with our TA

Dr. Salvador's cultural psych debut class was fantastic. You can tell she really loves the subject and that really got the whole class to participate and remain engaged the entire semester. There is definitely a significant amount of reading and time you should put in to get an A, but it is so interesting and so worth it. I 100% recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Inspirational

reviews.comment: SocPsych is far more interesting than Psych 101 was. Exams are much easier, Dr. Salvador is hilarious. Group Project was annoying bcs a lot of athletes in class don't care so others have to carry; she graded it very generously though. Very accessible, TAs very sweet. Her research is interesting and she is very caring.

Dr. Salvador is one of the best lecturers I've ever taken a class with! I've never been bored in her lectures as she makes them engaging with videos and relatable examples. The homework assignments actually help me learn the material and she prepares the class for exams extremely well. If you have the chance to take class with her, you should!

Professor Clifford is so sweet, kind, understanding, and open-minded. She makes the effort to get to know students and creates a positive class environment. You can tell she is very passionate about service-learning and the Durham community. She is also super helpful in finding volunteer opportunities!
The class is lowkey a lot of work and it can pile up, but Professor Clifford is a pretty easy and lenient grader. She is an amazing person and teacher, I loved taking Spanish with her!!
Professor Clifford is amazing! Super accessible, kind, and helpful! I really enjoyed the class and her teaching! Definitely reccomend

Dr. Clifford is is a pretty easy grader and tries her best to make the class accessible, even if your Spanish isn't great. There are no real "assessments" except for a few quizzes and timed essays, but these are open-note and take-home. Highly recommend for anyone who isn't super confident in their Spanish skills looking to take a 300-level Spanish

Dr. Clifford is a good professor and for a 300-level Spanish class, does a really good job of making sure that the class is accessible and meets the needs of students. She is very receptive to emails and happy to meet outside of class for help. Most of the class focuses on health disparities and the assignments are generally not too time consuming.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Clifford is the best! I loved the class and its content. She is super sweet and understanding and really wants you to learn. It's a bit hard with the content entirely in Spanish if you're not fluent, but she is very receptive of you putting in work and wanting to learn. I definitely recommend taking a class with Prof Clifford!

Definitely a great professor, and one of the better ones in the Duke Spanish department. She is very nice and cares about her students. I wasn't a huge fan of the course structure of 306, as I got an A- but I think I would have had to double the amount of work I put into the class to get an A. Lots of assignments but hard to score super high.

Profe Joan encouraged a lot of participation, and the videos and articles we watched & read were super interesting and I do feel like I learned a lot about health issues in the Latinx community. Beginning of the semester is very work heavy, but gets easier with time. You definitely need to stay engaged in this class & have a solid grasp of Spanish!

Dr. Clifford is one of the most caring and understanding professors I've had. At first, the class seems like a lot of work but she's always lenient with extensions and things get easier as the semester goes on. However, do need to have some experience with Spanish, and practicing outside of class is a must.

At first it seems like there is too much on the syllabus, but this gets less intense as the semester goes on. Research paper and community project at the start of the class, plus two tests and three in-class essays. Final group projects take up the second half of the semester. Great for improving Spanish-speaking skills.

I really liked Profe Clifford. She's a very nice professor and seems to be very involved in and passionate about her work. Grading was easy, but the last two assignments seemed to be graded randomly - everyone noticed a strange drop in score in the last two assignments. I really liked the service-learning component though. Would recommend!

Amazing professor. Easily explains Spanish concepts, and is willing to work with you outside of class. Was very lenient with due dates, so if you forget a homework it is not the end of the world. I hope I run into her again in a future course.

Joan is awesome. A fair grader, very understanding of the experience of learning a new language. She's very encouraging, and her work in the Durham Latino communities is inspiring. Spanish courses at Duke are designed by the Spanish department as a whole--lots of assignments. 1010 would recommend her as a teacher.

The sweetest professor I've had at Duke -- she's understanding about the fact that you have other classes. Overall, the class was a great experience (we even had some field trips!) and I would highly recommend it (especially if you only need 1 semester of Spanish credit).

I learned very little from her class. She is a very nice person, and is fair to everyone, but I didn't feel that she was a great teacher. We had a sub on a review day and I learned a ton that she had never explained clearly. Frustrating class.

Her accent's not native.  But she's a kind professor who, unlike a lot of the Spanish teachers, will grade your work very promptly and give good feedback justifying why she gave you the grade she did, and how you can improve.  I would definitely recommend her.  Spanish 301 can be a bit dull - at least have a good professor teaching it.

Clifford is very nice and approachable. However, she is rather unclear about assignment instructions. She is also not a native speaker and makes numerous grammar and vocabulary mistakes to the point where I don't trust her corrections on my writing and look them up myself.
She is awesome

Easiest 100-level Spanish class you'll be able to find, so long as you participate and follow deadlines.  Professor Clifford is incredibly kind and accommodating.  I highly recommend this class for someone who wants to take a "different" type of Spanish class.   It doesn't fit the typical mold as it's geared towards service.
Our class was disappointed in the easy grading rating she had (this is why I'm rating her now), because she never gave us good grades on recontares and many other assignments.

She is one of the most understanding and flexible teachers I have had this year. It might have been because I took 106A, which is a service learning class, but a lot of times she let us turn things in late and gave us extensions. She does grade hard on spanish grammar and writing, but overall it wasn't that difficult to get a good grade in the clas
I liked her ok. She's good if you have trouble with native speakers, because she is American and doesn't really attempt an accent. Her grading is so so, much harder on tests than orals. Decent class

Nice lady, great class.  We didn't do very much work and still managed to learn a lot about speaking Spanish.  She makes the class seem not stressful, and you get the feeling that it's alright if you make a few mistakes as long as you get the words out.  As far as I could tell, everyone did alright gradewise, too.
No Comments

Avoid her if you can, but you won't because finding a section that fits with your schedule is a crapshoot with the Duke SLP. She mispronounces Spanish worse than I do, but she grades harshly and doesn't even teach in class. She walks around the room pretending to listen as the class works in groups.

Jenny is the best! She is super accessible and truly cares about all of her students. Grading feedback on essays can feel a bit arbitrary at times, so make sure to meet during office hours to clarify. She's super passionate about the subject area. However, she's inflexible with absences, and FOCUS dinner gets old fast.

Jenny is great. She's v accessible outside of class, v understanding with necessary absences, and is extremely supportive of her students. Tech-free class, so be ready to handwrite. She's the gl of the Amex FOCUS, and Amex only has one FOCUS dinner absence (most others hv 3 or 5) which can be inconv. with club stuff first sem.

Jenny is the BEST. I took her History of Abortion Class and she was always super interesting to talk to. Readings are interesting and she makes it very manageable to get everything done. She really cares about her students and if you are having trouble with anything she is super easy to communicate with. She's just a very caring person.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Crowley was a super-engaging teacher. Her lectures were always interesting and interactive, with a lot of participation. The readings were often very long, and we would not go too in-depth due to time constraints. But this class covers a very broad range of ideas. She is also super accessible and great to learn more from outside of class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Crowley is a fantastic professor and truly cares about her students. She is incredibly kind and understanding, but also challenges students to learn and develop skills. It's important to complete the reading and have a good understanding of topics before class, but it makes class time more enriching.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Wood Crowley is such a great professor. Her life experiences are captivating to listen to and she makes the class environment feel so comfortable. She clearly cares a lot about her students. The topic of the class is also really interesting. It's different and very applicable to contemporary problems. Highly recommend!

Dr. Wood Crowley was great! She has solid insight into religious history in America. I was most impressed by how thorough this curriculum was and how neatly I could tie it to my own faith and heritage. Excellent discussions.

Jenny's feedback on papers can be sparse. The reading is sizable but not unreasonable for former AP History students.

I would avoid this class/ taking class with her as her grading rubric is extremely vague and she over-assigns readings for homework. She is a good example of how researchers don't necessarily make for good teachers/ professors.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Jenny is a great person, love her to death, but this class was not great. There were often upwards of 100 pages of reading per night (non of which I did, but still managed to get an A, so you're fine). The essays were decently easy, but feedback was sometimes vague. Would randomly give me a point off but not tell me what it was for.

It seems the less effort and thinking I put in, the higher grades I get. The class values agreement more than dissent. If you're obedient, or if you happen to agree with her on most things, it's an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Crowley is a very kind professor who clearly cares about her students. The material in the class was pretty interesting, and it puts a new perspective on a lot of American historical events. Would recommend if you like learning and discussing history.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Decent class. Way too many (often dense) readings crammed into the week, so huge swathes of it would just be in one ear and out the other. Felt like a waste of effort, sometimes. She gives good feedback in office hours, but rubrics could be frustratingly vague. Felt like the class started off strong, tapered off and became very boring and confused.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She almost never tells you what she wants to see on papers until after she grades it and then you have to rewrite it if you want a good grade; this class was honestly just a waste of my time
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Gives awful/ little to no feedback and has an arbitrary grading system
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Jenny was so kind and allowed all students to share their ideas in class discussions. She lets you rewrite all except the final paper for a better grade, and she is always willing to meet outside of class to give advice on your papers. The class wasn't too much work, and the subject matter was really interesting/well taught. Apply for this FOCUS!
There is too much homework, much of which is not necessary for understanding class learning objectives
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Doesn't give good feedback and grades inconsistently
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I absolutely adored this class - and you will too! The content is fascinating, Jenny is incredibly engaging, and you are going to leave the class with a great understanding of the course material. There is a lot of reading, and she can be slightly unclear about papers - but you can rewrite everything, and with a little work will get an A! 10/10
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: She is a super nice person but there is so much reading and unclear instructions for papers. To be honest, this class made me regret doing focus on Duke

Jenny was by far my best professor this semester, and IMO the best professor in the American Experiences focus cluster. She clearly cares about your development as a writer. She was always available to meet outside of class, whether for academic or personal conversations. This class had tons of reading though, but not all of it was necessary.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: I honestly did not really like this class, grading was very arbitrary and the readings were pretty boring.

One of the most genuine people Ive ever come across; she cares about your personal life and how you are doing in general. I understand the complaints that grading can feel arbitrary, but she wants to see growth and improvement and will always meet with you outside of class. Reading is heavyexpect 150 pages a week.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Absolute highlight of my first semester at Duke. Readings were super engaging, class discussions were very student led. Jenny always took care to make me feel intelligent, both in class and in office hours, never thinking a question is too stupid, and valuing every weird tangent. If you care about the material, youll love this class.
Jenny is incredibly caring and accessible outside of class but does not provide clear instructions or expectations for papers.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Jennys class was the highlight of my first semester!! Lectures were mostly discussion-based and almost always engaging. Get ready for a substantial amount of reading. She provides solid feedback on essays and allows you to rewrite every one but the final, so if you put in the work, a good grade is totally attainable. LOVE this woman
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Generally bad at teaching, doesn't tell you what they want on essays until after you turn them in

A great class but be prepared to be busy! Jennys the best, but will let you know when your papers arent. However, she allows rewrites on everything and is ALWAYS willing to meet outside of class. As someone without much writing experience, shes certainly prepare me for future papers at Duke. This is the only class she teaches so dont miss out!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Take a class with Jenny if you have the opportunity to! She taught our "Religious History of America" class for the American Experience Focus, and I seriously enjoyed every one of her lectures. Reading can be long, but reasonable. Super caring, understanding, and engaging, really interesting discussions, and a great professor to get to know!

Jenny is INCREDIBLE! I feel so lucky to have taken her FOCUS course, Religious History in America. If you have the opportunity, take this class! Jenny is kind and caring, and she's truly an expert on American religious history as well. I wish she taught more classes!!

Greatest person and professor ever. This is the only class she teaches because she is a dean full-time, but if you have the chance to take it, do it! Jenny is amazing and the classes were so fun. Made religious history not boring at all. You do have to work hard on the papers, but she is available outside of class and is very helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Very kind and caring teacher, all issues with the course are due to its structure, which isn't under her control. Always open to meet after class and explain things again, good sense of humor too.

Took MATH 260: Python Programming in Mathematics with her. 
Crifo is probably one of the nicest professors out there, but her lectures were ok. Did not teach us much Python, had to learn on our own. Nevertheless, super nice grading system and really available outside of class for office hours. Recommend working with a partner for the final project.

Dr. Crifo is an amazing professor, always willing to meet outside of class. She cares about her students' success, and although this class is content-heavy, it is not difficult given that it's pass fail. There's a consistent amount of work, but it's always predictable. She's a harsh grader, but regrades offer the opportunity for improvement.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Crifo is a great professor and is very kind towards her students. She taught 105L based off of Dr. Barr-on's syllabus and setup for the class, so keep in mind that most of the ratings about Math 105L regarding the large amount of homework and workload is not really her fault and mostly because she was teaching someone else's class for them.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: truly cares about her students. i wish she was my teacher for every class
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Took Math105. For a pass/fail class there is a lot of work. As long as you don't save things for the last minute, it is manageable. Definitely go to Dr. Crifo's office hours as they were very helpful. Dr. Crifo herself is extremely passionate about math and actually cares about her students.

Easy but cool class that I thought I got a lot out of. A few papers and a final project/paper. Participation but not harshly graded. Class is not insanely organized but she is so kind and grades very nicely. Take this class! You learn so much without a lot of pressure with workload.
Amazing woman and professor. She is clearly well-versed in her teachings and allows the students the creative liberty to decide own essay topics, etc!

Professor is highly knowledgable about the course topic and more. She is evidently passionate about her work. She provides flexibility in the structure of the course by encouraging student input on essay, prompt questions. Extremely receptive to student input. Easily accessible and willing to help.

There's little to no structure, but it doesn't really matter. She won't ever actually learn your names, so try to participate but it probably won't change your end grade. Just make sure you get a decent group for the final project or you're screwed.

Migration and Human Trafficking was probably the worst class I've ever taken at Duke. Lectures are the same. EXTREMELY unclear expectations. It seems like no one ever really knows whats going on. If you want a low maintenance class this is it but if you want to learn about the issue take a similar class with a diff professor instead

Class was laid-back and discussion based. Learned a lot from the assigned readings. Watched movies almost every week to solidify concepts covered in readings. Take her food class - she hosted two dinners and last class was potluck. Highly recommend if you don't mind short papers and a group project to finish semester.

This class was ridiculous.  Every lecture was almost identical - she just says the same thing over and over.  She assigned a huge semester group project and then didn't explain it at all, she just assigned us a country and gave no indications of what kind of project it was or what her expectations were and graded it completely arbitrarily

Dr. Crews is a great professor! I had him for Refresher Latin, and he had the perfect structure and challenge level to remove my rustiness and bring me up to speed. He's kind, funny, knows what he's doing, and is very clear in his lessons and expectations. The translations were sometimes heavy, but they did indeed make me faster at translating.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Crews is a passionate and caring teacher who clearly loves Latin. The class is challenging, with a lot of translation homework, but classes are paced accordingly. There are frequent tests, but always extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Crews is one of my favorite professors. He is very traditional and wants to enjoy the Latin. 203 had 6 quizzes instead of midterms which were very fair and on translations you have done. If you put care into learning Latin, you'll enjoy his humor and get used to the style very quickly. He cares for his students and is genuinely amazing.

I love this man. Although his classes are extremely difficult he makes them so interesting and makes a genuine effort to get to know all of his students. He is also very accessible in office hours and if you show him that you're trying he is very receptive. He also arranged a class trip to watch a play and invited us over his house for lunch.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Crews is simply an amazing professor. He's classic, formal, hilarious, and just loved Latin. Keep up with the class and don't slack vocab and you'll do well.

Best Prof I've had so far. He genuinely cares that all of his students do well in class. I hadn't taken Latin at Duke which I was worried about but it was totally fine. The class is a decent amount of work but if you put in the effort you can definitely get a good grade. Prof Crews will also do his best to make sure you're doing the best you can.

Professor Crews was a great introduction to college Latin. He makes class fun and clearly cares about his students' learning experience. He did assign quite a bit of homework. The tests were all very fair, and if you study a lot you will get an A. Also bonus points for the cool southern accent and calling students by their last name.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Caring

reviews.comment: Rex is genuinely an amazing guy. Very kind and wants you to succeed. But I think RMP is a reflection of what your experience will be like as a student. If you're a Classics major, great. If you're taking Latin just for credit, THIS CLASS IS HARD. Lots of work. Hard tests are most of your grade. This will require 6+ hours of work a week.

If you are going to take Latin at Duke, try to take it with Dr. Crews. He is passionate about the material and cares deeply about his students. The class is certainly difficult, but he sets clear expectations and makes himself readily available for outside office hours.

If you're going to take Latin at Duke, try taking it with Prof. Crews. After having him for both 101 and 102, I've ended the year feeling like I actually know the material. Keep up with homework & study for the (very frequent) vocab quizzes and you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Caring

reviews.comment: Proff. Crews is a such a sweet and caring guy! Tests are extremely fair (albeit pretty challenging), and he is obviously very passionate. Frequent quizzes, but they help you keep up with the material which is super important as the class is pretty fast paced. Decent amount of work, but not oppressive and he wants everyone to succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Professor Crews is the man! He definitely prepared our class for 300 level Latin. Class consists of 3 exams and a final, all of which is on material covered in class. He is willing to stop and explain things if you have any questions, and is very accessible outside of class. If you're taking Latin, go out of your way to make sure it's with Crews!!!

What more can I say? Dr. Crews is just AMAZING. I was merely about to have a try on Latin, but I now decide to keep Latin with me for life, thanks to Dr. Crews's great teaching and inspiration. Don't hesitate to take his classes if you are looking for some greatest experiences. Valete

Prof Crews is amazing! You can easily tell that he is passionate about what he is teaching, and he wants the best for all of his students. The class is very translation heavy, but Crews makes it enjoyable and is very funny in class. Take his class if you can!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Rex Crews is a delightful human being and truly makes you excited to come into his seminars each day. Also maybe the coolest voice I've ever heard.

I loved having him as a professor so much that I decided to keep sign up for his sections for 102 and 203 too. I had taken some Latin in high school, which made 101 an easy A. But as we started learning new concepts, he was great at explaining and was also available for office hours if needed. He genuinely cares about his students and teaching us.
Very knowledgeable and caring, and of course can teach latin pretty well. Homework can get a lot and the class is pretty fast-paced, but the quizzes and tests are pretty fair.
A solid choice for a foreign language professor. He really cares about and believes in all his students and will always give you the benefit of the doubt.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: I love this man. I took Latin for the history and the mythology, so I never truly enjoyed learning the language itself, but I loved that Professor Crews really tried to incorporate interesting discussion in our class. It's a lot of work, but he really rewards you for it. He really cares about the material and isn't cruel. Also, he has 6 cats.

I took both 101 & 102 with Dr. Crews and stand by that decision. "Magister mirabilis" who is truly passionate "de lingua Latina" and does his best to challenge without overwhelming. Tests and quizzes are fair & frequent (with extra credit), daily engagement with Wheelock's is a must, but the payoff is huge! Crews' Romanesque ties are also fabulous.
reviews.rating_tags: Inspirational--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Prof. Crews is my favorite professor at Duke so far! he's really there for the students and works with you if you're struggling or don't understand material. Participation definitely counts in his class and he makes class very interesting with tidbits and info. on Roman history and the like. I would definitely take another of his classes!

Rex is the best professor I think I've ever had a Duke. He put together a great syllabus and has the most endearing way of correcting students as they translate in class. If you have the chance to take one of his courses, take it! You won't regret it!

Rex is awesome. He is helpful in class and doesn't get angry if you are struggling on a passage. His quizzes/tests are pretty straightforward. He also invites everyone to his house at the end of the semester for a review and his house is straight out of the 1950s and is freaking awesome. So take his class.
Rex is the man! He is very enthusiastic about what he teaches and is willing to help in any way he can. All of his tests/quizzes are very fair, he does not throw any curveballs. TAKE HIS CLASS!!!!!

Crews is fantastic.  There are a lot of quizzes on vocab and grammar (usually at least one/chapter--we spent two classes on a chapter) but they're not tricky and can only help your grade if you stay on top of it.  He encourages questions, doesn't cut you down if you're wrong, and goes through the grammar. Take his class!!
One of the best professors I've had at Duke.  Such a nice guy, always helpful.  Easygoing.  He's difficult, but manageable.  Best prof I've had for Latin or any of the classics.

I took Dr. Cornes for Food, Farming, and Feminism and it was the most absurd amount of reading and outside of class work I've ever had for an elective course. Don't take unless you absolutely need to for a requirement. Def not as an elective. Also didn't know what my grade was until the last week of class.

The most self-centered and unclear grader I've ever had. Never gives rubrics and will take off points for the most unimportant things. Takes the entire semester to grade 1 assignment. Also assigns basically 100 pages as "light reading" per week. Attendance and participation is required.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took Food, Farming, and Feminism with Dr. Cornes. Overall, the course was very enlightening and good if you are genuinely interested in it. That being said, DO NOT take it as an elective because it is an absurd amount of reading every night with pop essays in class. You also won't know your grade at ALL until after finals. Decently harsh grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Saskia is awesome. She helped curate a wonderful learning experience through enriching opportunities (visiting DCF, making sauerkraut, different in-class thought activities each week, etc.). While the work isn't necessarily hard (difficulty wise), there is a lot of it. So worth it for me because I was thoughtful and gained so much as a result!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Saskia was thoughtful in cultivating a true learning community in Climate, Culture, and Identity, and she truly made the class interesting by having visits to the Duke Campus Farm and making videos instead of writing papers. Readings were dense at time, but she breaks down concepts and continues to incorporate the materials, making it feel fresh.
She's incredibly definitely recommend taking a class with her!! Really cares about her students and makes it possible for everyone to succeed!
an icon! highly recommend her class!

Hannah is an angel. Class is chill, she is incredibly understanding about students' unique situations, and she is always available for help regarding assignments. Genuinely passionate about the content that she teaches!

Chill professor class overall. Just make sure to do your readings and show up for lectures, and the course won't be difficult at all. Super clear about what is expected from written assignments and exams. Plus exams are open-note which was nice. Go to her office hours, she's really nice and open to helping students with their assignments.

I absolutely loved environmental history with Professor Conway. She is super knowledgeable and passionate about the subject and was kind and understanding with the students. Her lectures were lively and engaging. Weekly readings were long, but she encouraged skimming. The only major assignment was the final project.

Professor Conway is amazing! Super passionate, insightful, kind, and an incredible professor! Her lectures and assignments are thoughtful and super useful. Will definitely be taking a class with her soon!

Professor Conway is great. Super caring, understanding, and loves the subject. Lecture Tuesday, Discussion Thursday with 300-word keyword assignment analyzing LONG readings, but she encourages skimming. One note is that she won't take questions during lectures because she's so focused she doesn't see the hand raised. Kinda annoying, but minor.

Professor Corey made it easy to get an A in this class. He is super accessible, there are lots of extra credit opportunities, and you can replace lowest midterm with final exam grade. He is also one of my favorite lecturers at Duke with lots of memorable stories related to the content. Would definitely recommend taking 303 with him.

Joab is awesome. Super accessible professor and genuinely cares for his students. If you're a pubpol major and uncomfortable with Econ definitely take it with him. Don't expect it to be a breeze - exams are hard but you can definitely do well if you put in the work!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Definitely take 304 with Joab! He is very organized and cares about us a lot. The grading criteria are extremely clear, and there is minimal workload. Must memorize a lot of content for exams, but they are graded nicely. Imo this is one of the only pubpol classes that teaches relevant, useful information and life skills (like how insurance works).

MUST TAKE! Joab cares for his students so much. Designs the course to be manageable. Plans outside of class review sessions for exams that are extremely helpful. Not very difficult to get a high A on his exams. Rest of course is just putting an honest attempt. As Econ/Pubpol major, I wish Joab could teach the econ core curriculum courses.

The goat. Lots of content that is all very simple. Must attend lecture and discussion in Sanford, but class is so worth. Easy grading, exams mirror practice problems exactly. Funny guy with entertaining examples. Decent amount of memorization, though.
Take 303 or 304 with Joab. He's the man. Very clear with everything.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Joab is a professor who clearly cares about his students and their success. Every lecture was incredibly clear and made economics understandable. Grading criteria is fair and if you learn the material, you will be successful on the exams. If you have the chance, I would strongly recommend taking this class with Joab.

Awesome econ/pubpol course! Definitely take this for an econ elective, the workload is light and you actually learn meaningful ways to look at economic issues in government. He also does an amazing job representing both sides of political debates!

Joab is phenomenal. One of the best professors I have had at Duke. His lectures are fun and super easy to understand, and he is very clear about what will be on the test, so you can adequately prepare. His attendance system is a little weird, but honestly, going to lectures was fun, so I always went. Makes econ really simple and digestible.

JOAB IS FIRE. Take him if you can, he is so amazing and supportive and knows his stuff. His lectures are so funny and he makes learning econ so much better. I ALMOST wanted to become an econ major but the final was scary. He also has lot's of extra credit opportunities! W Joab.

the best pubpol/econ class ive ever taken in terms of teaching style, class preparedness, and clarity of grading criteria. Would highly recommend Joab to any pubpol student and no need to worry if u don't have solid econ knowledge

Joab is a great professor that truly cares about his students. I wish I could have taken my other econ classes at Duke with him. Grading criteria is clear, and every exam you know exactly what to expect if you've done the assignments. He makes class interesting and would definitely recommending 304 with him if you can.

Taking the honors seminar with Professor Connolly was one of the highlights of my senior year. She's kind, gives great feedback, and was instrumental in my research process. I learned a lot about how to conduct research in economics and would highly recommend.

Was the best Econ course I've taken yet. She is very funny and has an incredible knack for explaining difficult concepts and adapting to different students. Exams were pretty standard. Study and do the Psets and you'll do well.

A very understanding professor in terms of grades and does a great job of linking concepts together from the fundamental levels. The material might be confusing at first but everything makes sense once you go through it a couple times. As the others before me have mentioned, take this class with a friend to do psets with. Also read ahead b4 class.

she knows her stuff and is good at explaining the concepts. pretty easy grader (median final grade was an A this semester) and tests aren't hard. problem sets can be tricky though and you aren't allowed to go to office hours for help on them so good to have friends in the class. the logistics of the course were pretty disorganized though

If you're thinking about writing an Econ thesis, Connolly is the one to take. The seminar itself can feel a little boring with the endless presentations, but she is very cool/experienced, gives great feedback, and really cares about her students' success.
One day, a graduate TA showed up to teach in her stead. It was this day I realized how incredible she is.
Worked with her on an out-of-class. She was extremely dedicated, caring and went the extra mile to help the team succeed.

Took Econ 210 with her - hands down best Econ professor at Duke, especially for a large core class. Lectures were crystal clear, and she kept the material interesting. 10 problem sets, a midterm, and a final - go to class, listen to the lectures, and you'll do well. Extremely fair class, and I would take her again if she taught an elective.

Dr. Connolly is simply AMAZING. She is extremely intelligent, thoughtful, understanding and caring. She is fantastic not only as a professor, but also as a mentor and advisor. Her passion for Economics is evident and infectious! Definitely one of the highlights of my Duke experience and I would repeat it all over again :)

Michelle is one of the best professors I've had - her thesis class is chill, but you learn a ton about how to write, your topic, and your classmates' topics. The in-class problem solving was intellectually stimulating and fun, and also super helpful for refining your topic and getting help. It's clear that Michelle cares deeply about her students!

Michelle is a very inspirational economics professor, arguably the best at Duke. I took her EC495 and EC496 thesis workshop and she gives the most awesome feedback. Plus, we even have some of our classes off campus, like at Cocoa Cinnamon, which was pretty cool. Take her class!

Probably the best lecturer in the econ department - and I've taken a LOT of econ classes. Doesn't really use the textbook so going to class is a must - but you will enjoy it eventually. Grading policy is clear and lenient and the curve is pretty decent. Judging by my rank, at least 35% of the class got an A or A+.

Connolly was an okay lecturer at times but she seems to delight in a chilly apathy for the class and students. She often smirks while reminding you that she bizarrely won't answer any questions relating to the problem sets. Her material is somewhat simple, but the fact that she has no posted notes or lectures is frustrating.

one of the best econ profs i've had. the best prof among the core econ classes (101, 201, etc..), in my opinion even better and more engaging than nechyba. she keeps class engaged and interesting, and her lectures are crystal clear. she's really patient in explaining and making sure everyone gets it
chill and smart, very flexible for thesis but will provide a ton of advice/help if needed.

Connolly is a great professor. It is easy to get an A, here tests are easy, and there is also a huge curve. Her style of lecturing is interesting. There isn't an emphasis on reading textbook, but reading it helps. The final was a bit random in that she pulled 30% from material that was irrelevant to the crux of the course. Easy class

Great professor and genuinely cares about her students.  To people complaining about her curving Econ 110 to a C+, the other professors curve the class to a C.  It's easy to see why you did poorly in the class if you don't understand the concept of replacement value by now.
One of the best professors at Duke. She looks serious but the classes are really fun! Best way to enjoy Macroeconomics!
Great teacher, not hard. Easier core. I enjoyed

Connolly really is a good prof.  Her lectures build on theory, and the problem sets are suppose to be more applicable.  The problem sets can be vague, but she usually gets strong TAs which help clear up and reinforce the theory in class. She's fair, clear, and keeps class moving.  Will work with students outside of class with their goals too.

Professor Connolly was very clear and presented the material in a coherent manner.  I was not a fan of how students were encouraged to participate (grade booster for participating) because this often times encouraged people to ask questions that were off topic, just so that they would be speaking in class.  Overall a great teacher and good class.

I can see both sides to the Connolly argument. I loved her and thought she was a great teacher, but I also attended lectures regularly and kept up with the pace of the class which is extremely important! Lectures build on each other so it can be easy to get behind and then its all downhill.

I wasn't thrilled with the class, but I think that was because the material got to be too much. Connolly herself is fairly clear, tries hard to keep the class listening, gave a generous curve, and genuinely cares about the students. I've taken five classes in the Economics department and Connolly is easily the best Econ teacher I've had so far.

Just to get the record straight, for those who care... Professor Connolly presents the material in the most clear way. Anyone (seriously) attending her class can vouch for that. She is extremely helpful and definitively knows her stuff. Bottom line: some people lack the ability to recognize an excellent teacher. Their loss...
No Comments

I agree. Connolly is honestly one of the best teachers I've had so far. It's pretty hard material, but she is clear, straightforward, has out-of-class help sessions, and gets a lecture class more involved than I've ever seen. She is quality. If you came to class once in a while and listened, you might have done better and wouldn't be so spiteful.

I don't think the rater below was fair. I think Professor Connolly is a pretty good teacher. Her lectures are pretty clear and straightforward. Exams aren't that bad and are based mostly on lectures. She is very pro-American economy, which can be annoying at times. But she does make a genuine effect to get to know the students.

Prof. Connolly: I know that you read these, and I just want to say that you need to try TEACHING a class for once in your undistinguished career. Another thing to keep in mind is that your students are not nearly enthused as you are to hear each other speak in class...particulary when they reveal some tremendous hole in your horrible presentation.
Bad
No Comments
really nice, organized, looks young but knows her stuff!
Good class.  Good material.  Pretty easy on the grading.
Not a good lecturer, pretty confusing, and not engaging. Writes so small. Weekly or so canvas quizzes for attendance.

Made 230 super interesting and doable. I feel like I learned more in his class than any of the other 200 level ECE courses and he is always willing to meet outside class and answer questions. One of my favorite professors at Duke by far, if you can take ECE 230 with him you totally should.

Dr. Coonley is super nice and clearly cares about the students, even taking the time to learn everyone's name. Any problems with EGR105 are not his fault, and he's definitely the best professor to have for this course.
absolute goat

Maybe Python isn't Prof. Coonley's speciality because often it felt like he was learning alongside us, but I will say EGR105 as a class has structural issues and seems designed in a way that encourages students to seek information outside the class.

Coonley is a kind and caring professor, and most issues with the course likely aren't his fault. The class itself is confusing, with lots of work that doesn't really help learning. He sometimes struggles to explain concepts clearly but grading is easy. Overall, he's a nice guy and probably the best EGR105 instructor.

Dr. Corey is a very good professor for writings classes. I learned a lot without feeling any pressure about grades. She's also really awesome to talk to outside of class. If you see she's teaching a writing course, I'd advise you to take it.

Dr. Corey is very engaging and clearly wants students to grow as writers and as good human beings. She gives lots of feedback and can be tough, but her labor-based grading lets you write freely without fear of a bad grade. If you complete all of the work on time and participate, you'll love this course.

Professor Corey was a great teacher and the class was very entertaining! Graded on a labor basis meaning as long as you completed all of you work and a few extra assignments, you can receive an A. Super engaging class and taught me a lot about writing! Professor Corey is also the sweetest. Highly recommend!!

Dr. Corey is really chill and really cool if you get to know her. The class I took was really easy because she graded everything on completion. So if that's the type of class you have with her, it'll go really well. If she actually gives grades for assignments/projects, then I might possibly imagine her being a harsh grader. Overall Good professor.

Honestly, one of the better WRT 101's offered at Duke. If you're looking for a class to take that is moderately interesting and a for sure A (if you do the work), then enroll. Lengthy feedback will be given, and it will be harsh. Be prepared to feel like you're failing and then remember that the grading contract is all that matters.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Meet as much as possible to ensure a good grade. Tough but fair grader, make sure you do the essays well, nothing else really matters

Course: WRITING 271 Reflective Writing & Intern / Work.
Final Project weighs 50%, and grading is harsher than you thought. Definitely check in with the TA and professors before submitting your final project work. I do think the grading is a bit unfair.

I loveeeee Dr. Corey! This was a great option for writing101. There weren't a ton of papers, and most of them were actually pretty interesting to write since the prompts are open-ended. Also, Dr. Corey is a really great person and truly cares about her students. Class could be boring, but you watch amazing documentaries. Not a lot of reading too!

She is sweet and clearly cares about her students, but she is a very, very boring teacher. I often found it difficult to stay awake during class as she would talk at us for nearly the entire period. Hence, there was minimal class engagement. Heavy reading and homework and a significant amount of papers. Harsh grader for sure.

I took Criminology in Feminism and Activism with Prof. Corey. I did not consider myself a great writer so before taking this class, I was sure I would hate it. However, I got a lot of useful feedback from Prof. Corey and she was always ready to help. The service-learning project was fun too but our role could have been clearer.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: The class was great, and Dr. Rudin is very passionate about her work! Thoroughly enjoyed the class.

The quiz design is deeply frustrating. It emphasizes trivial details, such as exact method names or equations, instead of genuine understanding. Because it is weighted so heavily, missing a small nuance can have an outsized impact, while preparing for it takes time away from learning the most important parts of the topic in real depth.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Rudin is very nice, and I understood her lectures well. I will say that there is a lot of homework, and most of the grade is the homework. It's a little hard to email her, but I understand that she's a really busy person. TA's were very helpful and nice, class size was pretty big. It isn't hard to get a good grade, but she makes you work for it.

There are quizzes or exams every week, on top of a heavy homework load. The lectures are hard to follow because she tries to cover too much material. You have to spend a lot of time reviewing, including the weekly discussion problems, just to get a decent score on the exams, which are very difficult.
She does not know how to arrange her lectures in a organized way, sings too much and taught not important details.
LOTS OF TESTS AND HOMEWORK. Very tough grader.
Be her TA, don't be her student.

This class was changed from being a homework-only class to adding 3 midterms and 8 quizzes on top of the homeworks. Class is ridiculously hard with the staff focusing on gotcha questions.

2 facts:
1. Not a single midterm has median >70
2. Head TA skipped his lecture and then proceeded to have the audacity to "expect a crowd" at a makeup

1. Diabolic class design with 11 tests in total, wasting so much time for both students and TAs.
2. Some TAs are very great and helpful, but some are bad. They gave away what midterms questions  while claiming they know nothing about the lecture content as it is different from previous years.
3. Unclear grading scale

Pretty good notes posted online, but not a good lecturer. Class has way too much material unnecessarily. She is not very accommodative or accessible, and seems a bit arrogant. Assessments (particularly quizzes) don't test understanding of material at all, just how much you can write on a cheat sheet.
Be her student, don't be her TA.
She is a horrible lecturer, very disorganized, and jump to topics randomly. Her lecture quiz covers random terminologies that is not even important. And class size is a bit too big

She lectures well but is inaccessible (no office hours, discourages emails) and uncoordinated (teaches topics after they're needed for homework). TAs run the class, providing good homework (the primary source of learning). They have relevant discussion sections and accessible office hours. I learned from them, not lectures. Grading is generous.

This is a tough class for sure. I like it focuses on none-NN related theory as those are better covered in CS 675. Professor is great but very busy. However, the TA teams are awesome and is very helpful to support the class. Recommend the class for anyone who want to understand ML beyond using python packages. It has 4-5 hw and 1 final project.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class covers a broad range of ml topics. However, I wouldn't recommend taking her course without prior knowledge in ml. She does a poor job at teaching intuition and often skips over important motivations to understanding certain proofs and derivations. You're better off just watching andrew ng lectures and reading textbooks.

If you love decision trees, take this course. But you really learn nothing about NN's. And the few NN lectures we had were given by a PhD student who didn't seem to understand the material. Rudin explains things well, but she's a bit arrogant and inaccessible (doesn't want you to email her and doesn't have OH of her own).

Pros of this class: all lectures on youtube, 85% homework, you really get to know material through the homework, and Rudin is cracked. Cons: Rudin is cracked, and you need to know your shit to get her lectures. I had all the background necessary but was scrambling to learn numpy and pandas my first week. 10+ hrs/week HW. No collaboration allowed :(
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Awesome class and I definitely learned a lot. Homework takes a considerable amount of time and is very difficult.
She really understands the material insight out, and gives great, rigorous lectures. The homeworks take a considerable amount of time.
Shes a really good teacher. Homeworks were though but helpfull in learning the applications. She makse you work for it but it easy to get a good grade.

Great class, but lots of work. Homework takes a considerable amount of time. Her notes are great, in my opinion, but her lectures can be a bit dry sometimes. Overall, learned a huge amount, but this is a super fast paced class.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Agree with other ratings. Not my favorite class because lectures were poorly organized. The majority of lecture content was not required for homework assignments or take-home exams. She came off short sometimes, but overall, she was a fine professor. Understanding professor, although grading criteria and expectations were not always clear.

I enjoyed this class, even if Dr. Kuhn was a little cooky at times. She is incredibly informed on pharmacology and enjoys fielding questions from students. She did not do an amazing job with the transition to canvas, but it was hard for many of us. She can come off as short with students sometimes, but I think she's just a bit awkward.

Dr. Kuhn is the goat. easily the most unique and interesting class I've ever taken at duke, the format (paper + presentation, no exam) made the class super enjoyable with no stress. she emphasizes collaboration pretty heavily which is nice as well. definitely would take again if i could.

This was by far one of the best psychology classes I have ever taken at Duke. Taken during, the summer, Dr. Kuhn made class extremely fun to go to and was always willing to share information from her own experiences and as well bring in guest speakers who had knowledge about other topics relating to the class.

This class has been (by far) my favorite class I have taken at Duke. Dr. Kuhn is so smart and accomplished, and so willing to share what she has in her brain with her students. She's a fair grader and has flexible deadlines, which are lifesavers.

However, this is a very lecture heavy class, so make sure you show up!

you will learn a MASSIVE amount in this class. but tests are feasible. and class is ALWAYS INTERESTING. incredible and brilliant proff. this should be a pre-med requirement. she really pulls together the basics of pre med neuroscience, psychology, biology, physiology and medicine to make an amazing introductory pharm coarse. TAKE THIS CLASS.

lectures can be confusing. 2 noncumulative exams, 1 final paper, and 1 project (a study on drug use at Duke, or a prez at a local public school about drugs (by far the easier option)). Grades pretty fairly and knows a LOT about the subject. Kind of intimidating 1-on-1. Collected in-class exercises technically make attendance mandatory.

definitely worth it for premed students to get a new understanding of how drugs work. I thought the class was interesting although some of the materials was hard to understand/she wasn't very clear on it. Grading is the best--as long as you do the homework, go to class, and do relatively well on the paper and presentation, you ll be fine!

Excellent professor. Teaches very well and makes it applicable! I had a lot of fun taking her class. She tends to test on understanding the material which is a good thing. In short, this class was amazing and I definitely recommend it to anyone who has the time!

One of, if not my single, favorite class so far (from a senior about to enter the final semester). Grading is quite fair.
