*reviewing EDUC 111FS (Rethinking Schools) for FOCUS. Class was interesting because there were a ton of readings and assignments outside of class that we never discussed or did anything with. 1/2 the class was spent at service learning and other 1/2 was wasted in class (or she would cancel class randomly). SL was fun but actual class was mediocre.

Flipped classroom w/ engaging in-person activities. Didn't learn much from powerpoint lectures; 70% of content is from textbook. Professor is kind and fun in class, but not responsive by email. Class is not difficult, and not much work, but I feel like I didn't learn much either.

I still don't quite understand the format of the class, but basically you show up with couple other people every three weeks, have a lot of async assignments. I don't think I learned a lot but it was more like reflective class about my educational journey. Definitely easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Chill and understanding. Usually 2 assignments per week
Loved the class! Definitely opened my eyes.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: I heard great things about Dr. Daniels but I never really clicked with her. She was a fun lecturer but I never felt like we were learning anything about educational psychology. The class had very few assignments and as long as you put in good effort she was merciful with grades. I just think a seminar with her would be better than ed psych.

Dr. Daniel's Ed psych class was the easiest yet most useless class I have taken. The curriculum was unrelated to psychology besides one activity on different theories. Most assignments were group or small writing activities that were usually personal analyses of youtube videos or movies. Very easy to get an A. But don't enroll if you want to learn.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. D is AWESOME! She's not afraid to take risks to keep things interesting, and fun is one of her top priorities. She is so understanding and makes genuine effort to get to know each one of her students. Workload is light if you show up to class (most assignments are done in groups), but she always makes it a good time anyway. A rockstar!
One of my favorite professors at Duke! Her classes are very stress free, and she barely assigns any homework. She is very understanding, and lets you make up work easily.

The course is absolutely what you make of it. Dr. Sherwood is super accessible and kind. He genuinely cares about science and getting to know his students, which is super refreshing to see in a professor. The course is mainly discussion based with a few presentations. If you show that you're trying and participate, you will do fine in the class.
he is genuinely so funny
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment:
Cell was one of the hardest classes I've taken, but it was so well taught and rewarding. I feel like I have so much of a higher level understanding of biology. Dr. Sherwood is hands-down my favorite Duke professor. So passionate and so engaging. 
You get a cheat sheet for exams. They are difficult and make you think, but are very doable. Must take.

Dr Sherwood cares so deeply about each student, their interests, their engagement, and their learning. This class is SO unique. You get out of it what you put into it, but it is not demanding. Dr Sherwood clearly cares a lot about student development and is a great listener. Very willing to meet with students and cares about learning > grades.

Sherwood is a great biology professor and is very down to Earth. He goes a little fast so I highly recommend rewatching lectures as there is a lot of information you are expected to know. You do get a cheat sheet for exams. The class consists of 3 midterm and a final (the last midterm taken in the same sitting as the final) and 9 homeworks for EC.

Dr Sherwood is an amazing lecturer who shows great passion in the topic of cell biology, and also throw in some bad jokes and analogies here and there during lecture. The lectures are info-heavy but gives a comprehensive introduction to the topics covered. It can be stressful in exam season, but I learnt a lot in this class and loved it!

Good professor but the material was very heavy and he tests on a lot of the things. This class really makes you study for the exams and pay attention to the lecture. Make sure you have some background in bio before taking this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: King. It's so refreshing to have a professor who's so openly passionate about the subject, and I've never had a professor who cares more about their students' success. Highly recommend rewatching all the lectures at least once, definitely the best way to study for exams. The material can be difficult, but you couldn't ask for a better professor.

Fantastic professor. always joking around. always trying to make all the students feel welcome. and really loves connecting with each of them and hearing what they think. when a bad paper comes around, he will point out why. lending insights into what makes a great paper, politics of publishing, and what its like to be a researcher. great proff!

Amazing lecturer- super knowledgeable, brilliant man, and passionate about his subject. Tests are brutally detail-oriented even with the curve and cheat sheet. His class is a GPA downer but I learned more there than in any other class so far. Would have loved if the class format could be changed to be less pre-med oriented.

Super enthusiastic, great person, fast lecturer. Not to worry, the class is curved and cheat sheets are allowed on all tests. That being said, grade is mainly dependent on exams, and it *is* a lot of information. I found it interesting (cell & developmental bio), but others may not.

This class will kick your ass, but it's rewarding. He covers a lot of information, but you do get a 2-sided cheat sheet for tests. He'll throw some curveballs on tests, but for the most part they're true to what he lectured on. Only take the class if you're not afraid to do work.  Book is useless, use the online edition on Pubmed if you need to.

Sherwood is awesome, he really loves biology and this really comes out in his teaching. There's a lot of information for this class but all you have to do is know the lectures. Grade is based off two tests and a final and you get to bring in a sheet with all the facts written on it so not to heavy on memorization. Book not really necessary.
Prof Sherwood truly cares about his subject and his students!  Great class!!
One of the nicest professors I have every had at Duke. He is really passionate about the subject :)

Is the best professor for materials science, especially to pre-med students. He is very thorough in his explanations but the exams are extremely difficult. He loves materials and he doesnt underestimate the capabilities of students to learn science and mathematics. I really liked the course and I was truly inspired.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Prof. Curtarolo has an ability to present complex material in clear, concise, and engaging manner.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Great energy and quick pace in the classroom. You will learn.
Here for research, teaching is a requirement and a chore for him. Lectures hard to understand. Shows little ability to convey material clearly
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Hard to understand. Lectures/ homework/ text book do not correlate. Hard to reach out of classroom. Picked on a few students. Unclear grading curves.  Labs were cool.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Curtoralo is great. While his midterms and exams are hard, his lectures make them seem somewhat bearable. Do the practice problems, the homeworks and the lab reports by yourself, because they really help you understand the material.
Very good prof.  His lectures are very straightforward, but you need to read the book and handouts before class. The midterm and exam were based very much off the homeworks.

Hard to understand and does not welcome questions, lectures and homeworks did not correlate. Unfriendly and rude to students. Syllabus was not ever emailed, but given in hard-copy. Read though the entire thing, he has bizarre consequences and grading policies.
the midterm was simple. Overall a good teacher.
extremely talented speaker, passionate about his field... engaging and interesting.. incredibly knowledgeable. classes are inspirational.
If you want to learn about materials, skip the other sessions and go to see curtaralo.
cool teacher.
If you prefer structured classes that follow the book chapter by chapter, stay away.  Very free-flowing teacher.
The teacher is cool. He knows a lot and pretends a lot.
Good and helpful. Demanding, demanding, demanding. Always available to help.
Very cool course ! Hard but worth it.

Extremely intelligent, very well thought out and explanatory lectures, an incredible understanding and enthusiasm for the material. However, he's a very "intense" professor, and he makes a lot of people uncomfortable. If you ask a dumb question, you will sorely regret it. You will learn a ton from this guy if you pay attention, though.

Incredibly demanding class. Dr. Curtaralo expectations are the highest I`ve seen at Duke. Exams are fair/difficult but long and not impossible. I got a very good grade and learned a ton of info. The material is very tough and sometimes cryptic. Overall an excellent teacher. Take it, it is worth.

Very good prof. Problem sets and exams are extremely difficult, but you feel like you are learning a lot. His notes are your best friends in this class as well as a good study group. A bit intimidating, but don't be afraid to go to his Office Hours to ask him questions. Notes are hard to read but contain more info and understanding than the book.
Very tough course. The prof. is very fast but friendly. HWs are easy and exams long. It is not a course for everybody. Overall a great course.
The notes are difficult to read and almost useless for the test. The homeworks and book are the greatest help for the class. He is extremely difficult to understand.
No Comments

He's really a pretty funny guy and the accent helps. Hw seems hard until you realize no one actaully reads and grades it automatic 9/10 if have any answer. Test have 120 points but 90-100 A etc. Labs similar grades to hw. Highly recommend. PS he's awesome once you get used to him and you will because there is a class participation grade.
Wonderfull, clear and professional

I disagree with the negative comments about Dr. Curtaralo. He is a genious, indeed eccentric. I can forgive the sloppy notes. He is a natural innovator. Oh.. yes, he has tons of charisma. The TA, David, was very supportive.

One of the best teachers (if not the best) I have ever had. Prof. Curtarolo's energy is something out of wonderful in understanding the basics for this class. He was available any time. He is tremendously carismatic.
Hard class but he is generous with the grades at the end of the year.
develops topics with interest.
The coolest guy ever!! He is so funny. For midterm he gave a huge review session.

Classes like this were a major reason I dropped out of Pratt.  He is hard to understand.  The class is boring.  He gives you the printed notes, but they are sometimes illegible.  The labs were awful and useless.  He is a funny guy though.  Unfortunately, the material is horrible.  May not be worse than other ME83 teachers.

Notes are all handwritten with numerous scratches. Although he tries hard to be helpful, his teaching method is coarse. It's difficult to understand him most of the time. The textbook, which is confusing and arbitrary, will unfortunately be your greatest asset in the course. Tests are also long and meant to be unfinishable.
Hard class, excellent prof, easily one of the best professors at duke. The class was challeinging, but the presentation of the class was gorgeous. He is hot, but unfortunately married...
Good elective. Readings were engaging and relevant. Professor cares about class and students and is very knowledgeable about the field. Reasonable workload and good lectures.

I really enjoyed this class with Dr. Kiehart. He is a caring professor who is passionate about what he teaches, and was always available to help and explain challenging topics. I recommend this class for students considering going into a research setting after college. You read a review or research paper every week and present on it.

This professor is almost never clear with lectures. He likes to use the phrase, "The key thing is" without actually helping the student figure out what is important and what is not. Don't take this class if he is teaching.

Professor Kiehart's lectures are good enough to let you understand the important concepts of everything on the exams, but he doesn't really go over the small details of every topic, which you get from the book or the diagrams. As a warning, doing well on the ICQ's and exams won't necessarily give you a good grade, because lab actually weighs a lot.

Not the greatest lecturer. Also not very specific on what is on tests. ICQs and exams are multiple answer and are generally only on lectures and not on the reading material from the book. Labs are generally weekly and not bad.

Professor Kiehart is very passionate about the subject but is not the best lecturer. He often goes into way more detail than we need to be aware of, which is interesting but not very relevant to our success in the class. It isn't an easy A due to there being lots of busy work each week, but an A is very manageable.
Prof Kiehart is really bad at lecturing, mostly because he talks too fast. However, if you tape the lectures to listen to later and watch youtube videos, you will be fine.
I could see how this class is challenging, because the tests are very application based. The only thing on them is what he discussed in lecture, which helps. Really funny guy.

Prof. Kiehart tries hard to make the material clear, and is always willing to go over things again or come up with additional materials.  However, his explanations can be difficult to follow, and the tests were not always representative of what we did in class.  All in all, Molecular Bio is an interesting class and not as hard as people think.

There are lots of quizzes and tests, and they are all hard. There is a test approximately every 2 weeks and over 10 or more chapters. Kiehart is very nice and tech savvy, though! He seems really nice and approachable and genuinely interested in getting to know his students.

Very difficult for an "intro" biology course. Tests are multiple response, making it very tricky and the questions are critical applications of molecular biology--not the memorization that I was used to for bio.
Focus class was GREAT! Take it if you have the chance. It's a lot of reading and discussion but totally worth it!

Desimone is a chiller. Class is graded only on exams, but you can get 10+ bonus points from attendance, flunch, etc. I didn't do great on exams and got a B. If you score ~5/10 points above average, you'll likely get an A. Ranked MC makes exams way less stressful. Try and do well on the first exam and put the practice exam on your cheat sheet.
DeSimone is very cynical, so do all the extra credit and go to class. Pace of content is slow. Exams get progressively much more difficult, so do well on the first two.

Prof DeSimone is an interesting guy; he likes to ramble but he knows his stuff. The exams are fair enough. If he makes attendance "optional"-- you'll probably get bonus if you go. Also did a 16-version Final Exam to prevent cheating and made it significantly more difficult than the first two exams. Make sure to get every bonus point possible.
DeSimone operates the course in an interesting manner.

204 is just a tough class, hardest in the econ major - i believe he is better than the other professor that teaches 204 in fall - attendance is required and exams are a weird type of multiple choice and very difficult even as MCQ and psets are completion and either weekly or bi-weekly

Did a great job with offering support materials for exams given how much that matter. Doesn't want to screw over students and offered ample ways to earn extra credit to offset the weighting of the tests. Not the best lecturer, but possible to follow along and go over textbook to study. Allows cheat sheets too. One of the most caring profs I've had.

Chill professor, it's cool to FLUNCH with him. Class content is decently tough. STATA Assignments aren't as correlated to exam questions which are multiple choice. Best way to prepare for midterms/ final is really understand the practice exam/ go to office hours and understand the intuition behind each question.

The content in 204 is pretty dry but you can't blame DeSimone for that. Despite this, Prof. Desimone really does his best to make the class engaging and to help students learn the concepts. Material is not intuitive but is straightforward, exams aren't too bad, and generous extra credit. DeSimone is a great guy who cares about his students.

He can be funny at times and seems like a good dude, but the class content is tough and his lectures are not helpful because of how fast they are and his tendency to ramble. And, tests are very difficult; generous curves are to be expected. Attendance questions every class online on Wooclap to make sure you're present.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Why is he low-key funny
Chill and fun guy

80% of the course grade is based on his ranked-choice multiple choice exams, which were tricky and did not really measure understanding of the content. Jeff's class is easier than with Duncan in the fall, but I feel like I didn't learn much overall. Jeff is very nice, but his lectures have many tangents and are impossible to pay attention to.
Jeff is a funny and great professor! Makes difficult material accesible

Lectures were confusing bc all the professor did was read off the papers without guiding material like a PPT. Grades took forever to come in (sometimes never), exams were regurgitation of the material (the final was mult choice about specific details about the 30+ papers we read) so I felt like my grade didn't represent how much I actually learned

Dr. D really cares about the groups that he mentors, and will take the time to do a lot of research outside of class to help offer more ideas to consider. He holds students to a high standard, but I felt like he graded our major assignments quite fairly. He also provides amazing detailed feedback to implement for the future and acknowledges growth.

George cares a lot about student projects and will help them out a lot, but also provide his own input - sometimes too much. He is a bit amorphous in terms of grading criteria and his expectations, so just do what he asks and implement his feedback and chances are you'll be fine. Besides grading issues, he is a person who cares deeply about STEM.

Dr. Delagrammatikas, or Dr. D, is a great professor who was genuinely interested in my group's project. He is available for questions and gives advice on both the engineering and business (presentations, technical memos) aspects of the class. Follow rubrics and talk him through your work and he will grade fairly.

Dr. Delagrammatikas is a respectable person and engineer but has the tendency to grade relative to his own criteria, which are quite harsh for an introductory course and often does not match the rubric's given in the course. He will also constantly try to push his ideas onto you, regardless of whether they are feasible or not.

Dr. Delagrammatikas is an extremely harsh marker. He will assign grades for what he believes is right rather than using the rubric. He clearly understands about engineering, however, he puts the standard too high for freshmen taking this class.

Not at all lenient on attendance (even when valid excuse for health issue), no communication or concern for students throughout the semester to check on their progress, won't round up even half points (you are screwed with an 89.5). Just so difficult to work with and her negative attitude reflects in her boring lectures. Not the "easy A" you expect
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Della is a good teacher and she made 8:30 Italian quite bearable. There is nightly homework with the online textbook, but it is very doable. Quizzes and writing checks aren't bad at all, and she's usually pretty nice about grading them. Beware of being called on without raising your hand and participation matters. She also does a lot of kahoots.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Great class, do the work and you will definitely do well, not stressful at all and daily homework takes a max 30 minutes.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Chambless really cares about her students, and also is fluent in Italian and so she knows what she's talking about. Meeting 4 times a week is not necessary, so sometimes class is monotonous, but well structured. Fair grader and uses lots of different methods (speaking, listening, writing) to get us to really learn the material. Love her!

Della Chambless has become one of my favorite professors at Duke. She has a sense of humor, her class is lively and engaging, and she really prepares her students well for exams. Every class was a fun experience and kept me on my toes!
If you do all the work, you'll do fine in her class. She is a good professor but isn't going to blow you away.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: so much homework, lectures are terrible, hard to work with
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: There are plenty of great professors in the Italian department, and this is not one of them. Inflexible on deadlines and rigid style. Hard to work with. Did not know my name even after more than half of the semester - pretty shameful for a language class with 16 people.
Della is awesome!  Great professor, makes grammar concept simple to understand, and doesn't judge if you ask about topics that you should know.  Recommended!  Plus, she's a fairly easy grader.

She explains everything clearly, you have to go to class and do all of the homework in time to keep up. She's very flexible about some things and understands when you need to turn in something later, but she also has some set rules so pay attention to what she will be lenient towards.
So much homework, and lectures can be tedious.
Great teacher, however, classes can be slightly long and tedious

Professora Chambless Italian 1 class was quite easy, she was very helpful and the work-load is easily manageable. It is however, difficult to catch up on the course material after missing a class because the textbook is not helpful at all. I recommend taking Italian with this professor, so long as you make it to every class.
Della is very fair and very accessible.  She wants her students to do well, and an A- is very easy, with some effort an A is well within reach also.

As far as languages go, Italian is definitely one of the easier ones. Della's grading is relatively lenient, but tests are so short that missing points is easy. She also does not round up - you have to flat out have the grade you want.  Watch out for the final - it's much harder than the tests. An A- is easy, A requires more of an effort.

Easy class as far as grading goes, but the final is hard compared to the tests and midterm - you need to build up a buffer by doing well enough in the class so that your grade can take a hit. Pretty boring though. Attendance policy is horrible (you can only miss 3 classes the whole semester). Nice teacher and understanding.

She is an okay teacher. KInd of feel like you are in a whirlwind at first because she goes straight into full on italian speaking. Gives easy quizes, but the tests are pretty hard. Stern lady, but in the end you have a pretty good grasp on things

She is a very good teacher! Easy to Understand and makes the class interesting! Be prepared for tons of group work and speaking exercises but they are all very helpful! There is daily hw but it is not hard and is mostly easy to do!

He's a smart and nice guy but he's a bad lecturer, the lectures drag on and often include irrelevant tangents. You'll be fine if you take his class because you can go to other lectures, but if you can get someone else, I would.

he's disorganized and can't teach anything. duke chemistry might as well make orgo 1 into an independent study as opposed to having dewey teach it. at least then students won't have to waste their time going to lecture on the off chance he makes an announcement that he inevitably won't post anywhere else.

Don't listen to the propaganda - Dewey is the best chem prof at Duke. Regardless, you'll be self-teaching; that's just how orgo goes, and McCafferty is the most caring and accessible prof out there. Wants students to succeed and have fun. He'd ask us when OH would be convenient, and even came to campus on weekends to help kids. I miss him dearly

Literally just the boy. Does he teach.... no. BUT he's very good with giving resources and its pretty easy if you just self study well, don't even have to really read the book either. Grades are based on 3 midterms and a final, 5% is discussion which is based on attendance and then you're lab grade. Honestly had a blast and he's funny

the fate of the universe on the line, the martians have the death beam pointed at earth, you better TEACH orgo to these freshmen- i am NOT picking Mccafferty... but he is a hilarious guy that is very accessible outside of class. he wants u to succeed- although he is very disorganized, as long as you self-study the class youll be alright.

super chill guy, even though he wasn't the best lecturer and you had to teach yourself everything. his tests were easy though, so that made up for it. after taking orgo 2 with a terrible prof, I honestly miss dewey because he did care and was willing to help you out + make your final weigh more if you did bad on other exams.

Prof McCafferty was definitely a caring and funny professor, and his test were easy. The downside of taking orgo with him is that you need to teach yourself almost all of orgo, he does not teach the orgo material very well. if you want a good grade and are willing to sacrifice teaching yourself orgo I would recommend his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Hilarious--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. McCafferty was a blessing - he is understanding and cares about his student's wellbeing. While I had to learn a lot by myself out of class, I was happy with how he tested us on the content. Would recommend 10/10.

Horrible professor! He's a nice guy and very knowledgable about chemistry but doesn't know how to effectively teach these concepts to students. He rarely had practice problems that seemed applicable to exams. He was very disorganized. Lectures bounced all over the place, were not recorded, and had no logical order in the way that they were taught.

Dr. McCafferty is definitely knowledgable about the content, but I don't think he knows how to teach to students with no experience with orgo. Lecture-heavy, very confusing, and does not give partial credit on exams. Super nice guy, but a horrible professor. I would recommend taking it with anyone else.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. McCafferty is a great, funny person but he unfortunately does not teach Organic Chemistry I well. His lectures are disorganized, notes are not very helpful, and I often left class feeling more confused than before. Exams aren't terribly hard, but I recommend reading the textbook and going to discussion. Good luck.

Dewey genuinely cares about his students - he's very willing to meet outside of class and hosts reviews outside of class for all exams.

I had a really tough time at the start of this class but was able to significantly improve my grade.  Orgo is tough no matter who you take it with, and in my opinion, Dewey is likely the best of all the options.
McCafferty's a nice guy, but this class involves a lot of self-teaching

He does everything he can to make the class as easy as possible. In class you will learn absolutely nothing so just read the textbook religiously and you will be fine. His tests are not hard just read and do his practice tests and you'll be golden. I recommend him even though the class is "teach yourself" because his exams are so easy.
While maybe not a great lecturer, he cared about his students and did assignments, such as the review sheets, to prepare us. The other professor kind of left her kids to take care of everything.

Great guy, terrible teacher. One of the most confusing lecturers I've ever had. Kept talking about his research, his wife, and his life. Normally this would be fine, except nobody was understanding the chemistry he was teaching, and it was frustrating.

He's a really nice guy but his teaching could use a bit more work. He's been doing a lot to help all the students pass and get good grades. The final this spring semester is going to be multiple choice so yeah.

Pf. McCafferty really tries hard so that the students can succeed. He doesn't try to trick the students. He is a nice guy. However, oftentimes it's hard to get the core concept of the materials because he talks about other things in lecture that students can't understand.

Easiest Orgo professor at Duke , if you think he's the worst and most difficult Orgo professor reconsider your career path. He's a nice guy and he is very involved in other things outside teaching. TA's were extremely helpful. Exams were very fair and he didn't try to trick you.

Dr. McCafferty really cared for his students and wanted us to succeed. He even tried to create a more collaborative atmosphere, especially since pre-med classes at any college can get cutthroat. He was a very funny lecturer and an all-around nice guy. However, I wish he made the material more accessible to us... he wasn't the best teacher per say.

Dewey is absolutely hilarious.  His anecdotes and jokes make a class that would otherwise be very dull very funny.  He is an incredible guy and really wants to see you succeed.  He knows how tough orgo can be and is not trying to kill anyone.  Don't be fooled by the other comments.  Dewey is a great teacher to have.  Very enjoyable class!
extremely helpful professor. Always going out of his way to make the subject easier for the class
WORST PROFESSOR I HAVE EVER HAD. second semester orgo is so much better compared to orgo I with McCafferty.
not helpful or accessible at all; rarely responded to emails. honestly, the worst professor i have had at duke. STAY AWAY IF YOU WANT TO ACTUALLY LEARN ORGO

I really enjoyed having Dewey. Lectures were convoluted at times, but he makes up for it by being so accessible and helpful. Took problems directly from recitation and put them on exams.  A bunch of students whined that he didn't help, but that's because they didn't work hard.  Read the book and go to recitation and you'll be fine.  Hilarious guy.

Professor McCafferty seems like a nice guy during lectures; but he's not very approachable and rarely responds to emails. His off topic lectures are completely useless and he does not follow the textbook at all; expect to be teaching yourself organic chemistry all semester. Oh, and he curves it to a standard C+/B- now. This was not a fun semester.

Professor McCafferty is a cool guy, but orgo's a tough subject to learn without putting in adequate time and energy, so be ready to work. His lectures vary: some are very informative and well organized, others less so, others amusing. You will need to use the lectures and the book to study. You'll do fine if you read and do recitation problems.
The worst professor I have ever had at Duke. Lectures are useless.

awesome, awesome guy, genuinely wants you to do really well...lectures were not that helpful sometimes, but he'll give a lot of hints as to whats on the exams, and if you read the book and do practice problems you should be totally fine. orgo wasnt NEAR as bad as everyone said with dewey teaching it. one of my fav professors at duke!
go to class and read the back and do the problem sets... and you will do more than fine.. he wants you to do well and you don't **** around, you'll do great
Dewey is the man! I got my best grade at duke in this class. his curve is amazing, and it is easy to do well!
Have fun teaching orgo to yourself!!

"Dewey" needs to get his act together, lose the frat-boy persona, and learn how to teach.  While funny stories are always fun to hear, students care 100X more about actually learning something in class.  In order for this to happen, some semblance of organization and continuity of concepts is necessary from the professor.  Dewey lacks this.

Beware, the days of Dewey's "B+/A-" curves are no longer.  He told my class we would be graded as such and then decided to evaluate us completely differently for our final grades without any warning--pretty unprofessional.  He seems like a good guy at heart but he has a lot to learn about presenting material clearly and teaching in general.

Dewey rocks! Made orgo as easy as possible. Unbelievable curves on tests so that half the class gets at least a B+ if not an A-.  He may ramble from time to time, especially about steroids, but he is still a great lecturer.

McCafferty is a good guy. This was the 1st class he taught. At times, he was a bit hard to follow due to his handwriting and structure of his class, but it wasn't that bad. He tried really hard to make sure we did well in his class. Overall, orgo is not an easy class...period. You have to be involved, but if you follow his lectures you do well.

Prof. Panigrahi is one of the best lecturers I have ever had. He was capable of making complicated proofs easy to follow, and the logic is always clear throughout the lecture. I would be surprised if anyone cannot follow his lecture, and if one cannot, it is probably not due to the professor (as in 330).
Every day that I am in this lecture is the worst day of my life.

One of the worst lecturers I've ever had. If he co-teaches your future course, be prepared to go when he's not leading and teach yourself when he is. He doesn't speak clearly and he doesn't organize his slides clearly. The only thing he had made clear was that he should never have become a professor.

The lectures are very low quality. He skips very fast through extremely complex concepts and annoyingly and excessively emphasizes simple concepts. Almost everything he says is not on the slides, which makes studying extremely hard. You will need to self-teach with YouTube if you take him. I'd even recommend delaying graduation to avoid taking him.

I took his class when it was co-taught with another teacher and it made it clear how bad he is at making slides and explaining them. 3/4 of what he says is not on the slides and he usually skips over much of what is. He overexplains the easiest concepts and grazes over the most difficult ones. If you need to take 330, wait until he's not teaching.
Excellent lecturer. He explains things coherently. Homework is hard but exams are much easier and curved. A recommended version of 330.

Dr. Panigrahi is an incredibly talented lecturer who is able to explain advanced topics clearly. He engages the audience well and asks thought-provoking questions to reinforce material. Exams and homework are quite challenging, but the class is curved. Course is administratively run poorly, but that's not a reflection of his ability as a teacher.

Lectures were disorganized, notes were sparse and hand-written (very difficult to understand), homeworks are grueling, and office hour waits are 2+ hours. Prepare to learn most of the content on your own.

A poor lecturer overall, and a poorly designed class. Very disorganized, professors took weeks to get exams back to us. Sometimes the homeworks had mistakes that affected our answers. Co-taught with Rong Ge, who was a better lecturer. Overall a very time consuming and difficult proof-based class

Not sure why Panigrahi's ratings are so much lower than Ge's - they co-taught the course and you don't know who decided on the harsh grading!!! Yes, 330 is difficult and didn't transition well online with long OH queues, but Panigrahi himself was a solid lecturer who taught very difficult concepts well. He is also kind and very open to extensions.

I took the class Fall 2020, the first semester online. You need to make time for office hours (go earlier in the week, I recommend doing hw friday through sunday), and really think about the classwork on your own time, and work on comprehension instead of just fact digestion. I think if it clicks, its an easy class (I hated 250, but 330 was great).
Decent guy but very unclear, hard to understand, and grades difficulty. Not very understanding. Take class with just Rong Ge or another professor who cares more and explains clearly.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Algorithms are one of the most important things you can learn in CS. Too bad the online version of class is uninspiring, difficult, and run by overworked TAs. Lectures are unorganized and overcomplicate simple concepts. In order to even understand the homework, you have to go to office hours. Professors are so out of touch it's embarrassing.

Listened to student feedback after grades were curved down originally. I thought he was a much better lecturer than Rong Ge, and he had a great grasp of the material. Homework takes a lot of time each week, and take home exams (during covid) took hours and hours each time. Definitely learned a lot though

Professor Panigrahi (co-teaching with Professor Ge) was an okay lecturer and explained the concepts to a certain extent. Some clarifications, whether it be through office hour TAs or synchronous lectures, were needed to clear up the confusions through some parts that were touched on but not elaborated on. Very understandable with long exam slots.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I took both 230 and 330 with him, and as a senior I think he's probably the worst professor I've had at Duke. His explanations are useless (pro-tip: yt channel "Stanford Algorithms" is amazing for 330 instead) and confusing, hw and tests are much harder than other profs (like donald for 230), and he dgaf about students (curved down during covid)
Avoid if you can. Curved CS 330 (a harder class) students grades DOWN during covid times to fit his preferred percentiles. Way to punish everyone who tried harder this semester.

230 is definitely not an easy class with Panigrahi, but he makes the learning worth it. Once you get past the slight accent, his lecturing is one of the best among CS profs at Duke. Step by step, logical, and comprehensive. Cares 100% about helping you understand the material. Homeworks are tough but TA's are super accessible and willing to help.
his lectures were very boring an hard to follow. the homeworks and test were ridiculously hard. the only positive is he will recognize your effort if you try really hard.

This professor was substituting for Dr. Ge for CS 330. I really enjoyed the lecture he gave and he kept the students engaged by asking questions and explaining everything. No clue how he is overall as a teacher but based on the one lecture, I feel like his rating should be better.

Like a few of the other comments said, if you take 230 with him you'll have a much worse time than with any other prof. Most of the content we covered was never covered in any other 230 prof's class (or even my friends at Stanford/MIT's discrete math courses) because it went so much deeper into the material.

CS230 in the past has been a bit of a joke class but Panigrahi (who usually teaches 330) decided it needed to be upgraded and made it a very difficult class that was quite confusing and not fun at all. His lectures were just him saying things and not explaining the concepts.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Panigrahi did a good job of tackling 230, given that Duke is trying to make it a more rigorous class than the joke it was before. His lectures were clear and straightforward and he made sure people could always ask questions/clarifications. Weekly HWs that were graded a bit tough, but very fair midterm/finals.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: His lectures are alright, but his tests were ridiculously hard compared to other 230 professors. Our midterm averages were in the 50s and 60s, which is way lower than any other semester. The homeworks are difficult and he just makes the class absurdly hard for no reason. Do not take 230 with him.
A truly amazing professor. He really care about his students and is always available if you reach out. You have to work for a good grade in his class, but you will definitely learn a lot.

He is, by far, the best lecturer I have ever had. He has clear examples of each algorithm, and does an amazing job of answering students' questions in a class that is normally the "most difficult" or the core CS sequence. One of the best profs. I have ever had! Exams/curve are difficult, so make sure to put effort into HW.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Great course, great lecturer.
Hard class but great lecturer
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Dr. Panigrahi was great. Sometimes he goes a bit fast during lecture but he's always willing to slow down and explain things better, and he's very helpful during Office Hours. Very hard class, but learned a lot!
I just remember her as an awesome professor and a great and caring mentor and I came back after years to rate her

Professor De Lorenzo has not taught at Duke since 2017. As a result, the claim that she has been racist in a 2024 course in nonsensical. She is the least biased professor I have ever had (and was a wonderful teacher).
This professor is really racist with me for the only fact I wear my hijab
reviews.rating_tags: So many papers--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class is a bit disorganized and the assigned readings seemed to be a bit beyond the level of French spoken in the classroom. However, Fiammetta is very knowledgeable on the subject and encourages students to participate.

A little bit on the boring side if you're not into Roman stuff but if you're into it this is the class for you. You can tell Dillon is infatuated with this stuff. Pretty tame as far as worrying about your grade goes, too.

The Roman Spectacle was super interesting and Prof Dillon was passionate about the topic and you could tell she really cared about her students. All of the slides, readings, lecture notes, handouts, etc. are on Canvas which makes it super accessible to study for tests. She also gives really good feedback and second chances on written assignments.

I had prof dillon in arthis104 and this was co taught by other teachers spring of last year. Her lectures were always interesting and unique perspective on material. She graded by papers and was honestly pretty generous. Her question did require studying beyond normal not-studying retention but she emphasized the important material

Sheila's the best! She's brilliant, down-to-earth, hilarious (she hits you with the best when you least expect it), and just perfect all around. The class I took with her was about women in the Ancient Athens, but my friends in her other classes have also raved, so just take whatever she's teaching. You'll love the class and you'll love her.

Women in the Classical World- Great class!  We ended up focusing only on Greek women because that is the prof's area of expertise.  Lots of discussion so coming to class was important.  Prof is very helpful and a fair grader.  Lots of papers but good choices of topics.  Highly recommend this professor; I'll definitely try to take her classes again!

love this prof!  she is obviously very interested in the subject matter.  Over all, introductory class was pretty easy.  Mainly had to be able to identify lots of images and remember all the pertinent information about them.  Yes, it takes time but not any more than any other class.  Had to write a couple papers but had a choice of topic and timing

She's a decent teacher and much of the material is straight forward, just be wary of assignments which have subjective grading (papers, presentations, etc).  Her grading with those are unclear and inconsistent.

Professor Dillon is accessible, enthusiastic, and friendly. This does not make up for chaotic lectures, unclear grading, and busywork. She sometimes makes fun of students in class. Still, if you like her sense of humor, she could be a good teacher.

She basically teaches the book, but the subject is interesting.  It is obvious that she has a passion for art, but the combination of a darkened room and her voice is kind of numbing.  She definitely does enjoy the nudes/homoerotics of the Greeks
No Comments
Loved the subject, relatively interesting lectures, would def recommend her as a professor
seems to like her job and teaching.  tests are easy if you study.  overall pretty cool.
She's nice, but fairly crazy.  Makes herself laugh during her lectures and makes some very strange statements, gets really into the nudes, etc.
Enthusiastic, knowledgeable teacher who is really in love with her work and very excited to pass on her passion to students.

Bronwen is my favorite professor so far at Duke! While the class is reading heavy, if you're into journalism or interesting news stories in general, the readings are very engaging. She gives very clear feedback on your writing, so it's not hard to succeed in the class if you manage your time well and participate. Definitely take this class!

Absolutely phenomenal teacher and person. Deeply knowledgeable, really cares about each student and their ability to succeed, and gives great, specific feedback. Lots of reading, but it's necessary so you know what to emulate, and the stories themselves are great reads. If you've got any interest in people, writing, or journalism, take her class!!!

Caring, smart, receptive. Truly cares about her students. Knows her field and gives great feedback for your writing (will write you paragraphs of key feedback). Lots of reading but that's the point of the class. Brings in amazing guest speakers. Do the readings and speak up in class and you will have a great time if you're into journalism!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Bronwen is a GEM! She takes time to create a welcoming class environment, cares deeply for each of her students, and is refreshingly honest and open. Her class on Profile Writing was phenomenal & it completely changed how I look at magazine writing and the way people tell stories. Definitely reading heavy, but so worth it!! My fav class at Duke!

Professor Bönker is very sweet and funny, but his lectures are kind of dry/boring because he doesn't use powerpoint or any visual elements. Lot's of reading but the tests are simple and clear and the papers are also graded very fairly (TA can read draft before submission). Attendance is mandatory but he's understanding if you have to miss class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof Bonker has a clear love of learning & is incredibly accessible outside of class. He primarily lectures and does expect you to do the assigned readings (he will ask specific questions about them). His capstone seminar had one 20-25 page paper, which he helps you with every step of the way. As long as you put in effort, you'll be more than fine.
Lectures are so boring and you get nothing out of them. Not an easy A. Do not take this class.

Dr. Bonker is an interesting guy, but this does not come out during his lectures. Despite taking a seminar with him, a lot of the time was spent listening to him drone on about tangentially related material. He's not a tough grader though, and while you may not learn a ton of relevant information, you will learn something.

Hist. dept. at Duke is failing. I wanted to learn military tactics, strategies, and operations - this class ended up being a high-school level discussion of social history with some war tossed in. Readings were interesting, but there was no incentive to do them. 2 paper prompts were laughably easy (no complaints), and the midterm was a vocab test.

Bonker is a really cool German prof. His lectures can get kind of dry/go over allotted time, and if you don't do the readings you don't really learn too much. However, the tests are pretty easy (especially if he likes you and you ask questions in recitation), and there's only 2 essays. Would highly recommend - interesting subject and an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Great professor, very enthusiastic about the topic! Just do the readings, go to class and take notes, and you'll be fine

Pretty easy class. Only have to read for the two papers you write (out of three). You can get an A on the tests just through class notes. Attendance is mandatory and he has a sign in sheet. His lectures can get a little boring because he basically just points out the important parts of the readings
No comments

I have no idea what kind of kids left reviews on here before, but I could not disagree with them more.  I took this class because I'm very interested in war/ the military and I came on this site and it  seemed like Bonk was the man... Ive never seen someone be able to take something you have an interest in and make it so boring. it's amazing
Bonker is one cool german dude. Take his class.
THE MOST AMAZING PROFESSOR EVER. His approach is excellent and he makes the subject matter very interesting. It is so hard to find a good, unapologetic military history course! A+

Great teacher w/ interesting opinions, especially interested in social issues related to war.  LOTS of reading, only 2 papers for other homework.  Pay attention during lectures and tests will be easy.   Also is a bald German, which is cool.
Lots of work but the man knows his**** and he doesn't grade that hard, it's just a lot of reading to skim.  His approaches are good.  You will learn a ton from the Bonkman.

Assigned a lot of work especially reading, but he lead good class discussions and he's smart as hell.  Great apprrroaches to the subject.  Doesn't grade that hard if you do your stuff.  Will teach you a lot.

Dr. Digby is incredibly kind & accessible outside class. However, her disorganization is an issue. Her Sakai page is disorganized -- it's hard to find information and grades. All assignments are discussed in class but she talks so fast it's hard to keep up. Assignment descriptions and syllabi are ESSAYS -- 2-3 pages and difficult to absorb.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I absolutely loved learning from Dr. Digby - she's really approachable and willing to really help you get a good grade in the class. It's a hard class, but as someone looking into doing field work, I feel as though it's great preparation for the real world. Also, you get to hang out with lemurs! It's amazing
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Dr. Digby taught me how to WRITE SCIENTIFICALLY!! This is a feat in and of itself. That said I worked soooooooooooooooooooo soooooooo hard, and this was one of the more difficult classes I've ever taken

Literally the most supportive, understanding, and helpful teacher I've ever had. Just as enthusiastic as me. If you work hard to learn, she'll work just as hard to help you. Only take this class if your willing to really work, it's definitely not the place for slackers. Tip: Don't mix up monkeys, lemurs, and apes. It's not hard, get it right.

Dr. Digby is by far my favorite professor at Duke! She's so enthusiastic and so willing to help students. She truly cares about students learning something from the class and having a great and educational experience. She reads over drafts, offers a lot of help, and gives amazing feedback on all the work. The class is all in groups, except papers.

I love Digby. She is enthusiastic about the class, tells semi-lame jokes, and is very easy to get along with. She posts all the test questions in an online study guide, so there's no reason to not be prepared for the midterm exams. Discussion sections with TA's are wonderful and helpful.

She's an awesome professor and very enthusiastic about the subject matter.  While her lectures might seem scattered, she gives a complete study guide for each exam that covers every possible question she might ask.  If you aren't serious in pursuing evanth as a major, however, I recommend taking this class with a different professor.

She was over zealous about the class. She asked us to cover and learn too much material for an intro class. I was really interested in this stuff at first, but she completely turned me off to EvAnth. Her tests were very confusing and hard to understand. I would never want to take a class with her again.

Outlines are scattered and hard to follow. Exams cover tons of information. TAs and tutors have all said she covers too much material for an intro level class. Expectation is far too high. Interesting material but take it with a different teacher.

The teacher's over-enthusiasm took away from the class. Her notes aren't clear and a lot of her test questions don't make sense. I took the class for two reasons: because I heard it was easy and I was somewhat interested in evolutionary anthropology. This class turned me off of evanth so much that I can't even stand looking at monkeys anymore.

I took BAA 144L because I wanted to take advantage of Duke's great Lemur Center. The course was very challenging, and while Digby is very nice, she is a very hard grader. I feel like she sort of picks favorites at the beginning of the class as well, so do a good job on the first assignment. Wouldn't recommend unless you love BAA and Lemurs etc.

Knowledgeable, honest, ernest, helpful and inspiring.  Learned things about primates that I see clearly now when watching fellow students on campus.  Went over my mistakes, encouraged me, and made me a better writer.  Best professor I've had so far!

I had Dr. Digby for BAA 143 and BAA 144L.  Both classes were great, and I would highly recommend them to anyone.  She's an amazing professor and spends more time than any other professor I've had making sure students understand and learn the most possible.  She spends her weekends reading rough drafts of student papers so that students can get high

Digby is great! She gives out a study guide a week before the exam with all the possible questions on the exam. About 11 of 40 or 50 questions will be present on the exam. You are able to talk to her about the questions and receive help from other students as well (the test is closed-book though). Wonderful outside help; she's really accessible.

Dr. Digby is very energetic, but she's really scatter-brained and unclear about her assignments.  Taking neat notes is an impossibility, because she'll always forget something and have to go back.  She doesn't usually give grades higher than A-, but she doesn't give very low grades either.

The class was not easy.  The test questions were unclear and her her lectures had lots of tangents.  It was very hard to tell what would and wouldn't be on the test, despite her "study guides."  Digby was unlikeable and seemed to making her class difficult to compensate for unimortant  subject matte

This is the most boring teacher ever.  if you are looking for an easy A, this class is ok if you dont mind sleeping through a class about monkeys.  Terrible subject matter, who cares about BAA anyway?
SO EASY. Writes the notes on the board, and gives you all possible exam questions a week before, then holds a review where you can talk to her about the answers. Three tests, only.

Gives review questions for tests, which is very helpful.  Also has one hell of a curve, despite the fact that she claims she doesn't.  Fairly interesting teacher, and writes notes on the board.  You get to watch videos, too!

Dina made fulfilling the psych methods requirement as painless as possible! She's really kind and provides dynamic lectures for otherwise dry content. Dina is always available to work one-on-one with you to understand class material, research project development, or even just to chat about what's on your mind.

One of the most interesting classes I've taken!The insructor was engaging and graded very reasonably very  much based on effort, which was great! Learned a lot from positive psychology research and the assignments applying those findings to my own life, which was really unique and helpful for understanding the material. Really enjoyed the class!
She seems nice but she grades really tough

I took "Am I a Robot?" The class wasn't much work, just a good bit of reading in the second section. The class changed my perspective on how I interact with technology and made me truly think about what I wanted to get out of college and life. Dr. Dimpfl comes off as a little accusatory, but it is out of love, and he is also really funny.
Life changing

Dr. Dimpfl is incredible! “Am I a Robot?” was never boring: mostly discussion, with him guiding the room and sharing insights that deepened our understanding of technology. He listened to everyone and was super understanding. Not to mention, he is so funny. Readings were assigned before class through the final, but they were manageable.

Dr. Dimpfl is the GOAT! He changed my the way I see the world in “am I a robot?”. There was a decent amount of reading (very manageable) and frequent writing assignments (not graded harshly). His classes are very engaging, and you can tell from day one he cares about his job and his students.

Absolutely loved his "Am I a Robot?" class -- good lectures, has strong opinions and is willing to have enlightening discussions about them, entertaining personality. A must take if you have first registration during your writing semester

One of the smartest professors I think I'll ever have at Duke. Every question asked by our class was answered in a way that always made you think in a different way, but spoken quite eloquently while relating to a multitude of concepts learned in class. I highly recommend his AM I A ROBOT WRI101 class.

Am I a Robot is an interesting class with the ability to change many of your fundamental views regarding technology and our world. Professor Dimpfl is rather crazy tho, often refusing to hear out other sides of the argument and sharing wild conspiracies in class. He often basis much of his analysis on a theoretical plane. The class lacks realism.

There are easier writing 101s out there, but this one is definitely worth taking. Dimpfl is personable and very interesting to listen to. Content was interesting enough and the workload was very reasonable. You actually become a better writer in this class.

Am I a Robot is such an incredible class. It will help you rethink the way you live your life and the way you interact with technology. My life is truly better after taking this class and that is not something I can say often. Be weary that he is a bit of a conspiracy theorist, but be open to the ideas the readings will teach you a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: I took Am I a Robot with professor Dimpfl and it was by far one of my favorite classes. It was a lot of reading and writing and occasionally pretty dense, but that's what writing 101 should be about. I grew as a writer and I thought a lot deeper into concepts of technology in modern society. He's the best and you should take this class with him!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Super interesting, funny, and nice guy. I'll echo that he might have some takes that you disagree with, but try to keep an open mind and hear out what he has to say. You don't need to agree with him 100% but I think he has some productive takes on where society is trending. Lots of reading in the beginning, but it tapers off in the end.

Dimpfl encourages you to think about the things you interact with in a completely different manner. Really tough to agree with him for the first half of the semester, but keep an open mind because some of the things he says are extremely thoughtful. Charismatic, personable, and funny. Takes so much time to make sure you understand the material.
Best Prof Ever!! Absolutely Hilarious and his class is so informative

Dr. Dimpfl is honestly one of the most interesting people I have ever met. The discussions we have in class are engaging, interesting, oftentimes controversial, but wildly entertaining. If you're looking for an easy Writing101, this is not it, but if you are willing to do the extra work, then I highly recommend taking Dimpfl's course.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Dimpfl is really knowledgable on technology and its implications on modern society. Really enjoyed his lectures they are super entertaining, super funny guy as well, and lots of discussions that makes you think. Workload isn't bad at all, mainly just a reading + discussion post for every class, a final essay, a podcast project.

About the only thing positive I could say about him is that he is an easy grader. But other than that he's a horrible lecturer and doesn't have clear instructions or criteria. But the worst part is that he seems to have lost his mind. Rambles on about wild conspiracy theories and will not accept any other viewpoint. DO NOT TAKE HIS CLASS AT ALL
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I had the pleasure of taking a writing class with Dimpfl about capitalism and the environment. The class was very interesting and Dimpfl had very intelligent takes on the subject material. Some texts can be very difficult to dissect and there can be a lot of reading but Dimpfl will guide you through it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: Greatest prof at Duke. Take the class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dimpfl is one of the most engaging writing lecturers I've ever had! He brings up some controversial points, but he really exposes you to how much technology has been built to control us. He can ask a lot in terms of assignments (for a W101), but he ensures that you do well in the class as long as you participate.

Dr. Dimpfl is the greatest. Absolute beast. Just make sure you do the reading even if it's just a skim and you'll be chilling. He may have some strong opinions but they are justified, intellectually stimulating, and genuinely fun to discuss.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Although the workload was a little intense at the start of the semester, it was worth it. The lectures are very interesting and you will learn a lot from this class. Grading wise if you put in the effort and get the work done it is not hard to get an A in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Dimpfl was a very respectful professor. He is very engaging in class, and you WILL leave the class knowing a lot more than when you entered. You will also become a much stronger writer as well, given the feedback he gives. There is quite a bit of writing involved, but it is very worth it and will be a highlight of your time at Duke.

If you are interested in the topics he discusses, take this class. It is quite a bit of work at the beginning of the course, but it smooths out later and the content taught me a lot. I questioned a lot of what I took for granted. He holds very strong opinions, and I don't share all of them, but he is clearly passionate, and it's contagious.
Quite a likeable man but a subpar lecturer especially by Duke standards

has some interesting hot takes and def don't agree w him on a lot of things BUT he is an amazing prof in that he keeps classes engaging, cares about what you have to say, facilitates insightful discussions, is open to questions, and very knowledgable. this is maybe the first class i did every single reading in.

Dimpfl is a really fun guy to have class with, and he gave me a whole new perspective on how capitalism interacts with the environment. He is very opinionated, but also very funny and caring. I genuinely enjoyed this class even though I struggle with lots of reading/writing. This is a great W101 option for anyone interested in environmental issues.

Dimpfl is definitely a character (very passionate, funny, and strong-worded) but I loved him! Guidelines for papers were often not clear and grading is tough, but he gives really helpful and thorough feedback. My writing overall didn't improve tons but the content was much more important. Dimpfl changed my whole perspective on life.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Dr. Dimpfl is extremely passionate/opinionated in his teaching. Class had lots of reading; forum responses were time consuming. Grades fairly. The information I learned in his Writing 101 made me reconsider my major, so I would definitely recommend taking his class if you're interested in the climate crisis.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Great guy, super passionate about the class. Expects you to read and then write a few paragraphs for almost every class, but he makes most of the subjects pretty interesting, so even for an engineer it was not terrible. Cares a lot and tells his students not to concern themselves with the grade, just their improvement.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Climate Crisis has been easily one of my most informative and inspirational classes at Duke. The course is thought-provoking although some of the readings might be a bit content-heavy and hard to understand (i.e. Marx). Dimpfl is a very knowledgeable and interesting professor, but keep an open-mind or else you will struggle to enjoy the class.

Don't take Climate Crisis unless you care about the subject. There are def easier writing 101s. Dimpfl isn't an easy grader, but he's an honest one. His feedback is very consistent and helpful. He cares about seeing you improve as a writer. An A isn't impossible, but you definitely have to work for it. I gained a lot from taking his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: In Capitalism: climate crisis and a world on fire he was by far the most interesting professor. Incredibly liberal, do not enter this class unless you are open-minded and willing to tolerate and respect views which you may not hold. Close minded individuals did not excel in this class. Dimpfl expects you to respect his class and work.

He is very liberal and pretty much a democratic socialist but his class was really engaging and informative. Some of my classmates thought he had a somewhat unclear grading criteria but I thought it was fine--almost everyone in my class ended up with As to my knowledge. Dimpfl is pretty funny in class too--I love when he tells his life stories:)

If you are not interested in work, economy, and politics do not take it. There is too much work and writing, and he does not give grades above an A-. It is very annoying. If you are interested, he is very knowledgeable and passionate about the topic. You will learn and read a lot, and have a good time conversing and debating with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Hes awesome! Grades so generously and really eye opening class. Lots of readings and some are very complicated but he is so awesome. Papers are only 300 words and a final is 1000 words, which is so low compared to other writing classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Professor Dimpfl is truly the epitome of a liberal arts professor. Although he may not be the easiest grader, he is a consistent one. He gives great feedback on essays and life in general. He is a very down to earth individual who is unafraid to speak his mind. To succeed in the class, you must have an open mind and trust his process.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Dimpfy is a gem! Take this class if you want to learn important stuff applicable to the real world, be challenged in your worldview, or just listen to fantastic rants. Mike can sometimes be difficult to understand when explaining complicated concepts and can be somewhat abrasive when presented with views opposed to his own. Grading is very fair.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed Dr. Dimpfl's class. The subject material is interesting and it's pretty eye-opening. The workload is very reasonable and so is his grading. If you think the topic sounds interesting, I would definitely recommend taking it!
Kind of an eye-opening class. Dimpfl definitely cares about the students and will challenge you to think harder and be more critical. Take this class!

I'm so glad I took Prof. Dimpfl's writing class! I've never taken a class at Duke that challenged students to question our own assumptions and critically examine the world around us the way his class did. The workload is manageable, the readings are eye-opening, and Prof. Dimpfl clearly cares about helping students succeed. Take his class!
Horrible. Honestly, DO NOT do this. I would rather graze my hands through cheese graters than ever do this again.
Great professor, great person. Really enjoyed his class. There is one long research paper (10ish pages) and a few short pieces. Some readings and films as homework. Great course.

Mike is a really cool person and a great teacher. The class has a lot of readings and a few papers, but three of the papers were really short (two 500 words and one 1,000 words). The material is pretty interesting. I highly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Would take again

reviews.comment: Mike is an great and interesting professor and person. He conducts his class like a discussion, and encourages students to pursue their own interests. His grading criteria was pretty clear, but I sometimes felt confused, especially on the final essay, on where I lost points. Pay attention and put effort into your writings and you will do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: You can pay tuition to Duke, but you can't make the professor teach.
Really good professor, but class is tricky. One of the most rewarding classes I took before graduating.

Very poorly designed class, not worth the tuition you pay. He makes you buy his own textbook, and class is entirely teach yourself (he doesn't actually teach you anything or give lectures). Way too much work (100+ assigns), but grade is determined by evaluative assigns+exams, all of which are graded pretty harshly. Avoid this class if you can!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Caring professor who gives good lectures. Class is a lot of work, but it has to be. Lectures were difficult to understand in the beginning but they improved throughout the semester. Exams were easy. Textbook is pretty good.
Really caring professor, good lecturer as well. Easily accessible outside of class
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Flipped Classroom is where he doesn't teach at all and make you buy the terrible textbook he wrote. Indifferent to students and gives ridiculously hard homework. Got a decent grade but would never take his class again, waste of tuition
He doesn't teach, very cruel, have no empathy on his student
Tough, but the goat.

100+ assignments including 3 mini projects masquerading as evaluative assignments. 4 exams !!! And tough grading scheme if you can avoid this class please do ! The flipped classroom concept employed doesn't work please Drew give lectures you are super amazing and your lectures will be insightful or at least make partial lectures available.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: The write up for all the questions are ridiculous.
The structure of the class is poorly designed

Hard to get through. There are over 100 assignments, each worth ~1% of final grade. It is difficult to keep up with the material, and stay motivated in the course. It is easy to get stuck on a single assignment and fall significantly behind in the course. To get to the projects (worth most of grade) you need to pass all assignments. Drew is mean.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Drew is superhuman with the workload he takes on, and expects the same from his students. Really demanding and has his own reasons on why the course is the way it is (and is very open about these reasons). Flipped classroom, tough exams & hw w/ no curve. Save your GPA folks, look at the CS department's algorithms course if you have the option to.
this class is loaded with unbelievable amount of work, the professor is so HARD the course is so HARD. NOTE drew is not mean but extremely HARD
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Hilton is one of the few professors that I have encountered during my undergrad at Duke who genuinely cares that his students learn the course material. He is available after class for questions, regularly responded to Piazza questions, and even helped debug compiler code if you asked. Lecture is very entertaining and worth attending.

The professor never gave a lecture for C++. All you have is a 10-dollar Google Play Textbook written by himself. Although it has videos for some problems, but it is still difficult to learn. If professor does not give a lecture, I think it would have the same effect if you buy the book and learn by ourselves.

Compilers is the most difficult ECE/CS class at Duke by far. Workload over 10 hours a week but Prof. Hilton makes it not so bad. He covers all the topics in class, but implementation is heavily dependent on reading and understanding the book. DO NOT take this class if you lack extremely strong programming skills as you will not succeed.

Drew is one of the best teachers I've had at Duke. He has incredible depth and breath of knowledge in nearly all ECE/CS fields and can answer pretty much any question you have. As the semester progresses, he become funnier and you learn to appreciate his corny jokes. You have to take a class with him before you graduate or you're missing out.
Drew is a great professor with great insights on Software Engineering. This is the best Computer Science course I've taken at Duke.

Drew is the bomb.  In this group software course, we got to implement the game RISK across a semester.  The cool part was that you could use whatever tech you wanted.  The lectures themselves varied in usefulness, but overall the class was great for learning and also had a cool theme.  Highly recommend.

Great Professor. Very, very intelligent - almost too smart for the students. Sometimes it can be hard to follow what he says in class (the material can be pretty dense) but if you meet with him one on one he breaks it down incredibly clearly. I personally didn't really care for the subject but I still learned so much from this class.

Overall great class. Good lecturer, though can go off on a few tangents sometimes. You'll understand his lectures better if you read the book. Always finds time to meet with students outside of class. His tests are really straightforward and he always gives a practice exam before. Also grades in a very timely manner and provides good feedback.

Drew is a relatively new professor, but it hardly shows at all. He is an excellent teacher and does an excellent job in lecture making sure you understand concepts. The course long project is quite difficult, but he is always available and very helpful at office hours throughout the semester. He even dedicated time on two weekends to help students.
Professor Waggoner was truly exceptional! A really cool guy (and he definitely introduced us to a lot of good music we were missing out on). Funny, respected, and kind.
Interesting and cool professor.

Expect dry, boring lectures. Never ends class on time and blows your eardrums away with the music in class. We had a 10-page midterm essay and a 12-page final ethnography for an INTRODUCTUCTORY level jazz class... while he's aware that most of us know nothing about music. At least he grades the essays pretty easily. Don't recommend. Waste of time
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: Very passionate professor, but it definitely feels as though he doesn't recognize that this is an introductory course. He tends to speak as though students should already have a background in climate science, when that often isn't the case and can make the course frustrating at times. Once again though, good energy and certainly knowledgeable.

Don't know my grade yet. I do well on hw and bad on quizzes. Professor Shindell puts thought into the slides and is super passionate. But he is constantly saying to focus on big picture concepts while testing on random details in quizzes and tests. Grading standards are unclear but seems like I'm doing bad even though I study and take notes.

This class is very clear and straightforward. There is not a lot required of you. Professor Shindell is super sweet and patient. His lecture style is a little slow, but he tries to make it more fun when possible through fun videos and clips.

Prof Shindell works in the field and is super passionate about it. Will literally show clips of him on shows, speaking at conventions etc. as class material. Homework is kinda confusing but hes super available in office hours and they can be resubmitted. All in all an awesome class
