Dr. Shindell is a leading expert in his field, and you can see it in his passion for the material. He genuinely wants to help students, and the class isn't hard, but if you're taking this class just for the NS requirement like I did, you will most likely get bored frequently and have difficulty paying attention during lectures.

Thoughtful, patient, and available during office hours and by email. Cares about his students learning and willing to answer any questions. Highly respected in the environmental science field but still down to Earth. Sense of humor. Love this guy.

Amazing and respected professor. Shindell is very well known in his field. There are only 4 grades - homework, 2 midterms, and a final project. The work is graded extremely harshly by the TA and the homework is not difficult but confusing. Shindell is open to meet often. Overall, a very important and interesting class if you like the subject.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He is so smart and impressive but still a really good teacher and he knows how to make topics accessible. Not a lot of work for EOS355
Easy and interesting class, though he spends half the lecture complaining about Trump
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: knows so much about climate change, good lectures about climate change, very chill guy.
Having a football game is not a good reason to not turn in an assignment. Manage your time better
He's strict on his due dates, but I respect it, because college students should learn to manage their time. Especially if they're an athlete. It's literally called STUDENT-athlete.
Take another prof
He has tenure. You people are wasting your time leaving bad reviews. It affects nothing.
This professor simply lacks people skills. Very unlikable and rude most of the time.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--So many papers

reviews.comment: Learned I was bisexual after taking this course with him. Not sure what that means
Bad professor, allows no extension for any reason and very harsh grader.
Shoulda gave him his extension
Bad professor no extension allowed
I got a A and it still one of the worst classes
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Won't ever give extensions to students under any circumstances. Not understanding at all.
Worst professor of all time
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: prof sucks

- Nice, funny professor
- Structures that class around Duke's history, which is a really cool thing to dive into
- Invites guests
- You can tell he tries to improve himself, a quality rare in professors
- Go to an office hours, get to know him, he's a nice guy
Professor Taylor did a great job finding relevant readings and guiding engaging discussions to discuss ever-changing race relations in America. He brought in great guest speakers as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Amazing professor who is funny and kind to his students.
Great professor
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Absolute goat.
good teacher!

At his core, Prof Taylor is a super nice guy, just not good at lecturing. He wants students to do well, is an easy grader, and tries to make class interesting. The midterm/final exam were MC and comically easy. Final project was essentially graded on completion. He gave a simple extra credit assignment that added 2 POINTS to your semester average.

(review for PP155) His lectures aren't engaging at all and it is so hard to pay attention in his class. There is little to no instruction on how to write the memos and so this skill isn't really developed throughout the class either. The undergrad TAs were more helpful than he was in terms of the memo writing and lecture content.

Professor Taylor is a nice person, and he did try to make class interesting. However, he is just not a good lecturer and it was obvious that he hadn't taught the course in a long time (which he hasn't). The guidelines for grading/assignments were very vague and I often got contradicting guidelines from the professor, the writing coaches, and TAs

I really do like Professor Taylor as a person. He is very caring and really tries to make the content of this class a little better. The class is graded by TAs but if you put in effort, you will do well.
Prof. Taylor is a little scattered but makes up for it entirely with how much he cares about his students. A great professor for Pubpol 155.

I really liked Prof Taylor as a person, but the class was erratic, with really unclear expectations for projects and other assignments. Lectures felt random and unrelated. I was disappointed to receive a B+ when I had never gotten less than an A on an assignment until the final (he never gave us feedback or grades for the final paper).

Didn't know what to expect before taking this class but Prof. Taylor really surprised me. He is one of the nicest and most caring faculty members I've interacted with so far and really enjoyed taking his class. There were times where I didn't know where I stood grade-wise but it is obvious he really cares about his students' learning.

DO NOT take 302 with Professor Taylor. The structure of the class was incredibly confusing and the lack of grading criteria became more frustrating as the semester went on. Harsh grading on midterm with no clear guidelines. Lectures were often pointless and even though he was well-intentioned, he seemed just as lost as the students at times.

Grading criteria is completely unclear, as are expectations for the class. In fact, the the syllabus (for grading) was changed 4 days prior to LDOC. You will spend all semester wondering what your grade is and won't learn anything of substance about the class topic. Be prepared to listen to an unorganized rant as your lecture. Would not recommend!

He knows the material well, but does not know how to lecture well at all.  You need to go to lecture but a lot of the time it's pointless and he goes off onto unrelated tangents. Grading is pretty arbitrary too and overall is a pretty frustrating class.
Taylor is great, though lectures are relatively unrelated to the material on the tests. Most tests are multiple choice, overall not too bad a class.

Lectures where sometimes without direction and exams were not always reflective of material; however, grading is very fair and he is helpful in office hours - but you have to make that effort to get feedback. Really nice guy, am taking another of his classes next semester. I learned a lot of great information in his class.
Nice guy but doesn't really seem to have a game plan.  He just kind of spaces out.  His grading is a little bit arbitrary too and his feedback comments (the few that you get) are not helpful at all

Comparative Health Systems sounds better than it is. He introduced some health reform info this semester, which I think was the best aspect of the class. We were never told what was important, instead expected to memorize seemingly random facts and statistics. He is funny, but lectures were still boring.
He was unclear and confused himself as well as the students. Had not prepared any of the taught material himself and was not very knowledgeable about the subject.

Nice guy. Class wasn't too difficult, not the nightmare I was expecting. Don is pretty much a goofball. Do all of the practice problems and all practice tests and you should be fine. Don't buy the book, totally unnecessary.

Incompetent. Did a terrible job explaining concepts and did so in a language that was more suitable for high school level. Just threw a bunch of readings and info at the class without being explicit about what was important. Terrible class control - tried to answer too many unproductive questions and wasted time.You'd learn more reading on your own

I really enjoyed this class. The concepts taught were not useless by any stretch- I felt I was learning USEFUL information for the first time at Duke.  Moreover, this professor was very helpful and took a personal interest in all of his students who cared for him to.  Awesome professor, getting better all the time, highly recommended.

Don Taylor is undoubtedly the worst professor I have had at Duke. He is lazy and incomprehensible. Instead of giving a final exam, which would take WAY too much effort, he gave a group project that required concepts that were not prerequisite and that he had no intention of teaching. I love PPS and get A's in the classes, but Taylor is truly awful.
This professor seemed to not really care about the class or the people in it and was often unclear. was not interested in grading students fairly at all

Lectures that are random and all over the place. Exam questions arbitrary and graded unfairly. No clear rubric and expectations are high although he doesnt list pre-reqs. He is also uninterested in you as a person and is unsympathetic and generally awful/awkward.

Oh my gosh. Do not take this class. He expects you to have a lot of prior knowledge although does not list any prerequisites.  He doesn't read through the assignments he makes us do. He simply "pastes" graphs in, even if they aren't the most up to day and thus make your life harder. He doesn't even understand the assignments he posts!
very very boring lectures and all multiple choice tests with random questions. not a fun class
Really cool teacher. Sometimes a little boring but really informed and you learn a lot. Not very hard class.
Best professor I've had at Duke hands down. His classes are great -- not a lot of work, but you learn SO much. He's a funny guy too.

Prof. Taylor rocks!  He's a really cool teacher, and I really learned a lot from his course (International Health Care Systems).  He really knows his material and manages to slip in funny jokes during lecture.  Good times Taylor!
Professor Taylor is the man. I learned allot in his class and he is a really cool guy.

The coursework is an intersection of religion, history, politics, and culture all throughout American history. Coates is so well-versed in the material. He welcomes participation and always encourages class discussions. Very clear grading criteria, follow the instructions and you can do well! Take this class!

super funny guy, this was the second class i took with him. if you do the reading and participate in class (aka go to class) and put some effort in the video essays, you will be fine and make an A. the movies he picked for 268 were quite interesting, and class discussions were fun.

Grading is very arbitrary. Even though I assume most of the class got an A, I think the topics are very ambiguous and unclear. I get it; it's hard to teach a class on religion, but some of the readings and analysis are just horrible.

Highly recommend Professor Coates. This class was amazing - one of my favourite classes I have taken at Duke! The readings are interesting, the in-class movies and documentaries are carefully picked to encourage conversation. Assignments are relatively simple, they just require you to have done the readings. Attendance and participation matters.

Easy but interesting. Most lectures were a brief discussion of the homework followed by watching some kind of film. Each unit starts with a movie screening (watching a whole movie over two days). Graded on participation, unit quizzes, three short essays, and a final project - grading can be tough but TAs are helpful.

This class is the perfect mix between a course on religion and one where you can watch legendary (or unfamiliar) movies and dissect them in an educational context. Grading is only dependent on 5 assignments really and grading is a bit tougher than expected by TAs. If you can get in a Coates class you should!

Not an easy A. Grading was a little bit harsh and there was a lot of reading and videos you needed to do before class which was annoying. Nice prof though and very available/willing to meeting for office hours.

I've taken two religion classes with Professor Coates and he's one of my favorite professors I've had at Duke. He makes every lecture engaging and interesting so even if you don't have much of an initial interest in religion, you will become interested and learn a lot. Plus in-class movie screenings were very fun. Highly recommend

Dr. Coates is kind, funny, and refreshingly in tune with the most pressing issues today. He wove in topics of class, race, gender, and more into discussions of film & religion. It was this multi-dsiciplinary view of religion & film that made the class so fun & applicable to our everyday lives. Most people got an A-/A, so grading is more than fair.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Class was not about religion. Racialized topics that had little/nothing to do with race during each class discussion. One of my least favorite class experiences so far at Duke.

take this course!! There's no textbook so the homeworks are watching videos he makes himself that are really interestingduring class you have a discussion while he goes over some slides. He's super engaging. I wouldn't say it's an "easy A" but if you put in work for the writing assignments (which are super short btw), then an A is totally possible

great class! not necessarily an automatic A, but definitely doable: need to put good analysis into discussion posts and final paper. however, very easy workload, and you learn a lot! class is just open discussion and with a 45-person class, so you don't need to participate that much. def would take!

Dr. Coates manages to make our class stress free while maintaining engagement. The religion in American life class is hands down the coolest courses. We watch his lectures and complete readings, then discuss once a week. Two papers and some smaller writing assignments (max 1 page). The material is truly interesting and applies to daily life.

Dr. Coates is a really nice guy who tries to make his students enjoy learning about religion and history, something he is clearly passionate about. Daily readings but not completely mandatory, but papers are based off of them. Only a few easy assignments and no final. Grading seemed a little inconsistent but gives feedback and welcomes questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Coates is hands down the best professor I've had at Duke. He makes material so accessible and the general outline of his classes are well-organized and thoughtful. He teaches in a way that makes you want to be a scholar of his subject. Truly an interesting and considerate professor.

Religion and film is an amazing and insightful class. Professor Coates is a great professor who is reasonable with his workload. He has clear expectations, but he is more than open to modifying the syllabus or any assignments. He also understands when his students just aren't getting it or when the material doesn't connect. AMAZING!

One of the best courses in Duke. The workload is incredibly light, yet you learn so much. Go to class, take good notes, and make a detailed cheat sheet for the exams. Don't miss out on the field trip to DUML.

Super accommodating and personable-- genuinely cares about her students. Lots of content. Trip to Marine Lab! Attendance is turning in homework within first 5 minutes of class or a one-question quiz. 2 sit-down exams, 1 take-home exam.  Get a 1-sided, handwritten cheatsheet. 2 group projects. Just show up and put in some effort and you'll do fine.

Professor Dunphy-Daly was seriously one of the best I've taken at Duke so far. She truly cares about her students in a meaningful way and her teaching style is both engaging and comfortable. Class is super interesting and very manageable. Definitely recommend taking if you can!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof Dunphy Daly is amazing! She's kind, clearly cares about her students, and a fun lecturer with engaging in-class activities and projects. The field trip to the marine lab was probably the highlight of my semester.

Meagan is such an amazing person. Marine Megafauna is such an interesting class and it was organized so well - expectations were very clear. Not a ton of homework but the readings were very relevant and interesting. Meagan is so accessible in office hours and really loves to get to know her students. DUML field trip was def a semester highlight.
best professor ive had so far at duke. dr dunphy-daly is super accessible outside of class (she leads a bass connections project) and class content is always engaging and interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Professor Dunphy-Daly is amazing. The content of Marine Megafauna is extremely interesting, and the tests reflect the content covered in the lectures. Tests not too hard, but take good notes and pay attention.

Meagan is a fantastic professor. She genuinely cares about her students, going the extra mile to ensure that everyone has what they need to succeed in the class. She's really receptive to feedback, which she constantly uses to improve her course (which to be honest, is nearly perfect). If you're looking for one of the best courses at Duke, take it!

I loved Meagan's class! She's a great professor, kind human being, and very accessible outside of class. The course was graded very fairly. It was easy to do well if you went to every lecture and just paid attention. She's a great lecturer.

Meagan is so supportive and understanding. Her lectures were really engaging and she made the material very easy to understand. Super generous with grading. There is no final - just a paper at the end of the class where you can choose your own topic. Highly recommend.

Meagan is caring, accessible, and she wants you to succeed. She is a very good lecturer. You have to know a lot of information for her tests but it is totally feasible to study and do well. The class is fun and the difficulty is not high. Beware of the group projects though. They can be really annoying if you get stuck with a bad group.

Loved this class! It's really chill and includes a trip to the marine lab. You're graded on a short reflection of a reading once a week (less than 250 words), a 15 min group presentation, a midterm on basic knowledge, and a final paper. If you need a chill class I would recommend. Meagan is so nice and really enthusiastic about marine conservation.

Professor Dunphy-Daly is perhaps the nicest person on earth. Seriously, she is absolutely lovely! Her enthusiasm and passion for marine biology are so infectious that you cannot help but fall in love with this field of study. I am an English major, but she made class accessible and exciting for non-bio majors. I cannot sing enough praise for her!

Professor Dunphy-Daly is AMAZING. I'm not a bio major, but took Marine Megafauna for my NS credit. Learned A TON, became inspired by the ocean, and did some really cool projects. Didn't get to go to the marine lab this semester because of COVID-19, but class was SO WORTH IT. One of best classes I have taken at Duke!

One of the highlights of the Nich School! She is kind, open, and ready to engage with students. Readings are light but lecture covers a lot. Dr. Dunphy-Daly also probes you to think critically. Readily accessible outside of class, accommodating, and willing to listen to students. TAs were nice but not informative and helpful.
Dr. Dunphy-Daly is incredibly kind and smart. She will help you with class work if you need it and has regular office hours. She wants you to do well and enjoy the class!

Very test heavy class, tough to do well if you can't join the discussion section. Tests are extremely comprehensive and challenging and make up the entirety of the class grading. Material was interesting but don't recommend simply due to class difficulty
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Do not ever take this course with her. The entire class is three tests with a bunch of things she never talks about. Even the TA doesn't agree with her methods. Horrible prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class is super interesting and pretty low-maintenance. You have to teach two lectures, which takes a long time to prep. However, once you present, it's smooth-sailing. Dr. Drea is very knowledgable and is always willing to help!

One of the worst classes I've ever taken at Duke. She has no compassion for students who are struggling and does not seem to care about her students. She is very passionate and knowledgeable, but not a very good teacher. Exams cover very random, obscure details that are barely discussed in class (despite what she says).

Took a seminar class with Dr. Drea. After the first few weeks, classes were led by students on chosen topics. In addition, we had to read some papers beforehand and write a reflection. Overall, it was a good class and Dr. Drea did a good job at helping guide these presentations both when we were preparing them and during the actual class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: I learned a lot and I genuinely enjoyed the lectures, but this course is 95 percent dependent on exams, which sucks. This course could do well with a couple group projects/presentations. For the exams, you have to remember a lot of tiny details and it's hard to tell what she's asking for in the short response questions. Great class, horrible prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Drea is super cool and a great lecturer, but the class can be difficultoverwhelming. It's worth it if you're into primateanimal behavior, and probably easier if you have an EvAnth background. Not an easy A. Optional discussion section has weekly quizzes to replace your lower midterm grade. Reading is supplemental, not really necessary.
Do not take, heard class would be easy, not the case. A lot of work

When she introduced herself by saying "My name is Dr. Drea, like the rapper" I knew she was going to be a cool professor. I was not disappointed. She is my favorite professor at Duke. So fascinating as a person!

Such a cool person. Dr. Drea is clearly very intelligent and will impart a lot of her knowledge to you. This class turned out to be one of the most interesting classes I have taken at Duke. It is tough, but fair. Dr. Drea is the bomb!
Awesome professor. She is very interesting with a really cool background. Get to know her! Interesting topic, pretty difficult but worth it

This class has a good rep because it's a fascinating subject with a good teacher, but don't mistake that for ease.  It is a very difficult course. You must got to every lecture to do well, but that won't guarantee that you'll succeed either. I highly recommend this class, but only if you aren't taking any other difficult or time-demanding courses.
Drea is the best teacher i've had at duke, and her class was absolutely fascinating. you must go to lecture to do well, but she is extremely organized and helpful. everyone should take this class.

Dr. Drea is an excellent professor. She is intelligent and witty, and her lectures are stimulating. The textbook is pretty much useless, but you only need to rely her powerpoints for the tests. Coming to class is mandatory if you want to do well.
Dr. Drea is very intelligent, and a great teacher.  I just wish she had more time to devote to students, but she has a lot of research responsibilities.

Dr. Drea is a fantastic teacher possessing a wealth of knowledge that she is willing to share with her class. Her lectures are very well organized and she explains complex concepts very clearly. She jokes a lot, which makes the class enjoyable. To do well, you MUST go to lecture. There is no better way to prepare for the tests.

Even though the class is called "Primate Sexuality", it doesn't exactly cover all the material you would expect...Still, it's a very interesting class and a pretty easy A.  Dr. Drea is a really skilled lecturer who has heard all the jokes before and has some pretty snappy comebacks!

Dr. Drea is an extremely intelligent woman.  She's by far the best BAA prof I've had.  BAA 171 was a great class, very interesting, thought a bit dense.  Some of the material was challenging, and the tests were not easy by far, but this is one of those classes you feel lucky to get a B in but loved every minute of it.

Whoever said that Drea was the "wicked witch of the west" is absolutely crazy.  Drea is funny, chill, very intelligent, and quite helpful if you show yourself to be both interested in and prepared for the content about which she is teaching. Don't let someone's misinformed opinion dissuade you from taking a class from one of BAA's best profs.
Very intelligent and taught a very stimulating class which you can take a lot out of if you are organized and prepared.
This woman is the wicked witch of the West reincarnate.  Particularly mean to girls. She is condescending. Makes the hair on the back of my neck stick up. Overall despicable.
Very intelligent, leads the most fascinating discussions. Her class decided me on a BAA major.

Sexuality and the Law with Prof. Duara was a good class overall. The class is very reading-heavy, and discussions were based solely on the readings of long, dense texts. The option to choose a paper or project for your final was nice. Final exam was fine, but it did require effort in studying. She is so kind, but the class itself can get boring.

Also took PUBPOL 209S with Prof Duara. She is a calm and kind person who is incredibly knowledgeable about the law & human rights. She assigns a lot of reading but I learned more in her classes than I ever have in any other class in my HS/college career. Participating is important but you don't always have to - just be attentive and show interest.

Overall easy class. Lots of homework reading and smaller writing assignments/papers but Duara grades fairly and leniently. Lecture itself is boring and can be very monotonous, but some of the topics covered were very interesting in terms of human rights.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Juliette is a very nice person but her classes are not engaging. She assigns way too much reading (100+ pages/week) and functionally every class is about regurgitating the assigned material - there is very little substantive analysis or discussion. Not particularly stimulating. She is accessible in office hours but doesn't provide much feedback.

Professor Duara is an amazing person! She is very empathetic and you can tell she is very knowledgeable on the topics we discuss. With that being said, she assigns around 100-120 pages of reading a week. It can be a lot, but it is interesting stuff if you're interested in Human Rights! Her assignments are fun and she offers useful feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Duara is congenial and pleasant, but the class subject is very boring and filled to the brim with reading. Almost all of the class's discussions go something like, "This atrocity happened. What can we do about it?" *students provide ideas* "We actually can't do any of those, but we can name and shame!" Regardless, it is a very frustrating class.

Dr Duara's participation in the class was nothing more than sitting back and letting discussions unfold. She didn't steer the conversations and there were no other activities throughout the term. The class was very reading heavy and participation was basically can you regurgitate facts. She's an odd grader on the papers too... a very boring class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Dr. Duara is clearly knowledgeable about her FOCUS course, Human Rights and World Politics. The class is very reading heavy, with 30-40 pages of reading (at least) every night. If you don't do the readings, it is hard to engage in class as 95% of the class time is spent discussing the readings with the other students.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Human Rights and World Politics was an excellent class; it was well organized and the topics get increasingly interesting. Aside from a few overviews and definitions, the majority of class is student discussion with little direction nor interference from Duara. However, she is very nice, knowledgeable, and happy to meet outside of class.

Professor Duara was amazing and I learned so much during the Sexuality and the Law class. Long and dense readings, but they are worth it and really important. Important topics from the readings are covered in class and tough topics are clarified. Fair grader. Very kind and overall really wants you to succeed.

Duara's human rights class was fascinating. The course was super well organized and the discussions were extremely interesting. The topics covered throughout the course were all so thought provoking! Duara could be a bit dry and condescending and I often felt like she was judging me when I spoke, but in the end I learned a ton and got a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Duara is super sweet and knowledgeable on ethics and human rights. I loved her class, Human Rights & World Politics, and I definitely learned a lot throughout the semester. The readings are pretty long but interesting if you like law and politics. Overall, this was a great class, and Professor Duara is an amazing professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Readings are interesting because class topics are interesting. I learned a lot and professor is always helpful when you have questions. Class is nice and chill and discussions are never boring.

Professor Duara is great, but the class is pretty much dependent on the readings. if people don't read, classes can be pretty dull, because participation/readings are a large part of the grade. however, I found the class to be interesting and learned a lot and would recommend for pubpol majors.

Professor Duara clearly cares about her students and is a pretty easy grader. The class has lots of reading and is discussion based which means if no one does the reading it can get kind of boring. That being said I learned a ton in the class and recommend it!

I had Human Rights & Legal Redress with Professor Duara and I really enjoyed it. However, participation is 20% of the grade, with 2 quizzes and 1 final paper being the remaining 80%. She does little to facilitate class discussion, so the class will be pretty tedious if you aren't interested in the subject matter already.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Duara really tried to facilitate an interesting conversation every class, but she assigns a lot of reading you should do. I wish I took the human rights intro class before this one so I could better participate. She was a little intimidating but really accessible; it helps if you attend her office hours and go over your papers with her.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Duara is pretty dry as a person-- class could get boring. Just don't be afraid to be yourself and try to make the class lively. She is very knowledgeable about the human rights system and really wants you to be. PARTICIPATION MATTERS A LOT! And be able to do in-class essays and take feedback on your writing.

I loved this class and professor Duara. She is a law professor who teaches this undergraduate course once a year. Definitely take advantage of getting to take a course with her. Sexuality and the Law is such an amazing class and also unique in the offerings. The readings are not bad and rotate each week who in the class presents the readings.

Not a free class but doable with reasonable effort. Lots of readings, movies, and TV shows as homework. Must speak 2x/class. Not accommodating towards late work/formatting errors (make sure 2x space, 12-pt Times New Roman or else it's an auto fail). Each 10 point assignment is actually 10% of your whole grade. Great community in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Not a free T-req class but doable. Must participate in every class. Assignments are short writings worth a lot. Lots of reading/movies. Final essay is free. Formatting and attendance rules are unforgiving. Read the syllabus! Dr. D is an engaging speaker and does a good job including everyone and fostering community.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: No tests, no huge papers/projects. Dr. D's class is an environment that demands preparation and participation, but since the content is light, everyone who shows up, follows the instructions, and tries their best excels. She is also an exceptional discussion facilitator. Don't take this class if you just want to sit in the back and coast.

Dr. Dubois is one of the best professors at Duke and is definitely the best humanity professor. Her class is organized, she lays it all out week by week on day one. The workload isn't horrible, a lot of watching movies and reading fiction, which is a lot of fun. She leads interesting discussions and they allow all majors equal input. Amazing class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Her grading is inconsistent and entirely based on whether she likes you. I got an A+ on every written assignment. Every single one. A- in the class overall. if 90% of the grade is based on assignments and 10 is participation, you show up and participate every single class period for a 90 you start to see what participation points arereally about.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I would not recommend. Dr. Dubois's grading is extremely vague, and you essentially have no idea where your grade stands throughout the semester. Participation is arbitrarily graded. It is an interesting class but do not take if you are not obsessed with romantic fiction. This class leans much more heavily towards English than History.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Dubois is excellent but you definitely have to put forth a lot of effort in order to preform well in her class. You do read a lot, so be prepared for that. She's amazing at feedback and very receptive to your comments too. She wants to give you an A, so work for it.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Dr. Dubois is incredible! She is the perfect combination of rigorous and supportive. She demands a lot of you in regards to reading, writing quality, and analysis. However, she will support you and give great feedback. She's also a good lecturer and made class really fun. Take a class with her!!!

Getting writing critique from a published author ROCKS- Dr. Dubois gave an whole page of feedback. The class is heavy in reading and writing, but Dr. Dubois makes class interesting with guest lecturers and snarky hilarity in class (e.g. chucking a particularly bad novel across the room day 1). However, she's hard to read and approach personally.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Dr. Dubois is awesome. She's tough and straight forward, but I have never seen such passion and enthusiasm in any other professor. Made me consider switching my major to History. She also has her followers: people who take her classes nearly every semester, even if they're not HIST majors...

Dr. Dubois is a really hard grader. Although she is approachable and helpful in her comments, she expects a lot and it's a constant struggle trying to figure out what to do to get a good grade. She grades not only on following the insturctions but actually writing well.

Keep in mind that the HIST83 comments are freshman who have never taken history at Duke before.  Dr. D is an amazing professor and truly cared about fostering good writing & research in her students.  She is rigorous but intellectually-engaging and an awesome professor to get to know. Also, a lot of the guys thought she was hot.

A very strong teacher, in every sense of the word. You will learn a lot, but the class is very difficult. She did cancel the Final, though, which was nice. Class participation is MANDATORY if you want a good grade. 40% of my grade last semester was participation.

Dr. Dubois is a smart woman and a good teacher. However, she does have an edge and is often hard to read, so get on her good side. You won't regret it. I learned a lot in the class, she's a fair grader, and DO THE READING. There's a lot of it.
Dr. D can be a little intimidating at first, but overall she is a good professor and can be very helpful.  She is a pretty fair grader. However, she may make you read/watch really weird things.

Dr. D really knows her stuff, and it takes skill to fill a 2.5 hour class.  She's a little unpredictable and sometimes overly defensive about her subject, but you will definitely learn things.  DO THE READING, otherwise your life will be hard.

Dr. D has been one of the most amazing professors I've had at Duke. She definitely expects a lot, and she doesn't take late work. She expects you to do the best you can do in her class, and her writing comments help improve your writing immensely. I'd highly recommend taking a class from her. (Do the reading!)
she's hard to read, has an edge, demands to be called "DR" but she's an ok grader

Do not recommend. He will make you suffer and tell you it's your fault you didn't do good enough. If you do not already know everything before this class, you will spend 20 hours a week with minimal help and still do bad. In-class quizzes are cruel. Did not care if you were ill. You get 0.

TAKE HIS CLASS! Professor Thomas is a very nice, caring, and encouraging instructor. 204 is an important step for higher-level classes and research - his lectures prepare you well for those. Office hours are super helpful and last very long. He made funny jokes in lectures and encouraged questions. Flunching with him has literally made my day.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: It's rare for a professor to send emails to students to check up on them and ask them how they are doing. It's rare for a professor to be kind enough to ask for feedback on the class. 8:30am lectures were brutal, but having him made it better. He asks for feedback like he actually plans to use it, not like he's collecting it for a secret bonfire.

Hardest but the most real class I've taken in college (lots of fluff courses in the Econ dept) You will actually learn econometrics and how to critique bad quantitative research. I finally understand statistics. Reasonable policy on pop quizzes; cold calling isn't intimidating, very available outside of class. I will look back on this class fondly.
If there's one person to learn econometrics from, it's Duncan. By far one of the most challenging classes, but certainly worth taking with him — you'll actually learn something.

One of the best professors I've had at Duke. Duncan's low pressure cold calling, combined with a commitment to memorize our names signaled his investment in our learning. He emphasized conceptual intuition and not getting bogged down in equations. Pop quizzes are curved heavily. Generous cutoffs was shocked to get an A, exam grading likely soft too

Spare yourself. If you still take this class after seeing these ratings, then you and your GPA will only have yourself to blame. If you want to graduate with even a mediocre GPA, take this with Jeff. If you're ok with a B-/C+ average (B if you score 10 points above average on both the midterm and final), then go ahead and suffer with Duncan

If you actually want to learn econometrics, take this class with Duncan. He gives extra credit, curves exams, and allows you to drop your midterm if you do better on the final. He cares about actually teaching you why concepts work rather than just telling you that they do. This is the best class I've taken in the major.

This was BY FAR the most interesting, applicable, and intellectually stimulating class I have taken at Duke. I was terrified going into the class and heard about how hard it was, but Duncan's lecture style makes complicated concepts simpler and the office hours make homework extremely doable. This class showed me how economic theory is applied.

took him because everyone said he was amazing. he is, outside of class. in class he's goes too fast. i've never been so COMPLETELY stumped by a final. still, he genuinely cares about his students and their education (which is super clear in office hours). all in all, spent over 15+ a week, and although i really respect him i would not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Although you learn a lot in his class, the material he teaches is so different to the homework (using Stata) and the midterm/final (not Stata, and full of trick questions). Lectures too fast and expects us to understand; hence very few do well on his tests. Take 204 with someone else -- the time spent on Duncan's course is simply not worth it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Can't believe my parents and I work our hardest and pay tuition for this guy to tell me I didn't try hard enough in a class that provides insufficient resources, exams unrelated to slides, and no curve to account for the fact that most students scored 60%. Unreal. But maybe I'm just ungrateful and entitled (I spent 15+ hrs on this class a wk) :)
Save yourself. Take with Jeff DeSimone with the rest of the smart people who managed to save their GPAs.
Wishing I could've gone back in time and saved myself from the confusing lectures, terrible teaching style, and brutal policies of Duncan.

Duncan made the class extremely unwelcoming and unhelpful for those looking to learn. His policies were extreme and unreasonable, and so were his grade cutoffs, with most students receiving B-s and Bs

In the end, reflecting on this course, taking it felt like an immense waste of time and effort. Nothing more I could've done could have saved me from my grade, and only those who came into the class already having previously deeply learned economics could have succeeded.

No student at Duke should take this class. If you are intelligent, you will understand that taking this class when you could take it with Jeff is one of this biggest mistakes you could make in your entire Duke career. Your GPA will suffer, your mental state will suffer, and you'll inevitably regret taking it. Spare yourself

If 8:30s weren't bad enough, Duncan's teaching style was incorrigible. His slides were consistently missing important content and there was no way to gain an understanding of the concepts even using in class notes, his slides, and outside resources.

He admitted to making the midterm impossible just to make people miserable and freak out over the final. Turns out even freaking out on the final didn't help as he made sure the final had an even lower average than the midterm.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: class wasn't even worth my effort. I spent immense amounts of time on the course just for the tests to be random conceptual questions with no relevance to what we learned and have 60 averages and be uncurved.

Final is 55% of your grade. No curve. Clicks through slides quickly rather than teaching. Doesn't record lectures. Doesn't include any relevant info on slides. Tests completely unrelated to material on slides, so even self studying doesn't help.

His policies reflect a general disregard for the wellbeing of his students. Since he did not accept stinfs, the class was repeatedly full of coughing students, and some I knew had to go to class even with COVID to avoid being punished in their grades with a 0 which each decrease your grade by 3.25%.

Sure the class isn't the worst. Just prepare to commit all your time and effort to get a mediocre grade. Unless you are extremely well versed in the subject, or you study deeply every topic taught beyond the slides, you will not escape the (B-,B,B+) range. The avg Duke Econ major will not be happy with their grade in the class.

TAs for this class have a background in math or stats. If you are just an Econ major you are going to have a hard time in this class. However, unlike other hard classes you may have come across, there is not a curve and the bar is unreasonably high.
Would not recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Prof. Duncan is not a bad guy. He really wants his students to learn and I indeed learned a lot. But I have to admit that his lectures are not always helpful. He tries to go through a lot of content but rarely gives a clue about how things are connected, why we learn this then that, and what we are heading to. It can be easy to feel lost.

It's an 8:30 class. He intentionally set a quiz in the first 3 min of a class sometime during the semester. If you are late, you get zero, which is equivalent to -3 in your aggregate mark. And there is no makeup.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: The class is hard. The class is at times extremely frustrating. It's also not unfair or impossible to succeed. Go back through each powerpoint after class and make sure you understand the intuition that is being conveyed. Ultimately you learn a lot, and he really does care when students are interested in learning more about econometrics.
spent 14 hours in each pset. Super confusing and useless lectures. We didn't learn anything on the tests and he mostly clicked through all the slides super fast in class instead of teaching
never posted on ratemyprofessor before but came on here out of solidarity. this was bad. lots of mistakes that confuse both the class and the professor and he assigns work irrelevant to the tests

Absolute horror. Class? 8:30am Monday and Wednesday. Pop quiz. Cold calls you. Slides are light summary. Exam? Full of trick questions. No curve. Want to get an A? Even if you think you've made it though hard classes before, this one's expectations are set so high you might never reach them. But hey, it's probably because you're lazy and entitled.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Don't expect Econ 204 to be an easy A like some of the econ electives you may have taken before. It's the hardest core econ classes. That said, Duncan is excellent at explaining concepts, and the class is highly organized with fair tests and quizzes.

Duncan is very invested in this class and is unarguably one of the best professors in the department. If you're serious about truly understanding econometrics, take it with him. However, if you're not prepared to commit 10+ hours/week (which I find completely reasonable for a core econ class) you always have the option to taking it in the spring.

This is either the hardest class in my entire life or Duncan wants to include too much in this class with not enough time/ability. If you're not someone who wants to do research, take it after you get your internships because this class will take up all your time AND cook your GPA. Overall very patient professor, I guess I am just not very smart.

Duncan is simply amazing. Econometrics is the cornerstone to applying economics, so I don't know why it's expected to be easy. It is an 8:30 & it's a rough curve initially. I mainly focused on class, didn't have to read the textbook. If you really truly want to benefit, take it with him. This class, and what you'll learn from him is worth millions
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Absurdly long problem sets, not a good lecturer, and beating the curve does not help you in this class.

This is the best class I've taken in econ. Duncan's class was at 8:30, yet it was super engaging. He has a very conversational lecture style, and everything is based on real data. This class is challenging, but you'll be fine if you put in the work and show up. If you wanna learn econometrics well take it with Duncan, if not, take it in the spring.

Pop quiz in early morning.Skims though each topic very lightly (reading textbook expected).Exam extremely convoluted and hard to show u know the subject bc u literarily have no clue what you're being asked. I read the textbook, took notes, attended all classes. Unless ur schedule is free and u dedicate your life to the class dont expect to do well
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Though the class is difficult, if you put in the work, you should be fine. There are pop quizzes, but each one is 1-2 questions that take less than 5 minutes in total. The average score on the final was low, but so was class attendance. This is one of those classes where you get out just as much as you put in.

This is a stats focused req for ECON majors who might not WANT TO MAKE STATS THEIR LIFE, something the prof expects you to do for the sem. Aggressive towards seniors due to his personal belief they should not take the class. Hard to understand lectures, unhelpful to exam. Pop quiz at 8:30 sharp are 15% of grade (5 quiz are 7% of grade, 1 is 8%).
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: JUST DON'T TAKE THE CLASS WITH DUNCAN. You'd study hard for the final just to get screwed by questions with outrageous wording that do not focus on the materials covered. Pop quizzes at 8:30 on the dot and you get automatic 0 for showing up 3 minutes late to class. For your GPA and sanity, DON'T TAKE DUNCAN'S CLASS!!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Finals were 55% of your grade and the average was a 60. This was because even though there were many intelligent students in this class, his questions didn't address the material taught.

Is this class difficult? Yes. However, I have learned more in this class than any other taken at Duke. These posts are simply a reflection of the heavy grade inflation at Duke, not Prof Thomas. If anything, he is one of the best. He incites critical thinking and challenges students. At 80k a year, you'd think you would want to learn something.
His “curve” gave those who scored 10+ points above average on both the final and midterm a B. Likely most students got below a B in his class due to his unreasonable grade distribution

This course was extremely difficult but not because of the content. Duncan's lecturing was extremely convoluted and he often became confused. He tested exclusively on topics we didn't learn in class. Both the midterm and final were unreasonable and the average reflected it with a D- average (1 point above an F (60)) & curve was almost non existent.

His grading scale is crazy. Midterm average was a 62 and final average was a 60. You'd think the curve would save you but no. That's your grade. On average his final grade curve meant if you scored 15 points above average you still got a B.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Duncan was truly amazing. Even though the 8:30 timing sucked, I wanted to attend all the lectures as I was able to learn so much. The material is super interesting and Duncan is always eager to help. The course is not easy and will take a lot of time, but it is so worth it. Duncan is also just a super interesting person with so many cool stories.

Professor Thomas was the most engaging professor I've had. His class was challenging but actually useful. I am now a commodities trader in New York and still use his notes. The class will be difficult and the problem sets aren't fun when you're doing them, but it's really cool to actually have a comprehension of what is taught in his class. 10/10

Humorous professor and interesting lectures but he spent too much time explaining the basics like hypothesis testing, leaving little time for the harder part. And the biweekly problem sets are super super long which requires nearly a whole day to complete, and pop quizzes & cold calls in lectures create a lot of stress, so I wouldn't take it again.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Hardest class at Duke. Dunc was not good and rushed through every lecture, not explaining math and expects students to intuitively understand everything. Exams were brutal (50% average across the 3) and homeworks were STATA, graded easy but so hard to really understand. He tries to be funny but he's not. Pop quizzes exist. Avoid if not econ major.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Duncan gives great lectures. This was seriously one of the best taught classes I have ever taken. This class has biweekly psets which take ~10 hours each, but they are graded reasonably. Tests are hard but heavily curved. Highly reccomend! Also, for your sake and for Duncan's, have some math skills going into the course.

Econ204 is a difficult course, but if you want to learn this material you should take it with Professor Thomas. He is an unbelievable teacher and will build your intuition for this subject matter so well. He is also really funny and approachable. This was the most well executed course I've taken at Duke and the one I've learned the most in.

Don't take the easy way out and take Econ204 with Duncan. You'll probably struggle immensely, but in the end, it's so worth it. Even at 8:30am with pop quizzes, this was probably the best and most useful class I'll ever take at Duke. Duncan teaches it so well and really tries to develop an intuition of metrics that anyone can absorb. No regrets.

One of the greatest professors in the Econ department if not the greatest. Taking this class with him at 8:30 AM was made bearable because of his funny jokes and engagement with the class. He's so helpful and is even willing to teach a lecture multiple times if he has to in order to help a student. Absolutely take Econometrics with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof Thomas is great - probably the best in the Econ department. The material is hard but very useful and applicable to real world settings. He makes the material as intuitive as possible in lectures and his humor helps to lighten the mood of the class. Expect to work hard but there is great TA support and Prof Thomas himself is super accessible.

Prof Thomas is a fantastic guy. He cares so extremely much about everyone understanding the material. If anyone has a question in lecture, he will happily reexplain the concept as many times as needed. A genuinely excellent prof and a very rewarding class. It will definitely be useful in the future.

Dr. Thomas is the most caring professor I've had thus far at Duke. His lectures are amazing and he genuinely + deeply wants every student to succeed and understand the material. Although there are lots of jokes that ECON204 is a class of nightmares, that is certainly not the case with Duncan. He does all he can to assist and has amazing TAs too.

Very, very hard class but also very, very useful. Duncan is extremely helpful and humorous. 204 teaches me an analytical mindset to approach real-world problems that I can apply to other coursework and actual research. The most useful course I have taken at Duke.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: This class takes up a ton of time (biweekly p-sets), but Thomas is incredible. Great lecturer, very fair and caring. If you just put in the work and make sure you don't fall behind, you'll do well. When you get this stuff, it's so rewarding and gives you such useful knowledge for your job and the real world. Hot take but really enjoyed 204.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes--Caring

reviews.comment: Honestly, this is one of the most challenging & rewarding classes I've ever taken. The material is absolutely difficult and homework takes around 20 hours. The exam is also not easy. But I've learned a ton in this class and they've been very useful. Would take it all over again despite the nightmares.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Thomas is easily the best professor I have had at Duke University. He genuinely cares about the learning of his students and does everything in his power to help students clearly understand class concepts. His class is the single most useful course I have taken at Duke. The class is worth the work.

Professor Thomas is the best professor in the Econ department at Duke. His lectures are engaging, and while the material can be tough at times, his humor makes it much more bearable. He also does a great job of making office hours welcoming and worthwhile. I wish he taught other econ core classes.

Econometrics is difficult but Professor Thomas is a really wonderful professor. He genuinely cares about his students and is extremely fair with grading. If you put the work in, you will not fail. Make sure to pay attention during lectures, do all of the problem sets thoroughly, and go to as many office hours as you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Hes a great teacher. Its a very hard course but its difficult to find ways in which Dr. Thomas could do better with the material. He made it very interesting and engaging.
Great professor who really understands the materials and tries to present it in an engaging manner.

Duncan Thomas is incredible, and his class was absolutely the most valuable one I took at Duke - no question (writing this a few years later). I know there are ways around Econometrics / easier profs, etc. Do yourself the favor of taking Duncan Thomas's class. and sit in front. This has come up in my career again and again when, little else has.

Started off as the most intimidating course I've ever taken, but Professor Thomas was super devoted to making sure we learned the material. Really enjoyed the practical applications of this class and even though I thought I was going to fail, he took care of my grade in the end. Even if it's harder with Professor Thomas I would still recommend
I think this class was hard to implement online. There was also weekly quizzes and biweekly problem sets but the concepts are pretty difficult to understand without an in person component

Professor Thomas is a great lecturer and educator, you can tell he loves teaching econometrics. I found the class really difficult to take online (unable to engage during lectures, hard to hear anything through recordings, etc). A little disappointed that he decided to teach in-person because it unfairly benefits those who are able to be there
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Hardest and most useful course for Econ major. Professor Thomas is very engaged and committed to his job and wants you to do well. You will need to keep up with the work and work hard to understand well the content. The class is pretty complex.

Rumors are true that this class is so difficult and is the bane of Econ majors. However, Duncan is so knowledgeable and kinda funny. He knows his material and I think the grading is pretty fair. The final accounts for more than 50% of your grade so that is a lot of pressure.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: BEST ECON CLASS AT DUKE, taught by the greatest professor at Duke. Ive never tried harder in any other class, and have never learned more in my life. Duncan and his TAs are inspirational, caring and responsible for his students. So long as youre willing to put in the work, they will put aside so much time and energy to help you succeed.

Prof. Thomas is the best teacher Ive ever had. He dedicates so much time to his class & students. If you work hard & engage in lectures/OH, Thomas will teach you the invaluable skill of thinking critically to solve problems spanning far beyond Econ. The class is demanding, but w/ dedicated effort youll learn a ton and grading is extremely fair.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Thomas is one of the few professors at Duke that truly care about his students' success, and it shows in the class. He wants everyone to do well by understanding metrics both mathematically and intuitively, so he makes lectures mandatory with pop quizzes. Problem sets are very hard and take long but worth it. Final grades are very fair.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He tries as much as possible to make Econometrics 'intuitive' - and it's clear that a lot of effort has gone into making the experience engaging. It's definitely the best Economics class at Duke and he's definitely one of the best professors on campus. Take a class with him, flunch him and stay on top of the work.

Such a great lecturer. He tries to make some pretty dry material interesting by applying it to real life. Metrics was difficult but he was easily accessible and helpful during office hours. Hes kind and funny but be ready to work for that grade. You earn what you put into it

Duncan's the best professor I've had at Duke. He is deeply invested in his profession and will go very far to help you. To give you an example, I once emailed him about a question I had on the material. He came to class 15 minutes early and made an entire presentation just to answer my question. He truly is one of a kind.

Professor Thomas is a great professor, and I would recommend you take the class with him. The class is not easy, but Professor Thomas is really good at engaging students to make sure everyone understands the material. There are problem sets every other week that take a lot of time, but if you are on top of your work, it is not too bad

Prof. Thomas is funny and really cares about his students. His class really pushes you to think critically about econometric modeling. Its a pretty fast-paced lecture, but he always makes sure everyone is following. Problem sets can be lengthy, but are only due every other week, and they prepare you more for the exam than in any other class.

I had a great time taking Econometrics with Prof. Thomas. He does an excellent job in conveying the concepts and structuring lectures in a very logical order. Although the material itself is quite challenging, once mastered, it will be easy to realize why he says the class will benefit you later on.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Thomas' econometrics class is incredibly stimulating. It's hard and his expectations are high but the lectures are designed to make sure everyone can keep up and he makes it very interactive. If you don't pay attention, he will notice but if you work hard, you will leave understanding much more about economics than just econometrics.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He is very cynical, but it grows on you. He makes fun of economists, the class, the university, and by the end I suddenly felt like I understood the real world of economics rather than a bunch of equations simplified and dumbed down for students, as I felt in even the most advanced econ classes before this one. Pay attention. Pays off big-time.

I highly recommend taking this class with Professor Thomas. His lectures are incredibly well designed and really encourages students to stay engaged and always ask questions. Huge focus on actually learning the material instead of just last minute cramming for exams. It's a rare treat to take a class as intellectually stimulating as this one.

This course is unequivocally thrilling. He shows you the intuition and the math behind all of the major quantitative analysis techniques-- allowing people who are both less and more mathematically inclined to "get it." This class is not the hell that people call it-- go over the slides, go to office hours and talk to him. An A is well within reach.

Take econometrics with him. This was the most intellectually stimulating class Ive ever taken at Duke. Duncan is caring, takes great care in designing the syllabus and his slides, and always goes an extra mile to make sure everyone is on the same page. Participate a lot, show that you understand the material, and you will get the grade you deserve

D. Thomas is excellent. He runs a tight ship. His expectations are high and he expects you to meet them; but most importantly, they are fair. If you put in time and work, you will succeed.  Unequivocally, ECON208 is the best of the core Economics classes. Also one of the great intellectual challenges of the department. A very rewarding semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I wasn't required to take this class but it was certainly worth it due to Professor Thomas' emphasis on building an intuitive understanding of econometrics. I therefore recommend the class to anyone who actually wants to move past the bs and actually understand how soc sci/humanities research works. The prof also comes with a great sense of humor.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Thomas is an amazing teacher! He explains the difficult econometrics concepts so well, and stresses the importance of building intuition as opposed to cramming formulas. Take this class with him, and you would truly learn concepts that you can apply in the future.

Professor Thomas is great. He truly cares about the students and is always willing to help. Not only can you expect to learn a lot from the lectures but also the problem sets. You can tell he spent tremendous time and effort in preparing for the lectures and designing the problem sets. The class is hard and demanding but that's how you learn stuff.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Professor Thomas is phenomenal. It's no secret 208 is a dreaded class, but he gives you the sense he's there with you step-by-step throughout the semester. He clearly cares about the kids in his lecture, and while the material is difficult he does a surprisingly good job of contextualizing it. If you can't take 208 abroad, take it with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Really good professor. Cares about his students, & most of all his students learning the content. One of the few Econ core classes I've taken where you absolutely need to go to class. He puts notes online, but the content is extremely difficult, & he does a great job teaching the material so class is necessary

Very inspiring and engaging lecturer. Really cares for students individually. Difficult material that is covered fast, but learned a lot in class. Favorite Economics class so far, and possibly the most applicable to any subject matter and life.

Duncan is truly passionate about teaching & really cares about your learning, and it shows in his readiness for lecture and his willingness to help students. The class is tough & the problem sets make you think, but if you put the time & effort into them & ask for help when needed, your learning will reflect on the exams.

The lectures are fast paced , so it is critical to keep on top of things. Office hours, class attendance, quiz preparation and a good study group are the keys to being successful in this course. The material is quite challenging, but what you put in to this class, is what you will get out.
Best teacher in the "worst classroom ever"! :)

Duncan is one of the most prepared lecturers I have ever had. knows every bit of his slides inside out and comes prepared to tackle any questions that students have. For grading, he is EXTREMELY fair. Take the class with him and participate, ask questions, and do the homework. He definitely helps your grade out if you participate and seem engaged.

I am 6 years removed from my masters , and for the previous 5 years I worked in an M&A consulting role.  This class would have been incredibly valuable in my prior job, and anyone considering a career finance/M&A/consulting should take this class.  You learn a ton, and Duncan is a great professor.  One of the best classes I have taken.

Professor Thomas puts in a tremendous amount of effort into helping you develop an intuitive understanding of some really tough material. If you keep up with lectures and put up with work you should do just fine.

Doing well in quant classes requires good math intuition. Duncan stresses on building this intuition for everyone in the room, and will do so tirelessly until everyone "gets it". He truly cares about making this a class that is worth the ridiculous sum of money we pay in tuition. Be motivated, be consistent, ask questions, and you'll do well.

One of the best professors at Duke. Funny and engaging; clearly very sharp as well. Wants you to learn something in his class, but doesn't give easy grades out. Near impossible to get an A unless you're a stat wiz to start with, or you're willing to give up a social life. But he'll make sure you actually learn something in his class.

Duncan is absolutely one of the best professors I've ever met in Duke! He teaches in a really different way. His course is difficult, because he lets you think and make your own judgment rather than just doing math. If you work hard on it, you will find it challenging but also fun. Take the course with him and you will learn a lot!

Prof Thomas taught my econometrics course, one that is required for the economics major. I dreaded taking the class; however, I found it to be one of the most enjoyable and useful classes I've taken at Duke, although it was very hard. Lectures are clear, help is abundantly available, there isn't a focus on grades, and above all, Duncan is fair.

Duncan is an awesome prof. The material is inherently challenging, but he is enthusiastic about helping students understand and is super accessible outside of class. Takes his time to slow down and make sure everyone is on the same page. Appreciates class attendance, demonstration of interest. Take this class with him.
I really don't understand the negative ratings.  He is funny, interesting, and approachable.  If you put the time into the class, he will do everything to make sure you understand the material.
No.

Professor Thomas is amazing.  He is a great instructor and explains difficult concepts in a clear way.  He definitely works to give students an appreciation for econometrics and not just the math behind it.  Outside of class he is a really nice and funny guy.  Take his class!
Awesome guy, great professor.  I learned a ton and enjoyed it.  Take econometrics with him!

One of Duke's best professors.  He made a very difficult subject understandable and even enjoyable.  He has a great sense of humor and his lectures are great.  If you put effort into the class, he will be incredibly open to meeting with you outside of class for any further questions you might have.  Awesome guy!

Definitely one of the best professors I have had. He really puts a lot of effort into the class. Make sure you go to lectures and do the problem sets, otherwise you'll be screwed for the final. This class was one of the most challenging I have taken/will take, but it is extremely applicable and useful.

Look at his CV, he is extremely accomplished. However, he has trouble toning down lectures to help students understand econometrics. His style of lecturing isn't boring, but his lecture slides will put any student to sleep. Lastly, Thomas whines a lot and is arrogant. Bottom poster praising him is clearly 1 of the 3 students who actually liked him
Lectures are somewhat useless. He simply picks on people to answer hard questions. Exams are challenging. TAs are jokes.

This class is very difficult but you will get a ton of useful knowledge out of it. Thomas puts a lot of thought into the lectures and they are very worthwhile. Definitely a class where you get out what you put in. He is very accessible outside of class and more than willing to help if you go to him with problems. One of the best professors at Duke.

Durrett is somewhat funny and pretty much exclusively does example problems during lecture. His exams are easy and he lets you use a cheatsheet, but the grade only depends on the two midterms and the final.

Really caring guy, but this class was bit disappointing. Lectures were just him reading off slideshows so most people didn't even show up. 3 exams make your grade. The slideshows were confusing, often with mistakes. He assigned NO hw. I dislike hw, but it's so essential in math class because how else can you retain math without frequent practice??

Dr. Durrett is such a wonderful person. He is a very sweet soul who cares about his students and tries to make the class as low stress as possible. He knows his stuff well, but explanations can be a bit confusing the first time around, so be sure to ask questions. Grading is very relaxed, and scores tend to be very high.
a once in a lifetime kind of person
Professor Durrett is the man. Math 230 is usually a tough class but with him it was a breeze. He's super smart and very chill. Would retake the class with him in a heartbeat.
easy class and he is so cool about grading
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Hilarious

reviews.comment: very hard. do not underestimate how difficult he is as a teacher.
Easy for a Math class, still tough to get an A.  Prof Durrett is a great guy and is very accessible during his office hours.

This professor is super chill. Sometimes make mistakes while calculating on the board. Does not expect too much from his students, and are less strict about many things (attendance, late hw, what to not use for tests) You can bring notes to exams.

Durrett is a super chill professor. Sometimes he would explain things unclearly or in circles, but the material is so straightforward you can basically figure stuff out on your own. Beware of few tests with very few problems with a lot of opportunity to make stupid mistakes. Although it's pretty easy, don't take it too lightly.

Lectures are pretty clear; material covered isn't too hard; homework and tests are not very difficult; he just wants to see that you learned and understand the information. Funny and quite chill guy, willing to help you if needed. Would definitely take MA 230 with him and would take another class with him.
Best teacher to take Stat 230Math 230 with. Really clear lectures and very fair. He teaches really well, and his jokes are great. Would definitely take another statmath class with him.
Prof. Durrett was very easy to understand, willing to help, and extremely reasonable with his assignments and tests. He also joked a lot, which made lecture more enjoyable.
Rick Durrett is great. Tests were based on homework problems and were very straight forward. Grading was lenient/fair.

Professor Durrett is a good teacher. He's a little old and sometimes gets lost in his own lectures/arithmetic, but he knows probability forwards and backwards and is always willing to go back and clarify. He's full of jokes that make class fun, and class examples/homework problems are exactly like the tests.

She is one of the best professors at Duke who will bend over backwards to help you out, whether it be in the class or as a Stats major. A lot of the comments here are from her FIRST semester at Duke so cut her some slack. She is amazing.
Dr Durso really cares about her students. Breaks down the most important and prevalent topics in stats. Very kind
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This was Dr. Durso's 1st semester at Duke, so the class was a bit unorganized/unpredictable. There's weekly homework, labs, and quizzes, but she grades super fairly- we got to drop 2 labs, 2 hws, & 2 quiz grades and the midterms are weighted most heavily on your best grade. She's super intelligent, experienced, and genuinely cares for her students

Learned very little statistics. Focused more on history of famous statisticians and random, irrelevant information than the material we were meant to be learning. A very easy A, but too frustrating to be worth it. All econ majors that need this class as a prerequisite for econ 208 were extremely irritated and disappointed.
Best professor at DUKE

I can say without a doubt that Dwayne really cares about his students. His lectures are always passionate and he's very well-spoken and eloquent. While the class was definitely a little unorganized, it was completely understandable given that it was his first time teaching it. Would definitely take again.

Dwayne was probably the best professor i had this semester. He cares about his students actually learning and was open to all of our different learning styles. The guy literally created 5 different syllabuses and we could choose which ever one we wanted to do. The course is so easy, and the content is pretty interesting. It is a lot of reading tho.

Dwayne is great! He's kinda ??? at first but you get used to him and everything starts to make sense after he rambles for a bit. He goes beyond just teaching about Asia and is able to speak about so many topics that you can connect to almost anything. He's super nice and is always down to talk about anything. I would highly recommend him!!

Prof Dixon is honestly such a great dude. While his lectures are often complex and confusing, I've learned a lot in the end and I genuinely enjoyed his class. He's super caring and is always down for having a discussion about anything really. Tldr he's pretty rad 10/10 recommend.

Dwayne Dixon now teaches at UNC. He is a great professor who is very unique in his viewpoints. He definitely advocates for minorities, self-appreciation, and activism. He believes in anarchy as a utopia I'm pretty sure, but he lets the students think for themselves and pushes on them to ask tough questions. This class is an easy A and three gen eds
Passionate teacher and super easy, laid-back classes!

After my glowing course evaluation failed to go through, I felt compelled to at least come here & highly recommend him. Great orator, funny stories, very approachable & just all around a cool rebel.
