He probably doesn't even know how much he changed my perspective when life had me down. Best class at UNC, I love this guy, wish you the best Prof D!!!

Incredible professor, changed my trajectory at Duke. His class wasn't much work, but we had amazing discussions in class. He would prompt student participation but jump in at the right times and relate our discussions back to key concepts. He's super passionate, inspiring, and supportive - I still meet with him each semester to talk and get advice.

Dwayne is one of the best professors I have had so far. He is such a cool dude and shares so many stories that he ties into the material. He is so passionate and it makes his lectures engaging. I wish he taught classes in my major so I could have him as my professor again.
Really bad professor. He knows a lot but spent no time on preparing a lecture. I didn't learn anything from his course. It really hard to keep awake during his lecture

He is a smart professor who cares about what he's teaching. I thought he taught the class very well and always wanted to make sure everyone understood the material and was keeping up. The homeworks were fairly tedious and not that useful but the protocomputer and final projects were cool (though rather time consuming). Also, he posts slides.

His ECE52 class has gotten lots of negative reviews before (I was terrified to take it) but he's changed it a lot (mainly the order of material covered). Protocomputer is easier and not at the same time as the final proj. Tests were actually quite easy. Made himself accessible by office hours/email. Above all he's smart and likes what he's teaching
Knows his stuff, but it's clear he doesn't want to teach. Grading and standards are unclear and confusing. Doesn't respond to emails, weight of projects,exams, homework, etc is misleading.

Horrible class, horrible professor. He doesn't want even to spend the minimum efforts on teaching. All classes are presented by students so he doesn't need to take care of any. Paper reading can be up to 50 pages. Merely provide any guidance or care about class project. At the end give you a horrible grade to show how horrible a class can ever be.

Terrible lecturer.  It was very hard to stay awake.  Very bad at scheduling things, so the lectures fell behind the labs, resulting in labs that were incomprehensible.  On one exam he tested material he had gone over only one lecture ago.  Material that had not been on the homeworks yet.

He is a horrible professor. I'd never recommend him. He made what was supposed to be my favourite class into a nightmare. He just reads from slides, lectures are unhelpful and sometimes the material of the homework is covered for the first time the day it's due. Labs are unclear and completely out of sync with the rest of the class. I hated it!

Dr. Dwyer is one of the best teachers at Duke.  He definitely knows his stuff and has a lot of interesting tidbits of information.  However, he is very challenging, but it is really rewarding when you are done.  I would definitely recommend him if you can get a class with him.
Dr. Dwyer was one of the best professors I had at Duke- his lectures were great. I think the projects were much harder than the exams but doable. Definite "recommend"
Not a good professor, lectures are confusing and exams don't reflect what you learned in class.

For dynamics: Really easy professor, honestly in terms of the dynamics I'll remember in like 3 years I'll remember the same as the harder professors as him. Easy exams, don't learn as much compared to other professors though.
Good
No Comments

This class helps create context for your life after Duke. Extremely valuable. Originally a B-school class. There is a lot of reading and weekly memo writing, but it's challenging without being too difficult. Professor has rich business and public service background, engages students on a one-to-one basis.

Professor Eacho is an incredibly accomplished man. His class is structured similar to a business school class, and I recommend it to anyone who may pursue business. You have to write weekly memos, but it is not too much work. Great inspiration!
This is one of the most valuable classes I have taken at Duke. I strongly recommend this class.
Great professor. I would recommend this class to anyone. He is very interesting guy and his class is super rewarding.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: This is a wonderful, relevant course. Professor Eacho is a caring and engaged professor. He has such an interesting life and professional history and is very generous with his insight, advice, and experiences. The course has weekly work but it is very manageable. There are pop quizzes on the reading, but if you do the work it will be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Amazing class-- would highly recommend to anyone
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Authentic Leadership with Bill Eacho was one of my favorite classes I took at Duke. He teaches very important lessons about leadership and leadership skills that are incredibly valuable for the future. He encourages insightful debate and engagement with Harvard Business School cases. There are pop quizzes and case studies but they are very doable.

Need to show up to class having understood everything you read. Class is basically a guided discussion of just reiterating what we read. The case memo are arbitrarily graded but fun to write. Highly recommend taking this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Really fun class, learned a lot about leadership. Workload is manageable, one page case memo every week or so. Bit of reading but it's usually pretty interesting and engaging.
Professor Eacho is one of the best professors I've had at Duke. The coursework is very informative and beneficial without being difficult. 10/10 would recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Interesting class, new professor. Supportive and fun.

She is incredibly approachable and funny. One of my favorite courses at Duke so far, it has very interesting material. Lots of class discussions that made the class engaging. She's accessible outside of class and has done really interesting research.

She really cares, is funny, and wants you to succeed. It is 4 things 25 each 2 papers 2 tests. Do the readings, go to the review session/office hours and you'll get an A. Also really interesting stuff.
You learn a lot but he is a demanding professor.

Professor Moosa is a hilarious guy with inspiring lectures. His class was slightly disorganized and I often didn't know what was expected, but after a few weeks you get the hang of it. The class has very little work with manageable readings and a few short reflections, but your grade is essentially determined by 1 paper worth 50% of your grade

While the subject material was originally hard to grasp, Professor Moosa constantly asked if we had questions or if he needed to re-explain a topic. I learned a TON; the most I've learned in a course. He is always telling jokes, so class wasn't boring. I would consider taking any class he teaches. He is my FAVORITE prof. I've taken at Notre Dame.

Prof. Moosa brings a lot of energy into the classroom and wants you to learn for the sake of learning. He is dedicated to improving the writing and intellect of each of his students. He does not use a TA and is fair with grading. His lectures are very entertaining as he makes many jokes. Highly recommend!

The professor is very funny and knowledgeable, so 2 1/2 hour classes were pretty interesting. But his talks can get very long sometimes (although I enjoyed it mostly). The TA was just terrible and an incredibly harsh grader... Make sure to check who your TA is before you decide to take Moosa's class
Dr. Moosa is helpful, but his TA is a very hard grader. The class was interesting and I learned a great deal about how religion functions in society.

Great guy, and great discussions in this seminar. He has so much interesting experience and loves talking about his travels outside of class with students. If you show interest and effort, he will justify giving you an A. Learned a lot too.

I am in Prof. Moosa's Islam class. Unless you have prior knowledge on the subject, I don't recommend his class. Even if you have prior knowledge, I still don't highly recommend this class. Moosa is nice, but he is not clear on assignments. Also, his TA is an incredibly harsh grader. This class is more difficult than it should be.

Talked for 2 1/2 hours straight and did not stop his rants. He expects his class to know what he has not taught and his TA is a brutal grader. I do not recommend Moosa if there is a better option. Moosa is a nice guy and knows a lot but is not for everyone.

Moosa is a great professor and his class is full of discussions and entertainment. Posting comments prior classes , on blackboard, is annoying especially when you have paper to submit or an exam. His grade is fair although I expected higher than an A-. The material is really informative and helpful. Attendance is important as he takes attendance.

He is hilarious and interesting, having been an advisor to Mandela. He likes to go out on a limb and talk about random stuff, which is usually fun but sometimes annoying. He expects you to at least skim the reading, which you can usually get away with. Reaction posts online after every reading/class were annoying as all hell, but overall a good cls

Not as easy as other posts say. Tons of reading, and exams are not based on class discussions at all, only small details of the readings. 1 quiz, 1 midterm, and a final paper/presentation. Teacher is very interesting and funny, but TA grades everything and so grading seems somewhat unfair.

Solid class. Pretty easy, do enough of each reading to write a meaningful response every week, then write two 8 page essays and you're done. Good if you're looking for an easier class and you might actually learn a bit about Islam while your at it. (He does take attendance sporadically, so you will want to go to class if you can.)

Pretty entertaining professor. He keeps the lectures from getting too boring and occasionally goes on some pretty funny rants. He's not too hard on the grading, although he's not the easiest teacher ever, either.
Not the most accessible class but incredible insight into the real problems our energy system faces and the challenges we face in addressing them

Dalia is an amazing person; I like how this class covered a lot of subfields in environmental science. A bit too focused on LCAs, I wish I learned more about enviro health. All in all, the professor is very nice, understanding of her students, and has a lot of office hours to ask questions. Would recommend taking!

I found the first weeks of class stressful, because Dr. Echeverri gave out bonus points to people who answered her questions, but everyone raised their hands so it felt like who got points was arbitrary. The first 3 assignments were tough but going to office hours helps a lot, and later ones are easier. The guest speakers are great.

Dr. Patiño-Echeverri should be teaching grad classes, not an introductory course to environmental science. She gives us a decent amount of chances to practice new models and concepts, but moves  quickly in lectures. I enjoyed the guest lecturers more. Grading takes a while, and skills were useful but overall kind of a pain.

Incredibly rude, awful teacher, taught what she wanted to teach and not the science and policy she was actually meant to teach. Grading criteria incredibly unclear, grading is super slow, expects you to understand what she does not convey. Would never take again do not take.
Not that great at teaching. Good at heart but has favourites.

The Professor takes the drive and do the talk for the lecture all the time. Homework is very hard. The Professor doesn't respond to students' emails (I sent her multiple emails asking about the class and homework, and she ignored).  The syllabus is kind of arrogant tone. I highly advise students not to take this class if it's not mandatory for you.

Nice professor, tends to run out of time during lectures. HW assignments are moderate difficulty but often has typos and sometimes takes a few reads to figure out what she's asking for. Annoying that it takes ~2 weeks for HWs to be returned, and (probably the TAs fault), grades not updated timely online either. Probably wouldn't take again. :-/

Many people feel his exams are too hard --- the fact is that he's a fair grader, and once you've really learned all contents in class, exam is not a problem and high grades are accessible. I suggest you take his course if you are (or plan to be) a math major student or you really want to learn, since his lectures are amazing.
dont take him unless u hate urself
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Efstathiou's lectures are well-organized and his writings are very clear. The structure of the course is clear and he delivers the lecture in an elegant and comfortable way. He is also very encouraging and always willing to answer our question. A great professor and a good course!
he was cool
Too many Quizzes!
The lecture and quiz are so difficult!

Professor Tower is a very caring and smart guy and is easily accessible in person/email. However, his lectures were very dry and often repetitive. Class attendance was quite low and a lot the grading criteria was quite unclear.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Extremely nice and caring! Always willing to spend a huge amount of extra time out of class to help you, and is very reponsive in emails and questions. The course materials turned out to be very useful not only for research but also for some industry jobs that involve policy analysis and policy design. Overall great learning experience!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Group projects

reviews.comment: Amazing professor, incredibly kind and approachable

Somewhat arbitrary approach to teaching and class in general, but charming old guy. Extremely responsive on email, but can be clumsy with technology. Grades are given back late, and you often don't know what to expect on the midterm/final. Can go on while teaching, and doesn't really know your name at times. Potential easy A for how unclear it is
Very Good Professor!!!
Amazing professor...easy class but extremely interesting..
Prof tower is awesome!  very helpful - great class! he has taught in dozens of foreign countries and consulted for the UN and world bank
Professor Tower is awesome.  He is great to work with on a one-on-one basis.  I didn't have him for a class but he helped me tremendously with a research paper.
No Comments
Cannot teach.

You will spend more time in CS308 than any of your other classes combined, but you will also learn more than all the others combined. If you are thinking about taking this class, be warned! This course load is tough with a good team and unbearable with a bad team. Take this class with people you know. Duvall is tough but fair.

This class destroyed my eating and sleep schedule and took so much time but I learned SO much. Probably don't want to experience the stress again but taking it was a good decision. That being said though your experience does greatly depend on your teammates, I was lucky and got good ones but I know people who struggled with horrible ones.

Duvall's CS308 is challenging but rewarding. The workload can be heavy, but you'll learn a lot if you put in the effort. Unstuckstudy was a big help for exam prep. Overall, a tough but worthwhile class if you have a passion for software development.

Duvall gets annoyed when you do not apply his concepts in class, yet the amount of knowledge you will get from this class is beyond comprehension. It made me a much better programmer, and I urge anyone who wants to truly get better at coding rather than breezing pass a CS degree with GPT to take this class. Lots of work but the ROI is amazing.

Unreasonable workload. HOWEVER, I have learned so much from this class, and I would take it again. Duvall seems a bit arrogant and pretentious at times too. But, apparently the class is being re-done and made significantly more reasonable, and if that is the case I would take it.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I learned a good bit in this course, but almost all of what I learned was from the projects where I taught myself how to do them. In theory, the class is a great concept, but Professor Duvall did not provide feedback on any projects or presentations, nor did he provide grades (aside from the final grade). He also did not really teach much.
Never received a grade until the end of the course. No assessments or graded projects so was left in the dark about grading the entire time.
No feedback, unclear grading criteria. Communication skills very subpar. Good programmer but very bad instructor

Duvall is tough but really knows his stuff. You'll learn a lot from the class if you have the right attitude. Not sure why people are complaining that he is condescending/doesn't respect his students. He does seem to have a low tolerance for incompetence but if you put in the effort you won't feel disrespected

Can't say more how much I've learned in this course. I look back at my code I wrote before taking this course and looks so bad. I had a pretty solid Java background, but still learned a lot. You can also learn from great team mates, and professor is passionate about what he teaches. But don't take if you're not as passionate about software dev.

I don't think this class could make significant improvement to a student's coding ability IF you are not somewhat already good at Java and familiar with polymorphism or OOP and such. That said, if you are already a good coder who has done super well in 201, you probably still need a bit of other knowledge to do well in this class.
I thought he was rather disorganized and didn't tell us about assignments that were on class websites.
Grades were arbitrary and only given for a very few number of assignments. You are better served learning this material from an internship or work than in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Class is VERY project-based (one a week), and there is a learning curve for new programmers. But, Professor Duvall answered specific questions on class forum in very timely fashion, always had extra office hours available, and would stay an hour after class to help each student that needed it. I had no prior experience. Now, CS 201 bound.

I had to sign up for CAPs after this class. No feedback/grading until you receive a surprise final grade. Senior Lecturer Duvall is condescending and single-handedly snuffs out the hopes of the ECE/CS. Impossible workload. This is a course where you can give it your full 20 hr+ a week best effort and end with a surprise B. Do not take.

The class promises a lot, most of which are useful skills to have in preparation for entering the industry. Unfortunately, the course is ironically designed poorly for learning. The lectures are pointless , and there is no feedback until the end making it impossible to gauge how you are doing with improving as a developer.

Started well, but it became clear he struggles to connect with students. Though he tried to be accessible to us, his lectures were long and pointless, the work was tedious or difficult, and prior computer science experience became almost essential. I did not enjoy attending this class and will likely not take another CS course because of it.

308 is by far the most useful CS class I've ever taken. Professor Duvall knows a lot about project design and in-class examples + labs make the topics clear. The projects and readings are a lot of work, but he does not expect you to implement every feature in the guidelines. I would recommend taking this course with three other easy courses.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Duvall and his class(es) are super tough, and the comments are correct in the expectation of spending 30+ hours per week outside of class on his work. He may come off as condescending in lectures but if you meet with him one on one or ask for help at any point, he is so there for you. He really cares about his students, and you can learn so much!!
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Beyond what others have said: The lectures lack structure and his exceptions can often be unclear. You won't have a clue what your grade is until after the end of semester. I know multiple people who dropped either ECE or CS in order to avoid this class along with CS 330. With that said, the class does give you things to talk about in interviews.

Okay, if you want to know about software, take this course. But keep in mind that this course will take at least 30+hrs of commitment every week, just as an internship would. With that said, students are often overwhelmed by the amount of work and claim that they haven't "learned" anything. However, if you put in the time, you will learn A LOT!

CS290 started strong with an incredible compilation of resources and examples for web dev. Duvall unfortunately is as poor an instructor as others note. Zero grading and zero grading criteria before the end of the semester. Ive never had a professor so disrespectful of his students  he is violent with our time and assumes the worst intentions.

He is certainly knowledgeable about coding, but is poor at running a class. We received no grades besides one midterm grade on DukeHub and then our final grade. There is no grading structure. Also, a lot of writing assignments with no feedback. Only learned due to personal research. A lot of effort and time, the projects are insane.

290 was better than 307 because it didn't have all the unnecessary documentation and busywork, but projects were still very time-consuming. Condescending, but it's never personal and you should just take it with a grain of salt. A LOT of work, but you will learn more coding skills in a Duvall class than almost all other CS classes at Duke.

This class was a lot of work. I don't think students are expected to actually complete the projects. Although Duvall may not have industry experience, he knows a lot about programming/Java and taught me a ton about good coding practices. Absolutely the most useful class I have taken so far at Duke, would recommend for people interested in software

Prof. Duvall is incredibly condescending in his demeanor, and his lectures are completely ineffective. Several amounted to nothing more than a "chewing out" of teams that had failed to pay tithe to the self-appointed "God of Agile" whom, afaik, has never worked a day in the industry in his life. Project feedback is infrequent and of poor quality.

Please dont take this class! The entire setup of the course makes it impossible to learn what he is trying to teach. Why setup a class on software design to have projects each with an impossible amount of features to implement? The amount of work required is absurd and made an isolated college experience in the midst of a pandemic even worse.������

Never got any grades throughout the entire semester. Very rude and condescending ending towards students. Lectures were not very helpful. Most of the learning for CS290 was done through analyzing his example code, Piazza or office hours. TAs were not great either. If you're interested in web development, maybe just teach yourself.

provides zero feedback or grades on projects so i have no idea what my grade is! made a group final project (40% of grade) into a solo project so way more work now. couldve done less work AND learned more thru coursera. STAY AWAY! dont think ur a smartass reading these comments and thinking ur special, cuz thats what i did and i really regret it.

Absolutely the worst. Absurd amount of work (30-40 hours a week) for an elective. He won't take work later than 1 day, but has only given grades for 1/8 projects (class ends in a week). Condescending and full of himself. Incredibly unclear grading criteria. Some code examples in class didn't even work and the TA had to fix them days later.
I saw the poor reviews below before taking this course, but thought it couldn't possibly be that bad and signed up anyway. Don't make the same mistake I did. He is that bad
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The course material is interesting, but the majority of the lectures are not helpful. There has also been a big issue with grading. We have had 5 projects for the course and he has only graded the first project, which we submitted the first week of February. So we have no idea whether or not we are doing things correctly or what our grades are.
Do not take a class with this professor. He is inconsiderate, condescending, and not a good instructor.
Awful. Spent about 80 hours on a three-week project, then had to write an analysis about it that was longer than most papers for a humanities class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: Terrible. Expect to work > 20 hours/week for this class and learn very little.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: By far the worst teacher I've had at Duke. He is extremely rude to students, literally made me despise programming even though I loved it before taking this class. He only criticizes people, and not in a helpful way. I swear he is only a professor so he can look down on students and pretend he knows what he's talking about. Honestly should be fired

Good: Answers Piazza OH are OK Material is helpful in industry Bad: Knows we have other work - continues to assign x4 amount of average 3XX STEM class We waste a lot of time on reflection instead of planning/design Material learned through rote Grading scheme v. unclear & unfair Nitpicky, arbitrary V. sassy Does not read/appreciate our work
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Group projects--So many papers

reviews.comment: he assigned a final presentation and final paper during reading period and finals week on top of the final project we spent 100 hours on in already hellish online semester. he genuinely has no idea that students have other final exams and final papers. i cannot fathom how he is still able to teach

Duvall is a terrible professor. I don't know how he's teaching the course when he has literally no software engineering experience. He doesn't even have a PhD. Expects a ton of work every week (upwards of 30-40 hours a week). It's like an internship in terms of commitment, but you don't get paid. Do yourself a favor and avoid him at all costs

We have a shortened semester. Instead of doing what a "normal" professor would do in a class like 307 (e.g. better grading criteria, one less project or cut back on unnecessary crap), he goes the opposite direction. The expectations are the same, the project requirements are the same, we have more pointless assignments, but you just have less time.

Duvall doesn't provide feedback throughout the course until he wants to berate the teams for an hour straight. And it's not constructive criticism, just criticism. I learned nothing, except that if my burndown charts look like a cliff instead of a straight downward line then I've failed the agile community.

Senior lecturer Mr. Duvall would roast terrible code instead of displaying good code in the weekly quizzes. You are expected to do pretty much everything in a full-time internship, but constantly chastised. Expect upwards of 10 hours a week doing pointless tasks and 30 hours a week doing the project. -400/5 Worst instructor I've had in my life.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Take a class with Duvall only if you are looking to get the life force sucked out of you. One of the worst professors I've had in my 4yrs of undergrad. Do not expect to learn much if anything. His lecture are boring, he keeps on droning, doesn't respect students. On the positive side, he makes sure you are up to deadlines and follows up personally.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: You're better off doing an actual internship. He brings in cool lecturers, but Duvall himself has never worked in industry, so there's no justification for how he acts like he's the god of agile development. Also, he tries to encourage participation and then belittles people that ask questions, sometimes not even answering the question.

I had to allocate time from my other 3 classes so I could finish everything. I felt there like there were an endless amount of pointless "boilerplate" functionality and useless assignments that we had to implement that could've taught us everything required for less. The class literally isn't even that difficult, it just conpletely drains your soul
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Group projects

reviews.comment: I entered to tag above sarcastically. Definitely the least caring professor ever. The class material is ok but literally any other professor would have done a better job than him. If you take this class just make sure you're mentally prepared for a bad experience. Wish there were better options for this important topic at Duke.

I've gone through internships at two FANG companies before taking this class. So I know what a heavy workload at a tech company could look like. However, he fails to consider that we may have three other classes that have work as well. He acts as if we're all just taking his one class in university and treats this class as our full-time job.

I learned a lot from 308. However, many of the enforced sufferings were unnecessary. The combination of his mindful learning (tons of text) and software development (tons of code) entertains me as a concept yet imposes pain in reality. It seems to me that prof. Duvall made genuine efforts to be nice to students while still aggressively assertive.

Extremely terrible. Not supportive. Acts like everyone who dares to ask questions are idiots, but then expect everything from us. Some of my teammates described him as "mean", and others say he's more like a "boss" than a professor. Well, we don't get paid for this class but expect more work than you'll get in even the most work-heavy internship
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This guy is the reason I opened a RateMyProfessors account. An absolutely horrible professor that sucks all the fun out of coding and is rude towards his students. The biggest issue is that he does not realize people have other work to do and creates countless pointless assignments. Do NOT take this course!

On paper, CS 308 sounds like a dream course: industry experience! AGILE! Java! In reality this class will suck your life force. Duvall doesn't understand that students don't have unlimited time. Prepare to spend upwards of 40 hours per week writing "beautiful" code, with no idea of how it's actually going to be graded. Only take if you're ECE/CS.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: All the skills you learn are mainly self-taught, could be learned in a couple of YouTube tutorials, and gained because of the immense pressure we are thrown under. There are no mental health breaks at all as you move from project to project, and despite what he says about bad groups, you have to make up for it on your own. This class was horrible.

A lot of these ratings are bad because people dont like being tested on their soft skills, but the design classes that Duvall expertly teachers are focused on developing the skills that you cant learn in other CS classes. Listen to Duvall. As tough as he seems, he gives the tools you need to succeed in his projects. Excellent projects!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Group projects

reviews.comment: I took 308 with Dr. Duvall and he was very helpful during office hours. If you're having trouble with the class, please don't hesitate to ask him. He really cares about how you are doing and is willing to help you succeed.

The only grade you ever receive is your final grade. Also, the rubric on the website is purposely confusing so you dont know what exactly hes looking for. Due dates are unclear, and the lectures give no new insights. If you want to learn whats taught in this class, it would be more rewarding to just search it online or do an internship.

Prepare yourself to work with self-proclaimed coding prodigies who throw in as many buzzwords as possible to emulate the software master, Robert Duvall. If the kids who take this class weren't insufferable enough, Robert is a playground bully who talks down to anyone who dares ask him such pedestrian questions. This class makes ECE/CS not worth it

Be prepared to sacrifice every other part of your life for this class at certain points of the semester. High workload, but if you're interested in software the assignments will be fun and you'll learn a lot just by looking things up and researching problems you run into while coding (arguably more than you learn in lecture), but grading is vague.

Funny how everyone complains that Duvall isn't good at lecturing/doesn't teach the right stuff when 85% of y'all are on Facebook the entire time in class. 290 and 308 mirror real-life software engineering -- if you think a real SWE job will be holding your hand through lectures instead of learning by doing and research, I have bad news for you.

Extremely unorganized professor. Expect him to release assignments late and then claim he released it days before and reject any of the students' attempts to ask for an extension. Also expect massively unclear grading criterions. Finally, he discourages people to contribute to class discussions by putting people down sarcastically for that.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Easy class if you already know some webdev and need to boost gpa + can pick up a new framework. Duvall is awful tho. Every single lecture/lab is from the documentation of that weeks language/framework as if hes learning them for the first time too (he might be). Never explains any theory, just the basics of implementation (off the tutorials).

Duvall is a terrible lecturer (very boring, lecture topics rarely relate to class work), and his systems of TA feedback are pretty poor. However, I did really enjoy how detailed and well-thought-out his assignments were, and he was very accessible and helpful in office hours. If you don't expect a typical lecturing professor, you might enjoy him.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Feedback was utterly nonexistent. Of the maybe 20 assignments/labs in the course, we got feedback on no more than 4, and he would actively ignore requests for feedback on Piazza. Then, final grades were a full week late. He seems like a nice enough guy, but his organization is inexcusable.
Lectures are useless and not worth attending. Having TA meetings are key to passing this class. The assignments take forever but I learned a lot from just doing them.

Prof. Duvall is of the "learn through the struggle" school of computer science teaching. However, he is aware of this, and tries to help you with that struggle. Not an easy professor, but you will learn practical skills from him if you work for it. Labs are not graded for correctness so you can play around with the technologies to learn them well.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: If I could, I would give him a 0/5. Horrible class. You're expected to learn everything by your own in your own time. If you really want to learn web dev, you might as well learn by yourself because Duvall sure won't teach you. Oh, and half of the TAs also don't know how to do most of the projects. One week per project + unclear grading criteria.
Very Hard Class. TONS OF WORK. :(

Duvall clearly knows the course material and has lots of good insights into software design, but his lectures are really dry and he tends to ramble some. The projects are a lot of work, but are good projects to teach basic design. Considering this is the one of the few programming classes in the department, it should be a requirement for the degree
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Software design and maintainability is extremely important- however Duvall does a terrible job teaching more advanced design concepts, although the readings are pretty good. The amount that you learn is not worth the effort you put in- most people who say this is a good class are bad at coding. Don't take this class.

Software design is important, but Duvall teaches nothing about it in lecture. The projects are a ton of work, but they are just boring and tedious. Don't take this class for the "practical experience". No employer will care about your JavaFX applications. If you are signed up for 308, drop it and take a more important class like 310 or 330.

Duvall is smart and you will learn an amazing amount. It is a time commitment and it's hard to get feedback, but what do you expect when you're trying to learn software?  Also, everyone complaining about this class ended up with a A- or A. so quit complaining.

CS308 is a highly valuable class for any future software developer, and Duvall deserves credit for the projects he assigns.  Completing the coursework of 308 makes you feel ready to take on the world.  Other than that, Duvall is an awful professor.  No feedback, lectures aren't helpful, and he just doesn't seem to care.
smart as eggs. you'll learn a lot.

He's controversial, but Duvall is a great/passionate professor, albeit disorganized. 308 is a lot of work, and you're thrown into the deep end to implement your projects. However, it was one of my most satisfying classes to take, and I'm so proud of the work I did in that class. Learned a lot about programming and developing software. Worth it IMO.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Amazing
A lot of work that pays off later when interviewing for full time or internships

CS308 was terrible. Literally got 0 feedback on anything until I got my final grade. TAs are god-awful and don't seem interested or capable in helping out. Duvall is disorganized and his lectures are long (and basically straight from papers and websites). Going to class is pointless except recitation (which isn't useful either).
Not a good teacher. The projects are a lot of work. Grading for the projects is kind of arbitrary.

Duvall is very sarcastic and very disorganized. In CS 308 I went the entire semester with no feedback on my work whatsoever. For 308 you get 1 individual project and 3 group projects. Most groups pulled all-nighters the night(s) before the project was due even after working on it all week long.

CS308 with Duvall is honestly a kind of bad class. He is very disorganized and he teaches you very little in lecture. Honestly, you could never go to lecture and nothing would change. This is complemented by the fact that the course is an IMMENSE amount of work. Be prepared to spend 8+ hours a week.
Duvall is a pretty funny, personable guy. He knows a lot and is always willing to help if you ask for it. Was pretty unorganized though.
He is disorganized, but 101 is basically teaching yourself. The practice problems were useful for preparing you for tests. He's a good teacher to talk to outside of class.

Duvall is a friendly guy, but like others have said, he is very disorganized. Grading took forever. I'd never written code before this class, and the lectures weren't much help, but if you do all of the practice problems every week and use the internet (after all, this is computer science), you'll learn all you need and the class will be simple.
He's a good professor, tests are difficult but he's friendly and provides plenty of time to get help.  Passionate about the subject too, you can get the grade you want if you put in effort.

I found this class somewhat easy; I learned that if you pay attention in the first month or so, you can learn enough CS to get by for the entire semester. However, the entire course is VERY disorganized, and I did not find out my grades until the very very end.

This class was extremely frustrating at times because Professor Duvall is not prompt on returning grades for projects. At the end of the semester, I still did not know my project grades. However, I think he is a fair grader and he really wants his students to learn. True passion of compsci.
Good guy, but this class was a disaster. Little to know help was available for those who weren't excelling from the getgo. Also not taught in the format of an intro-level course.

Professor Duvall is a smart and kind person, just not a good teacher. His class would not be that difficult if he could be more helpful during class. If you spend time studying by yourself after class, you would get an A.

Professor Duvall took a class that in the past has been very manageable and interesting and turned it into a class that is impossible for students to follow and had expectations that were absurd. He made exams way too difficult and didn't teach anything in the lectures. The TAs had almost as little idea of what was going on as Duvall did. 0/10.
Lot of hate on here. I had a good time in this class. Although lectures didn't have a whole lot of content, I really appreciated the fact that he tried to make the material applicable

This class. There are days where even the TAs in lab don't know what were learning. I had to use past instructions from former teachers to understand what to do in projects. Midterms were even more unclear and 10x harder than midterms from the past. The stress from that class was very unnecessary, I had to set up a meeting with CAPS for my sanity.

I am an undecided freshman, and I was considering majoring in compsci. However, this man has drained all the passion I had for the subject from me. Too many times have I been huddled in a room with a group of friends as we try to learn the basic concepts behind the subject all by ourselves. We basically didn't have a teacher, and he is not funny

Nothing more to say than terrible. There is NO help with this class no matter where you go. If you have no experience with coding, don't take this class. I felt like all of the kids were gamers in there.. it should not have been an intro class. He does nothing to teach material.. just shows you more "efficient" ways of doing it.

Professor Duvall should not be teaching a 100 level class. He is disorganized, unclear, and has expectations which are ridiculous for those who had never coded before.  The first midterm was much more difficult and longer than his practice tests led us to believe.  I took this class wanting to try something new. I'm wishing I hadn't.

He is very disorganized. He tries to fit way too much into the lab periods, which leaves the students with extra work. His classes don't teach you necessary skills for the problem sets/tests. The tests from previous years we did in labs were way easier than his test, and therefore did not prepare you at all. Because of him, I am not majoring in CS.
This was the most frustrating class of my life. Duval is not helpful at all and he seems to have no idea that this is a beginners level course.

The class in general was disorganized and understaffed. Grading was slow, lectures failed to cover key concepts on practice problems from week to week leaving students struggling unnecessarily,  and there was no timed practice before the midterm. This class made me reconsider studying CS in the future.

His lectures aren't particularly useful and you get no feedback, so you will be expected to learn on your own. However, he sets up CPS 108 so that if you are willing to put in the work, you will learn a lot of very practical software design practices. He also seems to really care about the students and is more than willing to help after class.

Duvall is a really smart guy -- he demands a lot from his students and in turn you find yourself able to figure out things you never thought you could. If you want to improve your coding and software design:: take it!

Duvall is quite possibly the slowest grader known to man. As I recall, we did not receive feedback on our FIRST midterm until after the second midterm, at which point the course withdrawal deadline had passed. Isn't really a huge issue if you're self-driven and confident in your abilities, but for someone who values feedback, it's a pain.

There is very little guidance in anything, Duvall does not teach much during class. You have to learn a lot on your own, and some things are very tricky. Grading was slow. Nevertheless, Duvall is extremely smart and he tries to be funny.

An intro course for people who are interested in CompSci. If you are just looking for a QS or have no background, I would take 4 or 72 instead. I found him to be helpful, as he often explained the pros and cons of different approaches to a problem. He was unacceptably slow with grading (and tests were sometimes too long), but was otherwise not bad.

If you are taking his class for the focus program and have never programmed before, frop out immediately. He skips some of the basic stuff and as soon as you get into some more complicated projects you will be lost. His tests are impossible and he is very hard to get help form in class when you don't understand what's going on.

he's ok. he makes it way harder than it needs to be (i.e. he needs to give way more guidance for programs, like at least poitn us to useful methods). tests are very hard, although the final i found to be easy. brings candy though =)
His tests are extremely difficult. He's funny in class, always very excited about the material. Huge load of work, but it's not busy work. Enjoyable class.
He is not very helpful and you will learn most of software design principles from your reading or project. The course load for this class is huge. Prepare to spend whole semester doing his projects
he is nice if you know how to program. if you have never programmed (which you shouldn't have because this is the basic class), he is NOT helpful and is extremely condescending.

Great professor, IMO one of the best professors at Duke in the CS dept along with Coach A!! Great lectures, very interesting - will keep you interested throughout the class but you must atleast have a small desire to learn something. Projects were fun, and he let us form our own groups on the last one. Grading wasn't harsh either, very fair.

PRO: Good lectures, knows the material well, always willing to help if you ask him questions.  CON: Terrible organizational skills.  For example, we might know about a project for a week, but not get details for what we have to do until a day or two before it's due.

Excellent professor. Very funny guy, and pretty nice too. Can be a little blunt when appraising your programs, however (although he generally goes easy on the grading). Beware though, CPS 108 is a hell of a course... substantial projects with a lot of work. But overall it was really rewarding, and Duvall was a great guy to take it with.
Thought we had to learn Java way too fast - but other than that, he was awesome.  Nice guy too.

Most important: I went to every class but 1 and never saw him not wearing a festive Hawaian shirt. If you ask a stupid question, he can be pretty harsh. Buys lots of food for class. Extremely disorganized leading to frustration when code he gives you constantly changes. Very nice away from classroom.
Great Professor.  Always nice and willing to help.  Turn your stuff in on time though, late work is penalized pretty harshly.

Was sometimes a jerk and could be very harsh on students in class setting, but overall definitely above average.  Very available outside of class for questions and enjoys a good conversation.  I liked him for 124, he got really into the material and made the class a lot of fun.

Duvall's class was challenging and a period of real growth for all his students.  His classes were very engaging and interactive, and he was eager to help at any time, during or outside of class.  A very nice guy to just chat with, too, but kind of pushy.

Went through material a bit too fast, and is very delayed in grading.  Tried hard to get students to understand difficult concepts (classes and recursion, e.g.).  If you can do weekly problems and classwork, you'll be in good shape for tests.
such jerk - hated him.  Go back to Brown!!
Such a great and enjoyable professor!  He challenges you, but makes you a better computer scientist and person for it.  Such a joy!!!!
Great guy. Very reasonable. Some people love him others hate him. Just do what he says and you'll be golden. He truly does care about the students. Very entertaining in class.
Avoid at all costs. He will give you a zero if you solve problems the smart way. He does not care about right answers, only wants you to do problems the dumbest, slowest way possible.

Shaughnessy is the man when it comes to Fluid Mechanics (the book is his). He is the most caring prof. I've had at Duke who teaches with passion and wants everyone to understand the material. While he is extremely entertaining and the class is great with him, it is a huge time commitment- 5 3hr exams, over 200 hw probs, and 15 short films to watch.

He was very clear with the course expectations.  Super knowledgeable and some of the most helpful feedback on my writing I've gotten as an undergraduate.  This class wasn't easy, I took it as a freshman but I felt I grew a ton.

My favorite professor at Duke so far. Very passionate about the subject and a great lecturer. There is a lot of outside reading but it's not entirely necessary to do it for every class Midterms were pretty easy overall (gives you the essay questions). The research paper takes a ton of time but isn't too hard. Overall great teach. TAKE HIS CLASS!

Probably one of the best professors at Duke.  Balleisen is an amazing teacher, puts a ton of effort into his class and really cares about his students.  There is no doubt that this class is a ton of reading and work but don't shy away - it's worth it and if you put in the effort you won't get a bad grade (average was like a high B+)
Balleisen ins THE MAN.  You don't necessarily have to do all the reading, just cover the main ideas for each class.  He puts a ton of effort into this class and it shows, and he's a baller
Good professor...very intersting class...lectures are not at all boring..makes you think as you listen
Balleisen is one of the best professors I've had at Duke so far. His lectures are intellectually stimulating and he knows his stuff. Fair grader and very helpful. LOVE him

I thought the class was hard when I was in it because I didn't know how to work the system. Just read enough so you can make one good comment in class; wikipedia the rest for the tests. If you meet with him about your paper you're golden. Go to class and say a few things and you'll get an A; partitication is 20% - really boosts your grade.

This professor conducts a difficult class that requires a lot of work. Don't take it if you want to coast.  However, if you want your money's worth... if you want a teacher who will challenge you- if you aren't afraid of doing some work, he is the best.

Balleisen gave a TON of work but he made that clear in the beginning. He was a great professor. His lectures were outlined well. I was on the verge of getting an I for the class because of my term paper but I didn't...I sat down with him and he proofread the entire 10 page thing with me.
Ridiculous expectations. Not warm - doesn't make you want to work for him.
This guy is miserable.  He met with everyone to discuss their term papers and when I walked into his office he just sat and stared at me.  Very unhelpful, very bad lecturer.
He's ok.

Dr. Pinuelas is a pretty cool guy. The class itself is pretty easy, with basically no participation necessary at the beginning of the semester, but by the end, things really get crazy. Overall, pretty standard professor.

Such a bro. Would definitely chill with him outside of class. Not only that, but he is clear what he expects in his assignments, so it is your own fault if you don't do well. The reading can be extensive some nights, but it helps you with your essays and weekly responses so I would strongly recommend you complete them.

Prof. Pinuelas is great! The course load is really light towards the beginning of the semester, but it can get pretty hectic towards the end. He's a chill guy and an easy grader. He will always meet with you to discuss your papers before turning them in.  He gives you great advice and specifically tells you what to fix.

Class on the slave narrative wasn't particularly interesting but course load was very light and he's an easy grader.  Makes a lot of quirky jokes in class and is overall  a good guy and a nice grader. Great writing 101 class to fulfill the requirement as class was considerably easier than most.

Didn't think I would really enjoy class going into the course but I ended up learning a lot. Professor gave good lectures, was not a harsh grader, was very relaxed and approachable, very lenient with problems regarding papers. However course was held at 8:30 and I would only take if you are interested in race and feminist issues.

Slave Narrative: Professor Pinuelas really knows his stuff. The class can be a little dry and often feels too discussion based (as students come in with little to no experience on the topic). Sometimes the class feels "led" rather than taught. Overall a nice little class to fill your requirements with a pretty light workload.

Rhetoric of Slave Narrative:Although the classes were sometimes boring, I thought that he was a lenient grader on essays. Some of my drafts would be done the night before and done poorly but somehow I still ended up with a good grade. He is really nice about excusing absences and he is pretty quirky in class. He does help improve your writing style
Best prof at Duke hands down

the actual goat, so interesting and nice - always has athletes in his classes which is cool and great speakers come to class regularly and share experiences and insights - highly recommmend any class he teaches, must take a class with him before graduating
best professor at duke, clearly cares about his students a ton and makes classes very interesting with awesome speakers

Ed T is the goat. He cares about his students so much and has become like a father figure to me. He makes sure his students succeed and don't ever have to stress about his classes while still learning. (And if it's any indication, most of the bball team is in his classes every semester).

If you need an easy A this is your class.  Good guest speakers, some pizzas.  You need a course like this to balance out the hard ones at Duke, although this one costs the same as the real classes :(  Try to make friends with a basketball player, they seem to get the answers to quizzes before the quizzes are taken.  LOL
super easy. Automatic A.  I didn't do any of the reading but still got the A.  Nice guy, but not very challenging.

Ed T cares about his students, is always available outside of class time, and wants to see everyone succeed. MMS 370 was an excellent primer for students wanting to work in the business world. Ed T was a wealth of experience, and really knows his stuff. He brings in amazing guest speakers who are leaders in the industry.

very knowledgably and made a very tough class fun and interesting
great working in teams and great guest speakers

The most useful class I've taken at Duke by far. We talk about current events in the economy and do group presentations on publicly traded companies. Ed T is extremely knowledgeable about the stock market. His lectures are interesting and funny, and he's a lenient grader. The topics we covered really helped me with investing and personal finance.

Ed T is the man. He just wants to see his students succeed and is incredibly supportive and nice. The class has a midterm, some group projects, and a final essay tailored to your choosing. Not much work, incredibly useful as a primer to finance. You get out what you put in. Highly recommend.

Ed T. is the absolute MAN. I took him for managerial finance and business of sport. The guy knows his stuff, and has such a great background and set of experiences to share. Gets his class pizza, gifts, etc. He really loves his students, and it shows. Usually just one midterm a final project and a few in-class competitions for grade - not hard

Dr. T is an amazing professor and human being.  I have taken several of his classes, and would take him again and again.  He LOVES his students, and encourages you to go and see for yourself those people/places around the world that intrigue or inspire you.    Participate and learn!  Grandfatherly yet refreshingly witty, he is a gem.
Hands down the best professor at Duke. He is so sweet and nice. I didn't do any reading and got A+. Absolutely loved his class.

Professor Timke was definitely my favorite professor this semester! He is so kind and made online class as fun as possible. The assignments were creative and interesting, and he really cares about his students.

Fantastic, caring guy with genuine interest in his work and in teaching. The kind of professor you want to FLUNCH (post-pandemic, of course). Class is usually on East Campus which kinda sucks since he takes attendance each class and you can get in trouble if you have someone else write your name. Otherwise super easy work and worth the bus ride lol
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Such a genuine and nice professor. very inspiring how passionate and interested he is. he really wants the best for his students. one of the nicest professors at Duke.

I loved being in Timke's class! I took "Advertising & Society: Global" with him during my freshman year. He's probably the nicest professor I've had during my entire college experience, and he's very accessible outside of class. His lectures are interesting and the workload is very reasonable. Absolutely take his classes if you have a chance!
Class had clear grading criteria but lecture was generally not very engaging/hard to follow.
I really enjoyed taking this class! The content was very interesting and very applicable. All of the readings were short and easy to digest, and the quizzes were open-book.

I'd say he's a nice person but not a great lecturer. This class was the most confusing class I've taken in global health because he said that the textbook is wrong BUT he kept assigned chapters for reading. Also, he made the final exam in-class when all the other quizzes and exams were take-home (they were all closed notes).
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof Egger is a nice professor and cares about his students doing well. His class is not a lot of work, however I found his lectures to be dry and the tests/quizzes were difficult even though I was paying attention and taking notes every class. That being said, he does curve fairly.

All the materials needed to pass the exams are included in the lectures and he makes it easy to stay focused with his weird little quips.  Fabulous orator and someone I could learn from over a beer just as easily as during his courses.  Excited to see what comes next with Mr Egger.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Articulate, with well-timed jokes that keep you engaged throughout his lectures.  He asks check-in questions periodically.  If there's one critique I can make is that he's not a great dancer.

Dan is the worst professor I have ever met. He think so high of himself that he refuses to teach anyone anything, but of course, wouldn't mind the paycheck. He bully students and possess poor management over lectures and TAs. Please avoid his course at every cost!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Worst professor ever. He does not how to teach, and somehow become a professor, and this is the greatest SHAME that I have ever seen in this world!

Dan Egger is probably the worst professor I have ever had in my life. Not a single thing was positive in his class: He does not know how to teach, the grading criteria was not clear, the resources for the class were terrible, all the assignments were in excel (the class was in a data science program). Good riddance.

His lectures are kinda boring, but I love listening to his British accent. Straightforward exams, he tells you exactly what slides you need to study so it's pretty low-stress. You have to do 1 presentation during discussion, but the TAs are super nice about grading. Overall, it's an easy, chill class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Boring class. Exams are easy but a little catfishy. Almost no room for error on exams as they are worth 69% of your grade and each question is worth like 4 points. So it's easy but you have to pay attention to every single little detail. Don't be overconfident and you will be fine.

Tests aren't too bad as long as you study a substantial amt (key words = crucial), and tests fully represents what he tells you study. Lectures can be boring, just study well for the tests (especially the second one, it can easily screw over ur grade). Super nice and charming guy, doing his absolute best for sure. Chill TAs.

Though the class feels a little introductory and lectures can be boring at times, Tobias is a fantastic professor who makes the best lecture he can out of it. I get the feeling he is very influential within his field and research-driven, so I think a higher-level class with him would be perfect. Chill course, and take it the semester he teaches.

The class is lecture heavy, and sometimes they were a bit boring, but overall, it was an easy class and Professor Egner does his best at the end of the semester to give everyone the best grade possible.
Solid professor. Clear lectures, fair exams, and kind discussion TAs that aren't looking to sabotage your grade. If he's teaching 212, take it and don't think twice.

This class is very much a show up, listen in lecture and study for the test (which he is very clear about what you need to know) kind of class. Theres not much else to it. Very low stress and straightforward. Covers interesting and relevant topics. Dr. Engner is sweet and a solid prof. Highly recommend!

This dude is a beast. Definitely take 212 with him. His lectures are very straightforward and clear. Expectations for the exam are set out as he gives a study guide with respective slide numbers to study. Questions on the exam are basically straight from the slides, so study the slides well. Super nice and caring guy. Wish all profs were like him.

Prof Egner's intro to cognitive neuro class is interesting, sure, but the best thing about it in my opinion was how straightforward it was. Grade is based off of three exams, for which he tells you exactly what parts of lecture to study, one presentation and attendance. You def have to study for the exams, but they aren't hard by any means.

Fairly low workload class. Two presentations and 2 papers. He is quite a caring guy and pretty chill grader. I found the TA to be the more annoying grader but isn't that the case with most classes lol. Just participate and ask for feedback on papers and presentations, and you should be just fine!

Professor Egner is awesome! He really cares about his students. The grading for this class is a little bit unclear as there are two presentations and two papers. But otherwise, it's a very interesting class that just requires you to show up and listen to your classmates present. Would recommend for a pretty easy writing class!

Egner's a great guy; he's not teaching 212 anymore but in case he does in the future, take it with him. Lectures were a bit dry but the material made sense and the exams were very fair and lecture-based. Read lecture slides, no textbook required. Discussion was annoying but only 2 group presentations per semester that were generously graded.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Caring

reviews.comment: You can tell he is passionate about cognitive neuroscience. The lectures can be more engaging, but the material was interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: His exams were lecture heavy. Pay attention in lecture and read the slides after class.

I took the psychology thesis GwD class with Dr. Egner, and it was incredibly helpful for keeping me on track with my thesis. The main assignments for this class included things that you were already doing for your thesis. He gave a lot of helpful feedback on the sections of my honors thesis paper that he looked over.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Class was unbelievably easy if you can memorize things well. He tells you what to memorize so its fine. Lecture was mandatory this year which was really annoying since lecture is pointless, but you can do other work in class so its not that bad. Overall an easy A.

The class is definitely memorization-based and specific, but all the information needed to succeed on the test is on the slides (I never used the book). Going to class isn't essential, but I found Professor Egner's explanations of some experiments to be beneficial. He also has a good sense of humor and is very knowledgeable about the field.

Good class, Dr. Egner is a good lecturer. The class isn't too difficult, my only complaint would be the tests can be very specific. The questions come directly from the slides, but it's a lot of information to memorize, so start studying early!

Prof. Egner is a very clear lecturer. 6 short essay responses worth 25% which are not too hard to do well on (96) if you follow the prompts closely. 3 mid-terms (75%), non-cumulative, which can get very specific, but Egner does provide study guides to simplify you're study. Get really good at memorizing 7-9 lectures every test.

Boring and kind of annoying. Dull lectures. and tests are really specific... like very specific.... its kind of unreasonable. turns simple concepts into annoying memorization messes. try and avoid him. but he's not the worst. no-one goes to lecture

Dr. Egner is a good professor but he does not correct the exams for the course, so your grade really depends on who your TA is because exams are NOT multiple choice. Egner does not enjoy when you talk about grades with him, in fact he gets downright mad! His lecture slides are very clear but going to lecture definitely helps for exams.
Unbelievable professor. He is very clear, and always up for answering questions. Powerpoints are very clear as well.
Fantastic professor. Powerpoint presentations are extremely clear and he's a really nice person.

I really liked Professor Egner--his powerpoint slides and lectures were VERY clear and helpful and he was very good about answering questions.  The class is fairly straightforward and the tests are not difficult if you go to class, since nearly all of the material comes straight from lecture.  I'd really recommend this class!

Eileen is one of the kindest professors I've had at Duke. Everyone gets an A. Very little work required. Easiest Spanish class I've taken so far. Tests are given @ the department level and are very hard (one tradeoff to the class being easy is that she doesn't teach to the test very effectively)...block of your weekend before an exam to study.
Profa Anderson is deeply devoted to service and makes this class super fun! She creates a welcoming environment for beginners.
Profesora Anderson is one of the best professors in the Spanish department. She is incredibly knowledgable about linguistics and uses this to better her students' understanding Spanish.

Professor Anderson is super sweet and creates a classroom environment where students are comfortable answering questions without the fear of being wrong. I recommend taking her class because it is not very time consuming and she is an easy grader. She also makes class fun and interactive.
Absolute W professor. 10/10 would take again. If you're taking Spanish, take it with her.
She is the best Spanish teacher. Wouldn't recommend anyone else! Caring and empathetic are just two of many positive words to describe her. Knock that requirement out of the way with Eileen :)))))

Eileen is amazing. She is kind, uplifting, and engaging. She never made you feel dumb for asking questions and was always willing to meet outside of class. My class had so much fun with her. She came up with interactive games to help strengthen our understanding of course material and was clear with assignments. Love her!!!

Honestly, I had such a blast in this class. I totally recommend this course if you're looking for a fun environment and an easy A. Eileen is so funny and easy-going. It was also a service-learning course which I think was awesome. Take this class!!!!

Professor Anderson was very laid-back and created a stress-free environment to develop language skills. If you're looking for a challenge, I wouldn't recommend this class, but if you just want to complete your language requirement-- she is the professor to choose. Quizzes are manageable and she gives good feedback on any writing assignments.

When taking an advanced spanish course, I expect the materials to be *in spanish*. I expect the professor to attempt organization, provide clear instructions, and pretend to care about the course. Very frustrating when your professor doesn't care about the class. Is apparently similar w/o pandemic.

She is my favorite teacher at Duke. She is extremely easy going and a hilarious teacher. Her class was very easy and it is the type of class that what you put into it is what you get out of it. Take a class from Eileen if you want an easy, fun Spanish class. I spent most of the class joking around with Eileen, love her
An absolute gem of a professor in terms of ease and personality. Really cares about her students and will put in the effort to make sure you get a good grade.

If you want to actually learn any spanish at all, don't take this class with Eileen Anderson. You will do no work except for the bare minimum, and be very unprepared for any tests or quizzes. Works out great online if you just wanna finish the req but if even an ounce of you wants to learn don't take it with her.
Anderson is amazing. Makes class fun and is not too harsh.

Best Spanish prof at Duke! She really cares about her students, so she does not grade harshly or set unrealistic expectations. Go to class and participate and you'll get an A. She is also super funny and nice and a wonderful person. 10/10 take her for any Spanish class.
She is an absolute gem, easily the best professor I have had at Duke!
Awesome 303 professor, fairly easy to do well and very manageable workload. Also low stress environment which is huge for a 300-level FL. Highly recommend.

Prof. Anderson is one of the nicest professors I've had at Duke. She's very approachable, easy to understand, and you can do well pretty easily as long as you participate in discussions and do what she asks of you. The class was fairly easy, and she creates a very positive class environment. If you see 303 with her, take it.

I really enjoyed taking this class.  Class meets three times a week and was very relaxed and easy to learn, but attendance does matter.  However, tests are written by the department so are harder than the class is taught for.  Studying is a must and it is a time consuming class.  If you have to take it, definitely take it with her.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: If you are going to take a Spanish class at Duke, I would reccomend taking it with her. She understands that there are a lot of assignments for this class and is very reasonable. She is also very personable and easy to talk to.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: While allowing for a laid-back classroom environment, la profesora is very unclear on certain aspects of the grading that carry large percentages. The tests are written by the department so anything she prepares you with is only speculative. Class requires large amounts of time outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: She was very helpful in meeting outside of class. The class was taught in Spanish, but there was a lot of English involved. She is very kind and thoughtful. It was overall easy to get a good grade. You should take her classes.
Great teacher-very laid back environment and extremely willing to work with you. If you can take a Spanish class with her, I highly recommend it.

This was a fairly basic course and Prof. Anderson is great. She's incredibly helpful and has an awesome personality. As long as you try she'll like you (although I don't think she dislikes anyone). The tests take a lot of studying but they're really straightforward and come straight from the textbook. Definitely take her course.

she's really nice and definitely an easy grader. i hardly spoke a word in class but she always gave me As for participation. make sure to study vocab for the tests. put a little bit of effort and you'll get a good grade. super sweet
she's really nice and is an easy grader. really approachable
TAKE ANY SPANISH CLASS WITH HER. she is a saint and an angel. If you do the work and participate maybe even a little, youll get an A
so so nice and understanding. go to class and participate and she will like you

I had Anderson for two Spanish classes. She is very chill, reasonable, and encourages participation. She'll change the syllabus if necessary and has given extra time on writing assignments if a lot of people request it or seem to be struggling. She's also pretty funny at times, reminds me of my Mom lol
the boss, she mad cool
Professor Anderson is very nice and a fairly easy grader. Make sure to speak up in class to get good Discussion grades.

a truly insightful class on dante's divine comedy-- a must-take (saying this as math/cs). it requires grappling with the text: there's 3 essays, a midterm and final. while challenging, this class is incredibly rewarding. eisner is the best lecturer i've seen at duke, and it was a pleasure to learn from him. we gave him an ovation on the last day!

Gives great lectures, does not post slides but the emphasis of the lectures will be reflected in the exams so would highly recommend attending. Lots of reading, easy to get behind on because poetry reading can be time consuming
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Eisner is an awesome professor who genuinely cares about what he teaches. He assigns a lot of reading every class, but usually just for discussion so you can get away with skimming. The whole course is graded off 5 written assignments, participation, and the final paper. Pretty loose grader as long as you put effort in.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed Dr. Eisner's class. There was ALOT of reading, but you can get by with skimming. I loved how passionate he was about all of the books we read, and he always had something to say when discussions were becoming dry. He gave us feedback on our assignments, but you don't get anything graded till the end. Great class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Excellent professor. Eisner is caring and very responsive. He really shows his passion for both teaching and for literature on a daily basis which I found refreshing and much needed. Beware of the midterm and final which require more studying than you would think!

Best lectures I've ever had at Duke. Eisner takes something incredibly complex and makes it relatable to the 21st-century student. Did an independent study with him -- after I had finished all his classes --- and none of them counted towards my major or minor.

A very interesting class with a lot of reading - towards the end a lot of people stopped reading, but prof was always able to keep the conversation going. I learned a ton. I'd recommend taking notes on discussions in class - helps a lot with papers. The one downside to this class is the unclear grading criteria. It felt pretty arbitrary at times.

A great professor. Have had him before, but he really shined in this one. This is clearly his primary area of study, and it really shows. He also excels in a seminar setting. This course had 13 students, which was perfect. Great discussions when the students did the reading, and he covered pretty well when we didn't. A very good class.

You can learn so much from this professor. Class discussions sometimes died down among students, but he always had interesting things to say. Paper feedback is very valuable and grading is not harsh. I never thought I would like Med/Ren lit, but after his course on the Decameron I'm quite interested in it! Definitely take this class.
take it take it take it. you'll never want to miss lecture. tests are stupidly hard, but his grading isn't. he's a fantastic lecturer.

This is a GREAT class.  The exams are definitely the hardest part, but the papers are graded pretty generously, and you learn SO MUCH.  Eisner is just a wealth of information, but inserts a lot of witty comments into lecture. He's also pretty attractive.

Eisner is an amazing professor.  He is young, knowledgeable, and engaging.  Even if you are not particularly interested in Dante, the class is awesome.  However, be prepared to read and do work - the midterm and final in particular are difficult.

Prof. Eisner is great; he's extremely knowledgeable and engaging, as the other posts here have indicated. He is a fair grader. However, his TAs are difficult graders who seem intent on keeping average scores low for extraneous reasons, which is frustrating. Unfortunately, it's they that grade the vast majority of the work in this course.

It is astounding how much this guy knows about Dante, Boccacio, Italy, Italian, Latin classical works and art.  He loves his subject so much that even if you have no prior interest in reading Dante, you will leave the class happy you took it.  Papers and tests are rigorous, but in the end, if you stay on top of things, you'll get at least a B.

Eisner is AMAZING! You learn so much from the class, not only for academic use but also just for personal knowledge.  He knows SO much, and is extremely helpful.
