Grading may seem hard, but at the end you'll definitely get a good grade (if you put the work in). I'd say most people get A's and B's. TAKE HIS CLASS!!

Professor Eisner is amazing. He is very funny and engaging in class and knows so much about Dante. If you don't think your writing is strong meet with him outside of class. He is very helpful and will guide you as you formulate your ideas. Most people get A's or B's in this class and you learn an unbelievable amount.

He is a really nice guy. He knows so much about Dante and you will learn more than you think. Some of his TAs grade much harder than he does, but that was the only problem in the class. If you are really clear on what the assignment asks for you should be fine.

Great guy.  Liked Dante coming in, loved it by the time class was over.  Very funny, made me laugh everyday.  Keeps you engaged, likes to interact with students.  Keep stupid comments to yourself, but other than that definitely recommend.

Amazing professor. Very knowledgeable but still very interested in hearing students' thoughts and opinions. You learn and unbelievable amount, plus he's very flexible on papers and not a hard grader whatsoever. Take this class and enjoy it, and get a good grade!
He's very energetic, and his drawings of maps on the board are hilarious. nice guy, young, fun, and very very knowledgeable. also gives a ton of flexibility on papers.. i would def. recommend him!

She's very sweet and she explains the readings thoroughly through padlet posts. There was an activity each class so even if you don't do a reading one day, you will understand what's it about. Would take her again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: 10/10 recommend. She always made sure her students understood what she was teaching and checked in to see that the workload wasn't too much. I loved this course, such an amazing and caring professor.
The professor is very nice, quickly responds to emails and provides constructive feedback. I would definitely take her everytime i get the chance

One of the best professors, love her hands down. She is very sweet and will include all different races so that everyone feels included. The workload is very manageable and easy. Overall recommend taking this class

Passive aggressive and behind visage of bubbly kindness. Cannot be direct w/ students so awkwardly confronts them. Pretends to care about you. If you don't immediately say something in line with her world view, she'll cut you off and lecture at you why you're wrong without letting you finish your thought. Take someone else.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Nicole Eitzen Delgado is a phenomenal professor! Her lectures are outstanding and provide her students with compelling and relevant material related to the course. She genuinely cares about her students, their wellbeing, and their growth as scholars in the field. Overall, I'd recommend any course that Dr. Delgado teaches!

She is very supportive in your growth as a write and learner. If you cannot attend class she is understanding and sets clear expectations for what is needed to be successful. There are a lot fo readings but they are not too challenging or time consuming, and are really interesting and diverse. I've never received such positive feedback on an essay.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Was their only student in Fall 2020. They were not too flexible; they want to 'challenge you.' Will grade you down on the first paper as 'incentive' to try harder on the final -- in the end curbing your grade. Claims to be radical and teach with a decolonize approach but still acts like a professor. LONG and lots of writing.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--So many papers

reviews.comment: An amazing course taught by an amazing professor. She genuinely cares about her students and is willing to go off the books just to teach us something interesting and/or relevant.
What a chill and thoughtful class, really cool professor, the work never felt stressful

Dr. Chow is a great professor who connects well with her students and fosters a good classroom dynamic. She's kind and makes an effort to treat her students with kindness. Chinatowns is also an interesting class that presents a variety of interesting topics.

Chinatowns was fantastic with Dr. Chow. Definitely one of the courses you'll look back on and be happy about. She's simply a caring person and made the content really applicable. She's understanding with deadlines and will try to make the class less burdensome. Highly recommend.
Easy class. Learn about Asia. No tests or quizzes. Light weekly homework and a few papers that are also short. Great choice. Almost everyone gets an A

Dr. Chow is one of the best professors I've had at Duke. She is incredibly knowledgeable and truly cares for her students. The course readings/viewings were manageable and made for great class discussions. She is also flexible to revising the syllabus according to students' topical interests.

Chinatowns was an amazing class. Projects were very interesting (interviewing waiters and managers at a Chinese restaurant, entire-class roleplaying game, etc.) and weekly assignments were just readings and Sakai posts. Took away a lot about Chinese immigration that I never knew beforereally glad I took this class.

Chow is super enthusiastic & knowledgeable about CTs! Though the course is not very structured (and she doesn't really give grades/feedback on work throughout the sem.), she incorporates activities that are super helpful in solidifying the course content in our minds. Fun, interesting, and engaging class!
reviews.rating_tags: GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Only like 3 assignments (group projects and papers) and graded very easily. Participation, however, is pretty important as there's only one class per week and you just need to show up and say like two things in discussion to show her that you were there. No one really does the readings for posting on a forum --  don't even have to do it on time

Professor Chow has provided an incredible class and possibly one of my favorites at Duke. The class is structured well, extremely engaging and completely unique (in a very good way). For those of you looking for an interesting class, or even just a break from the soul-crushing academia, take a class with Professor Chow.

Professor Chow is awesome- enthusiastic, thoughtful, and very familiar with anime and willing to debate the merits of various shows. The class is very participation based and the projects are in-depth, but they're pretty freeform and Professor Chow definitely rewards creativity.

If a student has an opinion that is different than hers, she makes sure that the class knows the student is wrong. Overall, one of the worst professors I have had at Duke. The course should be labeled "Eileen Chow's opinions about politics". While the subject could be interesting, her teaching methods ruined my interest.

The class itself is interesting for those who are interested in anime or have no background in it. Chow is knowledgable but goes off on tangents, which sometimes makes a lecture go from engaging to dull. A fair grader who always listens. Projects are fun and interesting. Just contribute to discussion and do the projects and you'll succeed.

The class is very laid back, and filled with students from very different backgrounds. Many love anime, some know nothing about it. Either way the class isn't difficult, and overall interesting. Professor Chow loves what she teaches, and really engages and cares about her students.

She's one of my favorite professors I've had so far. She really knows how to get you interested in the class topic. Class discussions are always interesting and projects are always fun and engaging. She's extremely kind and flexible when it comes to work and grades too. Just do the readings and go to class. You'll get more out of it that way.
she's pretty random

His lectures are more confusing than necessary but it wasn't the worst thing in the world. He definitely goes pretty quickly and at times it was a little frustrating but overall manageable with some effort. He's really nice about giving plenty of opportunities to get a good grade and gives a lot of partial credit.

He's a solid intro stat professor, much better than other intro course professors I've had. The coursework is pretty heavy and is frustrating at times, but I feel it really helped me learn a lot. Spring 2020 was the last time this class was offered but if you gotta take an intro class with him, I'd say go for it.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Homework is hard and long, went to a lot of office hours. Weekly quizzes that were insanely difficult. Posts slides online but he talks about most of the information in class so you shouldn't skip if you want a decent grade. Had a huge feeling of dread every time I had to go to this class. Would not recommend taking unless absolutely necessary.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Very smart professor that is willing to help. this class is always annoying in terms of weekly homework, weekly lab, weekly quizzes but eisinger is willing to help. he does have pretty high expectations and his quizzes/tests tend to be on the harder side. however, do the homework and office hours and you'll get at least a B
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Eisinger is awesome. He's a good lecturer and keeps you engaged in class material. We had weekly hw a quiz each week and a lab, but nothing was too hard and you get to drop some stuff in your final grade. Super clear course expectation and he does a really good job of making sure you understand whats going on.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Bob was a great professor for an introductory Stats course. He is very patient with students and willing to answer their questions. Tests are fair in both difficulty and grading, allowing students to ask for regrades.

He is a great guy and very willing to help you out. This course has a very high workload between homework, studying for frequent in-class quizzes, and labs. The grading breakdown is very favorable, but constant quizzes can be very stressful.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Bob is a solid, straightforward teacher and helpful outside of class. make sure to stay on top of the material as there are quizzes almost every class that are worth a lot. overall pretty easy class except for a few tricky concepts. go to ta OH for problem sets. there's no curve. funny guy for sure
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I truly believe that Bob is a good teacher, he just goes through lectures SO FAST that students have 0 time to absorb material. He also gives quizzes almost every class with no warning on the material or whether it's group/individual (he may test you on material he taught 10 min ago)! The homeworks are really tough but the TAs will help you out.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Nicolas is a really nice person who obviously cares about his students. He wants his students to participate and is always there if you need some extra help on your papers. Go to office hours-- he provides valuable feedback on your papers. Also, go to class, because he notices who goes and who does not (and it counts towards your grade).

Really laid back and easygoing, although there is a ton of small projects and busy work. Directions aren't always clear, but if you ask him, he's more than willing to explain what he means. There's a lot of freedom to explore what interests you, although he does grade kind of tough. If you go to his office hours, he'll help you make a good grade.

Lots of work outside of class, but the deadlines and difficulty are very manageable. For essay revision, attend his office hours! He gives very good big-picture feedback. Excellent prof. overall, really cares about his students.

Great teacher. Focuses on writing as a skill larger than grammar.  His intro assignments can be vague, but he grades on quality, so you have the freedom to pursue related tangents that inspire you.  More busy work than needed. This is normally my biggest peeve with profs, but I'll cut him some slack. His class is worth it if you have the time.

Very nice and friendly, but gives lots of busy work and a relatively high workload. Is sometimes unclear about his expectations are and when things are due, so make sure to check the online calendar often! Does not stick strictly to the syllabus and bases grades mainly on how much effort you put into the class. Also, he's always willing to help.

Professor Eilbaum is more than a professor to me. He cares about his students, he cares about the Durham community, and he is the most genuine and honest person I know. Definitely take his class if you are slightly interested in the topic or simply because you want to be friends with a knowledgeable professor. The workload is very reasonable.

Prof. Eilbaum is genuinely modest, friendly and lovable. He puts a lot of work into creating an intellectually stimulating and writing-intensive course. It definitely demands a lot of responsibility and care for details to post on different forums, comment, write drafts, etc., and it could be confusing. But it's a reasonable amount of work.
Way more work than other writing classes.

Very nice and helpful professor. He treats students just as friends and will help you as long as you want to learn and talk the course materials with him. Not hard to get a good grade if you put work into the course.

Took his Writing 101: El Norte, on Mexican immigration in the recent past. A applicable class, especially in Durham! The service-learning component: awesome! Really accessible to talk about papers and really nice  - encourages class discussion. Make sure to show evidence of the work/process of your papers -- it's not all about the final product.

Took unauthorized immigration with him for my freshman writing 20. Pretty easy as far as writing 20s go. First assignment was several short essays and was pass/fail. Grade based off 2 longer research papers (about 1400 words). Make sure you read the prompts they're usually pretty long (like a page) and may be vague, but he'll gladly meet with you
nice guy, 4-5 papers that are not more then 6 pages, put in the work and get the grade. great guy, relatively interesting. topic influences the type of people in the class if you care

This was my absolute favorite class! I would definitely recommend it! The topic is interesting and he gives (usually) very interesting readngs for class. He doesn't give a lot of work, a total of 5 papers(one of which was a group project).

Professor Eilbaum is super chill and the class itself is very interesting (lots of guest speakers and we even had a field trip). The reading isn't overkill and there is about 1 paper every 3 weeks. Take W20 with him; you won't regret it.
Professor Eilbaum is  a really great guy and is very accessible. Often his assignments are ambiguous which can be very annoying but that just leads to more freedom in topics.
Very helpful in providing sources to his students. Always available outside of class.

Professor Eilbaum is a great, even-tempered guy. For second semester, he made his class much harder than first semester and definitely made it more difficult to get an A. Getting good grades with him was still very doable, but definitely took more work on the writing assignments than advertised by students who had him previously.

Nicolas is a really nice guy. His assignments can be somewhat ambiguous, but he is always willing to meet with you or help out if you are in need. He encourages class discussion, and the class itself is really interesting. I definitely recommend this course.

Unless you like geometry proofs, AVOID THIS CLASS BY ALL MEANS...it makes little to no sense and the course description is a lie...Iris also is a bit scatterbrained which doesn't help with the clarity of this difficult subject. Just say no.

Do not take her symbolic logic class.  She cannot teach this particular course and you will be wasting your time.  You will regret it.  Take Brandon's session instead. She's completely incomprehensible and assumes way too much on the students.  Absolute blackball with no qualifications.

A little boring and was usually very rushed, which lead her to make mistakes and confuse everyone. However, she was friendly and helpful whenever anyone was in need of it - but you had to go after it yourself. She never made it a point of getting to know students like some other professors do. The tutorial sessions on Fridays were useless though...

I really enjoyed Logic. She is boring and sometimes makes mistakes, but its really just that she's dorky and absorbed in the material she loves. I think she really does care, even if she doesn't express emotions. It's not much work, but you need to do your work. It's easy and like word puzzles if you pay attention.
Made a possibly interesting subject very dull. Says a lot without saying much. Spent a lot of time on uninteresting topics. I was always bored and learned everything on wikipedia.

This subject was one of her strengths, and you could tell. She really packs a lot into lectures, but manages to keep things linear. Overall does a good job of relating to the student and encouraging productive thought.
best prof at duke. bunch of reading but even if don't understand them its chill

Dr. Guevara is honestly such a sweetheart. You can tell she is super knowledgeable and passionate about the content. While the course content can be overwhelming at times, she is very kind and accessible and wants to set you up for success. I would recommend taking a class with her!

She's very knowledgeable about every topic discussed. My impression is she doesn't like the idea of creating any stress and wants you to learn for fun, not for the grade, so as long as you engage you will get full credit. The lack of stress though inspires you to actually learn the material anyway.

One of the sweetest professors in the department if not at Duke. Takes time after class to answer questions and explains the material very clearly. Lectures aren't super engaging but if you enjoy evolution it is a very insightful class. Copies the practice questions she provides for every lecture directly, word-for-word for the midterms.

Dr. Guevara is incredible. I've taken multiple classes with her. My favorite professor I've had at Duke. She really cares about the subject she's teaching and is one of the most knowledgeable professors I've ever had. Take any class you can with her, evanth major or not. She's compassionate towards students and accessible outside of class.

Dr. G is amazing. You can tell how much she cares about her students. Grade based on reading questions and participation. (50%), leading class discussion for a day, and a final presentation (25% each). Class basically just lectures about specific topics. Super interesting!

Dr. Guevara is very friendly and clearly wants her students to succeed. She is very accessible outside of class. She provides study guide resources outside of class, which were super helpful for exams. Without them the exams would have been much more challenging. I would definitely recommend taking and Evanth class with her if you get the chance.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Guevara is amazing!!! She is really nice and grades very fairly. She also makes sure to give you a lot of resources (MAKE SURE TO USE THEM) that will help prepare you really well for her tests. You can tell that she is passionate about EVANTH and genuinely cares about the class!

I loved Dr. Sullivan! I took her Genetics and Epigenetics class as part of the Genetics and Genomics FOCUS cluster, and it was my favorite class this semester. She gives great lectures, she'll always answer questions inside and outside of class, and she makes sure everyone learns as much as they can without excess focus on grades.

Dr. Sullivan is such an amazing professor! I took her FOCUS class and she is so caring about her students and makes the class such a low-stress environment. I would definitely recommend her FOCUS class as well as her as a professor in general cuz she's literally the best!!

Beth Sullivan is an incredible scientist. She care deeply about the material and is passionate about her subject. Her classes are modern-research based are incredibly interesting and she'll give you everything you need to know to understand the material but make sure to do the readings.

Best stats 199 lecturer at Duke. Every other course forces you to write code in person under a specific time. If he ever offers the course again take it! Great teacher of R and super chill courseload.
Beware! Professor did not care about his students, he was more focused on finding his next teaching job than actually teaching the course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Knowledgeable and passionate about statistics, the class is comprised of a lot of coding homework in R so if you've done any coding at all you should be ok.
he's nice.

Such an incredible, caring, and wonderful professor. Always tries to make lectures interesting. Class is super straight forward if you pay attention. I had my software crash for a major exam and I emailed him and he was so understanding and let me turn it in without penalty. Exams were take home, homeworks and labs were doable. Absolutely loved him

Professor Meyer was amazing. He's caring, passionate about what he teaches, and makes the class understandable for all. I genuinely enjoyed lectures because they were interactive. Workload wasn't too heavy. He's always willing to help, and he truly wants all his students to succeed. Loved the class, and because of him, love data science more!

Dr. Meyer is an exceptional professor. His enthusiasm for the course was evident each class, he genuinely enjoys teaching, and he explains topics in a way that simply make sense. The homeworks and labs are based off class learning and help 1) apply topics to real world concepts and 2) learn new skills. I definitely recommend!!

I know he's leaving Duke, but in the event people from another school find this: TAKE DR. MEYER'S CLASS. I came in thinking of being a Data Science major, and this class confirmed to me that it was the right path. He made Stats interesting and applicable. I also had a few questions pertaining to personal projects and he was very eager to help.
"My time is yours"

Really nice guy, and his rating is probably so high because freshmen (who take stat199) have not been exposed to other higher quality professors yet. He's hard not to like because he is very caring, but he just doesn't know what he is doing. He can hardly write LaTeX. Typos and mistakes are expected from him. The questions he writes are ambiguous.

Professor Meyer was consistently the brightest spot of my day for the time that I took his introduction to data science class. He was incredibly caring and he truly was inspirational. He made the class understand that no question was a bad question and he always stayed after class to answer them. I entered a novice programmer and exited a genius.

Its is clear Professor Meyer really cares about teaching/ his students. This class is definitely easier if you have coded before. I have Humanities friends who struggled and STEM people that breezed through. Mostly, if you do the homeworks, pay attention in class, the tests are not terrible. Office hours amazing- I went to almost every single one.

Dr. Meyer was pretty engaging in lecture and was very approachable. This class is not conceptually difficult, but you will learn a lot and have a lot to do -- there was a steady stream of homeworks (1 every 2 weeks or so) and labs (1 per week), as well as 2 midterms, AEs (finished in class) and a final project. Overall would recommend though.
Professor Meyer is WONDERFUL!! Provides very clear and engaging lectures. He makes you feel comfortable asking for help or asking questions. Overall, an amazing class and teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Meyer is an amazing person and professor. He cares a lot about his students and genuinely wants them to do well, and is very receptive to feedback. He is very nice and approachable before, during, after, and outside of class.
Professor Meyer is a caring professor. Assignments can be tedious, but if you complete all of them and attend all lectures, you will get a good grade.
The assignments are very tedious and I don't think he taught me anything. It was a lot of copy and paste.
Elijah is an absolute dawg. He is such a cool professor and so young and lively. Stats 199 is definitely a difficult class but if you try to stay on top of it and focus you should be chilling.

Difficulty of class is extremely dependent on your past experience with coding. There is a constant stream of work with homework and labs, and it can be overwhelming if you don't stay on top of the deadlines. Meyer doesn't lecture very clearly, but he tries to be accessible and answer questions as much as possible.

Professor Meyer is an incredible professor. He teaches in a very applicational, hands-on way. He doesn't just stand up front and talk. He really cares about the success of all his students (even in a lecture hall of 179 students). He is super approachable. His instructions are easy to follow and clear. He makes the class as engaging as possible.

I took voice lessons for the first time with her and she was amazing! Her feedback and caring nature was very helpful, and I see a staunch improvement with my voice after just one semester with her, which is why I am continuing lessons.

Excellent voice professor. I was taking lessons for the first time this semester, and I can't be happier about my choice to study with Dr. Linnartz. She was excellent at understanding my vocal needs, what I wanted to get out of my lessons, and my other commitments. Wish I could continue studying with her in the fall.

As always, Dr. Linnartz is great. If you are a classical singer, it's essential to be able to pronounce the words of your foreign songs correctly, and this class helps you do that. Learning the IPA alphabet is not as hard as you might think, and if you ever do end up studying one of the languages formally in the future, you'll be ready. Work light.

Wonderful vocal teacher that made me want to pursue other music classes at Duke! She really improved my singing after just one semester.  She's really nice and supportive--everyone's mom, haha. Professor Linnartz does expect a lot from her students, so take the class seriously, and do your exercises on a regular basis.
Amazing teacher. Very helpful with improving technique and broadening repertoire. Enthusiastic and fun!
Excellent teacher and wonderful person. She makes music come alive and is a great technician. I can't give her a high enough score.
Ellen is so great. She is a great mentor. She gives great feedback. She's an accessible teacher. She's really passionate about what she teaches. She writes great recommendations. Highly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Amazing professor. Don't be afraid to take her class if you don't know anything about the topic.

Heavy on readings, No quizzes or test which were sooo great. But there are 2 10 page papers and 1 presentation in the entire semester. LITERALLY THREE THINGS!!! 

All you have to do is do the readings, show up to class, participate, and do weekly discussion posts. Then do your 2 papers and a presentation (which she gives more than enough time for)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Covered a lot of material I knew nothing about. Teacher is laid back but serious about the material. Class is about the overlaps (mainly) of Jewish and Muslim cultures (philosophy/ poetry/ mysticism/ music) in Andalusia. Interesting class. Includes a trip to the actual sites we study in Cordoba, Seville, and Granada.
She is really good, kind of all over the place and really knows her stuff. i took literary islam with her and it was good. lots of readings and discussions but not hard at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Ellen is a fantastic professor who really cares for her students. The overall course and lectures have been very well planned and cover a great breadth of content but also uniquely are able to provide deep, nuanced windows into specific topics. She is very flexible about the topics and mediums for your assignments One of the Best Professors!!

One of the best professors at Duke. I enjoyed her class a lot. Professor made the class a very safe space and she was always willing to help you academically or generally for life advice/mentorship. Definitely recommend taking her class if you want to explore the Islamic world.
Ellen is really cares about her students! Her classes are engaging and I also learned so much. Make sure you're present, engaged, and do the work on time. That's all she really cares about!

Each class I learned things I knew nothing about. It blew my mind that there are entire worlds occulted from our vision and consciousness because of cultural myopia. Ellen helped pry open portals in our minds to shed light on other aspects of humanity that had not previously been within my purview. Thanks for opening our minds but also our hearts.

Gives really good feedback to midterm and final papers. Submit a proposal and she will steer you away from the wrong path and point you in the right direction. Took a class she co-taught with other religion professors and she really shined. She took the time to learn everyone's names. If you get the chance to take her class, definitely do it.

Best class I ever took at Duke. Ellen has the ability to take students from all levels and types of acquaintances with Islam - from college kids with a Muslim friend, to Muslim students, to researchers of Islamic law, to professors of Muslim history - and make them all learn something new about themselves and religion in the U.S.. Thumbs up.
Professor McLarney is amazing. She is incredibly knowledgeable and so willing to help her students succeed. This was the second class I took with her and if I could I would've taken more.
Best class I've taken at Duke hands down.
Professor McLarney is amazing! She is so enthusiastic and passionate about what she is teaching.  I learned so much and the material was very interesting!

Professor McLarney's enthusiasm is single-handedly what makes her classes on Islam so fantasticshe engages really well with everyone from the freshest beginners to advanced readers. Local Islams is an amazingly well-integrated class. Readings were amazing too.

I like Ellen, but her Revolution on Screen class was disorganized and lacked any meaningful discussion. I didn't learn much from the class, and all we really did was learn basic history of the Arab Spring and watch some movies/documentaries. I think she's a good teacher/person, but the class was just bland, though it was her first time teaching it.

Local Islams was a super cool class!! We visited a bunch of different communities in the area, lots of culture, films, food, and direct knowledge about Islam and Muslims right in our own area. Definitely an eye opening classes. One of the best I've taken at Duke. Ellen is really responsive, enthusiastic, knowledgeable.

Class on the intersection of Islamic/Jewish/Christian cultures in southern Spain-- it really opens your eyes to the complicated history of these civilizations going back so far. She maybe tries to cover too much---but the material was super deep. Ellen's an accessible teacher & tries to make the material accessible too.
Dynamite stuff--the films blew my mind--a creative way to approach the topic. Really like the cultural approach to political issues. Really reccommmend.
Wish she hadn't taught this class. It's a cool subject, Arab spring, but she really messed it up. She also treats "her" students like 5 year-olds which is somewhat degrading and unnecessary.
yeah, Ellen taught Egypt starting with the revolutionsa and going back to Napoleon and orientalism. It was an interesting concept, definitely food for thought. She is a super sweetie!
Ellen is really nice and really helpful. I took her course Egypt:Mother of the World, and the structure of that course was confusing, but she's an easy grader, and really cares about her students.
God bless Ellen, she's mentored me & really helped me thru duke. Her classes really made me rethink the Middle east & Islam. She is helpful but tough sometimes. but its worth it.

don't listen. one guy in this class was a super insecure loudmouth that wouldn't stop blowing his own horn. he clearly had issues with a woman in a position of authority. this class ranks among the classes i have gained the most from. it definitely caused me to appreciate ideas and concepts i did not consider before. we love you ellen!

Ellen tries hard, but she simply isn't that great a teacher. Her lectures are schizophrenic. She assigns tons of reading and made us buy a dozen books. Her grading is erratic and inconsistent. Ellen knows a lot, but she's a very insecure person and as a result she dominates class discussions with her own opinions. Very disappointing class overall.

Very nice person!  Still a little green at teaching.  She is extremely interested in her subject field, but sometimes forgets that everyone else may not share the same level of passion.  She assigns a humongous amount of reading per class (100-200pgs) but doesn't always realize it.  Sometimes it can be frustrating, but she's totally worth it!
One of the most influential classes I ever took. Opened my eyes.
Great Teacher
Ellen is GREAT! On sabatical for now but she's the best arabic professor of all time! Only take 1 and 2 with her if you can!
ellen kicks ass. can be a bit hard on you, but an amazing professor

She tries to come off as nice and is genuinely interested in her field, but when it comes down to it, she's **** (anti-men) and is prone to screw a lot of things up.  Its a tough but rewarding class, and you'll need patience if she's teaching it.

Professor Klein is one of the nicest profs at Duke. Rocks for jocks was an extremely easy class, but it's very interesting if you choose to put effort into the class and learn the material. Klein is very approachable, has multiple office hours, and makes it clear what she's looking for from students. Very easy class, but an amazing, kind Professor.
Fairy easy A. Read the slides before each exam.

Great science class for those who just want to dip their toe into science - straightforward structure (lectures and tests based solely on them) - abstract concepts explained well - Professor Klein is a deeply likeable, kind, personable, engaging professor who is clearly enthusiastic about teaching and the subject matter - would always recommend

I took this class S/U for the NS requirement, but Professor Klein is very kind and engaged in her work. You don't have to go to lectures but it is a lot of vocab/content to cram before the exams (60-70 multiple choice). Not an easy A imo but if you study/use Quizlet it's very attainable. I recommend for anyone trying to fill an NS!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Really sweet and great professor. Textbook was not used after the first couple lectures and it is an easy A if you just show up and do your work.

Do NOT take this class! It is not rocks for jocks, and is extremely difficult. Even the homework didn't reflect the slides, which means nothing was clear! All of the questions on the exams required theoretical knowledge. Simply studying the 400 slides with 10 concepts on each didn't help you pass the test.

Rocks for Jocks was pretty easy. Lecture isn't mandatory, and the professor posts all of the slideshows. She highlights what's important to know for the exams on them. Homeworks on each section aren't too difficult, tests are fine if know basic geology/can cram well. Extra credit opportunities too, and she greatly curved the end grades

Seconding that this class made me hate geology. Take it with Glass, he's much better from what I heard. This class material was so dry, the lectures were awfully slow and boring. The tests were so much memorization -- one question I remember showed a picture of a rock and asked you to identify the name.

and if you made 10 questions wrong(meaning that you actually have 65 questions correct!! which is a lot), but you can only get 85/100 on this exam, and in turn, you might have a B for the final grade. The homework is not even just simply homework but small quizzes that you have to complete 10-20 multiple choices each week. I really beg for curve...

I have to commit that this course as an intro-level course and was taken by most of the students for the Natural Science requirement is even hard for STEM primary students as we are about to digest nearly 17 chapters' contexts and we have three exams which each one contains 75 questions and EACH ONE is in medium-difficult level....Overall, 93 is A
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: No idea what happened to her compared to other years but this class is so damn hard and there is only 3 tests so grading is super heavy. Not the rocks for jocks you here about, would never recommend taking this. So hard. Made me hate geology
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I honestly could not rate this professor because I simply never went to class but this course was so easy. I have friends taking it now with a different teacher and things are not the same. If you want and easy A take this class with Professor Klein I genuinely didn't even step one foot in the building this class was in all semester and got an A.

All lectures were recorded which was the best part. No midterm and final. Would definitely take again. The professor explains extremely well and is really passionate about what she teaches. Actually learned about our planet taking this class
Easy class but lectures can get really boring!

Great instructor and an even better person! As a humanities student with no interest in science, I still found the material captivating, especially due to the passion Prof. Kelin has for the subject. However, I don't think the class is as easy as people say it is. For each test, you need to memorize material over hundreds of slides.

Professor Klein is an absolute sweetheart! For someone who has never taken an earth sciences class, I found her lectures incredibly interesting and eye-opening. She also cares a lot about the well-being of her students, and is always approachable outside of class, whether for academic or non-academic matters. Highly recommend this course!

Easy class... interesting material, and Dr. Klein is cool. I don't recommend skipping class, because it's better to listen to her speak, but if you miss a class here or there, you'll be totally fine because the powerpoints are all online.

EOS101 is relatively easy. Theres minimal open-notes homework, no projects or essays, and 3 tests. The tests are all multiple choice and it is basically all memorization, so if you put in the time to memorize the powerpoint slides you should be fine. I also bought the textbook and did not use it once.

EOS101 is an easy class but you have to memorize everything on the slides to do well on the exams. I found the material interesting and relevant, and Dr. Klein is amazing. She is so passionate about the material and truly cares about her students. This class has made me want to take more EOS courses in the future! Great class, take it!

supposed to be an "easy A" class--definitely possible for an A but not easy, need to study a TON for the tests or you will fail them, the material and lectures could not be more boring or dry and the studying/homework is just a nuisance. not worth it for the easy A
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: At first I underestimated the difficulty of the class. To get an A, just know EVERYTHING on the slides. Going to lectures does not really impact your final grade as long as you study for the tests. Extra credit pushes you up 2 whole percent points, totally clutch.

Took rocks after the reviews saying it was one of the easiest classes at Duke. Personally, I found it incredibly hard to memorize the seemingly unconnected material. Since this class isn't curved at all, DO NOT take if you aren't interested in the material and are bad at memorization compared to other Duke students. Also going to class is pointless

You can really tell that Professor Klein really enjoys what she is teaching. She is very into the subject and that shows in her lectures though they can sometimes feel pretty long. The class consists of 2 midterms, a final, and weekly homework questions. If you study the powerpoint you are set to go, though attending lecture wouldn't hurt.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Perfect combination of wonderful professor and easy class. Klein was an absolute pleasure to have. I enjoyed her enthusiasm for lectures, even though most didn't go, and I cherished how straightforward she made the class. Advice-wise, just study everything on PPTs, and try to go to lecture to absorb the material better.

Professor Klein was the clearest, sweetest professor. She's very smart but really dumbs down the material for the class. I did barely any work and was able to get a good grade. You only need to go to the review sessions before the 3 exams and memorize absolutely everything in the power points the days leading up to the exam to do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Tests? Not many--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Easy A+. A true blessing for pre-law kids.

The class is a lot of information, but all the concepts are learnable and pretty easy. It is one of the easiest classes on campus. Klein is an incredibly smart professor who knows her stuff so well, that being said, lectures can be a bit dry.
I never showed up to class. For the last exam, I studied all the material 7 hours in advance. Literally all of it. Have fun :)
Emily Klein loves what she does. It's a pretty memorization heavy class, but you learn a lot of amazing things! Def take!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Prof. Klein is definitely the best professor I've ever had at Duke. Her exams are pretty easy and straightforward if you pay attention to her slides. Klein is also very approachable, passionate and knowledgable.

this class was harder than i thought. apparently it got harder this year because it used to be too easy. you need to memorize everything off of every slide for the tests. to put this into context, each test is around 5 chapters and each chapter has about 30+ slides. so, yea. 100s on the homework are a must because they add up too.

She's such a sweet person. The lectures are very clear, and she is always willing to help students outside of class. I recommend going to class though: it may be an easier class, but you still need to put the effort to get an A. Understanding and memorizing all the lecture slides are key for the tests. Overall, great professor.
Professor Klein explains things so thoroughly and cares about her students' learning. She is very willing to meet outside of class. Topics can be boring, but generally easy to understand.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Professor Klein was awesome, and EOS 101 was fantastic. The PowerPoint lecture method was very effective at communicating information, and she did an amazing job simplifying tough concepts. Take good notes and pay attention in class, and tests will be a breeze. Overall, EOS 101 was one of the most informative and interesting classes I've ever taken

Loved this class and Prof Klein is great.  She's always willing to meet with students and the TAs were really great.  Tests are straightforward multiple choice, just make sure to put in a few hours memorizing the slides. Textbook is not necessary.

Awesome professor. Clear, energetic lecturer with a witty sense of humor and a wealth of knowledge. Keeps class interesting with anecdotes and interesting examples. Her tests are straightforward, but you must memorize EVERYTHING on EVERY powerpoint slide - if you do, you'll be just fine!

Thought this class would be much easier than it was - don't necessarily have to attend lectures, although Prof. Klein is literally the sweetest woman out there and clearly passionate about the subject. Lots of homework and even two extra credit points to add to your final grade in the end, but the tests are pretty specific and tough.
Rocks for jocks with best teacher ever! Didn't attend a single lecture and got A+. Read slides with notes.

Material is pretty dull, but Klein does her best to get the class through it as painlessly as possible. She posts the powerpoints on sakai. Lectures help if you find the material difficult. Tests were harder than expected so make sure to study everything on the slides! Grading criteria is very clear with three major tests and minor homework q's.

If you're looking for the Easy A EOS101 class, you have to take hers. The tests are easy but you have to memorize the materials on power points beforehand. Also, don't get questions wrong on homework!
Good professor, very knowledgeable with good sense of humor. Not super demanding though it will definitely help to know the material before coming to class. I recommend.

If you need a NS or like Earth Science take this class! Attendance is not required, but it does help once test time comes around. Study for the tests and go to the review sessions. Klein is great and she is always willing to help you out.

Klein is super easy and nice. You don't even have to read the book to do well. Attendance isn't required but if you skip a lot your grade will prob suffer. Tests are easy AS LONG AS you study. I know lots of people who did poorly on tests because they thought they could do well without studying. Not true, but highly recommend this class for easy NS
Awesome teacher, super straighforward class. Literally EVERYTHING you need to know is on her slides. One of the nicest professors I've ever had.
Good teacher! She cares about us doing well in the class!! The tests are basically from the slides. Did not use the textbook and did well. It is important to memorize every slide for her class

Super easy, although it may not be too interesting for some people. You actually do have to study for the tests, though, but other than that the homeworks are easy (there were 3 short assignments) and there's also extra credit. Make sure to go to the review sessions before tests.

Very easy class. Reading the textbook isn't necessary, just go to class and review the slides the day before the exam. If you take it seriously, it's very easy. Prof is helpful and explains things clearly. Also material is fairly interesting. You don't have to put much time into the class outside of studying for tests (but do HW and extra credit!)

She's a nice lady. If you try then you'll get a decent grade. You don't have to make every single class but if you consistently skip you will see consequences in your grade. The exams are harder then you first think and there are only three, so it can be tough to pull up from a bad first grade. Just take it seriously and the class isn't that bad.
Prof. Klein teaches a wealth of interesting information in a clear and accessible matter. This class is very smooth and it's not hard to get a good grade.
Definitely one of the easiest classes at Duke. I wish I studied more because I got a B+ in it. Review the slides thoroughly, do the hw and extra credit and you'll get an A.

The easiest A+ I will ever receive at Duke. Class was totally optional and all you had to do was memorize all of the powerpoints the night before (which she puts online). She's a clear but boring and redundant lecturer so there's really no point in going to class. And you get 3 points of extra credit added onto your final grade. TAKE THIS CLASS!
Pretty happy to teach and very accommodating. course is easy if u study the slides before the exams

Easiest CLASS EVER! TAKE EOS 11 with HER! ITS A JOKE! NONETHELESS VERY INTERESTING. I feel badly for her because she is forced to make the class easy. LOVE YOU KLEIN! SHE IS AMAZING, FUNNY. and GIVES NO WORK! EASIEST CLASS EVER!

awesome teacher...really cares about her students.  3 exams, study for them or you'll feel like a complete idiot when you do poorly.  do all three extra credit assignments.  this class is cake as long as you don't completely ignore it.  going to class helps

Easiest class you will ever take. All the notes are online and the tests are simple memorization of the notes. Class attendence helps but isn't neccesary. And it that wasn't enough, she just gives extra credit away. Definately take this class.

This is not a difficult class, but you still have to study for the exams. Attending lecture is also important. The professor explains concepts very well and she doesn't focus on minor details. A lot of the issues are also very relevant (global warming, energy, floods, etc.) and are presented in a way that's more useful for non-scientists.

Alright, the class isn't a complete joke. Sure, it's an easy class with no actual work, but you've still gotta look over the material before the test and the questions aren't overtly obvious. But compared to the average Duke class, it's a welcome break. Definitely take it if you're looking for something that will free up your time.

Dynamic Earth with Klein is the easist class at Duke.  All the lecture powerpoints are online, exams are multiple choice, and she gives you up to 3 points extra credit on your final grade for the class.  Take this for a definite A.
Very Straight Forward, Just Go To Lecture
Great class. Amazingly nice lady who understands that most people are in the class to fill req.  Only 3 tests and no other work. Take it.

A great way to get a writing credit. Klein is like the teacher from the magic school bus show. the course probably only met 12 times all semester, and 5 of those were to go on field trips. You can't beat her, she makes you feel good about being alive.

EASY CLASS. Great class, no homework. I studied about 4-5 for each test. Klein is a really nice lady who really really wants everyone to understand the stuff. She knows that most people aren't really interested in EOS, they're just taking it to get science credit--she's cool about that. Gotta love a class nicknamed "Rocks for Jocks"
Emma is amazing! Very helpful in office hours for both class stuff and general recruiting advice.
Competitions are rigged. I'm convinced she meets in a secret underground bunker, vibe-checks the students, and picks winners based on astrology, favorite colors, and coolest names.
Emma is the goat.

The real problem is that expectations are unclear and she doesn't stick to them when she does give them to make her or her ta's life easier and then says she won't reply to student emails asking about it. Her lectures were pretty dry and most of the learning for her portion of the class is done through watching pre recorded videos outside of class
So funny, so smart, would absolutely take again. Great class if you need an extra half credit or have any interest in personal finance. Learned a lot of useful information!
Rate my professor reviews are skewed.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Emma pretty clearly has anger management issues, and can be extremely rude to students. She struggles to teach course content that must be applied to the class projects which make up the majority of the grade. Duke needs to find a new professor to teach its most important finance course.
emma is a great professor. she is rather intimidating in lectures, but once you flunch/attend office hours, she is really kind and geniune. super accomplished in her career as well. highly reccomend

you get out of econ256 what you put into it, she is obviously very smart and knowledgeable. since it is a huge class it is very easy to sit in back and coast and get a fine grade w/o paying much attention but can be very useful if you take advantage of it for finance prep
fairly easy half credit course, learn a bunch of useful stuff and she is very knowledgeable - few assignments that don't take too much time
She's really pragmatic and respects enthusiasm

Emma teaches first half of 256. Super boring lectures. She knows a lot about the financial markets and had a awesome career on wall street. Not a lot of work though. If you can last through 2.5 lectures once a week for the first half of the course until John takes over, its super interesting and a great intro to finance. Worked hard and got an A-.
If anything, interacting with her makes learning harder, not easier. She's condescending, dismissive, and seems to take personal offense when students ask questions.
If you dare to ask for clarification, prepare for an eye-roll, a sigh, or a dismissive remark that makes you regret even trying.
dont think she cares about her students at all. Went to her OH several times last sem but wasn't helpful. Class was ok but her attitude is condescending. feel like all her students are beneath her
While the class isn't inherently difficult in terms of content, the combination of her attitude, lack of clarity, and grading system makes it unnecessarily stressful.

Emma is condescending, disrespectful, and demeaning. Class isn't hard except the final quiz is worth a lot and has 20 random MC questions. People said it wasn't possible to get anything but As in this class but that's not true. Take ITP instead and pick a class that is actually going to help your GPA where you learn something interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Emma was unaccessible outside of class and her lectures were very boring and dry (i.e. projects an excel spreadsheet and starts reading numbers). She overall portrayed the financial industry in a poor light and was discouraging. John's second half of 256 is much better.
Consistently dismissive, unengaging, and condescending in class

No idea what happened to her ECON 256 this year, but this 0.5 cc seminar was chill and great. She wasn't condescending and lectures were actually quite interesting, especially the part on retirement savings. Course is easy, had several online participation quizzes and 2 mini projects. Useful bites of personal finance that could benefit a lifetime.

Pretty dry professor and comes off as condescending. The grading scale is super subjective because there isn't a set grading criteria for the group projects, which are a huge part of your grade. Final is a 20 question quiz. Not much room to make errors in this class without tanking your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Overall is a really dry lecturer that is overall not that helpful when students ask for help and treats students as if they are beneath her
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: She doesn't seem all that concerned about her student's wellbeing and learning. Doesn't teach all that well either, just kind of hostile
Terrible professor that shouldn't be teaching. Is persistently condescending in conversation and is passive aggressive or aggressive about everything, especially when you ask questions

Class time was pretty useless as all content was in videos we watched asynchronously -- pretty strange considering class is 3 hrs long. You're graded on few things, all by TAs who play clear favorites, especially with competitions. Emma's portion of the final quiz is a complete pain, and each question is worth 1% of your final grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Completely untransparent grading system that makes it incredibly hard to place what your grade is at. Professor is very insensitive regarding student concerns. Grading is incredibly subjective and based on what grader you get in terms of harshness.

Emma is very knowledgeable about the topics taught in 256 but gosh is she boring. Her videos were very hard to pay attention to and same with her lectures. She doesn't make them interactive or engaging, they're just straightforward, technical and packaged blandly. Definitely a good way to gauge interest in investment banking but John is much better

Emma's lectures are so dry. Definitely lean on the videos. Taking 256 is a great way to determine if you want to go into finance. The final (20 questions = 20% of your grade) didn't test high-level concepts and is too heavily weighted. Group projects are graded tough and there is no clear feedback or grading criteria.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: DO NOT take this class unless you are set on IB -- I thought she would teach concepts applicable to the general business world, but it is essentially just IB interview prep. Classes are deathly boring. She is also straight up mean to students and a living example of why you shouldn't go into finance if you have a soul. At least she's easy enough.

Lectures are fine but very helpful if you didn't take a decent personal finance in high school. Teaches the basics about investing which is helpful if your money is just sitting. Pass/fail class and really easy to pass if you show up and do the homework. I would take again because I learned a lot but if you know investment j skip this course.

Emma Raisel's lectures were consistently extremely unhelpful with the assignments for this class. We went over the simplest concepts in lecture and then proceeded to completely omit the actual skills necessary to succeed on the major competitions which accounted for a significant amount of our grade. She has a random grading scale. DO NOT TAKE
Class is easy A and modules are very helpful but she is extremely unfriendly and does not seem to care about her students at all. Rude, mean, and condescending.

Emma taught the nitty gritty terms of finance for the first half of 256. Her online HW modules were quite helpful and helped me study for finance interviews later down the road, but she is a boring lecturer. Hard to hear in a class of 200+ and she didn't engage at all. Easy grader, just pay attention. If you're finance take an elective with her.

This class had the easiest midterm I've taken at Duke (a fluke) and the hardest final I've taken, which was definitely curved. The class was interesting, and Prof. Rasiel is very good at explaining material useful for finance. However, the problem sets (worked on in groups of 3) and the final covered a lot of things we did not go over in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Rasiel is a nice person, but her lectures are very hard to sit through, especially since this class is 2.5 hrs long. For the group projects, make sure to work with people with some finance background, otherwise it is very hard to get a good grade on them. The final quiz worth 20% of the grade is based on random trivia from the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Let's be real - you're probably going to take this class if you wanna go into finance. Group projects, I mean they are what they are kinda hard but you figure it out sort of. You will get an A if you do the work, final quiz is pretty difficult so be in class and pay attention. Generally pretty manageable
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: For a half-credit class, Raisel sure did put in a lot of work. She's chill with assignments and understands that you've probably got a bunch of other things going on. That being said, this class is what you make of it. She teaches a lot of cool stuff, just make sure to listen. Also her sense of humor is fantastic, sad how only 3 people got it.

I really liked the course. She's a really cool professor and you'll learn a lot. She explains concepts clearly and she replies to emails quickly. She's no nonsense but that's what the real world is like - if anything, she's seriously doing us a favor.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great professor, very hard to have a prof like this in MEng program. Explain things detailly and encourage students to participate. Grading is fine but clearly not an easy A-level class. Impressed by how experience she is and how helpful even outside class. Highly recommend, and hope she can teach more class for MEng students in the future.

Professor Rasiel is incredibly helpful and knowledgeable. She is really attentive to student needs and very  accessible via email. Her Econ 256 class was challenging and time consuming, but it really does prepare students for interviews. The course could be organized a little better, but overall it was helpful. Professor Rasiel is amazing!

Came into this course expecting to learn about personal finance, did just about everything but that. Many of the lectures felt dragged on and irrelevant. I truly thought that this course had potential, given the lack of financial literacy many of us have in this generation. Disappointed to say that the course was lackluster without much substance.

Rasiel is stern, but nice. Extremely accessible via email. The class is not hard  if you put in enough work. The 3 projects are extremely time-consuming. Ultimately, the grading will work out, but you will need to spend a lot of time on this class.

Rude, mean, vague: overall a terrible person. Many terrible stories from personal encounters whether that be office hours or in class. Does not care about students and should not be a professor at any institution. Would think with resume, there'd be some level of professionalism, but nope. Unclear and bad advice.

This was the best class I've ever taken from a workload to practical knowledge gained perspective. The projects were quite challenging and fun, but make sure you have a team that is willing to be as invested as you are, otherwise they can become quite a pain. Emma is an excellent professor with a wealth of practical experience.

She is a very funny and entertaining lecturer. She knows what she is talking about and can explain concepts as simply or complexly as necessary. As long as you put in some work, you are on your way to getting an A.

A really bad professor that doesn't seem to care about her students at all. The class was an easy A regardless of two projects. However, what's the point of paying so much money and wasting three months in such a worthless class?

This class is not a high workload and does not necessarily offer a ton. However, it can be a laid-back class to take (apart from 2 major projects) while learning some applicable things for recruiting.

Don't bother enrolling in this class. You can teach yourself/sit in on the important lectures. Sometimes lectures are just panels or pointless. The grading is pretty arbitrary, and for group projects if you don't have a good group/upperclassmen help you're kinda screwed, bc you have to do really well on them/place to get an A. Emma is great tho

Lots of people come out of this class not ever wanting to have to do anything with finance again. Okay professor, who does care about her students, but goes pretty fast through the concepts. The 2hr30min stretch definitely wasn't for me. The final exam covered some concepts I don't remember being discussed.

This class is not worth taking unless you want to take it for the GPA boost. The fact that the Economics department does not count this class toward the Econ major depicts lack of information the course covers. If you're truly interested in finance, take ECON370.

I personally did not click with the material but she did an amazing job at giving us a background in finance. Her classes are lecture heavy but super useful. She's an absolute sweetheart and would recommend getting to know her in office hours or outside class. Very inspirational. One of the Duke's hidden treasures.

Not a huge fan of the class, since it's not very grounded in theory/mathematics. The grading on assignments is very volatile, since there is almost no partial credit, even though I somehow ended up with a good grade in the end. I learned a bit, but not as much as I would have wanted to in this class. She is an interesting woman to say the least.
Fantastic professor and course. Teaches you everything you need to know for finance recruiting - must take if you want to do IB or S&T. Grades based mostly on group projects and a final.

Take this class only if you're interested in a career in investment banking. I took it only because I have an interest in finance and want to be a better investor, but I have little interest in a career in investment banking. You will work on a couple of group projects which can be frustrating, but they will help with IB recruiting.

Take this class if you want a job on Wall Street and have no knowledge about finance. Do everything that she says, she KNOWS what she's talking about. Emma goes above and beyond to always be accessible and help you out with anything and everything. She makes it tough to get  B- or even B in this class, but you also have to work to get an A.

Rasiel is a phenomenal professor. She connects every topic to current and historical financial events. If you're interested in finance, you will find the material fascinating. Put in effort on all the problem sets, study for the final, and an A-/A is doable. But just know that about 80% of the material in this class relates to S&T, not M&A /banking
Emma's a clear lecturer and a pretty helpful professor. But grading is as arbitrary and volatile as the subject she teaches.
You will do well if you have a strong background in finance, even if you don't go for classes. But it is good to know Emma well though.

This is one of the easiest classes in "Econ". Weekly PSets are straightforward, plug and chug, as are the exams. Rasiel is clearly smart enough to make this a challenging and worthwhile class, but does not seem to care enough to put in the effort. I wish I'd just read a couple of books on it instead of spending a semester learning this material.

Very good class, you almost have to take it if you want a future in finance. Participation is essential - try to answer at least 3 - 4 questions per class, as it can have a pretty big effect on your final grade. Lots of group work, and the final exam isn't that bad. Problem sets are your BEST friend. Also, try getting to know her outside of class.

Rasiel is pretty overrated as a professor. I came into this class very motivated and was disappointed. Her lectures are useless, she essentially just stands at the front of the room and spouts random statistics about financial markets, which gets old after a couple weeks. Problem sets are definitely the most useful part of the class.

Emma Rasiel is awesome!  She is interesting, funny, and really good at explaining tough concepts.  Her class is amazing and I would recommend it for anyone, whether or not they want to go into finance.  Be warned: her curve is tough to beat.

She's very good at teaching and answering questions. She definitely knows what she's doing. Look at her credentials. She ridiculously legit. If you want a future in finance or banking, you need to know her.
I found that she was very clear and interesting. If you want to take a class with her, do it! You won't regret your choice.

Great Teacher and extremely clear. Teaches from a real world perspective as opposed to lecturing on theory. If you are interested in the Sales and Trading side of Investment Banking, this is the class for you.
great professor and class overall. very direct method of teaching and open to questions. holds review session and office hours and is very accessible to students.

Rasiel knows her stuff and is more interesting than any econ professor I have had at Duke. She has real world finance experience, and she follows the markets closely. She incorporates real world applications to her lectures, making her class interesting and very useful to students pursuing finance internships. Definitely recommend this class.

She's a good teacher who is willing to make her concepts crystal clear for her students. She uses her own little note/textbook but you can't get an A only using that. Seriously, do the problem sets, go to class and it's not that hard. She throws no curveballs, no tricks. Don't miss out on this class. You'll learn a lot about bonds, equities, etc.
One of the best professors at Duke.

Professor Rasiel worked at Goldman Sachs as a trader for several years so has a strong financial background. She was easily accessable outside of class and she brought in a lot of speakers from the financial sector. She's interesting, engaging and as long as you put in some effort and do the extra credit you'll get an A.

Found prof very pleasant/ personable.  Those in 55 who find lecture boring don't know what they are in store for in some upper level econ's.  Even though busy with departmental duties was great about responding to emails, etc.  No surprises on tests.
fairly interesting course.  she is really nice, and clear most of the time
very funny.  held weekly reviews on sundays at students' request after first mid-term.  second mid-term and final- really easy.  sticks to ppt notes during lecture.

This was one of the boring-est classes I've ever taken. Dr. Rasiel lectures the entire time, and she doesn't write much on the board, so you need to listen carefully to what she says. It might be good to bring an ipod or something to record the lectures, because it's hard write all the impt things she says down. The homeworks are short + easy.

She is one of the most helpful professors I have ever met. She answered every blackboard discussion post and often stayed after during lecture.  Her ppt slides are really helpful and although she is fairly boring during lecture, she makes you understand the material.  The diff. of her exams vary.  Love the British humor. She knows her stuff!
my worst ever econ instructor ... terrible sense of humor... but class not too hard.
No Comments
Very boring lectures, and attempts at humor. Lectures are good in content, but she needs to move through them faster. tests are very fair, and she is very helpful as a teacher outside of class

I loved this class because she made it very interesting.  The midterms can be seen as difficult for some, but you just have to realize that these are different tests than high school tests.  Get interested in the material and understand the concepts and you will be fine.
good class,good prof,bad final which screwed me up.
Good class
Amazingly good teacher.  Teaches to the tests, makes sure her students do well. Makes a subject that could be terrible rather interesting.
I don't like her as a person or as a teacher, but she is clear about what you need to know and the class isn't hard. Plus she gives a ton of bonus points.

She's really entertaining and smart... everyone sleeping is more due comfortable seats in the theater. I like her a lot, and she doesn't want the class to do poorly. A kind of difficult midterm was followed by an easy one. thumbs up
Great teacher.  She made the subject matter interesting and understandable.  Her tests are straightforward and fair.
Good professor--made the class a lot easier than it previously was. Helpful and knowledgable and good for the level.
Too easy, waste of a class too bad its a requirement

she was very helpful in office hours, and her TAs were great.  sometimes the problem sets took sooooo long, but other than that, the class is not very difficult.  take her if you have to take this class for econ/pps major.

She's a great professor and had some excellent TAs.  It's a big class so if you're having trouble understanding concepts or getting HW done, go to office hours (hers or TAs)!  She wants her kids to do well and writes straightforward tests.

She took a class that was very hard under the prior professor and made it ridiculously easy. She's very nice, has a funny British sense of humor, and her online notes are superior to the awful textbook. Her notes are so easy to understand they make lectures too slow and boring. You can skip them.
She's so nice, eager to help students. Her tests are not hard compared to the past exams, and if you attend the lecture, and do the homeworks, it is easy to get good grade
She made this class much more difficult than it had to be.  Her exams do not test what you learn in class, but your ability to think like an economist.

She is good-natured, eager to help students, and very clear in her teaching of the material and in communicating the expectations of the class.  I fell asleep each class because lectures moved slowly, but I won't hold that too much against her.  Learning from her was a pleasant experience.

If you are not an Econ major, this class is miserable.  Lectures are completely powerpoint and hard to follow because she clicks through them so fast.  Tests in this class are TERRIBLE because they do not measure your knowledge of the material, but simply your ability to think like an economist.

So...in a class of several hundred people, it's hard to connect with students, but she's very helpful if you can get to her. She also has a very dry, british sense of humor that makes the class go quicker.

Dr. Parks is a great professor for freshmen! She is very understanding and consistently allowed the class to push deadlines or have extensions when we had exams in other classes or busy weeks. There are 2 papers in the class worth 70% of your grade. You have plenty of time to complete both assignments and she is very available to give feedback!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Amazing professor. While the content of the course can be difficult, she is awesome. Caring of current and past students, entertaining, and all around great.

Professor Parks is an awesome professor; she really cares about her students and wants them to progress in writing. My favorite part of the class was the content. Rather than just reading a book and learning how to write an analysis, we learned how to write scientific papers about an incredibly interesting topic. 2 big papers, one is a group paper.

Dr. Parks was a great professor for writing. I was scared going in and seeing how heavily graded the two main papers were, but she really does take into consideration everyone's individual work and how much you do. Readings could grow a bit tiresome, but they could be used in your paper, so it was definitely relevant. 100% recommend!!
Dr. Parks is an outstanding teacher who genuinely cares about her students. Her class is incredibly informative and engaging. I would highly recommend it to anyone with an interest in neuroscience.

Professor Parks is one of the most engaging professors I've had. The courseload for Neuroscience in Society was very intimidating at the beginning of the semester, however, as the semester went on, it gradually decreased. She teaches you how to research and write academically. Would recommend, especially for those considering pre-med or engineering

Dr. Parks is an incredibly genuine person, whose bright demeanor and attitude bring joy. However, the class is very work intensive with activities and evaluative papers, which are graded harshly (although there are many opportunities for feedback). Class is great for med-oriented students who don't want as easy of a class as other writing classes.

Dr. Parks is a super engaging professor who truly teaches you how to write. More reading and writing at at the start but slows down as you start writing the longer projects. The projects did feel graded slightly harsh at times for a Writing 101 class, but this did not take away from the learning experience regardless.

Dr. Parks is amazing, the class is not too difficult and she really cares. There are small assignments due before every class (outline, small 200-word response, find 2 pieces of evidence and notes, etc.), but the class is mostly graded on two big papers that we take our time through. One is individual and one is group paper. Best class I've taken.
She is one of the best professors I have ever had.  This class is the best Writing 101 class!

Very very sweet professor, I enjoy her as a person, however very expectations are very unclear and the grading criteria was very inaccessible. She is an extremely hard grader especially for a writing 101 class.

Super caring, accessible outside class, goes out of her way to help students.
You'll need to research/write (def doable) but you can get feedback from the first paper, and she wants you to succeed more than she cares about grades, so communicate to get help. You learn interesting stuff. Would take again
Go to class btw. Mornings are tough :(
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Parks is a really nice person. However, WRITING 101 class this semester was very difficult, and it felt like she graded papers very harshly
Easy class, but she is very hyper and overwhelming. Only two papers so not hard to do well, but very unclear feedback and review process.

Dr. Parks is one of the kindest professors that I've had the privilege of having. She makes time to meet outside of class to discuss assignments and provides incredible feedback. Out of all of the Writing101 courses, it sounds like this course requires the most writing, but I argue that taking this class from her will best prepare you as a writer.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I took Dr. Parks for her "Backstage Science" class, and I think she's an incredible teacher. Super helpful, very kind and generous, and has very clear goals for each step of the course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: While she's v v kind, caring, over-caffeinated, and charming, she fails to provide feedback and minimizes time outside of the class. You won't get much out of this class at all.
