It's very easy, though (low workload), and you can get carried by your team for sure. The one semester-long project is drawn out, making class unrewarding. Easy class!

(Backstage Science) Dr. Parks was great! Super enthusiastic about the class and really put in a lot of work to be accessible and give feedback on our work. Super interesting class, although a lot more group-based than I expected.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: Dr. Parks is one of the most thoughtful and caring professors I have ever had. She wants to get to know you on a personal level and is more than willing to adapt deadlines to the needs of the class. I took Backstage Science with her, and it was one of my favorite classes. She is very passionate about science and writing. Definitely take her class!

My writing class was backstage science and the class was pretty easy, and Dr. Parks is one of the best professors I have had. She is so caring, very lenient with due dates, and actually cares about producing meaningful writing and developing your skills over your grade.

I took this class in Spring 2020 when all Writing 101s were S/U. Dr. Parks made the 8:30 experience much more enjoyable than I thought it would be. Her class structure and feedback process allow for creativity and walk you towards earning the grade you want. I truly enjoyed this class and feel as though it made me a better writer.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Parks is a gem. She made an 8:30 more than worth it. Her technique to teach writing are really effective and she makes herself accessible to answer questions. You can tell she's passionate about what she does and cares about her students.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: All effort. If you put in effort in your papers (go to writing studio and discuss your papers with her) you will get an A. Most students get an A or A-. It's also extremely interesting to work on the final paper - you really learn a lot about neuroscience. Her in-class instruction is filled with activities to keep you interested. Dr. Parks is great

Emily Parks is a really amazing professor. Her class is very engaging and she is always there to help. Also very understanding when it comes to issues that might prevent you from meeting a deadline. The essays do take a lot of time but are very rewarding. Class is essentially 2 essays and participation.

Dr. Parks is amazing and by far the most caring professor I have had. While her writing101 is more difficult and requires more work than other writing101s, there is a reason people fight for this class. It is a class planned with every detail in place and Dr. Parks is always wanting to improve. She is an absolutely wonderful professor and person!!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Dr. Parks is an amazing professor and person. Her Neurolaw writing class is interesting, there are only two papers, and the class atmosphere is very welcoming and comfortable. The second paper is long but done with a peer: like a real scientific paper. This class prepares you for social/natural science academic writing, she'll inspire you, take it!
Super fun, engaging professor. Take her writing 101 neurolaw if given choice.

Dr. Parks is by far the best teacher I've had at Duke! The topic was neurolaw, and as an expert in the field, her enthusiasm for neuroscience and its potential uses in the courtroom made the class. The workload was appropriate and manageable, and she makes herself extremely accessible for any help. Definitely take a course with Parks!
Such a sweet woman! Definitely the only person I could ever survive an 8:30 with! Academically, I also feel like she has really helped me improve my writing.

Dr. Parks is a really nice person and a great professor. She makes class interesting and you learn a lot. This writing 101 was neurolaw which was fascinating. There are a lot of readings but it's really not too bad. She wants you to succeed and will help you become a better writer.

I LOVE Dr. Parks. The class I took was focused on neurolaw, but the writing skills she taught us are applicable to all scientific/research/academic writing. She was always kind and truly cared about the class; it was obvious how much effort she put in to the course lessons.

Dr. Parks was super engaging, fun, and sweet! She was really interested in the topic of neurolaw and sparked my interest as well. There were 2 papers; one 3 page and one 10 page (with a partner), which was easy to work through. She highlights the revision period. Definitely not an easy A, but I improved my writing a lot and ended up with an A-.

Not that much reading compared to other 101s, and really interesting discussion (neuroscientific, ethical, etc.) So passionate about both the subject material and her students; I would definitely want to take a writing class with her again-- and I hate academic writing.

Dr. Parks seems to do it all and I admire her for it. Pros: she really reads your rough drafts to get to know your writing and provides tips, also understands if you're a minute or 2 late to class, and little homework. Cons: the lectures were a tad dry, the readings she assigns at the beginning weren't necessary, she grades tougher than expected.

She is so positive, passionate, and invested in making her students better writers. She is also so happy and willing to work with you outside of class. If you put in work, edit your drafts, and go to the writing studio, you will do great!

Great professor, really cares about her class and her students. Super accessible outside of class and is very knowledgable and passionate about her field. Reading assignments are manageable and writing assignments are drafted throughout the semester so they don't become stressful. Overall wonderful class!
Her way of teaching is very faced paced and note taking is almost impossible in her class. She seems sweet and a nice person but it's almost impossible to learn with the way she teachers the class
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I love this class. I'm not even done yet and already writing about it! I find Professor Sposeto to be an engaging lecturer and great teacher. If things seem unclear, she explains them in English to ensure total clarity. If you do the homework and assigned work, you'll be completely find. There's never a dull moment, and I'll miss this class dearly

I find it rather unfair the critique some students assign her. A very fair grader and if you do your work and study you should be good. Is extremely energetic and happy, something I value very highly. Is clear in her methods.

Horrible teacher, as hard and bad as you can get for Italian. In class she isn't helpful (very confusing lecturer) and she assigns a ton of busy work that she actually collects and grades for correctness. Most Italian teachers give full credit for completion for HW, Cultural, and Participation, but she grades very hard and makes the class miserable

I'm not sure if something happened over the past few years since she got such great reviews in the past, but she is the worst. Avoid Sposeto at all costs. Everyone takes italian for the requirement and she thinks her students need to be fluent by the end of the semester. She assigns more work than any other class I have and isn't clear about h/w

Im biased because I think the language req is pointless but this class/her is horrible. The Italian department is a joke. This class is full of busy work. They have very strict attendance rules even if you have say a grad school interview. She is a hard grader. She is openly super feminist. So if you are girl then you will do good otherwise avoid!

Pretty good at explaining the mechanics of Italian. From America, speaks perfect Italian and English which is extremely helpful. Particular about grading. One of the better professors in the department.
Makes italian fun, one of the harsher graders in Italian 1 I think, but A- is fairly easy to attain

Great teacher, everything is super clear and tests reflect exactly what you learn in class. If you take Italian 01, take it with sposeto! She makes learning about culture fun and interesting and although you have to meet 4 times a week, it goes by pretty quickly.

Great prof. Makes the class as painless as possible. Your grade will be pretty much equal to the effort you put in. She's not a really tough grader but you do need to try on the graded written assignments. Other than that, if you don't totally suck at the language you'll do fine on the tests. Did I mention she's really hot?
She is way cool. Towards the end she starts to lose focus and hardly talks in italian. she's really helpful and knows what she is talking about.she is a picky grader but it helps you learn more.

The best professor I've ever had. The reading workload is quite heavy, but you don't need to go through every page to participate successfully. Prof. Ho is excellent at guiding discussions in meaningful directions and allowing the ideas in the syllabus to unfold naturally. He's also very funny and inspiring. You really should not miss his class.
Aside from the boatload of readings, lectures was very interesting, prof very knowledgeable about everything, and approachable.
Brilliant prof.

Honestly the class itself wasn't bad. However, there are a ton of readings to do. His lectures are very confusing and he doesn't tell you what he wants from you at all. The class is on global culture but we only talk about asian culture especially china. The syllabus has no dates. Don't get me wrong, he is a really nice guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I really thought that the readings were interesting (although long), and as long as you show up and participate you will do well. There is very little actual work in the class except for a paper at the end. Classes can sometimes be painful and long to get through since nobody wants to participate.

This was honestly a perfect class for a science major. Fulfills almost everything you could think of (writing, seminar, cultural exploration, etc.), Ho is brilliant (Harvard alum), and class is very laid back. Participation needed if you want him to know you and give you a good grade. Readings every week, which are interesting but long.

Professor Ho is an amazing professor who is super knowledgeable and interesting. The materials were hard but he could always make everything clear in his lectures. You should be able to earn a good grade as long as you put in the effort. But I would only suggest you taking the class if you were considering Culanth major or minor.

Enseng is a pretty interesting guy...CulAnth 117 (Global Culture) was once a week and it was brutal to get through (he really only prepared for like 30 min of the 2 hour session)...very low work though (1 page of typing per week) and he turned it into an International Finance class which made it pretty interesting

This course has more daily assignments than many of the other languages offered, however, you will be thankful for having these points in the gradebook. Endo-sensei gives straight-forward and useful feedback, so participating in class is a good idea. Setting up meetings is also encouraged. Put in work and you will be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Here's objective view: 1. Homework and project and skits and lot of things that require everyday work.  But just know that they are not hard. 2. Requires participation. Grade might seem harsh when you FIRST take the course but when u get used to the test format (cuz they never change), if you at least, study japanese 11.5hr/day, u will get 90.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Really demanding as far as keeping up with the classwork and expectations - but very nice if you show you are trying your best. Very very energetic
Great teacher! Can be a little harsh when correcting mistakes or answering questions, but still makes sure everyone understands. Very funny! Be prepared to work hard because it is a lot of work.

I enjoyed having Endo sensei. Yes, she can be strict and is serious about the material, but she is a funny and enthusiastic teacher. The fact that she said "ne" all the time as a filler word bothered me a lot initially, but I got over it. She taught well and helped make me confident with speaking Japanese.

Endo sensei is an amazing Japanese professor. She's really good at teaching you Japanese IN JAPANESE. I would choose her section over any other section. She may seem strict but she's actually kinda funny. TAKE HER CLASS.
Endo sensei expects a lot from you, especially after you've been in Japanese for a year. But she's extremely helpful and (tries to be) funny. Work hard and ask questions when you need to.
Endo Sensei is awesome!  She has a sick sense of humor that is simply hilarious.  She does not tolerate lazy people or people that don't try.  Go to class and do the HW and you are golden!

Always willing to take questions and explain things again (outside of class) if you're uncertain about something. Encourages involvement with Japanese culture outside of class. No tolerance for laziness/excuses and very strict grading & absence/tardiness policies. Getting better at not interjecting "ne" every other word. Overall, good professor :).

Endo sensi is great! JPN2 is basically the same format as 1, except more compositions and a speech involved. Endo sensei is always great at explaining Japanese grammar and she really believes in you. The only reason people thinks she is "scary" is because she really expects a lot out of you and is disappointed if you don't meet her expectations.

Endo Sensei is one of the best teachers ever.  She is funny and will always make time to help you out.  As long as you study and put the time into it the class is a piece of cake.  She knows when someone failed to study and thats when she gets upset.  So just study.  You are going to Duke right?
Interesting class and Endo-sensei does a good job of teaching it.  She can be pretty tough on those who makes mistakes speaking in class though so be prepared.
As other people said, she lacks people skills and the lectures are really boring and the same format everyday. Grades rather harshly. Just hope you don't get her for interviews.

Very rude instructor.  I took this class as a freshman.  When I didn't do so well in my interview test, she had the gall to ask me how I even got into Duke University.  She's a competent woman, but she has lousy people skills.

The thing to know about Endo sensei is she expects alot out of you. If you're not a natural linguist she will be disappointed in the interview when you have no clue what she just asked you. But if you're ok with that then I can't fault her. She's excited about the subject and very willing to help. Just don't take this class expecting it to be easy.

Like all language classes, memorization and practice is the key for success.  Overall, class is somewhat dry.  Just hope you have some funny people in your class; they definitely make class much more interesting.  Probably easier than other languages classes, and seems to curve moderately.  No matter what, you HAVE to attend classes.
Endo Sensei makes the class so interesting for you. She is clear and helpful and assigns useful homework!

Endosensee is quite a good language teacher.  Japanese is a difficult language however, so don't take it unless you're interested and willing to put in the work.  It's an unusually fun class--I highly recommend!
Smart, but horrible horrible teacher. No high level considerations, just derivation and detail after detail. Would not take another class with her.

lectures uninterpretable. copies her own notes onto the whiteboard (full of mistakes) and ask students to LaTeX what she copied and post on course website several weeks after class or never. hw requirement can change even after you've completed them. Attacking back and being very defensive when many  students complain on course forum.

She has lots of research experience and a famous advisor... but as a teacher, she is absolutely worthless. Does not have any notion of what it means to convey new concepts to others. Tons of errors in her lectures. Very disorganized. Most importantly, does not give any coherent introductions or high level overviews of topics.

Her presentations are rushed, disorganized, illegible, and full of mistakes in equations and concepts. She gets very flustered if any questions are asked and assigns homework problems which she hasn't worked through and therefore doesn't thoroughly know the answers or approaches to. Finally, she blames the class for mistakes she makes on the board.

Writes a bunch of illegible stuff on the board. Makes mistakes and then says, "Oh, you know what I mean". Homeworks are based on one really specific topic that's glossed over in class. I don't think anyone in the class knows what's going on.
deriving formulas all the time, with ambiguous notations throughout. little effort spent on explaining and defining the problems and notations

Jack is a super nice guy! He is always available outside class.He wouldn't mind explaining stuff all over again if you didn't understand it in the first place. Although people think grad students, like himself, aren't clear, he is clear and is always open and cares about you. He's a  tough grader in labs, but he is always willing to help you.

Jack is really nice and funny, and his lectures are easy to follow. He makes himself pretty available outside of class, but the class itself is not long enough to cover - and especially practice - all of the (difficult) material that he is forced to teach. Very tough grader on tests and especially on labs. Hard class but solid teaching.

Jack was such a nice guy and was really clear and concise during lecture. I would definitely recommend going to class, because he was really entertaining but also helped clarify things in the homework. I also went to the help room and he was always really helpful and was available outside of class for help. He is also super cool!

Jack Enyeart is just a really nice guy. As a graduate student he is open to criticism and is eager to learn from and along with his students. He is supremely approachable and is a very fair grader. He may not have all the answers immediately but he will do his very best to address your queries in a clear and concise manner.

Ennis is an interesting guy and easy to work with. Fair grader. Not the lightest writing 101 workload, but also not the heaviest. He gets really into the course, which can be good or bad, depending on how into it you are.

A nice person and a nice grader. Sometimes I feel like I'm turning in the worst essay in the world, and still end up with 18/20. Though at first I wasn't interested in the topic (pirates, pilgrims and pagans), as I learnt more about the subject (through the huge amount of readings) it became more interesting.
Boring class. Not the easiest writing 20 nor the hardest.

Professor Ennis is a nice guy who really cares about his students. He gives A LOT of readings which can be a little dense/long, but you don't really have to do them as long as you know their general idea. His paper topics are super random and difficult to write about. Overall, pretty easy class, but boring.
Had him for writing 20, Pirates Pagans and Pilgrims. Good class, a lot of reading, tho sort of interesting for the most part. really nice guy and not a terribly harsh grader either.

Great teacher. Very generous grader. The work is very manageable and the readings are never too overwhelming. He is a very nice and easy going person. He knows a lot of about the subject and is helpful if you need help with essay topics, sources, etc.
Good Professor.  Actually felt like my writing improved.  Very helpful, writing we did was useful.  Good class.

Ennis is a good guy and generally a very helpful teacher. My only complaint is that at times I felt like he knew what grade he was going to give me before he read my paper. However, that's not to say he's an extremely difficult grader. He's fun, very nice, very knowledgeable about his topics, and very willing to help. Show him drafts of papers!

Ennis is a really good guy, and he sincerely wants to help you become a better writer.  I took a SciFi writing 20 with him w/o knowing what the actual class was about (it said "Alternate Histories, and I'm a history major).  Take him for a good writing 20.  He doesn't grade that hard, but make sure you write what he wants to see/hear.

Great professor. Will try to accommodate any problems that might arise, meaning you can ask for an extension on papers if you have a good reason.Made W20 a nice experience.Genuinely helpful and nice. Knows what he's talking and teaching about. He's sorta' like Indiana Jones:)

VERY nice person, very understanding, easy grader.  Once I had a bunch of exams and a writing 20 paper due on the same day.  I emailed him, and he pushed the deadline back for the entire class!  Easy grader and lets you rewrite papers.  On top of that, just a very interesting guy who knows a lot about the subject and is very engaging.

Wonderful professor who is always very enthusiastic and engaging about what he's teaching. Knows a lot about his subject (and others) that he brings up in class. Manages to balance the class very well between lecture and discussion. Interesting reading assignments for class. Grades papers fairly. Enjoyed this class very much!
Very great professor, unfortunately this is his last year teaching.

Prof. English is awesome. His class is easy, interesting, and doesn't take a lot of work as long as you pay attention and interact in class. He's an easy grader, assignments arent too tough and English is such a nice guy. He's a former MD so he's very smart, but not pretentious, and here because he likes to teach and enjoys working with students

Dr. English is a really interesting professor and a great guy, and if you are interested in the topic you will enjoy the class.  Assignments are not hard but require you to work. Grading by him is certainly fair and straightforward.  He assigns a lot of reading but not impossible.  Only drawback to the course is that you never get to debate.

Really wonderful lecturer, he loves teaching and loves the topics that he teaches in his classes. very friendly and nice in person, interesting to listen to. his classes require a ton of reading that you have to do for class, but they're all very interesting.

Professor English rocks.  He is definitely one of the best professors at Duke.  He got a teaching award this year.  He is a very fair grade.  The assignments are long but reasonable.  As long as you put into effort into the class, you are sure to get good grades(at least B+).  I would definitely take more class with him in the future if possible.

Very nice man and always willing to clarify problems. Felt that his grading was somewhat ambiguous at times, and the lectures tended to be pretty boring. There was a ton of reading for a non-majors course...

Although this course requires a LOT of reading, most assigned books/articles strongly apply to the class discussion topics, and most are actually interesting to read. Professor English was a very strong lecturer (none of the lectures seemed like torture). Plus, he's a very easy grader. I highly recommend this course to anyone interested in medicine

I have taken both 104 and 190C with English. I am pretty sure he is an idiot. I have gotten A's in both classes so Im not disgruntled. He IS a physician. His approach to the material is very straight forward as in What happened, when? He requires no real analysis which is what makes history interesting. Take a history class with a REAL professor.

Had him for food, fat, and famine. Great teacher with a great sense of humor. Research modules are the only time-consuming part. Topic is trivial and easy to understand from day one. Interesting pts. Highly recommend especially for history majors. Very interactive class.

i don't know how someone could be disapointed in this class...it is a thorough review of 20th century medicine...the readings are right on point- althought there is a lot, this class is great and English is a very good teacher...if you take this class and like it, I think it's a better indicator that chemistry or bio that medicine is for you.
Very disappointed in this class. Boring.

History of 20th Century Medicine is one of the best classes I have taken here.  He is a good lecturer, not too strict about attendence, a very fair grader, and the readings are very interesting, although there is a lot.  I highly recommend this class for anyone thinking about a career in medicine.

The class is incredibly participation-dependent. Make sure you go to office hours and get to know Dr. Mlyn well.

Outside of that, Mlyn has a genuine passion for the class and topic. He is willing to spend so much time with you and is very open to other ideas, and wants you to have opinions that are different than his. Would recommend the class.
tough grader with lots of confusing feedback
Mlyn was a very harsh grader and did not make my experience comfortable.

Has favorites, and essentially made office hours mandatory for a good participation grade. Unclear grading policies, and puts too much stock in student behavior. Do not recommend, find another class!!

Cares deeply about the subject of his course and does an excellent job of making space for different perspectives and encouraging disagreement. Readings can be heavy, and grading criteria for writing assignments are vague sometimes. For the two exams, just pay attention and take notes in class and you'll be fine. Would recommend this class!

Dr. Mlyn is great to talk to and has engaging lectures, but the stress of grading and competing for participation made the class rough. I felt like he just expected way too much from the class. No clear grading rubric and lots of disparities on directions for assignments.

Dr. Mlyn's class felt disorganized and stressful. His lecture slides were poorly made, the grading lacked clear rubrics, and the environment became toxic and competitive over who could meet with him the most. He played favorites, and the course ruined my FOCUS experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Super interesting person and great lecturer, I really enjoyed all the class topics. Good amount of reading and there's a midterm, 2 forum event posts, final paper (relatively long), and take home final. Vague grading rubric but take notes on what he says in class and that guides your papers/exam answers. No surprises on the exams, would recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Eric Mlyn is an amazing professor! He is very engaging and his lectures are not boring---even when the material is dry. However, there is a lot of reading to do for this class (which he says he cut down). This is typical for classes in this discipline, so just keep that in mind. He is also a tough grader and doesn't have super clear rubrics.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Nice guy, but it doesn't feel like a seminar class. He talks a lot, and there are lots of writing assignments with ambiguous grading criteria. He gives you random reflection assignment without specific dates.

(CESC201) Dr. Mlyn is a caring professor who cares a lot about his work. He is genuinely interested in what his students have to say and values opinions that differ from his own. Class isn't graded on much, but the mid-term offers a lot of flexibility and the final is take home. Readings were pretty interesting as well!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Mlyn is excellent. His lectures are so engaging, there is intriguing class discussion, and not an overload of assignments. There is a lot of reading required, but they are usually interesting. For all assignments, make sure to pull from readings and class discussions and you should do well. I highly recommend taking a class with Mlyn.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Mlyn is awesome! Expectations for the class were pretty clear, and his lectures are very insightful. You definitely have to put time into the class, to prep for lectures and exams but it is doable for any type of student and there is a lot for you to gain through the class.
I loveeed this class. There were a lot of readings, but they were usually interesting. The classroom had a great, casual environment, and the discussions were always fun. Take this class!
Good class.

A great professor! He might seem too hard at first but he is very good and not as tough as his appearance may suggest. All you have to do is go to class EVERY TIME and listen closely to what he says will be on the test. He will never mislead you. Just by paying attention to the material that he likes, you save yourself reading useless stuff.

Really nice, very clear professor. I, personally, loved his teaching style; he highlighted what was important and made things easy to digest. Definitely need to participate, and does not like it when you are late.

Took this class through my FOCUS program and loved it. Eric is a great professor who I plan on staying in touch with throughout my years at Duke. Readings are lengthy and required but there is only one test and it does not count for that much of your grade. The work is fair and participation is really needed if you want an A.

awesome af she really cares about her students and her job - ppl who say they were forced to overshare didn't really get the point of the class, the class is supposed to help freshman connect with each other while we all get thru super new, uncomfortable things. participation matters a ton, but that really just means showing up and being a human
goat but MAN were some of the papers long ahh. caught me off guard how much time I spent writing compared to studying for my stem classes 😭

MY QUEEN👸. Sheryl is kind, understanding, and eager to know you on a deeper level. I would recommend her class to SOME people: those who are vulnerable, willing to connect, open-minded, and feedback-oriented. If you aren't ready to get deep and emotional, this class isn't for you. If you are, Sheryl and her class will bless your first year💙
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Sheryl ruined my mental health and is a terrible, negative addition to Duke University. Her writing class tought me very little all while putting so much stress on me, forcing me to write about trauma i did not want to share in this class.

Sheryl is an amazing individual and truly cares for your wellbeing and learning in this class. She is the sweetest soul and always available for flunch/walks. Love love love this girl please take her class! (plus she brings snacks for friday classes)

I LOVE SHERYL SO MUCH. Truly anyone who had Sheryl will not hesitate to tell you how lovely she is. She is so accessible and loves going on walks + doing yoga + getting lunch with students whenever she can. This class is extremely introspective and you learn so much about yourself through her methods. You will never have a teacher like her again!

Sheryl is amazing and is the most caring professor I have ever met; her writing101 is a course I'll remember for the rest of college. She takes time to check in on us and care for her students, and stresses the importance of introspection and empathy for her writing course. It's very intimate and personal, but fulfilling. May not be for everyone.

I always stalk rate my professor and had to make an account to talk about Sheryl. She is the best teacher I have ever had. I always worry about grades but you will do well if you are vulnerable and care about your writing. Class is so fun, you make such strong connections with other kids, and she brings snacks every Friday! This is a must take.

This woman is one of the sweetest, kindest, most inspiration souls I've ever known. She cares so deeply about each and every student and encourages your best work. It's an extremely introspective class, we get snacks, do yoga, and so many other things that help make it such a unique experience. If you love yourself, take this amazing writing class!

If you land Sheryl for Coming of Age and Happiness, congratulations! You have essentially found gold!

If you're a person with a soul, you will love this class. I promise the negative reviews are people who struggle with themselves. 

Sheryl is genuinely the greatest professor I've ever had. 

Live, Laugh, Love Sheryl.

My writing class was a mixed experience. The professor, Sheryl, cared but was strict. She put a lot of pressure on us, and the feedback was limited. The class structure was good, but it felt like too much work at the end. I didn't like the emphasis on oversharing. Some found it boring, and grading was tough. It had its pros and cons.

Sheryl is a supportive and kind person and really cares about her students. The Case Study in this class is a lot of work and I wish it could be more anonymous because you have to share really personal things to people who you barely know. The grading is unpredictable - I had no idea what my grade was until I saw the final grade in DukeHub.

I took this writing class to improve my writing skills, but left feeling frustrated and discouraged. The professor was very strict with the curriculum. I think the class also struggled to get me to write, and I struggled to conform and share. Sheryl is caring tho I would not recommend this class to people looking to improve their writing skills.

Sheryl put wayyyyyy too much pressure on me during case study time. I had to pull all-nighters to get done while moving with the super limited feedback she gave me.  I liked the class structure and what we wrote about, but I think sheryl needs to be more accommodating and put less emphasis on one asisgnemnt.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: I am not a fan of Dr. Sheryl. I think the class forces all of its work on you at the very end of the semester. It also made me very uncomfortable as I felt pressured to overshare and "trauma dump". I also don't think the class helped develop my writing skills which was something I'd hoped to have gained from this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Sheryl is a great teacher. Class discussions were fascinating, and the snacks were awesome. Sheryl also cultivates a great class community. I did find the class incredibly boring and the grading to be incredibly harsh. Would not take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Sheryl is so sweet most of the time, and if you show up with a positive attitude, you can make a great connection with her. The class isn't easy though. Some weeks there was ~5 hours of homework and the final paper can be stressful. Know that this class is a lot of trauma dumping, and you have to share it with all of your classmates.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Sheryl is the GOAT. Her class changed my life. She is the most understanding professor I have ever met in my entire life. She has a whole new approach to learning that is so much more holistic. She also got me into yoga.

To put it simply: Sheryl is genuinely the best professor at Duke. Her class is exciting and makes you learn more about yourself and your peers, and she is the most caring and friendly human on the planet. I could not recommend taking her class more.

Being quiet opened me to being stereotyped. Sheryl was biased towards her favorites. She'll grant extensions for most, but struggling and quiet, no. She said I was "just not doing work" after an 80hr homework stint. Sincerity isn't necessary, other students demonstrated this. This class became an echo chamber for developing ideas without critique.

Sheryl is not only an incredible professor, but one of the most caring professors at Duke. Years later we still text. Coming of Age is so important, as reflection during one's first year at Duke is so necessary when it's such a hectic year for most.

Best Writing 101 at Duke hands down. She's literally the kindest and most caring person I think I've ever met. The case study at the end of the class is really introspective, but it's caused me to understand more about myself and my own personal struggles. We start each class with emotion check-ins and yoga, and she really prioritizes our happiness

One of the best Writing 101s at Duke! Sheryl is super wonderful, caring, and will help guide you to becoming a better writer. You spend the entire semester writing a case study about yourself, and class time is for peer review. We also have "Happiness Days" where we bake cookies together. Taking this class pushed me to become more introspective.
Sheryl is one of the sweetest professors I've ever had. Her class is very interesting and the introspective nature of this course is very unique. You will never want to miss a day of this class!

LOVE Sheryl. I took this class first semester of my freshmen year and it was the best choice I ever made!! Really inspired me to do some soul-searching and dissect an aspect of myself that I'd never gotten the chance to explore. Also, the readings are really thought-provoking and led me to re-evaluate my path at Duke. So caring and sweet.
Sheryl is very caring as well as very charismatic. Loved her class.

Classes with Sheryl are tight-knit and she makes you feel safe. It feels like you're in a therapy session during class. Makes you incredibly creative because you're not afraid of judgment from your risky/outrageous ideas.

Sheryl is the best professor I have ever had, and this class truly have been the highlight of my first semester. Sheryl was not only my professor, but my friend, and that made this class so enjoyable. I think everyone should take this class, as it has meant so much to me and allowed me to learn so much about myself.

Sheryl is the most amazing professor I've met. She not only cares about you as a student in class, but as a whole person. She was helpful even to talk to about things outside of her class. Definitely made my freshman year at Duke 10000000x better!!! The WRITING101 course was also very fun and engaging because of her.

Sheryl is honestly one of the best professors/people I have met at Duke. Her Writing 101 wasn't my first option, but I'm so glad I ended up taking it. The class focuses on a case study you work throughout the semester on yourself and class time is a lot of peer feedback. 10/10 would recommend.

Would 100% recommend this course to any incoming student. Sheryl is truly an incredible professor and person - she truly cares about you and is amazing to talk to. If you want to write about yourself, this is an amazing course. I loved writing and doing the work for this class, and my first semester at Duke was better because I enrolled in it.
the best class choice i've ever made, sheryl is a wonderful human who is super supportive and caring. the class is relatively easy but super interesting at the same time

Sheryl is one of the best professors I've had at Duke. Coming to Age at Duke has been one of my favorite classes!! It is so obvious that Sheryl cares so much about her students, and really goes out of her way to make you feel like your voice is heard. She helps you grow not only as a writer, but as a person.

Sheryl is not only one of the most genuinely caring profs I've ever had, she's one of the nicest people I've ever met, period. She's able to sustain a delicate balance that promotes student growth and high-quality work, while ensuring that student needs are met from day one. Taking this writing101 section has helped shape my growth as a person.

Sheryl is the best professor I have had. She truly cares about all her students and makes herself very accessible. All readings (there aren't many) are provided and most grading is by completion (she gives great feedback). The final project is case study on yourself that you receive and write feedback from/for all your classmates and Sheryl.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Nicest teacher I've ever had, makes a real effort to befriend students. Very understanding for extensions and always responds quickly to texts and e-mails. Some of the readings are uninteresting, but overall, the class is great for learning about how yourself. For grades, as long as you complete the assignments you will most likely earn an A

Sheryl is an AMAZING professor who is also very caring and encouraging towards her students. She wants each of her students of excel and she always provided detailed feedback for all of my essays. Definitely take this class with Sheryl if you like descriptive & introspective writing and you will absolutely love it!
Hands down the best teacher I have had at Duke university. She is passionate about her work and really cares about her students progressing.

Sheryl is a great person in general and she is really passionate about her students. Her class is not too hard, but the case study due at the end is a huge paper so you better put in your due time for it. The class is what you make of it, so put in the extra effort to actually rigorously look at yourself and introspect. It will be worth it!

I already know Sheryl will be one of my favorite professors at Duke. She is incredibly passionate about first-years and helping us transition into college, including catering to different learning styles. The final project - a case study on ourselves that forces us to dig deep, learn about ourselves, and connect to peers - is life-changing.
Sheryl is the most amazing professor I've had at Duke. Coming of Age is a fantastic class and helps you reflect A LOT about yourself. The workload is relatively light. Would definitely recommend!!

Sheryl is one of the best teachers that I have had in my whole life! I took her class for Writing 101 my freshman year and she transformed me as a writer and I actually love writing now- I avoided it like the plague before. Take her class if you can, you will regret it if you don't. Also be ready to register for it quickly because it fills up fast!

TAKE THIS CLASS. Not only will you become a stronger writer, but you'll get the chance to be instrospective and think about yourself.  Sheryl Emch Welte is a wonderful person and so approachable and understanding.  You will really enhance your understanding of yourself if you take this class, and your Duke experience will be improved. Must take.
great professor! very helpful and easy to talk to/understand. not a ton of work, not much reading. main focus is case study on yourself, which is not very difficult. class was fun and interesting.

Sheryl is an amazing professor. She is extremely personable and keeps class interesting, even when the material isn't. The course title is very misleading, it is essentially an educational pysch course.  The case study project is intense but not that difficult.  Graded fairly.

Sheryl is fun, interesting, smart, and makes class enjoyable. However, she is a very tough grader, and, if you're not interested in educational psychology, good luck. This class is a lot of work, but Sheryl is very accessible and always willing to meet with you. Overall, I didn't enjoy the class very  much because I didn't write the way she liked.

The best class I have had at Duke so far. Definitely not a traditional lecture format with an authoritative teacher. Sheryl breaks apart what it means to learn, to be in a classroom, to be the student versus the teacher, etc. If you are at all interested in education or want an invested, intelligent, and enthusiastic teacher - take Sheryl!
Super nice and easy grader would recommend to anyone. just make sure you self-study from time to time and take notes in class because it's easy to zone out and get lost in his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great lectures, gives breaks in between class time, easy to understand, good at answering questions during class, very respectful, and responds to emails quickly. 10/10 would take this class again a little bit of general bio and chem is also helpful but not necessary if you just go back and read the slides.
Best mentor and great teacher. Highly Recommended!

Professor Weinthal's class was extremely interesting. Her lectures are very engaging, and her deep knowledge and passion for the material really comes through. The homework is exclusively reading, but I found the material to be very interesting. She truly cares about learning. That said, she can be somewhat intense and short on patience.

Professor Weinthal is extremely respected in the field of environmental policy, but her teaching style is intense. I oftentimes found her to be condescending, lacking the kindness you hope to see in a professor.

I would not recommend taking one of her courses unless you are passionate about the material. In my case, it was an unbearable course.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Weinthal is a very respected and well-renowned academic in her field. Her lectures and chosen course topics are very interesting. The homework is always reading, but a very manageable amount. She can come off as kind of condescending and her patience level is rather low, but overall a good class. The forms of assessment are very doable.
Overall, interesting lectures. However, she was very biased and quite condescending.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She is a good professor. Compared to others I have had at Duke she can come across cold but she is also very considerate of her students and explains things in a very simple way for beginner students. I took her Israel / Palestine class and enjoyed learning about the class through her environmental lens. She is a true expert in her field.
Horrible and unkind. Does not pay attention to her own rubrics.
Boring lectures, unclear about expectations for assignments, class had no real purpose. She thinks she's very funny but comes off as condescending most of the time. Overall: eh.

Professor Weinthal is a very well connected professor in her field of environmental policy. She co-taught this class with Professor Rebecca Stein on the comparative perspectives of Israel and Palestine. A very interesting and thought provoking class. Professor Weinthal focused on water and other natural resources in the region.

This was Bass Connections on Energy and Peacebuilding through film. It was an interesting topic but there isn't really any reading or traditional coursework which could be confusing at times but overall an enjoyable experience. Erika is really nice and super connected in international environmental policy world.

Professor Goknar is insanely knowledgeable and a very engaging lecturer. Each week, there are about 3 assigned readings (ranging from 6-40 pages each) that you are expected to read before class. The classes are mainly a discussion of the readings with some lecture included. Assignments: a few short writing, one midterm, a presentation, final paper
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Goknar gave super interesting lectures and is clearly very knowledgeable on his subject; the content can be a little confusing at times, and he has pretty high expectations in terms of participation. He grades pretty fair on the assignments that matter and provides great feedback on papers.

He is extremely intelligent but very disorganized. This class was extremely interesting but was hard to enjoy since he wasn't the clearest about grading criteria nor was he the most available outside of class. The majority of the tests and quizzes are lecture heavy, which isn't terrible if you pay attention.

Goknar is absolutely brilliant. Incredibly sharp, has very interesting perspectives, and I learned a lot just from how he put readings in conversation with one another and how he framed the course. Readings are on the challenging side, but worth it. Definitely a must-take course and professor during your time at Duke.

This class changed my fundamental perspectives on the Muslim world and taught me so much I didn't know. Professor Goknar, while sometimes unclear with deadlines, syllabi and grading, is clearly incredibly intelligent and is an engaging lecturer. He expects participation and attendance but is also pretty easy-going otherwise.

Goknar's class is one of the best courses I've taken during my freshman year. I learned so much from it even though I was kind of familiar with the course content. You really learn a lot of skills that come in useful throughout the rest of your time in college. The intense readings he assigns definitely will change your worldview.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Great course. Managed to learn so much from it; very enlightening. He knows how to keep you intellectually engaged. Goknar is tough but in the end of the day, you get whatever you put into your work.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Prof. Goknar is a very good professor and this class was difficult. There is a lot of dense reading, short writing assignments, pop quizzes, and a final paper that is very demanding. He expects quite a bit from his students. It's worth it though - I do feel much more informed about the Middle East and Central Asia.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Goknar is definitely intellectually engaging--he'll make you think about concepts and ideas in ways you haven't before. Unfortunately, that is coupled with sporadic grading and often unclear expectations. The grade I received in the class was good, but there was a huge amount of work and stress-of-not-knowing that went into getting it.

best teacher at Duke University. I am a senior, Middle Eastern Studies major and am so happy I had the chance to take a seminar with him. I wish more teachers at Duke were as intellectually challenging and curious
I LOVE THIS MAN.  I took my FOCUS class with him, and he is one of the best professors I've had.  The course itself is hard and has a lot of readings, but he is willing to help out if you go to him.
He is great. Take a class with him if you can. He is incredibly intellectual and will open you up to new worlds.
Truly changed my outlook on the ME and my interests. What you put in is what you get out of it though.
I love Professor Goknar! He's hilarious and incredibly interesting. I definitely recommend taking a class with him. Trust me, you'll learn a ton and have a great time.

While this class may seem very difficult and a little arbitrary at first, it is amazing how much you learn by the end of the semester.  I am really happy I took this course; it was overall very rewarding.  He is super intelligent and really does help you become a better writer.  There is a lot of work involved especially towards the end of the year

Great Professor. In the beginning, the readings are difficults, and may seem to completely contradict each other. But as the semester progresses, themes and central ideas emerge, and start to weave together beautifully. It's a great class, and Goknar loves his subject, even one as seemingly obscure as Turkish History. Also teaches you how to write.

His FOCUS course was the most reward of the semester. The work is challenging and the reading can be intense, but the variety of assignments really get your brain working on the material. Because the grade is out of a series of smaller assignments than one big one, you don't need to worry too much about your grade. But stay on top of the reading!

FOCUS class.  Certainly much more difficult than most FOCUS classes.  The concepts can be hard to grasp, but once you understand them, the class is very rewarding.  My grade in there steadily increased throughout the semester because he helps you become a better writer.

Prof. Goknar is very knowledgeable and intellectual, although a bit hard to understand. He assigns a lot of readings but if you're interested in the material you'll learn a lot. Also grading is fair and guidelines are straightforward.
GREAT Professor. Absolute genius and you learn a lot. Prod him for his thoughts on current events and do not be afraid to express your own viewpoints. Could get into an interesting debate

FOCUS class.  incredibly intelligent, an encyclopedia of knowledge on politics, literature, philosophy.  fair grader, gives great academic advice (however he does take off pretty fast at the end of class)
Quite a bit of work, but very, very fair.  Also very well taught - an awesome class.
He co-taught 316 this semester, and students were consistently frustrated. Whenever he lectured in place of Professor Yang, he was difficult to understand and often seemed unsure of the material.

He did not teach anything. However, the class and assignments were so easy. I had already taken this equivalent class in high school, so it didn't matter to me that we weren't learning; however, for someone new to the content this class would be a struggle as you would have to teach yourself.

Prof Fouh is not as bad as most of the reviews say. Although lectures weren't the most clear at times, I appreciated the quizzes rather than exams, woto's at the start of class for review, and didn't feel rushed to complete projects. The class may be a little difficult for anyone without Java experience but generally wasn't too bad with good effort
Chill and funny guy overall. Gives short quizzes instead of midterms and provides lots of extra credit.

He is a nice person, and you have to actually pay attention in class to understand the content in the lecture. Textbook is very helpful too. No midterms/finals, only a group project in final week. It's not hard to get an A if you put effort into the class
Not as bad as others are saying, but lectures are boring. Participating in class is helpful.

Professor Fouh is a very innovative guy, though his teaching style might be a bit ahead of its time for us college students to fully understand. You will love him as long as you skip his lectures:)
The content itself is easy—just make sure you understand his slides (which btw are the same ones he used at UPenn) and you'll do fine on the "KC"s.
The course is extremely disorganized. The professor felt like he was winging it basically every lecture. Didn't learn as much as I would've hoped.
Horrible professor. Do not take him.

Ruined CS for me. Pay attention at CS discussion because lecture doesn't teach anything. He fully pulled up Claude AI in lecture to generate code. He tracks your location on your device for your attendance to count.
Chill guy. Funny man.
He needs to be fired. Awful teacher, spends way too much time talking about himself, chatgpt everything and gaslights
Watched him generate a syllabus with ChatGPT. Does not know how to teach
He made an easy class so hard. Do not take CS 201 or any classes with him. Class was so disorganized and I felt like I didn't learn anything from it.
DO NOT TAKE ANY CLASSES WITH FOUH.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He simply does not know how to teach. If there's a course required for my major and this guy is the Professor, I'm dropping the major. Never again.
Incomprehensible and unorganized
horrendous! extremely difficult to understand what he says
Easy, removed all the interesting topics of the class (minimum spanning trees), awful lecturer, talks too much about his day (no one cares). Teach the content.
Terrible professor. Never learnt less in a lecture. I always hope that class is cancelled before I step foot in the same room as this guy.

The structure of his class is vastly different than 201 in years past. The structure itself makes the class manageable( 6 “Knowledge Checks” in place of exams, are multiple choice and can bring notes) and projects are split into cycles so you only have to do three/7. HOWEVER, I have never learnt less in a lecture. He's nice but passive aggressive.
Really hard to understand, didn't learn anything from lectures.

Terrible professor. His lectures work better than any sleep medicine. He tracks the location of students for attendance. Do not take him!!
He ruined CS201. Every TA agrees.

This class was frustrating. Expectations and organization were unclear, and Fouh didn't handle feedback on this well. It was manageable with prior experience on the programming side, but Fouh's lecture style was ineffective, and his spiral towards student blame and rants during class made lectures feel like a waste of my time.

I feel rlly bad for him. It seems like he has problems understanding student feedback. I'm not sure if I would take his course again (definitely the worst professor and learned nothing, but it was an easy A if you had a pretty solid backend dev. background). But I definitely would not recommend taking his course. Very confusing/disorganized course.

Prof. Fouh is one of the worst professors I have had at Duke. He is incredibly disorganized, wastes class time constantly, and he is not compassionate towards his students. I only learned things by self-studying for his difficult and incomprehensible exams. I would not recommend his classes!

Prof. Fouh is incredibly disorganized. One time we wasted 30 min because he couldn't log in to something. He is very temperamental and his reponses show that. He called us anxious and avoidant & accused my friends of cheating. No accountability, doesn't listen to feedback, never apologizes. Grading criteria were very confusing/unclear. AVOID!

Wow. Had to go out and celebrate the end of Fouh's reign of terror. main takeaway from this class is DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS or actually ANY class w/fouh if you want to leave with your soul intact. he will call you anxious and avoidant in chatgpt-generated responses and his gaslighting powers are so strong he will make you question your existence.

I enjoyed the content(mostly the slides), but the reverse lecture didn't add anything to my learning and felt like a waste of time. Also, the way he treats students is concerning: dismissing questions, blaming the students, and constantly revising guidelines. You never know what he really wants-the grading often felt arbitrary and temperamental.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Avoid this professor at all costs if you value your sanity. I completed CS at Duke, and this is hands down the most incompetent instructor I've ever encountered. He's set to teach 201 next sem—pray for those students. Just look at his UPENN reviews...yikes. He's not just a bad professor—he's a liability to the reputation of Duke's CS program.

Eric Fouh is on a power trip. His 'flipped-classroom' meant a 25min quizlet, a 20min rant, and a 20min poor explanation of concepts. His tests weren't fair representations of the material we barely learned. The whole class felt like it was made by ChatGPT-it was a surface-level, shotgun of content. And he berates students for not getting it.

He is truly the worst professor I have ever had. The majority of time in class was dedicated to explaining everything that is wrong with students rather than teaching, after which he would express his continued disappointment as students did not understand the untaught material. Seriously—avoid! The class is not worth your time and energy.

On our third midterm, there was a section on Tokens, something we never learned. There were no notes on it. We were all confused. Right before the final, he quietly unpublished the missing lesson and acted like it was always there. He did not nullify the missing points. This was the first class that ever made me cry out of hopelessness. He's awful.

Fouh is the worst professor I've ever had. His class is extremely disorganized. He required students to attend course staff meetings to give feedback, but dismisses their critiques and weasels out of any responsibility-a pattern for him. He's a professional gaslighter, and I hope the CS department wisens up and fires this fraud asap.

While I appreciated his perspective on SWE, the course's value was overshadowed by disorganization and unclear expectations, specifically with the major group project. It was frustrating to figure out what he wanted, and his apathetic attitude toward students seeking clarification was off-putting. The class has potential but needs improvement IMO.

The material is just self-taught as homework. He isn't an organized person, but he responds well to emails. The tests are hard compared to the material. Those who have given harsh reviews are those who think the real world to be the same as just attending lectures with clear guidelines for their work on how they are graded.

Eric often dismisses his students when asking questions and expects you to learn everything outside of class on very long slides. Additionally, the exams are significantly harder than the material taught. For an elective, this is possibly one of the most confusing CS classes.

Tries to paint himself as a good guy, but has no tolerance for ppl trying to learn his weird class structure and CS topics and while he barely understands the material. Looking at other reviews from colleges he's taught at, very apparent that I'm not alone in this impression...ironic he teaches a human skills class w his blatant lack of compassion.

Professor Worsham is deeply committed to fostering an environment where students can explore and engage with real-world and really cares about what she is teaching. She aims to cultivate a new generation of social innovators who are equipped to drive meaningful change in society.

Med/high work load: in-class lectures, pre-reads/vids, written assignments, & group project (6 hr/week). Very engaging prof w/ energy, fun activities, & inspirational guests. Great way to learn how to meaningfully impact the world. Genuinely cares about students. Pretty tough scorer w/ 0 accommodations, but curves final grades & offers xtra-credit.

Very nice and knowledgeable professor. Graded on: 2 group projects one with a presentation, 5 short memos, and participation. You need to participate in class and need to do at least some of the readings. None of the assignments were too difficult and the topic was interesting to learn about.

Took this class as a non-GH person and found it manageable/enjoyable. Dr Green is kind and very responsive over email/Ed. Quizzes and homework are graded kind of harshly. Open book but timed so still prepare. Final assignment is a study proposal that's actually really fun and can inform future research you want to do.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Straightforward and interesting class. Dr. Green is a passionate lecturer who shares great experience. Good amount of HW reading but very manageable and open book + dropped grades make the class less stressful. Great overview of health research in general. If you do the reading and work, you'll do fine and learn a lot.

GLHLTH 271 is a really interesting and fun class, especially for non-STEM students interested in global health. Professor Green is super nice and is very much rooting for his students to succeed inside and outside his classroom. Pay attention to the deadlines and the homework; even though it's rarely checked its helpful to understanding the class.

Green was super understand about grades and deadlines. He worked with students to make his class manageable and was lenient with grading. He made what could have been a bland class entertaining and engaging. Course was very well organized and there are plenty of resources. Would love to take another course taught be him!!

Professor Green is a great lecturer, especially for the methods class. He uses a lot of real world examples from his own work in global health as well as from other research. The quizzes are difficult though, especially because they're timed, so don't rely on the fact that they are open book.

Dr. Green is a great professor who is explains things very clearly. The course was structured well and there weren't any surprises. The quizzes are pretty difficult, especially because they are timed, so studying is a must. A lot of the class topics are basic research skills, so if you have research experience, you'll be just fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He is a talented, incredibly engaged, enthusiastic lecturer. Honestly, that's about it. He knows an incredible amount of knowledge about Global health and research and is willing to help students, but on his own terms which often means offering literal riddles and puzzles to find the answer. Very strict grader with little rhyme, reason, or feedback
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Green will assign 3 or 4 articles to read for a nightly assignment without specifying what to look for and only 10% of all of the articles will actually be relevant. Lectures are exciting because he is a good lecturer, but it would be easier to get engaged if I hadn't spent most of my time preparing for class reading irrelevant material.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Dr. Green's class is tough. He makes you work for an A. Grading is hard but class has a large curve. He really puts in effort to make sure students get a hold on the material and everything we learn is super practical for global health research. Go to his office hours/reviews for homework questions and you will be rewarded.
One of the less great global health professors at Duke. Class material is quite boring and lecture-heavy, Green makes the class much more difficult than it needs to be.

Flipped classroom that is not super organized, but maybe will be next time. The weekly IRAs can be challenging, but if you study the videos/readings you will be fine. No midterm and final was not bad at all. He tried his best to make the material interesting!

Green is my favorite professor at Duke. This is my second class with him and he's the reason I'm continuing with Global Health. He is super understanding, relatable, willing to help, and is clear about his expectations. His class isn't an easy A but if you put in a decent amount of work you'll get an A. Learned a lot, had fun doing it.

This class was very interesting because it was extremely project based. We worked on teams to design a proposal for the Duke Start-Up Challenge. The readings didn't relate very much to the class other than for the quizzes.

First year at Duke and Dr. Green was great from the start. He's enthusiastic, young, relatable, and very very smart. He is really focused on applicable learning - not a lot/any content lecture, mostly do-it-your-self projects. It's hard but fun. I wasn't into tech before but I like it now
A wonderful and kind professor
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Great Professor and Anesthesiologist at UNC.

Doctor Professor Shenita is one of my favorite professors. She is very kind and caring and patiently explains everything in depth to all of her students.She is also a great Anesthesiologist at UNC Health.

Dr. Prof Shenita is easy to talk to and very kind and patient. She is definitely missed at Duke by all of her students. I had a great experience taking her classes and enjoyed every moment of it. I heard she is currently teaching at UNC and sure all of her students love her there also.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: My favorite Professor at the University of North Carolina.I took her Anesthesiology classes and learned so many new things from this great teacher. She is very kind and helpful and is accessible outside of classes as a mentor. Highly intelligent and highly educated.
I love this wonderful and caring Professor. I was lucky to be able to take one of her Speech Language Pathology classes at Columbia University in New York City.
Best Professor ever! Her courses are well presented and easy to understand. She loves her students and it shows.
Great Experience even for someone totally unfamiliar with theater! She is an amazing and understanding professor

One of the best professors I've had at Duke. She has a great selection of course contents that covers the overall theater area holistically in terms of style, and allows you to engage in multiple aspects of theater. Her class and the discussion questions are very intellectually stimulating and combines art with humanities thinking. A must-take
Really amazing professor who knows her field VERY well.

Lee is the best! She's enthusiastic, knowledgable, and her lectures will make you gain an interest in Korean theater even if you're not a fan. No exams, just discussions, a couple of vocab definitions, blog posts, and a final presentation on a topic of your choice. If you're thinking of studying abroad while at Duke, take Duke in Seoul with her!

I cannot stress how great her class was. Three tests and one group project, come to lecture and pay attention and you'll make an A. She's really understanding and the class is engaging. Wouldn't take it if you're not into both theatre and history but her perspective is unparalleled.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Professor Lee is an awesome addition to the Duke Theater Department. She is generous in grading, but reading in addition to a variety of assignments can get disorienting at times. The plays are too experimental for me. But overall, she is a great lecturer on theater history and genres.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Her class was poorly structured and I didn't learn anything from it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Very tough grader

If you are expecting this to be a seminar class, it's much more of a lecture. Her grading criteria makes no sense and her explanation of artwork is confusing. This class was not what I expected it to be. I would avoid if I were you. By far my least favorite spanish class at Duke.

Gabara is a very special professor. There is no doubt she is outstandibly smart.BUT her teaching style is terrible. The class was suppose to be seminar format but she did not let us talk about our commnets or opinions to a reading. She dominated the discussion and made us feel stupid when we shared our thoughts. Need improve her class structure

Much like prince Eric in the little mermaid he saves the day. You have a question he has a well thought out and detailed answer. You're behind it's okay, spana will save the day. All around amazing professor and great person.
Spana is the absolute best. Probably my favorite professor I've ever had at Duke.
10/10 guy and truly cares. Great at explaining stuff. Is not messy. Does not mumble.
Spanazing!!! Great professor! Great class! Amazing everything!
Spana is a great professor! Def take him while he is at Duke. His explanations are great and understandable. He is very friendly and helpful!
Spana is a great prof and gets his class pizza
reviews.rating_tags: Hilarious--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Genuinely one of the kindest professors you will meet. Very understanding and just a cool guy!
Wow. What can i say. Dr. Spana is the kindest and most considerate professor. Great hair.

textbook is not helpful, the test questions are super strange even though I went to every lecture and felt like i understood the content. I definitely didn't enjoy the multiple choice format at all. you can tell spana isn't the one writing the tests, and the lecture they use as review before every quiz does not help either.

I dislike Biology and Spana did nothing to help that. Average teacher at best, his lectures were boring and he was not good at explaining the material. Bi-weekly quiz format was trash (multiple choice, choose up to 4) which was the same for all the exams and made the class harder. The linked genome sequencing lab was sick and super interesting.

Hard class tbh. Took AP bio and still got lost in the last 3rd of the class bc I'd never heard of 90% of what was being covered. Dr. Spana himself is rly down-to-earth and nice and he's not the one making the exams either, so I have no ill will towards him, but he is a little disorganized while lecturing. The teaching team is receptive of feedback.

The lectures are helpful but also confusing at times if you have no background in biology. Other than that, there are a decent amount of assignments that have to be kept up with throughout the semester.

BIO201 was a very organized and manageable class. It's a very good introduction class to bio if interested and sets you up for success for later courses. Spana is not the best lecturer - sometimes was very confusing in lecture - but the team of other professors was very accessible outside of class and made it easy to succeed in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
BIOL110
Dr. Spana is a great teacher. Sometimes lectures can be challenging because there is a lot of content, but he is accessible outside the classroom. You can go to his office hours, and he'll help answer any questions you may have.

(BIOL110 DKU)

Dr. Spana is very friendly and welcoming, as well as very accommodating when students need help or have suggestions regarding assignment/due dates (Ex. Changed midterm date for an optional trip)

He doesn't believe in memorizing the names of every little protein and enzyme, and cares more about you understanding the concept.
He is honestly so nice and cheerful, always ready to go over stuff if you miss a lecture. You can tell he really cares about what he is teaching.
Very engaging class, I learned a lot. Professor Spana has a very good character and is very friendly.

The lab was so fun! We got to work on the same project all 7 weeks and really produce some data! The lectures can be a little confusing, but its not too bad. I hope Dr. Spana will come back to DKU often!

Really kind, funny guy. Clearly very passionate about flies and his research and wants to have his students get in the nitty-gritty of what a lab is like. A lot of his students end up on publications through this class for not a ton of work and end up learning a lot. The 4 hour time slot can get kind of brutal though, but often we end early.

Co-taught 220 with Sherwood. Spana's material and questions were easier with far fewer details. Chill guy, great sense of humor, and extremely available to help if you need it. He did have a tendency to go on tangents, but he also tested from them, so write down everything he says.

Spana is the Man-a. Before 205, I was in his 118 class and thought he was a pretty good lecturer. But he really shines in a smaller seminar/lab setting like in 205. 205 was probably the best lab course I've had at Duke.
One of the worst professors I have had at Duke. Cares much more about memorization of small details than an actual understanding of the material. Was very unhelpful when I met with him.

Spana is a really great guy, but he does talk a little too fast.  The material he covers in Bio 118 is hard though so you really need to know it and do all of the reading for the tests, or at least really understand the lectures and then supplement with the book later.  His practice old exams were very similar to ones he actually.  Good prof.

Very smart guy, lectures sometimes hard to follow but he posts his lecture notes online for you to study off of. Be sure to read the recommended chapters of the book on research methods because half his test is on that.
Amazing professor!

spana is ok. he's a pretty good lecturer, but when asked questions not directly related to what he's teaching, he really beats around the bush and doesn't really end up giving you an answer. to be honest, he seems like one of those professors who hates teaching and only does it because he has to. tests are hard but he curves fairly

A great professor. Sometimes he mumbles, but he's happy to go over stuff you may have missed. Provides really good analogies for better understanding. Very approachable. His exams are difficult (not impossible), but they are curved, so don't stress out about the number too much.

He had really, really easy tests and was overall not too bad of a lecturer. His biggest problem was that he mumbled quite a bit, which makes it really hard to hear him if you're sitting farther back than, say, row 5.

his lectures are a complete waste of time.  just mumbles and is very confusing.  he does have useful lecture notes and EASY exams.  if he cared about teaching, then he should have been much more prepared for lectures.  nice guy, but way too inexperienced. a terrible teacher
He is vary knowledgeable and sometimes is hard to keep up with him. He will help you a lot during his office hours and advise you on how to work on problems.
He was very useful and easy to talk to after class. His oractice test are somewhat difficult but prepare you well for the midterm.

Diaz makes math 103 way worse than it has to be. He often gives very theoretical explanations for a lot of concepts, and ALL the midterms are based his practice tests...see him during office hrs before tests!! One good thing about his class is that he'll give you a A if you nailed the final, regardless your performances on midterms.
What do you classify Anthropology as..? a history..?

I thought this class would be awesome (Alcohol & Culture...). It wasn't. Uninteresting prof turned it into a torture session. Classes were painfully boring, discussions were not intellectually stimulating, and final was a killer. Prime example of why you should take a course for the professor, not the subject matter.
she reminds me of a grandmother, never getting mad or frustrated at anyone and always trying to make everyone feel open to talk during class
Very nice person, but a terrible professor.  Vague about grading policies and project expectations.  Incredibly boring.  Turns interesting topics into dull, nonexistent discussions.
Really boring and vague about her grading and attendance policy
make interesting material boring
Boring and Not So Knowledgeable.
No Comments
