Ewald is very knowledgable about history and Africa in general, but the seminar is unspecific and boring for the majority of the semester - almost feel like I wasted my money.  The 20 page paper was difficult to write, I spent 2 weeks writing and had 15 sources, and still got a B+ on it...

Do not recommend this class at all. Usually an assignment for completion every week or two, none of which are helpful. Class itself is boring. Stopped listening completely after the 2nd week. Paper is the only real assignment and it's a pain. Ewald is not a good teacher and was unorganized, boring and not helpful. Took forever to grade papers too.

Course was very chill throughout there semester. No homework was assigned except for the final 20 page paper, which isn't too bad. Prof Ewald is goofy, but in a good way; straight legend material in my opinion. Always there to help.

I took this course expecting some general insight into some African  public health.  What I got was little insight other than what I found on my own while scrambling to write a 20-page research paper.  Professor Ewald is extremely confusing and assigns confusing readings.  She was disorganized and based my grade only off the paper itself.

I took GH205, health and healing of africa, and janet was ok. the class itself was pretty boring, but it almost had no written assignments. we had 3 books to read (but i know some people in my class didnt turn a single page and were fine) and one final paper. the grading was ok, but she was very demanding.

Janet was a useless teacher. The topic had so much potential to be interesting, but her middle passages class was a waste of my time. I seriously regret taking her class. I was bored throughout, and received no help whatsoever in writing my final twenty paged paper, which we found out about two weeks before it was due.

Seems like an easy class at first, you do absolutely nothing all semester until a 20 page research paper at the end. She doesnt give enough feedback to give you any idea how good your research paper is and it is frustrating. You have to be obsessed with the topic to do well which is hard to do. Don't recommend the class

One of my favorite professors, even if I'm not interested in AAAS. She can get somewhat off topic in class, but it's still interesting. Really tries to get to know her students, and is very understanding. Generally an easy class with almost no assignments until the final 20 page paper, which she really guided us through from beginning to end.

I recommend Professor Ewald. She is very nice and an extremely intelligent. The grade is based on a 20 pg research paper, but she helps you write it sooo much; most of our assignments, especially towards the end of the semester, help us with the research paper. She won't let you fail!!

Prof Ewald has done some amazing research and can teach you to write a great research paper as well.  Somteimes she's a little scatter-brained and unclear, but for the most part she's very interesting to listen to.  She is very excited about history, and she somehow was able to make me excited about writing a 20 page research paper.
Fabulous teacher. Makes history interesting! Very understanding if circumstances cause your assignment to be late. Always willing to help!
interesting subject, but her lectures were very scattered. she gave very helpful comments on papers. I did learn how to write... but it wasn't an easy class.

COMPREHENSIVE: Dr. Hepler-Smith is obviously very passionate about the course material and has a radiant positivity, making the lectures feel moderately interesting. Attendance is not mandatory, but be sure to go to all workshops. The semester-long project requires a decent amount of writing and source analysis. Submit discussion posts on time!
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Unfortunately I hated the subject of this class, but you could tell this guy loved it and did his best to encourage you to love it as well. Lectures could have been more engaging, but again, I wouldn't have enjoyed them anyways. Overall as a professor, Dr. Hepler-Smith did a great job, but I would only recommend the class for real history nuts.

Professor Hepler-Smith is one of the nicest people you'll ever meet. He's also super passionate about the content of the class which makes you excited to come. If you just do your work and contribute to your semester long group project than an A is EASILY attainable. Highly recommend taking this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Hepler-Smith clearly is fascinated by history. It is inspiring to see someone care so much about a topic. People take it as a GE and it is evident in attendance, but he never skips a beat, continuing to share his knowledge. If you have an interest in the more historical side of science and don't mind conquering a group project, take the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Hepler-Smith and the teaching team are nice, and the course content is solid. When half the class can AI generate their way to an A without attending class past the first week and genuine attempts to engage with the content are punished, however, I can't help but feel a bit salty. Only take the class if you are interested in the premise.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class totally changed the way I think about studying history. The readings, lectures, & discussions were engaging. Also have great conversations in office hours. Coursework was manageable and lots of support on semester-long project. Overall, he is an intelligent, caring, interesting person who you can tell puts time and effort into his class.

Great humanities class for a Pratt kid. Lectures & readings were interesting, & you only had to read what interested you. Semester long group research project was paced w checkpoints & very manageable as long as you tailor to the specific feedback the instructors give you. Would def take another class w Dr. Hepler-Smith!

Best history class I've ever taken. He welcomes every perspective, so discussions are often deep and engaging, and the feedback that he provides on assignments are so clearly thought-out and encouraging. The work load was very manageable, and the semester-long project topics were chosen by each student; everyone can take something from this class.

Dr. Hepler-Smith is one of the most helpful and supportive professors I've had. The semester long group compound history project was separated in three checkpoints and was it very manageable with his thoughtful feedback. If you put in the work you can get an A. I definitely recommend taking his course or just knowing him in general.

COMPREHENSIVE: Dr. Puffer is interesting and kind! Her years of mental health work make the class feel meaningful, and many class topics are broadly applicable. Exams require comprehensive memorization of slides and readings (esp. methods, results). Grading felt strict at times, and make sure to ask for project feedback before submissions.

Iconic. Every class is very interesting and informative. Got to know a lot more about global mental health. Def take this class if you're a psych/global health major wanting to know more about the research happening outside the US.
Ironic that this class is about mental health yet the heavy reading and lack of guidelines made me have poor mental health. She has a sweet voice but her homework and assignments are not so sweet.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The class is very organized and structured. Every class is a lecture followed by a team-based activity. Attendance is taken. Lectures are easy to follow and assignments are clear and simple. Eve Puffer does wonders in making the material easy to understand and preparing students well for the exams. Great class!

Professor Puffer's lectures are always engaging and very interesting. There are weekly readings and two page papers that go along with it. In my opinion the TA randomly assigned grades to the weekly papers but will most likely leave you with an average of an A. Two pop quizzes throughout the semester but usually hints they are coming. Amazing prof

Great course. It was 2.5 hours long, but Dr. Puffer kept my attention because the material and her lecturing was just so great. There's readings, a two page paper weekly, and an occasional quiz. The midterm and final were not too difficult either. If you do the reading and go to class, you will be fine!

Prof. Evinson was fantastic. She's super open to conversation and related well to students. There are quizzes to make sure the reading was done (but they are easy). Also, the handouts were very thought-provoking. I feel like I learned A LOT.

As a native spanish speaker her class was easy but the texts were still very interesting and the class discussions were good. It is a good class if you want to get your fl requirement. However I will say she is a very opinionated person and definitely includes her own beliefs into what she teaches which is not good.

As a Spanish major, I will never take another course with Prof Evinson. This course was one of the most disorganized I have ever taken at Duke, the readings were dense and long, and the written assignments were impossible to decipher. She was not responsive over email and repeatedly accused classmates of AI use when it had not been used. Avoid!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Evinson was very caring and understanding. While the class was a lot of work, it was interesting and enjoyable. Would take again.

Professor Evinson is a great, very knowledgeable woman. Listening to her speak is certainly impressive, however, I found the assignments to lack instruction and the requirements would change during class. The readings are very hard and long. While I think the class was interesting, it was a little stressful to keep up with it from time to time.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Katryn is incredible - so intelligent & passionate about what she teaches. I always looked forward to class. Although some texts were difficult, she showed us compassion, did her best to make them accessible, & appreciated our contributions. She gives great feedback, is involved in campus life, & even took us to the Nasher with a 'pica-pica' after!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: We read a lot of very complicated texts and tried to tackle very complex topics without ever really fully fleshing them out. I wish we had more writing practice throughout the semester given that our grade depends heavily on final writing assignments. Kinda disorganized course, not a lot of "popular" literature.

Prof. Evinson's classes are super engaging and made me see literature in a whole new way. She cares about what students think, which is awesome, but she also expects you to put in the effort. There's a lot of reading, and participation is a big deal, so if you're just trying to check off a reqs, it might not be the best fit.

Professor Evans is a great professor who keeps class entertaining. The assigned readings for each class are not that long and are relatively easy text compared to other 300-level courses. The quizzes are also not bad if you prep beforehand. The one thing to watch out for is the two papers, which are both due at the end of the semester.

Quirky guy but great Latin teacher. We had 2 final papers and 5 translation quizzes. Quizzes were graded easily if you knew most of the translation. You have to prepare a solid amount of translation for each class. Professor Evans was accessible for office hours, and was very helpful in pointing out grammar concepts both in class and office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Evans is an incredibly nice and caring professor, who teaches well. The class itself, however, was very difficult especially compared to other foreign languages at Duke. Lots of translations due before every class, a quiz every week, homeworks due at the end of every week, three midterms, and a final - e did prepare us well for the exams though
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: if ur a native speaker, you know more Spanish than her but she thinks shes an expert in the language

I took Spanish 211 (could not recommend more)!!!!! Professor Ewing is a very encouraging professor that wants her students to succeed!! Pay attention and participate and class and you are set up for success!!

I am so grateful that I had Professor Ewing as my SPAN204 professor. She made the classroom such a welcoming environment and encouraged students to speak the language in a non-intimidating way. While her grammar lessons could've been more detailed, she made up for it with how encouraging she was. She definitely increased my speaking confidence!

She's very nice, but lots of busy work. Felt like the topics she wanted us to discuss were too theoretical and difficult to talk about, even for advanced Spanish class -- a ton of marxism and cultural studies -- but I definitely learned new stuff. She's usually very lenient with grammar mistakes, but grades harshly for the final essay

Very caring professor who understands students' needs, super flexible, organized, and an easy grader. Would highly recommend! A lot of busy work - but that's just a spanish at duke thing. Put in the work, and there's no reason you can't do well in this class! I absolutely enjoyed it and our class built community to boot.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professora Ewing is nothing short of incredible! Not only does she care deeply for the mental well-being and academic success of her students but shes also an excellent instructor who pushes her students language skills forward. The workload is steep yet ultimately manageable. As long as genuine effort is applied success is within reach! 10/10
I have learned so much from her this semester; highly recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I really loved Ewing, she tries to keep lectures interesting and creates a great environment to practice Spanish. I never felt embarrassed or scared to make mistakes. She will also meet outside of class to have coffee chats with you in Spanish, which I did and really loved. Obviously, there is work, but if you try you will do well.
Definitely a great prof for spanish 204. If you put in the work, you will get an easy A. She is very caring and wants to help her students succeed in the course.

She's a very nice person but not a great teacher. She assigns so much busy work and is a tough grader. I don't think she realizes that we take other classes. Also, it was at 8:30am which was not the best ... the course seemed pretty manageable and easy in the beginning but then it started ramping up. The quizzes are hard but not too bad. No exams!

Rebecca Ewing is one of the most disappointing teachers I've had at Duke. Such a subjective grader and gives an excessive amount of busy work. She honestly doesn't care or recognize effort either. Don't take her class.

One of the best professors I've had at Duke. Not only a great grammar teacher but also extremely involved in the community and willing to help her students with other endeavors. As long as you do your work and try your best, she'll help you succeed.

Really enjoyed this class. Professor Ewing did a great job of creating a comfortable environment that encouraged class participation, and because of this, I spoke up without any fear of being criticized or harped on when incorrect. Fair amount of homework, but the assignments made the quizzes and tests easier. I enjoyed the group/partner projects!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I took the service learning version of 204 (now 205) with her, and she was a very fair grader and the class was overall pretty easy. Sometimes a lot of busy work, but other times no work at all. Only 2 tests and no quizzes.

So incredibly nice and extremely helpful. She does her best to make everyone feel as comfortable and anxiety-less as possible. She's not a native speaker, so she understands what it's like to learn español from scratch. She'll accommodate to your circumstances and learning styl and will happily explain any concept. Work hard and you'll do very well

Super nice and approachable. She is always willing to meet with students outside of class if you email her in advance. Only Spanish professor I have had the encouraged participation, and this proved to be very beneficial for my own learning as well as fostering a good vibe in the classroom. Enjoyed her class, and she will prepare you for the final.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: She is amazing. Very kind woman, very approachable, and her expectations are very clear. Her grading is very fair and she really wants everyone to put forth some effort.

Professor Ewing is super nice and keeps the class entertaining for the most part. Not a super easy grader, but she was definitely fair in my opinion. Approachable and wants her students to succeed. Need to go to class and participate. More challenging than previous professors and Spanish classes  (102 and 203), but still not a difficult class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Love her! For 303, she's super helpful, but always has a lot of homework and random assignments. She def expects a lot more from her 303 students, so be wary if you place into 303 without taking 204. Overall a really enjoyable class, and you could tell she really enjoyed the special topic and teaching her students.
Amazing teacher - super helpful and very friendly. Expect a lot of busy work, but she always gives feedback when needed or asked to. The exams are hard but she prepares you well for what's on there.

Profesora Ewing is wonderful. This is the first Spanish class that I've enjoyed! Class is fun and yet you still learn the whole time. She always has new class activities that all really do help learn vocab/grammar. You do a lot of speaking practice in pairs which is laid back but great for learning language. She is upbeat and wants you to succeed.

Prof. Ewing cares about students and wants them to succeed. She is kind, helpful, and offers in depth feedback, creating a positive class environment. However, grading can be a bit hard and little details don't go unnoticed. Participation is crucial and tests can be pretty tricky.

I really liked this course. Prof. Ewing is helpful, sweet, generally understanding of language gaps, and her material is interesting. I've found the other reviews on here gave me a completely inaccurate view of her. There is a fair amount of work to do but it's not that strenuous and I maintained an A without too much effort. I would recommend!

Unlike the other reviewer, I found it very broad and interesting to learn about concepts like identity and hegemony regarding latinos in the US. She is a very enthusiastic teacher who's always there for you. The grading is not easy though- getting an A is tough. If you put in the effort tho, youll get an A-B+. Dont be scared by the first lectures

After wasting a lot of time in high school with teachers that weren't able to properly teach Spanish, I finally found a teacher that I was able to learn something from. By speaking entirely in Spanish, this class really helped me with listening, speaking, and writing, and overall I feel much better at the language than when I walked into the class.

Professor Ewing is a subjective grader and really only cares what you have to say if you agree with her opinion on a subject. Her views on Latino culture are very narrow and thus the class is pretty repetitive. Take a different 303 section if possible.

Dr Evans was an extremely organized and responsible professor. All the materials were available weeks before they were covered. Though the homework and assessments were difficult, questions were very well designed and graded fairly. The lowest 1-2 scores were dropped in several areas, and the overall curve ended up being quite generous.

Professor Evans seems like a really nice person, and he does care about his students, but he is a terrible teacher and doesn't explain problems well. The class is flipped, so you have to do everything on your own. It sucks to learn one formula on a paper and then apply it to a billion different complex scenarios with basically zero instruction.

I also took it over the summer and thought Dr. Evans was very nice and helpful. You do have to learn a lot of things on your own, but that is expected from summer class and flipped classroom. He doesnt give grades less than a B so you might be better off in his class than during the year.
Do not take his class over the summer; it's flipped and you have to learn everything on your own because he barely lectures

Dr. Evans is great. He is retired so the only reason he still teaches during the summer is because he truly cares about the subject and his students. People say that he is condescending, but I disagree. He's a man that finds life humorous and will laugh at anything, not YOU. He pays attention to the effort you put in so work hard and u will do well

Professor Evans, despite his intellectual arrogance, is one of the best teachers I've ever had. He's the first teacher at Duke that I've found that truly grades you based on demonstrated effort, not simply to fulfill some bell curve or quota for grade distribution.Highly recommend him, for his grading philosophy alone .

Evans might be the smartest prof I've ever had. The material is tough and his class is very difficult, but he says flat out that he doesn't give any grades below a B unless you really suck it up.  Because he's so smart, he's also very condescending, but it's probably tough not to be when everyone's dumber than you.

Takes super long to grade assignments, classes are basically guest speakers and powerpoint lectures. It's an easy class but is graded on the curve so you in comparison to where your peers are is really important. He doesn't really teach much, just reads off powerpoints.
good teacher. classes are short but memorize the slides

Decent class, but nothing special. Lectures are nominally interesting, and Jones routinely lets class out very early (~45min avg on a 2.5 hour class). Beware group projects - find a good partner or you're screwed. Exams directly from slides. Straightforward class, nice albeit uninspired prof.

I respect what he has done in business, but as a teacher, he's useless. Runs through slides, but literally expects you to memorize them for the test (and that's after he tells you the test won't be hard). I took this class because of the subject material. Big mistake.

The class is the epitome of boring.  Although the material is straight forward and easy, the tests were written poorly and actually graded kind of tough.  I would say the least interesting of any MMS class I have taken.
Easy class, but incredibly, insanely boring. Exams consist of memorizing the slides. There are better things to do with your life, seriously.

All the great things you heard about Entrepreneurship with this professor are NOT TRUE anymore. He flies through boring slides then rushes out the door. Lectures are dry, the articles assigned are repetitive, and the multiple choice exams are full of ambiguous questions. His class was disappointing and a waste of time.
The class work is easy but he grades kind of hard/arbitrarily.  tests weren't put together particularly well.
great professor with entrepreneurial experience, interesting guest speakers, straightforward assignments.
If you are decently good at Korean, this is a super easy class for lang requirement. I never studied but I did well on my exams. There's a decent amount of homework but overall, solid class.

Professor Kim is very kind and always available to help! Homework is every day, but short; frequent quizzes with quiz lists provided in advance; tests not difficult if you studied. No grades posted in Sakai though, you only get to look at quiz/test to see mistakes and then hand it back to her.

Felt like she didn't care about teaching the class. Stopped giving homework after week 3 because she kept forgetting to upload it, never graded a single test, never responded to any emails, and put content on exams that was not found in the study material. No clue what grade was until posted to DukeHub after finals week. I barely learned Korean.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Kim gives off a vibe that's like your best friend's mom. Taking her course is literally a mental health remedy. She is very very understanding and always gives 100% energy to teaching.

Professor Kim is amazing and will help you become more fluent in both Korean language and culture. If you have concerns, talk to her - she's very kind. Not an issue with her but the lack of a native track makes classes at the 200 level difficult for nonnative speakers in general. Either self-study or get ready to not understand your classmates.

Professor Kim is a very caring professor who understands that most of us are taking Korean to fulfill the language requirement. That being said, she always tries to engage us during class and provide us with outside opportunities to learn more about Korean culture and language

Kim Sunsaengnim is honestly the sweetest professor ever. She's great at teaching and cares about her students. She does have a bit of homework but it's certainly manageable and she's chill with due dates. There are a lot of quizzes and whatnot but she tells you what you need to know and as long as you review you're good!

What can I say that hasn't already been said? Very focused professor who is passionate about what she does. Entire class likes and respects her. Great class for anyone interested in the Korean language!

Nicest teacher at Duke! She is extremely flexible and helpful with work, and is very approachable in and outside of class. Korean 305/306 could be a lot of work for non native speakers, but classes are very entertaining. If you're a native speaker (about elementary or middle school level) this will be one of the easier classes you take.

By far the kindest professor I've encountered thus far at Duke. Kim Sansaengnim definitely moves quickly and assigns quizzes and tests left and right, but I'm incredibly thankful for the ways that she has helped me expand upon my Korean skills. Literally love this woman! She's hilarious and so lovable.

Professor Kim is a wonderful professor and a great person in general. She cares so much about her students and is there to help you. I learned a lot of Korean in just one semester. She also really wants you to do well. The class overall is not difficult as long as you put in some work.

Professor Kim is my favorite professor at Duke! She is such a nice person who actually cares about you as a student. I would love to take her class again just because she's teaching it. If you're decent at Korean, this class will be an easy A.

Professor Kim is super awesome. She loves teaching and makes the class fun. She does a really great job of making the class fair for everyone, even when some people are at an intermediate level but others are just learning.

She is the nicest professor ever, and she makes sure to speak slowlymore clearly if you need it. She makes herself very available via email or in person if you feel like you  need individual help. Overall great professor

She is just so nice and a pleasure to have class with.  She is so clear. If you're not sure about Korean, maybe try the first day, she's so approachable. You have to do a bit of work, but the cler structure def makes learning Korean easy.
Kindest teacher at Duke. No one else comes close. If you want to learn krn, just take her class. its amazing. glhf
Eunyoung is the chillest, coolest teacher ever.  She's extremely helpful, very lenient on due dates, really enthusiastic about Korean, and she's just adorable in the classroom.
eunyoung nuna is so cute ;)

Professor Kim is awesome! Really nice lady and extremely helpful. I learned so much from her class (KRN 1, 2) If you have any interest in learning Korean, TAKE HER CLASS. HIGHLY RECOMMENDED INSTRUCTOR
Amazing lecturer
Very good professor. Too bad he's leaving. Not a fan of the large discussions though, I wish the class were a bit smaller. Otherwise, awesome.
Amazing class.  Make sure to take it while Euben still teaches it.
No Comments

Great class, I gained a ton of new insights. Euben is a unique and great lecturer, and the sections clarify what is a very difficult reading list. If you keep up with the classwork, its not difficult to do well, but it takes effort.
Cross-listed with Poli Sci. Get in his class. Best professor at Duke. Informative and entertaining lecturer. Not too much work. The stuff covered is really interesting too.

Euben is easily the best professor I have had at Duke. He cares deeply about his students and his classes. The material is fascinating and challenges you to think in ways you probably have not before this. Best seminar facilitator ever. Grades based on participation and a paper. Stiff paper grader, generous overall if you participate.

A very interesting and engaging lecturer.  He commands the attention of each student and talks extremely intelligently on the topics that are being covered.  He leads discussion very well also.  Paper topics are decided upon democratically with input from all students.  Perhaps fitting to the class.
Euben is an awesome lecturer.  Pretty much just confirming past comments.  Very open to alternate views but doesn't entertain ideas for no reason- perfect balance.

Euben is the man. He gives great lectures which keep the class moving and involves students in dialogue throughout class. He presents the readings from many points of view and is not afraid to take on a controversial issue. Funny guy
Awesome lecturer.  The class isn't easy, but I came out of it with knowledge that will help me in the future.
He is the best lecturer I've ever heard

Seemed like a nice guy so I decided to go to lecture to give him a shot. Got used to the accent, though it was thick. He gave straight-forward lectures that corresponded with the text, good real-world examples. I relied much on the book to solidify what was said in class.
His English isn't perfect but thankfully the textbook is an adequate substitute for class in Econ 55.
He very hard to understand because of his accent. Sometimes there are mistakes in the powerpoint. It's much more efficient to read the book and do the problem sets. exams are reasonable.
Has somewhat of a thick accent, so can be hard to understand. Not particularly exciting or helpful; I personally found reading the book myself to be more useful than attending lecture.
Easy to fall behind in this class, it would be wise to do all of the optional homeworks. I found no problem with the accent that other reviewers have pointed out.

Eylem is AMAZING+so kind. Her small accent is not a problem and I PROMISE you get used to it soon. 218 was tough+lots of work (in any section), but she helps you so much especially in office hours. Those who didn't like her teaching imo were ones who didn't put enough time/not going to office hours. I recommend taking ANY class w/ her.
Accent makes her difficult to understand. Didn't really teach much because the video lectures were delivered by Mike Reed.
Really fantastic

She is so accessible and willing to help explain things to studentsand she's responsive to student requests about deadline adjustments, etc. The exams for this class were pretty easy and fairly graded, although there was some time pressure

Good class, I would recommend it over 212. You learn everything you need to. It sticks very closely to the textbook. Participate if you can. HW and tests are easy. If you understand the textbook, you'll understand the tests. Very few proofs. Lots of partial credit on HW and tests.

Yildiz is a decent lecturer. She expects u 2 read the textbook b4 class, so doing so is very important to keep up during lectures. HW easy. Very receptive to class feedback, which is super refreshing (ex. some days asked if we would rather see examples vs concepts) Tests could be hard but generous partial credit (so try your best!) Final worth 35%
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She's really nice and I don't understand why she has bad reviews. She is really fair when she grades and gives half credit if you deserve it. She tries to engage the class so that no one is left behind and is very open for office hours.
Terrible teacher. She is difficult to understand, doesn't explain concepts well, and grades too harshly. Definitely try to get in a different section if at all possible.
Good teacher, very helpful and explains concepts well
Terrible teacher. Hard to understand, doesn't explain concepts, grades harshly without explaining why.

Dr. Wei gives great lectures and explains the material well. However, there isn't much material to cover; most of the class is applications of the material in clever ways, so be ready to truly understand the material (Dr. Wei's lectures do the job) and apply it on midterms. Midterms & Final are very difficult, but curve is more than sufficient.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Fan Wei is a very smart; her teaching style entails examples that are worked through in class; many questions are very difficult and have specific tricks to frame the question in a way that makes it easier to solve. 2 midterms are both hard, but the final is fine, and the final curve is very generous. Overall it's difficult, but more than worth it.

She is very smart and takes the time to explain every concept. The homework is excellent, and she provides practice midterms and final. One midterm was brutal, but the curve prevented it from affecting our GPAs. She genuinely cares about students, is always happy to discuss topics, and asks for feedback mid-semester. Overall, a great professor.

Professor Wei knows combinatorics very well and it shows. She covers concepts a bit quick, but she is fair when she does it. Usually when that happens, she realizes and supplements and never punishes you. You learn a significant amount and practice is needed. She will curve when an exam is more difficult than anticipated (time is a killer)
Honestly learnt a good amount in this course, she is very friendly! Some of the content was pretty challenging but overall the grading was fair

Professor covered advanced concepts (martingales, Azuma-Hoeffding) beyond intro combinatorics level, without proper prerequisites. Relatively poor explanation of the material, but had very fair grading.

This class was beautifully cathartic. Professor Fox is an excellent writer and mentor to her students. There is a fair amount of reading and writing, but it's all purposeful and interesting. I looked forward to this class every week AND she made it easy to get know new classmates which made class fun. I highly recommend any class with her tbh.

Great, compassionate teacher. Gives excellent feedback and structures the class well. My writing improved greatly. Throughout the pandemic she has been very accommodating too. If anything, it seems like there is a little too much busy work. Grades are also pretty uncertain throughout.

Great class, great professor!! A lot of work but you will learn so much. My writing skills have increased dramatically and I have found a love for writing poetry through this class. Prof Fox is engaging and really wants her students to learn.

Professor Fox is awesome... very nice, very helpful with your writing, and with a strong sense of humor. This class was simple: you do the work, you get a good grade. However, there's a lot of work, and it's pretty particular stuff. A lot of online deadlines and numerous readings can make things tough to keep up with if you're not organized.

Professor Fox is awesome. She is so giving and helpful--her door is always open and responds to emails quickly. She will always read over your work and comment. Class was informal and fun. Great teacher!

There is a lot of reading for this class and a lot of work, but Fox is a cool teacher. She is funny sometimes and generally pretty helpful with your writings. Grades are based on progress over the semester.
Utter aura. Strict but well-meaning grader. Probably the most fashionable professor on campus. You'll adore him and he'll bully you. Ignore the bad ratings this man is the goat.

One night I had a dream that I would meet god, in human form. He would have the intellectual capacity of a German, the bald head of a wiseman, and a fashion sense rivaled only by Young Thug. The next day, I met Professor Farred. This man will change your life...take his class.

I cannot believe these awful reviews. Professor Farred was one of the most incredible professors I have ever had. He pushes you to become the best version of yourself. You will learn so much from him. There is plenty of time to get assignments done and his lectures are engaging. He jokes a lot, and be prepared to be challenged. Take his class!!!
Actually the worst person I have met at Cornell.
absolutely awful
Best teacher I have ever had

Do not take a class with Farred! His feedback is not related to your writing but to how closely your interpretation aligns with his own. He never gives out rubrics, so you have no idea what he's looking for. When students ask him questions to get a better grasp, he goes on tangential rants. He gave everybody B's and C's in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This is for Cornell students: NEVER EVER TAKE HIS FWS!!!! He gives the hardest readings and little instructions. For the writing assignments, there are neither grading rubrics nor feedbacks. Most of his class time is dedicated to make jokes about his students, and contains no useful contents.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Cornell students: Do NOT take his FWS The course title has nothing to do with the content. He just rambles on about Marx and Gramsci every class. The course assesses your understanding of political theory, and nobody feels like they've actually developed as a writer. He does not give concise grading criteria nor feedback and only gives Bs and Cs
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Lots of reading, most of which is not used for essays. Lots of essays on specific ideas and subjects, where there is a right answer despite the question being open-ended and ethically/morally based. Essay comments often contradict themselves, and good grades are REALLY rare because his definition of a good grade is not the typical student's def.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: hes a real gem i like him alot he taught me how to right

Just an absolutely awful teacher. In his seminar "on thinking" he forces ideology down students' throats without encouraging them to think critically. When students raise legitimate questions about the text, he either philosophizes without answering the question, or pontificates about importance of the author of the text. DO NOT TAKE HIS CLASS!
Grant Farred is no longer at Duke.

WHAT an ****! He's bitter, cynical and untrusting. He calls out and criticizes his students, bringing an uncomfortable negative energy to class with him.He is resentful, pretentious and unforgiving. Iam certain that I wrote a good final paper and actually did all the reading, but I got a D bc he didnt like me. His terrifying brilliance makes mean
No Comments

To cite a song: "You only get what you give." Easily the most interesting and compelling course and approach to literature I've ever encountered. He takes his course and his students very seriously, and has very high expectations. The flip side is that he's not above punishing those who don't work.
Very disrespectful of other students.

Be prepared for a challenge and lots of in class discussion, as well as erudite lecturing.  He really knows his stuff, and expects you to pay attention at all time.  Grading is tough, but there are only 2 papers.
most complicated approach to literature that I have ever encountered. very intelligent
he dresses nice, and his lectures are fun and upbeat. did i learn anything?!@!
funny, very intelligent, high expectations for students
No Comments
No Comments
No Comments

This teacher is irresponsible and doesn't pay attention to the teaching. Lectures are from AI and notations are inconsistent, bad for first time learners. Learn it completely by yourself and don't listen to her misleading lectures.
Everything is from AI...

A terrible experience. Dr. Li was disorganized and spent much time lecturing students on "how to write properly" (despite her subpar writing and presentation skills). She would criticize students in front of the whole class. Her criticisms can get personal. She also at one point projected everyone's homework grade on the screen during class.

This course is SACRILEGIOUS! Course materials, exams and case studies are naive and boring, but you'll still lose points since grading is extremely tough. Don't expect an A even if you are a straight-A student. Avoid at all cost. Worst course that I've taken throughout my college life.

She's mean during OHs. Not familiar with her own assignment (apparently copy and paste elsewhere). Cannot learn anything during lectures. Highly disorganized.

Instead of you avoiding the professor, Duke should get rid of her completely. She should know that both TEACHING AND RESEARCH are her responsibility.

Her lecture is terrible. She didn't bother to read the slides (written by others) before class and paused constantly. The content itself is OK but she made it extremely hard to learn with inconsistent info. Change group to individual project making the workload 5x heavy. The worst prof ever (I've been a uni student for 8 years). Run. Run faster.

Mean and condescending to ppl; poker face during OHs and in-person contacts. She raps through 100-page-long slides often and considers everything trivial. Changes group project into individual due to some biased complaints. Tests are fair if you self-study the stuff. BTW she's pretty interested in politics, the only thing making the course funny.
the worst period
The worst teacher I've ever met, she has been steadily bad for the past ten years as a teacher.

Professor Li's teaching style is disorganized and unclear, making it hard to follow the course material. Her lectures are often filled with tangents and her grading is tough with unclear expectations. Feedback is lacking and often unhelpful. Her communication skills need improvement for a better learning experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Li's STA440 class is a nightmare. Her teaching style is disorganized and her lectures are riddled with tangents, making it difficult to follow the course material. She provides inadequate guidance and unclear expectations, leaving students lost and confused. Despite your efforts, don't expect good grades. Avoid at all costs!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Avoid Prof. Fan Li for Stat 440. Poor lecturer, tough grader, and lacks useful feedback. Unclear expectations and arbitrary grading criteria. Not recommended.

Professor Fan Li's teaching style is abysmal, making it nearly impossible to grasp the material. Her lectures are incomprehensible, leaving students bewildered and lost. She fails to provide any meaningful guidance or feedback, leaving assignments and exams feeling like a guessing game. Avoid her at all costs if you value your academic success.
A mean, petty, and dishonest person who lacks a basic understanding of scientific concepts.

This is the best class and professor I have had at Duke. Unsure why all the reviews are so poor, but I wanted to clarify that she is absolutely at the top of her field in Causal Inference and explains concepts succinctly, and understandably without using confusing jargon. I came out of it learning so much more than I ever thought to.

Fan's first semester teaching 440, so giving her some slack for being somewhat disorganized. She has a very underrated sense of humor, but rambles a bit when lecturing (often surprised by own slides). Would hope to get quicker feedback on interim reports and actual reports

Fan Li is a poor lecturer and a tough grader. She offers almost no useful feedback during feedback sessions, and does not hold back in her criticisms, often in the presence of the entire class. The expectations for assignments are not clearly defined, and she defines arbitrary grading criteria after assignments are due. Do not take her class.

Don't take a class with Fan if you can avoid it, especially for 440. 440 has a heavy workload with homework and reports due every week. Fan's feedback has been mostly useless and always too late. Her report feedback on how to improve doesn't explain how she provides grades, and when she does provide useful feedback, it's always past the due date.

Final warning, DO NOT take any course with her. If you ignore this advice, you will REGRET. She gave hindsight about how to do homework and what is expected every time AFTER the grade is posted. So never expect a high grade from her even if you tried your best. The worst professor to take a class with. Avoid her with all costs.

Save yourself a ton of time... take Stat111 with Prof Banks instead.  Prof Li is fairly nice but her slides do not compliment lecture well (too wordy), her english is very poor, her handwriting is tiny and illegible, labs are time consuming and there is little guidance, and there is often miscommunication about logistics with the class. Just don't.

She's terrible. Insults students for not understanding her lessons that make no sense. Instead of helping students who've never used R before the course while most students had (not a prereq) on the R based homworks she tells them to "just google it" at office hours. English is very poor. Even if it was good lessons still wouldn't make sense
The worst professor I have had at Duke. period. She is terrible. Absolutely terrible.

Absolutely awful professor. Her classes are the biggest bore, and even if you tried to listen she doesn't make any sense. Her office hours are just as useless... for your own sake please don't take a class with her
Worst professor I've ever had. Doesn't speak english, doesn't teach well, disorganized. Just overall awful, avoid at all costs.
No. No no no no no no no. No.

Dr. Ferguson was amazing and it is so clear that he cares about his work and his students. I was challenged in this course but in the best way possible. I learned so much about the world around me, and Dr. Ferguson went the extra mile to made sure all of his students understood everything he was talking about.
course materials are outdated and not fit for emerging environmental issues.
Super easy class... His lectures are really clear, but overall the material just doesn't seem like it should be at the grad level. Only two labs the entire year.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Idk why score is low but his class was wonderful per my experience with very clear explainations and interactive games (you can bascially just use notes to prepare exams). Maybe he got much better with teaching after a few years. He's also quite humorous. Exams are somewhat challenging but balanced and fair to the course level.
Good course, good Professor, and good workload
He doesn't explain any of the concepts properly, just read the slides. You need to self-learn everything. Being online also doesn't help.
PPT reader. Good grader. Difficult final.

This class is still online despite covid being over a while ago. 

All the class is cheating, and it seems he doesn't care. If you want an easy A, take with him.....if you want your money to actually return something and learn take with any other Professor.

Prof. Zhang seems to be a PPT reader and he focuses too much on reviewing ECON201. He explains too much about simple knowledge, and I feel he cannot grasp the points where students find it difficult. The homework is quite different from what is taught in class, and it is of great difficulty.

Took "ETHICS450S: What Should I Do With My Life? The Art of Choosing Well" with him and Katherine Jo. Most formative class of my time at Duke. Changed my outlook on life and senior year for the better. Incredible selection of readings and thoughtful feedback to really make you think—about what you want and why; values; what makes a meaningful life.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Christian thrives as a seminar educator. He's kind and understanding and just someone who is fun to talk to. The class is made into a welcoming environment and people accepted into the program ask interesting questions. I didn't like the What Now class either, but don't let that stop you from taking the seminars!

COMPREHENSIVE: Very easy class to pass … just attend your designated weekly session and write a reflection that is at least somewhat introspective. People like to hate on this class for being a waste of time, but it honestly is worth it to have an ~hour long period every week where you can reflect and calm down. Try to be in the smaller sessions!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Ferney's class was easy. You show up, and you get participation points.  According to the rubric, if you submit the weekly discussions on time, you should get 100% automatically. That was not the case for me, I received 5/10's because the graders did not agree with my opinions... Regardless, class did not teach me much.

Considering its a requirement to take, it is not bad. Sure some parts are boring/painful to sit through, but overall the class is not hard. You also end up getting to do alot of different things (yoga, visiting the gardens, etc.) in addition to discussions about topics that don't get talked about. Not as bad as what the other reviews make it seem.

Forced co-req to many sems/W101s. To attain S, all you have to do is show up and write a short weekly reflection. The most difficult part about this class is staying awake. You're being spoken to for the entirety of the time, primarily about topics that are of zero relevance to your life. Overall, not a bad class, just boring.

Required S/U co-req for many freshman seminars and W101 classes. Wouldn't take if I didn't have to. Most classes are lectures that aren't engaging and you're just being talked at for the whole class about useless topics. A lot of people stop showing up after a while (you can miss a certain # of classes). Easy but not engaging and felt pointless.

The class itself is not very engaging. Some classes were insightful or beneficial, but a lot of the time the lectures just felt like we were being talked at for an hour. Had office hours with Professor Ferney, and he is very nice and interesting, but I wouldn't have taken Ethics 189 if it was not a co-requisite for a lot of good W101/seminars.

Honestly, the class wasn't very hard. It very much felt needless, but if you're stuck taking this for a good writing class, it's not the end of the world. You need 235 points to pass. You get 20 points a week (10 for attendance, 10 for reflection). Get those point fast so you can forget it exists. Then a pretty easy ~1000 word capstone at the end.

Honestly, one of the most pointless classes ever. The class was so disorganized and things were all over the place. He doesn't start putting in grades until the semester is almost over so you won't know if you're going to get an S or U until like one week before the semester ends and you won't really be able to do anything about it.

Christian Ferney is the most narrow-minded, passive aggressive, and honestly horrible teaching staff I've interacted with. This man is full of himself. The class is easy and bearable if you avoid him. I understand you may have to take this. Stay away from him, you'll be sane. God forbid you email him for an extension - he is terrible.

During this class, I saw Christian no more than twice - once on the first day, and once at an activity that he messed up the scheduling for. Despite Christian's disorganization, this course is worth taking due to the amazing seminars/WRITING101s attached to it. Plus, some weeks are kinda fun (e.g. yoga, Duke Gardens, existential discussions).

Fairly easy pass/fail half credit class. Attendance of class every week is mandatory (even though you may not get credit for going since they often mess up attendance records). To pass you just have to go to class (meets once a week) then write a 250 word reflection so not bad overall but the class is very disorganized with no structure

Christian Ferney is an Engima. The man himself was only ever witnessed once in the first day of class and then, just like that, he vanished forever. Except when he returns with a passive aggressive personal email. The definition of caring about things that have no relevance or importance to anything, yet less my education. Honestly, don't go.

Ferney led dinner course for Ethics FOCUS. The class was pass/fail and all you had to do was show up. That said, the whole thing felt like a huge waste of time. Tbf, this may just be because it was hard to adapt what is usually a dinner course to a Covid world (where we couldn't eat dinner). I still would recommend Ethics, but this class was snooze

I had him as a FOCUS teacher, responsible for the dinners. We've had a few conversations at random times during the semester, and he's a fairly chill human, albeit, a bit cynical. As a professor, his class is mainly a participation pass/fail. You show up, stay awake during dinner, and leave- you'll pass. What more do you want?
It was a very interesting class and the workload was super manageable! She is super kind and understanding! Take her class!
Lovely and kind professor. Class was not incredibly rigorous but you get out what you put in. She is very caring outside of the classroom as well.

Contemporary Social Problems with Professor Maria Febbo is a great introduction to sociology. The class strikes a great balances between being interesting and relatively easy. Professor Febbo is so kind, knowledgeable, and truly cares about her students and the subject matter. I would totally recommend her as a professor!

Lectures weren't stimulating even though the topic was interesting, and most students just ended up getting work done during that time. She grades too harshly and is not willing to help her students out even if they are close to an above letter grade. Your grade is solely based off of tests and a paper. Does give partial credit on tests though.
reviews.rating_tags: So many papers--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Expects you to know even the information she barely discussed during lecture for the exams. The class is unstructured and grading can be very arbitrary. She said she's adding a service component to the class, so watch out.
She is super kind and supportive. Good class
Easy A but didn't learn anything. Lectures mainly repeat intuitive facts. Almost no readings; the readings are short (often less than 10 pgs), and you can get away without reading them.
One of the most caring professors at Duke. Such a gem in the Sociology department and beyond. Take as many classes with her as you can!

Absolutely loved this class and Dr. Febbo. She is such a nice person and very receptive to student feedback/needs. Readings are extremely interesting and lectures are engaging. Grading is based on 5 reading quizzes which are easy if you read, a midterm and final paper, both of which are fairly straightforward and not graded harshly. Loved it! 10/10

Dr. Febbo was fantastic! This class was asynchronous, and her lectures were the best of any class I had. The grade was determined by 4 quizzes (which were easy if you did the readings) and a midterm and final paper. All content assigned was super interesting and relevant. Will happily take her again if I have the opportunity!

I've had seminars with 15 people that were less engaging than this class with 150 people.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Folch is an amazing professor who knows A LOT about anthropology and the world in general. Her lectures are funny and engaging... Her expectations for essays could be a little clearer. She also does "In-Class Writing Assignments" at the beginning of class, so don't skip or be late.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Christine is a very sophisticated, fun, and cool professor. She makes the class entertaining with her silliness, especially the shawl that she wears around her neck. Lots of reading but you'll get used to it. The material is quite easy to learn and you learn a lot about the world and people in general. Definitely recommended!

Folch definitely cares about what she's teaching and puts a lot into her work. Lectures are interesting, but she's super sarcastic. A LOT of reading which you actually have to do because she tests you on it with in-class writing assignments. Learned a lot, but felt like I could never finish the readings (usually over 60pgs/class).
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: THE BEST PROFESSOR I'VE EVER HAD IN MY ENTIRE LIFE. Dr. Folch is an actual genius when it comes to anthropology/life in general. I walked out of every lecture feeling like the time had flown by and feeling like I saw the world in a completely different way. SHE'S AMAZING. And go to her office hours because she is so supportive and fun to talk to!

JFo is absolutely the real deal. Do everything you can to take Shakespeare & Financial Markets with him—literally the best, most unique class at Duke. If you can't get into that, definitely take Behavioral Finance in the spring. He's incredibly open to meeting with students and giving career, investing, and life advice. Epic guy, epic classes.

JFo is the best. He has phenomenal selection of material and works hard to ensure lively class discussions. He is one of the most caring professors and takes additional time to connect with students. 

Ownership of content is on you. If you have the pleasure of taking one of his classes, please read before class to get the most out of the lesson.
Professor Forlines is epic and you should take his class. He is a really great guy and this was unlike any other class I took at Duke
Terrific class. Amazing life lessons and perhaps the most helpful professor I've had at Duke. If you can get in to the course, you're in for a treat. Wish I could take this course again!!

This class is the most dynamic course you'll take at Duke. It's the epitome of why you're at a liberal arts university. If you are particularly interested in behavioral econ, this class will be especially rewarding for you. Class is always fun and the highlight of my week.

I actually took econ 368 with Forlines and he was amazing! The guy is just so smart and has amazing life experiences to share with students. He is the most caring professor I have ever had at Duke. You can literally go to him for anything -- basketball tickets or help rebalancing your portfolio. Definitely take one of his classes.

He's a really nice person who is always willing to get to know his students better. He gives out basketball/football tickets as prizes for pop quizzes. The class material definitely made me think. But, I found the lectures to be long and dry at times, and the material to be a little superficial. Not focused on financial markets either.
The GOAT. Never enjoyed a class more in my life. A truly special man, I'm blessed to have met him.

I absolutely love Forlines. He is hands down the best professor I have ever had at Duke. Every lecture is engaging, entertaining, and enlightening. He cares deeply about his students and their interests. The class is part Shakespeare, part Financial markets, part random knowledge, and part self-improvement and self-reflection.
Shakespeare & Financial Mkts is one of the best classes at Duke

Awesome professor. Class was extremely interesting. It's not your typical academic class.  It was about learning and thinking how to make better decisions, rather than just doing assignments.  Forlines cares about teaching and I highly suggest taking a class of his at Duke.  I really liked the seminar teaching style and class discussion.

Fantastic Professor. He's extremely interested in his students and is a finance savant. You'd be hard pressed to find someone as knowledgeable in behavioral economics as he, and he has a lot of experience in the field. If you show up to class and participate, you'll be greatly rewarded. A must take class at Duke.

He loves talking to his students. I went to office hours before class once and spent hours just chatting with him, both about course-related topics and life. And you can definitely tell he likes teaching the course.

The class is about virtual museums and it is very engaging, energetic and very useful for any job in the field of museums/cultural heritage/CRM. Lectures, readings and activities are inspirational and innovative (super cool the eye-tracking experiments at the Nasher Museum). Prof. Forte is a great and passionate lecturer and discussant.

He's nice and his research seems interesting, but really poorly organized and expectations unclear. The whole class is just discussing a bunch of readings that say the same 5 things, lectures are just him ranting. Lab portion nonexistent; you don't learn how to use any of the tech he talks about. He doesn't grade anything tho so at least it's easy
Dr Forte ran his seminar really clearly despite the pandemic. The readings were really interesting, and as long as you pay attention in class, the grading criteria is also really light.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Prof Forte runs his seminar very well. Practically the entire class is based on discussions, and he is really interested and knowledgeable in his topic. He loves to promote interest and discussion among students, and is always welcoming to new ideas! Highly recommend him for first-year seminar, his class is very manageable yet stimulating.
Very engaging class, lot of discussions, nice readings, really cool stuff.
Awesome lecturer very inspiring

Tangential and unengaging rambles for lectures. Can't figure out what's going on in his head, and very unapproachable. Very abstract readings that don't correspond well to lecture, and he makes no effort to parse them out. The worst professor I've had in my years at Duke. Avoid at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: This is the writing class you want. She's not the most popular one but her class is definitely so much less work than the others and she makes everything done in steps and it's very manageable. I came in with low expectation cuz it's not anyone's top choice but was very surprised- she's a very kind, smart prof and her class is not bad at all.

I took this class because all other Writing 101 classes were full. Ended up being one of my favorite classes so far. One out of the three readings was boring as hell. The other two I would have read even if it weren't for class. Her mannerisms are odd, but her feedback is excellent. She is passionate, caring, and funny! Would take again.

She is one of the best professors I have met at Duke. Her classes are more informative than educative and she's so knowledgeable in whatever subject we would discuss. She is strict in class but fun as well so please behave during class. The final paper prompt is well-defined from start of the semester so you have a lot of time to work on it

Had Dr. Ford for Writing 101: African American Literature. Her class involves a lot of reading, but most of it is pretty interesting. Classes are discussion based, but as long as you participate a little bit you'll be fine. She's super nice and funny and you can tell that she really cares about the subject.

Had low expectations for this class but actually found it to be extremely interesting. There is a lot of reading homework but she is very helpful if you are unsure of anything, always willing to meet outside of class hours. Good sense of humour and not strict as long as you do what you need to do. Class isn't that hard if you are a good writer.

Overall, Professor Ford's class was a great experience.  She made her classroom into an environment that emphasized the importance of teamwork when it comes to writing papers.  She also encourages us to seek help from her and several outside sources (i.e. - writing tutors, librarians, etc.).

Very tough grader, but teaches interesting material for her Black Eros Writing 101 class and knows a lot about it. Isn't very helpful outside of class but is willing to meet. Slow on grading papers (of which there are few) but feedback is definitely there, though grading criteria is very unclear.

Decent prof, but I felt that there was little new info covered each lecture, just a few points on music. Another issue was his harsh grading claiming that even a "B grade is a very good grade and an honor to get". So this makes it tough to maintain a high GPA. Little info learned, but there are opps to do in depth work so theres some there.

Because I was already in 3 STEM classes, I was looking for an easy Writing 101. I made the right choice- most of the semester has minimal work (no papers, just reading a few short articles). Prof Font is very kind and just a cool guy. The final paper is a lot of work, but easily managed if you stay on his schedule (but he's flexible with deadlines)

Professor Font was an amazing professor. Class is not too difficult and very interesting. He made class enjoyable every time and the class improved the quality of my writing overall. I would 10/10 recommend this professor to anyone skeptical about taking one of his classes.

Class was no work until the final research project, which was a lot. He is very unclear with grading criteria and would take off points unnecessarily for everyone. However, our final grades were out of 110%, with 10% for "breathing room," and he "rewards hard work" so my grade worked out in the end. Nice guy but leaves things very open-ended.

Professor Font is a fantastic professor. He is a very easy grader and is extremely cool. Writing 101 is a required class, I had three basketball players in my class. That is how you know this is an easy class. For a writing class, there is not a ton of writing. We have been working on one essay this entire semester.

Very nice professor who cares about students and is willing to help; participation really matters. If you engage yourself you'll do well. Also he doesn't give too much direction and leaves directions intentionally unclear sometimes. Doing these projects is a great learning experience; you'll learn how to do similar projects in the future.

The class is really easy and occasionally interesting.  However, the professor doesn't really give any direction, and I have no idea how he gives grades.  If you're into modern art and avant-garde stuff, you'll like this class.  Otherwise, its just an easy, confusing class.

Prof. Font made some pretty esoteric material ("Sound, Art, and Abstraction" is weirder than even the title suggests) accessible and very interesting. The assignments were easy and sparse, which didn't help me improve my writing much, but discussions were awesome. He met with us individually more than once and brought in cool demonstrations/guests.

Sound, Art, and Abstraction is probably one of the best Writing 101 classes. Font is a very soft-spoken man, but he takes the time to meet individually with all of his students to discuss their progress in his class. The class is easy, and interesting if you're interested in music/sound-related topics. Mostly discussion, not many assignments.

The subject itself was extremely scattered (World Music in the Post Digital World) and the course lacked direction. This made it even more difficult for students to grasp what was asked of them of the course of the semester. Grading was nit-picky and arbitrary, especially for a basic, freshman seminar requirement. DO NOT TAKE
Professor is great. Load of work is very manageable, and his classes are special because you can tell his passion for the theater studies.
Interesting class. Really fun and you get to know your classmates very well.
really interesting mixed media class. great change up from just boring readings. very knowledgeable, approachable. great overall!

I really loved this class, and gained an ongoing appreciation of Opera from it.  I also learned a lot about film.  I can't think of any downside from the experience.  Prof. Foster also wrote me a good rec.
booooooooring
awesome class, awesome professor.  I can't see why he was rated badly.  Very easy, funny, helpful, and smart.

Incredibly smart, well read and helpful. Some classes can be dry, but the class discussions are excellent. He is very approachable and I think a very good professor. I think he can be kind of generous with grades sometimes too.

Such a Jerk...very full of himself, doesnt help anyone out...stupid essay formats that you have to follow or you fail....such a bad guy, such a bad class, dont take it unless you are into causing yourself great pain
Very unhelpful, very boring, very BAD teacher and BAD class

Great class to work on your writing and speaking. She did a great job bringing our voices out in a seminar style, and her feedback was detailed and kind. There's lots of room for you to explore your voice and style through the many different forms of writing her assignments allow. Highly recommend.

Madame Florand is a such wonderful professor. Her class is extremely fun and very easy as long as you put in an effort and do your homework. There are quite a few homework assignments, but most of them are pretty interesting and help you grow as a writer. I would highly recommend this course!!
Mme Florand is such a nice person. Her classes were interesting and she would give you 100 for everything if you show effort. Definitely take a class with her if you need/want to take French.

Take any class with professor Florand. I took 308S Manger. I only took it to meet my language requirement, but ended up being a class that I am so thankful I took. Mme. Florand couldn't possibly be kinder. My french is not great by any means, but she made me much more confident in my skills. Best teacher in french department. An absolute saint

Laura Florand is so kind and helpful and gives great feedback on writing! She makes the class accommodating for people who aren't the strongest in French. Also, 301s is really fun and laidback as a whole.

Laura is such a kind, well-spoken, and caring professor who gives extremely personalized feedback and is always accessible outside of class. I highly recommend this class to anyone; it was fun and not a lot of work. Probably the most down-to-earth and unserious professor I have had at Duke. Cannot recommend enough.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Amazing person and professor. Gives good feedback about your writing and actually listens to her students. Definitely take any of her classes if you have the chance!

If you take French at Duke, you want to take it with Madame Florand! She is a wonderful professor who is incredibly amiable and caring towards her students. She provides good feedback and you will be more than ready to write your final portfolio. Be prepared to read and do your discussion responses (200-300 words twice a week). She's the best!

Awesome class. If you're a little weaker in French, (i.e. <4 years experience, 4 AP score) it's completely manageable, but prepare to be challenged. She's super understanding and pushes you just enough: you can make this class as hard as you want. About 2 200-300 word papers a week and 20 pages of reading.

Professor Florand is easily the best French professor Ive had at Duke. She genuinely cares about her students and adapted well to teaching online. Expect lots of homework, but she is a generous grader as long as you put in the effort.

Madame Florand is so sweet and genuinely cares about her students. She always come to class with a positive attitude and makes sure to ask everyone how they are before beginning her lessons. She does ask her students to write a good amount, but the assignments are not too difficult and she respects if you put in effort.

kindest person ever. expect multiple hours of hw per week, but if you put a little work in, can get an A or A minus and learn a lot from a great professor. definitely take if you're a writer or want to improve your writing!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Inspirational--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Very sweet and nice teacher but can be very strict. You MUST do the work on time and be prepared and ready to participate! But as long as you do this you will be fine.

Good professor who cares about her students and wants you to succeed. Be sure to do the readings, watch the movies, and know your stuff extremely well or she'll think you didn't do any of it and penalize the entire class.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Madame Florand is fantastic! She does a great job of shaping class discussions around the material (almost all of which was very interesting) and letting students share their thoughts. Was always in a great mood and made the classroom a very welcoming environment. Would definitely take her class again!
She did a great job explaining the details of grammar topics, and always gave plenty of time for individual feedback on writing assignments. Great professor!

Madame Florand is a lovely woman, very caring about her students. She really wants you to do well. She doesn't post her powerpoints and the quizzes are difficult, but most of the writing assignments are short and quite enjoyable.

Madame Florand was a great French professor!  She came to class every day with a cheerful attitude, she was very clear in her expectations all semester, and her workload was manageable.  She was a very fair grader, always giving feedback along the way.  Would highly recommend taking a class with her.

daily grammar hw for completion,5 essays total - reviewed them in class & gave feedback. For 1st 2 essays, edited our final essays& let us turn them in again.) 4 grammar quizzes. A little more work than other lang. classes but not a hard grader/participation counts a lot so u can't skip. worked to make our class very tight-knit. understanding/kind!

Fun fact: Madame Florand is also an award-winning novelist! Which is a cool aspect I wish more students knew. Adv. Writing Workshop was a fun class where you just learn about 5 different writing styles, with some grammar review in between. Very reasonable workload. SHe really works to make a great small group learning environment, would recommend!!

Madame Florand made French, a class that I did not much enjoy in high school, one of my favorite classes of my first semester freshman year. She is understanding, flexible, and always willing to help you out. Her tests and essays are also very fair. Lastly, she comes to every class enthusiastic and I have never seen her in a bad mood.

Mme Florand is the sweetest and most understanding teacher ever. I had her for French 76 as a freshman and I am so glad I got her class. There is grammar homework every night, but it's fairly routine and easy. The films studied in class are interesting and varied. The exams are not too bad either and re-writes are available for essays.
Real nice and fairly standard.
Best french professor I've ever had.
Awesome!

I LOVE Mme Florand! Having had her for both 63 and 76, I can say that she is a great, interesting professor, a fair grader, kind and understanding, and always available if you need extra help. There is consistently homework every night, but none is too difficult. She lets you rewrite your papers, which is great. Highly recommended!

Florand almost killed my love of French. She always insisted on insipid groupwork. The sketch project was a huge time drain & frustration. The class's tone was also thoroughly anti-Semitic. Some texts used Jewish stereotypes, & Florand told us  it was hard for the French to think of the Nazis as bad people, since they were so charming in person!

You will have a lot of work and you need to do it in order to participate in class but Florand is very fair. I didn't like the class the first few weeks but by mid-semester I loved it. Do your blog weekly or you'll regret it in the end. Shes really helpful if you talk to her and if you can handle the work, def a prof I recommend.

Florand is very nice and a great techer but she is a ton of work and somewhat expects French to be your world all semester.  I'd recommend her as a great teacher but not someone I'd choose if I'm just trying to get my language requirement fulfilled
She is really uptight
Madame Florand is a really great French teacher.  She makes class interesting and has a creative teaching style.  The work isn't too hard and she isn't a very hard grader.  Recommended.

This class was mostly grammar review, so it's relatively easy if you have a strong background. There are daily homeworks, and all grammar must be self-studied. Classes were generally based on speaking, which was very helpful. The tests and papers were fair, as was the grading. Prof. Florand encouraged participation and taught very well.

I think there was maybe one A in my class this semester.  Other 76 teachers give check pluses on homework because its supposed to raise your grade, but she gives mostly check minuses which ends up killling your final grade.  If you see that you have her, switch into another section.
She's really tough at first, but seems to get easier as the semester goes on.  Her quizzes and exams are fair and she really gets the whole class involved.

To be honest, I was soooo scared of her at the beginning of the semester, but she's awesome once you get used to the class. She's really great at getting the whole class involved and is very clear as to her expectations.  great prof!
