very nice- great teacher to have if youre entering french or have a weak background. i will definitely look for her for other classes- she is an easy grader and very understanding
she's really nice and very patient.  she has a really heavy american accent when she speaks french and goes slowly, but it really helps you learn.
She is very nice and she never makes you feel stupid for not knowing how to say something. She creates a very safe and honest atmosphere in her classroom and she teaches the language well.
Really willing to help her students out.  Very clear as to what is expected of her students.
Really really strict about being on time to class and turning homework in on time, but you will learn a lot from her.  Very nice.
Fletch is the best TA I have ever had. I hope that one day I'll grow up to be as articulate and intelligent as him.
Dr. Rydell is a god. We orz him ten times every single day.

Dr. Rydell has got a whole bakery in the back. For this reason, it's extraordinarily difficult to pay attention to his lectures. I put "online savvy" because he demonstrates expertise in navigating Web2 with tools like IE.
Dr. Rydell is one of the most caring and understanding teaching assistants that I have had up to this point. He is always available outside of class, even at 1am!

Rydell is not only funny but cool. He is savvy but approachable. He is intelligent beyond words yet one of the best communicators I have ever encountered. If anyone has the chance to have Rydell as TA, I could not recommend it more; it will literally change your life.
One of the best TA's I have had the opportunity to know. He is amazing and insightful; truly a once-in-a-lifetime human being.

Too many Duke students think online material can replace showing up. Brian's a strong professor: clear lectures, fair tests, and if you do poorly, that's on you. Attendance and effort have dropped hard post-COVID, AI isn't helping, and grades show it.

My king. So nice and caring. His tests are so incredible difficult but he is an amazing teacher and curves well. I learned so much from him. Definitely go to his lectures even though they aren't mandatory.
extremely passionate about linear algebra

Easily my favorite professor from the semester I took him. Highly caring, easy to approach and talk to. Make sure you go through all the past midterms, because the midterms are tricky and hard! Overall, an amazing experience I would love to have again.

One of the best professors at Duke. Really easy to tell that he put a lot of time and effort into structuring the course because it was so organized. Go to lecture and actually do the quizzes/problem sets that he assigns. Do as many problems from past exams as you can because all three midterms were pretty hard, especially the last two.

Amazing lecturer, clearly explains each concept with his slides. Homeworks are tough though - do get on them early. Really helpful outside class to help you with doubts. 

Exams can be a bit tough/confusing but are fair.
He was an ok lecturer, he seemed passionate about this class, but the course is much harder than it needs to be and he sometimes seemed dismissive of questions.

THE BEST MATH PROFESSOR YOU WILL HAVE AT DUKE!!! His lectures are super engaging, and he is always happy to answer questions. You can tell he is passionate about what he teaches. Could not recommend this class more!!!

Bfitz is an awesome guy and an even better lecturer, I highly recommend going to lectures so you can engage in the content rather than just using his YouTube videos. Tests and topics are definitely hard, but doable if you put in the work. Final was easier and more straightforward than the midterms.

bfitz is great, lectures arent required but i recommend going to them. he articulates the lectures well and OH r very convenient because theyre between lectures so definitely ask question then. the tests are hard, but very doable as long as you ensure you fully know all the content and he has lots of past tests available. will miss this class

Professor Fitzpatrick is amazing. His website is structured well, and his lectures are cohesive and clear. The midterms were a bit tricky, so definitely practice with the past midterms that he provides. The course is based heavily on the midterms and finals. The course is challenging but very rewarding. Best math professor I've ever had!

Truly one of the best to ever do it. Makes math fun, engaging, slightly difficult, and rewarding. Each lecture was a treat, and his jokes always kept the lectures lively. I highly recommend this course

Best professor I have for the semester! His lectures are very clear and easy to follow, and his resources like video lectures and past papers are very useful. The midterms might be a bit hard, but it's 100% manageable if you do the past exams and make sure you understand everything in the quizzes and problem sets.
He is a good teacher exams can just be difficult. I would recommend being careful in studying for every midterm they can be make-or-break for the class.
I wanna jump to his bear and snuggle up all inside of it.

So so so bad. His midterms are so much harder than the content covered in the class, and his lectures are so unhelpful. He doesn't teach well at all and he's horrible with giving partial credit. Just overall a horrible class. Don't listen to all the glazers!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: By far the most efficient and organized lecturer out there. He explains concepts better than any Math prof I've ever had. It doesn't get better for Duke Math. Take every practice test and you're more than well prepared for the midterm. Though attendance isnt mandatory, the in-class experience sets you up to do well and you walk out prepared.

Truly he is been the best professor I have had at Duke. You actually learn the material, yet you are set up so well for success. The way he teaches is so organized and thorough that I felt so prepared for the midterms and did not have to do much outside studying. He has designed this class in the most optimal way for students to learn the concepts.

This professor is AMAZING. Easily one of the best professors at Duke and made this subject one of my favorites (even as someone who doesn't like math). Although you may not feel like you did the best on the midterms, the grading is extremely fair, and BFitz is always willing to help students. Super cool guy and recommend FLUNCHing him.

I recommend doing the problem sets right after lecture for reinforcement. Take every practice exam and be able to verbally explain your work as vocabulary and process is fundamental to understanding. Stay on top of things if you take this in the summer, the class moves fast.
Do all the practice exams (think of them more as puzzles than straight computation) and check your problem sets with a group. Go to office hours!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Bfitz deserves nothing but applause. He is truly the best lecturer at Duke. The class covers some pretty complicated topics but he explains exactly what you need to know, nothing more or less. I walked out of every lecture of his feeling motivated to get started on the homework.

The material is challenging, but Bfitz delivers amazing lectures that make it much easier to understand. The practice problems are incredibly helpful, and the numerous assignments provide plenty of opportunities for improvement.

BFitz emphasizes problem-solving over computation in 218. Test questions require deep understanding of the material and are tricky. This increase in difficulty is balanced by the fact that BFitz's lectures are prepared and organized extremely well. As long as you carefully learn everything covered in the lectures, getting a good grade is doable.

Amazing lectures, I would highly recommend going and engaging in them. Brian is accessible outside of class, along with many TA's who I found to all be super knowledgeable and helpful. Take this class seriously even if you have been successful in prior math classes and you will be fine.

A lot of the class will have taken linear before, so don't expect a curve to save you on exams (and they are brutal). BUT, know that you've got a great support system with BFitz and his TAs. Do the practice exams, collaborate, and reach out for help early on. Make this course your priority. If you put in the work, you will be greatly rewarded.

Came into Duke with high expectations for BFitz and can confidently say they have all been met and then some. Clear and engaging lectures, relevant homework/problem sets, and plenty of resources to help you succeed. Although the exams are difficult and require extensive preparation, they are still certainly doable with the resources provided.

He is a very good professor, and his lectures are excellent. Do all of the assignments, both for your grade and for the sake of practice. Take notes too! The exams are not easy, but he gives partial credit. He is very accessible thru office hours and his TAs were great. Would recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Definitely a difficult course, and I don't plan on taking another class with him, but he was engaging and the concepts were interesting. Great professor, just be ready to study and work a lot outside of class, even if high school math was easy for you.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Bfitz was an outstanding lecturer, you can tell he really spent a lot of time preparing each lecture. He explained topics very very very well. This being said, his test questions were definitely tricky, but if you do all the practice tests you can succeed. I came back from a C on the first midterm to an A in the class. PRACTICE!!!!

For preparing for the final, I recommend redoing exams I, II, and III together for practice, and also revising all of the factorizations, how they are helpful for solving different questions/simplify the process (ex. A=QR can make solving projections easier), and how to create the factorizations from a matrix.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Best math prof I've had so far! Lectures are not mandatory but highly recommended. bfitz lectures in a clear manner that is easy to follow and he also makes classes entertaining with occasional jokes.

In the midst of confusing grading criteria, subpar lectures and irksome online materials that marked my freshman fall, Brian Fitzpatrick was my oasis. 218D2 is a wonderful class that reflects years of intelligent refinement, setting you up wonderfully for further math and imparting a love of the subject (if you take the time to appreciate it).

Very engaging lectures, excellent at explaining material, and a great sense of humor as well. Homework load is decent, but most problems are easy and collaboration is encouraged. Test questions are mostly written so that they look incredibly complicated until you notice small details, so know pay attention to details during lectures.

BFitz has a deep passion for not just LinAlg but also gives a lot of thought to his teaching style. Lectures are very engaging; he is a skilled orator and communicates very effectively. His problem sets are helpful in better understanding computation. If you consistently stay with the material over the semester, the midterms aren't all that bad.
The lecture goat. Truly such an interesting class and he explains everything so well. Do all the practice midterms he provides and you will do well on the tests.

One of the best if not the best lecturer I've had at Duke. Attendance not mandatory but GO TO LECTURE!!! Everything taught out of lecture. Weekly HW, not many problems for each but enough to force you to think. Accessible out of class, Bfitz and his TA's office hours are very useful.

BFitz is the best teacher I've had at Duke. He forces you to engage in lectures, has a good sense of humor, and is accessible outside of class. His course website is very easy to navigate and I feel like I was set up to succeed. I also got tutoring through ARC that helped keep me on track with psets. PRACTICE EXAMS PRACTICE EXAMS DO THEM

Bfitz is one of the best lecturers I've ever had. He is engaging and truly cares about the topic. He is kind, and his office hours are super helpful. There is a good bit of homework, but his tests aren't too difficult if you study well. He is very accessible and really wants his students to succeed.
The best professor I have had so far at Duke
Fantastic

Huggeee B.Fitz fan. He's a great lecturer and a funny, up front guy. He organizes the material in a very logical, easy-to-follow way. Tests are often only 5 questions, and the hardest part is figuring out what you need to do not how you need to do it. Can def suck if you don't know how to do one of the problems.

The class was hard for me personally, but you can tell he put tons of effort into preparing his lectures and lessons. Prof. Fitzpatrick is extremely approachable and humorous; he also brings great enthusiasm and energy when giving lectures. Make sure to take advantage of FLUNCH opportunities to meet up with him outside of class!

One of the best math professors at Duke. Very organized website with accessible notes and practice material, timely lectures with humor sprinkled throughout, and many hours offered for extra help. FLUNCHed him early on in the semester with a few of my friends and can say that Bfitz genuinely loves this course and dedicates many hours to his work.

B. Fitz teaches through PowerPoint that very helpful. The homework is much harder than what the notes teach but with the help of classmates and TAs, you can figure it out. He has a fast teaching style but he gives you many opportunities to ask questions and clear up any confusion.
He is just perfect

Best professor I've had during my time at Duke so far. His explanations are very clear and his lectures are amazing. He provides a reasonable amount of homework and is always willing to help students before/after class. Extremely well-organized class. If you attend lectures and stay on top of the content, you'll end with an A.

Bfitz is a an AMAZING lecturer. The way he explains things and the slideshows he uses during lecture make sense. He is awesome at teaching a problem solving mindset. This class is difficult, no doubt, but there is no better professor for the class.

Lecturers like this are tough to come by. Very few subject experts can convey their mastery of the subject in simple terms. I'm always amused at how he breaks down those high-level concepts in the simplest of terms. 

Tests will require you to practice, but only from whatever he teaches in class + past papers. Have fun in this one!
Incredible lecturer, fair tests and grading. Best math professor I've had at Duke so far.

Fitzpatrick is an outstanding professor and makes linear algebra simple! He puts so much thought and care into his PowerPoints. He recommends that you come to lecture although old lectures are on YouTube. Lots of psets.
Great class, great professor. Recommended!
Great class. Would recommend.

Bfitz REALLY cares about helping students and always stays after class to help people. 

Only con is that he is pretty irritable and can get upset over certain things which kinda makes lecture anxiety ridden. 

Class itself is really easy and just lots of material to remember. Tests are all fair.

BFitz is by far and away the best lecturer I've ever had. Extremely engaging and makes learning something thats honestly quite boring pretty interesting. Midterms are really tough, he tends to use types of problems you haven't seen before, so you need to actually understand the content and not just know how to do problems. All lectures are online.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: My best experience with Duke math so far. Super engaging lectures but attendance is not required since all are recorded on YouTube. Exams are fair. Homework is very helpful and manageable.

BFitz is literally the coolest dude ever and his lectures are amazing! Great teacher because you actually learn and his lectures help you when it comes to 3 weekly comprehension quizzes and problem sets. Good amount of work but it helps a lot when it comes time for the tests. Take this class!!!
BFitz is the best professor in the math department.
BFitz made me want to be a Math major. Guy is awesome even if you're not in Pratt I would take this class. If you do all the HW you will do fine on the midterms.

Fast-paced but excellent lectures (the class covers lots of things). Weekly homework take ~2hrs. His midterms contain some "tricky" questions. It's a light class, as long as you come to lecture and don't slack off. He's very helpful if you have questions after class. If you fall asleep/don't show up, he has online lectures on Youtube.

B Fitz is the GOAT. Definitely made learning linear algebra an enjoyable experience. You can clearly see that he is passionate about the material he is teaching. Lecture slides and notes are clear and easily understandable. His lectures are a bit fast paced but his explanations of concepts are thorough and he usually takes questions during lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Bry Guy is the GOAT! Explains things very thoroughly and methodically. Reasonable homework and is VERY accessible to help you with it during office hours. The best math prof ever, and you can tell he is in love with teaching linear algebra.

Caring professor that is passionate about the material he teaches. Homework sets were difficult for me but he is very willing to help clear up any confusing concepts and provide tips during his office hours. Amazing class.

B Fitz is a great lecturer and makes the course pretty easy. The course is quite boring, but B Fitz makes the class as interesting as possible. He also has all his lectures on youtube, which was an awesome resource.

I love bfitz. He's an amazing lecturer, and is always willing to help students (he'll stay after class, respond to emails, etc). His passion for math is so refreshing. That said, his class was extremely difficult--his exams make you apply concepts in new ways, not just applying formulas. But, if you need to take linear, it better be with bfitz.
Absolute GOAT
Duke has 2 GOATS: Coach K and Coach BFitz

Bfitz has a clear style of lecturing (if you aren't comitted to office hours, lectures are the only interaction.) They're fast but it never feels like there's anything irrelevant, and he takes all questions in lecture. The way he weaves together older ideas later in the year is straight captivating. Always energetic and funny when he needs to be.

Math 218 was great with Professor Fitzpatrick. The first midterm was rough but he was willing to curve it significantly. Even so, the average for every midterm hovers around a B/B- so you do have to work for an A. The lectures are great and I highly recommend attending all of them.

Take 218 with Fitzpatrick if you can. Really clear lecturer that can explain all concepts seamlessly. Granted, I think the class was probably a bit too easy (no midterms, not super in depth into content), especially as I hear now what people have to do in 218 now. Easy A if you go to office hours/discussion
Math 218 isn't the easiest class, but Fitzpatrick was an amazing professor. He's the most helpful prof I've had so far at Duke. He genuinely cares about you understanding the content and succeeding.

Prof. Fitzpatrick's lectures are clear and concise. However, I find the lectures to only dab on the concepts, and I was only copying and pasting the formulas most of the time in the homework problems. I emailed him once to ask for a proof of a concept and he quickly emailed back a good one. Overall, he's a great professor, but I didn't like MATH218
Good lecturer. Prerecorded lectures are short, I wish he gave more examples. Discussion section & OH are very helpful, they'll walk through homework with you. He's very friendly and conversational.

Brian made math my favorite class which is pretty uncommon at Duke. His lectures are amazing and his tests are very fair. The way he explains concepts made me excited about math and I actually understood the theory behind it. He responds to emails very quickly and overall he's a nice down-to-earth guy who genuinely loves math.

I would recommend taking Linear with Fitzpatrick. He always made an attempt to explain clearly and was very accessible (3 office hours per week!). He is very organized. The tests are pretty similar to the homework. His class is a little easier bc he stuck mostly to definitions, formulas, and examples though, so sometimes felt like regurgitation.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I took the experimental engineering section of 212 with Fitzpatrick, and let me just say Dr. Fitzpatrick is fantastic! He's really great at explaining not only what the concept is, but why we'd want to use that concept. The class is challenging, but not overly so, and he will answer all of your questions without becoming condescending.

In the world of suckiness that is Duke Math, Prof. Fitzpatrick is the sole bright spot. Easiest math class I've taken at Duke, simply because he's amazing at simplifying and explaining concepts. If you take linear with anyone except Fitz, you're making a mistake.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Hilarious teacher and easily the best math teacher that I have ever had. However, the class goes very fast (new topic every lecture) so you really need to keep up with studying outside of class because it is a difficult class and the tests are not easy.

The class is hard, but he is an exceptionally good math teacher - he lays out the logic behind the concepts step by step in lecture, and will stop and explain it again in more detail if you don't understand something. He is also super accessible through his office hours, which are really helpful.
Great teacher and good class. Definitely would recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Fitzpatrick is a fantastic lecturer he is clearly passionate about math and has a knack for making tough concepts accessible. His class is a lot of work, with weekly quizzes and three midterms plus a final, but he preps you well. Discussion sections are required, but entirely useless. Overall though, great class.

218 with Fitz is awesome. hes funny and a literal genius. the clearest teacher Ive ever had. This class will likely be my first where I won't be close to the A range, but I would take it again in a heartbeat. grading is exceptionally fair, and the tests are tough but representative of what you know. couldnt recommend this class more. take it.

He does not assign too much HW and his exams are computation heavy (work fast) but representative of the lectures. He helped me become better at deriving formulas instead of simply memorizing them. Definitely take Math 218 with him.

Fitzpatrick is far and away the best professor I've ever had for a math class. The class covers a lot of ground and every week builds on material covered in preceding weeks, so you need to keep up. Exams make up most of the grade, but the homeworks are useful practice. Super funny, accessible through email and office hours10/10 would recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Hilarious--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Fitz is an amazing lecturer, is clear and understandable and stops lecture for anyone with a question. He was clear with grading and was available outside class where he would gladly answer anyone's questions. He genuinely cares about students' success. The class was very difficult, however, and you have to put in the work if you want to do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Not the best lecturer, read off the slides. He went fast through lectures so it was easy to get lost in what he was saying. Weekly quizzes but they were not worth a lot. Very useful to do the homework but it's not mandatory. Tests were challenging, try to get copies from previous semesters to prepare.

Great professor. If you study the slides, prepare for the quizzes and understand how each topic pivots to the next, you'll do great. By far my most enjoyable math experience at Duke. Make sure to continuously revisit past material - it builds up pretty quickly.

I thought Brian was great - his lectures are very clear, and he is good at answering questions about the material. Office hours are helpful for completing the homework or just trying to understand concepts better. Tests aren't easy but are graded fairly. Plus, his occasional tangents can be hilarious!

Brian's a great professor. I really recommend going to lecture -- it was helpful to me and Brian does his best to make sure the material's clear. Attendance and homework are optional, so weekly quizzes and exams make up the bulk of the grade. The weekly quizzes are straightforward and midterms are fairly doable. Work hard, and you'll be fine

Fitzpatrick is a very clear and engaging lecturer, and he is very good at answering questions in office hours. The homework he assigns is not very representative of the test difficulty though. There have been several questions on each test that required on the spot creativity, which is especially difficult under strict time pressure (v. long tests)
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Math at Duke is very difficult, but Brian is definitely one of the best professors and explains concepts very clearly. The exams are much harder than the homework, and there are weekly homework quizzes and discussion assignments, but it's a relatively manageable class . Definitely take this class with him if possible.

Professor Fitzpatrick is the best mathematics instructor at Duke. His lectures are very clear and what he displays on the board is what you need to know. He does an amazing job taking more difficult concepts and simplifying them without compromising their features. Study the notes for his tests and you'll do great.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Fitzpatrick is an excellent teacher. What he writes on the board is what you need to know, so showing up to lecture is essential. HW is lengthy at first, but textbook solutions are online and the AHP answers are given in discussion. The test questions are straightforward and follow practice problems done in class. Doing old practice exams is key

Brian is incredible, one of the best math professors I've ever had. He's able to take challenging concepts and teach them in a clear and simple way. Go to class, his lectures are helpful and funny. His tests are challenging but if you study enough you should do well. He also really wants to see his students succeed and will help outside of class.

Brian is funny, but that's about all he's got. Lectures were generally unproductive. He would go through the same example during two different classes but would rush through it both times. Class was tough but not unreasonable. A mediocre professor.

Brian is one of the best professors I've had at Duke and you should definitely take any math class you can with him. He's a great lecturer and the workload is fair. The tests are straightforward and if you study you'll be fine. Such a cool guy also, if you take his class, make sure to FLUNCH.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Brian was amazing! Super helpful when I went to him for help outside class

Brian is funny, doesn't care about little things, and his tests aren't impossible. However, I found his lectures in the second half of the semester unhelpful, as if he had given up or just gotten too far behind to elaborate. He also communicates very poorly outside of class on grades and help. The textbook for this class is absolutely atrocious.

Math212 is a hard class. Brian does the best he can to make it easy on you. His tests are fair and if you do the homework and pay attention in class you can do fairly well on them. However, the final is a block final and Brian's tests tend to be easier than some of the other professors', so watch out.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Loved his class, great professor

Brian's a real gem -- half of the people who went to lectures weren't even from our class. Brian's such a great teacher that people sit in on our class just because Brian's so good at delivering the material in a digestible manner. He's a big guy with a big personality and he's fairly hilarious. 10/10 would recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Hands down the best math/science professor at Duke! He always finds a way to make convoluted concepts intuitive. You know the prof is awesome when you don't feel painful walking into a math class. He also writes easy tests!

Take his class!!! Brian was hands down the best teacher I've ever had. He does his best to make the material accessible, and his tests are truly to see if you've attained a solid foundation in the material. As long as you keep up with the homework and study the class notes, you'll do well. If you've struggled with Duke Math, he's a true hero.

Brian was dope. Super smart guy who's very passionate about math, funny, and really wants his students to learn. Also very helpful and friendly during his office hours. Multi is a difficult subject by nature, but I found his tests very reasonable. Make sure to study hard for the course-wide final though: it's very tough.

BEST TEACHER IVE EVER HAD. covers difficult material in the clearest/most straightforward way ever. hilarious digressions. very helpful in office hours/more than willing to meet with you separately. likes when students ask questions. midterms not horrible relative to other sections. graded very fairly. such a nice guy. take multi with him!!

An absolutely brilliant and amazing math professor. Tests (not too hard) are graded very fairly.  Knows the material inside and out and can teach it better than anyone. Really helpful when it comes to answering questions.  He is the man, doesn't care about BS things like notation, and ensures all his students know the material very well.

Brian is one of the most caring members on the faculty. His office hours are the best, for he is willing to answer even the "dumbest" of all questions. His lectures are a bit abstract, but he is more than willing to work with you outside of class. His exams cover quite a bit of material, but if you talk to him and do practice exams, you're set.

Brian is an amazing teacher and he will explain all the concepts extremely well. His class notes are priceless as they basically cover everything needed in a precise and concise manner. If attend his class and do his homework regularly, you will do well in Multi.
He keeps the class interesting and is a great teacher overall.  Having a PhD student as your professor is genuinely helpful because they are more interested in the material and keep things fun.
Hands down the best

Math 111 is going to be hard regardless of who you take it with. Brian is the man and one of the best professors I have ever had. His tests are tough but they are good preparation for the final. He made me love math and I felt bad whenever I skipped his class since I knew that I would learn something meaningful every day.

Brian is one of the most helpful professors I've had at Duke. His digressions in class are hilarious, and he does a good job of engaging the class. It's really clear that he's passionate about math, and that helps to liven up the material.
Great teacher. Explains everything clearly, very eager to help out, tests are difficult and has a lot of high expectations.
Fantastic teacher. Tests might be harder compared to other sections, but the preparation for the final is worth it. Very helpful, accessible and always entertaining and funny.

Calc 2 is going to be hard with whoever you have. Brian's tests were extremely challenging- but not the hardest of all sections. The difficulty prepared you for the final(same for all sections). He also made himself really accessible out of class STUDY LIKE CRAZY FOR THE FINAL and know labs well! The final is a huge factor in determining your grade

Brian is a pretty helpful guy. His tests are difficult, though-if you're not a math expert, this class is not for you! Why are they hard? He teaches straight out of the book, so you don't learn the logic you need to do well on the tests. Many times, I've found my other friends in other 41 sections can explain the material to me better than he can.

Brian has an awesome beard and is a great teacher.  He is a chill grad student, really knows his stuff, and is good at teaching it.  His tests are tough but necessary preparation for the final which is the same for all 41 classes.
Carol is extremely fair at grading and really wants students to succeed. Very knowledgeable and willing to help.

One of the nicest and most genuine professors at Duke.  Genuinely interested in your development as a person and a student.  Quirky as all get out? Yes.  But that's what makes her so awesome.  She's smart as heck, but also relates well to her students.  Don't miss a chance to take a class with one of the coolest college professors you'll ever meet.
One of my very favorite teachers at Duke. Hated Russian fic before this class; now I think I'm going to get more into it. Extremely willing to work with you on "outside the box" projects.

Professor Flath's Dostoevsky class is one of those courses that reaffirms why I never want to leave Duke and why I love literature in general. Reading Dostoevsky is so applicable to contemporary life, you'll be amazed. Take her classes, you won't be disappointed.

Definitely a little crazy but you love her anyway.  I took her for lit (i.e. in english) and I wish the class/lecture was a little more structured since she seems so smart and the random tangents detract from that.  Nonetheless, I loved her.

Incredible teacher.  She makes Russian fun and is very fair.  Russian is a hard language, but the classes are normally small and she knows your strengths and weaknesses and will help if you ask for it.  She has students over for cookies in her apartment every week.  She's wonderful.  Take this class!

Prof Flath rocks.  She's crazy, but that just adds to the fun.  Ask her about goat-blow if you get a chance.  Actually, ask her about anything if you get a chance.  She's one of the most interesting people I've ever met.

One of the best professors I've had at Duke. A bit disorganized in lecture and the administrative stuff, but at the same time brilliant on subject matter. Grades tough, but fairly. Gives a lot of constructive criticism on papers. Extremely friendly outside of class. Guarantees a B for just doing the work, what's not to like.

Possibly insane, but that's what makes her so cool.  Yes, she often gets off on irrelevant tangents-even in language class-but really, if she didn't we'd all be sleeping through normal russian grammar lectures, and who wants that?  Fair, but not easy. Always willing to make time for you. Great prof!
Very nice lady, likes to bake cookies, but she is  prone to wander off on tangents.  For example, "Did you know that life is grammar?"
Goes off on tangents, but makes for one heck of a hilarious class. Extremely interesting personality.
Very intelligent lady and is good at explaining things one on one.  She tends to wander a bit in grammar explanations in class though.  Grading is fair, and she makes lots of cookies!

Prof. Flath is what a true college professor should be.  She's interested in the topics she teaches and in teaching in general.  She made a subject that I couldn't have cared less about interesting.  Take a non-language class taught by her if you can.
Made a subject that was seemingly horrible so interesting.  Great sense of humor.  Genuinely interested and caring.  One of my best academic experiences.

Time Travels is I think the best writing 20 available--there can be a lot of readings, but the reading is usually very interesting, and it is hardly necessary to do all of it to get a good grade.  If you can write a clear paper, its not hard to get a good grade in this class, and there's not a ton of papers.  Fletcher is incredibly clever and kind.

Really great and inspiring teacher.  Subject matter is presented in clear and interesting manner.  Best class i took as a freshman, wish i could take it again.  ps. you don't have to like science to like this class.

He was my W20 instructor (Time Travels). He is helpful, entertaining and extremely intelligent. He's really prepared for lessons since he teaches this course for couple of years now. Definitely a teacher and a class I would recommend to anyone.

Time Travels was the best class I've taken so far at Duke. He's not particularly easy or hard - I guess you could say fair - but he's so interesting and helpful and you will undoubtedly reference things you've learned in class in conversations with friends. Fantastic prof!

Really not as bad as people say - her lectures aren't amazing but the first midterm was literally exactly like the practice one with switched numbers, the tests are generally predictable and if you know the content you will be fine.

Do not rely on her lectures or notes at ALL, she assumes that everyone has a lot of background knowledge in chemistry even though it is an introductory class. She does not listen to the majority of her students when it comes to feedback. I have had several friends who took college level chemistry who did poorly in her class.

Dr Franz is an EXCELLENT professor. She's awesome, funny and very respectful.
Her lectures tho were not great. She went to the expecifics before the general. She used to overcomplicate basic things. She is a great chemist, probably great professor for advanced classes but not for 101
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Franz was awesome! I truly enjoyed talking to her and learning from her lectures. However, her lectures weren't always clear and fully representative of the important content we needed for homework/exams. The posted study materials and her office hours are very helpful, but If you aren't putting hours outside of class, it's hard to succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Franz is intelligent, and she's really passionate about chemistry. The class structure as a whole was very organized; no complaints about that. However, she could have been a better lecturer--at times, she would make mistakes that would confuse students. (Personally, 70% of my learning came from the textbook as opposed to lecture.) Overall, good.

The course was extremely disjointed, and the midterms were fairly challenging (although not overly difficult if you studied). The final was much harder than anything we had ever seen during the course. It was sheer luck that I was able to get to some of the answers. Study hard for the midterms to give yourself a cushion for the final.

This course and the way it was taught has discouraged me from taking another class in chemistry ever again. Very very very hard for 0 reason. It would be awesome to genuinely learn chemistry instead of just learning how to solve problems for the exam.

Very smart/kind person but one of the worst teachers I've ever had...she doesn't explain anything fully and goes off on tangents about some irrelevant fact only she understands. She also makes random mistakes on notes and doesn't correct them until someone points them out lol.
Half the class skipped her lectures for Martinez, go take her instead

moves so quickly during lecture you literally quickly copy something down and as soon as you look up ITS GONE
not very good at lecturing and doesn't actually explain concepts in a way that allows you to understand what's going on
just go with martinez

Dr. Franz is an amazingly kind and intelligent professor. It's a shame that only a semester is dedicated to inorganic chemistry because she really makes me want to learn more. But due to the time constraint and the required amount of material, lectures do tend to be slightly stressful as one is usually forced to write as fast as humanly possible.

She is a great teacher who wants her students to learn, though she tries to cover all the material too quickly everyday that she teaches. I guess she has a lot to say. The tests are pretty fair overall and the averages are usually in the 70s.

Dr. French is a passionate, humorous, and educated professor. He knows his work, through and through. The class is only 5 essays. You don't receive your grade for each essay until weeks have passed, and his feedback is vague and varies for each essay, so it's hard to improve for the next essay. His grading is very harsh, prepare for B's
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Dr French makes me gouge out my eyeballs while also being one of my fav history professors. He's an extremely hard grader, and most of the class is based on essays. His lectures are incoherent and unstructured, but he's an extremely brilliant and knowledgeable man. He WILL tell you when you're wrong, but he does care. Know what you're getting into!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor French is one of the most knowledgeable professors I've had. He is very passionate about Latin American history and politics. If you appreciate him and work hard in his class, your grade will reciprocate! Not to mention you'll learn a lot, too.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Undeniably one of Duke's better History professors. Don't buy into the other comments, French is very knowledgeable and willing to help. Amazing professor.

He's a really sweet guy. Ya, he's disorganized and everything, but it's just because he's so smart. Don't be discouraged from taking his class, whatever he's teaching at the time. He has a lot to offer, give him a chance. And express an interest and participate in class, and you're good. It is a lot of work though!

Easily the worst teacher I have ever had in my life.  Doesn't respond to emails or phone calls; is late to class and lectures off the top of his head with no clarity or coherence.  I would rather read a 10,000 page volume on tax codes than attend his class.

I actually LOVED his Afro-Brazilian Culture and History Class.  He would play Brazilian music at the beginning and show clips and movies.  The lecture was slide show based and clear.  Grading was a sinch: an ongoing journal that you got graded on two or three times and then at the end.  Basically if you showed up and took notes, wrote/typed neatly + then tried to be creative you did well.  I learned a lot about Brazil from that class and felt enriched.
This class is the definition of boredom and poor quality.  His lectures are incoherent and his organizational skills leave much to be desired. Do NOT take this class

Very frustrating. I was interested in the material beforehand, but was bored to death by his lectures which he seemed to improvise on the spot and were subsequently illogical, rambling and irrelevant to what we read. Grading was based on how fast you could copy your notes, not what you knew.

I admit, he is bad lecturer, but the guy is nice. If you have signficant interest, he'll help you out. He tries too hard sometimes, but the class is easy = OPEN NOTE TESTS and TAKE HOME ESSAYS. like if you read his assignments, then you are golden.

This professor is unquestionably the worst one I have had at Duke. This class was awful, painful, poorly run, and unclear in its expectations. The lectures were rambly and off topic, WHEN the professor bothered to show up, and not just have the TA show a movie. DO NOT TAKE A CLASS WITH JOHN FRENCH.
This professor is the worst one I've ever had. DO NOT TAKE HIS CLASS. He is boring, mean, and unapproachable.

Owen was a solid professor who made his lectures more personalized by frequently interjecting colorful stories from his personal life which were enjoyable in my opinion. This man also literally knows everything, and I was constantly impressed. I know several on here are concerned by name dropping, but this wasn't something that lowered his quality.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Dr. Flanagan was a cool guy, but the grading of the class is not really fair. There were only 3 grades in the class worth 1/3 each: participation, midterm, and final paper. Our TA did all the grading and did not grade with clear criteria AT ALL, so it's tough to know where you stand.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: He is a really really nice person and knows a lot about the subject. Admittedly, he sometimes went off-topic, but the stuff he talked about was really interesting.

took his summer class at berkeley. generally speaking, when anyone asks a question he will simply name drop and then move off topic. however, he was incredibly entertaining because anytime this one kid Adam would raise his hand Owen would either completely disregard what he said or make him look like a total idiot. It was awesome.

Pretty smart guy; however, his teaching ability is unfortunately not correlated with his intelligence. His lectures and lectures go off on tangents way too often. Readings are generally much more useful and tested upon. Grading policy is very subjective, and it's surprisingly hard to make a good grade (considering it's philosophy).

Not only did Flanagan not stay on topic, but at times he even knew it. Talking about his dreams: lusting after Audrey Hepburn is no way related to dualism. Does no teaching, just name drops. We had 7 textbooks that were written all by him or his friends. Class is self-study only, yet his rants are attendance mandatory. Don't take his class.
Well versed excellent content fresh
If you want to hear someone talk about how great they are for an hour every other day and rely on 2 TAs for your grade take this class.

Owen is SO cool and I would definitely recommend taking a class with him. However, he doesn't do any grading at all and relies on 2 TA's who don't always seem to know what they're doing. There is very little work, but the TA's grade somewhat arbitrarily. It is extremely easy to get a B or maybe even B+, but getting an A was surprisingly hard

Owen is, frankly, a brilliant instructor, interesting fellow, and what I would call an "okay dude".  His advice to me has always set me in the right direction, and his approach to the material is both informative and accessible.  He's a bit of an elitist, but that works for him.  If possible, take one of his classes.  It is definitely worthwhile.
Flanagan is GREAT! He likes to drop names but the stories attached are always fascinating. How many profs at Duke know the Dali Lama? Knows his stuff
Good class, not too bad.  Don't take it at 8:30am.  By the end of the semester it's impossible to stay focused during lecture because he tends to move fairly slowly.

An amazing, personable, easy-going, and extremely accessible professor who also happens to be one of the most prominent modern philosophers of our time.  Class discussions are always interesting and he does not waste his students' time on busy work.  Highly recommended!

Owen is an excellent professor.  He is genuinely interested in what he teaches.  He even got me reading phil books in my free time.  Great professor.  Class difficulty is ideal.  Readings were very intriguing, loved the prof, loved his course

Owen is passionate about philosophy and very knowledgeable, however, he spends only about 1/3 of the time on topic. The rest of the time he will talk about topics ranging from the Dalai Lama, to his son, to his Vespa. If you have a fundamental grasp on the material, there's absolutely no need to attend his lectures.

Loves dropping names: Shav, Demarcus, the Dalai Lama, etc. But his lectures are never boring. It is true that he leans heavily upon TA's, but he does teach about half of the philosophy department's courses (an exagerration), so at the intro level this is forgivable.
Gets off topic and runs over, but makes for an interesting class. Intelligent, funny, easy to talk to, interesting.
When I took the class, he seemed more interested in being friends with Shavlik Randolph and some of the football players than to see us learn about philosophy.

I always felt relaxed and eager to participate in his class.  He is very good-natured and relates to students well.  He used his personal experiences and his vast knowledge to supplement our learning.  His lectured tended to wander, but no one's perfect!  I hope I can have another class with him.

Owen makes philosophy fun.  I looked forward to going to his class more than anything I did that semester.  Grades are deceptively difficult--he grades papers a little more strictly than you'd think, judging from his easy-going approach.  But if you know that, you'll be completely fine.  Meet him!

During class, all he did was talk for 75 minutes and rarely allowed students to ask questions or make comments.  Delegated all of his work to 2 TA's; one of them couldn't even speak English.  Go figure.
Owen is awesome (he makes you call him Owen).  He assigns a lot of reading, but it's completely worth it, and he's really eager to learn from students.  Seriously, take his classes.  You'll love him.
Owen is really really really cool. He brings up awesome topic and really makes you think. He's really down to earth and is friends with all the students. Take his courses!

I took Zach Fredman's Heavy Metal Music mini-term course and it was really amazing. The lecture was informative and inspiring! In addition, Zach is so kind and allowed me ti tried out some of his guitars and pedals. But be prepared to read and explore a lot if you are not a zealous metalhead!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Fredman is one of toughest if not the toughest professors for this course. I think for a freshman-level required common core class he is much too strict and intense. Papers were graded harshly with feedback that was hard to understand. Lectures were interesting but he is a cold-caller, so be ready to have read every line of every single reading.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: He made us play a diplomacy game which was fun but the class style generally was discussion based which was complete mess.  He is a junior faculty so has a lot of sense of self-importance. Also, expect a lot of readings on Chinese Civil war the subject of his dissertation and first book. Ruined my interest in history with trivializing everything.
Prof. Fredman is very nice, however, that does not come in use when you are looking for constructive feedback to improve your works. Grading criteria are not clear and vary from student to student.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: He is a tough grader but gives amazing feedback. He is very accessible outside of class and office hours are extremely helpful. He tells you what you need to do to improve and if you do exactly what he says you will do fine in the class. He greatly encourages discussions and wants students to lead the class.

Yes he is a tough grader for freshmen so do be prepared and practice your academic writing in EAP and whatsoever!! Hes not being harsh for no reason. And he does facilitate lots of discussions instead of lecturing. I personally love this. Also quite available outside of classroom. Dont hesitate to meet w/ him if you get bad grades on homework

I made this course CR at the end. The grade I got for this course was the lowest I received at DKU, so I wouldn't say that HIST201 is an easy course. But professor Fredman is nice and responsible. He's accessible outside class and willing to help.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Tough grader

reviews.comment: HIST 201 was very engaging! Professor Fredman did a good job accommodating students with extenuating circumstances. The first half of the class was a historical roleplay simulation, and the second half was a historical research paper. He's very strict about citations, but he provides guides to help. If you can write academically it's not too hard
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Another history class at DKU. I would recommend history classes taught by Professor Guy more who gives much better lectures and grades. Professor Fredmans grading is tougher than normal DKU professors. However, you can still get a satisfied grade if you did everything he asked. But I may not take more classes from him...
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He is a tough grader, especially to freshmen. Also, he doesnt give good lectures. The whole course is basically a discussion with your peers, which is not worthwhile to the high tuition fee you have paid. Ive heard some students recommending to take HIST201 with other professors. I wish I could know that earlier. Anyway, avoid Zach Fredman at DKU.
Never take this course if you are a freshman!!! Prof. Fredman has a really high standard for writing and citation.

A great professor who introduced America Imperialism through different insightful writings. Really learned a lot from him and I was impressed by his technology-free policy in class. It would be really good to spend time discussing and interacting with real people and leave phones and laptops out. Get ready to read writings regularly.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Super nice guy and learned a lot from his history class. Didn't have an insane amount of readings or assignments, but what he did include really helped me understand his class. He loves role-play stuff, so don't be surprised if you end up having role-play/group work. Would take every class with him again!

He is an amazing professor. Fredman is a very good explainer and gives a reasonable amount of work. His discussions and papers make you really think about the course and help you understand the subject even better. He is always accessible, friendly, and a fair grader. He also gives excellent feedback and definitely is a professor worth taking.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment:
I went to her office hours to get an understanding of why the citation portion of the rubric, which should have been easy points, was this odd amount, something like 2.7 out of 5..

Couldn't get a word in, she talked about everything BUT the citations, my reason for coming, vague and inactionable until the moment I left.

Hasso was one of the worst professors I've had at Duke. There was an insane amount of busy work, pop quizzes, and vague assignments. It seemed as if she was trying to make her class a weed-out class. She had no care for others' opinions; unless you agree with her, you are incorrect.

Don't be fooled by the negative reviews - I avoided taking her class because of them and was horribly misled. Best prof ever. It is rare to find an instructor who is kind and empathetic while also pushing you to be your best. She is a fair yet generous grader and is well-connected to other scholars, so she brings in cool speakers regularly.

This Professor only gets bad reps from entitled students and I am a first generation immigrant student. She is a compassionate instructor who is knowledgeable on many topics and has a standard which should be met, rightfully. Simply, if you put in the work her classes are bound to change your life! You will leave better than you came!

I've taken a couple classes with Hasso and she's one of the best professors if you're truly looking to grow. Her approach perfects critical thinking, analysis, and academic writing. Naturally, she expects her students to come prepared, having read all the material to maximize discussion. A+ if you're looking to elevate your analysis and writing.

Steamrolls. Self-Important. Narcissistic. Cites self during lecture. Talks loudly over anyone who tries to contribute to class. On an entirely different planet where there is no other opinion but hers. 0/10. Run.

I have NO idea what the other reviews are talking about. I almost didn't take this class bc of those but I'm glad I did. She does assume some basic knowledge but is willing to meet outside of class. We had pop quizzes (lowest 4 dropped), 3 assignments, a midterm, and a final project. Readings/discussions were normal for a GSF class (I've taken 8).
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Came into this hoping for the best, trying to ignore the warnings, but failed. Hasso is condescending, does not care about her students success, arrogant, and drowns you in unnecessary work. She told me I was not capable of writing a good research project (I got high distinction!) and Duke GSF is investigating her - thats how bad she is.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: From how the class was structured, it felt as if she expected the worst from her students and prepared for worst case scenarios from us. I understand the need for rigor and all of that but this was anxiety-inducing. The class is all about her. I would not recommend taking a class with her, because the cost of doing that on your being, no.

I heard the stories. I thought, "No, she can't really be that bad." Oh how was I wrong. Let me compose a haiku encapsulating my experience this semester:  My legs chained to desk, Wanting to flee Medusa, But I cannot run.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: This is one of the worst classes I have ever taken at Duke. It takes a true level of skill on the part of a professor to make even the most intrinsically fascinating content utterly frustrating and annoying. Hasso is a NIGHTMARE. Won't let you disagree with her. Won't let you stay home even if you have the plague. AVOID AT ALL COSTS.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I had Professor Hasso for Gender & Sexuality in the Middle East and North Africa as a freshmen seminar. Hasso is extremely organized. She follows her syllabus and all the resources you need are always available through SAKAI. She's into small-group discussions based on the reading/watching. She isn't too clear when answering questions. She's great.

The seminar Gender and Sexuality in the Middle East was extremely eye opening and introduced me to many things I may have never explored if it weren't for this class. I learned a lot from her, and it is because of her that I may be pursuing a women studies minor. She is very passionate about her subject and that is clear from the way she teaches.

Professor is condescending to students and unable to listen to student opinions. Grades down opinions that disagree with her standpoint. Most of the class is a bunch of vague theoretical readings. Long readings and movies assigned and never discussed in class. The professor always seems stressed about time but class is full of tangents.

If your opinion isn't in line with hers then your grade will suffer. Very inconsistent and arbitrary with grading. Self important and not open minded. We had to learn what she liked and agree with her views so it was difficult to learn anything in the class. Worst class I've taken at Duke.

Interesting professor, but grades somewhat arbitrarily and harshly. Not an easy class at all, you'll learn tons, but you won't have fun doing it. Very passionate, which is a plus, but it's hard to latch onto her passion sense what she's talking about is not common knowledge. Take the class if you want to work your butt off.
self-important, unorganized lectures,  extremely harsh grading for an intro course.  This class was the most awful class I have ever taken at Duke.

Hasso definitely thinks what she's teaching is important. That can be both good and bad. If your perspective differs from hers, you're in for serious deductions on the assignments. Her grading style is haphazard and very ambiguous. Beware: this is not a blow-off seminar. Attendance and weekly written assignments are required.
Best professor I've had at Duke by far. Definitely take a class with her before graduation.

Allan Friedman is one of the nicest, most caring people you will ever meet at Duke. Chorale is not only a way to connect with music, but to find a great community at Duke, and Allan deserves a lot of the credit for fostering such a welcoming, inclusive environment.
Great director of the Chorale! Really sees each student as a person first and cares deeply about each memeber.

One of my favorite courses. The professor introduced a lot of new music, and seems like he himself listens to a variety of music. Final is creating your own playlist focused on one of the musical elements discussed in class. If you like listening to music def recommend.

Dr. Friedman is so funny and nice. I always love going to chorale. he creates such a great community and is really attuned to the students. he is patient and understanding. i love the music he selects and all the work he puts into chorale!

Chorale was a wonderful singing experience! He was new this semester, so there were a few logistical kinks to figure out, but Allan created a mutually-respective environment between himself and the choir, setting us up for great performances. Overall, Allan is just a nice, approachable guy to be around. Would highly recommend taking Chorale!

For ME 424L. Easily the worst professor I've ever had. Not very helpful with term project and strongly biased. You will get a very bad individual contribution grade no matter how much you contribute to the group project as long as she dislikes you, as she simply lacks the ability to properly and objectively assess students.
Bad teacher
Definitely do not recommend. Find somebody better if you can.
I'd advise all students to NEVER learn from her. Absolutely horrible experience and interactions. Not thoughtful and I didn't learn anything useful.
excellent course and instructor

Dean Franzoni is best described as a mom. She likes the students and wants everyone to do well but doesn't give out easy grades. Her lack of preparedness, poor organization, and insistence that grades be primarily a function of bogus test grades make the class frustrating and often a waste of time. Use class notes, not the book, for tests.
He has amazing lectures, super interesting!

It was a blessing to take a class with Sr. Furtado. He puts his heart into leading each class discussion and assigned very thought-provoking movies for class. I learned a lot about the technicalities of cinema and grew as a Spanish speaker under his guidance.
One of the best professors I've had at Duke! Really engaging lectures, and I loved the material. Participation matters a lot.

A truly brilliant professor. An expert in the fields of Latin American history and literature. Promotes critical thinking and gives inspirational speeches often. One of the best professors I have had at Duke. His Perspectives on the Amazon class was awesome! You should get a good grade if you do the readings and participate in class

Latin American Cinema was not my first choice, but Professor Furtado made me glad I took it. I was surprised and impressed by his eloquence and insight. Since it's a small class, you're expected to contribute to discussions regularly (30% of your grade), but it's not at all hard as long as you aren't zoning out. The rest is 3 essays (no final).

Really great teacher, I had him for Latin American Cinema and I learned a lot from his class. The homework amount was reasonable and his feedback on papers was extremely helpful. I would definitely take another class with him. The movies we watched were amazing (though quite depressing) and taught me a lot about the history of the region and cinema

Professor Furtado is incredible. One of the most engaging and thought-provoking classes I have ever had. The readings were sometimes tough, but he doesn't expect you to understand everything the first time you go over it. He's much more concerned with having an open discussion and hearing everyone's opinions. He is very eloquent and brilliant.

Gustavo's favorite part of the class is the discussion. He has great ideas and wants you to share yours too. The assignments were harder, but he just wants you to have a fully-formed understanding of the material.

Prof. Furtado is amazing. He clearly cares about the subject and shows up prepared and excited. He won't give undeserved grades, but he understands Duke students have a lot going on. Amazing lecture, supportive, and excited to teach. He loves to teach so much that it really does make it a privilege to be his student. Take his class!!

Gustavo is a gem! Great class for nonmajors. Time commitment b/wn watching movies and reading is significant if you want to make an A, but if you are inconsistent with the work the class isn't hard to keep up. He's hilarious, kind, passionate, chill yet challenging. He's prepared and excited to teach everyday. TAKE HIS CLASS. I'm so glad I did.

This is the class that I imagined when I was a kid fantasizing about college. Prof. Furtado has a passion for cinema and has mind-blowing lectures.  He covers a wide range of topics about Brazil and adapts to our language needs and interests. Take this course; your Portuguese will advance and so will your reasoning skills. I would it take again!

His class is among one the best I have had at Duke. The readings and films range from a variety of themes/topics and were interesting. He makes the class and discussions interesting and relevant. Great professor! Great discussions!  He was enthusiastic about this course.

Gustavo is an incredible, knowledgeable professor that challenges your views, sparks amazing conversations and, most importantly, makes you think. He is critical, caring, and helpful. I took his class for a requirement, but it ended up being one of my favorite classes. If I had the chance, I wouldn't hesitate taking a class with him.

The best screenwriting professor I've ever had -- he has so much experience in the film world and shares the coolest stories about his life. He's super caring about his students' wellbeing and gives great feedback. I wish I could take this class again

Prof. Hawkins class is awesome. Incredibly smart, interesting and funny guy who cares about your learning and helps you improve as a student and you have fun doing it, highly recommend any and ALL of his classes to anyone
Best professor I've ever had. Learned so much. He's the goat

This dude is a legend. I'd watch lectures on 2x speed and burst out laughing from his jokes and have to rewind to listen again.. Seriously though he knows his stuff, definitely experienced in the industry and has a lot to offer.
Gary is the best, hilarious & spacey but knows his stuff & is willing to help if you're willing to give him your attention. Come in with an open mind & you'll enjoy his class more than any others
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Gary is the man. Super cool guy, with a lot of experience in the movie industry. He was funny and really passionate about film. Would definitely recommend taking any class he teaches. He also said on the first day that pretty much everyone would get an A as long as you show up and do your work, so that's also sweet.

Phenomenal. I would take any class offered by him.  His disorganization is what makes his classes so unique/entertaining.  I LOOKED FORWARD to this class, for a change. He gives enthusiastic & personalized feedback and will spend numerous hours outside of class helping you. Don't go into this class with a closed mind, be flexible & you'll love it!
Good teacher, a little crazy but very smart and helpful. Keeps long classes interesting. Not too much work. Recommend!

Very helpful professor if you put in the extra time to ask for help outside of class.  Can be very unstructured but you will still learn a lot. Definitely take advantage of his out of class film opportunities.  These can be more fulfilling than the class itself.
theres no structure to this class.  the guy is awesome but completely lost 80% of the time. brilliant filmmaker just a very "divergent" thinker as he put it.
Helpful and easygoing, but sometimes can be hard to understand and is completely in his own world.
No Comments

I actually took LAS101 with Dr. G. The class has so many readings. Participation is necessary. If your class doesn't lock in, she will give pop quizzes. Essay prompts are often unclear, but Dr. G is incredibly willing to help. Very accessible out of class. Interesting class content, but a little too hard for a 101 class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: It was clear she had spent a lot of time preparing for each class, bringing in so many customized materials, on paper, and on slides. She kept the dsicusion going, and I always looked forward to going to class because it was consistently interesting. People felt comfortable speaking up and responding to each other with curiosity first and respect.

Professor Gasparowicz is a kind woman, but she has a long way to go to become a good professor. She was the assistant prof in this class. Her lectures were often unorganized, with occasional factual errors. Her feedback wasn't clear, which made it hard to improve. She has potential, but her explanations were hard to follow and often confusing.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr. Gasparowicz is very sweet. It's important to participate in lectures or else there is awkward silence. She assigns very dense and long readings for homework, but it is not necessary to read in depth before class. Decent amount of writing. Class was often extremely disorganized and I can't say I have a good foundation for Latin American history.

The most minute details of a 40 page long reading will appear on the weekly quiz. It's hard to pinpoint what to focus on when reading, especially if you try to read portions over a few days. Also impossible to "study" unless you just memorized everything from the reading. DON'T TAKE THIS CLASS, ESP IF YOU'RE A BAD TEST TAKER!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This professor doesn't like to teach. He is more than helpful when it comes to finding research, but there was probably one day in the whole semester when he actually "taught" us something. Everything is based on LONG textbook readings and quizzes, which is unfair to those who aren't the best takers. I wouldn't recommend this focus.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Beware of this FOCUS class, it's really hard. Lutzoni is a kind professor but he tends to ramble and assigns a lot of readings and homework for the weekly quizzes and writing assignments. The final paper is by far one of the worst parts of this class. It's a 15-20 page research paper that you get absolutely no guidance for. Please avoid this class.

Lutzoni is a really amazing person and cares deeply about his students, but the genetics focus is SO difficult. Prof was very helpful when I was struggling. I learned a lot that I'll take forward in my education and career, but overall I think the stress of the class wasn't worth it for a first semester freshman. Consider a different focus.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Oh my god. Genetics focus ruined my first semester. I was constantly stressed about passing the RATs and felt stupid when I got bad grades. I was reading about microbes when I should have had time to socialize and adjust to college life. DO. NOT. TAKE. GENETICS. FOCUS. I don't care how passionate you think you are about the topic. Save yourself.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment:
Lutzoni is very passionate about Symbiosis. He tries to share this enthusiasm to his students. He is a very tough professor, and expects you to read 3-4 research articles a week to prepare for hi weekly Readiment Assessment Tests and Short Writing Answers.
The hardest Focus class out there but also one of the most rewarding!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Lutzoni is extremely passionate about microbiology and cares about his students. However, the method of teaching in this class focuses on reading dense scientific articles and taking hard quizzes on the material. I learned virtually nothing in this class and the quizzes caused me lots of stress. Only take this class if you love microbiology.

Be prepared to spend 5-7 hours reading the background material for class each week to prepare for the weekly 10 question quizzes and primary article essay. Easily 20 page research term project due at the end of the semester as well. You do learn a great deal in this class though, but by far one of the hardest focuses classes out there.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Lutzoni is brilliant and cares about the FOCUS cluster, especially if you want to do research, but the lectures can be pretty confusing. On top of that, there's a ton of readings, quizzes, and writing assignments every week plus a massive paper at the end of the semester. Not an easy FOCUS class by any means.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr Lutzoni is very passionate about the material, which makes it much more engaging. I found the readings (mostly primary research articles) difficult at first but absolutely worth it because now (at the end of the semester) I feel much more confident in my reading and analysis skills. He is great at helping with research involvement.

Smart guy, good teacher. The highlight of the class is digging into papers. Would recommend some stats background or at least the ability to learn it on the fly. That said, he is not the one to count on for support or flexibility/willingness to work with you if you run into hard times while taking his class- gets somewhat frustrated instead
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Be wary of this class. It seems really cool but the volume of material they want you to memorize is intense. And I do mean memorize. Straight memorize. We had a particularly bad metabolism unit taught by a guest lecturer where we just had to memorize dozens of random bacterial enzymes. No comprehension. Just memorization.

Dr. Lutzoni is a really great professor! He has definitely used the feedback he got in the past to improve the class a lot. He meets one on one with the students and he is such a sweet guy. Also really enthusiastic about the material! BIO212 was the best class I've had at Duke!

Without a doubt one of the best professors I've had at Duke. I have taken two courses with Professor Lutzoni and he is not only extremely knowledgeable about the material, but also so enthusiastic about it that it carries over to the students and makes you want to care as well. Also - FLUNCH him. He is a great guy and getting to know him is great.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: coolest prof. always willing to help inside and outside of class, a really nice guy. although i feel i didn't learn much in the symbiosis focus class (it was super easy too), the clear passion he has makes it enjoyable.
competent
Prof Lutzoni was amazing. Helped us both in and out of class. He is a great guy, and would definitely recommend his course.

I had Dr. Lutzoni for the Genomes focus. His class was incredibly dull and boring by subject matter, but he was passionate about it, so it made the class bearable. However, if you aren't on his good side, like I was, your grades will tank - overall I just cannot bring myself to recommend his class. Steer clear of Dr. Lutzoni.

Dr. Lutzoni is a funny guy and fun to be around. He's always willing to help student both with in class stuff and anything beyond the classroom. Sometimes he can belabor a point, but it's clear that he is passionate about what he teaches, which makes his class enjoyable.

Dr. Lutzoni has majorly revamped BIO 212L. He opened my eyes to a lot of interesting research in microbiology which, quite frankly, I believe is unjustly glossed over in intro bio courses. The lab component was also one of my favorite labs at Duke. We got to run our own bacteria experiment and the beer we brewed came in handy on LDOC.

My favorite professor of the semester. He is super helpful with getting involved with research and is very passionate about biology. If you are taking the Genomes Focus, apply to his class because, even if the topic seems boring, the way Francois talks about it makes it seem like the most interesting thing ever.

Professor Lutzoni was definitely my favorite teacher freshman year. He was interesting and put a lot of time and effort into making sure his students understood the material. Also, he was a big help in the process of getting involved in undergraduate research.

It seems to me that BIO212 (old 103) has changed a lot since people last rated the class.. Prof Lutzoni's super helpful and he'll tell you what you need to study to do well. The tests are straightforward, just follow the lectures and the textbook. Plus the labs are much more interesting than the intro bio  ones! Definitely recommend taking BIO212L!

Francois is a super nice guy and very helpful. He truly cares about his students and wants them to succeed! If you are unsure about something, don't be afraid to ask for clarification. He will be happy to provide it. I loved having him for Focus!
He is nice and helpful, and really passionate in what he is teaching. A must-take in Focus!

Francois is a super cool dude! He is flexible and more than willing to meet with his students outside of class for help and guidance. Sometimes his questions are unclear, but if you express your confusion he is good at clarifying what he meant and is fair about dropping ambiguous questions. I very much enjoyed his class!
