I'm a biology major. 103L, though it could have been a really interesting class, was horrendous. His tests made no sense. The TAs were even baffled. Worst professor I have had at Duke. DO NOT take 103L if he is teaching the class.

On the final, he asked a question...that wasn't a question. Even after extensive questioning by both the students AND the TA's, he wouldn't admit he was wrong. BUT IT WASN'T A QUESTION. This is just one example of how his antics.
Awful professor. Tests were on a ridiculous amount of reading and were so specific that it just came down to luck. avoid this professor at all costs.
What he has going for him: he's obviously very intelligent. Keeping that in mind, he is awful. His tests are random and not even coherent. Wow.
Hell. On. Earth.
He's a nice guy, and sometimes is funny. But at the end no one really goes to lecture, because it's useless. He just doesn't teach that well. You will live by the book.
I'm a Biology major. Dr. Lutzoni is one of the worst professors I've ever had. Half the stuff he teaches is like irrelevant, and he way overassigns stuff.
Worst professor. Very hard, no cohesiveness, assigns ridiculous amounts of unrelated reading, just doesn't get it. Nightmare.
No Comments

Very caring and interested in student perspectives. Graded on participation and either a semester-long paper or 3 oral exams, which had very specific questions. Heavy reading for each week (long academic papers, then full books for the last 4 weeks) and participation is important, but as long as you make a genuine effort, you'll get an A.

The more you invest in the readings the more you get out from the class discussion; participation is mandatory but there's no stress to speak up a lot -- If you speak up once in each class and make a constructive comment, you will get full participation. Readings are very insightful.

I took GSF89S with Prof. Rosenberg this semester. Each class we had readings to do prior that we would discuss. We had 2 pass fail papers and one graded paper, along with a group project at the end of the class. Everything was graded easily, although discussions in class were sometimes a bit deep. Would take again and prof is very insightful.

Masterful at leading class discussions. Intellectually rigorous, great at taking contributions seriously while guiding seminar in better directions. Very accessible outside of class. Understands where students are coming from. Good balance of good-faith lenience and high standards. Pushes students to think outside of comfort zone.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: *I took GSF89S (first year seminar called Critters) with Rosenberg. Cool dude, super chill, very easy class. Grade is based on participation (just say 1 - 2 things per class) and 3 papers, 2 of which are "pass fail" (turn in a paper and get an A). Class was all about animal ethics/rights which is an odd topic but overall a nice easy course.

Amazing professor that genuinely cares about his students. One of the most interesting classes I've taken at Duke. Course materials are incredibly engaging, and Professor Rosenberg is just generally a really interesting guy. Take a class with him and you won't regret it!

Professor Rosenberg is a wonderful professor. He genuinely cares about his students and helping you learn and think through complex subjects. He only assigns one reading per class so you actually get to discuss everything you read (very refreshing at duke). He is also great at tailoring class discussions to what his students are interested in.

Gabe Rosenberg is my favorite professor I've had at Duke. This class was socratic seminar style, readings were engaging, and class was looked forward to by all every time. Get ready for a diverse group of students / opinions. Gabe is absolutely hilarious, as are class discussions. Caring teacher and friend, generous grader, and an absolute genius.

Took Sexuality 199 with Professor Rosenberg and it was a really interesting class! Participation is worth 40% of your grade followed by three short papers. He's really smart/articulate and engaging. A bit pretentious though. it's not necessarily an easy A, but if you're prepared to do the readings and work with him on your papers you'll be fine!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: An okay course taught by an okay professor. Won't take a class with him again. The whole time we were all staring at the clock counting down the minutes until we could leave. Lectures were so boring but mandatory b/c of pop quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Rosenberg is brilliant and well-versed in sexuality studies. The readings he assigns are long and variably interesting; you might find yourself frustrated by how little time he spends discussing them in class. His seminar discussions can be a bit tangential,  but you'll learn a lot about modes of thought necessary for sexuality studies.

I LOVE Dr. Rosenberg. He is seriously the best professor I've had. He is extremely helpful in office hours and will literally give you ideas to play with for your essays (which are also very easy). Show up to class because his notes are crucial to understanding the course and he gives pop quizzes, but they're very easy. He also has long readings.

This class is definitely worth taking if you care about the problems within our society's food culture. Don't be hesitant by the womens studies classification, this topic is much broader than that. You can't use laptops so be prepared to hand write a lot of notes! and DEFINITELY take notes- it will help for the final

Rosenberg is great! The class is entirely discussion based. Movies/TV shows he assigns are usually pretty interesting and easy to watch. The readings are harder but he doesn't always get to them anyway. He discusses really interesting topics and presents them in an easy to understand way. Def recommend this class for those who like pop culture!

Professor Rosenberg is incredibly nice and incredibly smart. I swear, he made everything sound super profound and interesting. He's also a fantastic teacher, which can be a bit rare. He's great at leading discussions and probing the class on when we're confused. I would 100% recommend his class -- just be prepared to work and actually think!!

(264L)Prof Gao was absolutely delightful--she's hilarious, caring, and did a great job at walking through physics in a chronological way. I loved her as a person, but at times she lost touch with how we just learned complex material a class prior and weren't proficient quickly...not her fault though. Final also replaced lowest exam (but no curve)

very understanding/approachable, relies pretty heavily on textbook problems for homework/exams. The lectures do tend to focus a bit too much on derivations of stuff that doesn't really come up afterwards, but all the lecture notes get posted and you can always refer to the textbook for what's going to be on the tests. Also this is physics 264L

Horrible professor. Terrible lecture organization. DO NOT expect to learn anything from the lecture. It is generally more confusing to pay attention in the lecture and try to follow her thread of thought. There is little connection between lecture material and homework problems. This is PHYSICS 264, by the way

I think this is one of the more difficult physics classes, and I struggled with it. However, Professor Gao's lectures are fairly easy to follow with a strong mathematics background. She was very open to questions during class as well. Her exams were very challenging, but homework was 40% of our grade and was not graded harshly. Great Textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Gao is super nice and I really enjoyed her class. The class, "Intro Seminar on Big Questions in Physics", was only a half credit, but throughout she was very accommodating and just wanted the students to learn/be interested. She also is doing pretty interesting research on the side and is willing to share with you her work.

Professor Gao is really nice and interested in all physics. Our class was quite open-ended but it gave us numerous opportunities to explore anything we wanted in modern physics and exposed us to useful resources to aid us in our investigation. Professor Gao is fair in grading, but she can be a little upset if you don't put in enough effort.

Extraordinarily helpful, in and out of class; she will ALWAYS answer your question in a straightforward way instead of that "let me *lead* you to the answer" rubbish, while making sure you understand each step. Extremely approachable and sweet. Slight accent, but easy to understand. Doesn't thrive on humiliating you like some other rec. profs.
Very knowledgeable; teaches a thorough course.  Slight accent shouldn't be much of an impediment for those paying attention.

She doesn't teach very well. I had no coding experience coming into this course and found labs, quizzes, and projects to be very difficult since I had learned nothing. That being said I didn't do bad and it isn't too hard to get away without learning.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Lipp is a very helpful, considerate, and passionate professor. However, the structure of EGR105 itself was confusing and difficult. If you are someone who has never seen python code before, you will be bombarded my numerous assignments, labs, projects, and quizzes, and it'll give you whiplash. The whole course feels like you're playing catchup.

Avoid taking this class with her; it is unnecessarily challenging and frustrating. She is truly the least helpful person I have ever met, and the assignments are incredibly complex just for the sake of being complex, not for the sake of learning. She is condescending to students, and the TAs are not given proper guidance to help with the projects

Dr. Lipp is fine but her class EGR 105 is not. I wanted to learn how to code in python but this class taught me almost nothing because the structure is weird. Most of the class is spent begging the teachers/TAs for help on an assignment that we have no time to do, so you never have time to understand what you are doing and it is never explained.

I had her for EGR105 which is a brand new course. I think she is the best of the selection. Coding is difficult alone but with the background knowledge you need to complete some of the projects it can get super overwhelming. However, she is super accessible and met with me privately several times to help. The grading policy is also really generous.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: ME344- one of the best ME professors and classes I've had. Do the extra credit homework and go to class to get the extra grade point and the tests were very much like the homeworks and practice problems. Her lectures were good although I did learn lots from the book as well. She actually let the students work dictate grades instead of being harsh
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: If you can avoid taking this class with Dr. Lipp, please do. I do not want anyone else to experience what I went through. She is very nice, but she doesn't lecture. The grading criteria is strange. If you don't do well on one project or one quiz, you go from an A to a C automatically. It's a lot of pressure, and the workload is not assigned evenly.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: While ECE 382 (Not EGR 103) is a lot of work, I feel like Dr. Lipp is, in actuality, a very caring professor who is willing to give you lots of chances to succeed in the form of extra credit and 3 no questions asked extensions. I don't want to discredit the other reviews, but I've personally only ever seen Dr. Lipp being kind.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. Lipp is very nice, but one of the worst lecturers I have ever had. By that, I mean she doesn't lecture at all. This entire course was essentially self-taught, and I had to put many hours into understanding python code that I had never seen before. The only reason I was able to score well in this class was because I went to office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Lipp is also the most condescending professor I've met. I don't think she genuinely cares about students. The course is good simply because the materials used are well-designed.

Not sure what all the slander is for, any time I've asked Genevieve for help she's been nothing but friendly and answering any question (no matter how trivial). I always went to her instead of Drew for 551 because she seemed a lot more willing to help you get to an answer. Great professor and super helpful, at least in my experience.
she is okay best of the worst

Lipp is probably the most condescending professor I've ever had. Her snarky comments in response to questions are uncalled for. She doesn't often finish her class notes or does practice problems, leaving the class to figure out this extremely hard class on their own.

She treats us like high schoolers. Quiz on the last day before break and a massive lab report due over break. She misdiagnoses what the class doesnt understand and fails to adequately teach the hard concepts. Her mathematical, rather than physical, explanations make small issues even worse. She is not empathetic but puts on a kind face. Horrific

She's a nice person but she really cannot teach this course. Some of the materials are complicated and it's hard to get clear explanations from her. Exam is hard and grading is very tough. Unless you are super confident with your coding skills, think twice before taking this course .
I didn't think she taught the material very well. She's a really nice person, but when it came to exam time, she wasn't the most helpful.

Dr. Lipp is an incredible professor. The class I took was objectively very difficult (and at 8:30 am), but her engaging lectures and thought-out note sheets made the material manageable. She cares about her students and does everything in her power to guide them toward success. I really hope to take another class with her.

This is one of the best professors I've had. Dr. Lipp is energetic and enthusiastic about what she teaches. She cares about her students and is more than willing to have both casual conversation, or be good resource for those who seek her advice. I felt like, despite getting a B, this was in some ways my best class this semester.

Little homework, class graded entirely on 5 open-note midterms on Canvas (60%) and the final (40%). However, lectures are confusing and Price rushes through slides (which aren't accessible outside of class). Poor pacing, doesn't follow syllabus, and extremely slow grader (still hasn't graded first exam after 6 weeks)
Professor is very engaging, knowledgeable, and helpful. Sometimes assignment instructions can be unclear, but he will clarify them if you ask.

Gareth is a fantastic professor. While he might adjust the syllabus throughout the semester, he always clears it with his students to find out if they can adjust without adding extra stress. He is honestly like a British Teddy Bear.

Price is an incredibly caring professor who strives to make critical discourse theory and linguistics accessible to beginners. Feedback on papers was always helpful and the small-group setting made for good discussions. Class greatly improved both my writing and media/critical discourse analysis skills.

Prof Price is an incredibly caring individual who wants his students to succeed. His lectures are very fast-paced and sometimes hard to keep track of when in class as most information is spoken to you rather than shown on a powerpoint. The only things are Price is hard to get in contact with outside of class and takes his time to grade papers.

Professor Price was overall a good lecturer and was helpful in answering questions. However, he tended to explain complicated concepts a bit too fast and did not allow students to access the powerpoints outside of class. He also took a long time to return tests (up to a month) and did not provide feedback on free-response questions.
Makes himself super available and geniunely wants to help you succeed, class was very discussion based but the only thing was he lags behind on grading and posting assignments sometimes

I can feel that he is passionate about what he teaches. He tries to make the concepts very clear and makes it easy to understand. The tests were not that hard, as he focuses on making students learn rather than stress over them. Recommend this class to ppl interested or curious about linguistics.

Prof. Price is one of the most attentive and funny individuals I've encountered at Duke. Classes are discussion-oriented with thoughtful contributions from the professor, which makes this course very engaging but very reliant on students' contributions. Readings are long but manageable. Especially recommend for people with multilingual backgrounds.

Professor Price stands out for his passion in the subject of language politics and his eagerness to have students engage. This FOCUS seminar is great for people who love exploring theory and applying key terms. Readings are long but we never cover everything in class. If you love anthro & policy definitely take.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Gareth is such a king. He cares so much about his students and genuinely wanted to hear what we had to say. Even though none of us really knew what we were talking about, he encouraged us to participate and I looked forward to class. Such a great man and professor.

Dr. Price provides a great environment for welcoming discussion and for you to voice your opinions / experiences. I'd say there was heavy reading for the linguistics focus class I took, and though some quite jargon-y, we still discussed some pretty relevant points in class. He's a very energetic and understanding professor!

Language and Politics is a great course that covers a lot of key concepts from both linguistics and political science. It was hard to participate over Zoom at times, but be prepared to participate as he really emphasizes the "seminar" aspect of the course. There is also a lot of reading required and they can be very dense at times.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I appreciated how he realised this class is meant to motivate people to learn linguistics (as opposed to say Chem 101 is meant to weed out students), and he did a fantastic job delving into the foundational topics of linguistics. He's funny and caring, if not a little disorganised. The exams were so easy he had to curve down a bit, but still 10/10

Prof. Price is an energetic lecturer and he definitely cares about his students. If students need help understanding something, he will spend as much time as needed until everyone gets it. Online quizzes every few weeks are very reasonable and basically the only workload (you can do well without doing the reading). Great class for an easy SS

What a gem. He is very knowledgable, passionate, funny, kind. Class is not super difficult, but can get repetitive at times bc the focus is more on discussing hypotheticals than applying or learning theories abt language and policy. Makes sense tho bc it's still a young field. Overall a great choice of prof, just get ready to participate and think

Overall, Professor Price was great. The material was really interesting, and if you go to class (mandatory) and do the readings (1 chapter every 2 or 3 weeks), which doesn't come out to very much time, it's easy to do well. Smart, good sense of humor, genuinely cares about students. A little disorganized occasionally, but that's my only complaint.

besides the final, rest of your grade is open-note sakai mini-exams which come straight from class notes (so make sure to go to class, since he doesn't post slides/recordings). cool guy but a bit disorganized and sometimes we would spend so long on one activity or just watch a documentary, that kinda devalued the class. u can't use tech in class

Amazing guy who really knows his stuff. Easy exams and interesting lectures, but he doesn't post slides online so show up to class. One of the most caring professors I hadhe made the final take home so we wouldn't stress over it. No homework besides reading. Highly recommend taking Intro to Linguistics with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Prof. Price is a great, caring professor. His grading criteria are not super clear, but I still made A's on both papers. Some weeks he gave a really heavy workload, but not consistently. We received little to no feedback on our papers. His FOCUS class is an easy A and very interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Good + funny lecturer. Just show up to class and pay attention and you'll get an A guaranteed. There's technically textbook readings but its possible to get by without it. I learned a ton about Linguistics as well (x-bar sucks though). 10/10 would take again.
Super nice guy, class was also very relaxed. Very easy to get an A/A-. Be his friend, it helps a lot and participate in class.

this guy is awesome. Idk why anyone would hate on him. Easiest class I've ever taken, but also totally fascinating. literally all you have to do is show up to class and you'll learn stuff. No homework, u don't have to do the readings, the quizzes are open book. If you want an easy class and are interested in linguistics, 201 is perfect for u

Gareth is a bit scatter brained at times, but he totally makes up for it with his entertaining lectures and easy course work! You pretty much just have to show up for class and all the tests are open book! He is very responsive to questions and makes sure everyone is clear on what is going on.

The best professor in the whole world! LOVES his subject, teaches it in the most engaging and interesting manner, creates an incredible atmosphere in class. His British accent is to die for. He will help you outside of classroom. Very kind and understanding. One of the best courses I have taken at Duke, recumbent it to everyone.

Gareth was kinda disorganized in the way he taught. Ran out of time to get through all the syllabus. But he was funny and kind, and I loved the topics we learned. Very interesting course which put words and concepts to things we take for granted in the English language. Easy/fair tests. We analyzed our own vowel formants, which was p cool.
Gareth Price is a wonderful guy. He tries hard to keep lectures interesting and funny and keep everyone engaged. He will help you out if you're having problems.
Ling 201 with Price was a great, highly recommended class.  Good to satisfy reqs, and Price was very open meeting outside of class.

Very interesting-he's super into what he teaches and tries to answer all questions! A bit unorganized-its almost the end of the semester and I have no idea what my grade might look like but overall great class!

The class is a lot of fun, and a very interesting first look into linguistics. It moves slowly and has almost no assignments. Price is an entertaining professor, but incredibly unorganized and doesn't give back grades for months.

Super interesting class (FOCUSPolitics of Language) that tackles a lot of difficult linguistic concepts. Professor Price loves his job! He really wants to know if you understand and will help. Needs to be reminded to send prompts sometimes. With it being an election year, wish we had gotten a little more into the "politics" part of the class.

Price is one of the best professors at Duke. He's a slightly tough grader and challenges you, but it's not too difficult to get an A. He's always energetic and passionate and hilarious, and he makes the material fascinating - I recommend his class to everybody I know.
Great Professor! Thought I would hate the class, Cold War Texts did not sound interesting but Professor Price made it one of the best classes I have taken at Duke.

Power of Language was an amazing class! And Dr. Price is perhaps one of my favorite teachers at Duke! He can be a bit unorganized, but he is always so nice and willing to help, so if you have an interest in linguistics, definitely try to get him as a professor!

Gareth is probably my favorite professor I've had at Duke. He is hilarious and SO enthusiastic about his topic. I tell all of my friends to take Ling 101 just to have a class with him, even if they have no interest in linguistics. He's not the most organized person ever, but he is such an interesting person and great professor!

The Politics of Language class in the Power of Language FOCUS was the best class I've taken at Duke. Professor Price is respectful of everyone's views, wants to hear everyone contribute, and gives great feedback on papers. He is also helpful to talk to if you want more feedback outside of class. Go to his office hours!

Prof Getz explicitly said that he made the course slower-paced (e.g. no Lebesgue Integral) than previous years, which I think helped with fully absorbing the material. Regularly connected concepts to other fields of math. He also made the tests very approachable. Definitely recommend taking this class with Prof Getz in the future.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He has shown genuine care about math, always brought a pile of handwritten proofs into the classroom, and sometimes added in some topics valuable for a future mathematician. I felt that his way of teaching aligned with my goals of this course.

Very hard class. Lectures were fast-paced, with new concepts each day. The lectures were standard; he did a good job explaining and answering questions. Grading was 70% HW, 30% in-class midterm, but the curve at the end was extremely generous. The exam wasn't horrible, there were just too many things to study. Overall, a good continuation of 501.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
This is for Math 502. Algebraic structures. 

I learned a great deal about algebraic structures. However, it was not because of Dr. Getz who is a condescending know-it-all. He  has a high opinion of himself and a low opinion of every student. It was sad. He's not a good human, he may be a good mathematician.

Professor Getz is pretty kind. However, I don't recommend his class to anyone who hasn't taken another high level undergrad math course such as topology or 501. Hw questions feels too abstract from the chapter topic and his class is very fast paced.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE THIS PROFESSOR. He is not caring about this class, reading straight from book. Hard to learn, and exams are highly difficult because teaching is not good.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Just read through the entire textbook, doesn't care about the student
Literally does not care about the class and lectures right out of the textbook. Also, exams are unreasonable in scope and length.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: A very hard class, went into Lebesgue theory which is not normally taught in 531. Homework takes a long time but exams are reasonable. Professor Getz is good at explaining things if you are truly interested in math. Overall great choice.
Very tough class, but Getz is really nice and brilliant. Take real analysis with him if you want some serious intellectual challenge.

He's not a good teacher, moves far too quickly and just reads from the textbook. Nice guy, but 501 was really hard because of his lack of engagement with students and the material. Would not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: He's fairly good at explaining material, has very reasonable homework and exams, and makes the final take home. All around a solid choice.
Great teacher if you really are interested in math
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LECTURE HEAVY--Would take again

reviews.comment: Jayce Getz is a great teacher and mathematician. If you want to go through multivariable calculus with the bare minimum knowledge needed to pass, do not choose this teacher. Rather, if you would like a challenging experience -- one where you may have to seek help from time to time -- you will learn more than you think from taking Dr. Getz's class.

Pretty cool teacher and loved his Mario kart analogies, but every example he did in class was extremely abstract and many of the proofs he did had no relevance to the course. He rushes through all the material and doesn't really get into how it is applicable. He also makes a ton of calculation errors so all the students have to catch them.
Brilliant person in general, but doesn't care at all about his class. He just reads from his notes and does most of the math wrong.

Jayce Getz is an absolutely brilliant man and an inspiration to us all. However, he is really bad at teaching Multivariable Calculus. He is unclear and often does problems wrong. Be prepared to do a ton of work on you own if you want to pass.   P.S. definitely get him to sing for the class

Jayce has his moments, both good and bad. The good consisting of an occasional joke, the bad consisting of anything math-related. He knows the material, but it is difficult to follow along in class. Be prepared to read the textbook if you want to learn this stuff. With that being said, the man is a stone cold fox.

Like many professors in Duke's math department, Professor Getz would be a better teacher for a higher level math class that would cater to his expertise.  Um, other than that, he's really cool, and if he ever references a song in his lectures, be sure to ask to sing it for the class.  He would be absolutely delighted. :)

There is so much that adds to the enigma that is Jayce Getz that it is impossible to encapsulate his persona in this mere description. We are not on his level. Not intellectually or physically.  Jayce "Getz Money" is someone you will never forget.
Amazing, caring, and thoughtful professor. 10/10 prof.

Incredibly caring and smart professor. As long as you turn in your work and pay attention in class you'll do well, he makes an effort to make sure everyone understands what's going on. The classes aren't always the most interesting or entertaining, but you will definitely learn and do well as long as you put in a little bit of effort.

Monsieur Choffart is an incredible prof. He's super caring and energetic, and overall a really fun guy. His lectures can get a little boring sometimes, but overall the class is a great introduction to French. Homework can be a little much, but it ends up being manageable. The grading is super lenient and there are almost no assessments.

Monsieur Choffart is amazing. So kind and lecture style is great (open discussion). Take FR302 with him!! Not too much work like the typical FR203/204 classes. Assignments are very chill - no quizzes just discussion posts, a few short papers, and final group project. Lecture content was very interesting and felt like I really learned from him.

Best prof I've ever had. I was afraid to take French in college but he made French 203 my favorite class. Always enthusiastic and patient. Gives decent amount of homework but that's how most language classes are like, and you can really see your improvement.

Germain is easily one of the best professors at Duke. He understands the excitement and challenges involved in learning a new language and uses that to transform the classroom into a fun, stimulating environment. It's okay to commit mistakes in his class, as he pushes you to see them as a way to improve. Also, just a super accessible, caring guy.

This was the best french class I took at Duke. Germain Choffart is an exceptional professor. He came to class everyday with lots of enthusiasm. The class DOES include a moderate workload (roughly 4-8 hours a week outside of class), but Monsieur Choffart makes it obvious that he wants his students to learn french instead of "get everything right".
Great professor. It was a 101 so very basic material. Loves participation even if you get it wrong so as long as you try you should be good. Have fun!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Best French professor at Duke and the best I've had ever. Great professor to start learning French with. He knows how to keep the class entertaining and he is always very energetic, which comes in useful since the class meets four days a week. His grading is clear and as long as you do the work and participate and show the effort you'll get an A.

Literally the most incredible professor you would ever find at Duke. Yes, the class has a lot of homework and is a bit (a lot) time-consuming, but Monsieur Choffart is amazing; he buys us Pain au Chocolat and other french candies, and you can see he really loves what he's doing.

One of the greatest professors I've ever had. He puts so much effort into his class. I dreaded taking French at Duke, but now I'm excited for French 102. The class requires a lot of work, but it's 100% worth it.

Monsieur Choffart expects a lot, but he's an amazing prof (even in COVID) and you can definitely see your growth. He genuinely cares about all of his students and offers consistently useful feedback. His passion for teaching is evident and makes the class genuinely enjoyable. Be prepared to work, but he is a phenomenal prof. Highly recommend!

I would highly, HIGHLY recommend Professor Choffart. He is hands down one of the best professors I've ever had. Kind, supportive, passionate, interesting, understanding and helpful, he made a challenging class downright enjoyable. I learned so much and am honestly emotional now that it's over. Take this class with him 100%! Great, clear grader.

He is such a lively and energetic professor that makes the class so fun! Personally I took 4 years of french 2 years ago and it was great review of basically everything I have learned so the course is pretty fast for a 101 class and there is a lot of homework, participation matters as well. But overall it's a very rewarding experience!
Super energetic and passionate about what he does! Makes learning a new language fun, and his enthusiasm motivates you to learn so much faster! Amazing language prof

Choffart is amazing. He cares a lot, makes class really fun and engaging. He has super positive energy that made me genuinely excited to go to class everyday. Starting a new language is hard, and involved quite a bit of work, there is no getting around that, but he is also an INCREDIBLE TEACHER!!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Hilarious

reviews.comment: I have heard M. Choffart described as a Disney villain and that's seriously not too far off the mark. He's really animated and theatrical, which is actually really helpful because the entire class is taught in French, and all the gesturing really helps you understand what's going on. There will be homework. 10/10 would take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Germain is super nice and outgoing. IF you are a shy type this class will defintely force you to come out of your shell as participation is nearly every class. Although the theatrical shtick got a little old, his enthusiam for teaching is defintely apprecated. Get ready to do lots of homework and outside projects
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Very enjoyable class. Dr. Choffart is very engaging; I was honestly surprised by how much he got 12 college students to participate. Totally reasonable amount of work, and he's not that tough of a grader. Definitely my most fun class this semester.

All of Choffart's classes are in French, even 101 ones. This helped me a lot to learn French quickly in a short time. All classes are group activity-based, which can be annoying sometimes but are generally pretty helpful. There are quizzes after every chapter, and you'll have Hybrid Days which are pretty hard. Take 101 with him. He's hot too :)

Germain is an amazing and very passionate teacher. He is pretty strict about his policies, but he makes these very clear. There is a decent amount of homework which gets annoying, but it's nice because you won't have to do a lot of extra studying. If you put in a decent amount of effort you'll make a fine grade. He knows how to teach french!

Professor Choffart is one of the most enthusiastic and helpful professors I've ever had at Duke. He's well-organised and his expectations are very clear. Only thing is he's very strict about rules especially concerning missing homework and lateness.

Great guy, wish he would go slower considering a lot of 101 kids have no experience with the language. Mostly had experienced kids do stuff on the board which didn't give those of us that hadn't taken the class before as much of an opportunity to practice.
Fantastic

His feedback often not constructive, and pretty demoralizing. I came from a high school with a very strong French program, and this class made me very insecure in my French speaking abilities because he is so picky. Also, your grade is not related to how much effort you put into the class, but rather how good your absolute french skills are.

Loved Prof. Choffart. He's funny, enthusiastic, and overall a great professor. One of the best I've had at Duke. Tends to give everyone the same participation grade, though. But that doesn't change the fact that he's amazing. Take French with him if you can.

Germain was the best language professor I have ever had in either high school or college. He makes going to class fun and learning french enjoyable. The class moves quickly but Germain is very good at explaining everything and is a consistent and fair grader. Would highly recommend to anyone.
SOOOO picky when it comes to grading. clear teacher though, he tells you what he expects

Love M. Choffart! He makes class so fun and is very enthusiastic. While I have caught some of the "errors" that he has made in class (like conjugating faire wrong...) they're minor and he's still a great professor.

M. Choffart is awesome. Our entire class loved him. He manages to make the most boring grammar lessons really fun, and brings a lot of energy to his teaching. He is also a very fair grader, and it is not hard to do well in his class. Plus he's adorable ;)
Great professor! Nice and funny. So glad I took French wit him.
He's an amazing professor! Really engaging, and always exciting and relatable. After high school, I hated French, but he made me love it again.

He's such a cutie pie!  For a college professor, he's extremely enthusiastic and helpful, and class is a lot of fun. It's great to have a real French teacher for an intro level language class, and he makes French easy to learn.
Very understanding teacher who is eager to help his students out.

Absolutely fantastic teacher. Is very understanding with late homework and prevents intro french class from becoming a drag (which is quite an accomplishment considering how many times lower level language classes meet). Makes expectations very very clear.

I learned SO MUCH French from this class. Awesome teacher. The tests can be confusing at first but he acknowledges it when you are clearly trying very very hard. A very good class, I highly recommend this professor.

She is one of the kindest and most caring professors I've had. She really knows her content and lectures amazingly basically off the top of her head. It's a bit harder than some of the other 201 sections but your understanding will be rock-solid and she will work with you to be better.
Great teacher and would recommend

Her lectures are really concise and clear. HW was sometimes time-consuming but was also accurate reflection of the tests. Her class is harder than other 201 sections, but grading is fair, and I understood concepts a lot better. Going to recitations and asking TAs questions was really valuable as well. She cares a lot about her students too.

I loved Professor Geri. Great lectures and really cares about her students. Tests were slightly more difficult than other EGR 201 sections, but all were very fair and the difficulty bump allowed me to fully learn the material.
Really great lectures.

Readings are dense but the conversations in class are really great to engage with. Professor Rousseliere tries to break down each reading and help you become an overall better reader/writer! Participation and attendance are very important.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: What a great class. Professor Rousseliere leads great class discussions and really tries her best to break down texts in a way that is easy for her students to understand. I was intimated by her on the first day and thought I wasn't going to like the class, but it turned out to be one of my favorites. Nice that it only met once a week too.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Rousseliere is very nice and funny, but this class is quite a hassle and very unstructured. There is a lot of reading, but you can get through most classes without doing it. The grade is based on 3 papers, a podcast, and participation, but the papers are graded by an outside TA. The grading rubric is vague and feedback is very limited.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great class. Professor Rousseliere led amazing discussions and assigned exceptional readings. We didnt simply reiterate the readings; she analyzed them with us on a much deeper level. You will learn a lot, but prepare to put in a lot of effort in this class. Hard work definitely pays off.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Loved her class. She's a very interesting lecturer and facilitates really cool discussions. Readings for the class are very long and dense (some of the harder theory I've read) and you need to work very hard in classroom discussion. However, grading for the papers and forum posts is fairly easy. If you work hard and participate expect a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Rousseliere is absolutely fantastic. Brilliant, hilarious, and caring. She leads the best class discussions - rather than just giving us the analysis of our material, she guided us through so that we could make the breakthroughs ourselves. She also consistently picks fascinating readings. Must take!
Professor Rousselière ran the class like a seminar and facilitated some really great discussions. Participation is very important, so show that you care and you will certainly do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I hope Professor Rousseliere could be more open-minded to opinions that differ to hers and more willing to provide constructive help to students.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: he assigns TONS of hw. midterms are reasonable but alot, and final is hard

Oliver is a very straight forward teacher, is very clear and concise, teaches straight out of the book and tests come almost directly from the homework.  If you pay attention and do the homeworks, you should be fine.

Oliver is a good guy. His tests are pretty difficult but he bases them mostly on homework problems, so do those and you'll be fine. Slightly quiet but a cool guy in general. Grades pretty decently. Probably the better option for Math 26L.

This guy is HOT.  He's a grad student from Macedonia... kind of shy, but really friendly and funny in a dorky way.  His tests may be slightly easier than those given in other sections.  A lot of homework is assigned, but it's the same for all sections.  We had fewer quizzes than other sections.  All in all, I'd suggest Oliver over another teacher.
Lots of games and reading
Jshahajsjxhajahshshsjshhahhw
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: AMES188 was easy for GPA, but I never learned anything useful from this class.

AMES 188 was fun, (dropdown didn't give me the option for this course), but Shai is very unclear in his instructions, and be prepared for a lot of readings outside of class. There are never any due dates on assignments, so it always feels like a guessing game with this class.

He is one of the best professors at Duke, and is definitely my favorite. He is sincere, helpful, extremely insightful and very knowledgeable. You can tell that he believes in the value of what he does, and he makes you believe in it. He is very considerate and therefore reading loads are flexible.

Great teacher who really takes care to go through things step by step. The films he assigns are all fascinating as long as you're interested in Jews, and he is understanding if you need help with essays. You have to write short essays very regularly, which can get annoying, but all worth it in the end. No exam at the end, just papers.

Class size is very small, usually between 2 and 5 people, so attendance is absolutely mandatory. There's a lot of work, especially typing, which gets cumbersome without a Hebrew keyboard. The teacher is very knowledgeable, however, and eager to help. Easy grader too.

This course is rigorous and requires consistent effort throughout the semester. The material moves quickly, so strong time management and persistence are important to stay on top of assignments and concepts. Students who attend class regularly, engage with the content, and seek clarification early will be best positioned to succeed.

This class was challenging and amazing at the same time. She was a great professor who provided a lot of assistance and encouragement to her students. The material itself was tough at times but I learned a lot. Please do not go into the class hoping to get a good grade but learn and grow!

Professor G is terrific! She meets students where they are at the beginning of the semester and structures the course so that each unit builds on the last. Her lectures ground abstract economics in real-world examples, preparing students to conduct meaningful policy analysis. Prof G is engaging, friendly and genuinely eager to support your learning
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. G is a kind person, and a fair professor and grader. The class is very, very organized: she sends out a message at the beginning of the week as an overview for what's upcoming, problem sets are graded promptly, and tests are reflective of the materials. Lecture slides are consistently good and accessible.

I thoroughly enjoyed taking Econ 303 with Professor Gennetian, who brought economics to life for pub pol majors. Her lectures were engaging and thought-provoking, often sparking class discussions around the assigned readings. What truly set the course apart were her unique and interactive projects and paper, making learning both rigorous and fun!

Prof. G is so caring and kind. She does her best to inspire you to think about how econometrics can be used to research various policy-related questions. The class can be fast-paced at times, but it is manageable. You also learn a lot about Stata (shoutout to the TA!). I also loved having guest speakers during lectures!!

Professor Gennetian is great! Economics can be intimidating but she makes an effort for it to be engaging like beginning classes with conversations and case studies. The class is not easy and you will need to work but the exams reflect the problem sets. She also offers an extra credit opportunity and the final project is not too much work.

I was scared of taking 303, but I really enjoyed Gennetian and ended up finding the class enjoyable. Gennetian gives great lectures, is always happy to help, and is very accommodating if you talk to her outside of class. Would take another class with her for sure!

Pubpol 303 is a tough class, especially if you go in without any econ background. That said, Prof. Gennetian is incredibly caring and accessible outside of class. She truly wants to help students learn, and I enjoyed the course.

While 303 is a difficult class for those who are new to economics (like I was), I found Gennetian to be a good professor who took care to make sure we understood and did well in her class. She has a dry sense of humor that I think some interpret as rudeness, but she really does care about students and was always very willing to help when asked.

Dr. Gennetian teaches micro through policy examples, which makes you realize why understanding economics matters in helping people. She gives clear instructions for exam prep: (1) know everything on problem sets and (2) be prepared to answer questions quickly. I'm usually a slow test taker, but I did well. Nice prof who wants students to succeed.

Professor Gennetian is very unaccommodating and not very understanding of her students. She is very demeaning when she speaks to students. While she is very intelligent, she is very inadequate in teaching so be prepared to teach yourself EVERYTHING before the midterms. The problem sets and presentation are the only way to do well.
Great professor, great course. No complaints.

Prof G is one of the best at Sanford! If  u r into social policy, def take her. This was a new class she was piloting on empirical methods for social progress. You learn the basics of Stata and working w data. A must-take for those doing a thesis. Makes me wish I could go back and take more econ/stats earlier on at Duke! Also her work is so cool

Prof Gennetian is nice, but she isn't flexible or understanding. While the content is interesting, she presents it in a patronizing manner that discourages many from participating in class. The tests are super long, and the MC questions are 2 points each (same as short answers), so if you miss some MC, your grade won't recover.

If you are a public policy major and have flexibility on when to take 303, I highly recommend taking it with Professor Gennetian. She was more than willing to field questions from students (especially about her research). 303 is not a cakewalk, but Professor Gennetian creates opportunities for students to boost their grades and is very supportive.

This class was super engaging and I learned so much from Prof. Gennetian. She definitely cares about this topic and has a wide breadth of expertise, but she also encourages student engagement and exploration.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I have never taken an econ class before and only took this because it was required, but Prof. Gennetian completely surprised me! I ended up loving the class. She's super approachable and makes the material engaging. There are opportunities for creativity and extra credit

Professor Gennetian was exceptional. She is so knowledgeable across the many subtopics within poverty research, but she is still eager to center student perspectives. Even as an undergraduate, I always felt comfortable participating. Lectures were engaging, and the case study was a uniquely formative exercise. . 

I highly recommend this class!

If you are going to take 303, take it with Gennetian. Course material can be a bit bland at times but is never too hard. She is a very caring and understanding professor. Not too hard to get an A in; very clear guidelines.

Professor Gennetian is one of my favorite instructors. She is incredibly knowledgeable about poverty and policy--not only were her lectures very informative, they were very clear. Moreover, she guided some very productive discussions during class. She cares that her students actually learn and understand the material.

Prof. Gennetian's class, "Poverty, Policy and Pandemics" was my favorite this semester. Lectures were incredibly relevant and accessible. Readings included sources like newspapers, podcasts and popular books as well as scholarly journal articles and white papers. Great, expert guest speakers who added depth and nuance to the topics we discussed.
Professor Gennetian is a great professor with a clear lecturing style and a caring and fun personality! Lucky to have her as the professor of my first econ class here.

I loved class with Prof. Gennetian. She is relaxed and warm, while still very knowledgable and eager to learn. She may not be perfect in instructing on every subject, but she is incredibly open to feedback - she takes that feedback seriously, and will share it with guest speakers and authors.

Highly recommend Professor Gennetian for PubPol303. Really cares for her students and makes lectures interesting. Lot of extra credit opportunities. Interesting group project at the end of the semester. And can opt-out of final if you're happy with your grade. Great professor with fair expectations.

She the only professor that I chose to take 2 courses with while at Duke. She gave interesting supplemental readings that weren't long, and made an effort to get to know every student - I was calling her Lisa by the end of the semester! Policy, Poverty and Pandemics was a great and relevant seminar. Take any of her grad-level courses.

Dr. Gennetian is one of the most caring professors I have had, and she really takes the time to get to know her students. She delivers lectures in unique ways so they don't get repetitive. Really cool opportunities to take what we learn in class and apply it to what is going on in the world. And cool speakers that come in to speak.

Professor Gennetian is an amazing professor. As someone who has taken both 303 and 590S with her, she has been one of the most caring, engaged professors I have had at Duke. The readings are very interesting, and she always has great insights in class discussion. Fair in grading and what she expects from you.

She's a very passionate, caring and knowledgable professor. The class is very interesting and engaging with a light workload. Keep up with the readings and stay ahead on papers and this can easily become one of your favorite classes!

Professor Gennetian could not have been better this past semester. As a student without any economics background whatsoever, I was super nervous for the class especially given some of the reviews on this website. They couldn't be further from my experience. As long as you do the work and stay engaged, there are many opportunities to succeed.

I love her and this class specifically!!! There are 3 papers which are your entire grade which could be kind of tough but she's really accessible outside of the classroom and willing to give feedback as you work on your drafts. She also gave us extensions which was amazing! She just wants the class to really work for you so take advantage of that!!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: This class introduced me to how vital economics are in the creation of policy. I learned so much in this class and Prof Gennetian was inspirational and challenging. She is definitely my favorite Duke professor. When the class transitioned to online, she was very flexible as long as you made the effort to do your best and didn't take advantage.

This class is relevant, interesting, and it really made me think! Prof Gennetian is passionate about her students and challenges you to do your best in a very caring way. She is also really understanding when it comes to needing some flexibility. She's knowledgeable, funny, and really helped me with deciding major life decisions outside of class!

This was my second time having Lisa as a professor and it was just as fantastic as the first - I learned so much in this class and it was clear that Lisa had a wealth of knowledge and expertise in the topic and really cared about her students. Definitely one of my favorite professors during my time at Duke!

One of the best classes I've taken at Duke! Mixture of seniors and grad students. Very self paced, self designed research, & discussion based class. Very intellectually stimulating. Her lectures were always engaging. Lisa is so thoughtful and an amazing professor to learn from. During the pandemic she shifted her attendance policies to be flexible.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Lisa is a very kind and caring professor! The 303 curriculum is hard for anyone who isn't quantitative inclined. It was challenging to me when the course was in person, but when it switched to online halfway through the semester due the pandemic it was more flexible for me due to the open note structure.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Gennetian did a fantastic job framing otherwise dry and abstract microeconomics concepts within day to day examples. She clearly cares that her students engage with the material and assessments for the course are straightforward if you learn the material. Its unfortunate to see negative reviews - they dont truthfully reflect her classes.

After hearing about Dr. Gennetian's research in child poverty I was excited, but she appears to know nothing about the reality of poverty and studies it in a voyeuristic way. This was evident in not flexible she was after the shift to online, and didn't consider that maybe her students live in poverty? she made her class harder instead. ridiculous

Gennetian is well-intentioned and kind, but ultimately lacking. The class was extremely disorganized with many errors in the powerpoints and no grades posted to Sakai the entire semester. Her lectures were very dry/unhelpful and most people seemed to learn more from the TAs. However, the tests were pretty fair and similar to the problem sets.

I was excited for the class the first week as Dr. Gennetian has had a really interesting background in child poverty. However, it was apparent that this was her first semester at Duke. There were mistakes on the slides in almost every PowerPoint, and lectures we incredibly unclear and uninteresting.

Professor Gennetian is a very dry lecturer. I had to read the textbook carefully and go over lecture slides in order to absorb anything. That being said I thought the tests were pretty fair and the final project was fun
Professor Gennetian was more than willing to help outside of class and responded to emails within the hour. Her tests are challenging but she gives a ton of extra credit to help you out

Dr. Gennetian is caring and sweet, but her lectures were dry and hard to follow. The tests always had some discrepancies in terms of wording/grading. My TA was awesome, but she expects you to use your TA for help more than her. A knowledgeable woman, but since this was her first undergrad class, it was clear she wasn't sure how to hold engagement.

Before COVID-19, Professor Gennetian's course was challenging but fair. I felt that the problem sets resembled what we had been doing in class and she was easily accessible for questions. With the transition to online learning, she has added more assignments, set stricter deadlines, and gives harsh grades. Good professor, but not very flexible.

In the wake of coronavirus, Gennetian has implemented a stricter syllabus, with daily quizzes and problem sets crammed in into a limited timeframe. Her exams are unrepresentative of class material. During a pandemic, she has made the course tougher and has not offered flexibility in her grading policies. This demonstrates a lack of student care.

This class was taught jointly by Dr. Gibert and Dr. Rachel Wadleigh. Both were so kind and it's obvious they're seriously passionate not only about the topic but about teaching. It has 3 open note exams online in a word document that were very kindly graded. attendance is mandatory in lecture and discussion but overall, super easy bio class.
super kind professor, extremely understanding. class was based on SimUTest readings graded on completion. classes were collaborative and interactive. TAs also made discussions really interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Jean is a super kind and caring professor, and you can really see his passion for ecology in his teaching. The course covers extremely similar content to intro environ so it was a bit boring learning the same things a second time, but if you don't have this background the course is a great intro! We had wonderful discussions and lots of group work.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: This class was easy and sweet! It was a basic ecology course (during covid) and it was fun. Wasn't the most interesting ever but I enjoyed it. Professor is very kind and I would take a class with him again. Fun lecturer and animated!
This professor is a clear communicator. He gives good feedback, and is very approachable outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: He is 100% the best professor at DKU. Super caring, super friendly, makes CC2 super interesting.

Joe is amazing and passionate about teaching and the subject! Despite this being a 2 credit course, it is a lot of work. The readings are lengthy and complicated, but his in-class discussions clear things up and he's always available outside of class for guidance. I always got great feedback on essays from him and learned a lot overall!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Joe is nice and patient. Everything's explained in detail. And he responds to emails very soon. But in-class readings are hard and require a time commitment, which makes me feel pressured sometimes. Don't expect it would be easy and take little time even if it is a 2-credit course......
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Joe is the best Professor at DKU. He is super attentive, gives thorough and specific feedback while keeping you motivated. Although the readings can be difficult to understand, he guides you through this process and is always available to resolve doubts. If you're looking to improve your writing and analysis skills this is the course for you.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Available out of class - you can easily book an appointment with him. Feedbacks are amazing and helpful. Will definitely get his classes again. I love his lectures - engaging and interesting

Professor Joe is one of the most caring and dedicated professor that I have ever met. I often asked for feedbacks and meetings outside Office Hour, but he always helped me as best as he could. Your writing skills will be improved a lot after a few meetings with him. Highly recommend if you are looking for a course that offers unique perspectives.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof. Giacomelli is the best professor that I have ever met at DKU! He is so awesome, considerate, patient, caring, and intelligent that only half an hour's talk with him is worth 10 times as much time more than others. He is always willing to meet with you when available. Each of my classmates loves him so much and spoke extremely highly of him.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Joe is a thoughtful, caring professor. His classes are fascinating, and I ended up enjoying the course a lot although I initially had no interest in the topic. He gives very detailed feedback on the essays and really helped me improve my writing. I can't recommend GCULS108 enough!

I really like Joe. He is nice, caring, and available for discussions about homework. The readings are hard but he explains them well. He gives detailed feedbacks for writing and also recommend good ways to approach readings. He always leads the class with care and respect for diversity.

Professor Gillespie is very funny, kind, and extremely knowledgeable on political philosophy. The content knowledge of this class was fascinating. He can be a harsh grader, but if you put in the effort, you will get an A. He's also very funny, and attempts to make a mundane subject matter very interesting and entertaining. I loved this class!

Prof. Gillespie's class is as boring as they come. Every class, he rambles about vague political concepts and never fosters discussion. I would have gotten just as much out of the class if I only did the readings and didn't show up. And to make it worse, the paper prompts are confusing and no grading ctiteria is provided. Avoid at all costs.

He clearly knows his stuff, but his lectures can get a bit too ranty and repeat the same cliches over and over again. Lectures are not very based on the assigned texts, and don't go into a lot of detail. It takes a lot of convincing myself to get up and go to his 10:05 classes at Gross Hall

Lectures and assigned readings were confusing and hard to follow- I did most of my review from material outside of class. Easily the hardest of the four classes in the VoF cluster- only take if you're up for a challenge and don't mind getting an A-/B+.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Gillespie is a very interesting guy with good stories. I wish he would make his grading criteria more clear on papers. This class is exactly what you would expect for an intensive introduction to political philosophy, and I definitely learned a lot. However, be ready to read a lot of dense text and write.

Hoo, boy. I do really like Gillespie. He's an articulate, fascinating, humorous guy, and he truly does care about his freshmen. But he is not the easiest to follow, and with complex material like this, that's not always fun. The questions he asks in class are notoriously difficulthe will ask everyone to answer, even if the first one's right.

Pretty typical polisci class. I'm not polisci, but I took it because I thought I was interested in political philosophy, but I realized after this class I'm not. Would recommend to someone who is interested in political philosophy. Overall, not the worst class I've taken, but definitely not the best.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Do not take his class unless you LOVE dense philosophical texts. Even if you look at the reading and say, "Wow that looks amazing!" Even if you read the reviews and think, "I'll just work extra hard to get an A," because you will not get an A, and you will regret your decision every time you go to class, where he rambles for 75 long, long minutes.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Prof Gillespie is a great! It is very hard to get a good grade, but you can learn a lot. GO TO HIS OFFICE HOURS!

Professor Gillespie is a very intelligent professor, but very boring. He gets caught on tangents very easily and very rarely spends class talking about the actual topics. I feel like I barely learned anything from his class and it has only motivated me to not take any more political science classes.
Incredible Professor with very interesting lectures.

Gillespie is a fantastic lecturer, delivering most lectures from memory, and providing valuable insights with down-to-earth examples. Doesn't assign too much reading, but is a harsh grader on papers, where he is loath to give out an A. All in all, a great, amiable man with an excellent intro course, but put your money on a B+.

Nice enough, but to be honest, he is really overrated as a professor. His grade deflationary stance (which he loves to tout) gets in the way of teaching because if you know the worst case scenario is you get a B but it's gonna be near impossible to get an A, then why go the extra mile? I'm a senior, and I'd say he's an avg teacher based on experien

Incredible professor who gets the best out of his students. Guides discussions effortlessly and make connections to everyday life. Great, meticulous feedback on writing. Hard though, Gillespie doesn't buy into grade inflation, he'll give you what you deserve. Best class I've taken at Duke so far.

I have taken two seminars so far, and both are among the best I have ever taken. Not only did I learn 19th Century Political Philosophy in the German tradition, but I learned quite a lot about how that relates to German literature as well. He makes ample time for his students and goes above and beyond to help them achieve their best.
Wonderful, wonderful professor. Makes himself extremely available to students--coming from a non-humanities background, this was critical to my success in his course. Highly recommended.

The class is hard because he is a very tough grader, not because of the content. I took the class knowing it would probably be my lowest grade (I was right) and I regret it somewhat. I definitely learned some stuff but not as much as I would have liked considering the hit it took on my gpa. My advice is to take a different pol phil class.

Gillespie is obviously a brilliant guy. Anyone can tell you that. But his teaching style, which relies a lot on circuitous reasoning and hypothetical scenarios, doesn't jibe well with a beginner in political philosophy. And he grades hard. A rich but frustrating intellectual challenge.

this class is such that the more you learn and understand the material, the more you get out of it. Before you really understand the philosophers, the class may seem random and abstract. In hindsight, class organization and discussions make great sense. Professor Gillespie is thoughtful, and his help is easy and beneficial to seek

Great class.  Dr. Gillespie makes himself available to his students night and day and addresses any concerns in a very helpful manner.  The workload isn't too big, but the papers are graded pretty hard, but fairly.  I recommend his class strongly!
Gillespie is a truly excellent teacher. He really cares about his students, and it shows. His class is difficult but absolutely worth it. I highly recommend taking his course.

Don't take this class and expect to get an A. The workload is not intense, but the grading is extremely difficult. If you like political philosophy you'll love this class. Dr. Gillespie is friendly, and very good at teaching. That being said, I probably regret taking it in hindsight due to the GPA hit I took. Would have had a 4.0 if not for it.
Amazing professor. Hard, but absolutely brilliant. Class discussions were extremely interesting (and frequently involved elaborate hypothetical scenarios). I highly recommend him.

Great professor! Interesting class discussions, although i would learn more from him lecturing than I do from the class discussions. Assigns broad topic essays and grades very hard, but not unreasonably.
Fantastic! Best class at Duke!
the class is interesting - he's a good lecturer and leads great discussions.  the paper assingments, however, were vague and graded rather harshly.

she is SO passionate about this material and watching her talk about it was genuinely fun. She makes ancient roman drama feel very accessible regardless of experience with classics. Dramas we read were very interesting! She is also so nice and makes a genuine effort to connect with students.

Prof G is AMAZING! Super interesting readings, and she expands them in eye-widening ways in class that make me look forward to the lectures. The course includes 3 creative writing assignments that are fun to write. A large portion of your grade is based on completion-based assignments, and Prof G gives out an extra credit opportunity every week.

She is such a gem! She will never cold call, class discussions are super interesting, and the "final" is a project that has choices as to what you will do! Take this class! It is great! Outside of class she is available through email/office hours/etc. and super supportive of your personal interests as well!

You're going to have to translate 140 lines a week (3-5 hours of work), but no cold calling. Participation matters so you can volunteer when you're confident. Quizzes are easy, 6-8 lines from 200 possible lines (easy to memorize). EC on every quiz. No final exam. Most of grade from quizzes and completion-graded forum posts. TAKE THIS CLASS!

My favorite professor at duke. If you are planning on taking any classics courses, Professor Ginsberg is the absolute best. Super clear grading criteria, allows retakes of quizzes, and does not cold call.

Professor Ginsbergs Age of Nero class was fascinating - I learned so much from her and the course. The readings assigned were reasonable and meaningful, but sometimes a bit long. Her final project was awesome, and its clear shes a great professor. Shes really kind and funny, and everyone should take this class (for fun or the ALP attached!)

I loved Professor Giles's lectures, but they often felt like a mishmash of random music and history trivia rather than a class. Most of the actual learning took place outside class through readings and researching for papers. Grade based mostly on essays (~1 per month), and she does not provide much specific feedback for improving your writing.

Dr. Giles is an amazing teacher and clearly loves the material she teaches about. Despite my lack of background in music, I felt engaged. The essays were rough but she was understanding if we needed an extension. Overall, this was an amazing focus and an amazing class.
She is really nice!! There are just some essay throughout the semester. Work hard on them and you should be fine :)!
Amazing professor! Goes on Renaissance music rants and the papers and readings are genuinely interesting. Great Focus class and great Focus in general!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --So many papers

reviews.comment: I have mixed emotions about Prof Giles. You kind of have to vibe with her and some of the lecutures can be dull. Every once in a while, a quiz/test felt kind of weird because I didn't know what to study for it. But the grading outline is clear and the final project was a paper/presentation about any album of our choice. The class also isn't hard.

A midterm the day after spring break, a final research paper on the last day of class, AND a final exam. Overall, a lot of work was due at extremely inconvenient times and rather than being understanding or working with us, she was cold and distant. I was also personally annoyed by her need to show her own personal vacation photos in class

In order to like Dr. Giles, you really have to vibe with the content she teaches and personality. For example, although her class was a music class it was actually a renaissance history writing class in disguise. She is very unclear on her instructions for papers and meeting with her does not do anything to enhance the paper.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Very passionate about her bunny and music! Love her so much

Her lectures are vivid and informative as she herself is a really funny and witty person. Honestly this is the class I enjoy the most in the fall of my freshmen year. Her grading is moderate (not chill but not hard either), and she is very helpful during her office hour. And please flunch her if you have the chance.

Dr. Gheith is a really sweet lady! She makes it her mission to ensure everybody is able to take something meaningful away from the class. However, there is A LOT of reading and writing. Expect to read and/or write multiple things for every class. The class requires lots of personal reflection, discussion, and deep thought, too.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: AMAZING professor. Would absolutely recommend taking classes with her.

Really nice, wonderful person. But she isn't always clear on what she wants from you and doesn't like  writing that goes outside of basics. When she says she wants reflection from you, she actually doesn't want original ideas where you chew on the idea and digest it, she just wants you to nibble on it a bit and then spit it back out on the page.

Take a class with Dr. Gheith! She cares a lot about her students, and while she has a ton of experience in her field, she's always open to hearing everyone's opinion. We had great class discussions that made me think, and readings were very interesting and not too heavy. She also brought us candy and snacks sometimes "just because"!
Helpful, easy to approach about any topic
Super fun!
Mrs. Gheith is one of the best professors at Duke. Her Focus class is very interesting. She is very caring and helpful. I could take any single class she offers. She's absolutely awesome!

Professor Gheith is probably the sweetest person you could ever encounter.  She is so understanding and helpful.  She always seems to really take an interest in her students.  The readings and films we read/watched were also very good.  The workload is not at all unbearable, but she is actually kind of a harsh grader.  I never got a 94 on anything.

Took Dostoevsky class with her and she is easily my favorite professor at Duke so far.  Also probably one of the nicest people you will ever meet.  Even if you don't have any experience with Dostoevsky  i recommend taking this class because she makes it an enjoyable experience.
She is an awesome teacher. I took ICS 200 with her and she is absolutely amazing. Great Prof.

Jehanne is unassuming, but absolutely brilliant. She could take the most inane question and use it to generate a valuable discussion. She respects her students no matter what their level, and their level improves visibly. She is truly a Friend of Us.
Jehanne is so sweet and totally genuine.  I love her so much!  Definitely try to take ANY class you can with her, she is fantastic.  She is passionate about her subject and her students.
Jehanne and David are both wonderful people, David is definately not an assclown.  They both give student work their all and are wonderful friends as well as teachers

Jehanne is so incredibly nice and helpful. Her classes are intriguing and she does a great job fascilitating interesting class discussions. She is incredibly sincere and cares about all of her students. Wonderful person and professor.
she is an amazing teacher. she is so intelligent and is so kind in guiding discussions and helping students. she is a teacher definitely worth having
