Took Russian Lit (Dosteovsky) as well as The Beatniks and the Russian New Wave. Very nice, sincere, and clear in expectations. She makes the material and her thoughts accessible. Watch out for David Need - he's an assclown.
Jehanne is easily one of the most engaging, nicest, most helpful and most intelligent professors I've had at Duke.  Sacrifice other classes in order to take something from her.
Most likely one of the nicest teacher's I've had....ever.
Profoundly insightful, caring, and interesting. Great class, highly recommended for anyone interested in quantum.
great class. Highly recommend

it is clear that Gleb knows the subject, but he has this amazing ability to make a potentially interesting topic into something extremely boring. Moreover, he only reads from the textbook during the lectures. I find it helpful to study the materials on my own instead of wasting my time in lectures.

Finkelstein isnt a great lecturer and 362 was definitely one of the harder classes Ive taken at Duke. The material is cool but youll be mostly using Griffiths to get through the class. Overall hes a well respected researcher and a brilliant man and Thankfully he makes exams in the class very easy but the actual teaching is subpar.

If you are interested in EM, you will learn a lot in this class. It covers a wide range of topics, and clear derivations of the topics are provided in lectures. He is very smart and knows his stuff, a great course. The tests are easy if you review and do the hw, many people get 100 on his tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Very sufficient content. Probably the smartest professor teach this level courses.

Seems like he disliked lecturing us just as much as people disliked his lectures. Hardly anyone went to class. Great physicist, but absolutely terrible lecturer. Exams were impossible no matter how much you prepare. Avoid if possible.

One of the worst professors I had at Duke. Made Statistical mechanics VERY boring (much more then it is). Basically the whole class is just him talking to the board and writing some formulas almost without any comments. The first exam was unreasonably hard, there were only 4 questions. Final was very easy. Take the class with someone else.

He's obviously smart and knows his stuff, but the lectures are SO boring. Even super dedicated students start skipping lecture sometimes because it's just hard to get anything from it. If you interrupt him to ask a question you'll usually get a pretty good answer. His exams are weird and pretty difficult but fairly graded.
Have Fun

Amazing professor and probably one of my favorite classes I have taken at Duke. If you do the readings, show up, and participate you will get a high grade. Lots of reading, but everything is very interesting and relevant to the course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I would 100% recommend for any course about slavery, the Civil War, or Reconstruction. Prof Glymph's lectures can be a little bit dry at times but she's super knowledgable, smart, easy to work to with, and cares about her students.
Awful. Passive aggressive and not that helpful. Pretends to care but not so much. Not that tough grader, though.
She does most of the talking. But when students participate the class gets really good. A lot of reading, but very interesting.  She's very nice and easygoing.

Perhaps the most boring class I've ever taken.  The course load was light, except for the reading, which was extensive and incredibly boring.  Picture an entire book filled with boring examples of court cases.  I am sure she is a nice person, and a fairly easy grader, but this class was so boring it was painful.

She is a great person when you get to know her and she cares about her students.  She knows her stuff, and with a class of people who  are lively and open, her personality will shine through. She has a great sense of humor when appropriate, but she is about her business too.  There is much 2 gain & little to lose. Brings interesting guest speakers.
Professor Glymph is interesting, a little quiet at times. Class is easy and stimulating, definitely recommend it.
Seems really mean at first.  She wants people to agree with her.  But, just when you think you're going to make a C+, you get an A- or B+.  Her grading seems really arbitrary.  Go to office hours!

Just avoid. Lectures are overall not very useful/barely help with the homework, so you will mostly be teaching yourself. Not many office hours. Tests are hard and heavily test memorization of every formula in the textbook. Overall grade is curved harshly. No instructions nor grading criteria were given for term paper worth 10% of your final grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Lectures went along well with the book and were especially helpful if you look over the chapter ahead of time. Had lots of interesting stories from his career as a biophysicist and expert in lasers. His office hours were really helpful and if you can't make them, he's happy to schedule a time for you that works. Overall, a really good professor!

Lectures are inaccessible and too fast-paced. There is little help with tests, no practice problems given, no real indication of what could be useful to study, and no lecture notes posted. The term paper is a ridiculous waste of time given the little instruction given. I felt very unsupported in this class and learnt very little from Prof Edwards.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I honestly have no idea why there are so many bad reviews. In 162, he is not rude at all and explains things very well. He goes over homework problems in class so that the assignments aren't as tough, and the exams are almost identical to the homework problems. He doesn't go in as depth as I had hoped, but he is a great lecturer and a nice guy.

Horribly cocky. Copied and pasted a random question on the exam that did not pertain to the lectures and then told class "I wonder why you all missed this easy question". I'm glad he finds it easy, with an answer key.

Hardest class I took in my life. Dr. Edwards is a nice professor and is willing to help if you reach out, but the exam/quiz problems were significantly harder than the homework problems for no apparent reason. At times it was like I understood the physics but couldn't comprehend was the exam question was even asking me to do. Def harder than 141.
Harder than Phys 141. His lectures weren't super clear (especially after the transition to online learning halfway through the semester), and the tests could be very hard.

Edwards is an awful lecturer. He is openly rude and also speaks EXTREMELY quietly - he explicitly said in the first class that he will NOT speak up, and if people have trouble hearing him then "deal with it". He could not give a damn about teaching, and he made it clear he just wanted to go back to research. I was very lucky to have a great TA.

Overall, Glenn's lectures didn't seem to pertain to the tests; he went through a lot of derivations but the quizzes and tests were on completely different material and much harder than HW. After transitioning online in March 2020, the class became MUCH harder too since the transition wasn't done well. However, Glenn was a really nice person
Literally the hardest exams but they're curved so it ends up being okay. Get ready to read your textbook (and other professors' textbooks, and other outside resources, etc etc)
Just avoid. Pretty useless. You will be teaching yourself.

Very cocky and rude. Said he can "look around the room and see who will get an A" and other very strange things like this. Then he said he would never write a test that blows people out of the water, and immediately the next test had a failing average. He doesn't even explain concepts and he just copies and pastes questions on exams from textbooks.

Worst professor I've had at Duke. I got through this class by using online materials from other universities. His lectures were horrible. He's unable to answer questions or explain concepts. I disagree with comments saying he's nice. That was not my experience. He's arrogant. If you're scheduling and see that he's teaching 142, take 152 instead.

He is genuinely the worst professor I had at Duke during my 4 years here (I took this class as a senior). His lectures consisted of doing textbook problems and explaining NO CONCEPTS. You learn no physics in this class, and he copies and pastes CHALLENGE problems to put on tests (actually copy and paste). He is completely inept and useless. AVOID.

You have to work super hard in this class. Make sure to ask questions and get clarity. Utilize outside resources to learn the material. This class is far from being a walk in the park, but if you ask Dr. Edwards for help, he is willing to help you understand the material.
Could go down as the worst professor at Duke University.
Pretty chill teacher. Didn't show up to a single lecture and still got an A

The final for this class was the hardest thing I've taken in my life. His lectures don't prepare you for the quizzes or the midterms. He writes very faintly and very small, and he doesn't speak loud enough for the whole class to hear. The test problems are worded weirdly and don't mimic the homework problems.

He was such a boring lecturer. All he did was go over specific practice problems. The class itself was tough because the grades ranged from a 100% to a 18%. He was always willing to discuss grades and show you ways to improve.

Dr. Edwards is an amazing lecturer and person. He is happy to spend time with students outside of class to help them succeed, and he is a very fair tester. His lectures are very relevant to the material that he wants/expect you to know. It is definitely not an easy class but he makes it possible to enjoy the material and to succeed.

Dr. Edwards is really cool and personable. A genuinely nice guy who really wants you to succeed. That said, I didn't really like his lecture style. He was all about proofs when I think example problems would have been more helpful. Plus, he prohibits calculator use while giving problems that require it.  I liked him though and would take him again.

Dr. Edwards is a great physics professor. He is very detailed and derives concepts in class. Although don't like his methods, the derivations help with the understanding of concepts. The class is undoubtedly a lot easier for students who have taken AP Physics C. The class is very fast-paced. Don't skip class!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Great at explaining physics concepts. Class is indeed a tough grade, which I suspect is the source of most students' frustration. Demonstrations in class are great, and his lectures are very clear.

Honestly he's a super nice guy. Go to his review sessions because he will work out problems in their entireity and make sure you understand. Also ask questions in class because it is almost 100% likely that other people are wondering the same thing. Lecture really isnt toooooo helpful because it is just proofs.

Honestly, PHYS 141 is a tough course. You really have to work for it. But just because the class is tough does not mean its the fault of Dr. Edwards. He was really nice, and went over many examples in class. I just wish he didn't squeeze in a bunch of material towards the end of the semester. Work hard and you will be fine!

Probably the worst professor I have ever had at Duke. Was not responsive if you couldn't attend the few office hours he had, and made learning Physics terrible. I honestly regret taking it with him, and wish I had taken the class over the summer. AVOID AT ALL COSTS if possible. His lectures are also all proofs and no practical material.

Edwards is a nice guy but the thing is there is no curve in this class. An A means actually getting 90% on all exams. This is very hard to do. Edwards will try to help you so if you have questions go straight to him. Recitation was a bit of a bore and not super helpful, but they had pretty hard quizzes that were similar to the midterms.

Hardest class I have taken at Duke! I was a straight A student before I took this class -- there is SO much material, exams are very challenging, and Edwards' lectures are dry and monotonous... he makes concepts that should be easy WAY harder and there's no way to get an A except by learning the material on your own time or if you've already had AP
He is a nice guy, just as him things and learn things and you will be fine.

Although Professor Glander is very old-school, he's still a great lecturer. He may be a bit dry at times but the course material is quite interesting. The only annoying thing is the massive memorisation process that everyone undertakes before each midterm.

Very memorization-based, with much of the info being from hs bio or intuitive. Not a difficult class, but go to lecture; his ppts aren't stellar on their own, and his recording doesn't always work. Get into the discussion section if you can! It'll replace a bad test grade. Tests are straight-forward, basically just regurgitation
Excellent professor! Very knowledgeable on the subject and would recommend as a nice easy class to take.

Arguably one of the easiest classes at Duke. Glander can be boring, but some of the material can be very interesting. Many of the concepts are learned in high school biology classes. Attendance is optional, but definitely go because he will say things that arent on his powerpoints that appear on his tests.
One of the nicest and most interesting professors at Duke.

EvAnth 101 with Prof. Glander was a great experience! He has over 40 years of field experience, and so his lectures not only are very interesting but he is the most knowledgable teacher I've ever had about a particular subject. Yes, he shows old videos, but they relate to what we learn in class so they're interesting nonetheless.

He has been teaching this class for 38 years. Considering the only thing he does in class is read from his slideshow and show monkeys washing potatoes, you would expect the quality of the presentations to be really good. They're not. He had info from the 70s in one of his presentations. Wouldn't recommend taking this class.

This guy is very cool. He is an expert in the field and has done a lot of cool things! He is also kinda fun, makes jokes every class but no one laughs. Definitely recommend this class. Makes me wish I would have taken more evanth classes!

The class isn't hard, but Glander can make the lecture a bit dry. I loved the material however. He's a nice guy and covers all the important info, it's just not thrilling - definitely just an introductory, lecture-style class. Lectures aren't mandatory and are posted online, but discussion is required but can replace a bad midterm grade (take it!)

I really recommend taking the discussion. It replaced one of my grades in the class, and it gives context for what you're learning. It's not hard but it does take significant memorization. You don't need to go to class but it makes studying easier. If you don't open the book you will do fine but there are always a few questions from it on his exams

Take the discussion section if you are worrying about your grade in the class. It replaces lowest grade on midterm (30%). Also course seems like useless memorization without discussion.  If you actually spend time studying for the tes (powerpoints + brief textbook) you should get an A no problem.  Class Attendance is completely optional.

He's insanely boring, but the material isn't that hard. Take the discussion because you can drop one of your 2 midterm grades for your discussion grade if it's higher than either of those. Lectures are posted online so you don't even need to go. He's boring..

He isn't the most interesting professor, but he does a good job for a huge lecture. He always tries to keep students interested though. There are a lot of movies. You don't really need to read the book but some questions from the test are taken from it. Very interesting introductory class.

His lectures are pretty boring, but fortunately he posts them online so if you zone out you can review them before a test. A couple days of reviewing the powerpoints and skimming the book prior to the test got me an A in the class even without taking the discussion. I would recommend it ONLY if you want to take more classes in the department.

Very easily class, so long as you pay attention to the lecture/read the slides. Reading the text is probably a good idea if you're shooting for a good grade, however, as Glander's fond of throwing in random questions on things never mentioned in his lectures that are in the book.
No a very hard class if you read and pay attention in class.  Reading a lot more helpful for second test than the first one.
Very interesting lectures.  Really go over powerpoints prior to the test and at least try to skim through the book.

This class was a waste of time. He just showed videos and gave basic lectures, then tested on ridiculous details from the textbook. Also he didn't seem to have best personality in class, although I never talked to him personally.

If you are looking for an easy NS course, pick a different BAA class because there are classes that are still easy but much more interesting. I am a BAA major and I hated this class because the material was easy/basic/boring, and Glander is not a very interesting lecturer. He also repeats himself a lot.

This is not an easy A.  If you take it, take the discussion section.  It is really the difference between failing and passing as your lowest score gets replaced.  Also, he's not really the nicest guy in the world.  He tends to talk down to people and make them feel stupid in front of the entire lecture section.

Heres the deal. Look at my scores with a grain of salt. With glander, the class is easy as LONG AS YOU TAKE THE DISCUSSION SECTION. In this section they drop a bad test and pretty much tell u what to study for. No joke, I have taken higheler level math and chemistry courses, and without the discussion section this was my hardest class at duke

Take the lab section. It could be the difference between an A and a C in this class. One bad exam and its over basically. The lab tests are usually easy and you can expect an A on them. Exam questions are ridiculous. Option b on a multiple choice question on one exam was "a and b". I mean give me a break.

Glander is a jerk. Flat out jerk. Seriously, do not take his class. It is def not an easy A, more of an easy B,B-. It is incredibly hard to get an A because he tries to trick you in his tests. He will never answer your questions, only talk down to you. On his tests, he asks extremely obscure questions that aren't even relevant, like dates or names.

Really, really, really not an easy A. Thats the only reason I took it, but that definitely backfired. He is the least helpful teacher I have ever had. Make sure to study dumb facts like who discovered what and what dates and locations things were found in.

Not as easy of an A as most people think. Tests are based completely on power points. Your grade is based off of three tests and if you mess up on one, you're screwed. Best advice: TAKE THE DISCUSSION!!! and study things he says aren't too important [like dates and such]
NOT AN EASY CLASS!  3 TESTS DETERMINE YOUR WHOLE GRADE!! MESS UP ON ONE AND UR SCREWED!!

Pretty simple class, especially if the material interests you somewhat. Easy tests, expected them to be much more detailed. No homework. You can just study the slides on powerpoint and still do well. Made me decide to minor in Bio Anthro
I definitely enjoyed this class. Kenneth Glander was the man.I personally got a lot out of the lectures and found them very interesting.

Glander seems to be pretty stuck up and short with his students. I wouldn't mind if he made the course interesting, but he fails to even do that.  The class is a joke if you take the discusion though.

Glander was an interesting teacher. He went back on a lot of what he said in his powerpoints, he lost his voice a lot, he let us out early, and could be pretty sassy. The tests are random, and despite studying I never felt prepared for his questions.  It is not necessary to go to class, but I would sign up for the discussion.
Very intelligent guy. However, tests are a bit too detailed. Definitely take the discussion section to boost your grade.

I went to lecture and found the class fairly easy. No assignments are a plus, just show up for tests, which are just m.c. and t/f. Doing the discussion section gives you some freedom to screw up on a test, but I found even when I didn't study for my second test, I managed an 88, so its up to you. Its really easy though, so there's not much risk.

Tests are extremely arbitrary.  As a BAA major, I felt that the questions he asked reflected common sense more than knowledge of the material.  Though he was obviously not very excited to be teaching intro to BAA and it showed in lackluster lecture performance, I have heard that he really is a smart and decent in classes at higher levels.

not as much of a joke class grade-wise as you would think seeing all the athletes flock to it...no curve, so miss 6 of the 50 MCQ on the midterms and youre down to the B range, and some of the ?s are kinda tricky...no real need to go to lecture since he posts all his powerpoints on blackboard and basically just reads them to you for lectures...
No Comments
Dumb class. I did better in Orgo than in this class b/c this class was so boring/unengaging. Ridiculously stupid material, unpredictable professor
the professor is a really nice guy who's not only interested in the subject he teaches, but also in his students and how they're doing in his class

TERRRIBLE class. Not that easy after the summer of '04. Many people did worse in this class than in harder, more important chemistry classes. Tests focused on the most ridiculous details. Glander was sometimes disturbingly moody/scary. Interesting character, though ... I guess.

This class is easy and fufills a Natural Science requirement.  If you study the book and power point slides there is no reason to ever go to class.  Taking the dicussion/lab section is optional and somewhat of a pain but it will probably help your grade.
very boring, stupid, silly.

This class is really easy. All the lectures are on powerpoint and availible online. You have the option of attending discussion section. There are three midterms and a final, and everything is multiple choice. If you go to class you dont have to study.

If you study a lot, it will be relatively easy.  He's boring, but he likes to show videos, which are sometimes interesting.  He thinks he's cool because he did Letterman like 20 years ago.  If you have to get an STS, take these class. Otherwise, CHEM83
he's a really good teacher, even if his personality is lacking.
Very easy, but very boring class

The buffest 50 to 60 something year old around. This man is FIT. . .like gorilla fit but not like man in gorilla suit fit. Easy tests (average grade: 88), just come to lectures, and watch movies about monkeys.
Negligent, Self-centered, Vague
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Just no. Insensitive to student communication. Did not teach whatsoever, yet expected us to be 100% engaged. No regard for student wellbeing. Talked about students to other students behind their back.
he is an evil man, avoid.

Avoid this man at all costs. Sometimes I think his job is to bring students down and ruin their enthusiasm. He would act irritated if I reached him for advice, as if his job was not AN UNDERGRADUATE ADVISOR of Classics department. Also, he shows strong favoritism towards specific students. He never responds to the emails either. And quite rude

Super nice guy! 30% of grade is 6 reading quizzes (lowest dropped), 20% participation, other 2 25% are group presentation + final paper. Class is just reading prepared translation, and if you get lost or are struggling through a passage, he helps you out and is very encouraging. His accent is not as bad as others claim.I have him again next sem

He's awesome and very caring, taking time outside class for us, and sets us for success, grading quizzes leniently and helping out in-class translations. Only 6 quizzes (lowest dropped), group presentation (sources preassigned), and final paper. Cold-called to translate and reading lots of lines for hw. His accent is not as bad as people claim.

He's great. You will be fine if you have completed Latin through the intermediate level - and he grades quizzes quite fairly (e.g. he'll make corrections but won't take off very many points at all for it). He clearly cares about his students, and I signed up for another class next semester partially just because he's teaching it.

Professor Gonzalez started off the course by saying his one goal was to make sure all his students continue to take Latin, which I think he has done by making the course enjoyable. There is a lot of homework (preparing Latin for class/quizzes) and a high-stakes presentation and final paper, but you will be fine if you put in the work.

Dr. Gonzalez is a brilliant professor who really cares about his students and tries to create a classroom environment where everyone can feel comfortable during discussion. He assigns a lot of reading, and it can get repetitive, but I think that's just the nature of the class that he teaches. I would definitely recommend taking a seminar with him.

Jose is an incredible professor. He knows the material thoroughly and seemed to enjoy teaching a freshman seminar this year. Apart from weekly readings, the class was not very demanding in terms of workload or difficulty. The class also fulfills many distributional requirements. Definitely take a seminar with Jose if you can!
Really intelligent and caring professor. Great readings and someone to look up to if one is interested in both science and classics.
Very knowledgeable. Good communicator.

I think Professor Gonzalez is reasonable.  There were no pop quizes, just a midterm,presentation and paper.  His accent can be a little difficult to understnad, but not that bad.  All in all, I thought he was a great teacher who really has enthusiasm for what he teaches.
I loved professor Gonzales! He's a nice and helpful guy.

He is a horrible teacher.  He will give you the impression that it is an easy class, but then really surprise you on the quizzes and everything.  He says that grades aren't important and that he just looks for progression, but he really grades very harsh.  AVOID THIS CLASS--TAKE ANOTHER ONE--OR AT LEAST SOMEONE ELSE. Makes you learn useless info.

He has a very strong accent making it impossible to understand him. You must always go to class even though you learn hardly anything. Pop quizzes are annoying, and his scheduled quizzes are impossible. Even though he grades easy on tests, studying for them is ridiculous (memorizing 100 dates) etc. Don't do it.

She is so sweet and really caring and understanding. However, there is a lot of homework for someone who is just looking to fulfill the language requirement. But if you do the work and participate, you will likely get an A as she is a very lenient grader.

Mme. Gonthier is the absolute GOAT. I'm a Math/CS major who took 303S to fulfill my Trinity requirement, but I left the class with an in-depth knowledge of French politics and culture. Incredibly interesting class with tests and oral exams that will really test your mastery of French. As long as you show effort though, you will get an A.

I loved Dr Gonthier's class. She is a very kind soul who genuinely cares about her students development and wellbeing. Would 1000% recommend. 

The class had a moderate amount of homework - expect 3-6 hours per week of reading and listening stuff. However, all assignments are very generously marked and easy to do well in.

Learned a lot about French politics/society from an everyday perspective. Lectures can occasionally get boring, but group work/projects balance it out; good amount of homework. Exams are straightforward and grading is lenient. Madame cares far more about participation and putting in effort than your actual French ability - try and you'll get an A.

Gonthier is such an amazing professor who loves teaching and interacting with students. I highly recommend this class to anyone who wants to improve their French, but It's definitely not the easiest low 300 level course. HW 3x/week takes anywhere from 30 minutes to 2 hours and there are several small projects, like presentation and voicethread.

HALLELUJAH CHRISTELLE. She really cares about teaching more than grading, somehow the class was heavy in work and content but low-stress. She makes such an effort to compliment and encourage you, and it definitely shows that she cares about your experience.
She was the first French professor I had at Duke and her class was so interesting! Highly recommend as she is very kind and the content is very relevant to current events.

French for Current Affairs has been my favorite class at Duke so far. The structure of the class has variety, including lectures with opportunities to participate, group activities, readings, and oral assignments. Gonthier really cares about her students and is always willing to help. This is an incredible foray into French culture and politics.

Prof Gonthier's class was always a lot of work, but she really cares about helping you learn French. She is consistently available outside of class, and she will go the extra mile to teach you French as it is actually spoken. She is one of the most kind professors I've had at Duke, and a very fair grader who cares about giving feedback.
Amazing professor! Had her in the virtual format. Super nice and encourages a lot of classroom participation. Beware of a lot of homework though.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: French For Current Affairs was one of the best classes I have taken at Duke. It was online, but Professor Gonthier brought energy to every lecture and made the homework relevant and interesting. Highly highly recommend, and she is also a great person to get to know!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Madame Gonthier is among the best professors I've ever had. Her incredible kindness and accommodating nature can only be matched by her vast knowledge of French culture and society. I cannot overstate how highly I would recommend anyone interested in French to take a class with Madame Gonthier. You will be incredibly glad you did so.

Gonthier is the best professor in the french department. She is so kind and encouraging to students, especially if you are clearly making an effort and progressing. Also the material is definitely the most interesting and relevant out of any of the french classes i've taken, so the homework is actually interesting. Great professor and cool class!

One of the best French professors I've had at Duke. Mme Gonthier genuinely wants her students to succeed and she is passionate about the material. This class has lots of homework, but the grading is lenient and expectations are made clear. I found her class very rewarding and my French skills improved a lot.

If angels fell from heaven they would manifest in the form of Christelle Gonthier, I just want to hug her everytime I see her. 2nd time in her class and I learned more about political/social issues from her than my 3 PubPol core classes combined. Your French will improve so much, she gives you a ton of chances to get an A, and lenient w/ late work.

I loved Mme Gonthier's class and teaching style! She was so helpful, kind, and made classes fun! I definitely learned a lot from her and would love to take another class with her! Can't recommend highly enough!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Prof. Gonthier makes you work hard for your grade, but after taking this class, you'll be glad you did. She is extremely kind, knowledgeable about French current events, and fantastic at creating homework that enhances your understanding of the topic. Your French skills will improve immensely in her nurturing and constructive environment.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Mme Gonthier is possibly the best French teacher I've ever had and if you're interested in politics/current events this is the class for you. I learned so much! She's a pretty chill grader and her quizzes/final are not difficult as long as you learn the material. However, she does lowkey assign a lot of homework.

Starting out my first semester at Duke, I am so glad that I got the chance to have Madame Gonthier as a professor. She not only made sure that we were all confortable with the material during class, she also made herself extremely accessible outside of class if we needed anything. Her class was incredibly engaging and I felt like I learn a lot.

Prof. Gonthier is perhaps the most caring professor I've ever had--she really gets to know each and every one of her students and is invested in everyone's success. Although this class was a constant source of homework, assignments and presentations, I could not have thought of a better way to end my 9-year French education. She's simply the best!
Super nice person and a fairly lenient grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Gonthier is the nicest professor I have had at Duke so far. She really cares about her students and how they feel about and engage with French as a language. She is really kind, supportive and helpful and does everything that she can to give her the student the best language -learning experience possible.

PLEASE PLEASE do yourself a favor and take French with Madame Gonthier! I have struggled with the language requirement for the past few semesters but she really turned this around for me. She cares deeply about her students and will do her best to make sure you really learn the language. She is also a great lecturer and leads good discussions.
Would highly recommend taking her class. It was the best class I've taken at Duke. The material is interesting, and her teaching style is refreshing.

Prof. Gonthier is the best French professor I could have asked for. She cares about each student in her small class, she knows everything there is to know about French current affairs, and she is a generous, constructive grader. Her homework and in-class exercises make learning easy and reinforce knowledge of the language.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Honestly one of the best classes/professors at Duke. Low stress, high reward in terms of learning. Do whatever you can to take this!

By far one of the best professors I have had at Duke. Clearly well-informed on a matter of subjects, excellent at conveying the material and gives fair, clear assignments. Overall, an incredible person and professor.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Mme Gonthier is always there if you need help with clarification or if you want to review before an exam. She is also flexible with her office hours if you can't make it to her usual ones. She is super nice and I highly recommend.

French 303 is my favorite French class that i've taken at Duke. You learn a lot about the political, educational and social structure of the class. Prof. Gonthier is the best professor at Duke. She goes above and beyond for her students, and is the nicest person I've met here. Definitely recommend.
She is just so sweet and wants you to do well. I love going to class and my French has dramatically improved.

Christelle Gonthier is the best French teacher I've ever had. She makes you work to get an A, but my French improved greatly and she is such a kind individual! If you can, definitely take French with her!

Let me emphasize that I really hate French, and I loved this class. It was mandatory to go, but I never wanted to miss. She's kind, helpful, and an easy grader (compared to other profs in the department). Do whatever you can to take a class with her.
I love Chriselle! She is willing to work with you to help you in the class and with your French in general. She's an awesome professor and I learned a ton in this class.

If you put in a decent amount of effort, pay attention at least a bit, and participate often enough, you can easily get the A-. But it's a big jump between A- and A so be prepared to work really hard if you want an A. Other than that, she's very engaging and fun.

If you get the chance take a class with her. Any class. She is so sweet, enthusiastic, and spends a lot of time preparing her lesson plans. I loved her class and will genuinely miss it now that the semester is over.

Christelle is the best teacher I've had at Duke so far. She's the kind of teacher where you WANT to do well in her class, and you put in the time and effort to do so (although the workload is quite a bit). Going to French class is always an enjoyable experience with her.
Christelle is the best professor I've had at Duke. She is extremely sweet and very knowledgeable of the subject material. I would highly encourage anyone interested in french to take a class with her
Great class overall! The grading was not too difficult, yet my French improved tremendously and I learned a lot. Would definitely recommend taking this class or any other class taught by Gonthier!

Gonthier is simply fabulous! Class zooms by because the conversations and lectures are so incredibly interesting. I improved my French immensely over the semester and had a great time doing it. She is the epitome of an amazing professor -- not to mention her impeccable style and "Frenchness." Contemporary France is a must-take class at Duke.

Mme Gonthier is LITERALLLY the best french professor at Duke. She is SO nice... its unbelievable how much she cares about her students and their progress in the class. I really wish all the best for her in the future because she has had such an immense impact on my academic career :')

What a fantastic professor! She's brilliant and engaging... she really makes you passionate about the language, and the amount of improvement everyone in the class has had is incredible. She's funny and very sweet and understanding. One of my best professors so far!
Prof. Gonthier was a really sweet professor. She was always enthusiastic and encouraging. Her grading was better than fair.
She is really nice. Probably one of the best professor's I've had at Duke. She's really leniant and understanding, and you'll actually learn a lot. Must have as a professor

She is so nice! And a great teacher. Able to organize engaging class discussions and integrate interesting forms of learning through media. I would highly recommend taking any French class with Mme Gonthier. And grading isn't too difficult either.
She's an incredible teacher, and very engaging.
Really helpful and makes clear what to expect. Not necessarily the easiest, but she definitely shows interest in her students.

French 101 (advanced grammar) should be the most boring class in the universe, but with professor gonthier it's somehow not. She's very energetic, smart, and dedicated to helping her students get better at french. very helpful feedback on all assignments. Take any French class with her!

Gonthier is my favorite Duke prof so far and cemented my decision to continue French in college...she is extremely nice and very helpful, and the class material is really interesting. Not a hard class, but she gives great feed back so it makes you want to try.

Gonthier made me fall in love with French again.  Her class is everything 63 and 76 should be: informative, open, enjoyable, and straight forward.  She is always available outside of class and will go the extra mile to help you out if you get caught in a bind.

I did mediocre in both 63 and 76... but loved 100 with Gonthier. Subject matter is much more interesting, focus is on WHAT you say/ your opinion on contemporary french issues and therefore less on grammar and technicalities... plus she is a great teacher, makes class interesting and always available to help.
Madame Gonthier is one of the nicest professors at duke! extremely helpful, not a hard grader, makes class interesting. take a class with her if you can!
Prof. Gonthier is a great French teacher. She is available all the time to help, really nice about taking late hw, and a pretty easy grader. She also does a good job of reviewing for tests.

I think Goldston was a great professor and his lectures/readings were super interesting. The class was pretty test heavy and not graded on many things. But if you study, its easy to do well. Not a ton of work outside tests and 2 short papers + 1 long paper. Discussion section was pretty disorganized and not very helpful. Grading took sooo long.

I only put OK because he seems like a nice person with a passion for psychology, but the class wasn't very good. It's extremely test heavy. There's no homework except for 3 papers so there isn't an opportunity to make your grade better. Grading anything took extremely long. Overall I just didn't enjoy this class and esp how long it took for grades
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Wish I didn't take this class. Took very long to grade and grading was harsh. He lowered my grade from what my TA gave me but didn't know I could see from end. I emailed and I "wasn't supposed to see that". They took 16 days to grade our paper and 14 to grade our exam. We got finals back before these midterm grades. Lectures weren't clear/helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If she's teaching ECE356 I wouldn't recommend it. There's so much content, with each lecture containing over 100 slides. This class is just straight memorization, but is made all the more challenging with how uninteresting the lectures are. They're very dry and she goes through the content quite fast. If you're trying to genuinely learn, good luck.

Came to learn? Nope. Get your brain ready for some ultimate memorization bc thats what all you'll be doing in this class. Worst lectures ever in existence, actually so boring and she never explains her slides or understands them. This class is entirely SELF STUDY! you came here for amazing lectures? NO. LEAVE. embarrassing. most disorganized class!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Get ready for a GPA tank! Her tests do NOT test critical thinking / problem solving. You will be tested on how well you memorize her infinite slides!! You would think spending a lot of time on the labs and projects that actually test your knowledge from this class would reward you well SADLY NO. Only your memorization will reward you the most!

This class is honestly a joke to learning. I was hoping to be challenged but the tests are just pure memorization of the most minuscule details from her slides (each slide deck 100+ slides). You basically will spend 90% of your time on the labs and project for 15% of your grade and spend 1-2 days studying for the pure memorization final to be 40%.

Lectures are so boring, losing people always. Lots of quizzes on huge beefy topics. Exams r brute force memory copy paste from her infinite slides, no critical thinking ever just brute force memorization. Horrible prof. Crazy hard homework with no help from TA or the professor. Honestly worst class ever I have taken at Duke and that says a lot.

Just took the final exam for fall 2024. The lectures are a bit dull. Most people are on their laptops. The exams require straight memorization of the content on the slides, which is doable but not fun. The router project is interesting and doable. Not as difficult as some of the other 300 level ece classes.

Slides aren't the best. She breezes pass slides fast. Router project is hard and confusing, but doable. Midterm is medium level. She's a decent lecturer, but be prepared to do lots of self-studying before quizzes. Luckily networks itself isn't a tough class. This class is just a regular class: nothing crazy, nothing bad. Average but interesting.
Not a bad professor. Lectures were good. Assignments and quizzes weren't that bad. The last lab is a lot of work, but manageable. The midterm wasn't tough.

This is the worst professor I have had in my entire life. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS IF SHE IS TEACHING IT. She is horrible at teaching, her assignments are all copied and uninspiring, and the router project is the hardest, most unclear, and worst project I have ever done. Honestly, her professorship is an insult to Duke and the occupation of teaching.
Her slides only makes learning harder, get ready to learn by yourself. But don't worry too much cause this is not a hard course, and her homework are easy to follow.

The class was super interesting and the lectures were clear, well-structured, and easy to follow, although a bit dry at times. The assignments (particularly Lab 2 and 3) were harder than what I had had in other CS classes at Duke, with no online resources or materials on the lecture to help us with it. It was a lot of work, but I recommend her.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Nice person, but a terrible teacher. Her lectures are very hard to understand and her explanations are very confusing. Her assignments are also very incomplete, instructions for projects are unclear, and she doesn't teach the information needed to complete projects because she takes them from other professors.

Dr. Golonka is one of the kindest, most wonderful professors at Duke. The topics she covers in class are interesting. You will get out of this class what you put in, but either way you will likely receive an A. She creates a class environment that is about learning and asking questions, rather than being stressed about a grade. Amazing woman.
If you get the chance to, take this class with Dr. Golonka!! The assignments and homework were extremely reasonable, and she makes writing the final research paper incredibly simple. AMAZING CLASS!!!
The whole semester is spent working towards a final paper, and Golonka provides great feedback along the way.
Super chill professor, supports you outside class, wants to help you succeed. Most of the class is athletes. Start working on your final paper early and this will be a breeze. A gem of a professor.
Dr. Golonka is the best teacher I have had at Duke. Do yourself a favor and take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. G is the absolute best! My favorite class I've taken so far. The class is so interesting for students of all majors. Lectures were amazing and so engaging. There are short readings for every class and 6 reflections throughout the semester. The final research paper is a lot of work, but you are guided through it. Please take this class!!!!!

Probably my favorite professor at Duke so far! She's so caring and always puts the needs of students first. She is clear about her grading criteria and is always open to questions. The classroom environment was so warm and inviting despite the tough topics we discussed at times! I absolutely love her! She wants all of her students to do well!

Dr. G is the best. She is extremely accessible and has very clear deadlines. Her grading criteria is very easy to follow and explains what she is expecting on all assignments. I learned so much during this class, and she has incredible stories that engage the entire class during discussion. You should take a class with Dr. G!

Dr. Golonka says that she doesn't want this class to be stressful, and she means it. You learn a lot without busywork with meaningful assignments that require you to reflect on the material. If you are having issues, she will also work with you. Overall, I really enjoyed this class.

Dr. Golonka is one of my favorite professors I've had! Class is super engaging and always has a brief lecture about the topic followed by discussion. Her expectations and grading are clear. She also clearly cares about her students and is super welcoming. Highly recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Golonka created a warm, friendly environment for class discussions. She had clear expectations for exams and writing assignments and gave helpful feedback. I felt like she actually cared about my success in the class. I learned a ton with very little stress.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. G is honestly one of the best people on campus. She is so caring and smart and will do anything to help her students succeed. Also, lowkey extremely funny. Intro to Child Policy is a engaging class as well and is a nice way to get a research credit if you need one.

Prof Golonka is absolutely fantastic. Emerging Adulthood is also a really interesting topic, and the readings are easy to get into. Golonka is super helpful and approachable inside and outside of class. She structures the class so that you actually learn to write at a college level without sacrificing your GPA. Definitely take it if you can get in!

Prof. G is a great professor and she is very helpful with your writing. She is very passionate about the topics and it shows in the level of interest she puts into the students writing regarding emerging adulthood. I would highly recommend taking her class if you can.

This class is definitely one of the better Writing 101 courses offered. Professor Golonka is extremely sweet, enthusiastic, and helpful! Class consists of a few very easy readings and blog posts in the beginning, then three major writing projects that you get plenty of feedback on.

I highly recommend any course taught by Prof. Golonka. She goes above and beyond to help her students. All papers are allowed revisions before a final grade. She is fair and enthusiastic. You can tell that she genuinely cares about her students and what she is teaching. She is by far my favorite professor this semester. Take this class if possible.
Professor Golonka is the nicest! She's so helpful and easy to talk to. The Writing 101 class on Emerging Adulthood is pretty easy and very interesting. I highly recommend taking a class from her.

Professor Golonka is great! My favorite professor at Duke so far! She is extremely helpful and is always willing to meet and discuss your essays, either before and after they have been graded. The topic of "Emerging Adulthood" is also super relevant - it's about people our age! Highly recommend taking a class with her.

She is an awesome professor! And the class is fairly easy but really interesting. There's no textbook, so you don't technically have to read anything for class, and all the material overlaps. None of the material will be tested on.
Arbitrary, unexplained grading criteria

While somewhat interesting, the course had many logistical problems. Comments I received on my papers were unhelpful and often irrelevant. Grades seemed to be determined by how similar your opinions were to Dr. Gold. Given how upset she'd be when you emailed her about your future absence, you'd think her lectures were life-changing. They were not.

Dr. Gold is an amazing professor! She is is super passionate about the death and dying, and you will learn skills in this class that you won't in others such as empathy, open-mindedness, and the ability to talk about sensitive subjects. The service-learning component of the class greatly adds to the experience. I definitely recommend!
Dr. Gold is a good professor. Her grading can be harsh, so make sure you carefully examine the guidelines for each assignment.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The readings are plentiful, and you absolutely must participate. Based on the other reviews, some people don't like how particular she is, but she basically gives step by step instructions for how to do well on the big assignments. Make sure you are prepared for the time commitment of service learning. It's no joke.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I had Dr. Gold in 2004 and while reminiscing about bad professors on RMP I saw she's still receiving the same feedback in 2021, so BEWARE that these aren't one-offs, and she's not likely to change. I still remember her capricious grading standards, unwillingness to consider alternative viewpoints, and lack of sensitivity to underrepresented groups.

Extremely opinionated and grades papers harshly and subjectively. If your opinion isn't hers then it isn't 'right'. Unnecessarily specific about style and format for papers even though she doesn't provide a rubric. Listen and take notes during class so you know what she is looking for on assignments and don't have to email her after (she'll be mad)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: Probably heard the same stories about aging at least five times throughout the semester........
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This was the best course I have ever taken in college, maybe ever. Dr. Gold is an incredible professor who teaches an interesting subject and manages to have an engaging discussion even over zoom. I went to class and did the readings because I genuinely wanted to learn and enjoyed the class. She is fair in her feedback and cares for each student.
If you're a student of color, you will find that she can be pretty unsympathetic and commit a bunch of micro-aggressions during lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Don't know why she still teaches; she obviously hates it.

Probably one of the worst professors I've had at Duke. There's a reason people are critical of tenure. Most of the her lectures consisted of past memories teaching the course. During one lecture, she very explicitly used a racial slur against Asian students (in the context of explaining another person's words, but it was still cringe-worthy).
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Gold is one of my favorite professors. Very smart and funny. Just shoot her an email if you have a question about an assignment and she will get back to you. We spend an entire day discussing the big assignments (midterm and final) so you know exactly what to do. Service-learning is definitely the largest component and is rewarding.

She really isn't available after class to discuss papers and projects that will determine your grade. And when she gives you a terrible grade on a paper for apparently "not following directions," she will blame you; as if it was your fault that she didn't answer your emails or questions about certain prompts on the paper. She needs to be replaced.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Unsure why anyone has posted a negative review. This class is easy and useful! If you didn't do well you either didn't read before a quiz or blatantly didn't follow rules or show up to service learning. Very heavily discussion based class which I loved because you can sit bit and listen or jump in and engage as much as you want. Dr. Gold is a gem.

Not much of a class. You just sit there and listen to Dr. Gold repeat stories about aging, and share your own experiences with the service-learning component of the course. Her grading criteria is super strict, and she doesnt provide you a rubric. Made a mistake taking this class..
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Gold isn't the best professor in the sociology department. Her lectures are somewhat scattered, and most of class time is spent discussing about your time volunteering with the service learning portion of the class. Her assignment criteria is super strict, and she doesn't do a great job of explaining exactly what she wants. Would not take again
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: I've had a number of pretty bad sociology professors at Duke, but Dr. Gold definitely would top the list. Her lectures are just her re-hashing some past experiences that she repeats over and over again. She's also unnecessarily nit-picky when grading.

Dr. Gold is an amazing professor. She is caring and dedicated, and an overall joy to be in a class with. She can seem strict, but if you follow her guidelines for papers (which she is very explicit with) you will be fine. Highly recommend, especially for anyone going into a medical field.

Funny and sweet. She's sassy and is very outspoken and liberal. Sometimes she says really weird stuff, but everyone loves her. Quizzes easy. Just show up and say stuff in class sometimes. She's great, and loves talking with the class. you basically just share your opinions/experiences on death and healthcare. didn't learn much though. fun class
Dr. Gold is a wonderful person and teacher. She's very sassy and sarcastic, but also very caring and willing to help you if you're struggling.

Dr. Gold is an experienced educator and has a lot to tell. Her Medical Sociology class, while insightful, focused heavily on the elderly and end-of-life care (her specialty). If you are interested in this, I recommend taking this class. Service learning is incorporated heavily into class discussion. Follow her guidelines for papers carefully.

Death&Dying was so interesting, and Dr. Gold is so inspiring. There were weekly readings and two reading quizzes that were super easy. There is one big final paper. She wants it to be done in a very specific way. If you follow her guidelines, you will be fine. It is a service learning course, only 2 hours of volunteering per week. Take this course!

Last rating's a bit rough- she's a great speaker esp for newcomers to the subject, but some seniors found potholes in her arguments. Class devoted to discussing service learning and topics of interest; reading needed for only 3 quizzes. Only hw  reflections, annotated bib & final paper. Very passionate & clear. Follow directions, you'll get an A.

Dr. Debby Gold is an amazing professor.  She is tough, she makes you think, and she will pull your best out of you.  Get ready to write . . .you will do a lot of it and she will critique hard, but you will be a better writer for it.  Can't phone this one in.  She will give you what you give her.  Brilliantly witty.  She should be cloned!
Dr. Gold is the best at what she does and is passionate about sharing it. Great experience in several different classes with her.

Great class. The class doesn't give too much work and the lectures/class discussions are quite interesting. Follow her instructions carefully for the midterm/final papers and you will do fine. Dr. Gold may seem kind of strict, but she's a real sweetheart. Highly recommended class for all students, especially pre-meds. One of Duke's very best profs!

Great class, the most work outside of class is the mandatory service learning (2hr/week) but that is more fun than anything else. Make sure to participate in class and talk to her about your papers and you will do well.

She's an interesting lecturer and doesn't assign too much work, but does make you think. You'll question yourself in this class, and become a better person for it. It's not an automatic A, but it's not a hard class if you put effort into your papers. She's very helpful. Take classes with her. One of the best profs at Duke.

I took her Death and Dying course in the fall of 2005. It is one of the few courses that have stuck with me. She was insightful, helpful, and friendly. Her lessons extended beyond the course. I would take the course again if I could.  By the way, I never found her grading to be strict or unreasonable. She gives you what you give her.
Such a great and engaging lecturer. I loved her and her amusing e-mails. She had a ton of insightful comments and was truly interested in each student. I plan on taking every course Dr. Gold teaches.

I heard great things about Professor Gold and her class, Death and Dying, before this semester, so I chose to take her class. I have been disappointed. Class lecture has been repetitive and discussion stagnant. This, however, may be a symtom of the failure of sociology as a discipline.

Dr. Gold is a great person and someone you should take a course with. She does seem intimidating and fussy about attendance/requirements etc, but in reality she really cares about students and is extremely helpful. Paper grading is tough, but she will help you during office hours. The best part about her is her responsiveness to emails.

Excellent professor. Very very very open to talking with students. Passionate about subject. Doesn't go over reading much, but she appreciates it when you make references in class. Make sure to consult her before writing papers and you will do well. One of the best professors I have had at Duke.

Decent teacher and often amusing when it comes to class lecture.  However, if you aren't on her good side when it comes to the essays you probably won't do very well.  Her expectations are very unclear which can screw you over big time on the midterm and final essay.

Took her focus class: She's very particular about the format of papers, but she will give good feedback on your essays if you turn them in early + let you rewrite papers. Very helpful and enthusiastic about the topic.

Interesting topic.  Assigns tons of readings, but only few students in the class seem to do them.  Sometimes she gets to talking and won't go over any of the readings.  What she wants in papers aren't clear.  However, she is pretty flexible and understanding.  If you have a problem just address it with her.  Overall we covered interesting material.

Good professor until it comes time for the assignments--class is good but she has a tendency to be unclear on papers and then blame students for not understanding an assignment.  For one paper, she explicitly to me to do one thing, took points off for it, then said "I'm sorry I didn't explain it well" without changing the grade

Deb has an attitude. Class can be very tense at times. You do not want to get on her bad side because she can be very harsh. Her lectures are very interesting and very clear. I She certainly knows her subject matter. When writing research papers, it helps to state your research question directly in the intro or have a very defined argument.

Deb Gold is the best.  A really good teacher- interesting discussions in class.  Very helpful with writing, but make sure you know exactly what she wants.  Very good.  I plan on taking another one of her classes.

best professor i've had in my freshman yr. she's engaging, pursuasive.. might be a little bit intimidating at first, but if you are a potential psychology major, her classes are must-take's. you'll love her/ her lectures/ psychology.
Excellent class if you have interest in the material.  She really makes you think sometimes.  Very little work during the semester, but the midterm and the final will hit you hard.

Dr. Gold is very nice and leads great class discussions (but be forewarned that they are a bit morbid and on the liberal side). The major problem is that she isn't very clear on how she wants assignments structured, which can really screw you over when it comes to grades on big essays.
Sucks.
Nice lady, quite funny, but be ready for the workload.  Kind of screwed the whole class on the midterm essay too due to not laying out her expectations very well.  Also, quite the **** liberal.

When you first walk into clas, she seems really intimidating. She kinda stares at you when you talk, and its scary, so she seems like she is mean. But really, she is a softie. She is really nice/caring, and helpful. She will answer any of your questions quickly through email.

I didnt learn much in her class, but it was pretty easy.  Except for her essays.  Make sure when she says a research question is needed that it must be in the form of a question in the essay.  Too much reading too.  Tends to also badmouth conservatives, or presume that her class is of liberals.
easy but being an athlete other than bball did not help me out at all....talks about death alot and is morbid and sarcastic
really smart and always available through email

A GREAT professor.  Knows her stuff, enthusiastic, difficult for anyone to dislike.  Raises great issues in the field of geriatrics.  Highly, highly reccommend, and I'm a science major, not a basketball player.
No Comments
Good teacher

Seriously the sweetest professor! She cares so much about her students and is a pretty easy grader. Her grading can be a little random but its never really anything bad. There's daily homework but it's all easy and more about preparation for class rather than being graded on accuracy. I loved this class with her!!
Super nice and accommodating, has your best interest in mind, not much work outside class besides studying for quizzes and short home works.
Great professor. I really enjoyed this class!
She was incredible, I really enjoyed taking this class and the professor was a major part of it. The group projects were engaging and I had a lot of personal engagement with the topics covered.

rlly sweet. arbitrary grading but lenient if she's knows you're trying. not very good at explaining topics, but i had seen most of the material before so it didn't matter for me. homework every class, but nothing insane.

spanish 301 is a tough class, lots of writing so you definitely have to know your stuff. there were multiple quizzes on grammar and vocab + timed written quizes in class that were basically essays which were tough + homework assignments every class with a ton of writing and the class culminates in a large presentation + essay

Mar is a very nice professor who cares about her students. That being said, most of the learning in the class comes from the textbook and her quizzes are pretty hard. This class if very participation focused and has lots of group projects. If you have her, make sure to study all of the vocabulary!

She's a nice person, but she's not a good teacher. As a native speaker, she doesn't explain the reasoning behind a lot of things because tbh, she doesn't know either! She also doesn't tell you how to write the papers and such until AFTER you submit them, which was annoying. Be ready to participate in class a lot b/c you will lose points otherwise.

Horrible class. Nice person but terrible prof. Lenient but arbitrary grading. Group projects usually random with quick turn around times. Have to learn everything from textbook and then she poorly/quickly explains the concepts afterwards if at all. Never knew exactly what would be on quizzes. Worst class I've taken. Take it with another prof.

This class was not taught well. She is an awesome person and considerate. She's a lenient grader if you show her that you are trying. She doesn't go into depth about specific topics that will be on the quizzes and expects you to learn from the textbook. To truly learn you have to find other resources.
Mar created an extremely welcoming class environment and you can tell that she truly cares about each of her students. This class was so fun to be apart of and there were a lot of group projects.

I think she has good intentions but was not encouraging to students struggling in the class. Judgemental about wrong answers and often told students to learn something after class even if the whole class could benefit. I would not take 203 with this professor if you have any choice, so much busy work and unclear deadlines.

Mar is an incredibly kind person however her class was one of the worst I've ever taken. Deadlines are unclear and are often changed without warning. Concepts aren't actually taught. If you know what's happening your Spanish is too good for 102 and if you're meant to be in 102 you'll have no clue what's going on. Wonderful person, terrible class.

Absolutely LOVED 204 with Mar. I had a weak Spanish foundation and found the course fun. Participation is important; she doesn't mind if you have to look up a word. Pay attention to her feedback on essays & reflections. Course follows a structured pattern; quizzes are based on vocab and grammar. VERY nice, prioritizes learning, grades leniently.

You have to participate a lot, but Mar scolds you if you say something wrong. I was scared to speak in her class because she was so judgmental. She is also (from what I understand) tougher than most 203 teachers, but I don't think I actually learned anything in her class. That said, it's not hard to get a good grade as long as you put in effort.

Mar tries but she is not very good at explaining concepts and is resistant to meeting outside of class. The material itself is not very hard but it is presented in a confusing manner. She is also a very subjective grader and the grading criteria was not always clear so effort and understanding do not always pay off.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Once you get used to Mar, she's great. Tip: participate in class so she'll like you more and grade you better. She likes to correct you in the middle of sentences when you speak in front of the whole class, which feels uncomfy at first, but just tough it up and you'll learn a lot. In the end, she's really cute, especially when she dances on camera.

Profe Mar takes a little bit of time to get used to. I had a very different type of teacher for 203 so it took me some time to adjust to her, but once I did, she's very caring and wants you to learn. She is a little bit more fast paced than other professors, so it's important to utilize the book (especially the reviews at the end!)

Majority of your grade is not based on tests or quizzes, but rather her subjective grading, to which can be advantageous or disadvantageous. But, I think generally, she was tough on grading, and her quizzes were exactly like the review. She can seem a little condescending at times, but I don't think she has any malicious intent. Ask for help anyway
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I really disliked Mar's teaching. She is occasionally very sweet and other times very jarring and seemingly disinterested. I felt like she was not good at all at understanding what the class was feeling or had trouble on. She did a very poor job of explaining answers or teaching concepts. I think most of us relied on studying on our own time.

Mar is super kind and cares about her students. Also a great teacher. Definitely take time to get to know her as it will help in the class. Also make sure to raise your hand a lot because participation matters. Grades a bit harder than other spa102 teachers.

If you have to take Spanish, take it with Hobson. This professor puts up assignments less than 3 hours before they're due and if they're late you receive a 0 even if you did the work beforehand. She doesn't take time to explain concepts well when students don't understand during class. Very rude.

Mar is a lovely human being, but I wouldn't take her again. Her grading is so arbitrary, and it's unclear what she cares about. She'll be strict about something one day and not care about it the next. She's not a fair grader at all and doesn't recognize how much effort you put forth. Make sure you participate A LOT to the point that it's obnoxious
Somebody teach him lectures are supposed to be for us learning somethinf rather than him revising for next semester. ugh

He made me actually enjoy taking linear algebra. His English is a bit hard to understand sometimes, and his lectures can be pretty boring, but he's extremely caring and helpful outside of class and is actually good at explaining when it's 1-on-1. Attendance dips so as long as you show up to class he's very kind and understanding. Recommend!

He is a nice professor, might be hard to understand sometimes, but he is good and knows what he is teaching. And will curve the final exam based on class performance. He will give you additional points for participation, hard work, and improvement from your midterm to final.
Super nice guy. Wasn't sure what to expect from this class, but very pleasantly surprised. He creates a great classroom environment and cares a lot about his students.
total gem of a prof. easiest class I've had. On day 1 said that he'll give everyone an A as long as you do everything. Class is completion basically.

Professor Hong is amazing. He genuinely cares so much about his students and is actually hilarious. He also doesn't go out of his way to make his classes unnecessarily hard.... in fact it was so chill

Hong starts the course by saying grades don't matter. He's hilarious, kind, and always positive. Class requires participation, graded by Canvas discussions, readings/movies, and presentations. Great T-rec class, though content is very heavy/depressing at times. Take this class or anything with Hong!

Professor Hong is one of the most caring professors I have ever had. He is incredibly knowledgable in the content he teaches, and "lectures" involve him freely teaching without the stress of having to memorize every small detail. He is focused on deeper understanding of other cultures, and is extremely effective in achieving this goal.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Prof Hong is an amazing professor, funny and really engaging. Attendance is strictly mandatory, but the content is interesting, so as long as you try to engage in class, you'll be good. Overall easy and fun class, and convinced me to get an AMI certificate.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: This course was fairly easy (for a grad class). Participation is a must and you should make sure to attend all his classes. There is a final paper/project, but if you work closely with him, it will be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: This class was extremely easy. I only spent around 2 hours a week writing the weekly blog posts that we're required to write. Attendance is mandatory, but if you go to class every week and do the bare minimum, you'll get a good grade. The two group projects and the final project were basically graded on completion.

Having no interest in media studies, the class did well to keep me engaged. Prof.Hong's freshmen seminar was gently guided-He allowed us to explore whatever we wanted and never really assigned harsh deadlines. Brought in many highly skilled guests and took us on explorations in Durham. A gem of a professor; just an odd class for 89S. Learned iMovie
His first year seminar on Visual Culture was very easy! Just make sure to go to all the classes and do the work, and you are guaranteed a good grade. He makes the topic very interesting!
amazing prof, really knows his content, a little rambly at times, but very interesting. too bad he doesn't teach more classes. chinese cinema was easy&awesome

Spring 2010 got shafted for this class. We were required to watch 6+ hours of film (instead of 2 hours) and submit a 750 word response each week. Also, there was a 8 page final paper and a group project. Hong demands in-depth film analysis from his students, which typically involve throwing around words such as 'diegiesis' and 'spatiality.'
A nice class to start off the first semester. Prof. Hong can be strict over attendence and participation, but otherwise, he is a very tolerent professor; you'll get an A as long as you make effort.

Prof. Hong was one of the best profs I've ever had.  he inspired me to continue asian film studies!  i just got back from a trip to hong kong, where i felt right at home in the theater.  P-L-U-S the prof is super cute :) which makes class even more fun!  TAKE THIS CLASS!  (the TA was a nazi!  but she's gone now)

While this class was a slight disappointment,we did not really watch films(a few small clips)it was interesting & I would highly reccommend it.Prof Hong is awesome.We had to write 6 2page responses (graded based on if you did it) & 3 projects and one final project.Prof Hong really cares about his students& I would def take another course with him.

Definately an easy class. Met once a week to discuss the readings. There was a weekly 2-pg response paper to the selected readings and 3 group projects which were quite easy. Final project was the topic of your choice and a final paper but it wasn't too bad. Great professor! He was enthusiastic about this course.

Decent class. Good discussion on films/analysis. But readings were often overly lengthy and not too relevant. Grades are assigned solely on weekly responses (so just respond to the movies rather than readings) and midterm/final paper, which are graded leniently. So just do work according to the syllabus for an A/-. TA is somewhat of a Nazi though.

I took ECON 203 with Prof. Gu last semester. Never used the textbook. I listened to her lectures and condensed them into cheat sheets. The final was fair and her lectures were well-taught. Many econ majors aren't numerically inclined and expect an easy A like 201/204. If you put in 20 hours weekly, you do well. Period. Not everything needs a curve.

I don't care if you have to take an 8am or even a 3am DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. makes hard class unnecessarily difficult. absolute GPA destroyer. Zero care for students clearly. No office hours! Insane amount of hw assigned super late. Genuinely considered changing majors. Made me depressed. I'm sorry if you are taking her class :(  praying for you
She made a class named "Linear Regression" unreasonably hard. God have mercy on the next person who ends up having their GPA ruined because of her.

Learned so much more from the TA than the professor. She fails to explain the mathematical concepts behind formulas. In addition to that she never responds to emails. Lectures are only theoretical and not related to the exam in anyway. The TA is of great help. Class would be unbearable without the TA. Don't take this professor unless you have to.

Easier to change majors or transfer schools than endure her wrath. 
She made me depressed and hate econ. 
Hw assigned Thurs and due Sun. Say bye to your wknds and friends! 
The homework had no relation to the lecture content.
Also difficult exams, with the class average being a 40 on the midterm and NO curve. 
Learned more from TA than the prof.
Does not respond to emails, virtually inaccessible outside of class hours.

CLASS WAS HORRIBLE. Gives homework impossible to finish in 2-3 days and only releases them on the weekends. Say goodbye to your weekends. NOT ENOUGH TIME FOR MIDTERM AND FINAL.
