Gives parts a-e for each question and expects you to be done in an hour or less. Don't take this class unless you have to. Made me rethink my major as a whole.

Prof Gu is cramming 28 weeks of Duke Econometrics (two 4-credit classes) in 7 weeks. This isn't out of free-will, and in fact, I think she did a great job. It's one of the toughest UG classes! My recommendation: the lectures may be long, but try listening to her for once in the class, and you'll realize that she's actually a great professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The final exam only tests basic knowledge while emphasizing complex English vocabulary. This is unfair to all students who have studied diligently. We have worked hard all semester, not to determine whose English proficiency is better in the end. English proficiency shouldn't be the purpose of this course. PartA of this final exam can be insulting.
Not so good

She clearly hates teaching. She doesn't reply to questions, ignores your emails, and just has an overall bad attitude. You feel as if you are really bothered just because you asked a simple question. 

It's so bad that you can't avoid her as an economics major.

Econometrics is a hard class (and it will be with any professor). Professor Gu does her best at teaching, exams are hard but fair. 
She may improve a little in terms of answering emails faster, but she is quite good explaining really hard concepts.

God-awful, to be avoided at all costs. Sloppy course design and unwilling to listen to students. Very difficult and long homework that feels utterly useless. Doesn't respond to emails or takes forever. Boring, theoretical lectures without any practical component. Infamously difficult exams. gpa killer fs. Genuinely shockingly horrible.
Her lecture is just sooooooooooooo boring. I learned NOTHING at all.

Teaches core courses on Econ so not avoidable for econ majors. Knows her stuff but exams are exceptionally hard. And lectures are quite boring. Also, she does not grade on a curve so it is hard to get a good grade. DKU should really really hire a senior econ faculty, who knows how to teach the core courses!!! Very inaccessible out side the class.

I LOVED having Prof. Gu as an instructor. Yeah, there are some things to work on, like the insane amount of Aplia assignments or unexpected superhard homework during the last week, but that cannot change the fact that Prof. Gu is an incredible lecturer. She made me genuinely excited to take more Econ classes.
HARD TO COMPREHEND WHAT SHE SAID, HARD EXAM WITH LIMITED TIME

Ming Gu is the worst economics professor I've ever met in my entire life. It always took her days to reply to my emails, and her lectures were insanely puzzling and elusive: everything was purely math instead of economics! Her assignments were very difficult as well. If you're not good at math, this class should be horrible as hell. Very Nice
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Avoid Gu Ming. ECON203 was very difficult and I learned nothing. The homework was very theoretical which when paired with awful lectures, meant I often spent 8-10 hours on each homework assignment. And don't think that Gu Ming is understanding and flexible, she won't respond to your emails or listen to student requests.

She never replies to emails. NEVER! I have learned more about mathematical proofs than I have about real-life model building and analysis using STATA. The homework is not only TOO MUCH but is also useless and of little practicality. It was a very poorly designed course. She is inaccessible outside class and not a good explainer.

Professor Guy is a really caring and inspirational professor, she gives amazing lectures and try to include everyone, she gives clear and good feedback, the workload was okay and she always tries to include field trip in her courses.
Great Professor, very caring and helpful!
Prof Guy is really nice and friendly, she has clear grading criterias and clear curriculums for her classes. Highly rcm her!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: she's great, but her class is a bit hard. maybe she can offer lecture online at the beginner and let us know some of the knowledge before going into deep dive into it. overall, she's decent, and knows her stuff, but kind of doesn't make it understand for students.
Really a good professor! The class is engaging and interesting!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Very very very good prof. caring like a mother of us students. GCHINA101 was a tough experience except getting together with Prof.Guy. Much love.
The most amazing Professor!

Prof Guy supervised my Signature Work (the DKU equivalent of a thesis). Throughout the process, she was supportive and enthusiastic about my work, and made herself available to me whenever I had questions. She gives great feedback. What is most special about Prof Guy is her ability to speak from a position of empathy about the college experience.

Prof Guy is also a very nice Professor. She cared a lot about her remote students and made sure to have us all be as engaged as possible with our classmates. Her classes were also very fun to be a part of but there were a lot of readings. One of the best 2-credit courses I took!

Assigned readings and discussions are very engaging. Group projects are fun and are great way to get use to basic research. Papers are short and are graded fairly. Knows a lot about the subject and loves discussions about seeing things from a different point of view.
Professor Guy was great! Her discussion was interesting and all the students like her. Her grading is fair and she gives good feedback. A professor who really cares about her students!

Peck is genuinely passionate about the content he teaches. He also held exam review sessions, which were very helpful for brainstorming our exam essay prompts. He is very generous with office hours when writing our papers. Guidance is really available to those who seek it.  Listening to lectures carefully is crucial for an A. The best prof ever!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Passionate guy but such an unstructured class. Each lecture was an echo chamber of the same few students talking instead of him actually teaching. Grading criteria never clear & arbitrary based on your TA. Assignment instructions always vague. Every time you reach out for clarification you walk away more confused. Discussion sections are pointless.

I think Professor Peck is extremely caring and means well. However, this class was not very structured as I only received 2 out of 6 grades during the entire semester without explanation as to how my final grade was calculated. The content discussed in class was interesting but sometimes presented arbitrarily.

Professor Peck is a fantastic person to learn research from. He is one of the few professors at Duke who truly respects his students' ideas and will go out of his way to support you. You get back what you put in. If you are willing to engage and be curious you will find yourself talking about the work you did with Prof Peck in every job interview.

Professor Peck is a very inspiring lecturer and he is clearly extremely knowledgable about the topics covered. He can be quite eccentric and it is sometimes difficult to know what aspects will be important to cover in assignments. The final was a 14 page essay in 24 hours. He is a good lecturer but the structure of the class was challenging
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Took this class in F'20. Zoom wasn't great but you could tell how much Peck cared. He accommodated all issues I had and was able to teach me a lot about the history of immigration and its role in American racecraft.

overall a pretty good class and a pretty good prof. lectures are mandatory and a little bit rambly but the content is interesting. super writing/reading heavy. weird prompts too. honestly though you dont have to even do the readings except for the ones that have a writing assignment due
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor Peck is an amazing professor. He truly cares about his students and is very passionate about what he is teaching. Very knowledgeable. Definitely one of my favorite classes at Duke so far. Would definitely recommend taking a class with him.

Peck is the man! He is so cool and genuinely cares about his class. North American Environmental History was the best class I've taken so far at Duke. He really gets you thinking about the topics, and the readings are relevant and very interesting. You'll learn a lot. The papers are work, but they are enjoyable.

Professor Peck is extremely passionate and is very knowledgeable about all things immigration. He can confuse students sometimes and not be super clear, but the class is mostly essay-focused so make sure you're a good writer. Discussions can be awkward and a little intimidating, but Peck is a great guy and is very fair.

Professor Peck is THE BOMB! His lectures are always very interesting and you can tell he is extremely invested in his classes. He is also extremely approachable and willing to help students. The class had a lot of work in terms of readings, but most of the time they were interesting and painless. Great teacher!!!

Professor Peck is a very genuine and caring professor. He is very into environmental history, and he helps make it relatable for his students. There is a lot of reading but it is definitely worth it. I think that seminars may be more his style than lectures, but it was still an interesting class.

This class (PPS 116) was great. Peck really does well to discuss topics that are interesting and pertinent. Class is entirely based on 2-4 page essays; re-writes are available for a higher grade. No exams. Peck wants his students to succeed and is happy to help with writing assignments and course content. Take his class!
Great professor. More than helpful, especially when I was struggling with a lack of sources with one of the papers.

I LOVED this course, though-warning-there was a lot of reading. I highly recommend for anyone interested in the environment; it's a different perspective on how we arrived where we are and will definitely get you to think (if you let it). In-class discussions were always interesting and engaging.

Professor Peck's environmental history class is extremely interesting. More philosophical in nature than you would expect, you cover a wide breadth of topics including food production, industrialization, among others. Highly recommended.

You may not realize the benefit of Peck's class until after you graduate, but I promise you will long for the discussions and material you covered in this class. Few professors care as much about their students and their course as Peck. If you're down with nature, food, and the wilderness ethic, you'll love his course.

This professor rocks.  His enthusiasm is infectious and he really helped me uncover a better understanding of my relationship with my environment.  I highly recommend this class from a wonderfully helpful professor.  Definitely one of the best classes I've taken so far at Duke. And one of the best History classes I've heard of.

I honestly don't know why  Peck only has a so-so face on RMP. Before, I never gave much thought to ethics, but after the enlightening/complex discussions & comment writing I improved my debate, writing, and thinking skills. This is what pubpol classes SHOULD do,  and most don't do it as well as Peck. And really, the workload is not that demanding.

Engaging professor. The requirements laid out in the syllabus are quite confusing and demanding. It was very difficult to get all the work in on time. Leads a good discussion except the topics can be very bland at times, then again I wasn't too interested in ethics.
Very intelligent guy...doesn't respond to emails and sometimes his requirements are unclear...a LOT of reading...often takes over discussions to input his opinion

Interesting professor.  Great for 116!  He has good set up for the ethics course, and facilitates great discussions.  However, in environmental history, he can be a BIT preachy and requires a larger amount of reading (200pgs per week) than is necessary.
****her is a dude.  He's really chill and though a little philosophical for some, knows his****.  Strongly suggest him for environmental hist or pub pol 116.  the man

Prof. Peck is awesome! I have no idea what these people are talking about, but my class with has been awesome.  He has interesting lectures and his class one of the best I have ever taken.  I have never learned so much.  If you are interested in the environment, take a class with him.  Such a great guy, I recommend him to anyone.
Had a good time in this class.  Would take him again.

very nice and intelligent guy; however, not a great profess, did not make it clear what he wanted in class papers and the TA's were useless; topics were interesting but discussions could have been more intense and better organized

Professor Peck is one of the most caring professors @ Duke. The material is scattered and jumps from topic to topic, but that is necessary to prevent boredom. He really values discussion so you have to come to class and do the readings.  But he is fair. TAs do the grading, which can go either way.
The readings and discussions for this class are wonderful and interesting; however, the organization of the class is something that could definitely be worked on.
Does not take alternate points of view well- very liberal and biased in discussion/grading.
Interesting material but he kind of killed it. Class is boring and unless you say what he's looking for, you're dead.  He also takes attendence.

I really enjoyed the class, the professor was very reasonable, he listened to all the students worries and tried to make the class better for everyone to understand. However, I feel we covered a lot of material and some parts were superficial. But overall he is a really good professor and tries his best to teach the course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dynamic Earth and Oceans should be 2 different courses, yet another instance where DKU's 7 week sessions do not work. Considering this, Prof Gu makes it work as much as possible. Lectures can feel long and dense but he adds cool videos and polls. For exams he is generous with cheatsheets. The group project is environmentally cute and graded fairly.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. Gu always comes to class well-prepared. Though he may not be the most energetic, I find him very effective in his lectures. He's crystal clear in communicating. He adds spice to the usual by showing documentary-type videos, using polls and viewing Google Earth Pro now and then. He is also approachable outside class.

I love Professor Green! The concepts aren't very difficult (especially if you've taken AP Gov) and he makes lectures fun. Reading quizzes every class, but you can bring in notes you took on the readings. Some essay prompts can be challenging, but he grades fairly.

This class is almost an exact replica of AP Gov. Lectures were sometimes boring but also sometimes had new and interesting information. Reading quizzes every class, but these are open book and doable. Three essays and received good feedback. Hard to do bad in this class. Dr. Green puts a lot of thought into his work and is a great professor.

Really good professor, class material is relevant and interesting. Attendance is technically not mandatory but you have to attend because participation and discussion is very important to your grade. Be prepared to participate. Cares about his students and is understanding.

242 is entirely discussion based – no lectures and all readings done outside of class. 150+ pages of reading each week, but you eventually learn to read it efficiently. Green is incredibly insightful and covers course content well. 70% of grade is based on 3 memos and final group presentation. Definitely attend office hours before writing memos.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Amazing class and professor - super passionate. Although attendance isn't graded, you have to show up. Heavily discussion-based.

Professor Green did an excellent job teaching POLSCI116D. His lectures were clear, organized, and informative. The class was the perfect introduction to Political Science, so it is a must-take for anyone considering the major. You'll learn a lot. And you'll be happy you took it with Professor Green! Highly recommend!
The best. Love him with all my heart.

Prof. Green is fantastic! He is incredibly knowledgeable about campaigns & the class discussions were always lively and engaging. He assigns a lot of reading and the response memos are graded harshly (but fairly). Go to office hours BEFORE you write your memo - it will improve your grade immensely. Attendance and participation matters.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Green is very kind and cares about his students. The campaigns class is very discussion-based so make sure that works for you before signing up. The class would have been better with more Professor instruction on the readings, but overall it was not difficult and Professor Green was nice.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Grade is based only on tests: 3 midterms and a final. If you don't self study like hell, you'll be even more lost than if you went to the lectures expecting to learn. He seems like a nice dude, but he definitely can't explain new concepts, especially if it's new or unfamiliar. The lectures are often irrelevant and tests are difficult. Don't do it
Just don't do it to yourself... It is not worth it...

Entire class is based on 3 midterms and a final. The first midterm is only based on the first week of content, which based on the rest of the class is far too easy. The next 2 midterms are incredibly difficult to learn the necessary material. The final has problems and material that was never covered in the class or any practice exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Grange is an okayish instructor. Unfortunately, you'll have to self-study everything because the lectures are not relevant. Very tough exams but grading is a bit lenient.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's an intelligent guy, but should NOT be teaching 100's level classes. In MATH101 class, I was expecting to learn without having had any prior experience. However, he conducted the class under the assumption that everyone already KNOWS calc. He taught calculus WITH CALCULUS. Do not take if it's your first time taking/learning calc.

Prof. Grange is a competent lecturer that knows how to explain concepts well and make connections between them. However, beware that the lectures are proof-heavy, and for some, it may seem tedious and useless. He also grades exams quite leniently (my actual exam scores would exceed my expected grades by more than 20 points sometimes).

Dr. Pascal Grange is knowledgeable and inspirational, with academic and industry experience. Getready to be challenged in lectures and not to understand certain details in his formulations during the lecture itself; however, Dr. Grange helps address your concerns during/ after the lecture, and he is especially caring during office hours.

I'm in his lecture now. He just spent 40 minutes proving/explaining some nonsense. I 100% believe  everyone in this classroom understood nothing. I recommend everyone only come to the recitation since the TA is so good.
Teach nothing

Very nice and knowledgable guy but horrible at teaching. Will basically just solve problems on the board the whole class as if he was alone. I self taught most of the content. 3 midterms and final make up your grade. He is a very fair grader and will give partial credit for reasoning.
Awful, like a demon resurrected from hell to torture me.       Extra: obsessed with his formulas (often traps us with that).       Overall: bruh, plz, be a human not a demon

Pascal is very nice, but unequivocally slow and obsessive about formalization and notations. He will often take a whole class to prove something tangentially related to the course or to do one problem. However, he is a very easy grader, and will give often give you full points for your "reasoning" although your numerical answer may be incorrect.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Not accessible, gives no examples, grades only based on exams, unhelpful lectures. Only take if you already know the material bc u won't learn it in this class.
Only exams, no hw

Lecture material often does not remotely resemble what you will see on exams. If you ask him a question you will likely get a 35 minute lecture on something completely random, probably out of inability to explain certain mathematical concepts as he is a neuroscientist not a mathematician. Grades are also 100% exams- nothing else.
Prof. Grange's lectures were quite confusing and did not prepare us for the test. His grading criteria and feedback were very vague too.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The lectures are totally unclear. The final exam is hard.  a lot of writing in homework, and you should notate every single stuff to get the max point. "Do not consider this an essential part of your knowledge of Calculus; it is just a nice exercise."  after 2 hours spending time on the exersice
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Do not take this professor. Pascal was condescending, consistently unhelpful, refused to answer questions, etc. He did not teach anything; just did proofs and expected us to understand. Practice problems were more proofs. He spent a week on notation rather than teaching us what we need to know for future math classes. Very stressful overall.

MATH 105 was so stressful that I cried multiple times during the course. Professor Grange was unapproachable and had high expectations for the class. The grading criteria were never clearly outlined until Week 5. I had to self-study the ENTIRE CLASS for fear of confusion by asking Professor Grange for assistance. TAKE "IF YOU'RE SMART ENOUGH"
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Grant sent a bunch of weird cryptic emails at the start of the semester. Seems to think everybody has it out to cheat in lab. He doesn't do sections though, so just pray you get a good TA and prepare to be spending up to 3+ hours on postlab reports

don't let the reviews scare you its not the best class but its doable and besides the molecular modeling lab most of the online assignments only take 1-2 hours so its not a huge workload. the lab reports are pretty unclear in what they want sometimes and it takes a bit to figure them out but honestly it all comes down to your TA

Calvin Grant was not really kind, and he could have done more to ensure a stable class. Lab reports and online labs were tedious; be prepared to spend over the said amount on them. The entirety of this class was disorganized. I had a really good TA, though, and I'd say it really comes down to that.

dr grant is very passive aggressive. never saw him a single time but he sent out many passive aggressive emails at the beginning of the semester. the class itself is a lot of work. labs are 3 hours long and post labs take forever. there are also online labs during off weeks. all the grading is done by TAs.
Very unforgiving and never once showed up to my section. Instructions provided are vague and poorly written. Your grade lies in your TA's hands, just hope you get a lenient one.

hes the worst most unforgiving professor i have ever had. he literally wants you to do poorly and fail. he is so mean and the TAs do all the work he showed up to lab one time for two seconds and thats all he did. genuinely felt like he wanted us to fail.
Super angry grrrr

Grant's chem lab at Duke needs to be revamped if not abolished. This so-called "0.25" credit class is nothing short of a full credit course. 4 hours in lab every week + 4 hours MINIMUM on post-labs, which are subjectively graded with obscure rubrics. Also useless for the actual class. Literally chinese water torture--long, painful, and pointless.

It's meant to be 3 hours in lab and 1 hour post-lab but you'd be lucky to spend less than 4 hours on a post-lab report, not to mention the online labs that were 6+ hours of work. The due dates are very oddly structured and the post-labs were often confusing. You don't choose but prepare yourself. Unrelated, but don't have A. Sheinberg as your TA.

The labs were manageable, however, I often asked my TA questions about procedures. The most difficult part was the post-labs. The directions were unclear, the questions were very difficult and I often used outside resources to both understand the question and answer them. Lab reports took more than 4 hours each week. Lots of pre-lab assignments.

I WOULD NEVER RECOMMEND DR.GRANT TO ANYONE!! NOT EVEN MY WORST NEMESIS. He is the worst professor I have ever encountered. He is not considerate let alone caring for his students. The TAs do all the work and your grade lies in their hands. Dr. Grant does not respond to emails and is so inconsiderate. NEVER! DON'T MAKE THIS MISTAKE!!!

Had a terrible time dealing with Calvin Grant. Unresponsive, unkind, and not empathetic at all. Understand that his lab course is required as a part of Chem101, but do not expect any lenience or empathy. Or a response, tbh.

I feel bad rating Dr. Grant low because he genuinely seems really nice, but this lab is awful. Treats 0.25 credit lab like a full class. Lab report instructions are incredibly vague and then graded on nit-picky details. Labs on content not even REMOTELY covered in class.

An amazing professor who truly wants to see her students succeed! A great instructor who cares about the topic and can teach in fluent Italian, while also helping her students understand what she is saying, and assisting them to learn. Would 100% have Prof. Granacki again!

Alyssa was an incredible professor. She was helpful, always answered my questions, and had the best interests of her students. At the same time, the class was a lot of work, my Italian improved thanks to excellent instruction. I would definitely take another Italian class with Prof. Granacki.

Professor Granacki is very nice. The class has a lot of readings, but I usually skimmed them the night before and did fine in class. She told us to try to speak at least twice in class, so that was my benchmark. The portfolio entries are the main component and don't have to be very long. Good and interesting class.
there are a lot of readings every week and you should be prepared for it. The readings are very challenging and takes you a lot of time. Overall good class.

Professor Granacki is generally a super nice prof, but doesn't always know how to explain topics clearly. The Italian program generally has a high workload and since this was her first time teaching this class she didn't always know what was going on. However I still greatly improved my Italian in her class and overall really enjoyed it

I highly recommend Professor Granacki! The workload is reasonable with reading and a few short writing assignments. She was very flexible and clearly passionate and knowledgeable about the topics we discussed.

Dr. Granacki is amazing and I definitely recommend taking a course with her! She's an easy grader, and just wants to see her students learn. Not too much work (other than reading) outside of class, and she was very flexible with what little we did have to make sure no one was drowning in assignments and readings! Super fair, very kind, love her!

This professor is completely unsupportive. I took BME 504, and during office hours he often refused to answer my questions, saying “I already covered this in class, don't waste my time.” His lectures are terrible, never clearly explains definitions. The exams are extremely difficult, with questions that were never discussed in class.

Dr. Grill puts his lecture slides up on Sakai before class, but they're not detailed enough that you can skip class and rely solely on reviewing slides. Expect lab every week (either a computational MATLAB simulation lab or a wet lab usually involving dissection) with a full report each week and weekly homework assignments.
Excellent professor. Hands down best at Duke BME. One of the very few profs that are both a great researcher and a great teacher.

Hands down best professor Ive had at Duke. Lectures are amazing, and as a leader in both teaching and research within his field, there is a ton to learn from him. Class is sort of tough, but if you give it a good effort, its manageable.
Great lecturer and professor. He explained all the concepts in depth and made sure to cover each topic thoroughly for students to understand the material well.

Excellent lecturer, he makes the material very interesting and clearly knows what he is talking about. He encourages class participation especially, and it was actually a factor in our grade. His exams are completely unforgiving though and will be very tough. Homework was also quite difficult without TA help.
arrogant sob. good lecturer but a f'ed up person.

Fantastic lecturing. Material is hard though, but exams arent much harder than homework. And the textbook is abysmal, though that isnt grill's fault. definitely take his class. he doesnt curve but funnily enough the mean is always about 80 i.e. doesnt need a curve. ive heard von ramm or malkin are much worse.

The subject of this class is extremely hard, but Dr. Grill did a really good job of explaining the material. Even though he's a great teacher, it's still very very hard to do well.  I would recommend him as a teacher, but don't expect the class to be easy in the least even with a great teacher like Grill.

Grill is a spectacular lecturer. Lectures are invaluable, the book is alright, but can be dense. I have heard that he can be unfair and or arrogant about partial credit/regrades, but that is the extent to which I have heard negative comments about him. Otherwise, I can safely say one of the best profs I've had at Duke.

This professor lectures clearly, but is a terrible person at heart.  He is of no help in office hours, and goes on vacation during test weeks.  After a test has been graded, he absolutely refuses to reconsider, even when he acknowledges your grade as unfair.  Overall a very arrogant individual, and definitely one to avoid.

hard class hard tests.  tests arent very representative of hw at all.  he doesnt care about students grades and will cause alot of ppl to fail/almost fail etc.  he claimed that he curves the class but in the end doesnt and screwed alot of people over.  other than that, hes a good lecturer.  my advice is to understand the material very well

Dr. Grill was one of the few professors I had in the engineering department who was both an exceptional researcher and an exceptional teacher.  I admit his class was challenging, but it was very well taught.  If you want to take easy classes you shouldn't be in BME at Duke anyway!  My advice is to take any class you can with Dr. Grill.

BME101 is interesting but Dr. Grill just didn't teach it right.  I feel that the class really suffered for not having a reliable resource available. (be that printed lecture notes or a good text)  All knowledge had to be gleaned from lecture and if I didn't get it the first time around I found it very difficult to get help.

Dr. Grill is a great teacher and  if you go to class you will know how to do all of the problems on his tests.  He hardly ever used the textbook therefore if you take him GO TO CLASS. also, the labs are tons of matlab simulations and the TAs sometimes grade harshly.  dr. grill is a very nice guy and actually cares about teaching (rare in bme).

BME 101 is one of the most interesting classes, but Professor Grill was in my opinion a bad professor. He was unapproachable at times. His tests were much harder than homework and way too long. Further, when asked to consider questions after a test he would not listen and was often rude. He grades tests poorly. During lectures he could be funny.

I strongly disagree with the previous negative comment - that student obviously bombed a test or the entire class, but certainly by no fault of Dr. Grill's.  Grill is a charismatic brilliant professor who relates complicated material extremely well.  Highly reccomended.
Very good professor. Uses clear examples in class. Helpful outside of class and seems to really care about the class.

I've heard the class really isn't that hard when taught by other professors, but Dr. Grill was a terrible teacher. He hardly went through examples in class and the homework problems were MUCH easier than the test questions. He definitely made a simple intro class much more difficult than it should have been. He's just a bad teacher.

You can't bring prepared answers to the exam anymore, but you can bring two pages of notes. A lot of the time there was too much reading for me to finish before class, but the lectures were great so I was able to understand everything anyways.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Test heavy

reviews.comment: Unfortunately a great example of a famous academic who doesn't care about teaching. He knows Marx inside and out, and is good at explaining complex topics, but is incredibly disorganized and doesn't really have grading criteria to speak of.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Hardt is very nice. 90% of the grade is made up of exams, which don't have very clear grading. However, he provides a decent amount of feedback and allows for answers to be prepared beforehand and brought into the exam.

100% made me a much, much better writer and person. he gave me extensions upon extensions when I was ill and protesting at universities and staying at encampments. but he grades very fairly---not to stress you out but to truly make you a good writer. I will miss him so very much.

Michael genuinely cares about getting his students to understand Marx and political economy -- the readings are occasionally dense, but he's able to clearly explain difficult concepts through classroom discussion. You can prepare answers for exams ahead of time and he is accessible outside of class. Made me want to wake up at 8:30 to go to class!

This class was so fun. I actually looked forward to going to certain lectures. You don't have to do the readings - just pay attention in class and you'll be fine. He is really nice and accommodating. I learned so much about Marxism and I was able to tie concepts into my other classes too!

He's a really amazing lecturer and the content is fascinating. He explains everything well so you dont need a background in Marxism. Lots of readings and three exams but you can prepare entirely beforehand so thats really awesome. Gives great feedback on the exams and doesn't grade too harshly. Overall awesome professor, I'd highly recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Easy-going and very nice. expected to learn a lot but his classes were not well-organized. He seems to rely heavily on students' discussion can't answer students' questions very well...Grading is very much about how much you say in class, not whether you're really hard-working or not For papers, very quick feedback but the suggestions helps little.

The lectures are very great but as someone with background in social science I wouldn't say that its "life-changing". It's a very well-paced class and definitely engaging. Basically you read, Michael talks about the readings, and you write essays on topics discussed. You can basically prepare for all the essay exams beforehand so that's really nice
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Michael is a great lecturer, makes Marx's works very clear, and is passionate about what he is teaching. Tests are a bit difficult if you haven't done the readings or paid attention in class, but certainly not impossible. Hardt also cares a lot about students and cares more about the content than grades. I'd definitely take this class!

Marxism and Society is the best class I have taken at Duke. I had no prior knowledge of marxism, but Dr. Hardt is an expert in the material and makes even the most complicated philosophical concepts easy to understand. Exams are composed of a few essay-style questions and are manageable as long as you attend lectures and review sessions.

Marxism & Society might be more theoretical than expected, as Michael is more interested in theories than real-world examples. Long, dense readings, but Michael dissects and explains clearly, which is very helpful in understanding. There are 3 exams, on which you have to write 3 essays on concepts in readings, but this can be prepared beforehand.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He is really interested in the class material and knowledgeable, however his lectures tend to be non-engaging and drawn out.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Great professor with interesting discussion. Sometimes can get off topic and confused, but I learned a lot about social movements. He's very caring about his students and what they're learning.

He knew all of our names (50+ people) by the second class. He's brilliant, passionate, and cares about teaching. Classic philosopher who takes forever to make it through a sentence. Clear grading criteria, sensitive to students, and really interesting material. Don't pass up the opportunity to take his class.

A decade later, Hardt still remembers my name, agreed to meet me for coffee with the same enthusiasm and willingness to share thoughts as before.  What I learned in class has shaped my attitudes toward taking ownership of my labor and broadened my definition of love and understanding of existing social structures . For those who think deeply.

One of the most intelligent professors I've had. Took his global protest class and the front in was a little theory heavy but he's a good guy and very passionate about the material. Has written several books on the topic and is an expert in the field.
He cares about your learning,  goes out of his way to help and clarify difficult concepts, very knowledgeable and humble. He is one of the best professors in Duke.
Abysmal teacher who assigns readings that are unclear, pretentious, and obscure.  Still thinks it's cool to be a Marxist, and analyzes everything through this lens.  This class is a waste of time.

Marxism and Society has been a good class. Professor Hardt is really nice and I would recommend taking a course with him at some point during your time at Duke. He really makes his students think, but does not pressure people to participate. I was also impressed that in a class of 40 or so students, he learned all of our names by the second week.
The best professor I had at Duke!
Very spacey, loses his train of thought a lot, thinks out loud too much. Nice guy but his teaching style is frustrating. Would not say he is one of the best professors I have had at Duke.
hot

I took this course fully expecting to learn a lot, but have to put up with a small-minded political ideologue.  What a surprise.  Hardt is genial, funny, unpretentious--and brilliant.  He's an expert in his field, and a great guy to boot.  A real wonder.  It's a shame the class is so big, though.

Hardt is the most interesting person here at duke. his ideas are original and thoghut provoking, his down-to-earth socialist perspectives makes class a learning experience not a regime. Readings are relevant to everything in life, you will come out with a different, more polished view on so much.

the marxism readings were dense-lecture was usually helpful in clarifying. he can ramble and  not make sense but the review sessions and having open note tests made up for it. overall a very interesting course. he's an important figure in lit and political theory, also quite nice to look at

Thinks he's Engels.  Knows Antonio Negri.  Is really nice and lets you take your time with exams.  Is really cute when he tries to be authoritarian.  But doesn't contradict anything and doesn't tell the morons in class that they are morons.

Taking a graduate special topics course with harry is an excellent opportunity. He has a thorough understanding of the material and is eager to answer questions related to it. Be sure to come prepared for class to get the most out of lectures.
Brings snacks. No curve but lenient grading. A smart guy who knows his stuff. Good teaching too.

Very funny and caring professor. Really enjoys students engaging with the lecture and asking questions, and will often bring candy for those who show up. Provides practice exams that are reflective of actual exams. Very accessible outside of class through Zoom and email to answer questions.
An amazing professor who is always there to help. Supports students well and gives great practice tests which make it easy to prepare for exams.
Topics can be tricky, but you get a lot of repetition throughout the course. A super nice professor, always brings good chocolate to eat at the end of class.

Dr. Wang truly cares about his students and wants them to gain a deep understanding of the material. Tests are difficult but he allows test corrections and wants all his students to do well. Highly recommend taking this class with him.

Amazing professor. Truly cares about the content and makes himself available outside of class so that all students may succeed. Gave us doughnuts on the last day of lecture and held additional review sessions before exams.

Pickford is clearly very knowledgeable and also a really interesting person. He has high expectations of students for a first-year constellation class. Frequent readings that were often confusing and assignments that are graded arbitrarily (no rubric, unclear instructions). But class discussions were thought-provoking, as he is super well read.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Hard class, but very glad I took it. Pickford definitely equipped me with a new lens for viewing the world. Don't take if you're not ready to dedicate yourself to the class. Pickford is tough but clearly cares about learning and his students.

He is a pretty nice and fascinating person when you get to know him. His course for the FOCUS program was definitely too hard, and he does not have a rubric for any assignment (feels like he's grading off vibes). Overall, I enjoyed the experience and made some trauma bond friends through the course

Pickford knows how to select good readings, and his tests can actually be pretty enjoyable because he allows for a lot of creativity and he is interesting in reading your ideas. The material can be tough, but you will become smarter through taking his course because you train yourself in thinking.

Sets an amazing basis for Philosophy class. Honestly should be taken by anyone, regardless of major, as three of the most important thinkers of all time are discussed in the class. The professor is easily accessible and genuinely interested in teaching and learning more.
I did an Independent Study with him on Late Wittgenstein. Overall he's a very knowledgeable and accessible professor who provides great feedback.

Sets an amazing foundation for philosophy/literature courses. Very strongly recommend for those interested in philosophy, literature, psychoanalysis, critical theory, etc. The course also provides strong foundations for writing philosophy papers. If you do the readings and go to office hours you will be fine. Slightly more difficult than average.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Prof. Pickford is an excellent professor. His Marx Nietzsche Freud class is essential for anyone working in the humanities and social sciences. Tough class with lots of reading but worthwhile if you decide to care.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Absolutely terrible. Such an excessive amount of reading for a 200-level philosophy course. Posts hours of lectures each week, constantly making the content harder than it needs to be. Unless you're in love with Marx/Nietzsche/Freud's work, stay far away.

Henry is a great professor who really cares about his students. He fosters a classroom atmosphere that encourages discussion and he's great at explaining material, especially in response to student questions. Also does a great job of making himself available outside of class, if you ever want to discuss a paper or even just chat with him a bit.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Really enjoyed this class! Pickford's a great lecturer and the materials were engaging. Readings can be a lot but you should do them if you have time.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He is really nice and into the material but makes you read like 500 pages per week and then just re reads it in class. Material is very hard and he doesn't really help your understanding. He's a great guy and very accommodating but the material was so boring. Would not recommended unless you are like OBSESSED with German philosophy or something.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: I took a seminar with Professor Pickford last spring, and it was one of my favorite classes. He's a very intelligent guy who really knows his material. Gives great feedback on essays, but is a generous grader who is accessible outside of class for extra help. Only caveat is he's a little spacey, so make sure to remind him about any meetings.

Amazing lecturer. So, so smart and very approachable outside of class. Really takes time and effort to grade your papers and presents thought-provoking alternatives to your arguments. Genuinely fascinated by the material he teaches, which feeds into his students.
Take the class if you care about philosophy/literature, and you'll learn a lot.

He's a good professor and he genuinely cares about how well his students do. Very knowledgeable on his subject, always there for office hours. Gives great advice on essays, but isn't specific enough on homework corrections. You'll learn a lot & the class is super useful. His teaching style takes some getting used to, but his class is worth taking.
Professor He is both kind and understanding. She was always really chill about people being out of it or slightly late since our class was at 8:30.

He Laoshi is so sweet, caring, and understanding. She makes an effort to make the class as fun and engaging as possible. I learned so much in Chinese 101 and 102 with her! While the course itself isn't too difficult and is graded generously, there is daily homework with short quizzes twice a week, so it can be time-consuming.
He Laoshi is very kind, and teaches the class very well. I only do bad in the course because I am stupid. There also is a lot of homework and 2 weekly quizzes which can get to be a lot.
The absolute sweetest and very caring and lenient. Expect a decent amount of readings and to be called on in class. Very interactive, and chooses interesting topics for us to read about.

loved her! chinese class structure helps buffer your grade, so if you do the hw (which there is a lot of) on time, you will have a great buffer for the exams. really kind. took me a bit to keep up w/her speed in chinese, but she's really understanding that not all have the same experience. flexible w/students who communicate their circumstances

He laoshi is a great professor. She can be intimidating because she talks pretty fast, but she's very nice even if you don't know what's going on. You will get called on every class but it'll really help you learn. Quizzes twice a week but you get used to it and they're nothing crazy.

Starting Chinese is hard no matter what so the Profs give you plenty of practice through daily homework and quizzes 2x a week. Professor He is understanding, funny, and a great teacher. Her and another prof teach 101 and 102 together and they're both amazing. Would definitely recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She was amazing! I was the only non-native speaker in a class of 4. She was very helpful and motivated. I often feel some language professors just know the language and got a education degree, but Prof. He really studied the language and knows how to teach it effectively. She also knows the content is tough, and broke it up with fun activities.

Quizzes twice weekly in discussion, daily writing homework (writing characters). Great professor. She teaches well. You don't have to know a single word of Chinese to take this and do well. Make sure to go to lecture: you have to because it's part of the grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Prof He is pretty funny and a good lecturer. The class is hard no matter who is teaching it, but she does a good job of keeping students engaged. There is a ton of homework and there are quizzes twice a week, so studying is pretty necessary. Once finishing the class, I felt confident for 102.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Love it! Learned a lot about classical Chinese without much busy work. Class environment was close & fun (only 6 students). I also loved Prof He. She's very understanding and lovely, and is very flexible. The lecture was just VERY long (once/wk), and we have a vocab quiz every time. Work is doable, and most HW/writing assignments can be typed out.

Great Chinese 101 professor. Kind of jumps right into Chinese the first week which seemed scary but allowed us to adjust quickly and teach us a lot. Expect a lot of cold calling to answer questions. Definitely cool foreign language teacher, but easily the most amount of work of all my classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He laoshi is a fantastic teacher and really makes sure you understand whats going on. The class is A LOT of work (multiple quizzes, homeworks, essays, recordings a week) but you'll be shocked at how much Chinese you'll learn in just a semester. One of the best classes I've taken at Duke.

He Laoshi is an amazing professor. She is super helpful and wants her students to succeed. That said, this class is a lot of work and requires the student to stay on top of their studies. If you work hard and study for the review tests, this class turns out to be not that bad.

There is a constant stream of assignments, quizzes, and exams to keep up with throughout the semester, but He Laoshi is a very caring professor who will go the extra mile to help her students. She always allowed me to stay an extra hour after exams to finish. Keep up with the work and ask for help when you need it, and you will pass the class!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--Caring

reviews.comment: He laoshi is an amazing professor. Her classes are always engaging and she always explains concepts well. Although this class definitely requires participation and practicing outside of class, I'm amazed by how much Chinese I've learned in just one semester and how much fun it is to learn!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: There will be nightly homework and a weekly writing assignment (about a paragraph long). He Laoshi is very funny and engaged with her students. She loves when you speak Chinese, but don't be afraid to speak English if you don't know the Chinese words. Still, the effort to use what you've learned is always appreciated. Would recommend to my friends!
moves quickly but the class is very interactive and fun. my fav class of the semester.
I've had the best semesters in Chinese with He Laoshi. She's very helpful, funny and will make you love 101/2 despite having to meet everyday of the week.
Great teacher and always ready to help, but chinese will become one of your hardest classes and you will be doing it every single day.

Learning a new language is hard, especially Chinese, but He Laoshi made the transition so much easier. Expect lots of work - written quizzes twice a week, oral quiz once a week, and graded homework three times a week. But the amount of Chinese I learned in the past semester (with zero background) was impressive.
A lot of work, but its really not that hard. In general Duke Chinese dept. is pretty easy on students.
Very nice lady who is always willing to help out students. Chinese 101 is straightforward and not too hard.

I love He Laoshi.  She is hilarious.  I was really nervous about tackling a new language, but she made it a really great experience.  She cares about her students and encourages you to get to know her outside of class.

He Laoshi is absolutely fantastic. She's hilarious, and cares deeply about each and every one of her students. After having her for Chinese 101 and 102, I'm very upset that she only teachers first year Chinese.

He Laoshi is the best.  She is so funny and encouraging.  She practically begs us to come to her office hours because she wants to get to know all of us individually.  She really goes the extra mile to reach out to us. Awesome class.  Learned so much.

He Laoshi is really encouraging and makes a very comfortable class atmosphere to practice speaking Chinese. There are small daily homework assignments that aren't that bad, and tests and dictations are fairly easy. Overall the class is pretty straightforward, just make sure to not fall behind in homework.
She is both helpful and nice. I learned a lot in her class

He laoshi is really nice and completely willing to help you outside of class. she is really invested in her students success and if you put in the effort in class, she will put in the effort as well. she is a great teacher, but chinese at duke is HARD and very fast paced. there are 2 quizzes a week and tons of homework

Good class, great teacher. She encourages speaking in class, tries to make sure you understand. A lot of characters to keep up with but that is the nature of the class. Highly recommended- you will learn a lot!
She's amazing.  Very patient and clear-- I learned sooo much in one semester.  Way better than any of the other profs.

He Laoshi is awesome! Unlike some Chinese professors here, she won't make you intimidated to speak in class, fearful of making any mistakes. She is very friendly and always helpful. She has a sense of humor and really relates to her students! Take Chinese from He Laoshi!
omg! a chinese prof w/ a sence of humor! He is soooo helpful and friendly. best chinese prof in the department
Very helpful, clear, and effective. If you want to learn Chinese, take it from He laoshi.

Look, is this class easy? No. But Healy is a genius (seriously look him up online, he's kind of famous). This class actually taught me more than any other social studies class I've taken at Duke, so there's that...

I really enjoyed this class and have no clue how Prof. Healy doesn't have high ratings on this site. Super approachable, helpful, and accomodating guy. I learned a lot in this class but never felt stressed. Highly recommend a class with Prof. Healy.

DON'T DO IT! Only Duke professor who has made me feel bad for advocating for myself and trying to learn. The TA grades everything harshly and with little feedback - I went to the professor about it, and he did not express much interest in helping me. He's knowledgable, but lectures are confusing and he'll belittle you when you don't know something.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Good professor, make sure you read though.
He puts in absolutely no effort. In terms of learning, he's the worst professor I've had at Duke.
AVOID AT ALL COSTS. Incapable of teaching anything. Doesn't take a single question during class just mumbles while showing incredibly useless slides and then assigns insane homeworks.

He is very knowledgeable, but his lectures can be boring at times. Not responsive to emails, and not helpful outside of class. Lots of reading and weekly writing. Grading Schema is unclear, and your grade will mostly come from the TA with exception of the final. Rubric for final was vague and you are graded very strictly and unfairly.

This class was very easy with very little work, and I found the content to be an interesting intro to data visualization and programming with R. Professor Healy was knowledgable and I found him very funny and accessible. The only thing bringing him down was that his lectures could be a bit dull and fast. (This class was pass/fail due to covid)
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Not the most interesting class but you will learn how to program in R. Healy is a nice professor and is flexible about assignments. Would recommend if you would like a teacher to help you with basic R programming but if you have experience already, you probably won't get much from this class.

No clear grading criteria. Does not provide study guide/materials for the final. Does not post lecture slides. Does not reply student's emails. Very difficult to follow. By the end of the course it's difficult to tell is something/or anything has been learned.
Okay lecturer, but speaks very fast and not too audible, with a slight accent. Not very accessible and does not really make clear grading criteria
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: He's a decent guy with an easy class. Lectures are pretty decent and interesting. Discussion sections with the TA were my favorite.
Learned nothing valuable the entire semester. You have to go to class to do daily tophat quizzes. After the quiz, I basically just sat on my phone and took notes when he switched slides.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Staying awake during his lectures is VERY hard. He makes no sense when he talks and has so many tangents it's ridiculous. I walk out of the class learning nothing. He seems like a chill dude though. Quiz every lecture so you have to show up, but if you left after them you'd be fine. Discussion is cool sometimes. Very easy, barely any work class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Interesting guy who talks about interesting topics. However, he tends to ramble on and it's hard to tell what you actually need to know. Grading isn't super clear but I ended up with an A. He isn't generally too available for students to meet, however. You'll need to catch him either before or after class. Really smart guy.

Dr. Healy is really charismatic, but sometimes his lectures move too quickly and it can be hard to tell what is important for notes and what isn't needed.  Very difficult to get the material if you miss a lecture.  Kind of intimidating, the TAs said he's so smart they are afraid of him.  But his Irish accent makes everything sound more interesting

He's funny. Obviously intro Soc isn't super inspiring, it's all pretty intuitive. Just show up and listen and you'll get an A. No midterms- just a final, quizzes and easy discussion assignments. Final questions were all old quiz questions.

not really sure how I stand in terms of grades since there is only a final and daily quizzes. Interesting person, interesting lectures. The one thing I have a problem with is the lack of organization and clarity in his lectures. Sometimes he talks very quickly and at the end I wonder what the main point was. Tophat sucks.
grading is very arbitrary, not willing to meet with students, does not make you feel like you can succeed

Actually, she is not that bad. Go to office hour and talk to her about the assignment requirement, try hard to meet the requirements, and you will get a high grade. The grade may be between 80 and 98, depending on how well you have done. So, she is not a so-called tough grader. Do EVERYTHING she asked to do, and you will be fine.
Escape plz. Boring class, crazy professor, heavy readings, unhelpful assignment instructions
Attention please! Don't choose this professor for a high GPA!

I want to say that she is a good professor and if you want to learn something more, she is a good choice. However, if you want to get a high grade, don't choose this professor. What's more, her workload can drive you mad.

Professor Hiller is a responsible and caring professor who teaches English for Academic Purposes. She always has her courses well-prepared and gives clear instructions for every assignment. I would recommend her without a doubt!

very nice guy who clearly cares about students and is very knowledgeable. The class once a week for 2.5 hours at nights is pretty rough and gets boring but he tries to make it more interesting. Had a group project and midterm + final with weekly reflections that are pretty light

The professor with the biggest heart at Duke. Such a GOOD person, cares about his students beyond class, really wants you to succeed in life. Super approachable. That being said the class itself is super easy and kind of boring. The in class activities are interesting but the content is so easy it is boring. Participation grading is tough.

Hicks is a really nice and caring teacher. Content is too easy for a college course which makes it boring. Grading for the project and homeworks is easy, tests are all multiple choice, and even though the content is somewhat common sense, a lot of the answers make sense so you actually have to study. Harsher grader than expected for participation.

Steve Hicks is a great professor! Slightly different format from the old MMS197 class, as it includes two exams, a presentation,  and class participation but is an easy class and Hicks is a great professor who cares about you as an individual.

Prof. Hicks was a solid professor. The class was fairly easy, but he made it interesting every time. The timing (late at night for 2.5 hours) was difficult at times, but he gave ample breaks and tried to keep us active.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Good teacher but Harsh Grading Policy.

I've loved all of my professors at Duke except this one. He's rude, poor at explaining his slides, doesn't answer questions well, has inconsistent and unclear grading policies, and was difficult to reach outside of class. This is an important class so it's unfortunate that so many students have had such negative experiences with this professor.

Although the class was stressful, I learned a lot. The lack of partial credit was stressful. Take advantage of Dr. Massoud's and TA's office hours. He is always willing to help. He is also very nice and has cool stories. Stay on top of your work, pay attention in lecture, go to office hours, and don't be afraid to ask questions. Write good code too

Professor Massoud was the worst professor I've ever had. He expects students to already know the material, making it difficult to learn new concepts. He was inaccessible when I needed help, and his refusal to give partial credit led to poor midterm scores. Even after seeking help from other professors, my performance still suffered.

Horrible man. Lectures were just him reading a word-heavy slideshow that you cant follow. No partial credit. So many people go 0-10% on one of the midterms that he got mad at US and scheduled another midterm in 3 days. For an intro class, he expects you to already know all the material. Don't take this class with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Massoud's class is extremely difficult. He offers no partial credit on tests that make up a large portion of your grade. While meant to be a lesson on real-world problem solving, it makes the grading very stressful and unforgiving. Otherwise, Massoud is very knowledgeable and willing to work with you extensively outside of class.

Caring and approachable. Liked him overall. Too many bad comments from students pissed off from bad grades. He teaches you what being an engineer means through his grading style as well as his personal life stories. Students should ask him more questions, he is always happy to answer.
Edit, for whoever taking it: Do textbook problems Do textbook problems Do textbook problems

Taking this class with little/no previous knowledge about circuits and circuit theorems is a challenge. If you want to do well attend lectures, practice problems from the textbook, and go to office hours. Lectures are wordy slides but include key information. Massoud makes himself very accessible and that should be taken advantage of.

Do not take this course if you are not a text-based learner. Lectures are very text-heavy, and he reads off the slides most of the time. Often gets off-topic during lectures. 
Be prepared to learn most of the material outside class. 
Midterms are open note, but no partial credit at all. 
Overall, not a good class, very stressful and confusing.

One of the worst classes I have ever taken. He doesn't give partial credit and will ruin your life. He doesn't teach the material and reads word for word from the slides without any actual explanations. For an intro class, he expects you to know a lot. Avoid at all costs!!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: A lot of students scored bad on a midterm, so instead of going over the midterm, he scheduled another one 2 days in advance to "force us to study." This speaks to his stubbornness in his old school teaching style (reading slides verbatim) and refusing to give any partial credit (resulting in poor scores). Please don't take this class.

Got almost 100's on my two midterms and a B- at the end, because there is no partial credit. Also, one question is usually 20 or 25 points. 

His lectures consist of him reading through his slides and nothing else.

If you give him a question he will solve it using an answer key. Sometimes he gets the equation wrong and the answer correct.

Awful.

ECE110. Lectures are unclear while he goes off on lots of unrelated tangents. When he does use his slides, they are full of paragraphs and equations that he reads word for word without much explanation. Gives no partial credit on tests and doesn't follow the same structure as other profs, which makes the topics in lab different from in class.

Took ECE110 with Massoud and he goes off on tangents and also reads word for word from slideshows without explaining much. Expects you to have lots more prior knowledge than an intro level class. Gives zero partial credit and uses questions from the textbook for the exams and exams are open note.

Dr. Massoud is incredibly knowledgeable on just about everything. Lectures and notes are insanely comprehensive. Assignments are challenging, but he regularly holds office hours.  Exams require code scripts to run equations and there is no partial credit on assignments, but he does allow corrections. He will make you a better person and engineer!

Teaches from dense but exhaustive lecture notes. Super organized. Embodies old-school ethos, but he really cares about teaching and makes himself super accessible to students. Tests are as challenging as the homework. Makes you write Python/Matlab scripts to use on homeworks and exams.
One of those hard-but-informative classes that you take to learn in rather than boost your GPA.

Extremely tough grader. Lectures are very confusing as he briefly goes through hundreds of equations without actually explaining what they mean. Makes you pay $200 for an unhelpful textbook that he created (wonder what his profit margin is?) Incorporates parts of ece331 because he believes it should be mandatory. All it does is makes you bad
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Massoud is a top dog in microelectronics, be aware that he is one of the most valuable resources in the entire industry as he teaches your class. The textbook was meh, don't look at it. The key to success in this class is writing every single equation in his lecture notes into a matlab script with input variables ACCURATELY.

Extremely knowledgable and friendly! His approach to making a super dense subject into a logical and interesting one is fantastic. I don't think I'd ever understand how electrons and holes danced around inside MOSFETs without Dr. Massoud. If you're into semiconductor devices and you're lucky enough to be at Duke - TAKE HIS CLASS!
Awesome teacher.

Massoud is very knowledgeable and is very approachable than given credit. Doing well  involves engaging with the material and asking questions throughout the WHOLE semester, not just right before an exam or after having bombed one. You will learn in his class if you put in the effort, and realize that its more than just memorizing equations.

Massoud makes an easy subject very difficult. He drones on for an hour and 15 minutes reading long equations off of his slides, but never explains what they mean. The classwork mostly covers 40 year old technology, and the homework is very computationally heavy. Unless you absolutely have to take 331 with him, find another class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Only take this class if you really want to be an electrical engineer. He treats it like the real world, hates it if you skip class, can't use computer/phone in class, homework is 20+ hours a week, labs are awful.   but if you want to be an ee then he's great  I don't
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Learning in this class was extremely limited, most people left without the knowledge of what a transistor is but a ton of memorized equations. Tests were graded without partial credit and homework problems were difficult.

He is a brilliant guy who accomplished great things at one point; however, would not recommend taking this class with him. Lectures are difficult to follow/unhelpful, tests are difficult and there is no partial credit. Grading criteria is unclear other than he replaces your course grade w your final grade if it's better. Take someone else for 230.

Massoud is probably my favorite teacher in the ECE department. Extremely knowledgeable guy who is always there to help and explain. The subject matter is difficult, and so are his exams, but if you work hard you can expect a good grade in the end. Also, go to class. Even if it doesn't seem to help, it will.

If you're in this class for the learning, you will not leave disappointed! Massoud is an absolute expert in his field and explains even the most difficult concepts with great clarity. If you're in this class as a requirement, you may be frustrated by his binary grading at some point or another.

Massoud is intimidating in the classroom, but really nice and helpful if you see him in his office. The lecture notes cover everything you need to know. As long as you have MATLAB scripts written, you'll be fine in this class. It takes a bit to get used to his binary grading style though.
He is excellent! He can give perfect answers to any question. His physics is so good and make the extremely difficult part to be pretty easy

Dr. Massoud was amazing! He really cares about whether you learn the material, which is why he encourages questions and has open office hours WHENEVER you need help. He provides great notes and teaches well. Only problems were that the class had much work, it was hard to know how you were doing (grade-wise), and he can be intimidating.

I was very disappointed with Professor Massoud.  First and foremost, he seems to have no regard for grades.  He grades tests almost arbitrarily, subtracting 5 points for the tiniest errors.  He has no course grading standard that he follows, so students have no idea how different parts of their grade wil be weighted.  Also, he's too condescending!
Dr. Massoud is a GREAT prof...he is SO helpful in and outside of class...his lecture notes r crystal clear and he is just an all around great guy!!
Extremely knowledgeable and wise professor, helpful after hours, and knows the answer to every question. Great teacher!

One of the best professors I have had at Duke...Immensely helpful. One can drop by his office hour anytime...He will spend hours with you and make sure you get the point. Very friendly. The class is kinda dry because of the content but  he tries his best to make it an interesting class..overall a great professor and a great grader!

lectures are dry, but then again how can they not be. the class setup is strange, can't say i like or dislike it.  it's pretty much one huge lab. massoud is pretty amazing intellectually, just not the best lecturer.
Extremely dull, boring lectures. Has unreal expectations. Very poor communication about assignments and such.
Great lecturer and overall professor.  Homeworks can sometimes be challenging and vague.  Book for the course is not the best choice.  Tests are usually reasonable if they are take-home.
Fairest system for grading students. Gives you the grade on the final for the semester if its better than your performance for the year.
I felt like I learned some useful skills.  It required some effort, but completely doable and she prepared you for what you had to do.

Hillygus's Public Opinion class is a class that all Political Science majors should take. It was the perfect balance of interesting and not difficult. I learned so much about surveys, got to conduct my own research, and never felt overwhelmed. It was intellectually stimulating and practical. Highly recommend. She is also very renowned in the field.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Super awesome teacher! Clearly wants all of her students to do well and so gives very clear instructions for assignments/midterm. I think the class was super interesting and makes you rethink stuff you see on the news. She's also an expert in surveys, like worked in the Census Bureau, and would talk about lawsuits she worked on about surveys.

Really nice teacher who grades leniently. We had one exam, which was super straightforward. She made it clear that the class was going to be about survey methods during the first week, so I don't get the complaint in the comment below... 201 is a useful class to take and an A is attainable with minimal effort. Recommend taking any class with her.
Great class. she is extremely smart and clear with her expectations for tests and assignments. Everything she finds important is covered in class and the lectures are helpful and fairly engaging

Hillygus is really respected in the field and she definitely knows what she's talking about. Gives out a point of extra credit if you spend an hour on a research thing which is really nice. Would definitely recommend

Took in her in BIO89S (aka the first year seminar). Was sweet and cared about students, but a tough grader and not the most supportive/understanding when it came to being sick or technical difficulties. Not a hard class, but definitely more work than other intro seminars.

I LOVED Alison Hill & Bio 201. The quizzes are easy if you do the practice exams and pay attention in lecture. She gave us a ton of resources to prepare for tests. The only downside I have about this class is not directly related to her, but make sure that you come to your lab section promptly (otherwise they take an automatic 33% from your grade).

Flipped classroom = waste of time & singlehandedly ruined bio for me. Exams were too difficult and depended heavily on prior bio experience. Dr. Hill's 'in-class' problem solving was even more of a time waste. She seemed to care abt students, but was all over the place as a professor and simply was not it. V poor class/prof for a key pre-med req

the format of recorded lectures was unhelpful. spent first class giving us a lecture about why lectures are bad. Uses recorded modules from years ago and often forgets what topics she covers in them, frequently makes basic mistakes during lecture, like confusing which nucleotides pair with which. wastes class time instead of helping us learn

Flipped classroom was terrible. Needlessly defended the teaching style despite lack of rigorous evidence for its superiority. Multiple true false exam questions were unnecessarily challenging. Didn't know how to prepare for exams, open note was used as an excuse for an extremely wide scope of content. Also, this class didn't need 3 professors.

Dr. Hill is the best professor I've had at Duke. She is passionate and the most caring prof. I got a C on a quiz & contacted her afterwards. She walked me through the whole quiz & then proceeded to email & talk to me consistently for the rest of the semester checking on me. Flip classroom is actually good for me because I'm a slow visual learner.
Absolutely not a fan of the flipped classroom. I loved biology in high school but this course was incredibly dry and uninteresting, and her recorded lectures were not at all engaging.

I really do not like flipped classroom formats and it turns Bio201 into a boring experience. I enjoyed molecular biology before this class but it really removed the joy out of it. Class is underrated in difficulty, and Dr. Hill is a very average professor. Amazing how such a great subject becomes a chore with harsh grading and boring lectures.

The class is taught in a way that is opposite to what we are seeking out at a university like Duke. This class aims to trick you and make you take the long route (not the smart route) at every step of the way. You will learn a lot, but dont expect your grade to reflect your learning. Tests are 20 Questions but every question is a 5q true or fals

Had Prof. Hill for Bio 201 - I don't think it would be hard class no matter who was teaching, but her explanations were solid, and because TAs are dispersed throughout the class you can always ask them for help if something is unclear in lecture.

Great choice for clearly delivering information effectively; she clearly knows what she's doing, where students get confused, & what to do about it.
