Dr. Hogan is a good teacher, but the ridiculous amount of busywork and micromanaging of participation/studying/reading made for a poor experience. I'd only recommend taking the class with Dr. Hogan if you're a first-semester freshman who needs that kind of hyper-structured environment.

0/10 class. Busywork which does not help you in the slightest way possible. Labs are way longer than they should be and quizzes are too hard (though they are a small part of your grade). Midterms are MCQ mostly and relatively accessible but the lectures are so boring and she tracks attendance through in class questions. Again, do not recommend.
Class was fun, and she is a good teacher. But can be very passive-aggressive. Didn't love her as a person, but enjoyed the class and understood her teaching.

The content is very interesting & applicable to research. However, the course structure is poor, the labs are too long, and your experience (and grade) are dependent on your TA. The lectures are tedious, especially with the mandatory attendance, and the multi-select quiz/test questions are annoying since it's not clarified which qs are multi-select

Great teacher overall. Quizzes and Exams are very similar to practice problems during lecture. Only criticism I have is of the Learning Catalytics software used during class (where if you don't notice and answer a question being put up, you lose some attendance points for the day).

Interesting course content, but sometimes lectures were boring or sped through quickly. Lecture is taught by several, which I didn't like. Quizzes are generally harder than exams, and there's quite a bit of hw. I liked how there were many opportunities to drop a low grade, including an exam. Lab experience is pretty dependent on the TA.

As a bio major, I found the class content interesting. There is a fair amount of hw, but it reinforces your learning during class. In my opinion, the quizzes were always harder than the exam. The class is quite flexible, with a hw's, a quiz, and an exam grade dropped. While the teaching style may be annoying at times, I definitely learned a lot.

COMPREHENSIVE: Not as bad as other reviews depict. Hogan is a fine lecturer, but lectures are usually divided between her and another teacher. Mandatory attendance is very annoying and the lectures are hit-or-miss. Make sure to utilize all class resources. Midterms: average, quizzes: harder. Labs are interesting but too long. Overall, meh.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: The course material wasn't particularly difficult, but the lectures were heavily focused on application-based questions, which often left me feeling like I had gaps in my understanding. The exams are select all that apply formats without indicating how many answers are correct. Not the best class structure to effectively learn bio.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Everything about this class comes across as a tedious trial rather than an opportunity to learn.

This class is absurd. Hogan is very monotone and there's no point in going to lecture because it is a snooze fest. She thinks assigning groups and seats will prevent cheating or something but it just makes being in her classroom miserable. Learning catalytics is also useless because I filled them out from my dorm room.

It's hilarious how bad this class is and the professor. She's just a negative nelly tbh and feels so judgy. I asked her a question one time and I could tell she was just wondering why the sky is blue or something. She doesn't care about her students and sits there when Schreve is teaching like a tiger mom waiting for her child to mess up.

They hold your hand so much in this class it felt like middle school. 2.5 hour labs that could have been done in 30 minutes if they didn't stop you every 10 minutes to go through a slideshow. So much busy work (prelab, postlab, grq, mastering) that it piles up for no reason. not to mention the 30+ staff watching your back during lecture everyday.

She is just not a nice person. Rude and condescending for no reason. I was studying her face one time during a quiz and her jaw was clenched and her fists were balled like us students were the bane of her existence. There are 25 undergraduate learning TAs and I couldn't tell you the name of one. Everything about this class is extra for no reason

she made a fun and simple class HARD for NO reason at all... exams & quizzes were WAY harder this semester (spring 2025) compared to fall 2024 (why?!?). LOTS of unnecessary busy work, mandatory attendance, BUT very clear grading criteria. lab is not bad at all, just very long... make sure u stay consistent with your studying if u forgot AP bio
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This class felt incredibly infantilizing. The assigned seats, the teaching team's rude attitudes, the amount of busy work, the learning catalytics... It was all very high school. The class content is not too difficult if you took AP Bio, if you haven't you will need to study a lot.

Decently structured class with fair grading across multiple items. Participation/attendance matters in lecture, and Dr. Hogan herself was a pretty clear lecturer anyways. Slides were super helpful to prep for quizzes and exams. Lab was probably the worst part as they were unnecessarily long and often boring. Just put in effort and it will be fine

The material isn't difficult, it's a lot of content. If you go to class, you'll be fine. The homework is a lot of busy work and Hogan always says she's not trying to confuse you on quizzes/exams...that's a lie. Regardless, the class is fine just keep up with the work. In my opinion, Hogan is a very engaging professor, but she seems condescending.

She's not great - quizzes are intended to trick you, attendance policy was pretty annoying, & there's an enormous amount of busywork that's irrelevant to the tests. The assigned seating policy was absurd & she treats students like they're toddlers. Finished labs in ~30 mins & just sat there for the other 2 hrs. Doable, but a waste of time.

Exam and quizzes are too hard and written to trick you. Every question is multiselect. Expects you to have taken AP biology or some other robust biology preparation. Assigned seating randomly 1/3 of way through course completely disturbed any learning dynamics that were established among students in first third. Very Condescending.

Exam and quizzes are extremely hard and written to trick you because every question is multiselect. Expects you to have taken AP biology or some other robust biology preparation. Assigned seating randomly 1/3 of way through course completely disturbed any learning dynamics that were established among students in first third. Very Condescending.

Yes, Kelly treats you like you are a kindergartener, but she is a good professor. Her lectures clearly explain the topics and the amount of busy work forces you to learn the topics. The busywork also helps with grade cushioning. I only used her slideshows to study for tests, and I did fine. The tests are about content covered in class. Lab sucks.

Tests are extremely tricky and feel like you're reading a brain twister. Focus on GRQ's and slides, and honestly if there's a way you can take it at the Marine Lab or abroad it will probably be more fun.

Yes, this class is a lot of work and the tests and quizzes are tricky but genuinely, you will be fine. All the exams/quizzes/tests are doable, and you can do well in this class. It is not impossible. Professor Hogan sets the class up so that you actually learn. The few times I have spoke to her, she was very helpful and kind.

The class was very boring, but attendance was tracked. I would not recommend taking any class with her. The tests are also made to trick you; all multiple choice questions have anywhere from 1 to 4 correct answers, and you won't be told if multiple answers are correct.

So much busy work. Her attitude was bad and she seemed like she didn't even want to be there half the time. The HW assignments are a waste of time, and the tests are designed to trip you up. I wouldn't have taken this class if I didn't need to for my major.

Not a very nice person overall, lecture is pretty useless. Very condescending and just a little weird overall. Labs, while interesting, are pretty useless for the amount of time spent. Overall everything is cookie cutter until it is time for the quiz.

Bio 201 is one of the most useless classes at Duke. Hogan is pretty condescending. Lectures are absolutely useless and the class is just a ton of busywork–if you took AP Bio, you will learn nothing here. And don't even get me started on the 3 hour labs. But all premeds have to take this class. Just why.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: the class was OK but i really believe the homework/having lectures 3x a week class was VERY unnecessary...filled busy work, the content of the class forces you to stay on top of the work, so expect to put at least 8-10 hours for the course. it is not that hard, it's just application based so they try to make it hard for no reason at all...

She acts like her students are children. 20 year old college students don't need their professor to give them topics to talk to each other about. The course is extremely time consuming and the quizzes contain much more than what's taught in class.

She was personally very condescending to me and I found our assigned lecture seats very juvenile. The class has no business being three times a week and if you have high school bio experience you will breeze through. Not a kind person and gave way too much busy work. Lab is cool but long. The quiz/exam schedule really keeps you on top of it, though

This class is much more application-based but had less memorization than my AP Bio. Pay attention to class examples and practice questions, and textbook/Mastering Bio content are irrelevant. Lab is also fair game for tests which are very short and all multiple choice. This class is made for everyone and is easy to succeed in with minimal effort.

Well-structured, way too much busy work for HW. Believes in redundancy so lectures are disengaging. Labs are tedious, but my TA was fabulous (s/o Rachel). Exams are easy, mainly MCQ. Take the class, but wasn't the most effective way to learn molecular bio -- felt like very surface level content/no depth. Will be a BREEZE if you have taken AP Bio.

Very passionate about the subject; course is well-structured with lots of additional resources. Course is mainly designed for students without a background in AP Bio, so homework and lab assignments often feel tedious.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Hogan is a fine teacher, though sometimes the in-class participation feature gets annoying. The class material is very easy, and the exams and quizzes are fair.

The class is set up so that you learn material beforehand and are expected to come to each lecture prepared. Tons of busy work and 5 quizzes + 3 midterms through the semester. You're also assigned to a group that you're expected to sit with through the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Hogan as a person and lecturer is great; it is very apparent that she cares about her students and and wants them to learn and not just memorize. The class felt a little bit bogged down with assignments that ended up feeling like busywork. There are so many opportunities to drop grades on HW/quizzes/attendance/midterms, which was clutch.

Dr. Hogan is a great professor! Her style of teaching requires outside textbook reading, and what you learn for homework is reinforced during lecture. You will not have to cram for the exams. She is always providing practice questions that require critical thinking, which leaves you well-prepared for the test questions (and the MCAT, too).
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment:
The class is like a "flipped" setup- you teach yourself from an overpriced e-textbook and deal with busywork hws. If I'm doing all the teaching and learning myself, why am I paying so much tuition to take this class?
The lab is a drag; we do THE SIMPLEST tasks but get stuck there waste your three hours everyweek without learning anything from it.

Attendance was mandatory but moved so slow, most learning done before class with ridiculous amounts of busywork. She definitely cares but makes a lot of work mandatory when it should be optional. Hard quizzes and easy exams. Lots of lowest grades dropped and clear grading policies. I think she would be better in an upper level elective.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Woah... I'm shocked to not find some complaints here. She's a nice person but her class was outstandingly difficult. I spent hours/night on HW, a week studying for exams, & STILL did poorly. Just barely got an A that I worked my ass off for - relied on boosts. Also ran a flipped classroom & never explicitly said that (you do all learning outside).

Dr. Hogan is the best! Her lecture style makes it so that you aren't just listening to her talk and go through slides, you read and teach yourself ahead of time and then practice in class which is really effective - never feels like you are cramming or memorizing. Can drop lowest midterm of 3 and tests are not bad if you go to class.
Dr. Hogan is great! The class is a great intro to Biology but feels very slow and easy for those who took AP Bio in high school.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: one of the best physics professors at Duke. really well organized and knows what's up. it's a shame I bombed the final

Hazel is great! Definitely take a class with her. She is well organized - all lecture notes, homework, announcements were on time and clear. Each lecture began with a review of previous topics which was so helpful. She was excited to present material. Homework was interesting, not just plug n' chug. Review before each lecture and read the textbook.

Hzael is one of the best physics professors I've interacted with. The course itself is challenging, but she makes very clear on each concept and derivations, and she's open to questions after/during class. I learned a lot from her lecture. The lectures are also very clearly strucured and carefully planned.

Hazel is clearly an expert in the field. P-sets and exams were rather challenging, but not unfairly, given the tough content. Lots of material covered made lectures feel somewhat heavy or rushed, but Hazel encourages/answers questions generously. She adeptly connects textbook, lecture, and exam. Great course-enriching lab. Much work, much learning.
will not suggest taking a class with him
Extremely awkward that takes away from clarity of instruction. Wouldn't recommend. Grading was a blackbox and arbitrary boundaries applied at the end.

Hughes is a great professor really kind and really willing to meet you where you need it. The class itself is hard and while he does grade forgivingly it can definitely feel like a struggle. Overall I would highly recommend taking a class with him.
Very nice guy and good lecturer. Gives a lot of extensions. Recommended.

The beginning lectures were a bit confusing for someone with little linear algebra experience as it dives into hyperplanes and other concepts without much background, but the latter half of the course was very smooth. The tests are extremely fair and the homeworks can be a bit long.
Hughes is really nice, the content of 221 itself is rather difficult but take advantage of office hours and you should be okay.

Good lecturer, goes pretty slow but makes linear algebra more or less approachable for those with less experience. more rigor could help since it doesn't prepare super well for harder classes like 401/501 or 431/531.

Prof. Hughes is young, passionate, and very nice. I learned most of the content in class without the textbook. He actively seeks class feedback to improve, responds to emails quickly. Homework is reasonable, extensions are generous. Exams were very easy (finished final 1 hour early, full score), but I wish they were more rigorous as a proof course…

James is so nice and sweet and very willing to help students succeed. However, he is inexperienced in teaching so sometimes he might struggle when explaining concepts. Prepared to spend a lot of time self-studying outside of classes if you are new to Math. Tests are relatively doable.
Amazing professor. Extremely responsive to questions outside of class and conveys information well. MATH221 would have been so much worse without him. One of the nicest people you will come across.
230 may be a tough-to-grasp class, but Hughes is very to the point. The HW is always representative of the class and exams. In the event of lower-than-expected grades he will curve as needed.

A little dry and sometimes flustered in class but does everything a professor needs to do well, and is responsive both online and to student opinions about changes in difficulty or content. This class does just about double in difficulty over a few weeks from extremely easy to somewhat easy

Prof. Hughes is a kind professor. He tries his best to make sure that everyone is doing well and understands the concepts taught in lectures. He is willing to help as much as he can and I have yet to see this in other Duke faculty. He is a generous grader: he curves his exams. His homework is also very representative of what you learn in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Cares a lot about his students, gives extensions, VERY responsive on forums/emails/office hours. Attendance was part of the grade but you could miss some classes and work with people on homework for credit. Midterms are very fair (same type of questions as examples in class). Homework is a bit harder, but amazing class. My favorite class so far.

Professor Hughes is incredibly sweet and means well, but he is not very good at explaining the material and often seems flustered in class. He is very generous with partial credit, but the midterms often get curved down. Expect to learn most of the content on your own time, outside of lecture.

Professor Huo is absolutely amazing! I learned so much from him, and his class made me truly interested in math. There is a decent amount of work required, but as long as you pay attention in lectures and go to his office hour, you will survive for sure.

I can't recommend his class enough. Despite getting a very low grade, his class forced me to learn the contents and I got a much better grade on a later retake. Prof. Huo is a truly caring professor and his lectures are very clear and well designed. Very accessible during office hours, he tutored me until he was sure I understood the contents. Kind
Good lectures and the content are clear, but a tough grader
Too difficult to get half the mark of exams. Make me regret choosing mathematics as my major.
Terrible grader. Arbitrary reduction of grades in homework. Very stingy about curves. Go through theorems and proofs super fast. No time to digest. Would not recommend.
Too many homeworks. Boring lectures. There is NO NEED to go to the lecture. Just open YouTube and search "calculus".
Math105 is a VERY hard class, but Zhengui Hou is imo a good choice. He doesn't curve but isn't a tough grader either. His exams though are hard, but he teaches pretty well and cares a bit.

Professor Huo is a really great teacher!! Despite my grade, I have learned so much from him. He provides lecture notes and is really caring if you approach him outside of class. There is a lot of homework problems per week (85-98), and there are quizzes every week, so truly be prepared. The exams are quite difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Huo was a very caring professor who was accessible outside of class. The content of lectures was a lot, but he was willing to further explain if needed during office hours. The homework was a lot, but the professor would offer extensions to the class if it was evident the homework was too much.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof. Huo is a really nice person and his lectures are helpful, but the class is just too much content to cover in 7 weeks. Homework is over 100 questions per week. His exams/quizzes were fair. Overall not a fun class but I think he is a solid choice to teach it.
The best Chinese teacher! She's super nice and explains very well. Highly recommend her for any level Chinese. Learned so much and was very fun.

I literally just created an account for my Chinese instructor because her teaching skills are nothing short of exquisite! She goes the extra mile to explain terms and their nuances in a way that's incredibly accessible for non-native speakers. Her classes are an absolute joy to attend, making the learning experience both effective and enjoyable.
Probably the best 201 Chinese teacher at DKU! She is very caring and is good at teaching, everyone I know who's had her loves her!
Hui Yao is a great teacher! She is super nice and her class was really fun!

Hui Yao is super accommodating to students and she's very comforting. If you pronounce something wrong or say something wrong, she is able to correct you in a polite way instead of making you feel dumb.  She also wakes up at crazy times (4am) to teach, which shows her dedication.
Yao Laoshi is very friendly and outgoing. She does not grade too harshly and tries her best to accommodate all students. I would highly recommend her!

Prof Hussain's Freshman Seminar at Princeton, American Identity at a Crossroads, was my favorite course freshman year! He is a devils advocate, promotes respectful civil discourse from all viewpoints, and introduced me to many fundamental texts in oppression and power dynamics in American history. Field trips to boxing match and NBA were awesome.

Professor Hussain nails it — connecting sports development and game changers to major societal shifts through Bourdieu, Weber, and de Tocqueville. He fires up critical thinking, cracks jokes, and actually welcomes debate from both the left and right. Best class I've taken.

Engaging trips were great; Durham Bulls, Duke vs UNC WBB, NC Courage etc.

Professor Hussain makes lectures super engaging with interesting stories, relevant discussions on influential athletes, and great jokes. The class is fun and insightful, with field trips that bring topics to life. Grading is based on a final paper, presentation, and participation. Highly recommend if you're into sports, media, or culture!
Would not take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Hussain is available to meet outside class to discuss your papers (we had two in a semester) and will often challenge students to explore ideas from different perspectives. In his own words, he seeks to provide "the best possible counterargument" no matter the side taken by a student, which I found both engaging and enlightening.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Genuinely one of the best professors I've ever had. If you're taking the class to genuinely learn, you will gain a ton. He cares for his students as well and makes sure every one has what they need to succeed.

Knowledgable professor who relays information well. He is cognizant of other classes giving work and is extremely flexible with classwork and homework. Class is primarily made up of discussion and it is a good way to practice sharing your perspectives. Discussions are always interesting and are very relevant. Great professor and a great class!

HANDS DOWN THE BEST PROFESSOR AT DUKE! Truly one of a kind, and a professor that you will cherish for life. I highly recommend Prof. Hussain as he is super flexible and will teach you life skills that no one else will at Duke. I went through a journey of enlightenment with Prof. Hussain. Highly recommend any class with him.

Extremely knowledgeable professor who never fails to keep the class engaged. He is aware of workload from other classes and doesn't assign ton of work, and the course is structured well. The class provokes deep thought, improves communication skills, and forces you (in a good way) to listen/debate to views you may disagree with. Great prof!
Very poor class-organization and very poor content.

Prof. Wang is a great teacher who clearly cares a lot about what she is teaching. You won't be allowed to use any technology during class which is inconvenient at times but her classes are very engaging and she gives extensive feedback on essays. Some parts of her class are quirky(Friday 6pm due dates) but she as a professor is excellent.

Professor Wang is very understanding. While the course content itself can be a bit boring at times (which I believe is mainly because of the nature of the cc3 rather than the professor's teaching), the professor tries their best to make it engaging. Grades started off lower but improved steadily, so don't worry too much if you struggle at first.

Prof. Hwa Yeong Wang is truly knowledgeable and professional in her area and has wonderful insights on the intersection of Confucianism and Feminism. It's very rare for professors to offer a systematic lecturing without losing significant details in a 7-week session, so it should be understandable she also has high standards on students.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She does not allow you to use any electronic equipment in class, you can not even use your laptop to take notes. She stares at you every time. When she thinks you are not listening carefully, she will directly call your name and ask your questions. She is really a hard grader, she gives the lowest score among all CC3 professors. RUN!!! RUN!!!RUN!!!

No phone and limited laptop use. Lecture heavy and everything is focused on reading discussions. The 2.5 class is like: lecture on reading, discussion for 5min, and then sharing insights, repeat. It is so suffocating I feel like im sent to jail for ten years. Harsh grader. Always find new perspectives to torture you with your essay, trouble-maker
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment:
Prof Hwayeong Wang, Ph.D. may seem friendly initially, yet she graded lower than all other class by half to one letter grade lower. 
- Disallows phones or laptops during class. With the exception of readings.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: PHIL115 - She is definitely well-educated on this topic. However, don't take this course unless you could handle 60+ page readings in one week for 6 weeks, response papers each worth 10% and a final paper worth 50% of your final grade. The workload for this single 2-credit course took up more of my time than my other 6-credit courses combined.

Professor knows the material very well, and is incredibly passionate about it. As this class is also HIST101, there was a histoical aspect to it, but discussions and philosophical discourse prevailed. She provieds a lot of context to the philosophers, slides are clear and analytical. I will take one of the classes she designs! She's very caring!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Genuine, nice, and caring prof. He focuses on the understanding of how to solve problems intuitively & big picture of all the main theorems of how they're interconnected. He cares about his class if he sees everyone struggling with a topic he accommodates his students.
Underrated professor. Overall good lecturer, and a manageable course.

Very nice prof. He genuinely wants students to succeed and as a physics major I'd definitely recommend him to others, he really helps you understand everything even the difficult concepts. Good at teaching the big picture of physics and applications. Derivation-heavy tests, no actual calculations.

One of the worse profs in the whole school. The math he teaches is beyond what is required by prereqs. He does not upload annotated slides or recordings, despite his whole lectures being written during class time. Spent 40+ hrs on hw alone. Not supportive at all. No extra credit ever. 4 question midterm and no partial credit

I had to take physics because of being a stem major but NOT a physics major. Hwang wasn't the worst, his lectures were very animated and sometimes had cool demonstrations. Lectures did NOT align with lab at all, making lab reports difficult and time-consuming. The midterm only covered the first 2 weeks of class, making the final terribly difficult.

He does not offer recordings at all. In the second half of Physics 121, we learn about the oscillations and waves. Professor Hwang approaches this topic in a mathematical perspective. There are so many mathematical derivations. Even in this case, we do not have recordings and even course slides. His notes are very messy. His exams are so difficult.

Professor Hwang is very caring. His short lecture recordings made Physics 121 enjoyable despite it being online. Sometimes, I would struggle to understand his accent, but overall his explanations are very good making the class very enjoyable.
He is so caring and helpful to his students. Very knowledgable and open to new ideas and discussion. You will learn what you put into the class. One of my favorite professors!

Professor Kim is one of the most thoughtful professors I have ever encountered. He really promotes an atmosphere focused on learning rather than focusing on the grades. It's much more about the process, at least to him. This is refreshing and I would highly recommend his North Korea class.

Hwansoo is such a nice guy and basically only gives out A's (he said that himself). This class (North Korea) has weekly readings that are very interesting. What you learn in this class, you will learn in the readings and in Hwansoo's initial lecture section, because the class discussions are usually useless. He cares a lot about his students!

Prof. Kim is a gem. He engages all students in thrilling conversations and allows, if not enables, tangents. He respects students so much that everyone feels like they have a voice to which should be listened. The discussion environment he creates is unparalleled. He assigns good readings too but the class is all about discussion. Go to class!

I took this class just to get my CE credit, but it was so interesting! Despite having to take bus to the Doc Studies Center from West (beware of this), I looked forward to class every time. Homework is very reasonable, grading is very clear and fair. "Engage" projects had a learning curve (didn't know editing) but were fun if you're not too shy.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Amazing professor. You can tell that she genuinely cares about her students, and she will go out of her way to assist you whenever she can. Overall the class was super easy, graded on 3 quizzes, which were basically: read the material and you'll get an 'A'. Read the 15 pages of weekly material, and it's an easy 'A'.

Katie is one of the best professors at Duke! She really takes the time to get to know all of her students and cares about how well they are doing in this class. As long you do the readings, show up to class, and participate its a pretty easy A. One of the best classes I have taken!!!

Katie has the most interesting and mind-blowing materials. Her materials about documentary ethics and seeing are the most educational materials I have ever read/learned from Duke. She listens and thus understands people. When she makes a statement or says something, it's not empty, theoretical, words but things proven from fieldwork/experiences.
Dr. Hyde is a very kind woman who cares a lot about her work. You can tell she is passionate about doc studies!

Bio major took this class to fill ALP and ended up being my favorite class at Duke. Katie is so caring & does an amazing job of making classroom a safe space. She gives a lot of feedback on assignments & is always willing to meet outside of class. Material was SUPER interesting, her passion made class so enjoyable and engaging. TAKE HER CLASS!!!

Interesting class, great but many readings. Many athletes. Gives impression class is easy, but isn't. Two quizzes over readings which are fair, two 3000 word essays graded hard, and a presentation. Participate 2 times per class, amazing,lovely prof, but you'll work and read lots! I, in Pratt,found this class to be slightly difficult work-wise

Katie is a caring, inspiring and wise professor. The class is taught as a small seminar which provides a great opportunity to discuss education-related topics. Moreover, the service-learning component  is a space for you to put the LTP methodology to practice. I recommend this class because it is interesting and well taught.
Katie is incredibly helpful and kind. She is very passionate about photography and she certainly loves to share and talk about it. Absolutely would recommend her freshman seminar.

This class may suffer in time due to the size of the course. The readings are really great and diverse for the most part. Katie is really nice and explains the material well. Participation is mandatory which she ensures through assigning occasional group presentations. Her main course is LTP, which probably gives a much better experience overall.
Take this class! It knocks out grad requirements, the material is interesting, and she is so kind. Participate a lot and ask good questions

Both of my classes with Katie were wonderful! She is so sweet, approachable, and caring toward her students, their well-being, and their education. I've learned so much from the classes I've had the opportunity to take with her. I recommend her classes to anyone that asks!

Katie is an awesome professor. Her lessons are interactive, interesting, and she uses a range of teaching methods to keep students engaged. She is also very approachable, helpful, and patient and genuinely is passionate what she teaches.
Professor Huettel is an amazing EGR101 professor. She was very enthusiastic, kind, and supportive throughout the semester and genuinely cares about her students.
Lecture notes are not posted so you have to go to the lecture, but overall the lectures are pretty good. The tests are very different than the homework and practice exams.

Lisa is super kind and caring. By pretty much every definition, she is a great professor. However, ECE381 is not designed well. The tests do not reflect the homework at all, and homework does not count for your grade. Therefore, everything is based on your tests and final (which is not cumulative). Kind of painful since you'll never have a buffer.

Dr. Huettel is an amazing professor. She is very kind and also extremely helpful during her office hours. The course was also taught in (what I've heard) a much better way than other current ECE 110 professors teach it, and her midterms and final are very reasonable. I would not hesitate to take another class with Dr. Huettel again!

Be on top of things. This class is VERY assessment-heavy. While partial credit is quite generous, you don't have that much wiggle room so stay consistent on midterms and exams. Dr. Huettel is an amazing teacher who is dedicated to her students, so utilize her office hours and help sessions.

Dr. Huettel was the best professor I've had. She helped me improve my grade from a 50% to a 95%. She will schedule extra OH to help students, and she will set you up for success. I am confident my academic career at Duke was shaped by her kindness and willingness to help.

Phenomenal professor! Writes notes out while lecturing so that it's easy to keep up. Explains things very thoroughly and clearly. NEVER refuses to answer a question, even if it stalls the lesson. Cares about deep understanding. I went to her office hours every week with homework questions, and she helped me understand every nuance of the problems.

She explains concepts very thoroughly. Sometimes, she spends too much time going through an example, which results in the class failing to cover a few concepts towards the end of the semester. The second midterm is difficult (time crunch). The final is easier, and the final isn't a time crunch. Homework is graded for completion.
Great teacher who explains concepts well and cares about her students. Exams were not too bad if you studied
Incredible lecturer, and an interesting class. Very helpful at office hours as well, so overall a great instructor. Beware of the final, which is NOT comprehensive contrary to what we thought.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: Best professor I've had, ever. She truly made me feel like she cared about me in office hours, and made every question i asked feel valid (even if it may have been stupid). She is patient, kind, and insanely intelligent. I mean the woman got the IEEE award for best undergraduate teaching: what more could you want? Just don't skip class!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Huettel is the best professor I've had so far at Duke. She is very caring about her students. I missed the first week of class, and she went out of her way to catch me up. Her lectures are straightforward, and she gives you all the essential information you need to do well in ECE (unlike Dr. G, who overloads his students to the point of confusion).

Her lectures are great, and she is always extremely helpful and always willing to answer any questions you have. Her office hours are extremely underappreciated and will help you understand the homework assignments she gives out weekly.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Huettel is  one of the best professors I've had at Duke. She explains everything so clearly, and makes the material seem so interesting.  Problem sets are  sometimes long (as expected in an engineering course)  and the tests are very fair and straightforward. I would rearrange my entire schedule if I could take another class from her.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Her class, HW and test is not so hard. It's just what you expect from normal class. The other ECE 110 class is taught by Dr. G. Compared with that class, her test is easier. Homework from both classes is based on the same textbook problems so comparison wouldn't matter at all. If you want good grade, take hers. If you want to learn, take Dr. G.
Sweetest ECE professor ever. She is so helpful and super fun to talk to. Recommend 5/5. People love her for good reason. If you don't take a class with her, you are missing out.
Great prof;  she is literally always there for you for anything; she asks great questions on the test too... hws can be a pain (6-8 hrs) but still.
Definitely the one of the best professors in the ECE department
Best professor for this class. Tests are pretty straightforward, and her class notes are great. She's also one of the nicest professors I've had.
Huettel is a doll. Please take a course with her if you are in ECE. Easily the best ECE professor I've had, not to mention the sweetest.

Dr. Huettel is extremely nice and extremely clear during lectures. Her office hours are also immensely helpful in completing the assignments. However, it's a very difficult course, and while she does her best to help students, it really takes a lot of work to do well. She also doesn't really curve, so be prepared.

Great professor, very helpful out of class. Wish there was more time to meet with her - the problem sets are 10x harder than the stuff you do in class.. should have started earlier so I could go to office hours. The tests are based on the p. set problems, so it is a fair course.

She is so helpful and willing to work with students outside of class! She lectures very clearly and at a good pace. She cares about having her students understand things at a deep level: her tests tend to be more conceptually difficult and surprising, while Ybarra's focus more on the math behind the concepts. She is so great, take it with her!
Tough class+tough exam+tough grading, no curveball at all=you get what you get.  But she's very helpful and pretty good at explaining the material.  Not an easy class to take in senior year
Great professor. Accessible out of class, answers every question you have until you completely understand the material. Course, however, is a lot of work.
She is very helpful outside of class. However, her tests were really tough and I hated never ending labs.. This is a full lab course.
Not the easiest class in the world.  Projects are fun, though.
Awesome professor. Highly recommended.

Prof Huettel is by far the best prof I've had in Pratt so far. Her lectures are very organized, and if you have trouble with the material, meet with her and she will work until you understand it. Very enthusiastic too
great teacher.. great lecutres... very clear!
A professor who solves the homework she assigns. Very organized. Very friendly.
One of the best professors here in Pratt. Her lectures are very organized and engaging, to the point that reading the book is optional.

You'll never meet another prof. in Pratt who teaches a class in such an organized, clear, and engaging manner.  Not an easy class, but Prof. Huettel is accessible and always ready to help students understand the material.
Professor Huettel is very organized and engaging. Material is tough but she is helpful and makes it interesting and meaningful.
No Comments
Most friendly teacher you'll have at Duke. Doesn't exactly hand out the A's.
No Comments
Professor Huettel is very clear, give good notes, fair tests and shows enthusiasm for her subject
Huettel is the best Engineering Prof I've had in my 2 years so far in Pratt.  She is super competent- oraganized, clear, and extraordinarily accessible and helpful.

He slices dense pathways into color-coded, story-linked steps, so the load feels manageable. Exams are little tough yet fair—30 % application, 70 % recall, generous partial credit. After this class I went straight into metabolism grad programs, but never thanked him.   Best prof I've had at DKU.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Kim has taught me biochemistry and other courses, and his support has meant a lot. He genuinely cares about students—not just academically, but also about their future. At the same time, he's professional and serious about teaching. His lectures are always well-prepared and clear, and I felt his class truly helped me grow academically.
I liked the lectures, the course itself may be tough with tones of chemistry and biology, but he made it easy enough for me who may not have through Biology background. Respect!

Textbook is heavy and lots of to learn, but his lectures definitely clarify what are important.  I know there are other instructors teaching the same course, but I am very glad to take his.  Most question and exams are original, and require either simple or thorough understanding . He provided clear-rules of grading type of grader.

Make sure to send the assignments on time. He offers a generous amount of extra credit overall. The test is relatively simple and not very complicated.  Lectures are content heavy, and some, but not all, attendance is mandatory. Exams are original, and require thorough understanding in order to apply the concepts.

Wonderful professor. He knows what to focus on and what to ignore, rather than insisting 'everything is important'.  Passionate about the subject and teaching. He really tries to make his students enjoy the subject, focusing on subject  and exploration. Helpful with independent research, study, and cookies!

NOT GLHLTH364 - Laidlaw Special Topics: PubPol290. Dr. Huynh is kind and accepting, sometimes viewed as "too woke." They often indirectly shared one-sided opinions - guest speakers were similar. An amazing person to learn from, and always willing to provide grace and engage with students. Class starts easy, then elevates with a group research paper

Dr. Huynh's materials were okay, covering the same concepts repeatedly. Their commentary for our discussion class is underwhelming, especially for a class that can cover much more nuanced, unique conversation. The class is not as interactive/engaging as it could be, partially due to them. Work is not demanding, however. Is a bit strange?

Dr. Huynh is super chill. They bring a lot of experience to the table but still recognize that his perspective might not be correct for everyone. They were my grader for our final paper and his feedback was so helpful. He is extremely kind and if you bump into them outside class, they will always make conversation. Hy is the best!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Ibanez is an aggressive, boring lecturer and is unsympathetic towards students with respect to regrading or reaching out via email. She genuinely does not want to give A's, and doesn't engage the class appropriately, instead calling out students to participate rather than creating an open environment for discussion. I dreaded going to class.

Nice professor and makes class engaging (a lot of group stuff) but a decent amount of work and time required for good grade. Class is entirely in Spanish. She's good with feedback and clearly cares about her students.

Professor Ibanez makes you work for your grade and is a very strict grader. She is confusing at times, but if you ask for help she really wants you to succeed and will meet with you outside of class and give you suggestions on how to improve your scores and ability of understanding Spanish.

She takes everything really seriously and has a grading rubric for every little thing so nothing comes easy (read: no free 100s). Nice professor who wants you to do well but does not make it easy to do so, she has high expectations all the time. The course isn't impossible but you really have to put in a lot of effort to have a shot at getting an A

Spanish 203 is an unfortunate class that many people have to take to meet the language requirement. Professor Ibanez unfortunately does not make it any easier. She is difficult to understand in class but she tries to help when she can. You'll have to a lot of your own teaching.

Señora Ibañez was by far the best language teacher I've had in my life. The Duke Spanish curriculum is kind of flipped (activities in class, learning content outside of class), so it was fast-paced, but fabulous.  She was enthusiastic every day, her grading was fair, and I wish I could take every class with her. Work hard and do well.

Ibanez is so sweet and wants everyone to do well! I enjoyed every single day of class with her, and I wish I could have her for my future spanish classes. The class is taught only in spanish, which is hard, but that's just how Duke does it. If you study the text book, you are basically guaranteed to get an A. Love her so much!

Super easy class, gives everyone who shows up an A. As long as you turn in homework and essays on time you're guaranteed a 100% homework and participation grade and at least a B+ on essays. Doesn't check if you actually read. Easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Mme. Iber is a great teacher who really cares about her students. This is my third French class at Duke and I really enjoyed both the class (which she designed) and her teaching style. It's mostly discussion based, and participation really matters. She puts an emphasis on written French and is a hard grader when it comes to both content and writing
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Mme. Iber can be intimidating at first, but after getting to know her, she is super nice. She really cares about her students and wants us to do well (corrects our grammar in essay rough drafts although other profs don't). There's a ton of homework in this class though and can be kind of stressful. Not an easy A - might be best to skip to 300 level

This class is participation heavy, but everyone only gets one chance to speak per class. In between each speaker he tends to take 5-6 minutes to give his opinion on it, but not particularly in a way that helps you grasp the concept better. The readings are difficult and he is a tough essay grader (at times arbitrary). Very knowledgeable though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor MacMullen cares a lot about the subject matter, but usually this results in him interjecting between every student who speaks during class "discussions." The more you make your papers sound like him, the better you'll do. The class is interesting if you like ethics and political theory. Make sure to do the readings and PARTICIPATE!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Participation is super important and the papers are pretty hard. He is available out of class but the grading feels really arbitrary sometimes. The multiple-choice test on political philosophy was a bad idea and tanked a lot of people's grades. Overall very eccentric and fine, and the material will make you look at your world differently.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor MacMullen is definitely a nice guy. However, he has a weird discussion style in his class where he interjects between each student with his own idea/interpretation, which gets kind of annoying after a while. However, the material is pretty engaging. The readings are long and quite philosophical, but interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Really great guy- cares a lot about the material you're learning; tests are super hard but he's very accessible and if you meet with him outside of class to review all the memo material you're guaranteed an A on those. Particiption also matters a lot, so make sure you read/take notes ahead of time!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Reading heavy and very hard to understand. Very philosophical, most of the time discussing unrealistic theoretical view points, and does not attempt to relate it back to current policy. Good guy just a style of teaching that was not for me.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: An eye-opening class. I learned about different viewpoints that I never thought of before. BUT does require hard work. Difficult readings. 3 essays that are hard but manageable. Requires a lot of brainstorming (he is very nicecessible outside of class so use this to your advantage before writing your essays) Insightful participation is mandatory
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Although there is a lot of reading, the subject matter is engaging and relevant. It can be frustrating when Professor MacMullen seems to bend students' comments to his own opinions, but he's a genuinely nice guy and is very invested in the material. As long as you participate (!) and use the texts in your arguments, he's a forgiving grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Professor MacMullen is a very intelligent man. He knows the readings well, and will tell you exactly how he feels about your contribution to the class. I disliked the way his seminar operated for this reason; instead of allowing classmates to respond to one another, he would speak between each student. Be prepared for a challenging class.

I would not be shy about taking PubPol 302 with Professor MacMullen. The reviews are harsh below, but keep in mind that usually only the extremes post about professors. MacMullen is ALWAYS available for help outside of class, and is very knowledgeable about ethics. If you read the text carefully, you will get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: While you do need to be prepared to read and participate a lot, I didn't find this class unreasonably difficult. If you do the readings (or part of the reading) and come to class prepared to say at least one thing, you can get a decent participation grade. He does look for specific answers to his questions in class, but the material is compelling.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Daily quizzes and tests are very complicated and based on very complex philosophical readings. Seemed more suitable towards political science. Intense grading system.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: MacMullen is a great lecturer, but has transformed a political philosophy class, which he has clearly taught at a different institution, into a weak way of evaluating the ethics and values of public policy (PUBPOL302). Class is bizarrely weighed on your ability to break down complex philosophy BEFORE you attend lectures. Little to grapple with.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Class is run terribly. The whole grade rests on three essays, participation, and one project. You need to know the boring readings extremely well, since he will dock participation points for not giving the input he's looking for. They're also important for the essays, which he grades pretty arbitrarily.

Though the course is titled "Policy Choice as Value Conflict," you will learn absolutely no policy related content in his class. MacMullen is not receptive to different opinions and is incredibly condescending when you ask questions. He also has no concept of time management when he lectures and often has no time left to cover important material.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Frustrating class. Grading structure aimed against you. Don't take unless you're good at philosophy.

MacMullen is a great lecturer, but has transformed a political philosophy class, which he has clearly taught at a WashU, into a weak way of evaluating the ethics and values of public policy (PUBPOL302). Class is bizarrely weighed on your ability to break down complex philosophy BEFORE you attend lectures. Little to grapple with.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Overall knows the material that we read well and can communicate it nicely, but spends the entire seminar waiting for one of us to say what he wants us to say. Not super open to different opinions, harsh grader, and overall just not an enjoyable class. I dreaded every Tuesday and Thursday because of this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: no offense but worst teacher i have ever had. ruined my first semester of freshman year at Duke. Made me cry on multiple occasions. I dreaded waking up to go to his class. BEWARE.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: He is probably one of the worst professors at Duke. Completely incomprehensible in lecture, calls every problem trivial which they are not,and can't convey information at all.  Avoid his classes.

Dinwoodie is a bad professor because he just does not teach anything and you have to figure a lot out for yourself. Also his grading is annoying for midterms: there are like 12 multiple choice questions and if u get two questions wrong u have a B+. Very frustrating for what seems to be a very easy class. Midterms exactly like previous midterms.

Professor dinwoodie is very helpful if you go to the office hourse. His lecture is confusing, but if you read your text book, his lecture is very organized. It seems like easy class but you need to study to get an A.
Dinwoodie is really incoherent but in a really endearing way. Most people don't feel this way but I do! Anyways his class is easy so if you need this credit just take it, its not a big deal.

His lectures are possibly the most boring events I've ever attended at Duke, and he calls everything he does either "easy" or "trivial". This is frustrating when neither of these words necessarily describes how the work is to the students.

This class is a complete joke. He does all the hw in class, and the midterms are almost identical to his midterms from previous years. Tho he is a bad lecturer, his class is worth taking for the easy A.

not great as a lecturer and will call out students to answer questions.  however...knowing the answer doesn't matter and only does so to try to learn student's names.  does the hw in class (and the larger assignments too) and exams are basically directly from hw and previous exams (which are posted with answers).  good book, ends up to be easy-ish

Almost no work outside of class.  His lectures can be increadibly tedious and hard to follow, but he does almost all of the homework problems in class, and the tests are almost exactly the homework problems.  If you go to office hours his explanations are more clear.
one of the worst teachers I've ever had at Duke
One of many teachers giving this same class. I was very happy to be in this particular group and Prof Idzelis was great.
Very good professor.  Clear, open to student questions, and able to teach difficult ideas and principles.  Very approachable.

Idzelis has only a JD from a small law school without any scholarly achievement. Her class is super boring and she is the king of confusion. She does not have teaching skills and I dont know how she is grading the paper.It's highly recommended to change her class as it's wast of time and efforts without any real benefit. I do hate this class.

This class had asynchronous lectures with three synchronous sessions each week for quizzes and asking questions. I had Inma for the three 30-minute synchronous sessions each week. Shes very sweet, clear in her explanations, and gives good feedback on the quizzes.

Lectures were frequently all over the place, and she assumed things that definitely we're not prereqs for the course. Grading criteria changed often during the semester as a majority of the class was failing after the first test. Overall, very poorly structured and organized class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Way to hard, grades really harshly and is super nitpicky- you can get a question 100% right and still get 50% credit. Stay away
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Very knowledgable of subject. Attentive to his students, gives great feedback, and those eyes...

favorite teacher at Duke. learned so much about AIDS in America but w/ literature-- no real focus on science like Bio 46. Inrig is funny and makes his lectures interesting & relevant. discussion-based and really laid-back atmosphere. he's at unc now but i hope he comes back to teach a class!

Best teacher I have had here at college.  he is funny and actually makes his lectures enjoyable. there are a lot of readings for the midterm and final and a semester long paper on a topic of your choice, and he grades very fairly.  Very approachable and easy to contact.  He is a great professor.

Spells out Macro principles in a way that's easy to understand, slides are supplemental but majority comes from in-class chalkboard lectures. Take extensive notes to do well - tests match exactly what is taught in class. Excellent personality, easygoing and goes slow but steady which is necessary for such difficult concepts as macro.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: First time teaching macro and did a really good job. Lectures were a little bit slower than that what I was used to, but he really took a deep dive into a lot of the topics we covered. Would def recommend taking this class with him
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Cosmin is very hard-working, diligent and cares a lot about his students. It was his first time teaching a core Economics course at Duke and he did a stellar job.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Her teaching philosophy is that, and i quote, "I'm not hear to teach you - you read the book/lecture before class and you come to class with questions." Not my type of class at all.  It's her first semester at NCSU - syllabus is really confusing and she hasn't offered to fix it.  No one understands it.  Never organized for class.
Alright professor - made 76 a lot more work than it needed to be. I'm not big into French, so I was just trying to get my requirement out of the way, and she made it hard!
Hard to understand and a very hard grader.
Best French Instructor

Overall, a very energetic environment. 

Was a fun class to take, and I learned a lot. 

The big thing about this class is that there are a series of projects you have with the same partner, so please try and get along and get a good flow going so that everything else becomes easier.

She's fun and understanding and can help with time management!

She's very good at teaching and it's easy for me to understand the topics through just lectures. She's always ready to talk to students outside of class and gives detailed feedback.  The exam is not too difficult, just make sure to understand the concepts and revise. The workload can be a bit much for an intro class, get ready to read a lot.

She possesses all components of a great professor! Her lectures are super amazing with illustration and small discussion. The content of the course is undeniably mind-blowing! Besides, Prof. Soboleva is more than willing to connect and discuss with students outside class. She has quite clearly grading criteria and always gives thorough feedbacks.

Prof. Ira is one of the professors that makes me really want to go to her lectures and learn as many things as possible from her. She seemed intimidating during the first lecture, but she actually is an extremely nice professor that wants her students to succeed. Definitely recommended, and you will not regret it.

Professor Ira is really a gem. She is uplifting and motivational and also very knowledgeable of her academic discipline. Even though the class was demanding in terms of its workload, it was very rewarding and I feel that I learned a lot.

Professor Soboleva is the BEST! She's very passionate about behavioral science and political behavior, and she's definitely an expert in her field. She provides very good, constructive feedback, and really wants to see her students succeed. She also enjoys having conversations with her students about the material, which is always really enjoyable.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Soboleva is literally THE BEST. Her way of teaching, plus the way she plans out her courses is great. She also knows her subject really well, so not for a moment could I doubt her excellence. Stay true to your work, and you'll do great.

She is a very confusing and difficult professor. Her grading can be rough and she doesn't prepare you well for tests. In addition, she is horrible on getting back to you and is very unclear about what she wants. This class will end up taking up way more time than necessary, and if you can avoid Rios Torres, do so at all costs.

This class seems easy from the outside. I mean, two-thirds of the title is "film and popular culture", right? Nope. The whole class is literature with some telenovela thrown in the last three weeks. She grades hard on essays and is not very lenient with her disproportionate expectations of her students. Tough way to get rid of language requirement

I started the course loving spanish, but that quickly changed. She's unnecessarily difficult and expects you to produce a level of spanish writing that a proficient native speaker can produce. Seriously, I would just not take the class. The amount of time I spent on spanish detracted from my other classes and ended up ruining my GPA.

He is pretty organized for his great idea of "questions of the day", and provides concrete examples along with abstract ideas from the book. He's easy and approachable, and is pretty lenient with the grading. Good professor.

Iwen is fairly straightforward. Homework and a quiz once a week. The homework was maybe 3 hours a week. He starts each class with a "question of the day" which helps give an idea of what to pay attention to and helps provide an example to the abstract concepts explained in class. But I'm fairly into math, so I might be biased.

This teacher was excruciating. **He's not an inherently bad guy**. But he's a useless teacher, who really is just a math-major but takes no effort at approaching math at different angles. Plus, math 103 has enough material that he is overwhelmed with staying on track, so he justifies rushing through the material in a rote unremarkable way.

Daubechies is a genius, and it is cool to learn from her. She is also very nice and cares for her students. However, her class and lectures are incredibly difficult and confusing. The homework took 10 hours per week, but did not even help prepare for the difficult exams. I tried harder in this class than I ever have in my life and did not get an A.

She is very intelligent; however, she fails to explain concepts at a level students (with little background) can understand. Her lectures are disorganized. She makes up the examples on spot and so many times these examples do not work. Exams are very hard. Keep in mind she thinks getting a C on an exam is a good grade.

Prof. Daubechies is brilliant but a terrible teacher. There was no syllabus or any plan, she just wrote random stuff on the board. Never really explained much at all and the homework proofs you just had to take shots in the dark.

Professor Daubechies is a genius in her own right. The course is designed for people with no strong mathematical background, however if this is you, you might find it quite tough. Also, this course covers a very wide range of topics, including information theory, probability, measure and integration, real analysis, dynamical systems, and topology.

Dr. Daubechies is very nice and willing to help. This course may be difficult if you have not been exposed to the concepts before (real analysis, measure theory, dynamical systems) as it moves fairly quickly.

Dr. Daubechies is really a kind woman and an incredibly accomplished mathematician. There were homework about once every 1.3 weeks or so (more often than not) which each took me around 10 hours. This was my first introduction to rigorous proof-writing so maybe if you're a more experienced math major it might be easier. She ultimately grades p easy.
Professor Daubechies is a mathematician of tremendous renown. Duke is very fortunate to have her.

She is a brilliant mathematician, but not so great at explaining concepts to non-math people, which are the majority of people who take this class. I just needed a math requirement, and this class was pretty much as miserable as I expected it to be. Problem sets every week but no tests at least!

Took multi with her 2 years ago. Her contributions to mathematics have been very meaningful, so I consider it a privilege to have learned from her. Tests were difficult, but your grade should be fine because of curve + block final (which will be probably be easier than your exams). If you show a genuine interest, you can get a lot out of this!

Make no mistake, Math Everywhere (designed for non-STEM people) was no joke. I'm definitely not the best at math but tried really hard and would spend 20+ hours on almost every weekly problem set and papers weren't graded easily. BUT the topics are interesting, Daubechies is super brilliant and very nice, so take it if you're willing to work.

She's way to smart.  She  doesn't know how to explain things in a way that regular humans can understand.  She doesn't prepare before class, so she just makes up problems from her head that never turn out right.  I don't think you could even call her a teacher.  I had to learn the who thing from the book or my friends.

Definitely one of the most intelligent Duke professors, period. However, she's not too good at getting down to the students' intelligence level and as a result is very difficult to understand at times. Her tests are kind of hard, but she doesn't make the final so it's not too difficult. Make sure to study the easy stuff for the final.
Daubechies is incredibly intelligent and as a result I had trouble understanding most of her lectures. Tests are brutal but the final will seem easy in comparison
Fantastic professor. Always willing to take questions and help her students. Difficult tests. But Multivariable Calculus is difficult in general.
It's true that her exams are a bit harder than other professors', but if you really wanna understand multi, take her class and do her tests.
Great teacher. She is very helpful, mostly clear (some accent, but not terrible), and extremely bright. She's not the easiest, but there are definitely harder teachers and she wants you to succeed.
Incredibly smart. She has very long office hours and has plenty of time before tests to review material. Tests are difficult but she is a forgiving grader. Homework is helpful.
Brilliant, but not a great teacher.  Tests are impossible.  Maybe if you are a math major, she can relate to you -- but if you are an engineer, try to take math 212 with a different professor.

Absolutely brilliant professor. Extremely patient, always willing to discuss every/any question you have in office hours.  Tests are impossible, but in the end, with the curve and other factors, you'll receive an accurate grade. Extremely in depth, changed my approach to/understanding of mathematics, if you like math you MUST take a class w/her

There was way too much unnecessary calculations and unpleasant numbers, the main concept could easily be overshadowed by the unnecessary changes in variables and trig identities. Even if you're good at number crunching, don't take it with this professor.

Her tests are generally pretty difficult. You must, must, must study the concepts and review them in order to get a good grade in her class. She's very intelligent and genuinely knows what she's doing, just not the best teacher. Better than some, though.
Nice teacher, incredibly knowledgable, IMPOSSIBLE TESTS. If you're a math major, you'll be alright, anybody else try to avoid this tough class.
Her tests are awful. Easily among the hardest in the department. Try to take math 212 with another prof.
Loved the class - one of the highlights of my senior spring. Would highly recommend taking a class with him before he leaves

Professor Jaffe is one of the kindest and most caring and dedicated professors I have ever had. He's clearly so passionate about the subject and cares about passing on his interest to his students. Classes are free flowing discussions and I learned so much about Buddhist meditation and how to view the world around me. The whole class flunched him.

His class has no grading criteria and at the beginning of classes he says that he is accessible outside of class and will go over drafts but does not follow through with that. For a class that is 70% based on 2 papers, this was such a surprise.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Cool guy. Lots of readings but if you don't understand (or didn't do them) he goes over questions in class. Good class to overload hard sciences with.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Jaffe is one of the most caring, patient and knowledgeable persons in the world! The course is easy and interesting.

You have to write a journal entry of 250 words weekly on the previous week's readings. There are two 6-7 page papers that are worth 35% each. He's a really nice person and will work with students to accommodate everyone. You can only miss a few classes and participation is also 10% of the final grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Really caring and funny professor. The lectures feel like informal conversations but you end up learning so much. Great learning environment, and he has guest speakers and trips to get a lot of exposure to different Buddhist disciplines. Just 2 essays that he gives plenty of opportunities for edits plus short quizzes that are very easy.
Great professor; very understandable and cares about the subject material.

Jaffe is the sweetest & most caring professor I have ever had. He genuinely cares about the subject matter and expects you to participate but the small seminar style is very conducive to participation. Short 5-question quizzes after every class, 2 papers, and an oral presentation -- minimal work and not a tough grader

Without a doubt, my favorite professor at Duke. So, so caring and radiates kindness. Is more than happy to talk to you outside of class, and is the first professor whose office hours I've shown up to, honestly just to get to know him better. A wonderful professor and an even better person!
Pedantic scholar.  I was bored to the skull.

Dr. Jaffe is not only a good professor, but also an extremely kind and humble human being. I enjoyed taking Buddhism with him even though my interest in the subject was fairly minimal. His old school scribble-notes-on-the-chalkboard lecture style was refreshing with a schedule full of powerpoint presentation lectures.
Dr. Jaffe is a great professor and was always very helpful to every student.  He is especially very clear in his explanations of often murky subject matter and enjoys getting to know his students.

This professor does not use a grading scheme and therefore his grades are arbitrary and pointless. That having been said he is nice, and some of the readings are interesting.  Otherwise watch out for suprise grades.
Very nice teacher but don't take this class unless you intend to do all the readings.  The papers were difficult and required a very comprehensive understanding of the material.
Great instructor! Kind and very helpful!
It was a good class to de-stress. Lectures were a bit boring but expected as it was a 2.5 hour class. If you interact the class becomes way more interesting. Professor is a nice guy.

He's a cool cat in his own psyc prof terms. I took his PSY 324 which was motivations in social psychology. He's a wealth of knowledge - could be boring for those not interested, but for those interested in social psychology, it's like listening to a live podcast - one that will give you a wealth of knowledge and you will want to remember them

Dr. Shah's lectures were quite boring, and the textbook seemed to outline the concepts much better than him. You don't have to attend lectures, just study the slides and textbook. The class is all exam-based with the final counting for more than half your final grade. Try to take with someone else, but this course is not harder with Shah. Nice guy!
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Shah reads right from the lecture slides, which are not written well. Nonetheless, the tests are pretty straightforward. Just read the book and go through the slides on your own, and you'll do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Interesting material, clear expectations.

Terrible professor but very interesting material. Lectures are pretty boring and slides are not the best written. Also, your grade is dependent on a midterm and final entirely, which include four essay questions each. This class is curved (not noted in syllabus but he does), and in our case, this was a negative curve that hurt us. Who does that?

Dr. Shah read directly from his presentation slides. Slides matched textbook exactly. Exams matched slides and textbook. Despite motivation science being an interesting topic, this class was extremely boring. We met once per week and Shah cancelled about half the classes. It's an easy A but so uninspiring.

this is the easiest, most straightforward class at duke. we were graded on two easy tests. review the lecture slides and read the textbook, and you should do great. content is common sense. lectures are boring and dry, so it is hard to stay awake during the class, but attendance was not graded, so thankfully, i didn't have to show up to class.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Reading the textbook and memorizing the slides are strongly recommended because that's where everything on the exams comes from...
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Lectures are incredibly dull. A 2.5 hour 8:30 lecture on a FRIDAY? Oh gosh. Read the textbook, learn the slides kinda, and you'll be set. Super straightforward class but midterm is worth like 30% and final is 60% iirc. Tests are really easy; he's looking for basic comprehension and little memorization, for the most part.

I felt that his monotonous and dry lecturing covered a million points every second, and then you need to memorize that. Overall, I was very unhappy taking this class and I felt taking the midterm sick was a nightmare and the class was just extremely dry. Plus on top of that, the class is filled with annoying PiPhis that make everything 2x worse.

Your entire grade is pretty much midterm and final, but the tests themselves are pretty easy. Social psych was interesting, but he wasn't really an interesting lecturer, especially at 8:30 am. Going to class isn't really mandatory since the exact material is in the book and he posts the slides up online.

Shah is a pretty boring lecturer, and you can't use electronics in class.  I took this class as an easy A and ended up working a little harder than I thought I'd have to, but overall, it wasn't bad. Even if you never show up to class, as long as you look at the powerpoint slides, you should be okay.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Don't need to go to class- boring lecturer and pretentious. Easy A, except that he did not word his questions well and did not tell us he wanted verbatim what was listed on his powerpoints.
