If you want a good grade, memorize the powerpoints and spit them back out on the two tests, no original thought needed.
It is what it is. Not much effort needed.

Great guy. Very helpful when you have questions about studies. Lectures feels dry and very long, especially being at 8:30AM. Textbook is a must. Over time there were only around 20 people who would show up to class. Pure memorization of the slides. Midterm was 35%, Final 65%. Each question worth a point on your grade. Questions worded terribly.

just a really poor lecturer who clearly doesn't care about teaching. very monotonous and boring who doesn't change up his teaching style at all. it's no surprise the class attendance decreased progressively throughout the semester, even though it was an 8:30. the midterm (35%) and final (65%) is ridiculous, but generally easy to prep for

There are two tests - midterm (35%) and final (65%). The "final" is really just another midterm that covers only the 2nd half of the course. He posts his slides and they are not clear, but if you review them along with the textbook (especially key terms), you never have to go to lecture (which is great because he's pretty boring). Great guy though.

Shah is an incredibly boring lecturer. Slides don't have many words, but he manages to talk for minutes on a single slide. Your grade is based off of 35% midterm and 65% final (four-choice multiple choice questions), which weren't too bad if you reviewed his pp slides online and read the textbook (I loved the textbook).

This class is NOT and easy A. There are only 2 grades, a midterm worth 35% of your grade and a final worth 65%! The material is interesting but the lectures are boring. Shah was a good guy and did explain stuff well, but I couldn't stay awake to listen. The tests are also based primarily on the lectures, but know key terms from the book!

Very poor lecturer. Boring, monotonous, and repetitive. It's just as easy to skip lecture and just take notes on the power points and book vocab. If you're looking for a breeze of a class, this is for you.
Social Psych was a total breeze. I went to lecture and everything you needed to know was gone over in great detail. He's a really nice guy too. A bit monotonous, but just grab a coffee beforehand.
Great Professor. Very informed and topical. Shah takes the time to work with you if you are interested and have enough intelligence to keep up.

boring professor. easy tests (if you know the slides and main terms from the readings). I enrolled into psych of consumers very interested in the topic but didn't really enjoy it very much. I also thought i could handle a boring professor in an easy class, but ended up hating it. I wouldn't recommend it...even for an easy A.

I took social psy w/ him. The topic was really interesting but the class was terribly boring. Lectures are monotonous and not really necessary, since he posts the powerpoints online. We only had 2 grades, which doesn't help if you don't do well on one. If you like psych, don't take it with him.
classes are interesting but everything is posted online.  he is a very brilliant man but has a voice that will lul you to sleep. be careful!

Shah is a ridiculously boring professor. No need to go to class. Only 2 grades: midterm and final. The midterm was way too hard and as a result the final was extremely easy. Loved the course material but not the professor.

There were only two grades in the class, the midterm and final, and both were fair and had generous curves. Shah isn't a great lecturer and his powerpoints are often redundant. Still, a nice guy and cares about his work
easy class, easy tests, nice guy.  he posts everything on ppt slides so theres no need to attend class. he mumbles a lot and gets redundant and boring and awkward at times, but very brilliant

I'd highly recommend any ballet class with Professor Strong. He genuinely cares about his students growth both in and beyond the classroom. His classes are challenging, but supportive, and he creates a positive environment that helped me rebuild my relationship with ballet and actually look forward to class. Best ballet class and he is the best.

Loved taking ballet with Prof. Strong! Really cares about students and offered helpful corrections. Classes were structured well and designed to help students of differing skill levels improve and challenge themselves.

Great guy and great dancer! Mr. Strong is a kind and thoughtful teacher who really pays attention to each student. I would recommend taking a class with him--there is a lot of great stuff he can teach you!

He's the sort of professor that gives you the impression you're doing quite well only to slam a bad grade on you at the end of the course (for Dance 121, this was).  Does not give sufficient feedback at all. Has unclear expectations throughout the course. Clearly inexperienced teaching at a college level. Would not recommend.

I'm grateful to learn once again from Pierre. He's experienced, passionate & gives the utmost care & attention to his students. He's encouraging & always willing to chat outside of class. I'm actually learning how to speak, read & write in Creole with confidence & competence. Phone apps are no substitute for real language learning! Take his course!

Pierre is a skilled & charitable professor, extending his expert Kreyòl knowledge to us w/ great care, going to great lengths to meet w/ students outside of class––rare traits among university profs. He is easy to approach, has a warmth about him & a great sense of humor, also rare in the often austere halls of higher ed. I cannot recommend enough!

Professor Pierre's Zoom class has been essential in improving my Creole. As a heritage speaker, I've gained stronger reading and writing skills. His passion for Kreyòl, Haitian culture, and current events makes lessons engaging. I highly recommend his class to anyone interested in learning Kreyòl.

Prof. Pierre is really passionate about this subject. You'll start speaking Creole pretty fluently by the end of 102. By the time you reach this level, it's focused more on the culture, which is vast, complicated, and interesting. I highly recommend taking his class!

He's a good and dedicated teacher. You'll learn a lot both about the language and Haitian culture in any of his classes. Make sure to submit all assignments in on time, he'll get frustrated and only give partial credit if you don't, even if it's by a minute. Only negative issue is that he runs over class time nearly every class.

I took Creole101 with Pr. Pierre and had a great experience. He pays close attention to every student and stays extra time to explain and practice. Lessons connect real-life language with Haitian history and culture. You need to practice a lot, but Pr. Pierre creates the perfect environment to succeed and is always here. I recommend this course!

Professor Jacques Pierre is very passionate about teaching Creole language and culture. His dedication and commitment to teaching allow his students not only to learn the language but also important aspects of Haitian culture. There are several assignments to submit, which help students stay consistent with the language. I recommend this course.

This professor cares a lot about the language and the culture around it. He is passionate and wants his students to excel in this course. Taking this course means learning the language practically every day. There's a lot of homework, and the tests are very long. Overall, I enjoyed taking Haitian Creole with this professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I had Prof. Pierre for Creole 101, 102, and 203. It was a great experience. I went into the class with little to no knowledge on Haitian Creole and he made me able have whole conversations in creole! In 203 we talk a lot about Haiti's culture and that allows you to learn a whole new set of words and phrases. Would definitely recommend you take!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I highly recommend this course for anyone interested in Haiti's history and language. Each session is filled with rich content that keeps you engaged and encourages active participation. The atmosphere is fun and dynamic, making learning enjoyable. By the end of the course, you'll leave with a deeper understanding of Haiti and its language.

Jacques Pierre is very knowledgeable about language, history, and news. He teaches students material that they will not find in a traditional academic book. I was able to work with him thanks to an independent study funded through the FLAS Department of Education grant. I encourage every graduate student who studies the Caribbean to work with him.

He is a great Creole teacher. You will learn to read, speak and write in Haitian-Creole very quickly. You have a lot of homework but you can work on it at your own pace Once you get into the 200-level classes, there's a lot more focus on speaking. The class also teaches about Haitian culture. I highly recommend taking it!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: A very helpful class if you are truly trying to learn Creole. Make sure you pay attention and do the readings because you do not focus on speaking a lot, it just assumed that as you go along you will pick up on words and be able the speak more fluently. He calls on people a lot and asks a lot of questions.

A phenomenal class and professor. He is one of the best language instructors I have had. After the first term, I already had an elementary understanding of the language. While his classes are intense - you always have to be engaged and ready to participate - this is an extremely effective way to learn.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment:
The class was good. You can tell Prof. Pierre cares and wants people to learn the language. I will say, class did move fast at times even for 101. Pay attention. He is available to help you before and after class as well. If you put in genuine effort, no way you can fail this class.

disclaimer: i put a difficulty of 2 as i have prior background

Prof. Pierre has the best method for language learning. I felt I've never learnt so much in just four months. He is also amazing with Zoom, so the class was dynamic and good even during these Covid times. He really loves to teach and he engages students with the contents of the class! He has inspired me to continue learning creole with him!!!

Jacques was incredibly supportive in and outside of class - he truly wants students to succeed. I came away from the class inspired by his deep appreciation for the culture, and excited to continue practicing the language. Even in one semester, I developed a strong foundation in Creole that allowed me to hold my own while traveling in Haiti.

Jacques is a great teacher! All assignments were available online from the first day of class, so there is no surprise as to when the next assignment will be due. He teaches the course with the philosophy that language acquisition is best when worked on daily. Thus, there were homework assignments 3x a week.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I knew some French going in, so keep that in mind. But he did a good job of keeping his Creole simple enough that newcomers could understand (with time). Sometimes lectures seemed a little tangential, but they still lent insight into Haitian culture and Haitian issues.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: I think deep down Jacques is a nice guy, but his lectures are incredibly unorganized and all in creole (and for an intro class? ridiculous how you're expected to understand any of it). Doesn't have clear grading criteria at all. Seemingly much easier if you know French.

If you know French, it's an easy A. If not, be prepared to work very hard. It gets progressively more difficult and different from French as the year goes on. Jacques is hilarious and cares a lot about Haiti and Kreyol. 10/10 would recommend this class to anyone who speaks a lil French.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Hilarious--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Jacques is a great professor. After one semester, I have conversational knowledge of Haitian Creole and a healthy understanding of Haitian culture and some of Haiti's issues. Jacques' passion for his country manifests in the way he teaches - each class consists of discussion - in Creole - of the textbook materials and Haitian culture.

Jacques is awesome. Not only did we learn Haitian Creole, but we also discussed Haitian culture. He is accessible - I went to office hours all the time. His passion for his country and his country's language emerges clearly through his teaching. Classes consisted mostly of discussion in Creole of the textbook material and of Haitian culture.
He is an awesome professor!! Haitian Creole is a beautiful language and he made learning it less challenging and exciting. I highly recommend anyone to take his classes
He is just a great professor! He makes learning a new language less challenging and fun! highly recommend anyone to take his classes
So nice and genuinely wants you to learn the language and use your skills in cultural contexts

Dr. Izatt used to have a reputation of giving a lot of homework, and seemed to realize it so he toned it down a bit. He's genuinely a nice guy, and is more than willing to help out if you need it. Not the most clear guy in lecture, although he is easy to understand. He often times says things wrong, but its not that big of a deal. Take it with him.

Dr. Izatt often wrote things incorrectly on the board or said things incorrectly in lecture. He often confused himself during lecture, but was able to clarify questions after class. Willing to help, but not always available (traveling). His tests were inconsistent though. TAs were life saviors.
I can't believe these great reviews... we're we in the same class. And I like how the other guys mentioned the terrible TAs. Amen

The best professor I have had so far. Izatt is a very effective, clear teacher. He really explains the material very well, and you certainly learn a whole lot by the end of the semester. The homeworks are very long, but there isn't a lab so it balances out in the end. Tests are straight forward if you do and understand the homework.

Great professor, very clear in class, workload was reasonable. He has a wonderfully sarcastic sense of humor. My only criticism is his choice of TA's.  The TA for the design course (Kenny) was a real jerk - arrogant, condescending, and useless.  I've heard the TA for 171 this semester (Fall 2008) is even worse.

Not a great professor. He is disorganized which just isn't acceptable for a design class. This is probably easier than the other design classes but his TAs are jerks (especially Kenny) and all have an air of arrogance that doesn't make sense for a learning environment. I would not recommend it.

Lectures were kinda dull, but if you can get past that, he genuinely cares about his students and provides good examples in class. Homeworks are very hard, but the TA is great at explaining things, so go to the help sessions!
My favorite class and professor.  He is very conscientious and accomodating, and his lectures are really clear.  Pretty easy grader.

very helpful and accessible to students by email/available to meet outside of class (although even he himself says he's not always at his own office hours). Tests are very fair.  Not many example problems worked in class made things more difficult but not an impossible course by any means.
Great Prof!  The course is challenging though, pretty fair
Wow--what a jerk at times.  He liked to tell us how we didn't work as hard as he did as an undergrad.  Could have done without taking his course.

Assigned a lot of reading that was tested but also was genuinely interesting. Quizzes included both individual and group components. Stay attentive in class, keep up with the readings, and form a study group before exams to be well prepared. She was an incredibly kind professor!

102 was an interesting course but boring. Wernegreen's connections allowed her to bring in a few cool guests and we took a really interesting class field trip (my first since early HS). I attended few lectures but watched all of the recordings on 1.5x speed. Lots of writing but graded easily, they can tell if you put in the effort.

GENOME148FS is simply one of the best FOCUS classes offered at Duke. The course is divided into 5 engaging modules where students can work collaboratively to complete assignments, present readings, and discuss answers for team-based tests. Wernegreen does an amazing job lecturing the intricacies of symbiosis, and is very knowledgeable in her field!

Prof. Wernegreen is a wonderful teacher and truly cares about her students. Enviro102 was very light from a courseload perspective and it was extremely easy to get a good grade if you just do the work

TAKE IT! An amazing way to get your NS credit. Class is extremely low-workload (optional readings + discussion response once a week) and very interesting, and a field trip and guest speakers at the end are super fun. Jen is genuinely so caring and compassionate, and you can tell how much she cares about the environment! Go to lecture.

I had been wanting to take this class for a while with Professor Wernegreen but after spending a semester in the class she fell short of my expectations. Her lectures are not stimulating and sometimes the information can get lost because of it. I think the best part of this class is the discussion component since it is where you actually learn.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: One of the best professors I've had. Course is structured really well, she cares about students. Readings can be heavy sometimes but overall fine. For RATs, answer the questions she gives along with the reading assignments. Lots of extra credit opportunities. Final paper was great, she's always willing to help.

Took the class when it was S/U. The course is not hard at all but Wernegreen is such a sweet individual and truly cares about her students' wellbeing. I wish I had been able to take it in person with her.

I took ENVIRON102 when it was online, so I didn't get to interact with Prof Wernegreen often but she is so soft-spoken and kind. She truly understands the amount of stress students endure from other classes and commitments, and she makes sure the material is diverse and guest lecturers are interesting. Definitely recommend if you need an NS credit!

Wernegreen is AMAZING. This class was super great. Lectures are interesting, tons of guest speakers, really interesting discussions. Exams are lengthy but relatively straightforward and easy. Wernegreen is super accessible and approachable, caring deeply about you doing well. Fun extra credit and really engaging. Fantastic class!
Professor Wernegreen is a genuinely nice person. Her lectures were good, clear, and interesting. The class is easy if you do the required work.

Jen is amazing! She's really kind, understanding and SO easy to approach. I don't think the material was difficult; it was just A LOT of memorization. Grading was really fair and there's plenty of extra credit !! Don't really need to go to class to pass b/c she posts the slides, but had pop quizzes in class sometimes.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Jen is the most caring professor I've had at Duke. She genuinely wants her students to learn and enjoy the material in the process. Jen offers lots of feedback and is very willing to help/answer questions you may have. She frequently goes out of her way to make sure that we understand everything that's going on. Overall, nice and knowledgeable!
Lots of scientific article readings. Jen is incredibly sweet!

Professor Wernegreen was a great professor whose seminar-style, team-based-learning class was both engaging and informative. The structure (doing reading outside of class then discussing in teams in class) was very helpful for deeper understanding of the material, and graded coursework was fair and varied.

Jen is very sweet and genuinely cares about students engaging and learning from the material. Class is split into teams for the semester. Regular small assignments don't take too much work. More than willing to meet outside of class and frequently asks for feedback, which she incorporates into the course. Very reasonable and clear grader.

Professor Siegel is such a wonderful professor! I took the class as part of the "Peace or War?" constellation [not PubPol297] and enjoyed the seminar-style class. Great lecturer, although her lectures cover a lot of material in a short amount of time. She is very supportive and wants her students to do well. I would definitely take her class again.

Incredibly knowledgeable professor with a deep bench of knowledge relating to intelligence history. Extremely engaging lectures and very accessible outside of class. Would 100% recommend the course to anyone. Fundamentally changed how I see the world.
Truly captivating, changed my perspective on history. She's great at blending history and public policy. Get coffee with her and get to know her for sure.

Professor Siegel is a really great lecturer. Speaks very quickly, so make sure to take notes, but lectures are very engaging and interesting. Tests aren't too challenging, but you need to have a strong understanding of the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Siegel is great, very knowledgable + nice. But, she talks for 85 minutes in a 75 minute class if you get what I mean. You cannot look away. Write it all down. Needed for exams. That is kinda annoying, wish we talked more. Get VERY clear understanding of what the assignment for paper is...gave one set on instructions then graded something else.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: It was an interesting class and I felt the readings were generally applicable to class. However, its graded on very few papers so make sure to start them early. Lectures were mainly discussion based. Overall, I felt like she genuinely wanted her students to succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Siegel is incredibly compassionate, knowledgable, and generally excellent. I had her pubpol302 class during (I believe) her first year at Duke. Essay grading standards were a little unclear, but I think that's just because it was a new class for her. The lectures are discussion-based and participation is mandatory, so make sure you read.

Siegel is awesome in 509! She is an expert in intelligence history and she knows her stuff. I would highly highly recommend 509 for a super interesting and engaging pubpol elective, especially for the upper 400+ elective. Only assignments are 2 essays and 2 "exams". Take advantage of office hours/FLUNCH and get to know her... she's awesome!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very flexible and loves meeting with students. Great lecturer.
Super friendly professor and be willing to help you all things

Pretty chill half-credit class, ok even if you miss a few lectures. But decently engaging material, and this class will be pretty helpful for 360 and 432. (also good to take along with) Nice professor, pretty clear in explanations.

Professor Reiter was great! Clear lectures, accessible outside of class, clear grading, and reasonable midterm and homework. Was cool to understand the math behind regression. As long as you put in the work and keep up, this class is very manageable.

Reiter is a nice guy, teaches the class well, and is very accessible outside of class. Unfortunately, the grading and tests are ridiculously unfair and he grades very harshly on exams without a curve. If you make a small error your exam could drop half a letter grade. I was 1000% Sure deserved an A in the class and got screwed by his harsh grading

Reiter is clearly very intelligent and well respected in the field. He explained the content well even though lectures could be a bit dry. He was always super accessible outside of class and you will do well if you go to office hours.

Jerry is a great professor and is very accessible outside of class. He's always willing to help students and answer your questions in detail until you get it. The material for this course was not super super challenging, but the tests are graded out of few points so if you get one question wrong it can affect your overall grade by a lot.

An ideal professor. I struggled with this course but he was very accessible and helpful at office hours, and in lectures he was super engaging and excited to tell you about his field. He gives you everything he can to help you succeed.

Excellent professor and class. Great lecturer and also posts very useful R scripts. Clear grading criteria, very helpful in office hours, and also teaches very important/useful real-life skills about regression. I definitely recommend taking STA210 with Prof. Reiter.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Would take again

reviews.comment: Grade is composed of 35% homework, 50% tests, and 15% final project. Tests are very short, but missing one part of a problem will hurt your grade by 10%. The median was in the 70's for both tests. Reiter is a very energetic lecturer, but a lot of the material can be learned by reading the slides and going over the scripts covered in class.
Super energetic and caring! If you want to take a stats class, take it with him.

Jerry is a life savior. I'd really gg for this course if it weren't for him. He is always willing to talk to students outside of class and treats everyone equally, regardless of whether you are doing the major or not. Lecture is extremely engaging and fun. With him, it's hard not to do well as long as you have the interest and stamina.

Reiter is always very enthusiastic, and he really tried to make things interesting, but the subject of surveys in general was just not very fascinating for me. Definitely don't take this class if you are more interesting in statistical modeling. If you have a solid foundation in basic probabilitystatistics though, it should be a relatively easy A.

Took this 2 years ago, one of the best classes I've taken at Duke. You learn to code in R (bit of a learning curve at first for everyone, so expect to put in time in the course) and you learn how to analyze data. The class is great at pairing lecture and examples, including examples with code and R output in lecture. Very energetic . Very nice.

WORST CLASS! Do not take a class with Reiter: you are guaranteed not to learn. He drowns you in meaningless assignments then destroys your grade with impossible exams. Absolutely do not take a class with him unless you don't mind losing your sanity.

Reiter is very peppy, which makes people think he's a good professor. But he doesn't actually teach, so I'm confused why his ratings are so positive. Everything is out of class as students work on homework assignments that usually take over ten hours to complete. Not worth the time.

Dr. Reiter has a fundamental disconnect with the intellectual level of his students. His lectures are very difficult to follow and he provides no background information on complex ideas. I hardly learned anything and got a bad grade to boot.

Very practical class, but also very time consuming. Not conceptually hard but hw is a lot of work. Reiter is a wonderful teacher - super smart, funny, helpful, and attractive. The class will not be easy, but you will learn a lot and have the privilege to look at his beautiful face twice a week. Definitely recommend if you're willing to do the work.

One of the best professors I've had at Duke. His approach to statistics is laid back and thoughtful, instead of being formulaic. He explains the concepts behind the material, instead of just telling you how to do it--he wants you to think about how stats applies to the real world. Office hours are incredibly helpful, too.
Dr. Reiter is a truly wonderful professor!  He is extremely helpful and his tests/grading are very fair.  I highly recommend this professor for stat 101!  P.S. I think he's hot :)

Definitely a great professor.  I had no interest in stat and needed it for a QS.  He is engaging in lecture and very helpful.  He does everything he can to help his students do well.  If you have to take stat, take a class with prof reiter.
One of the best, if not the best, classes I've ever taken -- also one of the hardest.  This is the class that turned me on to statistics and made subsequent stats classes intelligible to me.

he is a very nice guy, understanding. But you really do have to work hard for this class (hw, projects, outside work etc). His lectures are pretty helpful, if you can bear it. He really cares about his students and very accessible outside of class. If you are prepared to work hard, take his classes!
SOLID CLASS, GETS A LOT HARDER IN THE SECOND HALF... MUCH MORE MATH
This class is boring, but I don't think there would be any other teacher who could teach this crap as well as Reiter. Good guy, down to earth, but boring info. Plus it's kinda tricky. Take 101.

While Prof Reiter is enthusiastic and helpful, his teaching leaves much to be desired. He is unclear, and his lectures are completely useless. Do expect to work hard and learn everything on your own. He will quiz you on material he has yet to cover, and can be irritating in other similar ways.

Jerry is a great professor, but if you haven't taken AP then expect to work really hard in order to succeed.  He will bend over backwards to make sure that he can help his students and everything he assigns (even labs) serve a purpose.

Sure Reiter is enthusiastic, but he is one of the worst teachers I've ever had. My high school statistics teacher blew him out of the water. His lectures are completely useless and seem like they're longer than the unbearable 75 minutes that they actually are.
amazing professor.  one of those "wow, this is what a college teacher is supposed to be like" kind of guys.  just make sure you stay on top of your hwork.  but work aside he is worth it.
very enthusiastic, nice guy always wants to help.  Expectations are very clear and you always know what to expect
Great professor, very engaging, the class was a lot of fun. Tries hard to make sure people understand the key concepts. Will even teach how to be a 'dark ninja master'
Good Guy, Fellow Dukie, Not bad, probably easier than 101
One of my favorite professors ever.  Makes the course really fun.  Great energy.  All around great guy.
Really nice guy, very helpful, great professor.
No Comments

The instructor seems overly self-important, which is pretty ironic given how frequently their comments miss the mark. It didn't take long for the class to notice they appeared threatened by a few of the stronger students. I'd steer clear of this course unless you're fine putting up with snide, cutting comments. more trouble than it is worth.

Despite their oversized sense of self-importance, they frequently seem quite clueless. The whole class could see they were unsettled by a few of my peers. Unless you're ready for nonstop sarcasm, I'd avoid enrolling in their course as it just isn't worth the trouble.
joined an administration and let in 20 million people across an open border. an awful lecturer to boot. thanks professor!

This person has an inflated ego, which is amusing considering how often they come across as unintelligent. It was obvious to the whole class that they felt intimidated by some of my classmates. Avoid taking their class unless you're ready to deal with sarcastic remarks. It's really not worth the hassle.
Extremely ineffective.
He was and still is a shill.
Difficult to understand what is fact and what is opinion, but if you just swallow his politics and pretend, you can do well.
Poor communication and grading standards.

I've never rated a professor before, but Dr. Jentleson is the best professor I've had at Duke. On top of his incredible experience in the foreign policy world (worked at State Department and was a close advisor to Al Gore), he is also an amazing educator. You can tell he cares about each and every student deeply. Could not recommend him more.
Awful.
He is surprisingly narrow-minded as a globalization professor...

Prof Jentleson is a fantastic professor & mentor. He truly cares for his students and is extremely respected/knowledgable on foreign policy & fed policymaking. I'm thankful I took 301 w/ him, not just bc I learned a lot, but bc he has been invested in my success since. He is the kind of professor that you came to Duke to take advantage of, so do it

This guy has a huge ego which is funny because he sounds incredibly stupid most of the time. He very clearly felt threatened by some of my classmates, and it was apparent to the entire class. We all made fun of him for it behind his back. Don't take a class from him unless you're willing to put up with snide comments. It's just not worth it.

Really awesome guy. He has tons of experience in his field and is willing to talk about individual student interest. He shaped curriculum around current politics. Participation and 4 memos are pretty much your whole grade. great class/guy
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Hated him

One of the most rewarding classes I've ever taken.  You will have to put in a ton of work to do well in this class, but it's just a matter of him pushing you to be your best.  Don't expect an A for anything less than true A-quality work.  Aside from Feaver, you won't get another professor at Duke with his level of foreign policy experience.
Jentleson is a cool guy, and has a lot of experience with foreign policy. I don't really know why he was "teaching" this class, Carnes could have done it by himself. He's fine, though.

He is at the top of his field both academically and in the policymaking world, but still has a clear passion for teaching.  Very organized and supremely knowledgeable.  You will read a lot and he will not give you an A for less than excellent work; that said, if you're interested in IR or related subjects, you need to take a class with Prof J.

A little boring, but if you're interested in international relations, you may want to take 114 with him- he uses a lot of those kinds of examples.  To get a feel for what the content of his course is like, visit GradeGuru.com, go to advance search under the main search box, type in the course name and select Duke.  You can see what I've posted from

Prof. Jentleson is a great guy, and the class is interesting. Feedback on papers often were very helpful. Grading can be tough. Reading is extensive, and you'll find yourself in a mess at the end of the semester if you haven't done any. Lectures interesting, though 2 1/2 long can be tedious, but that's the nature of most classes that long anyway.
No Comments

This class was interesting initially, but the topics became dull after a while. Jhun was a knowledgeable professor and was willing to help outside of class. Her lectures however were hard to follow at times, especially since she did not use slides and would write in small handwriting. You are graded on 3 papers, without a rubric.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Although I found the material dry at times, Prof. Jhun teaches it enthusiastically. She's also very willing to give feedback outside of class and help out in any way possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Jhun was a great professor, I enjoyed her enthusiasm and casual spirit. She made a philosophy class enjoyable. The content can be dull at times but overall a good class, would recommend.

Professor Jhun was an above average professor, but this class was not- lectures were dull and hard to pay attention, and material just wasn't engaging. However, an easy A- / A if put in the time and effort for the essays, and being able to miss class pretty much whenever was nice. Overall a meh Econ elective, wouldn't take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I was a huge fan of Dr. Jhun's philosophy of economics class. She is super helpful and a really good lecturer. She covered topics in micro, macro, game theory, and philosophy of science. If you love economics and philosophy, this class is for you- and it isn't super time-intensive. However, if you don't like philosophy, I'd caution against it.

One of the best Mathematicians I've ever met. Lectures are super organized and exams are extremely easy. You learn a lot without any threat to your GPA. However, you need to wait for a long time until next time he offers MATH 356.

personally disagree with the bad ratings. jianfeng lu gave fantastic lectures and reasonable HWs (3-4 hrs/wk). exams were long, but most problems were basically copies of HW problems, and letter grades were curved well despite harsh raw scores. attending lecture and doing all HWs sufficed for a good grade, and you learn a lot from great teaching
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The course can best be described as domestic terrorism

didn't know what my grade was the entire semester until 20 minutes ago and the final was three days ago, assigned hw during reading period and gave awful exams, not to mention the class is 90% midterm/final and 10% homework. office hours consisted of “check the textbook”, convinced the positive review was the TA or Lu himself
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Just don't. Do not take this class. Take 353 or literally anything else no amount of stress and frustration is worth it, you will be constantly grasping at like cryptic straws Prof Lu lays out for his class and exams. Final was graded before half of the homework and I left without knowing the grading scheme at all(syllabus is 50 words long). Don't.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Lectures focus too much on derivations, Homeworks are unnecessarily long and repetitive, exams are completely unlike any of the material he teaches and do not match the course structure at all, incredibly pretentious lecturer, grades insanely harshly on exams which are comprised of 1 midterm and 1 final and make up 90% of the grade.

As someone who hates to speak poorly about the Duke Math Dept, this prof really shouldn't be teaching such a fundamental course to the major, the grading scale is nuts and the partial credit scene is wild, no standard rubrics and insanely test heavy. Great lectures, despite some minor mistakes and awkward moments. Ditto to whoever said headache…

Good lecturers, but horrific grading scale. Would provide no practice for midterms or finals and expect the class to perform well. Occasionally made backhanded comments like “oh this is obvious” or oh this is so easy when no one understood. Wouldn't recommend as an undergrad AT ALL.
This guy should not be allowed to teach undergrads. Final worth 50% midterm worth 40%. Would use textbook for EVERYTHING. Actually my biggest headache.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Brilliant mathematician, great experience to learn from him! Class was challenging but office hours were helpful, also helped that content was interesting.

Too smart to be teaching this class. Final exam was 45% and it seemed like he was expecting that we already knew a bunch of stuff. For things that no one could answer he would say things like "is the answer too obvious" and such. I recommend someone different for math356
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: He is the best CS professor at DKU. Just do your best, and you will definitely succeed in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Really great！Recommend for all CS and DS students in DKU

Tries to condense 15 weeks of material into a 7 week session, had a mental breakdown last year and had questionable behavior on his class and with other students/faculties. Teaching is solid but need to be aware if he breaks down again....
He is one of the best teaching professors at DKU. He is very knowledgeable and patient. If you want to build a strong foundation in CS, take his classes.

Be prepared well to do lots of homework if you want to take the course. Don't be afraid of spending time on this course. Prof. Long is very very very kind, nice and caring. Love from DKU! Prof. Long, yyds!

Extremely hard class. Everything came from 20 weeks of Coursera lectures compressed into 7 weeks. Workload is too much to the point where you can't even attend office hours to truly learn the subject. There is quite a bit of extra credit and exam curve so even with failing exam grades, an A- is still possible. Traumatized from this class...

The lectures were poor quality as professor lifted all the content straight off of Coursera. Workload was also very intense, a new homework assignment (about 4-8 coding exercises) was assigned every day we had lecture in addition to projects. I would recommend having some familiarity with programming/java before taking this class.
Love from DKU

I think Prof. Jiang is a nice guy. But there are a lot of discontinuity in the course with the lecture and the assignment and test. Plus, writing code on an iPad is simply not clear or effective. He usually cannot explain things to the point and thus make people confused. Also, there are so many open ended group project which is disorienting.

Don't even bother taking this class if you don't have prior coding experience. By week two you're basically coding minesweeper and the workload is almost laughably intense. But if you can get past that, the prof is nice and wants you to succeed. He is always available.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: workload nightmare

Though this course is helpful and Prof Long is nice, his course is known as one of the toughest courses in Duke Kunshan. So, I would suggest that if anyone wants to take the course, make sure to make full use of the tutoring sessions and ask other people questions. This can make your study effective.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Excellent professor! I learn quite a lot from this course. Very worth your time. If you truly want to gain a good foundation for computer science, definitely go for it!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Too much coding assignment. Not friendly for new learners. Also, he can't answer questions clearly and most od time just repeat the content in videos
Prof Long is a great teacher. But his course has very few grading criteria. Also, most of the post-class assignments were little relevant to the class material.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Jiang is one of the most prepared professors you can find at DKU. He comes directly from industry so you will gain a lot of skills you can use for interviews or an actual job, but also strong theoretical knowledge. My problem was with the grading system. The exam was half of our grade and the post-class assignments felt unnecessary.

Prof. Long is a terrific computer scientist and taught us great many things in the course of 7 weeks. However he was mostly inaccessible for online students and the lectures were rarely recorded and available for students who cannot attend in person. The final exam was a huge percentage of the final grade, but we had no midterm/ practice problems.

Hey guys, I really love this professor. If you indeed want to learn substantial & true computer knowledge, you definitely need this. Prof. long is a hardcore computer programmer, so the course content & assignment is very heavy, but really worth to do. You may need spend 50+ hours per week to learn this course, but you will learn a lot!

He is really the best professor I ever met, he is so nice and he would answer students' questions late till midnight. Though the course is tough, and homework is heavy, you can get a good score as long as you are willing to pay.
Great class. Little structure.
What a guy. Truly.

Loved taking his FOCUS class! I had never taken philosophy before, so I will say the readings can be rough at the start. But as long as you can ask questions and try your best to discuss, you will get an A. Super fun to talk to during office hours!
Funny, smart, super talented professor. I would definitely recommend taking his class.
Cool guy, class was a little boring at times though. If you're particularly interested in ethics, you might not be stimulated as often.

Very fun and easy class! Homework was very easy but sometimes thought provoking. Would recommend and want to take more from him in the future. Also a great balance if you have an otherwise difficult schedule.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Summers is a great teacher. His ethics 101 class was very insightful and not difficult. We were assigned readings for homework and then would have group and class discussions based off of the readings in class. Assignments were straight-forward and simple. The final is based off of all the readings from the class. Would recommend!

Professor Summers is great. While I don't think the subject of Ethics is really for me, he actually cares about his students and will always go the extra mile. Definitely take any class you can with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: engaging discussions and projects, well-selected readings, definitely a highlight of my semester. cares about students, really receptive to feedback, and contemplative/insightful person. highly recommend
my favorite prof. if you are able to take a course with him, do it.

I look forward to this class every week & thoroughly enjoy the in-class discussions. There are lengthy readings to be completed before every class, but they are interesting & the conversation that follows is always engaging/thought-provoking. Professor Summers creates the perfect environment to deepen your understanding. Rat beings follow rat laws.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: My favorite professor since I've been at Duke. Really cares about his students and ensures that class is always interesting and engaging.

I took his ethics seminar for my writing 101 course, and he was really great. Class was generally for open discussion, with not much outside work besides the main capstone project. He's definitely open to different opinions, but if you're too vague, he'll most likely have you keep elaborating. Overall great guy, would highly recommend.

This is a philosophy course, but Summers made sure that the class was not intimidating. Accessible and approachable, is patient in talking you through your papers. The three graded essays allow you to scope your essay however you like. Summers gives you the freedom to do your papers at your own pace. Also really good at choosing readings.

Took his class called "what do we owe each other?" as my first-year seminar, and really enjoyed it. He assigned short readings and writing assignments every week, as well as 2 papers building ethical arguments. He doesn't cold call, and leads discussion very well, which to me was ideal. I'm not interested in studying ethics, but loved his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: He's super chill and gets that the reading is tough so you don't really need to be super tryhard in understanding it fully. Be sure to participate in class anyways because the course is graded on two essays and participation
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: If you can take a class taught by him DO IT! This is the only class, ever, that I consistently left happier then I entered. He is an amazing professor who enjoys teaching and makes philosophy interesting. The class is almost entirely discussion based which is intimidating, for those with no prior knowledge, but over time you get used to it!

Professor Summers is clear, accessible, caring, and funny. I really enjoyed him as a professor, but the class was sometimes frustrating -- there were no lectures, so it was entirely discussion-driven, meaning that it was confusing for those without a philosophy background. There were little-to-no homework assignments. Overall, I would take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Really cool teacher. Cares about you as a person. Essays dont feel pointless. He cares more about ideas and you engaging critically with material than pointless formalities. TAKE HIS CLASS!!!!
Great at explaining the nuances of arguments, won't let you get away with just being vague. Hard to know which minor assignments were important sometimes, but not too much work anyway.

Summers is the man, and as long as you show up and contribute to class, you'll be fine. I went out of my way to ask for more help with his major assignments and he was really helpful, made time for me, and my grade was better for it. He's a genuinely nice and interesting guy.

Professor Summers is a very interesting,  funny, soft-spoken, chill guy. He is always willing to meet outside of class if needed and will go out of his way to help students with anything. The class can be a tad bit philosophical, but Professor Summers makes it interesting. The books he chose for reading were very intriguing and contemporary.

He's really funny and nice to all the students. The class is somewhat philosophical, but you will get a lot out of it. It isn't hard to make a good grade, and there are two papers (5 and a 10-15), but he gives you plenty of time to get the work done. Classes are very chill, with a usual discussion on an article.
I would not take a class with Prof. Summers again. He is a cool guy and also very funny, but lectures are rather boring and too philosophical. I found the feedback I received in my papers
Very interesting class, sometimes a bit redundant. Dr. Summers is a very interesting guy, soft-spoken, and funny at times. Very philosophy heavy, not too much writing.
He's a great professor and the material was very interesting
Genuinely cares about everyone doing well in class. Generally an easy grader as long as you put in a good amount of effort.
He is just such an amazing teacher.

He's very professional, especially for his first year of teaching. I really like his teaching style and how he arranges the seats to make it easy to interact with classmates. He provides extra grammar materials to help us understand better. He's also caring and funny and honestly one of the best 101 professors I've had. +Not that strict on grading.
I have no idea why people are giving her such a high rating. She's not a caring professor and will sometimes ignore your questions. The only good thing is that the attendance is not mandatory.
Very nice professor, pretty solid lectures. She is super kind and willing to help. She has a very clear grading policy, and extra credits are easy to earn.

Prof. Jiajia is goated, super kind and helpful outside of class when I had questions + very clear about what was going to be on the tests with extra credit and practice tests to help prepare. I'm really happy I got to take this course with her.
Her class is really hard but she is a good lecturer, and cares about students. Her curve is "I will grade more generously on the test" so there is basically no curve.

Very sweet and friendly prof. Not the best lecturer; spoke softly and rushed through some tough content. Teaches way better during office hrs, which are an absolute necessity if you want to do well on exams (lots of proofs and intuition tested). Not too much HW with lenient grading. Put in the effort and you will learn a lot and be rewarded.

Lecture and pacing are HARD without a level of math maturity, but if you put in the effort consistently, go to OH, and clearly try to keep up, and NOT just before exams, she is the most caring and patient professor who will make sure you don't do poorly. Exams are very similar to her lecture notes, and in OH she makes it clear what's tested.

The professor herself said in class that she "was not good at English". Explanations in class are poor, and notes are unclear. Jiajia Yu seemed uninterested in both the subject material and her students as individuals. I would not recommend taking this as an elective when there are similar courses at Duke that cover the material better.

Jiajia is the most kind professor I've had. I learned a lot about optimization and how mathematicians characterize machine learning algorithms. There are no courses on optimization techniques, and think this course is probably the closest to it.
Such a fun class! Very nonjudgmental environment and you get to explore your interests however you like. I definitely would recommend!!

I hoped that film editing would be a fun and easy course, and it didn't disappoint. Jim runs a laid-back class; weekly workload was usually one reasonable editing assignment + some short reading. Most days we watched cool film clips and had good discussions. Not much feedback if you don't ask for it, but Jim is always happy to talk about your work.
Great Teacher, Great Class, highly recommend.
Very easy class, you learn tons about editing and watch movies completely differently. Highly recommended, be sure to do your work and you'll be fine.
Class was very easy and simple. You get what you want out of it. Grading policy is very lax and laid back... as is Jim. Professor is very easygoing and chill. Obvious GPA booster. Highly recommended.

Prof Haverkamp is a really nice guy and makes class very interesting. He is geniunely interested in every students projects and very understanding when it comes to technical difficulties in filming, etc. Overall, great class to take. I would highly recommend taking any film class with him.
The exam can be calculation-heavy. She makes it clear how certain results are applied to real-world situations.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Jing An is an excellent and enthusiastic teacher. The materials are hard, but as long as you work hard, you will be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The worst professor I've had in the math department. Lectures were dense and difficult, questions were answered dismissively, and she was inaccessible. The final (which was identical for all sections) looked nothing like our classwork, and her finals and homework were difficult and unlike what she explained in class.

She teaches exactly as it is in the textbook. The only problem is that she glosses over concepts that are crucial for the course. Her homework assignments are helpful but very lengthy. In general, this class is not difficult, but she moves quickly.
her tests are more calculation-based than concept-based, so get good at integrals and trig. it doesn't matter as much if you actually know anything about differential equations.

Jie Liu gets a bad rep as a lecturer and it's true he is quite hard to understand but he is also so kind. It is still very possible to get an A even with him as your professor. Most of the tests aren't even based on the lectures anyways but discussion section problems so if you self study a little it won't be too bad.

Do not take a chem class by him. In lecture, he does not show his work, speaks too quietly, and unfortunately most students could tell couldn't understand him with his thick accent. Not worth taking a class if hes the teacher, though hes
very sweet.

This professor is nonsensical in lecture to the point you will never get an answer from him, or he will fail to explain basic concepts. Almost all students have left going to lecture and watch recordings of other professors, as his lectures are near pointless. stay away!

This course is already ridiculous, but if you survived fall semester of quantum, you'll probably survive this spring. Easier, but certainly not clearer. To his credit, the exams are made much more doable, but dear lord is waiting for grades nervewracking with how unclear some things are.

The only way I did well in this class was going to office hours. You can succeed if you put in the time and the effort. However, expect to know everything that is on his slides and how to apply it. The texts are SIGNIFICANTLY x10 harder than the posted practice exams. Do the textbook problems and ask questions in office hours. Dr. Wu is very kind.

Dr. Liu is a nice person and incredibly knowledgeable in his field. That being said, this class was extremely dull and difficult. Tests were much harder than the practice ones posted, and lecture doesn't help as Dr. Liu seems confused by his own slides and believes the material is very easy and thus doesn't give further explanation.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Liu wasn't a great lecturer. A good deal of class time was spent watching him work through problems on the board then correcting them. I felt as though I needed to read the textbook before lecture in order to understand what he was trying to get across. That being said, he was pretty willing to meet one-on-one to discuss specific confusions.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He literally gets his own questions on exams wrong, has arbitrary grading, and has the most unclear lectures possible. You think you're doing well until he comes up with some obscure reason you aren't, and when you try and point out what he did was wrong he just laughs it off.

Dr. Jie Liu was, in all honesty. the worst teacher I have ever had in my Duke career. His lectures frequently contained errors in content and I quickly learned his lectures were a complete waste of time. His tests were jokes, requiring little less than 3 hours of studying the night before. Warning: there is a negative curve in the class.

Dr. Liu is a very poor lecturer. Material-wise this class is not that hard and the exams are straightforward if you take them seriously (I didn't). It can be harder than expected to get a high grade as the cutoffs can vary and are not transparent. I ended with over 92%, which was a B+ according to Dr. Liu.

Communication sucks and explanations create more questions than answers. The material itself is not too bad, but his grading is rough since points awarded are barely defined and mainly arbitrary to the grader. There are only three tests so there is no room for error, especially since that the cut off for an A- in the course is over a 90% avg.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Tests? Not many--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Dr. Liu (CHEM 210) is very friendly and helpful one-on-one. He's not the clearest lecturer though. Lab (25%), recitation (7.5%), Saplings (7.5%), 2 MTs + Final (60%). MT1 and the Final were quite easy provided you knew how to do the Saplings, MT2 was more difficult, but one of the two MTs got replaced. Decent amount of work but straightforward.

Dr. Liu is very nice, and, to his credit, exams are clear and passable. He tries his hardest, but he often appears unprepared for lecture. As a result, lectures can be long, confusing, and, sometimes, unbearable. Homework is not assigned, which is nice. Overall, not a very exciting course. The textbook is the gold standard.
Kind of bad

Dr. Liu is a genuinely nice guy- but just not a good lecturer. He's often quite hard to understand his English and his train of thought- but his tests were fair and he made sure you knew what would be on them. Most of your learning will have to come from the book.
Dr. Liu is a nice guy. Lectures are on powerpoints so it's very easy to go back and review. Pay attention in class and review in the test and you should do fine.

Very nice professor and very eager to help if you make the effort to go to office hours. Lectures consist of textbook material as well as random real-world application factoids he likes to throw in. Fortunately, he's clear on what's test and what's not. Overall, the class is not too difficult if you put in the effort, but be prepared to study hard.

Liu is a pretty nice guy. That being said, you can't rely on just the lectures. Go to them for an intro to the material (c'mon, don't be lazy). Then READ THE BOOK. Then go back to the lecture ppts and they'll make sense, plus they highlight what he thinks is important. Tests aren't bad, neither is the curve. A good class, as far as premed reqs go.

His lectures are pointless to attend. You have to teach yourself from the textbook but thankfully he follows the text book closely. He is hard to understand and says nothing of use during class. He just reads off slides.

Completely unhelpful and actually condescending when I asked him questions one-on-one. I learned way more from the book than from him. His tests were difficult. The class is doable but not fun, especially with him as a prof.

Liu is a nice guy, but be prepared for powerpoints (mostly screen-shots from the book) in lecture.  He added some of his own stuff that will be terrifying and incomprehensible (e.g. solid state chemistry), but he didn't end up testing us on it.  32 isn't fun, but it was definitely doable.

Doesnt teach the concepts at all, if you take his chem class, you are expected to teach yourself everything. lectures are incredibly dull and whatever is helpful from the lectures is directly from the textbook and he just recites the explanations. everything else in the lectures is completely useless and is mostly special applications

Professor Liu is awesome! He's always available during office hours and is super coolz and chillz even though he likes apple products. Tells important chemistry stories, brings pizza to class sometimes, and even lets us go early other times. Definitely take his classes!

Lectures were boring because he just read off the slides (which were based directly on the textbook). However, Liu was very friendly and funny (at least he tried to be). Most importantly, the tests were very reasonable/easy for a chem class. Class average was a lot higher than the other section. Highly recommend for Chem 32 (even for an 8:30).

Dr. Liu is a really nice guy. The class is some of the hardest material ever, but he is really jovial in lecture, and he encourages students with lots of partial credit on exams. Working problems with students is great, though he also often works proofs, which can easily lose you unless you're a whiz at math. Has some accent but is understandable.

Amazing professor! Cares a lot about his students and really wants to help you succeed. The class is super fun if you have friends in it. Also, a pretty easy A as long as you show up to every class and submit everything on time. Would definitely recommend taking this class!
Great professor! There is a little more work than was I had initially expected signing up for this class.

What a king. Took devising theater with him this semester and it was my favorite class. He consistently checked in with each of us and contributed to a fantastic collaborative dynamic. Take a class with him if you can - you won't regret it.

Awesome professor! Super funny, engaging, and insightful. Gives great direction and feedback. Taught lots of techniques that really helped me improve as an actor. You will get out of Johann's classes what you put into them. You have to do a good amount of reading, but that's typical for this course regardless of professor. Highly recommend!!!

Really funny and nice professor but gives so much homework and readings to prepare for class. Also gives an assignment or group project every week which also added onto the rest of the work. Would not take for an elective but would recommend taking if you are actually interested in linguistics.

Joan is the GOAT. Without a doubt the best professor from the Spanish department. He's hilarious, energetic, understanding, and his course on Spanish in the US is fascinating. It is definitely a lot of work (though the grading isn't harsh) but the content makes it interesting. I would take this course, or any course with Joan, again in a heartbeat.
Genuinely a great guy! This class was super interesting, and he catered the topics to what the students wanted. Would definitely take a class with him again.

Profe Munne is an absolute king and everything you want in a Spanish teacher. You'll actually learn Spanish but never feel embaressed for making mistakes. 204 is pretty easy, with 9 low-stress writings, online text book HW ($60), 3 tests and 3 boomalangs. Live Laugh, Joan Munne
Gem of a professor: super funny, thoughtful, and kind, and classes are always interesting.

If you're actually a native speaker (no "yo no sabo" losers), this class is an easy A. The course is heavily participation-based, and Munne is a fun professor who also gently corrects your grammar and intonation. There are a couple papers and group projects but nothing too stressful. As long as he sees you're trying, you'll do well in the class.

Joan is a very sweet man and is very passionate about what he teaches. There is a lot of busy work (article readings + answering questions). At the end of the semester, he assigns a lot of unnecessary projects that couldve easily been disbursed throughout the semester, which was very stressful. Overall, good class besides the final projects.

A decent amount of busywork and a fast pace especially if you've never taken Spanish before. However, Prof Munne is super accesible, nice, and caring. If you care about Spanish and give an effort you'll absolutley get an A.

!Él es increíble! He's one of the most caring professors I've ever had and he creates a class culture where it is comfortable to speak and learn muchísimo. Honestly, he makes it easy(er) to enjoy class at 8:30 every morning. As long as you are interested and care about learning Spanish, you can do pretty well.

Joan is a phenomenal professor. I took his abroad class and had the best time--the only class I've ever been excited to wake up early for. He makes class interesting and interactive, and is passionate about helping you learn. Best Spanish prof I've ever had, and in my top 5 professors ever. Participate and show interest, and you'll do well.

Joan is an incredibly kind and helpful professor. Always would give the student the benefit of the doubt and was a very fair, sometimes easy grader. Did assign a lot of readings but I was able to do well without reading that much. The guy really cares for his student and if you put in some effort you'll do great.

Spanish 302 (advanced Spanish grammar) was a very difficult class and it took a lot of work to get an A.  That being said, I would definitely recommend any class with Professor Munné.  He's extremely helpful, clearly outlines/explains what he expects, and is overall very comforting in a difficult subject environment.  Munné is great.

Incredible professor. Class was challenging, but he was willing to meet frequently and go over the smallest concepts. In addition to being a native speaker, he really gets the grammatical explanations. Gave study guides and review sheets that were exactly like the exams. Possible to do well if you put in the work. Homework was sometimes helpful.

Professor Munne was very responsive to how the class felt about a particular subject and his expectations were clear. There really isn't an excuse to do poorly in the class because he's the kind of professor that wants you to do well.

Prof Munne was a great teacher. He helps you out whenever you want to double check a translation and is always very clear. Be ready for group projects and working in teams. The class was fun and went by fast.
The Alicante 101102 program is not easy, but you will probably leave with an AA- if you put forth the effort! Best time of my life!
Great professor! Awesome guy, easily approachable. Native spanish speaker so obviously knows the language well, but also great at teaching a class and formulating assignments. Definitely recommend.

By far the best Spanish professor I've ever had, one of my favorite professors overall. Really nice, incredibly helpful and patient, willing to sit with you and work on a tiny concept forever until you get it. I don't recommend him for intro courses because he has high standards but as a 300+ level teacher he's fantastic.

Profesor Munne is excellent at teaching and is very enthusiastic in interacting with the class. It seemed like we were assigned with more work than the other sections did, but the homework really helps. I don't think he really liked me, but the class was enjoyable. It's not difficult at all if you put the work into it.

BEST SPANISH PROFESSOR AT DUKE. period. He's not an easy professor, he expects hardwork out of you but he also extremely helpful and teaches very well. Wish I could take his class again. If you can, do it!

Fantastic professor, great guy. Favorite Spanis teacher I've ever had, and I've had some good ones. Expects a lot out of you, especially with participation, but gives a lot in return. Office hours are very helpful. If you are minoring or majoring in Spanish, you would be doing yourself a disservice not to take a class with him at some point.

Best Spanish professor I've ever had. Period. I took his class as a part of the Spanish Intensive program in Alicante. The class was very intense, but Munne was always willing to help. He is a very difficult teacher, but if you are prepared to work the rewards are great. Very clear with lessons and expectations. Highly recommended!

Prof. Munne was a great teacher. I took his Spanish for Heritage speakers class and I can honestly say I got everything I wanted out of the class and more. He definitely helps you improve your spanish writing and grammar. He's a fair grader too. Overall great class!

Joan is amazing.  By far the best Spanish teacher I have had here at Duke (out of 6).  He asks for your participation and your commitment, but he brings it in return.  Always prepared, engaged, interested and on the ball.  Totally suggest a course with him.
Excellent Professor! Class is never boring. You will have a lot of work, but you will learn and it won't be boring.  Highly Recommend Joan!
Very Good Teacher. U will work, but u will learn tremendously.
Joan is an amazing professor!  I enjoyed his class much more than my other Spanish classes at Duke, and I learned more as well.
Very good teacher, but also very tough grader.

Joan is a great teacher, best I've had in the department, actually.  He speaks clearly and does really try to make his students understand.  I didn't find his grading excessively hard, actually, nor was his extraneous "work" demanding--it was more for clarity! Don't look a gift horse in the mouth.

Professor Munne definitely made spanish class interesting and kept his students engaged, but was a very difficult teacher and hard to please. He was very by the book and never cut his students any slack. No compassion, but good professor.

I don't know what you all are whining about. Joan is an excellent professor, keeps you engaged and interested and genuinely cares if you do well or not. I <3 Joan and anyone who doesn't is a whiner and STUPID.

Professor Munne is wonderful. My entire section loved him, enjoyed his class, and was very successful.  I would HIGHLY recommend him.  Everyone who posted negative things here must've had some other Joan Munne.

He IS a nice guy but he is also the hardest professor in the spanish department teaching the the first 4 introductory levels.  You will be doing AT LEAST twice as much work as all your other friends in Spanish.
I do not recommend this professor. He is a very hard grader, and makes class torturous.
DON'T TAKE MUNNE!
sucks, sucks, sucks
No Comments
Doesn't give a **** if he assigns too much work. Worst Spanish class I've ever had.
No Comments
she is very nice. i understand about her context, in words of her: "yah."
perfect, can't find anything bad about her
She is the beeeeeeest! Kind and lovely

sooooooo good
Wonderful professor
I love her very much
Junyi is one of the best language professors at DKU. She is kind and caring. If you work hard enough on your papers, you are highly likely to receive a high grade from her.

i loved professor werlin! she is SO knowledgeable(so it cant be a bit intimidating at first). there are a lot of assigned readings, but she gives a variety and i felt so educated after. class was mainly disucssion based and we had 2 papers. she allowed first drafts, and gave really helpful feedback. if you put in the effort, you will do well.

Professor Werlin is absolutely amazing!!!! I 100% recommend her class to anyone. She gives excellent feedback that helped me significantly improve my writing and critical thinking. She is so knowledgeable about everything related to the topic, cares about her students, and it has been an exceptional privilege to be able to learn from her.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Really did not enjoy this professor. Lots of reading, which I usually don't mind at all, but barely have time to properly discuss anything. Disorganized lectures which are mostly her talking at you + strict attendance policy. Exams and quizzes easy but came away overall with a bad taste in my mouth -- found her to be very condescending and rude.

I really enjoyed this class. You definitely need to be doing the reading as there were reading quizzes and quote identification on the midterm/final. Professor Werlin clearly cares a lot about what she is teaching and wants students to do well.

The class itself wasn't too difficult and you could get away with not doing the readings, but the grading in this class is super arbitrary. We had three papers that were each 20% of our grade but our first "paper" was a 15 minute timed paragraph in class that I had no idea was even graded. However, Prof Werlin is definitely very knowledgeable.
Professor Werlin may seem intimidating at first (and lowkey still does), but she is super nice! She is very knowledgable and extremely eloquent. Make sure to do the readings and speak up in class :)

Professor Werlin is very knowledgeable and really is a fascinating person. She makes lectures super interesting and respects her students. Midterm and final are fair. 2 papers with broad topics & a lot of creative freedom.

Professor Werlin is clearly very passionate about what she is teaching, which pushes you to engage with the material. Lots of reading, but it all served a clear purpose and gave a nice foundational context for the topic. Papers challenged you to really work on writing skills and tests were fair if you stayed up to date with readings and discussion.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Werlin is very knowledgeable and promotes great discussion among her students. I love the class itself, and the homework for each week is not that heavy (read a set of poems and an article then do a blog post) but can get long. Her paper prompts, however, are SUPER vague and really tough. She never gives you a rubric.

Almost all grading is done by TAs who seem to have an extremely strict rubric. Paper expectations somewhat unclear. Meeting for help was unhelpful. I felt frustrated and unable to meet their expectations.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Prof. Werlin is incredibly knowledgeable about Milton and poetry in general. While the workload and grading are fair, class lectures have been really illuminating as well. That being said, Milton is a challenging writer and writing essays on him can be very mind-boggling. But one should still take the class for how brilliant the writing is.
I took a First-Year Seminar: Shakespeare and Storytelling. I enjoyed the discussions and readings. Assignments were straightforward and I felt well-prepared for the papers. Great class!

Min Jun is an exceptionally sweet person, but lectures (directly from textbook) and exams (Midterm 1 much too hard) not great. Doesn't always answer Qs fully, little engagement with the class. Homework graded liberally, sometimes hard to determine exam focus. Too reliant on textbook. Need more examples. Some lectures end early, for better or worse.
I thought that he could have given slightly more relevant homework questions but overall, he explained concepts relatively well and grades very fairly and leniently.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very wholesome class, where he really cares about the students and content. Note the class is more about the theory of fluid dynamics than what the title actually says.

Respectfully, do not take this class. This professor gives tests that stray away from the homework and the lecture material. Additionally, he makes fun of his students for asking him questions during the lecture (if he accepts any questions at all), and he rarely takes the time to explain a concept people are confused on. Grades extremely tough.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Jun Yang is a great professor himself and is a super nice guy. He explains things clearly and his expectations and work load are very fair. However I must say that this course was super information heavy, and you are introduced to so many new concepts every lecture, that it is hard to manage remembering everything.

Class concepts are extremely difficult but the teacher was really good and the grading is very balanced and fair. Projects/homeworks matter a lot which is very helpful. For undergrad, would recommend 316, but this is doable

Prof. Jun Yang is very kind, approachable, willing to answer questions. His slides are amazing, and homework are well designed and reasonable. However, in his lectures, he can sometimes go too much into detail in explaining a slide, which makes you lose track of what's the big picture message.

Most charismatic and caring professor at Duke. He patiently helps students with debugging code and homework problems. Exams are reasonable and open-notes, and he curves the exam if the avg score is too low (

He is the best teacher I have ever met in my university life. He is quite responsible, and is always eager to help. He is a gentleman, and is always patient with his students. He is always eager to help even if you ask quite naive and stupid questions. He is the person who really loves his students. It's very lucky to be his student.
