Jun Yang is a wonderful human being and I absolutely love him. He is always willing to help and the class is graded very fairly. However, cs316 is so boring I wanted to rip my hair out. The exams test you on very specific details.
Lectures are good and he explains concepts well

Prof Yang really cares about students and is willing to help you with even the dumbest of questions. His voice is also very soothing lol. The cutoff for an A was a 93 which is very fair, and if you do the extra credit throughout the semester you should be fine for the course. The project is a lot, but you have all semester to do it.

Professor Yang is a great lecturer and his office hours are really helpful. He really cares about his students. Teaching and managing a course for 300+ people is difficult but he does the best he can. The person who posted about the extra credit and A cutoff posted before the cutoffs were released today, and it was a 93% which is very normal lol

Jun is one of the best CS lecturers I've had. Course content is paced well, with small examples to solidify understanding. His office hours are amazing-- such an in depth knowledge of the material and skilled at tailoring explanations. Would take again.

Prof. Yang himself teaches well but the "extra credit" assignments are actually mandatory if you want to get an A, since the cutoff is increased (you literally can't get an A without close to 100% in the class) and this wasn't communicated at all. The class content is also essentially just the SQL documentation. Tanked my GPA for no reason.
Incredible professor that cares for students and lectures well.

Jun Yang is one of my favorite professors I've at Duke. He is a wonderful lecturer, and explains things at a great pace to allow for learning. I also greatly appreciated how much he cared for his students, which was seen from his office hours to making accommodations for the class given the hardships of the pandemic. Truly a professor I'd recommend

Prof Yang really had a way of making dense concepts digestible, and he encourages students to find him after class/in office hours to clarify any questions. While the final project + final exam did get hefty at the end of the semester, he assigns the project early on and provides a lot of support with project design. Highly recommend his class!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Jun is a great lecturer and makes great slides. The homeworks are lengthy but actually a lot of fun, as is the group project. Overall, grading is reasonable. Jun makes 316 a really enjoyable CS elective

Probably one of the best lecturers I've had at Duke; he breaks complicated things down really well in an easy-to-understand way. Also definitely one of the most caring professor's ive had as he was willing to change the course structure when students expressed that they were overwhelmed.

Yang is respectable and kind, but this class needs restructuring. Having a final exam + a project due in the same week is unbearable. Especially because the project is 90% learning web development on your own and 10% database. There is a huge learning curve, and on top of that, you cannot get above a 90% without EXTRA features. Absolutely terrible.

Prof Yang is a really great professor and is willing to meet with students during office hours to help in any way he can! The tests in the class are pretty average, but it's pretty easy to get 100s on the homeworks if you attend office hours and put in the time. The course project is also really rewarding and fun to complete! Overall good CS class!
Awesome prof who really cares about his students. If youre gonna take 316 make sure to take it with him!

I highly recommend Prof. Yang and his database course. He obviously cares about his students, gives very clear lectures, and can explain concepts in multiple ways. HW is pretty light so you can work on your semester-long group project (some kind of data-driven app). Exams are curved to a B if the class average is lower than that. Definitely take!
Best teacher in CS department. Would definitely recommend taking this course for one of your electives

Jun has mastered the art of the lecture. Read the slides on your own, it's incredibly dry. When you go to lectures, you magically understand everything. He really knows his stuff, and can actually teach what he knows (a vastly underrated ability among professors). Take one of Jun's courses at least once while you're at Duke. 10/10
Good lecturer and nice guy. Light workload for a CS class, although the course material was a little dry at times.

Very clear lecturer. Fully understands the content and presents it in an interesting and fulfilling way. Homework is also useful in conveying the content to the student. Semester group project is entirely reasonable and tests are based on lectures heavily (though slides are available on course site). Take the class! Learned a lot!

HE"S SO NICE!!!! Gives a ton of extra credit. Great at explaining concepts and always there for students. Really excited about the material and knows it well. Absolutely loves the course project and his passion shows. Also makes a  lot of Simpson references!  Puts a lot of effort into the course.

Clearly among the best profs in the CS department. Very fair, great at explaining concepts, puts work into the class and truly cares about the students (all of which is rare in CS). You'll leave the class with a working understanding of databases and a useful skill set. I'd suggest that all CS majors take this class with him.
Amazing professor, really knows his subject well and is very good at passing his knowledge along.

Jun Yang is the best professor that I have had at Duke. His lectures are informative and easy to digest. He is wiing to work with you outside of class and has a real interest in talking through concepts with you. 1010.

I took Intro to Database Systems with Jun my senior year -- I wish that I had taken it sooner because I would happily take any class he offers. He's such a kind professor and explains things extremely well. He gives you all of the tools in order to do well in his class (which isn't always the case with the CS department). TAKE HIS CLASS!!!!!

Professor Jun Yang is an incredibly bright professor, and his course is very useful. I would highly recommend taking his database course, as it is not too difficult, the material is very interesting, and he is a good professor. Make sure you do the assignment ahead of time and do the practice midterms.

Professor Yang is the man! I loved his class on database. He's actually one of the cool professors at Duke who really cares about his students and wants them to succeed. Tests and homeworks are really reasonable (He helps you along the way too). Very understanding and a lot of office hrs for students. Oh, and he gives out tons of extra credits.

I love Professor Kadivar! It was such an honor to be in his class! He is such an inspiring and smart person! I learned so much about the way I view the world because of him. I recommend anyone to take his class! I am literally looking to see if I can join another one of his classes next semester.

I took a different class. Very low quality.
1. Hard to understanding what he's saying. Drones. Hard to get through lecture.
2. Doesn't really add anything to the material. Not good at answering questions. Frequently misunderstands what students are saying/asking.
3. Didn't really learn anything.

I loved Dr. Kadivar! He cares a ton about the material and definitely wants to see you in class. The readings are kind of dense but we hardly ever got through all of the content in class. I took Muslim Ethicsd and Islamic Law as a seminar, but there was much more lecture than discussion. Definitely focus on analysis more than summary for homework.

Ditto the last comment, Professor Kadivar is one of the best professors to have on all things Islamic. His breadth and depth of knowledge is amazing, and his enthusiasm is something many professors fail in showing. Always emphasizes finding the wider point in the readings as opposed to insignificant details, one of my favorite courses I've taken.

Best class I have ever taken at Duke. I'm simply writing this to counter the negative comment. He is one of the most famous men in  Iran and his brilliance as well as bravery (he was imprisoned for speaking out against the republic) are quite humbling. This passion translates through his teaching. He inspired my major. There will be a lot of work.

He is very passionate and personable. He is also extremely knowledgeable and dedicated. I love his class. It is not an easy class by any means but he makes it great. Definitely take a class from him while he is still around!

This is the worst professor I have had at Duke...this is my first post on rate my professor. He is awful... I can't believe it! Unclear expectations, unreasonable workload, arbitrary grading...DO NOT TAKE HIS CLASS!
The worst professor I have had at Duke. She cares and is a nice person, but for tricky content she is completely out of touch for how it should be taught.

Quite responsive to questions, helpful, and practical. Content ranges in difficulty and appeal. Scholberg creates great summary and FAQ sheets for each lecture, which are from Schroeder's book (+?) and sometimes dry (-). Exams are tough and lengthy, though some relief on final. She is kindly mindful of length of P-sets, though HW can be tricky.
Scholberg's lectures were the clearest out of all the physics professors I've ever had.

She prepares for lecture, so notes are really solid in the course. Also provides summaries after every class, so it is really clear what you need to know how to do. Practice tests were provided and comparable to exams. She is a strict rubric-guided grader, however, especially for homework assignments, so average final class grade was a B-.

She was a so-so professor. The matlab problems she assigned were a tremendous waste of time, and all I got out of labs was a good laugh when some idiot tried to break a board over his head. I only approached her a few times for questions, and each of those experiences was very negative. Also, the lectures were boring, even with the demos.

Scholberg does cool demoes and tries her best to keep the lectures interesting. She's probably just a so-so professor from my experience. Assigns useless MatLab problems and writes some hard test problems. But if you like physics, it won't be torture.

The lectures aren't interesting until the very end when the demos get pretty cool. The last four lectures are the only useful ones because the material gets ridiculously hard. The matlab problems are a waste.
She is nice and tries to do a good job but she spends a lot of time in lecture solving stupidly easy problems and doesn't go over the harder ones. The material is interesting but she makes in boring.

The reviews before mine are surprisingly negative.  Prof Scholberg is extremely helpful in office hours and very willing  to answer questions and gives good answers.  She has made 211 very manageable thus far.  Midterms are generally 8 questions, 75 minutes as previously commented.  Not too challenging but work fast!  Go to office hrs if ur stuck!

You will love her exams. This is my second class with Prof Scholberg (first one was 143), and I must say that I feel extremely unfortunate. I don't know why she thinks the faster one solves problems the better, and if she doesn't, I don't know why she gives 8 problems for a 75 minute test.

scholberg tried to make the class interesting and seem approachable for office hours but failed. i went to her office hours twice and always left more confused than when i went in. there were always 10 + students and it was nearly impossible to get her attention. Her lectures were also boring and hard to focus in. she is a nice person but not prof.

Her lectures were incredibly clear compared to some of the others I've had to sit through. Reviews were also pretty helpful, although the recitation instructor will probably be the main source for outside help.
Very unhelpful. Class material is not particularly challenging, but she does not make it any easier.

She briefly covers all major aspects of modern physics in the course.  The homework is rough because there is no time to do example problems in class.  Luckily, the tests are much easier than the homework.  However, the class isn't curved, so you can't afford to miss much on the tests.  She's very helpful outside of class for concepts and homework.

Take her class only if you prefer amount to depth.  She just superficially goes over all the topics in modern physics as much as she possibly can.  Test questions are ridiculously easy but that doesnt mean you would get a good grade because a single mistake can possibly destroy you.  Given the number of problems, you virtually need to know EVERYTHI

Scholberg is very nice and very laid back. She certainly knows a lot about her specific field and does very interesting research but she does not really seem to know much more than the book tells her on basic astronomy. Often lectures were a little bit longwinded. A kind, reasonable and understanding professor

He did a flipped course which required students to learn by themselves. About 40% A and A-, 40% to 50% B and C. Compared to other 221, be ready to work harder to get an A. He is OK but not the best choice since he is really busy with his own things. A good person, maybe better for leading discussion in MATH 218.

takes solace in making his versions of exams exponentially harder than other professors in same class and does not lecture

nice guy but 221D or 221 with Hahn is so much easier and you will learn more :)

I would rate Soham a 6/5 if that wasn't mathematically impossible. Take this professor. Rearrange your schedule. Drop another class if you have to. Hilarious guy, makes LinAlg so fun, clearest explanations for complicated concepts, lenient final grading, SO caring, and AMAZING office hours! You will want to major in linear algebra. Also, FLUNCH!!

The class was flipped so we watched the lectures at home and did problem during lecture. People have different opinions on this, but I think it's great. Prof Karwa is kind and understanding. He's knowledgeable but it's still clear this is his first sem teaching 221. Difficult exams, even compared to other 221 classes, but all doable.

When I took math221 with him, we had a flipped classroom which made things a bit different. It was very hard and time consuming but he is super caring and accessible. Goes out of his way to help students, office hours are super helpful, and is helpful if you ask questions in class. All in all great guy and definitely take his class.

He was my discussion lead and made this class way more enjoyable! He was great at dissecting the indigestible chunks of content hurled at us during lecture and breaking it down so that we had a better understanding. Overall great guy and fun to talk to!

While he may be better than joe, i wouldn't recommend him as there are other professors who care about their students more.  Save your time and try to go D2 over the summer if possible since he is in his own world.

Really good lecturer -- prepare for a lot of homework but that's standard in this class no matter who the professor is. The tests end up being a lot easier if you get all the practice in during the homework

Great guy. For 24-25, Soham led the discussion sections for MATH 218D-1. He was a great resource and genuinely inspirational after my Flunch with him. I encourage you to sign up for Soham's lectures, as I feel he explains concepts in a more understandable way.

Spanish 303 was great! Definitely a good amount of work outside of class but he really personalizes his lectures for all of his students and it's evident about much he cares about the class. Highly recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Teaching style comes across as somewhat sarcastic at times, and gets easily frustrated during class even with prepared students. Students who attend regularly, stay on top of assignments, and participate well should have a positive experience and be able to follow the material without difficulty.

My least favorite Spanish teacher at Duke that I've had. Grading and coursework is fine and fairly standardized but he was very snippy, made blunt comments, and constantly jumped to conclusions before knowing what a student was actually talking about or doing. He claimed to invite questions and mistakes but seemed to get annoyed everytime.

Harry is the best! Easy grader, but he really forces you to improve your Spanish. Assignments can be tedious but as long as you show an effort, you'll do fine. He can be a bit slow on returning assignments and answering emails, but he definitely cares. He was one of my few professors to genuinely follow up and check my wellbeing if I missed class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: easy grader especially with in-class writings, amazing professor with knowledge in literature. loved him.

He does a good job of forcing you to develop your Spanish skills in class. Pretty steady workflow of assignments throughout the semester but as long as you put forth visible effort on assignments and show a willingness to learn you'll do great. I appreciated how Profe was candid with me about my language development throughout the semester.

As long as you do the assigned work in this class you'll be fine. He's a funny professor, but sometimes can be overly sarcastic. As long as you are trying on the in class writings and presentations you will get a good grade even if you make mistakes. The homework is a bit time consuming without any real point, but if you just do it you'll be fine.

Harry was fairly good: courteous and accessible certainly. This class wasn't super challenging, so I wish it was more in depth. Harry brings in fascinating examples, but he forgets words and switches to English a bit too often. (I'd rather he struggle in Span. than breeze through Eng.) Interesting course, repetitive structure of three units. Kind!

Class is an easy A but there is a fair amount of work. In my opinion, Spanish 303 is a great way to satisfy the foreign language requirement since there are no tests whatsoever. Though some of the assignments can be time consuming, Karahalios is a very easy grader.

Professor Karahalios is an excellent professor and teacher. He always makes sure to bring energy to the early morning classes, which was really helpful. There are no real examinations, just quizzes and writings in class, along with a conversation at the end of the year. Your Spanish skills will also improve. I highly recommend taking this course.
Class is composed of consistent, tedious work. Sometimes the class gets annoying, but he usually grades fairly leniently and is there to help. Difficulty depends on past Spanish experience

Harry is a terrific teacher! There are many small assignments, but none of them are too stressful. The class environment is great, and the grading is not harsh if you put the effort in. Also you will improve your spanish a lot throughout the semester.

The Intro to Spanish sequence isn't that hard but just filled with a lot of busy work. He's super nice and will talk to you outside class if you need help with anything. We had a bunch of group projects and small quizzes but they were graded very leniently. Chill professor, recommend to take it with him

The first half of the class is a LOT of work while the second half is more chill. He is really nice and wants you to understand the content. He explains in English sometimes. If you do poorly on the exams but do all the other work well enough you can still can get an A-B. You can only have one unexcused absence and he counts tardies.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Harry made 301 much more difficult than it needed to be. Ambiguity & contradictions in directions made it hard to complete assignments in a way that he would like. He also always encouraged us to ask questions but got visibly annoyed when we did. Emailing him was always hit or miss. I would recommend taking the course with a different professor.

I have never written a post on here, but Harry's class was so bad I wanted to make sure future students know to not sign up for it. He is extremely condescending and his large ego dictates the class. He is a slow grader and does not provide clear feedback. He makes you meet with him outside of class just to criticize you. This class is not worth it
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Harry is a good dude. I was intimidated at first because he looks like Vin Diesel, but he is truly an amazing professor. His lectures are informative, interesting, and funny. Classes were so productive that I rarely had to study outside of them. Harry clearly cares a lot about his students.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Group projects

reviews.comment: Harry is the man, best Spanish prof and the one you want. 301 writing is structured the same way and taught same by all profs, it's just a very busy work class. He's very likeable and easy in class, super helpful and accessible outside. He wants you to do well and understands class is a lot of work - just the nature of 301 so don't be afraid.

Harry is the best professor I've had at Duke so far. His passion for the material is inspiring and he is great at keeping the class engaged. It's a lot of work but as long as you put in enough effort, it will pay off. He is dedicated to helping his students and is generally a super cool person outside of class too (also looks like Vin Diesel)
One of the best professors at Duke. Will make you do the work, but is very manageable and sees through to the fact you succeed.  Loves teaching and is a great guy all around.

Harry's passion and dedication to the course material makes this class very enjoyable and entertaining. He cares a lot about each one of his students and constantly offers his assistance in and outside of class.
Harry is both personable and effective as a teacher. He grades fairly and is as good as you will find in the Spanish department. I highly recommend taking spanish courses with him specifically

Harry was awesome! Very friendly and approachable, though he may seem scary at first. Never hesitate to meet with him. He understands that the work isn't easy, but is good at teaching the grammar and workshopping papers so that you can get the best grade possible. Actually do the homework and the quizzes won't be hard.
Fantastic teacher. Take Spanish with him, bottom line. Fun, quality teaching, and easy.

Harry is well-organized, available to help, and a friendly guy.  That said, Intro to Cultural Studies is HARD!!! Don't go in there expecting an easy A because it's going to take up hours and hours of your time each week, unless you're really good at Spanish. I spent more time on this class than on Orgo and got a worse grade.

Harry is awesome. Take as many classes with him as you can. Spanish is hard and you'll have to put a lot of work in, but Harry really works hard to make it fun. He's always available out of class, so if you're struggling, definitely go to his office hours!
Harry is awesome! He's really funny and engaging and the class isn't too hard as long as you do all the work
Harry is a great teacher. He makes classes fun, and is available outside of class to help with difficult concepts.

Very nice and incredibly helpful. His goal is to do whatever it takes to get you to learn, but not kill you with lots of work of tough grading. If you speak English in class, get ready for him to call you out.

Great Professor! Goes against everything i've heard about the Spanish department at Duke! He also does a lot to insure that everyone understands what is going on. Participation is mandatory so be ready to be called out in class but he's a great spirit and never makes anyone uncomfortable. Definitely take spanish with him if you get the chance!
I wish all Duke professors were like Harry.
Amazing professor. Keeps the class engaged, constantly. He really wants his students to learn and makes the class more of a learning experience than one based on grades.
He is one of my favorite professors at Duke. A great guy and very accessible outside of class. Really interesting person too.

Harry is really chill. Spanish will be a breeze as long as you put in some semblance of work and don't slack off completely. Harry is a very fair grader and legitimately cares more about your understanding than the actual grading itself. I highly recommend taking as many Spanish sections with him as possible.
He's a great guy and always willing to help. Be prepared to participate in class, but no worries, he's willing to help out after class if you need it. An overall super interesting guy.

This professor negated every bad statement I had heard about Duke's Spanish department.  He is helpful, always available and just an over all great guy.  The difficultly of Spanish depends on your own ability/desire to learn a language, but it's kind of difficult to not participate in class and enjoy his teaching.  He is the man.  But do your work(
helped a lot with learning content but generally not really flexible with things.

Love the structure of the class. Once a week for 2 hours, a few prep assignments over the week and then group labs all during the class with a few lectures sprinkled in. Ken is super chill and amazing at helping fix bugs in programs. Feedback on assignments was consistently strong.

Professor McKenzie is one of the most interesting professors that I have met and he really grows on you as the semester goes on. This class is for physics majors and so while it is mandatory don't expect too much work from Ken.

Kenneth is a really chill professor and will help you as needed. The grading is all done by the TA so its dependent on that. The class isn't particularly "physics" based but more an intro on how to code for physics and the stats behind it.

Ken is supportive in 165. The experimental process is easier after 164, but sometimes the course sequence feels too long. Lab reports are good practice, though gap between completion of lab and report writing can be undesirable. Interesting experiments and engaging course. Reasonable and practical approaches. Choose a good group, communicate often.

Prof. McKenzie is really sweet and cares about his students. The class is pretty easy if you have some coding experience. Some of the labs are a bit tedious. TA grades meticulously and criteria can be unclear, but there's good feedback so you won't repeat the same mistake twice.

Ken's 164 is the place to learn Python and lab notebook keeping. He's helpful, so ask for clarification when needed. However, goals are sometimes unclear; deadlines or assignments can be uncertain... will probably improve as Duke gets accustomed to Canvas. Useful feedback on assignments. Labs can be a bit tedious, error propagation always is.

Low work load and group work the whole semester. TA was a little harsh on grading, but you get used to it. Nice introduction to python for those with no previous coding experience. Most of the class was coding and writing lab reports, but the experiments overlapped nicely with our lecture.
sweet guy, not the best at explaining things but overall pretty decent prof, cares about students

Sometimes did not make grading criteria known before submission of notebooks or lab reports but started to towards the end of the semester which was helpful. TA graded harshly. Overall, Ken was a compassionate professor who was passionate about physics. He made weekly expectations clear and was always there to help students in and outside of class.

He made an online physics lab, which has questionable functionality, an experience conducive to learning and interesting experiments. It's code-heavy, and the code is just taught in readings before the class. However, if you're confused, he takes the time to explain. He responds to emails quickly and cares about the well-being of his students.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Prof Stewart is very caring about her students and wants to provide research opportunities whenever she can. However, the quizzes are a little difficult as their all open-ended and her lectures don't provide much information. You're better off doing all the readings. Attendance also isn't specified to be mandatory but she keeps track.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Really cares about her field and brings up interesting topics in readings, but does not execute/do justice to those topics in lecture or discussion. Is definitely a workaholic and expects her students to be too. The case studies are interesting but I don't think I gained a good foundation for ethical principles. Dolores Umbridge come to life.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Stewart is a sweetheart but a harsh grader. She is so knowledgeable about the course and caring towards her students. Decent amount of reading but you can get by with skimming. Always willing to meet students outside of class and excited to FLUNCH. Easy to get an A-/B+, hard to get the A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Great person and professor, but it is NOT an easy class. Lots of reading and thinking and frustration, but she gives a small curve when needed. I certainly learned a lot about current ethical problems in disease control, which was great and interesting. TA does the grading, and expectations could have been more clear.
Incredibly interesting and engaging. Some of the most I have ever learned from a class.
The best professor I had so far at DKU. She's incredibly intelligent about every possible subject and her classes are always engaging

When I told another professor that I was taking her class, the first thing he said was "Yeah... She's really smart." Prof Wu really makes you think and find new conclusions to things you haven't thought deeply on before. I enjoy her discussions a lot even though they can be difficult. Just make sure you come to class prepared!

Love love LOVE Welsher!!! Truly the kind of professor every student hopes for. Brilliant, authentic, caring, relatable, and effortlessly funny while also conveying p-chem super clearly. Despite the minimal workload and fair exams (all based on hw and past midterms), I left the class with a solid understanding of the content. Highly recommend!!!!!

Truly a gem of a human. He made a difficult subject manageable, and it was clear that he cared deeply about his students (remembered all of our names + brought snacks to our final). Funny, down to earth, and responsive to feedback. He also makes himself super accessible to students via office hours/Ed Discussion.

If there are 100 members of the Welsher fan club, I am amongst them. If there is 1 member of the Welsher fan club, I am the only one. If there are 0 members of the Welsher fan club, I am dead. Cares about his students so much, hilarious and chill, and makes pchem super manageable.

Dr. Welsher hosted office hours 2hrs 2x/week and even stays after class if needed. You have to work hard because even though the class is curved to a B+/A-, it is not easy and a few kids skew the average. He also gives the opportunity to replace your letter (excluding plus/minus) course grade with your final exam score.
Like others have said, Dr. Welsher made 8:30 Pchem manageable and honestly fun sometimes. Very caring professor, super accessible, and is very fair all the way around.
He's fantastic. He makes Pchem, which has hard material by nature, as straightforward and as fun as possible. He's funny and relatable. Don't be afraid of Pchem if he's teaching it.

Kevin Welsher is the best you could ever hope for in a pchem prof! He's really accessible outside of class and wants you to actually learn the material so you can succeed. Go to his office hours! The content is hard but he makes it as easy as possible.

Kevin is everyone's favorite scientist, and for good reason! Pchem is not easy, but he approaches pchem from an intuitive perspective and only goes over the heavy math when it's truly necessary, otherwise he focuses more on its applications. Really makes this class accessible to everyone and is super accommodating of our schedules.

PChem was the first (and only) 8:30 am class I was actually engaged in. Welsher is hilarious and does a fantastic job explaining complicated topics in a simple manner. He makes himself super accessible outside of class and is always willing to help. Tests are super fair, be sure to do the problem sets and practice exam to prep.

Dr. Welsher is pretty much the GOAT. He makes getting up at 8:30 3x a week for fairly complicated material somehow enjoyable. Lectures really well, is accessible outside class, and gives really fair tests and homework. Would definitely recommend even if you're not a chemistry major.
Kevin is my favorite scientist.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Kevin is a gem. The best professor I have had at Duke. He is so accessible outside of class and really cares that his students are getting the material. He is an awesome dude and makes you want to go to the 8:45 pchem lectures... quite a remarkable feat. He cares about his students and is good at breaking down tough content into something graspable
He will know your name by the first week of class and be there to support you in any way until you graduate. A real gem who deserves everything in life! Kevin is my favorite scientist!

I had Kevin for Pchem and absolutely loved being there even tho the class was an 8:45. All around interesting professor who makes a somewhat boring topic interesting and is not an incredibly difficult grader.
I would also like to add that kevin is my favorite scientist
Taking CHEM301 with Prof. Welsher has been one of my most memorable experiences at Duke. Such a genuinely kind and socially aware professor. Is he really a chemist?
Kevin is also my favorite scientist
Kevin is my favorite scientist

Kevin is quite possibly the best professor I've ever had at Duke. He's an engaging lecturer and does an excellent job working through some of the challenging topics we cover in the class. Exams are reasonable and grading is fair, office hours are the best. He's willing to work with students and met with several people outside of class. Awesome guy.

Would love to talk to this guy outside of class, as he is passionate about music. Taking his class is a different story. He loves cold calling and watching students squirm. there's homework due every class, and he can be super patronizing at times. only take this class if you're serious about music theory, which most students are clearly not.

If you're thinking of taking Music 146 and have no music background, feel free to take it. It was amazing learning about the history of Motown and Soul through his story telling. It was always a good time to listening to the music during class. There are 2 quizzes that are not really stressful at all- just a good way for you to retain more history.

Professor Kelley's enthusiasm about music is infectious, and he is a really engaging instructor. However, when I took this course it was paced pretty poorly; we learnt the meat of the course material very quickly, and essentially just wasted time for the last couple weeks.

In class, he had each student come to the piano and improv on the black keys.  Professor Kelley would shout encouragements and clapped the loudest for each of the 40 students. Kept the momentum throughout. Such a beautiful way to make every student feel confident and welcome. I'll never forget it. Professor Kelley is a true gem.

Not sure why there haven't been any recent reviews, but Kelley is as awesome as everyone else has been saying. The class was pretty difficult and a lot of weekly homework, but he fostered such a caring environment that all of us students became close by the end of the semester. If you need help, ask for it and he'll be available for the most part.

Probably my favorite professor at Duke. He is super passionate about the subject, and he is also just an amazing person (he even threw an end of year party at his house!). You will have a decent amount of work, but his classes were worth it.

Kelley is an amazing dude who deeply cares about all of his students. He called our class a "family", & even held a brunch for us at his house. That being said, music theory is very challenging & the class is a LOT of work - think graded hw every night. But he's always willing to meet outside of class & will push you to be your best & succeed.

Professor Kelley is my favorite professor at Duke. I have taken two classes with him and I am signed up for a third. If you are serious about music, or want to get serious about music, Kelley is your man. He will take you under his wing, push you, and inspire you . He can't contain his own excitement for music, and it's infectious.

A truly inspiring professor - I've taken two classes with him and hope for the opportunity to take more. He is brilliant, passionate, encouraging, and laid back (in some senses). But, at the same time, he pushed me to do things that I did NOT think would be possible. And that, I think, is the mark of a great professor. High point of Duke.
Dr Kelley is my favorite professor!

I loved music theory before this class.  I still like it, but no thanks to Professor Kelley.  Lots of work, and I didn't even do as well as I would've hoped.  He was even condescending towards me near the end of the course.  Class was interesting, but avoid Professor Kelley like the plague.

LOTS of work. the class environment is very fun and the professor really cares about your performance and dedicates a lot of time to his class. lots of homework every night and sometimes, those take an avg of 1-2 hr. learned plenty. least favorite part of class was the lab. make sure to get a good ta!

Professor Kelley is the kind of teacher you pay your big Duke bucks for - he's passionate and talented in his field, and wants to share his interest with students, without being imposing.  I had no musical background and little interest, but he definitely changed that.  As long as he sees you're trying, he'll work with you.

Dr. Kelley is a great composition professor. He knows how to push you artistically, but at the same time help you cultivate your own style. When you've hit a wall, he's fantastic at choosing music to show and inspire you. Lessons are always a blast, even early in the morning. Highly recommended.

Fantastic professor. He's extremely enthusiastic about what he's teaching, and I never left class in the morning without a smile. Word of warning though: his class is a LOT of work. You'll be annoyed at the amount of work you're getting, but this is one of the few classes where I can say it all pays off in the end. Highly recommended.

Dr. Kelley is an amazing music professor who truly made me enjoy theory. However, the class is incredibly time-consuming. He gives an extreme amount of homework. At the same time, I am SO SO SO thankful I took it. I LOVE theory thanks to him. Take this class if you want to reap awesome rewards at the expense of a lot of work.

DEFINITELY take this class if you need an ALP.  Professor Kelley is amazing and an easy grader.  The class is also interesting and fun/interactive.  Seriously, take this class if you're considering it at all.
What a good man.  Professor kelley is the best teacher I've had at duke he's extremely passionate about music.  Kind of hard though.

Professor Kelley is a real great guy. He has absolute passion for music and it shows. He likes to get his students excited about music theory and does a good job of it. The only drawback is that he is a really hard teacher, gives a TON of homework and likes to keep the class moving at a fast pace. But in the end you learn a ton.
No Comments

AWESOME professor!!  Everybody loves Professor Kelley!  We have parties in his apartment before going to see a concert together as a class.  We have four essays in the class.  He's definitely one of the best professors I've had so far at Duke.
No Comments

Awesome professor, so smart and loves her students! Class was interesting and not very hard with a few group projects over semester and not much else! Such a great professor would take every class she offers

Omg best prof ever. Basically no homework, group essays, and amazing professor. Knocks a course requirement out and had fun. Love love love Dr. Keister. Plus, you get to hear from some cool speakers in Socio 211.

Professor Keister cares about every single student! Her lectures are interesting, she brings the best guest speakers, and she makes the time fly by. This class makes me want to take every class she teaches! Highly recommend! She will brighten your day every time you have her class!
Nicest teacher at Duke. So supportive and empathetic to her students. Class is not difficult/stressful. Take any class with her that you can - an amazing opportunity to connect with a great person.
she rocks

Easiest class I've ever taken with the kindest and most supportive professor probably at Duke. A few group projects but little work, she really wants everyone to do well. Take a class with her and it will be the easiest A you'll ever receive.
take anything she offers! amazing

Highly recommended. She's absolutely amazing - one of the best teachers I've had at Duke. She cares so much about each student &  she'll go above and beyond to help. It's really sad how many of the professors here aren't like her.
There are so many other ratings, but she is really incredible. I had to say it!! Take this class and anything else she offers.

Great professor, truly one of a kind. Performance was based on 3 papers, which were graded very easily. She also happens to be incredibly hot, which is the only reason I showed up to class. Professors like these are a rarity at Duke, and you would be stupid not to take this class. I would take anything she teaches.

The topic is super interesting and useful for real life purposes. We talk about personal finance and how the top 1% made it to that bracket. She rewards students for showing up to class and grades papers really nicely. Definitely take this class, especially if you're a senior!

Lisa is a blast. You can tell she loves the course material, and her excitement for it can make you excited. She has a few interesting guest lectures come in, and tries to make her class applicable to real-life (with skills you will use in the future). Grades are based on 3 papers. Not too hard if you go to class, and spend time on the papers.
this class really helped me figure out what to do after graduation
Best professor ever!

A beacon of enlightenment. What an awesome professor, not only friendly and super nice, but an inspiration. This leader of her field is truly one of the best profs at duke, super helpful, kind, and knowledgable (not to mention accomplished and well connected). For those interested in sociology, socioeconomics, business, or just life in general, take a class with Keister
LOVE HER!!!!! one of my favorite professors at duke. take her class. seriously she's great.
awesome!!!

I love Professor Keister!! She's super nice and REALLY enthusiastic about what she teaches. She's really good about responding to emails and helping out with papers. Organizations and Management wasn't too hard and it was actually really interesting! On the last day of class everyone hugged her goodbye- I would take anything she teaches!
hotttttttt
she rocks.
There are tons of ratings already, but i had to add one more. professor keister is really cool. i'd taake anything she teaches.
She really is great. I'd take anything she is teaching. Very accessible.
excellent
Super!
Professor Keister is amazing. This is an absolutely wonderful class....too bad there aren't more profs out there like her!
Best class I have had at duke!
No Comments

Dr. Kirk is extremely eye-opening. She does an amazing job on keeping you engaged while being extremely understanding and flexible on what you turn in. I had a major interest in health and she was able to provide me chances to learn about what I already liked while informing us about new perspectives on current events. Duke is lucky to have her!
Professor Kirk is amazing! She is the only professor that I am willing to wake up at 8:00 for. Amazing stories and lectures are always interesting! Does not assign busy work. Highly Recommend!
Prof Kirk is so funny. She has stories for days and will always make lectures engaging and fun! She is very fair and understanding.

Dr. Kirk is the best! She has clear expectations and always prepares you to succeed. There is no busy work or wasted class. She is an engaging storyteller and is genuinely passionate about what she is teaching. I was excited to come to this class, even at 8:30, because of how awesome she was. You can tell she genuinely cares about her students.

Professor Kirk is a very knowledgable and engaging lecturer. I took this class at 8:30 am and was always very interested in her talks. Some of the grading expectations are unclear and there are not many grades in the class, but as long as you try you should do well. Reading heavy but no homework during the week and nothing too dense

Professor Kirk has such an incredible depth of knowledge and truly intriguing life experiences. Her amazing work really makes the class so much more meaningful. The course is not difficult, provides a well-rounded foundation in human rights, and is interesting. I highly recommend it!

I had Kirk for Intro HR + an IS. Both were phenomenal. She's well-versed on everything (ofc..!), deeply engages in your interests, and pushes your thinking/skills to another level �� She offered hugs, personal guidance, & her home to me. She's unparalleled @Duke: empathetic, dynamic, engaged, brilliant. Take her course; you'll never regret it.

Horrible professor, should have listened to the avoid at all cost review. save yourself and never take a class from her it will be the biggest mistake you ever make at Duke. Almost thought about transferring after finishing this course. I have never written one of these but could not let another person suffer.
She's super cool, just life experiences and lecture wise. That being said, her paper expectations are super unclear, and her feedback is pretty unhelpful.

Prof. Kirk is wonderful and very insightful; her lectures are very engaging, and she welcomes online and in-person participation in discussions during lecture. The class is required for the human rights certificate and has an ALP!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Great professor... very knowledgeable and cares most about students actually learning rather than grades
unclear with expectations for writing assignments and unclear grading. boring lectures
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Bass Connections team. Robin is a wonderful professor because she engages with you academically while also remembering that you're a human who struggles with other pressures outside of class. Inspirational; encourages discussion; funny -- makes you want to work for her class from the heart. Great advocate for her students.

Robin has been an inspiration for me from the time I first met her.  If you're interested in human-rights, activism, social movements or related matters, definitely take a class with her. She will challenge you and help you grow. Her experience as a human rights practitioner and her support to her students are two things I appreciate the most.

This class (as part of DukeImmerse) is probably the most challenging class I've ever taken, but at the same time, one of the most rewarding. She really really pushed us to understand and questions the material, other viewpoints, and ourselves. Her writing feedback can be kind of harsh and demeaning, but deep down she really, really cares.

The class was so interesting. Robin is an awesome professor with a ton of real-life experience. She was super awesome as far as teaching and in class, but her grading was hard and the workload was a ton. I took it through Immerse and the program was pretty interesting.

Prof. Kirk, while passionate about what she taught and was generally a nice person, was confusing and unclear with a lot of her expectations. The class was confusing and random at best and an absolute bore except for the few times she showed interesting film clips.  Would avoid her at all costs, Hasso is probably better.

One of the best classes I've taken at Duke. Completely disagree with the the first post. She's always willing to meet with students, is incredibly down to earth, and is flat out an excellent teacher. If you're interested in learning about human rights strategy, this class is a MUST take.

He is a really kind professor who obviously cares about his students. The class can be unstructured at times, and the in-class discussions aren't very helpful for the exams, but the exams themselves are not that difficult if you study the reading. Also, the material itself is very interesting if you are interested in neuroscience.

Dr. Kimbrough is a really nice guy, even if the class isn't for everyone. The tests are based very closely off the readings, and if you put in the work, you can get an A. The class is slightly unstructured with the open ended discussion, but the tests are relatively easy if you pay attention to the fine print in the readings.

Yes, this is the only class in the Neuro/Law FOCUS cluster that is not a free A. However, if you're interested in decision-making or neuroscience and you enjoy open-ended discussions, would definitely recommend. Not for everyone, but Dr. Kimbrough is a great guy and class is interesting if you choose to engage in the material. Plus final was easy
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Try to just not take this focus, but if you're already stuck in it, don't take this one. Many ppl had to pass/fail to save their GPA(almost every one of us is pre-professional). He's too smart to teach freshmen, and I haven't learned a thing. His K-type questions are evil and look at footnotes for test answers btw, even if in very small font.

Very kind & caring! Taught our class with slides from his neurology students, and the rest of the content for our exams was fair game from 100+ pages of reading scientific papers and 2 of Sapolsky's neuroscience books. We ever learned in class, only had unproductive random student group discussions about long readings most of the class didn't read.
reviews.rating_tags: So many papers--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Nice guy, bad professor. I learned absolutely nothing in class, we self taught each other before exams. Test questions are taken from miniscule sentences within the long readings. The course had no structure. The exams were very difficult, nothing like what we went over in class. It is insanely difficult (for a focus class) to get an A. DO NOT TAKE

He is nice and tries to work with you and he teaches it like its med school. All we did in class was talk about whatever we want, and the test material was unclear. We didn't know what or how to study which made the class very stressful. Multiple people had to pass fail.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I have never taken a class with so little guidance on what will be on the tests or how stuff is structured. We asked for a practice test from a year prior or even an outline to what our test would look like and he said he was unable to do that. The tests included K type questions that were very difficult. Multiple people had to pass/fail this class
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Took Post-Apocalyptic Fiction: Super easy - if you don't do well, it is absolutely your own fault. Books are decently interesting, and he cares about your participation in class discussions. Relatively low amount of writing. Cancels class a lot. All in all, probably the least painful W101 you could take.

This is literally the easiest class ever and easier than English 9 in High School. Casey is so nice and he respects every opinion as long as you put in someee effort. Attendance required but if you skip a few times it don't matter. Post apocalyptic fiction for the win
Attendance is technically mandatory, but I marked otherwise because Kevin held so few classes that I attended less than in my non-mandatory lecture courses. Greatest professor of all time.

Kevin is a very nice professor and will make the class particularly easy. The class is mostly organized around discussion of the novels being read which are the only time commitment outside of class aside from the assigned essays.

I took him for writing 101 post apocalyptic fiction. The class met in person around half the time with the other half being either online or cancelled. Great guy and enthusiastic about the topic, and seems like an easy grader. Not much work beyond reading, which wasn't bad at all

Great class!  If you like post-apocalyptic fiction the books are genuinely interesting. Prof. Casey is great and super chill about everything.  As long as you actually write your essays you should get an A.

Nice guy. Classes are mainly discussion based, so it is important to speak up. Seems like most people end up with an A so long as you put in effort. Attendance is mandatory. Total writing is about 5000 words about 3 novels that are discussed daily

Best writing101 class. Everyone agrees. Take this. You read 3 novels, write 4 short essays, and a longer final essay. Very engaging and fun. Workload is undoubtedly the lightest out of all writing101s and its an interesting topic. Best prof out there.

Course itself was easy, a lot of your grade is based upon in-class discussion. The papers were very manageable and the readings weren't difficult making the class a pretty easy A. Discussions can sometimes become very long, as he tends to go on tangents about certain topics for a long time. He doesn't grade super fast, but grades pretty easily.

You just read assigned pages and talk about it in class. Participation matters to some extent, but don't worry too much if you're quiet. Very informal, including the short writing assignments which feel more like brain dumps. ~5 assignments for whole semester. Easy grader. Very understanding teacher if you want a deadline moved/need extensions.
Assigned 3 books and discussed them in class. Workload very reasonable. Very passionate and really appreciates student participation, although can sometimes ramble.

Kind, easygoing and loves books and writing. Chooses good books. Workload is not heavy, concentrated in a few short papers spread out through the semester. Wants to see effort above everything else. Warning: can be long-winded, which kills discussion and makes lessons repetitive and boring. Then again, few people attend this class out of interest.

Professor Casey is very friendly and an easy grader. The class was solely discussion based and participation mattered. Even though this class required more reading than other writing 101s, it was definitely one of the more interesting choices and I would highly recommend. Sometimes he could drone on a bit though, but Id take another class with him

Casey is awesome. Took him for Big Difficult Books. The entire class is based on reading two pretty approachable novels then talking about them. There are five really short papers that are graded very leniently. When we went online I was sad, because I had enjoyed coming to his class so much.

Casey is one of the best professors I've had at Duke. Do your readings, write your papers on time, put in at least a little effort and you'll make an A. The class title is intimidating but it's easy if you like to read and show up. You have personal reflections throughout the course which is an easy grade boost.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Great professor and a fun and approachable guy. If you do your work on time you'll make an A. Class was focused mostly on discussing the book, very little work.

Professor Casey's WRIT 101 class requires you stay up-to-date with the reading but besides there is little homework. He is good at fostering discussion in class and is very understand of what it is like to be a stressed college student. If you can, choose his class over any of the others. You will do well and actually enjoy it.

I took Stranger than Fiction. I enjoyed the books, and assignments were easy and straightforward. Casey paces out deadlines well so that coursework is pretty light throughout, and you feel well-prepared for the final paper. Great class!

Took Stranger than Fiction with him. Good class, and the books are interesting. Not too difficult or too much work, and he gives you a lot of room to take whatever direction you want on papers and assignments. Take the class with Casey if you can, but spots fill up fast.

I took Stranger than Fiction with Professor Casey. He's a great guy and will help you become a better writer and thinker. Spots fill up fast, but if you can take a class with him you should definitely go for it.

I absolutely loved Professor Casey and highly recommend his writing 101 class Stranger than Fiction. All the books we read were intriguing and he was very flexible for our final paper. Great class everyone should take it, and the class discussions are great!

He's very good.  Readings, writing assignments, discussions, and workshops were engaging, and he was very willing to allow people to bring their own interests into writing assignments.  If you're looking for a moderately challenging but interesting Writing 101, take this one (Stranger Than Fiction).  He's a little awkward at first but very nice.
He's fantastic. Take a class with him. Expect to read and write a lot, come to class (because he leads awesome discussions), and you'll get what you want and need from the class.

Casey is definitely the most chill, down-to-earth professor I've had. The books we read were awesome (though extensive) and he promoted a round-table discussion that worked really well for the class. Also, if you go in to see him for your final paper, he'll really help you. Take this class. It's worth it.
professor casey is very nice and chill. he talks A LOT even though part of your grade will be based on participation. open-minded and not a hard grader

His Writing 101 course on Cormac McCarthy's novels was very interesting.  He was willing to help if you took the time to turn in drafts of your papers EARLY-- basically gives you everything you need to do to improve your paper to get a good grade.  Nice guy, fair grader, respected.
A challenging class but worth it. A noticeable improvement in my writing abilities.
To be honest, Prof. Casey is a total bro. Take him. He's not obnoxious or pretentious. Down to earth, cares what you think.
Prof. Casey is extremely helpful when I needed help. He promotes classroom discussions that help us understand what the author is trying to convey--very useful skill in reading/writing.

Great teacher, boring class. But I think the most important thing was that Casey was very willing to go out of his way to help you whenever you needed help. I took the Art of Storytelling -- the class itself was rather dry, but the books and Casey made it worth taking this class.

Casey is young and excited about teaching the class and listening to students. His class is discussion based, so be prepared to participate. He does make his views clear, but leaves room for other students' opinions. Writing workshops were helpful, but the class involves much more reading than writing; it's more of a lit class. Solid amount of work

Dr. Khanna is a great teacher and extremely intellectual. She cares about how you engage with the content and your writing. She is a bit busy since she's the head of the humanities institute so your communication is crucial. You need to stay in contact and push for meetings and deadlines. Definitely will learn a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This is not a blow off class by any means. It's very difficult because much of the reading is philosophical and she provides very poor explanations for these sections. Very little work day to day in the class, but lots for the 3 essays.
No Comments

Taking a class with Boutheina was a big mistake I've made. She is not a fair grader, and she made the class super demanding for what it really was. She will show a terrible attitude if she feels triggered, including reminding you of the times when she helped you (yes, & this is coming from a professor). I would not recommend at all!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She is the most helpful prof. i have ever had. If you need help and go to her office she goes out of her way to help u 100%. She always pushes her students to always go the extra step in their assignments and i can honestly say because of that i learned more in this class then any other class in my life.
Boutheina hands down is one of the best professors i have ever had. She is very helpful but strict and tough on us nd this is a plus not a minus.
She was a great professor. Very knowledgeable of her subject and very patient. We miss her

Bouthenia is a decent teacher, but if you can get someone for Arabic 1, I would try to.  This class is pretty easy at first, just the alphabet and basic vocab.  She makes it harder than it has to be, because she is confusing/ed and new to Duke.  Worth taking, but needlessly stressful at times.
Stay away if you can... or wait until the old professor comes back

You should only expect an A in this class if you show up to every single class and are incredibly engaged. Don't be deceived by the .5 credit: there are many writing assignments and "Engagement activities" over the course of the semester (standard for all dance at duke?). This class was more of an extra academic burden than a dance class for me.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Great modern dance class! Have to show up and try, but a lot of fun! Looked forward to every class.

Keval is great in that she cares about you, but she wants everything to be exactly how she likes it and won't accept anything else. There is little room for artistic freedom. I did like the class though.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Keval is a decent/mediocre professor. It should have been a fairly easy course but somehow she made it very difficult when it came to grading.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Grades given are very confusing. Would not recommend unless taken pass-fail. Otherwise, you can attend every class and work really hard and think you will get an A and then end up with something much worse.  In terms of class material, the dance class feels more like yoga. Would recommend looking at other classes like Ballet or Jazz dance.
Introductory Modern Dance class - pretty chill in general, the prof is nice and encouraging.

Absolutely ludacris that this class is allowed to be taught at a University that prides itself on innovation and intelligence. Khalsa attempts to use modern physiology to explain the benefits of yoga (mostly erroneous claims) and teaches in a rather cultish fashion. If you have any respect for the advances of science, DO NOT take this course.

She is amazingly nice but don't let the word 'yoga' fool you! it is an actual class! there are tests and a legit research paper! Its an easy A if you try. but dont expect it to fall in your lap.  there is a lot of reading and several writing assignments.  but it was a really fun class and I am glad I took it.

While Keval is indeed a little outside the box, she has a good heart and she cares a lot about what she teaches. Show her you're interested in the topic and you'll do well. Don't laugh off reading and writing assignments, she grades them tough. Go to class and don't get behind.

There's only one word to describe this one: loopty-loop! But yoga is cool so take the course. Hint for the final: Sikhs avoid meat not because of compassion for the animal, but because humans are not designed to ingest the adrenaline flowing thru the animal at the time of slaughter. You were not going to get that one right.

Good modern teacher, helpful in corrections and personable, although can be a bit moody sometimes. I definitely learned a lot from her, esp. in terms of style--she can be very dogmatic about style! In generaly, I liked her class, though!
i got a B+ in this class and did so much work , only missed 3 classes and made up 2, and did extra bonus out of clsas work.  she gave someone a C+... she's moody and weird. avoid her if possible
i previously had assumed that professors needed some degree of intelligence. khalsa taught me never to assume anything.
No Comments

Words cannot describe how horrible this class is.She is completly unprofessional and dedicated in a cultish way to a belief system that shapes the entire class. readings were absurd and yoga useless. ruined the entire discipline for me. i am ashamed that a university like Duke supports this kind of shoddy teaching. AVOID AT ALL COSTS
No Comments

Surprisingly difficult, and Prof Khalsa isn't very understanding.  Pay attention to the syllabus - we weren't allowed to miss a SINGLE class, and that gets tough after a while.  I was so excited to take this, but have ended up hating it.  Unless you're REALLY serious, I'd stay away.

I thought this dance class was going to be a lot of fun, but instead, it's a lot more work than I thought it would be and there are not many As.  If you're looking for a fun, relaxing dance class (as a beginner, I was), this is not the professor for you.
The yoga sessions are great, but she pretty much just reads straight from the readings during lecture.
A great class and friendly teacher. Attendance to both the yoga sessions and lectures are a must. You won't have to do the reading if you attend lectures.

Sweet guy. Make the effort to talk to him outside class and show interest in what he says. This class in an easy A+ if you simply care and put in effort into your essays. Just be an honest writer and you will be just fine.

Class began strong, and I was excited about diverse topics, but quality and niceties dropped after drop/add. Advanced Hindi, but no focus on grammar or spelling. Grades based solely on writing style and views, revealed late-- essay grading super arbitrary and random. Unnecessarily stressful, even for a native speaker. Had to make it S/U.

Satti Ji is a wonderful professor. I thoroughly enjoyed his class and the wide range of topics we covered; we watched several films, read some great Hindi literature, and thought deeply about Indian society, culture, and history. Highly recommend going to office hours to practice speaking Hindi. Caring and kind. Show that you care !
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--So many papers

reviews.comment: Satti Ji is an extremely interesting person and very open-minded. He makes you think about topics that you wouldn't think about otherwise. The main issue was that it was hard to understand what he liked in our essays. Based on my experiences, he likes emotional content rather than research-based essays. The content was very fun though.

Took Hindi306 with Satti ji. He's a great prof who thinks deeply about the smallest of things, and that reflects in the work that he assigns. Your grade is based off your midterm, final, and weekly essays. The classes are fun and not too heavy given they're 2.5 hours long. He is a tough grader though, you'll have to impress for an A.

Definitely the most frustrating class I've taken at Duke (and I'm an engineering student lol). Your entire grade is based off of 3 short videos that are graded very subjectively. Yes the class is no work, but the only people I have seen who have said they enjoyed the class are those who ended up with A's and trust me not everyone gets A's.

Prof Khanna is super cool & relaxed. He thinks very deeply about art, filmography, & culture. He tends to go on tangents that are hard to understand & extremely profound. But all in all, the films he assigns give great insights into Indian culture & life, even for those from an Indian background. Assignments graded easy if you show you care!

Satti Ji is one of the most compassionate and insightful people you will ever meet. I took his class years ago but he still remains one of my favorite instructors. If you can't get along with Satti Ji, you have serious issues!

I really liked Sattiji as a person, but not so much as a professor. The entire class is in Hindi, and each week you have to write a 2-page paper. Grading is very arbitrary. I never once got better than an A- on an essay. Fun topics, but the readings are hard to understand, and the class itself is challenging if you're not a native speaker.

The class is not too difficult, he expects you to write a 2 page paper every week and record it. But to be honest, it's pretty low key. Sometimes we listen to each other's recordings in class and it can be really funny. We'll also watch movies in class and go through all the readings together to make sure we get it all

One of the most confusing classes I've ever taken!! At the beginning of the semester he said we would be graded on the writing assignments on each of the films. At the end of the class he revealed our entire grade was based on "exercises," which were these bizarre short films he had us make on our iPhones--nothing to do with Indian Cinema at all!!

Sattiji makes class a fun experience and the discussions are very engaging. You'll write an essay, do translations, read bits of a story, and watch part of a movie every week so it can be a bit time consuming (but not too difficult). Grading criteria was somewhat unclear though.

The class requires very little work, and you can get by with doing almost nothing. But, your entire grade is based on short videos. Sounds easy, except for the fact that he offers no clear expectations whatsoever. When asked for clarification, he makes the prompt even more confusing. Brilliant individual with great insight, but bad class.

He's a very intelligent professor but the movies to seen in this class are very off-beat and old, however some of them are amazing. His grading criteria is quite vague but if you show effort and follow his prompts you'll end up with an A

Satti Khanna is a very intelligent professor with tremendous potential which is unfortunately marred by his desire to have students agree with his point of view. He can not accept differing points of view, even if they are substantiated, and grades accordingly. I find this antithetical to the core of a liberal arts education!
Brilliant
Satti Khanna is an exemplar of wisdom and dignity.

The best professor I have ever had at Duke. He is extremely knowledgable and challenges you to explore yours. It is not hard to get an A, if you do his work diligently and participate in the class discussion actively. He deserves some sort of recognition from Duke! I took 3 classes with him, loved them all.

He is amazing! Such a wonderful man and is really kind to all of his students.  His assignments are fair and you do need to put effort into whatever work he asks for in order to get an A, but it is not difficult to be interested in the material.  One of the best professors I've had at Duke.

One of the best professors! Even though both of the Hindi classes I took with him were 2.5 hours long, I never felt bored. He is not a harsh grader and if you really put your heart into the class, you will be surprised to see how much knowledge you have gained by the end of the semester :)
Spectacular
Satti ji likes when people come up with crazy ideas and stuff, he doesn't really accept normal thinking.

Satti-ji is different from any teacher you'll have - he operates at a completely different level. He really should consider teaching philosophy classes as well. Some people find his style frustrating, but I thought he was fantastic. Very supportive and loves any type of creativity!

Great teacher- very interested in students who take an interest in the coursework. Does his office hours at a coffee shop. One of my favorite professors at Duke. That being said, you get in what you put in. He gives his students a lot of creative freedom, and if you really put yourself into your work, he is appreciative.
Worst teacher I ever had

Satiji is extremely deeper than any ocean that exists on the planet. His analysis of literally anything is so deep that you really leave each class amazed that anyone is that deep. Other than that, expect Hindi 100% of the time, a good amount of work each week, and some enlightening discussion. As for grading, easy to get an B+/A-, hard to get an A

Prof. Khanna is very welcoming, but this was the most poorly taught class that I have ever taken.  The class did not focus on the literature but on the author's "innerness."  (e.g. Our major paper question: of the works you've read, which activates your powers the most?) People who literally never showed up or did anything did well in his class.
At first I was perplexed by his style. I was upset that he accepted nonsense assignments from other students as valid coursework. Then I let go and just enjoyed it. Fantastic.
Most amazing course/prof. ever.  So interesting and a real joy to listen to
No Comments
Real easy, no problems. mostly cool about things, but can be boring sometimes.
He's an awesome guy. Dont' kiss up to him and be yourself. He's very easy going and really chilled out. Great thinker-- very intellectual.
Really great, and deep intellectual thinker. Can have some truly interesting conversations if you probe him. Should probably also be in philosophy too.

Midterm was easy and based off of homework questions. Final was extremely hard, average was in the 50s. He did not email us the syllabus, but gave us hard copies the first day of class. Bizarre expectations from students, but minimal expectations for himself. Unprofessional and rude. Hard to understand. Lectures and homework did not correlate.

Ok, Dr K is a TERRIBLE professor. Lectures are pointless as he only teaches off a powerpoint with his stupid touchpad which makes lecture even harder. He will take points for ANYTHING. And dont even try to ask him a question. His response,"Do more problems". Nomatter the question. Extreme expectations! WOULD NEVER TAKE A CLASS WITH HIM AGAIN!

Worst teacher I've ever had. Assigned more work than all my classes combined. Unreasonable expectations. Said he would curve the tests, then didn't. Everyone got a lower grade than expected. Changes deadlines with no notice. doesn't cover topics until too late for work. doesn't respond to questions quickly, if at all. avoid at all costs.

Worst experience I've had along the engineering track so far. Transformed a challenging but manageable class into a living nightmare. Any learning I received in the class was incidental, and occurred in spite of him rather than because of him.

The WORST professor I've ever had, by an huge margin. Absurd workloads, including labs/projects which he does not release documents on how to do until a day or two before they are due. The tests are NOTHING like the material we have learned, and his strange partial credit system is the only thing that keeps the average at the 66% mean it is now.

TERRIBLE professor. Assigns an absolutely unmanageable amount of work. Tests & problem sets are MUCH harder than and different from anything he covers in class. Gives you the wrong instructions for labs, and doesn't correct them until the day they're due. He doesn't like answering questions in lecture. AND the final is on LDOC. AVOID.

A very fair class. He was pretty good at teaching until he started using the touchpad technology, which made the material not as clear. Homework and exams were logical and fair extensions of class material.

Probably the best instructor I ever had.  He is always available, explains the material clearly and writes everything down on the board. His teaching focuses on understanding rather than grades.  He will make you work hard on a few homeworks, but it turns out to be to your advantage.  It is thanks to Professors like him that Duke shines.

To be honest, most of the other reviews are too harsh in my opinion. He's not a bad teacher. He understands the material and teaches it relatively clearly. He also returns grades very quickly. However, he is a very difficult teacher, and he's relatively new at teaching. By taking his class, you will learn the material, but your grade may suffer.
Possibly the worst professor I've had at Duke. Can't explain concepts well and entirely focused on grades rather than learning. Avoid this teacher if at all possible

He's very helpful if you go to his office hours. Reading the book beforehand definitely makes the lectures easier to understand. Overall, I feel he's a good professor, and he'll definitely respond well to you if you put in the time and effort.
Not a great professor, likes to use new technologies (such as touch pad tablet) but does not add to learning experience and can interfere. Focuses too much on grades. 4/10

Worst professor I've had in 6 years at Duke.  Doesn't explain anything well, makes you learn everything completely on your own from the book, and gives homeworks which he doesn't even cover half of the material that's needed to actually do the homework.  Makes Duke look bad... take a class with him at your own risk.
Needs to get priorities in order, he lives for grades. He loves to give quizes when no one goes to his 8:30 so he can screw students over (which are pretty hard regardless). Made me hate dynamics.

Klein is one of the better writing profs at Duke. She gives amazing feedback and is always willing to meet with you and discuss your grades and writing. Fairly easy class with not a ton of work and the ability to rewrite the major assignments for some points back. Definitely a cool topic but only take it if you care because participation matters!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Klein is the best writing teacher I've ever had. Gives great feedback and really pushes you to improve as a writer. Decent workload but definitely manageable. I wouldn't call it an easy A but as long you as you work hard you'll pass. Take this class if you really want to develop as a writer. She's super knowledgable and cares about students.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.
