reviews.comment: I took the writing about monsters course with prof. Klein and it was an amazing experience. She has a special way of teaching. Even when she is teaching the most fundamental writing skills that I am very familiar with, I still can learn something new from her.

Everything you could want for a Writing 101 class. Extremely helpful and nice, and she gives the opportunity to rewrite for 10% more. Not too much work, extremely manageable as long as you dont put it off.

Great professor! She gives excellent feedback on papers and encourages lively discussion in class. While she does make you write a bit more than most Writing 101 professors, that's why you take a Writing 101 course - your future papers will thank you. Would definitely take a class from her again.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Hilarious

reviews.comment: I took a special topics writing course with Prof. Klein on monsters and it was a lot of fun. There were six of us in the class (DKU campus) and we would discuss monster media. We watched Ex Machina, Pan's Labyrinth, and the original Godzilla and wrote essays on monster media of our choice using the ideas we discussed. She made the class great!

As long as you show up, do the work, and participate in class you should do well. Can't really ask for much more in a Writing 101 class. Professor Klein is a good professor and cares about her students' success.

Professor Klein's Podcast class is such a steal for a freshman writing class. Some reading but mainly just listening to podcasts (varying from 10 min to 90 min of listening). She also allows revisions which is a guarantee minimum +3 percentage points from your original essay as long as you show effort.

Podcasting class was super cool. The class is based mainly off a couple of big assignments but you get to resubmit assignments for a better grade at the end of the semester. Dr. Klein is a great teacher and will make you a better writer. If you can take this class (it fills up quickly) then do yourself a favor and take it.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: popularity of podcasts- not tons of work outside of class besides listening to podcasts, but you can multitask while listening. turn in rough drafts for completion and get edits before final draft. you also get revisions after the final draft to raise your grade more. only 3 major assignments: 800, 1800 words, 8 min podcast.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Truly wonderful prof. I highly recommend her for Writing 101. Very detailed feedback on papers, cares about her students, and clear objectives for the class.
She really cares about what she does and the students in her class. Overall, pretty chill. If you show up and do the work, you'll be fine.

Absolutely loved this class and this teacher! Professor Klein is extremely caring and supportive of her students and cares a lot about their personal growth- she doesn't grade based off of whether you're a good actor or not, she grades based on how much you've personally progressed and that you've demonstrated efforts
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Very relaxing and fun class! No acting experience necessary. Class front loads reading and writing assignments in the first few weeks, then it is mostly rehearsing. The plays and readings we used were super interesting. Talya will meet you at your level and help you grow. Big recommend!!

Talya is a gem of a professor! Her class is a wonderful intro to acting and a great stress relief compared to other classes. Most classes are for performing drafts of scenes, and there are a couple 2-3 page writing assignments to do throughout the semester. Take Talya's class - you won't regret it!

The directing class is an upgraded version of the 145S acting class, both in terms of commitment and artistic standard demanded. But Talya has been caring and constructive and you will achieve growth as a director if you put in enough work. Text analysis is time-consuming but feels useful at the end of the day.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: I LOVE THIS CLASS! Minimal work load, fun class, relaxing warm-ups. You will get really close to your classmates, but be prepared to get out of your comfort zone. Prof Klein is simply AMAZING. She is very understanding but is never scared to push you. Some readings, 3-page journals for each of the 4 group/individual scenes.

Talya is an amazing actor and director who just makes you learn a lot. She is thoughtful and caring, but participation really matters. The texts selected by her are also tremendous. Do the work and you will be fine.

She is a great acting professor who really taught me a lot; she gives great feedback on scenes and creates a welcoming, fun environment. There are very few assignments (about 4 acting scenes and response papers for each scene), and participation is very important. Easy and fun class overall. Previous acting experience is NOT required nor needed.

Professor Klaits does his best to keep class interesting. Unfortunately, he is so chill and soft-spoken that it's hard to pay attention. He assigns more essays than most writing 20 teachers and requires more reading. You can always get an A on your papers if you write exactly what he tells you to write and not what you think.
Interesting and engaging, but at times can give a lot reading. He knows his stuff, and my writing has improved!

Klaits gives more papers than others, but this class is very easy to do well in. you literally never have to read a thing if ur that lazy. take good notes in class and he summarizes for you. LISTEN to his emails about your drafts, if you do he'll automatically give you several more points on the final draft. Easy A if you know how to write at all

klaits is the man.. definitely one of the smartest people ive ever met... very helpful on papers, very clear in class.. makes it interesting. leads discussion a certain way sometimes, but the way he does it is genius.   a lot of work but if you go to class it's easy

Dr. Klaits is a good teacher.  His W20 is LOTS of work.  Reading and class discussion was always interesting, though sometimes the hour-plus class period seemed long.  I felt like my writing improved: you have to have a strong strong strong thesis and very clear paper that follows from the thesis to do well (which can sometimes be difficult).

His class was a ridiculous amount of work. Take it only if you're THAT interested in the topic. Looking back on it now, the class was interesting, but it wasn't worth it for all the work. Apparently a 20 page research paper is considered a "short paper." He definitely hijacks the discussion a lot too. I don't think my writing improved much either.

Klaits can be a really strange guy--there were some pretty awkward moments at times. And he assigns a ton of work (at least compared to other writing 20 profs). BUT the topic is really engaging and interesting. Though a lot of times he also hijacks the discussion. But overall a  fun class, but if a challenge is not your thing, then don't take this.

Writing 20: Defining Diseases.  Overall Klaits is a good guy, if you seek his help he'll definitely sit down and help you.  The class will kick your ass though, he definitely assigns significantly more work than most other writing 20 professors.  If you're trying to learn, take his class; if you want an easy writing 20, stay far, far away from him.
Super nice professor. Love Kusum!
Best teacher I've ever had.
Kusumji is so kind and helpful. She is a must take.

KusumJi is one of the best professors I've ever had. I've taken both her Hindi 101 and AMES 191 (Indian Literature of Marginalized Society) courses. She is extremely kind and compassionate. She's super sweet and truly cares about her students. I would highly recommend her classes!
Slightly tougher than 100 level but equally as fun. Take it.
The GOAT. Best class I've taken at Duke.
Really caring, super accessible. Love this prof and taking more classes with her :D
Incredibly sweet instructor that genuinely cares about her students.

Kusumji cares about her students and plans several cultural immersion activities such as cooking classes and poetry writing sessions. First-time learners: don't be intimidated. Kusumji is incredibly accommodating and easily accessible outside of class; she made my journey from 101 to 203 at Duke extremely enjoyable. This is a must take.
Amazing.

Kusum ji is so accommodating for her students and really cares about creating a fun learning environment. She gives templates of the quizzes ahead of time and while her homework can get tedious, it is easy and meant for you to learn Hindi from. Highly recommend her class if you are looking for something relaxed. She is also very nice and funny.

Kusum Ji is awesome, best professor I've ever had. As long as you pay attention the class is super easy but you'll learn a lot. She is super nice, super helpful, and really funny. There's a lot of homework but it's easy and necessary. She does a lot of fun activities. Definitely take Hindi with her.

Kusum Ji is such a great professor. Even though there's a lot of homework, it's not very difficult and the pacing of the class makes it very doable. The quizzes and tests are very fair, and your overall grade is distributed across a bunch of assignments. Kusum Ji is also a very easy grader and I enjoyed the fun activities we did along with lecture.
Love Kusum Ji! She is always ready to help and makes sure you understand all of the concepts. Class is super fun, and I'm so glad I decided to take Hindi at Duke.

Very easy class and you pick up the material super quickly. Kusumji is a very lenient grader and the workload isn't that much. There are many activities in class to keep you engaged while also learning the material. Overall, great class.

Kusum Ji is a literal gem. She does her best to make Hindi fun by having cooking, art, and dance classes. I learned a lot of Hindi through her 101, 102, and 203 classes. If you pay attention in class and do the daily homework, it's an easy A class.

Very easy thermo class. Lectures introduce relevant questions and tests are very easy. Makes the concepts very digestible and makes it very clear what's in the tests. Easy labs. First half of the class is harder than the second.
Super easy tests, get nothing out of lectures- horrible lecturer. Can learn all you need to know off of youtube.

I think this class was pretty good since I do feel I learned something by the end of it. Lectures were pretty dry but I think the labs are really well made and that's where I got the most out of the class. Tests are pretty straightforward and Knight gives you a good idea of what you need to study beforehand.
Horrible lecturer, provides no notes, super easy tests

You actually have nothing to worry about if you show up to class. I don't believe the class curves, but you really shouldn't need it. Thermo has a bad reputation in colleges, but with Knight, it's easy. Lectures can drone and be boring, but slideshows make sense and are easy to interpret. Tests are free. Don't stress, trust me.
This is the worst class I've taken at Duke. An easy A, but you will learn absolutely nothing, and that'll come back to bite you in Fluids/Heat and mass (later classes). Avoid if possible.

Uses a lot of practical examples and brings in things to show. Lectures can sometimes ramble but you can tell he is passionate about what he teaches. Very kind and understanding. Recommend attending class as the lecture notes and recordings are not the best. Tests are not difficult, but not a lot of practice problems.

Knight is a kind professor who really knows what he's teaching, but sometimes can go off on tangents. Despite his knowledge, the lectures can get a little stale and boring at times, but if you find thermodynamic interesting then to a much lesser extent. Grading is in the middle difficulty-wise, but if you study you'll do fine.

Professor Knight is a breath of fresh air in the ME department. I learned a lot in his lectures, and probably retained more information about the class (Thermo) than I have in any other ME core classes because he focused on us learning the core material. Tests and assignments were straightforward and he cares about helping you learn most of all!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: hw didn't match the difficulty of examples covered in lecture, but tests were easier than hw. Content is dense and there's a lot of information thrown at you with little accompanying justification/explanation. Knox explained things clearly (except when she had a cold) and was lenient when grading exams. She provides some practice exams.

Class is fine but the material is confusing and there aren't many opportunities for office hours. The homework is usually unreasonable given the class material as it is usually unrelated. However, you get cheat sheets for the tests and the lowest midterm is replaced by the final.
She was never accessible outside of class.  Her tests were hard but she gave good partial credit.  Lots of homework.  Posts class notes, but goes too fast in lecture.

Dr. Knox's lectures perfectly blend mathematical theory with practical examples. Homework can be challenging, and the labs for the class are fairly lengthly. However, Dr. Knox provides all resources to do well such as office hours, detailed notes, and prerecorded videos. The course is highly cumulative, so be sure not to slack off at any point.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: She is a good lecturer and does a lot of example problems in class that are covered on the quizzes and tests. She is accessible outside of class and is very helpful during office hours when you have questions about the HW or lecture material. I would definitely recommend taking a class with her.
Really friendly with worked out examples in class. HW can be hard but fair given the lecture. Respects your time.
great prof. has very organized lectures and consistent homework
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Knox was great. She was very available outside of class, worked to make sure the syllabus had reasonable expectations, responded quickly and thoroughly on piazza, and went through tough hw problems in class. Definitely don't skip a lecture. Also, material is highly cumulative, so don't drop the ball halfway through the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Lectures were a bit boring but very helpful, you learn a lot and she does a lot of examples to solidify your understandable. Would recommend going to her office hours. She does a good job prepping you for tests and makes you work for a good grade.
Takes an interest in her students and is super-friendly outside of class.
She is very bad lecturer. People say problem sets are hard but its solely due to her poor methods of teaching Book which is pretty confusing is still better than going to class.
OK Professor but extremely condescending and very passive aggressive.. will get angry if you point out a mistake in a very childish way. Take her if you must.
Great prof, very fair, reasonable tests. Moves a bit too quickly in lecture but is great nevertheless.

She teaches at an extremely fast pace. The lecture notes are clear, but homework sets are fairly challenging. She is really helpful in office hours, despite being intense all the time. The tests fair and there's some extra credit to help you out as well.

Very organized professor who knows the subject. Teaches at a super fast pace, so nothing can really be absorbed in lecture. Homeworks are very difficult and strict grading on tests. Still quite helpful if one manages to find time outside of the weekly 4 hour homework to see her.

Discrete math is a difficult subject, and Shao-Heng does everything he can to maximize student learning. Class policies are shaped in a way that places emphasis on student growth, with multiple retake opportunities with no penalty on all homeworks and one retake opportunity for each exam. Prof available outside of class to help further

Amazing and caring instructor. Discrete math is a very difficult topic but Shao-Heng structured his class in an understandable way that gives the most leniency to students while still ensuring we learned the material.

Shao-Heng is the best instructor I have had at Duke. Discrete math is conceptually difficult but SH created a welcoming environment for students to learn. He made coffee for students in office hours and was extremely accessible. He remembers the names of all 120+ students and will do everything in his power to help students succeed.

Though he's a grad student, he's the best teacher I have ever had at Duke. It is clear he genuinely cares and prioritizes that each and every student learns the material at a high level. He was also very accessible outside of the class, holding office hours for 4 hours every day during reading period.
Loved Shao-Heng's class!
He's the goat
An amazing instructor. The concepts in the class are pretty difficult (at least for me) but it was clear that Shao-Heng is passionate about teaching and caring for his students.

Technically, Shao-Heng is not a professor... yet. But, he is one of the most caring professors I've had at Duke. While the content is hard and he has high expectations for the class, his passion for education and dedication to actually having the students learn the content makes the class seem easy. Couldn't have asked for a better 230 experience.
Great notes and sets you up for success. Do not hesitate to ask her for help she's more than willing to get you the best grade that you can on homeworks.

Professor Kolba is a real gem. She was always accessible during office hours and was happy to accommodate my needs with extended time on tests. She conveys material well and grades fairly, and if you do the work and study you always know exactly what the tests contain.
Kolba is one of the greatest teachers I have taken. She is very helpful when needed, gives clear, comprehensive lectures. The only downside is the homework every class.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: As a person, she is amazing: patient and considerate when offering help, but there are cons to every pro.  During lectures and her office hours, she tends to become a verbal textbook, allowing most of our attention to fade away. I see her love for stat, but she needs to be fully engaged in the classroom when it comes to learning something new.

Outstanding, a natural when it comes to conveying new ideas to students. Test are challenging but to the point where you will learn something but not take a huge hit to your grade.  Notes are incredible, as she writes everything she says in the board. If you put in the time to arrive at class a little early for extra help you won't regret it.
One  of the best professors there is

John Komlos is the boom dot com.  He makes economics realistic and easy to understand.  He uses real world topics to demonstrate principles taught in class.  The best professor I have  had in 20 year academic career.

Class material is very interesting, all powerpoint based. Grading is fair, most of your grade is made up of online quizzes which you can do in groups. Komlos is very well known in his field--if you're looking for an easy econ elective, this is the right class to take
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Make sure you read the assigned material.  The professor is strongly inclined to advance his own ideology and dismiss studied figures who do not agree as corrupt or incompetent.  Would not recommend taking the full class: just show up on the first day, get the syllabus, and go through the readings.
Great lecturer.  Hilarious.  Favorite professor in my 7 semesters at carolina.

An exceptional professor. Took his class at UNC this semester and I have to say, I really enjoyed it. The class is not boring or dry and he often butt heads with some know it all in class. While some others would less likely agree, if you have an open mind and an appetite to learn, you'll see that he's quite inspiring. :)

Professor Komlos can seem pretty strange and old-fashioned at first, but over the semester, the class becomes very close and you realize Komlos is a great, intelligent man. Workload was pretty light. All of the assignments were graded easily. Even offers extra credit. Pretty easy class as long as you go to every one.

The preeminent scholar on the economics of human biology (height and weight) in the world. Great guy, really nice and wants students to be stress free. Much more focused on learning than grades; midterms and final/final paper are very fair and graded easily. Take the class.

amazing prof. interesting stuff, just walk into class and listen.  assignments were very easy given you spent an hour or two before the midterm and final.  pretty liberal, but open to hearing different perspectives.  take one of his classes!

Awful at giving expectations and contradicts herself all the time. Doesn't care about her students, can't lecture herself but is very critical on others. Impossible to communicate with and never constructive. All assignments are filled with '?' instead of actual feedback. Don't take this class

Not as bad as Morris, but not good. Poorly designed course, very disorganized lectures. No overall structure to the course. Grading is completely arbitrary and based on subjective terms like "poor" and "satisfactory".  No numbers and you never know how you're doing in the class.  We met with our TA every step on a project and still got a poor grade

Ugh, probably one of the worst professors I've had. She lectures in a very disorganized manner & seriously needs to learn to stop saying "um" 20 times a minute. Grading is completely arbitrary and based on subjective terms like "poor" and "satisfactory" (never good/excellent) - we never get numbers. It's a poorly designed course & she doesn't help.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: So, so extremely bad. Lectures are so unorganized, she just goes through 1-2 slides and then starts writing unintelligible things on the board without clear explanation. Extremely unclear on guidelines for assignments - points are taken off for the most arbitrary things because no one ever knows what needs to be included. Avoid her at all costs.

Don't take this class unless you like to be graded subjectively on creative projects! A lot of seniors take this class expecting a good grade, but the average was a B+. Koelle made no effort to know her students, and papers were handed back with tons of points taken off but no explanation given. Completely unhelpful professor. Avoid this class!

Good lecturer (can be a bit fast), always ended 20min early. Answers Piazza Qs and responds to emails quickly. Really nice guy who cares about students - he's very accessible at office hours and readily grants extensions for reasonable justification 24h before due dates. Don't need the textbook. Would definitely take another class with him.

George is a great professor. Very passionate and always available for students - whether it's office hours for class related help, or meetings to talk about interesting research topics. Super friendly and approachable. Homework can be difficult but the class is graded on a slight curve. Tests are pretty easy if you pay attention in class.
He is very clear and invested a lot of time into the class. Slides are very clear. Materials are easy and covered much less than the breadth of textbook.

He was very helpful and clearly wanted everybody to excel.  Had passion for AI.  He made himself very available to students who wanted help with homework and studying for tests and answered questions on Piazza quickly.  I thought he was a great teacher and I hope he stays at Duke.

Great professor, knows his stuff and explains concepts very clearly.  Homework can be challenging but tests aren't difficult. Excellent addition to the CS department, definitely recommend him for Intro to AI!

New professor, so he's still clearly figuring it all out, but a great, very involved guy.  I barely came to lectures (I never go to ANYONE's lectures) and he was still super friendly and helpful anytime I came by office hours.  Always very quick to answer questions on Piazza.  He's a quiet guy, but don't let that fool you - he really cares.
I didn't find her to be an effective teacher, and the concepts weren't communicated in a clear or accessible way. If you can, I'd strongly suggest choosing a different instructor.

This professor is not a good instructor and does not explain the material clearly. I would recommend that students avoid this professor at all costs. The instructor would be better suited to work for a think tank and present data to fellow data geeks, rather than trying to teach at a college.

Her teaching style can feel unclear and difficult to follow, especially when it comes to grading written assignments like memos, which often seem to lack consistent criteria or feedback. classroom atmosphere tends to be discouraging rather than supportive. While she delegates some responsibilities to TAs, they are greek life nepotism
Ridiculous class and grading style. She is obviously going to push one narrative and if you or the TA does not like it, then you will be harped on it. Do take care to avoid this all.
inconsistent.
not good, not good at all! teacher—grades memos arbitrarily and generally creates a negative atmosphere.

So this professor uses TA's who are in the same greek organizations as some of the students in her class. Above all, she has a certain political bent that will lower your grade if you are perhaps not of the same normative priors. DO NOT TAKE!

Sarah was the best professor I had all semester! She breaks down a tough topic in a structured manner. That does not mean her course is easy, though. You have to work hard and show up which explains the disgruntled ratings. But she is passionate about teaching and if you put in the effort, she provides all of the resources for you to get an A.

Loved Professor Komisarow! I had her for PUBPOL822. Her classroom is a flipped style, where we would watch video lectures at home (I always did mine on 2x speed) and she reinforced information in class. She is funny and genuinely cares about her students. If you do the readings, attend lecture/lab you are pretty much guaranteed a good grade

Professor Komisarow is a tough and direct professor. However, if you pay attention in her class and make an effort, you will easily be able to learn the content and apply it to real-life applications. She makes an effort to engage her students in the MPP program, and I would definitely take her class again.

Professor Komisarow is amazing! She gives clear lectures and let's you know all you need to know to do well for projects and presentations. There are no surprises on the test, overall a great professor!

Professor Komisarow is great. Her grading is clear, consistent, and she gives you good guidance on all assignments. She explains concepts well and provides video lectures before each class which helps to clarify.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Terrible teacher - memos graded arbitrarily, bad vibes generally

Sarah is so concerned with proving her own intelligence (and confronting her lack of experience) that she belittles her students. She is overly pedantic and an authoritarian in the classroom. She is best known for dismissing the contradicting views of her students and refusing to present any sort of rubric. Do what you can to stay away.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She cant be bothered to respect her students. Even though she is so young, she is overly concerned with proving her experience by belittling her students. She is pedantic and quite frankly an authoritarian as an advisor.

She will form an opinion on you and then never change it. To be clear I worked hard and got an A but I had to kiss up to her non-stop. She picks favorites and offers those students more access and assistance than other students. She is pejorative and disrespectful and believes she knows everything (even though she has no professional experience).
Cannot echo enough what others have said. To put it bluntly, she is awful.
Not accessible, grades hard just for the sake of it. Submitted for a regrade and my score went down.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
awful
1)hellbent on enforcing her liberal bias- forced to memorize the speech given by a liberal talking head (my year barney frank)
2)memo grading is completely arbitrary because TA's in the same srats/frats/orgs will receive the A's-lucky me
3)0 care to help students with their grades, no office hours,TOOK DOWN SAKAI
true under penalty of perjury
No criteria for anything.

Komisarow does a great job teaching the 155 material in a way that is extremely easy to understand. The memos are somewhat challenging but if you go to her extended office hours before the memo is due she gives very specific feedback on what you need to improve to get an A. Extremely organized and managed the transition to online class very well.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: DO NOT take a class with Komisarow. Worst decision I've made, one of the toughest classes. She makes 155 (already a bad class) one hundred times worse than it needs to be. Expectations for memos are extremely unclear and there is no grading rubric provided. She tests unnecessarily hard and does not seem to care all that much about her students.

DO NOT TAKE PUBPOL 155 WITH HER!! The class material is not hard and her midterms are relatively easy, but the grading criteria for memos is so unclear and completely arbitrary. Her lectures are okay, but she talks to students like we're in elementary school and repeats herself way too much. It's also possible she curves the class down.

Would never take a class with her again. Her class and grading are really arbitrary, confusing, and impossible to prepare for. She lectures like her students are 5 yo but the tests are literally genius level its so hard. There is NO RUBRIC for grading memos so you are on your own there and even the TAs seem unaware of what she expects. CANCELED!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Lectures move slowly, but you have to go to class: it isn't recorded, and posted lecture slides are entirely unhelpful. Exams are easy, though, and entirely multiple choice (with a couple fill in the blank). Overall, not a great professor, but the class is easy if you keep up with the work.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Komisarow is a good person with caring research goals. This class is always going to be a mediocre/bad experience for every student, but there are ways to make it better. Her communication with students and TAs was not existent, even TAs did not fully understand assignments/expectations. She does not understand students, needs practice.

Professor Komisarow is a good lecturer and seems like a nice lady. The content of this class is not very difficult. The tests are very tricky and the memos are graded incredibly arbitrarily by the TA's. Tests are not many questions, so missing three questions can amount to a C. Do not take this class if you are not sure that you want to major in PP

Sarah is great. People really don't give her enough credit. If you want to do well you need to go to class every day and go to Office Hours. Sarah & the TAs are so helpful if you put in the work. the concepts are easy but the problems tricky. go to class and you'll be fine!!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She's not a bad teacher, definitely a helpful lecturer, but there's absolutely no communication at all. The memo grading is insanely harsh, and at the point at which she doesn't even tell you what should go in a good memo, it's hard to fix mistakes. TA's are also all over the place on grading.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Lectures are boring and pointless because she presents material with the least amount of explanation possible. There are no rubrics for memos, so it is hard to tell what she is looking for The tests have few questions and all multiple choice, so small mistakes can tank your entire grade. Only take if PUBPOL major!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: just avoid any class that she teaches

Grading for memos is arbitrary. She has to curve down to a 2.7 so her tests point distribution are set up for you to get a bad grade. Her lectures are redundant and she explains like we are middle schoolers.

She spends too much time in class going over easy subjects and then proceeds to be very vague about important topics such as memo writing. Once she didn't answer a basic question because "she wanted to put that question on the exam." How are we supposed to know it if she doesn't teach it. Overall, poor communicator.

When it comes to teaching communication is the name of the game and sadly asking to clarify things is not an option. She will continue to be polite but anger often vibrates in her voice as she speaks to students. Fair warning she does believe in stupid questions even if they are valid

Professor Komisarow is a great lecturer and professor. She always works to make sure that concepts are understood, as do the teacher assistants. However, the direction she provides for memo assignments is very vague, and she seldom is on the same page as the teacher assistants when providing direction for memos. Also, the class is hard overall.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The content of the class is not difficult but the grading is arbitrary and the professor does nothing to help.

Grading isn't clear--the content of the class isn't difficult at all, but the grading is too tough. You just get taken points off randomly without being aware or having been warned before. Memos are tough as usual, but she doesn't necessarily help with it. Been to office hours for a memo that received F and was told it didn't seem so bad.

Honestly, she's sweet. People in my class were very aggressive and rude so the combination of the semi-hard material and clashing personalities made a terrible atmosphere. Only reason I wasn't a fan of the class was because of arbitrary grading and lack of communication between her and the TAs. Also the Sanford bell curve is trash but not her fault
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Lectures were great and she explained the material clearly. But as a professor, she was quite rude and aggressive, and her grading criteria was arbitrary and inconsistent. She refuses to share her rubric with any students which I never had happen to me with a professor before. She is willing to give feedback if you manage to book an appointment
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Very organized in her lectures and does has a very clear schedule of what needs to be done when. But she's anal and rude. She's got a chip on her shoulder about being a new teacher and it translates into this weird aggression towards students. This class was easy in terms of material but the grading was quite unfair

Some correlate their grade with how they like the teacher, but even though I performed well this teacher is not worth taking this class with. Individual meetings with her are great but as its a 100 kid class its unrealistic to have just that. Those of you who got meetings during the memo periods and before a test congrats but for the others :(
Tough class, but you'll be alright if you keep up with the problem sets and attend lecture. The memos are tricky, but overall she was a good professor.

As someone who went to pretty much every lecture, I can say that Prof Komisaorw is one of the more clear profs I've had in terms of course expectations. I can see how it would the material would be hard for people who didn't show up to class, bc the slides aren't super specific. She cares a lot about her students - get to know her outside of class!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: 155 is a hard class, but Prof Komisarow was really clear in her lectures. She uses the slides as a starting points and if you actually attend lecture than she has really specific notes that she writes on the board, so if you complain about lecture slides you just aren't willing to do the work. The memos are hard, but I hear that is normal.

I think the comments on here are unfounded. A lot of people in my class were being rude so she said if students continued to be, she would let the TA's stop office hours at anytime. I thought she was an incredible teacher and very accessible. The memos are hard, but the rubric was gone over in class after they were graded, telling us how to improve
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Basically: you'll get bad grades, you aren't allowed to ask why, and when she explains why it will be vague and you won't see a rubric Find another prof!

Why make slides you post so vague you cant understand them when youre looking back at them? She is the first professor I feel like Im actively having to sensor myself around and feels like im actively working against. Is that a healthy academic environment?

Literally the most arbitrary prof. I know. Heres a few things she did terribly; wastes class time with rants about her students being "disrespectful", disregards all criticism from students, threatens to take away TA office hours, actually takes away Piazza, gives you nothing to study with for the finals, unclear expectations- even TA's don't know

I found her a fantastic teacher, just a tough grader and you have to go to class. She always explained the concepts extremely effectively and in clear concise ways, she was explicit with her expectations, and always willing to help. I recommend her, because you will leave the class with a clear understanding of the basics of public policy.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: She is a good person but a terrible teacher. She spends more time in class listening to herself than her students and won't accept ideas or suggestions on how to improve the class. If you're willing to stifle your voice and sit in silence you can probably get a good grade but if you ask "how was this graded?" you're in for it.

No textbook. Slides are purposefully scarce on information which makes it hard to study. Loves the sound of her own voice but not yours. Good luck if you plan to take this class, just smile and compliment the teacher a bunch than she might like you.
Flipped style

She is caring but lacks teaching ability. She often uses a flipped-classroom format, which is very ineffective. However, she has very clear grading criteria with fair grading and retake opportunities. Overall, it is a very low-stress class but don't expect to learn anything.

Professor Stephen-Martinez was an ok professor. Talking to her outside of class its clear that she cares about her students. However, the mandatory classes with quizzes and assigned seats really sucked. The homework is tedious and you don't learn much. The midterms are very easy and exactly the same as the practice. Take for an easy A.
Lectures were not helpful and the grading policy was not clear whatsoever. Would not recommend taking any course with this Professor.
worst person ever to talk to
worst teacher at Duke.

She was not very responsive to students' demands and she does not communicate effectively, leading to students being confused and left to tend for themselves. Specifically, lectures were not helpful at all and I am perplexed as to why lectures were mandatory. It's crazy that a 95 is an "A" in the class. Do not take her class.
Literally the worst teacher I have had at Duke. Unclear grading criteria on exams. Condescending attitude towards students. Do not take her class.
KSM makes me want to KMS

Genuinely the worst prof I've ever had. have to teach yourself everything lectures are a waste of time where you fill out useless attendance forms and grading is ridiculous. above 95% is required for an A and exams are entirely on things that are never covered in class. Extremely tedious and heady workload just to learn nothing. just dont.

There is no clear reasoning why she teaches the class the way she does. She talks at her students like grade-schoolers even though she teaches adults. Spends all of class time yelling through a bunch of mandatory forms that do nothing to foster learning. Most of the things I learned to do in this class were from online sources.

Such an annoying class for how useful it is. Has no clear grading rubric for Midterms and thus can tank your grade for small mistakes. She also is quite condescending in class and treats you as a 2nd grader.

I have never felt the need to write a review about a professor before and I am almost done with the CS major. I have never encountered a worse professor. She has no care for any of her students and only takes pride in being right. Her empathy for students is low and this affects how she sets up the class. She tries to trick students- it's strange.

Genuinely the worst teacher I have ever had. If she spent even a fraction of class time explaining concepts rather than showing us the results of forms that we fill out, maybe we would actually learn something. Flipped classroom style sucks and students end up having to learn everything on their own. Terrible teacher, 216 is a waste of tuition.

KSM is an absolutely abysmal teacher. She doesn't make her own video modules, and class is mandatory. 5+ hours a week of class / modules. To make matters worse, she is a terrible teacher. Going to class is absolutely useless except for the fact that it is mandatory. I genuinely think that going to class puts 75 minutes directly into the trash can

Very interesting topics, though lectures can meander, feel unbalanced. Kruse is helpful, a lenient grader, and p-sets are relevant. Some lectures canceled and lots of content (though not too intense) means throughlines may not be clear. Accessible prof., but I'd appreciate a bit more structure and depth over breadth. He has neat research!

Dr. Kruse is very knowledgeable on the material. This class is an intro to quantum mechanics, relativistic particle behavior, and particle accelerators, so there is a lot to get through, but he does his best and does not test you on the hardest concepts. The class itself is graded very leniently, I would highly recommend taking it.

Co-taught this class and wasn't present for half the classes.  He's a nice professor and is helpful in explaining physics concepts, but the class was horrible and he supported a really unfair grading scale.

Astronomy is hard to make boring, but he did it. Really nice guy, but he showed up for lectures unprepared with long slides and it was hard not to sleep through. He didn't do any demonstrations and answered emails 50% of the time. Didn't learn anything and grading was easy. I recommend taking with someone else.
Just listen to the words of wisdom that he speaks and you will definitely get an A in the class. His Kiwi accent makes my heart melt.
Great accent. Solid lecturer. Thorough in his lectures and his explanations. Performs a couple cool demonstrations too throughout the course.
Definitely recommend Kruse. Very clear lecturer, interesting demos, and fair tests. He also throws in some fascinating stuff going on at CERN from time to time. Learned a lot with Kruse.
Mark Kruse is the coolest guy.  Don't know why he is teaching this class considering he researches at CERN but he is a great teacher and his explanations of the material are really solid
Not too much work but not the easiest A since he grades the entire class on a curve with only 40% or so getting an A- or higher.
Best class I have taken at duke. Class is made up of 3 presentation/book reports. Extremely low stakes. if you do them you will get an A.

Best 400 level fecon at duke. Kreicher is super chill and lectures about securitizations pretty well. Class is made up of 3 book reports and a group project. Also 3 guest appearances from head of Barclays securitizations division

Exams are graded with no partial credit and questions are often mutli part. So if you make a minor miscalculation on part A, you automatically miss parts B,C,D, etc. Which can end up being 8-10 points on a 40 point exam. The entire grade is basically just 3 midterms and he grades on a curve so only the top ~20% gets As and the next 20% get A-'s.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Kreicher is a nice guy, and while his lectures can be a bit dry, you can easily catch up by reading the class slides. Tests were somewhat difficult but he is extremely generous with grading. Just score a little bit above the median and you should be able to get an A. Definitely learned a lot in this class and very useful for any finance students.

Solid prof. Although dry, the class was well-organized, fair, and consistent. Barely any work for the class - 3 midterms + 3 short psets +  completion worksheets in class + a 2-sentence summary/week on a news article. Pretty quantitative but not too complicated - plug and chug. Said was graded on a curve but I did a tad above the median and got A

Classic trade between easy A and interesting class. Dry lectures, and the professor often talks beyond class ends. It is not worth going to the lectures since everything is on the slides. What the professor teaches is different from what he tests, but the exam questions are essentially the same every year.

Hes a nice teacher with lots of knowledge. He cares about his students. However, because of COVID, all tests are all or nothing with no partial credit so it is a hard transition. Also, the classes were asynchronous but he had 3 hours worth of office hours.
Awesome teacher, awesome person, love this class. One of the best teachers for core classes
Great lectures, not too much work, and very fair exams
Best 205 professor, especially if you take this after taking 201 with Marta
Amazing all around, great person to be around and an awesome professor

Professor Kranton is one of the kindest professors I have had at Duke. She truly wants everyone to succeed and is often available to help answer questions. In the beginning it was difficult to apply the broader lecture topics to the exams, but once acclimated it gets a lot easier to perform well. The exam policy is also forgiving which is a plus.
Incredibly kind and great lecturer. Exams were fair and she really strives for everyone to succeed.

One of the best professors in the Economics department. The course was organized with excellent detail and she truly wanted all of her students to succeed. She made sure we all followed along and was amazing at answering questions. Compared to Nechyba's large lectures in 201, Rachel was able to effectively personalize the Econ learning experience.

Professor Kranton is probably the most caring professor I've had at Duke. Once you get used to her note taking style, the class is easy to understand, especially since she pauses often to make sure the students are still with her. Super nice teacher, helpful at office hours, topics cant get convoluted but will take extra time to elucidate things.
Great professor all around. Makes sure that we are all alright.

Kranton has much improved 205 from previous years. She is aware of negative feedback in the past and actively makes an effort to help students. Tests are also not very difficult, and there is always an opportunity to get an A as all midterms can be replaced by final.
Easy contents. Quizzes will be announced beforehand and only the best 5 will count.

Awful Lecturer. Takes way too long to explain topics and you're left more confused at the end than in the beginning. Doesn't use examples in class so you have to rely on TA's and discussions for examples of what she's teaching. Does not take in-class feedback well.

To pass Duke econ you need a good teacher, textbook, or TA. Kranton had none. Her lectures deviated largely from the TB, so there wasn't another way to learn than by attending lecture. Lectures had few to no examples and quickly become convoluted. The practice exams and PS are the same, so again, there were few examples of the material.

Brutal class -> you really have to put in the work. Clear lecturer. In class quizzes/hw, but plenty of notice. TA grader was awful (so many regrade requests) but not Kranton's fault. Genuinely cares about students and tries, just very hard class so I think alot of ratings are just people who did bad
Lecture-heavy, but Prof. Kranton is there to help you understand and navigate, definitely one of the better experiences I've had.
Definitely higher on the spectrum of core economics professors at Duke. It's challenging material, but Prof. Kranton makes it make sense.

I don't know what's up with those five super negative reviews but Professor Kranton is definitely one of the better economics professors here at Duke. She makes the material accessible and straightforward, and will go to lengths to make sure students understand.

Really fantastic professor who puts a lot of effort into making the lectures clear to students. She's made many changes to her class that really motivates students and makes learning economics interesting. She is also SUPER accessible. She's so caring and makes an effort to get to know you and help you out.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Terrible Lecturer
Professor Kranton went to great lengths to make the material more accessible.

Kranton's not all that bad honestly. Exam's are tough but definitely doable as she posts several past exams. Lectures were pretty clear too, but it certainly helps if you did well in 201. There were apparently a bunch of disgruntled kids in the class, seeing the reviews below, but I thought she was pretty close to the "average" professor in Econ.

She is a nice lady, very motherly. She is also a distinguished scholar in the field of economics. But there is a serious disconnect between what she teaches and what she tests. She dwells in the theoretical model, spends too much time explaining simple concept. Possible to self-study though. Her notations on her slides are also confusing.

Terrible class. A shame because I actually enjoyed some of the material. She clearly does not care at allll about students and our concerns. And her TA was the most condescending and unapproachable instructor I have ever had. It is even more frustrating when she makes the TA handle all the grading and test making Never take 205 with her.

Literally the worst. She curved the class to a B, and not only to just a B, but using the median, which was a lot higher than the mean. She said at the beginning of the semester that if the entire class did well she'd give everyone an A. Was complete bull. The average was really high and most people did well but she rewarded us with a B average.

I usually try to mention good parts of each professor, but there are none for her. She's just the worst teacher I've ever had in my life, let alone professor. She doesn't care about students in any way. She will have ridiculous curveball questions on exams. She refuses to help students and does nothing to address concerns. Avoid her at all cost.

She is a TERRIBLE lecturer and makes so many mistakes during class that it's almost impossible to understand what the points are that she attempts to make. You can tell that she doesn't like that she has to teach this class (probably since it's a core lecture class) and she isn't good at answering questions clearly. Don't take her class. Seriously.

Doesn't care about how her students do AT ALL. Tests will be nothing like lectures, which are useless. Averages around 50s. Barely any resources or help available. Doesn't monitor TAs. Answer keys have wrong answers and most aren't explained at all or adequately. Would. Never. Take. Again. Literally the worst Econ professor I've ever had.

Naoko Kurokawa is truly my favorite teacher at Duke. She is understanding and, overall, a great teacher! The first few weeks of class might be hard and a bit heavy if you're not already familiar with the language, but it does get WAY easier.

Kurokawa Sensei is genuinely the best professor I've ever had. Japanese is hard, but she makes the language extremely accessible. There is a lot of homework, frequent quizzes, and a lot of Japanese speaking in-class, but this kept me from ever falling behind in the class. Highly recommend Kurokawa Sensei and JPN 101!

Kurokawa sensei was an INCREDIBLE professor. The class is structured to give you plenty of speaking practice, and the activities were fun and engaging. Kurokawa is so kind and is always willing to help you improve. First few weeks were difficult since I didn't know hiragana/katakana but it gets much better after. Overall highly recommend the course
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I highly recommend taking Japanese if you want to learn a new language at Duke. Kurokawa-sensei is very caring and the class is well-structured and interesting. The class moves quickly but I learned so much. Expectations for exams and homeworks are clear. Daily homework and participation in class required.

Kurokawa-sensei and JPN 101 are great! HW every day, but usually only 2-3 worksheets, quick feedback too. 2 quizzes per week. The syllabus says you should spend 1-2 hours per day studying, but I def spent less time than that. I'd recommend memorizing hiragana and katakana before the course to make adjusting to the fast pace of the class easier.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Kurokawa is an amazing professor. Just know that the class moves FAST. We go through the first 9 chapters of the TB but I know other JPN101 courses that do just 6 chapters. Class is 4 days a week and there is around 2 hours worth of homework and review you need to do before each class, so it's quite a bit of work, but do it and you'll be rewarded

Kurokawa-sensei is an amazing teacher who really cares about her students, and will help you get to a great level of beginner Japanese, even in just one semester. The course itself has quite a bit of work (homework/quizzes almost every day), but it is worth the effort, as you will come out learning a lot and having a lot of fun!
Kurokawa is such a nice and awesome teacher -- if you are gone for class, make sure you let her know ahead of time! otherwise, amazing!

Kurokawa-sensei is a sweetheart and incredible teacher. I've taken two classes with her and you just LEARN so much! Do the work and you'll get the A, not much to it. Work is graded extremely fast and there's always feedback. Italian and Spanish may be easier FLs, but Japanese with Kurokawa is so rewarding.

Kurokawa is amazing. Makes learning the language enjoyable and manageable. Very nice and has a good sense of humor. Class is very clear-cut: syllabus includes no surprises and there are plenty of opportunities to get a good grade. Easy A if you do exactly what she says.
She was so nice and had a wonderful attitude!

Kurokawa sensei is definitely one of the best teachers I've ever had. She teaches the material well, is enthusiastic about Japanese, and engages great conversation. She is always very helpful, and I always feel at home in her class. Give Japanese a chance! :)

Very good teacher, always willing to take questions. Encourages (very strongly) class participation, and gently corrects any mistakes anyone might make in speech. Like Endo, strict about tardiness / absence, but to a lesser extent. Unlike Endo, if you are missing something, she will not demand why, but rather will just ask you to bring it next time

It's a shame that you have to get both Endo and Kurokawa for the Intro/Intermediate Japanese classes. Kurokawa is happy and helpful all the time during class. She is never boring and really engages you in the class. She also has a sense of humor that Endo seriously lacks.
Kurokawa Sensee is awesome.  She is very helpful in class and also accessible outside of class hours.  She is also very nice and encourages class participation.  One of Duke's best
Kurokawa-sama is awesome. She has a good sense of humor and is fair and good on quickly correcting grammar so you dont make the same consistent mistakes.
A truly great language professor.  Her class, while certainly difficult, is a lot of fun.

Very helpful and friendly. Always manages to keep your attention and keep you focused and on point. Taught me a lot about Japanese. Would like to take more classes taught by her and continue to learn from her. One of the best.
No Comments
A professor who loves her job. She is organized and clear in her explanations. Class might be tough if kanji is a problem. Else, it is an ok class to take
Fantastic reading material and very engaging in discussions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Such a nice guy, super understanding with deadlines and whatnot. Very willing to help outside of class. Relatively few assignments (only 2 papers and some written work) but there are readings to be discussed every class. Workload is very manageable. Definitely recommend taking a class with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Ku is the bomb dot com! I took his Asian American Gender & Sexuality class and he was always helpful. As a seminar class, classes were big on discussion and Dr. Ku was able to facilitate class discussions well. He gave us many interesting reads for the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I took Asian American Gender and Sexuality, which was a seminar that was very discussion based. You'll be able to think critically about texts and their historical/political context. He guides the discussion so that the students can reach conclusions on their own. Although the reading isn't mandatory, you do want to participate in discussion.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Hard love is how I would describe Li Laoshi. She can be intense but at the end of the day, she offers up a lot of extra time outside of class and puts in maximum effort for every student to improve, no matter what level. Course does have a lot of homework though and marking can be tedious, especially for quizzes and homework. Need effort for an A
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Li Laoshi is probably the most approachable professor I had this semester because it is clear that she cares about each of her students. There is always upcoming hw but very rarely did I feel it was busywork. Quizzes are pretty frequent but helpful to learn the material well. The good thing about this is that a bad quiz grade or two won't ruin you.

Lee Laoshi is no doubt an incredibly difficult teacher as evidenced by all the reviews here, but there is no question as to why she is the head of the Chinese department at Duke. She is immensely hard working and genuinely cares about the advancement of her students' Chinese skills, frequently offering up her time outside of class.

I was placed into this class with no knowledge of Chinese characters but Lee expected us to have a strong foundation. Nevertheless, Lee personally gave me a lot of supplemental help so I likely did way better in this class than I would have. This class does assign a ton of homework though.

often assumed that we knew the use of the grammar so did not explain very well, and then when we were incorrectly using it, would make faces. she would often tell us that our discussion opinions were wrong. kept us late (

Lots of these reviews say that li lao shi is scary but that's honestly so far from the truth. She is a caring professor and I would gladly take her class again. There is quite a bit of homework, and participation matters if you genuinely want to improve your Chinese but li lao shi's classroom environment makes speaking pretty welcoming.
Discussions could be ran better at times but she has very clear grading criteria. Homework takes a lot of time. Not a hard class if you do the work every day. Overall a decent class.

As others have already pointed out, Professor Lee is both incredibly intense about her course and fantastically efficient in teaching Chinese. This class was very, VERY work-heavy, but every assignment had a purpose and a tangible learning outcome. This class is woefully difficult, but you will learn Chinese better than you thought possible.
hard to talk to. If she doesn't like you, she will grade your work biased

I started with Chinese 1 in 2002; it's 2009 now, and I speak Chinese fluently. Li Laoshi's class is a great place to start, and if you don't follow her instruction on tones and pronunciation, then you'll really never be able to speak Chinese.          I wonder if Frank Zhang is still a TA for the class... He was great as well--insane, really.

The others who have rated her are right. She's super-intimidating, and anytime I have to speak in my class I'm in perpetual fear of making a mistake. If you work hard you'll learn a lot from her, for she is a good teacher, but don't make any mistakes!

Chairman Li, as she is known, is dictatorial, demanding, and takes pleasure in making people feel stupid and small. However, she has been the most willing of all my professors to meet with me and try to get me to learn the material. I personally can't handle her intensity, however. Excellent teacher of fundamentals. Not a very warm person.

While she is a very, very good Chinese teacher (you learn a ton), she is one of the scariest teachers I have ever experienced.You go into the classroom in complete fear of messing up in even the slightest way, but feel what might be the purest sense of happiness when she screams "HEN HAO!" whenever you get something right She makes Chuck Norris cry

Man, she is intimidating. She made this old woman that was taking our class almost cry. However, she really knows her stuff, you learn sooo much in a such a short time. The chinese-militaristic structure of the class makes for a sink or swim atmosphere, most swim.

Chairman Lee is a beast.  She's intimidating, condescending, and pretty intolerant of issues arising outside of class.  You have to pass through her to move on to higher Chinese classes, though, so just DO ALL OF YOUR WORK.  And praise to the CCP!

Her teaching ability is of no doubt one of the best, but she oftentimes intimidates students with frightening smile. If you do all the work she assigns, you will definately get a satisfactory grade. But this is is NOT a joke class, Prof. Lee is known to be the toughest Chinese teacher at Duke.

Acquisition through terror.  Make sure you preview and review exactly as you're told.  Tests are rough.  This class is definitely a running start to Chinese.  Not for the faint of heart, but definitely worth taking if you love languages.  Will gain control of basic characters and grammer structures.
No Comments

I went into this course not knowing much about Middle Eastern Economic History& left being knowledgable. I still wish I didn't take this class. The lecture was 2.5 hours long &his lecture style was pretty boring and traditional. He doesn't post lecture slides to promote attendance. There is a midterm and final that are ultra specific to readings.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Highly recommend ECON 351 if you are interested in economic history. Prof. Kuran specializes in middle eastern economic history and is one of the most knowledgeable professors I've had. However, don't take the class if you're looking for an easy A. There are a lot of readings (200 pages/week) and the final paper is pretty big.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you read any of his works, you'll realize this guy is a genius with extremely thorough arguments. However, do not take this class. It has a midterm, a final, a term paper, and readings that you have to do for the midterm and final. On top of all the work, the grading is pretty strict. Respect the professor, hated the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Took this class for Econ elective credit and seminar requirement. Professor Kuran covers a lot of really interesting subjects involving the development of civilizations throughout history, but with this came a LOT of reading. On average, a full book every week. 4 short tests and one 20-page research paper, but I was always intrigued by the lectures

Professor Kuran is really well-respected and one of the top thinkers in his area. He has interesting arguments. Took Islam and the State with him which was a relatively large lecture class but his lectures were mostly engaging.
Kuran does his best to make a relatively boring subject accessible to the average student. I wasn't very interested in the material, but his teaching style made the 2.5 hour lectures tolerable.

He is the best professor I have ever had. His class on the economic history of the Islamic Middle East was a great learning experience. He inspired me in many ways. He listens carefully to his students and responds clearly. Really, do not graduate from Duke before getting to know such a phenomenal professor.

Timur Kuran is a great professor.  He's excellent as an instructor, he's an incredibly knowledgeable scholar, and he's a leader in his field.  This class met for two and a half hours starting at 8:30 on Monday mornings, but I had no motivation problems when it came to making it to class.  Kuran is a true intellectual in pursuit of knowledge.

Professor Kuran made a 2.5 hour class totally manageable and engaging from start to end. Expectations were clear and I felt as long as I put in the effort to meet with the teacher and/or TA I knew I was going to do well. Highly recommend this course to any political science or econ majors.

Great Professor!  Smart, clear, and knowledgeable--he is one of the foremost scholars in his field and is also an incredible writer.  I would recommend this course to any economics major, as it was my favorite at Duke.
Feedback on papers was very helpful. I would take this professor again.

Professor Kustra is a great professor! He cares about his students and was very reasonable with work amounts. His class was very interesting, and I learned many new things about international relations. I recommend taking this class!

Professor Kustra is very responsible and knowledgeable. He made the online discussions quite interesting, engaging, and thought-provoking. The lectures given by Prof were also easy to follow and grasped all of the essences of the concepts. He replies to emails whenever he is available and always offers prompt and detailed feedback on our papers.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: As one of his first students at DKU, I can say that professor Kustra truly cares about his students, as was very understanding of timezone difficulties (of which there are a lot at DKU). I was impressed with the level of insight he could give into each reading, and the recorded pre-class lectures really helped me iron out the difficult theories
He's an incredibly professor who really knows his stuff. I've learned so much in his class, but it's a lot of work; don't take it while overloading and make sure to stay on top of the readings.

If you love foreign policy and readings 400 pages a week, this class is for you. Otherwise, skip it. It is a TON of reading, you need to be able to memorize everything in order to do well on the tests, and Kuniholm is the most intimidating professor I had at Duke. He is super intelligent, but made me feel stupid.
professor has tons of knowledge; class taught me a lot; major problem was that i got wrecked on class participation when i diddnt even realize attendance mattered

Kuniholm piles on the reading, but the books he selects are very good readings.  His classes are intense and you can't get away with normal Duke B.S. in class discussions.  If you really want to understand Middle Eastern policy, Kuniholm is your man.

I took both US foreign policy classes with him and thoroughly enjoyed them both. He is a little intimidating at first. There are a ton of readings, but they are very interesting, and if you can more or less keep up, the class should be a good experience.

Kind of a scary guy...brags sometimes about being a marine and a tri-athlete...he expects a lot from his class, but he has clear ideas of what he wants and translates them well to his students (he's big on "gettin down to the nitty-gritty")...if u keep up with the reading, u should do well

This professor does a really good job at remaining personable to allow easy and encouraged communication between students and teacher. His teaching style is to create an open dialogue with the class to keep students engaged with the material. He explains material in an easy to understand manner and clarifies complex topics.

Dr. Lafata is a passionate teacher who cares deeply about both the course content and his students. He sets reasonable expectations and will do everything he can to help you meet them. His lectures are also engaging and encourage participation
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Lafata is very knowledgeable and enthusiastic about teaching the material. His lectures were designed to encourage students to engage with the topics and think more deeply about them. He welcomed open discussion and questions and ensured that the main concepts were clearly understood by everyone.

One of my favorite professors throughout my academic career. He truly cares about his students' understanding of the material. I always felt like I could ask him any question and receive a thoughtful response. His lectures were dynamic and engaging, driving home why we were investigating a topic and how they tied in to the rest of our studies.

Dr. Lafata was very engaging in class and gave great lectures. He always welcomed questions and was happy to go over concepts with students. The class was very fun and I learned a lot of new concepts at a reasonable pace. The homework prepares you very well for the exams and the group project was a good application of the material.
Amazing professor that cares a lot about his students. Very relatable and makes sure classes are fun and enjoyable.

Dr. Lafata is one of the most passionate, knowledgeable, and committed professors that I have taken a course with. It is clear from his lectures that he cares about the success and learning of the students and that he is confident in his expertise. Concepts can be difficult to grasp and even more difficult to teach, but Dr. Lafata did so with ease.
Very knowledgeable on the subject. Genuinely cares about his students future success!

He is one of the best professors I've ever had! I've learned so much about how to formulate research questions and approach them methodically. Moreover, he's taught me how to use "undesirable" results to tackle even more fundamental problems. He is fantastic at teaching material in a way that's comprehensible and relevant to your work and at large.

Kyle is an incredible mentor. He is always ready to give feedback and position you and your work in a way that is helpful to you as an individual and the larger ecosystem. His lab's research is super cool, and it is evident that he really cares about bringing up his students. Highly recommend getting the chance to work with him!

By far the best professor I've ever had! He really cares about his students and makes every effort to make sure everyone is on the same page. Kyle is also an excellent lecturer and makes complex concepts as digestible as possible while connecting them to practical applications. He's super accessible out of class and is a great mentor as well!
Lectures quickly and gives lots of relevant content.

Dr. Lafata showed that he cared for the students' learning by encouraging our participation and explaining things in such ways that we can understand them by working from the fundamentals up. I wish he taught more classes since his explanations and humor helped me closely follow each topic he talked about.

Dr. Lafata is a great instructor who generally cares about his students knowing the material. He is extremely patient and kind in answering questions, and goes out of his way to make himself available outside of class. He is also extremely knowledgeable on the subjects he teaches. His lectures are both insightful and fun!

Kyle is good at bringing an interactive aspect into his classroom to help solidify concepts. He is also an excellent professor when it comes to interdisciplinary ideas and combining multiple stem fields into one, like computation, physics, math and biology. You can tell he enjoys what he does and what he teaches, so will always be happy to help

Dr. Lafata was approachable and available to meet students. He gave presented mathematical and biological background information, showing conceptual relevance. I have a strong background in biology, so I spent less time on readings and studying than most peers, but I still learned so much! He was happy to help fill in gaps for those who needed it.
Wonderful professor who is extremely well versed in teaching and always available to help students explore further into their interests.

Dr. Lafata is an awesome professor. He is super smart but also very approachable. His lectures are clear and concise but he does speak very fast. His class had just the right amount of assignments and readings without being overkill. 10/10 would take him again.

Hands down one of the best profs I've had at Duke, Dr. Lafata is both a great lecturer and a great researcher. He explains concepts very clearly and does lots of exciting research so there is always a ton to learn from him. He truly cares about his students' success and never hesitates to schedule meetings to discuss additional topics.

Dr Lafata gave clear, clean and concise lectures for MEDPHY 507 - Radiation Biology. His lectures were very informative, without being too dense. Dr Lafata was respectful of all the students in the class and was available and willing to answer any questions we had. I would wholeheartedly recommend this course to any interested student.

Good at teaching and homeworks were fair. 2 midterms, both of which def weren't easy and were curved leniently, and a final covering everything in the semester. Exams def required a lot of problem solving - just knowing the concepts wasn't enough. He posted amazing lecture notes before each class so it was easy to skip - please dont (i wish i hadnt

Bad at lecturing. Can't solve problems he doesn't have the answers to. He tried solving one in lecture, got it wrong and told us to not review those questions. Homework is graded randomly (also no feedback). Office hours at inconvenient times (i.e. 10 or 11 am). Had to rely on Math help room for guidance. Prepare to self study everything.

He explained topics decently well in class but made tests really hard (exam averages were 80 and 67) and didn't have a clear curve. Never posted grades on final exam. First exam was very fair but second and final were very hard. Wish he had a third exam before final. Homework takes a while and is graded by checking random problems.

He's a cool guy and a good teacher. You can tell he cares about the subject matter and teaching. Lectures are good and he makes sure to provide you with good lecture notes. Stay on top of it, and you should be able to perform well. The tests vary in difficulty, but your final grade in the class is on a curve.

Lectures are hard to understand and refuses to explain homework problems that do not make sense. Hard to learn from him, TA office hours were much more helpful. Homework does not receive feedback or is graded. Puts difficult material on test, class average was 67.5. Curves to a B rather than B+, so makes it hard to get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Liss is a fantastic professor! he is always willing to provide clarification and answer questions after class in office hours. Multi is a hard class but he had very organized notes and lectures that were very clear. his tests and grading are fair. I would take his class again, it was challenging but he was attentive, patient, and supportive.

Some of his exams are fair. Makes concepts hard to understand in lecture. I understood a topic he was trying to explain for 10 minutes in under 2 minutes from a different professor. Homework is graded weirdly, hard to get feedback. Office hours are during popular class hours. So unless you miss class, it's hard to go to his office hours.

Kyle was a great lecturer. 212 is difficult because it's hard to visualize things and content gets confusing especially at the end because there are so many moving parts, but Kyle delivers content in an extremely clear way. His lecture notes are a life-saver, and his tests are definitely fair. Go to OH and understand all your homework!
Liss is a great lecturer. He delivers content

The homeworks and exams were long and tough. But now, many months after the course ended, I realize that I learned real analysis extremely well - I am readily able to apply it to problems in my research (especially emphasized topics eg. compactness), typically without referring back to the text. I credit this to his focus on intuitive explanations.

If you haven't taken multi before, Math 212 will be really hard. Even if you've taken multi before, it might still get hard at the end. Liss is probably one of the better professors to get because he makes exams pretty fair, but he's not the best at teaching the basics. I only survived multi by watching professor leonard/multi lectures on Youtube.

Professor Liss intentionally wants students to get bad grades in his class. 531 is full of Duke's brightest students and he went out of his way to demoralize students and ruin GPA's.
