There are plenty of professors who do not prioritize undergraduates, but Professor Liss gets joy out of making students suffer.

took fall 2024 and the flipped style was painful. couldn't answer questions about the content and expected us to watch another professor's videos before class. grading was unclear. tests were super easy but lecture was boring

1. A beginner in DS can even handle this course. 2. A course filled with too much stuff, where many of them do not provide valuable outcomes. 3. Grading is too strictly followed, which may be good, but the ESNU rubric is too arbitrary. 4. Prof. KSM is hard-working and takes things seriously, but has absolutely no idea of what ChatGPT can do.

Took as elective for stats major. Flipped lecture style leads to a lot of busywork/wasted time. Only need 90% on HW to get full credit. Worst part is ESNU rubric - it is much better to copy her explanations exactly to get E instead of trying to think through the content yourself and write your own answers. Useful content but bad class structure.

dude idk what ppl on here are talking about. cs216 is so chill. you practically have infinite late days on HW assignments, in-class exams are almost identical to practice, and the final project is graded super easily. ive used the python data stuff in this course in my own research since this class so its pretty useful too

Actually absurd. Her research is in student performance/improvement so we had to collaborate with the people in our ASSIGNED lecture seats. Teaches nothing and relies on someone else's videos. Asked for mid-semester feedback to tell us why we were wrong instead of changing anything. Makes grading so complicated for no reason. 95 for an A cutoff

KSM was communicative and easy to talk to. She was forgiving and very willing to work with students on deadlines, help with assignments, etc, and responded quickly to emails. I liked the flipped classroom and didn't find any of the homework too much. It was a manageable workload.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Anyone complaining about this class has clearly never taken 250, 310, 330. The cutoff for an A is a 95 because the content is for middle schoolers. If you spend 1 hour/week on this class you will get an A. The tests are EXACTLY like the study guides, just with different numbers. All tests, homeworks, and projects can be redone for a new grade.

KSM is not necessarily a good professor, but her class is super easy so I can't complain. Definitely the easiest CS elective and a guaranteed A for anyone who puts in even the slightest bit of effort. Not super interesting content but Python/Pandas/SQL definitely useful for data science/CS resumes. Grading super straightforward. Would recommend.
The grading policy is really unclear and the Professor hasn't particularly helpful
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Take a different CS elective is Prof. Stephens-Martinez is teaching this course. The content itself is comprehensible, but Prof. Stephens-Martinez's grading policies are unclear, harsh, and unforgiving to students. The grading system needs to be updated to be a proper representation of every student's abilities.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Trust me: 216 may be classified as an "easy" CS elective, but this class is not worth taking at all and I completely regret it. Cutoff for an A is a 95, grading is not clear, and lectures are absolutely worthless/waste of time (they're mandatory). Whoever said KSM makes me want to KMS ate because that is to true.

She was not very responsive to students' demands and she does not communicate effectively, leading to students being confused and left to tend for themselves. Specifically, lectures were not helpful at all and I am perplexed as to why lectures were mandatory. It's crazy that a 95 is an "A" in the class. Do not take her class.

She has a lack of communication with the concepts she teaches, and would benefit from a better mastery of the knowledge she's supposedly educating her students on. To do well, you must do most of your learning outside of class.

KSM really cares about you learning the basics of data science, and her exams are very straightforward. The ESNU grading can be a little tricky, but it's definitely a good foundational class and is very manageable. When I took it, I had only taken 201 and I found the course pretty easy still.

It's hard to judge the class because KSM grades on a different scale, but the content was very easy and the courseload was definitely manageable. She's also very lenient with late work and the exams are very straightforward (coding exams are open note and basically just HW problems, in person are straightforward if you pay attention at all)

As a CS major, course is conceptually easy, but KSM creates a lot of busywork (comprehension quizzes & participation). KSM apparently specializes in CS education but I think she overdoes it and treats students like middle schoolers who need hand-holding. Still uses Fain's recorded lectures but attendance to her sessions + recitation also required.

Prof. KSM was understanding of individual circumstances and let us turn in homework late w/o penalty via slip days. Her lectures did seem a bit like review of videos that we watched for the prepares, but they were still good. The exams weren't difficult if you did the practice exams and homework, but the ESNU grading can be frustrating.

My background is about 5 CS classes and found this class as a breezy and properly-paced introduction to Python. KSM is very caring and accommodating outside of class. My final grade was rounded up, ty. Every test has a retake which made things way less stressful. Spent around ~3 hrs weekly. If u finish assignments u will def get an A
The grading criteria is vague for exams but other than that this course was amazing
I loved CS216, and learned so much from it despite having no Python coding experience in the past. Strongly recommend taking it!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor KSM teaches using a reversed classroom system since she believes that students learn more effectively this way. This results in students learning from a separate professor that has no involvement in the course through video lectures, while Professor KSM wastes 3 hours of your week doing random surveys through class and teaching nothing.

The videos from Fain are good. The actual teaching is hideous.
Also the grading system is hideous. What an embarrassment.

In class, you can learn almost nothing. The professor is just asking meaningless concept questions and reading the PPT. From this course, what I only learn is that it is really easy to become a professor, Prof.Kristin just reads PPT and uses OTHER PROFESSORS' VIDEO AND PPT to teach!

KSM is a "CS education" researcher, so she gets very defensive when people complain about her incredible research-backed teaching style of making you learn all the material outside of class from video lectures by a DIFFERENT prof, and spending all of every actual class period giving pointless quizzes, each of which gets taken twice for some reason

Everything useful I have learned has been from Brandon Fain or the TAs...because it's flipped and we use Fain's videos (which are helpful). The in-class peer instructions are not helpful, and her explanations are vague. Extremely inefficient lectures. Unless you want to be a guinea pig in KSM's CS ed research experiment, don't take this class.

KSM is a perfect example of academia failing in the real world. Class is focused around education research, but in practice, this turns out awful. Flipped class w/ videos from other professor. In-class portion is waste of time w/ 4-5 mini ungraded quizzes and time for practice. Everyone goes on Zoom and few pay attention. Feels like coursera...

To be honest, this is the most useless and boring course I have ever taken. The nature of the course is the coursera course. Moreover, the exam is hard and the grading is really tough. Some minor mistakes would drag you to A- level. You can only pray when doing exam while learning nothing in the class.

KSM is not a good professor. She knows very little about the material and relies on other professors' work to teach her class. Yet when you use outside sources to aid your learning, she doesn't allow it and marks points off because it doesn't "demonstrate your own understanding".

CS216 is a very easy class. However, KSM does not want her students to do well. Instead of making her class more complicated and advanced. She just tries to screw students over in other small ways by making trick questions or excessively deducting points for formatting and other things.
NOT DROPPING THIS COURSE IN DROP/ADD PERIOD IS THE BIGGEST MISTAKE I HAVE MADE AT DUKE.
All materials are from another professor in their group. Only exercises in lectures. Ridiculous mode of exams. Lack of trust in students while her mode of exams would simply lead to misunderstanding.

Prof. KSM is very caring and understanding of individual circumstances if you approach her outside of class. The course itself is flipped classroom and most likely more than 10 hours of work per week on average due to pre-class videos & quizzes and homework assignments. There is a semester-long group project that is very open ended and not too bad.

Pretty sure she writes reviews on here to pad her own rating. Often rude and unsure about her own assignments, heavily relies on the TAs to help students out. Does little teaching of her own and if you can't learn via youtube videos you won't gain anything from this class.

Does flipped classroom but has required in-class activities so you'll end up spending twice as much time as you'd spend on a regular lecture on class alone. Homework is often unclear, and there's a lot of it in addition to a final project and four exams. Only saving grace is it's open note, but that doesn't make up for the brutal course schedule.

"Oh I heard KSM is teaching CS216 this sem. Does she teach well?"
"Umm she doesn't really teach, so I don't know what to tell you."

She made the class flipped and all the videos are from Brandon Fain (much better than her) Doesn't teach much in class, and has all sorts of different kinds of works and assignments scattered around, which makes the class hard the manage. Really feels like a Coursera class to me, makes me wonder why the hell did I pay all my tuition for this.

KSM is a great professor that genuinely cares about our learning and success as students. The flipped classroom turns some people off, but she if you go to class she puts a lot of effort into making sure you understand everything. She also has a very forgiving late policy.

I took 101 with KSM and really didn't want to take another class she taught again. 216 confirmed I will avoid her hereon. KSM's has her focus on CS education and in turn caters her teaching style and lectures to be new and inventive. However, it ends up being quite esoteric, and many students seem to lose respect for how unfamiliar the class feels.

Best Computer Science teacher at Duke. Everything she does is to guarantee your success in the class. If you put in the work to pay attention and learn, you will get SO MUCH out of the class. There's busy work, but it's to make sure that you are keeping up with the material, which I appreciate.

KSM is very good at what she does but she operates on a flipped classroom model so I don't think a lot of her students get to see that. She is very caring and accessible outside of class to help you, but beware you will have so much outside work because of the flipped classroom. Also, too many group projects with no accountability for others
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: SHE DOES NOT TEACH THIS CLASS. It is like watching youtube and learning by yourself. The exams are also weird. Would not recommend taking this class with her.

Professor KSM's class was literally an EdX course. The flipped classroom was so annoying as class time was basically wasted. She was not good at explaining stuff and made simple things confusing which is not ideal for an intro compsci class.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Completely feel like a Cousera course

KSM's CS216 did not even feel like an actual class. There was no point in coming to class because it was flipped. All you had to was complete the weekly assignments. The material itself is not hard, but KSM deserves this rating because the recorded online lectures were not even taught by her so she genuinely did nothing for the class.

My course with KSM might be the single least-engaged Ive ever seen a professor. The course was a flipped classroom where she didnt record any of the lecture videos and spends >50% of each class - the time where we ought to be asking tough questions - silent as we work through trivial group work. Class is easy but comically un-engaging

Not really sure why she seems to be so polarizing here. I thought she was a pretty good professor. She helped me get interested in the subject and taught the class well. Was nice and caring. I had a friend who hated her though, but again I'm not really sure why.

Literally worst professor ever, turned me away from the CS department forever. Incredibly unclear at explaining even the simplest concepts, I would always leave class feeling even more confused than before. Attending class is completely and utterly useless other than to get your participation credit.
Worst professor and class I've ever taken. Do not take a class with KSM

I enjoyed this class a lot. Dr. Stephens-Martinez explains the material well, and COMPSCI101 has many resources to get help. This class is extremely organized which helps to stay on top of the assignments every week.

Although KSM might not be the best at teaching, she's a professor who genuinely cares about her students . Her assignment instructions can be unclear at times, but her open collaboration policies made things much easier. It's a lot of work, but I learned a lot also. But, don't be discouraged from taking it despite what the majority of reviews say!

Honestly KSM is an okay prof. My main point in writing this was to say not to be discouraged from taking Compsci 101 just because she gets bad ratings on here. I took it as a non-major just because I was interested and really loved the class. If you're going to get help it's from TAs, so even though KSM isn't the best, it really doesn't matter.

Many lectures felt unnecessary because they were repeating the textbook, but you had to show up for attendance points. Pacing can be awkward (lots of time on easy stuff, little time on hard stuff). The content itself isn't too difficult, but there's a lot of busy work. I think achieving an A is definitely possible even if you've never coded before.

CS 101 was pretty easy. I think KSM tries too hard. Lectures could have been engaging but rarely were. Her strategy of gauging participation was very annoying and honestly disincentivized asking questions. There were too many moving pieces for such a simple class. I think she could do a better job of answering questions. It was fine.
She was the absolute worst. Extremely condescending, didn't care to help, thought everyone was a computer scientist. do not take a class with KSM
Great professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: It's a very easy class. Go to class to get your 75% of participation points, and you can teach yourself the rest using the textbooks and the guided assignments. APTs are fun and help you develop a good coding intuition. Showed up to class a few times after MIdterm 1 but still managed to pull my grade up from an A- to an A. Lectures feel frivolous.

ksm is not a good teacher, but don't let that deter you from taking the class, bc the structure is great (txtbook, apts, and assignments help you learn). she tries, but has random metaphors/can't explain things well/is just bad at teaching. but very manageable class, even if you've never had any coding experience, just stay on top of work.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: The lectures do not really help with this class, however, they are good refreshers. Reading the textbook and do the hw helps the most.

I really enjoyed this class. Lots of work, yes, but very rewarding. It is a big lecture hall, but KSM is good about making things clear and encouraging participation. Expect to spend quite some time outside of class coding and completing assignments. But don't say that I didn't warn you: coding can be addicting. You may find yourself coding at 2am.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Though her lectures and teaching strategies are sometimes boring and borderline cringeworthy, you can tell that she genuinely wants the best for her students, and is very flexible with grading. As long as you do all of your assignments and not fail the midterms, you should be fine.

reviews.comment: do not like. she answers your questions by asking YOU questions. she might be a brilliant computer scientist, but she sure is not a good teacher.

reviews.comment: Although her lecturing style can take some time to get used to, the class was enjoyable and made me interested in CS.

reviews.comment: Kristin was a good lecturer. Her card system for student participation was a little stressful, and she could be confusing at times, but the lectures and questions within lecture overall were helpful. reviews.comment: Compsci 101 was a nightmare with endless homework don't take it with her!!!!!!

Every morning this year, I would decide if my day was going to be a good one based off this one simple rule- Will I see this professor today? She was the worst. I highly recommend everyone to avoid taking a class with this professor.
Honestly- have you ever heard of a G.O.A.T. ... shes the W.O.A.T.
She just had an annoying voice and always expects you to understand her when she uses bogus analogies
Bad at helping students learn- leaves them out to dry
She tried too hard and it ended up back firing. Professors try to act like students cant grade professors too

Kristin Stephens- Martinez is genuinely a horrible professor. She is not helpful to students and is not a clear lecturer. The class is completely self taught with really hard problems that are out of the complexity of 101. The amount of busy work is a complete nightmare, and you do not get a good coding skill set from this. Do not take it from her.
Not fun
Terrible

Honestly she did a poor job in teaching a 200 person lecture hall. There is no doubt she understands the material- she just does not know how to teach lectures. She tries to make it like a 10 person seminar. Not approachable at all. Just not a good person and you will get so much busy work. You end up teaching yourself the whole class.

KSM is not a good lecturer. You'll learn everything from assignments and APTs, which can be time consuming but actually kinda fun and so satisfying when you're done. Tests were harder than previous semesters, but practice a lot and you'll be fine. There are many places to get help though! GO TO UTA HELP HOURS! Not an easy A but Python is useful.

reviews.comment: KSM is by far the worst professor I have had at Duke. Although CS101 is a 200+ person class, she tries to make large lecture like a small discussion. Her lectures are more confusing than informative, leaving students worse off (ironic bc her research looks at innovative CS education methods). Her tests are much harder than earlier semesters.

KSM offers a great introduction to the world of CompSci. She breaks down the concepts so that people who are beginners are able to pick them up easily. She assigns quite a bit of busy work and the daily quizzes can be tedious, but they are not very difficult to do. Overall she is a very good professor to take 101 with.
Lots of assignments, nightly readings, and difficult exams. Lectures are optional but can be helpful, though half the content is usually unrelated

This course is a lot of work and if you don't think you'd be good at Computer Science, then I wouldn't take it since it is kind of difficult to get help and there are so many kids in the class. She is nice, but the work was not worth it.
Really cares about her students and always wants to improve her class to make it easier to learn and reach more students!
Good Teacher.

reviews.comment: Great professor, lectures can get boring but she really really cares about her students and their understanding of the material. Definitely have to be on top of your work and deadlines because she gives soooo much work. However, learned a lot about coding and would def take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: CS101 is a lot of work, but not too difficult. KSM does her best with a class that is hard to teach through only lectures. Lectures aren't super informative or engaging but there are attendance quizzes. Learned a lot.

Class is pretty doable if you stay on top of the work. There are A LOT of assignments (anywhere b/w 2-5 hours of projects + 1 hour of readings per week) so stay on top of those. Lecture's are kinda useless, most of learning comes from readings and assignments. Consulting hours are really useful. Her OH are also really useful
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Very nice but lectures not always helpful, spends some lecture time focusing on unnecessary material like vocabulary and study tips rather than material relevant to course

Professor Martinez can be kind of harsh and rude during lecture but she can also be very kind. I dont like when used the random color generator to pick people in the class for participation. The lectures are online so if you miss class, you can easily catch up. There are ALOT of assignments, so stay on top of them. They require time to understand.

I thought KSM was decent overall. An average lecturer, but very caring and willing to answer questions. This was her first semester and Astrachan basically ran the class, so she had to lecture off of his slides. I think she'll definitely improve as she gains more experience and autonomy. The course is not too bad, but stay on top of the work.

Kyle is organized, clear and patient with all his lectures. He is willing to explain everything with 100 percent dedication and care. Lecture contents and homework are difficult at times, but Kyle and his TAs are always ready to help. I have learnt a lot in his class and developed strong interests in data science and machine learning.

Kyle is as close as you can get to the perfect professor. His class is excellent: very well organized, excellent homework and projects, amazing lectures. He is just top notch. Grading wise, you won't get an easy A, but he is fair. Overall I could not recommend him more.

Kyle's is an amazing professor. His class are super clear and he is constantly motivating to learn. The class were super well organized and the material (textbooks) were adequate. Extremely recommended.
Kyle is probably the best teacher I had. He is dedicated, professional and always looking to make you learn something.

Talking about his NEUROSCI 102. He is a great professor, giving a bunch of extra credits, and is willing to help you with the questions you raised. He also invited guest speakers to share many of their insights about neuroscience. However, his course is fast-paced and requires a lot of preview and review to understand, make sure to prepare for it.

Dr. Kwok is passionate about research in cognitive neuroscience. He has a lab in Shanghai and introduces a lot of recent research papers in class. He is extremely willing to hear comments from students. However, the grading criteria are not clear, which makes me very confused when I want to improve. Also, he talks little about basic concepts.

Kwok is awesome. We abandoned a traditional course schedule and spent the entire session forming a research project. He is super laid back but a genius at the same time. You will learn a lot from him because he knows what he is doing and he has had tons of experience with neuroscience and research!
A professor who is very passionate in research. Very good in workload wise. Highly recommend if you are looking for research experience
A professor who is very passionate in research. Very good in workload wise. Highly recommend if you are looking for research experience.

reviews.comment: He's the most overrated professor ever. He claims that everyone gets an A, but that's SO not true. You have no idea what you're going to get on a paper or quiz or midterm because the TA grades everything and Kwatra doesn't care if the grading is unfair. Hope you love gliobastoma research because it's basically all he cares about.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Sweet funny guy. loves to joke around and just chat about science. Very disorganized though. you don't have to do that much for class to make him happy. he just wants to connect with students and is very passionate about curing brain cancer. recommend! he basically brags about how everyone gets As.

I really wanted to like his class since he preaches that learning is more important than grades. However, his grading system is very arbitrary, and you have no idea what assignments are actually important, and which ones are complete BS. I think he's made the class more difficult than past years, because this is not an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Prof. Kwatra's attitude is that his class is what you make of it - readings are mostly optional, and the focus is on learning rather than the grade. This results in a relaxed class environment with a minimal workload. Dr. Kwatra himself is extremely funny and full of advice for aspiring researchers and premeds - I would recommend his class for sure

You won't learn in this class unless you are interested in the topic yourself, but there is literally nothing bad I can say about Dr. Kwatra. This is the only undergraduate course he teaches cause he's a busy guy but he's super accomplished, interesting, and funny if you get to know him. Volunteer in class occasionally and you'll be fine

Clearly, there are very polarizing opinions about Dr. Kwatra. His method of teaching is not for everyone. He is a funny guy, but I don't know if that makes up for the lectures, which really are boring. Attendance is randomly taken, so you have to go to class. Assignments mostly consist of writing papers. If that's not your thing, avoid the class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Took this class senior year and it is perfect for an aspiring physician. The class is really laid back and you still learn so much about a subject you may not have thought about. Still have to read the assigned papers but if you do you'll be fine. Plus the guy has a great sense of humor. Also good to see a fellow minority teaching sciences
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Dr. Kwatra's instructions on assignments are definitely not very clear, which leads to a lot of confusion on what he actually expects from the students. Most of the time, there were guest lecturers, which were sometimes pretty interesting. His own lectures were dry, unless you happen to be extremely interested in the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: One of my favorite classes. Dr. Kwatra's primary goal is for you to become an "expert" in the field, so he cares more about you learning the material than about grades. If you show up to class and do most of the readings, you will do well. He is hilarious and is one of the easiest professors to talk to. Honestly confused about the negative reviews

He usually doesn't give grading criteria for assignments, so you never know what kind of grade you're going to get. The lectures are pretty boring. More often than not, the slides just consist of screenshots of papers and websites. YAWN.

Nice guy, horrible professor. He makes up random assignments on the spot, and never gives a clear grading criteria, so it's really confusing. Things he tests of midterms usually aren't from lectures, but from the LONG and BORING readings that he assigns.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Great professor that likes to keep the learning environment lighthearted. The course is based in reading journal articles and the tests are very straightforward. Dr. Kwatra encourages people to get excited about topics and his passion for them does not go unnoticed. If you dedicate yourself you will learn plenty and get a good grade in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Lectures are boring, though he doesn't care if you pay attention or not. Midterms are impossible to study for, and the grading criteria makes no sense. Did not learn a thing from this class.

reviews.comment: he's a humorous guy and makes the class super easy yet fun and informative. my favorite professor at duke!
Best professor I've had
My favorite professor at Duke.

Very interesting course and passionate teacher. Learned a great deal and found the content helpful to me as an aspiring researcher and physician. It is a very unique course. I appreciated the not-as-stiff, relaxed atmosphere of the class and really enjoyed attending and learning.

This was his first time teaching this class, so I'll go easy. No one read the (long) papers he assigned, but he didn't care. He tried to instigate discussion, but we were largely unmotivated. His tests were really easy; I'm not sure he even read our answers, and just gave everyone 100s. You'll only learn in this class if you do your own reading.
A good teacher all in all. Clear with lectures, but a ton of in-class work. Constant group assignments and pairing up. Also, beware you need to participate.

Dr. Mauger's class was amazing this summer! The subject matter was really interesting and the lowest grades in each category are dropped so it's relatively low-stress. I would highly recommend taking this class with Dr. Mauger

reviews.comment: I absolutely loved Dr Mauger when I took her class this summer! She is SO available and truly loves what she does. She drops your lowest grades on assignments, and is super personable and fun. Exams were a little tough but she allows plenty of opportunities for help before. We all had a blast in her labs! Dont hesitate to sign up for her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Mauger's Class is great. Took this in summer of 2021, and she was always happy to provide help and clear up any questions any of her students had. Super nice lady, has incredibly clear criteria, and even tho there was a lot of hw it really helped me learn the material. 10/10 prof right here.

Dr Mauger's biology class is quite loaded. I took it in the summer as an online course so all everything was VERY condensed. The way she assigns work can get confusing and disorganized, and the answer keys to our assignments are not always clear/helpful. Overall, I learned a lot from this course, and she is very responsive over email.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The class is based on a million different assessment styles (problem sets, group quizzes, individual quizzes, labs, exams, etc.) and her questions always had ambiguous wording and mistakes. She kept changing dates on us, and overall was one of the more disorganized profs I've had. You'll prolly get an A but it won't be enjoyable.
He has an accent so you need to guess what he is saying in a lot of times.

Gentle, passive and kind, no finals, the quizzes allow a cheat sheet and almost one third of the questions on it are for bonus. He will give you so many easy opportunities for bonus points, such as giving a feedback on an educational game.

I enjoyed the projects in this class. The lectures are often boring and he reads directly off the slides. The tests are difficult, in the way that, you don't know what is on them and it is typically very specific things. However, if the class is doing bad enough he does have easy quizzes or questions to raise grades.

This is my favorite class I have taken at Duke. You will either love it or hate it, but the class is worth investing your time and energy into. I came away with a new worldview. David is great at what he does and very willing to help.
David + this class is very fun and transformational ! highly recommend the most unique class at duke
My GOAT. Literally so different from any other class at Duke. You'll either love it or hate it
He explains everything super well, and the grading is fair.
Amazing. Inspired my love for math. Take his class!

Great professor! He clearly knows a lot. I experienced a very steep learning curve and had to put a ton of time into the problem sets, but eventually things clicked. Be patient and lock in during lecture to do well. Review every homework before exams.
Awesome professor. Explains concepts clearly, super patient and energetic, and takes much care of the students

Amazing professor--made me love math all over again! Super caring, responds to ediscussion and emails within minutes. Lectures are easy to follow and he posts them afterwards. Homework is a little long and requires a bit of self-teaching (grader is a little harsh), but exam materials are fully covered by his lectures. Very enjoyable professor!

Genuinely the sweetest and best professor I've had. He is so willing and happy to help you if you have any questions, answers on Ed and answers emails within minutes, and holds office hours very often. The homework and material is hard but he genuinely cares about helping you and provides many resources to help you succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Best math teacher I've ever had. Extremely kind and wants you to succeed.Take advantage of all the resources offered (detailed explanations to homework assignments/questions on ed, frequent office hours, happy to answer questions during lecture, read book before class), and the class will become much easier; Don't be scared of bad reviews.
Great professor and class. Tests and grading are extremely fair. He really wants his students to love math.

Professor Saper is perhaps the best professor I have had. Hes the right amount of quirkiness as he will through the chalk out of his hand as he explains Vector Value Functions. He is incredibly passionate about math and it shows through. For the class, he grades super fair and offers many office hours (at varied times!) and wants to help you!

The greatest professor Ive ever had. I had him for 221 & 222, and he convinced me to become a math major. A truly brilliant man who also knows how to teach! I know hes already the head of the math department, but they need to give this guy a promotion.

Brilliant professor and great person. He not only teaches exceptionally well, but he also genuinely cares about his students. I truly feel privileged to have been taught by Dr. Saper. Fairly challenging class, but if youre willing to work hard (and show up to office hours), you can succeed.
Very hard class, like very hard but the professor is a very lenient grader.

Very high energy guy and a fantastic lecturer. He will always respond to your email five minutes after you sent it (even at 1 am, I don't know when this guy sleeps). I highly recommend for linear algebra.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: A genius that cares about his students and wants them to do well. He is also and inspiring lecturer that will challenge you. Definitely not an easy A tho.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Saper is a wonderful prof. He gets off topic sometimes, but it often benefits you. Make sure to attend all lectures and office hours! He wants to help you succeed!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Great Lecturer; answers questions really clearly

Easily one of the best professors I've had. I was challenged continually, but never felt like I couldn't do well in the class. Homework is difficult and heavy, but it's nothing too ridiculous.  Top quality lecturer, Saper also put in a ton of time during office hours to help students out. You'll get out of this class as much as you put in.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: The transition to college mathematics can be difficult, but Prof. Saper does an amazing job at guiding students through proof writing in linear algebra. His lectures are clear (which is absolutely necessary with a less-than-perfect textbook) and he offers us his time and wisdom in office hours (which you should definitely attend). FLUNCH him too!
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Caring

reviews.comment: Great teacher! He offers a lot of Office Hours and is very careful towards his students.
Super smart professor, explains concepts clearly and in many ways, but lectures are long and therefore boring at times.
Great professor

Professor Saper is VERY fair. He's a really good teacher and genuinely wants his students to understand. He will work at office hours and at scheduled appointments to see his students succeed. His tests aren't too impossible, either - usually many students get As. My advice would be read the textbook and do and understand all the homework problems.
One of the best professors at Duke: Amazing teaching, always available during and outside of office hours, and extremely passionate. I'd have him teach all my math classes if that were possible.

This man is, simply put, brilliant. He knows literally everything. His instruction is so clear that, even though the lectures started at 8:30 AM, it was worth going to every single lecture. I am the type of guy that normally skips a lot of my classes, but never have i missed a single class of saper's because he was just that good.
Good professor, knows the material very well, can clarify any question in 5 different ways. Very helpful and nice, made a hard class not as bad.
Perfect. He ie sxtremely helpful and very fair in grading.

Awesome math dude. very clear instruction. His notes and study tests are extremely helpful, and make the class so much easier. You can get an easy A as long as you pay attention in class and do the homework. I got awesome midterm scores, although it seems that he is determined not to give perfect score. He is the course cordinator for math103.

Tough class but not Saper's fault. There is a lot of material to cover in not a lot of time. I liked him better in retrospect, after hearing how (un)prepared some other classes were. I like the note packets he hands out, and he is very willing to help students after class. Incredibly nice guy but not great at answering questions in class.

Class is difficult because there is so much material to cover in such a short amount of time. The typed up notes are very helpful. He'll meet with you outside of his office hours if you need him to. His tests were not as difficult as those of other professors.

Decent Math 103 professor.  I like the note outlines he passes out before he lectures, and he is always willing to help outside of class.  However, he is not the most clear in his teaching style.  Not an amazing prof, but a pretty good one.

Good, solid choice for a 103 professor. He does a good job of explaining the material while moving at the fast pace of a 103 class. Lecture notes were amazingly helpfull both for studying and for freeing us up in class to pay more attention to the instruction rather than hustling to write down notes. Does a good job of helping thoes who struggle.

Such a caring and kind teacher! Very accessible outside of class and a great lecturer as well. I personally found the class to be very difficult and took a ton of time studying outside of class for the quizzes. However, if you love neuroscience and are willing to put in the time, you should be alright. If you are not a neuro major, be a tad wary.

Dr. White is one of the best profs I've ever had - he's incredibly knowledgeable, enthusiastic about the subject, and kind and approachable. I ended up switching to premed in part because of this class. The class is technically a medical school course, so there's a ton of information, but if you stay on top of it, it's manageable.
Dr. White is a truly brilliant professor. I have learned so much from him. His neuroscience class is difficult, but that is the nature of the highly complex subject matter.

In the top 3 teachers of my life. He mostly teaches med school so his teaching style makes Medical Neuroscience mega hard, but so impactful I changed my career to study neurology and brain-computer interfaces. Hits the holy trinity of being 1. Highly respected in his field/research 2. Sweet and compassionate human being 3. Great at teaching.
She is fun, smart, and passionate about teaching.
She's cool.
Professor Lloyd totally inspired me to get a PhD.
The professor was great! I really enjoyed this class and see poetry in a totally new light now!

Really great guy who clearly wants his students to succeed. The exams were fair and based directly on practice material and problem sets. He cares a lot about real-world applications and focuses more on concepts than math.

Class moved at a slow pace, which made learning the content easy if you paid any attention (there wasn't that much of it). I mostly played minesweeper during class, but as long as you study for a few hours before each test, you should be chilling. The content summaries posted on Canvas were very helpful, brief, and covered almost everything.

Andrea's accent can make lectures difficult to follow at times, but I appreciated the concise chapter summaries he posted, which made exam review straightforward and efficient. The midterms were fairly easy, and earning an A on both was not difficult. The final exam, however, was significantly more challenging.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Not sure what happened in Fall 2024, when most of the negative reviews are from, because he was a great professor this semester! He's accessible during office hours, welcomes questions in class, and his tests and problem sets are fair. His lecture notes can be hard to follow without context, but he provides strong summaries of each chapter.

Entire class is literally 6 problem sets that take like 2 hours a piece and midterms that are very similar to past years. Just do the past exams and read over the textbook page he uploads and you'll get an A.

I'm not exactly sure what happened in previous semesters versus this one but Professor Lanteri is hella chill and nice. His lectures are also very easy to understand and cover all of the content that you will need for the exam. By far the easiest of all of the Econ core classes. Frankly if you don't get a good grade in the class that's your fault
knowledgable about the topic but it was a pretty dry class, attendance was required - class is basically all exams and problem sets, that were actually pretty tough

IGNORE THE BAD REVIEWS. This class was 10 times easier than Curtis Taylor's diabolical Econ 205 class. Andrea builds the course from the fundamentals to more advanced topics and the pace of the course is amazing. The textbook helps a ton with intuition and the tests are very fair if you study the textbook, review sessions, problem sets.

reviews.comment: The class can be frustrating at times but he's a good guy.

Prof. Lanteri is definitely underrated here. He gives great lectures that explain the concepts well. However, he doesn't have slides so go to the class early and sit in front of the room. It will be very hard to understand the contents on your own without paying attention to the lectures. Textbook can be helpful to review before exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He's a really bad instructor. Paying attention in class doesn't help with homework or exams. Notes are just random scribbles that come to his mind. Homework and Exams cover things never mentioned in class.Textbook is your one best friend and it is you and the textbook against the world. His TAs are also clueless. One good thing is he curves.

The course was frustrating while taking it as the textbook was sometimes better for notes and there wasn't a lot of practice for exams. However, I think Prof Lanteri cares about his students and wants them to do well. Sometimes it doesn't come across that way, but in the end, he was always accessible for OH and final grades were curved quite a bit.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Not the best teacher, but nice guy who makes sure material isn't too challenging. Curved class at end. Textbook helps a lot. You learn about all that fascinating microfounded behavior.

Underrated nice guy, really just required an intuitive understanding of micro-founded models. Does want students to succeed but the class could seem a bit tricky at times. Definitely get access to the textbook, it's a lifesaver.

Everyone here likely didn't pay attention in lecture. I did not for the first 2 midterms and was focusing on other things. When I realized I had to ace the last pset final, I paid attention in class, took notes, did the psets on time, went to discussion. Got 100 on Pset/ 90 on final. Just listen and read textbook in depth. Great teacher who cares.

Dr. Lanteri is a great guy who really wants the entire class to succeed. Yes, his lectures are a little random but if you follow his notes and read from the textbook this class is very doable. He gets a bad rep and a lot of the bad reviews here because the midterms were a little random. He ends up balancing the overall grade at the end with final.

reviews.comment:
There's a blueprint for success. The secret to acing this class is reading the textbook. Just relying on lecture notes alone can be difficult for processing the intuition behind most of the concepts and seeing all the shifts in a model. 

Tests and problem sets really do not deviate strongly from the textbook material and are somewhat predictable.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This was actually one of my top econ classes at Duke, Dr. Lanteri really tried to teach us real world applications of econ concepts and I found his lectures interesting. lectures were unclear, did not care about student learning, and was excessively harsh in grading and had a terrible attitude

reviews.comment: I can't understand why we cannot get feedback based on two midterm tests and also why we cannot ask questions about our homework before they are graded. Tough Lectures and heavy homework make this course the best in my course history.

Horrific class. Wondering why you got points off on a test? He won't tell you bc he won't give “individual feedback.” Need help on the problem set? He told the TAs they can't help until after it's graded. echoing what others have said-extremely disorganized lectures with illegible notes. condescending towards people who ask questions during class. didn't even show up to his own office hours whenever i went. arbitrary grading on problem sets (which were returned with no feedback and after the exam date). arbitrary grading on exams w no practice exams

reviews.comment: Worst econ core i've ever taken at Duke. I learn by teaching myself with the textbook.

Class is extremely test heavy. The rubrics have ZERO guidelines and if you get something wrong you have no idea what you did incorrectly. How many points will you get deducted on a question? reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Ignore all the positive comments on this guy.
Very condescending professor, acts like he's super chill but is not a nice guy at all. The hardest econ core course I've taken.

He's not as bad as the others say he is, especially when it comes to exams, which are easier versions of the pset. Your textbook will be your best friend, because he leaves things out in lecture and doesn't always explain things well. It is also annoying that he doesn't let the TAs help you with psets, so discuss the pset with classmates.

Lanteri isn't all that bad. The tests really aren't that difficult if you pay attention in lecture and the homeworks are fine. The worst part is the TAs. Many have no idea how to explain anything even if they've taken the class before. Don't expect to learn anything from them.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: There are aspects of his teaching style that I don't enjoy. He is condescending towards students asking questions in class (which creates a more intimidating atmosphere that isn't conducive to learning). At the same time, I think his lectures are well designed and the homework sets he gives help with exam preparation (which follow a similar format)

I truly do not even know how to articulate how miserable this class is. You can't even ask questions because he makes fun of you if you're wrong or if your question isn't up to his standards. His lectures consist of writing illegible notes that cannot even be used for studying. He also refused to tell you what is remotely on the midterms.
It's you and the textbook vs the world.
if you enjoy mental torture, take it

Why does Andrea make fun of people who ask questions in class? Why are TAs not allowed to answer any questions about problem sets until after they are graded? Why are we not allowed to see why we got something wrong on the test? Why was the average a 72? Why has my life crashed and burned since taking this? He should not be allowed to teach.

reviews.comment: i actually cant in this class. i thought I could, but I cant. i wish I still lived in a world where I never knew this man, this class, these tests, these lectures, or this life. i am so sad every Monday and Wednesday from 10-11:20. lik don't even know where to start studying, i don't know who i am anymore. but you should take this course, super fun

reviews.comment: The lecture style is 80% yapping and 20% writing down a few lines of messy math/graphs. Barely any slides. It is extremely hard to follow since he goes on so many tangents. You also can't ask about anything on problem sets before they are due. The textbook doesn't align perfectly either. You basically have to self-teach and pray for the best.

One of the most confusing and unorganized classes I've taken. I study, do homework, and attend every lecture and am completely lost in the class. He gives minimal resources to prepare and almost makes fun of those who asks questions. Class is not at all designed for students to understand the content or succeed.
He is awful. condescending and extremely rude. Doesnt explain anything and TAs are forbidden to answer questions about problem sets

In Lanteri's class, it's chaos and haze,
His notes like riddles in a tangled maze.
Questions cut short, no help from TAs,
And grades? Pure whims in mysterious ways.

Arrogant, blind to the struggles we face,
He leaves us all to run our own race.
If you take his course, here's what you'll find:
The textbook's your guide—keep that in mind.
lectures are very disorganized as there is no structure on his notes in class

Professor Lanteri focuses on teaching the intuition behind macroeconomic concepts and truly cares about the value that his course provides students. He routinely stops for questions during lectures and explains concepts in a very understandable manner. If you have to take 210, definitely take it with Professor Lanteri.

If you show up to lecture and pay attention, you will succeed. He does not post any lecture notes because he just uses the board, but he had engaging lectures and asked questions. The homework questions were good review for the test, but the only materials he provided. The class was quite easy content wise, and I didn't need to use the textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
Knowledgeable professor who's passionate about the subject. Little homework assignments & non-cumulative tests. The content isn't too hard, so if you study, attend lectures, and do the homework, you'll be fine. 

Unclear grading criteria, and lectures aren't structured. You have to attend class because there are no slides/recordings.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: You need to teach yourselves and each other everything (lectures aren't helpful other than for knowing what you need to go read in the book). The actual material is really easy, but he was so annoyingly vague about what would be on any exam that it made the class really stressful. Be warned, take it with someone else.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof Lanteri will test you on all the information he teaches in the lectures and will void information that may be mentioned in the textbooks. Lectures are disorganized and have little to no lecture slides. Discussions were more helpful than lectures because TAs tried to teach the material. Prepare to learn on your own if he is the professor.

Ignore everyone else's ratings. This class was amazing, and Professor Lanteri was inspirational. With the World Cup going on it made sense he wanted to be respectful of student's times and didn't have to host office hours. Tests and finals were straightforward from content in the book and content taught in the class. I 10/10 recommend!

do not take this class with him. no grading criteria, no general info about the class and what you need to know, no lecture slides, no hw/exam help, no TA sessions during final week, doesn't answer questions, extremely disorganized. seems like a smart guy but obviously doesn't care about this class very much
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
No practice exams or practice material in a *core* econ course? Seriously?

Don't take it with him.

Believe everything you read about him being a "disorganized lecturer".

No lecture slides at all. Does not go through how to actually solve exam or HW questions in class.

Also, no practice exams? Why?

Besides that he's a very smart guy. Even if the lectures are disorganized, they are engaging. Not worth taking 210 w/ him though.

The most disorganized lecturer I have had at Duke... no slides, no lecture notes, and messy handwriting on blackboard. He also often goes off-topic and skips sections in the book so it's hard to keep track of what we have covered. Problem sets are hard and the TAs are forbidden from answering questions related to hw. A very frustrating class.
Terrible lecturer, extremely unclear with explaining course materials. The course is disorganized and grading is hard&again unclear. I felt like I learned nothing. DONT take 210 with him.

no slides, every lecture is just spoken so if you are sick too bad. very unclear what we need to know from lecture - he likes to go off topic and talk about random things. he is not flexible at all. i needed to miss a midterm for a very important thing and he said no which is very upsetting. tests and hws are hard. made 210 harder than it should be
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Chill new prof to duke. take him for 210 if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: How can a professor who has a PHD in economics not understand what he's teaching about and only reads off the slides? Although he is nice, that trait does not help students learn the concepts. It's difficult to say I'm the only student suffering in his class, but I know many are unsatisfied and disappointed with his methods.

Prof. Peiyuan Li is very caring and kind. Although the course is rigorous in terms of HW and Quizzes, he makes sure it is very doable if you are willing to put in the required hard work. Exams are easy if you pay attention in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I would say he's a kind person but his lecture come off as too heavy slide reading with little engagement with students. Exams are diffcult (even compared to higher level econ I took later) but he deploys very geneous curves.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took his class last year. It was easy, but he had a lot of trouble explaining even the most basic idea. He is willing to help, so that's nice, Tests are also easy.
best 201 professor in DKU ever, no kidding
helpful professor :)
He doesn't understand the material well, so he can't properly explain anything. It was a lot easier to read the textbook and self-learned that trying to follow the class.
Pieyuan Li is one of the most caring professor.
You can clearly see how inexperienced he is. He is unable to explain basic concepts and complicates everything.
He is very kind, but he may not know much about what he is teaching...

He was repetitive, didn't know the concepts well, read a lot from the slides, and had a hard test. A lot of people CR the class, because there was a lot of uncertainty about grades.

I do not recommend it.

Professor Smith's class is organized well and the different kinds of writing projects and discussions keep things interesting. She's kind and cares about her students. I never heard her express her own opinions on topics in class - she just pushes you (in a good way) to support your arguments with evidence. Take the class if you can!

The content isn't difficult, and if you put in a solid amount of effort you'll be fine. Lindsey's course structure is very restrictive, and it's almost like you're graded on how well you can regurgitate her opinions. She actively rewrites your work and essentially puts you in a box with respect to how to write and think.

Dr. Smith is sweet but WAY too nit picky. She cares so much about citations/formatting. She grades the first papers way harder than she should and then the group paper pretty easy. Class in the gardens theoretically sounds fun but is not. She makes you walk 10 miles to get to the meeting spot and the trip is inconvenient when living on east

Tries to be nice, but can get harsh when you disagree with her. Mostly cares about her students regurgitating her opinions rather than arguing for their own points effectively. Open outside of class to give feedback, but that feedback is vague and inconsistent. Class was ultimately an easy A, but felt like a chore.

This was an eye-opening class! I didn't expect to learn as much about environmental justice. Readings were diverse which kept things interesting. Writing assignments were not difficult if you pay attention and take advantage of opportunities for feedback. The final group project was actually fun. And we had class several times in the Duke gardens!

Professor gives feedback based on whether you echo her opinions, not on if you put out good work. Doesn't make you grow as a writer, class felt like a waste of time. Cares more about style/formatting than making good arguments.

Standard writing 101 class. Don't take if easier classes are available, if not, she's super chill and invites good conversation. Write with a lean to the left though, go green and what not. Easy 101 but boring if youre not super into the environment and climate.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Smiths class was enjoyable and interesting. Her assignments are doable, fairly graded, and she uses a drafting process where she gives good feedback. The course content is very interesting if you're a nature lover/like city planning and similar subjects. She could be a bit more clear with her grading criteria from the beginning of assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Smith is extremely kind and inspirational. I loved having her for Writing 101 and learned so much.

The class has a manageable workload. Readings are lighter and more digestible than my other classes. She can be quite restrictive about the structure/style, but that also means its easy to get a decent grade if you follow her instructions. Revise your essays in response to feedback because it counts for grades. Choose good final essay group mates.

Biophilic Cities is a great class! I learned much more than I expected and Prof Smith gave helpful feedback and made class interesting. She's also just a nice, understanding person. I was worried about the final assignment since it's a group project but it turned out to be really fun. Definitely take this class if you can get in!
This is an excellent Writing 101 if you want to get involved in scientific writing. Definitely an easy class if you have an interest in nature.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: she's very forgiving
So kind, and her course is very interesting. Pay attention to what you're learning because it's honestly really interesting and she's a great person to talk to.

Professor Smith is a great professor. The content wasn't difficult, there were only 3 major writing assignments, and she provided extensive feedback on drafts. Beyond the writing assignments, there were reading responses due before class until the final project. She supports you through your writing process and is really caring. Highly recommend!

Pretty balanced workload. I learned a lot without spending a ton of time working on assignments. Very particular about how she wants papers written, so not a lot of creative freedom. Highly recommend getting her feedback on drafts. Don't hesitate to ask for extra help. Reasonable grading. Overall enjoyed the class, would highly recommend!

Dr. Smith's Biophilic Cities Writing 101 was super chill. We only wrote a few papers, and never had to read books. Class had a lot of engineers, and it wasn't very hard to do well. I stopped doing the readings halfway through the semester once she stopped requiring reading notes, and was able to just take notes during our class discussions. Easy A.

Biophilic Cities is probably the best Writing 101. The course was interesting and the readings were relatively short and interesting. We wrote three papers, and they were graded pretty easily for first drafts, and Lindsey always gave good feedback so that it wasn't hard to get an A on each paper, so long as you did the revisions.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Pretty boring but stable class. All of the readings you do deal with how great nature is, and this theme is repeated nonstop throughout the course. Grading isn't that harsh, probably because essays are pretty cookie-cutter. Just do your reading and write about how great nature is, and you'll easily land yourself in the A range for this class.

I took her Biophilic Cities writing class and it was really interesting and eye-opening. I definitely grew as a writer and Dr. Smith did a great job of making class fun and engaging despite all of the covid challenges. I definitely recommend this writing class if you can get into it - the topic is unique and shes a great professor and person.

She is pretty nice, but can be super tough and stingy with grading. This W101 is WAY harder than others and requires way too much time reading and citing sources. While the content can be interesting, it gets super repetitive and some of the assignments feel like busy work. If you have to take this class it's fine, but I wouldn't recommend it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Smith is a wonderful professor that really cares about your overall growth as a writer. This class has quite a few readings, but they are really interesting if you are curious about primate cognition!
Professor Smith is extremely kind. Her Monkey Mindreading class is good for the first 8 weeks but after that is just repetitive. Make sure to follow the rubric exactly for assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lindsey is a wonderful professor who will teach you a lot about scientific writing. This is a great class for you if you plan to go into research or have an interest in anthropology.

I took her class as a Math&CS student, but I enjoyed it very much. Instead of having a lot of concentrations on specific ecology knowledge, her class aims more at strengthening the general academic writing skills. Feedbacks were thoughtful, and class atmosphere was great. The workload might be large but it is definitely worthy. HIGHLY RECOMMENDED!!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Prof Smith is very kind and not a hard grader. Shes very passionate about what she's teaching as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Smith is great! She's super nice and you can see that she cares about the material and her students. The workload is heavy but if you have any interest in science or primates, this course is a must-take! My writing has improved a lot and I've learned so much. The only real negative is the final paper which is in groups of 2.

Lindsey is super friendly and excited about the class material.  The topic is super interesting, although the readings can get extremely repetitive. If you're looking for a zero-work, blow-off writing class, this isn't for you, but this class is not too much work and will help improve your writing.

Dr. Smith's was awesome! She's super nice and funny. Yeah, she has high expectations, but if you put in effort and pay attention to feedback, you'll be fine. Going to office hours doesn't hurt either. My writing got a lot better over the semester. And we went to the lemur center! :)

A great teacher, though she can be rather cold/aloof. Monkey Mindreading was straightforward in that if you did what she asked you to do (which was reasonable) you got a good grade, though she wasn't afraid to count off for minor mistakes. Always turn in a draft! Interest in science is a must for this class.
Lindsey makes this class extremely difficult for a writing 101 class. Don't take this class if you don't like to read or enjoy science. She's nice at times, but overall is a super harsh grader.

Throughout this class I was also having just a difficult semester and was struggling to reach deadlines well. Her brash feedback made it even more difficult to read through edits and understand. She is a tough grader no doubt but the staunch disrespect for struggling was discouraging. Not every student who isn't doing the best is slacking off!
She's definitely wants to become a great writer, but she's very nitpicky. She takes off a lot of points for errors in citations or formatting. There are also quite a bit of readings in the course.

Amazing professor! Her class takes dedication, but if you work hard you will do well. You actually do improve your writing, especially if you're going into the sciences. The topic is incredibly interesting and you'll be well-versed in cognition by the end

Great class. The work load is very manageable, only 3 papers. The readings are interesting and not too long or too many. Very EvAnth based. We take a field trip to the Duke Lemur Center. :) This class actually helped me become a better writer. It isn't an easy A, but if you put in enough effort, it isn't hard to get a good grade. Smith is awesome!

She is such a great teacher and person overall. She is very helpful and puts in a lot of effort to help her students do well in her class. A fair amount of writing in my opinion since it actually is interesting and useful in the end, ie. in understanding scientific papers/writing.

Great teacher. Expects a lot, but the class is set up so you have a lot of time to write and read things. Reading was kind of interesting, and I found the writing topics to be very engaging and thought-provoking. Very funny professor who is good at engaging the class and making her students think.
Great teacher, helped my writing a ton. Demanding but fair.  Also best looking professor I've ever had in college.  Wow.

This class is very research driven and while it is repetitive you really come to be knowledgeable in the area of animal cognition.  Unlike many of the other classes I've heard about, Professor Smith's class is one where you really do come out a better writer. It's a lot of work though so be prepared!

Lindsey is super nice and helpful, and the class itself isnt too boring. We rarely read, but we have so so much writing. It is incredibly writing intensive and all of the assignments are fairly difficult. I would say the material is interesting but repetitive. Don't take this course if you dont want to work hard. GO LINDSEY!

Professor Smith is a super nice person! She's a super nice person and very willing to help students. Grading is fair and not that tough. Not too much reading every week, but have writing assignment each week. The reading material are kinda of same every time, but it's definitely interesting if you like learning more about apes.

It has been 7 years since I graduated Duke and the bad taste from this class hasn't still left my mouth. I am a VP at a top tier PE shop now and look back to my college years to remember this as being the worst experience ever. She was almost intentionally giving engineering students a hard time. Her instruction was absolutely unintelligible.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Absolutely terrible experience... 2 years after graduation I still remember how bad her instruction was. She does not provide any textbook, notes, etc. And is very extremely demanding of engineering students who, she knows, has to take a class outside their field to graduate. It is almost at the level of hostility... Do not take her class!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Extremely bad experience in this class. She has no interest in whether students understand concepts. No textbook, no notes. Whatever you can copy from her complicated and unintelligible drawings on the board is your notes. I regret taking this class. Impressive how incompetent she is in relating to students...
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: don't take her eos202 class, if you are an engineer you will regret it forever.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Lozier is too smart for her own good, making her very inaccessible during lecture. She gives out homework on subjects before teaching the class how to do them, then gives a pop quiz on just one of those quiz problems that counts as a large portion of your grade. Not enough credits for the amount of formulas you must learn to manipulate.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: The class has like a handful of 15 total grades, so everything is weighted heavily. However, the subject material is interesting although dense, and she is extremely smart and knows what she's teaching. She knows the name of everyone in the class and is always willing to answer questions. But theres only one midterm.

Every other rating of Lo is extremely accurate. Took his class for FOCUS, get ready for LOTS of reading. He clearly is incredibly well versed in Middle Eastern scholarship, but lectures are hard to follow. He stays connected with past students and will help you get connected within the Middle Eastern Studies department if interested!

Very funny lecturer, makes the focus incredibly worthwhile. Well-respected scholar of the middle east, has travelled all over the world so is very interesting, insightful. Brings tea to class and cares about students (wont learn your name until november tho). Has tenuous connections to al-Qaeda. surprisingly adept with technology.

Geopolitics FOCUS class- Class is demanding, but easy grader. You will learn a lot, but the work load is high (essay a week and hundreds of pages of reading). Lo is a knowledgable funny professor but discussion gets hard to follow. Definitely will ask you a question but point at someone else and call you the wrong name. Fun class, brings tea.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Lots of readings but you will learn a lot. He is always ready to share and talk to students. His grading is unclear at first so it's more trial and error to understand what he wants.

Lo is the type of guy to say "you're in group 3" while looking at you but uses his fingers to point to another person. He's funny, accommodating, and has a deep bag of knowledge of the Middle East. He's very disorganized, bad at tech, but his humor and leniency in everything makes up for it. Lots of readings but can get away without reading them.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Lo is peculiar, yet it is one of his best qualities. He is exceptionally well-read within the field and has a treasure trove of knowledge. Not particularly tech-savvy, but he knows when to make things clear when it matters. He takes a serious topic and makes it digestible, all while creating a real connection. I highly recommend him.
reviews.rating_tags: Hilarious--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I took this class as part of the Duke in the Arab World program. Lo's class was super interesting, and he has so much knowledge about the region in general. He's a really funny guy as well. He isn't the most organized, but you'll be fine if you participate and just try to learn. DAW has been one of my favorite experiences, and I highly recommend!

Professor Lô is amazing. Truly. His lectures are always hilarious, and he is a true gem when it comes to spitting-out bits of wisdom here and there. He is incredibly intelligent (speaks SO many languages) and always makes times for his students. Incorporated Zoom classes into learning well, and you feel valued and smart. Choose him for Arabic 101!!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Lo is probably the best Arabic 101/102 instructor at Duke. Highly recommend. His class may be disorienting at first (a lot harder, depends more on participation) but your arabic will surely improve because of him. This class requires a lot of work outside of lecture and moves pretty quickly (a chapter a more a week). However, highly recommend Lo!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Lo genuinely wants students to learn, but his methods are frustrating. He deducts points for speaking English in class, but doesn't teach the vocabulary necessary to ask questions in Arabic. This discourages questions altogether, but he deflects any questions asked. Tons of homework, but if you want to learn Arabic, there aren't many other options.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: If you like clear guidelines about grades and expectations, I would avoid Lo (and most of the Arabic department). He's super unclear about what he expects, and is SUPER disorganized. I also took part in the Morocco study abroad program he runs and it was the most disorganized mess I've ever experienced. No one knew what the plan was the whole trip.
Lo is an easy A, take him for Arabic.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Professor Lo has a great sense of humor, but he is also very wise. I learned so much not only about the Arabic language, but the culture of the Middle East as well. The class itself is very easy, and if you put in at least a little bit of effort you will likely get an A. My only complaint is that guidelines for assignments are sometimes unclear.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Dr. Lo is a great teacher - he's very accessible and willing to help. However,  I personally thought he was vague with grading. He dodged a ton of points of my attendance, and didn't give extra credit points for things he said he would (such as attending Arabic events). I got solid A's on all exams and homework's, and still got barely an A- overall

Took Arabic with Lo but this was a culture class we took in Duke in the Arab World (Morocco). Class was kind of all over the place, there were interesting discussions but no real structure (Lo loves long tangents too). Syllabus was super vague and so were assignments. Lo is great but the class was unnecessary stress when abroad..

Lo is a really cool guy and I enjoyed the class. Arabic is a hard language, but he makes it relatively smooth. Grading is forgiving, make sure to go to his office hours if you miss a day, forget to turn in something, etc.. Don't think he gives anyone less than a B. Lectures are pretty confusing though and he tends to go off on tangents a lot a lot.
Arabic is a tough language and professor Lo takes you through it pretty fast paced. It's on you to keep up with the material. Be ready to devote lots of time to homeworks and just plain studying.
He's a great language professor for beginners.  He's very helpful and wants to see people do well.  The lowest grade he gives is a B+.

Professor Lo was a really wonderful professor. He is extremely passionate about the topic, and he is a wealth of information about the Middle East. He is not always clear and understandable. However, he is always open to meeting with students and addressing any concerns that they may have. Just be in class and on time!
Really helpful professor. He made Arabic so easy. He always brought some tea to the class and asked students to come to office hours if there was any difficulty.

ustaadh is a bit crazy and more scatterbrained in the second semester but he is super nice. he hates people being late but he frequently brings tea for the morning sections. the book is helpful for learning but he relies on it mainly for exercises which can be annoying
