Ustaadh Lo is the best. Despite the fact that he is a troll and can be unclear at times, he has made Arabic 101 a fantastic experience. He curves the class heavily and his grades rarely reflect what the paper actually says. Do you homework and learn the vocab and you'll be fine.

Professor Lo is the man. He is very bright and knows a ton of languages, which is why sometimes he can be unclear but he is lenient with making up work/exams. Although Arabic can be hard, Lo is crazy lenient with grades (the lowest he gives out is B+, and thats to people who should fail). If you show that you are trying you will absolutely get an A

Professor Lo really pushes us, but he is also really accessible for any type of help. He really wants you to learn Arabic and to be interested in the culture. Just give some effort and he will give you a good grade. Sometimes he's a little unclear, but that's more of a cultural thing.

People have said that the class can be confusing. It definitely is, and some of that is resultant of communication. But that's deliberate, he throws us in over our heads and pushes us to work hard to move past that confusion. Really cares about each member of his class. He can be extremely funny. I recommend working with and getting to know him.

Professor Lo is an awesome person. Sure he's a bit disorganized and unclear with assignments, but he is so helpful if you work hard in the class and show interest. I really loved him he is such a great guy. Make sure you take Arabic because you want to and be willing to work hard or you will be disappointed in the class as a whole.

The worst professor I have ever had.  Languages are my passion, and I am doing very well in his class, so this isn't revenge in that way.  If his goal is to be utterly incompetent and discourage students i give him an A+.  How is such an idiot at Duke?

Professor Lo is a genuinely nice guy and a relatively easy grader. However, he is not the most organized teacher and he is often extremely unclear when giving directions/answering questions. And be warned, he will berate you in front of the whole class if you walk in late and he DOES notice if you don't come to class.
Lo is a lot of fun. Not the most organized professor and I'm often confused about what the homework is, but he's really understanding, smart, an easy grader, and makes the class a lot of fun.

Professor Lo is the best. He can be a bit intimidating at first but once that subsides you'll be hard pressed to find a more caring professor. Plus he says some of the greatest things ever during lecture. TAKE ARABIC WITH HIM!!!!
amazing professor. Really cares about teaching. He's the reason why I decided to major in Arabic.
very intimidating and challenging at first but once you get to know him he is funny and entertaining! he's the man

Hands down my favorite professor at Duke. He really desires that his students learn to love the language. I cannot recommend him enough. Those who do not like him are usually those who just search for a grade instead of trying to appreciate the language.  And watch out, he sometimes makes up proverbs on the spot to fit a situation. great man

I alternated between loving and hating him because he can be unclear or avoid questions, but overall, I love the class and the man, and it is easy to do well if you actually study.  On a side note, he can be intimidating for the first month of class, but that subsides.
Simply the best teacher at Duke University.  Everyone cannot help but to love Arabic after the year.  The definition of a great scholar, professor, and mentor.

He's a genuinely nice person. However, he does play favorites, which can be annoying at times. Sometimes it seems like the grading is subjective. He can be very difficult to understand sometimes. He likes to answer questions with proverbs, which is not helpful at all. All in all, he's a great professor and makes Arabic easier than you would think.

Professor Lo is the man! I am not going lie, Arabic is hard class, in terms of the time investment, but this is the case for any new language, especially one not based on the english alpahebet. Prof. Lo is REALLY helpful, the quizzes are ok if you learn the study. The first five weeks are vital, because of you NEED a solid base in the letters.
Great professor.  Very well versed in the language, both traditional and colloquial.  Not difficult to earn an good grade if you put in the work.  Hands down, my favorite professor at duke.

Extremely nice and quite funny professor, always willing to tutor if you don't understand something.  Doesn't always explain things the greatest, and sometimes tends to jump around and skip over things at times, so you will have to spend time outside of class using the book.  Overall def good experience though

He knows a lot, but he doesn't know how to teach beginners. He starts off by telling you how difficult the language is and how he doesn't expect you to know certain things,but then towards the end of the semester he expects you to know all those tiny details he had earlier bypassed stating that they are too advanced. Tough to get a good grade!!

Mbaye is a very knowledgable man whose lecture sections are slightly disjointed, but if you don't understand something he will tutor you until you do understand it.  He's very generous with encouragement and constructive with his critiques of your grammar, which is just bad in intro arabic no matter what you do.  You will have to work hard for him.

Knows a lot, but is disorganized and has an imperfect grasp of English - not a problem in conversation but definitely when explaining grammar!  Relies heavily on hand-outs which creates clutter, and skips around in the subject confusingly.  You will learn from him but it will be a hard slog and you will have to put in a lot of work.
Not a hard class, but lots of readings.

The course structure and grading are a little unclear, but the class isn't hard and you either participate or you don't. Saying that the class is boring because you aren't engaging is unfair to Lynch because he does make the class thought-provoking for the people paying attention. Lynch has a unique humor, but I wouldn't say he is offensive.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The negative reviews are very harsh for Professor Lynch. He is engaging, but it is discussion heavy, therefore if one does not participate then it can be boring, but that is more of an independent issue because no one is forced to talk. He has a specific sense of humor but not offensive. The class is reading heavy, but not hard to stay on track.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The negative reviews are mystifying to me. Dr. Lynch is brilliant, funny, and a great teacher. Statistics is a challenging subject, but he makes it approachable and interesting.

I am not even finished with this class, and I felt the need to write this review. The class is boring and the professor is problematic. He made many offensive comments during class. He should NOT be teaching a sociology class as he lacks humanness.

He is a super funny guy, but the structure of this class is awful. He does not really teach and just makes other students present the material. He basically has conversations with himself during discussions after presentations. The exams are pretty easy, but also subjective. Very boring. Very repetitive.

If you had one hour and fifteen minutes to live, spend it in an online lecture with this guy because they all felt like an eternity. Honestly though, just find another statistics class to take at Duke. There are plenty more professors here who are more available and can actually teach.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The worst and hardest class I've ever taken as a sociology major. The tests are really the only thing you're graded on besides homework. The tests are hard and he's not accessible outside of class, he just refers you to the TA.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Its a required class for soc majors but is still the hardest class ive taken at duke. He seems like a good guy but the lectures are boring. hey thats stats tho. You only have 3 tests and the final and the only other grade is homework. Dont fall behind and make sure you pay attention in lecture

Professor Smith-Lovin is amazing, & her happiness seminar was rewarding. The papers she assigned weren't super hard, & the readings we read for class discussions were interesting. The blogs she had us write allowed for personal reflection on what we talked about. The final paper allowed for exploration of a topic we touched on in greater detail.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Not the overarching intro to sociology I was expecting - just focuses on one theory created by the professor. Really caring professor, but classes aren't super engaging. Don't get any grades/feedback on projects/homework throughout the entire semester, but if you show up, do your work, and participate, you usually end up with a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Tests? Not many

reviews.comment: Not a very engaging or stimulating class. The entire class is essentially focused on Affect Control Theory(which she is an active creator of) and while interesting at first, easily becomes more than boring. Certainly the nicest professor I've had thus far, however. Genuinely cares about the students and gives everyone As, literally.
Smith-Lovin is one of the most enthusiastic professor I have learned under. She is super excited about the topic and loves to teach students.
Focus class. She's really nice, a good intro to sociology. Not hard, everyone ends up getting an A, but you do have to do the work.
Professor Smith-Lovin is really nice. The class is pretty easy, but the readings are long, dense, and sometimes boring
Professor Smith-Lovin is very friendly and nice and wants to help you. Unfortunately, while the class was easy, it wasn't particularly engaging and the readings were ridiculous.
No Comments

Very deep understanding of subject material, she really wants students to understand and will put in as much effort as you if you have questions.  Unrelated to the course:  One of the most interesting minds I've met.

Lydia is a great professor. Her lectures were above average and her exams were very fair. She is willing to meet and answer any questions. Lydia is also very understanding and hilarious. Take her class if you need to take 353.

Hilarious professor - she's very human, very mortal, tries very hard, and it's just a fun place to be.  I zoned out during lectures, but I've never taken a class where that doesn't happen - she was pretty engaging regardless.  New professor, so she's TOUGH on grading.  Take her if you're here for fun and learning, not for the A+.

Pretty funny lecturer. People generally get disappointed because ODEs are hard and prolly they don't put in the effort. I'm not a fan of the material, but had to take it (engineer); if I had the choice, I'd take it with Bilinsky again. She always responds on time; dunno why people give less than 5 in helpfulness.

Pretty funny lecturer. People generally get disappointed because ODEs are hard and prolly they don't put in the effort. I'm not a fan of the material, but had to take it (engineer); if I had the choice, I'd take it with Bilinsky again.

First thing: It is not an easy class. Take this class if you are going to put in the effort. With that said, take MATH 356 with Bilinsky ; she will make the lectures much more enjoyable. She will make sure that you understand the material and deviate a little bit. She always responds; dunno why people rate less than 5 in helpfulness. I liked it
just awful
She didn't teach well and the tests were not representative of what she taught, but rather what she thought we learned but really never did
She is a pretty cool professor. Give you extra credit for showing up in class. Lectures are clear and she's always willing to help. The material (diff eq) is quite easy and so are her tests

This course takes in so much more time than you would expect (20 hr service, 13 hr practice). Dr. Lyle's grading nitpicks a lot which is not conducive to learning the material. For the last half of the course, we learned nothing during class time and were expected to practice and prepare for upcoming events and still come in to practice for 13 hrs.

Chem outreach was probably one of the best classes I've taken at Duke. It's great. Just make an effort to improve your presentation skills and go to events consistently, and you'll do great grade-wise. Highly recommended for science majors, it helped me remember why I chose to study this stuff in the first place. 10/10.

Dr. Lyle does not carefully read most of the stuff.  If it not explicitly stated, he views it as not being their.  For someone who has a strong composition background, I had always wrote 95% percent of what I had meant to say in the intent that the reader will fill in the last 5% as they see fit.  He wants 100%

If you're searching for fair assessment of grading, look elsewhere. Lyle, though benign, is a VERY subjective grader. He expects everyone to be bursting at the seams with enthusiasm, but if you're anything less, he's unsympathetic. Fortunately you can be rewarded by your outreach experiences regardless of whether or not you win his favorites game.
Dr. Lyle is truly a great guy.  He really loves chemistry and works to get his sutdents to understand the concepts he is trying to teach.  Very helpful and easy to meet with outside of class.
Dr. Lyle is a great guy. His demos keep you awake in lecture. However he is not the best lecturer and his test was much harder than the ones written by MacPhail. Overall helpful though.

Liu Laoshi is AMAZING. You actually learn chinese in her class (unlike some of the other professors) She places emphasis on class participation, short phrases & grammar before doing any robotic contextualized drills, which help so much! Keep in mind you MUST prepare the dialogues and actually make an effort to learn, then she will reciprocate! 很好老师

Overall shes a good teacher. I just think her style didn't fit what I needed. When joining her class from another 老师 I felt as though she had expectations of supplementary vocab we should know. She sometimes is not able to answer your questions. Or I had said something wrong but she didn't explain to me why it was wrong. Overall very nice.
I LOVE this professor. Classes are fun, she's caring and understanding.

(Chinese 102) Liu Laoshi is absolutely fantastic at drilling fluency in an engaging way. She is very flexible and receptive of students' feedback about workload. Most of all, she is a bubbly and incredibly caring person, making classes a wonderful experience every time.

Prof. Liu is a caring professor and I think she's great for beginners to take. I took her class online, but this was not an issue as she ensured all students are engaged equally. Her grading is appropriate to beginner learners, and if you have any issues, she'll be happy to address them. Her class is challenging but engaging, and you learn a lot!

Liu Laoshi is an incredibly caring professor. Her lectures follow a somewhat simple structure of review, grammar, practice which is easy to get a hold of. She calls on students during class, but even if you don't know something it is not a problem. She's also flexible and is happy to help during her office hours. I would definitely recommend her!

The class has kind of a basic structure - you learn a chapter before class, go over the content in class, and then you have a quiz. You'll always have homework but it's never too crazy if you stay on top of it. Don't come to class unprepared because she will call on you and you are evaluated on your class speaking.

Liu Laoshi is a very detailed, organized, and, just simply, a very good Chinese teacher. Her lectures are very engaging as she would call on the pool of students to answer questions taking this class online made me feel like I was stuyding Chinese in China without being in China. A challenging class and one that pressured students to be best.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Truly one of the most amazing professors here at Duke. Fall 2025 is her last semester before retiring from teaching. I urge anyone to take one of her classes while they still have the chance.
Truly one of the most amazing professors at Duke. Spring 2025 is her last semester teaching before retiring and I urge anyone to take one of her classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: The lectures for this class can be very dense and difficult to understand, even if you have prior knowledge. However, Wahneema is incredibly caring and goes out of her way to support her students. If you put in effort, she will put effort into you. She is always willing to meet and help you revise writings or discuss the readings. She really cares.

The coolest professor I've ever had. She's brilliant and caring. Her lectures are difficult to understand, especially if you don't do the reading. But if you can do the reading, and are willing to say what's on your mind, that's what she cares about. She's involved in modern and historical culture too. She inspires me!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Lubiano is a true gem at Duke. She cares deeply for her students and takes the time to help you process the course information. Most importantly, the course material is critical and life-changing.

Professor Lubiano is, by far, the best professor I've had at Duke. She's brilliant and has such an immense capacity for love. Her lectures are always engaging and rich with analysis. I feel compelled to write down every word she says because of how articulate and insightful she is. Truly an inspiration.

Took Global Inequality Research: Global Blackness with her and Darity. She's incredible and so smart and done really amazing things. Her lectures were way over my head at times but she's brilliant and pretty willing to be supportive if one seeks out support.

Lubiano is amazing.  One of my favorite professors at Duke.  She assigns dense and long readings, but other than that the class is pretty much discussion based, and your opinion in life experience is worth as much as the readings.  Learned a ton from her this semester and really enjoyed going to her class.  Such a nice person too

Super nice and incredibly brilliant, though not always very interesting. The readings are long and tedious, but necessary for discussion. If you participate in the discussions there is a good chance you will get a good grade, but this means you must be prepared to do the readings (which suck). Very nice lady though.

Very smart professor though speaks quickly and quietly (hard to catch all she says). Uses a lot of literary terms that assumes students are aware and knowledgeable. Makes excellent points however and provides great comments on papers.
Nice Lady. But the Class is unbelievably boring.
Probably one of the most boring classes ever, the material painful. I do not recommend unless you like listening to people try and impress you with their rich and extensive vocabulary

Wahneema was one of the best profs I've had here, she is really smart, and her history is amazing. Some of her lectures will be over your head, but you  will come out of that class knowing so much more than when you went in.

Brilliant, you'll never meet another Wahneema -- she will have you coming out of class with your brain swelling. Always there to talk, although at times she has problems with her health. Her writing is excellent and fairly well known. She and her life are fascinating.
Craaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaazy smart!  Definitely take her if you can, but preferably not for Lit 100.

McAdams is the goat. Take this class if you can get in. Makes game theory very digestible and fun. Tests are pretty easy - he wants you to get a good grade. Just make sure you know how to do the PSets. McAdams has a genuine passion for teaching. He's a great guy and class is so much more fun if you contribute and get into it. #watertribe

If I could take a class with him every semester I would. 390 was one of the most engaging and exciting classes where we were still able to learn from it. His commitment to the material plus the silliness of tribal competitions made this class the highlight of my week SHOUT OUT FIRE NATION

Take this class. It was the most fun and interesting class I have had at Duke. There is a decent amount of work, but lectures are so fun that it makes up for it. McAdams is perhaps the most dedicated professor I have seen at Duke, and wants his student to learn a ton whilst also having a great time. RISE FIRE NATION!
HE IS AWESOME. I would take this class again and again if I could. I would take a class with him every semester if I could.

ZORBS. ARM WRESTLING. MOVIES. GAME THEORY. 
your superdominant strategy is to take this class!!!! 
#firenation

Attendance isn't mandatory, but idk why you wouldn't show up. Trust me you do not wanna miss out on tribal competitions, in-class games or coups. David truly wants you to succeed on quizzes/tests with the abundance of materials and practice he provides. To future students: fire🔥 >>>

This is the first time McAdams has taught an undergrad class. If you can take a class with him, do not miss the chance. Everyday was full of exciting activities, from scavenger hunts to chief elections. You'll never have a class experience like this again at Duke, and I am sure it will be one of the legendary classes at Duke in a couple of years.

Prof McAdams is a rarity amongst college professors. He reintroduces fun into the classroom with various games, point systems, and team-oriented activities. Some course concepts can be difficult, but he is readily accessible and provides abundant study materials, making it a breeze. 100% recommend.

Professor McClain's film class was such an interesting introduction to how race intersects with film. Now, I feel I am a much more thoughtful consumer of media. Professor McClain is really renowned in the field, so I was grateful to take a class with her. She is very knowledgeable and provides great feedback on papers. Highly recommend!

Dr. McClain is the best professor that I have ever had. She takes the times to tell you the little things. She encourages you to pay attention to detail, the things that we don't often prioritize in college. She is a teacher in every true sense of the word. If you enter the class open to learning, this will be a wonderful experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Great professor. really knows her stuff but most of the textbooks for the class have been edited by her, which sucks because if you didnt understand it in class the books wont help. GO TO THE TA's OFFICE HOURS. They grade everything!!! Prof. McClain just teaches the class.
Terrible class. Think about the most anal high school teacher you ever had. Multiply it times ten. There you go.

This woman is amazing. She is scary, in that she will roast you in front of the whole class if you don't know what you're talking about, but so so so good. She's also hilarious which leads to an interesting combination. She *carries* a 2.5 hour class. Every week was a fever dream, but I learned so so so much about writing, and television.

This woman scared the Jesus out of me. I would like to preface this by saying do NOT take her if you're timid or sensitive. She is blunt, but so very knowledgeable. She gives wonderful feedback, and does not take BS. I've been acting for years but I still felt like she helped me learn new techniques to grow. Please do yourself a favor and take her!

I really enjoyed this class! Professor McAuliffe is funny, interesting, and a great director. I always feel like I've learned something from class, and I also feel like there's so much more I have left to learn! Class is improv for the first few weeks, then we transition into play scenes. Come prepared, turn in your work, and be enthusiastic.

The best practical screenwriting class I've ever had. Jody is hilarious and she made the 2.5 hours fly. This was a very memorable class, and you'll learn a lot. Only homework in the class is a 60 page script worked on in 6 weeks. it's creative though and easy to manage.

I took 89s improv with Jody. It was a great class to meet other freshmen and lighten up the day. Jody is funny. She can be a little much at times and really butt in the way but she means well. Just take everything as a joke and every class will be a good time. Take her classes with friends for even more fun.

YOU WILL LEARN to analyze plays, communicate w/ actors, stage a scene, & execute dramatic text into tangible, believable, and relatable scenes. Be prepared to read a lot of plays & participate. Prof. will call on you in class and call you out for being wrong. Only complaint: disorganized... Just email her when ur confused. Not an easy A. hard work
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Best prof I have ever had, made me switch from engineering to English major.

Although I was at first a bit intimidated, Jody became one of the professors I would insanely love and respect. She always gives very constructive comments to help you improve for the better. Participation is certainly encouraged. You'll learn a great deal by the end of the class.

As this was a performance class, participation definitely matters. Jody is someone who you will love, insanely respect, and be slightly terrified of (but in a good way). She genuinely cares about her students becoming better actors themselves and as an ensemble. She is an amazing person to work with.

Jody McAuliffe is a truly insightful, challenging and engaging genius! She is always willing to assist outside class. She is definitely demanding and expects a lot from her students in terms of quality of work. However, I was very appreciative to find her giving us "busy" work for the sake of it. My best professor at Duke.

I honestly can't decide whether I love her or am terrified of her.  I think it's a little of both.  Jody is incredibly intelligent and very creative, class is always interesting.  She is NOT afraid of confrontation and does NOT take bull from students.  Not a good prof for the insecure or easily intimidated.
Amazing Professor! Very nice very engaging very helpful. She made me fall in love with philosophy.

Prof. McWilliams is an amazing human being. She is knowledgeable and gives helpful advices. You just want to listen to her during the class because she makes everything clear and easy to understand. My favorite professor.
Creates a very positive environment
Professor Emily is one of those people that is just so brilliant that you can not help but learn from her. She can teaches philosophy in a way that is clear, precise, and stimulating.

This was a new course, China in the World, compared to the typical Chinese Politics course she teaches. Was very informative on how to interpret Chinese actions in a global context and provided clear background deep into chinese culture. Professor Manion is hilarious and makes class fun. Grading criteria can sometimes be ambigious.

Chinese Politics is a great intro to those uninitiated with Chinese govt, pol econ, history. Manion is a top-tier China scholar, genuinely hilarious and incredibly helpful. One of the rare professors here that actually feels like a human being. Allowing us to choose 6 out of 12 short-essay over the semester allowed us to customize workload.

This is one of my favorite classes that I have ever taken at Duke. Prof. Manion is very passionate about the field, and this course really helped me understand the frameworks of corruption (and political science in general) in a more profound and less rote-memorized way than anything else.

I came back to write this review a year after taking Professor Manion's class, and I realize it was easily the best course I took at Duke. The concepts and ideas we explored in class continually reappear in my studies, reflections, and political thinking in general. It was the only 830 class I attended without ever missing a session.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Prof Manion is a charismatic, funny, and knowledgeable professor about corruption (and more specifically China, her area of expertise). Her stories and background in the field brought this course to life, and I was elated to have gotten to Flunch her in the middle of the semester.
Imagine being told 2 weeks before the final that you need a 95% to get an A. Otherwise, really great class and learned a lot. Corrupt grading scheme sadly ;)

Hands down the BEST professor I've had at Duke. She's charismatic and inspiring in every single way because she is SO passionate about what she studies. She genuinely cares about her students and respects what they have to say in class. Definitely very empowering for females out there; I wish I could take another class with her

Prof. Manion is incredible! She not only assigned great content in our class on Global Corruption, but also taught us to read work in the social sciences with a more critical eye. She took full advantage of the seminar format, allowing us to take the discussion where we wanted and providing guidance when needed. Definitely take a class with her!

Professor Manion is one of the best professors I have had at Duke! She gives amazing lectures and is so knowledgable in her field. She can be a tough grader, but it still fair. If you go to class, pay attention, and give insightful comments, you will do well and gain so much knowledge along the way. I highly recommend taking a class with her!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I took Mesha's advanced fiction class. Mesha is one of the highlights of Duke. She is very upfront with you and thus gives you incredible advice for your writing. She is also just such a wonderful and inspirational human. You have to take her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Inspirational

reviews.comment: This is an awesome class to take if you want to become a better writer. The class is workshop based and you just work on being critiqued and reviewing the work of other classmates. The first half of the class there are more readings, but its manageable. Gives you a whole new perspective on creative writing.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: She is a great professor for an intro class - the writing is structured in the beginning and open at the end so you build up the confidence to write what you want to. She also gives thoughtful feedback on your pieces. It's never negative, so if you're self-conscious about your writing, definitely take it with her over other professors.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Gives good feedback and really nurtures your writing. Def take

I really loved being in Maren-Hogan's class. She's sweet and thoughtful, and she's also clearly a very sharp writer. She gives good critical feedback without making students feel like her feedback is criticism. Being in her class has definitely helped me to write more, even outside of class assignments.

Prof. Maren-Hogan is a wonderfully nice and helpful teacher who actively encourages creative thinking. She assigns reasonable readings and her grading on creative pieces is lenient if you follow her rubric. As long as you are prepared for the easy reading quizzes she gives every few weeks and you put in the time for 2 pieces, you'll be fine!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Worst and most annoying class I've taken at Duke. All busy work, attendance mandatory at 8:30, with 0 leeway. There are assignments due every Sunday, Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Friday. If you miss a few classes or forget an assignment in its own category it becomes hard to pass. Easy content, but difficult to stay on top of all the assignments.
A great professor for getting your feet wet in econ. Very funny too.
Worth doing 101 with him. He's very helpful one on one as well.
Great Econ 101 prof, loved his class. I'm taking another class with him.

COMPREHENSIVE: Not a bad or hard class. However, tough to pay attention after the first few lectures (gets boring fast, especially since the pre-class readings cover the upcoming class content). Lots of busywork for a 101 class, and was honestly overkill with grading. Medema is average but can be funny sometimes. Make sure to do DOLEs on time!

Seriously do not take econ 101 with him. There is no reason we should have a final in econ 101. The most pointless lecture, literally just talks about whatever he wants with like 5 minutes of actual learning. Because of him I am not majoring in econ, worst professor I have had at Duke.
Impossible exams, zero feedback, and jokes that land like bricks. Feels more like a livestream troll than a professor. Honestly, I've never seen boredom weaponized like this before.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: All the negative reviews are really disheartening because Prof. Medema is genuinely a great guy and a really caring professor. Yes, the lecture content is a little boring (it's econ 101 no shocker) but he does his best to make it entertaining and he is genuinely a funny guy. Great intro to econ and super easy to pass! 10/10 TAs too.
His lectures were clear, but I think there was too much homework for the amount of information we were learning.

Seriously so boring. I cannot sit through a lecture. Tries to be funny, is not. The course is so annoying and the grading is extremely excessive. Do not take econ 101 with him, wait until a different professor.

Econ 101 is a joke of class in terms of difficulty. However, Medema tries to make the class as annoying as possible. The class is S/U but has mandatory attendance, meets 3 times a week, has a discussion, 3 canvas quizzes per week, a discussion PSET, weekly HW, a midterm and a final. It feels like there too many easy but pointless assignments.

Disgrace to the Duke econ department. Actively looks down on and laughs at his students and tries to fail them with impossible tests. Worst professor in the history of Duke University. It is so stressful to listen to him.
Disgrace to the Duke econ department. Actively looks down on and mocks his students and tries to fail them with impossible tests. Worst professor in the history of Duke University

This class is incredibly boring and feels like a total waste of time, especially if you've already taken AP Econ. The constant attendance checks are irritating, and the material is so basic and repetitive.

The 8:30 class is so annoying. But super easy to pass if you show up. I don't feel like I learned too much. I think the pass/fail system isn't too engaging. He's a super nice guy. The discussion problem sets had odd examples.

Okay lecturer who relays content decently well, but lectures are boring. Attendance policy is brutal and the grading is very stringent. Weekly problem sets were often weird and often featured topics that were not classroom appropriate. All in all decent for ECON101 but take different professor if given the choice. If not, he is bearable.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great insights into how econ analysis sheds light on law - this class incurs my passion for econ! 3 exams (60%) and 1 paper (20%). Exam grading can be harsh and arbitrary, but the curve is not bad - yet might be concerning to pre-laws. Make sure to discuss your paper with him! He can give critical feedback on whether you are on the right track.

Good prof. Funny lectures and good overall exposure to law basics. However, I found the content (and the grading) to sometimes be a bit arbitrary, which makes it hard to study. Barely any work you have to do for the class - 3 midterms and a paper, but very manageable. Don't need to do the readings

Great prep for pre law, essentially what you'll learn in 1st yr law school from an econ perspective, which is nice to get a primer on. He lectures the whole class, has classic old guy humor, passionate ab teaching & answering questions, accessible out of class. 60-70% of the grade were due the last month, which was annoying, but grading was not bad

I thought Professor Medema was amazing. I took his Economic Analysis of Law class and thoroughly enjoyed the content SO much. He really loves the content and is excited to talk about it with students. The class was quite easy and straight-forward by putting in the necessary work. Would DEFINITELY recommend any course with him!

She's an amazingteacher and gives very comprehensive lessons! I had her for CHIN 101A-101B and she was an amazing. guide for starting from absolute zero. She also shares her lecture slides which are extremely helpful study materials. She is a bit more critical on tones during the dialogues, but it's helpful in improving and she gives good pointers.

Prof Meng Wang is amazing, she's very energetic and encouraging in class, the Chinese curriculum is tough but it's manageable with Prof Meng Wang. She will help you no matter what your chinese proficiency level is and cares about your learning. 10/10 would take again.

Genuinely one of the best Chinese professors. Very enthusiastic, positive, and you can tell she makes a lot of effort to make class very engaging while being informative as much as possible. She really focuses on helping you.

Wang 老师 is one of my favorite Chinese teachers. If you come early to class she will engage in conversation with you. If you mess up, she will correct you but it does not feel condemning. She focuses heavily on tones.
Wang Laoshi hen hao! Ta hen ke ai! The way she organizes her class is very good and she's always spreading positive vibes! Chinese classes in general are homework heavy so it's not really her fault

Prof. Wang has great humor and presence in the classroom. Her approach is clear, fair, and student-focused. She'll work with students during her office hours on skills they need to improved, if students would like to do so. The curriculum is restricting her from doing an even better job. She's always smiling and being positive inside class and out!
Great professor, very engaging and honestly the best Chinese teacher I had throughout 2 years.

I've had classes with Chen laoshi since CHINESE101, and she is the best professor if you want to learn. She is very sweet, approachable, and very patient with the students. Her grading for field tasks is better than that of other professors, but she expects you to put at least a little bit of effort to learn the dialogue.

Her grading is harsher than others, and she seems to treat her own class as an "honors class". I heard many students complain about her approach. Regardless of your level, her expectations are INTENSE and not always the same for every student! Take her only if you're okay with that level of pressure and criticism for a required 2-credit course.

Chen 老师 is better at teaching more advanced grammar structures in Chinese. I would be interested in taking her with a higher-level class. But for a 101 class, it felt as though our learning was behind the other classes, this was apparent in the final. But she did grade according to the class. Its just difficult when switching to a new 老师.

She is as good as a professor teaching-wise as the other Chinese professor. I've had 3 different Chinese professors; she was by far the most strict. The disparity between her grading and the other laoshis teaching the same course is insane sometimes. Protect your peace, don't take her class.

I think Chen laoshi is the best option for Chinese at DKU, although you definitely need to make an effort and participate in class. Last semester she was a harsher grader than other profs, but since course feedbacks I think she has been making an effort to be more lenient. She is very understanding about issues as long as you email her in advance.

I enjoyed having Professor Chen. She's friendly and encouraging, and if you communicate any issues to her via email she's generally accommodating & quick to respond. She doesn't really call on people during lectures though, so actively volunteering is a must if you want full credit in participation.

Chen Laoshi is a very good teacher but a much harsher grader compared to the other professors. I found the lectures to be really engaging and not too stressful, but if you are not fully participating throughout the entire lecture she takes points off. I think students in other classes get better grades, but you will learn the most from Chen Laoshi.
Prof. Chen is a good choice. She gives timely, detailed and helpful feedback. She is also patient and encouraging so I feel like I have a safe space to make mistakes and improve my Chinese.

For someone who doesn't like being called on out of nowhere (like me), she's a very solid choice. For someone who likes the cold call style of learning, she's not the best professor for you. That being said, she's a very nice person regardless of the style you like, and she still encourages everyone to speak up.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Probably your worse option for 200 level Chinese. She won't call on you during lecture so instead of practicing Chinese you'll gain skills in playing chicken with your other classmates as you wait for someone else to respond first.

I liked the way Prof. Chen taught her classes. Engaging and less pressure for students and in this way, students may have been able to learn a lot. She gives timely feedback and is a very outgoing person. Highly recommended!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I did not felt pressured during the meetings, as it often happened with other professors. At her class, I was able to contribute to the discussion whenever I felt comfortable. Prof. is very understanding and responds to emails quickly. Overall her class is pretty easy if you manage to keep up with all the deadlines.

She and other professors designed and taught course using 'flipped classroom' approach. We had mandatory attendance "to practice", but during zoom meetings we did not get to "practice" much. Course organization was very poor. They made SAKAI more complicated than physics. also super hard and meaningless IPAs. I regret taking her class.

Professor Chen is friendly and gives good feedback. Her class used the flipped classroom approach so students must have studied in advance. Her facilitation skills can be stronger to allow for smoother flow of discussion. Her time management also needs work because planned activities towards the end of class often aren't done/ done hurriedly.

Professor Reisoglu is a wonderful professor and lecturer. Classes are lecture-heavy and this class requires a decent amount of reading, but his lectures are enjoyable and the topics are interesting. Papers and projects are graded easily, and are are not too time-consuming. I would recommend this class to anyone interested in the horror genre.
Very easy class but a lot of reading (summaries are available...). One midterm (which everyone gets an A on) and a project. Overall super easy and interesting class.
Great reading list, engaging and sweet professor, not too difficult, and felt inspired.
Goat spanish professor

Profesora Merschel is the sweetest! She provides clear rubrics for all of her assignments and grades them accordingly. The class is front-heavy, with work lightening significantly towards the end because she gives lots of time for our essay assignments. She's also super accessible, after class or at her office hours.
I was dreading my language requirement but she has been very helpful and encouraging. Class is a lot of writing, but grading is fair and effort is rewarded over correctness. Highly, highly recommend.

As someone who is not super confident in their Spanish abilities, I felt that Professor Merschel created an environment that allowed me to thrive in spite of my challenges. Her instructions and grading criteria are clear and reasonable. I highly recommend this course and this teacher to anyone looking to take a 300 level Spanish.

Prof. Merschel is an amazing professor. She really cares about her students and is very willing to provide feedback on essays or other assignments outside of class. In each class there is usually a lot of work due (6 short writing assignments, 2 short papers, 4 grammar quizzes one final paper, etc.) but keep up with the work and you'll get an A.
There is a decent amount of work on a weekly basis, but the grading is very generous. Professor Merschel wants you to succeed and is very nice. Class is pretty engaging.

I had a terrific experience in Merschel's class. She is the most caring and encouraging professor I've ever had, which is great for your confidence when speaking in Spanish. Grading is kind as long as you show effort, and she is happy to meet outside of class if you ask. She made the class very reasonable and enjoyable. Absolutely take if you can!
A Professor who truly cares about how you do in the class. 301 is a ton of writing but if you make it clear you are making an effort she will grade you well. The grammar quizzes are the hardest part.

I heard the spanish department here is harsh, but sra merschel is such a gem. virtually no work, and i got an A on every assignment with very little effort. definitely learned a lot at the same time though, and she's very fair. 10/10 the best teacher to end up with

Lisa was my favourite Spanish professor out of the three I had (101-203). She is sweet, patient and understanding and will work hard to make you feel really at ease when speaking Spanish. If you keep up with assignments and put in the effort, it should be a good and not too hard class: she cares a lot about effort, not just success.
AMAZING. So incredibly caring and knowledgeable. Always willing to meet with student outside of class.

I. LOVE. HER. she makes class so interactive and teaches in a way that makes you learn so well. She's not a native speaker and so she knows what it's like to learn Spanish herself. Very compassionate and just an awesome person.

Professor Merschel is extremely nice and helpful. Always has a lot of energy and is willing to help. Assignments are easy, but there are a decent amount of them. Final was just like the tests during the year, not hard. Definitely recommend Spanish 102 with her.

Lisa is so sweet and nice. She's also very easy to understand and wants to be your friend. Take her over any other 301 teacher. Do your work well and you will get an A.  The quizzes are worth only 12% but that's more than you would think so take advantage of how much she wants you to succeed and get help outside class if you need to.

Absolutely loved taking class with Senora Merschel. She is an amazing teacher who explains concepts well and genuinely cares about her students. As long as you put in the effort, you will make a good grade. Take Spanish with her if you can!
Lisa Merschel is one of the most clear and caring professors I've had at Duke, and this is really important when taking a language.
She's awesome
I took intermediate Spanish with Dr. Merschel for the Duke in Alicante summer program. She is an amazing professor who truly wants all of her students to be successful and could not be more helpful.
She's fantastic. If you're taking 204, take it with her.
Best professor ever! She is super sweet and always willing to help/ clarify if you need. Definitely take her class :)
She is awesome! Definitely recommend taking a class with her! She really wants her students to do well! Pretty easy A
Professor Merschel is awesome! She is extremely sweet and very helpful. She is a fair grader and is always willing to answer questions or explain concepts.  She made Spanish a very enjoyable class.

Lisa was an AMAZING professor. She cares so much about all of her students and goes out of her way to ensure that everyone understands the material effectively. She was a relatively easy grader, and always very understanding if you missed class or an assignment was late. Take her 204 class!!!
Best Spanish professor I've had at Duke. Very nice, easy to understand, and the class was pretty easy because she prepares you well for the tests. definitely recommend taking her

Sra. Merschel is AMAZING! I took 101 with her in the fall, and I was less than excited when I went into the class. I don't like writing in general, and doing it in Spanish is even more daunting. Merschel made the class very enjoyable and not terrifying at all. I strongly recommend taking a class with her!

Literally the kindest professor at Duke. She is amazing, and even though I absolutely hate Spanish, she actually made the class bearable. If you want to/need to take Spanish at Duke, take it with Señora Merschel. She's absolutely incredible as a person and a teacher.

Profesa Merschel is a great teacher. I've heard bad things about the spanish department at Duke but she proved them wrong. I feel much more confident in my verbal and writing Spanish skills. The class was also enjoyable and a nice break from lecture style classes.

She's extremely helpful and easy to understand. Always enthusiastic. Genuinely interested in knowing her students. Very kind. The homework is more difficult than the class itself, but that's because it's all busy work. Take any class you can with her!
Nicest lady ever and a great professor - take her class!
BEST TEACHER EVER!!!!!!!!! IF YOU CAN, TAKE A CLASS WITH HER!!!!!!!
so nice so helpful. is completely american. learned spanish when she was 19 in college. a lot of assignments though.

She is from NC, so understands when to abandon Spanish and teach you something in English. She does as much work for class (or more) than we do - puts tons of things online that make it easy to know what you need to memorize and gives you handouts with notes so you can just concentrate on learning. GET HER IF YOU CAN
She's the best

Great teacher. Slightly less strict than most of the others, very enthusiastic, and she made spanish much more comfortable than it ever had been before. Only spanish class I've ever had where I wasn't afraid to speak in class on a regular basis.
Prof. Merschel is a great professor to have for those of you interested in Spanish 14!  The class really bonds, and going to class is as painless as eight sessions a week gets:)

Sra Merschel was awesome.  I had her for 8 class periods a week and i still always wanted to come to class.  The class became very tight and we even had dinner at one of the student's house.  She loves to teach and you will love having her.  Great woman!

A GREAT teacher.  I have class at 8:45 every morning yet she is enthusiastic and I rarely feel like I am going to fall asleep.  She is very understanding and helpful.  She is not only a great prof, but a great teacher!
GREATEST PROFESSOR EVER!!!
EXTREMELY helpful, enthusiastic lady.  Provides great review and study guidance for the tests and makes the class fun.  All-around reasonable teacher.

Lori's class is a mixed bag - she can be tough, but engaging with her system pays off. unstuck study and reviewing the textbook helped me stay on top of things. Not the easiest, but worth it for the knowledge gained.
Lori Leachman acting as punitive as she is with her students is pretty wild given the documented indiscretions of her prog3ny who also attended Duke. Consequences for thee but not for me hij0.

leachman is just old school and expects kids to take her class seriously. as long as you don't take the course lightly bc its a 101 and you 1) pay very close attention to her vernacular in lecture and repeat that on exams and 2) know what info won't be on the exam you'll be alright. i learned a lot of econ & how to study.

I get previous ratings' frustrations with Leachman, but honestly she's not terrible. She's definitely knowledgable but she expects a lot. Just because this is a pass fail class doesn't mean it should be a cakewalk and I respect the fact that she made us work for the pass. This class was hard, but I learned a lot because of it. Would take again tbh.

Lori Leachman is an rude professor who gets off on bullying students. She gaslights students on mass emails to embarrass them. Handwriting - menacing. Tests - sacrilegiously long for one hour and her grading is ridiculous. She had a mix up with the custodian about opening a test area and went on a swearing rampage -in front of students. Dont take.

lol person who spammed this page below is definitely a freshman that just copped their first C in college. Lori is a decent prof that wants her students to get a solid understanding of econ principles and how the world works. While her tests are pretty hard if you put in the work you'll pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Tough grader

reviews.comment: As an Econ major, I was excited to take this class, especially with how prestigious Duke Economics is. Turns out a department is only as strong as their weakest link - Dr. Leachman is that link.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Extremely difficult course. Requires an unreasonable amount of time outside of the course just to barely pass SOME assignments. Tests are way difficult and although leachman is very intelligent, she's very passive aggressive and expects who to have some basis knowledge. Not for students with limited econ experience despite a 101 course.

As far as teaching goes she's alright, obviously knows a lot about economics, and can verbalize concepts well. But the tests she makes are so damn hard, and so damn specific. Also, she's just plain rude to students who asks questions and creates a pretty hostile classroom environment. Whatever you do, stay away from Leachman for 101.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: If you value your sanity, don't take this class.

This is the worst professor in Duke's econ department. She is rude, humiliates students, then yells at us when we do not attend discussion. She is not qualified, cannot answer questions, is very sexist against men and makes terrible, useless unreadable notes +lectures that barely connect. Shame on Duke for hiring her/letting here teach. FIRE HER.
Assigned work and quiz on our wellness days. Speaks volumes about the type of prof she is. Very difficult to talk to and incredibly rude to students. DO NOT TAKE IF POSSIBLE.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Take econ 101 in the fall, she is awful. Teaches poorly and is very condescending/passive-aggressive to students
The class average for the first exam was a fail. That pretty much tells you all you need to know about how competent Leachman is.

If you want a class with a condescending professor who definitely shouldn't have received a professor role at a university, then go ahead. She has the most convoluted lectures, completely illegible notes, and doesn't even answer questions well in her office hours -- she just makes you feel like you're the incompetent one, not her.

Absolutely don't take 101 with Leachman if you are taking *any* other classes. No one has the time to live up to her extremely unreasonable exam expectations and you should expect to routinely fail exams if you don't sell your soul to her office hours. If you're willing to do that, go for it. Take it with Fullenkamp.
Tough and can seem a little mean on the surface. But she's great at answering questions and will definitely help you a lot.

Lori is a real econ genius. She knows the answer to every question and will expand your knowledge about the practicality of economics. I learned so much about not just econ theory but also its applicability to the real world in Econ 101. She's tough and not particularly kind during lectures but she clearly cares about students and is nicer 1 on 1

Econ 101 was never meant to be a walk in the park, hence why it's S/U. And while Prof. Leachman definitely doesn't hold your hand the whole way through, she explains things clearly, answers questions well, and really cares that you understand the material. Go to office hours. Exams are challenging but are a fair representation of a difficult class.

If you ask questions during or after lectures, email her questions, go to office hours, do extra credit, and all quizzes and homework assignments, Dr. Leachman will do her best to help you pass the class (S/U). Once you get to know her, talking and learning about economics becomes very fascinating. Tests are very difficult and harsh grading.

Professor Leachman moves through material quickly and covers a lot of ground. You definitely get exposure to a lot of different topics. Exams are long, but a fair representation of the material covered, and she provides many opportunities beforehand to get you prepared. She can be gruff with students in lecture, but is generally approachable.

All content is learned in lecture and there is no textbook to go by so it difficult to see information except in specific scenarios. Exams are difficult and MC has more than one right answer. Definitely a weed out class, AP Micro/Macro HIGHLY recommended. Expects participation in lectures but is sometimes dismissive of students
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed this class. If you're thinking about taking Econ101- don't be deterred by the previous comments. There is a direct correlation between how hard you work and how you do in the class. Professor Leachman isn't easily approachable, but if you get over that and go to her office hours you'll get a lot out of them. Midterms are manageable

Prof Lori is smart, but that does not mean she is a good teacher. She is often intimidating and sometimes disrespectful to students -- not a sustainable learning environment. Her grading is ambiguous and seems unfair. The material is hard, but her teaching style makes it harder. Take it elsewhere.
Very thorough, invested in your learning, you should go to lectures and pay attention to do well.

Most people go into her class expecting to be coddled and prodded along during the process of learning economics. But this is not the case and you will have to work hard. However, should you put in the effort you will be rewarded immensely. Highly caring and intelligent professor who rewards hard work.

Professor Leachman knows her stuff and is very invested in teaching the students who want to learn. If you put in the time to go to class and office hours, she will put in the time to help you understand the material. She was always willing to stop for questions and paused class after difficult material to ensure everyone was following her.

She is one of the most supporting teachers I have ever had. She makes an effort to get to know all her students, but get ready to study your ass off. The class is not curved, so the natural econ students get an A. Those who are not are screwed. Besides the difficult grading scale, it is an amazing class and highly advise taking it.

Professor Leachman, although portrayed by many as being really hard, is in actuality a great professor that really cares about her students. She is always available after class for questions and provides really good help before exams if you look for it. Tough class but enjoyable.

At first Leachman is definitely intimidating, but if you put in the effort and show up to office hours to ask meaningful questions she will like you.  This class was definitely tough, but I learned so so so much.  My biggest complaint about this class is the test grading.  I swear that the people who do really well are able to read Leachman's mind.

This is a hard class intended to weed out the people that aren't willing to work hard. The econ curriculum only gets more difficult from here. Lori is a great professor that really cares about her students. Even if you want to hate her because you're failing the tests, it's impossible. Go to her office hours, she will help you prepare for the tests

Professor Leachman is one of the least nice people I have ever met, and carries a clear bias in her teaching.  Tests have seemingly easy questions that are graded very harshly (taking of points without explanation). As much as I wanted to hate her, I have learned more taking this class than I have in any other class, it's truly amazing.

She's rough. Tests are stupid hard when the material isn't that tough. However, she does present the material clearly in lecture, although she does do it too quickly and expects you to pick it up like it's nothing. I recommend taking it with the other teacher. That being said, it's not the end of the world if you take it with her.

Her lectures are not clear, and her answers to students' questions are not helpful. She will often contradict herself from one lecture to another. Her exam questions are vague and harshly graded. Gives office hours, but she communicates terribly with the TAs so they are of little help. You will probably end up teaching yourself. Take elsewhere!!!

Her lectures are lengthy but helpful and she's pretty clear although her handwriting is basically illegible. Be prepared for lots of work and also don't miss lectures! They are extremely important.  She is definitely not that kind of amazingly nice professor and apparently doesn't care about what others think of her. Can be intimidating.
Avoid if you are not planning to be an ECON major. She is a terrible lecturer but its passable if you study hard for the tests and have a balanced schedule with this as a class. (Avoid the rattail)

Leachman creates an environment in the class that makes it difficult to learn. She is disrespectful to students. Her lectures are boring, and her handwriting is unclear. She never uses the textbook, and the only way to do well on tests is memorize her notes. Class isn't curved.

Don't bother buying the textbook for this class if you are taking it with her but I would recommend taking it with a different professor. She teaches well if you have already taking AP Econ, but otherwise a lot of studying is required. I recommend taking it with another professor. She is very blunt and doesn't care what people think about her.
lecture is very conceptual/broad, but her exams are very specific, never uses the textbook, not worth buying, illegible handwriting on her lecture notes
This class is hard. Don't buy the textbook. You will never use it. Lori seems like a cool person but is not great as a teacher because there is no curve and tests are hard to prepare for.

Oh Lori. Memorize her lectures to do well on the exams. I wish I had gone to her office hours more often because she actually was helpful. She's a pretty interesting person, don't be intimidated by her. Also, she does NOT curve at all. Overall it was a decent class, not easy but not too difficult either.
Leachman is an unfair teacher who makes an otherwise interesting and easy subject miserable.

Overall a rather terrible professor. The tests reflect your ability to understand her strange mentality and logic over economic principals and theory. She strongly pushes her opinions as fact and is unhelpful and often flat out rude to students who seek her help. (Her handwriting in the notes is also illegible)

This is a class where you need to stay on top of the work. Memorize everything on the slides (yes, everything). The first part of the test is about 60 points or of spitting back information you memorized from the slides. Manageable if you do this, but if you don't you will get destroyed. Case in point I didn't figure this out until midterm 2.

This is a very difficult class, but certainly not impossible. Her tests are hard, but fair. Know her lectures, like memorize them. Don't worry about the book. Stay on top of things, go to TA hours, and do the extra credit. I didn't get the grade I wanted but that was due to my study habits. LECTURES LECTURES LECTURES!

To get a good grade you basically have to memorize everything she says. The tests aren't necessarily too difficult, they are just very detailed. The fact that the free responses all involve regurgitating patterns from her examples shifts the focus from understanding the material.

if you want to pursue econ, stop reading these ratings and just take the class. it's a difficult class, but very worthwhile and i got an A even though i'm not an econ person. she's an amazing person, so go to dinner wither! do the extra credit, WATCH THE ONLINE LECTURES, put in the work, and you'll be fine. don't bother opening the textbook.
Very high demands for a professor who has the math and spelling abilities of a 10-year-old

The class material wasn't hard (though there are some tricky bits) and the tests range from easy to ridiculous. Go to class if you can, because sometimes just looking at the recordings/lecture notes might be hard to follow. Keep up with the work and you will get the grade you deserve.

Great teacher, but tests are pretty challenging and require a higher level of thinking than the examples done in class. If you put in the work, you'll get at least a B- (what I got). Go to office hours, do the hw and extra credit, and learn the lecture material inside out, and you'll be just fine. Also, flunch with her because she is awesome!

Dr. Leachman is the best teacher that I have had so far at Duke. She is very clear when explaining her lesson, plans enough time for the questions, and is very organized. She spends the beginning of each class going over what was covered in the last class, and the rest teaching new material. Classes are recorded online and tests are very easy.
Her class itself is easy but the exams are tough. You really need to know what you're doing.

great class. it really helps you gain a better understanding of the world, especially in relation to current events. make sure you keep up with the news. getting extra credit points on the test really helps out your grade. it's definitely a doable class. just keep up with it.

If you don't do well in her class, it's your own fault. Leachman is incredibly clear and explicit about exactly what she wants on tests. She even spends class time reviewing to make sure that you understand things. Her liberal bias is noticeable but not important. You will get the grade that you deserve in this class. Fight for every point.

Professor Leachman really knows her stuff and truly wants you to know it, too. Don't be turned away by her somewhat condescending attitude and sense of humor.  If you express interest and put in some work, she will definitely be there to help you. The book is next to useless. Most material on the tests comes straight out of lecture.

She can illustrate everything very clearly, and point out everything that will be on exam again and again. She is very dedicated to her work. The review sessions are always full of applause. You can really learn a lot from this class, and it's not hard.

one of the best professors i've ever had, and one of the most interesting women i've ever encountered. her class is tough, but study hard and go to office hours/review sessions and you'll get a B, at the very least. take her up on her offer to flunch, she's a fascinating woman with some real life advice to share.
She has nice hair, for starters. She has a voice that carries throughout the room. Don't need to use textbook much, all about the lectures. Also, she is a dime.

Very good lecturer. She is intimidating at first, but if you show her you are willing to learn, she is willing to help you. The class is definitely tough, but if you attend lectures and office hours (the TAs are not the greatest) then you will do okay. Large class but she teaches it just like a normal 30 person class.
Pretty good professor altogether. very clear not as bad as people make her out to be.

Lori knows her stuff. What is hard about her class is that what she teaches is not everything on the test. If you attend lecture and take notes/study, you should get a B if you work hard. That A needs the thought process of an economist who has been in the profession for over five years. She thinks she is requiring us to "think".. yeah right Lori.

Professor Leachman is a great lecturer and although there were over 250 students in the class, I still think I was able to learn a lot. The post-doc TAs, however, were awful at grading and unhelpful throughout the course. They make way too many mistakes in the grading and are unresponsive to e-mail. They have trouble doing basic stuff like adding.

Smart, knows her stuff, but doesn't care what you understand- just what you memorize. Grading is a joke. I had answers word-for-word from her notes given 0 credit. Random "-1's" on tests. Threatened to dock points for submitting for regrade. I learned more reading the extra credit book in 2 days than I did from taking her class. Terrible experience
She's intense, brilliant and a great professor. If you listen to her lectures you should do fine on the exams. The material is not easy; you have to do the work but it's definitely worth it.

If you asked me who the most awesome person in the world is, I would probably say Lori Leachman. She is a fantastic lecturer, so I can overlook the fact that she does liberal things like read the New York Times. My only regret is that she is not my best friend. If you think this class is hard, you are wrong. Go major in sociology.

Very clear lecturer. Tests aren't too hard, but you do have to rush through them a little and there's alot to remember. Lecture is good for asking questions, but even more importantly, watch the recordings online (so that you can pause/rewind)--I never went to lecture and did this instead. Book reading is helpful, but optional. Very little HW.
She is a really good lecturer.  Her tests are really hard, but there is a great curve on the grades.  She is not very approachable.

Not as good as Fullenkamp, but knows the material well and teaches well. Although she gets the rep of being a very tough teacher, it seems like most students end up with a grade in the B range (source: www.gradeabase.com/Duke%20University_econ_51.htm ).

She is a tough teacher. I'm a conceptual student, so I usually try and understand material to pass classes, but for her, it was rote memorization. If you are able to memorize a lot of material, then you will succeed. A lot of the tests were simply applying her straight logic and wording right onto the problem given. Not for me.
Great teacher although not very approachable.  Tests are hard.

Though it is clear that Leachman knows her stuff, she makes her tests very difficult and the average is usually between a 72-75 and she never curves it.  If you work your tail off, study, do the homeworks, and go to office hours you can probably get a B/B+.
Don't take this class if you've never taken economics before

Honestly, she's a pretty good teacher. But due to the large class size she has to make her class non-curved, which makes it unfair for people who actually try very hard but aren't geniuses at Econ. I did learn a lot, and she goes at a fast pace that I appreciated.
She is a little intimidating, but overall pretty good. Class seems pretty easy until the tests, a little bit of a weed out class.
extremely fair. tests required intense studying but were not impossible. all lectures were reproduced (visual and audio) online for reference or if you decided not to attend class

Great lecturer; she ties current events into her lecture well.  Changed the way I read the paper.    Ignore the textbook.  Use lectopia (even if you write the best notes do it) and you'll make an A.  Highly recommended.

I actually enjoyed this class!  Leachman is undeniably brilliant, but very abrasive and often rude.  All the notes are videorecorded online which is VERY helpful - went to class only a few times.  Exams are tough, but I got an A- fairly easily - I crammed the night before on each test (including the final), went to bed by 2am, and still did well.

It's completely up to you to do the work and learn the material.  She puts it out there and doesn't care if you make an effort to learn it.  She does, however, make the material clear (definitely not easy, but clear). So if you're willing to work hard and pay attention to her lectures, it's interesting and you can get through it.

Lori is a good lecturer. She manages to keep it fair for everyone in a huge class of 400 people. Yes, her class is pretty tough and, if you don't work a minimum, you might fail, or get a C- rather easily.. You do not need to read the book but do listen to her recordings. Also, go have dinner with her, it'll change the perception you have of her.

Leachman's a very smart woman. She is also a good teacher. However, if you slack off (like I did) your grade won't be good. I don't like her grading system. The average in the class was around a C. I think she would be a hell lot better if she put a curve.

She gets a bad reputation, but I really don't know why. She's a great professor who really does know exactly what she's talking about. She can be very intimidating at first, but she's not scary at all. Her class isn't easy, but if you put the proper amount of time into it, you can coast.

she has a reputation of being hard, inconsiderate and unreasonable but for the life of me i don't know where that's come from.  i can't unerstand why people don't like her. she's absolutely amazing. great lecturer.brilliant.very fair. really cool person.wants her students to do well but won't compromise their learning. can't wait to take her again!

I don't get her bad rep.Shes an amazing professor that knows all the material. I am dumbfounded by her ability to at the beginning of class basically recite last lecture in 10 minutes. Hard class, but I would say easy B if you just study the week before the test (and do the practice). Would take again in a heartbeat. Go to dinner with her for sure.

She is actually a great professor, though one may get intimidated by her at first. Quite clear and straight forward in teaching and if you don't get the material you can go back and listen to it online. the test is hard. you can't ask for too much when in a 400 people's lecture.

Pros: Leachman knows her stuff. She'll just start lecturing from memory, without any notes.Most articulate teacher I've had. Cons: I got a C in the class and I put in a fair amt of time. Tests are completely arbitrary, points taken off randomly. Good class for learning econ, but if you want to keep your GPA, then don't take it.

She knows her stuff, but the class has a terrible structure. No curve. I got a B when I did MUCH better than everyone else. The average grade was probably a C. Audit the class because its interesting, but DO NOT take it for a grade if you want a high GPA.
This class was a lot better than I expected. Lectures were online, final was optional, and she took kids out to dinner. She's scary smart but real nice. Leachman made me want to major in econ.

Leachman is a straight up character. The strut, outfits, and laugh made class real entertaining. Knows the material by heart and tests exactly what she says. Cares that her students learn. Download the lectures because you can pause when she goes too fast. Put in the time and you will love her. But if you slack off you will wind up out of Econ

Best professor I've had at Duke. Comes off as intimidating, but is actually cool and cares about her students learning. Get to know her. Great lecturer; homework is a gift. Answers to questions in class are entertaining. Tests are tough, but keep up with the lectures (you can download them) and an A- is no problem. Take 51 the semester she teaches.

I have all A/A+s at Duke except for one class: Econ 51 with Lori Leachman. Her tests are ridiculous, and after the bottom  25% of the class withdrew (they were failing), she still curved the class to a B- and only 5-10 students got As in a class of 300. Her lectures are actually really good, so if you don't care for a good grade, take her class.

I have all A/A+s at Duke except for one class: Econ 51 with Lori Leachman. Her tests are ridiculous, and after the bottom  25% of the class withdrew (they were failing), she still curved the class to a B- and only 5-10 students got As in a class of 300. Her lectures are actually really good, so if you don't care for a good grade, take her class.
the ratings say it all.... except its the opposite of what they say. so yeah.

people say that she took pleasure from failing students and i got the same impression until i actually spoke with her one on one. she will sit down with you and explain things. she does want you to understand the material you just have to understand that this is a weeding out course it's supposed to be hard
Worst Professor I've had at Duke. Incredibly unhelpful and tests are ridiculous and do not test your understanding of economics. do not take Econ55 with her.
This woman removed any interest I had in the subject of Economics within one half of a semester. Definitely not recommended for students wishing to "dabble" in the field.

Lori Leachman is pure evil. She enjoys the failure of her students. She makes an interesting subject matter as boring and mindless as possible.  Then, she grades you terribly for not giving the exact answer she wanted for papers, tests, questions, etc. Pure Evil.

Grading is incomprehensible.  You will answer questions correctly but get them graded wrong because most of the 100 possible answers were not on the key.  You will do badly on papers if you do not address the topics in her hidden answer key of sub-topics she wants you to write about, but refuses to disclose beforehand.
Lori is knowledgeable in Economics, but that's all she cares about.  She wants you to know how smart she is.  She is not helpful, nor encouraging.

Leachman is a very smart teacher but a horibble test maker and grader. She's so ridiculous that you just have to laugh. This is a quote from one email she wrote to us. "all of you are smart...this also means that while you were "special" in your previous life- the fact that all of you are special means that none of you are...this is the beginning o

material was pretty easy, tests were ridiculous by comparison.  the grading was absurd as well.  the graders were very incompetent.  she does a good job of simplifying the concepts to an understandable level.  i always thought i understood the material at an A level, then got b's.  sent a rude email after people complained about grading on test 2.

Leachman is a great professor, but she should not be teaching an intro course. She really knows her stuff and lectures are interesting, and PACKED with information. Extremely helpful that lectures were online. TA's were worthless. The tests were graded unfairly at times. No HW really, but tests required a huge amount of studying. Got 89.3, A-.
