this lady is the absolute devil... DO NOT TAKE A CLASS WITH HER ... her tests are vague, she goes off on tangents too often, she gets angry when you ask a question and should not be teaching any course here at duke... her tests do not test how well you know the material and she is an absolute ****!!!!

hm i'm pretty sure more than 10 people had A-... i got an A- and i had less than 90. well anyway, the tests are ridiculously hard, and you often have to be able to read the prof's mind. my biggest regret is buying the textbook, it was so expensive and so unused. however this means all you have to do is listen to lectures to do fine.

Ridiculous. Wow.. In a class of 450 people, 10 people had -A and up. No curves. That's about 1/50. Arbitrary grading. Very rude at times to students. Open criticism. Impossible tests. All you ever do is memorize. Really worked my butt off for this class and I think I'm gonna get B+. Ridiculous......
all you have to do to succeed is learn how to read leachman's mind. that's all. in one semester.
No Comments

In a 400 person class where the lectures are posted on blackboard (audio/video/transparencies) you have no reason to go. I actually improved my test scores by listening to the lectures at home rather than waking up early to go. I would take this class again but I wouldn't waste my $ on the textbook. You don't need it. Homework is a gift so do it.

Really, really hard tests - the scary kind where you can walk out afterwards but totally clueless on how it went, because the grading is so arbitrary. And the fact that there is no scaling really hurts considering the test averages are 68-70ish. Despite the rat-tail, she can be scary and means business.
No Comments
No Comments

There's no room for interpretation on her tests-- if it didn't come out of her mouth (can't use textbook answers), it's not right. Her lectures contradict the textbook, her tests are ridiculously hard, and she is a very malevolent woman. She will demean her students during the regrade. In a frustrated email, she said her student's weren't "special"

Leachman is a smart woman, and her lectures are for the most part clear, but the grading on the tests is horrible. Any creative attempt at answering a question is harshly punished... you must say exactly what was said in lecture to get full credit for a question. Shame that such interesting material has to be ruined with stressfull, unfair tests.

Professor Leachman is brilliant & I learned a lot from lectures.That said, she is a v. malevolent woman. Ask someone from 51 about her email. Her lectures are great, easy to follow, but basically, you must memorize them for the test. The tests, oh god the tests. Right now, only 10 of 450 have an A in the class. Something is wrong with her grading.
Really the worst I ever had. I did not enjoy the course at all.

If you're willing to work out of class before the exam this class isn't impossible. I didn't  do anything (read, go to class) before the second exam and got a solid A by watching the lecture video online and taking notes, then pretty much memorizing those notes.. Lecture video! Why don't all lectures have this?

Dr. Leachman is a really great teacher I think.  Although she is somewhat intimidating at first, she is really nice (especially if outside of class at office hours, etc.).  She makes everything clear...and at the beginning of each lecture sums up what she spoke about at the last class.  Also there is usually an optional final- so thats a plus.

Dr. Leachman is one of my favorite professors this semester.  Her lectures are very interesting and you can tell that she really knows her stuff.  My only complaint is that the tests are pretty hard and there is no curve, but if you listen to her lectures online and go to class, you'll do just fine.  All of her questions come straight from lecture.
Average for the exam 2 was 68.5!!!! Before taking the test, I felt pretty much prepared and confident, but after getting my test back, I freaked out!!!! I wish I had taken Econ 55 instead of 51D!
Worst of my professors in Duke. Not taking anymore econ because of her

One of the worst professors I have had at Duke.  She answers questions in a demeaning fashion and tends to snap at people.  Her lectures are pretty haphazard and she seems to think that she is teaching a lot more in depth than she actually does.  The grading is pretty rough, and don't expect her to budge.  Also, please cut that rat tail off.
Her lectures are quite interesting. Tests are not too difficult, but there's no curve.
Lectures are pretty good.  Online homework is ridiculously easy and does not adequately prepare you for the tests.  Tests are needlessly difficult and hard to prepare for.

She really knows her stuff, but I feel that her lectures tended to be closed minded and hard to follow.  The only thing that saved me was that she posts her lectures online that you can download.  Don't expect much sympathy from this lady, and don't even try to question her reasoning.  And try not to get destracted by her rat tail...

Leachman's lectures were difficult to follow. When asked to clarify a subject her explanations were often quite different than her original explanation.  Here exams were difficult. Though the long answer essays tend to be pretty straight forward her multiple choice questions often have you wondering if you've  attended the same lecture covered.
As cool as a class average of a 79 is in an intro econ clas is, maybe a little bit of a curve at the end would help.

Leachman is a great lecturer - she manages to engage students in a HUGE class (350+!!).  Yea, her tests are pretty hard and she does not curve..some students could hate her for that...  Personally, I liked her a lot, and i would recommend her.  She's VERY smart, she has the lecture routine down pat - and she has a sweet rat tail!
Her tests are IMPOSSIBLE!
lectures are hard to follow.  doesn't curve and gives tests that are hard to prepare for.  she's gotten alot harder recently.  take this course from someone else if you want to get an A
leachman is a great professor who makes class easy and her tests are ridiculously easy if you have any brains at all and can memorize well
No Comments

Dr. Leachman speaks to her students as if they were first graders. Her tests are arbitrarily drawn from material that is not covered in class or the textbook. She is also a flaming liberal who allows her political bias to taint every lecture she gives.
No Comments
she was unbelievably clear and consise and I learned so much

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. Grading is arbitrary, right answers are wrong if it differs from key on exams. Prior econ knowledge will actually hurt you because you will answer differently from key.  Exams are uncurved while the average is in C range. Lecture is really unclear and bad.

Dr. Leachman is a stud.  She knows her material like the back of her hand and really knows how to teach students - they even put the transparencies and lecture recordings on BlackBoard now so it's very accessible.  The tests, on the other hand, are REEEdiculously hard!

Leachman is a ****. Go to class just to see her, she's an interesting character and a good lecturer. The class is easy, esp. with her new online homework system. Best teacher I had this semester, by far.

Econ 1D is a good class and Dr. Leachman is a GREAT lecturer.  Her tests are fair and truly measure whether or not you know the material.  If you study a lot, you will do well.  Lectures are easy to follow because she draws out every graph on an overhead projector and knows the material by heart.

Lori Leachman is a very straightforward, fair teacher. She knows all of her material by heart, brilliant woman by all accounts. If you understand her lectures, you will do well to very well on the tests. Great class.

I love her. She makes a large lecture interesting, and she's easy to understand. She's a tough lady, and a little wierd but you gotta love her. You learn some fun stuff, it's not really hard and it's a good experience.

Not a very friendly person... and a little bizarre with the rattail, etc. But she knows her stuff-make sure you read chapters first and REALLY understand the concepts, she elaborates a lot more than the book.. the tests are REALLY ridiculous.

Great Class. Learned a lot. Take it!
No Comments

Not too difficult of a class and fairly interesting.  Lectures are clear and exams generally straight-forward.  She is quite the character as well - her outfits, stylish rattail, strutting, and responses to questions always kept me very entertained in the early morning.  A worthwhile course.
Dont even think about it...
No Comments
Just make sure you take the time to understand the material before the tests if you're struggling. That is the only pitfall with this class. Otherwise, really great.
Helps to see her outside of class, the tests are ridiculous
meh....cant argue, but tests are really hard
It's not too bad if you keep up with the work.
exams are too hard, too long, and too confusing
Kind of a mean lady, but good professor.
Not at all a difficult class (for economics), and the lectures are presented clearly.
Great teacher
If you do the reading, the homework and come to class..you can do well.  It is also helpful to go to office hours, but in general, it is the easiest core Econ class.

Very good teacher.  Relates subject matter to real situations very well.

Very good prof, not an easy one but the best for the introductory courses
Did everything I could. Hard to reach. Still didn't get A.

DO NOT TAKE HIS CLASS. HE MOST UNORGANIZED PROF ever. He is honestly pretty detached from normal ppl, and his entire course is in one 50pg syllabus doc that was generated by AI so all the dates are wrong. He grades all the hw w/ AI, and it's clear that he doesn't care. Don't take "Entrepreneurial You". ur time is better spent mopping floors or smth
Loved Professor Moyle. Forces you to think really hard and put yourself out there.
He's great
Great professor with invaluable experience. Gives his students really cool experiences throughout the semester in a course with real world application. Really cares about his students.

I loved the class! Yes, there are many group projects & unclear assignment guidelines. However, he was upfront w wanting us to learn deal with ambiguity, which many students struggle with (see negative reviews). If you need handholding & constant validation, take w another prof. If you want to learn, be creative, & grow professionally, take w shep

To quote another student, "I've been shocked by how disorganized he is and how unaware he is of his students feelings." He also gives NO feedback on his grades but will doc points. I even asked how I can do better and he said to "do my best," which has made it hard to make progress since I didn't know what to change. Take it with someone else.

I think Professor Shep is awesome. He brings with him a lot of industry leadership and entrepreneurial experience, which reflects in his discussions in class. There are many group projects, but I realize their utility in terms of how fruitful my learning was working with different dynamics. The true value is the in-class resources he imparts!
One of the more useful classes I've taken. If you listen to what he's saying he is teaching. Group work heavy. He listens to feedback and loves Duke, but definitely the CEO type.

While I'd agree that there were plenty of assignments, many of which were ambiguous, I push back on the review below. I've enjoyed Shep's class and particularly think the conversations we have in class are the teachings, but I suppose you get out what you put in. I think the shortcomings are in how much (or little) work your group will put in.

He hardly teaches and gives complex assignments that you have to learn completely on your own. I've been shocked by how disorganized he is and how unaware he is of his students feelings. We have multiple group projects going at once. EVERY WEEK. I want to like him but the amount of coordination/scheduling & time this class requires is over the top.

I took Chindu for Diff Eq at CU and he's a genuinely good dude and insanely smart. His lectures can be VERY theory and conceptual heavy but his exams are based straight out of the textbook so there is plenty of study material. My class was 85% exams and 15% quizzes with no homework. He's very fair and will help you as much as you need.
Had him for an easier math course for freshmen, was very clear to students who were behind and had very easy and accessible office hours. Taking him again next semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Chindu is an extremely difficult professor. He is smart and knows his topics, but he moves way too fast and does not offer extra credit. There is no group work and there are heavy lectures each class and a quiz every week. He is also a tough grader. He is nice, and has office hours, but I do not recommend taking him. -Fordham student
Chindu is not bad at explaining concepts and demonstrating examples. The problem, however, is that his midterms and problem sets are so tough that not even PhD students can solve.

The other reviews are cap. Chindu is an amazing person and professor. He offered OH all the time, he would explain concepts as many times as needed. Yes, his tests are hard, but definitely not harder than other calc 2 instructors (ie Niny). If you want to go well, I recommend taking it with him/Sarah. All the other reviews are unfair towards him.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Tests are way more difficult than other professors in Math 112. Barely assigns homework and takes forever to grade things. If you don't understand notes/lectures in class you're not going to do well. Curves usually don't make sense and seem designed to make everyone get a B, super hard to get into the A range.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: -Tests are overly difficult (class average is less than 50%) -Not accessible for help -Met with him to figure out how to do better, told me to just "do better" -Gives graded homework that even other math GRAD students are unable to do, which he is very proud of -Gets very frustrated when people don't understand, won't explain it differently

Knowledgeable, engaging, generous, thoughtful, values active participation in class, values effort over perfection, funny, an active listener, great outfits. Once walked through the door in a purple fluffy coat and sunglasses, unfortunately for her students.

I took Existentialism with Professor Moi. She is one of, if not the best, professors I have ever had. She gives great lectures, is hilarious, and highly knowledgeable. I couldn't recommend taking a course with her more, even if you do not study literature or philosophy!!!

I am not a fan. She could be very supportive engaged with some students in class, but then for no apparent reason, be rude, dismissive, even going out of her way to humiliate someone for a simple question. I don't think she likes it when her thinking is not reflected in her students.

Professor Moi is intimidatingly smart. Behind this, she is also a brilliant teacher, mentor, and professor, caring for her students and always being available outside of class when you need help or just want to talk. She has introduced me to some of my favorite authors and subjects, which I never would have found otherwise.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Toril Moi is among the worst academics I know. She does not respond to students questions and she is unable (or unwilling) to explain the texts that she assigns. She doesn't understand that the core of teaching is meeting your students halfway, giving them enough information and explanation to understand the topic as you understand it.
She is one of the best professors I have ever had.

Toril's class on Sex and Gender was so disappointing. She  was unable to answer the simplest questions about the textbook. For example, when I  asked her to explain in simple terms a quote from Judith Butler, she changed the topic. A teacher's job is to help the students to understand. Toril is not qualified to teach.

By far the worst teacher I've ever had.  She had only one argument (and it seemed, only one thought), and it was the same for Every Text We Read.  She was an awful discussion leader as well, frequently cutting people off who were actually making interesting comments that she didn't understand.
Great class, great professor. She is a tough, but fair grader and a very friendly teacher.

I really loved this class and professor. She is EXTREMELY knowledgeable about the topic and clearly passionate about it as well. Also, I found she did a great job tying in what we were reading with current events and attitudes. Class discussion was encouraged. Generally, excellent class--would definitely take a class with her again!

Prof Moi is a good teacher,to do well in the class you just have to do the readings carefully  and be prepared to talk about them in class. She gives great feedback and I recommend her as a professor.

Professor Moi is a brilliant scholar and an amazing, caring teacher.  Those who question whether she is "as smart as she thinks she is" need to check out her scholarship and her CV.  Toril Moi is already one of the foremost scholars and theorists of our age, and deserves to be respected as one.  We should all count ourselves lucky to study with her

Instead of encouraging class discussion, she cuts you off before you finish a comment and does not care to hear anything that is not in line with her personal views.  As others mentioned, she believes she is far smarter than she is.  Here's a hint: try listening to what others have to say!

She doesn't seem to care about the course, and definitely doesn't seem to master most of the content.  Her lectures are boring, and rarely uncover something you wouldn't guess on your own or find out after cursory research on Wikipedia and Literature Resource Center.  Don't waste your time.
No Comments
She can be helpful, but she is completely narcissistic and not nearly as wise as she thinks she is.  She can't understand what she doesn't already agree with.
Excellent.  Brilliant thinker, good teacher.

Good professor and wonderful lessons. I learned a lot about the humanity behind medicine and how that can be captured through documentary photography. You have the option to passively listen during class, but it helps to actively engage.
The project is pretty fun, but the seminars are not helpful.

Very kind and clearly cares about his students, but there is no direction to class at allwe just sit and he talks, clearly has not prepared at all for class, and somehow holds us late after not talking about anything for 2.5 hours. No editing skills learned, few interesting discussions, and yet all classes were mandatory attendance.

Dr. Moses is really cool. He allows students to see medicine through the lens of the camera and experiment in that. Also, the readings for the class are amazing. I'd recommend for students interested in arts and health, or just curiosity. The classes are in the evening though.

The grading criteria were unclear and difficult. There's a word limit for assignments, yet you're expected to include every single detail. I'd go to the TA's office hours, and she'd say one thing, but then deduct points on the hw because what she said was wrong. The exams were open note, but because of this he's looking for very specific answers.

Expectations for assignments tend to be very unclear. He often deducts points for not making a specific point that he does not emphasize in class. This is what makes his grading very "arbitrary." The class has interesting topics and he does want students to understand. Has inconvenient office hours (during typical class times).
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Interesting and applicable class topic, but the toughness of the grading took away from the actual learning. Some topics could have been better explained to prepare students for the graded assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: this class demoralized me so much that I don't ever want to take an ecology class at duke again. the grading criteria are unclear and arbitrary. All of my friends in the course share the same sentiment.

This class had the potential to be very interesting, but unfortunately the grading system made the entire semester unbearable. Professor Morris seems very kind, but this class is completely disorganized and the grading is to tough and arbitrary that it does not matter how hard you work. Made me hate ecology and I would leave office hours in tears.

Great course material - However, the professors refused to change their methods for teaching and grading the course despite feedback from students. Groups have attempted to ask questions in office hours and based on experience, the students often felt that their concerns were being completely disregarded- let alone resolved.

Getting a good grade in this class felt largely out of our control. Grading is based on a strict rubric that we aren't provided with beforehand, and it is difficult to satisfy this rubric given a restricting word count.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This is the worst class I've taken at Duke. Grading is completely arbitrary and unnecessarily harsh. You're expected to somehow guess every detail on their rubric or get 7/10 or worse with no curve (worth 10-20% of grade). The 2 profs and TA are not helpful or accommodating. Half the class is taught by other students. Stressful for no reason.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Worst class I've taken at Duke. Grading is arbitrary and incredibly harsh. Professors are frustratingly stubborn and will not listen to students even when the entire class is struggling with grading on assignments. He directly contradicts the guidance he gives and the points he takes off. He can't explain tough concepts and slides are bare.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Do NOT take this class. There are multiple professors and one TA that don't communicate well with each other. They are extremely harsh graders. They give strict word counts, but then take off points for not explaining. I went to office hours and then got points taken off of my assignment for stuff I was told was correct. Worst class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Horrible class. Taught by 2 professors, which means you have to chase down the one that you are asking questions on. Students teach some lectures, which means hours of group meetings outside of class and arguments over what semantics the professors will arbitrary knock you down on. They aren't willing to explain grades.

One of the worst class experiences I've ever had. Half of the course is student lead lectures, so he's not even teaching. The worst part of the class are the assignments. If you don't answer the exact way they want you to they will mark you off points, a point marked is essentially 1% of your final grade. Feels like he doesn't want you to succeed
Grading is so arbitrary.

The class is essentially group presentations and writing assignments throughout the semester. Dr. Morris knew his stuff but, because most lectures were by students, it was very hard to follow the material.

Overall, this class is pretty disorganized but the topics and papers were interesting and relevant to important ecological principles and human health topics. Morris is nice and helpful; he will explain/answer his practice questions if you ask, which is super helpful to the quizzes/exams (all written & open-note).

Lectures are unorganized and useless; for half the class, students are teaching one another, rather than the profs. Grading is completely arbitrary and subjective- the questions and grading rubric are completely disconnected. We don't get numbers but rather low-satisfactory and zero feedback. He is unhelpful, unapproachable, and unaccommodating.

reviews.comment: Prof Misir should take the reviews on this page into consideration. I'm surprised that all the things people said by now still apply. CS201 was not the worst, but he lacks the qualities of a good teacher in so many ways.
He is evil. DO NOT enroll any of his classes(also capstone).
The classes are fun and he teaches well. The exams can be challenging but he gives lots of bonus questions.

reviews.comment: Friendly. Give extra points in final exam. Thank you for your A my hero.

COMPSCI 309 taught by Prof.Misir is one of the hardest classes for Computer Science at DKU. It covers a lot of content in 7 weeks so a lot of time after class is needed, but his explanations in class are very clear. He has a super high standard for the group project, which "can be published as a paper". But you can also get useful guidance from him
Be prepared for group projects
The project requirement is weird as well as the grading policy. Sometimes mean, but maybe he is just joking but I may not have that sense humor and do not get it.
Hard to comment
He is a very very kind person!!!
Never select him as your Signature Work mentor. You will get lots of weird requirements, useless suggestions and a really bad grade.
Very mean guy at times

Horrible mentor gives useless suggestions for my work.
He is very mean to student's progress and work, and show no sympathy. He gave many bad grades to his mentees (while other mentors always being helpful and give good grades) and had a history of writing bad reference letters to grad school.
NEVER SELECT HIM AS YOUR MENTOR!

I love Mine! She's so funny and makes lectures really engaging with live coding. She taught me a lot about the aesthetics for data visualization & the final project is super interesting and open ended. Even the homework, although long, is interesting and useful. All in all, I had a great time in 313!

Good lectures, very easy course with clear expectations and grading. Homeworks were a couple of hours of work per week, exams were very fair and very easy if you had any previous coding experience. Very interesting course material.

Very easy class but very annoying experience. She refuses to accept or even discuss any reasonable new approaches to problems that's different from her own, and refuses to provide answers for labs or hand back the midterm as study material for the final without a reason. No need to avoid if you need it for a requirement.

Maybe it is because she massively improved her grading policy this year, but Professor Çetinkaya-Rundel does NOT deserve such a low rating! She is a very caring professor that is easily accessible outside of class, and most of the students I know ace the tests effortlessly. Her rubric for programming assignments is a little confusing occasionally.

She was kind and excited to talk about Stats!! Don't worry! Going to her OH helps for project. Grading and code style is specific. Make sure to watch Prepare & review AE to see what she expects. Start HW early. Highly recommend the AI grader! It's not always right but great for understanding the rubric. I ran it a few times on each question.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She is exceptional at statistics, but nothing learned in lecture actually translates to homework or exams. Her grading is extremely harsh, and often she will not give productive feedback until after the deadline. Her pre-lecture videos are helpful, but this class is quite time-intensive if you are taking it for a requirement as a non-stats major.

I can get why people may not like Mine as a professor because the lectures and labs may not be everyone's learning style. However, Mine is not a bad professor. She provides videos and the textbook which are extremely useful. You need to attend a certain amount of lectures, but there is flexibility. If you pay attention and take notes, you'll pass.

this class was super chill! mine is very overhated in my opinion- the class really is not that bad. it's just generic intro stats with R coding.

there's weekly homeworks which are a bit tedious but not that hard, as well as an intensive final project. lectures are engaging with a live coding component. she's locked in & knows her stuff.

STA 199 is not that bad! As long as you go to the lectures and do homework (actually understand how it works), an A is very, very attainable. The group project and lab are a bit demanding in terms of collaborations. I would recommend taking this class with people you know. 
Mine is over-hated too. She has done a great job curating online resources.

super overhated!! fantastic lecturer whos genuinely passionate about stats. gives sm material to prep for exams which are similar to the practice ones and not bad. we never got hw or lab rubrics, so grading wasn't great, but there were drops and the project was nitpicky, but getting feedback can help get a good grade. serious but amazing overall

Load heavy. Passionate about her area, yet not a good lecturer. Don't expect to get full marks in any of her assignments. She's being really harsh on HWs and Projects. Meanwhile, exams are hard. The content is easy. But she's just trying to make it as hard as possible, such as asking you questions that weren't really useful.

Don't fully understand the dislike she gets. If you're interested in R or coding and have little to no experience this is a great class, the guidelines are clear and work is very well organized. If you do the pre-class readings and videos you will have no issues keeping up, and definitely go to office hours if you have questions.

The class was not too hard if you have a little bit of coding background. Lectures were the exact same as the videos and readings she had us do before class and were extremely boring. Homework and any coding assignments were graded a little harshly with unclear guidelines, it was hard to know what they wanted. Not as bad as most reviews say.

Taking STA 199 for my major requirements, was worried initially looking at her ratings, but Mine is great in my opinion! She provides adequate resources for the material she teaches in class, her in class coding exercises are very useful and are representative of the exams. Labs, homework, and project were reasonable! She is also very active on Ed!
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I don't understand the low rating, was my easiest class this semester. Only need to spend 3-4 hrs/week to get a good grade. Mine is caring and serious about teaching too.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Mine is very knowledgeable in her field, but this class was very disorganized. Getting feedback from the TAs on labs normally took quite some time and made it difficult to apply any feedback given before doing the next assignment. Office hours were normally packed as well which made it difficult to get any help. Avoid this class if you can.

I honestly think she's overhated -- I will admit that she can make petty comments and that lab grading can be subjective, but it's 100% possible to do well in the class. Mine responds to Ed questions promptly and lets students have a cheat sheet for in-class exams. My one major complaint is the group project (very annoying if you have a bad group)
Horrible Horrible
The content of the class is pretty easy, its basically just an intro into coding with r, but the professor more or less just repeats her videos.
This class was hard for no reason. TA's were not helpful and what we learned in class was not what was on the tests.

Unless you are a stats major STAT101 is unnecessarily challenging. You only have 2 tests that count for most of your grade and the final doesn't relate much to what we've covered. She instructs the lab TA's to grade super harshly also.
Great class, lectures and labs very well thought out.

It's a great intro class to get to know R and simple data applications. The lecture style is helpful, with frequent examples. Labs have very nitpicky grading and tend to be fairly long, but they form the backbone of the course and you'll learn a lot. Just be aware, it's literally all coding.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment:
Instead of building basic statistical intuition, Mine focuses on teaching statistics 'the right way', leading to  a course that math/stats majors find easy and others find confusing. Unclear assignment grading and limited exam study materials do not help either.

Median grades:
Labs: Ranged from 91% to 97%
Midterm: 91%
Project: 94.5%
Final: 88%

IF YOU ARE PREMED TAKE STAT101 INSTEAD! While Mine is very kind, she is not a good lecturer. The short practice exam we were given as a study aid for the midterm and the final were not representative of the material tested. Labs were very harshly and arbitrarily graded. The project at the end of the class took an excessive amount of time.

Apparently, Mine course has become more difficult this semester, but the course itself can't be that bad. It's a typical intro level course, with no prior stats background knowledge assumed. Mine is passionate about R (she worked in R studio) but I def did not enjoy having to do almost 20-page labs weekly. The grading can be pretty harsh.

Professor Çetinkaya-Rundel is a smart statistician, but this class lacked clarity in grading and content explanation. We were assigned a large group project with little guidance throughout, and our labs were graded harshly, with petty points taken off.

Mine was completely incapable of managing an intro level course. She clearly is an expert, but has trouble bestowing her knowledge on others. The class itself shouldn't be too difficult, but she is boring and borderline insufferable during lecture, while also being rude and short during office hours and when asked for help.

Mine was ok. Stat199 is brutal for those who don't have prior coding experience. TAs that grade your labs are extremely petty and WILL take off points for minuscule things. This class was apparently easier in previous semesters but became harder this time around.

Group project is a double-edged sword- it will either make or break your grade.

The class was fine. While labs and exams are unclear/harshly graded, you have multiple opportunities to do well and succeed. Mine is knowledgable, but unclear at times - going to office hours definitely helps. Do the work, go to lectures, and you'll be fine.

Mine is a good lecturer but can get less engaging near the end of the semester. Weekly labs take a lot of time but are doable if you've been paying attention. It's a bit of a learning curve if you've never coded before and this isn't your forte but doable with a little extra effort. If you do all the prep videos, you will be fine. Project inst

The class wasn't too difficult, especially if you have any experience with coding or statistics. Mine was an okay professor but was sometimes a bit condescending to students. Labs were a big proportion of the grade and took a lot of time, but working with others was allowed. Easy midterm and final. Definitely more of an intro to coding than stats.

Mine is fine, everyone here is butthurt. This course is very watered down for all of the humanities majors that need it for their major. Mine's lectures are not very engaging, but data science is not of interest to the majority of the class. The grading is all by TAs and seems overly subjective. Overall, the work is doable and the class is fine.

Very disappointed in this class. I was required to take this class for my major, and was genuinely interested in a field I knew nothing about. However, it met my expectations that I would end up hating stats largely because of the professor. I didn't learn a single thing about statistics and instead can now basically copy and paste r code.

Mine is by far the worst professor I have ever had in my academic career. She was extremely condescending and did not have a good learning environment. If you have little to no coding experience I highly advise you to stay away from this class and professor.

Honestly all these bad reviews here aren't the real issue with sta199. Yes she can be a bit condescending, but who cares, take the high road. The real issue here is this class just doesn't teach stats. It's a coding class for R, plain and simple. Never learned central limit theorem or odds or t scores, threw in Conf Ints but no real interpretation.
One of the easiest stat classes at Duke. Might not be the nicest, but it's good to weed out kids that should not be near another stats class.

Mine is a great and smart person. She is incredibly kind. Just beware of this class. Super hard and the lectures are unhelpful to doing well on the labs. The final and midterm are unfair and this class is just hard to do well in.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: It's unfortunate that an intro-level class causes so much stress. As a senior pre-med STEM major, I've found that at Duke, effort typically translates into grades I'm proud of. In this class, however, condescending remarks deter engagement, and unclear grading criteria for labs (worth 35%) add frustration, making the experience discouraging. Avoid!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Mine is by far the most heartless, condescending, rude and irresponsible teacher at Duke. Please do not take this class. Labs are arbritrary, TAs are not on the same page, course lacks ANY type of guidance and Mine is overall just a horrible lecturer and has no empathy for anyone. You might think im saying this because of the grade but be warned.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Not a good teacher by any means. Lacks empathy and is condescending. Labs take long and the grading is so harsh. You're not really learning. No quality study material. Long story short, she's an expert, but some experts aren't meant to be teachers. I hope she reevaluates her behavior/class and Duke reevaluates her.

This class is not an intro to statistics nor suitable for students with no coding experience. Lab grading is unclear, exams lack study guides, and the final project has a vague rubric with inconsistent TA guidance (this is not their fault). The instructor creates an unwelcoming environment by targeting late students. This course needs reevaluation.

Brutal final week with a project that takes hours every day (with awful unclear instructions, no examples, and no clear grading rubric) and then a cumulative final exam with nearly zero study material or instruction.

Mine is very knowledgeable about the entirety of statistics and most of the people leaving bad reviews are quite frankly bad at statistics. She might be harsh at times but some people really do have bad questions. She teaches at a Duke standard and people hate it because they think 199 should be a free class. You can learn so much from Mine.
Although the class was not the most interesting, she was a great instructor and had clear expectations.

I wish I could upload screenshots of the Ed Discussion. Mine responds fast on there, but seems to get a kick out of making a student feel stupid. The TAs are awesome. They try to pick up the slack Mine leaves. I had to take this as a STEM major and I wish I took anything else. Do not recommend at all. (TBH sometimes the labs were fun though)

Class aside, Mine is one of the most hostile and heartless people I have ever met. She consistently embarrasses students in front of the entire lecture, makes snarky comments, and places unfair expectations on everyone. I wouldn't let her babysit my kids, let alone be my professor. Frankly, she has no business teaching anyone.

She is actually so horrible, no empathy, and the content is supposed to be easy but her grading overcomplicates the statistics class and teaches it like its for stats majors. The class is copy paste code but youll never get full points because her rubrics are arbitrary. Just avoid, take Stats 102, premeds just avoid please.

She is actually one of the worst professors I've ever had the misfortune of having> although her lectures are meaningful and class time makes sense, the whole basis of this class is just copy and pasting code and even if you do that, you'll still lose points on the EXTREMELY arbitrary lab grading policies. Please just avoid this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Amazing! Best Class

Mine is a horrible professor. She will not answer direct questions students have. The class does not actually teach statistics. Instead, you regurgitate code for 25 page labs while having to worry about an in-person final and in-person midterm which she gives no good practice for. This is a horrible intro to stats for any student interested.

Do not take this class! While the content covered isn't conceptually very difficult, assignments (labs) are graded very harshly, and the lectures are extremely boring. I would definitely recommend taking something else or skipping this class altogether if possible.

Despite extensive stats experience, Mine fails at the most basic parts of being a professor: unengaging "engaging" lectures, condescending/accusatory responses to any student questions, longer than necessary labs, unclear grading criteria for labs and the group final project, and unfair grading TA-by-TA basis. Glad there is a new professor for S25.
no words. awful experience.

One of the worst teachers at Duke. She's the type of teacher who pretends to care but quite literally couldn't care less. Extremely condescending and hurtful. Not that great of a teacher and honestly not that great of a person. You could be the most knowledgable person but does not make you a teacher. That takes genuine kindness & compassion :(

This is my senior year, and this if by far the worst professor I had at Duke -- I overloaded a bunch my first two years, so I have had a fair share of bad professors already. She is the most condescending person I know, and she is very rude even when students ask genuine questions. She'll find a way to make you feel bad for being curious in class.
Really boring lectures, and they are very picky on tiny details in lab assignments.
not caring, genuinely the worst experience I have ever had. Will not be pursuing statistics. PLEASE heed this warning and pursue literally anything else.

For people taking it as a requirement: good luck. 
For people with interest/background: you'll be fine. 
I fall into the first camp with zero coding experience and being bad at stem. Horrific experience. Lectures don't make sense, labs take forever, tests are hard. Often found myself lost and frustrated, dreaded this class every week.

Good introduction to using Rstudio for coding. Most of the course is just learning how to make graphs. If you are interested in learning the code behind making graphs, then take this course. If not, don't.

Mine is very knowledgeable and good at helping students outside of class and is a decent lecturer. The course is structured poorly and grading criteria can be unclear, especially for the final project. It was hard to figure out what was acceptable for the final project and though it went well, it was not a fun experience. Don't avoid, but be ready.
TAs LOVE to dock points for insignifigant things on labs and exams. Grading criteria is often very unclear. Mine is an engaging lecturer.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Mine is an expert at scaffolding and exemplifying topics clearly. Lectures are very straightforward. Show up to lab and lectures and you will have no issue in class, regardless of coding background. Group project grading is a bit unclear; more weeks should be given to project. Mine answers questions readily, especially on Edstem. Knows her stuff!

Mine's lectures were helpful when learning the types of codes. However, the labs were difficult to complete in full without the help of the TA's and friends in the class. Mine was accessible outside of class but gave relatively surface-level advice on how to succeed. Tests were hard, but if you study you should be fine.

i don't think she's that bad, class was p doable as someone who had no coding experience. takes points off for stupid things, but go to OH and ask Qs in lab, never got less than 48/50 after that. make sure you understand lecture + watch videos, and you'll be set for exams. group proj is vague and there's no guidance, so do well on test and lab.

Class is unfriendly to statistics newcomers. No clear criterion on grading for labs, making it difficult to succeed and demonstrate skill on a consistent basis. Poor instructions for group project and little feedback on exams. Office hours are your friend, but avoid this class if possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class was fairly hard (but manageable with friends) if you have NO background in coding, whereas the course material would be fine, if not easy with a background in coding. She is extremely condescending when answering questions, barely any instruction on group project + poorly worded in class exams - take with a diff professor if you have to!

Condescending responses, unclear grading, a horrible group project, and poorly worded tests are some of the treats you can expect! While the material is by no means hard, it seems like Mine overcomplicates work to increase difficulty and time needed for labs. She is sometimes nice and very accomplished, but I can't say I enjoyed the class at all...

This course is not a hard class by any means, but the second half is significantly more involved and gets a bit more difficult. Her rubrics are consistently unclear and you will get points off for things you didn't know you had to do. The group project is awfully put together and has barely any instruction. Would not rec if you don't need.

313 is an awesome stats elective! It is my favorite stats class at Duke so far. Content is super interesting and helpful for every field. Learn more about ggplot, animation/art, and Shiny apps/Quarto dashboards. HW assignments are pretty lengthy and involved, but that's the only work in the class (no exams). Take for a fun and useful elective!
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Don't take if you don't want to code. She promised the course would not be coding-heavy, but almost every assignment was coding-based. She was also VERY unapproachable and downright mean at times, especially when you needed help. She was accessible outside of class if she chose to respond to you though

I would advise against taking STA101 with Dr. CR. The class only tests your ability to regurgitate code and properly-worded statements, so you don't develop any reasoning skills. The lectures are repetitive and the textbook is poorly organized and impossible to follow. Take 199 with another professor bc then at least the exams are take-home.

I highly recommend taking a different intro stats course. Mine was so rude, unapproachable, and unfair when it came to grading and generally treating her students like people. Unnecessarily difficult course for an intro class. The content is also very coding-heavy, which is not helpful for most majors/ actual stats knowledge

I did not know classes could get this boring. It was tumor-inducingly boring to the extent that I could not sit through the whole lecture. Unnecessary amount of work for an introductory class that 99% of people take for general requirements and general requirements only

Mine is very knowledgable but poor at explaining. The class is lecture heavy and graded on exams, projects, and labs. The labs are harshly graded; the exams are nopt reflective of lecture material. The projects are fairly easy. It was a poor introduction to stats because of the organization of the class and definitely not an easy A.
dont do it, the grades are really hard and the content is mad confusing. mine does not help much either and is not open to criticism.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Mine is not the professor you want for an intro to stats course. The work is confusing and the grading is EXTREMELY HARSH. Be prepared to lose marks that make no sense and then not get an explanation or a chance to call out the grading boundaries. Your success will also depend heavily on your TAs as well, and a bad TA can tank your grade.

Professor definitely knows what she's talking about but doesn't do a great job of helping students. Don't take this class if you don't want to code. She promised at the beginning of the year that work would not be code-heavy when the majority of assignments and tests requires coding knowledge.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Lecture and teaching style isn't easy to follow. Exams are hard and don't include things gone over in class. Really harsh grader.

This is one of the best courses in Statistics at Duke. Mine's lectures include a lot of interactive activities that make it easy to remain engaged, and most people in the class were pretty much pros at data visualization in R by the end of the semester. Homework is heavy and graded strictly but really helps you learn the material.

I had no coding experience before this class, and I don't think that hurt my performance. Attendance is not mandatory, but lectures help a lot. Prof. Mine is very knowledgeable and accessible, so take advantage of that. However, the group project in this class is an absolute nightmare; very poor instructions and unclear grading criteria.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She grades extremely harshly and will take off points even if your answer is entirely correct if you're missing a certain term. Directions are vague. A large part of the grade is based on a group project with little instruction. Not easy if you don't have experience coding.

I really didn't enjoy her class; lots of points were deducted for simply not having the correct vocabulary/wording, even if the response itself was correct. Her lectures are incredibly boring and unhelpful. You're better off milking office hours and finding which TAs are helpful. She might be accessible, but she is also unclear in explanation.

The course wasn't structured in a way conducive to learning. The professor doesn't explain things clearly. There are a lot of examples which is good- but she jumps between each example quickly and doesn't do enough general explaining to get at the bigger picture. She also doesn't define key terms, she only explains them with examples.

Poorly explains concepts; either rushes through or explains same thing over. Assignments were mostly useless in terms of the content. The coursera specialization is called Statistics with R. If you don't already know R (even though it's for beginners) you'll have a tough time. She doesn't teach how to use it, only poorly explains stats concepts
Class had a lot of work and Mine is a tough grader, but overall the content is really interesting if you enjoy statistics or computer science.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Was a decent introduction into data science - class was essentially coding in R. Boring lectures, although I imagine stats is probly pretty hard to teach in interesting way - material was basic and repetitive. TONS of homework just cause you run into bugs when coding - she's accessible anytime on Slack but can't always help so find friends in class
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Homework and tests are graded very very specifically. You can get the answer correct but more than half points off for something aesthetic/subjective. Good chunk of grade is participation even though class is an 80 person lecture. Class has no CS prereqs but class very difficult w/o previous CS experience. Very infuriating class overall.

Mine unnecessarily cuts points off labs and hw. Don't be surprised if you get everything right but haven't made the fig sizes good or have more than 80 ch of code per line. The problem is we're not told what we should be doing to get all the points - no one tells us till AFTER it's too late. Getting answers to questions right is just not enough.

I like the content of her course. The information are well presented with a lot of very good graphs and nice presentation. I highly am not interested in her character. She is propagandaic and tries to bring all of her belief into statistics. She actually made me think that statistics is more of a tool for people to prove their sad/bad intention.

Really interesting course - great for those interested in coding/statistics/data science. The assignments and material were extremely interesting, but the course takes up a lot of time - expect to spend many hours on assignments if you really want to do well. Expect to use R frequently and do a lot of group work. Attend office hours - very helpful!
She is a hardworking instructor who cares about her student very much. BUT way too much unnecessary work!!!
Tough but great. Made stats super interesting and made sure we understood stats by the end.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Great lecturer, two thumbs up. Very clear and detailed approach. Definitely is one of the best lecturers in data analysis. But be prepared to study hard.
Great professor! But class requires a lot of time outside of it. Take stat101 with Mine if you want a good teacher.

Mine is super organized, good at explaining the material, and makes herself open to feedback. Your team makes up a lot of your experience in this class but Mine makes an effort to help teams that are struggling. Most people take this class as a social science major req. (pubpol) so if you have to take it definitely take it with Mine.

Dr. Cetinkaya-Rundel expects a lot and the class will take over most of your time in the semester. That being said, if you screw up on one component, it will not break your grade (unlike in most other classes). She is extremely knowledgeable and a great teacher. While her lectures may be redundant at some times, it has been a good experience.
Very nice prof

Mine spends office hours to help you and she cares if your group isn't collaborating well, but still hope her tests could be more reasonable and the grading more human. Honestly Mine tries to make herself accessible. Appreciated. But can never like this class. Don't understand the point of a prof crashing students' gpa. Really don't uderstand

Problem set grading was tough and took a long time to get returned. Like after the test returned which wasn't very nice because it was like hey guess what else you didn't know for the test! ha! Tests were for the most part straightforward with some more obscure multiple choice questions. ALOT of work and assignment so it is kind of stressful.

No access to the professor in Coursera. The lectures are missing subject matter discussed on the quizzesexams. R studio used, but no comprehensive introduction to how to use it. Reading textexercises stated as optional, but actually mandatory. Not an intro to statistics as described. Most students have taken stats. Discussion forum is useless.
She's a great professor and really cares about her students. The class is a little difficult but she's always willing to help.
Thanks prof for being so natural and so comfortable with the course. Anyone can follow and enjoy your course

I loved Dr. Rundel's Data ScienceFocus class and I highly recommend it to anyone in the What If? Focus cluster. Although she doesn't hand back assignments in a really timely manner (she's extremely busy so this is not that surprising), she is a GREAT teacher and is always very clear with the way she presents the material and is always accessible.

She is one of the best professors I had at Duke. Even though the class is huge and she will try and take the time to remember you. She is extremely helpful and the class is extremely well organized. I was skeptical before taking this class because I hate math, but she made me like it. All her tests and exams are reasonable.

If you have to take Stats 101, take it with Mine! She is super helpful and really tries her absolute hardest to help you. That being said, this is a tough class with a lot of busy work assignments and a ton of group work. Avoid it if you can, but you usually can't.
Her course is really well organized. She has made impressive materials to teach her class.

Her class in incredible well-organized and she is a great professor. She tries very hard to make sure that you completely understand a topic before moving on. The class has a lot of busy work, though-- there are online quizzes, in-class quizzes, labs, and projects, which can get annoying. She's an awesome professor though.

Professor Rundel is articulate, engaging, and knowledgeable, and is prompt at answering questions posted on the class forum. However, for some assignments, her expectations were not clear until the assignments were returned to us, graded. I would advise students to play it safe--ask when there is any uncertainty about expectations.

Expectations are EXTREMELY unclear. The grading is so arbitrary. The material is easy enough to get an A easily, but since standards are really unclear you shouldn't expect anything out of this course. I would avoid taking this class.
Clear but demanding. Meet with her in office hours. Uses a good, free textbook that she co-wrote. You must attend class because of quizzes. Hard but fair.
She's awesome!

I had no prior statistics experience, so this class was more challenging than it should be. The curve is skewed since there will be a lot of students who've taken AP stats in the past. Rundel is very patient and clear. If you're not interested in the class, you simply won't get the grade you want. Stay on top of the work or risk falling behind.
Not a good lecturer and sometimes unclear in examples and explanations. Homework took a long time and tests were harder than practice problems. There is also a final group project.

SO much work for such a big lecture--homework, labs, and quizzes every week. Also clicker questions in class so attendance is mandatory. She is accessible outside of class. Moves quickly through lectures so many get left behind. She tries but the class is hard and a lot more work than expected

The best professor I have had at Duke! She is very good at what she does, and unlike other professors, who do not have the "best" teaching skills, she takes you through the course as easily as a HS course! I knew NOTHING about Stats going in, but now it's something I'd consider minoring in. If you do the (easy) work, you'll do great!

Ã?etinkaya-Rundel is a good professor. Definitely need to be on top of your work if you want to do well in the class though. There are homework and quizzes every week and the hw is time consuming. There're clicker questions for every lecture so attendance is basically mandatory. She's very helpful outside of class and respond to emails fast.

If you want to save your time and your grade, do NOT take this class with him. He is probably one of the worst teachers I have ever been with. Poor and bad communication. He is planning not clearly, so fast and not organized. I regret taking it with him, honestly.

Super smart and knowledgeable at what he does - so much so that he can't explain things in a way that's easy to understand. If you love math, you would probably like his focus class but be prepared to leave class being incredibly confused.
Yikes. Avoid.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This is one of the worst classes I've taken at Duke. You  may be guaranteed an easy A, but you won't learn anything and you'll be lost in the class the entire time. This class inspired me to go on RMP and share how bad this class was.

Probably the worst professor I've had at Duke. I've never posted on RMP, but he has inspired me to do so for the first time. He is not available to students outside of class, particularly before exams. His lectures are not helpful and he often gets equations wrong, and students have to correct him. Either doesn't care or doesn't know the material.

Probably the worst professor I've had in my 4 years at Duke. I think he made an effort, and I think he knows the material, but it definitely didn't show. Stick to Wikipedia and do the exercises and you'll be fine
Terrible class, terribly boring professor. You're better off sleeping in.

He says he found out he was teaching machine learning  two weeks prior to the semester, which hopefully explains why the class was so bad. The class is pretty much entirely theoretical. Despite the supposed emphasis on data and empirical applications, we never even so much as looked at a dataset. It's an easy A, but I didn't learn very much.
Great professor.

I can't say I learned anything in this class.  He's a very nice person, and he understands the concepts.  But he gets flustered when he tries to explain them and then gives up and makes his exams easy because nobody learned anything.  One of the nicest professors I've ever had, though.
awful, gave me the wrong grade
No Comments
funny guy, easy class

Professor Tuna cares a lot about his students. He is against tests, so don't expect many of those. The readings could feel like a lot but they help you get a better understanding of the course topics. I took this course as a freshman because I needed a seminar, and found it super interesting and not super work heavy.

I took 2 classes with Professor Tuna, and really enjoyed them! It's a lot of reading, but you learn so much about world history and contemporary events. We also got to work on a cool group project, where we designed our own NGO using all the theories we'd learned, and it was so inspirational that I'm actually applying to an internship at the UN!

Tuna's classes were very lecture heavy and often boring. You left without fully understanding the material and he often went on tangents that did not relate to what we had read/the class discussion. His grading was also often arbitrary. However, the relation to current events in Turkey were interesting/forced you to keep up with the news.

I had BMBD this year, and I thought it was a pretty decent class. There was a lot of reading, but you weren't ever tested on it so it wasn't the most important thing in the world. Very knowledgeable. However, he isn't a fan of grading so much of your grade relies on the final project, which you must do well on if you want an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Possibly one of the worst professor I've had at Duke. His readings are lengthy, while there's nothing wrong with that, they are usually unrelated to the discussions in class. There's no correlation with outside work and in class work. His grading is almost based on no criteria. He lets his personal opinion on a matter interfere with grading.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: He's very bright and knowledgeable about his subject. Be prepared to read 70-80 pgs with a quiz each week. Besides that, there's a large group project. If everyone gets into it, it actually is really fun. Definitely go to office hours. He cares about his students. Doesn't care about grades, just learning.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Interesting class and the great thing is theres no final exam. however you better like reading!

Excellent instruction.  There is a considerable amount of reading the students are responsible for each weak if they want to "keep up" and weekly writings which I found helpful when it came to discussions.  His exams are rather difficult, even if you did all the readings.  I learned a lot in his classes.

Interesting, insightful lectures and clear expectations.  Well thought out syllabus with a variety of stimulating readings. Incorporates literature and film.  Professor Tuna himself is brilliant.  If you have any interest in Russia, Imperial Russian History (1700-1917) is a great place to start.

Just terrible.  Weekly reading includes 100's of pages of boring nonsense.  Lectures are insufferable.  He is also one of the least helpful professors I have ever had.  His expectations seems arbitrary.  He will give you study guides that are literally completely unrelated to his exams.  I learned nothing in this course.

Professor wasn't great as a lecturer and in terms of grading. Final grading was extremely unclear and confusing and he refused to explain. Tests feel impossible to study for but make up a huge chunk of your final grade.

His favorite phrases were "I will not go over this is on the slides," and "You should have already seen this before." Honestly very lazy teaching, didn't go over proofs in class, and slides weren't in-depth or very helpful. Refused to answer questions, specially about how final grades were calculated. Take the class with someone else if you can.
Slides feel like he puts very little effort into teach the class.

Professor Munagala is an entertaining lecturer who's passionate about the material. However, the lectures were pretty dense notation-wise and hard to follow. For grading, it's almost all exams and he likes to shoot for averages in the mid-60s. Curves generously to B+ at end of semester though.

Kamesh is a good lecturer and very passionate/knowledgeable, but he does go pretty fast and his exams are difficult. I spent a lot of time working on the homeworks (which were thankfully done in groups of up to 3) and reviewing for exams. You'll learn A LOT, but this is more of a pure math course than a CS course tbh. Lectures are recorded yay.

Honestly, didn't expect I would have been spending much time on this course, but turned out tests got tougher throughout the course. The course starts off very easy, but accelerates in difficulty. That said, the professor seems to really like what he teaches. This course is not CS, not a pure math course. If you don't like math, don't take.
Solid class. Learned a lot, and Kamesh was very good at presenting material.
One of the best courses I've ever taken. Course materials are super cool and lectures are clear. Wonderful professor, this is Duke after all!
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Solid
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Kamesh either has no clue what he's doing, or he doesn't care about undergrad education at all. Either way, he is one of the many massive embarrassments that Duke's CS department so deeply suffers from.

This is the worst professor I've had. There were two midterms and a final. In both midterms multiple students received around 10-15 +points when they submitted regrade requests. But, this was not allowed for the final. The professor is unaccessible, lacks communication skills, and doesn't care about his students at all. Not Duke calibre.

Clearly knows algorithms inside and out, but not good at communicating with his students or helping them understand. Expectations were often unclear. Not a professor you need to avoid at all costs (he teaches the classes you have to take for the CS major anyway, so it wouldn't matter if he were), but definitely not one to seek out either.

Everything I learned in this class, I taught myself by reading the textbook, reading tutorials online at GeeksforGeeks, or watching youtube videos explaining problem-solving techniques. Proofs for algorithms covered in lecture were often extremely weak and provided no insight. Any questions asked in lecture were often given convoluted answers.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: HORRIBLE PROFESSOR. Cannot teach. Gives NO advice on how to do well. Tests are not related to homework. Lectures are not helpful because professor makes vague implications and assumes "it works" without details on why it works. Grading is very sketch. Arbitrary points that are not consistent among students. Would NEVER take again. Very bad prof.

He's smart and clear in lecture. His tests are hard but people still somehow manage to get 100's on them, so they can't be that bad (avg. is around 70). I will say that the tests are usually harder than anything you've seen in the homework and there's usually a curveball. Interesting class overall.

Very smart professor, knows a lot about algorithms and applications.  I found him to be good at explaining, but he expects a lot from the students. He goes in depth and proves everything, beyond what you need to know for tests.  The homeworks, rather than the lectures, prepare you for tests.

Great professor and incredibly smart. Fair grader and patient and very clear explainer. Not very enthusiastic becuase he prolly does not feel that the students are enthusiastic (which is not his fault)

Lectures can be dry and difficult to follow, but that's mostly due to the material, not the professor.  Sometimes I felt like the info from lectures and the textbook wasn't enough to solve all the exercises in the homework.  Grading is fair.

He is very smart person but that does not mean he is a good teacher. He is too smart to teach people. His lecture is very boring and I found that people often have trouble to understand the course material from his lecture.
Amazing teacher! Very smart. Presents hard material in a very clear and interesting way. You learn a lot, but the work-load is relatively light. One of the best teachers I've ever had.
a bit of a jerk and very full of himself
No Comments
No Comments

I learned he left Duke finally. I could say anything while he was at Duke. Matt Nash exploits international students. he did a lot of inappropriate things in his office. It was but no one dared to do anything. he knew how to ick his victims, the ones scared for their visa
AVOID. I know no one wants to say the but many students already know this man, Matt Nash, and what he does inn return to get an A. You know it and we know it but we can do nothing about it.

I took Matt Nash IE261. Was one of the biggest regrets of my life. This man is sick. He seeked inappropriate things from me in return of a grade. I complained to the University and knew he was fired because I sent his text messages to the officials. he is no longer with Duke.
Narrow-minded---one view. No dissent allowed. Not democratic. Very disappointing, since we have a Democratic society.

Professor Nash is super enthusiastic about I&E and has tons of experience and connections that make the class really interesting. The workload is definitely light, with most homework being readings (not entirely necessary). Lectures are long but mostly engaging and filled with smaller activities.

Great class. Interesting material overall and great guest speakers. But of busy work, but nothing unmanageable. Prof Nash is a great person and is super understanding and wants his students to succeed. Definitely recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: Took social innovation with Matt. He's a really cool and interesting guy who has a ton of unique life/career experiences, which makes the class interesting. Other than that, I wouldn't say I learned a ton of info in the class, but did walk away better aware of the world and possible career paths and fields out there in social impact/innovation

Nash is a nice guy, but I didn't find his class (PUBPOL256/Social Innovation) very compelling. Teaching social innovation by having us incessantly mindmap and literally make quilts (?) is not a very effective strategy. The guest speakers were excellent, however, and the class isn't a difficult one, just a bit busy work-y. 6/10.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Nash is very passionate about social innovation and I&E at Duke, and he really did a great job with designing and presenting this course. Not too much work, weekly readings that are discussed in class and a few group projects with individual aspects to the course that help you better understand social innovation. Great guest speakers.
Great class. Engaging Lectures.  Exposed to many guest lecturers and the team assignments weren't as daunting as they seemed.  The class lectures were pretty interesting and Matt is a great guy.

Lots of guest speakers, even a field trip. Long lecture once a week but its a fantastic, pretty easy class to take. Readings are hefty but not really necessary at all (barely touched on in class). Prof Nash is enthusiastic and knowledgeable about social innovation, I would definitely take again.
Very lenient! the goat, has helpful OH

Professor Litchinitser is always incredibly well-prepared for each class, making every lecture engaging and interesting. She's also really approachable and easy to reach if you ever have questions, which I truly appreciate. In particular, she genuinely cares about her students' success more than you might think!

Prof Litchinitser is always prepared for class. She always takes her time to give thoughtful answers. Cares about the students and gives inspirational lectures. If all instructors were like her, I would be a better student. I would take the course again just to be in her class.  Tough homework but fair tests. Always available for office hour.
The first few problem sets are hard but the class really eases up over the course of the semester
She is the goat. Loved her class and the TAs

She's not the greatest lecturer but the material itself is quite dense. Reading the textbook is a must in the class. However, she's one of the nicest profs I've had and was especially understanding during covid situations.

Super super nice professor. She was very open to questions and was very accessible outside of class. There was one homework due every week and one midterm and one final. The exams were relatively straight forward and similar to homework questions. Homework was meh.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Not the best lecturer - there's a lot of dense material that can get really boring. However Dr. Litchinister is one of the sweet profs I've ever had. Super caring and kind to her students. Easy A.
Dr. Litchinitser spends the entire lecture time lecturing. Her slides are easy to follow, and she uploads all of them. Quizzes and tests are open book. Barely took notes and got an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Professor Jokerst was an amazing EGR101 professor. She was very caring and gave us a lot of advice throughout the semester. She was very generous with grading and engaged with students and the course material a lot. When our team had conflicts, I wish she would step in more because some team conflicts are difficult to resolve.
She was great, helpful, and a nice grader.

Dr. Jokerst was an absolute pleasure to have as a professor! I would even go to say she is one of the nicest you'll meet and she is very understanding. I would definitely take a class with her again, just make sure to be on top of your work and you'll have a great experience in her EGR 101 class!
Great class and Professor Jokerst was very knowledgable.

Dr. Jokerst is a great EGR 101 professor. She is very kind to her students and helps guide them in the right direction. While sometimes her grading is a bit off of the rubric (sometimes unclear about what she wants to see), she is the nicest professor I have had at Duke and very knowledgeable on the topic of engineering.
One of the best professors in Pratt and an incredible mentor to have as a first-year student at Duke. Would definitely try to take EGR101 with her!

She was both my professor and client for our EGR 101 project. Super upbeat and also insanely competent. Always helpful in technical work and even willing to help resolve our team's internal problems. She'll make an effort to help you, but if you don't give the effort back, good luck.
Super nice! Very energetic, but helpful.
Excellent, caring, kind professor. Gave extremely helpful advice and supported us in any way needed
An amazing professor that genuinely cares about her students. Dr Jokerst has made this class one that I look forward to, no matter the time.

Myer led my discussion session for 221. She carefully reads over the proofs that you present and offers good, solid, feedback. She is also capable of spending time with you after class to go over concepts. Some ppl complain about having "no proof-writing help" but don't actually present their HW during discussion sessions. They can be ignored.

Dr. Myer was an incredible resource for this class. I was initially struggling, but Dr. Myer really helped me get a handle on the course. Even though she was primarily teaching the online course and I was an in-person student, she was willing to invest time to make sure I understood the material. She is an amazing teacher and person!

She seemed like a very nice person, but just wasn't ideal as a teacher. Lectures were not clear and time wasn't spent on developing the approach to problems. I was fine for the most part teaching myself using Pauls Notes and the textbook, but when topics weren't covered by those materials (like Sturm-Liouville), her explanations didn't suffice.

Goes way beyond what's needed to learn for the class and doesn't explain it well. First half of class was fine but her lectures became increasingly unclear and uninformative. Her tests were also extremely unfair and overall I hate her (im sure shes a great person but shes a bad teacher) and never want to hear her voice on 2x speed ever again :)

The lectures tend to lacking concrete examples of how to do problems and are very abstract. Dr. Myer reads everything from her notes and isn't that great at answering questions clearly. She is very unclear with how the class is graded. I would not want to take a class with her again.

Dr. Myer is very dedicated to her job and helping students succeed. Go to her office hours and let her know when you're struggling and what your problem areas are; she's a really reasonable person. Sometimes things aren't clear in lecture, but if you keep up with reading the textbook and going to office hours, you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Bad at answering questions. Makes the topics harder than required. Lectures arent clear and reads from her notes. Doesnt explain things. Wouldnt recommend her class.
