Lecture notes are well organized, and the professor is readily available outside of class to help students understand concepts. I've struggled with this course in the past (this was my third time taking it), but she was by far the best instructor out of the three I had. Definitely make sure to ask questions and ask for help during office hours.

She seemed lost during a lot of the lectures. Not good at answering questions. Doesn't really prepare you well during the lectures for the exams. If you take this at 8:30 you're probably going to fall asleep during most of the classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Tests are tough--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I'll be very honest, I usually don't rate professors; However, this professor has been the hardest, most intense professor I have ever had to which I would like to give a warning to future students from taking her course. No clear essay criteria, a very strict and critic professor, Students are often confused too. Just be warned, she is tough.
Great proffessor, really recommend taking her class, grading system is awesome. Classes are interesting!!!!

Professor Chu is a great resource for global cultural issues and it is clear that her reservoir of relevant knowledge is filled to the brim. The online class led to somewhat of a disconnect between the students and the professor, but she guided discussions well and made sure that the key points she was looking for in our essays were made known.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Prof Nellie always provided in-depth, timely feedback on assignments. She was also quick with responding to emails. The coursework for Culmov 101 was admittedly on the heavy side, but I always felt like I could reach out to her if I had any clarifying questions on the assignments or the material itself.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She's great, though CULMOVE101 wasn't the most exciting class in the world. The topics we covered were really interesting and class time probably would have been better if it wasn't so late at night for me (props to Prof Nellie though for teaching at 12AM). Assignments were pretty straightforward and she wasn't a harsh grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: She is a really great professor, definitely recommend her. Lectures are interesting, and she makes sure that every student participated in the discussions. Also, I always felt comfortable in her classes. Her feedback is clear and very helpful.

Prof. Nellie is very caring. She understands the difficulty faced by the students and is willing to adjust her class to fit the students' needs. But her two credits class only meet once a week, you need to go to office hour to learn more. The writing assignments are challenging but manageable.

I love Professor Chu! Her classes were always interesting, and her grading on assignments was fair and constructive. The work amount was always reasonable, and she really cares about her students. I would recommend her class to everyone!

Professor Chu is an excellent professor that will teach you how to write analytical papers. Instead of just giving you feedback on your papers, she is very involved and helpful in the writing process. She has lots of knowledge on contemporary China, and is a fair grader. I very much enjoyed her class.

I really love Nellie Chu both as a professor and just as a person. She makes class and learning so much more interesting by making class like a conversation. I remember studying about the overexploitation of factory workers, and we ended up having a long conversation about the Oscar-winning movie Parasite. Her content really applies to daily life.

Prof Chu knows her stuff. She will happily spend tons of time outside of class with you discussing her areas of expertise or anything else. She often allows the students to steer the discussion as long as it remains productivewe would spend hours discussing the points we found most interesting, and she would adjust the plans to explore that more.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Chu is passionate about China and brings this passion to light through a variety of engaging seminars and lectures that focus on areas of transformation and modernity in the 20/21st century. She's incredibly knowledgeable about areas like Fast Fashion, which she was able to incorporate into conversations about manufacturing in China.

Take this class if you are at all interested in theater, creative writing, or being in a fun environment. The class consists of writing a play every week and then casting your classmates to read them out. Neal is awesome and very willing to help outside of class. It's a lot of work, but so worth it if you want to get better at writing.
Absolute chiller. As long as you come to class and participate, you'll get an A. Super nice guy and I always looked forward to going to his class.

Let's be clear, Neal slays. He is quite upfront about expectations, the one super long script, and gives you enough time to get it done. This class is a lot of self-pacing, which most aren't good at-- myself included. You watch some interesting movies, and some short films --> specifically request the Norwegian short film. snacks encouraged.

Nice professor and fun class. The time goes by really quickly in class! People take turns casting classmates to read in class what they wrote during the week. Very cool and easy class. Highly recommend.
TAKE DRAMATIC MONSTER! It's such a hidden gem of a class. You watch horror movies and discuss them in class, and then at the end write a treatment for a horror movie you come up with. So much fun.

Took the course on dramatic writing and thus met my favorite professor and best friend at Duke. Neal is a father-like figure, caring and always supportive of his students and their projects. Very accessible outside of class and gives super honest and helpful feedback. If you're an aspiring dramaturg or filmmaker, you MUST get to know him.
Absolutely amazing professor! Super friendly and knowledgeable.

I took the Playmaking class that he co-taught with Jeff Storer--hands down one of the best classes I've taken at Duke. Neal is generally quieter than Jeff, but he is a real source of kindness, amazing feedback, life-lessons, and even some humor! He taught so much more than I expected to. If you have the chance to take a class with him, do it.

I don't know anyone who doesn't love Bell.  Such a chill guy and an awesome teacher.  No matter what your level is when you come into his dramatic writing class, he treats your work seriously and will give you plenty of help.  Plus he's funny and will say anything.  Wonder when he's offering the horror movie class again?

The lectures were very boring and you could mostly get what you need from the textbook except the Mohr's circle and shear moment diagram lectures. If you ask questions either in class or on Ed Discussion, he sometimes can be very passive aggressive and demeaning tbh. Exams were not bad, but def more work compared to the other EGR201 teachers.

Content and lectures are quite dry, however his exams are very reasonable and its definitely possible to do well on them. He is definitely very knowledgeable on the content. Lab reports are an absolute pain and homeworks can also be extremely tedious. Overall okay but I would take a different professor if you would like an easier class.

Dr. Nadeau is a great guy and for those who like mechanics/structures, his class is enjoyable and interesting. He teaches in a very easy to understand way and homeworks + other assignments are helpful for mastering content. Sometimes the class can be a bit dry and equation heavy, but success is very possible and it's important to stay engaged!

Lectures are quite boring. Sometimes he'd pause for like a minute straight for no reason. I learned everything I needed to know from the textbook, TAs, and YouTube videos in a fraction of the time his lectures take. I feel quite neutral about the class as a whole. I just really wish he would lecture faster or with some inflection in his voice.

Going to lectures might be helpful, but not critical for success in the course (go to the Mohr's circle lecture tho). Use the textbook checklist that he provides to keep up with topics and just make sure to understand all HW problems. Practice tests prepare you well for midterms. Final exam was harder than midterms, but still doable with practice.
Maybe the most boring lecturer ive ever encountered, easy grader and straightforward tests though.

This might be my least favorite class/professor in all my time at Duke. Lectures are the most boring thing I have ever seen, labs are just breaking a piece of metal, and he doesn't give solutions to any exam. Egr201 and Nadeau are the definitions of a bot. Even drinking caffeine doesn't help you stay awake in lectures. Prepare to be bored to death

His tests are easy (a lot easier compared to the ones 10 years ago. The class is overall not difficult. You will do fine as long as you do a bunch of practice tests because he tests similar concepts. If you do not go to class, which I do not think is necessary, make sure to read the textbook and understand homework problems. Go to his office hours.

Starts out easy and slow but ramps up a ton after second midterm. Homework is time consuming but there are online resources available. Can have cheat sheet for exams which is incredibly helpful since problems are all similar to HW. 3 Labs over course of semester. Other lab blocks are problem solving sessions with TA - most helpful part of course

Professor Nadeau was incredibly flexible and understanding during a difficult pandemic semester. Though his lectures were somewhat dry, he was still very clear and willing to take the time to explain difficult concepts. The lab reports sometimes seemed somewhat disconnected from the rest of the class, but the exams and grading were very fair.

From what previous ratings have said, Professor Nadeau has come a long way from a few years ago. Professor Nadeau has been extremely patient this semester and is very understanding of his students - he goes above and beyond to make sure everyone understands the concepts. The grading for the exams/class overall was very fair.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof Nadeau was a very understanding professor during COVID era. His class structure was extremely accessible, and he showed a lot of empathy towards to entire classhe listened to the concerns of his students and often adjusted his course to better fit our needs. In addition, his content was easily digestible and delivered well!

This class is incredibly within reach to any student, but it comes at the expense of needing quite a large time investment to master the pretty expansive course material. Class is completely unnecessary but you run the risk of him noticing and being disapproving. No solution processes are ever posted which is both lazy and impairing to learning.
the best thing I can say about this class is that it's fairly assessed and pretty easy. very dry though. homeworks are tedious.

Lol he is horrible and condescending what else can I say? The final is like completely different from what we were exposed to and is like 30% of the grade nice! He's also the only professor that I had in my life that only posts the answers but not the whole solutions. Like does he want us to learn or not?

Overall a good teacher. The lectures were slow, but easy to understand. You don't have to go to lectures, you could just read the textbook, but by going and paying attention, you'll complete the homework a lot faster. If you do the homework and understand it, you'll be fine. The tests are almost identical to the homework problems.
Nice guy.  Class is very structured so there won't be any surprises.
Overall one of the lowest-stress classes in the engineering department. Homeworks are tedious, but they make the tests super straightforward. Dr. Nadeau is nice and willing to explain things.

Vicious. It could definitely be worse, but honestly this guy just is not helpful. He does ok lectures, but office hours have been nonexistent. I wish I took a different teacher. At least he's better than Bordeau I guess...

You do NOT want to take Nadeau's class. Not only does he assign ridiculous amounts of work (weekly prob sets can take upwards of 10 hrs, & sometimes w/ lab on top), he is completely unavailable for help. He is condescending. He will not directly answer questions & belittles & embarrasses you for asking in the first place.
Nadeau is a thorough lecturer but lectures can get boring. Tests are reasonable but final exam is pretty difficult. Only 4 labs throughout the semester. Required class for all engineers except for EE
if you are a civil engineer don't hesitate taking his class. the material is not that hard but his problems sets are. great professor. dont skip class his explanations make the class so much easier

Is a great professor. Goes pretty slowly in class to make sure students understand the concepts. His problem sets are difficult and require a lot of work, and his tests are pretty challenging. If you really want to learn the material well and are willing to put work into it, take him.
The problem sets were hard, but we learned A TON in his class. He was always helpful during office hours and had very clear lectures.

Never experienced a more boring lecture in my life. No one can make semi-interesting material as boring and miserable as Nadeau. Really nice guy, but gives a ton of work every week that takes forever to finish. Good luck with this...
Excellent teacher.  Very thorough.  Challenging problem sets.
Conceptually easy, but workload was maaasssive. He offered a lot of office hours which was good, but the problem sets took days to complete. Teaching was clear and thorough.

Great at explaining concepts, but his homework sets were very time consuming. I definetely recommend his class if you are a civil engineer, since he is a very good teacher. However, for a BME, it might not be worth all the work. The old tests online were very helpful. Learned a ton, got a pretty good grade, but put in many many hours to get it.

Basically a continuation of physics. Tests are just like the old exams posted online and the homework really does make you learn the material.  Very accessible, friendly, and has a golden retriever.  Lectures are helpful and he really tries to make sure everyone understands the topics.

Nadeau's lectures are painfully boring and impossible to stay awake through if you are easily distracted.  The homework is a lot of work, but not necessarily hard to do.  He never knows what's going on in the homework and has trouble answering questions about it.  Also Nadeau is very partial to females and not to males in office hours.
Lecture is useless. Tests are not as hard as they seem. His HW assignments are equal to that of 4 other classes put together. Very time consuming, but not hard. VERY helpful, and adorable professor.

engineering will never be "easy" but as engineering classes go, this one's not bad.  great professor, lectures interesting and well-organized (although sometimes a little slow, but that also makes it very easy to follow), labs were even interesting.  Study old tests - tests are fair and straightfoward.  HWs a little hard, but great class overall.
Great class, great professor. He's very helpful and is really interested in the success of his students.
Hard class, difficult exams, but solid teaching.
No Comments
No Comments
No Comments

Mark Anthony Neal is the GOAT. He's super funny and is a light grader. Idk about these other reviews but he's been great both semesters I've had his courses. I recommend taking a course with him at least once before you graduate. He helps in more ways than you can think.

Mark Anthony Neal is a legend. Super respected in his field and for good reason- he's a genius and really funny. The class was very discussion-based, but often you didn't even need to do the reading to be able to participate. Only weekly homework was to submit a discussion question, and there were about 2 papers.

I truly dislike him. Hes cocky & and treats his students like theyre stupid because they dont know the things that he is supposed to be teaching us!? He plays favorites with the basketball players and literally fawns over them and brings attention to them every chance he gets. He needs to do better. Tragic.

Avoid History of Hip Hop at all costs. As a graduating senior, this is the worst class I've taken at Duke. Neal's ego and arrogance is astounding and his TAs are shockingly unresponsive and unhelpful. This class is so desperate for an academic appearance that it loses the interest of the class and any hope of actually teaching hip hop. Horrendous.

I wouldn't recommend this class. I didn't find his teaching to be clear and I didn't learn much, if anything, from the semester. We were assigned a ton of reading every week but it was unrelated to the classes. I felt like to get something out of this class, you had to already know the history of hip-hop pretty well. That said, low workload.
Loved the class. Incredibly well versed in black culture and history from hip hop to jazz to reconstruction to the civil rights movement. Awesome and fascinating lectures.
He's glib and unintelligent. Took History of hip hop, do not take the course if you're looking to learn anything at all
Super cool professor. Very interested in course material and really knows his stuff
Very cool professor. This class was an 8:45 class and I loved waking up for it! I highly recommend taking any class with him.

He is the man.. Incredibly intelligent. Very interesting discussions and he is more hip than any of us will ever be. He can seem intimidating sometimes but he has a great sense of humor and is very fair
He didn't seem interested in teaching the class.

Most intelligent professor I've had my entire time at Duke.  No nonsense, lots of interesting facts and anecdotes to tell.  My favorite class of all time, take anything with him, do your work, and get a good grade.  If you love anything about cultural currency, take his classes.
Best professor ever!  Very hip, incredibly intelligent, a little intimidating, but very approachable.
Favorite class so far...A definite must for all students who want a deeper understanding of issues facing the black community.

Prof.Neal is a man of great intelligence, not only in his area of study.  At first the classe felt overwhelming, but i soon found my comfort zone and was able to learn alot.  I recommend this class if anyone is willing to work hard and get alot of information back that applies to everyday life!
Hip-Hop Aesthetic class, but he also teaches other AAAS courses, including 106. Definitely take his class, he is an excellent and very laid-back professor!

he was an okay professor, his lectures are extremely dull and not engaging. the quiz was usually fair with the occasional niche hyper specific question with no drops, the group activity was always extremely difficult and tedious and not helpful what so ever. one bad quiz tanks your grade but there is generous extra credit at the end of the semester
Super super amazing professor. Quizzes every week were hard. Midterms hard. He does an amazing job of teaching it but it is definitely not an easy class.

Took this class over the summer with Orgo 1 and 10/10 experience. Learned a lot but exams and quizzes are open note so it helped take away some of the pressure and allowed me to focus my efforts on orgo.

Took online over the summer - it was a lot of work but it really was not bad. My one complaint is that he recorded his lectures ages ago and does not update them even though they are missing information. Also, apps are pretty damn hard but if you have a good team you will be fine. No complaints though!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I absolutely love Prof. Newpher, and this class was well taught and incredibly fair. The lecture slides are organized and the assignment expectations are clear. I became really close with my team; his style of team-based learning is awesome and helped me learn and feel excited for projects. He works hard to provide students with meaningful APPs.

Great prof! Approachable and genuinely wants students to do well. Gave an extra credit opportunity so everyone in the course could get an A (if that was their goal). Flipped learning with iRAT and tRAT on Monday and APP on Wednesday. Does a helpful review session before iRAT.

This wasn't too hard of a class, but he was a bit of a boring lecturer. Class was 3 times a week with Monday's being lecture, Wednesday was an individual/group quiz, and Friday was group work. Your grade is mainly determined by the individual quizzes so do not slip up on those. Though, he ended up replacing 2 of the quizzes for your highest grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Newpher is an amazing professor! He explains concepts really well, is very approachable, and the class is well-organized.

I went in with less of a Neuro/Bio background as a Psych major and was able to do well and learn a lot and Newpher is a big part of that. He has very clear learning objectives, is very accessible, and the team based structure of class actually works. If you put the energy into this class, you will get a lot out of it.

High-quality course that's TEAM-based. The groupwork aspect actually makes this class enjoyable. Lectures are very thorough and cover stuff straight from the textbook, which is nice b/c the textbook is dense and wordy. Weekly quizzes so be prepared to put in the work. Not the easiest course, but very rewarding.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I learned a lot of interesting things in this class! It does take a little bit of work because there are quizzes, team work, and papers to read every week. However, none of the work is impossible. He is very kind and laid-back. You can also tell he's really happy about and interested in what he's teaching!

Amazing prof. Caring, laid back, but also helps students truly learn. Actually makes TBL work successfully. Study for the weekly quizzes, engage thoughtfully, you'll be just fine - and it's a great experience.

If you're Neuro/Bio, Dr. Newpher is a MUST have professor to take a class with before you graduate. Challenging but at the same time never learned so well and the class structure definitely sets you up for success if you put the work in. Set the bar higher for how I wished other Duke professors taught.

You cannot go wrong with any class taught by Newpher. He's just a chill man with so much info in his brain. He is so sweet and understanding, but is also a very good lecturer and teacher. He exudes genuineness and is really just here to help you learn and grow.
Although the class topics were only moderately interesting at best, Newpher's passion for the subject made it a lot more interesting. One of the nicest and most caring people I've met.

How does someone master lecturing, I'll never know but this man has! Not only are his talks well-designed, but his expectations are actually reasonable and he makes sure everyone has the resources to do his assignments. Nobody does poorly in the class, and he's super understanding and caring. Just beware if your assigned group procrastinates.

I absolutely loved Newpher! He's one of the best STEM profs I have had and when I took his course, I was really questioning whether I wanted to be Bio but his class reminded me why I'm in this field. He is dedicated to his students and truly wants you to do well. His lectures are very information heavy, but so is Neuroscience.

I really enjoyed Dr. Newpher! His lectures were amazing and everything was outlined very clearly from the start. It wasn't the easiest class I've ever taken, since the material is just generally tough, but Dr. Newpher does a fantastic job at breaking it down and making things make sense. Best Bio/Neuro prof I've had yet.

He really is one of the best Neuro Profs at Duke. Most other profs aren't the best at teaching, but he really knows how to teach well. Super kind and always willing to help you outside of class. He was also super accommodating when we had to transition to online learning. Take a class with him if you can.

Very clear class. Might be the best class I have ever taken in all of my education so far. Everything you learn is relevant and is presented in a straightforward, simple, brief manner that is also engaging. The grading criteria is crystal clear with extra credit at the end to raise your average by 3%. You learn a lot and is well worth the time.
I enjoyed this class a lot. It is memorization heavy for sure. Dr. Newpher was eager to help and answer questions. He makes the classroom a great learning experience for his students.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Newpher is a great lecturer. His expectations are very clearly outlined and his quizzes/tests are very reasonable and straightforward. Skimming the textbook before each lecture helped me digest the material, as his lectures move pretty quickly.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Newpher is hands down amazing. He is very passionate about the material and it shows in his lectures. Very accessible and cares about the students (easy to make up missed work). Learned more in this class than any other, starts out fast but you get used to it quick. Quizzes every week but big extra credit opportunities. Definitely a must-take!

Dr. Newpher is a great professor who cares about his students. The TBL quizzes are challenging and ensure that you really understand the content. Pay close attention to what he highlights during lecture , as this is where the majority of questions are targeted. Prepare a lot for the exams, messing up on one is a quick way to go from an A to a B!
Dr. Newpher is the best teacher I've had at Duke. He truly cares about the subject matter and each individual student. He was a great lecturer and always willing to meet outside of class.

Quizzes are tricky, TBL isn't the funnest. but he's an amazing teacher and lecturer. he really does care. A fantastic teacher. really energetic and passivate. if you read the book closely and show up and take notes you will be ok. highly recommend. best neuro professor in the department by far. he also gave extra credit options
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Very nice professor. Super helpful at any questions you have and the TBL style really makes you learn efficiently. Highly recommend taking neurosci 223 and 353 with him!!

Newpher was a great professor. He is very laid back and is able to explain the information clearly. He's super accessible outside of class if you have questions about the material or grades. He made 223 manageable and not as scary as people made it out to seem.

This class sparked joy! It was taught like a high school class. The material was laid out logically and she made clear connections. She's not just a great mathematician but a great teacher. (she's also very nice which is a bonus)

I thought Prof. Nelson was good. The lectures were clear and engaging. However, her tests were harder than those of other sections. If you go to the lecture, take notes, review her lecture notes (which cover the material well), do her practice packets, and go to office hours, you will succeed. It's a lot of work though, but wasn't too bad.

While Dr. Nelson is a very kind and caring professor, her lectures were sometimes confusing and overwhelming. Lots of information packed into 2 lectures a week. The midterms and quizzes were challenging, with averages running around 70 for each. While her teaching style was not my favorite, she made the study of Diff Equations somewhat interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Nelson is very understanding. Cheat sheets for all tests, and helpful lectures telling you exactly what the steps are. Dr. Nelson runs the DiffEQ class like a highschool class. It's a great experience with small class size, call-and-response, and lots of group work. You genuinely just have to look at her lecture notes and you're going to do it.

Dr. Nelson is a sweetheart. She loves questions, and will do her best to either answer the question or spend time seeking the answer. However, she is not very sympathetic in terms of grading. The tests are difficult to get above an 80 on, yet the class has only two points worth of a curve. Tests also do not reflect understanding of the content.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Anna's lectures were clear. Definitely go to office hours if you need help; they were helpful. Responds to emails within a day, and always answers questions in the emails to a good extent. On exams, prepare to be bombarded with long questions. Although each individual question wasn't bad, the shear volume made the tests difficult to finish.
Good prof but lectures were very slow. Projects were very cool but support was limited.

Significant setbacks with reused lab materials from Stanford and an outdated 2012 Ubuntu VM. The grading system was fraught with glitches, showing erratic behaviors and frequent failures, requiring constant VM restarts or TA help. Office hours were often canceled unexpectedly, around 14 times, particularly near crucial deadlines.

Many small things went wrong. Office hours were often cancelled. Grading criteria for labs weren't clear (e.g., if I had known that getting 7.5/10 on the Autograder == full credit for lab 3, I wouldn't have spent 20 hours debugging non-deterministic errors that costed 2 points). Lab infrastructure is too old. I loved the lectures though.

Assigned a good amount of reading, although not mandatory or necessary. Didn't have a strict curriculum, therefore, lessons tended to go off on tangents. Overall, very nice and interesting course topic.

Boring but laid-back with lots of open-ended discussion. Readings rarely come up in class, so it's not strictly necessary to keep up with them. The coursework is ridiculously easy—two six-page essays and a final research paper on literally any topic you choose. As long as you submit your work on time and show some effort, you will earn an A.
The topic of this class was pretty interesting. There are a lot of readings and your participation in the discussion matters.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The Law & Language has been one of my favorite classes at Duke -- Prof. Newcity is knowledgeable and presents material in a way that encourages discussion. Newcity provided relevant examples and discussed current cases as well. Graded on 3 papers, highly recommend for people interested in the intersection between law and linguistics.
Very discussion heavy class, but the discussion was always fun! Professor was very easy to talk to and most of our grades were fro participation and three essays.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Hilarious professor with lenient grading. Classes are very informal, but also entertaining. Readings are optional as we often go off on random tangents, but this was a great transition into college.

Michael is an amazing professor and very knowledgeable. He is hilarious and keeps class very interesting. There are a lot of readings but you can get away with skimming them. There are two 6 page papers and one 10-15 page final research paper, but he grades very graciously. Overall, I would definitely recommend taking it.

The class is a great dive into the regulation of cyber law. Makes you reflect on the ethics of the internet and technology. Professor is hilarious and likes to make fun of Supreme Court's oral arguments a lot. Also don't tell him you use DuckDuckGo as the search engine, if you plan to sit out silently the whole semester

I was skeptical about the class at the beginning but ended up LOVING it after we started dealing with the actual law. Newcity is very knowledgeable. His presentations are very helpful for essays and papers, but he doesn't upload them. If you decide to take his class do take notes!

Professor Newcity is a great professor if you're interested in law! Information was very insightful, though he was often talking in class without much engagement from the students. Readings, I would say, are mandatory to assist with the 2 6-page essays. The final paper is a 15-page research project.

The class can be kinda boring if you're not interested in the topic, as the whole thing is basically seminar-style and just discussion about moral dilemmas. Readings honestly are optional as you don't really need to do them to participate in the discussions. There are 3 five-page papers and one final research paper.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Class was not the most engaging at times looking back at it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I appreciate a professor who has a respectful demeanor yet is fun and casual in approach. The class was not what I thought about learning 'leaglese', instead focusing on freedom of speech. The content was interesting and motivated me to think both more deeply and laterally about language and speech, and I am a better linguistics major for it.

Super chill professor. The grade is just based on participation, a midterm paper (six pages), and a final research paper (ten pages). We haven't actually gotten the midterm paper back yet, but I've taken two classes with him before and have never gotten less than an A on a paper, usually A+

The class could get a little boring and monotonous sometimes, but he's a nice guy and fun to talk to outside of class. I felt like I learned a whole lot through our group discussions, and taught me to see society and mental illness a different way.

If you are in Focus, this is an amazing class. Classes were based around the readings (Just skim, don't read!). Newcity is a very smart professor and loves open discussion. Show up, put in a solid effort, and make an honest attempt on your papers, and I don't see you receiving less than an A- in this class. Just remember to start your final early!

A really chill class to get those gen ed requirements and is interesting. Lectures are entertaining and Newcity is hilarious but makes you think. Your grade depends on only a few things (the final paper making 40% of it), but Newcity is always accessible and is a lenient grader. I learned so many new things from this class. 10/10 would recommend
Great prof & fairly easy class.

Newcity is funny, approachable, and an easy grader. This class was for the FOCUS program. It is a great way to ease into Freshman year with a low workload. He is NOT there to kill you, he just challenges you and makes you think. If anything, this class taught me how to think on the spot when someone (invariably) challenged my opinion.

There is very little homework or work, you just show up to class and talk about your individual opinions on certain issues. The readings that he assigns are not necessary but interesting and do help you contribute more to the conversation. You do not learn much in this class. Newcity is a very nice professor, and is caring and easygoing.

I took Newcity's class Law, Ethics, and Responsibility for focus. The class was discussion based, with about a third of the course centered around thought experiments like what level of moral responsibility do Zombies have. He's an engaging and caring professor who doesn't take himself (or his student's lol) too seriously.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Michael is a great professor. I really recommend taking his class in the Focus program, as he is an easy grader and a great professor to start with freshman year. He is relatable and approachable. The classes are discussion based and the readings are interesting.

I'm always skeptical reading "This was my favorite professor at Duke" but that being said this is the one professor through almost 3 years I'm certain is my favorite. Amazingly engaging lectures, super personality, wants to get to know his students. Attend classes and actively participate and you will learn so much while getting a good grade.

Professor Newcity is the boss. Honestly these reviews don't do him justice. He's such an organized, funny, and engaging lecturer. I usually don't speak in class, but in a class of 40 students, I surprisingly felt comfortable answering questions. Grading was pretty lenient, but that's TA dependent. Show up to class and you'll be good.

Newcity's Law, Ethics, and Responsibility class was a lot of fun. Minimal homework, but our class discussions and papers were always very thought-provoking. Would definitely recommend his class to neuro and law FOCUS students.

Professor Newcity is a true jewel of Duke University. He is incredibly knowledgeable about many aspects of Law and First Amendment rights, Russian history, and most importantly, is an incredibly nice and caring instructor.
Took Professor Newcity and his Eastern Europe class. Absolutely fantastic guy. Would strongly recommend him to future students.

Loved taking Prof. Newcity's class on Eastern Europe. Highly knowledgeable on Eastern European and Russian affairs with a sharp wit at the same time. I would definitely recommend him to future students.

Michael is one of my favorite teachers I have ever had. The guy is absolutely hilarious and his homework is incredibly easy. Only major assignments were 3 essays and a research paper. Sadly though, I didn't put as much effort as I should have and got an A- instead of A, which means I got a 3.7 in my easiest class.

A funny and chill professor. Always very objective and genuinely open to all opinions. The whole course is hugely discussion-driven - didn't feel like I learned much legal and neuroscientific knowledge as expected, but it was still quite intellectually stimulating. You don't actually need to read the readings. 3 essays & 1 final paper. Easy A.

Professor Newcity is a little scatterbrained and unclear about assignments, but he is an intelligent and funny professor. Most of class was spent discussing random tangential topics. Easy to get a good grade, mostly papers.

I took this class for FOCUS. It was very interesting. You don't necessarily need to do the readings. Professor Newcity is funny and accessible via email. This is probably the easiest class in the CogNeuroSciAndLaw FOCUS cluster. Nothing negative to say about Professor Newcity. He's a chill guy whose class can be boring at times, but is pretty easy.

Newcity is awesome. This class on obscenity and free speech has hilarious and insightful. If you want to hear your professor swear A LOT, take this class. Very informative on free speech difference between US and other nations. Assigned papers are open-ended and graded fairly leniently. Readings are interesting. Take this professor!

Class is easy. Readings are rarely used in class, so out of class time is rare. Three major papers are writing throughout the semester for 75% of the grade and participation makes up the remaining 25%. Class is interesting and Newcity is extremely knowledgable, although the class does tend to be repetitious. Overall - solid class.

Professor is useless.  According to his syllabus, he teaches 15 classes; student presentations make up the remaining 12, excluding exams. His midterm questions are incommensurate with the level of instruction; he predominantly picks esoteric facts.  Missed attendance is penalized harshly, despite the fact that it's a HUGE, BORING lecture. Sucks.

Power of Language Focus: Language and the Law. It was a fun, low-stress class with interesting discussions. He is a reasonable guy with a lot of interest in what he's teaching. If you're looking to improve your writing, though, look elsewhere. Essay comments are not helpful.

Newcity is a very knowledgeable professor who is genuinely interested in law.  He is a bit unorganized at times but his class discussions are very stimulating. The work done in the class is meaningful and not too difficult.  Overall very pleased with his class and would recommend him

He is a very boring professor, honestly I felt that it was a waste of tuition money. But if you need an easy class where all you need to do is attend and do crosswords the whole time then this is the professor for you.
class is boring and unstructured, and assignments are vague and he takes forever... forever to get them back to you.  there are better ways to spend your time than sitting in this class

Newcity is a nice guy who is very lazy.  Class can be a bit boring at times.  It's basically just discussion and papers.  You will surely end up falling behind the syllabus, as it takes him a very long time to grade the essays.  He grades pretty generously though.
dont expect to get your papers back soon, it takes forever for him to grade anything!!

really easy class, newcity's got a great sense of humor. the class can get kind of dry at times and sometimes repetitive, but doing the reading isn't entirely necessary and he's a really chill, helpful guy
He's lazier than you are, which means you won't be doing much work.  Class is pretty boring but you can space out or not show up at all.

Very nice person. Truly cares about his students. Possesses a sense of humor unlike any professor I've had at Duke. He's someone who relates to his students and embraces them as friends. What can I say, if I were to aspire to become a professor, he is the person I would strive to emulate.
Really nice guy.  Class presentations are boring.  He does repeat himself but you come away with good background in the material.  One of the easiest MMS courses.
He's great. His class is so interesting. We had the best intellectual discussions I've had at Duke. Rock on, Prof. Newcity!
Really, really boring class.  We seemed to discuss the same stuff in every class.  But, overall Newcity is a nice guy who cares about his students.

Crash course in E.Eu problems. Should be an exciting class, but ends up being ghastly boring readings and discussion where you don't have to say much. His fav question is "but what do you do about that?"  You will have to prepare yourself for the midterm, and the term paper is a pain.
He's got a very great sarcastic sense of humor.  The class is purely a discussion class.  Getting a good grade is not very hard.  Pretty interesting.
Newcity is organized but repetitive. Overall, the class was enjoyable, and he was very knowledgable about the subject matter.
Prof. Dr. Newcity is a pompous fool.  Future members of the Russian FOCUS Beware

Prof. Thanh is very knowledgeable and experienced in international environmental politics and economics. His presentation and written assignments are great for learning an envir. topic in-depth. However, readings are heavy and aren't always discussed in class. People yawn often in lecture. Also, sometimes, it feels more like an econ class instead.

Professor Thanh is so kind and accessible. He's really there to help the students learn. I took the class online, and he really made an effort to get to know the students. Make sure to pay attention in the readings. The reading quizzes are really specific and detail oriented (asking dates, number of signatories ect.)

His lectures arent the most entertaining but he does occasionally slip some anecdotes, which makes it more interesting. The questions for his quizzes arent conceptual but are about very specific events from the assigned readings. For group presentation, he doesnt give us a rubric so there were some surprises

Professor Thanh is incredible! He gives A LOT of readings, however he also summarizes most of it during the lectures. It is so much easier to remember everything. He also tells a lot of anecdotes, making it easier to concentrate during the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Barnes possesses a unique brand of self-confidence where she assumes that her lectures are even slightly worth listening to. Getting a decent grade is easy as her opinions on the topic are evident, and she is so enthralled by students' agreement with her that she will give out As as long as the "right" opinions are safely regurgitated.

Barnes is egregiously delinquent with grading as marks are only clear very, very late in the semester. Barnes seems to be extremely insecure about both herself and the subject she's supposed to be teaching, frequently complaining about scientific medicine and telling us about her son. Lectures, as a result, are not worth going to.

Honestly, I think that Professor Barnes is extremely intelligent and a decent lecturer. She clearly is very interested in the topic, it's just that I wasn't. The real problem for me was the discussion questions we were asked to do weekly were routinely posted the night before for a class that happened once a week, which really sucked.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I LOVE DR. BARNES. TAKE IT. Doable, engaging, difficult but rewarding history course. Dr. Barnes's knowledge and enthusiasm about the topic make it so fun. She's open to class discussions. She's honest and understanding, but really puts us to work early on our paper so that we get help along the writing process and don't procrastinate.

Prof. Barnes is cares a LOT about teaching and her students. She's been teaching history of chinese medicine for a while and its structured really thoughtfully so that concepts build over time and contribute to writing your final paper. The process she sets up for writing the paper is also really helpful and constructive.

I have nothing but great things to say about Dr. Barnes. She really cares about her students, as long as you put in the work and effort (which is a lot at times). I don't know how she manages to travel to conferences, teach, lecture, hold office hours, and manage a family, but that just shows what an amazing, hard working professor she is.

Very difficult course. Pop quizzes are very specific and difficult to answer. She expects us to read upwards of 100 pages before every lecture. Would not recommend for someone who is hoping for an easy class.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: class was cool i learned a lot, light assignments, interesting conversations, and our professor was very knowledgeable but also open to learning from us

If you have a basic understanding of social justice frameworks and contribute to discussion here and there you'll be fine. You can tell the prof cares for what she talks about and is willing to break stuff down. My only downside is that TA's take off points for the most minute things but other than that I really recommend this class

Dr. Washington is very well versed in the things she lectures about, accessible outside of class, and wants her students to succeed. For assignments, read instructions extremely carefully because the instructor team will take off points for the smallest things ngl.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This course reflects many of the issues seen in higher education today. The material is heavily left-leaning, and on day one we were told free speech wouldn't apply if it might “harm” another student. Many students may feel out of place, and the class often reinforces a sense of pervasive victimhood.

Professor Washington offers an expansive introduction to sociology and its importance to the field of computer science. It is a good class with only a few big assignments, and interesting lectures. Professor Washington also routinely updated her slides with new *very relevant* examples. It's not too hard to do well. I recommend to every CS major.

Almost impossible to not get an A. Professor is very passionate about the topic, but all discussions is linked back to experiences of black women. I think if you were a cis-gender white male, you would feel targeted in this class. Very polarized class she perpetuates, and she has so much biases in class but claims to be unbiased. Easy class though.

Prof. Washington has many valuable insights and is very encouraging/nonjudgmental despite the nature of the topics discussed in class. There is a one day grace period on all assignments (weekly reflections & 2 book reports) and pre-class materials are very interesting (ranging from podcasts to news articles to documentaries/videos).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Worst professor I have ever had. I wish Duke didn't hire her. She acts like the world is out to get her and she has a huge chip on her shoulder. She is very rude/unhelpful to students and assigns a ton of work. I truly just don't understand how this woman is a teacher. I would give her a 0 but 1 is the lowest. AVOID HER AT ALL COSTS.

Really insightful and understanding. One day grace period on all assignments. Gives a lot of interesting material to review before class from podcasts about race to youtube videos on gender. Weekly reflections and pre-lecture material, 2 books and an essay for each, and a final presentation. In all, very fair workload, trust me! A MUST take!

She is an awesome professor. She does not like to complicate things and is very generous with the grading. This is an awesome CS elective to take because it enhances your gpa too. She tries to make the topic relevant to the current cultural discussion of race and gender and does a marvellous job at relating that to computer science.

A good social and ethical perspective on tech that makes a good companion to more technical-heavy classes. A good intro into topics like DEI, identity, hiring, and algorithmic bias, but personally I felt the topics were covered a bit surficially if you already have a solid understanding of them. Overall, light workload and relevant material.

Dr. Washington was an OK professor. Not great, not terrible. Lectures are honestly kinda useless but it's easy to do well in the class as long as you stay on top of things. That being said, I don't know that I would want Dr. Washington as my professor for a class more difficult than 101. Ended up teaching myself most of the material this semester.

More of a social science and ethics discussion class than a technical CS course; very accessible to both CS majors and nonmajors. Really enjoyed this class because we learn about identities (disability, immigration) and social movements that sometimes get glossed over in such discussions. Great selection of readings, podcasts, and books.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Nightingale herself is a pretty good lecturer, however the course structure is awful. There is one exam at week 7 worth 30%, meaning lecture only matters for the first half of the class. It takes them over a month to grade assignments and requirements/feedback are often extremely unclear. Labs are often tedious and take well over the allotted time.

One of the best professors I have ever had! Nightingale is extremely knowledgeable about medical devices and respects/helps those who put in an effort to learn. Lab reports and labs can be tedious but you learn a lot. Only 1 midterm exam (that is difficult), and weekly psets. I highly recommend taking 354 with the medical device imaging GOAT!
Highly recommend taking BME354 with Dr. Nightingale! She is a passionate and clear lecturer.

Dr. Nightingale is an awesome professor! Lab and lecture were combined for my section of the class, and I found that she did a really good job of getting straight to the point and emphasizing why things were important, and she was very willing to help us with our projects when we were stuck. Had a great time, would highly recommend.

I thought Dr. Nightingale was a good professor, very enthusiastic about the material and willing to answer questions. She was very accommodating with COVID stuff and, with a smaller class this semester, gave really interesting lectures that we could ask a lot of questions about.

Dr. Nightingale is a great professor. I took 354 with her in the fall. Highly recommend. She is caring and spends a lot of time making sure 354 was an engaging class. If she does the combined lecture-lab version of 354, be sure to take it. Some people did not enjoy it, (maybe 8:30 Chesterfield was why) but it was one of my favorite classes so far.

Based on the previous ratings, I came into the class fearing the worst, but something must have changed, because I thought Dr. Nightingale was a solid lecturer overall. She seemed very enthusiastic about the subject and was approachable, although a little slow to respond on Piazza. 354 is really all about the labs, anyway.
Does not explain concepts well in class and then is rude to students in office hours when they try to ask for help. Very prejudiced towards some students, and plays favorites.

Pretends to care about her students, but in facts cares very little after teacher evaluations are completed. Takes a long time to answer a question without actually answering the question. Overall bad professor.
Very nice lady and really takes the time to explain concepts to you. Very approachable and tests reflects how much you learn in class
Very good professor, made a rather dense topic (Random Matrix Theory) pretty accessible to a diverse class
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --So many papers--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Cooke is very nice, and has frequent office hours. The homeworks can be challenging at times, but they're very helpful for the exams (so is the textbook) and not too long imo. Even though the final exam was a bit harder than the midterms, he applied a curve at the end of the year.
Challenging material but very thorough lectures

Lectures are pretty lucid. Homework sets (mostly 2-3 computation problems and 1-2 hard proofs) are short and accurate preparation for the exam . Cook is obviously caring and commonly adds hints and revises problem sets. Exams are short (i.e., possibly high variance) but very fair.

Go to class. Not an easy class, but very interesting if you take the time to engage with it. HW are few questions, but test your knowledge. Std amount of time for Duke math course. Prof. Cook is helpful during office hours, so go for any questions you might have. Also posts solutions after homeworks and midterms which are quite helpful for studying

He only does proofs in class and barely goes over any examples. is able to make such a beautiful topic in math boring. hw sets have so few questions you have no idea if you actually know the content. not good at explaining or lecturing. would not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Lectures weren't all that necessary, reading the textbook is more helpful. Professor Cook wasn't the best lecturer, but his notes are a good reference. The difficulty of the class definitely ramps up as the semester progresses. Homework is pretty lenient, taking 1-2 hours a week, and the long exam slots (24 hours) during COVID were nice as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The homework took a while, and is kinda impossible to do by yourself, so form a study group early on. There is enough time, as tests were take home this semester, but they could take 6-10 hours. I never really got to know him with zoom, and he didnt make an effort to connect with students, but he was perfectly good at teaching. Good class overall.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Cook was a decent lecturer; dry but teaches all the info you need. Content was not particularly hard. HW was challenging but graded pretty leniently. HW takes 5-10hr/wk; expect 1-2 tricky questions per set that stretch you. DEFINITELY collaborate to survive. Tests/final hard but given lots of time. Hardly unexpected for a 300-level math course.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Really liked mechanisms of animal behavior. There is a decent workload with multiple presentations both to create and watch of other groups. Tests are FRQ and can test niche content, but overall a solid bio elective. Prof is very caring and makes an effort to tell a joke every lecture
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Great class environment, super interesting topics, very easy grading. One of the rare professors that actually wants to get to know his students: meets with groups to personally discuss projects and actually learns people's names. Nowicki goes above and beyond to make class interesting and improve based on student feedback.

Amazing professor and I learned so much about animal behavior in this class; he used a ton of cool examples that I never would have heard of. Grading is very lenient with lots of completion based grades as well. You read a paper before each class and also have some group presentations. Exams were FRQs and not hard either. Highly recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I absolutely loved Professor Nowicki! He was always accessible outside of class and cared about how his students were doing, not only in his class but generally as well. Wasn't a lot of work but taught me so much about how to think scientifically. This was my favorite class this semester. Easy A.

Dr. Nowicki is a great professor and over all good person and fun guy. He is probably my favorite professor so far at Duke. I really liked the way that taught the class by keeping us engaged with different examples and case studies throughout the class. You can really tell he knows what he is talking about.

Mechanisms of animal behavior was a wonderful low-stress class, but you still learn a lot! Dr. Nowicki is one of the best profs I have had at Duke. I highly recommend him. He makes learning easy and fun.

Dr. Nowicki is incredible. He is a brilliant researcher, and he knows how to teach. I enjoyed his class on the mechanisms of animal behavior a lot because there are lots of little assignments that make up the final grade in addition to three midterms. He is also very keen on teaching students "how science works". 1000/10 recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Nowicki is the greatest! He cares so much about his students and really wants to see them succeed. I definitely plan on taking another class with him. He is very knowledgeable about bio and animals, and his assignments are usually very clear. He breaks down grading on the first day. Definitely take his class if you can!

Although he's a Dean, Nowicki is so invested in his students (he invited our class to his house for dinner). Meet with him outside of class! He's fun to talk to & knowledgeable about things even beyond his teaching scope. There was minimal work, but I feel like I still learned so much, especially in discussions. He genuinely wants us to succeed.
Awesome teacher.  Amazing class. Super easy with minimal work. Highly recommend regardless of major or interests.

rated a 4 for easiness bc you have to do the work to do well. but the expectations are super clear/work isn't hard. steve is so understanding of his students. he brings food for us every class and makes a topic that I'm not that interested in interesting. he engages the class well and I honestly have fun in class. MUST TAKE!!!! also counts for NS

Professor Nowicki is incredibly approachable. I was so pleasantly surprised by how much he did to get to know me personally -- even though he's so high up in the Duke administration. He's an incredible professor. I highly recommend him.

Professor Nowicki is amazing! He is extremely knowledgeable in an array of subjects, yet open to the opinions and views of students during discussions. He's also very approachable and willing to help students outside of class.
I don't know if Dr. Nowicki will ever co-instruct this class again as he is a Dean.  But if he does, by all means, take it with him!
Awesome teacher. enthusiastic, eager to help out his students, ready to clarify more confusing material but also ready to admit that he doesn't know all the answers.

He really cares about his students' success. He's a great explainer, and often takes a good amount of time with students' questions to make sure the class has a solid conceptual grasp of the material. Highly recommend!

Amazing professor. Very kind, detailed in explanations, and always happy to answer questions. Super helpful outside of glass as well. Able to find many ways to explain the same concept, which is extremely helpful in learning. Homeworks are definitely difficult, but if you know how to do the homework, the tests are very fair. Would highly recommend.

Dr. Nolen is a nice person and an excellent professor. His lectures are sometimes confusing, but that's the material's fault than him. He is always happy to explain something if you ask, especially with homework during office hours. His grading is also generous. Out of all professors I've had so far in the Duke Math department, he is my favorite.

Overall great professor. Very kind, always willing and able to answer questions (and explain a concept in multiple ways to ensure understanding), and very fair grading. Sometimes his proofs are a little confusing, but he explains them very well when you ask. Also relates the material to the real world regularly. Would definitely recommend.

He's a really engaging lecturer and explains the course material really well. Generally flexible on deadlines if you speak to him ahead of time, occasionally will just give the whole class an extension if a bunch of people ask. Just a really good guy and good teacher
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Nolen is super nice and a great lecturer. Content gets increasingly difficult as the class progresses, and homework problems are very difficult. Hence, office hours are a must but he is very accessible via email. Nevertheless, Nolen is really kind and always encourages group work and taking care of ourselves. Exams are hard but fair.

Nolen is an amazing lecturer who always starts by developing intuition about the concepts before writing the formal definitions. His 'reality checks' always help to understand abstract concepts in a very natural way. Homework is good and helps you prepare for the exams. He is also caring and accessible.

The class is very tough, but Dr Nolen is extremely caring and clearly explains very confusing and counter-intuitive concepts. He is very accessible outside of class during office hours. The homework is tough and proof-heavy but the tests are fair.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Caring and Smart professor. The class is tough, but if you put in the work it is rewarding and worth it.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Super kind and caring, makes explanations easy to understand with great examples during lectures. It is a very tough class with hard homework and tests though, so be warned, but it is doable.

Great professor, bought whiteboard for online class, very organized and relates a lot of enlightening math concepts, can totally think of future use Tough class, very challenging but same time rewarding, proof heavy But the overall expectation wasn't so unclear, making it hard to predict the grade Do think he eventually curved us up a little bit

Nolen is very organized, and he explains concepts well during the lecture (although he is very soft-spoken). He is also extremely reachable during office hours/outside of class (which is good because the textbook is pretty unhelpful). Tests/homework are very hard, but the class can be worth it because you will learn a lot. Good teacher to choose.
He is very prepared and always gives good examples, which is so good that I could remember for all future use. He gives the best probability courses I have ever taken. Very enlightening.

Smart guy. Not a great teacher; very soft spoken (especially for a morning class). Horrible text book with little to no explanation. Tests are very difficult (extremely difficult final).  Concepts are challenging and the professor sometimes gives lax explanations, which makes it even more difficult to learn. I would not suggest taking his class.
Good teacher, challenging but you learn a lot.

Prof. Nolen is amazing. Attendance not required, but will help in the long run. His tests are not super difficult, but you still need to study. He does rely heavily on the book, so read it and do the homework! His extra problems also greatly help with understanding. Probably the best math professor I've had at Duke.

G.O.A.T.
G.O.A.T.
if you take physics 2 make sure he is your discussion instructor. life laugh love norby
Professor Linke is amazing. He understands that weekly quizzes are hard to keep up with and will actively try to teach material he knows will be on exams/quizzes. He is also super funny

Excellent Professor! Clearly passionate about genetics and Star Trek. Assignments are interesting and very doable if you pay attention and/or read the fairly short readings. 100% recommend and would take again.
Fascinating, vivid, logical. Amazing lectures.

Flipped classroom in the spring, not really a problem because Noor's online lectures are very clear. In class, we just do problems, sometimes there are lectures but Noor is only there half the time. Concepts are easy, tests and quizzes aren't - there are always trick questions. Not a lot of work, but NOT an easy class because of the tests.

He's a really nice guy but I took Bio Genetics with him in the spring so it was a flipped classroom. All we did in class was go over 4 or 5 questions he posted online. He always put one or two weirdly worded or trick questions on the tests.

Great lecturer!  He synthesise the material really well and watching the online lecturers saved me a huge amount of time reading textbooks. In-class problems really help the quizzes and exams. That being said the exams are tricky, so make sure you read the question carefully.

The class is a flip class so all of the lectures are online however he creates a lot of test questions based on small detailsconcepts he explains in class so if you don't go to class there's no way you'll do very well on the tests. I wish I had attended class more. The material are also very interesting, but the labs are kind of irrelevant.
Noor's videos for the flipped class are very clear. However, the tests are poorly and ambiguously written and do not reflect the class's material very well, and they are worth a LOT...

If you're taking Bio 202, take it with Noor in the Spring. One of the best professors at Duke. He uses videos instead of class lectures, and the class is flipped, but his videos are GREAT and easy to understand.  Only downside is that tests are worth A LOT. Make sure to not screw up on tests, and the class will be very easy.

The class is not difficult, but more challenging than I expected. The quizzes and tests are very tricky, but I did horrible on them and still managed a B+ because there are so many other grades in the class. Going to class is helpful and stay on top of the videos, don't fall behind!
He's an amazing professor. Also, he really loves the subject and uses a lot of examples that make it interesting. By far one of the best professors I've had at Duke.
I have Medical genetics this semester, and my university instructor's lectures are not useful at all. I found Dr. Noor's online course. he is a life saver!!

Great professor! Incredibly knowledgeable and enthusiastic about genetics and evolution. Goes the extra mile to be accessible for help, and the in-class lectures are easy to follow (as are the online videos). Don't underestimate this class, but study hard and ask questions early and you should be okay.
This was a wonderful class. I'm doing it again because I enjoyed it so much the first time.  It's not easy but Prof Noor explains things so well that I understood.

One of my favorite professors at Duke. So knowledgable and has a love for teaching-- hard combination to find among research-oriented professors! Even in a class out of 400 students (+ hundreds online through Coursera), Dr. Noor still knew my name and hung out to chat with students before class.

One of the best professors at Duke. Incredibly enthusiastic, always willing to help and explain difficult things, or just hang out with students and talk. He makes class easy, even when things aren't interesting by themselves.

Best professor ever, and chair of bio! 400 person class, but I still was able to get one-on-one help from Dr. Noor and his TAs. Exams all multiple choice and easy to ace if you spend time with the material. Lectures recorded, attendance not mandatory. Dr. Noor took time to speak with every single student in labs. Nicest, chillest guy ever.
He is a piece of Art!!!.Best proffesor I 've ever had (and I've had too many).Thank you once more Dr Noor!!!!!

Noor himself is a great professor. There's no denying that. Overall, it was a great class. However, you need to be careful. Tests are 20% of your grade, and 20 Q Multiple choice/missing one drops your grade 1%. If you're careless, you'd probably do better elsewhere. Also, the online Coursera format was very irritating. I like learning in person.
Astonishingly good! Don't forgo the opportunity to take Bio 202 with Dr. Noor!

Professor Noor is the best professor I have had at Duke so far. He is passionate about the subject matter and makes time out of class to address any questions related to the subject matter. Taking this class with Coursera and online lecture videos made it easy to study. The class was fun and interesting thanks to Professor Noor.

Dude, Noor is my man! He's so awesome. Most dedicated professor at Duke. He cares about his students so much that he even meets with us in lab sections. Having that said, tests are not terribly easy. You still gotta watch every video on Sakai and attend lectures. Overall, gerat class but no curve. So make sure you double answer choices on tests!

This guy is hilarious. You can tell he actually CARES about teaching undergrads, and that's getting harder to find at research-heavy schools like Duke. Tests are straightforward, but are not insultingly easy. If you have to take 202, it's worth waiting to take it with Noor!
Awesome teacher! So friendly and enthusiastic about his field. Definitely recommended!

He is the nicest and most helpful professor!!!! He tries hard to make the class enjoyable and for his students to understand the material and do well. He even learns the names of students (those who go to class) despite it being a 400+ lecture. HE IS AWESOME!!!!!!!
It was an online class through Coursera. Excellent video lectures. Easy to listen to and clear. A nice guy. Class size = 20K.
Professor Noor is a genius and a funny one! I loved his class, he is so clear, dedicated and likable

Dr. Noor is awesome! He is so dedicated to his teaching and tries to get to know his students--even in a HUGE 400 person lecture. Also, he is very clear in his expectations and reasoning. Definitely take his class!

Best prof I've had at Duke. Convinced me to declare bio. He is SO DEDICATED to his students (as in, in a 400 person class, came to each lab section each week to talk to each student individually) and incredibly helpful, as well as really interesting to listen to. Safe to say I'm obsessed with him.

He was probably the most dedicated teacher I've ever had. It was such a big class, yet he went to every lab section and personally asked each student if they needed help. He is also very clear in his lectures and the class is pretty easy.

Noor. Is. Awesomeeeee. Seriously, I could NOT imagine a better professor. I never really attended lecture (which was at 8:30 for me), but he's nice enough to have them recorded and put online. Also, every couple of weeks he comes to every lab and asks each student if they have questions. Simply put, take class with him!!!

The class is interesting, mostly because of Noor. His lectures are necessary to understanding the material, but they're all recorded, so it's alright to miss class. Basically, if you keep up with the lectures and problem sets, you'll do well in the class. Problem sets are easiest when you check them with a group, so definitely do that if you can.
Great class, GREAT professor....highly recommend!!
Always excited about biology and did a great job making you excited. He is extremely funny and good at explaining all of the terms. His tests were pretty easy as well.
While Jakob is a harsh grader, everything else about this course was really interesting, and Jakob's dry humor was really entertaining and made the culture of the Vikings parsable to the modern day.
Great professor, super interesting class. A bit harsh when grading assignments but it is a higher-level English class so it is expected.
lots of reading and work, but a very engaging lecturer. the only downside of this class is that much of the writing is graded by a TA. however, it is easy enough to get an A if you do your hw.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed Fairy tales with Professor Norberg. He's accessible outside of class and is just such an icon. He's a very good lecturer (make sure to take notes because the tests are based completely off of them). The grading isn't easy but I've been getting As by just attending class, taking notes, and putting in effort for the papers.

Good Advice 89S freshman seminar. Norberg is one of my favorite professors at Duke! He is so passionate in every lecture and makes it an awesome class. He is very accessible for office hours and provides extremely clear, candid feedback about your work. There are 5 papers in this class and they are graded quite difficult, but hard work pays off!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: The most boring German class at Duke. I dont even know how one could successfully butcher Norse mythology. Hed run out of things to talk during class and there would be moments of awkward silence. Easy, but not worth it. There are so many awesome professors in the German department - skip Norberg if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I LOVE NORBERG. HE IS THE MOST AMAZING PROFESSOR IN ALL OF DUKE UNIVERSITY. EVERYONE SHOULD TAKE FAIRY TALES GRIMMS TO DISNEY
Professor Norberg is awesome. I didn't want the course to end. It is an interesting topic and I learned a lot.

Really helpful outside of class. Pretty awesome professor (being a Swedish speaking fluent German and English). Class could be a bit on the boring side, but grading is fair. It's not an easy A, but an A range grade should not be hard to obtain.

Lectures are extremely dull and a waste of time. After 20 min he said everything he planned to and questions the class on tangents. Essays are extremely subjective and he gives everybody a B unless you come up with a completely new idea. Worse part is that he never teaches you anything about the essays. Though the exams are straight from the notes.

Very helpful professor and interesting class about history, psychology, literature of fairy tales. Need to work hard for an A and put in effort into essays. Fair workload and a good balance to semester. Makes an effort to show us model essays and criteria to avoid subjective grading.

One of the most efficient professors I have ever had. Everything is made immediately clear in class, and students willing to put the work in will receive a strong grade. Does not use TAs and grading is not subjective as others have complained. Difficult to score extremely well, so do not expect an easy A: You will have to work for it.

Norberg is an interesting and funny lecturer, but he sometimes runs out of things to say after only 20 or 30 minutes. Grades seemed arbitrary, though this was perhaps because of all the TA's grading. if you're interested in fairy tales, mythology, fantasy, etc., I would still recommend this class - just be wary of surprise subjective grades.

Norberg is easily one of my favorite professors from my time at Duke. I have had him for a German language class and for fairy tales. He is extremely interesting, will teach you a ton about culture, and he loves talking to students and making their lives easier. Take his class. Period.

He is one of the funniest professors I have ever had - great guy.  If you are GOOD at writing, take this class.  Otherwise it is not an easy A.  The professor is great but I thought fairytales were rather boring.
Grades seem to come from no where and classes are incredibly dull. Work load is very light but stressful because only a few things add up to your final grade.

he is crazy. he's an associate professor on the most epic power trip of all time. as a friend said, 'i get more stupid every day i sit through this class'. fairy tales are great, i love them, but he manages to make them boring while being completely INSANE.
HE IS AMAZING. The material is interesting and the stories are just fun to read, so I would highly recommend the class. With any other professor, I can't imagine the class being as fun.
This class was a great way to learn about reading and writing in different contexts and genres. The work-load is low-stress and worthwhile!
No Comments

Prof. Norman is quite good. Although I came into the class not super interested about some of the "philosophical ideas" behind play/games, after being in the classroom, it became very fascinating. What's even better, is that for the main assignment, you get to choose whatever topic you like, and apply the ideas of the class. Also, he is very funny.

Do not take this course. Listening to Norman inaudibly ramble on for 2.5 hours every Thursday has slowly tainted my outlook on the world. We are assigned readings by the dozen, and we don't adequately discuss them in class due to him dominating the conversation. So many people dropped this class early, I should have followed their lead.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The most useless course I have taken. We are tested on complex matter in the readings, but never discussed them or given the opportunity to clarify salient points.
