We were graded on in-class participation, but there were extremely few opportunities to do so. Please do not take this professor. Assignments involve doing his job for him.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I took his first year seminar on serious play this past semester. i was really excited about the topic and passionate about it, but that passion turned to resent pretty quickly. he spends 90% of class time rambling. don't be like me and take the class despite the poor reviews. the 2.5 hour lectures will drain your soul away.

Norman is a chill guy, but class felt like a huge waste of time. He would ramble on and on about topics not related to the readings. Some students loved him, but I found him supremely irritating. If you care about learning course content, take a different philosophy class.
Solid professor and class.

Professor Norman is an extremely intelligent, nice guy, but class time was usually spent with him talking about something random for an hour. Although the readings were very interesting, we rarely, if ever, talked about them, and Professor Norman has a tendency to dominate the conversation. I highly recommend the ethics focus, but not his class.

Honestly, I had lots of issues with how his class was run. If you have a desire to sit there and listen to incoherent ramblings for over an hour, sign right up. But for this being a "seminar" class, there was really no discussion involved - even though you are graded on participation. Overall, he's a nice guy and the grades work out in the end.

Very unclear about assignments. Grading is very arbitrary. Minimal work is actual required as essays and projects have little to do with most of the class discussion. He talks endlessly and goes on tangents unrelated to topics. He could have a "conversation" with you and talk for 25 minutes before you get to say one word. But he is a decent guy.

Dr. Norman is very passionate about philosophy, but  his lectures ramble and lack clarity. I learned very little from this course, and the few  grades received were arbitrarily assigned. While he is energetic during class, there is little open discussion as he dominates the conversation.

He is a smart guy, but not great professor. He talks, but not teach. His grades are arbitrary. His readings are never and will never be discussed. Focus ethics is amazing, but I don't know about this class.

Interesting guy to talk to. He has some very awesome ideas. However, not the clearest when it comes to assignments. Could blabber on about something totally unrelated for the entire lecture. His blabbers are quite enjoyable though.

He is rather... eccentric to say the least. His lectures are rambling, monotonic, and nearly indecipherable. He gives off the impression that he doesn't understand the material whatsoever. Also, he frequently goes on tangents.  Assignments are easy but boring. He may not be the worst, but he is far from the best.
Professor Norman is a great guy and has a lot of interesting things to say. Although class tends to sidetrack, you can still learn a lot from the various dialogue assignments.

Norman loves his subject, and his passion is obvious, but he gets bogged down with his own thoughts and it makes classes draaaaag. He is, however, a pretty entertaining character and can inspire some interesting thoughts if you manage to stay awake.

Norman can be cool guy when you see him in office hours. He's fairly knowledgeable, lenient, and understanding (he's part of a band, and stays up late like I do). However, his lectures are dreadfully boring- guaranteed to sleep, even at 10am. Don't bother reading often, we never get to the material. Just talk sometime and b.s. a paper or two.

Lectures are a bit all over the place. There's some valuable stuff to be learned, but you pretty much have to learn it from the TAs. The good news is that the TAs will pretty much walk you through the homework, which you do learn a lot from. The tests are also quite similar to the practice tests, but this isn't a great method of learning.

In all my years of schooling, I've never come across a WORST teacher. This is especially unfortunate since this man is teaching a graduate-level course. Here is why: -Does not provide any course notes -Scrolls through pre-written slides for the whole lecture and stutters the whole way through -Assigns the hardest possible hw

Lectures are super boring. He usually comes in and starts mumbling while never facing the class once. Lectures are typically hard to follow and no example problems are done, making the homework extremely difficult to finish. TA office hours are the key to passing this class.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: This was the coolest course I've taken at Duke so far and caused me to view the world in a different way. Prof. Nunn is super knowledgeable in his field and the course grading-wise is not too difficult if you pay attention because all the quizzes and the final are open book. Super engaging class and I would 100% take it again.
Prof. Nunn is an awesome lecturer. Really enjoyed his lecture. There's a lot of reading, but mostly easy and understandable. Definitely would love to take another class with him!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: It is beyond my wildest imagination that a school like Duke University would ever hire someone as incompetent like Nunn. Even as a teaching faculty it is just outrageous. I wish 0/5 is an option and Nunn does not deserve a 1/5. In any way. I deeply regret taking Nunn's class and I recommend avoiding him like plague
OH MY GOD NUNN IS A COMPLETE IDIOT AND THE WORST PROFESSOR EVER. THIS CLASS WAS A JOKE AND HE IS A GIANT JOKE

Dr. Nunn is a great professor who views his syllabus as a contract. Make sure to do all the weekly readings, review your lecture notes, and study so you can get good quiz scores (they are 40% of your grade). Also, he gives good feedback on the clinical brief, so make sure to send drafts for feedback. It'll improve your chances of getting an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Nunn is such a kind and invested faculty member, he so obviously cares about all of his students on a personal level. This class (Bayesian Methods in Stats) was really pretty hard, and it's not the best organized class I've taken at Duke, but he was really helpful and I am glad I took the class!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Amazing professor and loves teaching. Super interesting material and fairly low work. You have a daily 5-min quiz on last night's reading and you drop the lowest 4 grades. The final exam he like gives you the questions before. Lots of cool guest lectures too. Highly recommend for a chill and interesting class.

Dr. Nunn's class on evolutionary medicine is amazing! The content is very easy to understand and highly relevant to today's society. Daily quizzes are straightforward: just make sure to review all of the slides from the previous class carefully and glance over the readings. Not hard to get an A and would highly recommend!

The content is very interesting and I would have loved to learn it more in depth, but the 8:30 am classes with quizzes every Monday were a pain and he gave way too many articles to read every week. The TA grades the briefs unnecessarily harshly but the final was fair. Overall its surprisingly difficult to get an A
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Daily quizzes at 8:30 am were a bit of a challenge but the professor was engaging and really passionate about what he was teaching. Class was organized and TAs give out fair grades. Class gives a great perspective on global diseases and you don't necessarily have to be great at science to understand what is going on. I would recommend to my friends
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Nunn's evolutionary medicine course is engaging and content-filled. His lectures are great, but having the class at 8:30 and requiring attendance via a daily quiz reduced the benefit of the lecture quality. The TAs for the course this semester graded quizzes and assignments with intense rigor, and it's surprisingly difficult to get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: unclear about grading, and uses a wierd grading scheme.

Dr. Oas is more personable and personal than most other professors, especially for freshman students who are being introduced to college-style lectures. His online resources are abundant and he even has a sense of humor by creating a video about science experiments with his son - a real life Bill Nye!

I honestly he was a really nice guy, he just was frustrated by the fact that no one went to classes. He probably just was used to smaller, more intimate classes, whereas with our huge Chem class, he was frustrated by no one showing up. He was really, really helpful though, if you need help, he would put time in with you and give extra credit some.

Not a terrible teacher, but takes things WAY too personally. Seriously, if a class had low attendance, he would talk to us about why people aren't showing up and threaten attendance with random quizzes... in a chem lecture. On the plus side, he is always readily available and dishes out extra credit for emailing him and helping people. Very strange

Visual Cultures of Medicine was definitely a refreshing class to take. Dr. OJ adapted very well to the new online format of classes, assigning just enough work to hold you accountable, but nothing close to an overwhelming amount. Half of your grade is how you rate yourself. I used this class to balance a heavy STEM/pre-med load.

Jules was amazing to work with in the mainstage production, I learned a lot from her. Sometimes she rambles a little bit, but her feedback is helpful and she's definitely a joy to see when you're tired and have to rehearse.

I had Jules for a mainstage production course I was enrolled in, and I enjoyed every moment of it. Jules was passionate, inspiring, and very dedicated to drama as an art form and intellectual endeavor. She made the course incredibly valuable as a humanities student, and she was very helpful outside of course if you wanted to talk. She's fun, too!
Jules is awesome. Most fun I've had in a class at Duke. Definitely recommend it. She's super sweet and always more than helpful. Pretty light work load too.

I took writing 20 with her in fall 2010. I got a B, but she is the WORST teacher at Duke. Literally went on rambling about stuff and expects us to produce magnificent papers as if we're professional writers. NEVER EVER TAKE THIS CLASS NO MATTER WHAT. I had a surgery and asked for a day's extension on some blog stuff-she gave me 15 minutes...

Even though I got a B+, DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS NO MATTER WHAT! You absolutely have no idea what I had to go through. She assigns way too much work than the other professors, and has a knack for turning an interesting class in to a really boring one. Honestly, if you don't want to ruin your transcript, stay as far away from her as possible!

I took her writing 20 class, documenting death. Truly awful! She LOVES to talk! Will go all class without letting you get a word in, gives WAY too much work, confusing grader, and the reading is EXTREMELY dull. Do NOT take!

I didn't enjoy the class but I hated writing to begin with. Her assignments weren't that tough, but I feel we did a lot more writing than the other classes. I preferred writing short 2 page essays every week over having to write 8-10 page essays monthly like my friends did, though. Just do your work and you'll do fine in the class.
She's a smart woman and you can get a good grade if you just talk to her during her office hours and she'll tell you exactly what to write and you'll get an A
Terrible professor. I thought this would be a great class - Im a science major. Unfortunatly, there is MORE WRITING in this class that any other. She can't give proper help and is really obnoxious.

She is ridiculous. I took CSI with her because it sounded interesting, but she absolutely killed it. She insists on talking at the top of her voice for the entire period and gives far too many assignments; she doesn't understand that we have other classes. She also makes really awkward comments and noises. However, she is vulnerable to sucking up.
Takes an interesting subject and turns it into a never ending horror show. Extrememly boring and will give you a bad grade regardless of what you write.
She really loves the material - but struggles to keep it at an introductory level. Extremely helpful but assigns way too much work.

i had her Crime scene imagination writing class- the subject material was pretty cool. dr. james is really nice and wants to help you get a good grade, but there is a LOT of writing assignments. Warning: she LOVES to talk- will talk straight for an entire class without letting you get a word in.
No Comments

She is a very helpful and approachable woman. She is also very good at giving advice for the huge paper if you're stuck on ideas. It shouldn't be bad if you keep up with the material and whatnot and involve her in the process as much as you can.
Great first year writing prof. She is really interesting and knows the field very well.
Very straightforward, but he didn't seem to be too interested in the material. Really focused on the method and reasoning behind the equations. Overall pretty solid professor.
straight and to the point. funny guy but rarely shows any emotion. I took a bar during my last test because it was so hard and then I didn't care about what I wrote down. I liked him.

While Omer gave good lectures that were clear, his midterms were much more difficult and he wasn't helpful during office hours.  Also taught 13 of the material in the last week of class which led to self-teaching for the final that is taken by all students.
Great professor. He was very clear in lecture. It's just a really hard class in general. His midterms were fair.
*better than some multi professors * worse than others * hard tests * will try his best to help you if you ask for it*
His midterms are really difficult. I basically had to teach myself all the material even though I went to all his lectures.

Omer is an AMAZING professor! I absolutely loved him! He is super clear, has very good structure in class, goes through all the proofs (even though sometimes quite fast). He color codes things and makes it very easy to take notes in class. Definitely consider taking him!! And he is not particularly hard, multi is just a hardish class.
Omer is extremely nice. He sets very reasonable examinations. Definitely consider taking a class with him.

Multi is just hard in general, but omer does a good job for what it's worth. he tries to make sure everyone understands the concepts, but sometimes his english is a little off and hard to understand. nice guy, and tries his best to be a good professor
Omer was awesome. Really funny teacher with a good sense of humor who taught well.

Omer was a great teacher and put a lot of effort into proving and providing examples for each concept. He was also readily available and hosted helpful office hours. He's got a sweet accent and will be glad to teach you about happy and sad parabolas if you ask
Omer is awesome!

Professor Olson provides students the opportunity to engage material beyond what they would on their own. He is well-versed in Visual, Media, and Post-Modern Theory and can contextualize any type of media and technology within the world of theory. His ability to stay current and his willingness to test any idea is what makes him fantastic.
Professor Olson is very accesible, very encouraging, and cares deeply about his student's projects. Hi assigned super interesting reading material.

The course is mostly guest lecturers and the exams focus on 'key terms' that can be reviewed in fifteen minutes beforehand. The lectures that Olson gives are very dull and longwinded. This is a mandatory course for VMS majors.
She's awesome. Y'all are tripping. Super easy and fun.
Super manageable class! Short quizzes every week and there are assigned readings but no busy work!

Dr. Ng is a great professor who was very enthusiastic about her subject area. Although the class sometimes felt a bit disorganized due to it being the first time being offered, her passion for neuroscience and her students was evident, and she occasionally brought snacks for the class!
Professor Ng was disconnected from the class and extremely unfriendly. They were the only professor I had in my entire 4 years at Duke who didn't seem like they wanted to be there.

Honestly, many of the negative reviews are EXTREMELY overblown. If you take the initiative to talk to Dr. Ng after or outside of class, she's awesome. I encountered extenuating circumstances during the semester and she was incredibly understanding & accommodating. I found the team-based format great; it's the better way to do this 150+ person class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I feel my neurons die around Minna.This is the worst class I have taken at Duke-- there is no standard difficulty level across weeks, grading is arbitrary on labs, demands dissecting insects, and also being asked to play with Play-Doh. Don't take if you don't have to. Psych major? S/U this class. Minna should not be allowed to teach.
Easy course as long as you do the weekly readings and it is flipped classroom.

This class was literally such a joke and a waste of time. The "flipped classroom" is an excuse so the professors don't have to teach. Minna was disorganized, always going back on her word and uncertain about the answers to the quizzes SHE WROTE. Expectations were so unclear. Also, Minna was condescending, treating us like middle school students.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Genuinely, the most condescending professor I've ever encountered at Duke. Other than that, the class isn't too bad. It's mostly weekly quizzes about assigned textbook readings and group lab activities. The quiz questions are often unclear, so make sure to read carefully. Overall, not a horrible class, but I didn't like the professor's attitude.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Avoid this class. There were moments when I was actually concerned about Dr. Ng's sanity when she was teaching this class. The best thing about this class is the camaraderie you build with your classmates while sitting through this godforsaken class.

As long as you do the textbook readings (manageable and easy to understand), this class is a breeze. The weekly quizzes are easy as long as you read the textbook. Minna is a little condescending and tends to mess up writing questions on quizzes, but she always gives you the points back. Content is fairly interesting too.

The assignments aren't too difficult, but the only way you learn is from reading the textbook. Ng is hands down the worst professor I have ever encountered. Her lectures are not helpful at all. She appears nice in front of the large class, but as soon as you talk to her, it's clear that she thinks very low of you and isn't afraid to show it
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Ng's NEURO102 class can be a mixed bag. The material is interesting, but her teaching style can be disorganized. Staying on top of readings and using resources like unstuck ai for study prep helped me get through the course successfully.
Her class was pretty simple, however she goes back on her word, she doesn't support her students' academic goals, and she doesn't respond to emails. You don't want her.

While this class was an easy A, it was solely teach yourself. In class you took quizzes on the pre-reading and then were lectured after submitting the grade. The quizzes were also wrong a good amount of the time, which got annoying because it confused the students. Professor Ng was very passive aggressive.

Easiest A ever but one of the worst experiences. Ng is very passive aggressive, wants to appear nice, but doesn't want to hear you explain your situation. You learn everything by watching videos and reading textbook OUTSIDE class. Class is just a simple waste of time. Not to mention the ridiculous scratchers design--you scratch one off wrong, 0 pt.

With a good group, it is easy to complete assignments and labs, but groups are randomly selected. Tougher grading on written activities, but good curve on daily quizzes. No way to pass without keeping up with textbook pacing. Lots of content, but it is paced well and does not feel too overwhelming. Few extra credit opportunities.
The class material is interesting. Minna is not great at explaining it, though. The flipped classroom stuff is really annoying so buckle up.

She's too condescending and passive-aggressive to students. The exams are not based on the material learned in class very well. The class is interesting but I'm not sure if it's taught well by her. Adjust expectations. Grading criteria can be more clear sometimes.

Just okay…makes mistakes during lecture and exams which won't be called out unless you say something. You have to prove your answers right sometimes because she's not sure herself. Can be rude with students sometimes and haven't had this problem much with other Duke professors.

Honestly the class itself and the material was not too bad. Professor Ng is a bit disorganized which can make the class somewhat hard, but as long as you show up everyday, read the text book, and do the end-of-chapter quizzes you'll be fine. Would only recommend taking this class if its required for your major

80% of the class is like pure participation.... but that last 20% (the final) was incredibly difficult. Just do your work and you will be fine and can do poorly on it. She is really really nice but is very strict about her tech policy and attendance. If you miss, make-ups are pretty much never given and you get a zero.

Minna made mistakes on quizzes throughout the semester, including the final exam. Had to submit a form to the Registrar to upgrade students' grades because of constant errors in questions, affecting final course grades. 
If you don't speak up, questions will be marked wrong. Class lecture time is not used effectively after quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The class was disorganized with many questions being miswritten. Your grade is spread amongst many assignments, with most being easy 100s. Minna never seemed to answer our questions directly and wasn't all that helpful. Given this requirement for the major, I wouldn't worry about the class, just have expectations going in. Guest lectures were fun.

WORST professor I've ever had. Never done a Rate My Professor before, but she enraged me so much that I had to. And what's crazy is that the class was so interesting. She wasn't. The textbook was. In fact, her lectures might have made me understand the material LESS. She is the sassiest, most demeaning professor. Can I rate her lower than a 1?
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I think Dr. Ng gets a lot of hate, but she is an ok person one-on-one. She is a bit neurotic and never really gives straightforward answers to your questions, but the quizzes and finals were based on the textbook so doing well in the class isn't hard. Just make sure you prepare for class and find something interesting to do during the lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: the class is mandatory for neuro ppl but good lord minna is the absolute worst teacher, nay person i have ever had the misfortune of interacting with. take this class knowing you are about to enter the most grueling mental torture of your life

Dr. Ng's class was great. Our weekly quizzes were easy and you did not need to get everything right. Taking quizzes with a group was worth a lot so that helped my grade a lot too.. I didn't do so well on one exam but was able to  resubmit answers and get a lot of credit for it.

The content is dense and requires lots of time outside of class. While the midterms and finals were difficult, it was good preparation for the many pre-meds who have to get used to digesting large amounts of text. Overall a good experience, but do not take this class assuming it will be easy.

Her tests (and final) were poorly made and had many flaws. After spending a week fixing my exam questions and even attending office hours, I still received minimal credit as she offered "corrections" because her test was flawed and unclear. Met with her to discuss this on Zoom with her and she was passive-aggressive/condescending.

The midterm was so horribly written that she had to offer a remediation opportunity. Same issue with the final. She tested us on things that we never learned, and then blamed us for not studying enough for the exams. The class itself is a lot of content and it's just frustrating when you put a lot of work into studying and it doesn't pay off.

Pretty hard to avoid taking her class if Neuro major or Psych major, but God was this class awful. Her new exams are literally impossible. Midterm was so bad we were all allowed huge remediations (at least) but she didn't give us this opportunity for the final (which was DETRIMENTAL for final grades). Nice lady, but horrible class structure

Definitely the worst professor I've had. She assigns unreasonable and trivial busy-work, and the lectures/labs are incredibly disorganized. The midterm was unfair and the class collectively struggled with it. Not to mention that she is super passive-aggressive and "fake nice." Don't take this class unless you need to. Waste of time.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I lowkey think she uses chatgpt to write her exam questions

Incredibly passive aggressive. Failed nearly evryone on first exam then let us do test corrections for some points back (bc she refuses to curve) then blamed it on us (4 QUESTONS ON THE EXAM ABT SOMETHING MENTIONED

100% recommend avoiding Prof Ng if you can. Exams are a much higher (unrealistic) application of the material covered. Hw is to teach yourself the entire semester [spending hours reading the txtbook & watching pre-recorded lecture vids.] The whole class failed our first exam and she didn't curve (& blamed us)!! Much more to say (hit char limit).
Absolute gem.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Hard class for intro level

This class was incredibly frustrating with the way that it was taught and set up; it almost discouraged me from majoring in neuroscience. Although we need to read lengthy chapters from a textbook, her lectures in class are a complete repetition of the homework. Midterm was awful with many errors - unfortunately this class required for neuro majors
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: She was the worst professor I've had at Duke but I had to take this class for the neuro requirement. Midterm was written so badly with mistakes that they had to offer a re-mediation opportunity. Very passive aggressive and unhelpful. My grade is fine but experience was terrible

This professor is hilarious in the sense that it is comical how horrible she is. Her lectures are horribly unorganized, constantly has to make changes to the questions she asks because they make little to no sense, and to top if off is extremely passive-aggressive. If you have to take this class for a requirement then be prepared for an awful ride.
Pretty easy class but I didn't learn a single thing

She is genuinely passionate about what she's teaching and even though she's confusing at times, I think she does a great job selecting the topics taught in an introductory class. She improves the class each semester and is making a genuine effort to make this class as good as possible. Love her

One aspect that truly sets Dr. Minna Ng apart is her genuine passion for teaching and her brilliance. A while back I was prepping for the MCAT and I got amazingly good tips from Prof. Ng about it. Got into DO school last year!

Dr. Ng's teaching style is engaging and captivating. She includes interactive activities to ensure that we are all involved in the learning process. Group work isn't always the best, but in the real world you have to do it in some way or another. Her class really facilitated my skills critical thinking and collaboration.

Minna is quite a character, but she makes the class interesting as we study a different aspect of neuroscience each week! Basically the only work is the textbook readings, where there are weekly individual and team quizzes. These questions often make up most of the midterm and final exam, too.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Forget these bad reviews - Dr. Ng is an amazing professor. You will learn a lot in this course and I loved the team component. If you do the readings and practice questions, you will have no problem succeeding in this course! Dr. Ng is always available to answer extra questions; this is a great course for anyone interested in the brain.

Initially Professor Ng seemed like she would be all over the place, and to be honest she was, but in the best way. NEURO 102 turned out to be my favorite class, Professor Ng is hilarious, kind of kooky, but knows what she's talking about. The work load is super manageable as long as your stay on top of your readings, which is not difficult to do.

I would highly reccomend taking this class to anyone interested in Neuroscience. I really enjoyed the team based class and Dr. Ng does a great job teaching beyond what the textbook can provide. Relatively chill class environment and the professor responds well to feedback as well.
Love Dr. Ng. She's a very caring professor and helped me learn to ask more and better questions. Great seminar, highly recommend.

Minna is a character for sure, she is a little cray at times but she grew on me. The class meets only once a week and the HW is to watch + take notes on a video per chapter - really isn't that bad. It is a team based class so if your team is chill the class is really enjoyable. Both midterm and final were take home, multiple choice, and online.

Forget all these bad reviews. Dr. Ng puts a lot of effort into making this class fun and informative. Course moves quickly, but the class's team-based format gives you the opportunity to work with others. Plus, you get to take the weekly quiz with your team and make some friends. Very stress-free class that can introduce anyone to neuroscience.

I don't get the bad reviews. Easy A if you have a solid group. Skimming the textbook the night before class is enough to pass the individual/group quizzes. Ng's quiz questions can sometimes be unclear. Even if most of the class agrees with a different answer, she won't concede. Class was 2.5 hrs, so it was hard to stay focused. Exams are open note.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dont know why so many bad reviews. Neuro102 team based was my easiest class this semester. Watch video lectures and read the textbook for homework, and short quizzes in class-only needed 7/10 to get credit. Non-cumulative final and it was online open notes.10/10 class recommend especially if you need a psych requirement bc easier than psych 101

Ignore the other comments. Dr. Ng speeds through class but tries to crack jokes + loves answering questions, and content is interesting. Just read the textbook: take bullet-pointed, organized, brief notes in a google doc (open book exams). If you don't have time: use the summary + questions at the end of the modules & the stop-and-check questions
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I would avoid her at all costs. She teaches the class like everyone in it is already a neuroscientist. She also lectures way too much for a TEAM-based course. She also told us after tests that we could stay after to discuss wrong answers to get points back. However, she would sit there and refuse to listen to our argument or give us points back.

My of my is Minna Ng an awesome professor. Never before have I had somebody teach me neuroscience so well and so elaborately. Have no idea who would write a negative review of such a well-established and respected academic is Dr. Ng. Could not imagine some student who themselves is so incompetent who would blame such incompetence unfairly on Dr. Ng

The funniest and most awesome professor I've ever had. Minna serves as an awesome mentor to anyone interested in neuroscience research too! She makes funny jokes in class and teaches the content very well. She is also very inspiring. So kind, so fun is Dr. Ng and her class. Sure, the class is not super easy, but that is because you are learning!

AVOID HER. I repeat, AVOID HER. Terrible lecturer, confusing class structure. Overall, a terrible experience. Any of these sassy positive reviews you see are absolutely written by her to try and save face. I have never had nor heard of a worse professor. If you are not going to heed this warning, you deserve to suffer the pain of her class.

Whoever is writing a negative review of Dr. Ng likely got a bad grade because they are individually incompetent. Professor Ng is incredibly caring and willing to help in any way, with understanding specific course content AND/OR personal matters...Top tier kinda professor all around. You're lucky if you get someone like her in your college career.

I loved this class! (online summer) Good pace, clear objectives, interesting text. Dr. Ng is incredibly kind, funny, and understanding. She genuinely cares about students. Lectures can be a little stale at times, but extra material is interesting. Groupwork helped enhance understanding. Tests/quizzes require some critical thought, but are doable.

Easy grader w/ chill assignments, but you won't get much out of the class other than the effort you put in to memorizing info from the textbook. Poor/disorganized lecturer, but a very caring person who wants to see students' grow. Great resource in general.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Excellent professor; took this course last year. Thought-provoking discussions, stellar guest speakers, and extremely manageable workload which also facilitated us to get to know each other better in class

Dr. Ng is by far my favorite professor I have had a Duke. I was amazed looking at other reviews, because of how phenomenal she is. She is very upfront with her grading and wants every one of her students to succeed. Her lectures are hilarious and thought provoking and easy to stay engaged. Could not recommend her any more!

This class was all over the place. Tests are all multiple-choice and very specific, and there are a lot of heavily-weighted group projects, so it feels like your grade is not in your own control. Lectures did not feel very organized. I would recommend against this professor.

This is the absolute worst professor I have had at Duke. If you are planning to take a class by this professor, DROP it asap. Her lectures are copied and pasted information directly out of the textbook. She simply reads her slides with no explanation. AVOID HER.

This class was probably the worst I have taken at Duke so far. She skipped over everything important during the lecture. Most of your grade is dependent on team projects where the grading is too harsh. All of the group activities are busywork and you learn nothing. The Final was the only test in person but was way to difficult. AVOID AT ALL COSTS.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This class was actually horrendous. The material is not hard but she makes it hard to get an A because the grading is completely arbitrary and the tests are SO specific (often about things not even discussed in lecture/the textbook). Also very unreasonable and frequently teaches material incorrectly/contradicts the textbook. Avoid her.

The grading was a bit harsh for projects that constituted a large part of our grade. We spent more time learning about research methods than actual neuroscience; then, we were given an in-person final exam that was tougher than the other tests we had throughout the semester. I was excited about this class, but in the end, was disappointed.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Decided to drop Neuroscience major after taking her Neurosci 101. Grading rubric is unclear, doesn't care about student's questions or opinions, will not accept regrade request. Does not care about student's improvement and learning in class.

The class is horribly taught: no structure, random tangents of info that seem unimportant but are on tests, and exams that make no sense and are way too specific. Tests are often blatantly wrong and are contradicted by or ignore textbook material, which is ironically the only real substance you get. The final was atrociously specific and misleading
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This course design is extremely insane! Everyone agrees that the team based component is a waste of time. You just stayed with your groups and answer some questions, which could in no way help you digest the materials. Minna Ng is never helpful. Don't let her teach this course any more! Otherwise, no one would major in Neuroscience at Duke.

This class is not very difficult in terms of content, but I did not appreciate having to rely on my team so much because their mistakes have impacted my grade on every major assignment. I wish the class was more individual-based. Dr. Ngs lectures are engaging and she helped me get involved with NMU, a great resource for me personally.

This was my first class as a prospective neuroscience major and I'm deeply disappointed. Dr. Ng is condescending and her tests are arbitrary, requiring regrades because there are so many appeals (which she is defensive about). The course is groupwork-heavy with unnecessarily harsh grading. Take this gateway course with another professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I came to Duke excited about Neuroscience; however, I have left this course with no interest in neuroscience or psychology. Minna Ng herself does not know what is going on in the course. The class relied on TAs who are tough graders, and exams which tested materials that were not taught. Avoid this class at all costs.

Minna is a robot in human form - no one goes to her lectures anymore, the only valuable lectures are given by the TA's. The TEAM format is a waste of my tuition. (don't quit neuro because of her tho!)

I'm a freshman and Dr. Ng is the reason I will no longer be majoring in neuroscience. Her tests constantly have mistakes, and she grades assignments WAY too harshly. She wastes an unimaginable amount of time during lectures, is not engaging, and excludes important info from lectures. Extremely team-based class, lots of busy work, waste of time.

I'm a freshman and came into Duke really excited about neuroscience. But, Minna Ng is the WORST professor. Her lectures are so disorganized. She skips through slides because she rambles on about unimportant material and then tests us on those skipped slides ? The most interesting lectures were given by the TA's
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Unnecessarily passive aggressive, unfairly called people out when she thought they weren't paying attention, as if this weren't college and we weren't in a pandemic where its hard to hear with masks. Discussion sections were a waste of time. Tons of busywork, assignments were uninteresting and learned nothing. Grading was nitpicky and harsh.
Course was super low intensity but I also didn't really learn anything. Would take this class again but would also be wary of taking classes with content that is difficult or important to you.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: Dr. Ng typically teaches the team-based Psy106, but they added that component to the "normal" Murphy 106 for this fall. I felt these assignments were too frequent, felt like busy work (scripted/fill in the blank to discuss research articles felt very condescending as juniors/sophs), and coordinating with teammates was unreasonabl hard in a pandemic

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. Do yourself a favor and do not take it. It's a flipped classroom so you would expect that you would do well if you just stay on track for the reading. HOWEVER, it doesn't matter how much you study the material in the textbook because the quiz questions and exam questions are ridiculously specific and don't make sense.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: a rude professor that doesn't care about her students, all you learn comes from the textbook, and she approaches students being very condescending and not helpful at all. do NOT take

Probably one of the worst professors I've had in Duke. It is an intro course to Neuroscience but wants you to cram information into your head. If all neuroscience courses were like this, I would probably lose all my interest in the topic.

HORRIBLE. I did well ONLY based on my own merits b/c she did not teach ONE THING. Its a flipped class, but she never goes over material learned. She just talks about articles she likes instead of answering questions on her quizzes, which are riddled with mistakes. Is unapproachable and passive aggressive . Can do well, but it's a lot of time.

Worst professor you will have at Duke. She doesnt teach a thing, writes quizzes and exams that she always has to revise after b/c students catch mistakes, and thinks shes the reason youre learning. Got mad at me for asking questions ABOUT HER QUIZZES b/c it wastes class time. Not a hard class, but the professor is awful.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Heavy reading and does not teach. must have a tutor or prior knowledge to learn any information.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: This class is flipped and team-based so you are in charge of teaching yourself as much as you want to know. Quizzes every class and only after the chapter quiz does she do a "mini lecture" on the topics. I literally learned everything from reading the textbook but since I enjoy neuro I didn't mind that. Not too hard if you're dedicated and try!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: While Neuro102 had amazing content, team-based learning made me regret taking the class. Teams of 4-5 complete online quizzes in class for a majority of the period (every class) and lectures are (somewhat) related to content but not directly tested. Reading heavy, basically a flipped class. Dr. Ng can be confrontational abt (common) faulty exam q's
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Minna is amazing! She is the reason I became a neuroscience major. Her neuro 102 class made me feel intelligent because I was actually learning. The class is designed for you to succeed if you put in the effort. Minna is always available and willing to listen about everything. Her lectures are way more interesting than the standard powerpoint

DO THE READINGS. Take notes on the readings. Space out during lecture portions if you must. Keep up in the textbook and get along with your team, and you should do fine on quizzes, exams, and team activities. That being said, I took the class a year ago, and I heard that Ng has made it more difficult since.

I found the exams very challenging and initially struggled on the weekly quizzes. But she is very willing to help and after talking with her my quiz performance really improved. The flipped style and team activities allowed for more in-depth, engaging classes which were enhanced by her humor and savagery! Prof Ng sparked my interest in neuro.

The class solely relies on reading textbooks. Her lectures are super boring and make people log on Facebook. Tests are fulled of strange trick questions that make no sense according to the readings. And she defends her answers that is apparently wrong even if related articles are given. just take neuro 101

Prof. Ng is such an amazing professor and person! She's sarcastic and funny, which makes lectures much more interesting. The team-based learning style of the class also really helped me grasp the material better than a normal lecture would have. I highly recommend Prof. Ng and this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Ng is great! Very knowledgable, and super willing to help outside of what is expected of her. The team based learning worked well for me, and I have made every effort to take a class with her again!
She is horrible. Don't take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Did NOT enjoy this class. Literally all the content comes from the textbook so class is completely useless, except for the tiniest, most random details that she put on the midterm. The in-class activities contribute nothing and class ended with a final and a 5-8 page paper (for a class with NO previous writing assignments) due on the same day.

Prof. Ng is the worst professor I have ever encountered. Her quizzes always have mistakes and were unnecessarily difficult. Midterm was impossible. She becomes defensive over her questions even when she is CLEARLY incorrect. Lectures do not help for her tests. Attendance is mandatory and if you do not show up, you get a 0 for the day, NO EXCUSES!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Honestly a really terrible professor. Lectures are boring and restate everything from the reading, the quizzes have mistakes in them almost every week she is unaccommodating of students, and her tests are way harder than expected. Can be quite aloof, super strict. Avoid as much as possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Brilliant professor with a clear passion for neuroscience. Zero problems with Ng, but there are downsides to the class itself: mandatory attendance, lots of quizzes, and it's easy to space during lectures. However, if you read the textbook carefully and take meticulous notes, you should do fine on quizzes and exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Prof. Ng was personable but could turn aloof and defensive when questioned. The questions on the weekly quizzes (which were allegedly crafted for hours) had frequent mistakes, and nary a week went by without questions being tossed out due to ambiguity. The team-based format can be frustrating if only some team members come to class fully prepared.

If you were an unpersonable nerd in high school who went home and memorized random brain regions, you will have an advantage in this course. Purely memorization with absolutely no critical thinking required. By memorization I mean specific sentences in the text. Everyone can memorize so everyone could pass, it's all a matter of your social life.

How can an introductory course be team-based? Nobody is an expert on the material, and if students are supposed to teach each other, you can bet they are not doing a good (or correct) job. You will memorize the textbook and then pretend to pass off as an expert on the material as you engage in mindless debates that are most likely factually wrong.

Okay, so the teacher doesn't teach. And team-based is supposed to mean that you are split into a group of five other students and help each other learn. This sounds like a recipe for disaster, with people telling other people wrong information or misconceptions that they have concerning the material. You won't learn. You will memorize the textbook.

Do not take Neuroscience 102! Take 101. The "team-based" learning is an absolute farce and just an excuse for the teacher, who doesn't know the material, to not teach. Instead, the students are supposed to teach each other, even though everyone is in the same boat. Doesn't make sense, now does it? Essentially, you will have to memorize the textbook

The teacher is incredibly rude and not accessible. She will actively call people out in front of the entire class and she says a lot of uncomfortable things. Also, the quizzes she administers are filled with errors and she really doesn't know that much about neuroscience.
Do not take Neuroscience 102!

Dr. Ng is a super cool person but also a savage. The class was team-based so she didn't do much teaching. She will walk around class to make students put their phones away and attendance is mandatory. She wouldn't let students go to the bathroom or leave early. Weekly quizzes sucked. I learned a lot, but mostly from the textbook and not from her.

I learned nothing in class would've been better off only reading the book. Mini-lectures are pointless and activities childish. Prof Ng herself is uncompromising and makes an absurd amount of mistakes in quizzes and tests, which seem like they're written by a toddler. Honestly just a bad class -- easy to get an ok grade, impossible to excel.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: She was very sweet and cares about her students. But she is VERY strict so make sure you get your stuff together for this course. If you're not on top of your work from the beginning, you'll struggle so get ready to put in a lot of effort. Quizzes were a bit hard and midterm was ridiculous. Team activities and mini lectures were boring and childish
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Class was moderately interesting, but I didn't find Professor Ng to be a very kind professor. She ran an extremely strict class, so much so that the environment was uncomfortable. Quiz questions sometimes from sections we weren't assigned to read and were unnecessarily complex. Team format was nice, but overshadowed by other frustrations,
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Class if flipped and team-based, so definitely not for everyone. Quizzes are fairly straightforward, read the book and you should be fine. Midterms are hard, read all require chapters for it. Prof. Ng is funny and knowledgable, class is design so if you put in the work you'll get an A- . Overall, would typically recommend.

The quizzes are unnecessarily complicated; even if you do the reading, it is still hard to do well. Lectures are confusing and boring. She is VERY strict, so much so that it is just not a comfortable learning environment. Would not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Ng is a total sweetheart. She'll really try to get to know you and help you. I didn't do so great on one of the weekly quizzes and she reached out to me to make sure everything was okay. The class is team-based and flipped, so it's not for everyone. She'll drop your two lowest quiz grades, which is really helpful.

Boring lectures that repeat all of the content you have to learn yourself. Silly application activities that remind me of 5th grade. Professor Ng very uncompromising and not understanding with any issues eg. MidTerm scheduling.   Would have learnt more just reading the textbook...
I loved this class! I learned so much! Flipped class,  so there's  a lot of reading, and there are quizzes based on the reading, so definitely do it!

DO NOT SHOW UP LATE. she has absolutely no tolerance for disrespect, lateness, cellphone use, etc. be prepared to get out called out publicly and points docked from your grade. however, she doesn't do it rudely. she'll scare you but teach you the course material better than you could've hoped. however, she's still helpful and kind with questions.

Professor Ng was AMAZING, and everyone interested in neuroscience should take a class with her!  The class was team-based, and while the material was difficult, she was a fair grader so doing well in her class wasn't.  Her teaching approach was really helpful- she's so funny, knowledgeable, and interesting, and she made class really enjoyable.
Big arms, big brain, straight forward lectures and tests. The curve wasn't too  bad - I don't know what is up with the reviewers below.
Held multivar calc with him when I was a freshman - Goncalo was so bad I had to attend class of another professor just to understand the material. I am sure he is a nice guy though.
In my first year at Duke, my seniors told me the Duke Math department will be a disappointment. I did not believe them... until I met Goncalo. Now I am a physics major, and am so much better off...

Lectures are clear and tests are relatively straightforward. Based on the reviews, other students seem to disagree, but oliveira was one of the better math professors I've had. His grading system is purposefully vague though, with students knowing little about what grade they are going to receive until the end.

A very unreasonable grader who did not consider the fact that many who take his class are self-selected math majors. I got a 89% on the final and I got a B+. I know many other students who felt the curve was unforgiving. DO NOT TAKE this class unless you are prepared to subject yourself to arbitrary standards.
Unclear in teaching  simple concepts. Didn't know one can add So much confusion rewriting textbook on the board

Prof. Von Ramm has lots of interesting stories from his years of experience. He is a good lecturer when he decides to stay on topic, but he easily goes off on tangents. The three in-class tests are fairly straightforward, but the final was decently hard (and unfortunately weighed heavily).  Labs meet every week and expect to stay at least 2 hours

Dr. Von Ramm made students VERY passionate about the class, and forced them all to work very hard. Unfortunately, he curved the class to a C/C+ and my hard work was rewarded with a B-. Very disheartening, but I figure this knowledge will serve me well in later classes. Cooper Moore was a phenomenal TA, the best I've ever had.

von Ramm is late a lot, gets off topic a lot, but this was a very enjoyable course. Cooper Moore was a fantastic TA which certainly helped but von Ramm certainly knows what he's lecturing on. 3x10% for exams, 40% final exam, so a difficult course but the material is all fundamentals of ece. von Ramm is hilarious when he rambles.
His idea of techi is to make student think, not to copy and past. he is great professor specially if you work with him in lab.

Don't do it. Just don't. I don't know why "Rater Interest" boosts HIS score so I just put it low. I actually like the subject and enjoy the learning, but he's a terrible teacher whose tests are nothing like the HW. Drop it while you have a chance. There are much better instructors for this course.

He's obviously a very intelligent guy but I really don't recommend taking his class. Doesn't stick to the textbook, lectures are only barely relevant to the HW, comes to class 15 minutes late, and makes this intro-circuits class much harder than necessary.

Dr Von Ramm is a great professor who focuses extremely on the ability to think. He also believes in understanding the fundamentals. An excellent man to take a core class from. His course is also more intensive than others who teach it.

Von Ramm is not the nightmare everyone makes him out to be. He really covers most of the material well, and he gives very little homework. The tests can be challenging, but as long as you have a decent understanding of the material, you can get a decent score. 50% is a passing grade in his class and 80% is an A, so he understands it can be hard.
Decent professor... likes to scare students, but other than that, his lectures are clear and his tests are straightforward. Hwk is also easy and similar to test questions. Good intro class.

by the way... he didn't invent ultrasound..its been around for over 50 years so he would have invented it when he was like 3. he contributed towards the development of 3d ultrasound...with many others
No Comments

Professor Von Ramm is one of the best professors I've had. Famous for setting killer questions on midterms and finals, he teaches with great clarity and insight, both drawn from his vast experience. Taking his class however requires great initiative to clarify and learn concepts. Not for the faint of heart but strongly reccommended nontheless.
Interesting class, have to learn some of the material on your own... not too difficult.

I took this class in spite of all the horrible comments on here and found that he was as bad as advertised.  He is utterly useless as a teacher, cannot explain even the most basic principles, and his tests are ridiculous.  Take it with another prof or don't take it at all.
dont do it

Worst professor ever! He comes off nice and congenial, but he doesn't know how to teach at all.  His tests are like the twilight zone.  I've never worked so hard in a class, but it didn't show at all.  He's the infamous DO NOT TAKE professor!

It's too bad that he isn't the professor that he was 22 years ago, then. He's horrible from Alpha to Omega. Makes waaaaay too many mistakes, yet comes crushing down on students for tiny mistakes. Could use a good kick in the rear from the administration.
I had Dr. von Ramm 22 years ago.  He was my favorite professor. Yes, he flunks a lot of people.  But his passion is infectuous.  I worked my butt of and got a B-, but I learned a LOT.

Whatever you do, please avoid a class with this man. He is rude to his students and has been known to fail an unusually high number of students.  His tests are way different than the material he lectures.

This guy doesn't really teach all that much. He kind of talks about a topic and then randomly goes off on tangents and asks how to make tests easier. Then he goes back to talking about math but never actually says what he is talking about and never gives any context to the lecture.

I had him for Cal III, and he's decent. He always shows up to class late, is a really tough grader for tests, and lectures straight from the book. On the bright side, lecture notes are posted on Canvas before classes, and tests are really easy as they cover the fundaments of the topics.

Took him for ODE. Always showed up to lecture late. Lecture is basically him reading the text book. Didn't prepare us for the homework or exams. Very ineffective teaching method and the guy had the gall to wondered at the end of the semester why the class average was so low. Avoid him if you can.

Professor Orizaga is a down to earth man. He wants his students to succeed and is willing to put time in to help everyone. He enjoys class participation and genuine conversation. I highly recommend taking a math class with Professor Orizaga, and I would recommend trying to get to know him because he is hilarious.

Dr. Orizaga was so kind and helpful, and explained difficult concepts in a very intuitive way. Class was taken in a non-traditional context in a 6-week accelerated program but he even managed to make 3 hour lectures tolerable. Really sharp wit as well, you have to listen carefully to catch some subtle jokes.

Dr. Orizaga knows what he is teaching and makes every effort so that every student in the class understands what he is teaching. Very approachable after the class hours to talk about the concepts, and get the doubts clarified. Weekly assignments are tailored so that a good grasp on the related concept is achieved.
He is a funny and knowledgeable professor who cares a lot about his students and just wants his students to learn. He makes Duke Math enjoyable and not stressful, highly recommend.
The tests are incredibly challenging but this man is a god. You can tell he cares about his students. It felt as though us students were trying to beat Duke math with him. Saulo is an inspiration.

Professor Ordog is an amazing professor. The course itself is challenging, but she provides a notes packet for every lecture that clearly outlines what will be covered that day in class, and she is also very accessible outside of class. She is always willing to meet with students, and usually stays before and after class to answer questions.

Ms. Ordog was a wonderful math instructor. For every class, she made a notes template (which was very easy to follow) that had all of the information we needed to know. This made missing class easier, although I would not recommend it! Erika is accessible out of class (via email) and is willing to help her students with whatever they need.

One of the better options. Always showed up early to class in order to take questions on the homework. Availible outside of class for questions as well. She wants to see you succeed; for one of the group projects some groups cheated which could have garnered a student conduct board. Instead, she just asked them to confess up.

One of my favorite professors at Duke! If you're just taking an art credit for fun, his classes are a great way to learn the basics of filmmaking while contributing to timely, professional projects. If you show deeper interest, he will open doors for you and do anything he can to support your development as a filmmaker. A great teacher and mentor!

Prof Orentein has made some hard-hitting political advocacy documentaries and makes sure to do them in a well-researched, thorough way. Its admirable that he takes his work very seriously and is passionate about the subject. If you would like an entry into purposeful video-making and have initiative to take full advantage of the class, enroll!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Terrible professor.  His classes are extremely boring and monotonous when the material is extremely interesting. Not only is it boring, it is unproductive and a waste of time. We could have achieve so much, but instead we just talked nonsense in circles to increase our participation grade.. I would advise you not to take his class.

The syllabus changed this semester and every student was responsible for their own project which included a full interview, oral transcript, and 10 minute video. Classes were useless and filled with awkward silences. Grading was completely arbitrary. If you don't have extremely liberal tendencies, don't take this class.

Great professor, great course! It is difficult to organize a large group of students to work on the same project[s] and this can occasionally be frustrating, but Professor Orenstein had everyone's interests in mind and really allows you to grow as a storyteller and experience valuable service.

I did not know this, but this particular class is a gateway into a Bass Connections program. CHECK THIS OUT BEFOREHAND. This was a waste of my time, both because I didn't want to continue with this and because he isn't a good professor. He wanted everyone to discuss, but couldn't direct anyone to get it started or continue it.

Avoid courses with Prof. V. unless you already know the subject. Lectures consisted of limited examples & quizzes were given prior to reviewing tough concepts. He pushes students so they may learn more, which is great if the prof. is tactful. BUT Prof. V knows not the balance between challenging and destroying, & just might crush you and your GPA.

He was awful at explaining anything on the homework, in class or on quizzes. Lectures consisted of convoluted explanations and stories and were painfully dull. Google was clearer and far more helpful. Also did not make grading expectations clear or known at all. Not recommended for any class, unless you like learning everything yourself.

Prof Teal is so nice and very helpful. Some of his class is just basic American history review, but if you work hard and participate in discussion section, you will get a good grade. Plus he has awesome Abraham Lincoln socks!
Very helpful and fair grader. Engaging class.
Very dedicated teacher and a fair grader. He will grade you on how you really express your thought on the paper. I have learned a lot from the class.

Extremely nice professor. He is also incredibly knowledgable, so lectures may seem to go on forever, but he tries to keep things interesting with different formats. Very fair grader, just make sure to do the readings and the work.
She really cares. But the class is sometimes very boring. Easy A.

She seemed to really care about the subject and the students. The problem was it felt like she was overwhelmed with work. Maybe she should have only taught 1 section instead of 2. It took her months to give us grades for work, and I had 1 grade in the grade book by December. However, she did try and make herself available to meet outside class.
Boring but easy. Ossi-Lupo is nice and usually available outside of class.

She is a great person and I can tell she is very passionate about her field. Took writing 101- primate play and growing up. It was a very science based writing class, but nothing too hard, and she is a pretty chill grader.

Took this during Fall 2020 where WRITING101 was S/U so grades really weren't considered. The class was very interesting though and she's a great lecturer. The assignments weren't hard and she frequently has time to meet outside of class and go over your stuff. She understood the issue with COVID semesters so definitely made it a bit easier on us.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Managed to get a spot in this class during registration as this is a relatively new course and students aren't aware of just how great it is yet. The topic itself is interesting and easy to write about (evolution of cooperation), and assignments are graded reasonably. The course includes a trip to the Lemur Center as well, which was fun!

For this class, he has a set of assignments students can choose to complete and depending on the number of assignments done and the quality of work presented, he will negotiate a grade with the student. Prof. is very approachable and his classes are incredibly fun to take, as his insights often offer a comedic delivery. Would recommend!

This is my second class with Professor Ben, and my second time being very happy with his teaching. He grades his religion class by incorporating your feedback on your own performance. He checks in with each student multiple times in the course to hear how they think they're progressing. Super caring guy, and I learned a ton about religion.
Professor Van Overmeire is very helpful, and wants everyone to succeed in class. He is always willing to support students and gives good feedback to help students improve.

Ben makes a genuine effort to know every student and open up as much time as possible for office hours. His grading is fair and his explanations of our readings are really good. I really enjoyed talking to him and am interested in taking more of his classes in the future.

GCHINA 101 with Prof. Van Overmeire was one of the best classes I had. He really makes time to get to know his students (i.e. he made extra online office hours in case students could not regular ones). No problem communicating with him in terms of having him read your paper or improving your participation in classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I was very lucky to get him as a seminar Professor. He's great! Very helpful. Somewhat a tough grader, but I actually think it's great - helps to push the bar. I genuinely enjoy his classes!

Overmeire is really helpful by providing very specific feedback without coming across as rude or condescending. He's very honest about his expectations and follows through. His primary focus on religion means that he has a fresh take on several topics and will happily share. He's very supportive of students and will show up to extracurriculars.
Good professor! Very nice and careful!

Nothing new but figured I'd add another - he is also one of the best professors I've had. Breaks down concepts simply, is very approachable, cares about his students. I'm really interested in game theory anyway though so that might have to do with it.

Awesome.  One of the best professors I've ever had.  He explains concepts really well and goes slow enough for everyone to understand.  He is also funny and can make boring material really interesting.  His tests are fair and straightforward but make sure you budget your time!

He's a really good teacher. Knows the material really well and goes at a slow pace (sometimes too slow but when material gets hard you'll be grateful). Really nice guy, funny and always willing to help. For the midterms: they're fair but go fast or you won't finish.

Beware of cold calling. You must be engaged in lecture the entire time, comments can be somewhat condescending if you do not know the answer. This being said, I do think that I learned the material very well because of it. Discussion is just TA office hours. Exams are unnecessarily confusing and do not reflect the problem sets.
Unclear grading expectations. Terrible lectures with rushed, scribbled, barely explained graphs. If you already struggle with Econ, do not take this class because Pfaff will be no help

Professor Pfaff is HILARIOUS. I was dreading 303 bc I had 0 econ experience, but he made the class engaging and fun. It's lecture-heavy and he cold calls but in a way that keeps the class going, and if you get it wrong, he never makes you feel bad. His midterms can be a bit confusing, but there is a strong curve. Pfaff is the best there is

Cold calls, but attendance isn't mandatory and he won't embarrass you if you don't know the answers. I thought the class was incredibly boring, lecture style is writing graphs on the board - very little policy application. Problem sets and tests are graded harshly, and the tests are really hard to finish on time. Give no study material.

Pfaff is an amazing and passionate lecturer. However, the lectures, problem sets, and unintelligible textbook do not adequately prepare you for the 2 midterms or final. If you like the feeling of watching every lecture twice and still being baffled by test questions, this class is for you. Class is structured like a 1970s Ivy League stereotype.

Professor Pfaff is a great educator. He is very clear and made microeconomics very interesting.  I had never taken an econ class before and I really enjoyed it.  He memorized everyone's name in the 50+ person class which I appreciated and was impressed by.  He will cold call, though isn't mean or rude when you don't know an answer.

Lessons were dull and difficult to follow for students who weren't mathematically-minded. Placed a lot of emphasis upon theory and calculations, while some of the other classes involved current events and topical applications more. If you struggle with the mathematical side of economics, I'd suggest you sign up with a different lecturer

Great teacher. Doesn't care if you come to class but if you do, prepare to be cold called! He's a very fair grader and you will want to do well in this class because he is so great. HIGHLY RECOMMEND ANY CLASS WITH HIM
GOAT. Dr. Partner is kind, warm, and engaging. He assigns super interesting readings and wants everyone to discuss. Take this class if you're a history major needing Asia geographical requirement!

Professor Partner is incredibly knowledgeable and his course was super interesting. Very reading heavy, but if you're interested in the topic then it is definitely manageable. Lectures are generally super interesting and engaging. Assignments outside of reading are minimal and manageable.

Simon runs the perfect history class. The first half of the semester is focused on thoroughly learning the history, and then the second half is case studies about more specific topics that interest the class. Simon is very good at engaging everyone in the class in interesting and in-depth discussions. A lot of reading, but it is very rewarding.

This class got harder by a good margin, but I still liked him as a teacher. I can't say the same for all of my classmates, who felt like some of the material was too esoteric. Do not take this course if you're just looking for an easy History course. You're better off in a different class. Take this course if you have a lot of interest in Japan.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: really nice guy. super chill. awesome class. very fair and engaging.

LOVE PARTNER. Funny guy with great lectures. You come out LEARNING so much from his classes. Tests are really straightforward and he gives you many of the questions/answers beforehand. Short and digestible readings, easy paper. A history class for non-history majors tbh. History majors will enjoy it too.

He makes it as easy as possible for you to get an A, just do the reading & learn your IDs. Tests were based on readings so lectures aren't absolutely necessary to attend (though it will hurt your participation and he does give pop quizzes), but he gives you test answers in the lecture. Also, his British sense of humor is great!

Very entertaining lectures (includes photos from Professor Partner's own visits to shrines and other historical landmarks). Loved to hear his stories of these visits.   Grade basically comes from five or so pop quizzes (based on readings), three midterms (memorizing dates/events/etc. not bad at all), and a 5-7 final paper.   Would recommend.
Great guy.  His class is basically a bunch of lectures with some tests that are really easy.  He is an interesting lecturer and an extremely forgiving grader

Prof. Partner is a nice guy, but, if you are a history major, this is probably not the class for you. His class structure, assignments, etc. are geared toward the general public to the point that, as a history major, I feel like I got little if anything out of this class. If history isn't your passion, though, his style might suit you better.

Professor Partner is a great teacher. He is super interested in Japan and really knows his stuff. He also takes time out of his evenings to have dinner with students. Papers and exams are easy enough if you put the effor in to study for them.

Class was extremely flexible in terms of assignments and catered to be enjoyable for people of all levels of interest. Simon definitely does his best to make the class meaningful for everyone, and focuses not only on history but culture, art, architecture etc. Reading was reasonable and meaningful, and discussion was encouraged, not forced.

Very knowledgeable, easy grader. Readings are either informative or enjoyable. Focus not just on historical events but also on culture and art. Participation required, but as long as you keep up with the readings for class, you'll do just fine.

How often does one get to read Hayden White, compare and contrast versions of histories representative of various countries and eras, do archival research and turn it in as a final creative writing project?! This class rocked!!
Simon is a good teacher...not too hard a class but still very interesting.  Afterward you'll feel like you learned something as opposed to other "easy" classes.

His class was, for a non history major, a very interesting and informative course to take. Considering history is not my specialty, the ease of the class catered to a non-humanities mind while still blowing my expectations out of the water with the knowledge I gained. Simon is truly a wonderful professor and makes his class(es) one of the best
Simon's a really nice guy--participate in class and do the readings and you'll do fine on everything.  Still a good class even if you're not a History or Japanese buff
Great professor. Very interesting class. Highly reccommend.

There was reading for every class, but never an overwhelming amount. The 3 papers were simply summaries of the 100-page readings on the topic. Professor is very nice and approachable. He sometimes talks about something off-topic and then ends up running out of time. Overall I enjoyed the class and hearing bits and pieces about Japanese culture.

Very laid back and engaging, best with smaller classes (20-some people) such as History 143A. History 143B is still good, but slightly less because of the difficulties of combining history with economics and management. Always ready to help if you just ask and communicate with him. He does his best to work with and help everyone.
Unorganized,  Very knowledgeable, but dont know what you'll get day to day and you won't know whats important.

Nice guy. Not too hard a grader. However, he would definitely benefit from a time management course. The last two weeks of the semester were hellish--we had two papers due (5-7) within a week's length as well as a final exam. Participation counts for a significant portion of your grade (30%). I though the class would be enjoyable, but it was a pain

I took Pfau's class in spring 2020. The review dated March 2020 mentioned his having a huge religious bent on the content. The thing is, the class was literally called "Poetry in a Secular World"--the course was about the theme of religion in poetry across time. Pfau is one of my favorite profs--he's super willing to build a personal relationship.

Mixed feelings about Professor Pfau. The material was interesting and he is clearly quite smart. However, he lectures way too much for a seminar. There is limited discussion at best and it really made the class boring. He is part of the divinity school and had a huge religious bent on the texts. He made fun of skeptics and cynics in class a lot.

Pfau was funny, smart, and caring, but the course content was unbearably boring, and his lectures were dry and long. Despite it being a seminar, nobody talked much besides him. He's a fine prof, but don't expect him to magically make you engaged in a boring class.

Although this was a class designed for freshmen, Pfau blew me away. 89S (The Enlightenment) involved a lot of complex readings, but Pfau could answer an infinite number of questions regarding them or any other topic. Come to class with a question or input. His responses astound  he's always the smartest guy in the room. Easy grader for us though
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Inspirational

reviews.comment: I think that he's very smart and has knowledge almost about everything. He's really funny and nice.
