I always enjoy it when he talks and explains things and I love love love when he talks about his wife. I actually want to meet her. I would definitely take his class again if I could. In fact I'm searching for other classes he may be teaching.

Professor Pfau is unbelievably intelligent and articulate. He uncovers layers of depth and meaning in the material and in life that are inscrutable to the untrained mind. The experience of studying with him is transformative & should be requisite before graduating. Also, in resp. to below, this class covered exactly what the syllabus said it would.

Pfau is brilliant and witty, but also dry and monotonous. Combine that with the fact that his class's subject was very misleading (we studied theological foundations of higher education instead of the advertised "University and Why It Matters") and I regret taking his class. He's a nice person and wants you to do well, but I barely paid attention

I don't even know where to begin with Professor Pfau. He is one of the most understated geniuses I've ever met. You know when you meet someone for the first time and they just exude knowledge? That's the sensation you get when Professor Pfau walks into the room on the first day of class. He is 100% willing to meet with you outside of classjust ask

Dr. Pfau has to be one of the best minds and profs at Duke.  In class, his comments are thought-provoking, witty, and intellectually stimulating.  One can almost feel his/her worldview being sculpted as the analyses the works at hand with a comprehensive interdisciplinary approach. He is a true scholar, not to mention a fair, punctual grader.

Thomas Pfau is an outstanding professor.  The course he taught was fascinating and eye opening and left me thinking way after the course concluded.  He has an almost encyclopedic knowledge of his subject which he is more than willing to share.  I would highly recommend him to anyone seriously interested in learning.

Prof Pfau has a superb command over the English language, and an incredible knowledge in, it seems, almost every literary field. He is able to convey ideas in a most accurate, engaging and ingenious way. Overall, he is insightful, witty and humorous. Personally I wish the topics in the class more focused and the direction of the discussion clearer.

Overall, Professor Pfau did an excellent job keeping the class engaged in conversation pertaining to issues today and through the reading of several texts.  I hoped there would be more assignments, but there were only two major papers.  There could have been better clarification about the expectation of papers, but overall a good class.

Prof Pfau is a fascinating and witty speaker.  He seems to have near perfect recall of a wide range of literature, philosphy and history.  He weaves these disciplines together for a compelling class discussion.  One must be willing to jump into the conversation rather than wait for the open ended question to signal class participation.

Professor Pfau is arguably the most intelligent and passionate professor on campus. He teaches by lecture using sharp. clear language and comical witticisms, but is also very encouraging of students asking questions as to better understand the material. He always outlines what he expects of his class. His life advice, though, is the best of all.

Despite being a FOCUS seminar, course time was primarily filled with Professor Pfau's lectures.  Almost zero discussion.  Course was otherwise not difficult-- grades based primarily off papers, which the TA grades the majority of.

I really liked Pfau in my Readings in Genre class on Lyric Poets. His classes are very discussion based, so that is great if you like to offer your interpretation of a work. The only grades came from several essays, which graded somewhat hard, but mostly pretty fair. Also, HIS GERMAN ACCENT IS AWESOME.

Great prof--absolutely brilliant.  Grading is hard, but fair, and an A is within the realm of possibility.  One of the best classes I've taken at Duke. Pfau cares about his students and genuinely wants you to succeed.

Brilliant professor. I ranked his easiness as 2, but that's only because his assignments require a lot of insight and critical thinking. It's not impossible to do well--An A is definitely attainable. Take a class with this guy and you'll see why he has such rave reviews. Rarely did I leave his class without being blown away
Great teacher. Smartest guy I've ever met in my life. He's not an easy grader and it's a ton of work, but honestly worth every moment of it.

Lots and lots of reading. His lectures are interesting for the most part but he can get into some really esoteric things that don't help you with assignments. Only take a class with him if you're already interested in the topic. Also, the TA for this course did all of the grading so expectations aren't entirely clear.

By far my favorite teacher this semester. Absoulutly brilliant, he can directly quote philosophers from the top of his head, page number and all. But his lectures are fascinating, I was intimidated at first, but Pfau if a funny, interesting, and hilarious teacher. Take every class you can with him.

Probably the best professor I've had at Duke. Pfau is a fascinating lecturer, with a seemingly endless stock of fascinating tidbits pertinent to the subject matter. In addition to providing (and fostering) insightful analysis of a given text, he brought the big picture of the rise of the novel to life. Take a class with Pfau if you possibly can.

This man is a genius. I was very intimidated by him at first, but now I realize that he is very kind and helpful. Although the TA does grade the papers, and she is tough. Otherwise just pay attention in class and there's no problems.
Brilliant Professor. Maybe the best I've had at Duke.

Very interesting class but can be very confusing. Workload is average, but the papers are hard. TA grades papers so suck up to him or get a bad grade. There were glimpses of a good class but otherwise just average. HE's really smart though and you get a lot out of his class discussions.
The best professor I've had at Duke.

Wow. What an amazing professor. While he takes a little getting used to, he is definitely one of the nicest, most intelligent professor at Duke, a rather rare combination. In addition, he is a brilliant teacher, and know so much without being a pompous know it all. Brilliant, brilliant, brilliant. Loved the class. Will stop gushing now.
He is so brilliant it is insane.  I loved his course.  I gave him a chili pepper because when he talks it's hot.  Being that intelligent is just sexy.
One of the great minds of the English department.  Humane teacher and intellectual.  Also, the funniest professor in the department.  He's well worth the price of admission.

Brilliant!  He is so well-versed in the subjects that he teaches, it's amazing.  He's not particularly exciting but his sheer brilliance more than compensates for his dry presentation.  He's one of those professors that truly changes how you think.

Dont get why the hate here but Prof. Sattler's lectures are quite engaging and humorous and effectively teaches textbook materials for 101. Exams are concept heavy with MCQ and short responses but are relatively easy.
Such a nice person, but such a bad professor.
He likes working with each student and wants to help each student be successful. If you put in the hours to work with him outside of class, you will succeed in his class.

He talks about everything except the course material. He goes in circles, and usually forgets what he covered in the last class. 

Only redeeming quality is that the class is super easy, and he believes any excuse you give him (so he always gives you more time for assignments).

I didn't know what my major would be when I took 101, but then I took so many econ classes with him. Sometimes he doesn't cover material from the textbook fully, but he adds a lot of life examples and financial news. He requires a lot of class participation and loves to ask questions. Homework and practice tests help you to prepare for exams.
Amazing professor, his lectures are very entertaining, he is trying to engage you in a topic outside of the textbook, he is very clear about what he will test on, helps you prepare for exams.
Prof. Peter is very flexible and kind. Even though he is a bit old now, he can definitely explain you things from scratch in quite good detail.

So if you're thinking of taking an Econ class to see if you like it or not definitely do not take his class. I haven't heard a single good thing about him, and my experience in his class has confirmed that... 
He is not fit for teaching. He always gets lost when he speaks, makes the content confusing, and is hard to reach. Don't take his class.
It's really sad. He should be retired by now. He is not in the best shape and has trouble stringing together a simple sentence. This makes class so boring and simple....

He talks nonsense all class and teaches barely anything.
Class is maybe too easy, that is unfair for anyone that is really studying...

I understand know why his class is completely empty. He doesn't know the material properly. Sometimes it seems it's the first time he has seen the slides...

His homework are a joke, and also the class.

Don't take with him!!! it was so boring and bad. He is always complaining about doing his job and never prepares the classes. The textbook was terrible, the homework was bad, and the test (was easy) but bad.

With all due respect, Professor Sattler should retire. You can see that he is losing his hearing, and because of that, he barely understands the questions from students. He is pretty repetitive and boring.

He doesn't know the names of any students and has problems explaining basic things.

He is extremely repetitive. It seems he always forgets what we covered last class. The class is not organized, and it is all over the place.

It's an easy class, he covered not that much new material compared to 101, so at least is an easy grade.

I don't understand what he is doing. He tries some activities that don't make sense. It hard to believe that with so much teaching experience he stills struggles to deliver a lecture.
I don't reccomend taking this class.
hard
Always talking about nonsense. But, it's quite easy to get an A ONLY IF you COMPLETELY IGNORE EVERYTHING he's talking about, and go to learn by yourself.
Graded almost only by tests
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Don't take this class (or any class) with him. He talks about everything except the material. Also, it seems he doesn't know the material too well, his explanations are always not good.

He is soooo boring. As other have mentioned he is never prepared for class so it's better to just read the book.
At least his class it's easy, so it should be an easy A.

As the previous guy mentioned, he almost never prepare for his lecture. Sometimes he got confused about what he's talking about and tried to learn it during class. But he tried to help with students' grade. However, it cannot save his poor lecture.

He was never prepared for his class. Probably has taken the slides from others and never look at them because he spent half of his time in the class trying to remember what's on each slides. Was easy on grading but that doesn't compensate his bad teaching

ECON 101 with Prof Sattler is good if you're accustomed to an American style of teaching. He uses a lot of examples in his lectures. Lectures reflect the readings, so if you're not able to make it and can only do the psets, that works most of the time. He's particular about the writeups, but if you follow the guide you can get a good grade.
Took this class for the core requirement of art history. It was an easy A as long as you put effort into the assignment every week.

Really great professor. Wants you to discover and develop your own style and appreciates creativity. First half of class is learning more traditional styles, then it transitions into independent projects.

Professor Lasch is excited to teach and give advice. While his lectures sometimes got boring, he lets you listen to music during class and 2 absences. Weekly assignments don't take more than 90 minutes. There are occasional critiques, but overall, if you show up and finish your drawings you will get an A. This class doubles as a destresser.
He is without a doubt the most boring, most repetitive, most mundane professor Ive ever had.

Took him in painting...  I absolutely hated this guy... years after I took this class I realized what a big fraud Lasch is, and how if he knew anything about actually teaching painting, he would have talked about something other than his bizarre tangents- never picked up a paintbrush himself the entire studio art class-- if that's an indication--
Absolutely no feedback, random grades! Lots of reading that is never discussed, and absolutely esoteric material. Pointless pointless class.
He is very open ended with his assignments, and if you can survive all his constant ramblings it is actually a good class!!! If you put the time into it you will learn a lot! Easy grader.
The class is not hard so do not worry about that, however it is not fun either. You simply have to live through it. If you put time into your assignments you will do great.

all he does it talk. and talk. and talk. so annoying how much he rambles. the class is really stupid honestly. i love art but this class sucks. unfortunately you gotta take it cuase its a prerequisite. i have felt that this class has not helped me at all with art. the only thing it has made me realize is how annoying he is

Painting. Pedro is really strict and I have seen him smile maybe once! He rambles when all I want to do is paint! I'm scared of him, he feels unforgiving. BUT: his high expectations make him a better professor.He wants you to stretch your mind; he is innovative. Technically-obsessed, he is legit, old-school art professor who's inonthe contemp scene

Was never particularly interested in gender/sexuality studies, but this class has been super helpful in learning about how many things relating to gender and sexuality are misconstrued in media by providing meaningful perspectives. Prof. Sigal is also a super great guy! Nice, caring, and engaging. He loves what he teaches, and you can tell.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Caring

reviews.comment: Very doable almost backburner class as long as you stay up to date with the readings and be attentive in class. Entire grade is based on 2 papers, group project, video project, and attendance/participation. Requires out of the box thinking and synthesis of material. Effort required but easy overall.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Caring and lenient

Chill professor, but the course is not interesting or informative. Every class basically repeats the same message. The course gives a broad overview of the materials but does not get deep into any topics. Two short reflections per week, two group projects, and two papers.
I like Sigal a lot but I didn't find the course to be as interesting as I anticipated. Weekly readings and online lectures are very manageable and the two papers are not too bad either. Fun projects!
Very good caring professor. Lots of discussions. Very openminded to dissenting opinions.

Great professor, great content, great experience! Dr. Sigal is clearly passionate about his teaching, and the lectures are interesting and engaging. There are usually some readings to do before class, but nothing too bad. I feel way more comfortable about myself after experiencing this safe and comforting environment he makes in class. 11/10 person
Very thought-provoking class that does not require an awful lot of engagement/participation. Assignments are varied and you can tailor them to your specific interests within the subject.
Pete is hilarious. Don't disrespect the pink mohawk-- he's a real genius under there. This is a class everyone should take before graduating from Duke.

Pete was the best professor I've had at Duke. Sexual Pleasure in the Modern World changed the way I look at the world and I think everyone should take this class for the experience. TRANSFORMATIVE!!!! Be creative, participate, ask questions, and keep up with lectures and forums. Watch the lectures, you can get away with just skimming the readings.

Dr. Sigal taught me last semester in the History of Modern Pleasure. I took this class because it looked easy enough and I had a pretty intense course load, but this class taught me so much. There are weekly assigned readings and some projects, but Dr. Sigal made it easy to ask questions and was one of my favorite teachers I have ever had.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: this class is the most interesting class i have taken at Duke content wise. Professor Sigal is a nice and caring guy; however, lectures can be boring and hard to follow. assignment expectations can sometimes be unclear. readings are interesting, but can be long and hard to follow also. overall, i would recommend taking this class for the experience
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Pete is awesome. This class is a lot of fun and extremely interesting. I think it is rare you would ever be able to discuss and study such explicit material in a classroom setting. This material, nonetheless, is so fascinating and very engaging. A must take class here at Duke!
His discussions are amazing and the papers were very reasonable.

This class was really interesting and great for people who may not be interested by most history classes. Show up to every class, do the readings, and submit your work on time, and you should succeed in this class while also enjoying it! Sigal is a great professor and guy - would definitely recommend this course!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Amazing professor! Highlight of my freshman year!
This was a great class with a great professor. Sigal makes history of colonial Latin America really interesting. Pay attention to lecture in order to do well on the papers and the final.

Prof Sigal is great. He's far from the stereotypically boring history prof. He really encourages you to be creative which is refreshing. I took his course on colonial Latin America and enjoyed it a lot. Whether you're taking a course in history to fulfill a general req or for your major I definitely recommend him.

I really enjoyed Sexuality in the Americas.  The readings are engaging and his lectures are focused and helpful to use on the assignments.  He really rewards creativity, which is a nice change from most mundane history classes.  He's also really interesting as a person, so I'd definitely recommend stopping by just to chat!

I really enjoyed Proffesor Sigal's class, Sexuality 120: Sexuality in the Americas.  However, it was not what I was expecting.  It was much more about the European sexual colonization of South American than current American view on sex.  He was a fair grader and the lectures were interesting.  He also gives a lot of leeway in papers and projects.
No Comments
Really good class discussion, interesting scenarios
Chill and easy
super kind guy. grading was generous and he gives good feedback for improving in the language. very chill class, highly recommend!! italian is the best foreign language department!!! no final exam!
I had the privilege of learning from this dude for two semesters and we all could not recommend him more. My favourite Italian professor.

Pietro was a great prof. He made every class funny and engaging. When we made a mistake, he corrected us in a way that didn't make us feel embarrassed. This class has a lot of homework after class, but that's necessary for learning a language. There is also some weekend group homework, so beware of that. The entire Italian department is great!!!!
I loved Pierpao! He was a great teacher, and I learned a lot!

Great guy, adorable personality, gives off cocker retriever energy if that makes sense (like golden retriever but less extroverted). Lectures are fun, he shares cultural anecdotes whenever he thinks of one while he explains grammar or phrases.

Professor Spagnolo is the best, kindest professor ever. He truly cares about students and explains Italian grammar so clearly. He's very accessible outside of class and wants you to succeed. There's a lot of homework, which is normal for learning a language. If you work hard, he'll appreciate it—and you'll get an A. I wish I could have him again!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Pierpaolo was a fantastic, supportive professor. He truly cares about his students and is always willing to help out with difficult concepts and grammar. Out of Italian 101, 102 and 203, 102 is known to be the most difficult because the course is packed with tricky grammar rules. If you can, take Italian 102 with Pierpaolo!

Great professor. Highly recommend taking Italian with Pierpaolo if you can. Very caring, understanding, and helpful. Genuinely wants you to succeed. Fun environment to learn Italian, and I promise you will improve with Pierpaolo as your professor. Just be ready to collaborate with other students on group projects/HWs.

Pierpaolo is great. There is a solid amount of homework and quizzes throughout the class, but they are generally pretty easy. If you put in the work, you will get an A. Also, Pierpaolo is very nice and accommodating.

Gerardo is incredible! I took Italian 101 with him this past semester and absolutely loved it. Class was always a ton of fun. Assignments and grading criteria were very clear.  The class structure was perfect for an introductory course. Gerardo was always accessible outside of class for meetings and office hours.

Great professor for an introuductory course. He makes sure you learn and are prepared for future classes without giving you much homework. The homework you do have is very consistent and easy to get into a routine of doing. I believe almost everyone got an A in his class, would recommend to anybody looking to start a new language.

I really liked having Gerardo for Italian 101. He's always really kind and passionate about teaching. His grading got harder as the semester went on. I think the class itself has a heavier workload, and I didn't love all of the extra assignments we had to do. I definitely learned a lot though.

I really like Gerardo as a professor. You can tell he loves to teach and is always excited when he walks in. At times, I do think the workload for homework is a little too much but it does help me learn.

Gerardo is one of the best professors at Duke. It is clear that he loves teaching and he comes to class excited every day. He has turned my day around many times. He is very good at explaining things and has an amazing personality. He is very patient and encouraging. I hope I have him for 102!

pimm is hilarious and his work through national geographic was so cool to learn about. although not tested on lecture content, the lectures were mandatory and for a good reason because they were unique, creative, and i learned so much. take this class!!!

Don't mention any "good" ideas around him, let alone work with him on a paper. He will turn around, try to get you kicked out through extortion, and then steal your ideas through publishing with a group of lackeys.

Great and respected professor. Has been canceled a bunch of times and brags about it-- which is kinda annoying. Apart from that, the class is very interesting and instead of exams he makes you film two short videos. Easy A if you keep up with the weekly assignments.

Professor Pimm is a great professor. While his lectures can be boring at times, this class is really easy if you put in the little work that there is. Would definitely recommend for a NS credit or if you wanna go into this field

Stuart's the bomb. Environ 210 D is just reading like 3 papers a week and writing really short summaries on each. There are two videos. Not a ton of work in this class, and Stuart's really interesting and tells really funny stories. a must take for environmental science majors
Absolutely amazing lecturer, loved by students, sense of wit

Pimm is a great guy.  He is this funny British man who is really REALLY an international expert in his field.  Our class was split grad/undergrad.  We had readings every week- most of which were pretty boring.  Lecture are also pretty boring.  It was an okay class for me, not too much work or anything but it was not exciting. Pimm is pretty good.
The workload was so intense, it felt like I had signed up for a full-time job instead of a class.
The professor's lectures were as engaging as watching paint dry, and twice as long.

Atrocious professor who doesn't lecture at all and just dumps reading after reading and presentation after presentation. All you need to know is over half the class left before the drop period. Do NOT take this class unless you enjoy torturing yourself with no reward.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Do NOT take this class. I don't know who is giving this professor good reviews, but she is a terrible lecturer with unclear guidelines and an enormous number of busy work that is graded unreasonably hard.

Homework is incredibly tedious: You have to write a single-spaced page on numerous long articles (some paywalled too) every single week, and feedback is unclear. Lecturing is essentially non-existent; instead, you have to basically teach yourself and the class through projects. Professor has a drill-sergeant vibe w/ no exceptions allowed.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: She is hilarious and lectures are very interesting. Attendance is mandatory and you can get points off of your final grade if you use your phone or computer. Small seminar based and the class turns into a community. She makes an effort to get to know all students.
Pretty funny and really interesting class. Professor Tu really cares about her students and will make sure you succeed. Easy class.

Class was called Game Changers and the topics were really interesting and cool, but sometimes the lectures dragged on.   Prof. Tu doesn't give clear grading criteria, so you have free rein with your projects. You should really meet with her to get her input before presenting because she gives a lot of feedback.  Late work not accepted. Good class.

Pikachu's class is the perfect way to satisfy the MMS core.  She's super easy, really funny, and has a genuine interest to get to know every single student.  The workload is very low.  Highly recommend.
Rating below is totally accurate. Prof Tu genuinely cares about her students and wants to get to know you. Organizations Managament is by far the easiest core MMS class you will find.

Great teacher, funny and interested in what she does. Easy MMS class. Doesn't believe in memorizing, you get a cheat sheet for every test. Two group projects that are easy and everyone does well. Fun class, recommend taking it with her.

This is an excellent professor at Duke Law. I was very worried the class would be too difficult as it was a new topic and method but Prof. Lile-King teaches like a lawyer in trial. Students pay attention, are engaged in class discussions and she gives students everything they need to succeed. She is kind and funny. I wish she taught more classes.

Best professor I have had at Duke University Law or at London School of Economics. Caring, wants us to succeed. Makes lectures entertaining. Makes students feel welcome and valued even if we don't have always the correct work or answers. Encourages back and forth discussions. I wish I could take more classes from her. Take this class if possible.
If you want to learn analysis of common law and communication skills, this is the professor to take. She's engaging and teaches with learning by doing. Great lectures and very kind

My best professor at Duke Law School. Prof. Lile-King is a practicing lawyer, very smart and a very good teacher.  You should take her class if at all possible. She is a runner also and you can go on runs with her. Amazing amazing at lectures.

Great professor, wish I could take more of her classes She is very experienced at communication and teaching. This is a graduate level course and she works very hard to make sure the students do well. No other professor makes class exciting and engaging as prof Lile-King. I agree that we should rate her here as Duke Law's evaluations are private.

I really like Prof Lile-King. If you can choose to take her class, you should because she is the best prof I have at Duke Law. She makes class fun, even for a boring or tedious topic. She is funny and kind. You will learn so much even if it is a lot of work. She makes sure that everyone understands and succeeds.

This is a very hard class, and even though I didn't do so well, this is a great professor. The best. I wish she teaches my other classes because she makes her lectures clear and you learn to do legal skills by practicing in class. She is very available and will work to make sure you do well, but I procrastinated and did not take full advantage.

Prof Lile-King is my favorite professor at Duke Law School. She is committed to the students, available after class, gives amazing lectures, works very hard so that you understand. The class is challenging but if you work hard, you will succeed because this professor makes her mission for you to do it. Take her class!

This is a very good professor at the law school. She teaches by using examples and you learn by doing. She's the best professor by far I've had at Duke Law School. Very funny, cares about your success and will help outside of class so that you succeed.

My favorite professor at Duke. Always makes availability for the student, very caring.  Funny in class. Runs with students in the afternoons. Class is difficult for international lawyers, but very valuable to practice in US and to work internationally. Many readings and papers. Quite stressful. She is the most entertaining and interesting of profs.

Was worried about the class because common law is not familiar but Prof Lile-King gives clear lectures/examples. She teaches you learn by doing. She is caring and spends time out of class answering any question.I am glad to take Prof Lile-King because a very important skill to practice law in South Korea is writing. Prof Lile-King-great lectures!

I dreaded this class at beginning because it seems boring but Prof Lile-King is funny and keeps you entertained and makes you understand how important are class and skills.She is the best professor at Duke Law I had. Prof Lile-King is caring of the students, wants us to succeed, and spends time in office hours & after class to answer the questions.

Amazing professor, my favorite professor at Duke Law, very sweet person, always available for questions, quick to answer emails, kind and wants us to succeed. Her method of learning by doing is so awesome but the book is not as helpful. Take this professor if you can and you will learn so much about case law method and how to write in a clear way.

Great professor. Works really hard to make sure the student is understanding the material and the best way to write and learn the law. Always available for discussion and help out of class. The best professor I have at Duke Law.

Prof. Lile-King is a very kind person, always wanting to help you, especially with English expression if you are international. She truly loves the students and is so helpful. Take her class if you can
Really great proof. Best I've head at Duke. I recommend very much as she is very knowledgeable and kind
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Prof. Lile-King is a very solid professor. It is very hard especially in the beginning but if you work hard, you will understand and she gives all the help you need. She will work with you outside of class until you understand, she is very caring and the best of Duke Law school. I wish all the professors were this good. Amazing lectures. Exciting

Prof. Lile-King is a really kind and amazing professor. Her lectures are awesome. She works hard to make sure we understand, she is considerate and kind, especially if your English is not so good and you need extra help or time. She is very available for office hours. She cares for the students. She is a lawyer with experience. Take her class!

Professor Lile-King is the best teacher I have had at Duke. She is a great person, very kind and has very clear lectures. I recommend her classes even though the class is very difficult. She is a sweet person and will help you.

Prof. Lile-King is really caring and sweet person who wants her student to excel and succeed. She is one of the best professor I have had at Duke. She makes sure you understand the material. Very patient and kind.

very approachable professor
lectures are fine though it'd be better to have slides
exam is quite hard and very much depends on whether you can think of the right way to do it during the 3 hours

very interesting topics and papers discussed
he explains theory papers while let students present empirical ones, which makes sense to me

Phillip is amazing! His lectures are inspiring he teaches the ideas behind econ theorems. The course is certainly difficult given it is a foundational PhD class, but it should've been anticipated before taking the class. People overestimate themselves and complain about the difficulty of the course, but Phillip is a really good professor!

Clear that he is very smart, but not the best professor. The class was largely taught by students (I'd say 75% of classes were just student presentations on academic papers). Not very work heavy, but this means that each individual assignment counts a lot for final grades. Overall low workload, but not very interesting or well taught.

Interesting course content. Given he's a PhD professor, he doesn't stress grades too much. The class is curved to an A-B+ so no concerns there. I thought the content was very relevant and applicable outside of Economics.

This guy is useless. This is a PhD level course and he pretty much reads rubinstein's notes. Also, offers no solutions to the problem sets. His teaching and the problems on the exam have no correlation. I don't care if he has a PhD from princeton. But, he is the worst teacher and definitely unfit to be at Duke. Doesn't follow any specific text.
Almost just learn by myself during most time of his session. Confusing lectures and difficult  problem sets without clear solutions.
Never take Econ 701 with him
Very cool guy, definitely take his class! Low work load anad lots of learning. This guy has a  M.S. in physics and a PhD in econ! amazing dude

Had Professor Stern for Stuart and Tudor Britain and he was awesome. Engaging lecturer and his assignments have options that are not always traditional history papers- analyzing movies/tv-shows or creating a guide to a set of primary sources. We also read and discussed plays, novels, and philosophy books. Overall, great prof and class
Professor stern is great! I really enjoyed going to his class.

Professor Stern is amazing. A lot of his work focuses on British colonialism in India and he loves to relate other topics back to that. His classes tend to be pretty writing heavy but he tries to give a lot of feedback on what you turn in to help you improve your writing.

Professor Stern is one of the best lectures I have had at Duke. Very funny and makes class enjoyable. I have never had someone go over my writing in such depth. He has without a doubt helped me improve the quality of my papers. You get what you put in so prepare to do some work.

Possibly the best lecturer I've had at Duke - he engages with the class and makes the otherwise intensely boring material actually somewhat interesting. Endless and tedious reading, lots of writing - the most work I've had for a single class at Duke. Not an easy A and not for someone only vaguely interested. And definitely not for freshmen!

Tudor Class: He's an interesting person and I love him but I hated this class. There was so much work! I have never had so much work for one class. Also lectures are EXTREMELY hard to follow. He speaks so quickly that you can't keep up. Also his TA did all of the grading. I hope I get a decent grade but I doubt it...

The Tudor class: He's an engaging teacher and obviously very intelligent, but there was so much reading (that was not interesting) that I always felt like I was falling behind, which made the class less enjoyable. I got a good grade in the end, but I still feel the class was a challenge. Overall, hard class, great teacher.
best professor i've had at duke! smart, witty, incredibly engaging.
Excellent professor--very engaging, good lecturer, probably the most intensely detailed essay grader I've ever had. Strongly recommended.

This guy is just awesome. He's hilarious and makes the material easy to understand and interesting. He's into big themes in history, not so much the details and dates, etc. So as a result, he has very high standards about your writing. But if you put in the required effort and are a decent enough writer, you'll do fine. Loved him, loved this class.
Absolutely hilarious. Lectures are easy to follow. Gives helpful comments on written work.

Stern is awesome and hilarious, but his expectations can be ridiculous and he talks VERY fast. if you go to class and put in a decent effort, you will not get worse than a b, but you might go crazy trying to earn an a.. he expects A LOT from his students. this was his first year, so maybe he will become more reasonable in the future.

Stern just came to Duke from American and sometimes he has ridiculous expectations of students.  He talks FAST and his lectures are almost impossible to write down.  Nevertheless, he's really helpful if you talk to him outside of class and if you are interested in the time period (tudor/stuart britain) its a good class. be prepared to work though.
Best professor Ive ever had. Actually cares about students. Hands down my favorite

great professor! can be a little unorganized but is approachable and reviews the material with the student. she cares about student success and learning. she uses various media to keep the class engaged, one of the best lectures in the program. she must have been a great RN!
Interested in student success and creating the most educational environment possible.  Easy going.  Will not change grade.
Beth is always willing to help you out, and she truly cares about her students.
The professor was really chill, and helped a lot out of class. He also let us use AI when needed, specially during the coding part.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: he grades subjectively.

Very clear instructions and interpretations on each R command. Led the students to perform coding step by step in each class. Assigned reasonable homework that practices what was learnt in the class. Patient and open for questions.

The course is pretty challenging. The assignment is tricky, but you can get a better score than expected. However, the final exam is too complicated, and his grading criteria are unclear. You will deduct many points from your final exam (30% of your grade), although you got almost perfect scores on the homework.
If you work hard and preview the concepts, it is likely to do well
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Test heavy

reviews.comment: In my opinion, Prof. Santoso is not as horrible as people depict him to be. His lectures are pretty easy to follow and the final exam was fair. Still, I found the homework to be very challenging; it had little to do with the class content. If you have to take his class, I would not worry too much.

Professor Santoso delivers good lectures and is always happy to meet for office hours. However, the course organisation needs improvement, as it was very hard to keep track of the progress (no grades on the platform whatsoever), homework was graded by TA and it took long time to hear feedback, and the final exam discussed concepts we did not cover.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He gives clear instructions and lectures, uses many examples to explain the concepts. The new content amount and difficulty level are just right for a 100-level class. The assigned homework is in accord with the lecture contents. As far as I know, he is available outside the class.

The 1 star rating is misleading. Prof. Santosoo is very caring and give clear instruction. I appreaciate that he guides us throgh the codes step by step, which is very friendly for people who have no exposure to coding before.
He always took a leave for many reasons and could not explain concepts clearly in his class. The homework had little to do with course materials and the final exam was a disaster.

He didn't tell us to read textbooks but his test was based on it and he forgot that we didn't receive our textbook. His final test was quite difficult and the grades he gave us were really unreasonable. I worked really hard, but I received a bad grade.

TBH, IDK why everyone hates him here (I was wary. He does good job at explaining topics. His lectures are not boring and he is open to questions during lectures. I enjoyed taking his stats class, even though it was online. I learned great deal and my learning process was challenging sometimes but enjoyable overall.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Doesn't care about remote students as most of Duke Kunshan University remote classes tend to go
Taking Santoso's class made me appreciate lock downs as I was at least not locked indoors with him. Really uncommunicative
Long and uninteresting lectures. Poor communication skills. Does not answer questions. Workload and grading was fine, but some people are just not made to be good teachers.
I enjoyed taking SOSC101 with Prof Santoso and intend to take his class again.
Prof Santoso is kind and approachable. I enjoyed taking Sosc101 with him. The topics discussed in his class were deep and relevant to society

The professor's grade distribution is very low and unfair. Before I got the final grade, I had never seen the scores of every part of me, including participation score, assignment score, presentation score, examination score, etc. I don't think he had done enough to respect the students' hard work.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I had an awful experience with Prof Santoso. Santoso never explained the concepts clearly and his questions are worded very ambiguously. I did all the work but ended up with a C. The course's TA could probably explain the concepts better than he can.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I had a horrible experience with Professor Santoso. I did all of the course readings, participated in every lecture, and completed every homework assignment, yet ended up with a C- in his course. His grading criteria is very unclear and refers his students to other students or Google when we have a question.
Professor Santoso gave us minimal instruction on the class material yet graded our papers very harshly. He NEVER replies to emails and is not passionate about teaching us.

He explains things fairly well. He has high standards when it comes to homework. For example, he expects us to learn some coding functions on our own without going over them in class, so it is quite difficult for people who have never done coding before.
Santoso gives out a lot of work but hardly communicates with the students. The professor's discussion sections are lecture heavy and gets off topic easily.

If you are looking for an introductory class to astronomy, do not take this course. While Ronen is intelligent and is very passionate about astronomy, his teaching style is hard to follow and learn from. Be prepared to spend 10-14 hours each week on problem sets and learning the material.

As part of this class you do observations with telescopes and look at stars, planets, etc which is cool. However, much of the material extends gets very math heavy and into theoretical physics such as special relativity, good lectures and nice guy but only take this class if you like science and are willing to work hard on the weekly problem sets.

Ronen is passionate about teaching. He knows how to convey complicated ideas to the level of the students. His lectures are inspirational and the homework and exams are designed to teach us something new. Don't hesitate to ask him questions. He is always accessible after class and willing to lead us to explore the realm of physics.

Loved him, loved the course. I took it online but it was the most well-organized online course ever. Videos divided by topics, lecture notes, slides, everything you need was out there. He is that kind of prof who shares his passion and love for the field with you. And he gave excellent feedback on homework.

Prof Plesser is incredibly smart. His ability to come to the students' level is amazing. and he is able to explain things to your level so that he is able to inspire a love for Physics in you. He is also incredibly patient and he will re-explain things to you if needed.

Plesser is a gem! He loves talking about physics, and finds your level pretty fast, so the discussion is very student-oriented. Also, he would make his office hours infinite, as long as you are curious and interested in physics. His enthusiasm is catchy and he makes physics feel like an interesting puzzle to solve.

Favorite class. If you like physics, you're gonna love this class - it's not that challenging because it is an intro course, but it touches on lots of different topics in modern physics. The observations (3 of them) got a bit cold, but they were such cool experiences. You should really go to class, the lectures are amazing. Ronen is awesome.

If you are interested in Astronomy, Ronen is the man. As a humanity student, I haven't done physics for two years. I enjoy the class so so much. It is not easy, but really worthwhile. Amazing, amazing experience. Oh also, he could easily get too excited and talk too fast in the class. You just need to slow him down.

Dr. Plesser is definitely a very engaging professor that cares about his students and his material, a great professor. Observations are awesome too. However, I would not recommend taking the class unless you need to or really really care about the material. Homework, midterm, and finals were all too difficult for me to be worth it.

Ronen is a great professor, super knowledgeable and incredibly smart. He is a humble guy but very passionate about physics--sometimes seems aloof but inwardly he is quite friendly. For our class, midterms were extremely hard but the final was fairly simple (Got 99/100). If final>weighted average, final becomes your grade. Observations are awesome!
very pleasant to listen
Awesome guy, best teacher in Coursera but he ran his class only once.

Very engaged with subject and students.  Very helpful.  Explain things thoroughly and clearly.  Goes the extra mile to provide extra information for students who want to know more than can be covered in a lecture.

Prof Plesser does an incredible job to present the exciting field of astronomy from A to Z. The video demos he has identified and used during the teaching of the course are priceless. He is extremely immersed in the field and his enthusiasm is quite obvious. His love for the field is passed onto the student. A very highly recommended course+prof!
His lively narrative keeps even very complex subjects accessible to the rest of us
A very enthusiastic, energetic and passionate professor. His class was very intellectually challenging yet humorous. As demanding as his homework assignments to be, a great experience he will offer.

Ronen is the best professor I have ever had at Duke. He's enthusiastic about everything he teaches, amazing at explaining seemingly difficult concepts and gives homework assignments that are actually relevant to the world we live in. Would highly recommend this class to anyone. Do not expect an easy A though, effort and work is required.

Enthusiastic teacher and fantastic guy.  The only problems with his class are that 1) he is so excited about teaching the material that he rarely ends the class on time, and 2) on homework, the actual questions can be tricky to decipher because of all the background he gives.  I could have way, way worse problems.  GREAT choice for an NS req.

nice guy, really smart. some of the stuff in this class can go right over your head though. a basic background in physics will help you a lot. oh, and there is a lot of math. he makes an attempt to explain things to you if you ask.

physics 55 intro to astronomy... ronen is the man.. its a really interesting class that challenges u a bit.. labs in duke observatory where u look at galaxies and planets and stuff, really awesome. not the easiest class but definitely worth taking if you're interested

Very insightful; teaches a challenging but rewarding course.  Always willing to clarify, cuts to the chase on questions.  Not the most accessible outside of class, but makes up for it in efficient communication.  Highly recommended.
Great guy. Einsteinian intelligence.  Wonderful teacher- devoted as heck.
No Comments
Best lecturer on campus. Her notes are very clear and it helps when studying for the test. I'm not even an environmental track civil and I loved the class.

This is the first environ. eng, class I've taken and she is SO amazing at making things interesting and easy to understand for people with a lot of or zero background in chemistry and environ. science. Attendance is a MUST since she covers EVERYTHING in class. I'm in Trinity but I love her so much that she might be my favorite professor at Duke.
Plata is an amazing teacher. She knew everyone's name by the end of the class and always made lectures interesting. I would definitely recommend taking a class from her!
Plata is probably the best professor I've ever had.
Susie is an amazing professor.  I would highly recommend any class of hers!

Susie is super caring, accessible outside of class, will spend lots of time helping you, and will give you lots of valuable feedback that make you a better photographer. The class is manageable even if you've never had photography experience before, and even if it seems otherwise at first. Make sure to ask for help when you need it!

Susie is AMAZING- by far one of my favorite professors here. Her classes are a legit time commitment to do them well, but EXTREMELY worth it for anyone interested in photography or documentary work- you get out what you put in. She is incredibly caring and accommodating though, and will spend hours with you outside of class if needed.
Very fun, learned a lot BUT extremley time consuming, only take if you can dedicate 5-7 hours a week minimum. Susie is the GOAT, incredible prof very sweet and talented!

Susie is the best professor I've had at Duke. This is NOT an easy A class. This class is a LOT of work!!! But it is still one of the most rewarding expierneces I've had at Duke. The relationships I built through the service learning component of the clas are really special to me and I cannot tell you how much I have grown as a photographer!

Her class can be overwhelming if you're new. Also, she can be disorganized (assignments/info posted exclusively in different places can be confusing... box/sakai/email). Still one of my favorite professors ever though! She will give you HOURS of one on one guidance if you ask. Just an incredible person and professor!!

Susie is incredible! She has over a decade experience working at the national geographic doing some insanely cool shoots all over the world. She is very intense with very high expectations and demands. However, if you are passionate and willing to work hard you will see huge improvement both in photography and storytelling.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Don't take this class if you aren't ready to dedicate your entire semester to it and forget all other workloads exist. She is an extremely difficult person, overly criticizes you, AND makes you feel inadequate, even though it's an intro photography class. She has made people cry, from her tone and from the sheer amount of work she gave us.

Susie is a really experienced photographer, having worked at National Geographic for 20 years. As a teacher though she can be scatterbrained and relied on the TA to grade and keep her on track. Nevertheless, she taught me concrete techniques that upped my photography & editing game.

Susie is a wonderful Professor and cares about her students but her course is extremely hard and time consuming. If you put in the work you will get a good grade, but it will be challenging. She is very good at feedback and helping, but oftentimes I saw her demand too much from students and be disrespectful to the point where it stressed students.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Her photography class was very interesting, but it would've been way better if I took this class in normal years. COVID made me so hard to take pictures of outside world, and it was quite hard to understand her feedbacks and reflect them into my photoshoot. Also, there are four critiques, half-way shows, and finals. A lot of work.
Susie is one of the best and most inspiration professors I have had at Duke. She pushes you to be the best that you can be, which makes you produce meaningful work. Incredible and interesting person.
Awesome photographer
A very caring professor, works really hard to get across the ideas in the course. I enjoyed having a chance to get to know the community outside of Duke, too.
Although a very nice person, Susie was very disorganized when it came to class and our final project, which staying on top of projects incredibly difficult.
Single Greatest influence on my life as a photographer to date. Wish I had more time to learn from her! Cares more than any teacher professor I ever had, you would be lucky to study under her.

Really sweet professor, and very talented photographer. ALWAYS willing to help outside of class. However, very disorganized, unfocused, and unclear in directions. If you're looking for an intro photography class, I'd look somewhere else--courses with Susie are for more advanced students who don't need as much explanation.

Shelli is a very kind and unique professor. I am very glad I had her while at Duke. After taking 101 and 102 I felt like I had a good grasp on the language, and 203 was a fun application of my Hebrew knowledge.

I know other reviews say otherwise, but Shelli is a solid professor. Sure, you won't speak fluent in Hebrew but she does the most that she can. Taking 102 in the Spring after you take 101 in the fall is probably the best choice because that way you won't forget too much.

While Shelli has good intentions, she rarely speaks or asks us to speak in Hebrew. The focus of the class is on writing and reading, which is not ideal if you want to engage in conversation and quickly pick up the speakinglistening aspect of Hebrew. Often gets sidetracked, always in English. Discouraging for someone super excited to learn Hebrew.

Shelli is an incredibly nice, funny, and accommodating professor (if you ever don't understand something or if you have to reschedule an exam, she'll help you out).  Many of the lectures were disorganized, and I wish we did more speaking, but I still feel like I learned a lot and Shelli knows her stuff.  Shira (the TA) was fantastic.

It has been years since I took my last class with Shelli and I still think of her often.  I am very surprised by some of the ratings - not my experience at all. She is smart, thoughtful, and thought provoking.  She will teach you more than any language teacher ever has.
Shelli is interesting and knows and loves the language and culture.  The motivation level by semester 3 of a language requirement was almost zero so I applaud her for even showing up.

Great language prof.  Knows her stuff, knows the culture and history, very enthusiastic and approachable, treats students with respect, and really loves the language.  Only down side is the 8:30AM time slot...

It is a language class so lots of brainless stuff goes with the territory.  That being said, Shelli is the bomb.  She is quick, interesting, funny, and will go over things till we get them.  Class is at 8:30AM and I love it; need I say more?

Duke needs more profs like her! bad: she is disorganized and you will need to make an effort to keep things straight. good: she's very knowledgeable,  passionate about the subject, interesting (her "rants" r always thought provoking), amazing person and very accessible.  LOVE HER! thinking of minoring in Hebrew so i can take more classes with her.

Shelli is a very nice person and is flexible with due dates. However, she is completely distracted during class, goes on crazy rants during class time, and has no sense of organization. This class is an easy A but you will not learn much.

Shelli is an extremely nice person, but she is very distracted during class time. She often goes on rants that do not have anything to do with what we are studying. The class is incredibly easy and there is no organization whatsoever. She is very flexible and understanding about work. This class will not help you improve at Hebrew.

Shelli is one of the most amazing professors at Duke. Yeah, the class is easy, but you learn a lot of Hebrew either way and it's not incredibly intense. Shelli knows a lot and is willing to teach as much as each student wants to learn. Easy A, if you do the homework.

This is the worst class I have take at Duke. It's an easy A, but if you have any desire to learn any hebrew, this class is a waste of your time. It was supposed to be advanced hebrew, but we spoke hebrew for maybe 5 minutes every class. Our only two assignments were in English. I think my Hebrew got worse during this class.  Don't take this class.

Don't be fooled by Shelli...she knows her stuff.  however, the class is still a joke. because of the book, the grammar lessons and vocabulary are competely random. the class isn't too entertaining, but you can really get away with anything, which means, depending on who's in your class, it can be quite interesting. very easy to get a good grade.

Shelli is the best, and most underrated, professor I had during my 4 years at Duke. She is smart, interesting, open minded, and really knows her stuff.  She tells you from day one that what you learn will be up to you and she does not make you do more than you are willing to.  If you just come to class and do your work you will do well (though you

shelli is absolutely the easiest teacher ever.  we've had homework maybe twice this entire semester and all the exams are take home.  class is boring but if you have fun people its fine. sometimes she'll start talking about politics and her opinions are ridiculous.  she seems like a crazy hippie but whatever, its an easy class
This will be one of the easiest courses that you will ever take at Duke.  Shelli is also a really nice person.  However if you want a hard-core Hebrew class, this definetly is not one.
Easy, enjoyable language class. Lots of tangents on Israeli culture, politics.  You'll learn more than Hebrew, without working too hard.  Shelli's a nice person.

i can't believe she has a smiley face next to her name.  she is nice and you will get an A or an A - for doing nothing but if you have any interest at all in learning hebrew (and not suffering 4 days a week early in the morning) you are not going to learn anything and be sorry.  no offense, i mean she is real nice but i didn't learn anything!!

You'd be hard pressed to find an easier language teacher. As long as you do the assignments and show up to class 2 or 3 times a week, you'll get an A. She does tend to randomly not show up to class, which is especially annoying because it's always held somewhere ridiculously far away.

teacher stresses the importance of attendance with grading yet hypocritically fails to meet her standards as we must have gotten to class atleast 6 times and waited and eventually peaced out after the 10 minutes.
No Comments

Shelli is a real easy teacher. You learn your stuff. She sometimes goes off on tangents, and she randomly cancels class like 5 minutes before the start.  But she's a real nice lady, so if you don't do your work, you'll still get by

Professor Pourciau has to be the best lecturer I've taken a class with. The material is all super interesting -- some of the philosophy readings were too difficult for me to understand before the lectures, but besides that the readings/viewings were fun. Very fair grader too.

Super interesting course pulling from a variety of philosophical and cultural sources. Her Day 1 class was the most eye-opening lecture that I've ever attended at Duke. Not an easy T-req but definitely one worth taking.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Pourciau is one of the best professors I have had so far at Duke. Virtual Realities was an amazing course and Pourciau gave us an impressive crash course in philosophy in an incredibly attentive and palatable way. Her discussions and lectures were wonderful and highly engaging, and she truly cares about all of her students.

Weird Selves was such a great class. Prof Pourciau is an amazing teacher and the curriculum she put together was really fun. There is a decent amount of work per week, but it is very manageable, and some of it is just watching movies. She is incredibly smart and leads great in class discussions. Take this class!

Weird Selves was such an amazing class. The material was fun, professor Pourciau was very engaging when leading the seminar, I can't recomend it enough. If  you don't like too much abstract thought about stories then it might not be a good fit, but otherwise, amazing class, amazing professor, definetly take it if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I took Virtual Realities (not ethics oops) with Pourciau and she was incredible. Definitely the best class I've had at Duke so far. Not too much work, just make sure you kind of know what you're talking about and engage in class. She always approaches things from an unexpected but fascinating angle. Could not recommend her or this class enough!

I LOVE Prof Pourciau, you can tell she really cares about all her students, and I was constantly amazed at how smart she was. As long as you try your best to keep up with the readings and participate, you will get a good grade, and Prof is always available to chat. Definitely one of my favorite professors I've had and I wish I could have her again!

Prof Pourciau is a very caring and helpful professor. She is very accessible and helpful as long as you make an effort. The class has a very light workload but is still very interesting and Prof Pourciau does a great job of making you think.
Dr. Portier-Young is fantastic. She, however, doesn't grade your work. Your grade is determined by your preceptor and the grading practices vary depending on who your preceptor is.
The professor is amazing. Your assignments are graded by a preceptor not the professor.
IMO one of the most outstanding and rigorous Biblical scholars teaching today

APY is by far one of the best professors ever. Her expansive knowledge of the Old Testament is inspirational. She taught me how to actually study and learn from these ancient old books, and instilled in me a desire to learn more about the O.T.

Class was less than I had hoped. Lectures are scripted and are lean toward political correctness. Slavery was a real thing in the ancient near east. There is no way to rewrite the OT. Professor is brilliant and knows her field. She allows too many stupid questions during class. Defer to office hours. Overall, disappointed.
One of the best professors I've ever had.
One of Duke Divinity's BEST!
Brilliant woman! Liked her but the class was not what it potentially could have been if she allowed more opportunity for self-exploration of topics of personal interest.
Very smart and knowledgeable. May seem unapproachable at first but is very willing to listen and offer assistance.
Dr. Portier-Young opened up for me a whole new world within the Scriptures.  She draws your whole being into the text so that you emerge renewed and closer to sanctification.

She knows her stuff and when people in class stop asking stupid questions long enough to let her talk, her lectures are quality. My only complaint is that she isn't firm enough with certain students trying to hijack the class...

Extremely intelligent, but clearly unaware that her class is not the only class included in the courseload for her students.  Delivers lectures from a manuscript (not notes or an outline) that she refuses to upload and make accessible to students.  This would be beneficial since she does NOT allow students to take notes on laptops!!!
IM not going to any class with a Pope.

fantastic professor who really cares about her students' progress -- if you reach out to her she is incredibly helpful. as someone who loves poetry writing, this was one of my favorite classes at duke, not just because it was great to read and talk about poetry but because she is so wonderful and really knows her stuff.
She's a smart, sassy lady that writes well.
I've had a number of classes with Professor Pope--one of the most approachable teachers I've met. Excited about everything students do--go to her office hours one day, just to chat.  She's fantastic.
good poet, inarticulate professor. prepare to be bored. take askounis instead

Prof. Powell is a brilliant professor and a leading scholar in African American Art History. Demanding at times, Modern and Contemporary African American Art transformed the way I will look at art and culture going forward.
Professor Powell cares about his students' success and is always accessible to meet and discuss papers and projects to help you succeed.

If you enjoy reading for 3 hours every night, Powell is your guy. He requires so many expensive textbooks that make doing well in the class very difficult if you don't have the means to get those books. He's bad at communicating and does not make clear the requirements of his assignments. Lectures are hard to listen to and maintain interest in.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Prof Powell is great! Extremely easy and straight forward - one midterm, one 3 page paper and a final that was the same format as the midterm. His lectures are really long and kind of brutal sometimes but when the content was interesting they were super enjoyable. For the tests, he narrows your studying down to 40 images so its really manageable!

Powell's the man. Took two classes (Contemporary & Modern and American Art) with him and would have taken everything else if I'd had the time (and I'm not even remotely involved in art history). 10/10 recommend

I am astonished to see negative ratings about Prof Powell. Had him twice before graduating last year and have nothing but great things to say about him as a person and a professor. Highly, highly recommended.
Very nice man, but not much of a teacher. he's very specific but does not give much information on how to do assignments. Can be unpredictable. But he's a nice person.

He was absolutely the worst professor I've ever had at Duke (I'm a senior). He is arrogant, uncaring, unhelpful, mean, unfair, does not want the intellectual growth of any students. It was a tragic experience. Please do not take a class with him if you want to learn and enjoy the time.

Dr. Powell's Contemporary & Modern African American Art class is terrific. His incredibly insightful and eloquent lectures reflect his expertise in the field. He also sprinkles a bit of film history into the course, which is a welcome addition to the paintings and sculptures one typically encounters in art history courses. Highly recommended.

I took African Masqs Art History as my Art History non-western requirement.  Powell is extremely friendly and grades research papers very easily.  Slide tests are annoying but standard in Art History classes, so be prepared to make flashcards.  Powell was frequently unable to answer questions about specific pieces, but he never faked responses.

I really enjoyed this class.  His lectures were very structured and clear.  His passion for art was evident throughout the class. Except for the final exam, he told the classes exactly what was expected for exams and papers.  This is definitely one of the easiest classes at Duke.  I would really recommend it for a GPA booster, or an ALP credit.

he's very prepared for the lectures and was very enthusiastic about his subject, but not at all clear about what he wants on the test and could be a lot more simple when explaining things during the lecture. he totally changed what he wanted us to know ON THE DAY OF THE EXAM which was super annoying. definitely and easy A though.

Powell is really easy in his grading and tells you exactly which images you need to know for the exam. But he tried to pull a fast one this last exam by changing what he told us to memorize right before the exam.  But anyone who studies can get an A so if you want a GPA booster, i definitely recommend!

Professor Wald is not a strict grader, so as long as you put some effort in on the writing assignments and projects, you will be fine. She is great at leading in-class discussions, but there is a lot of reading, understandably.
Please take this class if you get a chance. Hands down the best humanities class at Duke.

LOVE Dr. Wald. Found class incredibly interesting and legitimately looked forward to it. She is so encouraging of her students and all ideas. Takes the time to learn your name and really cultivates a great environment for discussion. So thoughtful. I'm doing everything I can to take another class from her!

Dr. Wald is so precious. She is truly passionate about the subject and books we read. The point of this class is to have engaging discussions rather than "be right". Although I'm a science major and usually bad at literature, I enjoyed this class very much and it encouraged me to write and think deeply about interesting topics.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Dr. Wald is an engaging professor who loves intellectual exchange and welcomes controversial discussion, even if she does not agree with a student's opinion.  The class is not designed to be challenging; she wants everyone to do well. However, the readings she assigns are interdisciplinary and informative, so her class remains engaging otherwise.
Great prof, enthusiastic and caring
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: PWald is a great professor who truly cares about her students. She can really convey the importance of insightful humanistic and critical thinking. Very knowledgeable about genomics and related fields but can portray them in a rich social context like a story teller. Also lots of general knowledge and highly intellectual; can't go wrong with her.

Took Sci-Fi Film with Prof Wald. Easily one of my favorite classes at Duke. She's an engaging lecturer (would hint that she believes in The Matrix "Just look outside, it's everywhere") and wonderful for help at office hours if you seek her out. Watch movies, discuss themes, write a little bit, that's all! One downside: TA grading can be arbitrary.

She is awesome. Never thought i'd be interested in the topic, but I literally came out of class thinking and looking at things in a different way, which I think is an indication that a professor has done his or her job. Truly cares about her students, and is very passionate about her work. Take a class with her!!

No matter what your major is you MUST take a class with Professor Wald. She's incredible. Very enthusiastic, really knows her stuff, and encouraged discussion and participation even in an 80 person class. Wald is an absolutely fantastic teacher, and you can tell she really cares about her students.

She is the nicest person. Will write page-long e-mails to help you think of a thesis, incredibly helpful and great at explaining things. Can't say anything about grading yet, but the workload isn't bad at all, and the class is fun to go to. Highly recommended.

Dr. Pratson is an incredibly knowledgeable and engaging individual. If you want a great intro to energy, ENV 231 is the class for you. You must go to class (and you should!) as his exams are based both on his lecture slides and what he discusses in class. It can be difficult to self-evaluate learning before exams, but the class is worth it.

His lectures are super interesting and really inspired me to learn more about the energy industry. Your grade is based on 3 midterms (no curve) and there are lots of engineers in the class who this is mostly review for so the test averages are still high. Recommend going to lectures to get the most out of class.

If you are genuinely interested in the energy sector and its impact on the environment, the content of this course is super engaging. However, lectures get monotonous very quickly and the only grades over the entire semester are from 3 exams (which themselves rely heavily on memorization and are pretty difficult). Overall an okay experience.

Overall, it's a great class for understanding the basics of energy production/markets. You're only graded by the 3   exams and he doesn't post lecture notes (only slides), so make sure you attend classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Energy and Environment was meh. Some lectures were interesting, but many were boring. Only take the course if you're genuinely interested in the entire energy sector and its reach/consequences> The class is a very broad look at the industry, but not a very deep one. Your grade is 3 exams+optional extra credit; exams are tricky & memorization heavy.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class grade is determined by three midterms, two of which are weighted 30% and the one you do best on is weighted 40%. The averages on these tests are usually in the mid 80s meaning very few people pass with an A. Highly discourage people from taking this course unless you're absolutely set on the energy and the environment certificate.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures were recorded, so attendance wasn't mandatory; but lectures were great and it turned out to be one of my most favorite classes. Each day was a lecture that covered the basics of a new topic. As long as you studied, tests weren't bad; but were 95% of your grade so you couldn't mess up. Overall an interesting class, and would recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Lectures were very insightful into various technicalities about the energy industry. Although he posts outlines for each lecture that are very useful for studying for the exams that are 95% of grade, classes are worth going to for his insightful explanations. Exams are fair and the TA provides lots of practice around a week or two before an exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Would highly recommend this class. Class is not mandatory (I would recommend going but you don't need to as he records class and posts lecture outlines). There's no homework except 1 short assignment. Just study for the tests (which in my opinion are pretty fair) based on the outlines he posts and you will do well.

Lectures were OK and the class was generally informative, but assignments were very narrow and not critically engaging. I wish there would have been a more diverse set of presentations and assignments.

Class badly transitioned during COVID. Lectures were all async and were just Professor Pratson reading off of his notes. There was no application and the grade for the class is determined by open note tests and quizzes that are multiple choice.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class is interesting. The way he teaches it is not. He just reads off a script with no pauses and I had to stop every 5 seconds to take notes of what he said exactly. Sharing a transcript will make things a lot easier. Midterms are okay but sometimes the questions are worded in a confusing way. But they are not open to other interpretations :(

DEPENDS ON THE TA. Pratson himself is great. Loves what he teaches and is really accessible to students. The material is interesting and relevant. I don't have ANY math background and found it hard to get back into the physics/chem calculations at first. Like others have said, you have to work at it to do well (get an A).
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: What is Lincoln Pratson like as a person, you may ask? I have no idea. This class was completely asynchronous, and he seems to be reading off a teleprompter the whole time. The class itself, though, is almost unbelievably easy. 50% of each test is "calculation" questions that are entirely dimensional analysis (converting units). Easiest grade ever.

Prof. Pratson seems knowledgeable, but his asynchronous online class is very boring. Also make sure you double check that your technology is working. He penalizes students for technological issues. This is very frustrating. I might recommend this class if it was offered in person. Would not recommend taking it online.

Pratson is a really good teacher. All of our lectures were asynchronous online but he was super engaging and was really informative. The class was great and really allowed me to learn more about Energy & Environment. I would highly recommend this class and professor to anyone looking to take an environment class.

He recites off of a pre-written script and speaks fast, so you have to pause every few seconds to take notes. Doesn't provide slides with bullet points (only pictures?? of smokestacks?) so that is also awful for visual learners/ anyone who may have a language barrier. His tone is brusque and impatient in class announcements. Don't take this online

He's an awesome guy. Very well respected in his industry and clearly knows what he's talking about. Very easy to get an A if you take notes during the lectures and do the readings for the daily quizzes. Would love to take this man's class again. Highly recommend it.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy
