reviews.comment: Class is challenging but it is possible to get an A if you work hard for it. The exams are based off of lectures only- so you must come and take good, detailed notes. Slides are only pictures. Daily 5 Q quiz on the online textbook. There are basic physics and math calculations. Dr. Pratson is a great lecturer- the energy industry is fascinating.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Joke of a class where I learnt nothing. If you know how to do basic algebra (x + 1  4, what is x?), then you'll breeze through. Most of the quiz questions are converting a number from one unit to another. However, the tests are impossible to study for because there aren't any textbook/notes, and the slides are literally just pictures.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Pratson is extremely knowledgeable and fair. This is not an easy A but it is manageable and VERY rewarding if you put some work into it. I learned so many useful things in this class. It is also nice to see someone who is objective rather than being on one or the other extreme of the spectrum. Attendance is a must. Math involved.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor is knowledgeable. He uploaded slides for every lectures, but there are only pictures on the slides, so slides are not that helpful. Recommend recording every lecture and relisten to them before exams. I don't usually understand the materials in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Nice guy and the material is interesting but his lectures are boring and disorganized. Unfortunately, the tests are based off his lectures and he doesn't post lecture notes so you have to pay attention in class. Go to TA hours if you want to do well in this class. Light workload but definitely NOT an easy A as his tests are challenging.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Interesting class and I learned a lot. However, the tests have a lot of conversions and physics that he doesn't cover in class, so you have to go to office hours to learn it. No homework except reading, with a quiz every class. Tests are 75% of grade, and make you apply what you know to situations instead of just asking how systems work. Confusing.

Great class incredibly interesting would highly recommend. That said, tests are very challenging if you're not the best at math or physics, seeing as he doesn't teach much on them but they make up the majority of the tests. The little homework there is is very useful, interesting, and easy. Office hours are really helpful though

Good introduction to energy issues all around. Clear explanation of energy technology, though energy policy explanation not as strong. It's a pretty easy class - math is just basic unit conversions, lots of memorization. Exams are graded pretty leniently. He leans a bit toward fossil fuels but still does a good job covering renewables/other tech

Quiz every class on long chapter readings that are pretty irrelevant to the material that's going to be on the test. Very math/physics/chemistry heavy and definitely not an easy A. Seems to put rather obscure things on the test but is a nice guy overall.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I took it because I thought from the description it would focus mainly resources and the kind of material that I enjoyed in my high school environmental science class. Wrong. There is SO much chemistry, physics, and math associated with the material it's ridiculous. He's nice but this class killed any enviro science related major or minor for me.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Great professor with good lectures. I'd recommend recording them because he says a lot of important stuff that you might not be able to write down. He's also a great artist and good at drawing things on the board. A bit ditsy or boring sometimes, but he really tries to be there for his students and he's very understanding.

ENV330 is very straight forward.  Daily 5-question quizzes based on reading.  (Online text book is easy to read and has short chapters).  Lowest 3 quizzes dropped.  3 non-cumulative exams.  Go to TA hours before exams.  Lectures are very boring but Pratson is extremely nice and understanding. This class is NOT the easy A that people say it is.

The epitome of mediocrity. You'll learn some stuff in this class, it'll be kind of interesting, but this won't be one of your better classes in terms of actual teacher quality. His grading is also pretty arbitrary He gets the job done though I guess.

This was class was simple and straightforward. Listen to the lecture, do the relatively interesting problem sets, and take a couple of exams. This won't be the most fascinating or challenging class you will take, but it's straightforward and interesting enough if you're a non-major looking for an NS or SS credit.

ENVIRON 130: Energy and the Environment was the easiest class I had this semester. The material is straightforward, and very little time outside of class is required to do well. Also, the lectures are relaxed and interesting. I thoroughly enjoyed having Professor Pratson.
very interesting.  course consists of a huge project a bunch of really easy quizzes and some rough assignments.  But its not hard to do well.

Took both ENV 131 and ENV 130 with Pratson, and he is the man! Very pragmatic and passionate about what he teaches. Relatively straightforward assignments, quizzes, and essays. I found his lectures to be very interesting, but he doesn't leave time for student discussion (which is good IMO). He is super busy in general.

Energy and the Environment was a great class. Interesting material. Easy grader (as long as you do the work). Class isn't necessary, but interesting most days. Weekly exercises are terrible, but that depends on the TA and not Prof Pratson.
Really enjoyed World Trade and Energy Resources...good professor, seems to enjoy what he teaches.
Teaches Energy & the Environment and World Trade in Energy Resources - both great classes.  I'm sorry I'm not in the Energy Program now...
Taught middle of EOS 12 (dynamic oceans). Good class, good professor. He seemed a little scatter brained, but I still liked his class. puts all powerpoints online.

I loved this class! We watched interesting movies, series, and read 2 short books (one was a graphic novel). While there is a lot of homework for this class, I have learned A LOT and my French skills - oral and written expression and comprehension - have improved significantly. Mme. Provot is caring and would make jokes to keep us engaged in class.

Professor Provot really cares about her students, and I had a great experience taking her class in Spring 2025. It is not an easy A because it's a language course, but I did improve a lot in French with her.
Most unclear grader ever, mean person

Mme Provot is a native French speaker from France so she can come off as cold and abrasive at first. However, as time goes on, she'll get to know you better. The class definitely helped me improve my French very quickly but there can sometimes be a whole lot of homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: It's a lot of content. Not hard, just a lot to do. There is a lot of HW and group projects. Easy A class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: My French improved significantly with Mme Provot, but that being said this class was HARD! She really made me work for and A and I put in more time outside of this class than any other. If you want to improve, I would recommend her but be prepared, she won't go easy on you.

She's tough but good. She'll push you to learn French which is the whole point. Lots of work but I recommend. She's sweet and takes no bs which is refreshing at Duke. Don't mess around and you'll have fun and learn a lot.

Prof Provot is really kind and quirky, but she is an incredibly tough grader and sometimes tells you the guidelines after the assignment is completed. She assigns four textbooks and listed them as mandatory but we only ever used two so it was a waste of money. There was a ton of homework and projects and grading for the projects was very difficult

Karine is a fundamentally nice person, and my French improved a lot in this class. She can be, however, disorganized and temperamental. Take this class if you are serious about your education, and you will do well.

Mme Provot will grade you in comparison to native speakers, and assigns a genuinely ridiculous amount of homework (1.5-3 hrs/class, 3 classes/week). She often says in class that she loves errors, but would criticize students harshly for making them in class. I wish I had not taken this class. Find another professor.

Great lecturer who clearly cares about people's understanding. That said, she does get annoyed with the people who clearly do not care at all about improving and is not afraid to let this sentiment show. I highly recommend if you actually want to learn French; if not, you're better off with someone else.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I really liked Mme Provot. She is engaging. Her class has good energy. Yes there is homework. Yes you have to participate. These things are givens in a duke language class, and there were times when it was challenging and a little painful, but I also found her grading, assignments, and expectations to be very fair.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: She is a really responsible professor, passionate about social problems, teaches and explain things well. But be aware that she has really strong personal preference on students and a lot of students find her biased in grading. Take french from another professor if possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I literally made a RMP account just to air out my thoughts. Sure, Mme Provot is superficially nice (especially if you happen to be one of her favorites), but can be otherwise condescending; I felt like I always had to defend myself and my answers in her class. Way too much HW (expect about 1.5-2hrs/night). Take a different French class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I personally dont like her. She made me hate learning a language for the first time in my life. This class has A TON of work and there is no flexibility. Mme Provot is extremely particular about everything and you will lose points for little things so. There are too many elements being graded. She will expect this class to be your TOP PRIORITY.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Tough Class but amazing professor. Lots of homework but that's not the professors choice, the whole language program at duke is intensive. Expect about 1-1.5 hours of homework a night and attendance is MANDATORY. She is also very accessible outside of class and helps to set you up with tutors if necessary. Show her you care and she WILL help you!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Gives an absurd amount of homework, including many projects and writing assignments. Tough grader who pays attention to every single detail, but rarely gives clear expectations of what she wants. I will say that my French skills improved significantly from this class, but I would attribute it less to the professor and more to my own efforts.

Expect to spend a lot of time doing graded homework that if it isn't perfect, you will get marked down for. She demands a lot of outside work to be done. this is by no means the easy A that I expected.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Mme Provot is a great professor but gives too much homework. The workload of this class is alomost the workload of all my other classes combined, and she knows that she is giving out a lot of homework but just keeps it this way. I personally started to hate French a bit after taking this class. Would recommend to think twice before taking her class

Amazing professor. She is engaging and truly enjoys helping those who help themselves. Quizzes and tests are fair and Professor Provot is willing to help if you are struggling. Expect homework every night but know that you come out of this course with solid understanding.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Karine Provot goes through material quite thoroughly and facilitates great discussion about the assigned movies/readings. She has high expectations, but she's a fair grader. Engaging lectures and great person to talk to.

The first thing I noticed about Provot is that she speaks very quickly. But you get used to it quickly as well, and she teaches you lots of fun and useful vocab too. Participation really, really matters in this class. LOTS OF HOMEWORK AND IT WILL DRIVE YOU NUTS, but in the end, totally worth it. She is a fair grader, but she makes you work for it.
Prof. Provot is a great teacher. If you need help, she will take the time to meet with you. Your french will improve a lot with her!

Provot was wonderful! At first it took a while to get used to her speaking because she is a native speaker and spoke quite fast. But you grow to like her and in the end we all knew we would miss her. She is funny and gives you good feedback. She threw us a christmas party at the end of the semester and it was great!

She is a tough grader and expects everyone to prioritize her class. You'll really learn the language with her, but the class is difficult and demanding and only a few people came out with As. She's got an attitude that you need to get used to.
Madame Provot is pretty cool. She can sometimes be intimidating since she is a native speaker, but the workload is manageable and grading is fair.

Extremely clear and effective delivery of grammatical concepts. As an added bonus, she's a native French speaker, so she could explain the nuances of the language. Lots of engaging in-class activities to hammer in the vocab/grammar from each unit. Consistent but not too heavy workload. Overall, a straightforward yet highly enjoyable class.

Mme Provot is extremely helpful both in and out of class. She will always respond to emails and is willing to regrade essays as many times as you are willing to rewrite them. She is very honest in her grading and expects you to put in the amount of work that she does, though, and the class is demanding in its workload.

Absolutely wonderful professor. Lots of work in the class, and pretty time-consuming, but you really feel like you're learning the language. She's a native of France, so she taught us bunches of common phrases that we might not have learned otherwise. Extremely approachable and will help you with anything as long as you ask! Great French experience
Very nice and interesting. Has an authentic French accent, which is a plus. Definitely one of my favorite professors.

I found her incredibly helpful in all aspects. She was fun, interesting, and made the french class thoroughly enjoyable (especially considering it meets every day). The actual work was very tedious, and she expected a lot of us. We had daily assignments, weekly orals, and tests nearly every 2nd week.

Mme Provot is a fairly nice woman and a reasonable teacher.  She does play favourites, though, and much of the grading is subjective.  Overall, I'd take the class again, but I've definitely had better professors.

Provot is very nice and approachable and has a great attitude about the class. She is eager to get to know her students better, which helps create a positive classroom environment. Provot was also very understanding... she would grant extensions if you had a good reason. Lots of work, but not particularly difficult.
Currently taking BME305 -- engaging lectures, busy labs (TAs are great), a problem set evry 2 weeks, grading isn't too harsh. Dr. Chatterjee knows a lot and shares great stories!

BME305 and BME590 are rigorous but low pressure. Dr. Chatterjee is not a tough grader, but he gets you to learn really complex material in an intuitive way and is fun to talk to outside of class. 590 was really fun, and I even got a job after I took it because I could do Gen AI!
Great Professor and very knowledgeable

Dr. Pryer and Dr. Windham were amazing. The entire class consists of 3 open-note exams, around 20 homework worksheets (each is ~20 pages long), lab, and a lab practical. Everything was super easy (except the lab practical) and they're very accommodating. They're also married which I didn't realize until halfway through the semester

Class is an easy A if you put in effort. Some HW, open-note midterms, and every lecture's spent going over the HW you just did. Lab was pretty boring until you get to the plant anatomy section. Really helps to have an interest in botany, but you go over history, medicine, nutrition, etc. Dr. Pryer's kind, enthusiastic, and wants you to succeed.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS! This is the most boring class I have ever taken, the expectations for larger assignments are unclear, professor can be hard to reach, lectures are violently boring and dry, and the professor(s) will randomly triple the homework load without warning at the end of the semester. This class shouldn't even be offered.

his is the wort class ever. The lectures are almost 3 hours long and the entire time is spent going over the homework that YOU ALREADY DID. This is absolutely the most boring class I have ever taken and the expectations for projects and tests are unclear. If you need a somewhat easy biology credit, this class would work but it's extremely draining
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The course structure changes every time it's taught. Had 3 online at-home midterms and same for the final- gave 6 EC points added to our final grade too. Lab dumb and waste of time but 0 work for it - doesn't count for grade either. Not much work and easy A but lecture is dry and boring. Co-taught w/ Mike Windham - he does almost all the teaching

Professor Pryer is so passionate about plants and she and her co-professor, Professor Windham, are able to make some of the most seemingly dull topics interesting. They are true assets to Duke Biology and Duke. It also doesn't hurt that they bring in lots of plant-based snacks to their classes!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Pryer is a nice professor. However, certain questions on her exams are trivial and not contributive towards learning about plants. She is also surprisingly disorganized and sends assignments in an untimely manner. It's clear she cares little about the class. Worst professor I've had at Duke.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Extraordinary course. Pryer is loving, hilarious, down-to-earth, and all-around wonderful. The best professor and person I've met here. You must take a class with her!

You have to keep up with the weekly quizzes, because that is also your attendance. I found that she ended up dropping lowest quiz grades so my quiz average ended up being fine. The hard part about the class is that sometimes it is boring because it is all lectures and you scribble notes down and the amount of information you learn is a lot.

Professor Pryer is really nice. Although the assignments sometimes lacked clarity, I found the class to be fun and interesting. She loves to bring in fruit and vegetables for the class. Her grading system this semester was a little odd, and I worried that with the weekly quizzes would ruin my final grade, but I came out the class on good standing.

This class shouldn't have been hard but Prof Pryer's grading policy this semester made it almost impossible to get a good grade. The content was rather easy but there were often random, nit-picky questions on quizzes, or questions that had nothing to do with the topic we were discussing.
She really loves her subject and loves teaching it.
No Comments
No Comments
No Comments

She isn't the most clear in her explanations, and her lectures are boring. Also, the exams are quite difficult and graded fairly harshly, so I would try to not take the class with her unless you have previous experience in probability.

Dr Hebbar's Math 230 is a solid course. The content progressively worsens throughout the semester, so the lectures aren't the most captivating but the class is quite manageable. No tests, just quizzes which are graded very kindly. HW doesn't take too long either.

Not a great lecturer. Many times mis interpreted her own homework problems but was thorough when going through problems in OH. So many people posted exam questions on chegg tho and got away with cheating. Atleast she was receptive to feedback. Also replies to emails late and exams papers terribly (doesn't give method marks)

Super workload heavy class, and graded pretty harshly. Weekly problem sets take longer than CS 330 psets, ECE 270 (for reference). 50% of midterms/final are online Sakai quizzes with no partial credit. Dr. Hebbar covers basic examples but throws really difficult problems for HW and tests.
Solid professor and solid lecturer. Tests are pretty reasonable, and her policy of only including material covered in class and HW is nice.

She is a really really nice person who cares about the class a lot. Not the best lecturer, but is extremely open to questions and feedback during lecture. Office hours are very useful. Reasonable exams and weekly problem sets.

Definitely NOT an easy A. Grading is subjective and I had no idea what I was supposed to be doing half the semester. If you want to have any chance of making even an A-, talk as much as possible in class and make it obvious that you read the material on Canvas.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you're thinking of taking this class as an GPA booster, be prepared to speak at all times, even if you say nothing of substance. This class was a poorly put together with scraps of readings, speakers, projects, and "discussion" (where he talks the whole time). Uninspirational, condescending, and strongheaded is how I would describe Prasad.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class is disengaging, repetitive, and uninspiring. Though this class spans multiple weeks, you really don't go much beyond the basics of climate change. Prasad values class participation yet he lectures the whole time, repeating what is already in the homework. He is stubborn, condescending, and always tries to assert his knowledge. Drop it!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Despite the lack of rigor and intellectual engagement, he grades mostly on participation. Halfway through the semester, he slapped together a poorly thought-out, repetitive curriculum. Although he claims we grade ourselves, he gets the final say. He is poor at absorbing feedback and is not a teacher but a lecturer so you won't have much to say.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Kasibhalta told us not to look at his rate my professor at the beginning of the semester... I should have known. He is nice and very knowledgeable; however, his grading is arbitrary. He says you can grade yourself, but anything higher than a B, he disagrees, even though his expectations are unclear and hard to meet when he lectures all class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Prasad is good about answering emails and is accessible outside of class. Despite this, your entire grade in this class comes down to very few assignments that are graded as a group.
The grading criteria for this course is vague. This course has very few assignments and most of your grade comes from a series of group projects.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prasad's grading is all over the place. He is very vague and not descriptive with what he wants from the students. Make sure you participate as much as possible. Material is extremely easy. However, his grading criteria and lack of assessments and points makes it difficult to get an A. He is also quite closed-minded.
Prasad is a terrible grader, has unclear expectations, and is not willing to compromise much. Everything is vague. However, he is a great Professor in his field and very well known!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Be prepared to work hard if you take his seminar class! The class was stressful at times because the grading was unexpected at first. However, Prasad is a great professor and makes an effort to make conversation outside of class. Participate, put in consistent effort, and keep yourself on track and you will be able to succeed.

I felt like I was going to fail this class but put in the effort throughout the entire semester and you can get an A. Participate as much as you can every class, but Prasad will call you out or even challenge you if you don't know what you're saying. Find reliable friends in this class - tons of group projects. Grading is unpredictable and scary.

Prasad is very knowledgeable in his field. However, this class is entirely made up of group projects, which can be hit or miss. You're better off taking the University course if you are actually passionate about climate change.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prasad is a great, passionate professor. He delivers good lectures and grades very fairly. Tests were never too hard and material was generally easy to grasp.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Prasad--yes he makes his students call him by his first name--is by far one of my favorite professors at Duke. Even though I am not majoring in environmental science, his class taught me so much in such a short period of time. There are lots of group projects and he occasionally had guest lecturers. Always available whenever his students his help.

Prasad is very helpful and kind. The class itself is not too hard or too easy, but very manageable. Lecture is very important, note taking is essential as all material is up for grabs when it comes time for exams. The information is relevant and interesting even if you are not an environmentalist.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Prasad is very approachable and is somebody I expect to keep in touch with. He knows his stuff, and I am truly impressed with how much knowledge I gained in one semester. I highly recommend this class, but don't expect it to be an easy A. There are a lot of assignments, almost all of which are group assignments. Definitely my favorite class so far.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Prasad is by far the best professor I have had my freshman year. Accessible and very friendly. Discussions can be a little intimidating since he will call you out and rip out your soul if you don't know what you're talking about. Extremely knowledgeable about climate science, fair grader and generally tries to help you out as much as he can.

Prasad is a great professor. He's a little intimidating. But great class thought it would be super easy but turned out to be harder than I expected. Readings were quite lengthy and complicated. But Prasad grades fairly and easily so as long as you pay attention during lectures and use your brains while writing the midterms you should be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Prasad's seminar was one of the most fun I've taken at Duke so far. He is really caring and friendly, and wants you to do well
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Prasad is a really good guy but his class was often unorganized, repetitive, and his expectations weren't always clear. Knows a lot about the subject and cares about students. Overall, not the best class but wouldn't mind taking another class with him.

Prasad is a little tough at the beginning of the semester but becomes more relaxed as the year progresses. Blog grades and participation are a large part of your grade. So, as long as you put in a couple hours on the blog posts and participate in the class, you will get an A.

Freshman seminar. Took the class in 2011 and received an A +. Prasad is an amazing professor, to say the least. Interesting subjects, organized class, great discussions, and fair grader if you put in the work. Essays are more important as well as participation. Do the readings, ask questions, prepare your essays in advance, and you can get an A.

Prasad is the man. He genuinely cares about his students and is funny, very accessible, and a great teacher. We used a free, downloaded book for ENV179, which was an added bonus. He gives you clear expectations, never gets in over your head and will always slow down to explain when things get difficult. One of my top 5 favorite professors at Duke.

Prasad is awesome. TAKE HIS SEMINAR. Perfectly manageable workload and MUCH more interesting than other seminars. We wrote 3 4-page essays, 2 2-page blogs, and only had to read for the first half of the semester. Then we had guest speakers every day. And, we made a poster for 2 essay grades. He's chill-just participate and you'll be fine!

Had him for "What On Earth?" last semester; he definitely toughened up this semester after reading previous ratings saying his class was unstructured & easy. 2 pg single (NOT double) spaced papers every week, and 6-8 pg single spaced paper for the midterm & final. Grades hard on participation in class & on BB (counts for a lot of your grade).

Prasad's class is demanding and challenging.  Expect an essay a week (2 pages single spaced) and  two synthesis papers (6-8 pages single space).  The papers will be frustrating but you will learn a ton about Global Warming and the Environment.  Also, there are a lot of interesting guests.  Participation is really important both in class and online.

Seems like a nice guy, but really full of himself.  He doesnt really listen to what you have to say and then just says what he was thinking before you started talking.  His grading is somewhat arbitrary and he changes the weights of grades during the year without telling you.  I didnt learn much at all and really felt like it was a waste of my 50k

TAKE THIS CLASS! Prasad is the man, you don't need to read the articles/paperback text he gives and most classes we had guest speakers / group presentation. He likes people who participate so if you have a background in enviro science I'd def take it bc you have an edge. Papers get tedious (approx 6-8 3 pg papers all year) but worth it bc he givesA

Prasad is the man! You will not find a more likeable, fun and interesting professor at duke. I was in the "What on Earth?" seminar. We talked about all the envion issues esp. global warming. We wrote two papers in this class (so not that much work), he grades really easily, and the discussions were very interesting and enjoyable. Take this seminar!

Prasad is a genuinely nice and caring prof. his lectures are fairly clear (much clearer than chantal's) and he tries to make the class interesting (though his success is arguable). tests are pretty clear, and not even weighted that heavily. overall, he comes well recommended!

Prasad lectures fairly well. Really easy class: concepts were easy to sink in and tests were easy to ace; you just have to know fairly general concepts; nothing too in-depth. Very fulfilling class: gives an entirely new perspective on Env Sci/policy: the policy approach was new for me.

This class is boring, but it gets rid of an NS and it isn't too demanding.  Prasad is awesome-- I'd say one of the nicest professors I've had so far.  It's the woman that teaches the class with him (Chantal Reid) that makes it so painful.

This class requires a lot of reading! Grading is a bit opaque (75% of my grade was unknown to me after LDOC), and is equal parts participation, short assignments, final project, and final essay. She has a lot of knowledge.
Great teacher. So kind and funny! Take a class with her, you won't regret it.
Professor Psomiades is a phenomenal professor, in both lecture and seminar settings. She is always willing to meet with you outside of class. The workload is reasonable and grading is fair.
loved her Paradise Lost class. allows you to revise 2 out of 3 of your big essays and is super helpful during revision sessions.  funny and fashionable

Professor Psomiades has such an infectious passion for everything that she teaches that makes you really enjoy the class. You can revise two of the three papers in the class, and she's really helpful during her one-on-one revision conferences. She's a very thorough grader, definitely not unreasonably tough, and it's clear that she cares a lot.

Loved the Victorian poetry class. She is so much fun and a very good teacher! Really interested in helping people improve their writing and clearly devotes a lot of effort to commenting on papers. Class is never boring...learned a lot of useful English stuff and also random facts. Will make you work hard, but not unreasonable. Definitely recommend!

She's fantastic. Lectures are fun, you learn a lot about Victorian literature and culture, and she's incredibly helpful. The TA can grade harshly, but you will generally have an opportunity to revise your work. I recommend taking one of her classes in the highest possible terms.
She's hot, and has cute voices.

I had her as a graduate student when she taught at Notre Dame.  She is an amazing teacher.  She motivated me more than any professor I've ever had.  Not only is she brilliant, but she really cares about her students.  Take her if you can
one of the best around

Quite nice and VERY excited about Victorianism.  If she offers the poetry course again, consider taking it for the distribution requirement.  Readings are substantially shorter than in her Victorian novel class.

Very knowledgeable and enthusiastic professor with a good sense of humor. Be prepared to listen to historical sex anecdotes. Also, she doesn't like to write negative comments on papers, which can be frustrating if you keep getting B+s and don't know why.

Very typical hiding ball professor who informed us about the "likely" final exam format very close to the exam, with no practice at all, and did not tell us the percentage weight of each question. Do not use slides in class at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Purdy really brings archaic political philosophy to life! He knows how to ignite an interesting conversation and direct it toward a fruitful end. He's also willing to make time to meet with students and help them with their papers. It's a really long paper (30-45 pages) but it's a worthwhile intellectual exercise nonetheless.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Very knowledgeable. More engaged than most of my other professors, even though he usually teaches grad level. The class is not easy. It demands a LOT of highly theoretical reading, but it's worth it. I think he could improve a bit his organization/clarity. Since class is mostly discussion based, it doesn't always follow a logical order.

Purdy Is a law professor who taught a course on legal theory/the Constitution this year. He is brilliant, supremely kind, a wonderful seminar facilitator, like seriously brilliant, and my hero. I look forward to staying in contact with him next year and beyond. Absolutely take anything he teaches.

She is such a sweet person. Very, very easy class. I never thought I'd be able to do other work in a college class, but then I took this class. She is very passionate about the subject, but the lectures can be a little dull sometimes. She is such a sweet person though, and the class is an easy A.

her lectures are very interesting, especially because dance is a big part of my life. i'm not sure what non-dancers think but it's a great course for people trained in ballet, modern, etc. she really makes the readings come to life and explains the concepts extremely well.

Professor Shah really wants every student to understand the material she teaches. Make sure you understand each discussion because if you don't she will notice and call you out. Professor Shah is a great teacher and the material is not too difficult.
She is a great lecturer and the class is interesting.  She is accessible and will work with you to make sure you understand the subject material.
Professor Prasad is my favorite professor! She has helped me adjust to college so much and genuinely cares about all of her students. Her class is fascinating no matter your major.

You get out what you put into this class. This class is almost too easy. If you show up to class and do the minimal work, you will get an A. Prof. Prasad is just so nice, really caring and this was a stress-free class.

This was a great choice if you're looking to get an ALP credit. While we did have weekly assignments (watching a movie, reading one/two articles, and posting on the discussion forum), they were not at all difficult. The rest of the grade depends on the final group presentation, and this was not difficult either

Great professor. Clear expectations and relatively light workload. Just watch the relevant films and compose some thoughtful responses. She instills a lot of life into her lectures (even if the content is rather dry).

Leela is a great professor and great person. I learned a lot from Hinduism from the class and enjoyed the lectures, but sometimes she goes on long tangential stories about her experiences, which are still definitely cool to hear about.

Literally the best class I have taken in my life. Dr. Prasad is one of the kindest souls at Duke and just wants to share what she knows with her students and for them to not only learn but also enjoy the material. Her lectures are incredibly informative and interesting and her workload is light with most of the grade depending on participation.
Great lectures.
Don't leave Duke without taking a class from Leela Prasad. Amazing lecturer. Opens your mind.

Leela is a fantastic professor--sensitive, and most appropriate to teach Gandhi. She brings out the best from students while being responsive to their concerns and opinions. The class discussions are amazing and provide  wonderful insights. Here's some simple advise if you are considering this course:  Take it!

This is one of the best courses I have ever taken in my 4 years at Duke. I'm so glad I decided to take in my final year. I wish I had taken one of her courses sooner. Absolutely amazing teacher and fabulous course. Lots of insights that I will take away into the real world.
i took her epics of india class. amazing! tough but you really learn and have a blast. take it don't miss her at duke. my best prof truly. I took 2 courses with her
she is phenomenal. brilliant and compassionate but makes you work hard

In her Hinduism class, Professor Prasad didn't seem to understand that many of the students came from Hindu backgrounds while others did not, so she kind of taught like you already knew what was going on.  Created a very strange dynamic and an uncomfortable learning environment. She is very helpful though, and you don't actually have to read.

Leela is hands-down one of my favorite professors at Duke.  She genuinely loves what she's teaching and cares about her students.  She will go out of her way to help her students and is one of the nicest, most open people I have ever met. You will NOT regret taking her classes!
Leela is passionate about what she teaches, and if you show genuine interest in the subject matter, she'll teach you incredible things. Also the nicest prof I've had at Duke.
I really liked Leela! She's very enthusiastic about teaching and actually cares about how her students engage with the material. She's also very personable and down to earth.

She is awesome! My friends and I couldn't believe what others have written.  We decided to write and correct the **** comments. We never felt left out or treated like idiots. You have to take her course for the best education experience ever!

The best Professor I've ever had! I have taken two courses with her and the discussions in both courses were eye-opening to say the least. I found her to be tremendous in her sensitivity to various perspectives. Some bigoted people may have their opinons, but her courses especially the one on Sacred Space were spectacular. Don't miss her course!

This was a fantastic course--i can't believe the comments of some others. I know that many in my class share my opinion. Working on a project to create sacred spaces was awesome. Since I took this course at the end of my studies at Duke, I can say it was perhaps the BEST course I took at Duke.

This professor treated me like I was a total idiot, which I am not.  She is **** against white people and did not offer any sort of feedback that would help with writing or getting better grades.   Plus she shows really long boring videos about India from the 70's.

Prof. Prasad is great professor.  She doesn't care about tests and whatnot but actually wants you to learn and get excited about what she teaches.  Her expectations are a little high for work but she still grades easily.  She made my 2.5 hour class really enjoyable!
No Comments
bias, unfair, does not teach, which is unfortunate to those who actually want to learn and even those who want to do well in the course - she is a serious waste of duke's money
No Comments

Dr Purves is a really nice professor and the class itself is pretty interesting. Most of the questions he asks in class relate to his lectures. Presentations were graded fairly. As long as you talk to him about the final paper, you'll do well. Overall, pretty laid-back class.

If you want to do no work, this is your class. His grading is extremely arbritary as there are no tests- your whole grade is based on 2 presentations, 1 final paper, and class participation. Overall, if you participate a lot in class and discuss the final paper with him you will probably do well. The material wasn't as interesting as I was hoping.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: If you've never taken NeuroSCIENCE the class may be boring or intimidating, but regardless you still learn a lot and think about the real world. Its structured based on lectures, 2 presentations per student and a final paper. Dale is also really nice.
Nice, interesting professor; laid-back class environment, very knowledgeable -- But grading/attendance policies were very unclear. I had no idea what my grade was the entire semester.

Not a GPA killer, but just so boring and nervewracking; he calls on people to answer questions on the incomprehensible papers he assigns for reading, and continues to press you for answers even if you have no idea what he means. Asks long winded, "no-right-answer" questions, but seems miffed when you don't give the exact answer he wanted.
The class consisted of many short papers on concepts that were pretty unclear. Generally Purves is a cool guy, though, and if you work hard, you will be able to get a good grade.
Watch out for the final!! It is insanely hard! Dropped me a letter and a half for final grade. Extremely unfair!

A bit hard to understand at first as he as a raspy voice. However he is very knowledgeable and NOT arrogant at all (even though he is the head of the department). He is very nice and helpful outside of class so try talking to him in his office, etc. I think it helps with papers. The papers are pretty straight forward and easy to get an A.
Amanda lays down everything you do in the course in the syllabus with weights and everything, clear grading criteria, super chill and easy grader too. Super chill writing 101, would do again.

Professor Pullum acts like a maternal grandmother, and I mean that in the sweetest way possible. Super nice, caring, and gentle with feedback. Enjoys chatting, and her stories are usually more interesting than the dry class material.  Other Writing 101s may be more interesting, but her class remains a solid choice.

Dr. Pullum is one of the sweetest professors you could ever have.  She genuinely cares about all of her students.  The material is pretty interesting (very sociological), and she is a very easy grader.  Highly recommend this course

Dr. Pullum is the BEST. Please take this Writing 101 class with her. She is the sweetest, most caring professor you will ever have... and the work load is not that bad. Contrary to what everyone is saying, I actually found the material very interesting, and she tries to make it interesting too!

she's the sweetest lady ever and is always willing to help. pretty easy writing 101 class too. the topic is a little boring but she tries to make it interesting and sometimes class discussions are cool.
Dr. Pullum is an organized, extremely kind and passionate professor. She is always available for help and gives timely feedback. Definitely recommend taking her writing 101 class.

Dr. Pullum is passionate about the subject she teaches, and it comes across in her classes. They're well-organized, but sometimes it can feel drawn out a bit. That said, she is a very nice person and does a great job of being accessible to her students. I would absolutely recommend this to anyone looking for a low-key class with a kind professor.

Dr. Pullum isn't the most interesting professor and she doesn't teach the most interesting subject, but overall I would recommend this course to freshmen who are looking a laidback Writing 101 course. There isn't too much work and the work that you are asked to do isn't terribly difficult. Grading is fair and Dr. P always provides timely feedback

Professor Pullum's class may not be the most interesting, but i would recommend it to anyone for a writing 101 class at Duke. She gives you revisions for every paper and if you follow these revisions, you will get over a 95% on the paper guaranteed. Really nice lady and since writing 101 is required, I would definitely recommend taking this class.

Professor Pullum is a very kind and funny person, and very educated in sociology. She doesn't expect you to contribute all too much to discussion, you can usually get by with a comment or two each lecture. The class is mad boring but whatever. Definitely an easy A, take this class if you don't mind the boring nature of the material.

Amanda is well-versed in sociology but does not expect anyone to be. Discussions not too demanding and a little drab. Very pleasant professor who will help if needed. Didnt experience drastic gains in knowledge of writing or grassroots activism, but overall a decent choice for writing 101

Pullum's lectures are nap-inducing and she beats the interesting aspects of discussion to death. Overall the class was very boring and awkward due to her teaching style. Easy A if you can't find another writing101 class.

Prof. Long is kind and attentive to the students' needs like all the other two professors teaching this course. However, unlike two other professors teaching this course, Prof. Long does expect students to finish the readings before class. If you don't, you may feel a bit lost during class. The lecture is interesting and full of detailed examples.
She wants to see you put effort into topics that you care about and wants to hear about what you learned. She is very kind and lectures are interesting.

Prof Long Qian is a very knowledgeable expert in health systems. She requires lots of long readings, but skimming the longer readings is usually sufficient to participate in group discussions. She is very responsive in answering questions and willing to help or modify assignments to meet student needs. Highly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: DEFINITELY my favorite professor at Duke. She is knowledgeable, lively, and has so much presence. Very accessible outside of class, and always willing to talk to and help out her students (whether it's with something related to her class, or just about life in general). She allows unlimited rewrites, too, which is a perk.

Professor Quilligan is the most brilliant woman I have ever met. She has an immense knowledge base and can talk for hours (while never losing her listeners' interest!). She is funny, personable, and engaging. She challenges her students, certainly, but is always willing to offer guidance if you ask for it. TAKE HER CLASSES. Quill-dog rocks.

DO NOT take this class. Quilligan's lectures are incomprehensible. She rambles on about completely unrelated topics. Because a play is read each week, there is no in depth discussion or learning AT ALL. My section started with 100 students, and by the end only about 25 were attending.

Dr. Quilligan is, in a word, awesome. She is funny, engaging, and very passionate about her material. Very accessible outside of class and understanding about conflicts etc. *Do* the reading, as the exams will be much more of a pain if you haven't. Your grade is based on only a few assignments, so take everything seriously.

The TAs grade this class and are not fair at all. Quilligan refused to override their grade even though she told me it wasn't fair. I had high hopes for her, but I was very disappointed. She focused on the minutiae of Shakespeare's plays. Also, writing a paper on a performed play was impossible. Don't expect an A.

Quilligan is one of my favorites. She is like a magical fairy godmother of English who is always wiling to help. Somehow she even managed to inspire our class (most of whom were not theater people) to put on a successful Renaissance masque and enjoy it! English 90 has unlimited rewrites, and all of her classes have a reasonable workload. Recommend!
quilligan is hilarious...my favorite professor ever. really helpful and friendly. reasonable grader and reasonable work-load. take her classes!

She's a real character. It makes the classroom experience more alive. However, the only awkward thing is that she always asks questions that she has a specific answer to - not open ended. All papers can be re-written. Overall, a pleasant course, nothing taxing but still stimulating.

Quilligan's great; the class was fairly easy too if you took the time to rewrite papers. Really knowledgeable about the source material and historical contexts (from a slightly feminist angle), funny, warm and involving. Take her class if you like English-canon-type lit, acting projects or being invited to dinner at professors' houses.
She's very helpful and she lets you rewrite your papers so it's almost impossible not to get an A. She's really funny and she makes the material really interesting.

Prof. Quilligan amazing. I went into this class thinking that it was going to be hard (it covers Canterbury Tales--in its original English, Spenser's Faerie Queene, Midsummer Night's  Dream, Donne poetry, and Paradise Lost) and possibly boring. She made me love everything we've covered (I want to go back and read some of it for fun) and she's extre

She's the best teacher i've had at duke.  if you're an english major, you cant leave without taking a class with her. i knew it would be great when a medieval/renaissance lit course was packed on the first day at 8:30  :)

Worst professor I've ever had at my time at Duke (this is even worse given that I'm an engineer). This professor is new and genuinely doesn't care for his students. He also gives exams that are way too hard. For context, all other math 230 profs let you use a cheat sheet and a calculator, but Raquepas gives neither w/ exams. Avoid at all costs!!
Gives a lot of homework and is a very tough grader. Overall, he could use some work to improve his teaching skills.

Loved Prof. Raquepas. Probably one of the first math profs I have ever had that I confidently can say is a good prof. Very funny and approachable. Go to the lecture, and the grading policy is pretty lenient. If you can take 230 with him.

Ginny is an angel! It's a blessing to have her in your transition to Duke. The reading materials are well selected and thought-provoking. She gives very empathetic and thoughtful feedback on your reading responses. Yet, be prepared for some emotionally intense community engagements—it is authentic, so it's not a fairy tale.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Ginny is a very bubbly, talkative, and engaging person. As a professor, it is clear that she is well-versed in all the material, and, this sem, she even made course packs so we didn't have to use our e-print money for nightly readings! Class was definitely more engaging in the beginning of the sem, and the site visits weren't always enjoyable.

Ginny is super sweet and loves learners and learning. This class was pretty simple: read a bit and discuss in depth. Huge variety of topics are covered, like cell phones, sleep, neuroscience, and culturally-sensitive teaching, but the curriculum can feel somewhat unfocused. Great discussions, some lack of diversity of thought. Think, grow, bond!

Ginny is a super caring and funny person but this was a mostly boring class. Minimal work and essays were quite easy. Found that the second half of this semester, I could do literally nothing during class and still get an A. Participate at the beginning of the semester and you will be fine.

The best FOCUS professor! Dr. Ramirez-DelToro is passionate about teaching and cares about her students in every way. Her class was so much fun, and you get to engage in a lot of meaningful discussions. She values what you have to say and often lets the class lead discussions. Professors make or break the class! You won't regret taking this one.
Such a good class. Goated prof. Ez money.

Ginny is amazing! I took her class through the FOCUS program. While the class title insinuates that it is all about education, you will learn so much more. I genuinely looked forward to going to class every time. Ginny genuinely cares about her students, and is always open to help in any way possible. The workload is also very doable and engaging.

Ginny is amazing! I did not want to take the class, I was simply placed in it through FOCUS, but I am so glad I took it. Every class was amazing and she is simply like a friend in the class with us and is genuinely concerned about us as people, not just as students. I cannot recommend her enough and I wish I could have her as my prof in every class

The course description does not do justice just how incredible this class was. Awesome discussion, a fantastic classroom culture, and Ginny genuinely loves to learn! Every class is super fun, everybody brings their own experiences, you learn how to approach academia, and you can turn in your own thoughts for an A! 110% recommend Ginny for everyone.

This was the class that I was the least excited about coming into my first semester at Duke and it turned out to become the best 2.5 hours of my week! Ginny creates an environment where students can learn without fear of failure. Workload: Two papers, easy reading responses each class, AMAZING discussions, and free therapy. Totally take her!!!!!!
did not round 92.96

Professor Younes is actually very lecturer and cares about going above and beyond to provide the information needed to the students. If you take it with him, you will be better prepared for posterior courses in comp arch. He also takes academic honesty seriously, which I appreciate greatly.

Rabih does not know how to teach and this class, especially projects are a lot of work and hard. TAs and peers will carry you through it. Unlike other past profs, not only are the projects hard but so are the tests which are nothing like Sorins practices. Also, he is not lenient at all or clear. Take 250 with Sorin or otherwise good luck
I never understand anything Dr. Younes says. He is too smart.
He really struggled with engaging with students. This made it rather hard to grasp core concepts and his tests were significantly harder than previous semester.

Not a good ece250 professor at all. I went to every lecture but I should have stopped going because he made content more confusing. Homeworks are notoriously difficult for this class, but the professor didn't do a great job in getting students ready for those assignments.Ta's carry the class. Would not recommend Dr. Younes for this class at all.

Extremely inconsiderate. Students have to rely on TAs to learn anything remotely useful. If the wording or instructions on an exam question are confusing, TAs are explicitly instructed by Younes not to clarify. The saddest part is that the content could have been delivered in an engaging way, but that wasn't the priority this semester.

250 with Younes was a difficult and frustrating experience. The course focused heavily on memorizing/knowing specific technical details rather than testing for conceptual understanding, and the tests reflected this. Lectures felt dry, and with few chances to improve grades. Most students stopped attending lecture by the middle of the semester.

Harsh guy and an even worse lecturer. Does not allow students to ask clarifying questions during tests. Unknowledgeable and insecure about every concept he teaches. His goal this semester was fearmongering students rather than helping them learn. Inaccessible outside of class and tries to avoid student interaction as much as possible.
Do yourself a favor, don't take this class with Younes! Terrible experience.
Do not take this class with Younes! Quite possibly the worst class I've taken at Duke. Horrible lecturer and even worse grading system. Take with anyone else.

Lectures are super dull and not particularly relevant, practice exams don't match the actual exam. Dr. Younes seems uncomfortable teaching the class and seems unfamiliar with what content he wants students to learn and understand. Everything useful anyone learned in the class was from a TA.

ridiculously designed class that prioritizes memorization/digestion of 1,000+ lecture slides over meaningful learning. his grading is incredibly strict and unforgiving (no curves) and the long homework assignments only make the class a time sink. his inability to lecture well makes it so you rely on recitation/TAs to learn. do NOT take with younes!

Homework is hard but go to OH. Lectures are very boring and unclear. I got an A thanks to the amazing TAs, Recitation, and cramming everything. I don't feel like he made the course engaging enough to make me "care" about architecture. Felt like I crammed/memorized my way to an A. Tests aren't the worst but definitely tougher questions than the past

Smart guy but does not really care about teaching his students well. His lectures are boring and confusing, and the homework's (in general for this class) are difficult. I wouldn't recommend this class with Dr. Younes.

yeah hes a smart guy. at times condescending. no lecture recordings + lack of compassion behind an I treat you like adults policy. He bans clarifying exam questions, claiming exams already clear so u should have no questions. On fdoc, he flaunted some of you will drop. i've never had a prof be okay with that. doesnt promote love of learning.
Horrible Lecturer. Doesn't Respond to emails. Makes content harder to understand than it really is.

Don't take with Younes. Actually do, just don't go to lecture! You'll learn the same amount whether you go or not. I have an A in the class because of a couple very amazing discussion TAs. I basically learn everything that is needed by reading over the slides and going to discussion. Homework is time consuming but doable with TA office hours.

I have an A+ in the class right now, mostly thanks to recitation leaders. The exams are very easy in my opinion but the lectures explain not super clearly. The virtual memory ones were especially unclear. I think more engaging lectures would be helpful because it is hard to stay engaged.

Currently have an A+ in the class, but not bc of Rabih. Stopped going to lecture because he wastes everyone's time and doesn't know how to teach. Policies are extremely strict for no reason. HW isn't as difficult as everyone makes it out to be. Definitely easy/possible to get an A/A- in the class but if you don't have to take it with him, don't.

The worst teacher I've ever had at Duke- highly inconsiderate, tough grader with very little logic behind his grading criteria. Lectures are not thought out, homework is unnecessarily difficult, and he does a terrible job of providing additional resources. Smart guy, absolutely awful teacher.

(ECE 250) This is his first time teaching this class, and hopefully his last. The lectures are often unclear, and he speaks in a somewhat condescending manner. Doesn't answer questions during exams and sometimes during lectures. Intelligent person, but not the right fit for a "lower level" 200 ECE course. The course is hard, but he makes it harder.

This if for CS250 btw, Rabih is a horrible professor. He's a terrible lecturer and gives so much homework with very little consideration or accommodation. I'm sure he's a smart man but he has no clue how to teach. Would not recommend this class with Rabih.

"Decent" is the best word I can give, for lectures. Testcase for grading are not avaiiable to students, vague grading criteria, no answers for midterm and final, piazza often not answered in time (2 questions before final are still not answered after the final). Quoted from a fellow student, "It's an informal class with formal grading policy". LOL
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Did weekly quizzes, initially said that they're worth 0% of your grade and they're just there to help you understand the material, and at the end of the semester he took off 1% of your entire grade for every quiz you missed. Really smart person indeed, but don't expect to learn anything from lecture, the TA's teach you everything in the end.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Very understandable, great professor with amazing knowledge. Def rec him!

Professor Namazi is incredibly knowledgeable and effortlessly steers students through classroom discussions in a manner that strengthens their grasp on the demanding course material. The readings are heavy and the course is only graded on two essays, a presentation, and the final exam, but it generates a fantastic foundation for further studies.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Namazi is one of the nicest and most wonderful professors that we have. All his lectures are filled with interesting thoughts and approaches, and every contribution students make will be well appreciated. However, his feedback to essasy is very limted, unhelpful even, however, this was also the case with other instructors of this course.

Professor Rasoul Namazi is very understanding and will help you whenever you need it. Be proactive in his class and go to his office hours or stay after class to ask any questions you have. I enjoyed taking his class and hope one day I can take his other classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: This class is incredibly hard, but not necessarily because of Rabinoff or his teaching. He's a great guy and cares deeply about students, the material is just hard, and he covers most of its applications during the homework's (which is why they take 10-20 hours). Be prepared to put A LOT of time into this course, but Rabinoff is happy to support.

Professor Rabinoff talks very quickly in class field theory. However, he is extremely helpful in office hours. The content is great: it forced me to be acquainted with locally compact Hausdorff topological groups, which also show up in Tate's Thesis. He even helped me make sure I understand his notes in the next semester.

A solid professor who sometimes sings in class. Joe's been teaching MATH218 for years, and you can tell he's been continuously improving the course design.
Yes, workload is HEAVY but it really helps you build a strong foundation for future CS/math studies. Tests are easy if you do the homework yourself and understand his notes :D
Was a great professor who made sure to publish very clear notes. After taking his class, I decided I want to take more math classes at Duke.

Do NOT take this freshman year, made me question why I got accepted to Duke.. exam questions were either computationally hard (we could only use 4 function calculator) or extremely conceptual/abstract. Almost considered switching majors just so I could drop the class
Genuinely made me question my life & ruined my social life that semester because it took 15-20 hours each week to finish the homework
Homeworks take 16+ hours a week and the content after the first week makes you wonder why Duke accepted you in the first place. Rabinoff speaks fast and is condescending towards students.
Lots of homework that often took 15+ hours per week, even over break. Quizzes during discussion, exams are super hard. Definitely be prepared if this class is required

He's genuinely not a bad teacher. This class is great, well-structured, and very organized. The only thing is it is a lot of work for one class. Rabinoff is very knowledgeable and a very smart teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The professor is knowledgeable about mathematics but not very good at teaching. The homework doesn't really prepare for the test and is a time suck. Friends in 221 admit that even 221 is easier than 218 D-1. Terrible experience from the math dept. my first semester at Duke.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Joe's class made this my worst semester at Duke, and this is coming from someone who had pneumonia during finals last year. 218 is an awful class. The homework took at least 12 hours a week, contained problems the TAs couldn't solve, and were assigned over holidays. The only good thing about this class was the friends I made through trauma bonding.

Joe is accessible outside of class and always responds to ed posts. Lots of work but if you start early it's manageable. Just know this class will be your life for the semester. Don't expect to get an A (or a B even) unless you're really good at math. I worked harder in this class than any class I have ever taken and would've ended with a C at best
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Rabinoff's class is extremely difficult conceptually and moves at a very fast pace. Office hours are often necessary to understand the material, but even with office hours a lot of times I was left feeling clueless. Homeworks take extremely long, and even with studying the final was extremely hard. Try and take D-2
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Rabinoff is a professor that clearly cares about what he does, but his teaching style doesn't cater well to most of the students (including me) from what I hear. The lectures are essentially just repeating notes that he posts already (they're good notes), and homeworks outside of class can take upwards of 7-10 hours.

favorite person in Duke math! 218 is HW-intense (10-20 hrs/week, BFitz is 3-10 hrs/week). Pratt vs. Trinity 218: joe has longer HWs + similar exams (exam q's are fair); bfitz exams and HWs are short BUT exams are SIGNIFICANTLY harder (applying concepts to previously unseen q's). joe is also super nice and accessible in OH - ask him q's about HW!

15-20 hours of work per week. Some problem sets had upwards of 80+ questions. Rabinoff cares a ton about this course and will do everything possible to help you succeed, however you should avoid this course unless you have an easy semester and hate having free time. Grading is very reasonable on homework and exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: 15+ hours of homework every week. Gives you good practice for the midterms/finals but is tough to balance on top of other classes. Midterms and final felt discouraging with time constraints and was hard to demonstrate everything I knew. Lectures feel rushed but lecture notes are always posted online and are super helpful. Office hours are a must.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
DO NOT TAKE!!!

This class sucks. Homeworks are WAY too long. Each take at a minimum 10 hours. According to Joe, we should be happy about that! Lectures are useless because Joe just goes through the notes he posts online and rewrites them on the board. He crams way too much content into short classes. Too much learning on my own.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Worst class I have taken at Duke

This class is awful. Hard content mixed with 1000mph lectures and 8 hour weekly problem sets, which were both tedious and conceptually difficult. Every year students complain about the homework sets, yet nothing changes. If it weren't for office hours I would have failed, but even with them this class seems hopeless.

Prof. Rabinoff is funny and caring. has beautiful notes & well organized course website online. Very good at visualizing linear algebra, talks very fast and I learnt a lot from his lectures. Homeworks are heavy but they really helped prepare for the exams. The exams are in the exactly same format as the practice tests. His OH is also very helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: that was not fun gl
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The only thing that would prepare you for this class is taking a linear algebra course beforehand. The homeworks took more than 8 hours every week, and required office hours at least once a week or other forms of extensive collaboration with other students/TAs. Exams were much harder than homework. If you don't have to take this course, DON'T.

Class covers good content but really ramps up and gets annoying a few weeks in. Homework is long and tedious. Midterms/final were eh but I felt like I was just solving questions without understanding anything
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Joe Rabinoff is probably one of the most organized professors I've had ever since coming to Duke. His class is incredibly streamlined and his notes are gorgeous. Yes, the homework is quite substantial, but start it as soon as it comes out and come to office hours with specific questions and it's definitely doable. He really cares about his students

I LOVE JOE. He talks SO FAST and covers SO much linear algebra, but it is a VERY rewarding class if you put in the work to actually work at it and understand what's going on. The homeworks are extremely long, so it is in your best interest to start them ahead of time. Joe will always help you work out tough problems in OH too. go. i will miss joe.

The professor was good at delivering the content but the course itself is extremely difficult. It's a lot of hours without a guaranteed return. It honestly depends on how well you do the homework and whether you're good at recreating that on the test.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Rabinoff should be respected for his ability to pack in so much content in just one semester, all while making sure students understand every part. Sometimes I found his lectures a bit uninspiring though and combining that with 8+ hour homework sets each week, 3 midterms, and a difficult final makes this course a grueling marathon.

On and on and on. Every time I did a 218 HW set, I wanted to slowly give up. So long and always tedious, thank god for Ed. You don't have to pay too much attention during lecture since Joe's Notes are always posted, and the midterms aren't too bad after you finish the HW...

Rabinoff speaks at the speed of light. But, he posts his notes online and knows his stuff. He is very accessible outside of class. But, his tests are tough. Fortunately, he archives all old tests, and reuses questions, so take advantage of that. Office Hours are a MUST for homeworks.
Grades: 45% Midterm, 30% Final, 20% HW, 5% Discussion.

He might be a good lecturer, but he's been making the tests, course content, and homework harder with every year. The exams are really tight on time and leave you feeling like you couldn't demonstrate everything you know. The homework is also quite time-consuming. I like math usually but this class made me feel so discouraged
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Rabinoff is an AMAZING lecturer who articulated tricky, abstract math ideas very clearly. This is probably the first time since I was a hs sophomore when I felt this engaged and actually understanding everything at a conceptual level and not just memorization. His computer demos were also a huge plus in helping me visualize.

Rabinoff definitely does his part to help students learn -- I asked 10+ questions on Ed every week, and he always replied in the thread until an understanding has been reached. This was great since it was difficult to attend office hours. That all said, be wary of the homework as it can be a lot and take time, so it's best to start it by Friday!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: You will learn linear algebra really well from this course. The question, however, is do you truly want to learn linear algebra really well? The answer is probably no because youd just take math 221 then. Its a really great class but I cant completely recommend it because the workload is exceptionally high, probably higher than your work ethic.

Rly time consuming class because of long HW (avg 16 problems) every week and 3 midterms. But you definitely learn a lot if you put in the time and effort/keep up w/ content!! His lectures are really fast-paced, hard to keep up w/. To succeed, I recommend going to office hours, and getting started on HW EARLY.

You'll drown in work for no reason. Problem sets took minimum 10 hours and he would assign one every week but since the problem set is based on the weekly lectures, you really only have like 4 days to do it. Don't take this class unless you have to, take Math 202 instead!
Absolutely garbage professor. Teaches things way out of order and makes the class more confusing than necessary. I had better luck learning this all from khan academy. Avoid at all costs.

The homeworks are all extremely long and difficult, but they prepare you so well for the exams that I barely had to study at all. Professor Rabinoff gives interesting lectures and makes the material understandable. He's also fun to talk to and cares about his students. You'll have to work for an A, but it's absolutely doable if you do the HW.

Professor Rabinoff is amazing! His lectures were very clear and he made difficult concepts easy to follow and digest. He also had many office hours to help his students; I really appreciated that and I strongly recommend going to OH! While there was a lot of homework and it was challenging, they were useful in preparing for midterms and the final.

Joe was a great professor and overall a kind person! He delivers the content in an extremely clear and digestible manner. I did think that the HW was a little excessive at times, but it does prepare you really well for the exams. 10/10 would recommend!

Most of critques are on the workload but the HWs are so in depth that it makes studying for mt/final a lot easier. He's a solid guy and really cares about his students. Don't let the amount of work in a math class dissuade you lol, if you need 218 for a req rabinoff is your man
Good lecturer but he assigns so much homework. Exams are much harder than practice.
Insane amount of work and exams are unreasonably harder than the practice. Never again.
You will drown in work for no reason.

He's one of the better math professors here at Duke but midterms and quizzes don't really prepare you for the final. It's very easy to fall behind in this class and don't know where your grading stands. No need to come to class or participate to do well though as you are only graded based on quizzes and tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Mike clocks in as the greatest graphics professor I've ever had.

The goat. 
He wrote the textbook. He is the textbook.

He's one of those lifetime professors you remember for years to come. He has a contagious passion for analysis, and a teaching acumen. Lectures were prerecorded with class as a time to discuss problems and solidify concepts. I was never a fan of flipped classroom, but this class changed my mind. Also, a very fair grader who sets you up for success.

Dr. Reed is an absolute gem in the math department. He cares deeply about his student, helps you understand the true meaning of analysis, and is a seasoned lecturer who can make a topic as hard as real analysis digestable. My only complaint is he doesn't teach more subjects. Easily, the best math professor I've had in my life.

My fav prof at Duke. He's been around for ages, so he has a great feel for his students' needs in the class. He's genuinely caring and endlessly accessible outside of class. As long as you're present in class and earnestly trying, it's literally not possible to earn below a B. Quiz q's are directly from HW, tests are easy, except the last question.

Best lecturer I have had at Duke. Makes material super clear and understandable. Course expectations are crystal clear, and if you do what is required you're almost guaranteed an A. 1 quiz every week, 3 questions drawn from that weeks hw. Midterms are very fair, drawn from hw as well. He's very kind and acc, take Real Analysis with him!
