He was a great professor. I absolutely loved his class, so interesting. We did a lot of presentations which was really useful. He gave great feedback and had great stories. Absolutely recommend taking a class with him as a professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Class had asynchronous lectures with three 30-minute synchronous sessions a week. I had a different professor for the synchronous sessions. Dr. Reeds lectures were great, very clear. I feel like the course was well paced and material built on itself.

Probably one of the best lecturers I have ever taken. Real analysis and proofs were tough for me, but he made all the concepts easy to understand and intuitive. He explains the idea behind the proof before writing it out and genuinely seemed to want students to learn and appreciate the beauty of math.

Dr. Reed provided no benefit to my education. It was an online course during COVID-19 season and he was terribly unaccommodating and insensitive to the problems that his students were facing. Beyond that, his math seminar course consisted of very little math and absolutely no discussion. Grades based on your English ability rather than competence.

Grading criteria is very unclear. He offers no feedback on assignments until after and tells us to figure it out ourselves even when asked directly for guidance. Then he grades us however he likes. Grades are on your presentation and English skills, not content. He's very nitpicky, cares only about how you present, and offers no help on content.
A very good teacher. Moves slowly so that all students can keep up. Problem sets/ quiz every week.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Overall good experience in this class. Has a lot of experience in his field, so that is interesting. He is always making time to meet with us if we need help. After spring break, is when the work comes. Not impossible, but still a lot. The final will require some calculus, but there are practice tests. Not a fan of the final paper; c'est la vie.

I would absolutely recommend this class to anyone interested in the topic. Professor Reed is an incredible teacher in that he challenges students to think beyond the limits of their knowledge. The first half of the course is light on homework, but be ready to work in the second half - two presentations, a twenty page final paper, and a final exam.

Awesome professor. We cover very interesting topics in seminar and he cares a lot about us. However, he has high expectations, especially compared to all other first year seminars. An "excellent" final would get an A minus. A bit ambiguous on what he expects, which sucks since we only have one shot at the final and final paper. SO MUCH WORK.

Professor Reed is a great guy who cares about his students.  Class is incredibly interesting and he is engaging and funny. However, second half of semester will hit you like a ton of bricks.  Expects an incredible amount out of his students for a first year seminar.  If you want to learn a lot go for it, but don't if you want an easy class.
Hard class, but absolutely awesome professor. Truly cares about teaching and takes the time to explain how to think through the concept of a proof, not just how to remember one. Highly recommend!

This is the hardest class I will ever take at Duke. Professor Reed is a very good teacher, but once you get behind you will always be behind. I only understood maybe 1/100 of all the stuff he taught us. The lectures were impossibly hard to understand. Don't take this class unless you are really strong in math, otherwise you will live to regret it.

Great guy.  Will be more than willing to help you IF you have a very specific question.  Most of the time he just kind of sits and smiles and stares at you while you jumble around trying to figure out exactly what it is you don't understand.  Loves his job, loves his work.  Very straightforward.

The best professor I've had at Duke.  Clearly loves to teach and very enthusiastic about class.  Very encouraging (especially to females in mathematics).  Math 139 is rumored to be very hard, but he makes it do-able.  I love Dr. Reed!
waste of my time

theres a grading contract where if you do everything you get an a+. its not that much work. Shes nice and youll prolly learn a lil bit but not that much. If you mess up the grading contract she'll let you make it up. Shes nice.

Great professor, actually cares about her students. Class is very stress-free and low homework. She has a grading contract that essentially states if you don't miss class and don't have missing assingments you get an automatic A in the class. Easy grade, fun professor, would recommend to anybody.

I took this class fall 2022 when I just came to the US. My English was not good at all, and she was very patient with me. She was willing to meet/email outside of class to walk me through the assignments and ensure I understood the instructions. She is one of those teachers you want to have at least once during your academic journey.

I took Writing 203S, and it's been one of my favorite classes. The grading is very clear from the beginning, and the emphasis is on the effort you put in. She gives great feedback tailored to your project and is always willing to help. If you're interested in writing studies and want an introduction into doing research, I recommend this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Had her Writing 203s - this class was helpful. Great teacher who clearly leads the class in a lighthearted manner. Grading is very clear starting from the first day, and Dr. Scharnhorst gives constructive feedback for improvement throughout the semester. Great class if you want to complete research while at Duke - Dr. Scharnhorst is wonderful.

1924-2024: Writing at Duke was extremely boring; however, this class was a GPA booster because as long as you followed the grading contract you could get an A+. The whole beginning of the class was basically a waste of time so don't do the readings and be prepared to write a group "research" paper. I would retake the class simply for the GPA boost.

Cannot complain at all given the grading contract, which essentially gives you a guaranteed A if you do all the work on time (and by do all the work, I mean "reach the wordcount"). That being said, there is a lot of reading and archival research can take a long time and feel rather pointless, all things considered.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Dunno why such bad reviews about this class, since its basically a GPA booster as if you turn in everything you are guaranteed an A+(as long as it's related to the prompt and not just bs). Professor is sweet and kind, but don't expect to learn a lot from this class. The final project can either be really fun if u like archival research or boring.

Writing at Duke: 1924-2024 has a grading contract so it's not hard to get an A but there is sooo much reading for an unnecessary amount of responses during the first half of the semester and the second half is entirely a group project with very limited guidance/oversight to balance workload between group members. Easy enough class but a time drain.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Nice prof but total waste of time. My writing didn't improve at all and I disliked the group project format (archival research paper that ended up being more rambling than prose). Individual papers would have been more helpful than the never-ending & useless "reflections." Grading schema (turn everything in and get an A) was nice but demotivating.

Dr. S is personable but curriculum was not super. Big group project wasn't given enough time and its more work than other writing 101s. Felt like both too much and too little guidance in class but she's nice though so I did learn some interesting things. Class periods are run too slowly
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Seemed really cool in class, but got in my face once after class, and accused me of lying. I did not appreciate that and I should have filed a complaint against him for inappropriate behavior towards student. I've never been accosted by any other professor.

Seemed really cool in class, but got in my face once after class, and accused me of lying. I did not appreciate that and I should have filed a complaint against him for inappropriate behavior towards student. I've never been accosted by any other professor.

Ricky was a great professor. He understood that people were taking the class for the Econ requirement, and he taught and graded accordingly. The average grade when I took the class was right on the line b/w B+ and A-.

Cool guy, knows the name of everyone in huge lecture, but sometimes makes things more confusing than they are. Very responsive via email. I liked Ricky but disliked this class because it was AP Stat all over again.  Never used textbook except for a few HW problems.  Take this class over 101 - the "calculus basis" is not as bad as it seems.

Ricky is a great guy.  He teaches the material well and makes it really difficult for you to do poorly in the class. Homework, quizzes, and labs (which are basically gimme grades) are half your final average.  If you have to take Stat 103, make sure you get Ricky.
Awesome professor
Great Class, she makes the lectures interesting and learning about BioAnth very interesting. I would Highly Recommend taking any class she teaches

labs were great and quizzes not bad (20 questions), tests from slides although i thought the tests were too much useless memorization from the slides rather than complete understanding of the material. could be a little touchy sometimes but mostly nice
She's GREAT and really knows her stuff. Who couldn't love osteology after taking a course with Dr. Rhodes

VERY dry lectures.  Labs are really cool.  Quizzes are only 20 questions and are straightforward from lab.  Straight memorization of slides will set you up nicely for tests.  She really knows her bones and can be fun in lab, but her lectures can improve.  Definitely a good class to take alongside BAA 147L (Bodies of Evidence)
Very knowledgeable. If you're interested in the concept of the class (osteology) then definitely take it.  If you're not, the class is going to be very boring.
Not the nice guy that he appears to be.

Like no other professor at Duke. Taking Dan's class is such a unique and fun experience. His grading criteria is a bit unclear, but once you stop worrying about grades it is awesome. Dan wants all of his students to have fun and learn. A lot of the time (most of the time), Dan will stray from the actual subject matter of the class.

If you've ever had an old professor who's clearly brilliant but has a few screws loose, then you might have an idea of what Dan is like. He knows a lot about the subject he specializes in, but I don't think I walked out of a single lecture with a clear idea of what I was supposed to have learned. One word to describe his style: scatterbrained.

The depth of his insight, rivaled only by the depth of his beard, is a breath of fresh air for the teaching community. He wears his mind on his sleeve & lives every moment  with the conviction of showing students the beauty & mystery of asking "why?" He gave me a foundation of not only knowledge, but more importantly interest in pursuing my project

How he insists students address him should give it away: Dr. Dan is the most approachable professor I've had at Duke. He's your friend - a true child at heart. If you're honest with yourself and honest with him, you will love every minute of his classes. He's loves to ask why things happen and impassions you to do the same. Quirky in the best way.
He is the man!!! best at Duke
DR. DAN IS THE MAN! AMAZING
AMAZING!!!!! Best professor at Duke.
Dr. Rego was amazing! She was very inspirational. She clearly wanted her students to succeed and offered very good feedback. Ask her about her research!
Good professor. Very nice and gives good feedback. Projects aren't very difficult. The course has a lot of readings though.

The readings and course material were intriguing, and she does her best to make sure the in-class discussions are as engaging as possible. As a freshman in FOCUS, a full-fledged research paper can be intimidating, but she guides you through the process well. Prof. Rego also uses engaging, unorthodox teaching methods throughout the semester.

Professor Rego is super sweet and makes it so easy for you to succeed in her class. Class could be a little dry but the material itself for this class (writing about performance) was something I found interesting. She is easy to get a hold of and super understanding. Everyone did well.

Professor Rego is so sweet. The class that I took with her introduced me to the world of ethnography, which was super interesting to me. She gives a lot of flexibility with assignments, which can be difficult at first, but later you learn that you learn from it. Also work load isn't too bad, just make sure you participate. HIGHLY recommend the clas

a monotonous, repetitive, dry, frustratingly boring, waste of time. She's sweet. The workload is not bad. But if you are looking to be improved, challenged, gripped, enlightened, or anything of the sort - this isn't it.

Professor Rego is very chill and relaxed. Work load isn't heavy and her class seems like one of the better Writing classes from what I've heard. She gives good feedback and is willing to help students, but her class didn't really improve my writing. She cares about students and overall her class was a good experience and solid choice.
Professor Rego is extremely nice and fair, and it's fascinating to hear about her anthropological research. Definitely try to get into her class!

The class was the single most boring class I've ever taken. That being said, the teacher is also one of the nicest, most lenient teachers I've ever had too. It's a toss-up. Basically, you will learn a little. And also catch up on your sleep.

By far the easiest class offered at Duke. You literally can do the bare minimum and receive an A. But, attendance is mandatory and she has a monotone, heavy voice that sends you to sleep. You are also not allowed to use computers in class. If you want to improve your writing, do not take it. If you want an A, this is the best W20 there is.

Great class. Take WRITING 20 with Rego. No textbook, and there aren't many readings to begin with. Freedom to write about many topics for the two major papers, and the revision process almost ensures good grades on final drafts. Discussions usually are interesting. Rego is very approachable, helpful, and super lenient. Make sure you participate.

The content of the class is pretty interesting. I definitely recommend this course to any freshman who needs to fulfill their W20 requirement. She is a very fair grader and lets you be pretty creative.
Such an awesome teacher.

Just a good class overall. Prof Rego picked really good readings, but her comments on your paper were not always  helpful. Still, she will read your paper as many times as you want, she's super nice,  and easy compared to other teachers. Take her!

I highly recommend W20 Translating the Culture Shock, especially if you're interested in learning about how you view other cultures. This professor is great- she doesn't force class participation, is approachable if you have question, and genuinely wants you to learn!

I loved Prof Rego.  She made class interesting and didn't pressure people to talk in discussions.  Her class was laid back and interesting, and it wasn't too hard. She was really nice in class and outside of class.

Likes to give students lots of room for creativity.  Has very interesting assignments that force you to try a number of writing styles.  Fair and pretty generous grader as long as the effort is there.
Great teacher.  Very passionate.  Allows students to write about things that interest them.  Does a great job of easing into the workload so that students aren't overwhelmed.

Prof. Rego is a really cool teacher.  She makes good class discussions and the material was really facinating for my topic: Cannibalism to Anorexia.  I'd take her for any class because she is so nice and friendly to all students.  Don't hesitate if you're considering her class, she's definately a great teacher.

Prof. Rego is such a cool lady. Her class was so interesting, and if you just do what she says and make good changes in all your rewrites you will get a good grade. Class participation is important too. I would definitely try to get her as a teacher again!
Easy class, sometimes interesting material.  It can get somewhat boring at times though.
easy class if you do the work. it can be boring at times, but she is really flexible and easy to talk to.

Great teacher, I really liked her. She is an interesting Cultural anthropologist, it really brings alot to the class. The writing was pretty doable overall. Not a ton of writings. Good in class discussion. You get to watch a video every now and then too.
It was an easy class. As long as you do all the work and do it right, you will be happy with your grades. It is boring sometimes but still a doable class.
While she is nice and fair with grading, and overall the class is easy, it is by far one of the most boring classes I've ever taken.  A struggle because of the tedium.
Flipped class format, class discussions are repetitive and professor isn't very open to student's ideas
don't recommend
Rude, not very considerate of student's issues and has an almost arbitrary grading system. Get ready to have no clue what your grade is until the very end of the semester.

The school year is over and I've gotten only 1 grade back out of our 6 papers. She's very difficult to reach outside of class and also not good at replying to emails. I had no feedback from my other assignments to write the final paper so I have no idea what my grade/grades will be :) Class seemed interesting at first but then just got repetitive.

This class was really informative, and I greatly enjoyed the topics we covered throughout. The amount of writing may be a lot if you come solely from a STEM background, so you will definitely need to manage your time. Also, the lectures can sometimes get repetitive. Overall, this class is one I'd recommend to every student across all disciplines.
Amazing professor, best professor I've ever had. The class is so informative and is also not too difficult in terms of grading. Very cool.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Salsman is without a doubt my favorite professor at Duke. I have taken two classes with him and both have been exceptional. If you are really interested in PPE he is the best professor to take a class with. Genuinely wants to foster discussion and challenge peoples ideas.

Discussion based class on interesting topics. Each topic has readings and a short reflection, then everyone discusses the topic. Conversations can focus on the readings, recent news or any thoughts, really interesting class and Professor Salsman encourages all viewpoints. Learned a lot from other people in the class and Salsman, I recommend taking!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: A nuanced and balanced presentation of all sides of the political spectrum. Creates compelling lectures, going at his own pace, and adding his own insights and comments. He isn't afraid to call a spade a spade and invites disagreement. In a space where Duke students are getting spoonfed the same perspectives, he brings a breath of fresh air.

Very insightful and balanced in his perspectives. Approachable, kind, and even open to discussing things outside of class! The content is rich in thought provoking ideas and is a great introduction to the intersection between Politics and Economics. He encourages students to question what they learn and stay open-minded. A Great Prof!

Presents content in a skewed libertarian lens. "Other sides" are presented as strawmen, drawing from one thinker. The professor's argumentation is surface-level, lackluster, and does a disservice to all ends of the political spectrum. He solely asserts others are wrong, replacing reasoning with intimidation in lecture and when answering questions.

The readings seem out of place for an introductory course; the quizzes/midterm and trickiness of the questions (with vague wording) were frustrating; despite arguing that liberal professors are "brainwashing" their students, his lectures (which include non-credible sources such as the Heritage Foundation) are more biased than almost any other

I took the PPE capstone class with Prof Salsman, and 85 has a very clear discussion-based class structure covering a wide variety of topics. He gave us lots of flexibility in choosing topics we hope to discuss and write about, grader our work very generously, and provided thoughtful feedback. It's definitley one of my favorite classes at Duke!
Amazing professor and person. Truly cares about his students and pushes them to debate and question their own opinions/beliefs.
The actual goat. Highly recommend. He's a genius, lectures were so interesting. He's such a chiller and seriously unlike any professor I had. 100% take
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: He lectures very boring and those who participate in class probably have the exact same views as him--his lectures are him summarizing the readings, and it is like watching paint dry and there is no point in going to class after the midterm, which he administers too early, and overall, he is just a professor who I learned absolutely nothing from.

The course material itself is alright. Grading is reasonable. The main issue is that Salsman injects his opinions heavy handidly to significant detriment to the class, obviously a little bit is to be expected but, for example, his denial of anthropogenic climate change, meant avoiding real questions surrounding treatment of the environment.

I've had Salsman for two classes at Duke, once my freshman year (Polsci89s) and the PPE capstone. Both times he's been a great professor not just through explicit course material/themes, but also by facilitating reasoning and evidence-based discussions. Reading and writing work is manageable and necessary for a full understanding of material.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Highly recommend

insane amount of dense reading for homework (often not covered during lecture), dull and rambling lectures, extremely political/partisan bias to what is taught/assigned, vague and unclear quiz questions, does not respond to emails and is unaccessable, and is rude and condescending answering questions
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Salsman's class is relatively easy and expectations are made very clear. His lectures and lessons, however, are very right-leaning; our global health unit felt like an anti-masking soapbox.
Prof Salsman is so down-to-earth. Loved the way how he treated all of his students!

The worst professor I've had at Duke. Feels like he could not care less about this class. TA's had control of the class and had ridiculous grading standards. If you get a multiple choice question wrong it detracts from your grade. Prof. was once 30 min late to class. I would rather have the plague then take this class with Salsman again.

Professor Salsman was an amazing professor! I loved this class and him as a professor specifically. I am thinking about switching to Political Economy after taking this course, and it is because of Salsman. Couldn't recommend him more.
Amazing. Loved the intro 89S Capitalism For and Against class I took with him.

Inherently a bad teacher that has no patience for students and thinks too highly of himself. Not a pleasant person to be around, and very rude regarding questions or concerns about the class. Extremely strict on policy, worries more about following his own guidelines than ensuring students learn the content.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor was always very eager to participate and loved to listen to students' opinions and what we had to say. This class was a seminar and was a non stop conversation full of understanding and respectfulness.

Salsman was great, I took a first-year seminar and it was really light on workload. Class consisted of a weekly, take home, online quiz (open note) based on readings, participation in discussions, and a final paper. He was nice and willing to work with you to help you with your paper, and he wasn't biased in grading based on differing poli views.

Nice guy, well read, and well intentioned. However, the class glazes over an insane amount of content and does not go into depth on nuances, and he selectively uses every piece of material to support his views. This class has pushed me further to the ideological left than any liberal professor I've ever had.

Probably one of the worst professors I've had. He is a lecturer, not a professor, and is not hired by the department; hence why he has so little incentive to teach well and listen to student's concerns. He is not responsive to emails nor generally available. And the course is just an ideological argument for capitalism. The content is very biased.

One of the worse classes I've ever taken. Salsman is a right-wing ideologist who sings the praises of capitalism. The class is one-sided and he straw mans any view he disagrees with. Accommodation concerns were not taken seriously and he does not reply to email. Avoid, avoid, avoid.

Professor Salsman was a very interesting professor with a lot of interesting outlooks. The course covered a wide array of topics, and he did a great job analyzing issues from every perspective. Highly recommend this class looking to get an intro into econ/polisci.

Prof Salsman is a highly educated, kind, and humorous professor who values student opinions and fosters respectful debates. He lives out the pluralism he teaches, allowing diverse views while never condemning differing opinions. Dedicated to students' success, his course provides a strong foundation for meaningful discussions. Highly recommended.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Very conservative

Salsman is a passionate expert on the subject. He is opinionated and often "correct" answers correspond with his views. He discusses all perspectives though and encourages debate when there is time. The class is lecture heavy and they're online. Weekly open-book online quizzes are easy. I would recommend Salsman for a seminar also.

I will give it to him; he is passionate about capitalism! He is qualified to teach this class, and apart from the readings, which most people don't do, the class was not too difficult. On the other hand, he let his personal beliefs flood his teaching, which was often offensive or plain out wrong. His moral compass is determined by capitalism, yikes

This is the gateway class for Political Economy and it was supposed to give students exposure to various perspectives and topics within PE. Unfortunately, Salsman imposed his own views on students. He teaches every single topic with a clear right-wing leaning and preconceptions. I recommend taking this class with another professor.

I really enjoyed Professor Salsman's class! It made me think from a ton of new perspectives I've never considered and question things that I used to consider black or white. He is a very entertaining lecturer and quite the character. There is a lot of reading, but you are fine doing the bare minimum to still do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very interesting lectures, content not that difficult to grasp, leans conservative but presents all opinions

Professor Salsman is well-read and principled. His lectures can become boring as they are heavily derivative of the readings; however, if you find a balance between doing all the homework or doing none of it, you can stay engaged. He is wonderful to talk with and always open to good intellectual debate. Encourages intellectual diversity.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Salsman provokes very interesting conversation, but sometimes he feels accusatory if you don't agree with him (more conservative). If you're mindful of that and don't let it get to you and stand your ground you can learn a lot and have good debate. Sometimes the class got repetitive within the 2.5 hours if people weren't engaged.

Salsman is very knowledgeable and a good lecturer, which makes classes interesting. It is pretty test heavy (I think the midterm and final made up 65% of our grade) and the midterm was pretty difficult. The final is a bit easier, and he ended up curving grades. He is very clearly a strong libertarian, but is also a great professor.

Really enjoyed this class! There were online weekly reading quizzes that were a lot easier if you went to class, 2 papers, a midterm, and a final. Never had a super excessive workload for this class, I would spend typically 3 hours outside of class working on assigned reading materials. Prof's super engaging and interesting, 100% would take again.

he is right-leaning, but its not true that you have to conform to his views to do well in the class - i wrote papers left-leaning and got great grades. Salsman is big on "logic and reasoning," so he evaluates not on content but logical process. tbh its good if you disagree with his takes because he makes you explain why you believe what you do

Salsman loves participation and informed students. Take a stance, and make sure what you are saying is unique and insightful. Pay attention because Salsman will inform you on many things the average college student will never hear at Duke. He provides a unique take on Capitalism and allows you to see the system from many viewpoints.

Professor Salsman is one of the best professors I have ever had. He will push you to challenge your arguments and will help you become a better conversationalist. Such a nice, reasonable, engaging person. His class was everything and more that I hoped it would be.
Thought-provoking class enjoyed readings and discussions, difficult to get a good grade but not to much work

This class could've been good. It was supposed to give student exposure to a range of perspectives, but unfortunately Salsman imposed his own views on students and even marked students down for having opposing views. Half through the class I began pretending to have his political views and suddenly my grades went up. Coincidence, probably not.

The discussions in this class were awesome. Professor Salsman always facilitated great conversations with great topics. One of the only classes at Duke that you could speak openly no matter which side of the debate you're on. Salsman also was super accommodating when I had issues or needed help. Would definitely take again!

I've taken two classes with Professor Salsman and both were fantastic. He genuinely considers every idea you present and always will discuss it with you. Be ready to have everything you say challenged, but in a way that makes you think deeper about the world and its systems.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: My favorite class at Duke so far. Great for those interested in politics, finance, business, etc. Professor is openly libertarian but opens the floor for opposing views, even brought in contrasting guest speakers. Grading is easy if you put in moderate effort, quizzes are based on posted slides, test was solely from lectures, straightforward essays

Prof Salsman creates a very welcoming and forgiving environment for students to engage in discussions/debates regardless of skill level and understanding of topic. He is also one of the most flexible and caring professors I've encountered at Duke. Don't let the long syllabus intimidate you: taking polsci449 w/ Prof Salsman is worth it.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Prof. Salsman was an excellent professor in my seminar on capitalism. He did a great job at facilitating discussions on the various units within our course, and presented both sides of the debate over capitalism objectively and fairly, which is often lacking in other Duke courses in the field.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Professor Salsman's PPE Capstone class was a highlight of my final semester of senior year. It was unfortunate that it had to be conducted over Zoom, but, nonetheless, it was actually one of the better online classes I've had. He's really skilled at facilitating discussion and encouraging students to debate with each other.

Prof. Salsman's lectures provide a good basis for understanding philosophy and political theory. Sometimes the lectures were dry, though he incorporates interesting examples and sometimes has guest speakers. A frustrating thing is that he can be dismissive of regrade requests but ultimately will help you out as long as it is reasonable.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: My second class with Prof. Salsman, an outstanding professor. Teaches very neutrally while exposing students to many perspectives, creating an environment in which even the most controversial issues can be discussed civilly and analytically. Very approachable and fair. Always willing to meet with students. Passionate about PPE and a great teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Interesting readings but would not recommend taking with Salsman as he teaches with a clear (right-wing) political allignment. I think this fundemental PPE material would be better taught by someone who can explain and argue different perspectives. However, the class is easy(ish) so if that means more to you than learning then I recommend it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Salsman's PPE capstone class is the perfect dynamic for your last Duke PPE chapter. Each week's readings are very helpful for the intellectually stimulating discussions, but also for extracurricular knowledge. The final project provides you with a blank slate for you to research any topic that interests you under a PPE framework.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great class, discussion set up helped me learn a lot. Many classes set out for the students to learn from one another but it ends up being something involved, as a group project. With grades being less emphasized and learning at the forefront, I felt like I could go to class with the goal of picking up something new, not checking off a box.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Salsman is one of the most knowledgable professors I've had. However, lack of rubrics for commentaries (35% of grade) and lack of feedback (only ever graded commentaries in two clusters throughout the semester) makes this aspect of the class difficult. Would even call it subjective as his political alignment is clear, and his grading reflects such.

Distribution of Justice/Prisoner's Dilemma is a very interesting course if you are considering taking the PPE certificate. Although the readings are quite dense, lectures relate heavily to current event, and the grading is very fair. Through hard work and keeping up with the material and A is definitely obtainable in this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Prof salsman is probably one of the best professors I've had so far. I've taken two classes with him - capitalism seminar and a distributive justice/prisoner's dilemma course. No doubt, his classes are hard. There's a lot of dense readings that you really have to understand, but he is so caring, knowledgeable, and a great lecturer. Please take him!

Professor Salsman is amazing to speak with, provides insightful analysis, and comes at problems with experience and critical thinking. He will debate and discuss with anyone. Really a great person to have for advice, insight, and conversation.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Great professor that is really passionate about the material and cares about his students.

Really enjoyed the class! Decided to take the PPE Gateway online and it was amazing! Salsman's lectures made taking an online class in the middle of the summer much more palatable. Graded by 7 quizzes (multiple choice), 5 commentaries (750 word reflections on a topic), and a final. Grading was fair. Highly recommend!

I took this class as just another credit for my philosophy minor, but Professor Salsman's class convinced me to switch to the PPE program. He's an incredibly caring and great professor. As a non-American, the class was centered around the US quite a lot. However, Professor Salsman always appreciated when I brought my international perspective.

Prof. Salsman is a great professor and someone who can be easily reached outside of class. He's very passionate about what he teaches and the readings he assigns are well incorporated into his lectures. I would recommend doing the readings because not only is it helpful during lectures but also some test questions come from the readings themselves.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Salsman is a good guy, but lectures can definitely get stale. Took for Prisoner's Dilemma so 75% of the lectures were done by Munger which definitely helped. Don't let this deter you from taking his class, just know lectures can feel long.

Dr. Salsman is very insightful and has a ton of experience in his field. He's overall a kind professor and willing to meet students outside the classroom. Be prepared for dense readings, a tough midterm test, and reaction papers graded by TAs. But he also gives extra credit points, so if you work hard, you should be able to get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Obscene amounts of reading and useless lectures. Salsman claims he is fair, but half of the midterm (C average for class) tested students on specific lines from the readings, and his papers were graded arbitrarily by the TAs. He artificially curved the class by giving everyone 3 extra credit points and grading the final easily (92 median).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Salsman is a very knowledgable professor who is very passionate about his work. The course is graded on a mid-term, final, weekly quizzes, and two reaction papers. The midterm was very difficult, with questions on specific quotes from readings months before. The reaction papers were graded by the TAs with ambiguous grading criteria.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Unnecessarily hard, with many test questions on random quotes and not larger themes. Average on midterm was a C. Reaction papers graded ambiguously by TAs. Professor Salsman is very knowledgable in his field and challenges the status quo in academia, which is refreshing. But, lectures can get quite dry and boring. Much better one on one.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Hard Class but Professor Salsman is a pretty awesome professor

Dr. Salsman is so interesting and directed me to pursue political economy even further. He's a bit tough and the median grade was below a B on the midterm, but the students who actually attend class mostly did better than that. Great professor!
Professor Salsman is the best Duke has to offer. I've taken 3 classes with him. He has shaped me as an individual. Expected to have your views challenged. He is a true American hero and patriot!
Has some differing opinions, fueled good conversation, open to debate

This was one of the best classes Ive taken at Duke. Salsman likes to take you on a journey of political and economic history. Classes are contextual, evidence based, argumentative. If you like expressing ideas, or reading political economy, or simply want to indulge in the debate around capitalism, youll love this one. Super thought provoking!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Challenges a lot of your assumptions. Made me much more interested in political economy and capitalism.

Salsman is one of the my favorite professors at Duke. If you are really focused on learning, you will get twice as much out of the class as you put into it. He is always willing to meet with students and discuss any discrepancies in his grading. The PPE Certificate has been my favorite academic focus and his capstone perfectly wraps it all up.

Prisoner's Dilemma class, thought it would be more game theory but ended up being mainly political philosophy. Large amount of reading per week, tests on specific things from readings rather than large concepts. Salsman is extremely knowledgable in his field, but lectures were usually very surface level and basic which didn't reflect the tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Salsman is a great professor who may you work for your grade but is very willing to help you along the way.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Prof. Salsman is my favorite professor at Duke. This was the second course I have taken of his and if I was still in college I would take a third for sure. Salsman not only cares greatly about his students, but is the only professor that I have had who makes me excited to come to class/meetings ready to discuss readings or new findings and ideas.

Salsman is definitely one of the better professors at Duke. Definitely show up to lectures as he elaborates on the readings and helps you to draw connections between different scholars. The class midterm can be tough if you don't take the readings seriously seriously. Just stay on top of the readings and contribute in class and you'll be fine
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This is the second time that I have taken a course with Professor Salsman. He is the best professor I have had at Duke, and is a great resource to every student. He teaches neutrally, exposing students to different perspectives while unbiasedly helping them to strengthen their own arguments. I highly recommend taking a course with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Salsman rules!
Dr. Salsman is the finest professor Duke offers. Take a class with him and you won't regret it!

Dr. Salsman strives to make a classroom environment where people can truly discuss and think through different issues relevant to the real world. He embodies the classic "push you beyond your comfort zone/ introduce intentionally controversial ideas" professor. I didn't always agree with him, but I honestly learned a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Salsman is by far one of the best professors I have had at Duke. Coming to academia from his previous job in finance, Salsman brings a unique real world knowledge to the table that most professors do not have and it is very clear that he teaches because he loves to teach. Lastly, if you like a great discussion, I highly recommend Salsman.

Salsman really engages the class with discussion during lecture. Topics covered in class are very interesting, but there is a lot of reading. Class participation definitely helps your grade. Had both a final exam and a final paper, though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Professor Salsman is such a great professor! Always available outside of class at the local cafe for paper topics or just general advice. He really encourages debate and dialogue in class and loves to see participation. Will definitely take a class with him again.

Salsman seems to be a nice guy. Makes himself available outside of class and does his due diligence to make class resources available to all, and quickly. Lectures are boring, but still informative. However, he lacks a degree of empathy. Expects students to find coursework easy because he finds it to be so. Can be dismissive of student questions.

Professor Salsman is undoubtedly the best professor at Duke. His class introduces students to new ways of thinking critically about important issues. Your Duke experience is incomplete without a class with Dr. Salsman.
Amazing!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Would take again

reviews.comment: Professor Salsman is one of those rare professors who care about their students and their engagement with the material. His course is well-designed in terms of its capacity to challenge one's notions of morality and normative judgment and in terms of its inter-disciplinary nature. I'd highly recommend taking the PPE gateway with him.

Professor Salsman's overall idleness during lectures made it seem like we were having a slightly more lively version of a male Siri read off powerpoints for 1:15:00 twice a week. Despite the not-so-productive nor engaging lecture display, the material is habitually intriguing and the exams are easy if proper (not much) studying is done.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Tests? Not many--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Salsman is the best professor I've had at Duke. He truly care about getting to know his students, and is a huge proponent of allowing EVERYONE'S view to be heard. His lectures a riveting and engaging, and the material he chooses are essentials for a PPE background. Outside of the classroom, he is always open to chatting about anything.

Professor Salsman is a very engaging professor with an excellently designed course that creates multiple opportunities for interesting debate. The topics covered were genuinely thought provoking and discussion in class would always challenge my beliefs. Requirements are clearly specified and professor Salsman is always very approachable for help.
Professor is awesome and had interesting lectures not too demanding, a few pop quizzes that aren't really pop quizzes because he gives a heads up but do the readings and your fine

Professor Salsman is an incredible, engaging lecturer and gives some of the best analysis on Philosophy, Politics, and Economics. He appreciates participation and has designed his course to foster deep discussions as a class. It is clear how invested he is in the success of his students, and I hope to take another of his courses in the future.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Great Professor. Prisoner's Dilemma is dope.

Salsman's lectures can be boring, but the material itself is interesting. Honestly, I learned a lot from the class, primarily from the weekly virtual sections and readings (which you do not need to read). The essay grading is arbitrarily hard; everything is graded with a median in the 80s.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Great topics, and the overlap of Philosophy, Politics, and Economics, makes it very interesting for any major. You learn a great deal in class discussions. Salsman likes to hear the students' opinions on every topic, which makes the class very dynamic. The amount of reading is high, however. Very interesting class overall. Salsman's is very caring.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Loved this class! Learned a lot about political philosophy and economy.

Professor Salsman is a bit of a dry lecturer. Regardless, this does not change the fact that Salsman is very accessible towards his students and does want them to do well. The arguments brought up by Salsman are interesting, but delivered uninterestingly. Take this class if you want a though-provoking overview of the intersection of PolSci and Econ
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Salsman is a fairly good professor. While his lectures are typically pretty dry, he cares a lot about his students and their success. This is evidenced through his accessibility outside of class, his effort put into test reviews, and his clear grading criteria.
reviews.rating_tags: Tests? Not many--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I really liked professor Salsman. He was very approachable, and clearly cares both about the subject matter he teaches and the students.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: Super accessible outside class and super nice. No need to actually read or go to class because lectures are online. Easy for non-econ majors that want to learn more. Weekly quizzes that are super easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Had to take this class for my major. It wasn't interesting to me at all & it didn't help that Salsman whispers his lectures in monotone so you neither understand what he's saying or why anyone would care. He can present very different opinions than my own, which is good, but he was always kinda blunt about it. Not a bad guy tho just not my favorite
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Tests? Not many--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Salsman is good at lecturing and you can tell he knows a lot about the material. I didn't find his lectures very engaging, but I'm sure a lot of people liked them. He's a funny guy and I enjoyed getting dinner with him, a guest speaker, and a couple of the students outside class. He genuinely likes the material which is always good.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Professor Salsman's class was not too difficult and I thought that the grading on assignments was fair. The course only has one midterm and a final, and he was good at helping students on what to study. His lectures are a bit dry and sometimes they can get a little boring. A fair amount of the class did not show up to lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Tests? Not many

reviews.comment: Professor Salsman is an excellent prof and I would definitely recommend taking a course with him. His lectures are interesting, and he presented a wide breadth of challenging philosophical, political, and economic concepts in a way that was easy to understand. Encourages good class discussions.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Great teacher and great lectures. Not hard.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Very knowledgeable about subject. Some students get turned off by his monotone lectures but the actual content and the arguments he creates are interesting. Lots of interesting reading is assigned, but it is not necessary to read every day. Some student's claim he is "too conservative" but Salsman shows both sides of a debate.

Professor Salsman is incredibly knowledgable and an outstanding professor. He teaches very neutrally while exposing students to many perspectives, creating a classroom environment in which even the most controversial issues can be discussed civilly and analytically. He is very approachable and fair, and is always willing to meet with students.

Professor Salsman is great. I would highly recommend taking a class with him. He has a very casual and low key style and he encourages openness and discussion. He is very approachable and understanding. The content is always important and provides a solid overview of economics and political science.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Professor Salsman is one of the best professors I've encountered at Duke. I would highly recommend taking a class with him, especially if you are in a department like econ, where it can be tough to meet professors who truly care. His lecture style is more casual and he encourages discussion, so I found the class very intellectually stimulating too.

Incredibly dry lectures on basic economic concepts. Lots of intensive and long readings on the history of economic development instead of economic concepts. Went to every lecture and took notes/read every reading until the midterm when I realized I could have done well without even going to class. I would suggest this class for only polysci majors
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Really amazing guy. Especially if you take time to go to office hours or FLUNCH, you will love him as a person. His lectures can be tedious, but the concepts are easy to understand. Take ECON119/POLISCI145 if you want a big class with a wide overview of economics.
Salsman is a great professor and a really nice guy. He explains things really well and is always willing to help.

Salsman often teaches the class when Munger is unavailable. Although he lacks the flair that Munger has, Salsman is a good professor and cares about his students. The class balances out well with both of their perspectives and I very much enjoyed the course.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Prof Salsman is very knowledgeable about the topics discussed. Although the class is co-taught, he taught about 80% of the lectures. His lectures are extremely monotonous because he simply reads what is written on the powerpoints which are posted online. One can do the readings and read the powerpoints without going to class and succeed.
He covers some of the lectures that Professor Munger can not make. Don't go to class when he is covering, he cannot keep his class awake or focused.

Dr Rubin is extremely kind and a gem in his field. The amount of experience and knowledge he has about such a wide array of topics is incomparable to other professors. He's a beacon in the psychology field and is always down to chat! Sometimes his lectures can be confusing but it all makes sense in the end when you put it with the textbook. Take.

Class was the biggest waste of my money at Duke. No one in the class cared whatsoever, least of all the prof. He clearly didn't want to teach, so he just rambled, interrupted and said really problematic stuff at times. Lost any interest I had in the subject and never taking a class in this department again. I hope they get someone better to teach.

While the class was super easy, it's the worst class I've ever taken.  Class time was so painful that it couldn't make up for the light work - Rubin rambles incomprehensibly, interrupts, and said some problematic things. Class usually ended early because he didn't have plans and would berate students for not having ideas of things to do instead.

Dr. Rubin is very nice and he cares about his students but his lectures are incoherent and hard to follow (and very boring). 100% of your grade is made up of 3 tests but reading the textbook and going to discussion section will save your grade. I wouldn't take another class with him but don't let that stop from taking cognitive psych.

Completely graded on a curve for 3 midterms, so if you're better at memorizing facts from lecture and textbooks than the rest of your class, you'll get an A. If not, you'll get a B. Lectures are very hard to follow, so go to section and read the textbook instead.

Only reason I'm not giving a 1 is he is a nice guy. Unless you memorize tangents from class as well as every example/definition from text, you'll get a B at best. If you struggle w/ focus/memorization you'll do poorly bc lectures are disorganized & handouts have no context. B4 I used text for open note test I didn't know what the material was.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr Rubin is a very nice and sincere person. And he cares about students very much. He tried hard to make students to learn and find an interesting topic to explore in the class. And he is always willing to help. Very knowledgeable and inspiring professor.

Dr. Rubin is an actual gem in the psych and neuro department. If you have literally any topic you would like to research independently without pressure to produce something that is basically the professor's words written down and passed in, take his class. He is funny, absolutely brilliant, and genuinely wants his students to succeed in his class
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Rubin is incredibly well read and has such a kind heart and passion for the course. His goals for the semester are for you to learn in the class and to produce a quality final paper. I have never taken a class that values learning for the sake of learning. For anyone who is a psych or neuro and wants to explore their own topic without pressure.

Terrible professor, has no organization and procedure class by class and for the overall semester. Goes on tangents frequently. Strong Boston accent & slurps after each phrase, gets sort of annoying. Not a compelling professor, very hard to pay attention. Go to section, read the book, do the practice tests, and you'll be fine. 3 tests for 1/3 each

Only assignments are a few readings and one page papers for discussion and one final 15-20 page paper. Dr. Rubin is super chill and we only were in class for like an hour most weeks.  You get out of the class as much as you put in, but he basically guarantees everyone an A as long as he can tell you didn't start the paper the night before its due.

Worst class I have ever taken. Rubin's lectures are incomprehensible and do not align with information in the textbook. In fact, many of his lectures veered so far off topic that even the TAs had trouble understanding the point Rubin was trying to make. DO NOT take this class if you are at all interested in cog psych because you will learn nothing.

Rubin is pretty incomprehensible and the multiple choice questions on the test reflect that. His handouts make virtually no sense and there's little point in going to lecture when most of the info comes from the discussion section and textbook. Going to discussion is imperative to doing well though, so get to know your TA.

Kept going to lecture even though I stopped seeing the point before the semester was even halfway over. TA was great; highly recommend going to discussion so you stay on track with the class. Read the textbook and go to discussion and you'll be fine.

Not a great lecturer although a very sincere and nice person. Obviously well-versed in his field but struggles to convert that knowledge into a lecture setting. Read the book and attend TA sections and you'll pass.

Professor Rubin has the most confusing lectures I have ever attended. He mumbles and goes off on tangents, making the material very unclear. You have to read the textbook to do well in this class. Lectures are optional. Nice guy, very accomplished in his field, but not a great professor.

Prefers explaining concepts through demonstrations rather than just telling you about them. Overall nice guy and solid professor. Also, he is renowned in the psychological field for his pioneering research
Great guy who actually teaches outside the textbook and provides you with interesting demonstrations. Very helpful if you are a visual learner

This class is a joke. Rubin means very well, but is unhelpful. 90% of the class is him going off on random tangents that do not pertain to the discussion. However, he will give you a lot of freedom with your work and is an easy grader. Our class was centered around a research paper, which did not have many guidelines.

His handouts aren't very helpful, and in lecture he just does demonstrations, but the exams are pretty easy. As long as you go to discussion and read the textbook you should do well. Grades are based on 3 exams (2 midterms & a final), and he curves the class at the end of the semester. Easy, but if you want to learn the material, take a diff prof.

Had him for a psychology seminar and while it was theee most boring class of all time (he talks the entire time and while some of the information may be interesting, he doesnt make it at all) it was rediculously easy because all we had were ungraded weekly papers and one long term paper due at the end of the semester. strong boston accent

This class is very easy. The material is simple. Read the textbook, go to class, go to section, and you will have no problems. Unfortunately, Rubin is impossible to understand. His handouts are terrible, and he is about as incomprehensible as they come.
class was horrible. unless you had a good ta (which i didn't) then this class will pretty much make your life hell.

His Boston accent is laughable. You can barely understand what he's saying, and his lectures are disjointed. The material is interesting if you understand it, and thanks to a very knowledgeable TA, I did. Lectures are pretty mandatory, since Rubin does a lot of experiments. Overall, should stick to research, not teaching.

God knows what he's saying in lectures. Hated his handouts, but soon enough you'll be thankful you at least have his handouts. Texts he chooses for class are incredibly dull, altho cogpsy can be a lot funner. but still it's an easy A. in short, it's a boring/easy course. personally i'd rather take a fun/hard course, or PSY 91 if u r a psy major.
No Comments

Disorganized with a tendency to ramble. Hard to take notes on lectures, but show up and you'll do fine in the course.  Hated the textbook, but most stuff is covered in lecture/section anyway.  No homework or papers is a plus.  I didn't learn much more than I got from AP Psych in high school.
No Comments
Relatively easy class as long as you come to session, lecture, and do the reading. Hard to follow lectures because he jumps from one thing to another, but it shouldn't be too hard to get an A.
My GOAT. Learn mainly through the textbook, but she does a great job of consolidating the information you read about in lecture. Accessible outside of class. And super nice! Highly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I came in with little to no coding background. Do not let the bad reviews scare you: this class isn't hard, the lectures are just SO boring. You will do just fine simply reading the textbook and doing the homework. Homework is a lot but you will do well (auto-graded and infinite tries). She is just so boring.

The class is pretty straightforward - lectures can be boring but the material is manageable. Just stay on top of the work and you'll do well. For study prep, I found Unstuck study and the free textbook to be really helpful alongside the usual resources like ChatGPT.

If you gave a blind toddler access to a personal computer I would bet money that they could write a better software than the ugly, broken, unintuitive monstrosity known as JFLAP, designed by Prof. Rodger.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: absolutely anyone can succeed in this class if they attend office hours!

CS342: Although she was a bit dull when I took CS201 with her, in this course she was great: lectures were interesting, she explained the concepts thoroughly, and the course was structured nicely with good hws, projects, and exams. This may be because CS342 is more aligned with her area of research.

Class was flipped and used materials already available on her course on Coursera. Lectures were sometimes dry but the content of the class is easy. We got out after finishing the in-class assignment 10 minutes early every class.

This is an easy class w/ not too much hw, however: her lectures are extremely boring and did nothing to enhance my comp sci knowledge. Prof Rodger made attendance mandatory by having forms to fill out every class about the lecture but you don't have to be there to do it. She wasn't helpful in answering questions. If u skip lecture, its not too bad.
Professor isn't helpful or kind. Lectures are boring

Least helpful professor I have ever had. Learned nothing in lecture and relied heavily on the textbook that she didn't even write. The work itself isn't terrible but you have to rely on yourself to learn anything in her class.

I found CS101 to be a very fun and interesting class. However, I learned all of the material on my own, Prof Rodger's lectures did not add much. I had no coding background, and found the class extremely easy and the material intuitive. There is definitely a bunch of busy work though, with labs and APTs and APT quizzes and such. Tests are fair.
This class was completely new material for me but it wasn't hard. I thought it was paced very well, the exams were not bad at all, and generally the projects could be completed within a day.
Class itself was very easy for me, no complaints with the professor, she taught the topics pretty well. Lectures are not mandatory, labs are pretty easy.
I had some previous experience with Python so CompSci 101 was a fairly easy course for me. Prof. Rodger wasn't amazing but she was good enough. There are a decent amount of assignments.

Compsci94 with Professor Rodger is pretty easy. Use past exams to practice for tests and you'll be fine, especially since tests aren't weighed as heavily compared to other classes. Also, attendance is mandatory since your classwork gets checked off during class.

If you have any coding background, CS101 with Professor Rodger is cake. If not, prepare to teach yourself the whole course. Lectures are boring and bland - I was more productive skipping them than going. Assignments are fair and courseload is average. Those with no CS background might struggle early on, but everyone figures it out by finals.

Prof. Rodger is approachable and her lectures are informative (although sometimes not very engaging). The course is well-structured but there is a lot of work (APTs, assignments, labs) and can be slightly overwhelming to those who have never coded before. Overall still a great course and exams (& grades in general) are very fair.

Pretty easy class, tests are easy provided you take the practice tests beforehand. Assignments seem like busy work, but most aspects of the class are good for building a foundation of programming. Lenient with dropping points in categories at the end of the semester and things of that sort.

This course was one of my favorites that I've taken at Duke so far. I took it as a Focus class freshman fall which made it even better. This course is super accessible if you've never done anything with CS before. On the last day we voted on who had the best final project. The winners got prizes and she gave us all cookies!

Professor Rodger gets a bad rap from the reviews but I think a lot of the complaints have more to do with the general course structure than actually with Professor Rodger. Not the best professor I've ever had but her tests are more than fair and she gives out bonus points for filling out surveys etc.
Never went to class but CS101 was easy and her tests were clear, as long as you do the practice tests

Workload was manageable and material was really easy. Assignments are scattered everywhere so you have to keep track of due dates and it's easy to forget to turn in something and instructions are written in a weird way that's hard to follow. Lectures were boring, I would say I learned 90% of the material from doing hw on my own and lab sections.

This class had a lot of work but the content itself was not super difficult. There are textbook readings and short quizzes before every lecture (you get 3 attempts), APTs, assignments, and labs. The first few assignments were fun, but the last three are very difficult and almost impossible to do without going to office hours. Exams were fair.

Basically a self-study course. Stopped doing homework, lectures, etc. after the 2nd Exam. Exams! 4 of them! Ton of homework & projects. Projects are doable if you attend office hours. TAs are amazing. Professor is not involved. Doubt she even knows a single TA's name. Not terrible like everyone else says lol. But just doesnt care.

GOATed for real. Grade is split across many things, like APTs, Assignments, Sakai Quizzes (with 3 attempts each) etc and exams are fairly straightforward and cover content from class. 

Took this class for funsies and now considering a CS major!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Boring lectures, does not care about the students at all.

FOR HUMANITIES MAJORS THINKING ABOUT TAKING COMPSCI: Do NOT take CompSci 101 if you are a Humanities major. I thought I would try computer science as coding seems to be a really useful skill nowadays  and can help with hiring. This class moves really fast, isn't truly for people who have never coded, and requires a lot of work. Destroyed my GPA
Really awful professor. It almost seems like she hopes the students to fail. Sets a lot of work and the lectures are dry and boring.

Professor Rodger has an extremely anti-student approach. She refuses to help and will not hesitate to embarrass a student loudly in front of the entire class about something trivial or minor. During the first class period, she condescended to humanities majors. she has an incredible superiority complex and enjoys weaponizing her power.

This class is fine but nothing special. The lectures are pretty boring - if you read the textbook and do the quiz before class, you can skip and basically not miss anything. The assignments can be time-consuming and they're written in a way that makes it hard to understand what they're asking of you. Lots of opportunities to get help/feedback tho.

Two words: eh and oof. There was SO much work- APTs, APT quizzes, pre-class/in-class quizzes, assignment quizzes, assignments (take forever), labs/prelabs, and 4 exams + final. The work wasn't that challenging and the tests were fairly easy. Lectures were very dry and honestly, you don't have to go- just do the work and learn on your own.

Professor Rodger's goal is to punish & shame. She has a "gotcha" focus. It feels like she wants you to fail. She leads with fear. I will change my major as she sucked any passion I had. Students deserve a classroom leader who inspires & supports. I hope she forgives whoever hurt her so she doesn't bring her anger to the classroom.

Actually the worst class I've ever taken in my entire life. If you are a humanities major, like me, who wants to get a QS out of the way, DONT CHOSE THIS CLASS!!! the most boring lectures in the entire world. it's as if she wants to lull you to sleep with her monotony at 10:15am. I have the utmost hate for this class.

We have two textbook quizzes a week, and the added 5 apts or an assignment or both which take HOURS to complete. None of what we are graded on is discussed during lecture and we end up teaching ourselves how to do it. We have 4 midterms graded on paper which defeats the purpose of coding. CS101 is supposed to be intro but it's far from it.

Susan is the most boring lecturer I've had at Duke. She's also a tough grader and assigns lots of work. this class has weekly APT problem sets, large coding assignments about the dumbest things, APT quizzes, 4 midterms, in addition to textbook reading and daily reading quizzes.
Prof Rodgers isn't very engaging, but CS94's content is so elementary that you can leave early after completing your in-class assignment. Many opportunities to boost your grade that you won't need.

Let me paint a picture for you. Textbook quizzes are due twice a week. Assignments/ APTs that take hours to do are due at LEAST once a week and worth 10% of your grade. Unclear directions on said assignments. Quizzes on unclear directions of said assignments. If you have no coding experience/humanities major, this class is an absolute nightmare.

Ridiculous amount of work for an introductory course. Course was restructured this semester to include 4 exams and a final (so five exams in total), which is rather insane. On top of that, we've got long assignments, coding exercises, and the occasional APT quiz (which feels like another exam). If you can, go directly to 201. This class ain't it.

Emailed her asking to meet 1:1 for help, she flat out said no. Assignments have nothing to do with what she lectures on. Dull lectures, with material that is barely useful for assignments. Had more tests in this class than tests in my other 3 classes combined that semester, and they were not very flexible with missing exams (even for COVID)

This was the worst class I've taken at Duke. You are better off doing a coding bootcamp or YouTube tutorials. Assignments are due every other day. If you don't get help or become an expert cheater, you will fail. Straight up. If you want to keep your sanity, have a social life, or not run up your therapist bill... skip this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Rodger can be quite a dull lecturer, but overall, I really enjoyed her class! Just make sure you keep up with readings & videos, and it's not bad at all. I genuinely enjoyed the assignments in this class, and it made me want to take more CS!

Had her for 201 covid semester. I had taken the course before so slightly biased, but overall I thought she explained things solidly well, and I could rely on TAs for details that I may have still been confused about. Lectured quite slowly and good when it came to answering questions. Online version was asynchronous and fine as well.

I learned more in a one hour video on Python made by some teenager on YouTube than I did this whole semester. If you are a CS major, PLEASE just skip this class even if you don't have AP credit, you'll be fine for CS 201 after some brief Java tutorials. Such a waste :(

Lectures were very painful and involved filling out constant Google forms with other people in breakout rooms for participation. Assignments took many hours to decipher and most of the time you'll either have to beg TAs for help during office hours or teach concepts to yourself. It is evident that this class hasn't adapted very well to Zoom.

she will throw a four hour assignment with zero explanation or instructions. I'm extremely shocked that a university as prestigious as duke will still keep her around after seeing all of these horrible reviews that people left her. THEY ARE HERE FOR A REASON PLEASE LISTEN TO THEM AND TAKE INTO ACCOUNT. her class causes me actual anxiety

I think Professor Rodger is a great professor! She posts videos weekly that allow you go back a relearn anything in class that may be confusing. Overall, if you do the assigned readings and attempt to learn the material, the APTs and assignments are very doable!

Probably one of the more unfairly maligned professors at Duke. The material is super engaging and the APTs (short programming tasks) and assignments (longer programming tasks) are for the most part a lot of fun. This class might stretch your brain a bit at times, but still very much worth taking!

This class was honestly the easiest I had this semester. Had little prior experience but the content was easy if you did the reading and watched the videos, in which Pr Rodger was really clear (watch the videos in speed x1,5 tho). The assignments and APT were genuinely fun to me so they didn't feel like work. The labs are a bit boring tho.

Lecture was relatively dry but as expected in intro CS class. Useful topics were generally covered decently well; hard to cater to so many (usually distracted) students at once. Professor Rodger herself is extremely caring and helpful in office hours. Course overall very well organized for its size and provides a good gateway into future CS courses

Susan oh susan how you made this class so much harder than it is sis. Like work on your teaching game. Susan is really nice, but the lectures are extremely boring and unclear. The TAs office hours and discussions will save you so go to those. The class is not that hard but it feels that way cuz of susie.

Lectures are dry, useless, and can even detract from understanding the material. Expectations for exams are also very unclear as compared to past exams. Exam grading criteria is unnecessarily picky, and she is not particularly approachable. TAs and coding experience sell the class. However, she made sure to pass everyone during the pandemic.

Overall, I think Prof. Rodger is a nice person and I appreciate her being accommodating with grades and class structure when class got moved online. However, I think that her lectures could be improved as they were often confusing/dry and I would end up walking away from some lectures feeling like I didnt learn that much.

Overall a very dry lecturer. She is nice and quite knowledgeable, just her lectures are not engaging, which I think is reflected by her need to tell students to quiet down pretty frequently. The class itself though is great and the TA support system certainly raises her levels.

I've never rated a professor before, but I felt the need to warn others about Susan Rodger. Her lectures are extremely dull and she does not explain the material well at all. She is also unapproachable if you want her help. I was forced to constantly go to TA office hours where I learned more than every single one of her lectures combined.

The class is generally good. Make sure you don't miss a single lecture, even if you feel sometimes it's boring and you can study on your own. You can't fully comprehend them with the slides. By the way, I really dislike the discussion policy forces us to work with new people every time, the peak of my social pressure every Monday morning.

Professor Rodger knows her subject well but is not great at teaching. She relies on the flipped-classroom structure of the class, and is rather unapproachable. The material is easy to comprehend, but there is a lot of work due every week (classworks, assignments, online quizzes). Tests are very easy but can be super long and difficult to finish.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: CompSci 94 is supposed to be easy but Professor Rodger makes it so difficult to learn anything. She is not open to any questions or helping any students, her TA's do a better job at teaching than she des.
