Do not take this class if you're looking for an easy A or to learn anything useful about computer science.

Absolutely horrible professor. Was abrasive to questions, and when she did take them usually answered them rudely. Sometimes had 4 or more things due in one week with a midterm on the way. Clearly doesn't care about her students. Avoid at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Professor Rodger strikes me as someone who understands the material very well herself, but has a tough time imparting that to others. In short, a lot of the learning in her computer science classes has to be done on your own.

Rodger is really sweet and cares about her students, but isn't a great lecturer. I came in having zero CS background and was fine. The workload is extremely heavy in this class with nonstop assignments, but eventually you begin to get efficient at it. The tests, however, are extremely easy and are identical to previous years which are available

I underestimated the class... it was one of the most work intensive classes from my last semester. Be ready to work really really hard and be on top of your things even though I knew some python before coming in

Had no coding exp. but am math-sci guy. HUGE workload, but having old exams (easy to master) made class not too bad. I spent many hours with TAs, but do APTs and cool assignments, GET HELP, and you'll do fine. Lectures mostly tips, not teaching, but try attending. TAs are amazing, helpful. Most find 101 very easy or hard, depends on aptitude for CS
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: For a humanities major looking for a QS requirement, this was a very difficult class. The homework was never ending; once an assignment was completed after an all-nighter, another one appeared. Lectures didn't really help. It was trial by error, with a ton of error. I got a higher grade than I actually felt like I deserved, thankfully.

Dr. Rodger is a fine and boring person. Her lectures are very dull. I don't think she did a great job in teaching the class, however if you are a math and science person it will likely be an easy A. I came into the class already knowing python, and if you've had prior coding, it will be very easy.

This is a very time-intensive class (101) and there are so many reading quizzes/ assignments. Professor Rodger is very nice and aims to make the class enjoyable. However, I found that I was not able to understand concepts unless I self-studied from the online textbook. I was a bit bored sometimes, too but maybe that's because I didn't put in work.

Rodger really does try to be helpful to her students. There are a lot of resources to do well. What she often lacks is proper organization so that students can find helpful information. Lectures not necessary to attend, but are helpful. Readings necessary. Do the homework and do it well. You'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This class was a lot of work, but python is relatively easy and I enjoyed putting in the time to complete assignments. Did not pay attention to a word Susan said, only went to class to fulfill in class participation assignments, just read the super-helpful textbook and passed. Overall pretty good class and the best option to fulfill that QS.
Great teacher!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Sweet lady, but lectures are painful. There is a lot of work in this class, and I honestly don't know how people who didn't go to office hours passed. This class is an easy A if you're a compsci person, but if you're not, it's really difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Lectures are a  bit dry and recap the readings. Lecture slides are posted online but attendance is mandatory. Very assignment heavy class: weekly quizzes, assignments, APTs and labs. Stay on top of workload and you'll be ok - don't procrastinate. Rodger and TAs have lots of office hours and are very willing to help. Definitely take if interested.

Prepare to be lured, swept away, and absolutely enraptured by the arms of sleep. So skip lectures since you won't stay awake anyways.  Prepare to invest time on assignments (harder ones take 5+ hrs). CS101 is polarizing; people find it easy or hard without many in between, so experience it yourself.
Rodger gets a bad rep, but really isn't that bad and 101 is an easy A

Professor Rodger was tried hard to make lectures interactive, but they were boring at times. Lots of work, although not too hard and I learned a lot. Professor Rodger is also just a really nice person, she really wants her students to like Computer Science, and made us cookies and fudge sometimes!
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This class is NOT easy - you can get an A, but be prepared to do tons of busy work. Go to office hours w/ TAs religiously. Lectures are pointless - no one pays attention, but there are attendance points. APTS, Assignments, RQ, etc. - tons of assignments, you'll have several hours of work per week. However, I legitimately enjoy coding which is nice.

Professor Rodger is brilliant and quirky, but her class is a pain. I've never taken computer science before so it was very difficult. She teaches Python in 101. I found to give myself 4 days to do an assignment, and 3 days to do an APT, and to do the readings as soon as possible. GO TO HELP HOURS AT NIGHT THE TAs ARE SO HELPFUL.
This class is soooooo easy.  Recommend for anyone who can remotely handle a course that is not in the humanities.
Prof Rodger is a nice and approachable person especially considering how many students she has. She really wants you to do well and understands when things happen, like computer crash during a quiz.

Extremely huge workload and the pace of the course is way too fast. The amount of homework, assignments and APTs just make this course extremely hard and takes away any slight interest of me in Comp Sci.  Lectures are not very useful either. Prof. Rodger is very nice and is dedicated to Comp Sci, yet I would not totally not recommend this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: As someone who didn't have CS experience before this class, I wouldn't say that CS101 is a very easy class. You have to work hard. Beware: there are A LOT of assignments, APTs, reading quizzes, etc. You can't procrastinate! I promise you that your hard work will pay off. I asked for help when I needed it, stayed on top of my work, & got  an A+!

The lectures were not really helpful, but the material was very cool. There was a ton of homework, but it is fine if you do not procrastinate. There are help room hours multiple times in the week, and she is helpful in office hours if you go. Cool person who loves comp sci.

Rodger is an okay-professor. It's hard to concentrate on lectures because they tend to be boring and long. APTs can be challenging but they are doable, unlike assignments. If it's your first time coding, make sure to utilize TAs and DO NOT PROCRASTINATE, because assignments just take a lot of time. There are daily reading quizzes.
Hands down, my favorite thing about this class was that it forces you to keep up with material daily, so that when test time comes, you don't have to cram. Saved me many hours of sleep.

Not a good teacher, but you can't really hate her. She's nice, just has poor people skills. Many thought class was hard at first but difficulty really drops off around halfway through, and people start getting the hang of it. You just gotta keep coding. Having so much work every week was hard, but it was essential practice.
Easy A. Lots of work, but it's rewarding. Lectures are boring. Enough said.

COMPSCI 101 is a lot of work but that is with any professor. The class is so much fun! Dr. Rodger really tries to inspire students to go into computer science. Also, the assignments that we do are really fun. I loved this course. The lectures were boring, but everything else in the class really instilled a passion in me for coding.

I really love compsci but Rodger assigns SO MUCH WORK! Every week there's reading quizzes, a major assignment, a long lab, and an APT problem set due. This is easily over 10-12 hours a week for ONE CLASS. It's causing me to neglect other classes. From what I understand, CS101 didn't use to have so many things due every week - bad idea to change it.

Not really sure what the purpose of lectures are with her. The class isn't even flipped... it's somewhere halfway in between with each lecture feeling like a stream-of-consciousness from her. Lectures are quite useless while the amount of work in this class is more than all three of my other classes combined (no I'm not a history major or something

I really enjoyed this class. I learned a lot from the small and big assignments because I dedicated time to understanding the code and went to TA hours. The lectures are mostly pointless but occasionally very helpful. Definitely a class where you learn by doing. Time consuming but in a rewarding way. Take it if even the slightest interest in CS.

Class itself was really easy. Decent amount of work. Wouldn't have gone to lecture if  we didn't have to sign in for attendance. Learned more from TA office hours. If you want to learn some basic coding or want a relatively easy A, take the class.

The structure of CompSci 101 at Duke is very strong and clear. All of the expectations and guidelines are thoroughly laid out. Despite Susan's role as professor not being life-changing or ground breaking, she really cares about the class environment and the students' ability to master python coding.

Lectures are very long and boring, not really necessary but you need to sign in while there.  Lots of out-of-class assignments but nothing too challenging.  Very interesting class at times and not too hard to get an A.  Many pieces (Reading Quizes, APTs, etc.) can be submitted repeatedly until you get 100.  Would recommend.

Not a very good lecturer and generally lectures are unhelpful (though sometimes the online powerpoints have important code). If you can, take 101 with Astrachan (but it's not that important as long as you do the assignments). Overall, a class I would recommend.
Lectures are boring and often unecessary, but the class is difficult to succeed in if you don't go.  Professor Rodger can be dull in her lectures, but she really knows her stuff

Professor Rodger is chill, and she makes a clear effort to make things easy to understand for students, albeit a bit boring. Like every CS class, you are kept busy with assignments/APT sets, but TAs are there to help. Most people either just get it or they don't, so if you understand lecture and do the assignments, the class should be an easy A.

I thought Prof Rodger struck a good balance between a no-frills approach and covering interesting things during lecture. Readings were easy, most assignmentsall the mandatory APTs were easy (but hard APTs are available if you wanted them). It's better to do pastpractice tests in prep for her exams. Lab sessions are fast-paced but you learn a lot.

Great professor for CS101 at Duke. Lecture can sometimes be long but is always helpful. Also gives great help one on one but you have to take the initiative to go to get help from her. I highly recommend her for CS101 at Duke!

Prof. Rodger is a very nice teacher. Although her lectures are long and the material is not that interesting, she does try her best to make it fun and to engage students. It is impossible to do poorly in this class as long as you try.

Being an intro class it's not that exciting but I still enjoyed it. At times the workload is annoying but this class is easy to do well in so I didn't complain, recommend it for anyone and everyone who has room in their schedule
Lectures are very boring and seem to last forever. If there were not participation points, I would not attend. However, the class is not too hard and the exams are quite easy. Lab is very helpful.
Super easy class. It's definitely worth your while. Also, it's really difficult for a person to "teach" comspci so the amount that you learn will be based on you.
Lectures are worthless except for participation points

Online reading quizzes twice a week; large assignments once a week; 4 to 6 smaller assignments once a week; 2 midterms and a final; in-class online quizzes; labs. Easy to get an A because there is a lot of buffer. She is extremely boring in class - I never wanted to go. Lots of group work. Go to office hours early. Assignments get hard.

It's CS101, so the class is what you make of it. If you pay attention in lecture (which is a grind most of the time) and do the readings, you should be aptly prepared to do assignments and take tests. Go to UTA office hours. They will be LIFE SAVERS

This class does drag on a bit (it is a compsci class after all), but Dr. Rodger is EXTREMELY helpful if you would go to her office hours and her TAs are also very helpful. This class is easily doable as long as you reach out for help when you need it-- the help is readily available.
Overall, Professor Rodger is a good CS 101 teacher.

Tests are the easiest I've had in college. Lectures aren't the best, but it's a class that you really teach yourself. The assignments and APTs are amaaaazing for learning. Grading criteria crystal clear. Pretty open to help too! FREE AND AWESOME TEXTBOOK!

She's a meh professor, but the course is set up so that you learn much more from the APTs and assignments than you do the actual lectures. There are better professors out there for this class, but I'd still recommend taking it with her. If you do the homework you'll learn to code, and it is very easy to get an A if you try.

The TA's basically help you learn this class. Although she tries to help she can't always explain everything clearly. It takes around 3-5 hours outside of class every week to get the work done. The textbook is very helpful, as are the APT's. She isn't a tough grader,her exams are relatively easy. No need to cram because you learn as time passes.

Get ready to spend at 6-10 hours a week on homework. SEE THE TA'S FOR HELP! The TA office hours for this class made it super manageable. Lots of homework, but if you get it done, you pretty much get an A. Rodger was nice and tried to help, but I didn't learn much from lectures. The online textbook is free and pretty helpful!

Because CS101 is pretty much entirely self-taught, Professor Rodger doesn't play a big role in the student experience in this course. When you show up for lecture, she's pretty unclear and doesn't cover much. Do the reading, cruise the lectures, and take the course.  If you can find a more engaging teacher go for it, but not a must in 101.

CS101 is not a very difficult class. Susan is not an engaging lecturer, so skip class and just read the online text-book, it's way easier to understand. There is a TON of assignments in this class, but if you do them and understand them, the tests will be super easy, and you'll get an A.
This class was not too hard. The online textbook is great and you learn a lot through practice. Lectures are not all that helpful.

Her lectures are so monotonous and  dry that it's a real struggle to pay attention in class, specially when you have a computer in front of you. A LOT of work- weekly assignments+apt sets (be prepared to spend hours at TAs), reading quizzes, etc . But since the grade is broken down into so many small parts (+extracredit), it's easy to do well.

If you're taking CS101, there's plenty of opportunity for extra credit that will get you an A (plus you can check your work before you turn it in, re-submit reading quizzes till you get 100%, etc). The class is pretty easy with her, and she walks you through material at a mundane pace. Her teaching style is kind of boring so I skipped class alot.

Lots of busy work in this class. I was not expecting so many assignments, but they are very frequent. If you were to do all those on your own, it iswould be a very time consuming course. If you understand the material, the tests are very simple, but it's fairly difficult to keep up. Material is kinda interesting until you're drowning in work

She's really nice and helpful if you ask questions but lecture is boring and usually not very helpful, especially later in the semester. Assignments were interesting and I learned a lot in the end though. If you leave enough time to finish all the homework then you should get a good grade.

Genuinely nice lady who is passionate about the subject and cares about her students. Unfortunately, Comp Sci 101 is unnaturally difficult due to the number of experienced coders that take the class (despite being explicitly told on the first day of class that they should take 201), making this class much harder than it should be.
Lectures are extremely boring and directions for assignments are extremely confusing. Tests are moderately hard.
Don't take 101 unless you already have programming experience.

Goes by lecture notes, which are very clear. Most of all, the class was among the easiest of those I've taken at Duke. (Materials are easy and tests are super easy.) It was as easy as Prof. Klein's EOS101! Also, as far as I'm concerned, the class isn't curved, which is even more awesome considering that the tests are super easy.

I thought Dr. Rodger could be a bit muddled at times when she was giving lectures, but she definitely didn't mind answering questions. It helps if you consistently ask questions to clarify the information - else you might fall asleep.

Very fair professor who genuinely tries her best to help you when you ask for it. Provides many practice tests similar in format to the actual midterms, which is very helpful for studying. Overall a really nice person and good prof for smaller classes like 140; she does her best to know everyone's name.

She is a very nice lady who genuinely would like everyone to do well.  That said her class is pretty easy if you have the ability to teach yourself.  Lecture is all but useless and her voice is quite piercing. The assignments are disproportionately hard.  You have to have an interest in Compsci to survive a class with her. Class is semi-mandatory

I heard people complaining about  Professor Rodger way more than she deserved during the semester. Lecture was boring, but she genuinely wanted to be nice and helpful. She even baked cookies for the entire class (100+ people). The tests were fair with high medians, and she would give extensions on assignments if everyone was having trouble.

Freshmen taking this class their first semester are overly critical, not realizing that college material is not meant to be spoon-fed. She can be confusing at times, but she's nice & wants us to understand the material. She is quick to answer questions (on Piazza) and, besides a few assignments, has been fairly reasonable w/what she expects of us.
The course material is interesting.  But if Rodgers is teaching it, wait a semester to get a different professor. You don't want her as a professor, ever.
Professor is monotone and very difficult to listen to for an entire hour and twenty minutes. She is oftentimes confused by her OWN code. DON'T TAKE THIS CLASS.
definitely knows the matter but has a hard time conveying the matter. moreover, the assignments and labs and lecture don't seem to complement each other
Just not so helpful

She definitely knows the material, however, sometimes she has a hard time teaching it clearly.  Great class if you're willing to give 110% during lecture and pay careful attention.  Otherwise, give it a pass because it's going to be rough.

Do not take this class if you want to enjoy your semester! Professor assigns classwork that is to be turned in at the next class period every day plus one major assignment per week. Never responds to emails. Picky grader on exams and there is no proving her wrong. She sometimes gets confused about the program, Alice, herself. Lecture is BORING!
Professor Rodger is really nice, and her powerpoint slides are concise and easy to understand.  She contextualizes concepts well and her assignments were mostly enjoyable.
Terrible lecturer. Actually ignored my e-mails. Tests are harder than they should be. Do not take this class if you've had no prior Java experience - it's not worth the time.
Really nice lady.  Really crappy instructor.  Just gimme' the textbook and let me figure it out myself.

She is a very nice professor. She may not be the best lecturer but her lecture is very organized. Her test is reasonable. She is extremely helpful outside of class. She is lenient on late homeworks and projects. She cares about her students. It is very hard to find a professor with such a likeable character in CS department.

Not very helpful when you approach her with questions on tests. She's overall nice, but is a very boring lecturer.  She says attendance is mandatory but she doesn't even take attendance. Tests are reasonable...not hard to get an A- in the class.  Make sure to do all the classworks.  Teaches Java like we've already learned it, so Java is very hard.

Very difficult to understand. Teaches new and confusing concepts like we've all had it before and know what she's talking about. Hard grader and not very explanatory when it comes to the actual lecture. Very nice person, though.
Very lenient when it comes to partial credit, late work. Not the best at explaining stuff, but the T.A's usually clear things up.

I had prof. Rodger for compsci 4, 6, and 18S- if you are taking 4 or 6 try to get into 18S, which goes along with it and is like a half credit seminar, automatic A if you show up. Prof. Rodger is super boring but easy... sometimes she brings snacks
Not good at all at lectures, but pretty good one-on-one.

Instructor isn't fully prepared for lecture: sometimes gets confused by the programs, which the other CS6 prof actually prepares. Labs can be difficult and time-consuming but enjoyable. Overall, course is very good, but mainly because of the learning in lab. The first weeks of lecture are of little use but improve as we start working examples.

Boring lecture--it's ripped straight from the text book and she spends WAY too much time going over the easiest things, but on the hard stuff she barely talks about it at all.  Nice lady though, and you do do a lot of hands-on classwork.
Aweful lectures, poor instructions on assignments, and high expectations.  Boo on this woman!
Comes off as not really knowing much, give a dull lecture, but it's a really easy class.

literally the worst teacher I have had at Duke. She teaches her own opinions rather than what the textbook or what my friends have learned in this class with other professors. Her lectures are physically painful and awful. She makes demos for the class that make no sense and test you on them during midterm and final. wish I hadn't taken her class.

Horrible class. Seriously don't ever take. Grading criteria is super bizarre and you won't get feedback on absolutely anything. Tests make ZERO sense. Entire class centered around nonsensical demos that barely relate to class material. Prof completely inaccessible outside of class. Discussion section is pointless. You won't learn anything at all.

Joke of a class. Did not learn a single thing from lecture. Textbook actually teaches you but the tests are not on any information from it. Tests are on in class demos with her slides being impossible to take notes from. Does not post slides so you can even study them. Waste of a bad grade, waste of a class.

This was one of the most ridiculous classes I've ever taken. Lectures are incredibly boring and don't teach you anything about cognitive psych.Tests are absurdly vague and completely based on random things said during lecture (lecture recordings aren't posted and neither are the lecture slides so good luck). Doesn't respond to emails either.

I would recommend taking this course- as long as Dr. Day isn't the professor. She does not answer her emails, struggles to use the technology in class, and the lectures are extremely dry. The course is definitely easy to do well in, but be prepared to dislike the course if she is teaching it.

Psy 102 was the most useless class I have taken because of the professor. The tests are completely based off demos she does in class that do not make sense or feel relevant at all and the test questions are extremely specific and do not test the actual learning of cognitive psychology well at all. lectures are extremely boring and nonsensical

Dr. Day is the worst professor I've ever had. A week before the final and I can confidently say I've learned absolutely nothing in her class. Her lectures are mind-numbing and don't make any sense. She's a nice enough lady but likes to brag rather than actually teach. Take cogpsych with the other professor or not at all.

this was the absolute worst psychology class i have ever taken at duke. lectures are stupidly boring and tests are not on actual material but whether or not you can remember her stupid demonstrations from the first day of class. zero grading criteria on labs even when you ask for it. psych majors beware - do not take this course with this prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: For a prof. who offers the most unclear or absent grading criteria, she is a ridiculously tough grader. Lectures are so painfully boring but you CANNOT miss class because you're required to know every single stupid tiny demo that she goes over for the midterm/final which are obscure and in the strangest format. Psy majors- take Neuro 101 instead.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Her class is SO boring, even with the use of "engaging demonstrations". Terrible lecturer and loves to brag about herself and how many people she knows. Completely unreachable outside of class. As a psych major, truly the worst class I have taken at Duke. I also worked in her lab and she made us do grunt work and didn't value our opinions. Terrible

1 Tests aren't over material, it's over whether or not you remember a stupid demo from 4 weeks ago
2 Lecture slides don't actually have info on them and whenever there is, she reads it very quickly and moves on
3 Lab reports graded harder than orgo because the guidelines are VERY unclear.
4 If you miss class you are SOL because nothing is posted

Did not test on actual material instead just her class demonstrations. Does not post the demonstrations or any lecture material either so good luck studying it. In class slides are filled with stupid photos instead of actual information and when there is information she lets it sit there for 5 seconds. Horrible class, no test preparation will help

Midterm was not anything like I was expecting, very strange format. Does not post slides, but somehow wants you to know everything taught in lecture? Refuses to record any review sessions or office hours to gatekeep material. Lectures are all demo-based and don't cover the material at all. Grading on lab reports make actually no sense.

The 25% midterm exam was tested off of stupid demonstrations in class instead of real material from the textbook. She brags about how she actually cares about her students while actively preventing their learning by structuring her class in the most confusing and convoluted way. Impossible to take notes in this class and when you do, incomprehensib

Impossible to understand her. Tried to make things interesting by doing tons of demos and then tests are totally demo-based. Doesn't post any notes or power points so you're always rushing to copy down notes (which are nonsensical btw). Tested on opera and juggling demos, not any normal textbook things. Do NOT take this class. Worst class.

The class itself is full of boring demos and little actual content. Anything you do learn in this class is covered in PSY101. She doesn't ever put any info on her slides so good luck taking notes. Overall easy class but extremely boring and lifeless- go take social psy instead.

Dr. Day cares about all of her students and grades easily. Even though participation isn't tracked, go to lectures because that is what the exams are all based in. Lectures are not traditional and revolve around examples of cog psy topics more than anything. My least favorite psych class I've taken because course content felt sparse.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I learned nothing in this class. Dr. Day is a kind lady, but she refuses to change her lecture style--basically talking at you with slides. Slides are engaging, but useless. I would show up to class and zone out. Work was manageable: 4 2-page papers and research proposal, but grades are VAGUE. 1-5 scale with +/-, so we couldn't calculate grades
she is a nice person but oh my god her lectures are so boring. and half the time she's talking about herself. tests weren't too bad but don't put yourself through this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--EXTRA CREDIT--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She was super sweet and really cared about the topic. She makes an effort to engage the class through many demonstrations, which is why its important to show up (slides also aren't posted online). Most of your grade comes from a midterm and final (noncumulative) and a project where you create your own demo for the class which is fairly easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Extremely boring lectures. Textbook is great - cogpsych is super interesting & easy to understand. Day is smart & knowledgable, but too arrogant & not a good teacher. Only 2 tests, a project, and online labs. Tests were whacky and confusing - had to memorize her bad teaching to do well; actual knowledge didn't help too much. Waste of a bad grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Quirky, funny, and really enthusiastic about the subject matter. This class seems to be right in the wheelhouse of her research. Readings were rarely discussed in class, but participation and attendance were really important. No exam or final paper, but three short papers over the course of the semester. Easy but still interesting.

Professor Day is really nice, but a little full of herself. She thinks she knows everything about everything. However, this doesn't affect the class at all. If you go to every lecture and do all the reading the tests are super easy, and she's an easy grader on other assignments. The material is boring, but a pretty easy class.

This class was so unbelievably boring that it was the first time I distinctly looked forward to being out of a class at Duke. She clearly thinks she is the coolest thing out, and has a very superior air to her. I wouldn't recommend this class if you are just taking survey level classes for a psych major/minor. Take a different one.

Extremely boring class. The material is mostly uninteresting, her lectures have the appearance of being organized but are actually very difficult to take organized notes on, and she's rather obsessed with herself. She's always telling anecdotes about how much of boss she thinks she is from working at Yale and traveling around the country. Egotistic

She's extremely enthusiastic professor who uses very elaborate and clear ppt notes to supplement lecture. All of her examples are very applicable to real life, and I have personally found myself unintentionally using concepts learned in this class in others ones. Tests mostly based off lecture, so if u attend class & read the book, u shud do fine!

She's an extremely enthusiastic professor who uses very elaborate and clear ppt notes to supplement lecture. All of her examples are very applicable to real life, and I have personally found myself unintentionally using concepts learned in this class in others ones. Tests mostly based off lecture, so if u attend class & read the book, u shud do fin
Likes to brag. Not to teach.
This professor was very into herself and not helpful at all. The class was OK and assignments were random but easy.

Due to the boring and irrelevant teaching style, this was the worst class I have ever taken at Duke.  The material wouldn't be difficult if it was taught correctly, so my advice to anyone attempting to take Cognitive Psy: Please do not take it with Ruth Day.  She's kind, yet boasts of herself often&doesn't have the teaching abilities to back it up.

I'm a psych minor and this was one of the most boring classes I've ever taken. prof Day is very nice and certainly animated in lectures, but the material covered is useless. very few grades in the class - one midterm, one paper, one final, so if you mess one up it's hard to recover. wouldn recommend this class. not sure why others r so enthusiastic

Grading entirely based on short papers. Grades on papers are seemingly arbitrary and there are clear favorites in the class. Final grades are completely subjective and in general not reflective of effort put into assignments. Lectures did not do much at all to inform assignments, so much guesswork is involved.
somewhat self-centered, vague, apparently never gets enough sleep, verbose in lectures
A miserably vague teacher.  She mostly gets by on charisma, not substance.   Just can't structure a class.

Great professor--really enthusiastic and tries to make lectures fun with demos...though the format is weird, the tests are easy if you go to class. She really wants students to do well and tries to get to know everyone. Definitely take 92 with her!

awesome class, day does lots of demos to keep the class interesting, cog labs are very easy to get good grades on, would definitely recommend this class to anyone...this class is not boring! and people say her grading is subjective, but she tries to be very fair and understanding...day is a great teacher genuintely enthusiastic about what shes teac
Too excited for her own good.  Tests were oddly formatted, but alright in difficulty.  The 'CogLabs' were really hard to get a good grade on.  Subjective on final grades.

lots of demos, tries to get to know her students.  I can see why some people might not have liked the class itself, but I definitely enjoyed it and would recommend it - and would recommend Prof. Day for any class...

Good professor. Interesting lectures. Uses a lot of demonstrations. Easy tests (if you bother to read and attend class) and, although her grading scale is a little subjective, it is also fair. She also tries to get to know her students outside of class. I recommend taking Psy 92 with Dr. Day.

Agree that she is a space cadet, but I found that made the lectures a bit more interesting.  Her tests are not very hard, and she does try to get to know her students, even though this is a big lecture.
I tried believing the positive comments about her and it DID NOT PAY OFF. She is a space cadet who gives boring lectures, terrible tests, and has subjective grading.
pompous boring terrible exams- doesn't matter if you study
She's completely overrated.  Totally subjective, not objective in the least... People only say she's a good teacher, 'cause she hypes herself up so much, and they're too afraid to disagree.
If you like self-promotion, name dropping, and pompousness, take a class with her.  Class time was often wasted and dull.  Take 92 with anyone but her!!
No Comments
She was one of my better profs, actually cared and was enthusiastic, and fair too.
Excellent teacher, makes everything fun and class has tons of live experiments.  Fun and easy, take 92 only with her.

Professor is inconsistent, does not know how to use Sakai, and has poor communication. Clearly has strong opinions about the course but welcomes push-back from students. Class is overall easy and chill.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: i love her. teacher that really cares about her students and wants to make a difference. definitely a doable class almost everyone gets As, she will say a crazy thing here and there but laugh along.

Blatant lies, voodoo science, encourages political activism. Strong on "manipulating" patients. Encourages "stretching" medical records for political causes. Much more a political activist than honest MD. Really! Someone needs to review her records and billing practices!!!!!

She is one of my favorite professors of all time and I am planning on taking another one of her classes! She is really understanding and truly cares about her students and if they are engaging with the material - she just wants everyone to think and makes the seminar really a seminar!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Shes not the worst, but dont put your future in her hands. She doesnt give much guidance, often makes irrational and uninformed claims, and even believes zoophilia and bestiality are part of the LGBTQ community (dont believe me? Read the article LGBTQ...Z? Easy A but you wont learn or be challenged.

Worst prof I've had at Duke. Tells you incorrect things about science (like whales can time travel). Was supposed to be advanced GSF class but we didn't read a single scholarly feminist text and hardly talked about gender. Paper prompts were terrible, grading based on whether you agree with her. Interesting discussions though, makes you think.

Kathy is a caring person, class was interesting and completely discussion based (we throw out opinions and debate but we don't actually learn anything). But only 20% of your grade comes from that-- the other 80% comes from 4 essays. She doesn't teach you how to write or what she's looking for in these essays, so that sucked. Don't expect to learn.

Unclear grader, leads repetitive and boring discussions and comes back to the same 5 arguments all the time. Extremely easy class though, so if you're looking for a class with no work and 3 papers based solely on your opinion , then this is the class for you.

Besides the 3 papers based solely on your opinion (which are pretty short), there is absolutely no work in this class. We discussed interesting topics and the discussions were pretty informal and relaxed. The way she grades is very mysterious and unclear. It was an interesting class but very superficial. Would recommend it if you want an easy class

Nature, Culture, Gender was one of the coolest classes I have ever taken at Duke. Kathy gave us total freedom to discuss whatever we felt was relevant and made the class a fun and exciting space. The topics were super fascinating and very thought-provoking. She is a kind and warm-hearted person, too.
Kathy is one of the best professors I've ever had. Her passion and competence in her field are obvious. I would recommend her to anyone.

Rudy has a real interest in what she teaches. She picks great texts, with a few exceptions, and really got me engaged in the class. She's extremely flexible on deadlines, project ideas, and curriculum. Tries to mix different types of media for a comprehensive learning experience. My only complaint is that she can be a bit one-sided.

Dr. Rudy is a very engaging professor and all of the discussions and topics we cover are very interesting. She gets you thinking. There is not a lot of work for this class but you do learn a lot. Do well on teh essays and make sure to PARTICIPATE in discussion.
Amazing! By far one of the coolest Profs I've had at Duke. The class is pretty easy, but more importantly, will get you thinking. By far one of the greatest Profs Ive had...Take her class!!

Great professor. She gets you to think hard about ideas (relating to gender, race, and class of course) you take for granted in your everyday life. Definitely the best class I took my first semester freshman year. And, yes, guys should take this, too.
She is really fun and definitely knows what she is talking about. She streched my mind and the class has definitely affected by perception of who I am and the world around me.

Interesting debates, not too many books to read, but the ones you do read are great.  Only 5 easy papers based solely on your opinion.  Rudy some times pulls facts from no where to get a shock factor some times, which can be annoying.  She also has an agenda.  She wants you to adopt her opinion.  Other wise, easy, interesting A class.
best teacher here.
No Comments
Extremely interesting class. Professor knows what shes talking about and is very happy to share her opinions and engage in discussions with students.
The best professor at Duke
I think she goes for the 'shock factor' and ended up alienating me.  I think she really does care about what her students learn but wow.
Kathy is great but her co-teacher is not that great.  She (Tina Kampt)tries to make it a bit more theoretical than it needs to be and is not every clear sometimes.  But Kahty is a lot easier.
Dr. Rudy is one of Duke's greatest.  She's knows her stuff and she's funny.  Unfortunately, she relies a little heavily on TAs.
Dr. Rudy gave us false grades as part of a "social experiment." Not cool.  Other than that, the class was interesting and dynamic, and the books were terrific.
You have to read a few books, and her TA Lorna was annoying as hell, but the grade is entirely based on a few very easily-graded papers.  She's very knowledgeable and easy going.
wow, not a cool class...

She was a new instructor but had a lot of research experience. I liked the way she kept motivated in Biological mental disorder class. She went out of her way to help me with explanation with the research topic and gave extra credit to help improve class grades.

Dr. Gupta was more focused on making the class as hard as possible than engaging in any way. Exams were basically a test of regurgitating the textbook verbatim, and she tried to justify this by saying that we had it "easier" since we were online. She was not understanding of her students' concerns at all, and her lectures were unbearably stale.

Exams were tough and detailed, but within the textbook. This class was sort of Summer boot camp for neurology basic concepts. Dr. Gupta gave me time outside the class whenever needed and was encouraging. Extra-credit opportunity helped me to increase my overall performance. I enjoyed poll questions and discussion sessions. but too much work.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Mandatory lectures were not helpful or engaging -- read slides word for word with little explanation & slides just quoted the dense textbook. 3 exams (20% each) & 2 quizzes per class (out of 5 points each). Gives little insight for FRQs/writing assignments, causing mass confusion & frustration. Isn't the most understanding of student concerns.

Dr. Gupta's lectures were one of the most unhelpful and stale lectures I have ever experienced. The 1st test was tough on time, the 2nd was a lot more leniently graded, and the 3rd was unnecessarily in-depth. In addition, she assigns pointless (and sometimes outdated) research papers. Most of the class got an A- or A but the stress isn't worth it.

Kind professor but overall, the grading criteria was unclear - especially on the extra credit assignment she gave and short answer qs. Feedback was not great in class; created confusion. She needs more experience teaching because it was clear she didnt know how to best stimulate engagement in class and help students understand concepts.

She initially said that she will only give out +/- grades without just As or Bs or Cs. This made me withdraw from the class. She later changed her words halfway through the course that she will give out whole letter grades as well. I wouldn't have withdrawn if she said that earlier. Her syllabus was very uninformative in terms of grading policy.

There were two quizzes every class about the previous chapter and reading. A lot of question on the exam. Rarely provided her insight on the topic. Doesn't give you a clear answer to questions. Probably one of the worst classes I've had and lost interest in class. Avoid this professor if you can. Would not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Lectures are verbatim her reading slides, not really insightful answerer to questions. Daily quizzes on the previous chapter and the chapter for that lecture, not too bad just stay on top of work. The exams are really a test of time management. Take it during the year or if you are not doing anything else over summer.
so so incredibly boring, wouldn't take this class if you don't have to

Not the most inspirational professor I've had but pretty solid and knows his stuff. Lectures stick to pertinent material and what you need for the tests. Group projects are randomly assigned and hit-or-miss depending on how your group is. Tests are open note so can be kind of tricky, but overall fair.
He is such a boring lecturer but honestly is an extremely easy class. Definitely take it for MMS.

Dr. Donovan is the best!!! He is an engaging and insightful lecturer - and really funny! The assignments are really clear and he is very available to talk during office hours. You have to read/watch a lot of plays for this class, which can be difficult during busy weeks, but just time it right and you'll be fine. Recommend all his classes!
you were good sir

Ryan is an incredible and understanding professor! I feel that my musical theater performance skills blossomed in his class. I wish I could take this class again times a million. There were only a couple of written assignments, and they were actually enjoyable to complete!

Hands down one of the most inspiring, approachable, and passionate professors I've had at Duke so far. Every single person in our class made notable progress as a performer and experienced breakthroughs in our acting/singing skills. Would HIGHLY recommend this class to anyone even slightly interested in theatre/performing!

Ryan is an amazing professor point blank. Hes incredibly knowledgeable, cares a lot about theatre, and gives really helpful feedback in class. I made a huge amount of progress as a performer in this class and watched my classmates do the same. I even switched around my classes for the upcoming semester so I could continue to work with him. 5/5

Dr. V is amazing! The field trips are some of the most fun you can have in any class at Duke and you can really tell Dr. V is super passionate about fungi. Their is little to no work outside of class and there were constantly new things to do in lab!

rytas is truly one of the kindest and most caring profs out there. syllabus looks intimidating but our class was very chill. you wont know your grade until the end and there is almost little to none feedback on assignments but  if you show him you care about the material (even a little bit) its hard not to do well. we took a lot of field trips.

rytas talks a lot then quizzes you on absurd details and facts that are not really helpfult o learning. in essence you can litsen to this guy for hours and get quizzed on a small nuance that he covered barely or is jus tbarely in the textbook making it really a case where every last detail is potentially quizzed which is absurd and poor learning.
Dr. V is awesome! One of the chillest professors at Duke. He's really nice and also willing to talk with you outside of class. Fun class and fun professor!

Dr. Vilgalys is amazing! He's clearly so passionate about his fungal research, and he makes every topic in Bio 557L interesting. We took 2 or 3 field trips, which were really fun and educational. There's almost no homework (just a few blog posts about current microbe related articles) and if you show him that you care, you'll definitely do well!

Dr. Vilgalys is super chill and really tries to make class enjoyable. Asked us what kind of field trips we were interested in and took us on several to see microbio "in the field". If you pay attention and contribute to discussion, you'll be fine. He just wants you to learn and he's happy to talk to students about interests outside of class.

Dr. Vilgalys is incredibly knowledgeable and his lectures are interesting and funny. The class is long and heavily discussionparticipation based, so you have to read outside of class and show up, but once there, it's not a lot of work and no tests. Highly recommend this professor!

Microbio is NOT my thing, but Vilgalys was great. He and the TA both led the class. He's patient, understanding, and enthusiastic. Participation in didn't find out where I stood discussions are a must. I grade-wise until the end, but he is more than fair. No final, just a 5 pg single spaced term paper and presentation.

His tests are difficult.  It is possible to do well them if you memorize every facts on the lecture slide and study guides, though some poorly written questions can still throw you off.  Lectures were useless, but the textbook helped a lot to clarify and elaborate on things.  He's a very nice man and is glad to help if you go to him.

Take this class just for the lab! Lectures were so boring and not very useful (study guides are provided for tests).  If you do go, don't buy the textbook!  Beware the unknowns project - requires extra lab attendance outside of reg hours.  Tests were poorly written and on unimportant info, but still pretty easy.  I do admire Vilgalys' enthusiasm.
great teacher, clear and interesting lectures, fair tests, and helps if you need it! labs are useful too... lots of basic techniques.
Class is interesting, but the tests are on the most random information possible.  Class is good, exams are not.

Rytas is awesome, best prof I've had at duke.  teaches so that you'll remember what you've learned after the class.  really gets to know his students on a personal level.  one of the few times i've wanted to do work out of respect for my prof.  very laid back as well.
Professor is great - really loves his subject and wants students to understand.

Don't take microbio from this man; take it from the other teacher.  His lecture consists of reading from slides (which he puts online).  His tests are hard, involving random pointless details that really don't seem that important to the subject matter.  And don't buy the book, you won't need it.

Take this course if you enjoy classical worm and fly genetics, want to improve your ability to read primary literature, and want to improve your presentation skills. We read two papers per week, and each class was other students presenting each paper for 45 mins. Everyone presents twice and Dr. Baugh + class gives great feedback. Would recommend!

Ryan Baugh was an absent, uncaring prof who didn't rly seem to want to be there (and it showed). Was rude to students and didn't rly engage with them. Seems like the type of prof who is suited for research and research alone. Study for the quizzes, do well on labs, hope for the best.

The course is intellectually challenging and professors are nice, but not so good for my GPA. I got almost perfect on prelabs and postlabs, and slightly above the average on quizzes and exams, watched all the flipped classes, went to all the in-person lectures, even did 80% additional practice problems, spent a ton of time but still got an B+.

Taught Bio201 with Allison Hill. His slides were much better and much clearer than hers. His recorded lectures were also much clearer and easier to understand than Allison's. I never went to in person lecture due to the flipped classroom-but we did have open note so the exams were quite easy if you knew the content but not the little details.

Taught lecture with another professor, nothing special but relatively clear lecturing. TAs are dispersed throughout the class to help answer questions which makes a difference, also receptive to speaking after class.

You get graded on 3 things in this class - worksheets (completion), 2 presentations, and participation. He does rate you honestly by how much you participate. And even though the presentations seem long, he interjects during them (politely) with side notes if anyone gets confused. The papers can be difficult to present on, but he will help you out.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: This class has some challenging content, but the professors work really hard to make everything accessible to everyone. I personally like Dr. Baugh's lecture style -- I think having a flipped classroom (pandemic) helped, because everything was direct and to the point.

Nothing great or terrible, just not great at explaining the concepts properly as well as random asides and unanswered questions. Assessment were basically all memorization, and not conducive to doing well as a non pre-med. Don't think memorizing slides is the way to be learning material. Not a great experience, although generally a nice guy.

Take this class for your Bio capstone. Baugh is the best. No tests or papers. Weekly quick HW questions on readings and whole semester you just give 2 class pwrpnt presentations on a paper you read. Otherwise you sit and listen and say 2 things every class for participation. Super chill, give a good effort when presenting & almost everyone got an A

It doesn't matter who teaches 201, just memorize powerpoint information (or put on cheat sheet) for each test/quiz. Baugh was new to 201 this year - switches with Hill lecturing a powerpoint. He's okay but tends to be more confusing than Hill and likes to ask questions but not answer them and doesnt fully explain things well.
He is ice cold and extremely full of himself. He stands out simply as a mean professor among the mostly warm biology faculty. Avoid

Baugh is a really nice guy and a great lecturer. Bio 220 (cell and developmental) was tough for me, especially since I was not familiar with many experimental techniques. it's a great class, I don't know if I've learn more in a class than that. Genes and Development was a great seminar style class where you present papers. Baugh was very helpful
I had a really hard time with Bio220, but I don't blame either of the professors for it. Baugh is a pretty decent lecturer.

Meh. A lot of his lectures are heavily based on his research (C.Elegans) , so you better get familiar with worms. Overall the class isn't awful but make sure to record the lectures cause this guy goes 500 miles per hour through the material.
Great lecturer!

Class listed as Genes and Development at the time (now listed under Bio262, I think). Fantastic course and highly recommended to anyone who enjoys science. Very interesting topics/papers and discussions were engaging. That being said, those with a weak science background (who for some reason sign up for a 200-level?) will struggle mightily.

Can seem rather cold in this large course context, but mostly because everyone is always complaining about their grades. Very knowledgeable and enjoys talking with students about science. Bio119 is a hard class: deal with it.

Terrible Professor. One of the worst in the whole department--and I'm a bio major. He absolutely hates premed kids and thinks everyone only wants to go to medical school to "have a comfortable lifestyle" and "drive a nice car". He doesn't care about anything other than his precious C. elegans worms research.

Lectures were a little slow, but he very genuinely cares about the content, which is pleasant and inspiring.  You get out what you put in for this class, in terms of learnings.  The course itself is not difficult to meet deliverables.  But apply yourself and you can grow and build skills.

This class is relatively easy for military personnel because we discuss leadership on almost a daily or weekly basis.  All the examples of good and bad leadership have been shown in a JO's career for a typical sub officer.  This class is extremely beneficial for non-military students in building their portfolio.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Ryser was one of the best professors I have ever had. He was a clear lecturer, assigned reasonable homework, and presented fair exams. Occasionally he had in-class quizzes, which helped keep students on track. His office hours were a bit crowded, but they helped immensely. Also, he's pretty down-to-earth and understands students' circumstances.

Was a great lecturer when he was around, but he rarely made time for students outside of a couple of crowded office hours for 2 hrs a week. He went out of town during the toughest week of the course, so that definitely hurt us on the final.
Has low expectation.

FANTASTIC professor! Very accessible, very helpful, fantastic lecturer, great humor. No grades really existed until the final, but I believe my class's section did exceptionally well. If you need to take Math 353, take it with Ryser any day. His class was at 8:30 but I'm so glad I took it based on what I've heard about the other professors. 10/10

Silvia is a really chill professor - really nice grading on the quizzes and writings, and its basically just structured after the textbooks like the rest of the Spanish classes are- there are like 5 group projects but they're super easy and she really is so helpful! Overall easy class with nice grading and tbh participation matters, lots of easy hw

She really cares that you become comfortable in Spanish and focuses a lot on speaking/conversation/presentation. There's homework every night, but it's never too hard. Class participation matters, but she never pressures you to chime in. She's so welcoming and approachable.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Super nice prof! There is a lot of work for a 200-level Spanish course, but a lot of intro Spanish courses consist of work that isn't necessarily helpful. Silvia is very lenient with grading and is nice to all of her students.

do the work and you will be fine.  Don't do the work and you won't be fine. But its not that much work, so just do it. She makes topics clear and is understandable. Wish I could take another Spanish class with her. Learned alot!

Soo I took Spanish 102 with Silvia in my freshman year and it went pretty well! She's caring and she gave effective feedbacks, but she made 102 harder than it should be, especially with the presentations.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This class was just exceptionally boring which is not really the professor's fault. She mostly just read the slides to us and all of the work for the class was done outside of the classroom. I would not recommend this class, as it is just constant writing. There is a graded assignment pretty much every day. That being said, they're not very hard.

Silvia likes to group her students based on if she likes them or not. She also will favor students over others based on how outgoing or enthusiastic you are about Spanish, even if you do well and participate in the class. She would grill a couple of students in my class, including me, and she would make us feel less confident about our skills.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Silvia is easily one of the nicest professors I have had at Duke. She is easily accessible, and helped me improve my Spanish skills exponentially. Quizzes are hard, so study! Take advantage of her office hours!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She's a great teacher who really just wants everyone to do well. I took her radio class which was basically a semester long project so it was pretty easy to do well if you just did all your work. She really cares about her students and is super open to feedback about the level of work or if due dates are too sudden. Love her and you should def take
Profe Silvia is one of the best professors I have had during my time at Duke. Spanish is not easy, but she makes class interesting.

Silvia is wonderful! There is a decent amount of work for the class but I feel like everything was relevant, which is uncommon for most language classes. My Spanish genuinely improved. She's very friendly and just an overall great professor.

Silvia packs in way too many activities during class time and makes class unbearable. Also gives way too many assignments and busy work outside of class. Does not really offer outside help and is not friendly. Would not recommend.
Great professor.

Prof. Lai-Henderson is an exceptional instructor who made sure the classes were interactive. The workload is decent and comprises of extremely fun presentations and oral assessment. She is very caring, granting assignment extensions upon request. Highly recommended for anyone who wants to improve his public speaking and writing skills.
She is an okay teacher, her classes can sometimes be slow and does not provide clear feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: A very good class, one of my favorites. Professor Lai-Henderson does care about students. Your writing will definitely be improved if you take this class and follow all instructions. All readings are well-selected (some are long, but every one is worth of reading). Make sure to do critical readings those are super helpful when you write essays.

Prof. Lai-Henderson is a wonderful professor!! Her class is well-organized, with a great balance of lectures and discussions. She will provide you with helpful feedback and suggestions so that you could progress a lot throughout the course. Will definitely take her class again! Also, Lit 309 is a wonderful class, the readings are  interesting.

Professor Lai-Henderson is an incredible professor, with a focus on not just student participation but an active interest in her student's lives and how they connect to class material. She gives excellent writing feedback as well. Regarding class content, I think her courses are always well-organized and interesting regardless of the material.

Professor Lai-Henderson is caring about our difficulties during this COVID time. She gives us a lot of positive energy. And Professor Lai-Henderson respects our contribution and inspires us to dive into the reading materials more deeply. She conveys the material very clearly too and always tries her best to engage everyone into deep reflection.

Professor Lai-Henderson's classes are extremely interesting and lively. Throughout the course, she always encouraged us to share our opinions and the discussions were very pleasant. GCHINA101 is quite a heavy class, but Professor Lai-Henderson's very helpful and makes you actually want to do the work.

This teacher is very caring and goes beyond her duties as a teacher. During the pandemic, she was very understanding towards everyone's situations and would give extensions if needed. The class discussions were very intriguing and I enjoyed all of her classes.

Professor Lai-Henderson is a great professor to have under a difficult curriculum, as she will make sure that everyone understands the content during each class discussion. Amidst a course as rigorous as GChina 101, this type of instruction is really helpful for not being too overwhelmed with readings and deadlines.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Lai-Henderson is a very caring Professor! She is beyond just a professor that is trying to teach! She tries to help with every effort she can with the question or problem you are facing! I really enjoyed having her as my professor through the tough common core class, GCHINA 101.

Prof. Lai-Henderson gave many inspirational ideas in class about the texts and readings. You can learn much about American literature and history! Students are encouraged to have free opinions in their essays and forums!

Prof. Lai-Henderson is very friendly and inspirational!!! Her teaching ideas are surprising but meaningful. In her class, students can cover various topics and themes. The role-play and analytical essay helps me understand this lesson better. Highly recommended!!!!
Heavy emphasis on the debates, which take up a significant part of your final grade. This basically means attendance is mandatory.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: I had an extremely positive experience in this class with Prof. SLH. She always offers to look over drafts before you turn them in and will give feedback on how to improve. In-class debates are a solid portion of the grade but don't stress, she grades for well-prepared/smart arguments and solid effort more than just who "wins" it.
Dr Lai-Henderson has a slow pace of teaching which can be good if you are a slow reader. However, she does not push students to speak up so the small group discussions are never too active.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: I took ARHU101 with Selina Lai-Henderson. The pace of the course was very slow and I wish we learned more.

She is so caring. The class is super mellow, but I still learned so much. The debates can be a little stressful, but they became sorta fun by the end. We had class outside a bunch too so thats a big plus!!
it's a shame that this legend is no longer teaching at Duke. Fly high Paul Seli

10/10. Absolute legend. Miss his lectures. He just loves psychology and research (and teaching). He makes you really invested in the material. I even spent time out of the class thinking about topics we discussed. He was always available to answer questions too. By far the best professor I've had at Duke. Highly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: If you want to LEARN and THINK and GROW as a student, take his class. I can't stress how rare it is to find a prof as brilliant, engaging, and creative as Dr. Seli is. He doesn't care about busy work. He cares about helping students understand real world problems by applying cognitive theories / frameworks. I wish he taught more courses. THANK YOU!

Dr. Seli is the best lecturer I've ever had, bar none! He cares so much about his students, he's incredibly engaged and engaging, he's hyper-intelligent and creative, his lectures are full of passion and excitement, and he clearly cares so much about his students loving and learning the material. Prof Seli is the G.O.A.T!
Amazing professor and engaging lectures. Definitely recommend.
Don't get the hype with this professor. So incredibly disorganized and gives lectures seemingly with nothing to do with cognitive psych. But we still have exams pertaining to cognitive psych content.

Paul is the best professor I've had at Duke. He's super young, his lectures were like mini TedTalks, and he brings in the most interesting guest lecturers. He really cares about students, will change around the syllabus if you like a specific unit and want more of it, and is so laid back. He inspired me to take more psych classes. TAKE HIS CLASS!

Paul Seli is the most engaging lecturer I have had at Duke. I always look forward to his lectures, as he is a young, interesting, funny guy, who does cool research and cares a lot about his work and the students. I am not a Psych major but I would love to take another class with him.
This is one of the best classes that I have taken at Duke! He is super knowledgeable and very easy to reach if you ever need help. Overall would recommend this professor to anyone!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Paul really was one of the best profs i've ever had at duke. absolutely loved his class. the environment was very laid-back, yet dynamic. i learned a lot more than i had initially anticipated. Also, he is willing to discuss research and even help generate it outside of class. One of the most engaged professors ive ever seen. 10/10.

Paul Seli (rhymes with Eli, not Ellie) is an absolute legend. He genuinely wants students to engage with fascinating research questions and actively encourages further discussion on the articles we discuss in class. He's an incredibly nice guy who is super fun!!
Take his classes if you like drawing/art but haven't had an opportunity to explore that hobby. If you're more serious and want critical feedback, you may not get it.

He is a nice guy. But we did 76 sketches in one semester and he gave very vague feedback for the drawing since he wanted us to "find our voice." He is a nice guy though and he seems to have great expertise in the intersection of arts and science. Don't take traditional drawing with him.

He is very intelligent and knowledgeable but doesn't always have a plan for the class period. This particular class was very open-ended, but I still think I learned a lot. I would suggest asking him questions about his art and other artists to learn even more.
Bill's extremely knowledgeable and gives great feedback. I'd definitely recommend taking a class with him if you're interested in New Media / Art.
Bill really wants his students to be inspired and learn as much as they can. Great guy! He is also so knowledgable about so many topics.
Seaman is the sweetest! He cares so much about his students and is so passionate about his discipline. Unfortunately, classes are very long and a little boring, but the work is pretty enjoyable.

I loved the class! Prof. Yang is an amazing professor and a super friendly person overall. Be prepared, though—the quizzes progressively increase in difficulty, and the exams can be quite challenging. I found the class to be a little hard, but you will get a good grade if you put in the effort. She gives a lot of opportunities for extra credit.

Professor Yang was very nice, organized, and knowledgable. The class was mostly easy, except the tests were graded extremely harshly, no partial credit even for small spelling mistakes. The tests also emphasized listening comprehension which was easy for some people but not for me.

Professor Yang is very nice and sweet. Class is easy A. There are a lot of quizzes and tests but they don't carry a significant weight in the final score. However, if you actually want to be proficient in the language then put more hours and effort into the class.
She is a very nice instructor, and her class is fun and engaging. However, be prepared for the 4 tests and 8 quizzes with an increasing level of difficulty.

Professor Yang taught my discussion section for Korean 101, and it was so much fun! I got to improve my speaking and listening while having fun with my classmates and learning about topics that are really applicable for day-to-day life.

Holly is the sweetest. She is more human than most professors and cares about her students. She makes o chem super fun and interesting and makes the content digestible and wants all her students to succeed. Nearly everyone in that class applied to be her ta.

Dr. Sebahar guest-lectured a class last week. In those 75 minutes, my entire view of chemistry changed. It was as if she whispered the answers right into my head. This lady is more than a teacher. She is a magician, a poet, and above all, an inspiration. You are foolish if you take chem with anyone else. Dr. Sebahar, if you read this...I love you.
Very clear and helpful. Instruction surpassed that received in itro level chem courses.
nice

Dr. Sebahar is one of the most dedicated, helpful professors. Before tests (and all the time) she makes herself available to help everyone. She wants you to succeed and understand the material. She is an outstanding professor and great lecturer. Since she is so generous, everyone in the class tries hard so reading and studying are a must to do well

Holly was eager to teach, eager to help students, always thoughtful. If you didn't understand her explanation she found another way to explain it.  Taking her class is a must, learning orgo in her conceptual approach is 10 times more effective than the memorization approach to orgo most other profs take.

If Holly is teaching orgo, take it with her. She is clear, makes the material easy, and helpful. I would say the best way to take this course is to read the book sections she has on the outline before class, come to class and listen, and then do all the recommended problems and recitation sheets as practice for the tests. Great teacher.

Great instructor, very enthusiastic and encouraging.  However, the good things also have strings attached...because she is generous, the average is really high, so in the end, those who do their best are at times outshone by those who may just "get it."  However, a definite "must-take" if she is an option.  Very nice and kind.
She is so nice!!! I think she is one of the best teachers of chem. Explains well, eager to help, dynamic, understanding, and friendly. I couldn't stand orgo without her, and actually I liked orgo.
I was one of the few ppl who did not find Holly adorable.  I thought she wasn't that good of a teacher, and she was pretty impatient when I went to her for help.

Dr. Sebahar is probably the best professor I've had at Duke so far. She is not only a great lecturer, but also a good person and educator. In ADDITION to being extremely available during office hours (3x per week!), she posts TONS of worksheets to Blackboard that closely resemble test problems, as well as ALL of her lecture notes.
People told me otherwise, but to me she seemed nice and laid back. Obviously prepare to work hard cuz its orgo, but keep up w/ the material so u understand lectures and u'll be fine.
One of the best (if not THE best) professors I have had! Very approachable, like a mom next door.
Holly Sebahar is a ****.  Straight up.
OK KIDDOS!

Sebahar is absolutely fantastic! Her lectures are so organized and helpful; they make orgo reasonably easy to sink in. She is a very nice person and really wants to help you succeed, especially if you go to review sessions + office hrs.
Dr. Sebahar is one of the best professors I've had.  She is an awesome lecturer, and extremely helpful.
No Comments
Very organised teacher who makes her teaching material available. Posts helpful practice problems and is willing to help.
This course has a lot of readings. Not the mistake of Prof.Cho. But some unreasonable gradings of participations and group work. I don't understand. Will give you a scaring grade with smile.
Grading is all over the place. Class is online even after covid. A waste of time and money.

A very caring professor, taking care of her students' needs. Her classes are easy to take part in and participation grade is easily obtained. Her grading is inconsistent and many students couldn't predict their final grades. Strict grader from Week 1 despite students not knowing how to write the assignment given, but gets more lenient later.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--So many papers--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Tests were basically impossible. If you're good at strict memorization on random and obscure things that will never help you in anything else? Then sure, take the class. Papers were graded differently based on who graded (TA or Selig), and it's just not worth memorizing thousands of slides for no reason. Took it S/U and it was still a brutal final.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I thought Selig was a great lecturer: dry sense of humor. No recordings :(, but as long as you take good notes you'll be set for two midterms. They're worth a lot which makes it hard to finish with an A ( I got a 91and79). He gave me a B+ on my paper but I thought that was fair. I should've taken it pass/fail for NS but I still enjoyed the class!

Dr. Selig is a nice prof who is relatable to students. He is very interested in the topics and offers time outside class to discuss. However, this class was very difficult at best. Exams were pure memorization of anything he could've said during a lecture. No lecture recordings, and lecture slides(often 50+ per lecture) had little information.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Don't take a class taught by Keegan. Lectures are super boring, he can't answer any questions asked by students, and the tests are genuinely impossible. He reads directly off of slides in lectures and they hardly contain any info. He will test you over things you either never learned, or talked about for 5 seconds in a random lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Long story short: I'm taking another class with him now after doing one two years ago. Very accessible outside class, loves getting to know students, and is great to talk to.

I took the half-credit national security simulation class led by Schanzer and Valens Global. The class was relatively fun, and it involved working with a group to represent a country or organization in a simulation. However, the grading seemed very vague and hard to get an A for a half-credit class, so a lot of people took the class pass/fail.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took this class as part of Duke in the Arab World. Schanzer taught half the course, and I learned lots about the political development of the region. He is very funny and well-connected. There was a lot of reading, and a policy memo and participation were the only graded things. It is a lot of work for an abroad class but also very interesting.
Very difficult class and tough grading, but amazing professor!

Professor Schanzer is incredible! He is so knowledgeable about so many topics, which shines through in his class. He also sets students up for success by teaching them how to write a policy memo; it is difficult, but it pays off in later public policy classes.

Class is basically a discussion for the whole time, and he is awesome at pressing on your views, improving your argument skills, and gives thorough. 2 10 pg essays, and a group final project writing a 20pg privacy assessment for an emerging technology make up 80% of the grade. Rest is 2 250 word blog posts/wk & participation.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Professor Schanzer is amazing. He's a tad intimidating when you first meet him, but he's extraordinarily bright and cares a lot about his students. The class is challenging, as there are a lot of readings - but they're interesting and easy to talk about in a debate-type setting (seminar class). Dave also teaches you how to write an effective memo.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Prof. Schanzer is an excellllllent teacher! He gave us so many practical instructions and push us to think harder. I learned how to write a good and succient policy memo during the course and it kind of shaped my writing styles afterwards. Neat, main points first as well as talk things undertandable. He is not a hard grader if he saw you work hard.

This was my favorite class in my first semester at Duke. I took the class as part of the Middle East FOCUS group.
