Schanzer's class is primarily discussion based and forces you to reckon with different/opposing ideas as well as constantly defend your own. The memos are definitely hard, but his feedback is really great and makes you a better writer.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Great professor - he clearly has a detailed understanding of the topics he teaches on and pushes you to understand things better. Hard grader, but worth it for the knowledge.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Professor Schanzer is an extremely knowledgeable professor who inspires his students with his love of the material he teaches. Schanzer expects students to keep up with the readings, but is not particularly harsh if you miss a chapter here or there. His classes are run in a discussion based style. Highly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Probably the most interesting class I've ever taken. I came in knowing nothing about astronomy and left feeling like I gained a huge amount of knowledge. Professor Scolnic is kinda odd but really funny. The class isn't graded on much so make sure to do well on the midterm and final.

scolnic is overqualified, (studies the expansion of the universe) but, isn't the best at explaining things. he sometimes confuses himself and then expects us to explain it. he's an odd guy but cares and wants you to learn. the tests were hard. the labs get annoying, but the TA was really helpful. not the worst class, but i wouldn't take it again.
He's really funny, and it felt like he really wanted us to learn.  Maybe the best teacher I've had.

One of the most wonderful humans I have ever met. I am glad that Duke and the Science Community has him. He is completely overqualified to teach Intro to Astronomy. He breaks complex concepts down to the fundamentals and makes the laws of the universe digestible. He has various methods of ensuring students are engaged with class.

Very easy A without having to put any work in. He's an odd guy which makes his lectures pretty entertaining. He does graded in-class polls so you do have to go to class to get credit. The students write the questions for the tests so those are easy. The labs are a lot of busy work. There are assigned readings, but you're fine if you don't do them.

His lectures are interesting, and he's an overall funny and nice guy. In most cases he seems to know his stuff, but sometimes he would seem to get confused about a subject which then in turn confused me. The labs and homework are easy, and as a whole this is a fun class to take if you're interested in astronomy and cosmology.

The exams were very easy. Many of the exam questions were from student submitted questions. There were lots of students who got perfect scores on the exams. It is easy to get A/A+ really. Very cool content if ur into astronomy and astrophysics. You will learn a lot of cool stuffs from this amazing professor.
hard class

Scolnic is a real astrophysicist and really knows his stuff. Very interesting content, and he makes the classes quite engaging through poll quizzes in class. He is also very funny and makes great jokes. Unfortunately the labs done independently of those lectures are quite tedious and counts a lot towards your grade. His exams are quite easy though.

DO NOT take this class if you are looking for an easy A. Inputs 30% of the your grade the night before the final and makes it extremely hard to get an A in the class. Lectures are mandatory and the timer on the in class polls make it hard to get answers right even if you know what it is.

phys134: Prof Scolnic was fantastic. content taught in a way that was v easy to digest & learn & he made a huge effort to engage with us. From playing content related songs at the beginning of every class, to encouraging Flunch, to making jokes at the end of every question of quizzes, he made this the most engaging and stressfree class I've taken

Professor Scolnic made class super interactive considering the circumstances. He is incredibly approachable and made abstract Physics concepts easily digestible in class. Each class as some board-writers and note-takers, so participation is fairly required. In the end, I gained a newfound appreciation of Physics of Sports.

Best teacher ever. Most chill, funny, laid-back professor I know but he's also super knowledgable about ML. You get out of the class what you put into it -- hw/attendance not required. Also knows about different career paths/job opportunities, east to contact/will meet outside of class. Unique project-based class style, but unclear grading (worth)
Genuinely insane guy. Best professor I've ever had at Duke & helped me figure out my entire life/career path. Still genuinely insane. Also get used to using Slack.

Incredible guy. Much self-learning. His lectures are mostly answering questions/some concept explanation. Can skip them but you are missing out- his dry humor is one-of-a-kind and his life advice is invaluable. Super interesting person with lots of sharp and witty commentary to deliver. Take his classes. occasional dirty mind trick

fun lectures + interesting humor + helpful if you need life/career/Duke advice or emotional support. time-consuming projects during the semester BUT doing them + reading the textbook make the final (50% of overall grade) easier. most difficult class in MESS but has material overlap w/ STA110FS (Dr. Banks' class). learn python before taking.

His class was really interesting, although it does throw you into the deep end with code. Don't let the poli sci part of the description fool you, the class is all coding. De Marchi is knowledgeable about a lot of fields. He's happy to give advice on a lot of things, from career advice to classes, and he's pretty funny if you like dry humor.

De Marchi is an absolute legend. Gives life lessons during lectures and literally "doesn't care". Makes the best jokes. Be ready to code, listen in class and you should be fine. Very accessible outside of class if you need help.
reviews.rating_tags: Hilarious--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: TAKE A CLASS WITH DR. DEMARCHI IF YOU CAN. NO MATTER THE GRADE YOU GET, YOU WON'T REGRET IT!

His FOCUS class is weirdly the hardest class I have ever taken but somehow had the least amount of work. The content is challenging, but he makes it digestible. However, a lot of the readings are self-paced, so you either have to 1) hold yourself accountable or 2) spend 20 hours on the final.

I took his Intro to Machine Learning class as part of the MESS FOCUS cluster, and having stats and coding background is very helpful. Professor de Marchi is a very funny person, and his lectures are always interesting. He also gives really good advice. However, he was not clear in how he graded, and the content itself is challenging but engaging.
Really amazing class, you will learn things that completely blow your mind. Can be overwhelming, but as long as you ask questions and put in the work to understand concepts, you should be fine

I enjoyed Prof. De Marchi's lectures and learned a good deal in his class. He's a funny guy with stories to tell. However, he lacks clear grading criteria, does not give constructive feedback, and is not interested in building relationships with undergrads. He's wicked smart but focused on his own project work.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor De Marchi is my favorite professor that I have had at Duke. He is an incredibly intelligent yet personable professor who is also hilarious. Class attendnece isn't neccessary but I would be sitting front and center every class. There were only two assignments all year which were both due at the end of the semester. Would highly recommend.
Very unclear grading criteria and unclear what he wants from papers. Really smart and funny guy, but hard to gauge. Minimal work.

Professor Demarchi is great! I cannot rate him higher! Some students feel that his lecture is unstructured, but in fact they are very well planned if you do the reading. The reading is not boring at all in contrast to what we read in other POLISCI classes. He will also change how you see the world.

It's hard to list specifics of what I learned from his lectures since they lack definite structure (the opposite goes for readings), but his class as a whole imparts a better understanding of our methods of understanding the world. He's also an eccentric and remarkably accessible treasure trove of solid life advice.
Best Prof at Duke! Smartest one! Change how you view the world!
best professor I've had at duke. don't go into class thinking you know anything at all, and be willing to have your world views be changed. more of a course on life stuff than anything else, take it.
Scott will change how you look at things. Cannot rate him high enough. If you have a chance, any chance, to have him as a professor or to talk to him, don't hesitate and do it.

Brilliant guy and a humorous teacher, but wholly unreliable when it comes to showing up places or answering e-mails. Was interested in the learning of students more than in their grades, but was plenty willing to be lenient in his grading due to the tough nature of the course. Take his class.
Some uptight people on here.  He's cynical but goood.
Hard to understand but interesting -- way more fun than not though and gives a lot of high grades if you do rewrites.

His lectures have nothing to do with the reading and his assignments (papers) have nothing to do with lectures. You are left on your own to figure out how to write a paper he likes. The lectures are disorganized& extremely confusing. He plays dirty mind trick and you are always the one who lost the game on the final.
Ask him about his cage fighting days.
Can't believe this Professor's evaluations are so good in here. Then again, he is all about groupies. His lectures were always unstructured, unorganized, poorly connected with readings.
Scott De Marchi/He's the best/He'll kill some/and choke the rest./The good he'll mock/The bad he'll slay/Here again/To save the day...Take any class offered by this man. He is "the bomb diggity"
you'll love de scott!

He's a really neat professor. Teaches stuff we'll really need to know and will remember in the future. Doesn't go over the books much, though - which is a problem when you get to the papers and the final.
take anything offered if scott is the teacher. even if you hate the topic, take the class.

He's a nice person and is always willing to answer my questions. He's not a harsh grader. However, his lecture is a total disaster. He even confuses himself when trying to explain the solutions. I learned this course almost everything by myself and this course is more like a study session with a friend who has the answers.

I don't understand the bad reviews for Schaad at all, he explains things well and is clear about course expectations, covers everything in the textbook and his course prepares you well for future technical interviews, very glad I took it with him since this is the most important course for mechanical/civil engineers
I liked CEE132 with

I'm thoroughly impressed with Schaad's inability to teach. Lecture after lecture, I ponder my decision to attend Duke - seeing my tuition dollars drift away like a leaf in the wind. Using the word "lecture" seems unfitting. It's like a study session, led by a friend with an answer key - who doesn't understand what the question is asking. Get better

He is the worst professor I have ever had. He cannot answer questions or solve problems without looking at the answer scheme first. The lowest you can get on exams is a 68% (even if you get everything wrong) so there is very little point in studying. Lovely person, but terrible professor.

Dr. Schaad is one of the most caring professors I've had so far at Duke. He truly takes the time to get to know his students. There are five big group projects and a few individual assignments. The grading criteria is not always clear, but you will generally end up with a grade that is satisfactory to you. Go to class because the quizzes are hard.

Professor Schaad is the best professor in the world, he's very chill and very patient, and makes sure you understand the content. He is so much fun and very interesting, the class is all group projects, and they're super cool. There are lectures each week from faculty in different fields of civil and environmental engineering. I love you Schaad!!

Really great guy and wants to support his students as much as possible. Grading criteria is sometimes not clear, but you likely will get a final grade that you're satisfied with. Class is mostly independent, so can't comment on teaching skills. Acts more as an advisor.

Schaads grading criteria is arbitrary. If you take the exam the worst you can do is 70 which benefits studying very little. He is also unable to lecture, he doesn't know the material and confuses students. Take it with anyone else, he's awful. His class is truly a joke. If possible Id give a zero. There arent enough characters to describe how bad.

Far and away the worst professor I've had at Duke. Impossible to reach via email, good luck if you need help with anything. Tests are written so poorly he has to give instructions as they are going on since the problems are impossible to solve without further instruction. Lectures are incoherent, I learned everything online.

Loved him! He really cares about the students, always listening if he needs to shift homeworks or tests in order to accommodate tests from other classes that we may have. He also gives fun extra credit like a Chapel climb or whitewater rafting! Try to pay attention to class to really learn, but if not, he gives enough practice to really understand!

Class consists primarily of guest lecturers who were rarely engaging/met students where they were at, but it was a good way to get an overview of many aspects of CEE. Class does not require too many hours a week of work but picks up a bit at the end. Overall a great bonding experience for CEE students but a relatively disorganized course

Schaad is the GOAT, the GOAT. No but for real, he's a great teacher, not much teaching just because the course is group/individual project based, but he's there if you need him and he keeps spirits bright. Really chill guy and just really caring. Definitely take his class and get to know him!

This class is mostly guest lectures which Schaad is on top of, but lecture quizzes can be out of date or have wrong answers. Design projects are fun but can be stressful. Ask questions when surveying is taught if you don't understand. Start on shop training and surveying project early! Ask him and other students if you need help. Overall fun class!

Always engaged and willing to help. He's a bit hands-off during the main design project (he always says "it's your design" lol) but that actually helped us learn. Went out of his way to help his groups such as long drives or getting materials on short notice. Not strict and his grading is fair. Overall really enjoyed the class with him!

one of the most engaging lecturers i've had at Duke, very interesting/relevant subject matter, passionate about topics. more work than expected but still manageable. cares about students. one thing is though that his grading criteria is very unclear. he's an unexpectedly tough grader for how chill he seems during class
Dr. Schaad is a great Egr101 professor. Very helpful and easy going. I'm glad I chose his section.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Schaad was an amazing professor! Definitely recommend you take a class with him!

Pretty good, but inconsistent on grading. Gives you a lower grade without any explanation and when you approach him, he says you did everything good. He is, otherwise, a good person and is super approachable and super real with you.

Dr. Schaad is a great professor who is really passionate about the topics he teaches. This class is not a ton of work but the work does come in waves and you have to make sure you pace yourself with your design work or else it will pile up before each deadline. Overall love Schaad and think everyone should take his class whether in CEE or not

Dr. Schaad is incredibly caring and will genuinely do whatever he can for his students. This course is relatively straight forward. Each lecture has a Sakai quiz, some of the questions are related to what seemed to be insignificant information. So it definitely helps if you attend the lectures but not required. There are 4 group projects.

The class is an overview of civil and environmental engineering with a focus on gaining hands on experience, learning new computer programs, and working on group projects. He's a tough grader on the projects but offers lots of opportunities for extra credit. Overall, it was a really fun class, and I enjoyed all the projects and field tours.

Schaad is the nicest professor I've had at Duke so far. Very kind, and always smiling. His lectures aren't the most useful - basically him writing solutions to practice problems - but you can learn everything you need to from the book. Extra credit helps a lot. Labs are not too bad, and most homework questions can be found online.

Schaad is really cool and understanding. He can be a bit scattered so he is forgiving if you don't understand the directions for a project/assignment. His grading is super clear and if you put in an appropriate amount of effort you can get an A.

Schaad is just great. 205 is a little more work than I expected for a half credit course, but overall a solid class. Most assignments are out of class and you stop meeting after Fall Break. Overall a great choice though.
reviews.rating_tags: GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: This class was the most boring class I've taken at Duke. He is a bad lecturer (all he does is copy solutions from a solutions manual during lecture) and not helpful with questions. He also never replies to emails. Not really that hard though. Would avoid.

It's hard to say a lot about Schaad because I was in his CEE 160 when he was in Africa for a few months. We had almost solely guest lecturers who were mostly good, but the quizzes afterward could be done without actually going to class. His lectures were far better and were not missable; the quizzes were harder. Do extra credit for a pretty easy A.

Professor went to Africa for a few weeks Ended up lasting a few months Comes back to dumbass students who haven't learned anything Going to class is not entirely necessary because the quizzes are mostly google-able questions and the material you learn is very accessible. Labs are probably the easiest things you'll ever do. Not hard class
Cool class and very hands on. Prof Schaad is a really nice guy that will help with whatever you need. Definitely can take this class with heavier course load since it doesn't take a lot of time.

PAY ATTENTION IN CLASS. There's an online quiz after every class, and the lecture slides he posts do not help (they're mostly pictures) and sometimes google didn't even help. For the classes I brought my laptop to and zoned out I had a very hard time with the quizzes, but for the classes I paid attention and took notes, the quizzes were super easy.

Personally, I was a bit frustrated by the class. Schaad will tell you that the online quizzes are ~10 questions each while more are around 30 and they ask  minute details from the lecture so you have to write down everything. That being said, if you do a ton of extra credit you should be guaranteed an A. Schaad is fine but not a great teacher.

I have also had Dr. Schaad for CE 100 and CE 24. I adore the man. He is a great professor, and really takes an interest in each of his students. With what other professorr will your assignments include growing a plant (CE 24), a machine shop project (CE 100), and designing a bridge to be implemented this summer in El Salvador (CE 185). Great Prof!!
Takes a decent amount of time for a half credit class, but Schaad really is great and the skills you learn in this class are important.
He is the man.  All he cares about if you learning stuff.  Make sure you do as much extra credit as possible in order to be sure to get an A
Super chilled as a professor. "Great!," "Wonderful!," "Excellent!" are the phrases around him. If you show a minimal amount of attempt to do well in the class, you will do well.

He's great! He's really laid back and easy to talk to. All the assignments are take home, and if you have any questions he's more than willing to help you out. He's the rare type of teacher that cares more about you learning the material than the average on his quizzes (incredibly high). If you can take a class from him (all CEs have to) do it!

Dr. Schaad makes engineering humane and personal. He organized a "Rebuilding from Ruins" class about New Orleans in 2006, which included Spring Break to New Orleans. Also, when I was in a bind he wrote me a great rec in 2 days. I agree that he is the best professor (that I had) at Duke.
Really laid back guy.
Dr. Schaad is the best teacher at DUKE!
He loves history and is funny. Be ready to enjoy the class. He is an easy grader too and is open for corrections and regrade for homeworks. I love him. Mmwuah
He confused himself and confused us. But he was sweet.

Lectures were dense and didnt actually teach us how to use the material we learned. He tests on concepts not practiced in the homework, expects us to know things beyond the scope of this course, and made us hand back in our midterms to knock off points because the TA graded it too easily. Other professors sections got easy As while ours got Cs.

One of the worst professors I've ever met. Doesn't know how to teach, and don't want to teach. Got only one practice final exam, and the answer was hand-written and excruciatingly hard to read. Lectures hurt my understanding to the material. Just disastrous.

He's amusing and a nice person, but it is really evident that he does not know how to teach. He goes off on random tangents during class that tend to be really amusing, but ultimately I learned nothing from the lectures. Read the textbook!

G. Scovazzi is an extremely accomplished academic. He is extremely intelligent and is evidently doing really meaningful work outside the classroom in his lab. However he is a mediocre teacher at best. His lectures are way too theoretical and don't help at all in the learning of the material. You must go to lectures even though they are useless.

Scovazzi was a cool, nice, funny guy. He would tell stories in his cute Italian accent, and he'd try to give us pep talks. But I would say that very few people in my class (including me) actually enjoyed the material, and I found it extremely difficult to stay awake during class. He also made mistakes often, which could make things confusing.

Slightly more personable than Minna-- her lectures make more sense, but she's passive-aggressive and mispronounced my teammate's name the whole semester. If I could take the quiz at home, you would not find me in a single lecture. This is the worst class in the psychology department. I'm begging you to take literally anything else.

This class was literally such a joke and a waste of time. The "flipped classroom" is an excuse so the professors don't have to teach. Professors were disorganized, always going back on their word and uncertain about the answers to the quizzes they wrote. Dr. S was slightly more engaging than Minna, but still not an enjoyable class.
Very good professor overall - covered interesting material, made herself very available to meet outside of class, assigned a manageable amount of work, and was very considerate of students' needs.

Dr. S was great! She's super kind and is a great teacher. The class itself isn't very difficult. There are small homework assignments every week and one larger group project, but the group project is broken up into parts so it's manageable.
she was a great focus professor! Cleary passionate about the subject and did not put a lot of stress on us.

Easy professor and easy class. Not the most interesting material, but she's happy to help outside of class. I learned that neuroscience isn't my thing, but this may be rewarding for those who like drugs and the law.

Dr. S is amazing and clearly cares about her students. The class is very engaging and I learned a lot. There are small weekly assignments that are very manageable. I would definitely recommend taking this class.
Dr. S is extremely nice. I thought the first month of the class was the most interesting. This class is an easy A.
She was the best thinbg ever

Dr. S is v nice, and the first few weeks of the class were interesting. The class itself is unbelievably easy, and it gets a bit boring later on, but it is helpful having a filler class as a first-semester freshman. Group project/class discussion heavy, limited and brief homework. Take for an easy A!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: Love Dr. S! Such an interesting class where I learned a lot. There's a lot of hw but it's easy, and lots of group work as well so it allows you to get closer with your focus. Dr. S is super accessible outside of class and cares about her students and her work. No final, just an easy final project. You should take this class

Dr. S is honestly the mom that everyone needs at college. She is compassionate and is truly interested in helping her students learn. This was my favorite class during my first semester at Duke. This is a fairly simple class with a lot of content presented in an easy-to-understand manner. Take this class if you are in the FOCUS!

Not only is Dr. S super knowledgeable about the material, but she is caring and understanding. Don't be afraid to approach her about anything. The class itself has clear requirements, one big group project and one full research paper. She also brings in guest speakers who are really interesting.

If you have the chance to take Dr. S's Drugs & the Law classes, definitely do it!! The grade in the class consisted of one group project, one 15 page research paper, and small amounts of nightly homework. Dr. S is such a caring professor, and the material she teaches is incredibly interesting. I loved her and her class!!
reviews.rating_tags: GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Caring--Would take again

reviews.comment: AMAZING!!!!
Brilliant professor who is always willing to help students.
Great Professor! Extremely helpful and brilliant.

If you have a chance to take this Focus class, do it! Dr. S's class is really chill and relaxed.  She gives really good feedback on the paper that we have to write in this class as well as the big group project at the end of the semester, so you are almost guaranteed a good grade if you put in effort.  Interesting topic and she is really engaging!

Dr. S's focus class on Drugs and the Law was really insightful on the Public Policy and Psychological side of Drug Addiction. She's very clear cut and tells you exactly how she wants assignments, so no ambiguity. Also, she likes letting her students expand and researching their own topics and allows for a lot of free movement within the class.
Easy class but a little busywork

Although it wasn't my first choice, this ended up being one of my favorite classes this semester. Granted, it is a lot of work, there's around 3-5 major writing pieces throughout the course, it can seem overly tedious for just a Writing 101, but it is still a fun course. Sotelo-Miller cares about each of her students and the course as a whole.

As expected in a writing class, there was plenty of writing, but certainly less than in other Writing 101s. The films weren't the most interesting, but all the assignments were doable. Make sure you check rubrics/listen to her instructions, and you'll do great. Sotelo was very kind and valued in-class participation.
Very nice and caring professor. However, grading is somewhat harsh. And there is a lot of work. Topic is cool but get ready to spend time.

We did get what felt like a lot of reading sometimes, but we also got fun homework like watching movies. Her grading criteria is very straightforward and while she may be quiet I got the vibe that she really cares about her students. We were graded on an in class group presentation (very chill), two papers, and a final project. Overall a good class
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Sotelo gives great feedback on all projects and writing assignments and is super helpful with clarifying any confusion regarding assignment instructions. Her course requires reading articles and novels as well as watching some films, but the workload is very doable and it helps to come to class prepared to participate.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She's really nice. The class was nothing special but I liked her. She was super easy and cares about her students. As long as you put in minimal effort, you'll be fine.

She is incredibly sweet and understanding, and facilitates great discussions. Her grading is not harsh at all, and her assignments, while a little bit hard to keep track of sometimes, were definitely doable and never much of a burden. She knows so much and was awesome to learn from this semester.

Dr. Sotelo is super duper nice! She genuinely cares about her students and is just a nice human being in general. Her class is quite interesting although I went in not knowing anything about the course content.
Dr. Sotelo is a gem! I wasn't particularly excited about W101 or the subject material but she made it very enjoyable. The class is relatively easy but work can pile up if you don't stay on track.
She is an inspiring person and lecturer!! Really engaged us well with the materials

Not an especially difficult or memorable course. The pieces we analyze tend to be good, especially if you're interested in themes of race, sexuality, and migration. Surprisingly little actual writing for a writing class. Dr. Sotelo is super nice. Course website is pretty disorganized, so keep track of deadlines. (Though she's reasonably lenient)
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Caring--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I loved how supportive and kind she was. Took this class online and genuinely enjoyed all her materials. Prepped me very well for academic writing!!

Such a nice professor! I think there are a few older reviews lowering Dr. Sotelo's rating, but she always greeted us with a smile every lecture. The assignments were explained well in advance and she gives clear instructions on what is happening in each lecture. She is also so quick to respond to emails if you're ever confused!

Duke doesn't do a great job of ensuring that all the Writing 101 courses are the same level of difficulty, and G&S in LA film is definitely one of the easier ones in terms of workload. Sotelo is such a kind professor and cares a lot about her students. My only complaint is that her use of Sakai was super disorganized and I could never find anything

DON'T LISTEN TO BAD REVS! Dr. Sotelo is one of the nicest humans I've ever met, especially important in a subject which can be new and strange for students. Sotelo approaches her class with advanced knowledge and understanding, but effort is required! As a cocky high school student, I thought my writing was perfect, but Sotelo helped me immensely!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Sotelo is a super kind professor, as well as a reasonable grader. Didn't find her class to be too much work, besides the time it takes to watch the (often graphic but interesting) films. If you show that you're putting in effort to improve, you'll likely do well. Dr. Sotelo really encourages discussion and cares a lot about her students!

Dr. Sotelo is a wonderful professor. She is very devoted to the class and helping her students succeed. I think grading is pretty standard and as long as you improve throughout your drafts and put in the work, then the grade will be reflected. 10/10 recommend

Dr. Sotelo is a wonderful person who clearly cares a lot about Latin American Film. However, the class is more suited to be a film class as opposed to a writing class, and be aware that the films are intense! I didn't find her grading to be that harsh of a grader, however, and she does give individual comments on your rough drafts, which is nice.

She is really nice and if you are interested in the topic of the class I would definitely recommend the class. Most students last semester got either A-'s or A's, so it is not terribly hard to get a decent grade in the class. There are 2 large writing projects (the largest is 2250 words) and a presentation.

As a note about all Writing 101 professor ratings, most of them have such low ratings because Duke freshmen are coming in from straight A backgrounds in high school and getting their first grades in the B+/- range and getting salty about it. Thing is, that's normal for college and doesn't necessarily reflect a bad professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Nice woman and interesting topic, but shes an inconsistent grader whose comments do not match her grading. It often seems like points are taken off arbitrarily. Few assignments but not at all worth it. Sometimes critiques things in the final draft that she recommended doing in the first draft.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: As long as you do the work, participate in class, and watch the films, you will do fine. I really enjoyed the class and the professor. She is a tough grader, but it is not an incredibly hard class.

VERY hard grader for essays. Grades don't reflect her comments made on papers and she is intentionally hard for no reason. I definitely felt cheated because there are tons of better Writing 101 classes available. Don't take her!!!!
Very, very difficult grader. The class is VERY boring and you spend hours of your time watching movies from a long time ago that have no relevance whatsoever.

Really Nice Lady, but she is a very tough grader. Almost impossible to get an A, even for dedicated writers. The class had minimal work (literally just watching movies) but the papers were graded very hard.

Prof. Dasgupta is a lovely person, but the course is unorganized. There is some material that is lecture only and not mentioned in the course textbook, and lectures cover LOTS of material, so studying will heavily depend on your in-lecture notetaking. Proofs can feel complicated/convoluted, and hard to ask questions. Not worth the effort.

I think having a Putnam problem on the final says a lot. But otherwise, he was a caring professor -- but I think math 221 at Duke generally does not account for the lack of experience with proofs that incoming freshmen have. I only did well in this course since I'd previously taken linear algebra.

arbitrary grading, partial credit not generous at all. left students hopelessly unprepared for midterms (averages in the 60s and 50s), and NEVER accessible outside of class because purposely schedules office hours for when students have other classes. curve ended up being fine, but better off taking 401 with a postdoc than Dasgupta.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dasgupta lectures well, and the first half of the course isn't hard. However, he grades arbitrarily and harshly, and the requirements for certain assignments are vague. He's also terrible at following up on promises to post homework by a certain date. Also, he has currently never responded to emails. His bite (grading-wise) is worse than his bark.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Hardest class I've ever taken, prepare to spend a TON of time outside class learning from the book. He's a good lecturer and you can tell he loves the content. However, he can be sarcastic and dismissive, especially in office hours, but if you can deal with that, this is a rewarding class. Extremely hard tests but decent curve.
Great professor and an amazing class. He grades nicely and then gives most people A's. Make sure to show up to class as the lectures are very important.

221 is a hard class and it's no different for Dasgupta. Classes mainly consisted of him lecturing from the textbook and were clear but personally fast paced; reading the textbook on my own helped. Homework is heavy but useful, and quizzes can be very fast paced. 2 lowest HW grades and 2 lowest quiz grades are dropped so there is a bit of room.
If there's another option, take it. I have no idea about his other classes, but for 221, just no.
poor. beyond poor
Awful just don't do it if you can

Professor Dasgupta is incredibly smart, but is also dismissive and derisive of questions in class and office hours.  Though I credit his 221 class for making me appreciate proof-based math, I would not take another course with him. Math is hard enough without the professor being rude and discouraging help-seeking.

Came from a non-rigorous math background, class was extremely difficult. Exams were often significantly harder than peer professors (do ALL of the book problems in advance). Professor's a great guy, but aloof and undeniably difficult to get meaningful support from. Spent most of my semester on this class.

Dasgupta was a good lecturer, also very nice and accessible. Great class for early majors or math-curious (doesn't assume much prior knowledge), but still useful math fundamentals. Loved the seminar format (regularly work w others in class, present proofs on board, and write final paper and present rather than an exam). Grading scheme is generous.

Professor Dasgupta is simply the best Professor I have had. His energetic and charming voice draws you in, and combined with his teaching skills and knowledge in the field, provide the best lectures. Outside of being an amazing teacher, he is also an incredibly accomplished researcher. He quite literally solved century-old mathematical problems.

Loved this class! The professor answered to any kinds of questions we had. His exams were usually exactly the same as the practice exams, which you can freely discuss and solve with him to prepare for the actual exams.

Professor Dasgupta is honestly one of my favorite professors I have ever taken. I highly recommend taking any class he teaches. An inspirational and caring professor, and truly unique in the Duke Math Department for sheer dedication to his students. Oh, also he has adorable kids and is funny.

Best professor I met at Duke so far. He was like a real father figure to all of us-someone who made you delight in the material and learn it by yourself- yet always available if you struggled and needed his guidance. We spent 1 hour extra after normal office hours once, just asking him random questions about fields or rings or such. Great fun.

Dr. Dasgupta is one of the best professors I've had. He has a knack for understanding exactly where the student's misunderstanding lies whenever he's asked a question, and is great at clearing up misconceptions. Beware, though, if you miss class, you're likely to miss a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: He offers a mix of practical engineering, real-world insight, and genuine care for student learning.

WNS as a professor won't always have classes or necessarily be the easiest to reach out to, but his knowledge, understanding and willingness to help students succeed should not be undermined. He is here to push students to try and make engineering decisions with proper efficacy and analysis.

Class is terribly structured, and he shows up once very two weeks and is ill-prepared those days. There is no knowledge of the grading process, and it is impossible to study for the tests. Simmons is unreachable and demonstrates little care for the students. Worst professor I have had at Duke, and I hope ME421 is changed drastically in the future.

Dr. Simmons lectures are interesting, and the projects/tests aren't too terrible, but the worst thing about him is his attendance. Meaning, he'll go for weeks without having lecture as he travels for his business pursuits, leaving students confused. This leads to him rarely giving back graded material, and there's no clear grading scheme anyways.

Neal Simmons never makes students a priority. This is evident by the fact that he doesn't return grades, cancels class frequently, and never gives assignments that would help prepare for his tests. You can learn a decent amount from his lectures but 1) he VERY frequently cancels lectures and 2) his lectures don't prepare you for his difficult tests

Dr. Simmons is a very bright guy. You can learn a lot from his lectures. However, he is purposefully ambiguous about what will be on his tests. Students are not a priority; he frequently cancels class for business reasons (would be a good thing, except his tests are very challenging, so missing those lectures makes them even harder to prepare for)
I took her 310 Class and her 231 class. She is a good lecturer, and she provides generous extra credit on tough exams (THE EXAMS ARE HARD THOUGH!!!)

Took her Random Processes (Math 310 no options idk why)in Spring 2025—definitely one of the best professors I've had. Super clear lectures, great materials, and very supportive in office hours. Exams are tough (first one wrecked me), but she grades fairly with lots of partial credit.
Her overly fast-paced lectures were not very helpful and her accent caused confusion. I felt her tests were very unfair.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: When get past the accent, you'll see she is a good professor.

I really wish I had taken this class with another professor. This was her first time teaching probability, and she made the class WAY harder than the other professors for no good reason. The homework is absolutely impossible because she just isn't a good lecturer, and the midterm average is in the 50's. She makes herself very available, though
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Caring

reviews.comment: Si Tang is clearly very smart and knowledgable but her lectures aren't engaging and she makes the class way harder than it needs to be. The tests were so hard they just seemed unfair. It also is annoying that other sections of Math 230 were way easier than hers.
For assignments and exams, she will deduct points for the smallest things. Avoid her at all costs.

I wanted to give myself some time before rating Professor Santillan. After reflecting, I can honestly say I would have learned more from a middle school math teacher. This was the worst-run class I have experienced in my academic career. DO NOT TAKE HER unless you can't graduate in time.
She makes you feel humiliated for trying to learn, avoid her at all costs

Really confused by all the negative reviews here. Maybe since some time has gone by I actually appreciate Santillan now. Yes it was super tough (it's literally diff eq!!) but if you go to class AND OFFICE HOURS and put in the time, you will do OK on exams. She actually cares a lot about students learning the material and wants them to learn.
If graduating with Mechanical Engineering means you need to take classes with Dr. Santillan, switch majors.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I transferred back to my state school after this class.
She hates her students and her job, and she'll make sure you know it. Transfer schools before you take a class with her.

WORST PROFESSOR EVER. Her class pavlov dogged me into crying every time I hear "ode." I used to be excited about the world and future, Dr. Santillan showed me that with the right diff eq education, you can come to understand the world as a hopeless lifeless place. I genuinely think I will never recover from this experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Worst professor ever. She's the reason I quit engineering.
I hate her.

Don't do it. Worst math teacher I've ever had. It honestly seems like Professor Santillian may be dealing with something, because prior to this semester she had strong reviews. This term was a mess. She claimed there would be a curve, but my grade was 0.3 points off the next step and was not changed.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Her lectures notes are good but she's actually the most diabolical test writer in human history. Take this class with literally anyone else. Hardest section, worst exams, ZERO curve. She genuinely just does not want her students to do well in her class. I've done better in HARDER classes (math222 & 219) bc they weren't praying on my downfall.
Incredibly difficult professor for me. The texts were brutal and the quizzes were too. No curve. I felt like I was punished for learning.

I feel better about diff eq than I have about pretty much any other math class at Duke and its my lowest grade by far. Dr. Santillan's section is significantly harder than any other section and she's an incredibly harsh grader.

This is the most difficult diff eq class by a far margin. Do not take this class with her. There is no curve, and she is a very harsh grader. Midterms were unreasonably difficult and completely different structure-wise from the final, which was cross-section. Homework was far longer than other sections and involved coding.

Every time I walk into her room, life is drained out of my soul. She's ruthless with her grading and strange with her teaching (for ex, shell ask rhetorical questions to the class to make us answer and only vaguely explain what's going on). I honestly didn't even learn much bc I took ece 280 together and Dr. G (goat) taught me Fourier

Sophia Santillan is quite the professor (in the worst way possible). This class was honestly a nightmare, and I would emphasize that you should take diffeq with any other professor. ANY!!! In fact, take it abroad. She assigns incredibly hard tests, which don't actually prepare you for the final because other profs don't do it. Also zero curve.
Least favorite teacher I've ever had. Beyond frustrated with this course. If your only option is her, find a different class and wait a semester. You won't regret it.
Incredibly difficult professor who offered little to no support. Exams were unfair and the class average was significantly lower than other professors sections for this class.

Lectures are okay at best but she asks students questions on things and if nobody knows she just moves on and never actually teaches that topic. Be prepared to teach yourself the entire course and still get given an unfair grade because she doesn't curve and grades in a ridiculously harsh manner.

This was an unnecessarily hard math class. Professor Santillan seems oddly shallow, and grades incredibly harshly. I would say she is fair between her students, but that's about the end of the positives. Not the absolute worst I've had at duke, but she's close to rock bottom. Please reconsider taking her math and senior design classes.

Please take this class with a different professor - the hardest Math 353 section. Weekly quizzes were extremely difficult and graded very strictly. Teaching was inconsistent, and when the class could not answer questions, the professor wouldn't explain and moved on. This course could have been rewarding, but instead was stressful and not enjoyable.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Hardest Math 353 Section out there for sure -- was required to do programming/proofs/weekly quizzes. Teaching was alright, but could have been better as sometimes she asks the class questions and if the class can't answer, she refuses to tell us the answer and moves on. Grading is quite strict.

Pretty tough grader but explains concepts well in class. Weekly quizzes are in groups but are still hard. Cares about her students, and you can have a cheat sheet for every exam, but they're still difficult.

Kind instructor but extremely difficult section. Heavy questioning style, little direct teaching, strict grading, and weekly quizzes that were very challenging. Much tougher than other 353 sections. Worked harder than in any class and still struggled. Would not take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: DO NOT. I repeat DO NOT take with her. Ok lectures, but she asks oddball rhetorical questions and doesn't answer them. When talking about different solution methods, she'll ask students for guesses, and never rly give the right answer. Harshest grader and lowkey just lacks any compassion for her students. Hella regret taking w/her.
The course is tough, no doubt. But Santillan makes it bearable and clearly cares a lot about student success. I would recommend this class even though it almost killed me.

Single most work I've had in a class at Duke, and I put in the bare minimum. Not always, but in a single week, you may have a quiz on Monday, a group lab assignment due on Wednesday, an individual lab assignment due on Thursday, and homework due on Friday. Good luck if you've got any kind of personal life, this class is a part time job.

This is a tough class for sure. Weekly group quizzes. But if you put in the work, you'll do well. Dr. Santillan is super knowledgeable and great at answering student questions. You can tell she knows her stuff and genuinely cares about student learning.

Very caring professor with a true passion for math. Lectures were held at a good pace and she made an effort to memorize everyone's name within the first few weeks of class. Assignments were fair and well aligned with the curriculum/lecture content.

So! This class was really hard. It felt like I went into tests feeling prepared to find out I was not. That's not a fault of Dr. Santillan, but it shows how difficult the class can be. She's a great lecturer and can answer questions very well. I would say just take Santillan and don't panic. You'll be fine.

I think other people are being too harsh. The tests are very hard, but they are curved, so even when the average is a 65, average is still a B/B+. She is a pretty good lecturer, a bit boring but very informative and passionate. The notes she posts on canvas are great. Homeworks aren't too tough. The class won't be easy, but youll definitely learn.
Unorganized class, lab 2 is the worst lab I've done in my life.

Tests are very tough and not straightforward, and not similar to other sections' tests. Midterms are more about thinking on your feet, final was all about how much math you can do in 3 hours. Lectures usually consist of discussing a problem, then explaining what the concept we just used was at the very end, making most of the class very confusing.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: You could not pay me all of the money in the world to take this class again. I would rather saw off both of my legs by hand than do any of the out of class work we had.

Let's be honest, this was always going to be a tough class. And if you don't know that going on, that's on you. That said, Dr. Santillan is a really amazing professor who clearly cares about her students and is very knowledgable. Pay close attention to lectures and go to office hours for extra help. Would take her again for sure!!

Her lectures aren't great, doesn't focus on comprehension of concepts. 85% of grade is determined by exams. No Curve and tough grader. Barely provides any study material or practice exams. Slow to respond on ED, only 1 hour of OH per week, and no OH for final exam week. Put effort into understanding the homework, It's easy to fall behind.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Santillan is such a great lecturer but also a great professor - she makes going to class something to look forward to, and she always makes sure that everyone's question is answered, if not during class, then after class. She also brings in real world examples of the dynamics we're learning to class. In short, she makes learning fun.

Not a great experience in a class that's supposed to get you excited about engineering. Arbitrary grader; she didn't adhere to the rubric at all. She seems like a nice person but it also seemed like she didn't really want to be teaching this class.

Had discussion during an asynchronous class. Summarized complex 212 ideas concisely and gave good practice. Easy to talk to and likes to answer questions. VERY accessible outside of class. Emailed her a myriad of times and generally pretty fast response times. In emails, explains answers and doesn't just tell you. A gem in a hard class/semester.

Grading scheme can be unclear, and takes forever. However, can be helpful if you just ask. Approachable and gives good feedback when asked questions. Pretty laid back personality but unusually strict on grammar in technical memos. Harsher grader than other 101 professors.

She cares about her students. Even on Zoom, she made an effort to get to know us. Her math 212 discussions were very clear--she explained the confusing concepts from Bray's videos well and encouraged questions, always asking if it makes sense at the end. She is available outside of class to help as well. I would replace Bray with her easily.

The best thing she gave us was an opportunity for my team to bond over here stupid grading. She does not help at all with out projects and just criticizes it without providing avenues to improve our grade. Further, when grading, she did not take into consideration that we had 1/3 the time as this class usually.

She is an AMAZING math discussion leader. She helped ease a lot of the difficulties that Clark Bray gave us. She explains hard concepts with such ease and tries her best to make sure that we understand these hard concepts. She puts everything in context and is amazing. She is super approachable and helps you, if you want it.

Santillan is an amazing professor - she really made going to class something to look forward to, despite the fact that they were at 8:30. She really cares about all of her students and always makes sure everyone understands the concepts. 100% would recommend.

Santillan is a great professor - she makes learning the material enjoyable, and I looked forward to her 8:30 classes (and let me tell you, I'm the most non-morning person ever). She explains everything thoroughly and really cares about all of her students. Would strongly recommend!

Dr. Santillan wants her students to be successful. She is always available to chat outside of class about homework or not-class related things. She is not only sooo smart but she's super welcoming and approachable.

I loved Dr. Santillan's enthusiasm, but at times the class lectures were not helpful for learning the material. Too often we would skip a problem no one could answer and then the answer would be posted online but we never spoke about it in class. On the whole just a tad disorganized and too much extra work on the labs that isn't content related.

Dr. Santillan is an amazing math professor. She always makes an effort to be available to students and make sure that everyone in her class understands the material. She also teaches the material in such a way that you understand how to apply concepts rather than just regurgitating formulas.
this class nearly broke me, but in the end it perpared me for more advanced classes down the road. santillan is really smart and super helpful and wants you to succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Was a bad experience. She was very rusty especially in the first half of the course. Dynamics is a very hard course but the professor could have been better.

Class is difficult, but Dr. Santillan welcomes questions and provides plenty of resources (help rooms, office hours, etc) for students to do well. She genuinely cares about her students, but homework is excessive and grading at times can be very picky. Overall, concepts were taught very clearly.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Decent professor. Not the best I've ever had, but not bad. Lectures weren't mandatory, but there was a participation grade. Lab reports for EGR244 were awful. Extremely long and about things were didn't really learn in lecture. But Santillan wasn't in charge of lab; you'll get that in any EGR244 class regardless of which professor you have.
Chillest class ever at Duke. Study guides are given prior to exams and you have to just memorize it. I got A's on all of my exams barely showing up to lectures.

This was easily my best class of my last semester. Exams were pretty easy I would say and he gives you the questions before hand. Not only that, low workload 3 short p–sets that required using Excel, 2 exams, and an easily graded proposal. Grab your friends and do the p–sets with, it can be done in sub 3 hours each.
There is little to no homework, easy exams, and he is a compassionate professor. Marine field trip was also super fun.
Brian is the goat
I love Brian Silliman. He is so incredibly kind and supportive and gives real insight into research. I found the marine animals we were learning to be genuinely interesting.

Not a fan. Super easy class, but the exams weren't really related to lectures, which were disorganized. It felt like Prof. Silliman spent a lot of time bragging about his research career rather than actually teaching. I was excited about the class content at first but realized I learned nothing except for how to memorize species names/niche facts.

Such an easy class, but literally gained nothing from that class. He is super excited to come every day and teach you nothing. Whole class is graded off 2 exams (just 100% memorization) and like 2 papers.

While I really loved the course—the material was interesting, and the opportunities were enjoyable—my biggest frustration was with the tests themselves. The content we were tested on wasn't what we covered in class, and when it was, it was a very niche topic talked about once. A great introduction to MarSci, but not as in depth as I had hoped.

While this course is easy, and the prof is distinguished, he rarely shows for class and when he does lecture the content is VERY unstructured and has barely any connection to the content you're actually tested on. The prof is also pretty cocky, which doesn't translate very well in his lectures. Learned a marginal amount about Marine science.

He literally doesn't teach. The class is so easy so don't worry about that, but I learned approximately nothing. The worst part is that he thinks he is an amazing professor just because he is distinguished in research. I love marine biology, and was so bored in this class. The content is fine, but I wish the class was organized better.

Below comments is precisely it.

Don't take this class. Stay away. He was absent for half the classes too.

Professor has the most pride on campus. He specifically said, you came to Duke, not for the diploma, but for his recommendation letter. 

Also, bottom comments are positive only because this class is easy. But if you actually want to learn, don't take this. Attendance is mandatory for such a useless class.

I think Dr. Silliman is great and such a nice guy. I still remember the scientific name of Hawksbill sea turtle– eretmochelas imbricata. I learned the most studying for the exams. Easy class, one of my favorites I took this semester. His reviews are genuinely too harsh. Such little workload, no complaints.

Dr. Siliman is a great professor. He is obviously very interested in what he's teaching and loves using his own personal experience to teach about the content of the class. However, the exams are based on pure memorization of niche details that were only briefly mentioned in lecture or not at all.

Prof. Silliman seems like he has a wealth of knowledge, but he seems disconnected from the course itself. While the course itself is not difficult, you really don't learn much. For exams, while he does give you a bank of problems and terms to study from and chooses those for the exam, the questions are hyper specific and super tedious to memorize.

Professor Silliman is very passionate about the subject he teaches. However, he clearly cares more about his research (that he talks about constantly) than his students/actually teaching. His exams aren't hard, but preparing for them is pure memorization of hyper-specific information that you will forget the second you walk out of the exam room.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This was my favorite class taken at Duke. Dr. Silliman is so passionate about marine science and is doing a great job at making science / ecology accessible for everyone. The lectures are so much fun (he brought his shell collection) and the tests are easy, you're given all questions ahead of time.

Lectures are terribly disorganized.
Low learning and low difficulty. Professor Silliman goes on tangents for the majority of the class, every class.

I think that Brian Silliman is an extremely nice person who obviously knows an extensive amount about the world of Marine Science, however, his lectures are all over the place and it is hard to follow his lecture style. It feels like he tells more personal anecdotes than facts. I also find it weird how often he plugs his own research.
Attendance is mandatory. He talked about funny anecdotes, but the actual lectures related to contents are very difficult to follow.
I really liked Silliman. His class is very easy and the material is super interesting. However, his lectures are a little bit hard to follow and he really plugs his own research.

Top 3 favorite professors of all time, course taught at Marine Lab. Super helpful, super engaging, super informative. Class based on diligent note taking and a journal with daily entries discussing work we did on a self-created project. Project itself was tough, but Silliman offered phenomenal support. If you have the chance, TAKE SILLIMAN.

Pretty engaging lectures, though it was hard to take notes because of how fast they went sometimes. He tells a lot of stories as well that can engage but also can sidetrack the class. He gives out the questions he may ask on tests beforehand, but often has not answered those questions in class, which is frustrating. Otherwise a great professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class is great. 2 exams (final and midterm), 2 problem sets, and a really manageable paper. You don't have to show up to lecture, which is helpful since the course is at 8:30. Prof is an interesting lecturer though if you mind yourself waking up in time to make the class. Take if you need the NS credit.

He records lectures so you don't have to actually show up at 8:30, but still really engaging whenever he talks. Two exams (no final) with a question bank of ~25 essay questions released beforehand so you know exactly what he's going to ask. He chooses 5 of those and you have to answer 2. Was also fun to write the NSF proposal. Grades very leniently

Dr. Silliman is one of the best professors at Duke. He is highly respected and his lectures are entertaining and inspirational. He really tries to share his knowledge and connect with his students through lectures. Highly recommend (even though it is an 8:30)

Brian was a great professor and the class was super interesting! Despite it being at 8:30, the lectures were engaging and I learned a lot. The class was graded on two midterms, a final paper, and a few labs for homework. The questions for the midterms were released ahead of time and the grading was pretty generous. 10/10 I really enjoyed overall!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: MarSci 202 with Silliman is interesting and easy! There are two tests throughout the semester and all of the potential questions are released ahead of time. Highly recommend

He is a gem of a professor! If not an 8:30, this would definitely be the most lively class Ive been in at Duke. Although you dont *need* to attend lecture to get a good grade, people show up because his lectures are just that cool. Coursework is stimulating and doable. Marsci 202 is a must take! You get out what you put in.
Brian is a very charismatic professor who give really interesting lectures. He is always willing to talk with students and creates very engaging lessons and work.

Absolutely wonderful professor. Passionate about the subject and about teaching. He really tries to make his students enjoy the class and love the subject, focusing on field work and exploration of any type. Very accessible outside of class, helpful with independent research, and brings students on awesome field trips.

I wouldn't recommend his STATS 101 class if you don't have any coding background or don't want to do a lot of coding. Other STATS 101 professors had very different syllabi so if you want to do less coding take a different class. Very strict grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Sjur is an outstanding statistics teacher. His clarity in explaining complex concepts, passion for the subject, and approachability create an ideal learning environment. He makes statistics engaging and relevant with real-world examples. Highly recommend Professor Sjur for anyone seeking a top-notch statistics education.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Sjur is an amazing professor for stats, definitely the best choice at DKU. His lectures can sometimes be boring but if you read the textbook you will understand. He is very accessible outside of class and willing to listen to you. I was able to increase my homework grade after telling him my concerns. A fair grader, highly recommend

Yang Laoshi is a breath of fresh air. She is incredibly kind, patient, and genuinely cares about her students as people, not just learners. Her classroom feels supportive and encouraging, which makes learning Chinese much less intimidating and far more enjoyable.

Such a kind person, and truly cares about her students. Chinese is, by nature, a hard language for English speakers, but Yang is really amazing and gives the best possible introduction to the language.
Really caring professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: She was very friendly and I learned a lot of information from her lectures. Overall, I really enjoyed the class!

Really great professor!  She is very caring and sweet. Very easy to go up to and answers all your burning questions. There is a lot of homework, but that is Chinese lol. The homework isn't hard, but it is tedious so don't fall behind.

I had a great experience in this class, I would highly recommend taking a class with her; she makes learning Chinese very enjoyable. It is a sizeable amount of work and it's important to consistently study and stay on top of the work but she is all around a very caring and approachable professor, 5/5 would recommend.

He is very clear with what he expects your writing to look like, so your writing will improve a lot during this course. He is a reasonable grader and very knowledgeable in his field! Probably the clearest rubrics of any professor I've had at DKU.

Professor Snow is an experienced linguist. He can utilize many languages and regional dialects. He always encourages students to critically thinking, and that is why he only shares his ideas toward the endangered languages at the end of the semester. The WOC110 course is highly recommended for students who interested in languages.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: I think the class itself is misleading as its more an EAP course than a linguistics one. However, Professor Snow is good at giving feedback so if you need to improve your writing skills, I would recommend this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Snow is extremely knowledgeable and experienced in language study. I appreciated the personal anecdotes that he incorporated into his teaching. He really makes an effort to get to know each student.

Magda is one of the sweetest and kindest teachers at Duke. In addition to genuinely caring about her students, she puts a lot of work into making her lectures fun while allowing students to learn more about Brazilian culture. Definitely one of the best classes I've taken at Duke.
One of the best professors I've had at Duke. I loved going to class and, even though I'm Brazilian, I still learned many new things about Brazil in her lectures. Would totally take her again!
One of the kindest, most caring professors I have ever had. I really enjoyed taking her class and would take it 1000 times again if I could.

Magda is the best! Her class was super fun and engaging, and we learned a ton of Portuguese grammar and Brazilian culture/history. I would highly recommend this class, especially if you already speak a romance language. Magda brings energy to every class and it rubs off on her students!

Magda is so kind and enthusiastic. If you show effort and desire to learn Portuguese, especially above and beyond what is required, she will do the same. Presentations and papers are an opportunity to research parts of Brazilian culture that you would like to explore independently! If you're choosing which language to take, pick Portuguese!

Prof Silva is amazing! Her class was often the highlight of my day, and she has a way of creating a community. She is energetic and funny, and she makes learning Portuguese fun. The compositions she assigned were not hard, and she always offers help if you need it. The tests were not easy, but she passes out comprehensive study guides.

I have loved having Magda as a teacher! Her classes are always so fun and she finds a way to connect with all her students. She is an easy grader, so the onus is on the students to put in the work outside of class to make sure they can actually use their Portuguese outside of class. For me, this was a great system and I learned so much.

I really enjoyed this semester with Magda. She has an online course calendar, but it is very fluid and changes depending on how long the class needs to understand a topic. Expectations are established from the start, and she is helpful during office hours. The class is not too difficult, but I have learned a lot of Portuguese in three months.

This class was very disorganized. The work schedule changed all the time, and I did not learn much actual Portuguese from it. Magda is very kind, but she did not hammer in the grammatical/speaking concepts that are crucial to language-learning. She goes on a lot of cultural tangents. I DO NOT recommend this class if you want to learn Portuguese.

Magda is a super fun and passionate professor, and she really makes learning the language enjoyable. She's a bit disorganized (often takes a while to return assignments and goes on random tangents), but it's not a difficult class, as there are many extra credit opportunities, and she's always open to meeting to go over written compositions.

Professor Silva is amazingly awesome. You can tell she is Brazilian by her enthusiasm and passion for sharing her knowledge. Homework is key and the class is relatively difficult depending on your level of Portuguese, but Professor Silva is always there to help. She loves her students.

Magda is really amazing!  She enjoys teaching through conversation which decreases busy work.  She is so enthusiastic everyday and really makes you enjoy coming to class.  Sometimes she is a bit disorganized and is late giving grades back but she genuinely wants you to enjoy Portuguese and do well!  She'll help you with anything you need as well.

Magda is absolutely wonderful. She will work with you personally anytime, and will help you find a way to get to Brazil. Her classes can be disorganized at times, but they are graded kindly. You learn a decent amount and don't have to work too hard.

Magda is the best teacher ever! Her enthusiasm for Portuguese definitely translates to her students. Her class is VERY easy and there's barely any work. Tests are easy, especially if you speak Spanish since the two languages are very similar. Magda wants to give you the best grade possible and I don't think she gave anyone less than an A!

Magda is an awesome teacher and the Portuguese 1 and 2 classes aren't like any other language course. There is minimal busy work; we mostly learn through conversation. Some of the work can be hard, like the essays and group projects, and at times Magda can be disorganized with her teaching and grading, but it's really not bad.
Magda is awesome!! She makes the class so much fun and everyone comes away with enthusiasm for portuguese. Take this class if you speak spanish already!
Professora Magda is the best professor I've had so far! She is amazing and I would recommend her any time! Sometimes she does give alot of work at the same time but its still fun :-)

Magda is the best teacher ever!  She is honestly the best Duke has to offer.  Given the choice to go to class or not go and sleep in...I would go to Magda's class in a second.  She rocks and now I'm inspired to go to Brasil!
Best professor I've ever had. Even though it met five days a week, I still looked forward to it every day.

Magda is this incredibly energetic teacher that makes you love Portuguese. You actually end up wanting to do the work for her class, which doesn't happen a lot at Duke. Very helpful, very fun! And trust me, you learn the language quickly in that class because you can't help but talk!
Magda is awesome!

When u first see her u think shes a student, her vivacious attitude bursts the sec she enters the door and freely jokes about people's boyfriends in class to demonstrate verb conjugations. Awesome teacher, super fun and well-worth it class. Just watch out for her side-kick, Leslie Damasceno.

Took this class for economics elective credit and writing requirement. Generally difficult to keep up with all of the readings that he assigns every week. As much as he is a nice guy and I liked him as a person, it was really hard to enjoy the class with the long lectures that were very detail heavy + one quiz every. Tough grader.
The worst professor on the planet.  I HATE THIS MAN.  Completely irrational in his grading and out of touch with the students.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Professor Sloan possesses the rare combination of a strong teaching focusmentorship commitment with a huge prominence in his field. A true leader in his field, and it was amazing to have the chance to learn from him. He chooses very relevant papers that are excellent examples of the different research methodologies (which was the class focus).
Incredible professor. Class was very interesting and practical. Definitely recommend taking something with Sloan!

Professor Sloans classes  may be difficult to comprehend and sometimes he may lose track of thought or time. None of this takes away from the fact he is a  researcher of the highest caliber and holds himself and his students to the highest standards. Maybe a hard task master but he is willing to  put energy and time helping a student.

Overall I would say hes a bad teacher. Poorly structured boring class and he rambles a lot He is an easy grader though. Theres a somewhat low minimum amount of effort you have to put in find that min, do it consistently for the whole semester and study hard for the midterms. I can't really complain cause I got a good grade and didn't work too hard

Professor Sloan is one of the world's leading health economists and he knows it.  I found him arrogant, critical, and unapproachable.  His textbook and lecture notes and completely disorganized and hard to understand.  He himself makes simple concepts convoluted when he tries to explain them.  I was not the biggest fan..

If you are at all interested in health policy and economics, take a class with FS before you graduate. He is brilliant, and the best professor I've ever had. Selects relevant and extremely interesting published papers from the best people in the field. I honestly can't say enough good things about him.

464 is rigorous content, exams reflect this. Heavy reliance on Shankar's text (perhaps too formal for a first quantum course) and time-intensive P-sets. Socolar provides strong support -- office hours always available, answers emails, personable. Lectures sometimes lacking in exemplification, though Mathematica visualizations interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great class! Be prepared to read shankar though... had really good office hours and willing to review exams/questions with students! Curved exams too. exams require thinking though

socolar's a nice and approachable guy who genuinely cares about teaching, but his execution is substandard. the flipped classroom for quantum just didn't work. lectures consisted of him saying words about results or doing demos without actually teaching concepts, and shankar isnt a good intro text. you learn plenty, but will not leave satisfied
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: really nice professor, love to spend time after class with students and answer questions related or not related to course content. helps a lot in building my understanding of quantum mechanics

If you look to take this class because Acoustics and Music sounds interesting to you, I did that too and it did not pan out that way. Considering the class is a 100 level music and a 100 level physics class with NO PRIOR physics knowledge necessary, this class is incredibly physics heavy and unnecessarily difficult and not fun.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: I took his Acoustics & Music class expecting it to be interesting and relatively straightforward but I was very mistaken. The lectures were boring and confusing. He was constantly saying things and then realizing what he said was not in-fact right. 20-page final research project and super time-consuming and confusing assignments. Midterm avg was 64

Professor Socolar is a very enthusiastic professor. Not only does he have a thorough and solid understanding about the background knowledge about acoustics, he was also able to deliver those concepts to students through a very direct and interesting way (with nicely made demos). Grading is not harsh at all if you participate. Highly recommended!
