Socolar is a pretty good teacher.  His explanations are usually very clear.  But my class was a flipped class which I don't think works very well for Physics.  He is enthusiastic which makes class enjoyable, and his demonstrations are really cool.  He is very nice and approachable; easy to talk to.

He cares a lot about making sure students understand the material. He is clearly fascinated by the topics and tries to impart that enthusiasm to the class. I didn't always find his lectures to be as helpful or clear as the textbook (and I'm afraid to say the textbook wasn't very good). He also doesn't strike me as brilliant the way some others do.

Enjoyed this class immensely.  Although some of the labs were tedious, the home works were interesting and appropriately challenging.  Test were hard but, hey it's relativity and quantum.  Use of mathematic demos were cool too as well as historical significance of topic.

Genuinely interested in teaching, his students, and making sure that students learn the material.  Clearly dedicated a lot of time to being available and open for questions and providing resources to students.  Tests and grading generally fair.  The final was somewhat more conceptual than the problems we'd been doing all year. Excellent prof.
Dr. Socolar is clear, has great demos, and explains the physics so that I could really comprehend the underlying concepts. He's also great one-on-one clearing up misconceptions and confusions.

Although his lectures aren't always clear, his powerpoint slides are really helpful and his examples illustrate concepts really well.  Often, he is confusing and you have to get him to clarify.  He knows a lot though. Once stayed at a review session until 2 in the morning.
kind of boring lecturer.  his notes aren't super helpful later on.  I prefer brown who makes it more clear and relevant.

Better than Brown! That's enough to make it exciting. Overall, his powerpoint notes are not helpful later on for studying for tests. Lectures were more exciting than Brown, but still not as engaging as it could be. Sometimes explanations were vague.
totally cool dude, very smart, but possibly the worst lecturer in the brief history of the universe.
I had physics 61 with Dr. Socolar last year.  (Note only 23 students were assigned to this pilot version).  He's pretty easy at grading.  Provide helpful review sessions before exam.

One foundational exam early in the semester (all memorization), then light workload. Graded on weekly responses and class participation - readings can be long, but you can get by by skimming and picking out key points. Professor and TA are very accessible for feedback.

Prof. Sosin really knows his stuff and is very accessible and kind. That said, the structure of the class was very repetitive (sit in a circle and talk about the cases). I would not take his course unless you have a genuine interest in Athenian Law and are willing to get through 50+ pages of reading per session.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Overall one of the best teachers I've had. Definitely helped that I found Athenian Law really interesting but Professor Sosin also makes it really interesting. He clearly cares about how people are doing and gives very clear criteria for grading. Definitely need to be doing the reading and participating but overall great class. Definitely recommend

I loved Professor Sosin's class!! He was so knowledgable and really encouraged us to explore history. The class had a ton of reading, but it was all really interesting and Professor Sosin does a great job of explaining/building on the readings without just recapping the content. Pop quizzes are easy 100s if you've done the reading.

Sosin is by far my favorite professor at Duke. Dude is a modern-day Herodotus with regards to factual recall, but more notable is his understanding of what makes the classics such an intriguing discipline. If you're willing to do the reading and ask questions in class, you'll come away with a remarkably deep comprehension of Ancient Greece.
Well-versed in his subject, incorporates class interests into topics very well, has an answer to everything
best

Good guy. He lectures for about half or more of the class (which isn't a complaint, his lectures are pretty interesting) and discussion happens after. There are sometimes short pop quizzes just to make sure you're staying on top of the readings. He provides the reading materials or they can be found online for free. Really funny too.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Unclear criteria for participation grade, which makes up most of your final outcome
One of my favorite professors at Duke. Dr. Sosin genuinely cares about his students and makes everyone feel comfortable participating in class without the fear of judgement. Also funny as hell.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: really makes you think! the first month kinda sucks bc its a crash course on a single textbook with a huge test at the end, but the exam is fair and the lectures are entertaining if a little fast. After that, it's all discussion-based. lots of reading though. fantastic prof he's insanely smart, lets you curse, and wants you to dig deeper.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I liked Dr. Sosin as a person, but the class was not for me. He's pretty clear with what he expects of you. There's a lot of reading that gets boring if you're not really into history. Weekly quizzes, so you expect them after the first two. Weekly writing assignments that the TA's grade. Fine class, but make sure you like history before taking it.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Clear grading criteria--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Great, energetic teacher. Took his Greek History class and loved it. You will have to read a decent bit though, at least the night before the "pop" reading quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Very passionate guy but A LOT of reading! He makes you put in the work for the class. The pop quizzes are sometimes hard even if you do the reading. Overall very nice teacher and great prof

Prof. Sosin is extremely passionate about Greek History and he knows EVERYTHING. His lectures are engaging and often very funny. This guy has no filter. There is A LOT of reading for this class. Grade is derived from 10 short papers, attendance, pop quizzes (which are lowkey super hard), active pariticipation, and final. Overall, great professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: By far the greatest professor I have ever had during my time at Duke. He's engaging and funny and extremely helpful and although his class requires a lot of reading its so so worth it even for someone who just wants to fill a requirement like myself. Now, I'm even considering a minor in Classical Studies.

Best lecturer i've had so far at Duke. Made the material really interesting and easy to follow. There was a ton of reading but you really don't have to do all of it, just enough to pass the reading quizzes. Leaves are graded reasonably and it's easy to get an extra point on them. No tests, just weekly one page responses and final
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Sosin was an incredible professor. His lectures were amazing and detailed and he always left time for questions at the end. It's a lot of reading most nights but worth it for how interesting he makes it in class. His passion for Greek History made the class very enjoyable. Would highly recommend to anyone remotely interested in history/classics.

Professor Sosin is a highly engaging lecturer who always entertains. The majority of the readings assigned are primary sources, which he uses to teach the fundamental aspects of Greek culture from the perspective of ancient Greeks themselves. The very short weekly writing assignments that replace long papers allow room for feedback and growth.

Prof Sosin is an incredible lecturer and a great guy. He has an encyclopedic knowledge of the ancient world and packs a lot of information into each lecture. His class requires a great deal of reading but most of it is fairly engaging.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Not only one of the best professors I've had at Duke, but by far the best lecturer I've ever had the pleasure of experiencing. Had him for both Greek History and a summer course on Athenian Law. Sosin creates a perfect balance of informational and enjoyable by virtue of his own immense knowledge - he truly makes you want to engage with the work.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Sosin is an amazing professor. There is a lot of reading involved, and he lectures. But the discussions are always interesting, and he keeps you engaged!

This was one of my favorite classes the semester I took it.  Prof. Sosin is funny, engaging, and knows his stuff.  However, there is a lot of reading to do and needs to be done.  Going to him during office hours is the best thing to do for the class.  He cares a lot about his students and will give you pretty much all the time you need for help.

Professor Sosin is very interested in the topics he's teaching so it makes for a much better class. Lectures are important and expect a lot of reading, but he and his TA's are always willing to help with paper's and assignments. Sosin is always energetic and excited so his classes are fun to take and interesting despite your interests.

Awesome guy and really knows what he teaches. He is the kind of professor that you want if you are interested in the topic, he always is interested in what you have to say, and even invited the class to dinner at his house. There is a lot of reading and participation definitely matters, but its nothing overwhelming.

It was thanks to Professor Sosin and his class that I decided to become a Classical Studies major. The only reason I'm not taking his class next semester is because I can't speak or read ancient Greek.
Sosin is a hilarious and awesome lecturer. All around great guy and great class!

Greek History was a fun ride Sosin was a great lecturer (especially on the Iliad) and his assignments were fun and innovative.  I had a hard time figuring out what he wanted in his writing assignments, but I loved the class.

Greek History was difficult, with a lot of reading, but Prof. Sosin was a great lecturer. His comments on papers are actually useful and if you follow through you can actually improve your writing.  If you want to make the most of your education and want to take an interesting class, if you just want an easy course prof. Sosin isn't for you.

I recommend everyone to take his Greek history class. His lectures are actuallly fascinating to listen to, so you don't actually have to drag yourself to class. There is a big workload in terms of reading, but the exams and the papers aren't actually that bad in terms of difficulty and grading.
Dr. Sosin is awesome!  He is an amazing Classicist and is really dedicated to helping his students.  Plus, he is hilarious.
Not too easy, but at the same time its not too tough, very interesting class and if you put in some effort it shouldnt be that bad. He's very willing to help you, great prof!!

Sosin assigns a lot of reading, but he really knows his stuff.  Papers take some thought.  If you show some interest and put in the work, he'll be on your side.  One of the best lecturers ever!  I highly recommend his class.  Even if you don't like the Rome to begin with, you will!
Greek history was very hard last semester!  Tons of reading every night, very hard to keep up.  He is a very hard grader when it comes to papers.  Very nice, though, and a brilliant guy.

Dr. Sosin is a great prof., but his class is far from easy.  I felt that he made things especially difficult because he wanted to make sure students took his class seriously.  He is very open to student opinion and always takes the time to help students.  Politics often underly his lectures though.
Sosin is an awesome lecturer. The reading load per week is impressive and his rubric for grading papers is rigorous but still one of the better professors I've had here.

Greek history was tough.  Around 80-100 pages of reading every night.  Some of it was very tough.  A lot was very dense histories.  But the class was a challenge and that was good.  He can lecture like no one I've seen before.  He is very entertaining, and is quite funny a lot of the time.

Greatest class I've ever taken.  The reading load is intense and grading is tough, but Sosin is the most amazing lecturer I've ever heard.  His enthusiasm for the subject and flat-out brilliance more than make up for the difficulty of the class.

Zhou Laoshi is VERY flexible with policies: we asked her of many things and she literally changed the rules. We had a very small class (3 ppl), so it was boring, but she tried hard to making engaging, and taught vocabulary well. I had an emergency and had to go home, so she accommodated and held my tests personally online, late in December.

She was my only chinese professor, so I don't have others to compare. However, I found her classes super engaging and funny. The assingments and grading are fair. I think she is strict at a fair level, the expectations are clear. 10s are difficult, less than 8.5 are even more. I learned a lot with her and she is indeed patient to teach.

Zhou Laoshi is very strict in terms of pronunciation and handwriting. I am a really good Chinese learner, When I took Chinese200 level with other Laoshis, I would always get 10/10 all the time. Zhou Laoshi will find any excuse not to give a 10, always 9.75, 9.5, 9.25, 9.9, never a 10!!! I will never take Chinese with her again, avoid her classes!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She definitely grades more harshly than Chinese profs I've had before, but she also doesn't make it very hard to do well in the class. Quizzes were a little excessive because the 402 readings had like 100 vocab words each and super formal. She's very flexible with her policies, just make sure to show up and be prepared for discussion

Zhou laoshi is the best. I've taken all my freshman year classes with her. Someone mentioned she is a tough grader. Well, that is because she has to be fair with others too. Some students do really good in Chinese while others don't (like me). Therefore getting a B+ (like I did before), is still a lot.
I loved prof Zhou, she is so kind and her lectures are great. Highly recommend

Sophia Zhou is a tough grader. For things, one usually would get a 10, laoshi gives 9. You do much more work for a worse grade than in other Chinese classes. It is just not worth it. Classes are very fast-paced without any fun. It was stressful. Feedback is not really helpful cause it is just there without any explanation.
She is the greatest Chinese teacher
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Zhou is a great teacher. Her kindness and friendly attitude makes learning really VERY easy. She's very understanding too, but make sure you don't try to take advantage of her kindness. Keep your work on time, and be honest to it, you'll do great!

Zhou Laoshi is a great teacher. I always get nervous speaking Chinese but her kindness and friendliness make me feel more comfortable which helps a lot. I am impressed at how much I have learned with her, just remember to do your work and you will be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I love Professor Zhou! She makes learning Chinese so much fun. I was able to improve a lot over the course of the session thanks to Professor Zhou spending extra time to help everyone. Taking Chinese with Professor Zhou is the best choice :)

Sophia Zhou is a good professor, always responds to emails outside of class and her feedback is very helpful. She always pays attention to details and my speaking/pronunciation has improved thanks to her corrections.
Professor Zhou is amazing! I always enjoyed her class. She really emphasizes pronunciation which is helpful when learning a language. I would definitely take her class again.
She is amazing!! Zhou Laoshi gives really good feedback and pays attention to details. Definitely do not hesitate to take her class, she's the best!

Professor Zhou is literally so amazing. I was losing hopes to be good at Chinese. She lifted up my morale by encouraging me and helping me out. She's also a very considerate person and is very detail-oriented. TAKE HER CLASS. TAKE HER CLASS. TAKE HER CLASS.

Zhou Laoshi is amazing at teaching Chinese, and I'm super sad I won't have her for next year's courses. She cares about each one of her students and works to make classes interesting for us. Almost everyone who's come out of her classes has a great grasp on beginning Chinese.

Zhou Laoshi was so fun to learn intro Chinese from, and very attentive to important details that made the learning experience easier. She was picky about our pronunciation from the start, but that helped so much down the line. Also gives tough feedback but doesn't grade too hard. Chinese is a tough language but she's very accommodating.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Participation matters

reviews.comment: If you are taking CHIN 101 at DKU, take Professor Zhou's class (I promise you will not regret)! Puts great emphasis on each student's pronunciation and progress in general. Taking her class will never be boring. Since you are attending Chinese every day, you are required to do daily work, but no so much. Get excited to learn Chinese with her!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Zhou Laoshi is an amazing language teacher! Her approach is hands-on and super engaging. Students get a good deal of practice in speaking, listening, reading and writing Chinese. She chooses scenarios that students are likely to encounter outside class so what we learn is clearly relevant. Her feedback is detailed and very helpful too.

Professor Zhou is amazing! She has extensive experience in teaching beginning Chinese to foreigners and does so amazingly. She is a fair grader, gives useful feedback, listens to students, and is super approachable outside class. I highly recommend her!

Professor Smith is great! He cares about his students and is very flexible/understanding. Assignments have clear rubrics and graded fairly. Participation is very important and his classes are very engaging, also a lot of freedom to explore issues you are interested in. Easy to do well.
Dr. Smith has been my favorite Professor at Duke. He changed my way of thinking and influenced my future career plans. Could not recommend this class more.

Dr. Smith's class never ceases to leave me feeling like a better student and a better person. The passion he has for his material is unmatched. Every class leaves you wanting more and thinking about how you can make a positive change in the world. He truly cares about each student in his class and wants to see them evolve as a person and a leader.

Professor Smith is definitely one of my favorite professors at Duke. I was always excited to go to his class and learn new things. He is genuine and passionate in his teaching and cares so much about students' opinions. Would totally recommend this class to anyone!

An incredible class that I recommend all Duke students take. All he wants is for us to use our voice and think differently from how weve been socialized. Ask questions, participate, do the readings; youll learn so much. Best class I have ever taken at Duke, at thats on that.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Smith created a great classroom environment that made participation and interest in the coursework easy and attainable. He fostered some really thought-provoking discussions, was very invested in each student, and readily available outside of class for anything you may need. Easily one of my favorite courses and professor I have had at Duke.

Professor Smith was the best part of my first semester. The class is easy, but the material is relevant and interesting. Professor Smith could be disorganized and spontaneous sometimes, but he is incredibly intelligent, engaging, and makes a genuine effort to get to know his students. Going to his class never felt like a chore -- take this class.

Dr. Smith is one of my favorite professors at Duke. He is genuine and cares about the material taught in class. Dr. Smith really makes you think about race relations in the 1950s/60s and how things relate to today's society. Overall, great professor, great class. PARTICIPATION IS KEY.
Such an inspiration and wonderful class. Very easy but makes you care about issues you didn't even know existed

One of the best professors at Duke! He really cares about his students and is very knowledgeable about the topics. He makes time for students outside of class and will be highly invested in your personal success if you show interest and participate in class. Take any class he teaches!
One of the best professors I've ever had. Take his class even if you don't want to minor in Education. It changed my experience at Duke!
Dr. Smith was awesome, I took tons of econ classes but never really understood lagrangians until I had him explain them.
No Comments

Easily worst professor I have had at Duke. An interesting class was made miserable by his failed teaching. No resources, no syllabus, no organization, and no communication between professor, TAs, and students. Only reason his score is so high is that he gives out A's - but he taught us nothing.

I took both 110 and 270 with Smith. 110 was fine, a little disorganized but most ppl got As. 270 has been the worst class I have taken at Duke. No syllabus, no textbook, test averages in the 40s, constant mistakes and typos on slides/answer keys, bad lectures. Everyone will probably get As from his crazy curve, but I learned absolutely nothing.

Dr. Smith is one of the best professors I had at Duke. He has a very fair grading criteria despite considerably tough midterms. For ECE 110 he drops the lowest out of your 3 midterms and final. His exams averages are usually between 50% and 70%, but he compensates with very fair curve. Homework is graded on completion only.

Dr. Smith is an awesome professor and I truly enjoyed having classes with him in the Spring of 2023. He cares a lot about his students and he is very accessible outside of the classroom (even creating additional OH). Sometimes felt lost in his lectures but after reading the textbook it is fine.

Lectures were sorta all over the place and it took him/his tas months to get midterm grades back. Tests were not finishable in amount of time given. That being said, him (or his tas, not sure) gave a crazy amount of partial credit + he curved the class to an A- and made the final optional (albeit 2 days before the final was supposed to be given).

Dr Smith is a great professor but he explains in a way it can be hard to understand sometimes. He is very accessible outside classes and there are a lot of office hours. Be aware his exams are hard and it takes very long to hear back the results.

Smith is an extremely knowledgeable lecturer and cares a lot about his students. Lectures too fast sometimes but is always willing to answer questions outside of class. He also curved the class to an A-, was extremely generous with partial credit on exams, and made the final exam optional. I definitely learned a lot from taking his class.

David smith is super caring and knowledgable. His lectures arent super engaging but he will answer any question in-depth and cares that we understand the material. He follows the textbook closely and is easy to do well in class without attending. Our final exam got made optional which is wonderful. Take his class.

Professor Smith is very accessible and helpful in office hours and often is willing to make individual meetings if you can't make his normal hours. The tests were either stupid hard or stupid easy, but he curved the class average to a B+ I believe. Lectures are somewhat dry and fast-paced. Overall, I enjoyed his class by the end of the semester.

very slow lecturer but good at explaining things. also very accessible outside of class for one-on-one help and office hours. cares about his students, very kind, fair exams. felt like lectures did not prepare for psets tho, those were really really hard.

Homework is graded for completion, tests are curved mercifully, and he's easily accessible outside of class. Still, he's a fast and not very engaging lecturer, and you may need a few runs through a particular concept to make it stick. I don't know how much he cares about the class relative to other profs, but he cares about students.

David is extremely smart, and sometimes he assumes we know too much and goes really fast, or just does some derivations on the board that make no sense. He is also one of the few ECE 110 profs that gives out midterms, which are quite difficult. Bottom line: he is a difficult prof but you will learn more than if you took a different professor.

David Smith does a poor job explaining concepts. He assumes lots of background knowledge, and he lectures so quickly that even the smartest kids in class are lost. He will answer questions thoughtfully, and his office hours can be helpful, but he cares very little about the class in general.

Does not care about teaching. Tests have many mistakes and are hard, however, he curves nicely. Moves too fast in lecture but will explain better if you go to office hours. Assigns much more homework than other ECE110 professors, however, the homework is graded on completion.

I honestly really loved his course - it was covid semester (Spring 2020), but even before he was really understanding, adjusted grades, wanted us to do well, and would take time to help explain anything that confused you. Super nice dude, and smart. If he occasionally got confused he always resolved it after a bit so I didnt mind.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Smith is far more preoccupied with his research than he is being a teacher. He often cancelled lectures/assignments, and lectures were generally dry and confusing. Homework did not align with lecture and took lots of time due to having look up formulas and notes that were not in the slides. Lenient grading was only positive aspect of the course
Nice guy who cares about his students

Lectures move fast, but he takes the time to review concepts and answer questions if requested. Office hours with him and the TAs are very accessible. Exams are very difficult, but the curve for them is very high. Attend all lectures if you want the exams, labs, and homework to be as low stress as possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: He is extremely knowledgeable and he can sometimes get into a rhythm during lecture and go a bit too fast. But, he is more than willing to slow down, reexplain and take questions. Super accessible outside of class and really wants to ensure the students are understanding. Made more office hours for us when needed.
This was his first time teaching ECE110, and he wasn't clear in teaching the material.  However, in the end, he curved the grades pretty well.

def hard.  lots of hw, quizes every 2 or so weeks...but it also forces you to keep up.  only one midterm...and it was ridiculously hard (he wanted something to help him get a better distribution of grades) but at least feel like lecture is worthwhile, the book is fairly good and that you'll actually learn the stuff.
Interesting Class.
Very good at teaching, great online resources, and tests are very fair. Projects are VERY challenging.

I don't like this guy. His teaching style in class? Wonderful. His attitude anywhere else? Not kind. Not caring. If you can learn everything in lecture and never require clarification, you'll have a great time. If not, prepare to be degraded so thoroughly that Gordon Ramsay would applaud. Approach with caution, confidence, and maybe a therapist.

Best professor at Duke. Take 250 over 210 especially if prof is Sorin!! He is very passionate about the content and makes you love CS. The content is really hard but the lectures are very good. Easy to approach/ask questions, cares about students, effort to learn names. Tests are not hard but homeworks you need to start early and get help from TAs.

Best teacher for 250. The class itself is really hard and he makes the lectures very interactive. He's practically begging students to ask questions in class. Start homeworks REALLY early and get help from TAs. If you pay attention in class and do that, you should be able to get an A. Exams are pretty easy to balance the hard homeworks
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Sorin really loves computer architecture and makes that clear in his lectures. Its a large class but he really wants to get to know every student who tries and is very fair. Tests are really easy, projects are difficult but if you put in the time its an easy and interesting CS class.

Professor Sorin is the first CS professor I've had at Duke that made me genuinely passionate about the subject. He takes the time to learn every one's names, is engaging, funny, and great at explaining content that continually gets more and more complicated. He makes it clear how to do well in the class--start HW early-- and gave fair exams. 10/10!

Professor Sorin is great, and I think the class is amazing too! This class got me interested in hardware. Lectures are not mandatory, but I recommend going to them. His office hours are also a great resource. Test your code incrementally. Projects are not too bad if you do; it will save so much time because debugging is so time-consuming.

Prof. Sorin's lecture are incredibly engaging and well-designed, which makes the material much easier to grasp. Yes, projects are difficult, but at this point everyone has heard that you need to start them early so just be prepared to do so as well as go to office hours. Overall a great professor who is accessible and really cares!

START THE HOMEWORKS EARLY like no bs you will not finish them in one night. You also cannot cheat whatsoever so it makes it more important to do the assignments. The content is pretty confusing but he is easy to talk to and is very patient. He asked me on a coffee date and he was pretty cool.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Class is difficult with seemingly constant projects. Class policies are well-designed and prof is caring.

Great professor and person but stretched analogies way too far in this class to the point where I didn't understand lectures. I wish he explained some things directly in CS terms. Found lectures a bit slow. More could've been covered in the same time. I wish we used Verilog instead of logism and spent more time on important concepts like caches.

Prof. Sorin is awesome. I had a hard time getting up to speed initially and found the material to be challenging throughout (no previous background). Prof and TAs were helpful. Homework and debugging took a massive amount of time. I enjoyed it more than "easier" classes in CS.
The content is interesting and Sorin is a good lecturer. However, this class is a lot of work. Make sure to start projects well ahead of time and go to office hours.

Professor Sorin knows his stuff and lectures well - pay attention and you'll do well on the exams. You get ~3 weeks for each homework assignment, but they took me anywhere from 10-25 hours each. Start early and go to office hours.

Project heavy class, you will see this a lot: "Start projects early". Projects are long and not easy, but also very cool, interesting and rewarding. Sorin gives amazing lectures, very clear and engaging, plus he is also funny. He is always willing to meet outside class (do it). Exams are fair (kinda easy), and very similar to the practice ones.
Bro is funny, clear, and experienced. Sorin is the goat.

Professor Sorin is a respected, no bs type professor. Lectures are useful to go to in person.

One thing of advice: START HOMEWORK PROJECTS EARLY. They are lengthy. I did not do that on two of them and had to pull several all nighters. One homework I got a 70% on because I did so bad, and I barely managed to clutch up the A on the final.

I loved cs250 with Sorin. Lectures were great, he really distilled concepts well. Slides and recordings were made available. The homework was hard, but there was plenty of time to get it done. Examinations were easy in my opinion. Everything was fair, well graded and communicated. He is super approachable.

Professor Sorin doesn't want anyone failing his class. He makes it clear what you need to know and provides super helpful practice exams. If you put in a bit of effort, you will get an A in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: They tell you to start the hw early butt he class setup makes it easier to start the projects after you cover the material in discussion. The help rooms are crowded and you can't always get help. The slides are not always helpful w/o rewatching lecture but it's recorded.

Amazing professor: clear explanations, hilarious, and super enthusiastic every lecture. Although this class is often tough for students, as its usually their first "real" coding class, Professor Sorin makes the theory part of the class as easy as can be.

Professor Sorin is awesome. The lectures are incredibly fascinating and Professor Sorin keeps them interesting. The course and material is difficult and you will have to work hard to earn a good grade. At some points during the homework I felt like giving up, but with perseverance and dedicated effort every assignment is more than doable.

Sorin makes easy concepts harder than necessary in his lectures. He abstracts them too far and his examples usually aren't that helpful, so it's hard to get a grip of how things work. Also, projects are super hard and his lectures barely help you.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
Professor Sorin is obviously well versed in computer architecture and truly cares about his students.

Some people will complain about the class and it's difficulty and blame it on the professor, but he does an amazing job teaching, whether or not the class is hard. Definitely put a lot of time towards the class and its homeworks or you will do bad
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: One of my favorite classes so far, learned a lot about what computers are, and how they actually work. That said, I recommend starting the projects early (just because some submission errors can happen at the end). His tests are mostly straightforward but one mistake can cost a lot. Regardless of how you find the class, you'll def learn a lot.

Definitely that hardest class I've taken here at Duke. Neverthless, Sorin was such an amazing professor that I often forgot my struggles. He is an awesome person to talk to in general, whether it is related to CS or not. Also, shoutout to his TA's for putting in a lot of hours to help the students.

This was the hardest class I've taken at Duke. Each project easily took me 10 hours if not sometimes over 40 (MIPS). He's a great professor but it's just a lot of work. OH lines are long. You often had to wait 1.5+ hours before getting help, especially a few days before project submissions.

This class was exceedingly hard and my biggest stressor this year. Professor Sorin was caring, but I found he could be rather condescending. It was hard to get help at OHs and the TAs often gave conflicting advice. There is no collaboration or community in this class, it is very every-man-for-himself.

Personally, this class was brutal, but I'm glad the suffering is over now. Sorin wasn't a bad professor, but I don't think I liked architecture enough to understand it well. Once again, START YOUR HW EARLY (ESPECIALLY MIPS) bc sometimes OH would take 2.5 hours before I got any help....
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class was organized and the lectures were pretty good. The homeworks were very difficult and office hours would be extremely crowded near deadlines. Start the homeworks early so you can get help in office hours. The tests are pretty easy, but the final was fairly difficult.

This was a fascinating class and Sorin is a wonderful lecturer. That said, the projects are a massive time sink (although the material itself isn't too conceptually difficult and tests are easy). Start every assignment at least a week early; don't be me, assume you can tackle it all in a few days, and get a 60 on the first project :')
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Masquerades as kind, hip, down to earth, but nice profs don't put midterms SMACK in the middle of a hw projects. Feels like you're set up to fail in so many ways. 

If you don't have years of CS experience and confidence built up, AVOID, especially with Sorin. Take 210 or take with Bletsch. This class literally broke me.

Honestly, I think a lot of people overhype the difficulty of 250. With Sorrin, I thought the class was difficult but manageable as long as you start the projects early and plan out your time well. Also, attending the lectures and not reading the slides two days before the exam makes studying easier. Office hours were crowded, so go early.

I would never want to take this class ever again, but I'm glad that I took it with Professor Sorin because he is so nice, caring and accessible outside of class. This class is a ton of work on your own, and the homework projects are frustrating to work through individually. But I would definitely recommend taking it with Sorin if you have to.

Sorin is a great lecturer, always open to answer questions. Projects time-consuming (15hrs each 4 me) but feasible, start EARLY! Tests easy so balances out. Not being able to collab on projects worth 45% of grade is reasonable imo; I preferred it to hard midterms. You learn lots in this class (bits to HLL), very rewarding. Take this class w Sorin.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Sorin is one of the best professors I've had so far. His lectures are phenomenal, he explains concepts very well, and he's always accessible (he held multiple office hours every week with just a few students present). CS250 can be a difficult class, but Sorin makes the class just about as accessible and straightforward as possible.

One of the best CS profs around who gives clear lectures, passionate about the subject and is extremely considerate and caring given the current circumstances (virtual classes, etc.). Might be quite some work and non collaborative but he made it clear it helps us to learn and advise us to start early so idk why people are crying

Prof Sorin is the GOAT. One of the best CS profs at Duke, if not the best. If you're taking 250, take it with him. The bad reviews below are ridiculous - people crying over an actual CS class that exceeds 201 workload smh

Straightforward exams (though the final was a bit more conceptual) and Sorin is really caring and makes sure you understand the material. The main con is the homework, which really make you work, but still doable in the end and isn't unique to this class. Felt bad that the TAs were understaffed and overworked so it's hard to get help. Solid choice.

Dr. Sorin is something special. He has a distinctive passion for the topic and his students, and his fiery and comedic lecturing style keeps students engaged. Explanations are clear and thorough, and he encourages questions at all times. Homework can be challenging but is doable and covered in lecture. Start early so you can get help!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Baffled at the negative reviews. The class is hard with any prof, but Sorin is one of the best lecturers you will have at Duke. Classes are engaging and he explains things super well. Tests are just like practice ones. THINK OF THE HOMEWORKS AS HUGE PROJECTS, they're hard and take a ton of work. No collaboration sucks but Sorin himself is amazing.

Sorin is a great lecturer and his slides are clear and thorough. Tests are almost exactly like the practices and are pretty easy. The homework assignments (essentially projects) are what you have to worry about. Yes the class is hard but I learned a ton and I'm actually really glad I took it - just don't take it with a super heavy schedule.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I hate this class with all my heart. It has made me question my major. Prof Sorin does not allow you to work with others on the HW. It is nearly impossible to receive help from TAs because the help room is always full. You have to wait hours to receive guidance, and sometimes the TAs are not even helpful. If I could rate Sorin a 0, I would.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Very hard class, with little support this semester. Collaboration is looked down on, which makes doing hw very difficult if you need a bit of help or guidance. It makes no sense since collaboration is needed for engineering jobs.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: i would rather gouge my eyes out, contract appendicitis, and have every romantic partner cheat on me for the rest of my life, than take this class again. so awful and made me consider changing majors. it was the single biggest stressor in my life this semester, i had an overwhelmingly negative experience. sorin is a good lecturer though

Engaging lecturer and values that his students truly understand the material. Will talk after class as well as in office hours. Programming projects force you to understand the material and can take a lot of time. Tests are super straightforward. Best class I've taken at Duke so far, which is impressive because it was all online.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Amazing lecturer who clearly enjoys teaching. The other faculty teaching computer architecture use his powerpoints for their own classes. I was rarely confused in his class. A lot of class time was devoted to discussing papers and answering questions. Definitely one of the better professors I've had.
He is great, enthusiastic. Tests are not too difficult.

Sorin makes CS250 as straightforward as it can be. His lectures are clear and cover everything you need to know (I never used the textbook). Homeworks can be time-consuming but are otherwise doable. Two midterms and final were reasonable and similar to practice exams. Overall, clear expectations and makes the course manageable - highly recommend

Sorin was a great prof. No big surprises on the tests/final - definitely do the practice exams. The homeworks were definitely time intensive and pretty complex. Make sure to start early so you have ample time to go to office hours before they get swamped in the days leading up to the deadline. The textbook is also not necessary to succeed.

Sorin is who you should look out for to take this class. He is a great lecturer, and although less than a third of the class showed up on a given day, being in lecture and asking questions is useful and I'd recommend. Start the homework early, the late penalty is harsh. Exams have very high averages, and exams are almost the same as practice exams.

Sorin is an excellent professor. His lectures are very clear and they're engaging. I always felt like I understood the material from his lectures, so although HWs were sometimes a decent amount of work they were not crazy difficult. Tests are straightforward. He teaches well so it's not a hard class and I learned a lot. Recorded lectures a plus

Sorin is an AMAZING lecturer. His slides are well-prepared, and he knows the material. Going to/watching the lecture really helps you (no need to buy/use textbook). You will learn a lot in this class; take it with him if you can. Average in the course is B, and 30% of the class got an A/A-. Projects/HW are long, so don't procrastinate too much.

I loved Sorin, he's the best 250 teacher hands down. The class is still hard, and assignments are rigorous (though they are only every few weeks), but Sorin is a great teacher and really helps you understand what you're doing. He's also helpful, nice, and supportive. Do take 250 with him if you can, even if you have to wait a semester or two.

Great professor, clear in lectures and give very fair assignments/tests. The work load is not too bad if you manage your time well. Definitely less work than CS201. Some concepts might be a bit challenging, but overall pretty easy. Almost half of the class received A or A-

For any CS major, CS250 will generally always present itself as a challenge. However, Sorin does an amazing job with lectures, even if you are just watching them online. The feeling I felt after finishing watching all the lectures online was similar to the feeling after finishing a good Netflix show. Great prof, hard class, but very rewarding.
Great professor. Material is hard, assignments are hard, but easy tests.

Professor Sorin has probably been my favorite professor at Duke. He is one of those professors that absolutely loves his research as well as teaching. So many professors simply just read off of slides, but he barely even looks at the slides and still knows exactly whats going on. Really approachable and helpful too.

Sorin is probably the best lecturer I've had through all 4 years of ECE. He really cares about the topic and his students. The homeworks are fair and his tests are relatively easy given how much we go over in the class.

The assignments are extremely time consuming mainly because it is difficult to debug programs written in C or MIPS (or the wires in Logism). He is great at lecturing and explaining the concepts clearly. He is clearly very passionate about the subject and is always willing to help.

He is a good professor but somewhat condescending and a bit paranoid about following rules strictly. There are not a lot of assignments, but they are difficult and time-consuming. I would not recommend this course unless you are sure that you want to be a CSECE major.

Dr. Sorin is an overall good professor but his class is a bit too hard. It is crosslisted as both a CS and ECE course, so students in one or the other but not both can find topics in the other subject difficult. Also, assignments are extremely lengthy and difficult and you hardly get any help on them unless you try really hard to ask for it.

If you can get through the MIPS assignment you're golden. The class is tough and most of the work is done in the 5 homework assignments that are assigned during the semester (more like projects). These took ranging from 6 hours to over 20, so start early. Extremely helpful and understanding.
Dr. Sorin is an excellent teacher.  He cares about the students and helping them do well.  He also cares about the field immensely and is one of the best professors in the department.

Great professor. One of not many professors loves teaching and cares about students. Clear lecturing. Helpful outside class both in topic related to class and general advices. However, he's a strict instructor expecting students to manage time well. So very unlikely give an extension, also can be intimidating if reach him closely before things due

In this class, you either get it or you don't. Sorin is obviously really excited and passionate about the subject matter and is super enthusiastic about answering questions. If you don't understand, though, he's much less helpful - I think that he doesn't fundamentally get that students can work hard, but still not find this material intuitive.
Either you get it in lecture, or you never get it. Lectures are really interesting and important, but outside of lecture, he can be really cold/unhelpful.

Dr. Sorin is a really solid professor.  He really cares if his students understand the material or not and is extremely willing to help if you don't understand something.  His assignments can be challenging but would really recommend this guy

Sorin is a great professor who really knows about computer architecture and wants to make sure students understand. Between the project and homework assignments, you really come to understand how a computer works. He responds quickly to questions on the class mailing list, and always wants to talk to students about the class or the field generally.

Dr. Smith is the man! Such an easy class to get an A+ on if you participate. Super lenient grader who cares about individual students. Learnt so much about war in Africa, not so much about public health. Fascinating man who has lived all over-- ask him questions, go to office hours, FLUNCH! Intend to take him again! Amazing class.

smith is great, very knowledgable and engaging. I was kinda expecting everyone to get an A but i guess that wasnt the case. midterm was easy, final was an in class essay and the rest was participation. In the end, im very glad I took this class! got to learn a lot of important things in a non-stressful environment.

Dr. Smith is a very knowledgeable professor, but I didn't enjoy the structure of this class at all. We had no information about grading, and it was essentially split between participation, midterm, final. In a large lecture class, meaningful participation is difficult. Not awful, but wouldn't take again.

Prof Smith is a nice guy, but his grading criteria is unclear and arbitrary. We had a lecture-style class, with around 40-50 people in attendance most of the time, and participation was worth 33% of your overall grade. Difficult to participate consistently with that many people. Syllabus had no mention whatsoever of grading, adding to confusion.

Professor Smith is my favorite professor at Duke so far. Though the class was lecture-heavy and included lots of homework, he gives lots of extra credit on tests and quizzes if you include extra information. He is an awesome guy - I highly recommend a FLUNCH with him. If you take notes and do the homework, you will be great in his class! 10/10!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Prof. Smith wanted everyone to be engaged and to learn as much as possible. He has decades of experience in studying Africa and his expertise was evident. When it comes to grading, although there is the occasional pop quiz, it's this simple: if you show up to class and take notes, you will do well in this class and you will not need to worry.

Beware of pop quizzes! He will quiz you on things that you were tested on before so make sure you keep up with all the info from the beginning of the semester. Otherwise, he is very knowledgeable about Africa and has had so many cool experiences there. Class is easy and straightforward, with plenty of extra credit opportunities. Clear grading too.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: He was the absolute greatest. He is crazy knowledgable about Africa and has had the most interesting life. He makes class entertaining and really interesting. 10/10 recommend any class he gives.

Hilarious, easygoing, and his class is minimal work but you'll learn a ton. He's also been all over the world and was present as a journalist at important events like Nelson Mandela's election. His email response time is also around 5 minutes, making him the fastest responding prof by far. He loves learning from his students too!

This class was one of the favorites. There was lots of reading and class discussions, participation matters a lot, but I loved every second of it. He is more concerned with students learning and grades, which elevates a lot of stress. He is also extremely knowledgeable and experienced with situations in Africa, make sure you FLUNCH him!

One of the best professors I've had at Duke. He worked in Africa for many years as a journalist; therefore, he combines stats with his personal anecdotes. There's quite a bit of reading, and he can tell who does it. Be sure to speak up in class and sit near the front. Definitely will be taking a class from him again.
Gives A LOT of reading. Class felt very repetitive at times. He is a very harsh grader, however it was a very interesting class and I would definitely take it again.

Smith is super experienced and knowledgeable but he can often get wrapped up in his own ideas. He likes new innovative ideas but does not really liked to be challenged and can be very intimidating. You learn so much in his class though.

Smith is knowledgable about Africa but his lectures can be confusing and it's easy to get lost. Gives you chances to shore up your grade with response papers before the final. Not really necessary to do the readings. Some can be interesting while others are a bore. Take detailed notes, pay attention during lectures, and you'll be fine.

Stephen Smith is fantastic!! His  lectures are really entertaining and informative! He has lots of experience in Africa, and he is always willing to meet after class to help. He is a hard grader, but the material is not difficult.

I do not recommend Smith or his class, Intro to African Studies. He is difficult to approach and a hard grader. This is supposed to be an intro class, and it was not taught or graded like one. Lectures were very all over the place and I often left feeling confused. If you take this class, attend every lecture or you will do poorly on tests.

I LOVE STEPHEN SMITH! He is so eloquent and his lectures are fantastic. He has a very interesting past having worked as a journalist and radio host in Africa for many years, and living in various other places throughout his life. This class teaches you a lot of interesting stuff with very little work. Definitely take it!

Professor Smith is my favorite professor at Duke. I'm in my second class with him. He's hilarious, interesting, and awe-inspiring. Used to be a journalist in Africa so he personally knows most of the African leaders and has experienced most of what he teached about. Extremely interactive class and teaches by asking questions. Fascinating readings.

Even though this class was a 8:45 I loved it.  He was a wealth of knowledge and experiences.  I honestly have no idea why he is teaching at Duke because he is almost too interesting to be a professor.  While i would not normally recommend an Intro class I would recommend taking any class with him.

I took numerous courses with Prof. Smith over my 4 years at Duke--Hollywood and Africa, War in Africa, Conflict Resolution. He is perhaps one of the best professors at Duke.  He's a brilliant man, very kind and loves to connect with students. He has so much knowledge coming from a French-German background and having spent years in Africa. Take him!
One of the best professors I've ever had at Duke, human embryology was one of the most interesting, thought-provoking classes I've ever taken and I would 100% recommend to anyone
Human Embryology was one of the best classes I ever taken- highly recommend

Anatomy of Vetebrates is an extremely difficult course--so much memorization (think bones, muscles, functional groups for all the classes of vertebrates with practical lab dissections and labeling quizzes) and it's almost impossible to learn it all for the very specific exams. The labs quizzes are equally difficult and specific.
Awesome teacher! best class and teacher i've had at duke! even took her second class the next semester (208L). would love to take another one!
Kathleen's extremely nice and very accessible outside class, and 108L covers a lot of challenging material without being too demanding.

Dr. Spinner's lectures were incredibly informative and made learning about academic writing incredibly fun. She allows for revisions on the major writing assignment for the class. This is by far the best Writing 101 class at Duke.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: TAKE. THIS. CLASS. It was BY FAR my favorite class at Duke so far, and had such an interesting layout. Dr. Spinner went above and beyond in her lessons and made class so fun; every time that I showed up, it felt more like hanging out with a friend than attending a lecture. The subject matter is so interesting, and she allows for revision.

loved taking radical magic with Dr. Spinner, she's super chill and funny! walks through examples of model papers, offers opportunities for revision, and gives you a lot of freedom on assignments. genuinely looked forward to attending class

Super interesting and super easy class. Dr. Spinner cares about you as an individual and makes sure that you'll get a strong foundation in academic writing. Do the readings (you'll learn a lot!), come into class with an open mind, and you'll get a good grade.

Radical Magic is a fantastic class to take as a freshman! There's not a lot of work outside class; you could get everything done in class. She is an easy grader and lets you resubmit your paper after getting feedback from her.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr Spinner was amazing! Her writing class, Radical Magic, is talked about by a lot of students at Duke for being extremely niche and engaging! We discuss lots of feminist-related topics - from the witch trials to Taylor swift - read tarot cards, and the final is a spellbook! Her syllabus can be a little confusing but she will clarify once you ask!

Dr. Spinner is a wonderful professor. She clearly cares a lot about her students as people and genuinely wants to help improve their writing. However, grading/assignment instructions were at times unclear and the syllabus did change throughout the semester. With that being said, she is flexible with due dates. Overall, she's awesome!
reviews.rating_tags: Hilarious--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Nice Prof！ Highly recommended
Realllllllllllllly good Professor. 冲！

I took all my EAP courses with Prof. Sprague when I was a freshman. It was an amazing experience. Prof. Sprague is a great, experienced lecturer. You could learn so much in his class without feeling even a little bit bored. He's my favorite professor at DKU. I sincerely recommend his EAP class which can give your college life a great start.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Sprague is really interesting among all the EAP faculty, he is young and entertaining as his appearance and behavior can tell.

The course implemented oral exams, which were quite engaging with Prof Spaller. All content had to be learned outside of class and every class day was just getting into 2+ breakout rooms to discuss a scenario, so it got to be quite repetitive. In the end the course was pretty much common sense and Prof Spaller was nice and a fair grader.

Full course was a mess but Spaller is chill. He is straightforward and fair. Calls on students randomly which can be jarring but there's no shame in admitting you don't know the answer. Grades reasonably and isn't "out to get" anyone. Nice guy and solid sense of humor. Looks carefully at your references so make sure you cite correctly!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Global Challenges is a really logistically complex course to take online, and it is overly technical with innumerable acronyms (IRATs, TRATs, TBLs, etc.). Professor Spaller keeps things light in his recitations and is an all-around good person, which makes taking this class remotely less of a burden than it could have been otherwise.

I think he made organic chem the best it could be without sacrificing the course material. He would tell engaging stories related to the chemistry and had great lecture slides. The course quality took a major hit when we rapidly and unexpectedly moved online, but global pandemics don't happen every semester. Would take another course from him.
He was advisor many years ago. I was really a philosophy major, but he was such really a nice man i never changed majors.
Knowledgeable. Eager to share knowledge.

The professor knows his subject extremely well. He can discuss any topic unaided for an entire hour. He is also easygoing with students, always tolerable of late work. Very patient in explaining difficult points.

Would not recommend this course or any class with this guy. He has a very strong tendency to lecture on and on and on without end. This class had 6 students and was designated a "Seminar," but he remarkably spoke without end for 75 minutes each session. Nigh impossible to get a word in, and the grading wasn't generous nor were paper topics clear.
One of the best professors that I had at Duke. He is a very insightful man who is extremely knowledgeable in the field. Exams and papers are not too hard if you keep up with the materials on time.

professor is knowledgeable and experienced and has an extraordinary ability of endless, sometimes pointless, talking. so not clear enough and do not have slides or other tools to help understanding the materials. readings are good and if you do read you'll learn something.
Boring and not easy.  Difficult class.  Avoid it
Kind of boring
Boring as hell. Content is not that difficult to comprehend, but making it through lecture is difficult. Overal, average class at best.

Sometimes lecture was a little boring, and that's really all this class is.  Reading was also often dull.  That said, he is a brilliant man and really knows his stuff.  Exams aren't too hard, just regurgitate what he said in class.  Papers also not too bad.
Professor Spragens, despite being boring at times, is extremely knowledgeable and helpful...he always teaches great courses
Very approachable and knowledgable.  However, can be a little dry at times during lecture.  Very generous in grading.  Gives insight into a variety of political thoughts.
He dissected Jimmy in front of the class.
He was amazing :)
He is awsome!!!!!!!! :)

A very good lecturer tries to keep it interesting. Very helpful and open to answering math-related questions (not related to the class). He really wants u to succeed, loved his class, and would take it again!

While his lectures were good, they followed the textbook. So, initially thought I could read the textbook to get by. After I made a C on the first test, I began going to his office hours. They gave me a much deeper understanding of the material. He's an exceptional teacher if you go to office hours and a decent teacher if you don't.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Spencer was very respectful of his students and rearranged his office hours so that the greatest number of students did not have conflicts. He also held extra review sessions before exams. His lectures were clearer and more organized than many of my past math professors in the math department. The homeworks and tests were pretty standard.

Easily the worst class I've taken. Assumes you've taken a multi class before. Exams take way longer than you have to take them. Strongly recommend not taking his class unless you're certain you want to be a math major.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Just read the textbook.

STA 199 is a relatively easy class, especially if you have any prior coding experience. Professor Smith was very helpful with troubleshooting and made grading criteria very clear on assignments. You do labs with a group of two other people for the whole semester, so try to find people you know in your lab section so that you can work with them.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Yeah, echoing other comments. Those covid precautions were... wow. Class has a lot of group projects. Otherwise, I've never had a more boring lecturer. Overall, material is not too bad, and is generally useful. Take this class with another professor if you can, though.

he's a great guy and knows a lot but his covid precautions are way too extreme. wears an n95 mask while he lectures, so it's really difficult to understand what he's trying to say at times. he also does not let us drink water in class, which should not be in his power to do. youd think he'd understand how low a risk covid poses to young /vaxxed ppl

He's a super nice guy and none of the work is really all that difficult. However the class focuses heavily on group work for which you will have the same group all semester, even if they're incompetent. I ended up doing virtually every lab myself as well as the final project. Super easy A, but only if you have friends to take the lab with.

Extremely strange individual who makes no effort to make his lectures interesting in the slightest. Does not allow you to drink water in class due to extreme Covid fear Purportedly a statistics class, but really a comp sci class and all coding. Assignments are plentiful and tedious. Do not recommend taking this class, especially without friends.

He is the best professor I've had if not one of the best. Sure his lectures can sometimes be boring but he really cares about his students and is very understanding of their struggles and circumstances. Also very responsive via email

I am writing this comment solely to say that you better have friends or make friends in this class who you can work on the assignments with. It's a collaborative effort. Lecture is kind of a waste of time butttt reusing code from lecture exercises is sometimes very helpful so keep that in mind. One final group project that rly matters.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Group projects

reviews.comment: Even though I didn't have an interest in political science (from which he draws all his examples from and lectures about), I didn't find this class too difficult Two take home exams along with a group final project made going to lecture quite useless He also drops your lowest lab and problem set which benefits a vast majority of the. class

Smith is a really nice guy (mediocre lecturer), and very accessible outside of class. The class may seem daunting at first, but with the team of TAs, you can always find help. The class has A LOT of assignments  when something is due, another project is assigned. However, Smith grades very leniently, and if you put in the time, you will do well.

For PubPol majors, take 199 with Jacob! Had no prior coding experience, but have gotten internships because of learning R coding in 199. Jacob is a poli sci nerd, so I would totally recommend Flunching him to get to know his research. The first lectures may seem confusing, but stick with it! Work: 2 exams, 5 HWs, labs  group work, 1 final project
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Jacob Smith is very reachable after class and gives lenient grade for final project. Rubrics are very clear but the lab project (group work) could be hilarious. But definitely recommend taking 199 with Jacob !!!!
I didnt like the projects for this class at all, and they were graded pretty harshly

The content itself isnt hard, but the HW and take-home tests are SUPER time consuming. If you've never coded before, there can be a bit of a learning curve, especially because explantions of things sometimes aren't great. Many group projects so pray you get a good group. Jacob is VERY accesible outside of class and understanding w grace periods

The projects and labs are more time consuming than they are difficult. You have one group that you stick with the whole semester, so if they suck then you're screwed. Professor Smith is very understanding and gave many extensions and grace periods. He was also very accessible outside of class. I think it's a good class to take!

While he definitely could have diversified the statistical applications (every single example was about politics/elections which I found pretty boring), Dr. Smith was a really nice professor and definitely cares about his students.

TBH, did not enjoy this class too much. Super reliant on group work so if you're not a fan don't take this class. Exams took me way longer than they should have. Jacob is super nice, but lectures definitely dragged. One good thing is that he is SUPER fast at responding to emails so if you take this class, reach out for help!!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Good professor who is easily accessible at all times. Class is sometimes difficult, but he'll make sure he sees you through.

Take this class if you have the chance. You'll learn a lot about stats and how to use R. Class is humanities/politics based, but information learned is very practical and applicable knowledge. Two midterms and a final lab based project. Smith is a wonderful professor that cares about his students. Loved this class.
Jacob is very knowledgeable and passionate about Stats, and specifically about elections and election polling. He is very interesting. Definitely get to know him.
Super chill and cares about his students. Lectures not mandatory if you watch videos but he answers a lot of questions. Fair grading.

I would recommend taking any stat class with him. He makes the topic really interesting and is super flexible and accessible. Pick him also if you are interested in political science or public policy.
He is genuinely so interesting and chill and knows everything about American politics. He made statistics seem so relevant and I enjoyed his class so much that I'm taking Stat 210 next semester!

Dr. Smith is genuinely a great professor; I think my lackluster performance was partially because of the amount of effort I put into the class. The amount of effort you put in is the amount that you'll get back. He's super accessible outside of class and gives great feedback. He's also INCREDIBLY knowledgeable on American politics! Great professor
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr. Smith has impressive knowledge of US politics, especially about Congress. As an international student, I was worried I wouldn't be able to keep up, and though the other students were definitely more passionate about the subject than I was, Dr. Smith helped me do well. I learned a lot about Political Science and writing.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Great guy! He knows everything there is to know about American politics. Class was very chill, but be sure to participate. He gave great feedback on essays. Take this class if you can for Writing101!

Really knowledgable guy he knows just about every random political fact from the past 20 years. Class is super chill. Overall, he's a fun professor and is a very easy grader. Definitely take his writing class if you're interested in politics/public policy.
Great professor, he's super chill and tries to keep class entertaining. Also knows everything there is to know about American politics. I wish he taught more classes, I'd def take his class again.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment:
Physics 465 is part of a two semester course on graduate quantum mechanics. These are the main problems I have had

- Lack of lecture notes
- Not very knowledgeable outside her immediate research - couldn't answer many of my answers that were quantum related
- Not transparent about curves or grades
- Prof goes off course easily in lecture
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: My favorite physics class I have taken at Duke. This class is really difficult but also really worth it.

I have to say that her logic is not quite clear sometimes; yes she is following her schedule, but most of the time we are just confused about how she just jumped from one subject to another. Also: Tons of homework! Tons of stuff that isn't covered in textbooks! If you want to get easy grades then this professor is not your choice.
Exceptional and brilliant teacher. Typically what you would expect from a Particle phenomenologist for sure!

She's tough, and her tests are some of the hardest in the department. You've got to work for it and prioritize the class because of how many assignments there are. If you don't have the math background, you will be lost in her explanations. She's very helpful, nonjudgmental, and encouraging in office hours.

The class is flipped, so there are very few lectures, and even when there is one it's very confusing. You basically have to go in to office hours to get a good explanation, but when you do Professor Springer will spend as much time answering questions as you need. Basically she's awesome if you put in the effort to go in and see her.

This class is pretty much all problem solving instead of lectures now. The exams are difficult, and Springer is a bit prone to unnecessarily advanced derivations. But she's very enthusiastic about the material and very equipped to answer questions. It's like you have to exert a bit of effort to get her to be a good professor but then she's great.

No lecture, all information is supposed to be learned from a terribly worded book. She is useless at explaining. Does not even have personal office hours. Makes exams terribly hard. Forces you to go to a useless lecture. Terrible introduction to physics. My recommendation is to take 151 then 162.

Biggest headache of my freshman year. Her lectures are laden with derivations consisting of advanced mathematics (calc 2, multivariable, and linear algebra concepts). Her tests were ridiculously difficult, and the exam was a nightmare. Professor Springer is not suited for teaching introductory physics.

Not a great lecture but her tests were reasonable if you knew the material really well. Tons of out of class work required but if interested in physics it is stimulating. If you need help do ask her as she spends considerable time outside of class with questions and concerns. Honestly she expects too much out of her students for intro physics.
Class was as impossible as it is for an electron to absorb or emit a photon... ironically I have no clue why that is.

Professor Springer expects too much. She gives about 30 problems a week for homework which takes 2-3 hours, IF you know exactly what you are doing, and it i. Her grading is very unclear. The entire semester, she told us not to worry about grades because our final would be waited heavily. Then she gave an unreasonable final.
Highly Recommended
Not good at explaining/communicating concepts. Her lectures were hard to follow. Difficult class and then weekly problem sets take a long time to do. The textbook is sort of useless.
Dean Sue is the GOAT. Take any class you can with her. Wicked smart woman.

Words cannot describe how incredible Dean Sue is. The best Professor. The best class. Dean Sue is the GOAT. Find a way to take a class (or ten) with her while you are at Duke. She has been at Duke for over 50 years, and is so knowledgeable, caring, and kind.

Easily one of the best classes I've taken. Dean Sue is very caring and supportive of her students. She just takes the time to invest in personal relationships with the class. The assignments and major project are great experiences, but can require a good bit of effort. Any student interested in law or education administration should take EDUC 333.

Dean Sue is amazing! Her class is super manageable and she says at the start of the semester that she wants the class to be easy. She doesn't really grade off of the assignments, more about the effort you put into the class throughout the semester. I think everyone got As. Would definitely take another class with her.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Wasiolek was amazing. She cares a lot about her students and makes her class a community. As long as you turned in the assignments you got an A in the class. There wasn't any mandatory homework or tests. The class was a great way to meet people and get close with a professor!

Heard that she's leaving Duke but the most amazing professor I've ever had. Brought so many interesting guest speakers that truly inspired me to pursue Education beyond this intro course. Would take this a thousand more times if I could

Sue is the most thoughtful and caring professor I have ever had. She is passionate about law, education, and getting to know her students. Take this class because you won't regret it!! There is a fair amount of reading and writing but she is a very kind grader. Her feedback is beyond valuable. I cannot emphasize how much she taught me.

this class is only offered occasionally, but i would recommend it when it is. it checks off a lot of T-Reqs, and it is not that difficult. there are a lot of readings and heavy writing (but it is a R and W credit). the content is very interesting and engaging and i don't think there are other simple undergrad law classes like this.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: One of the most incredible professors (Focus). Learned so much that was extremely applicable to the medical field regarding ethics, patient rights, and the history of human research. Incredibly important to participate in class (graded), read (pop quiz), and listen to what she repeats in lecture because it will be tested. Preparedness is key.

Haga is a great professor but definitely be waring of this FOCUS class. It's the hardest one and there is a lot of intense science reading required. The weekly quizzes aren't so hard but her grading criteria is not clear at all so you could score a 50%. It's not hard to do well though, just study slides and participate a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Amazing professor, this is definitely one of the harder FOCUS classes, but all of the quizzes follow the lecture so as long as tou pay attention you'll do well. I'd recommend to reach out for office hours even if you're not struggling because she's an amazing person!!
