Very knowledgable about the content, which I thought had many real-world applications. There is a good amount of work for a FOCUS class, and she grades participation relatively hard. However, she is easily accessible and very approachable. I would definitely recommend this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Haga is my favorite professor I have ever had at Duke. Her classes are hard, but the best and most applicable. She is so knowledgeable about genomics and knows all the newest technologies, and such an interesting person and lecturer. She is also a really cool person and very accessible out of class, despite being so busy.

Dr. Haga is very intimidating at first but she's a great professor and is clearly knowledgeable about her field. This class was incredibly interesting, but she had 2 midterms, a final paper, a final, and 4 group projects throughout the semester, which is definitely more work than most FOCUS classes, but they are all doable. Her lectures were great!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Loved Professor Haga - super sweet when you actually get to know her and super knowledgeable. Definitely one of the hardest focus classes, but you get a lot out of it if you put in the work. Lecture heavy and tests were hard, but do the readings and Dr. Haga is always happy to help if you have questions. Oh and make sure to participate!!

Professor Haga is extremely knowledgeable in her field, and loves to give advice to students seeking research opportunities at Duke. This course is primarily taught through a series of lectures, small group assignments, and class discussions. The exams and term paper are not too difficult, just follow lecture notes and the main ideas in readings.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Prof Haga is a captivating lecturer, but the material in this course was very repetitive. The exams were very fair, but she was a very tough grader on the first one. She's a very harsh grader on participation, so make sure to talk lots each class. LOTS of group projects. Loved writing the final paper. Not hard to get an A if you put in the work.

Took Prof. Haga for one of my FOCUS classes and FLUNCHed her at the end of the semester. Wonderful person, very clear lectures, but somewhat inconsistent grading on participation. Tests are easy if you study the important ethical documents and are clear with your explanations. Overall, enjoyed the class and content.

Prof Haga is truly a cool person! Your performance in the class will improve by attending office hours as thoughtful participation is essential. Readings discussed in class are the only ones that matter - usually at beginning of unit. Tests can be difficult because it's only short answer, but just know key readings and lecture points.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: When it comes to Professor Haga, you can tell she loves what she teaches. When it come to her actually teaching, be prepared: boring lectures where participation is mandatory, but what counts as participation is unclear and subjective; reading (rarely useful and not entirely needed); and contradicting stances causing the confusion of some students.

Good but lengthy lectures. Posts the slides beforehand. Lots of readings but pay attention to ones mentioned in class-they show up on the midterms. Midterms are manageable-study the slides. She grades participation a bit unfairly-do your best to talk when possible. Gave us a final paper & a final exam. Start on the paper early and ask her for help.

Prof Haga may seem intimidating at first but is a really nice person and cares a lot about her students. She has a really impressive background and is highly experienced in her field. I feel like I learned a lot in class. She is always happy to answer any questions and to meet with you after or outside of class to help in any way she can.

I took Dr. Haga's focus class. Focus classes are generally pretty easy, but not with her. She gives out multiple exams and lots of work. I had to work very hard for the A- I got meanwhile my other focus class has minimal work and no exams. And the end fo the day I learned a lot from her though and found her lectures interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She may appear intimidating, but is actually nice when you talk to her and she really knows her stuff. I've taken 2 of her classes and they were both quite hard - definitely one of the tougher ones i've done in college - and during lectures she stands in front and talks without much interaction. But her classes are interesting and worth taking.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Haga is an amazing person, and for much of the class, there's not much you need to do in order to get an A. However, she is a tough grader on her midterms and papers, which take a heavy toll. She also grades things sporadically. An answer from one person will get a different grade than the same answer from another.

Completely espouses the new wave humanity style of teaching where you have many meaningless little busy work assignments—like make a social media page for a Jane Austen character—distracting from doing the readings well and writing quality essays. Did not intellectually challenge me. Wish she taught this course in a more traditional manner.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. Sussman is an incredible professor. She's very thoughtful and relatable. She values students' ideas greatly, lets students take the lead in class, and is very understanding when giving and spacing assignments. Very accessible outside of class and gives thoughtful feedback on papers if you seek her out.

Fair enough grading and encouraging during in-class discussions. However, unhelpful in terms of feedback for papers and lack of clear communication of what she expects in the writing. My greatest frustration was that she would NEVER post grades in a timely manner, if at all. I have been waiting for my finals grade for 3 weeks now.

This British Lit class was intellectually stimulating and SO interesting. Sussman is clearly passionate about the subject and loves to think through different ideas with students. We read books at a fast pace, but you definitely don't have to finish every single novel. The three papers were mainly graded by the TA and were not too difficult.

Professor Sussman is extremely nice and mostly a fair grader. She's very open-minded and eager to meet with students concerning papers. There's a good bit of reading and discussion participation is a must. Overall great Professor!

Jane Austen course: I came in with high hopes and walked away disappointed.  She's nice, but wasn't as enthsiastic about Austen as the class was. Lots of writing. I loved all of the reading, but the weekly responses were tedious and she gave unhelpful feedback with low grades.  However, if you show effort on the final papers you should do fine.

This class has compelled me to write my first review. Professor Wynn is an arbitrary grader, focuses on memorization instead of learning, assigns entirely too much busy work and exams are too lengthy. Do not take if you want to learn about the (public) education system or become a better writer or researcher. Worst class I've taken at Duke.

Professor Wynn is a caring professor, but there are numerous readings to cover. Her exams are pretty challenging, but the actual papers and group projects have clear guidelines, making them much more manageable. Relied a lot on class discussions, but if everyone has read, they go by quickly. One of the better classes I've taken at Duke.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Wynn is an amazingly caring individual who is clearly passionate about what she teaches. She relies quite a bit on in-class discussion, however she does a wonderful job at facilitating. All text is provided. Has quizzes when it's obvious nobody did the readings, which can sometimes be a lot. Aside from this, one of my favorite classes!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Caring

reviews.comment: Wonderful professor who deeply cares about her students' well-being. Some of the assignments did feel excessive and the pop quizzes were a bit of a hassle, but I enjoyed the class discussions and learned about a variety of topics around education in the US.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Caring

reviews.comment: She's a lovely lady but her grading is arbitrary. I took EDUC243S because I thought it would be an easy, exciting class with many discussions. Instead, it entailed difficult readings, long exams that ask remarkably specific questions, and paper after paper. Literally just don't take this class, it was in the Top 2 worst classes I've taken at duke.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: don't enroll in this course. She makes a supposed easy a class very challenging. it is so memorization based. will not recommend if you are looking for an easy or interesting class. it is so so so boring. almost fell asleep every class. bring 5 cups of coffees if you want to make it through

Horrible professor.  worst class i have ever taken .do not take this unless you want to be in hell. readings are literally way too long and way too much work due every single class. do not take this class. take another class if you are looking for an easy seminar

Dr. Wynn is a very caring and understanding professor. She gave break days when the university took them all away. There is a lot of reading and a quite lengthy final paper, but it's doable. As long as you put in effort, you will get a good grade.

Professor Wynn loves students that care about education and even though she shares her own opinion in class she is very respecting of other points of view. She really cares about making the course the best experience possible and is very receptive to feedback. She constantly asks students what theyd like her to keep and change about the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Wynn genuinely cares and listens to her students' needs. She does assign a significant amount of reading but is lenient if the class is engaging in lively discussions. Several papers that were quite lengthy but lots of freedom to choose topics and grading was not too harsh. Overall Dr. Wynn tries to make class fun and engaging.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Caring--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Dr. Wynn is a knowledgeable professor and knows a lot about education. She is great one-on-one! Beware of her pop quizzes. She dislikes students who do not pay attention or who obviously do not do the readings. Put in effort to this class and it should be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Well respected, knowledgeable teacher, but somewhat hostile to new opinions and gave a lot of reading/papers/presentations. Don't expect to blow off her class
Great teacher, great discussions, very engaging, and always willing to help. There's a lot of writing, but it's enjoyable.

Very clear in her teaching.  However, she can be very opinionated and unaccepting of others' opinions.  If you want to take a class in the Education department, she's a good professor to take from.  However, all classes in the education department are essentially the exact same classes.
Smart, enthusiastic, and so sweet. Pretty easy grader, but everything is super interesting. love love love her.
SO nice! great teacher, good class...pretty easy if you do the work.
She is an outstanding teacher!  Her passion for the subject is remarkable!

Prof Svetlova is legitimately the sweetest woman I've ever met. The class discussions are interesting, and she always makes an effort to ensure everyone's voice is heard. There are a decent amount of readings, but they're not difficult to understand as long as you dedicate time for them. Take ANY class that she offers!

Prof Svetlova is one of the most inspiring and approachable profs I've had. I ended up taking 2 classes with her. She cares about about every student and wants you to succeed. PSY335 largely focuses on children and there are a lot of readings both on theory and on experiments. If you have any interest in children or psych/ethics, take this class!

Dr. Svetlova is one of the most caring professors you will ever meet. If you put forth the effort, you will do well in this class. She is harsh on those who miss class and skip blog posts, so be sure to stay on her good side and this class can be an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: While I am sure Sylvie is a great researcher, she simply isn't qualified to teach. Her notes are useless and the homework she assigns has nothing to do with test questions. Even if you work hard to understand what she teaches, it's almost impossible to do so without relearning everything outside class. Avoid her if you can.

She was kind of a frustrating professor as she wasn't the best at explaining things but she was available to answer questions after class and in office hours. You can usually get away with not going to class if you do the work on your own. Towards the end, though, she seemed annoyed at the class because no one showed up. Coincidentally (or not?) our final was rather hard compared to the actual class.

There were typos in every powerpoint.  When someone asked a question, she often was unable to give a sufficient answer.  Sometimes it was because she misunderstood the question, and sometimes it was because she got herself confused.  I would not recommend this professor to anyone.

Sylvie is a GOOD teacher, regardless of what the others say.If you do all of the homework and just make sure you UNDERSTAND how to do the hardest problems, you will do just fine on the tests. She makes the tests tricky because she does not want this class to be a joke.(Something I am thankful for) Just do the work, ask questions, and you'll be fine
She seemed to take 0 interest in the class the entire semester, which ended with her showing up late for the final. I am embarrassed for her.

I would love to plot everyone's GPA in other classes vs. grade in this class. Sylvie gave a final with 12ish questions. One was worth 20% of the exam, and it wasn't statistics. It was a lot of algebra. Halfway through the final she informed us we would not be allowed all 3 hours. Not sure if that's even allowed...I agree with the last guy, take 113

Apparently Sylvie did not want previous comments to be seen but course evaluations will reveal the truth. Sylvie put hardly any effort into the class and was aware of this, asking if students gave her a "D or F" on evaluations form and laughing. Test averages were extremely low because of poor instruction. Stay away from this professor.

Uh, I dont know what everyone is complaining about.  Econometrics isn't an easy class, but he is a fair grader and he uploads all of his slides online so attendance isn't mandatory.  He isn't a very engaging lecturer but this is econometrics, not an erotic novel - it's hard to make it interesting.
Econ 139 is fascinating class. Too bad he is a terrible teacher. Totally unclear. Worthless to take the class with him. He definitely didn't want to teach econometrics.

One of the worst teachers at this university. His grading is totally random -- if you ever do badly on an exam, you have no chance to recover. Painful class to sit though. It's better to study on your own and just do the compendium.

The digital storytelling class and Professor Szabo were very intriguing and chill. Classes mainly consisted of discussions around readings each week, as well as several interactive activities with unique forms of media. Classes were engaging and fun; however, some readings did feel unnecessarily heavy. Grades aren't really something to worry about.

I had her as a FOCUS teacher this semester and really enjoyed her class. She keeps things engaging and fun while also leading important discussions. She is super friendly and caring as well. We were mostly graded for participation, though there were lots of readings that I felt were busywork rather than necessary. But overall still would recommend!
Hard to believe this was a course for credit at an elite university. I learned very little that I did not know by the age of 14.
[ ISS187 Digital Storytelling ] Extremely adept at facilitating discussions. Readings were sometimes long and dry, but the content was really interesting. Fun in-class activities.

Class is pretty straight forward. Professor Szabo will help you but likes if you try it out yourself first. Go to office hours. Lectures are boring but labs make the time go by faster. Take this class if you're interested in web design and learning coding.

Super nice and makes an effort to know everyone. A bit of reading and lots of writing memos, but detailed feedback is given. I love how Katzenstein explained the critiques of everything we learned too, very open minded and gives the opportunity to share what you think. No concern about grades due to pass/fail system and low grades getting dropped.

Suzanne pays her efforts to make a 75-person lecture engaging. Yet, the lecture is a bit short on depth. (It's a intro class; I can't complain much.) She's a wonderful person, and your memo would improve through this class. The quizzes are a bit annoying, but you won't even need to finish the reading to get a full score.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor K is a fantastic person and will care for you as a student as long as you put in the work to get to know her. She is very approachable and encourages students to attend office hours. Class is extremely reading and memo-writing-heavy.

Professor Katzenstein did a great job providing a solid introduction to public policy. She gave us plenty of chances to learn and practice fundamental skills like CBA and memo writing, while also delving into a bit of political theory. She is a good lecturer, explains concepts clearly, and is a great communicator overall. She's super nice too!

Katz is incredibly sweet, but not the right professor for 155. She's a fairly unengaging lecturer and is clearly out of her depth in such a large class. Makes a genuine effort to get to know her students. 155 with her was boring, but super easy to pass. Don't let 155 define the Pubpol major.

This class was extremely long and boring. I hated the weekly quizzes and the flipped class style, but I loved my group. Kat is a nice person and lecturer, but I only took 155 because it was P/F. I learned a lot of interesting things, I just wished it wasn't a flipped classroom. This might be my last Pub Pol class, but I'm glad I got to test it out.

Love her. This class is not as boring as people make it out to be. There can be heavy reading weeks, but it's no big deal to skip out. Daily reading quizzes are occasionally challenging, but passing this class is no concern. Lots of opportunities for extra credit, re-writes, completion grades, etc.

Professor Katzenstein is super kind and approachable. The lectures were a bit boring and the content at times felt very vague along with the reading. But weekly quizzes are easy if you understand the general concepts. Memos are straight forward. Discussion sections were a bit useless but easy class with a great prof.
Professor K is genuinely so caring, thoughtful, and an amazing professor. I am so lucky to have learned from her.

Super kind and willing to get to know students. Really cares about her work. The class' structure is a little bit boring, but think that just has to do with the makeup of PubPol 155. Loved Professor Katzenstein and hope to take a course with her in the future.

It's pass/fail, so very little stress and not much incentive to stay engaged. Memos are important, so put your best effort into them. Instructor just plows through 60-70 slides per lecture by reading off of them verbatim without meaningful discussion. That being said, Katz is one of the kindest and most caring professors you will encounter at Duke.
Katzenstein is great. Very animated lecturer, very clear guidelines. She's great.

Professor Katzenstein is the kindest and most genuine teacher I've had. She is so knowledgeable and intentional about everything she does. This course made me certain about my intent to be a Public Policy Major. Could not recommend more!

Professor Katzenstein is an excellent professor who truly cares about her students in a meaningful way. She makes lectures engaging and is a very fair grader. She's very engaged in and outside of class and listens to feedback well. Definitely would take her class again!

One of the most kind professors i've met. She is so caring and genuinely puts effort into her students. She ended up learning at least half of the names of the students names in our roughly 100 person lecture. She's awesome!

155 is a super boring but easy pass/fail class with lots of teamwork and small readings. Prof. Katzenstein cares a lot about her students and is very empathetic. If you are pub pol you have to take this class, and I would recommend taking it with her if you can. She provides a lot of extra credit opportunities as well!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Group projects

reviews.comment: There are 4 memos in total, and assigned readings (not that many) every week that come with quizzes. Prof. Katzenstein is really understanding and cares about engagement and participation. There isn't a lot of homework and it's an easy pass/fail class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: thought i like pub pol until this class. i hate the repetitive flipped class structure. it felt like i was as getting informed regurgitated back to me. so much reading, 2 quizzes/week. it was boring although katzenstein is a great lecturer i just did not like the structure of 155 at all.

Prof. Katz is a great teacher that encourages learning and participation, while doing a great job of teaching and promoting growth. There was a quiz a week that was based on reading, but not overwhelming at all. I recommend this class to anyone who is interested in policy and wants to further their understanding.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: 155 is a pass/fail class that is very easy to pass. Because of this, Professor Katz encouraged us to simply focus on learning and being satisfied with our best effort rather than constantly striving for perfection. She clearly cares about her students and our mental/physical health. Lectures were interesting and she fostered good conversations.

Professor Katzenstein is a great person! Her class is very relevant to Public Policy and pass/fail, so as long as you have a 70% or higher, you are golden. The only thing I will critique is that the team and individual readiness assessments are pretty difficult, even if you read the material throughly. There is also a lot of reading for each week.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Professor Katzenstein is the kindest professor at Duke. That being said, she sometimes goes too easy on students and can be easy to disengage with - but Pubpol 155 is getting a makeover so it will be far more interesting. If you need anything outside of class, she's always there and is so genuine.

Honestly, this class was not that hard I just think big lectures are unengaging. If you participate you are totally fine she likes that. Also this is all formatted around memos and they are not that bad you are allowed to do revisions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: This class is awful. It made me reconsider being a PubPol major. Prof Katzenstein is completely inflexible, unclear, and a boring lecturer. The class is pass fail, but if it wasn't I wouldn't even found it tolerable. There are quizzes every Tuesday for reading on super obscure questions, memos that are arbitrarily graded by Task, and tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Prof Katzenstein is a good professor who definitely really cares about her students, and makes an effort to create a good, friendly classroom environment. That being said, she is a really tough grader with inconsistent expectations, and I felt like sometimes she was creating extra, unnecessary work. She is definitely a bit of a hardo but cares.

I cannot say enough good things about Prof. Katzenstein. She is one of the most understanding, caring, and empathetic professors I've ever had, and she makes such an effort to incorporate student feedback into her class. Definitely one of my all time favorite professors at Duke, and I would highly highly recommend taking any class with her.

She is a fantastic professor who really cares about the material she is teaching. Women as Leaders was an amazing class, and the discussions were always really interesting. The project was confusing at times, but if you put effort in she will reward you for it. Talk to her about your paper in advance and she'll really help.

Business & Human Rights has been one of my favorite classes. SK puts an incredible amount of time into getting to know her students, giving detailed feedback, and finding readings/project topics that were both interesting and meaningful. It was amazing to learn from a professor w/ so much experience & knowledge in the human & business rights space.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: One of the best classes that I have taken at Duke. The readings were engaging and never extraneous. The discussions were energetic and interesting. Katzenstein was always helpful outside of class. The final project helped me develop valuable analytical skills. While the class challenged me, I am a better student and thinker after having taken it.

Women as Leaders with Professor Katzenstein is probably the best class Ive taken at Duke. Katzenstein fostered an incredible community of students that allowed for open dialogue. It is rare and telling for a prof to be flexible and vulnerable and Katzensteins willingness to be both helped us allow to engage with the material in a meaningful way

Professor Katzenstein is by far one of my favorite professors at Duke. I've taken two courses, Human Rights and World Politics and Women as Leaders, with her. She is passionate about what she teaches, compassionate, and great at facilitating discussion. Both classes had a good amount of reading and assignments, but they are always interesting.

Professor Katzenstein is probably one of the best professors I will have at Duke. Her class Women as Leaders was an amazing course. the discussions and readings were great and her guidance in discussions created a great seminar environment, as she always made sure there was space for students to share thoughts and the discussions taught me so much

Professor Katzenstein is a rare professor who is very real and down-to-earth. She is tough because she genuinely wants students to improve as writers & critical thinkers. She gives amazing life advice if you put effort into getting to know her. Also, her class is taught through a law perspective which is a bonus if you are considering that path!
She was a very passionate professor and she really cares about her students. You have to work hard to succeed in her class, but you get in what you put in. Take a class with her if possible!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I absolutely loved Professors Katzensteins class. The second two portions of the class are particularly fascinating. It was very discussion heavy but I always felt they were productive and easy to participate in. The essays are graded somewhat harshly and there is a fair amount of reading but overall the class was worth it for sure.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Katzenstein is extremely knowledgeable on the topic of Business and Human Rights and wants students to really understand the material. She is accessible outside of the classroom and sets clear expectations for the assignments. The course exposed me to a field I was unfamiliar with and topics that felt relevant to my life!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: I've taken a lot of great classes at Duke, but BHR with Professor Katzenstein is undoubtedly at the top of my list of favorites. She expects a lot from her students, but she gives a lot in return. Class discussion is SUPER important, but she does a fantastic job of fostering a classroom environment that is both challenging and comfortable.

Professor Katzenstein has an amazing amount of knowledge in the field of human rights, law, advocacy and ethics. She is always willing to help students figure out what they care about within and beyond the classroom. Her standards remain high, but it feels really good when you are able to meet them. You'll have a lot of fun along the way.

"Business and Human Rights" was such a great course. Prof. Katzenstein's knowledge and research into how rights work transnationally is so useful, and she is extremely helpful if you talk to her and are interested in learning about NGO and legal work. The class's lab work and the memos which we learned to write also taught me a ton.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: SK is incredibly respected & a nice lady--she is super accommodating if you need help, especially if you had a problem or if english isn't your first language. that said though the criticism that the discussions are disjointed and dry is valid. sometimes the class seems pointless and the readings don't follow each other well & are poorly integrated
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Prof. Katzenstein cares deeply about her students, and is always accommodating and helpful. While this class was more work than average, the assignments were interesting and prepared us for useful in-class activities (e.g. role-playing case studies, policy briefs for actual nonprofits, etc.). Overall, Prof. Katzenstein is an excellent professor!

Katzenstein knows a lot about the human rights regime, and the topics we covered were interesting, but class discussions didn't always flow very well.  Some people would say things that were not really relevant to the topic/not make sense and that was never addressed.  Also, we never took the conversation very deep in class
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: If you want to be drowned in work, then take this class. Yes, she is very knowledgeable about human rights but made such an interesting topic extremely boring. Do not take this class unless you want to spend hours and days writing papers.

Professor Katzensein is one of my favorite teachers at Duke. She is brilliant and knows so much about human rights. She gives a lot of readings but they are all interesting and relevant. Participation is necessary, and the class conversations are always around good themes. She gives good feedback on papers but is a tough grader.

Professor Katzenstein is a wonderful teacher with high standards. She is a tough grader, but she is very helpful in one-on-one meetings and gives good feedback. She is extremely knowledgeable on human rights, and participation is essential in her class.

Professor Katzenstein is extremely knowledgable, and I learned a ton about the human rights regime through her course. The conversation didn't always flow too well in class though, as people seemed to just throw out opinions instead of responding to someone else. Overall, it was worth taking, and Professor Katzenstein is very accessible.

Professor Katzenstein is a fantastic, clear teacher who is incredibly fair and caring to her students.  Her lectures can run a little dry, but overall this class is a great one and I would definitely recommend it.

Here's a general overview of Katzenstein: she's a remarkably intelligent woman who loves what she teaches. However, she domineers the conversation in a way that made my seminar feel awkwardly rigid. She can also be very confusing when explaining assignments. Fair grader though, and the class isn't that much work (minus the long readings)

Professor Katzenstein is one of my favorite professors at Duke thus far. She is such an intelligent and incredible person who really knows her stuff. I would like to take one of her classes again in the future.

Subjective and tough grader. Refuses to answer emails. Mostly group projects. Takes multiple weeks to grade projects because he's “busy” even though all he did was post prerecorded videos all semester. His class made me consider leaving Duke.

All reviews are true. He focuses on participation, u have to ask/ans questions a lot. 564 relies on Apple guides, with TAs creating all demos. The presentation rubrics, focusing on all non-tech issues eg. grammar, seems nonsensical. "Show me a UI with more colors and graphics" indicating he cannot see tech under it. He is a business mgr, not tech.

The topic can be challenging, expects fast ramp-up speed, but overall I think Prof. Telford is nice and knowledgeable on software engineering. Sometimes can be a bit hard to deal with as he marks you late 1-2 mins after class starts. Mandatory attendance & multiple-choice midterm exam, but he offers many EC options if you ask/answer questions.

Didn't really learn anything in this class that I couldn't have just googled. Professor Telford's lectures are very dry and have required attendance. The lectures cover random topics and don't cover important mobile development programming patterns in a clear structured way.  Midterm/final is also a waste, given that it is a programming class.

Real tough grader, he giving presentation grades based on his biased personal preference and never show us the standard grading criteria, which makes impossibly to improve the grades as the personal preference won't change the whole semester. B or B+ even you get full mark in final. Almost same content with much worse quality compare to MEng 540.

His behavior made nonsense sometimes. Firstly, his marking rubric is vague. They could not even tell why they deducted marks. Secondly, his course is full of presentations. Thirdly, his homework load is heavy with a lot of reading.  Lastly, RAISING HANDS TO ANSWER QUESTIONS IS REQUIRED.DON'T APPLY MENG DEGREE AT DUKE. Because MENG 570 is required
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: This management class is quite boring, but the grading is always hard. Giving some unclear instructions sometimes. I think this class is overlapping with another engineering class 540 and am not sure why both are required classes.

Ric was well-prepared for each class and helpful.  Expect to be putting in additional work each week as meeting HW requirements only bags you a B+. Homework builds on the previous week's. Project is significant chunk of the grade, so make sure to pick teammates wisely.  No curve in the class and no extra credit, but possible to do well.

Ric is the most punctual professor at Duke. Assignments are graded a day after submission, Piazza is answered within 30 minutes even at midnight on Sunday. The huge downside to his class is, in his words, "if you do my assignment you get a B." In order to get an A, you have to impress him, leading to excessive stress the whole semester

Teitsworth is a kind and enthusiastic prof who is helpful in office hours. I took his class as an easy NS and got the grade I wanted. However, most students found the lecture material a bit more technical and difficult than expected. It works out though since the HW and midterm are easy, and the paper and final presentation are graded leniently.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Teitsworth was one of my favorite professors at Duke. He has a wide breadth of knowledge in physics, and the sciences in general, and he's an all around great guy. He was very helpful with homework assignments, and every lecture was extremely interesting. I would definitely recommend taking his class.

I really liked his lectures  he was very caring, understanding, engaging and clear. I thought the class was interesting, but I expected it to be more technical. Rather than that, it was just an overall qualitative analysis of mostly things I already knew. Nevertheless, I would definitely have him again as my professor for any Physics courses!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: I wanted to learn about the technical aspects of energy issues, but most of it was pretty poorly explained. Take ENV231 (Energy & Environment) - it's a much better course and you'll learn way more. The class is super easy; he's very lax about attendance, basically all lectures and easy problem sets with a simple final presentation.
Extremely fair and understanding grader. Engaging lecture. Somewhat heavy reading assigned. Qualitative over quantitative.

Great professor. Interesting guy, cares about getting to know his students. Class was great, grading was lenient. He cares more about you understanding things than actually getting the correct calculated answers. Highly recommend.

Professor Teitsworth is one of the best pre-med professors out there. Fair tests that are not too complicated and based on weekly recitation quizzes, which test your basic understanding of the big picture concepts. Not nitpicky or crazy like other pre-med profs. Very enthusiastic and just plain likeable guy.

Explained stuff well when you had questions, and also took an interest in how individuals were doing. Sometimes he overcomplicated things and did scary proofs but also offered a new way of looking at some difficult material.

Absolutely amazing. Material presented beautifully, in the correct depth for first-years. VERY approachable/helpful and is willing to discuss more depth on advanced topics if interested. Tests and quizzes are simple and super straightforward. By far, my best professor. If I weren't in engineering, I'd switch into a physics major because of him.
Great Professor. Be prepared to be blown away by all his derivations but his tests are very straightforward. Definitely knows his stuff. Very helpful. Very approachable.

Wonderful teacher. Keeps everything simple when asking you for answers. Really wants his students to do well. Sometimes tries to derive too much stuff, but overall he makes sure you get the material. Definitely a teacher to take a class with.

I took this class last spring, and it was my best class by far.  He loves the material, and his lectures are interesting and energetic, though the derivations are hard. He really wants his students to do well.  It also helps that he knows the material perfectly, and can explain it to you without a problem.  Overall just a great teacher, take him!

Definetly my best professor so far.  Really knows his stuff, and loves it so much that he can't help but smile at the subject matter as he lectures.  Invites his students out for lunch to get to know them.  Drops your lowest homework and quizz grades.  I really can't imagine a better professor, and would take another of his classes in a heartbeat.

Absolutely brilliant man does a respectable job of clearly articulating a very complex subject to a class of first-year students, a task I think many genius professors often find difficult.  Very enthusiastic teacher & willing to meet outside of class for add'l help.  Material is way harder than straightforward quizzes, lab, etc often reflect.

I agree with below, but given it is an introductory physics class, he didn't expect us to know the derivations in-depth. Even if he did expect us to derive it on a quiz/exam, he'll have formulas on a formula sheet to help you. He's very helpful and friendly during office hours; even asked me about good places on campus to get lunch.

There was very little direct instruction from the professor. I found it difficult to get guidance when I needed it, and the classroom dynamic didn't make it easy to ask questions. The class itself is interesting, but expect to figure most things out on your own. Tantum wasn't very engaged with her students.

Overall easy A, good intro to a lot of basic ML algorithms. She is really good in her lectures at simplifying the math you need to know and explains it very clearly! Ethics cases were easy points. Only complaint: for A+ you have to do more work than required, making the margin of error for A/4.0 very small - just don't submit late and get penalized

This class has no place in ML curriculum. It doesn't cover more probability knowledge than MATH 230, and doesn't actually teach ML properly. I suggest everyone to take CS 671 to avoid ECE 580, and tell ECE department to provide replacements for this class. The professor attempts to abstract all the math into stories, which leads to more confusion.

I spent lecture trying to figure out whether she made mistakes in derivations. Concepts were occasionally defined in an unclear way and technical terms were used imprecisely. HW and quizzes (quizzes were easy) didn't correspond well to lectures, which was Math 230+218 but dumbed down. HW and the final project helped me improve my python skills.

Professor Tantum is a nice person but the class is just not the best. 8/30 of the lectures were used for these discussions about ethics which could have been interesting but were often about trivial topics (Tennis Replay systems) or watered down by unnecessarily long reflection prompts. Didn't feel that I learned as much about ML as I hoped.

Not a good professor in that she didn't really teach much. The class is design-based, but her feedback wasn't really helpful. She graded things much more harshly than they needed to be and often failed entire assigments  for minor errors. Wasn't very flexible or understanding.

Her machine learning sequence does not teach machine learning. I learned to use Latex, formatting nice documents, and ChatGPT, and how to write word salad in the class. Eight lectures are for discussions on useless things in ethics. The class wasted a year of my life. She puts equations on slides and spends 5 minutes taking the derivative.

Professor Tantum is overall a good professor. I enjoyed ECE480 and would definitely take it again. The lectures were okay but sometimes got very bogged down in theoretical math which contrasted with the application-heavy homework sets.

Dr. Tantum's class was arguably too easy. The first half of the class was review from Math 230. Very little homework, and the final project is no sweat. The grading criteria was strange, but in the end, more than half of the class got an A. Tantum's policies are forgiving, and she seems like a nice person - many late penalties were waived.

Honestly worst professor at Duke. RMP doesn't do justice. She deleted 50+ one-star reviews. We had 4 midterms, 3 of which weren't graded until after the final. She posted past exams but refused to give answer keys or help, so what was the point? Going into exams was like a blind man trying to drive a broken-down 1979 toyota camry with 3 flat tires

I took this class Spring 2022 and a litany of bad reviews came in for this class, but most are deleted now, so I want to warn future students--lectures are monotone and powerpoints are not helpful, we didn't get test grades back until 6 weeks later, and while other classes were given an 8 question final with extra credit, ours was extremely tough.

ECE580 is structured extremely poorly (do not recommend taking this course), and I think the class itself may have been more of the issue than Dr. Tantum. That being said, Dr. Tantum's teaching style was not very conducive to success -- she glossed over lots of important things and often sped through all the actually important information.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I decided to take her ECE110 course because past reviews stated that she was a good teacher overall. However, none of those previous comments are accurate of the current state of the class. The class is boring, unclear, fast-paced, and tough. It made me dislike circuits and question my desire to be an engineer. Would not take again.

Her lectures are a bit slow, but really nice and easy grader. Homeworks have unlimited submissions and TAs have a lot of office hours for help, but it is quite a bit of work. A good choice for ECE110 if you want a solid foundation in the topics and are willing to put in work on homeworks.

Okay, yes, this class has a lot of assignments: Usually one and maybe two per week. But they're super well-organized assignments and easy to work through if you A) go to class and B) know how to code. Dr. Tantum is also great at answering questions if you need help. She does rely on the TAs to do grading and the TAs procrastinated in the past.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: Professor Tantum clearly cares about her students; however, her slow pace of lectures was not the right fit for me. I think she is really liked by many students; however, I wish I could have experienced a more direct and energetic class format.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Take Dr. Tantum's class! By far the best ECE 110 professor out there. She truly cares for her students and provides A LOT of resources to help students succeed. She wants her students to learn the material well and has many little tricks to increase retention of the material. Her tests are very reasonable, and she gives partial credit on homework.

Dr. Tantum is an excellent ECE 110 professor! Her lectures aren't the most engaging, but she provides you with lots of resources to succeed (extra homework problems, book readings, lots of examples on the slides worked out in class). She also gives a lot of partial credit on the exams, which is really nice.

Amazing professor, you can't beat Dr. Tantum for ECE 110. Great at explaining tough concepts and tests are very doable. HW problems have posted numerical answers and are very similar to exam problems. Also just super nice and caring. Highly recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Tantum is an overall decent teacher but did not match my learning style (too much lecture/speaking), so HW was much more useful for learning. If you aren't able to focus for a LONG time in a (not very engaging) lecture without getting bored/distracted, it will be tough. However, she is super accessible and helpful outside class if you need help.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This was certainly my hardest class at Duke so far. We were assigned numerous, time-consuming labs, usually having to work on two at a time, and in the end, they counted for very little. The exams (both a race to finish) assessed our knowledge from labs, but we didn't receive over half of these back until AFTER the semester finished.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Data and Decision Science. Supposedly she is good for ECE but I wouldn't take any class with her again. She was rude, condescending and disorganized. After October 1st we didn't get a single graded homework assignment back so preparing for the exams and working on the group projects were difficult. Don't take this class with her, it was frustrating
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Prof. Tantum was irritatingly slow at grading everything and anything. Yes, she is amazing so she takes on so many projects that she doesn't leave any time to actually care for her students in class. Also her lectures always start out stupid easy and build up so fast that by the end you have no idea what is going on. Do not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Caring

reviews.comment: Prof Tantum is fantastic. By far the easiest ECE 110 teacher at Duke, and you will still learn all of the same material as the other sections. Pick Tantum. Her HW is on Sakai and you have unlimited submissions, no partial credit but the instant feedback is a lifesaver for analyzing circuits/keeping up in the class.

Professor Tantum was great. Her office hours are worth going to but it's a small space so go early. Her lectures were fast paced, but they're on power point slides so you can go back and review as needed. Her tests were killer in that I ran out of time to complete it, but there was a plethora of materials to review with. She cares a lot.

For the first half of the course, it's easy to just do the homework right before it's due and get by. For the second half the algebra gets pretty disgusting and tedious and its WAY more important to understand the concepts. Tantum gives a ton of partial credit if you understand the concept and she's awesome during office hours.

I wish I had taken ECE 110 with someone else. Lectures were organized and covered the material really well, but we definitely did not have enough material to practice for tests with. Lecture materials were way easier than the homework, and it got even worse for exams. She was also rude and laughed at students a couple times for their mistakes.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Prof Tantum is amazing. Very thorough. Plenty of resources. Consistent and on time feedback. Really has everything together for the students. Easy A and would definitely take again.

Dr. Tantum was an alright professor.  She was good at teaching the easier concepts but her quality of teaching deteriorated as she got into more advanced topics. I would not try to avoid her at all costs, but if possible would choose another professor from the ECE department.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Tantum is AMAZING!  She cares so much about her students and is a phenomenal lecturer.  I would highly recommend taking the class with her.  She is also phenomenal 1-on-1 so I would highly suggest going to office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Tantum is one of the best profs I've had at Duke--she just really understands the material and is great at explaining it. Her tests are super reflective of the HW so the class average is always pretty high, even though her class isn't based on a curve so you technically aren't competing with your classmates.
This is the worst professor that I have had in my time at Duke. She is not accessible and she is very rude.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: All around amazing professor.  Always helpful and genuinely cares about her students.  Some topics are unclear so I would highly recommend taking advantage of her office hours.

Very clear lecturer and cares a lot that you understand the material. Hard to catch up once you miss a class so go to class. If you don't understand something go to office hours; she is more than willing to help. Does not explain everything in class; you'll need to apply and figure some stuff out on your own but it's a great skill to learn.

Even though attendance isn't mandatory, you should go to class because once you miss one, everything goes downhill. Do the homework, it helps you understand a lot of what's going on in class and to put it in perspective. The Svoboda textbook is only used to assign homework questions, and the other textbook isn't used at all.
Great teacher, but catching up is hard

Dr. Tantum is in the minority of Duke ECE professors who care about their students. She makes every effort to ensure that you understand the material, and is extremely helpful during office hours. The material seems really tough at first, but she helps you break it down into digestible pieces.

Dr.Tantum is by far the best professor I have had at Duke. She is extremely kind and willing to take as much time as needed to help you understand the material. Her lectures are extremely coherent and exams are fair. If you do the hw and attend lectures, you will be fine. If you have to take this course, make sure you get in her section!

Dr.Tantum is hands down the best professor I have had in Pratt. She is extremely kind and always willing to help her students. Her lectures are extremely clear (I only used the textbook for hw assignments). She will schedule times outside of office hours to help you as well. If you have to take this course, get in her section!

Dr. Tantum is the best teacher I have had at Duke. Her explanations are crystal clear, and she is willing to go over even the simplest problems with you at your own pace. Her tests are also very fair and she tries to give you as much partial credit as possible. Take her class!

Dr. Tantum is the nicest professor you'll ever meet. She's really helpful in office hours. Her tests are really straight forward, and she tries to give you as many points as possible. Take ECE 110 with her!
She's great. If you have to take ECE, she's the one to take it with. Her lectures are really useful and she's very helpful if you have any questions.

He is very hard to understand but a nice enough guy. Easy to do well on tests because he tells you exactly what is expected. Also assigns 2-3 homework problems every class that are very annoying to complete.

Very reasonable guy. His lectures are rather incomprehensible, due to his low volume and accent, but he is always in office hours, gives out straightforward exams and labs, and gives you the opportunity to explain your thought processes on exams after grading. Great guy.

You'll find yourself just sitting in the back of class and nodding while he laughs, but he's really hard to understand. If you go to him one on one, though, he's actually extremely helpful, and the exams aren't too difficult.
Teh is the man. Extremely attractive.
No Comments
He's a nice enough guy and he tries to help, but he doesn't speak English very well and he is very hard to understand.

Arguably one of the weirdest and most frustrating classes I've ever taken at Duke (both in terms of grading and logistics), made mostly tolerable by a set of really excellent classmates. The only concrete due date seemed to be that of our final project (see: comment below this), and class discussions turned largely tangential and oddly personal.

We went the entire semester without a single assignment or grade. Granted, it was her first time teaching the class, but she was definitely winging everything. Every class was just discussion about the creative writing projects we were each working on. Tetel is, nevertheless, an engaging and thoughtful teacher.
Dr. Tetel was my favorite professor at Duke. I loved her linguistics class when I took it 25+ years! BDr. Tetel was so passionate and knowledgeable that I remember her and the class quite well.

I was not really interested in this subject at the beginning of the semester, but Dr. Tetel is so passionate about the subject that it sparked my interest. There is weekly homework and reading. It is not hard, just time consuming. The final paper determined our grade in the class, but she gave us plenty of time to work on it and was very helpful.

Great teacher with an obvious passion for her field of study. In the seminar class she allows for tangents and brings about many unique and creative examples. "Textbook" is dry and has yet to be fully published and weekly required homework becomes more of an annoyance than an interest. Long paper due at the end but plenty of time and help to do it.

Very interesting professor who's easy to talk to and get along with, makes the subject material entertaining and relatable. Grade depends on one midterm, one final, and one project, but overall it's not bad. I would take it again
Mostly a discussion-based class with one long final project at the end. Very nice lady, however,  just make sure to participate as much as possible.

Professor Tetel is great-- she's really passionate and is genuinely interested in what students have to say in class. She isn't always clear or organized, but you can always ask her to clarify and she is happy to. Really enjoyed Historical English Linguistics!

I took "Language and Evolution". The class was VERY disorganized, but I ended up learning a bunch of information and had a blast at the same time. She loves her field and exudes enthusiasm, and our class felt more like a family than anything else. Linguistics was not a prereq, and it probably should have been--but she explained what we needed.
best professor i have ever experienced. made focus sooo worthwhile. i had 0 interest in  linguistics but you would be crazy not to take her class! duke is lucky to have her.
Often disorganized. Tetel is a genius but can be hard to understand. Class participation is a must.

Professor Tetel was great in a seminar setting!  She encouraged discussion and we explored a lot of different topics depending on our interests.  The class wasn't too demanding; we did have a lot of reading, but just a final project and paper at the end of the semester.

I made an A in the class.  Yet, even with a whole bunch of hard and useless homework assignments, papers, and take home tests, I learned nothing.  The work is tedious, and Ling 101 should be a mandatory prerequisite.  Excellent writing skills help you get through, but it's painful to do the work and make it sound coherent.  Not worth it.

Do not take unless you have taken intro to linguistics. You will simply not have the knowledge that you need. There is a lot of work, and the TA's grade everything. Tetel does very little, and when she does lecture, she is incredibly spastic and scatter-brained. By no means is this an easy A.

I agree with a lot of what's been said here. Take 101 first. Class is a series of guest lecturers who all teach different things -- there's no continuity, I don't feel like I actually learned anything!  Weekly HW assignments are frustrating, midterm and papers are painstaking. Tetel is one of the most scatterbrained people I've ever met.

Tetel is a great teacher, but this course does not utilize her teaching; it's mainly guest lectures. What makes no sense to me is why Ling 101 is not a prerequisite; most kids are scraping by without the background knowledge. The textbook work (which there is plenty of) expects a pretty solid background in the subject.

More busy work than the class is worth. 3 papers, midterm, final, and horrible weekly homework assignments. Tetel is very enthusiastic, but all the grading is done by TAs. Linguistics 101 should be a prerequisite to this class to have a solid idea of what's going on. If you just do the work, a B will come naturally.

Really interesting class and teacher! However I would recommend not taking it before you've taken 101. The class assumes you know a lot that you probably don't. TAs grade everything, including papers. Needless to say, class is NOT an easy A -- it's a lot of work, with weekly HW assignments, three papers, and a take-home midterm (killer) and final.

Class is a drag with the work, and the assignments all assume you have a solid background in linguistic concepts. Tetel is amazing, but she does not lecture most of the time. Boring paper topics, tedious homework assignments, and horrendously long mid-term. Still, if you put work into this class, you will get a solid grade.

If you're an English major looking for a CTM, this is not it. This class should def have a pre-req, but doesn't. Assumes that you understand linguistic concepts already. Weekly assignments and tests have nothing to do with the lectures, which is annoying and frustrating. Papers are graded by TAs. Tetel was not helpful with problems.

Julie Tetel is an all-around amazing person. A little-known fact is that she is also a published author (of romance novels!) LOW was plus; the midterm was long tho & not on the class material. She only lectures 3 or 4 times all semester, so take a higher-level class with her and get to know her - she is eccentric but brilliant, and a great teacher.

Languages of the World. Pretty easy class, not much work and no need to do the readings. Tetel doesn't teach, the guests come in and lecture. Wish the lectures were more focused on culture/introductory phrases rather than their linguistics because I left knowing little about writing systems. Still, easy and fun.

LOW was generally interesting, but I expected more from it. Tetel rarely lectured; guests did. The class was basically a way for random lang depts to recruit underclassman. Lecturers varied WIDELY in quality, with the best being Cherokee and the worst being Arabic. Many didn't even take the time to speak to us in their lang! Still, easy & fun.

Great profesor. A bit random at times and spastic. But still good! She's pretty vague on paper topics and is very general about explanations, but is great about helping you out if you seek her out individually. She's a great professor overall. She really knows her stuff!
Really cool teacher, and knows a lot about subject. A little vague on paper instructions, but is really helpful as far as e-mail correspondence. Great teacher!

Tetel is amazing.  She's a Dukie herself and her kids all went here.  She jumps around a lot and is kind of spastic, but her knowledge base is very broad and comprehensive and she is extremely intelligent.  Very entertaining and engaging.  Fair grader, though she assigns a ton of reading.

Excellent professor!  Very knowledgeable and so enthusiastic about subject.  Good feedback on papers.  Does go off on tangents, and you will be overwhelmed by the amount of material she spins off the first day of class, but stick with it, and you won't be disappointed.
Was so fun to have!  Passionate about her subject matter, her students, and pilates!
One of the most entertaining professors out there.
No Comments

Very easy and engaging class! Readings are assigned but honestly not required if you have some background knowledge on Asian American narratives. Dr. T is super understanding and always willing to hear and analyze different perspectives. There are weekly discussions and a few major assignments that make up your grade.
If you are Asian and want to learn more about yourself, take this class. Easy class.

Dr. T is very nice and accommodating, and grading is quite fair. Lots of readings, but they were on very interesting topics, and I learned a lot about Asian American history. There are 3 papers throughout the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She makes her lectures engaging and I thought all the readings were very interesting. She is a little harsh when it comes to grading papers, as she takes off a lot of points for small mistakes, but overall I really enjoyed the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Caring

reviews.comment: dr. t is an awesome professor. im not much of a humanities person but asian american narratives was a very interesting course with interesting readings and i enjoyed the projects. not much work, readings before class and 2 essays and a final projects. she is also super nice and gives great feedback. would definitely recommend taking this class.
Class is an easy A if you give a good skim through the readings and go to her office hours before submitting essays. She's super nice, accommodating, and passionate about the course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment:
Dr. T is amazing, caring, and flexible. I have learned a lot from her class. I will say this class is tricky in terms of grading and the big projects are somewhat vague in how she grades. As long as you read the rubric carefully, participate, attend her office hours, you should get an A. 

I will definitely FLUNCH Dr. T w/ a friend next semester !!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr T is the goatttttt take writing 101 with her if you can she is very nice, accessible, and forgiving
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. T is such a great and understanding person, especially if you're an athlete—she was really accommodating. I think this is one of the easier writing classes. She assigns a lot of reading, but honestly, you can get away with not reading everything. The only downside is that we didn't know our cumulative grade until she submitted the final grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Her grading is a little unclear and arbitrary especially on the 3 assignments worth 20% of our grade. I would recommend on the Big Assignment she gives, don't go outside the box, I did that for Assignment 2 and got a B. Great professor and great insight in Asian American history but this will NOT be an easy A and you should not expect an A.

Very lax professor. Just show up to class with a general knowledge of the readings and you discuss with a partner for the majority of the class. Grade was just in-class participation (attendance), weekly discussion posts, a midterm paper, and a final project/paper. Low commitment and enjoyable class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Loved this class so much!!! Dr. T is the best. She really cares about her students and loves what she does. Even as a STEM major, I didn't find the class to be difficult at all. Definitely one of the best writing 101 classes at Duke. Workload isn't heavy, just readings and discussion post every week, and 3 papers throughout the semester.

Class is very low workload. There is a lot of reading assigned but you can get away with skimming it. Dr T is super nice and understanding. My only concern is that her rubric for essays is very unclear. Nevertheless, she is a fair grader overall.

Dr. T was amazing. Her classes were engaging, with active discussions every time. There are only 3 papers, so definitely utilize office hours to get an A, but otherwise there is only one required discussion post per week. She is kind, understanding, and offers guaranteed 72 hour extensions for all 3 papers. Would take again 100%!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. T was a pleasant surprise of a professor and I am extremely glad to have taken her class. She has a reading before every class, so expect to read dense but relatively short texts twice a week. She is also an extremely fair grader. I learned a lot about Asian American history and made a lot of great friends in this class. Highly recommend it!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment:
Professor is kind & class is interesting, but grades harshly. If you aren't a good writer and are a non-humanities major (unlike 95% of her students) get ready for a bad grade. Definitely opt for an easier W101 class as Asian American Narratives is not kind to heavy STEM loads.

Don't trust the other reviews from english/polisci majors if ur STEM!

She makes an effort to give voice to every person in the room and every experience of Asian American identity. Sincerely respect her scholarship and grateful for her kindness when addressing triggering topics. Great class, great professor, I loved every moment of it.

Dr. T is an incredibly kind, friendly individual. While I could have gotten through this class only completing the readings relevant to papers, the material was genuinely engaging and worth the time to explore. I'm not even sure Dr. T liked me, but she was still wonderful. Take this class!
Dr. T is great! Class is pretty low effort, as long as you put in work on the papers and participate in class it'll be easy.

Absolutely loved Dr. T as both a writing professor and a person. The readings she picks out are incredibly relevant and interesting. There can be a significant amount of reading assigned for each class, but it's engaging and manageable. I would definitely take her class again and completely recommend!
Dr. T is one of the sweetest professors I've ever had. She's extremely caring and puts her student's wellbeing first. I learned a lot about Asian American culture through this course.

Dr. T is so nice and caring and I have wonderful experience taking the class. The topic of Asian American sounds not interesting but she has made the class so engaging and meaningful. This writing class should be your first priority for first year writing. Highly recommended.

I loved Dr. T! Definitely assigns a lot of reading and you have to do it because she sometimes will call on people in class if they're being super quiet. However, she's super thoughtful and I found classes super interesting. Not a lot of homework besides the reading (only 3 essays including the final). Take her class, she's so insightful!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: She is the kindest lady ever. It may seem like there's a lot of reading to do at times, but you can skim over stuff and still be able to participate in discussions. As long as you put in effort and go to office hours before submitting a paper, it's almost impossible not to get an A. Highly recommend if you want an easy class with a nice teacher.

Listen to her feedback and follow it. Great professor that is passionate about what she teaches and holds office hours before big papers are due too. Easy discussion-based class, but you have to be passionate about the topic to make it through the readings.
the best, very accommodating and cares about her students
There are tons of readings but they are super interesting.

Amazing. I took her Human Connections Section in the midst of the pandemic, and I found the material interesting and engaging as the topics were direct. At the beginning of the semester, there was heavy reading, but it calmed down fast (the semester was also condensed so that played a role). Not too much Writing compared to other sections.

Dr. T has been my favorite professor so far! Her Asian American Memoir class was so informative and well-constructed. Although we had a lot of readings, they were all super interesting and I never felt like it was a burden. She's also so intelligent and extremely helpful when providing feedback for your essays. TAKE her writing 101 class!!!!!!!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Really, really good class. Such interesting readings, the discussions were so insightful. I also loved the variety of works we got to read and Dr. T was so engaging and thoughtful. Just make sure your papers have clear arguments and show critical thinking. Also, the workload is not bad, the final paper builds on the midterm. 10/10 would recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I really like Susan. I think she's an incredibly supportive and smart teacher. I thought her grading was very easy but some of my friends disagreed with me. I think she really cares about the content of your ideas and the amount of critical thinking you can put into your papers. Would take again she's cool.

Dr. T is amazing! I learned a lot about Asian American history and perspectives, as well as how to express my own. Most essays are completion except the 3 major ones, and I definitely think my writing improved!

Took her Asian American Memoir writing class. Pretty interesting content, lots of readings but they were kinda interesting. However, she is very open about her liberal beliefs and if you happen to be a conservative, you will definitely be uncomfortable in her class. Overall a good class.

Dr. T is the GOAT!!! Took her "Asian American Narratives" Writing 101 class and it was my favorite class I've ever taken. The class is super interesting; the readings are digestible and enjoyable (unlike some other Writing 101 classes with very dense and technical readings), and the class discussions, which she leads, are very insightful.

Dr. T is so cool & nice! Her Asian American Writing class was one of my favorite classes at Duke. The course weaves history and emotional stories into a beautiful culmination of what it means to be Asian in America. Her class made me reevaluate my relationship with my family history & debunked problematic racial narratives. 15/10 would recc!

Dr. T is one of the best professors I've taken a class with! I took Asian Americans and Civil Rights with her and even though she was not the original professor, I learned so much. She gives great feedback and she showed me research can be non-STEM related and so interesting. Really builds relationships with her students. Love her!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. T is an amazing professor at Duke. I suggest that freshman at Duke University should take her class, Writing 101: Ethnofuturism, if it is offered in that semester. The class is based on writing book and film analysis, which are usually a page, and then your opinion on it. In addition, she likes to give feedback to help improve your writing.

Dr. T is one of the nicest professors I've ever had. She's super passionate about her work, and she's very responsive to anything and everything students say. She is kind, understanding, and really easy to talk to. Ethnofuturism (WRI101) is also a really interesting topic, and I would highly recommend this class.

AMAZING CLASS! Took Ethnofuturism and the content was so interesting. Final two research papers were about Black Panther which was so fun and Dr. T is so caring and understanding. You spend a lot of time workshopping your papers so they're perfect and so you get a good grade. She really wants you to succeed and is always understanding about work.

Dr. T is one of the most caring professors I have taken a class with. Her class involves a lot of reading, but the works she assigns are not extremely dense and are very interesting. Since this is a writing class, obviously there are a lot of papers, but many of the small papers are in response to the readings, so they are not difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Prof. Than keeps her writing classes relaxed and engaging. Prof. Than chooses interesting and accessible reading materials. Thoroughly enjoyed this class, favorite of freshman year. I will say Prof. Than did not help me improve my writing skills but rather gave good feedback on how I should develop my essay topically.

Dr. T. is very great. She is like a mother us, as students. In the fall, we read 3 books total and then articles and movies and research, but the class is not overwhelming AT ALL. I was not supposed to take this Writing 101, but I'm so glad I did because Dr. Thananopavarn is a really kind, smart professor who is always willing to help.

Wonderful professor and person! She really does care about her students.  Most of the class made appointments with her to get feedback on graded essays. At first there is a bit of reading, but the readings do help with your essays.

I took her for writing 101. I never did the readings, but was able to still find easy reasons to discuss in class. The midterm wasn't too terrible, and it tied into the final paper (I only wrote a little extra because I could add to my midterm). I did the final and midterm the day before they were due. Ended with a B+. One of the easiest writing101
Very interesting course, would highly recommend. Great professor, clear grading. Do you work, and it should be no problem.
Doesn't like to give As!  But the class itself was fun.

I very much dislike writing, but this class happened to be my favorite out of Orgo, Film studies, and Sociology. Dr. T is super chill and tries to make sure you succeed. She taught Cultural Narratives of Illness and assigned doable readings every class, weekly 1 page writings, midterm, and final paper. Midterm and final connect, so pretty easy.

She gives a lot of feedback and returns papers in a timely manner. Not as easy as I hoped based on her ECU and UNC reviews, but she definitely tries to help you. This class should definitely be on your radar in case the easiest Writing 101 classes are taken.

She is a great teacher. In Writing101 Cultural Narratives of Illness she is very clear and makes the class interesting for people who don't specialize in the topic. There are weekly readings and writing assignments, readings are manageable and writing assignments are graded on completion. A midterm and final paper that she'll work with you a lot on
Robisheaux is the best. So sweet and so genuinely caring about his students and their learning. He really encourages you to see the world in a different way. :)

Absolutely incredible professor, super sweet and thoughtful guy. As said in other reviews, very willing to meet outside of class and incredibly dedicated and knowledgeable of reformation/renaissance topics. Lots of reading however, but worth it because you learn how to write/research well based on his feedback on you reading-informed work.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: AMAZING professor and super kind person - he really cares about his students. My writing & research skills improved significantly in his class thanks to his willingness to meet one-on-one and provide helpful feedback on my writing. The quality of the class itself (seminar style) depends on whether the other students have done the reading.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Robisheaux is extremely nice and gives great feedback on the essays. However, I feel like I didn't get much out of the class time. The class discussions seemed like they were lead by people who hadn't read and felt like a waste of time. As he seems incredibly knowledgable, it would've been nice to hear him talk about the material more.

Deep dive into four critical Renaissance figures with primary source reading and papers along the way. Prof Robisheaux is invested in fostering lively class discussions and seeing your improvement in research and writing.
