Absolutely incredible professor. Ridiculously kind and generous with his time. Clearly loves what he does and every class has a sense of energy that's really infectious. Absolutely take this :)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--So many papers

reviews.comment: The best professor I've had yet! He was so caring and genuinely wanted to help us become independent scholars and researchers. His lectures were very collaborative and he pushed us to think like a historian. His class inspired me to minor in MedRen studies. I highly recommend taking a class with him!!

Prof Robisheaux is a genuinely caring professor who loves his students and wants them to succeed. He has quite a bit of readings, but the material is not incredibly difficult and is interesting. His grading style is a bit abstract, sometimes the guidelines aren't very clear, but hes very accessible to discuss that with
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Robisheaux is a wonderful person, who truly cares about his students and the subject he teaches. He helped me improve my writing, while also teaching about some super interesting figures from the Renaissance. He is always available to help you if you need it.

Simply the best. Robisheaux is not only one of the most passionate and caring professors at Duke, but he is also one of the most genuine people on campus. He was a Duke undergrad himself, so rest assured that he puts his heart and soul into teaching. He cares a lot about quality of writing and provides great feedback. He is also very approachable.
A true gem who truly cares about the course material and his students. He will go the extra mile to help any student. Take a class with him before you leave Duke.

What a guy. Took Dr. Robisheaux's History of Magic, Religion and Science class and would definitely recommend it. Lot's of reading, and writing, but Dr. Robisheaux is always accessible outside of class and will give great feedback on your writing.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Hilarious

reviews.comment: I LOVE Robisheaux. You should try to take any class with him. He really wants his students to become better writers. Best professor that I had this semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Robisheaux is an incredible professor. He really wants his students to improve on their writing skills, and always makes time to meet with them after class. He really knows his stuff and is passionate about history!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: A real gem of a professor: kind, knowledgeable, and encouraging. You can skim the long readings to get the gist of them, but pay close attention to lectures and take notes-- lecture notes will prove helpful later on in writing papers. Wonderful class, wonderful professor.
Simply The Best.

Professor Robisheaux absolutely loves what he teaches, and he's incredibly knowledgeable about it. The assignments (while worth a chunk of your grade) are very straightforward and not difficult. He's a great professor who's always willing to meet with you outside of class. No textbook, mostly primary sources and books.

Prof. Robisheaux was my absolute favorite this semester. He really cares for his students. If you ever need help brainstorming a paper topic or are unsure about anything he mentions in class, he is always there for you during office hours. Robisheaux is extremely kind and wants to help improve your writing. I want to take another class from him!

Took Professor Robisheaux's Focus seminar on Renaissance scientists. He really cares for his subject! The discussions were really interesting and lively and he's very happy to talk to you outside of class. When I had some issues outside of class, he was very patient and gave me some extra time for work.

Interesting readings. Lecture's were okay, but the material is fascinating. It's too bad that the papers are graded harshly and it doesn't matter if you do the readings because all that matters are papers and the TAs can't tell who reads from who does not. Got a grade I did not deserve at all in the end :(

Robisheaux is the best! I took his freshman seminar, Renaissance Politics, but I would highly recommend any class with him! He genuinely cares about all of his students, brought us homemade cookies, invited us all out to lunch, etc. He loves his subject and wants you to love it too. Great feedback on essays. Much easier if you do the readings!

Very easy going and friendly.  He absolutely loves his topic and conveys his passion well.  Very supportive and fair, extremely approachable, and overall ensures an extremely positive/engaging experience.  Low key writing assignments, reading semi-mandatory.

Love Prof. Robisheaux. Loved his bow ties, and his general awesomeness. Class was very interesting. Readings varied of course, some would be incredibly interesting, others not so much. His grading is stricter with midterms, but with all the small writing assignments he's pretty chill. Also he's very approachable

Amazing professor. Is genuinely passionate about what he's teaching, and knows it quite well. One of the most knowledgeable about his field I've ever had, and really open and accessible to students. Short papers are graded leniently, term papers pretty strictly, but he really cares that you develop as a writer. Best class I've taken at Duke!

Interesting class and material for the most part. Some of the lectures and readings bore you out of your skull, but overall they are okay. He doesn't grade the take-home essays too hard. He's really nice and loves what he teaches.

SUCH a cool guy. his bow ties combined with his EXTREME enthusiasm for this subject make this course amazing. so so interesting. most of the readings are so intriguing and he gets so into his lectures. one of the most interesting classes ever at duke!

Pretty interesting class. He's obviously really passionate about what he's teaching. A lot of reading. Nice guy. Reading never gets mentioned in class. Lectures can be boring sometimes. Books can be really boring sometimes. But overall, good class and prof.

the MAN. Easily the most interesting class I've taken at Duke. LOTR, the exorcist etc. watched in class. Go to lecture every day and take good notes-if you do you'll be fine for the 2 midterms and final (sets of take home essays). Faculty lunch with T-Rob if you can, such a funny guy to talk to outside of class. His bow ties are pretty awesome too

Really great guy. It's obvious that he is truly passionate about what he teaches. If you talk to him beforehand, it's easier to do well on the essays. He really cares about his students & is very interesting to talk to.

History of Magic was a really interesting class and he's a good professor.  Class was really interesting and VERY easy.  If you looking for an A w/out much effort, this is for you.  All of the lectures, notes, and power points are all online.  While his TAs do most of the grading, 2 out of 3 exams were take home.

A professor passionate about his subject.  Not very accessible.  Section and lecture have NOTHING to do with each other. Lots of reading and writing that will never be mentioned in lecture.  Interesting material, but you will learn more about how to write historically than about history itself.

Dr. Robisheaux is one of the better professors at Duke. He is very enthusiastic in class and makes an effort to know his students. You will have to work hard in this class (mostly writing), but topics are relatively interesting and the grading is fair. He and the TA's are very helpful and accessible also.
Makes you read some of the most irrelevant and ridiculous books.  Very liberal.  Not a fair grader.
Great prof.  Gives a moderate amount of work, but if you do it you should be OK.  Very helpful and nice guy.

Robisheaux is the best history teacher I've had here. He LOVES what he teaches, and he LOVES students. Whatever class you are in, he will tell you it is the best he's ever taught. The funny thing is, he's not lying. He just gets so incredibly excited. Also, his bow-ties rock.

I loved this class! Robisheaux is so passionate and excited about history. I didn't go to class much and got a solid grade...he posts notes online. A few papers but nothing bad. I'd take him if I were you.
Genuinely makes an effort to get to know his students. Take advantage of this: go to office hours, chat him up, & you'll get an A.
Great History Prof. Loves his subjects and cares about his students
Very engaging and helpful. Keeps you awake in lectures with his odd vocal inflections.
Hes a passionate guy... Pretty easy grader. get a good TA
Robisheaux is the man. He is genuinely interested in history and therefore makes the class interesting. Wears ties occasionally... great class.
Good guy - just go to class you'll be fine.
No Comments
No Comments
No Comments
Very unclear grading criteria. Perfect attendance and completion of all assignments only warrants a "B" letter distinction. Only take this class if you have an abundance of free time.

Prof. Thompson is very warm, caring, and personable, and he genuinely wants to help and understand his students. The class itself was structured around class readings with few assignments throughout aside from our overarching theme/final project. I learned a lot both personally and academically, and the course was always a highlight to my week!

Professor Thompson is the most inspirational professor I have worked with at Duke. The course material focuses on various topics related to farmworkers including race, immigration, & environmentalism. This is also a smaller class that is based around student discussion & the service project. Professor Thompson cares about the material and students.

Took this class "Pilgrimage" expecting and easy ride, boy was I wrong. Charlie graded our assignments with checkmarks so every time I got a check I thought I was doing fine, turns out checks are B. Participated the most out of the 8 students in class, got a B- in participation. Put an incredible amount of effort into final projects, got B's. Yikes
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: He is a very casual professor but is very passionate about the subject matter. The class Food Politics was very interesting.

Best and nicest professor ever. He cares about this topic so much and you'll be so inspired learning about his work. Might be a little disorganized at times, but his enthusiasm and passion make up for it. Favorite professor at Duke.

Charlie is one of the most passionate teachers I have ever had. I took his FOCUS class in Humanitarian Challenges and my respect for him grew throughout the semester. He is a great teacher and gets you thinking in marvelous ways. If you are in Humanitarian Challenges, take his US/Mexico border class! You won't regret it!

Charlie is very deeply indebted to his work.  He has so much passion for the issues at hand and and presents them clearly for the class to see.  You'll find he is very likable and can spark a passion within yourself to work on the issues he is facing.  Definitely a professor worth having.

Loved that Tim's lectures went deep on the physics and chemistry behind energy technology and lots of real world applications while the assignments and tests were just based on the core relationships and concepts that folks will realistically apply!
Such a good professor! Tests were online and not bad at all. Super interesting lectures and overall such a nice guy.

Dr. Johnson is a standout professor who truly cares about his students and subject matter- he is very laidback and class can be easy with minimal work but if the topic is interesting, you'll find yourself wanting to do the work. Pretty group project heavy but he's a very fair and easy grader. can't recommend him enough

I took Transportation and Energy with Tim - he's a great lecturer, very clear. He's very nice, super smart, and responds quickly to emails. The class is pretty easy but lots of group projects (one big final assignment and one smaller group presentation). No tests or anything.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Tim Johnson is one of my favorite professors I have had at Duke.  He is truly a professor who is there for the students. I especially enjoyed this Energy Technology course, as it was current, relevant, and Tim was always willing to answer questions. I would definitely recommend this course.

This class is a joke and the least I have learned of any class at Duke. Dr Strauman cancels class left and right, is a boring teacher and lets you out twenty minutes early, few individual assignments, and midterm and assignments are a cake walk. If you want an easy A, he's your guy. If you want to learn and make use of this credit, look elsewhere.

Very efficient with class time, homework assignments were graded leniently, and material was all explained in an extremely clear and digestible manner. Overall, an amazing professor and an even sweeter person, absolutely recommend!

Such a great professor!!!! I was a little worried after 204, but he made the material super approachable, assignments weren't overly difficult, and he was understanding when it came to extensions/makeup exams. Best prof at Duke by far. 10000/10
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Strauman is the GOAT. Very efficient lecturer - we were almost always done before the end of class time. Clear with expectations and information, as well as being really funny. Lots of homework assignments, but deadlines were often extended, which I appreciated. Super knowledgeable about science and research and made this class fun and engaging.

Strauman is awesome! After going through 204 with Vieth, I was not too excited about what 205 would entail, but I feel like I was genuinely engaged in the material because you can tell he cares so much about teaching and the subject at hand. He always asks for class feedback to see what styles best fit the students. Loved the class!

Strauman is an expert in abnormal psych and his lectures are great. He's always willing to answer questions and encourages class discussion. He shapes his lectures based on what the class seems to be most interested in. Great class overall.

Professor Strauman is a great and silly guy and his class is very managable!  He's super chill and incredibly helpful if you go to see him. Lectures were engaging, tests weren't abnormally hard, and he was overall one of my favorite professors at Duke!

Take this class if you don't care about the material but need an easy A   OR   you love the material and have a super easy schedule. No need to do any readings or even show up to class. You learn what you want to learn. I wish I had the time to dedicate to this class because I'm sure it was really interesting. Got an A & spent total 4 hours working

Tim Strauman is one of my favorite professors at Duke.  He was always super easy going when it came to grading as long as you do what is expected and put effort in the papers.  He is also one of the nicest and most lenient professors I have ever come across and he is always open to help. Would take again if I could!!

Easily the best course I've taken at Duke. He knows psychology and also a ridiculous amount about TV shows. He always keeps class interesting and makes you really love abnormal psychology. 1010 would recommend.

AWESOME PROFESSOR.  He really knows what he is talking about and you will learn a lot.  the emphasis is really on learning, and not on grades.  If you show him you have learned whats going on, you will get an A.  He is probably the best and most helpful professor I have had while at Duke.

Great professor with a realistic but positive attitude--Strauman always makes classes clear, interesting, and even somewhat fun.  Plus, he cares more about learning than grades, so coursework is fair and grading is lenient.
Fantastic professor! Best I've had at Duke. Knows a lot about the topic and is always ready to help. Reasonable workload--keeps the readings interesting.
Excellent course!

Professor Strauman was awesome!  He recognizes what work is valuable and what isn't and accordingly keeps the class quite manageable while not falling into a cheap blow-off class. TAKE PSY 89S!! Dr. Thompson is amazing and he makes it doable for everyone to get an A so long as you try! He gives clear grading criteria, lot of example papers, and providing lot of feedback to an ungraded first draft!

Dr. Thompson's freshmen seminar on Empathy and Identity was a truly amazing class. The material we covered was made very central to all of our lives, and Dr. Thompson was great at both explaining material and helping us connect it to our own experiences. The readings for each session are a lot, but they are interesting and produce good reflection.

reviews.comment: Best class I have taken at Duke. Best professor I had at Duke.

He was, and I expect will always be, my favorite professor. Though you do have to work in this class, it is extremely engaging and rewarding. He truly loves what he does and it shows. The manner in which he runs the class is extremely conducive to both learning and growing in the field of psychology. It's a must take class that you won't regret.

This class really changed the way I think, both because of the nature of the material but also because Professor Thompson is such an encouraging, insightful professor. I  truly wish I could take this class again and hope to take at least one more class that's even close to the standard of this class.

Doctor Thompson is one of those professors that you will remember for all of your years at college, and maybe even beyond.  While the class is challenging, you get out what you put in, and Dr. Thompson is always willing to meet with you and give great feedback on your papers.  There is a lot of reading, but it's all interesting (for the most part).

Excellent professor. Professor Thompson was not only a teacher, but also a mentor. He truly cares about his students and wants you to succeed. His readings are very extensive and difficult though, and be prepared to do some work if you want to get an A. The effort is definitely worth it.

Dr. Thompson is one of, if not the best professor and advisor I've had at Duke. This class is tough with a heavy workload, but he is more than willing to meet with you for help. His expectations are clear and he is flexible and understanding. His lectures are awesome and he shares footage of some of his actual patients, which is really cool.

He is my favorite, most beloved, most amazing, and kindest prof I ever had! I still feel that he's my friend and mentor. His class gave me reflection, confidence, and inspirations. The only thing I regret is that I should have carefully read over all the assigned readings (he doesn't use a textbook, and readings are posted on sakai). DO READ IT.
I absolutely loved the discussion Dr. Thompson led. However, the readings to prepare for the class are extensive, and the papers you write are not at all graded easily. He's tough, but worth it.
He is the best prof I''ve had.

Best teacher I have ever had. Engaged, interested in the opinions of his students, and incredibly intelligent. He takes time to meet with us out of class and is always there to help when you need it. The class is interesting and really forces you to think and reconsider your perspective on the world. Lots of work, but well worth taking.
Amazing teacher and really interesting class!!!

Absolutely fantastic professor. Do the readings! They are worthwhile and participating in this class makes it extraordinarily interesting. Dr. Thompson really cares about getting to know his students.

This guy is awesome.  Lots of reading and pretty lengthy papers, but his feedback is so good and he's always there if you need to ask him something.  Our class also got to have dinner at his house, he's just a really cool person overall.

There is a substantial amount of reading, but most of the articles are pretty interesting.  As others have mentioned, his feedback on the papers is very helpful because he clearly pinpoints what you need to work on. Great professor.  Very helpful and understanding.  He really cares about the class and the well-being of his students.  There is quite a bit of reading, but if you keep up with it, it isn't too bad. Gives the best feedback on papers. So helpful! There is a decent amount of reading, but the papers are graded fairly and as long as you listen to the feedback you'll get a good grade! Class is so interesting and very conversational.

Wonderful class. He really tries to build personal relationships with his students. Interesting discussions and material. Provides a lot of feedback on essays so you know exactly what he is looking for. Entirely recommended!
Boring.. can't keep eyes open... avoid unless you are extremely interested in the subject
He is amazing, understanding, so kind, and brings in really really interesting videos of his clinical work.  Extremely interesting class.

AMAZING class and really good teacher, very understanding, brings videos into lectures

clearly cares about students and tries to make it interesting but still pretty boring, with dry lectures and a  tough class, lots of work to do between problem sets and frequent exams, think it was either 2 or 3 midterms plus a final, also makes lectures tech free so no phones or computer entire semester
Favorite Econ professor at Duke!
The best to take 205 with, and very easy. Don't need to review any lectures, just know how to do the pset problems and the exams will be easy.

Probably the best professor to take ECON 205 with.

Todd is the best professor I've had at Duke especially in the Econ Department. He really cares about his students and wants everyone to succeed. Sarver teaches his own curriculum with no logical progression. The only way to attempt to learn is by going to his convoluted lectures during which he poorly explains how to solve problems that should be simple. The biggest downfall for Professor Sarver was his inability to simplify course material, making lectures feel redundant as he was no more helpful than reading the textbook. BEST professor ever. Super clear lecture notes and easy exams. Do all the homework and mock exams then you will get an A.
BEST professor ever. Super clear lecture notes and easy exams. Just enroll his course.

Love from DKU

TOMASI THE GOAT!! He's the only professor I've ever had who's sample exams are actually representative of the actual exams, which is extremely helpful. The GOAT. Amazing lecturer and fair homeworks and exams.
Enjoyed his CS 371 Elements of Machine Learning. The best professor I have ever seen. It was him that took me on the road of ML/AI.

Tomasi is a GEM! Take 371 if you can! Weekly homeworks (groups of up to 3) and two very fair exams. Incredibly organized notes, very useful material, and definitely my favorite class at Duke. There are very few professors at Duke (Tori Akin & now Carlo Tomasi come to mind) that I would build my entire schedule for a semester around: Tomasi is one!

The class is very organized and the notes/slides are well-written. Dr. Tomasi gives very clear instructions in homework/exams. He is a highly respected figure in the field of computer vision, yet he is very approachable and super nice to his students.
Amazing professor both inside and outside of the classroom. Very knowledgeable, and is a great lecturer. Homeworks and exams can be a bit tough, but nevertheless I had an awesome overall experience.
Fantastic professor, flexible grading, very clear notes. I looked forward to doing the homework. Final was unexpectedly hard compared to all questions completed throughout the course.
Excellent professor. Really clear explanations on every topic. Easy grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Outstanding lecturer who can explain just about any topic. Class notes are articulately written and replace the need for a textbook. While the class is mainly theoretical, homework assignments are really well crafted and give the opportunity for some practical implementations. Exams were harder than past semesters, but they were fair.

Most organized professor I've had. Lectures are clear and videos and notes online will be enough to understand the material. The exams are easier than the homeworks, which can take a good amount of time, so make sure to start early.

I've taken both 371 and 527 with Tomasi, and I loved both. He is a great lecturer, and is great at explaining difficult topics. The class is a clearcut structure in terms of grading, and his exams are very reasonable. I would highly recommend any CS student take a class with Tomasi.
100% recommend taking one of his classes. Incredibly understanding, has great notes and accessible exams

Tomasi really understands what he is talking about, and has incredibly clear and well-constructed lectures and class notes. The homework adds a coding component to the class that corresponds well with the material. The class notes are incredible tools for understanding ML concepts and if you read through them, you will have no trouble on tests.

I was worried about taking this class as a 2nd yr, but Tomasi's ability to make complex concepts feel like common sense made this class my favorite over my time at Duke so far. The homework is done in groups of your choosing, the lectures were recorded, and the tests are straight-forward. He is a gem at Duke and I strongly recommend taking 371.

This class is one of the best I've taken. The perfect level of difficulty, lectures/notes are clear & concise and still full of info, exams & homework are VERY well-made and I genuinely looked forward to doing assignments. Tomasi is very knowledgable and makes the material very approachable. Put in a reasonable amount of effort and you'll be good.

The lectures were great, and the exams are easy if you read his notes, although they are quite dense. Homework takes a lot of time, so make sure to go to office hours if your code isn't working or need help starting on the question. Overall, great class.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Tomasi is one of the nicest professors I've had at Duke. He is a leader in machine learning and puts knowledge and learning for the students above all else. I have never had a CS prof as dedicated to the subject as he is. He would write up good responses to student questions and dedicates time to teaching. Note: the class is hard though.

You can tell that Tomasi knows what he's doing. Super smart, good at lecturing and explaining concepts, and really puts in the effort to help you learn (especially in adapting to the online format). Weekly homework can get difficult, but TAs are really helpful.

Tomasi is one of my favorite professors I've had. He definitely cares about his students, and his lectures (though somewhat theoretical) were clear and made the math behind ML very accessible. He's helpful in office hours, and also just gives great advice in general. Weekly HWs were reasonable and exams were extremely fair. I highly recommend him!

He's one of the best professors I've had and knows the subject so well (famous for it). It's a difficult and very rigorous class, and be prepared to read his notes (multiple times, sometimes), but you will become so much better at understanding (applied) math and really know the material. I honestly really enjoyed the class. Really organized, too.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Prof. Tomasi is very organized, smart and pretty sassy at times. The grading is transparent and fair, and he is always available to answer student questions. His homeworks are thought-provoking, and you probably will come out with a more organized and precise approach to mathematics and CS after taking his class. Totally recommend him for CS 230.

The most organized professor at Duke by far. Tomasi is incredibly intelligent and yet is able to empathize with students in his lectures. The homework is tough but interesting. He has a nice grading policy and the exams are really doable if you know the concepts well. He's always there to answer questions on Piazza and has a nice sense of humor.
Hands down. He is the man. The most organized class I've ever had in my life.

Very famous professor, very difficult subject. He teaches it well (as it's his bread and butter), but his voice can get a little boring at times. His notes are incredibly dense and require multiple look-overs to fully comprehend, but if you can do that, you don't ever need to go to class
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Has a smart, dry sense of humor and professorial sass that makes my life. Literally THE MOST ORGANIZED CLASS I'VE EVER TAKEN IN MY LIFE. From what I've heard, 230, which wasn't a difficult class with him, can be god awful with some professors. Obviously wants you to do well and is very straightforward with grading and tests.

Most organized professor I've ever had. Cool homework that really helps your understanding. Lectures can sometimes drag on, but are pretty interesting most of the time. Has a quirky, sarcastic sense of humor that's  kind of hilarious at points. Really knows his stuff.
Tomasi class was super organized and his class was easy, but he was SO BORING.

He loves this subject. I found it hard to focus on him sometimes, but the class wasn't terrrrribly difficult. For the first test the study guide was amazingly helpful, not so much for the final - it came as a bad surprise. Homeworks take some time, but either he or the TA (Yin Lin) is an easy grader.

seriously, tomasi cares about his subject more than anyone else i have had at duke. writes his own notes, and they are basically a textbook suited for his class--nay, they are better. there is quite a bit of work, but he is extremely helpful outside of class and a very fair, and fairly generous grader. best class ive had at duke

He is very helpful when you ask for help while you are doing your hw. His tests are sometimes very ambiguous but don't count much unless you do really poorly. The lowest grade he gave in Fall 2005 was A-!

Loves the subject. LOVES the subject. If you have trouble with homework just go see him and he'll really help you out. Coming to class is completely optional, he gave everyone 100% participation grades.
Very intelligent, but sometimes that can be a barrier for explaining things well.
Used a PDF rather than a legitimate text, made for a subpar experience.  Bad at conveying ideas, did not seem to care about students.
Extremely knowledgeable, writes and uses his own text, is extremely engaged and helpful with homework assignments. I have almost no math background and did just fine in the class.
Not a nice guy and not a good prof, enough said

Had a very difficult time explaining some concepts to us undergrads.  I remember specifically him telling us it was because he skipped multivariable calculus when he was an undergrad and it was difficult for him to try to teach us those concepts.

I speak for the grad course. He is the best numerical analyst here. He use his own books (only online available in duke, hyperbolic book is to be published) and he is definitely a extremely professional programmer. Learn C++ yourself before going to his class!

Absolutely terrible. Quintessential tenured math/sciences academic who is probably a genius, but couldn't convey the simplest of thoughts in a manner understandable to an undergraduate if his life depended on it. Avoid.

Dr. T is the freakin man if you're taking 107. For most math classes at Duke, lecture is nearly pointless cause you can just read the book, but Dr. T seriously knows his stuff and shows you his own methods to do everything (which are way better). Our section rocked the final cause of this guy.
He's terrible (had him for Math 124 - Combinatorics). See details at: evals.aas.duke.edu

Highly inaccessible outside of class, lectures basically from the book, not enlightening.  Exams difficult, do not correlate to book/lecture/hw material.  Bitter about teaching this class.  Nice guy, but don't take this class with him-- he's highly underqualified to teach it.

Very hard grader and teaches different from book, which made the class more difficult at times.  Also a busy man, so not easy to meet with for help outside of ofice hours.  Tries to be funny, but picks on the same people every day.
One of the best math professors at Duke.  Very engaging and helpful to his students.  The class is not easy though.  I highly recommend him for any class he teaches.
Sometimes it was confusing, just by the nature of the material, but Prof. Trangenstein always put up PDFs explaining unclear topics on his web site - very helpful!

Avoid at all costs. Definitely the worst prof at Duke I've met. might be a good person, but be prepared to sleep through all lectures without learning anything. He just read off the slides with no explanations. The final exam was long and tedious, relatively hard. Homeworks were also mission impossible as they had nothing to do with the lectures.

George Truskey is a prime example of a decorated researcher with zero teaching capability. Powerpoint slides were useless and homework is near impossible without going to office hours with the TA. He also downcurved the class. Tests are hard.

If you read the BME 260 textbook, you would learn infinitely more information than you will from the awful slides that were used in class. Worst class I have taken at Duke. Get ready to sleep through most lectures. Tests are seemingly random and the class was down curved. Avoid at all costs.
Terrible lecturer and completely unhelpful. I did not learn anything from this class and would not recommended it to anyone.
Literally gave the class a negative curve without a warning. Who does that? Lectures werent helpful, discussions werent either.
doesn't know what is on his own lecture slides or what he assigned as homework, assigns both a final project and a final exam, harsh grader as well
Very nice and helpful professor. Genuinely interested in helping students learn.

One of the most interesting classes i've had.  People leaving bad comments are simply not reading the book or paying a bit of attention in the lectures.  How are the hw and labs supposed to make sense if you are not even making the effort? Complaining about the professor is not a solution because Dr. Truskey is knowledgeable and helpful.

This is one of the best classes I have had at duke.  Dr. Truskey is knowledgeable, helpful, and very reachable outside of class, which is a lot to expect from prestigious scholars like him.  The lab&problem set are designed to complement the lecture.  Of course this is not an easy A class, but if you put in the effort it's def possible to get an A.

One of the worst teachers I have had at Duke. The lectures have nothing to do with the problem set. Also, there is no reason for the problem sets to be uploaded electronically. The labs are basically a statistics course.

Likes to throw in a bunch of random equations (not in the TEXT)in lecture without much explanation (like the Hodgkin-Huxley Model of Nerve Conduction???) and expects you to know everything already. Stat labs have pages of reading that covers a wide range of topics (e.g. from calculating variance to doing 2 sample hypothesis testing as a prelab)...

The thing is, whether or not he is charismatic has nothing to do with this course here.  He was definitely not helpful (he seemed clueless about the homework he assigned).  The "readings" were nothing more than research papers that had almost nothing to do with the material.  He was so spaced out in class, it was ridiculous.  Boo word limit.

True, Prof. Trsukey is not the most charismatic professor in the world, but he is helpful, caring, and clear. His lectures are slightly boring, but if you do the readings, you'll learn a lot and do well.
It's a shame that an academic department as highly vaunted as Duke BME does not have a single person who gives a gives a damn about their class.  Or if they actually care, can teach it.
Not terribly difficult, but it was ridiculously boring at times.
a little dull, but helpful and resourceful
No Comments
Never give feedback on your quizzes. I don't think she actually knows how to calculate the final grades. Too blur

As a human she is nice and gives good advice, but tough-grader. The best that you can get is A- (she takes pride in it) and the grading criterias don't make sense and are not clear. Moreover, she doesn't give feedback on the quizzes so you don't know where you did wrong.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Compared to same course by other professors, this one gives the lowest grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Participation marks are worth a lot and I feel like I didn't learn much bio because classes were just presentations and "adding on to what x said" to get participation marks. Recorded lectures are not as monotonous as other professors'. Grading criteria is often not clear, but she answers emails quickly. Rarely gives 100s for labs; easy 90s though
I love group assignments about this class.

One thing I love about her is she gets very passionate when lecturing and talking about biology. She is quite tough in grading especially labs and has said that she rarely gives full points. Sometimes she is a bit confusing when giving instructions, so don't be afraid to clarify with her.
Loved her! Cared a lot and gave amazing feedback.
Kate is a great professor. I would 100 percent recommend this class to anyone. This class is very interactive with a fun and engaging syllabus.

LOVE HER! Course itself is interesting and participation grade is based on completing short discussion posts. Class discussion is informal, you don't feel pressured. Her feedback on essays is incredibly helpful. Super accessible outside of class, SWEETEST PROF, VERY flexible with extensions. You actually learn & doable workload. BEST W101 class fs!

Kate is an incredible professor!! She is kind, engaging, and cares about her students and the genre. The material is a combination of fantasy novels, movies, and TV shows, which are very nostalgic and fun. Her class discussions are lively and interesting. She provides in-depth feedback on essays because she truly cares about your writing.

Kate is a great teacher who puts in considerable effort to make her class enjoyable. She's always accessible, understanding, and reachable if you need an extension or have something come up. Almost all important assignments have opportunities for feedback and revision. Plan for lots of movies, fun readings, and weekly discussion posts (+ 3 essays).
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Turner is awesome, any class she is teaching will be a great time, she is so understanding and kind. If you like reading fantasy you should 100% take her writing 101. 3 Essays throughout semester and weekly short discussion posts. Final project is very open ended.
Great at giving critical but positive feedback. Grading can be tough, but the class is fun and worth taking.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Van Tuyl is very nice and caring, but this doesn't make up for the lack of organization in the class. She is 10-15 minutes late every class and then holds you longer, she assigns homework at 10pm the night before, and she doesn't curve even if everyone in the class didn't do well. She just goes over homework in class, which isn't helpful.

This professor gives a ridiculous amount of homework and is somewhat unorganized with her resources. Her documents, worksheets, screencasts, etc. on Sakai have no form of organization and are all over the place. However, she is a thorough teacher and you learn a lot in this class. It 's just pretty intense.

The professor is perfect. Uses old but proven methods. Her teaching methods are very effective. The tests are performed several times a week, but they are very simple. Thanks to the professor, I really improved my Russian language.
I've taken 4 semesters w/ JVT (101, 102, 203, 204) & she's AMAZING!

Really nice teacher and she always wants to help. It's so nice to have such an understanding teacher during covid classes, and while she expects everyone to do their work, she's also human and will understand if something unexpected happens in your life. Having her as a professor made me very happy to pick Russian as my language at Duke.

JVT is a truly caring professor and wants you to succeed in Russian. Although she sometimes goes off on tangents about her life, it is great hearing about her anecdotes in the Soviet Union and such. She gives a lot of homework and usually checks, so the time commitment aspect is important. Tests/Exams are not hard if you prepare for them.

Good professor. She teaches Russian in a very clear way so you always know what's going on and you know what to expect on tests. Daily homework but that's what it takes to learn a new language. Really nice person, too.

While Russian is definitely a really difficult language coming from English, Professor Van Tuyl is really great about making it make sense and making the class enjoyable. There's a little bit of homework every night, and tons of vocab, but you're never unsure of what's expected of you.
Class syllabus and grading procedures are clearly laid out. She is more than willing to meet outside of class and help you, you just have to ask.
Great Professor. Definitely going to continue to take classes with her. Russian is a hard language but she definitely takes the time to help you out.
She brings us cookies and candies before each test!!
Easy if you are willing to put in the time to do homework. Amount of homework is not unreasonable at all. Confusing at times, but very willing to explain, usually crystal-clear by the second time.
Probably the best prof at Carleton. You won't regret it, she is amazing.

Professor T-B is really good at explaining concepts in a clear and precise manner. Only problem is the long problem sets and weekly "proof swaps" with endless deadlines, but they're worth it - my proof writing skills improved a lot with Prof T-B's proof swaps. Tests were also easier than other sections.

The class was difficult, but Professor Turnage-Butterbaugh was by far the best professor at Duke to take it with. She was always very clear in her explanations of theorems and had very clear expectations for coursework.

This class was extremely difficult, but I'm really glad that I had TB. She goes at a reasonable pace, cares about her students, and is helpful during office hours. However, this is by far the hardest class I have taken at Duke so far, and even putting in tremendous amounts of work each week I found it difficult to get good grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Caring

reviews.comment: Amazing teacher. She sometimes goes super fast but she's very helpful during office hours. She's also super friendly
Math 221 is a hard class, but TB is the best Professor to take it with. She's very helpful in office hours and her in class lectures are well-paced and organized.

If you have to take Linear Algebra, take it with Professor TB! Lectures are clear, although she does move really quickly at times. She cares a lot about her students and makes time to help out, but expect to spend 15 hours + on homework each week. Warning: Even with a great professor, this class is extremely challenging!!! Textbook is essential.

She lectured straight from the book, which I did not like because you're supposed to read the textbook anyway. So lectures didn't add much and I learned most of it from the book. But she's really dedicated to helping the students succeed; office hours are helpful. Linear algebra is hard, but tests are easy if you actually put effort into the HW.
Prof TB is an amazing professor. She is extremely helpful and passionated about what she teaches. The subject is hard, particularly for freshmen. Do flunch her, you will have a great conversation!

Professor TB is amazing.  Linear Algebra is really tough, but her lectures make things as clear as possible.  She goes at a good pace and really explains things.  She starts every lecture with a brief review of the previous one, and then gives context and the big picture for where she's is going next.  Definitely the best Math Professor I've had!
Amazing

Armand is an incredible French teacher. He is very clear when teaching the material and laidback. He is also understanding if there are any issues. He managed to make our 8:45 class enjoyable -- quite the feat!
Super supportive and intelligent. He is the reason why I fell in love with french.

If you're taking intro level french, you want him a your teacher. He is extremely clear in teaching the material and he is also very understanding of any difficulties you may have. Highly recommend him.

Her effort in teaching matches student's effort. You will get as much from her as your efforts warrant. She will coach, mentor, and tutor honestly and effectively. Don't waste her time. She won't waste yours. Great advocate for students who deserve it!
Not nice at all, yes you can approach her once, but after that look out, creates a hostile environment, not at all able to work with adult learners.

I love Kathy Turner!  She's very willing to help and cared about her students learning the material (as opposed to focusing on grades).   She's also assertive and tells it like it is.  She's top-notch.

Confrontational; always assumes you did the wrong thing; creates hostile learning environment; fails to build confidence in students; throws emotional tantrums when you question her authority; watch out

For 8:30 lectures, Twiss was decent. He's nice and cares for his students and is pretty communicative. Additionally, he's very knowledgeable and ties it to industry. But EGR121 is just a poorly made class, and lectures contribute nearly nothing to actual class learning. Upside is there're no tests about material - just project performance.

Twiss is incredibly helpful and truly cares about his students. Sometimes he is quite busy and takes a while to reply to emails, but he's truly an interesting person and does a great job working with undergraduate engineers.
Great guy, love him

Twiss is great! Such a nice guy. Really knows his stuff and loves to help out. The class is almost all group projects which I really enjoyed but doesn't mean it's not a lot of work. Some nights, I was in the lab soldering till 3am before deadlines but Twiss was there till around midnight bringing pizza and snacks. Really shows how dedicated he is!!

The course EGRMGMT 590.01 is Designing Customer Experiences. He really helped one to think outside the box.   I think he did a great job of encouraging us to look at everyday things and see how they could be improved and gave us some skill sets for testing optimizing user experience.

This guy was awesome. Super lax, gave great advice, always knew exactly what to tell you in order to make your projects more effective and succeed. All mechanical engineers must take this class, you should take it in the spring so that you get the combination of TwissWalter Simmons, total dream team.

Anna is just the best. She cares a lot for her students and understands that college is not all about class but students also have other stuff going on outside the classroom. The only downside is that the online system she used gave a lot of homework, not her fault.
Great professor

I LOVE Prof Tybinko. If you're taking Spanish 203, take it with her. Do your work and stay on top of due dates and there is nothing to worry about. She is so nice, so caring, and so enthusiastic every day. I'd hang around after class just to chat with her. Highly recommend.

She is an awesome professor if she sees you putting in the work and trying hard. She tries her best to get to know her students and understands that we have outside priorities. Tries her best to make class fun and mandatory exams minimal stress.

Super nice and perky which made going to her class four days a week bearable. I've heard horror stories about the Spanish department at Duke, but I absolutely love her. She's always willing to work with students outside of class, and I didn't ever really feel lost even though I had never taken Spanish before.

I was worried since I couldn't find anyone who had taken her before (it turns out it was her first semester teaching), but Anna is really amazing at teaching a new language. Definitely better than some other Spanish professors, and is accessible if you need her. Makes time for her students and wants to see you succeed.
He is a decent professor, but gives more work than what is expected of the class.

Prof. Carter is very responsive and caring, and has a great sense of humor as well. Very accessible outside of classroom. He also replies to your email quite fast. Love the course! Workload a bit big for a 2-credit course, but you will definitely learn a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Argumentation Across Disciplines with Prof. Carter is fine. If you wish to improve your writing, you will be benefited from the course. Yet, if you already reach a certain level in writing, the course may not be interesting. Prof. Carter expects students to go to his office hour and ask questions.

Dr. Tung is the most amazing professor I have ever had and likely will ever have at Duke. She will challenge you because she knows how capable you are and will support you the whole way: she is available outside of class, loves to answer tangential questions, and will teach you more than you ever thought you could learn. She is the best.

Professors like Jenny Tung are why I came to Duke. She's an expert in her field yet makes the content accessible. She'll cater lectures and content to the interests of the students and makes the effort to understand everyone's thought process. The first couple weeks will be a challenge, but it will 100 pay off by the end.
The class is challenging but really interesting. Dr. Tung is really accessible outside of class, and she is one of the best professors I have had!

Dr. Tung was one of the best teachers/professors I've ever had and I really enjoyed her class this semester. Lot more quantitative/programming work than I was expected and first few weeks were a little daunting but you catch on quick. Expect to get very fluent in programming language R in this class. MESS people this is a must take class!

I had Jenny for Evanth212 through FOCUS and she was fantastic! I came in with no interest in EvAnth, but the course material was SOOO interesting!! 35% quiz, 35% hw, 15% participation, 15% project. Homeworks coded in R & weekly quizzes but she drops the lowest 2. Shes available for office hours and truly cares about her students! Amazing lectures

Jenny Tung is the best professor ever. Don't be scared away by bad reviews. Anyone who says otherwise is dumb. She is such a smart woman. I could not be luckier to have had her this semester. I learned so much, and I learned a lot of life skills. Professor Tung is a great person to know, she is smart and so kind and funny. I will miss her class.

She's a good lecturer and funny at times which makes class something to look forward to. She does go kind of fast, but explains things well. She is willing to answer questions but sometimes comes off kind of condescending, but I think it's unintentional and just how she talks.

she is a certified genius (macarthur genius grant) and lowkey too smart to be teaching intro bio. she talks super fast and expects everyone to understand but no one does. but her lecture slides are actually pretty good so if you go back and read them at a normal pace you should be fine. all her tests and quizzes are v fair.
Talks too fast and doesn't seem to care much. This class was a hot mess this semester
speaks at approximately 500 words/minute. by my calculations, jenny  motormouth. besides that she is nice.

Was hard to wrap my head around an unfamiliar subject + she often moved at a rapid pace. Learned alot of good important stuff, but she is clearly extremely brilliant and doesn't understand why we aren't as much; can be a bit condescending. Won't give answers but "nudges" you in the right direction. if you have thick skin, office hours are v helpful
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Jenny is an incredible researcher and professor. The class was difficult, with a heavy course-load and a tough but fair grading system. Her lessons were fascinating and clear and she made sure to pause frequently to clarify any doubts. She also constantly asked for feedback, was responsive over email and encouraged students to attend office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Tung is clearly brilliant, and I actually learned a good bit from this class. The class can definitely be worthwhile, if you have the right mindset. Her expectations are very highshe expects Masters/PhD quality work. It can be frustrating, but if you are willing to put in the time and take her feedback seriously, you can learn a lot from her!

In my first semester into college, this class definitely gave me an impression of how bad a professor can be. As part of focus program, classes should be fun and inspirational. However, she taught like she was teaching a bunch of Phd students and I never truly learned a thing. Also, she graded so harshly. Never cared how students did on this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Not only was she condescending, but she never truly cared about her students. Every day she saw her class come 40 minutes early to study for a potential pop quiz and wait in anguish for the lesson to begin. She saw students struggle over concepts which she never truly taught. She graded students like they were professors trying to get published.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Extremely condescending to students. Students are fearful to ask questions. Teaching style is super fast paced. Does not post lecture slides. Does not help students outside the classroom. Too busy doing research to care about students
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Professor Tung is really knowledgeable and a good lecturer, though she can be a bit condescending at times. Her class is relatively easy, and though she gives pop quizzes frequently, they're usually very basic and if you have reviewed your notes and the material once before class you'll be fine. She also doesn't post slides so it's best to show up.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Jenny Tung is the most condescending professor I have had at Duke. She rolls her eyes almost every time her students ask questions. Her lectures are extremely fast paced and dry. The course load is not too hard. You only really have to read when you have papers. 10/10 would not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Jenny Tung is an extremely difficult teacher to learn from. She goes through material at a VERY rapid pace, and does not care whether students grasp the material or not. Do not bother asking for help bc you will not get it. If you want to enjoy your semester, do not take her classes.

Do. not. take. classes. with. her. Please do yourself a favor and avoid her at all costs. She does not care about her students one bit. Zero. She is here for the research and that comes off in her teaching. She does not post lecture slides, is extremely condescending when students ask questions, and gives pop quizzes often. AVOID
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: The professor is amazing and is passionate about the class materials. The problem is that I have no interest in biology or evolutionary anthropology. Though she only requires four papers, without any requirements of citations or whatsoever, it's just hard to write something based on papers that I don't really understand. I didn't learn much.

Class is broken up into 4 units, each with a paper due that counts significantly towards final grade. Papers are graded toughly, but fairly, with large importance given to analysis/synthesis rather than summarizing papers read for the unit. Homework is light (usually reading 1-2 papers), and classes are interesting (usually lecture + discussion).
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Clearly an academic and class seems to be (maybe unintentionally) tailored to the select few that really get it. First 1/3 of course was on primate social structure, which was not very interesting. No tests, just papers which are graded somewhat toughly. Doesn't give grades lower than a B.

She can be intimidating, but she's nicer during office hours and she clearly cares about her students' learning. She's brilliant, but she talks to students as if they're her academic peers rather than toning it down to an undergrad level. I worked hard and learned a ton

She came off as intimidating & cold at 1st, but eventually she warmed up to the class & showed her humorous side. Office hours were like pulling teeth--she won't give direct answers but rather just nudges you in the right direction. She is the kind of prof who is so smart that she doesn't get why students can't keep up. Love her though & no tests!

The worst class I have taken in my academic career. Dr. Tyson was passive aggressive to students, had no clear plan for lectures, and no consistent syllabus. Long periods of silence were frequent as Tyson refused to lead conversations and judged students for their confusion. The work was unreasonable and there was no rubric for assignments.
One of the most inspirational professors I've had the opportunity to learn from. He's demanding in upper level courses, but the work is well worth it and extremely engaging.  Course was a UW Madison
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Took his course last semester with a strong interest in the course material. I enjoyed the readings (though sometimes it would be 500+ pages/week) and some of the classroom discussions, but thought Tyson was terrible. Completely unorganized and often hostile towards students. He didn't return any of the weekly papers or even the final paper.

He is a funny, interesting guy, but I would NOT take the class. He did not respond to 7 emails this semester or any text messages. He was constantly changing the syllabus, and seemed to have no idea what he was doing. He also assigned 250+ pages of reading/week, so beware.

Freedom stories is a really interesting class, and Professor Tyson is incredibly knowledgable about the topic. He's pretty scatterbrained and not that great at replying to e-mails, but he's really helpful when you can get in touch with him. There were no grades in the class until the final, but I'm pretty sure that everybody ended up with an A.

I took this class as a UNC student, but since dook is his primary university, I decided to rate him here. This was the BEST CLASS OF COLLEGE. It has changed my life. The reading is interesting, the classes are amazing. The test was somewhat difficult but not killer. He (and his TAs) are fair graders. TAKE THIS CLASS!

Great class! It included students from Duke, UNC, and NC Central, as well as members of the general Durham public. Held at an old, historic church in downtown Durham. I learned a lot about African-American history. The class was a unique and fun experience!

Awesome. Take his class. Easy-going and fun, Tyson leads some great discussions in class--even if he is a little disorganized. This class is like having a book club with your favorite uncle--and he cooks you dinner on the last day. Highly reccomended.
The Science of Happiness is the best class I have taken at Duke so far. Patty is a great lecturer and is very accessible outside of class.

Such a sweet professor, really cares about the material and is extremely knowledgeable about the field of positive psychology. Emphasizes effort and participation. Recommend this class so, so, SO much!

Patty is a wonderful, caring, and kind professor. Her lectures are excellent because you can focus on the content instead of stressing out about studying it. This made the class much more enjoyable to learn.
Patty is great!! Super kind and engaging. Definitely recommend

The best class and the best professor I've ever had. Patty made me look forward to going to class. Her TA, Jenna, is awesome too. If you see her teaching a class, definitely take it. The material is very applicable, and the class is very low-pressure. This class made me excited to learn instead of working for a grade. Patty is also so caring.

Wonderful professor, amazing class! Professor Cappellen not only is an expert in the field but also a great lecturer who can effectively convey her knowledge to her students. Moreover, she respects different opinions and creates an environment for discussion where every can engage comfortably. Her classes are definitely must-takes!

Prof. Van den Dool is the perfect professor if you are looking to improve your writing skills. She is very organized and clear with her expectations. Her grading is fair because she gives thorough feedback. Her classes are not reading heavy but more writing heavy. She is observant with details so her class really helped me to perfect my work.

Prof. van den Dool is always accessible beyond the classroom and gives timely feedback. I love how she explains the concepts so clearly and takes us together to review them every class. She also gives good feedbacks and is willing to changed based on students' feedbacks.

The prof is picky and requires you to go citations her way. The class is not engaging and only had around 5 students taking it, due to poor feedback from previous students. Taking Pubpol209 with VDD has been one of my worst experiences at Duke (Kunshan) University.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The writing assignments take up a lot of time and the prof is very slow at providing feedback. Powerpoints are not uploaded to Sakai and lectures are not recorded...
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The workload for Dr van den Dool's 2 credit class is too high and she is very strict about the details of your essay
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--So many papers

reviews.comment: Prof is nice and approachable, but the class is disorganized and takes a long time to return feedback. The workload is too high for a 2-credit class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor van den Dool is such a great professor. I truly enjoyed being in her recitation section for Global Challenges. The in-class activities that students did were applicable to real life and she is always willing to help students seeking help in any way - you just have to go to her office hours or send her an email. Highly recommended!

Came for an intro to public policy, got a class on how to write textbook summaries. If you didn't read the textbook you wouldn't know what was going on at all. Class was kinda boring and lectures didn't add anything new to what I read the night before. She's nice, but this class isn't something I'd recommend.

She is one of the greatest Professors out there, she knows how to encourage students to improve writing skills and critical thinking for more interesting discussions. I cannot imagine how a Professor will spend her office hour even longer than usual just to show you how to develop sharp arguments in your essay and even talking about Chinese policy.
Her focus on class participation is a plus and if you are really interested in the class, that shouldn't be too hard.

Having Prof. van den Dool at DKU was the best experience. She will give assignments that will surely improve your writing. Easily accessible outside classes via office hours or just emails. Though she was extremely busy outside classes (her research and conferences), she will make time to give you valuable and detailed feedbacks on your essay.

Professor Van den Dool is a nice professor, and with the many reading responses, her class really helps with your reading comprehension and writing skills. The workload is pretty hefty and she grades relatively hard. It makes a big difference to go to her office hours and ask her to look over your drafts or even just talk.

Professor van den dool is a wonderful person and professor. She's incredibly experienced with public policy matters, which made her perfect to teach a course about crisis management in the context of environmental policy. Her passion for China shows, and her strong focus on academic writing helped me greatly improve through this course.

Such an amazing and intelligent professor. You need to take one of her classes; it will truly change your life. Captivating lectures and very important content. This class inspired me to minor in sociology.

Awesome professor. Very engaging in class and online during remote learning. Make sure to read the articles assigned because there are short quizzes every class period. As long as you participate and do the readings, you should be set to get an A. Dr. Valentino is very helpful outside of class and always has the best interest of students in mind.

this prof has transitioned to online classes awesomely, her recorded lectures are so good and you can tell she really cares about her students, didn't know what to expect from this class, but it really made me think about things differently

Valentino's class was one of the best ones I've taken at Duke. Lectures were insightful & I looked forward to coming to class to hear her clearly explain a new facet of social inequality. Weekly discussions let us hear classmates' perspectives and facilitated a necessary exchange of ideas. This class made me start to consider sociology as a major.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Valentino was definitely an amazing Social Inequality professor. She is genuinely passionate about the subject, and she is very thoughtful and smart. I would highly recommend taking her class; it reaffirmed my love of sociology. Also, you don't have to be a sociology major to really enjoy & learn a lot in this class.

Yesenia is really nice and caring, but lectures could be more streamlined. I think the class has too many topics to cover, and narrowing down a focus onto a couple of projects and topics throughout the semester would help. Game development and learning are all done outside of class, but grading is very chill and the class is very fun.

Lectures are interesting and easy to follow. I thought the exam was fair and reflective of what was taught in class. Projects are definitely a time sink, but they're fun if you're into creative hands-on work. Just make sure you get a reliable team for the group project, it makes a big difference.
Interesting lectures and fun projects. Velasco explains things well, even for beginners. Just know there's no debugging support, so you'll need to troubleshoot on your own.
Probably the most fun I've had in a class in a long time
Solid class. The assignments are long but pretty interesting. A good amount of hands on work.

This instructor is genuinely the worst instructor I have ever had. She knows her stuff, but is extremely ineffective at teaching and explaining. She was so off topic in lecture and rambled about useless things. Lectures became completely pointless and the only way to actually learn was to read the textbook. Do not take a class from her.

Good professor, she explains concepts clearly and is engaging. The workload is high but manageable if you're on top of things, and the assignments are long but fun and useful. Highly recommend for anyone new to computer science.
Taking 201 now and I'm crying.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor often goes on rants during lecture and spends times on things that don't really matter. A hard class, and you basically have to learn it on your own.

Tbh lectures were pretty boring and would regurgitate the information we learned over the book. Some of the labs felt very useless; go to tutoring and you should be fine. There is a lot of reading, so be ready for that...
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor is super down-to-earth and makes learning code way less intimidating. Her office hours were actually helpful, I probably should have attended them more. If you're new to coding, this is the class you want. You'll become more confident and ready to tackle more advanced stuff like 201.

Poor professor that lectures an already standardized class. CS 101 is one of those classes that can be taught by anyone. Velasco is nice, but in a class with objective grading, you want effective - which she is not. 

tbh tho anyone can learn CS 101 content on their own. if you have to take it with her, just learn on your own.

You will not succeed if you just listen to her lectures. The lectures are virtually useless, and you will learn the course entirely independently by completing assignments and working through the interactive textbook. Other than that, she is a very nice person, but that's all. I have no CS background at all and the course is free by just reading.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Caring

reviews.comment: Incredibly sweet and caring professor. Lectures were ok, but could probably be condensed into 1/4 of the time. Even with absolutely no prior CS experience, this class was very easy. Tons of office hours and helpful TAs. Wildly generous grading with lots of extra credit and easy exams. Projects took more time and were more complex but doable.

She couldn't explain anything she was doing. I don't think she would pass our tests. Lecture is useless just read the textbook. Study old exams they are very similar. So many long assignments but they are manageable and you can use AI to help. Use the TAs they are a great resource.

Fairly easy class. Lectures aren't that useful, but you have to show up to get attendance. Don't push back doing programming assignments. If you stay on top of things, this class is light. For exams, just study previous exams as they are very similar.

Did not understand the point of showing up to class, lecture not helpful at all and the first 15 min usually pointless, just use other resources and watch videos. Exams were not that hard, especially when you are allowed a cheat sheet.
It was a good class. I would highly recommend professor Velasco. Lots of work so be prepared.
Amazing class. Learned so much about pythons and various serpents.
outrageous. absolutely NO pythons; looking forward to my music class next semester on c#
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: the only reason people pass this class is because they're utilizing everything except the professor. she's corny and has never heard of being efficient in her life. honestly worth it to skip class, lose the attendance points, and use your time more productively.
Boring lectures but very easy content. Lectures were not helpful though. Class might be more enjoyable with another professor.

Her class was very much a "if you get it you get, if you don't you don't." If you have a good handle on Computer Science you could honestly skip going to class a lot of the times and just read the textbook.

Came in with no coding experience whatsoever. Prof. Velasco is very corny but very kind and organized and gives lots of outside resources if you need help. Assignments grow increasingly harder and can be frustrating but very manageable. Grace periods for assignments and free extensions help. Textbook info (free&online)>>> lectures (recorded).

boring lectures, assignments do not teach you for exams, APTs can be helpful occasionally. Exams are nothing like previously written exams so you have nothing to base your studying off of. But since the concepts themselves are easy you can  get an A.

The lectures are boring and don't actually teach you anything. I learned everything from reading the textbook myself and completing the assignments on my own. She doesn't write the exams until like 24 hours before the exam is given so you walk in blindly. She makes mistakes on the exams too and lies about what will be on the exam.

Professor Velasco was amazing! She is so good at explaining tricky concepts, and she is incredibly kind and empathetic to her students. I had a difficult personal circumstance during the semester, but Professor Velasco was very accommodating and made sure I got back on track. One of the best profs in the department for sure.

Super kind and inclusive. Yesenia definitely understands that we are all beginners. Made me interested in pursuing computer science! With that said, this class is A LOT of work, there is something due like every day.

Stephanos cares a lot about his students and teaches in a pretty refreshing, intuitive way. His lectures are sometimes incoherent/unclear, but he listens to feedback, gives his own notes, and is available outside of class. Grading-wise, it's easy as he's very lenient, so with some outside work, you should be fine. Honestly a solid 353 pick.

Do not recommend taking diff eq with Venakides! While I learned the material, it was at the cost of MANY hours outside of lecture teaching myself. His lectures were very dry and his office hours were of no help. No TA's and had to go to other professors teaching the course to get materials. No Canvas and final grades were only based on tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Awful at lecturing, usually loses his thoughts and barely does any examples in class. Had to self-study the course with my peers, since he assigns so much homework (some stuff he didn't even cover). Grading was very unclear and inconsistent; pretty much depends on whether he likes you or not. With all due respect, he is too old and should retire.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The worst teacher I have ever had. Lectures are extremely incoherent, with the professor never once doing a single practice problem the entire semester. Concepts are impossible to understand without outside help. He is very old and has lapses in speech and forgets what he was talking about. Lessons are unstructured and he repeats them.

He really cares that his students understand the material, but the way he goes about ensuring this is one of the most painful lecture styles I have ever attended. He really is kind and knowledgable, but his age is getting to him and I can't recommend this class in good faith. Take it with someone else.
The professor has deep understanding about mathematical physics with excellent intuitions. Learn a lot from him!
Don't take 353 with him.

Professor Venakides is really concerned with having students think more about math rather than using formulas to solve problems. He is very much concerned with learning rather than focusing on grades. Unfortunately, this made the homework hard to grasp at times but at the end of the class you emerge with an understanding of the subject matter.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This was a tough class, but Professor Venakides was very willing to help and really cares about student learning. Going to office hours was really helpful. My only complaint was that the class could be a bit disorganized at times. Overall, would recommend taking this class with him, you will learn a lot about math and thinking outside the box.

Professor Venakides is not great for online learning. My entire class was very confused for almost the whole semester, and without in person reactions and connections, prof V was not able to gauge that lack of understanding well. Homework was tedious and difficult at times. Maybe better in person, but HARD pass for online.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: If you need examples to learn math, DO NOT take this class. Examples are nonexistent in his class. Homeworks are a large time commitment (3-7 hours) and when asking for feedback about the homework and how long it takes, he was happy to hear they are taking 7 hours because "we are thinking". Perhaps he is better in person, but online is a no go.

One of the best professors I have ever had. He cares so much about his students and their understanding of the material. He will take the time to explain things many times until you get it. Wonderful person and professor

Venakides was the first math professor I've had at Duke that I felt truly cares about his students' success and viewing math as a way of thinking rather than just memorizing formulas and patterns. He will go over anything you need in office hours, and not that many students go to them, so it's a great setting to learn in a small group. He's a gem!

Venakides cares that his students genuinely understand the material. He stops class regularly to ask if everyone is following and he wont proceed until a majority of the class understands what hes saying. A bit cooky and when he grades tests he barely marks the page so youll have to decipher what you did wrong. Overall friendly and informative.

Professor Venakides is a really kind man who tries his best to make sure students understand what's going on in class. He bounces ideas off of everyone and slowly builds up to the main concept in an interesting way. The class definitely isn't easy and the homework is difficult, but going for office hours helps a ton.

Prof. Venakides was super super helpful. He makes sure to boil down the most important concepts in diff eq. (solving standard PDEs and ODEs) so that you are very well prepared for the final (which plays a huge role in your grade). You're grades aren't posted on sakai or anything, but you can trust him to be fair.

Stephanos is like the grandfather I never had. Such a sweet, funny, genuine man. Tough, but will truly change how you think of mathematics in a broader, conceptual way. Unfortunately will not ever actually do the calculations/details of an example problem. Tries to relate to students (jokes about dorm parties, apps, etc. ) and is very interactive.
