His lectures are really repetitive and don't really follow the homework. Use his notes! GO TO OFFICE HOURS! He is so helpful and is really willing to work with you once you get to know him.
Classes are very insightful. Unlike other math classes which are like memorizing definitions and methods, this one is like a guided mystery tour in the field of ODE and PDE.

I'm kind of torn on this guy. On one hand, he really cares that you understand the material (especially concepts), and was helpful during his office hours. On the other hand, the material eventually gets so difficult that his teaching style made it really difficult for me to learn. Take his class if you're looking for a challenge.

Venakides' class does not follow the 107 syllabus.  The class seems a disorganized.  However, he is a good lecturer and requires thinking about the material at a higher level.  Thus, his class is no pushover.

Awesome teacher. It is all about self discovery. People who are too used to doing homework and memorizing math will not find his style easy. He forces you to be smarter. Class was like a discussion of topics. very interactive

Go to his office hours, since I'm convinced he assigns grades randomly or based on how well he know you. Only gave two tests and a final. One of the tests was only 30 minutes long. Must go to every class since he doesn't follow the book closely.
Worst teacher ever, has no syllabus and you never know what is next or what came before. Avoid him at all costs or you will regret it.
Horrible teacher, I never knew what was going to happen, pretty tough class, I definitly recommend against taking this class.
No syllabus -- No one knows how he assigns grades and he won't tell you how he assigns grade.
Will give you help if needed, TRIES to give pop tests.
THE worst professor ever....  Never take his class....
No Syllabus + No Homework= No Motivation. Do NOT take him unless you're prepared to learn an entire class on your own.
No Comments

Sam does an incredible job 'wrapping everything together.' Great lectures that connect accounting and finance to real-world applications. Helpful in preparation for exams, challenges his students in lectures, and cares about the quality of our learning experience. A huge learning curve for me, but I feel like I've mastered new skills in his course.

Professor Veraldi is the man. He has real life experience and actually knows what he is talking about. Econ at Duke is BS, if you want to learn about business, take a course with Veraldi. I learned more relevant information in 2 MMS courses than in 3 econs.

I really enjoyed his Managerial Finance class.  It's very straight-forward and his lectures are pertinent.  Unlike most professors, he acknowledges our lives outside the classroom, so that understanding makes the semester really painless.  Not to mention, he's a really cool guy and deeply knowledgeable about the field.

Verladi's a nice guy, but the class is a bit of a snore.  There's a fair amount of busy work which isn't particularly pertinent to anything.  Clear favoritism is evident in class discussions, but it won't affect your grade.  It's a mediocre course with nothing special about it.  In retrospect, I wish I had chosen a more enlightening elective.

Literally no lectures the entire semester; I learned nothing. Expected to perform a lot of grunt work (10+ hours every week!) for some tiny companies that will soon be bankrupt. No assignments so your grade is entirely determined by your classmates' ratings on two fifteen minute presentations.

Coolest Professor at Duke, hands down. Helps you in job search and acts like a dad sometimes. Nobody cares about your future as much as this guy if you go to him. He expects good quality work, but its not that hard at all. Great stories.

He is such a dude...talks a lot about beer and Satisfaction. Very easy class though...he grades easily and talks mostly about his personal experiences and general musings about the quality of Duke students. Easy class and good MMS credit if you can get over how different he is from every other professor here.

Definitely full of it most of the time.. obviously doesn't prepare for his classes much but he could talk his way out of anything. He's obviously been able to BS his way into a decent career and some solid ratings on here
He is awesome, class is unorganized but very easy to do well in. Entertaining class.

Great Teacher!!  Definately take this class if you have a chance, you actually learn important stuff.  Work is minimal and class goes by fast.  Funny and gets you excited about what you're learning about.
sam is definitely funny, really knowledgeable, and sweet - very helpful during job searches... plus the course is good and is useful if you're interested in a career in finance/consulting
HOTTTTTIIIEEE you really need to take this class
Very good professor, helpful and clear. Even though people suffered in the multiple choice tests, definitely worth the experience.
great professor, learn a lot about the real world.
His classes are basically a joke in terms of work, but fairly worthless as well.
He's HOT! He's NICE! He actually KNOWS what he's talking about. He focuses on what will be useful in the workplace. He's just freakin AWESOME!

Just suck up and get to know him, and you will do well.  It's not hard - he's hot.  A refreshing class at Duke, because he actually has a real job, teaches real world information, and isn't a tenured academic.
Veraldi is a great teacher and the nicest person. I would take any class with him. He makes every class fun. And he was in Bull Durham...the movie.
pop culture persuasion.   if you take a writing 20, take it with her.  the class was easy, grading was good, professor was extremely helpful, and the duke basketball players were in the class too
boring topic...nice teacher

BV is one of the nicest people I have met and easily the best teacher I have ever had. The workload is very reasonable, and as long as you put in the effort it is not hard to get an A. BV herself said she does not have a problem giving out lots of A's. Just go see her and take her suggestions about your papers and you will be fine.

She is by far one of nicest professors at Duke. She assigns a lot of work, however, and is not an easy A. But if you do put in the effort and go talk to her often for advice, you do get to learn a lot in class.

not as easy as everyone seems to think! It is a decent amount of work. That said, she is an amazing prof and cares about her students. You can essentially pick anything that interests you to write about as long as you support it. See her outside of class- she will tell you what direction to go in. Pay attention to her comments on short writings.

she's a good professor, although the coursework can get tedious and boring at times. definitely go to class (helps you get on her good side + she will clarify what she wants you to get from each reading). she is an easy grader, but she assigns ample amount of work at times. as long as you make an effort, you'll get a good grade.

Betsy is kind and helpful, but the class can be pretty boring. You can make whatever claim you want in your papers as long as you support it with some sort of evidence. The readings are pretty pointless, and the class is not intellectually stimulating, but Betsy is a fair grader and the class does demand a moderate amount of work.

Writing 20: Pop Culture Persuasion. BV is a fun, silly, and easily distracted teacher. But you learn great stuff without even realizing it. There is consistently a good amount of work, but it is not overwhelming. Meet with her one-on-one!!! Her comments guide you exactly where she wants your paper to go. Bring up CSI and she will love you.

She's a great professor to have for Writing 20. She assigns a reasonable amount of work (2 small, 1 big essay, with short 1-page responses each week) and really cares about teaching. The class (Pop Culture Persuasion) was less interesting than I expected, but still worthwhile. I definitely recommend Prof. Verhoeven.

Professor Verhoeven is a wonderful professor!  The class is not an easy A, but if you do the work and talk to her, she is very understandable and willing to help you out.  She really cares about her students.  Take this class with her, you will not regret it!  Schedule meetings with her--her comments are extremely valuable as you revise your papers

Took Writing the People's Identity. extremely easy.  less work than most W20 courses.  each time you meet with her about the final paper, she will pretty much tell you how much more work you need to do for an A.  looks for positive aspects in everyone's writing.
believe me its no free A class.  So boring. lots of sh*t to write. i did all the work and still got a C. wtf

Great Prof, Betsy is very easy! Good wr 20 class..just go to class, read most of the material, don't even worry about partcipating that often. Do your 3 page papers  on time (it's not hard!) and see her a lot about your final paper-- you WILL get an A
Great teacher.  Changed her name to Verhoeven though.

Took her to Native American Lit. Perhaps the easiest class I've taken here, not because the class doesn't involve a moderate amount of work, but because Betsy is simple a great professor and a great person. Get to know her and she CANNOT give you a bad grade. Write the papers and you won't go wrong.
She's really sweet, and an easy grader. Class can get a little boring though because you don't really talk about anything, and don't usually have to take notes. Books are weird.
Betsy was one of the best teacher's I have had at Duke so far! She is so nice, so willing to help you and she really wants to give A's if you work for it. Take her class you'll love it!

Always peppy and happy, very encouraging.  Will even give you A's even if you fall asleep in front of her because she literally loves all of her students and class participation does not count.  Betsy rocks our world, and we wish we were freshmen to take her class again!!!!!!
Betsy's really nice and helpful.  Not too hard of a grader and very enthusiastic about the field.
Very good teacher, not overly challenging.  Easy A.
Not hard to get a good grade if you do the work.

Writing 20 - Native American Literature was easy for me. Loads of reading and lots of writing (~3pg-paper every week) but relatively easy grading for writing. Prof Betsy's really nice, always cheery. Material did not really interest me, but it's not a bad class.
This was a decent course overall. Midterms are memorization-based and somewhat unforgiving, however.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I really liked John (+ Nico) but this class was boring and test heavy. It did teach me a lot about the impacts of climate change on oceans, but I the tests did not assess my knowledge well. Get ready to memorize random facts and stats. The DUML trip was a highlight of this class (but if you're looking for an easy A marsci class, take 205 instead).
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Loved this class! It's really chill and includes a trip to the marine lab. You're graded on a short reflection of a reading once a week (less than 250 words), a 15 min group presentation, a midterm on basic knowledge, and a final paper. If you need a chill class I would recommend. John is also really nice and knows a lot about marine policy.
John is one of the sweetest professors at Duke. He's a top expert in his field and has worked for the World Bank on numerous projects and collaborations with other notable institutions.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Vidra is genuinely the kindest, sweetest professor I have ever had. Cares deeply about her students. The class is unique but it is extremely manageable and very little work outside of class. There is also a great field trip which was a semester highlight. Highly, highly recommend

By far the worst class and professor I have ever had. Extremely easy, but a frustrating waste of time. The class is so broad that we didn't learn anything at all. Vidra is not a subject expert and it often felt like I knew more than she did about the topics she attempted to talk about. Much of the class was random grad student guest speakers

The class is so easy that it's kind of a joke but also sort of an insult to the students who want to genuinely learn. The professor isn't accommodating, understanding or available outside of class. would love to have her actually practice the empathy she claims to have. Syllabus and grading materials should be clearly outlined at the beg of the sem

Professor Vidra was really good!! The class was super easy, and the main emphasis was on furthering your literacy on how to get information about the climate through news, etc. I almost wish that more was covered, but it was a great intro class and the professor is excellent and very caring. There were a lot of cool activities and speakers too.

The class was easy but you do need to attend because she does pop quizzes almost every class. The quizzes aren't hard they are just for attendance. She has a big presentation you have to attend on the Monday before Thanksgiving which is annoying and she is not willing to budge on moving it. Overall though the class isn't bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Vidra is very nice and the class is easy but impactful. There are some pop quizzes but as long as you skim the reading you'll be fine, it's mostly for attendance. We did have an activity that was worth 5% of our final grade on the Monday of Thanksgiving break which was annoying. Would recommend for an easy NS credit!
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I enrolled in the class a week and half into the year due to dropping another class and add environmental science. Before I enrolled, the class already had 2 attendance quizzes. I was given two zeros for these assignments and I wasn't even in the class yet. I sent her an email explaining my situation and she didn't care.
Evnrion 102 is so easy a 5th grader could pass it. Not worth the time really, but Vidra is pretty nice. Some of the assignments are interesting but lots of it is busy work
Both Professor Vidra and the TA's were excellent. Definitely an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Loved Professor Vidra. She is very caring and understanding, and is a great person to talk to. The class was interesting, but a good amount of the content is similar to AP Envisci. A lot of the assignments were graded by TA's, and the grading was inconsistent between them, but it is very easy to get an A in the class.

Workload was super manageable, no tests so your grade is mainly from reflection papers, a final project, and short quizzes she gives in class. Dr. Vidra is an extremely caring and sweet person, definitely get to genuinely know her during her office hours! Super chill and great class for an intro to environmetnal science

Professor Vidra was a very caring, knowledgeable, and passionate professor. However, the tests were extremely difficult and there were many obscure questions that were not focused on major key concepts but rather minute details from a lecture. Definitely not an easy class to get rid of an NS credit.

3 midterms, daily lectures, with certain lessons being a group discussion in place of the lectures. really intelligent, but sometimes glosses over topics that pop up on the midterms - I'd review key case studies and vocab in anticipation of every midterm to score well. midterms and assignments are mostly free response. fun class overall!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The class is a good pick for an NS credit. There is not a ton of policy information. Attendance is not taken for lectures, but you need to attend to do well on lectures. Participation is based on attending a discussion. The majority of your grade is determined by three tests that are heavily based on lectures (70%). She is a really nice professor!

Not a super hard class, but insanely boring unless you're crazy about environmental science. Attendance isn't mandatory but if you skip lectures you'll be completely lost. There's a lot of readings and the exams cover a lot of material so expect a lot of studying. Dr. Vidra is super sweet though and very passionate about what she's teaching.

Dr. Vidra is very kind, and she is clearly passionate about what she does. Her class is easy as long as you show up, since her tests definitely cover content not in the textbook. Most of the class content is pretty common-sense despite this being my first enviro class, so my biggest critique would be not learning a ton. Good pick for NS credit
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Professor Vidra is a really great professor for those interested Environmental Science and restoration ecology. She is accessible outside of class to help students find their passions within the field. Tests matter a lot in the class and the questions can be specific, but with sufficient review of readings, you will be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Vidra is a nice person but her lectures are boring and the tests tend to be super specific. Not necessarily the easiest NS.
Tests can be hard. Office hours aren't helpful. One time a student asked her about something, and instead of answering she replied to the whole class: "what do you think?"

As someone who is not scientifically inclined, this class was interesting but not necessarily easy. You have to put in time to study for the 3 tests. Some lectures are more better than others, but Professor Vidra is very knowledgeable and passionate about what she teaches. The readings are important for tests but not to understand lectures.

I enjoyed Professor Vidras class and found that she was very personable and accessible although I never went to her office hours. Not necessarily an easy A, but you can get one if you work for it. Her tests have weirdly specific questions but are not impossible by any means.

pretty easy class. make sure to participate in discussion/lecture, even though tbh i didn't and still did fine. make sure to go to class because exams are pretty specific on stuff she mentions in lecture. when in doubt, the go-to examples are: the red cockaded woodpecker, zebra mussels, galapagos tortoises, coral reefs, or north carolina hogs

Relates a lot of the material to current day topics. Didn't use the textbook very much. Final grade is 25% first midterm, 30% second midterm, 15% discussion participation, 30% final exam. All the exams are short answer and essay. Would recommend getting a person to study with and go over case studies/examples. Take good notes. Love her as a person!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Professor Vidra is so so nice! Her class was extremely interesting and not too hard. Just make sure you take very good notes and be prepared to review for the midterm much earlier than when it's scheduled. Lots of guest lecturers.

I enjoyed this course, as did my friends in the class. She was very knowledgeable and didn't work through material too quickly. The class is organized generally by case studies. You can tell she is passionate about the environment which is helpful. The exams are difficult and specific, so lots of studying doesn't always equal passing.
reviews.rating_tags: Tests? Not many--EXTRA CREDIT--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Was not expecting this class to be so difficult. It is very lecture heavy and if you miss a lecture you 100% need to get notes. Be careful of small homeworks because you will lose marks if you dont turn them in and tests are very obscure and specific and more based on how closely you do the reading or listen to lectures, not based on the course.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Class can be a bit boring sometimes. Let's just say, I love her more than her class!

Vidra is a caring person who will do her best to help her students. If you have any questions or are struggling in the class talk to her. She will help you get a good grade. Reading helps to understand the lectures although you can just read the end of chapter summaries. Tests are really specific so find a study group. Don't skip the discussions.
Get's a lot of flak, really cool professor and she scaled down her class a lot from past reviews. Fairly easy if you actually show up to class

She's a really nice person and offers a lot of EC but she recently changed the course and made the tests a lot tougher. You have to go to lectures and do the work but still, the tests are hard and the questions are crazy specific. Tough TA graders can kill you so take every opportunity outside of tests to help your grade.

Tests are hard, but workload is small. Can't vouch for how helpful she is because I didn't go to office hours. Good class for developing an interest in environmental science, but can be painful if you don't like the subject at all. Difficulty of the tests depends greatly on the TAs. And god bless the EC opportunities.

Vidra is a phenomenal, passionate lecturer, and I learned a TON from this class. While tests are tough and extremely specific (attendance and attentively doing ALL readings are musts for doing well), she is extremely helpful and just an overall really kind and interesting person, so definitely drop into her office hours before tests.

Vidra was by far my favorite professor this semester. She personalizes the material to her own life and makes it relevant to yours, rarely gives busy work, and offers fun and easy extra credit opportunities. Overall a pretty chill grader. The tests are rough though so definitely get a couple of people in the class to study with.

Interesting class and material, and professor Virdra is great. However, the final grade mostly rides on the three midterms which were really hard (and not curved). Would have appreciated either more tests or more assignments so the tests counted for less.
Not an easy NS. Vidra seems nice but her tests are ridiculous. Tests are based on the lectures (and readings) so you HAVE to go to class, but even if you go to every  class, the tests won't be easy.

Tests are ridiculously specific and graded really tough.  As someone only sort of interested in the subject, it seemed really like an unfairly hard class.  The lectures make it seem easy and clear-cut, but the way the tests are graded is ruthless.  Would never recommend this class to anyone.
Great teacher.
Great intro environment teacher, I would definitely recommend her. Tests could be a bit difficult, but she offers a good amount of EC and will make herself available to you for any advice.

Vidra is always there for you if you make the effort. The course is interesting and relevant. She is a wonderful professor (grades extremely fairly) and is very approachable. Her enthusiasm has made me want to take more classes in the department. Would recommend her to anyone, including those looking for an easy natural science credit.
Professor Vidra is very good in her field however I found that she was just an OK teacher. Nothing too extraordinary but not bad either.
I never went to class, but when I did, I learned a lot from Dr. Vidra. She was very enthusiastic and engaging, and the course was easy and very manageable.

Professor Vidra's lectures were extremely engaging and intriguing. She is extremely approachable and incredibly nice. The class atmosphere was so comfortable and her efforts to integrate both science and policy created a big picture approach that made the subject interesting, rather than getting boggled down in unimportant details. A must take!

She's a really great professor. Most intro courses require a lot of memorization and very little in-depth exploration, but this course was completely the opposite! Professor Vidra focused on concepts that are relevant to the world today, and I feel like I learned more/connected with the material more because of it. Take a course with her.

Great lecturer. Super passionate about the material and really tries to make it interesting for the students. Fairly easy tests, a lot of big picture questions with much smaller focus on little facts. Would reccomend whether or not are interested in the subject or even like science. Just really great class and professor!
Great professor and awesome person. Super helpful and personable. Extremely knowledgeable, yet humble--everything you could want in a professor. Take a class with her!!!
Rebecca is a great professor. She's really enthusiastic about what she teaches and class discussions are always interesting. I would really recommend this class or her as a professor in general

Awesome professor. Very down to earth, creates sincerely interesting class discussions. Extremely friendly and helpful! Invited us to her house for dinner at the end of the course. Course was pretty easy, and while I didn't think I would be that interested in the material (ethics) I actually learned quite a bit.
I really enjoy this class.  The amount of work is reasonable.  Good grades guaranteed if you work :)
Great professor...really enthusiastic about her work and light hearted.  Thoroughly enjoyed the class!
Very knowledgeable, both about writing and environmental issues! Highly recommended!
Good teacher.  Challenging, but that helped my writing.
Dr. Vidra did a great job of relating the material to everyday concepts to help us truly understand it
Dr. Vidra really helps her students learn to write about topics that are interesting. She is always ready to provide feedback and is fun to have in class. I'd definitely recommend her!

Huge letdown as a professor. Doesn't know much about writing, and was definitely from the bottom of the barrell that Duke usually scrapes up to teach this class. Unhelpful and unclear, and grades based on how much she likes you, not the quality of your work.

I loved this class!Prof. Vidra was great and really helped my writing with the revisions. Each paper had a different aspect of writing to focus on which was great!Her class also helped me with papers for other science classes at Duke and my other profs noticed.I would def take another class with her. She was clear on her assignments and very fair.
Helps you through most of your work but does grade pretty hard. take the class if you dont want too much work but be prepared for an average grade in the class.
This class was one of my favorites.  Professor Vidra is really nice!

I have mixed feelings about her. She was very enthusiastic, but classes were boring. The subject matter was too hard to form an opinion on. Both sides of every argument we covered all used technical data you cant possibly fully comprehend. Don't worry about grades. She hammered me on all my papers, but then gave me an A which I didn't deserve.

She seems nice at first but once she hands you back a paper of yours you'll want to break something.  (I broke my room mates chair.)  The work load isn't a lot but you wont get a good grade. She'll say the class is easy the first two weeks so you don't drop, but you should! Avoid her classes at all costs.
Enjoyable class as long as you are interested in the Environment.
easy and receptive, but bOring material, helped me write better though
No Comments

The class is pretty easy. She is not very helpful with papers. She'll say it's fine and good in conferences. Yet she really hammers down on you when she grades it. Discussions are engagingand she is knowledgable on her subject matter. But mediocre teacher for a mediocre class.

Loved loved loved her. So challenging, but very intellectually stimulating. There was a lot of reading, but definitely worth it, and everything tied in really well. The readings were a must, it was a lot, but totally worth it.
Great professor. Very knowledgable and approachable.
Great experience with this professor. Considerate of students and very knowledgeable about the subject.
He gave very clear lectures and was a fair grader on the exams.

The professor is inspirational for organizing a really amazing lecture. Admittedly, the lecture is somewhat challenging, but it's very inspiring and makes you think deeply about statistics. If you have a relatively strong stats foundation and are looking for an even better insight into statistics and math, this professor is outstanding!

The class was 70% tests and 30% homework - the HW was free grades for the most part but took a lot of time. The class itself is very difficult and there's limited resources/examples that were given to help us. He curves very generously to make sure no one fails fails, but its a very difficult class. Lectures are useful but his handwriting is awful.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The class is really test heavy (1 midterm, 2 quizzes, final), and the homework can be very challenging and time consuming. Office hours is very helpful to succeed in this class. The professor explained difficult concepts in a clear way and reading the textbook helped solidify my knowledge.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Bayesian is hard, and unfortunately, Alex failed to make it easier. He is obviously v smart, but assumes his students are just as smart and skips over explanations/goes too fast. And his handwriting sucks! But he's helpful in OH, and will patiently walk through concepts with you. It seems bad at first, but concepts usually makes sense by exam time.

One of the hardest classes I've taken at Duke. Homework gets insanely hard towards the end of the semester. Online final is OK. Make sure you go to his exam review sessions every time, because he doesn't post most of his slides on Sakai.
He made STA360 exceedingly hard
DO NOT TAKE STA360 WITH HIM! DO NOT!

I don't think anyone in his class actually has any idea what is happening; it's just him talking and there is one Asian girl at the front of the class asking questions. It is a hilarious class in the sense that when you lose the will to live anything can seem funny.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Overall, it's a rough class. He assumes students have a very thorough understanding of probability theory, and even when they don't, he proceeds forward. He is a nice guy and answers questions but loses much of the class quickly (about half the class typically drops). The book is very important.
The hardest exams I've ever taken in my life. Indeed you can learn a lot from this class but you have to spend a LOT OF time on studying.

If you have the opportunity to take Bayesian with Volfovsky, you should. Not an easy class, but he strives to understand common difficulties faced by students and take those into consideration in his teaching and grading. Also emphasizes the intellectual side of the subject by assigning several relevant academic papers, which I liked.

Shira was a great professor for calc 1. She really cares for students and gives an incredible amount of resources in preparation for tests. There's over 7 practice tests for each midterm, and there's more than enough for you to get the practice you need to get an A. She's super responsive and accessible, and just the best.

I am not a math person and I already took calc in high school with a TERRIBLE professor, so I can confidently say that Shira was honestly great. She gave SO many resources for practice before exams. I will say however, if you know that you struggle with math, you need to prepare yourself to do a lot of extra practice outside of class.

The class was difficult but Prof.Shira was available for office hours frequently, even while on maternity leave. She works hard to care for her students and be there to help you do your best. Office hours are a must, and the practice tests and previous exams are worth the time to do well on tests. Don't be afraid to ask for help.

Math classes are infamously difficult at Duke, & Calc 111 is a class that most majors have to take, so definitely be grateful that Professor Viel is teaching it! She very clearly cares about her students and provides SO many resources to practice/seek help. Definitely difficult/time consuming - especially the tests - but Shira's a great professor.

Negative reviews are prob just those wanting an easy QS and didn't like that they actually had to work. Shira is the most caring professor; she learns everyone's names & responds immediately to emails/Ed, even on maternity leave! You have to get used to the picky grading, but the tests and assignments are fair. You'll do fine if you put in effort.

Professor Shira explains concepts too quickly, making it hard to follow. I had to learn most of the material on my own because her explanations lacked clarity. The practice exams are VERY different from the actual exams, and she does not prepare you for the final at all, which is pretty difficult.

Way too difficult for Calc 1. I had credit for the class and still opted to take it and boy was that a mistake. The content covered is just over the top and the way in which its explained is extremely over-complicated. The methods you are forced to use to analyze and solve problems to get credit are overly redundant and annoying.

WONDERFUL PROFESSOR! She explains things well and is very patient. The reason I didn't do amazing in the course was due to the content's difficulty, but she was incredibly helpful. Would definitely recommend.
Engaging, clear lecturer

Honestly, I am NOT a math person and don't get me wrong, P.Viel was a good teacher (a bit confusing at times but), but I felt I put so much effort into this class and did so many practice tests and it still was not enough. Previous calc knowledge in high school goes A LONGG WAY. Just do not fall behind and ask every single question in your head,

Viel has lectures that overcomplicate the topics and homework that few could do without some TA assistance. While there are a lot of help hours, it feels unnecessary for a class that many took in high school. Class is saved by her extra credit policies

Professor Shira is amazing! She cares a lot about her students and is a good lecturer with a lot of energy. Her class is hard, but there are ample resources to succeed in the class if you are motivated. I would highly recommend taking this course with Professor Shira and taking her to FLUNCH!

I was a very strong math student in high school, but Duke's math difficulty level is just insane. Although this is not Professor Viel's fault, I do believe that she could have done some things better. The lecture questions and even some of the homework/lab questions were far easier than the midterms.

The class's homework structure is probably the dumbest thing I've ever experienced. You get weekly P-Sets, have exams, and then have to write an essay, AN ESSAY. Her teaching style is poor to the point that she had me second guessing derivatives. Sure I passed the class but no matter if I went to office hours or the math help room I was doomed.

Shira is very kind and clearly passionate about teaching. Lectures are recorded and attendance isn't required, so I didn't show up to any lectures yet she still learned my name and said hello to me on test days. The grade is very test heavy, but she curved it a little at the end of the semester and allowed test corrections for the first two tests.
Shira is a great professor! Math, especially calculus, is difficult at Duke, but Shira is approachable, kind, and caring which makes all the difference.

Shira is such a sweet woman! She cares deeply about her students doing well and does do her best to ensure that they do. That being said, her tests are pretty hard, and the course relies heavily on your grade on those. Additionally, the homework is graded with a lot of scrutiny but the TA's in the Math Help Room will help you do very well on those.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Shira is an AMAZING math professor and person. She cares so much about her students and is so open to helping you outside of the classroom. Some tests are challenging, but Shira does an amazing job at explaining concepts and how it applies to the world. She is the best! Take advantage of help room and her office hours! One of my favorite classes
Really tough class and the tests are especially killer.

Prof Shira was a great calculus professor, although she taught Calc 1 her class was definitely challenging and work heavy. However, there are several resources Prof. Shira provides to help her students. In order to do well on the homework and tests be prepared to study and attend any office hours if necessary.

Professor Viel has an attitude that can be compared to Dolores Umbridge's in the Harry Potter books. She's very nice but that gets a little bit annoying sometimes. Tests are pretty hard, and important new material gets covered in the last 10 minutes of the class, thus it can be confusing. Nonetheless, you learn a lot from this course.

Shira is a very sweet person but I found her leaving vital parts of lecture to the last 15 minutes too much. She cares to learn names even in a lecture hall. Take advantage of the recorded lectures, strong TAs, and Math Help Room. The tests are hard (even if you took calc before) but fair and you can correct the first 2 for half credit back.

Math 111L is a very demanding class, even if you have taken calc before coming in. The tests are 75% of the grade and are very challenging, even if you study for hours leading up. I think Prof. Shira does care about her students, but she often saves the hardest material for the last 5 minutes when nobody understands what's been said.

Professor Viel saves all the hardest problems for the end of lecture, grades on every minor detail, and does not understand your questions when you ask her. Tests are way harder than anything you learn in class; however, the TAs and the Math Help Room make the class bearable. Good luck.

She often speeds up and runs out of time during lectures but is a decent lecturer. Lectures and notes are often available online, but occasionally there is no sound for the video. Tests are difficult and focus a lot on notation and very particular applications of the derivative. Very difficult class even after taking calc 2 in high school.

I loved taking MATH 111 with Shira. Her grading is tough but she clearly outlines her expectations and is also super willing to help you. If you put in the effort and go to office hours you'll be fine. Before tests, take advantage of practice problems and again go to office hours. If you took AP Calc in high school the class will be pretty easy.

Avoid math at Duke unless needed, but if you have to take it, take 111 with Shira! 111 is difficult, even after taking Calc BC in high school, so be prepared to spend a lot of time doing HW and labs. However, Shira is genuinely so compassionate, cares about her students, and is extremely accessible outside of class on Ed and in OH. She's the best!

Pretty sure the previous few ratings are just students complaining because they got bad grades. Prof Viel is an awesome lecturer that deserves way more credit for teaching Calc 1 the way she did. Definitely recommend taking the course with her, you will learn a lot. The final was slightly challenging, but 100% doable if you studied properly.
Super difficult grader, final is difficult and hard to prep for, grad TAs make the quality of instruction unstandardized

Dr. Viel has this overly cheery attitude that can become quite annoying at times. She treats us like we're children. There was one class where she kept quoting Frozen 2 and I wanted to tell her, we are adults and not the right audience for this. However, her annoying personality doesn't make her a bad professor, her poor teaching skills do.
Awful professor. Wouldn't help out and would blatantly ignore my requests in my email. Just terrible, I am appalled.
That final clapped me ngl. Even if u study it will be hard

Shira is an amazing professor! Math 111 is a difficult course, but hard work pays off. Shira cares about her students and wants to do everything she can to help them succeed. Make sure that you understand the content thoroughly by utilizing the resources available to you (recorded and in-person lectures, office hours, and the help room).

Calc is hard to make appealing, but Prof. Viel goes above and beyond in terms of making the transition from high school to college calculus as pain-free as possible. My one regret is that I didn't show up to most of the lectures. If you plan on taking this class, I highly recommend trying your best to show up for the majority of lectures.

She is such a nice professor who will make you enjoy learning calculus. There were opportunities to earn points back on the tests, which was useful for improving your grade. Lectures were interesting, and she was easily accessible during and after class. Take this course with her!

Viel is very nice, really cares about her students. Her lectures are well done, although sometimes she spends too long on the wrong things (overall very helpful though). Tests don't seem to correlate to lectures very well, are a lot more difficult and require a lot of application of info. Offers several easy extra credit opportunities.

SHIRA IS AMAZING! The class was hard but what else can you expect from Calculus at Duke. I HIGHLY recommend taking any class w her. She is an amazIng professor and an even better human being. LOVE U SHIRA!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Shira makes herself incredibly accessible outside of class. I found her lectures to be helpful for a general overview of the topics, and the lab problem sets to be more specific. Be sure to set reminders for the readiness assurance assignments, or you can miss them.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Shira is incredible! If you have to take Calc 1 at Duke, take it with her! I learned so much in this class, and I really enjoyed our lab section. Our TAs were so much fun and the group work was a good time. I actually feel like I understand why calculus works after taking this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Shira is amazing inside and outside class. Math at Duke is quite difficult and she is aware of this so she tries her best to help in office hours. The lectures are important so if you miss make sure to watch them online as she does record them. You will pass and if you need extra practice do the tb problems, solve the labs and rewatch recordings.

Shira is very nice, but the class is hard. it moves quickly and goes into a lot of deep random knowledge. 3 tests and a final, for the first 2 tests you can do corrections which gets you half points back which is nice. 2 lab assignments per week with lab group, not too long. Take it if required for your major, but its not a fun class.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Group projects

reviews.comment: The most understanding professor I had my first semester. Gave an abundant of extra credit opportunities, and recorded lectures. Textbook is only needed if you want to use it for optional homework questions, and can be found online. Gave plenty of test review material. If you are deciding between 105 and 111, take 111.

I took this class online S/U because of COVID. Dr. Viel seems nice and explains concepts well in her lectures. HOWEVER, the new grading scale was harsh. On the hw, you have to go beyond showing your work and REALLY EXPLAIN your process to receive credit. Also, I often ran out of time on quizzes. Good prof. Hard class. Retakes saved me.

This class, due to COVID, was flipped and asynchronous. In spite of the difficult circumstances, Dr. Viel and her instructional team made things manageble and straightforward. Duke math is notoriously difficult, but she made it very doable.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: One of the best professors I have ever had at Duke. She was so accessible outside of class and it was very clear that everything she does is for the students. Calculus is already hard but she teaches it in a way that makes sense. I owe my grade entirely to her and the amazing effort that she put in to support her students.

Super great professor. Duke math has a reputation of being challenging to say the least, and this class is no exception. However, if you have to take mutli, take it with Viel. Her teaching style was great, and she is extremely willing to help out anyone who needs it.

Math is hard as is. Shira makes the material so accessible. She LOVES her kids and is so caring, it shows. However, exams are tough so you need to keep up with lectures and do the HW to do well. Show up to office hours and put in the extra effort - it will pay off. Love you Shira!

Shira is the most helpful prof I've ever had at Duke. Duke math is brutal, Math 111 is the hardest class I've taken, and I struggled, but I never felt like it was Shira's fault. She answered every question I had and genuinely wanted me to succeed. If you take 111, try and get her. Her tests can be brutal, but the final will be easy in comparison.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Shira Viel is one of my favorite professors at Duke. She is incredibly kind, but knows when to put her foot down. Her flexibility and commitment to teaching really shine through. She helps students who want to be there. She's a phenomenal lecturer, humble, and really does a good job of understanding what students are confused about. Loved her!

Professor Viel is so enthusiastic about math, and it comes off in her lectures. Her mood is infectious, and she's super understanding and caring. Quizzes and exams are very reasonable, she doesn't try to throw curveballs at you. Great class, take it instead of 212 if you can.

Duke math is pretty brutal, but Dr. Viel is the exception. If you can avoid 212 by taking 202, do it. Shira is so caring and really wants you to learn, so she gives plenty of opportunities to do well. There are weekly quizzes but good quiz grades replace bad quiz averages. Shira posts all her lectures and slides online so if you miss not a big deal

Shira's lectures are very clear and have lots of examples to help you understand. There are weekly quizzes, but the questions are similar to homework and the exams, so the exams are fairly manageable and expected if you do the homework. The final is much harder, but Shira curves it. Shira would upload lecture videos, so attendance isn't necessary.

Shira is, without a doubt, the best math professor I've had. Her lectures make sense and have lots of examples. There are weekly quizzes and three major tests which match her lectures, so there aren't any surprises on assessments. If you want to do well in her class, definitely go to office hours! She's incredible, humorous, and open to feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Shira is one of the best teachers I've had at Duke. She made calculus understandable which is a concept thats almost unheard of. Though the tests are hard, she was a very understanding teacher and always accepted feedback on how the class could improve. I recommend going to office hours if you don't understand something as she will take care of you

Shira really cares about her students and is pretty good at explaining concepts. The class itself is hard because of the tests she makes. Definitely get to know her outside of class because she decides final grades. The curve is pretty generous. Take math with her if possible.

I would say that she is definitely a super-caring prof and an amazing human being, but as a math teacher she's okayish. Her tests are insanely hard for no reason (there are no math majors in this class) and her presentations are not that helpful always. Make sure you go to OH and are on top of the material at all times-- it's where I messed up lol
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Shira is an amazing professor who really cares about her students - go to office hours and get to know her (bc she decides final grades). Always willing to help and has thorough, clear lectures. There are weekly quizzes that keep you on top of material. Definitely got harder as the semester went on - the material isn't that hard but the exams are

Shira Viel is the bomb. Super good at explaining things, so receptive to any kind of feedback (she literally changed the way she taught class halfway through because of survey responses). Definitely go to office hours, she is so nice and helpful! Actually makes an effort to know names and be personable.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Viel is honestly the most caring, sweet, and wonderful professor. Yes, her tests are hard, but what else do you expect from college calculus? She is so kind and so willing to help you outside of class. Her office hours are very helpful, and she has clear expectations. 10/10 take her for Math 111!

Dr. Viel is caring, very authentic, and an inspiring teacher. However, the material for Math 111L is very challenging and most of the exams are extremely difficult to do well on. Overall, Dr. Viel is a fabulous teacher and I highly recommend taking Math 111 with her if you can get into her section.
Amazingly happy human being. Permanent smile. She explains concepts beautifully. Her tests are hard. Really hard. But she's all about partial credit.

Prof Weissglass used a flipped classroom model for this formal logic class, so grade was based on the challenges completed in class and students read textbook themselves. This is quite creative and arguably better than exams given this subject. Otherwise, he is very caring for students and is always happy to have a chat
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I would suggest not taking his classes. He seems to go to another extreme after he said that he did not want students to think of him as an easy grader...... And his grading criteria are vague and are opposite to the criteria of other ETHLDR201 professors. I took his class in the 2020 fall, best luck to those taking his classes.

Prof Weissglass facilitated some of the most engaging conversations and student-led class discussions of my college career. He wasn't shy about pushing the envelope and getting us out of our comfort zones (in a great way).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Tough grader with great standard deviations! Without clear grading criteria! Some students got insanely high score, but many are very very low! Cautious!

Prof Weissglass made this class (begrudgingly taken at 7 AM on Mondays and 8 PM Wednesdays) lively and fun—his questions surrounding the ethics of love, work, and community were relevant, and the discussions he facilitated were engaging. Our class brought students from a variety of backgrounds and perspectives to bear.

Prof. Weissglass really pushes you to dig deep into your thoughts. He also really wants you to focus on learning rather than on your grade by giving you multiply opportunities to do rewrites and learn from previous experiences. He is always available for his students and wants to help in anyway he can.
Amazing prof. Easily ranks in the top 5 at DKU. A real joy to have conversations with.

Weissglass is a professor that actually cares about students, and it is apparent as soon as you meet him. He connects you with other resources, takes into account student feedback for his classes, and explains things very well if you don't understand them. I was never afraid to share my ideas, and he helped me think in new ways. 11/10 professor.

She's a cool person, an easy grader, and approachable outside of the classroom.

Reading could be a lot and hard, but she always explains confusing things clearly in class, and you'll definitely gain a lot of different perspectives and new inspirations. Materials are well chosen and structured, and you'd know she's super familiar with all of them.

Kathi is the BEST! She is SO smart and really knows how to lead a class discussion. I took GSF199 with her and genuinely looked forward to every class. 5 papers spread out throughout the semester was not bad at all and she's an easy grader. DO the readings! They are so important and the discussions are much more insightful if you're prepared.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very interesting class and I learned so much! Prof Weeks has interesting lectures and really makes the class great
Good lecturer and interesting class topic. The class is graded on participation and 4 papers. You need to do at least some of the readings and participate at least a once per class to be successful.

Professor Weeks starts really compelling conversations in her class--you will never hear a pin drop! She is also very willing to meet with you outside of class to brainstorm for your papers (well through zoom).
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Kathi is a VERY nice woman, but a harsh grader. Students should agree w/ her viewpoints on essays. Had a paper every week.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Kathi Weeks IS AMAZING!! I took her class Fall 2019 and she literally made me a GSF minor because she's so passionate about what she teaches. If you're looking for a class to change your entire worldview, but isn't incredibly difficult if you're passionate about what you write, this is it. TAKE THIS CLASS!!! HIGHLY RECOMMENDED!!!!

Kathi is one of the most thoughtful and caring professors I have had at Duke. She really encourages class discussions of the readings in class. She is happy to meet outside of class to talk about the material, essay structure, etc. The reading load is pretty fair, but not stuff you can briefly glance at. I highly recommend Kathi!
DO NOT TAKE HER CLASS!

I loved the reading, and she was such as wonderful caring teacher. She is always willing to meet with students, and is so understanding. She gets that students are busy and have other things going on in their lives (and other classes). Class discussion is always interesting and the course is structured perfectly!
Definitely would recommend. She loves the subject, makes it interesting, and wants students to do well. One of the better GSF profs at Duke.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Kathi Weeks is absolutely wonderful. She is very caring and understanding, is willing to meet to talk, and supports her students. Also, I love her class. The reading is interesting and informative, and the syllabus is really well done. You really should show up and talk in class, but overall she is a good grader.

Kathi is INCREDIBLE. She is clearly very passionate about what she's teaching and wants class to be an engaging experience for her students. She is also incredibly accommodating when it comes to due dates and is generally a very understanding and empathetic professor. She is amazing!!
Class was pretty boring, but also pretty easy. 5 short assignments and take home midterm and final essays. You also don't really have to do the readings, so very low workload.

Politics of Sex Labor with Dr. Weeks was wonderful. She is animated, enthusiastic, knowledgeable, and really knows how to encourage you to question your beliefs. She is also really understanding and helpful when you are concerned about anything in the class and gives paper extensions willingly.

This class was SO interesting! If you do the reading and participate in discussions, you will get a lot out of it.  She is not a hard grader.  Obviously, the subject matter is a bit graphic, but if you can get past that, this class will make you think.  She is so nice and understanding, and she knows a lot about the subject!
She is a kind professor and she knows a lot about global health. She is a kind grader as well.

Whetten has a lot of experience in global health and policy which was very interesting to hear. The class could benefit from more organization, but they are very accommodating. Sometimes I couldn't find assignments, but Whetten helped me when I emailed. Personally, I need a lot of structure so if you have anxiety or ocd, you might be a lil stressed
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: This course is the most unorganized class I've ever attended. It was hard to find any assignments or due dates on Canvas and sometimes it takes Whetten a long time to respond. There was absolutely NO structure. We would have to ask our groups when things were due and most of the time, no one knew. It could've been a fun class but it missed the mark
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: While Prof. Whetten is very kind, she is a terrible professor. She is extremely unorganized and didn't teach a single class period. Every class is a random group discussion OR random group presentations made by the students with very vague expectations. I would not recommend Prof. Whetten to anyone if you like ANY sense of structure.
dont take this class. professor is unorganized, assigns way too much homework, and is boring to listen to. unless you need the credit for a GH minor or major, spare yourself.

I was one of the youngest people in this class and I felt super accommodated and cared for. The professors would be happy to meet outside class and gave me great feedback. If Vivien is your TA, you're in for an incredible time. Dr. Whetten is super sweet and brings so much experience to the table-- do everything you can to learn from them!

Avoid this class at all costs. It is the most unorganized, poorly taught course at Duke. It is simply a waste of money. I cannot emphasize how much you should avoid this class. I can confidently say I learned absolutely nothing. This class made me lose my passion for global health.
Be smart. Don't take her class. You will not learn anything, will be annoyed at her teaching style, and just utterly disappointed. Completely regret taking this class.
Very inaccessible and bad about responding to student inquiries and concerns. Ironic how she is a professor...

Teaching for GLHLTH210 was left mostly to her two TAs and Whettan did very little actual teaching. At one point she just left for two weeks and neglected to tell us. The class ran over a lot because Whettan would go on long tangents about irrelevant things. For a class with graded participation, coming to lecture was actually fruitless.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Dr. Whetten has a lot of interesting experiences in public and global health to share, but a core course on global health ethics doesn't seem well-suited for her. She enjoyed facilitating debates on hot-button topics without deeply exploring ethical frameworks that could be used. Readings and group work were constant, and classes were unproductive.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: I think you actually need to "teach" to be considered a professor. She leaves the whole class up to TA's and the people that are trying to turn this into a team-based learning style class, who are worthless. Weekly quizzes are impossible even if you did the reading. Seems like it would be an easy class but due to the lack of direction, it is not.

This class is deceptively hard, but it really is a great class. Guest lectures are amazing and are very insightful into different health path. This class doesn't require too much work, but everything is graded too difficultly. Not an easy A, but a great overall class, especially if the subject is interesting to you.

Professor Whetten is an incredible person, and her lectures were usually engaging and interesting. However, she is so busy with her own work that the grading is left solely to the TAs. The graded papers were ABSOLUTELY RIDICULOUS. You basically had to write a published article to get a 10/10. Not happy, good luck.

Professor Whetten is so incredibly fun and such a good lecturer.  Unfortunately she is very busy with her other research projects so she depends heavily on TA's and guest lecturers to teach the class.  The grading is kind of ridiculous and I wish the readings had been paced better.

You have to take this class to get the GH certificate, and for intro classes, this one is not bad at all. Guest lecturers were always interesting (esp. Ariely, don't miss his lecture). Grades,quizzes,final,papers,& everything else handled by TA, so how hard the class is really depends on who the TA for that semester is. Overall, recommended!

"Global Health." Maybe it's because I had really high expectations for this class, but GH with Whetten was exceedingly disappointing. You learn absolutely nothing of worth; her teaching style is way too touchy-feely. Also, the class is graded so easily on everything but the AWFUL weekly quizzes that they end up determining your grade - so unfair!!

Guest lecturer is always interesting and has a lot of experience. Has a TON of experience and some lectures were interesting and informative. Quizzes are nitpicky. SO unaccessible. Lectures and schedule is disorganized. At end of semester, she doesn't lecture herself. The course could have been better

Somewhat disorganized and very unapproachable. She's off saving the world though, so you can't really blame her. If you take her Global Health class, just read the articles before your quizzes and you will be fine.

The best professor I had this semester. She makes the class lots of fun and I definitely learned a lot...the only thing is she doesn't have that much time to help because she's busy with her work in other parts of the world. she laughs a lot, which I really enjoyed, because our class was always fun.

Kate is amazing! I can see how someone uninterested in the field could see her as removed, but if you are self-motivated, or simply enjoy the issues discussed in the class, it is easy to become captivated. Many guest lecturers, but getting one-on-one time with Kate shows that she is much more interested & approachable than she may seem. Inspiring!

Whetten sucks. She's a global heath expert and i thought this class would be great, but it was all busywork, and she breezed through lectures so that no one understood what she was talking about. The class was a TOTAL waste of time.

Prof Whetten is an expert in her field and very well-informed. She's not always accessible and relies heavily on her TAs -- who were great! The class was interesting if you're a self-motivated learner.

Awful class, awful instruction. The TA was really good, otherwise the class was worthless -- all busywork (and lots of it). Whetten is unavailable to students and didn't lecture ONCE after late February. Save yourself: take a Don Taylor class instead.
Nina is an amazing teacher who cares about her students and is hilarious. I would recommend having some sort of jazz background to take this class.

I look forward to this class everyweek and am truly so luckly to get to learn from Nina. She has such an incredible wealth of knowledge when it comes to dance technique and choreography and it is really a joy to take her class. Great mix of conditioning, across the floor, stretching and short combos. I love her!
Nina is one of the most caring professors I have had in my time at Duke. She is also hilarious and so kind. Take her class if you have the chance!!!!

Nina is absolutely fantastic. She cares so much about her students and is a wonderful teacher. Her choreography is unique and she loves watching her students make it come to life. She also teaches at Elon if you want to read more raving reviews about her.

Truly inspirational professor. Amazing lectures, super interesting projects, and she even teaches you how to write clearly and concisely, much better than any Writing 101 professor. If you want to take an interdisciplinary course and work on a real-life project of your choosing, def take this class!

Wharton's class is worth the time, especially if you're not an ArtHist major. You can tell she is an expert in her field but still knows how to communicate the info to college students. She cares about the topic and it shows in her lectures. Straightforward material. Honestly the best readings in the class are the articles that she wrote.

Without question, top 3 class I have ever taken at Duke, and my academic career. Professor Wharton is an amazing lecturer and a joy to listen and learn from. The class is in Smith Warehouse but I assure you the unbelievable quality of instruction will be well worth your travels. She is so kind and caring for all of us and I cannot thank her enough!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Wharton is a wonderful professor and I would highly recommend her class to anyone. She made everyone in the class, regardless of prior architectural knowledge, super interested in the material. Plus, she gives a house tour at the end that was spectacular in its own right. I also thought the TA's were super helpful.

This is probably the most informative and interesting class I've ever taken at Duke. I had 0 architecture knowledge before, but left feeling like an expert. You can tell how smart and qualified Professor Wharton is just by the way she speaks. This class changed my world perspective and I now keep up with architecture out of personal interest.
Professor Wharton is an amazing lecturer! Loved this class and would recommend Professor Wharton to anyone.

Took urbanism with Professor Ladd. Good professor and class goes by fast.  Class readings and discussions are good.  She really critiques your writing - very particular about word choice - but overall she does make your writing more clear.

Architecture class for people that don't want to be architects. The lectures are extremely interesting. There is reading material for each class, not that necessary to read. The tests all follow the same format; stick to it and you'll do fine. Prof. Wharton is extremely passionate about the subject and knows it very well. Loved the class!
Dont let her age fool you, she is so vivacious and fun.  Has great knowledge and passion for her  subject, and does a great job of making the most mundane details exciting.

I took her freshman year for architecture and while I loved the subject, absolutely hated her.  She was completely not helpful outside of class and unfair in her grading.  I knew that she really didn't like me and made the mistake of taking her again for a senior seminar.  She made me suffer.  I worked my ass off for this woman and she was just cru
fascinating and engaging lectures. She is very passionate about her field which makes the class enjoyable. I didn't want to miss a single class!

This class made me want to major in Art History even though I had not interest in it before. Some people say her lectures are a little dull, but she does come up with creative projects and tries to tailor what she teaches to students' interests. Very nice lady
She certainly likes what she's doing.

Professor Whitt is the best professor I have ever had. He makes the material extremely engaging with in class discussions or blog posts on the readings. He gives amazing feedback on papers and works with students to help them develop and structure their ideas. He is also very witty and caring.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Matt is one of the best professors I've had. He is truly passionate and knowledgeable about Mass Incarceration & Democracy and similar topics, and he is very good at facilitating great discussions while separating his own personal opinions. He also taught me a lot about writing and made the class very manageable and enjoyable!
I learned a lot in this class, but definitely had to work for it. Provides a ton of support on the final paper and is very accessible outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: He's a very, very good writing professor, and he seems like a very nice person. He's very supportive of everyone's work and was willing  to talk with me about the final paper to help me narrow down my argument and direction. Also, I think that a lot of the readings in the class were unnecessary, but the class discussions were interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Loved Whitt's class. He's super nice and the class is fascinating. I learned so much and I definitely recommend the class. There's not a ton of reading, but a lot more than other Writing 101 classes. There's also a bit more work. If writing isn't your thing, you'll improve a lot but the class will be hard. If it is, the class will be easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS--Caring

reviews.comment: He's my favorite prof at Duke so far! There was a lot of reading (and work in general), but I definitely got out of this class what I put into it. He is very personable and give great lectures/leads very good discussions.  The grading is a little hard, but it includes good constructive feedback. 10/10 would take this class again.

Prof. Whitt is passionate about his subject and his students. This is NOT the class to take for an easy A. He has very high expectations, and you have to put in a LOT of time and effort into papers and revisions. Content is interesting, but only if you want to be talking about mass incarceration...

Whitt's class will legitimately improve your thinking and writing (and you get to learn a lot about the prison system). But, of course, all legitimate improvement is difficult, so be prepared for a heightened standard of effort and scrutiny. His grading is very fair, and it includes helpful feedback. Do the extra credit assignments.
Whitt is a great professor, perhaps the best writing 101 professor at Duke. Land of Free is definintely worth taking, and you will 100% improve your writing ability.

Land of the free was a difficult class, but totally worth it. Whitt is preprared and passionate and cares about the students. He is a tough grader, you really do learn how to write - I feel so prepared! Plus, he was so ready to meet to discuss anything. If you are lucky enough to take a class with Whitt, take advantage of your time with him!

I would definitely take Whitt's Land of the Free class again. He is a professor that is clearly passionate about his chosen subject and the class not only engenders interesting discussions but encourages you to look at the institutions of the United States and the concept of 'freedom' in a different light. Harder than other writing101s but worth it

I wrote a 1200 word letter to this professor that I never actually sent bc the letter was too harsh on his grading policy without giving him enough credit for being a phenomenal teacher. If you ACTUALLY want to improve your writing, take 101 with Whitt. But make sure you question how serious about that you really are bc he really makes you work.

Professor Whitt is overall an excellent professor. The beginning of the course was a little dry, and I the second essay in particular was difficultbut the course was great, which he definitely helped happen.

I strongly recommend taking Professor Whitt's class. I am sure there are much easier Writing 101 classes, but I highly doubt there is one that is more rewarding than a Professor Whitt one. Everyone who takes this class comes out as a better writer. You will have to work in this class, but will you be rewarded for every moment you put into it.
Interesting topic, great professor, good class overall
Fair grader. Learned a lot in this class.

Professor Whitt is very committed to improving you as a writer. He is also incredibly passionate and knowledgable about his subjects. Hard class but it's hard to get those two aforementioned qualities and an easy class at the same time.
This is an excellent class that really helps in the development of writing skills and is extremely interesting besides.

Absolutely great professor. Makes you look forward to his class. Definitely more time consuming than most Writing 101's, but incredibly worth it. Would take his class again just to relive the great discussions.

Prof. Whitt is an amazing professor. He is very witty, helpful, and passionate about what he teaches. While some of the readings can be a little dull, he makes them interesting come class time. He is a fair grader but expects you to come to class prepared. While it isn't the easiest freshman writing class, it is probably one of the most helpful.

I appreciated that Dr. Warren had office hours regularly, especially because CHEM 210 content is tough. He has done extensive research in his field, and it's really neat to learn from someone who is very knowledgeable. Make sure to review the slides for the weekly quizzes!

This class was unbearable. Lectures were boring and never recorded. Each person in the class felt very unprepared as no one was able to guess what material would be given on the exams. Worst professor I have had at Duke.

This was the worst class that I have taken at Duke. The exams are not reflective of given homework and recitation problem sets. The lectures are very difficult to follow and uninteresting. Exam averages were consistently 40% and the professor made no effort to improve our learning in addition to being very difficult to communicate with.

Do NOT listen to other reviews. Without a doubt the worst class I have taken at Duke. Lectures are dull, he doesn't explain concepts at all, refuses to post recorded lectures, and exam questions are nothing like discussion p sets/ homework (averages are 40s). Everyone I know in the class absolutely despised it. Avg curved to a B. Take it elsewhere.

really hard class but Warren is really supportive, patient and likes to answer questions. nice guy, got us cupcakes and gives chances to improve grades. his research is fascinating and he still dedicates a lot of time and attention to our class. willing to meet with students outside of class. tests are fair. do homework and really focus in class

Dr. Warren has a very difficult course for Chem 210 in comparison to other professors, however he curves the class to a B average. The test averages were in the 40s and were extremely difficult. I would wait to take with another professor.

One of the most arrogant professors I have ever had in my career at Duke. Made simple chemical concepts difficult. He is very smart bur he should be locked in a research lab and not allowed to teach students. Curves harshly, and does not provide class recordings. If you are goin to take 210, take it with Cox. Avoid this man at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prepare to hate your semester. CHEM 210 was the worst class I have ever taken with the worst teacher I've ever had. It isn't just the difficulty of the course or Warren's lack of teaching ability that makes it unbearable, it's the fact that Warren is so arrogant and rude. He is extremely smart, but it clearly doesn't translate to teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Warren Warren made a class that I dreaded taking worse than I imagined possible. He was rude, condescending, and explained things in such a way that even basic physics concepts were muddled by unnecessary derivations. He went way off the syllabus and tested students on his tangents. Also, why is a chemistry professor even teaching physics?

Professor Warren did not seem to enjoy teaching this class and often talked ab chemistry (we get it, youre a chemistry professor) and went on tangents that had no relevancy to the material tested. He was condescending if you didnt grasp physics easily. He made me truly despise physics and him. I feel bad for his co-teachers. Steer clear of him.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Warren dislikes teaching the actual content of the course, and instead goes off on meaningless tangents. This would be more palatable if he were an actually good person. However, he comes off as rude and condescending. Truly one of the worst professors at Duke.
Explains topics in way that goes over the heads of the students in the class. Over complicates material

Honestly, lectures went way over my head for a general chemistry class. Averages were in the 50s usually for each exam, but he curved really well in the end (I think). Textbook not needed, just his lectures will do. Very knowledgeable and well-respected researcher and seems to go out of his way to provide time for students.

Warren is excited about his subject and knows more about it than probably anyone else, so the lectures are very interesting but usually went way over my head. And his tests are extremely difficult. Also, it feels more like a physics or statistics course than a chemistry course at times.

As a person Warren is pretty nice and willing to answer questions.  But his written problem sets and his tests are INSANE!!! (nothing like the notes or homework assignments).  Does not feel like a general chem class at all.  Besides chemistry, make sure you are very good at physics.

Warren Sidney Warren is the most bestest, most interesting chem professor ever.  If you like to learn, and if you enjoy science and being challenged by the concepts introduced in lecture, you will love Warren.  Almost everyone I know loved Warren, was okay with Craig and then hated McPhail and Lyle for 22.

Second worst teacher I've ever had. Blabs on about things that don't matter, no study time to grade correlation whatsoever. TA's admit that tests are more about guessing than chemistry, and awful personality. Just awful.
Don't understand why everyone hates him. He's not a bad guy and will always help you outside of class. His lectures are boring, but honestly, no one can really give 'exciting' chem 21 lectures
Hard but the stuff he teaches is very helpful and if your a bio/ chem major, you'll be seeing a lot of it so you might as well learn it now.

Warren is intimidating but his class is not actually that hard. I ended up with a 70 average and an A. Even if his lectures are boring at least they are factual (unlike Craig's). Plus he is pretty helpful in office hours and he is definitely a genius. I would take the class again. I don't know why everyone hates Warren.

The class was honestly not that hard.
