The lectures were often pointless/useless and I and most people I knew never went subsequently but as long as you read the book and do the problems the material is not that hard.  Not to mention the tests are ridiculously curved, with the curve all you needed to get was about a 60 on the test for an A.

I do not agree with the previous post at all. The class was ridiculously difficult. The tests were insane, and very few people did very well. The exam written by Warren Warren was the hardest test I've ever taken in my life. It will blow your mind.

The other posts seem kind of ridiculous. This was the easiest class I took my first semester at Duke. Not a lot of work, just read the textbook before the tests and you'll be fine. Some of the test questions could have different answers depending on how you think about them, but in the end it doesn't really end up mattering. Warrens a good guy too.

Warren is really arrogant and an awful lecturer. I fell asleep more times than I can count. You don't really need to go to the lecture, just read the book and do the eduspace problems. It's an intro class, so its really not that hard.

Worst professor of my life. He is obviously a genius in chemistry, but he cannot and should not teach an intro level chem. he just knows too much, and his pompous self can't explain anything clearly. I dropped this class. best day of my life.

Class is absolutely impossible. It makes no difference if you go to lectures cause you'll still fail the test. Warren is a RIDICULOUS teacher that should have just stayed at Princeton. This class is IMPOSSIBLE -- go to the recitations, that's your only chance of doing well.

not at all good. he knows his stuff, but chem21 is taught very badly at duke (well, if it's warren and s.craig teaching). this is definitely not intro chem. the class is a joke and it's a miracle if you get thru.
dry
His lectures are very boring and fastpaced. His tests aren't too bad- if you do the eduspace problems and his practice problems then you'll do fine.

Prof. Warren isn't as bad as most of these reviews would suggest.  First, the current chemistry textbook used (Zumdahl) is much better than his book (which was used in previous years).  Second, he speaks very clearly and will help you in office hours.  It's true that his lectures don't review problems on the test, but links and practice tests help.
Lectures don't prepare you for the tests.

I'm surprised to see all these negative comments. I'm currently in chem 21L and not finding it too bad. I'm finding Warren (W^2 as he likes to call himself) to be a really good lecturer.. its really understandable and easy to follow. But if you haven't taken chem since soph year in hs .. this is all new and you'll have to put a lot of work in.

He's really not as bad a guy as everyone makes him out to be, and he's definitely willing to help you if you need it.  It's true, though, that he's a genius and probably should be teaching upper-level chem rather than an introductory freshman class. (Also, he gave out ice cream after the course evals were turned in, so it wasn't a bribe.)
Simply aweful.  If you like chem, well then you are in for hell.  Think you want to be a chem major? Yeah well I thought so too.  AVOID AT ALL COSTS.

I have to say, this man is a complete genious.  However, he is too smart for his own good. We learned things in class that students in PChem had not yet covered. And his tests were abominable. I think he would be a great grad student professor, but not one for students who have a weak background in Chem.  Avoid Chem 21L if it taught by him.

After finishing freshman year I cannot think of a more hated  professor. Avoid his course at all costs... seriously. I met someone who graduated Princeton 10 years ago-where he taught for ages- & mentioned his name & he smirked and told me how the kids hated him there too.If you like chem, wait until a better prof teaches so you'll actually learn.
beware

he was really confusing, and generally a pompous guy, take chem again when he isnt teaching. he may have been more interesting than palmer, but he was more confusing also. also tried to bribe students into giving good course evals by giving us ice cream right before we filled them out

He lectures about really interesting stuff, just he obviously cannot grasp what level his students actually are on--if you have already taken a physics or physical chemistry course, this is at your level. Otherwise...

As a lecturer, he can be incredibly confusing and definitely enjoys introducing high-level concepts that are outside the scope of the course. Outside class he is approachable and helpful, if you choose to make the contact.
No Comments
Smart guy, but horrible teacher. Good luck

Don't let anyone fool you. If you have never had Chemistry before (or bad high school chemistry), then you are screwed in this class. I did all the homework, read every chapter, did extra problems, got a tutor, studied weeks before the tests, talked to the man, and went to every recitation, yet my grade showed none of this. Cya, good GPA!

Dr. Warren is arguably one of the most difficult professors I have ever had. The class average on both of his exams was 53. While a few people did well, most did not. The key to doing well with Dr. Warren is understanding the material, not just knowing the textbook. If you can do that, and it's not as easy as it sounds, you should be ok.

Chem 21 is the INTRO chem course for people with weak chem backgrounds.When Warren took over he skipped the basics and went into more complicated stuff.There was no way one could understand his material w/o physics and chem b/c we didnt even have time to process the basics and his tests only tested on his material so you werent even guaranted a 30%

He is not out to kill general chemistry; he just wants to raise the bar and challenge intro students.  So, his material's challenging: lectures are fast-paced, subject matter is in-depth, and the book is difficult.  But if you stay on top of ALL of it--lecture notes, book, (helpful) online links, go to office hours, and work hard--you'll do well.
Warren is a horrible teacher. He is extraordinarily full of himself, and though, slightly interested in student learning, he is not effective in conveying ideas at all.

Warren Warren is the worst professor/teacher that I have had in 13 years of school dating back to kindergarden.  I had a high A when professor Palmer taught the class, but my grade plummeted when I started getting 40s on Warrens' tests.  It is amusing that he resembles the guy from the princess bride that says "inconceivable" all the time though.

Dr. Warren should not be teaching this course. We wasted several weeks attempting to decipher his book, which is dense and poorly organized, making it entirely inaccessible. His slides are filled with obscure quantum physics equations. His tests are difficult, and he prides himself on having low averages. Sadly, you will have to take this course.

Warren is not a very good professor. He doesn't teach general chemistry. Instead, he teaches high level physics & a lot of other things that have no place in his class. Don't even worry about going to lecture. It's not worth your time. I went to every single one & learned nothing. With a lot of work, you can scoot by with a B, but it's a challenge.
He knows what he's talking about but almost too much.  Language is difficult to understand and comprehend.

the worst chem prof I have ever had-pompous and while he does offer help, he doesnt actually help, he just makes fun. His book,which he requires you to buy because he can't sell it,is terrible&confusing.Hes smart,but should NOT be teaching gen.chem because he does not want to made clear by his teaching physics & calc & high level chem to our class.

To sum it up, he doesn't teach "general chemistry" but quantum mechanics and high level physics stuff one shouldn't be learning in GENERAL chemistry. He makes you buy his book(which isnt general chem) and doesnt follow main textbook.. very proud of himself, pretty condescending.. and oh his tests? they'll blow your mind...(not in a good way btw)

Material he tests on is largely quantum physics or obscure chemical knowledge that was not covered in the main textbook.  He mocks the students who do badly on exams, insisting in class that they aren't working, instead of acknowledging his unrealistic expectations. I used to think I wanted to be a chem major, but this class ruined subject for me.

Stay away! He is full of himself and raises the class to a level far above the gen chem level just to use his book that is all physics and math. His tests are not like anything you have seen before. He even tried to get rid of Dr. Lyle in the beginning, who is the saving grace of chem with his demos. He does tell some random interesting stuff.

Warren obviously thinks his students know more than what is expected of a gen chem course. His lectures were slightly more intriguing than palmer's but the sucject matter was ridiculously difficult and should have been saved for a higher level course.

He is arrogant and is more worried about making sure everyone knows that his book is intellectually superior to the main textbook than he is about actually teaching *basic* chemistry - He needs to realize that sure advanced quantum physics is behind all chemistry properties, but we need to learn basic chem first

Often comes off as pompous through his tendencies to always put down other authors and recurrently bring up his own research.  Makes  the class seem more like advanced physics on crack. Even tutors and TA's didn't always understand the concepts being taught....

his philosophy is that quantum is SUPPOSED to be bizzare and confusing to learn. Lectures are a bit too fast paced but with interesting anecdotes. Book was bad but he supplemented it with links to awesome chem tutorials online. very accesable outside of class. you must stay one step ahead at all times to do well: reading, links, office hours.
No Comments

Warren likes to teach directly from his book, which is completely incomprehensible and above gen chem level, just to show off. His tests are incredibly hard. However, his lectures are slightly more interesting than Palmer's.

I completely concur.  You don't go a day in class without hearing, "I taught at Princeton and Harvard for 23 years..."  He makes you buy his book, which is designed for graduate level physics classes, just to make money off of you.  Yeah, he's smart.  Unfortunately he knows it.  The tests are nothing like notes or homework problems.

Professor Whyman is a great lecturer and does a great job tying in a lot of different concepts and making lectures genuinely interesting. She's very clear about what she expects for papers and exams. You learn a lot and don't have to bend over backwards to get a good grade. Overall, one of the best professors I've ever had.

Whyman lectured for the entire class period, spoke super fast, and never had a single powerpoint. Impossible for me to keep up and take good notes. Shes extremely smart and passionate, just definitely doesnt have the ideal teaching style for most students.

Extremely knowledgeable and is clear and focused in delivering what she thinks is most important for students to learn. Very clear about exam structures and the researching for the papers helped me learn a lot. One of the best professors and classes I've ever had at Duke. She is also very open to really getting to know students and helping them out

One of the best courses and professors I've had at Duke. Very interesting material, which she teaches quite well. Grading based on two mid-terms (no final), several projects, and leading the class discussion on two occasions.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Would take again

reviews.comment: She's young but already an excellent teacher & clearly passionate about the subject material. Readings are helpful but only truly necessary when you're discussion leader. Expectations are clear (especially for exams): take good notes, put your time in, and you'll do fine. My only regret is I'm a senior & thus can't take anything else with her!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Would take again

reviews.comment: Wheatley often comes off as aloof and provides incorrect information. You can tell hes very interested in educational philosophy, but I think it can distract from the actual material. I wish he would provide more lectures and information rather than leaving everything up to group discussion. Would avoid his class...

Alex Wheatley teaches with a high school strictness and demands the respect of a world expert, while simultaneously knowing very little about geology! He enjoys having the reputation of being a tough grader and often sends rude emails

He is a little intense about the material, and not very understanding when it comes to your other engagements and responsibilities.  He relishes giving hard tests and the reputation of being a tough grader.

This is class is pretty much an easy A. I would highly recommend taking it- she is a great teacher as well. There are no tests and the final is a final project about whatever you want essentially. You have to attend class but you get 2 unexcused absences and if you miss more, she gives extra credit at the end to make up for it.

Whitney Trettien is a fun and great professor. Most classes rely on communication and group work, and most of the grades come from things done in class or small projects assigned for homework. She is very helpful and an interesting person to listen to.

She is innovative and quirky and her classes are interactive workshop-style sessions that bear an emphasis upon a variety of media forms. She was always communicative, helpful, and accessible. A great teacher and fascinating person.

Incarceration Nation (constellation so it was S/U). Professor Wildeman is knowledgable about his field, but sometimes forgets we don't know as much as him. Lectures are interesting but slides can be very vague (have to attend class to understand). TA's are helpful (shout out Garrett Baker who also teaches a version of this course and super well!)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very fun guy and gives decent lectures, but his slides are so bad lol. As long as you're taking notes during lecture and doing the readings, the tests should be fine. Glad this class was pass/fail for constellations, though.

Prof Wildeman is a great person, caring and funny. Incarceration Nation is an interesting class, but the organization could be improved upon. Most of your grade is 4 exams throughout the course that make up 60%. The class was pass/fail when I took it, and was relatively easy to pass. Be prepared to memorize facts/stats for the exams.

Wildeman is such a nice guy, and you can tell he enjoys teaching the content! The majority of your grade is made up of 4 exams, so beware of that. More graph interpretation than expected and a good amount of articles per week, but the material is interesting, and the tests are more approachable if you put in the time. Definitely recommend!!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Course is extremely interesting, especially for pre-law. It's reading-heavy and requires memorization of stats and graphs for exams, but Wildeman provides immense support. Studying in chunks makes the exams more manageable. LOVE interacting with Wildeman as a person and professor, and engaging with course content. Definitely recommend this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Doesn't quite understand classroom dynamics. Great at first, his performance dwindles completely by the end of semester.
Prof Winters cares so much about teaching! he gives great feedback and is reasonable with grading.

I took Race, Religion, and Film. Grade was made up of three 3-4pg papers, 10% participation (just show up to class) and one extra credit paper (max 3 pts). Papers were graded by TAs and you can get feedback on outlines/drafts beforehand so guaranteed A if you put in the work beforehand. Prof Winters is so cool too

Took Baldwin and Morrison with Prof. Winters. The class was fantastic especially if you haven't read these authors before. Prof. W knows how to lead a conversation and touch on the really important themes. The written assignments actually challenge you to think which is great. You also watch a couple of films in the class which was dope.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I'm taking an english seminar with him (Baldwin and Morrison) and he's my favorite professor right now. He really knows the material and leads engaging discussions about the books (reading is manageable). Gives clear feedback on essays. He's so caring and gave us a couple classes off already-- aware of students' mental health and energy levels.

Prof. Winters is an amazing professor. It is so clear that he is an expert in his field, but he is still able to communicate ideas to students in a down-to-earth way . He is very receptive towards students' ideas. I always looked forward to discussions in his class and I learned a ton. Definitely my favorite professor and class at Duke so far.
Great professor. Lead engaging discussions and tied in contemporary relevance well. Encouraging, kind, and fair. Also, very well spoken and knowledgable.   Awesome course, and wonderful professor.

Prof. Winters is awesome. He loves his students and hearing their ideas. He encourages discussion and questions. The class is reading heavy and requires short (250 word) responses weekly and analytical papers. Papers are graded by TA, so ask them questions for help -- you need to know your concepts to do well. Honestly, one of my favorite classes.

Awesome class, super chill. Not what I expected- intro to religious theory rather than various religions. If you contribute to discussion- which you don't have to read to do, and put a little effort into the three short papers you should get an A. Weekly responses are graded on participation, for papers just repeat what he says in class.

Took Hip-hop and religion with Professor Winters--one of the best classes I've taken at Duke. Winters obviously has a very strong background in religion and his love for hip-hop translates into an incredibly engaging and fun course. Weekly 350 word write-ups on the readings and two 8 page papers. Love this class and Professor Winters is fantastic.
Amazing guy and amazing professor. Loved by everyone and is extremely caring. Knows how to explain material well and is super accessible.

Dr. Witelski is an awesome professor, and a great guy. He's always there to answer emails/questions in office hours. His class is extremely hard, but you can see the common thread of the class from beginning to end. The course is well designed and well kept, and I learned a ton in it.

He's definitely an awesome Professor! He's always ready to help, both in and outside class. His class is super organized and the grading criteria is very clear. Go to class because his lectures are useful. Use homework solutions he printed out to review for exams.

One of the best professors I have ever had. Literally such an amazing, caring, and funny person. He seriously cares for each and every one of his students and will do his best so that they understand the material and get good grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: Lectures got to be very accelerated towards the end, and it became very difficult to follow along with what was going on. However, the three tests are very easy and you will be prepared if you do the practice midterms and review homework.
Best teacher I have ever had!

Witelski is an amazing professor. The material isn't easy but he is super accessible and willing to answer questions both in and outside of class. His lectures are extremely clear. Good professor, clear expectations, and a great sense of humor.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: Tom is like an awkward teddy bear who happens to kick butt at all things math. He is the best teacher I've encountered at Duke. He reduces complicated math lingo to clear concepts. He's also super approachable and has hilarious dry humor. Definitely do not miss lecture; he teaches diff than the textbook. Understand EVERYTHING before testing. A+++++
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Tom Witelski's lectures are among the best you can get at Duke. I would highly recommend his classes on Math. Modeling, Math. Fluid Dynamics and Applied PDEs. He identifies just the right application areas and examples to clarify abstract mathematical formulations for an engineering audience. As a bonus, his classes are also very entertaining!

Best professor I have ever had, but also really difficult. I have never learned so much in a class before, but it was totally worth it in the end. If you want to really learn something thoroughly, take one his his classes. Amazing teacher.
Amazing professor for teaching, lengthy/difficult hw and exams

A brilliant professor that makes difficult math much more understandable.  This may seem evident, but this is a graduate class and you will need to work.  Regardless of workload, Professor Witelski is the best math professor I have had in the past seven year of university study; if you are going to take the course, take it with Professor Witelski.
Very applied, very thorough. Great prof

Easily the best math professor I've had, he makes a very involved class much more manageable.  Prof. Witelski is excellent at clarifying topics if you have trouble with the first explanation.  If you put in the time at the beginning to learn the solution process, you will do much better than if you try to memorize specific cases.

As a grad student taking this class, I should say, I have never met a professor like this. He showed great experience in every course he teaches, and also perfect explanation for every question arising. Hope I could be his class assistant some semester in future.
A genuinely great teacher. Has the best sense of humor any mathematician has ever had. Makes retardedly hard math bearable. I wish I'd taken more classes with him. Nice guy to boot.
pretty good, cool guy
Insanely good. Never thought math could be taught so well.
He's one of the best
Tom is the best professor and teacher during my 2 years in DUKE.

Tom is very nice and a clear lecturer.  He is always willing to meet outside of class, but at least for this class, had some trouble explaining difficult material in a way that undergraduates would be able to understand.  Before I took this class, I heard very good things about him, so take one of his tried and true classes like 103x.
Totally awesome professor ... TAKE HIS CLASS!
Tom is AWESOME.  Take 103x just for tom.  He is seriously one of the best profs i've ever had.  His class is hard, but I'll take it over 103 anytime.

Tom is the best instructor during my 3-years graduate study. Clear lecture, gradually increasing the difficulty of the homework. O learnt a lot from the class, both in linear algebra and C programming.

clear lecture structure and funny classes. He has a passion for math that will positively influence every student he teach. I asked questions via email and got quick and detailed response. His classes have been a very rewarding and enjoyable experience! Hope the he will teach math 225 soon.
Tom's brain makes him hotter than Gregory Peck, or Spencer Tracy. meow

Makes tests ridiculously hard, but has a generous curve.  You will learn a ton in this class, way more than in regular 103.  Awesome guy in terms of keeping things interesting and being available if you need help.  My best prof so far.  Take him for whatever he is teaching, but study hard!

I never believed I could laugh this hard in a math class.  He's extremely accessible too, has something like 6 office hours a week and actually seems happy when you show up and have a ton of questions.  Take him for whatever he's teaching.  His class is hard but he's a fair grader.
Shows interest and concern for students.

One of the best teachers I've had in my two years.  32X is pretty damn hard, but he understands that and throws down a monster curve . . . I failed one test and still got an A.  Take any class you can with him.

Awesome professor. The tests were inhuman, but there was a very nice curve. Far, far better than the horror stories I have hear about the regular 32L program. Entertaining guy, too, and very willing to help in office hours.
Impossible tests, huge curves (I somehow managed a B+ with a 72% test average), funny, funny, funny man.  F is for... witelski.  U is... um, for witelski.  and N?  that's for witelski, too.
damn good class if you like math

Lecture heavy and textbook heavy for exams. She is an engaging lecturer but gets off topic sometimes. I had a difficulty following the syllabus because the class schedules ran behind usually. Disorganized but overall fun to take if you're looking for interesting psych classes.

Psych 103 was not a cakewalk. Dr. Wilbourn cares a lot about her students and what they take away from each lecture, often at the expense of teaching the content that will be on the exam. This was frustrating, but I feel like I have learned some important information for my future. Take this class if you like children.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Wibourn is a great+interesting lecturer, but did get behind often. Exams are easy as long as you study. Lots of textbook readings/info outside of lecture that you need to know. Grading is slow but TA's are great. Overall a good class, just a few annoying things. I would definitely take it again!

Dr. Wilbourn always got off track and never finished any of her lectures. Most of her last exam was information from the textbook or asynchronous lectures, none of which was taught in class. The info is interesting but there is so much content that it makes studying for tests painful. TAs were great tho

With the unenviable task of teaching developmental psych, which covers so may topics, she does a good job. She can be disorganized at times, but is fair and gives chances for extra credit. She's very knowledgeable and is an engaging lecturer. If you put in effort into the class, it is not hard. The amount of textbook reading is ridiculous though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class is not an easy A, and she tells you that on the first day. It's not a hard class either, but a LOT of work. The content is fascinating, and lectures are usually very interesting (they're also tech-free). The teaching team is painfully slow at grading so if you need your grades quickly after submitting assignments this is not your class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class is NOT an easy A, and she tells you that on the first day. However, it's not a hard class either, it's just a lot of work. The textbook readings are interesting but really long. Lectures are tech-free but cool. She and the TAs are painfully slow to grade so if you need to know your grades often this is not the class for you.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This is my favorite professor and class at Duke thus far, please do not listen to everyone else's ratings. I would retake this class over again if I could. Wilbourn mentioned, in the beginning, to get ahead on the readings, and if you do because the beginning of the class is VERY EASY, the class is a breeze. Amazing and funny lecturer.

Dr. Wilbourn was not a bad lecturer, but she frequently got off topic during class, which led to us not being able to finish most of the material. Over half of the material on the last exam was self-taught through reading the textbook. There was an essay assigned every week that felt a lot like busywork. Ramped up difficulty without adding meaning.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Dr. Wilbourn is a very engaging lecturer and it's clear that she is passionate and knowledgeable about psych. That being said, this class was incredibly textbook heavy and lectures alone are not sufficient to pass tests. There are very specific expectations for papers and she provides online resources to meet them, but it is easy to lose points.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Do not expect an easy A. Professor Wilbourn significantly ramped up the difficulty this year—time commitment easily 7-9 hours a week if you want A. Expectations are unclear, tests are horrendous (no direction for what to study), and homework offers little support for tests/graded more on English skills rather than content. Unnecessarily challenging
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Classroom environment was not welcoming and sometimes hostile. Professor could be condescending at times. Dr. Wilbourn is definitely a talented lecturer and engaging, but doesn't makeup for the other problems with the class. Half of the required materials on exams was not taught in class....needed to teach it to yourself via the textbook

Introduced class's relevance to all fields - learning from her was truly inspiring and interesting. She is the most engaging and entertaining lecturer I have had, and explains+connects concepts extremely well. Grading guidelines and assignments are clearly stated in syllabus at beginning of semester. Passionate + culturally sensitive. Fun section.

103 is harder than it should be. Lectures are disorganized: some topics span multiple lectures without warning, and Dr. Wilbourn ran out of time often, making taking notes stressful. 100+ pages of textbook weekly. Didn't respond to the one email I sent during the semester, but approachable after class. Multiple opportunities for extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Class was very disjointed. The TA's would grade harshly and were not helpful. Dr. Wilborn would assign us 150+ pages of chapter reading every other week and expect us to know 6 chapters for an exam with little to no information about what we need to know in the chapters. Attendance is taken each class. Avoid.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: She's good at lecturing and her tests are very fair - ready the textbook, listen, and you will do well. She's well versed in sensitive issues like race in America, but often uses "Asian" cultures as a monolith to provide the opposite cultural example to what goes on in America.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Wilbourn is hilarious! I definitely recommend taking this class because she's such a funny lecturer. It's interesting and not too much work too.

I think it was a hard semester for her as the class organization did not go so well. However, the TAs are super helpful, and the lectures are very enjoyable. Easy A overall. I think Prof Wilbourn lectures really well. Some of the takeaways from her lecture will benefit me for my lifetime :)

Wilbourn is an amazing lecturer but was basically absent for the second half of the semester. It's a shame because when she is there, I learn a lot. It seems that the TAs do most of the class work. I lost motivation towards the end because exams still covered so many things that she didn't teach us and it was essentially self-study. Disappointing

I'm gonna be honest, this semester was super poorly organized - it was never clear what the assignments were, what material to read or cover for the test, and the syllabus changed rapidly. Dr. Wilbourn is clearly passionate and absolutely HILARIOUS, but the confusion of this semester means I don't recommend this class anymore.

During this virtual semester we didn't get much interaction w/ the professor, just watch prerecorded lectures and go to discussion. Her lectures are very entertaining and easy to digest. Assignments were easy and grading lenient. Final paper at the end.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Dr. Wilbourn is the best. Incredibly kind, caring and accommodating for all her students. Section in this class is just to get you thinking about the material, but only counts for attendance (and participation efforts) - that said it's very interesting. Her lectures are funny & online tests not too bad. Would highly recommend!
Lectures were great and Professor Wilbourn really made an effort to be accommodating. Section is mandatory but pretty superfluous.
I really enjoyed this class!

Dr. Wilbourn is a dynamic lecturer. She was disorganized with following the initial syllabus, but she is a fair grader. Her tests are not analytical but heavily detailed. Make sure to memorize micro facts, have a good relationship with your TA, and go to the extra credit benefit of doubt opportunities.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Not as good a lecturer as Hard, but more energetic and funnier. Tests are multiple choice and focus a lot on what was said in lecture. However, there always are some textbook only questions, so you have to read it although it's annoying reading the whole textbook to answer a few questions on every test
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Definitely a good teacher and is part of the reason I feel comfortable with majoring in psychology. Compared to Dr. Hard who she co-taught with, her lectures weren't as engaging or interesting, but that's not to say they were not better than most professors I've ever had. Definitely a great class to take and a good professor.

Very unclear in her requirements. At the beginning of the semester she stressed that learning concepts was most important, but when the tests came around, it was all about micro-facts. In a psychology course.  Great person, despite all.  I would not take this class again.

Tests are random facts that need to be memorized. She considers herself a tough grader, but does not provide clear guidelines nor does she provide feedback for improvement. TAs are very helpful in this class, and their discussion classes have completely different assignments.  Work and knowledge from discussion classes are not tested on exams.
Great class and lecture, but Wilbourn makes you work for the grade and doesn't believe in giving out A's.

Wilbourn is a great lecturer. She's funny and informative at the same time. However, the tests can be very difficult if  you don't spend time memorizing little details, which is frustrating because the material itself isn't that hard.  Weekly papers are busy work. Overall, this class won't be much fun unless you're really interested in dev psych

Wilbourn is an all-around great professor. She knows everything about Developmental Psychology, shes is very clear about what will be on tests, and she makes the lectures funny and interesting. The class is very worthwhile and not very hard.
There's 2 tests and 2 papers both under 5 pages double spaced. Easy A if you go to lecture and take good notes. Really enjoyed it!
Definitely take a class with Makeba. One of my favorite professors at Duke. She's hilarious and makes lectures much more enjoyable to attend.
Professor Wilbourn is the best! Her tests are mainly lecture-based so be sure to attend class but the lectures are really interesting. Definitely my favorite professor so far.

Lectures were funny, entertaining, and clear. Definitely go to them. Try to stay on track with textbook readings. She makes the expectations super clear, so the exams aren't too bad. In fact, they are really fair. 2 exams, 2 papers. Grading can be a bit harsh at times, but I survived with an A in the course. Highly recommend her developmental psych
Dr. Wilbourn is great. If you are interested in developmental psychology, make sure to take it with her. You learn a lot and she makes lectures pretty fun! She rocks.

Dr. Wilbourn is an amazing lecturer. Always interesting with great examples. She made me want to continue learning about developmental psychology. Highly recommend going to class, Dr. Wilbourn definitely makes attending lecture worth it! LOVE HER!
Wonderful professor! Super helpful and great to work with. She made the class so interesting and fun.

Favorite class at Duke thus far. Kept the material interesting, fair grader. Tests definitely a mix of book and lecture. Got an A in the class. She's also very fair and reasonable.best to attend lectures.
She is an awesome person and wonderful teacher.

Dr. Wray is a great lecturer and is passionate about biology. I took 203, which I believe is not being offered anymore, and it was a great class. Be prepared to dedicate some time to studying and reviewing lectures if you want to succeed. Lecture slides are made available before class, and all lectures are recorded and posted. Great professor!

Dr. Wray is decidedly the better half of this class. His lectures were clear, and despite being entirely review from AP Bio, mostly engaging. He is also more than fair with returning points when he has made an error, with makes me respect him infinitely. If you did well in AP Bio, this class isn't nearly as difficult/as much work as they say.

Very passionate lecturer. Super knowledgeable about topic and makes molecular biology interesting! Tests are a bit tricky (he tests on the very specifics of the content) so be prepared to memorize info from presentations. Does not offer extra help beyond questions after class.

Wray was such a good professor and lecturer. Made tough concepts about Molecular Bio a little bit easier. Class was overall very difficult and just be prepared to be in a grind. Wray made it a lot better and was just so thorough on his lectures that included very tough concepts. 203 is not joke though and you kind of wish he taught it in whole.

One of the best lecturers I've seen at Duke. He made all biology content interesting and applicable to the real world. The class itself was a little annoying with a confusing curve and attendance checks for all lectures, but I highly recommend taking biology with Dr. Wray. He cares about the topics and his students immensely.

Professor Wray was amazing. His lectures are long and sometimes boring, but he will always get the content across. He is very respectful when you ask questions and makes himself available before/after class.

Only downside of this class is the weird curve that NO ONE knows how to explain.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Test heavy

reviews.comment: Very caring professor, always answers any questions during lecture. Uploads slides and lectures online. Is very clear with his teaching and the slides he uses to teach. Also super hilarious. His tests are super hard. Required mostly memorization. Be prepared to spend every other week solely on studying bio

I wish I could have gotten to know Dr Wray more. He seems very nice and his research sounds very interesting. His lectures were fast paced, covered a lot of material and quizzams every other week was rough. Only recommend if you really enjoy bio and have credits for it.

Prof. Wray is an outstanding professor. He teaches the first half of BIO 203 (the molecular biology half), and I much preferred his portion. Lectures are clear, concise, and interesting, and he's very approachable/accessible to answer questions. It's certainly not an easy class, but Prof. Wray makes the material as straightforward as possible.

This class was just so hard. His lectures were kind of boring because he mainly read off of the PowerPoint. He seems like a really great person, but I honestly didn't get a whole lot out of the lectures. The tests were crazy hard, and that's where almost your entire grade comes from. There isn't a final though, which is nice.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Great class! Expect 1-2 written summaries of primary literature each week, and a "grant proposal" paper at the end.
Wray is not the best lecturer. The class felt long, drawn out, and boring, and honestly, I can't tell you what I learned this semester.

He was a great lecturer, and I wish I had gotten to know him more. He seemed like he would be willing to give individual help, but since the class is so large it's hard to get to know him. The tests were multiple multiple choice and were very hard. Tough class for me.
Interesting class but hard tests
He is not a spellbinding lecturer, but he is more than adequate. I would recommend taking the class with him.

i really disliked this class, however Wray wasn't a horrible teacher. His slides contain a lot of information and quiz/test questions will frequently have answers that were said ONCE on ONE slide, possibly hidden in a picture, so those can be super frustrating. he does like to bring up cool examples and applications of the topics though

Very good lecturer. He clearly explains all the important concepts and why they're important, and he explicitly tells you what you're expected to know for exams. Only thing is exam questions are weirdly worded/hard to understand and are multiple response.

Phenomenal lecturer. Tries to make complex concepts as easy to understand as possible. Always willing to stop and answer questions. His sense of humor makes lectures enjoyable, and his enthusiasm for biology is contagious. However, be aware: Bio 201 is very difficult, and it is not curved. The TAs are in charge of assessments and grading.
Very good lecturer. The tests are hard, but you learn a lot.
really nice professor, makes jokes in lecture and has very clear powerpoints/lecturing style. it was worth taking it in the spring to have bio 201 with him!
Enthusiastic and helpful lecturer, definitely makes an effort to help his students. Stays after lecture to answer questions, and has a friendly sense of humor as well.

Took the Bio 101 with him and Hasse. I thought Wray had interesting, fun lectures and was really nice. He answered questions patiently and always tried to explain concepts to students in different ways to help them understand.

He co-taught this class with Haase my semester. Wray is definitely the more approachable of the two. He seems to be a genuinely good guy and is also a good professor. Can be a little bit more boring than Haase, but if you like biology then you'll be able to stay interested.

Really fun class, great lectures. The TAs were okay, but the professor was awesome. Your grade is not guaranteed in this class, but if you spend a reasonably amount of time studying you'll do just fine. Definitely one of the best NS classes at Duke (unless you're a science major).

TAs were terrible. Tests were often confusing and tried to trick you. Wray was enthusiastic and always made class interesting. Preparing for tests adequately enough for an A was time consuming and fairly difficult. No homework however.

Wray is hilarious and awesome at lecturing. However, this class was NOT an easy A. Exam material and grading was somewhat arbitrary, and he curves the average to a B-, so obviously everyone can't get an A. However, it is definitely a much better NS  option than most other science courses.. just don't take your grade for granted. Lots of memorizatio

G. Wray is the best! Dino Bio was the easiest class...no work except short quizzes graded for completion only!  All you have to do is attend lectures and cram before the exams. Pretty funny in a nerdy science way, and a really great person. I would take another one of his classes easily.

do not take this class unless you have an excellent memory.  it's strictly memorization and there are literally hundreds of things to memorize.  nothing is conceptual but it's a lot more difficult than you would think considering it is "dino bio"  i thought it would be a joke and i was wrong.

Do NOT take your grade in this class for granted.  You MUST attend lectures and take good notes in order to study for tests.  Wray is very nice and understanding, and a good lecturer.  A bit hard to find outside of class, and I'm slightly mystified as to how he grades, but the class is a great option for non-science people.

Sweet topic with dinosaurs and the tests are ridiculously easy with a bit of studying...BUT...he CURVES DOWN without any prior notification.  With a 95 average and an A at midterm I somehow ended up with an A- after getting a 95 and 97 on the tests after the midterm...an 82?...C+...why put out the effort to have it knocked down in the end?
Great option for non-majors to get an NS credit. I really enjoyed lectures and became interested in dinosaurs, not something I was expecting!

Easy class, to the point that I feel like my intelligence is insulted. You do have to go--it will make the tests way easier. Yet, still a good way to learn a lot about basic biology, and some really interesting Dinosaur facts.

The lectures are very well-prepared.  Going to lecture is a bit too necessary as the tests are based exclusively on lecture.  I am upset about how hard this class ended up being, but I learned a lot of really cool knowledge about the dinosaurs, and I am really sad this class had to end.  We watched Jurassic Park on the last day of class.

terrible at response rate.  scheduling makeup takes forever as he does not respond.  Not clear on his policies in general and has tendency to say the wrong thing in class leaving you with wrong information in your notes.
Not that much work outside of class (don't buy the book) and interesting lectures.  Tests weren't bad, just a lot of memorizing notes.  So-so curve at the end of the year.
Not that easy. Lots of memorization and TAs are picky. He gives you a lot of opportunities to bring your grade up though.
He missed appointments with me three times for a makeup exam and left me waiting in BioSci for him to come back and say he just forgot or got tied up in a meeting.  Ever heard of email?
Absolutely Awesome. Funny, intelligent, and easy.
Easiest class.  Just go to class and you're golden.
No Comments

Dino bio is the best class ever!  Lots of fun!! Dr. Wray is awesome... he crawls around on the stage pretending to be a dinosaur!  Don't buy the text book for sure, you won't be tested on it.  If you hate science classes, but need one for C2K, TAKE BIO47!

David is one of the best teachers I've had: very smart, humble, kind, and supportive. If you take his course, you will benefit not only from his knowledge and philosophical thinking but also his kindness and supportiveness. I am a professor myself now, and I aspire to be someone like David, even though I know I can never be as good.

Super kind, great professor, very interesting content. Would HIGHLY recommend you submit your essays for him to review before the deadline, and to do the readings. He gives great feedback and you'll do well on your papers.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I love prof Wong. You just have to speak on 8 lectures during the whole semester and the topics he chooses are all pretty interesting. Grading is writing 8 posts and 3 5-page essays, which you can submit to him beforehand for feedback. Would totally take this class again
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: An excellent professor! He lets you rewrite your essays and gives good feedback. He was also very understanding in general and easy to contact
Amazing lectures if you care about the class, fairly easy A with two rewrites on three papers if you don't. Great professor and TAs who give clear feedback for rewrites.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: One of the best philosophy professors here at Duke. 3 papers with two rewrite opportunities and interesting readings. He gives timely and insightful feedbacks.

Wong is genuinely nice, extremely caring, and wants you to actively engage with the material. Unfortunately, 75% of his class is either on social media or multitasking during lecture, so discussion is scattershot. Lecture can be dry esp. when he turns off the lights. Still, I learned a lot and he gives amazing feedback. Rewrites on all essays, too.

I took Professor Wong's Moral Change and Human Nature first-year seminar. It definitely was one of my favorite freshman year classes. Not too much reading, and the movies we watched were so interesting! I genuinely enjoyed writing the three papers, and they weren't too long (5-6 pgs). I've learned so much without too much work. I loved this class!

David's class had interesting moments but was generally pretty hard to stay connected to. I think he is a brilliant thinker and someone incredibly committed to helping his students learn. I like the way he presents and shapes discussions. Would take again. Grading wasn't too bad. I think participation is pretty important for him.

The overall grade for the class was just based on three 5-6 page papers. Professor Wong gives good feedback on the papers, two of which you can rewrite for a better grade. He's also a really friendly guy and is in depth in lecture.

About 2 reading assignments a week that are relevant to the papers and in-class lectures. however, Dr. Wong is very thorough in his lectures, which makes writing the papers very easy. The class grade is determined based on posting on the forum and three 5-6 page papers. You are allowed a rewrite for the first two papers. Great teacher.
Graded off 3 papers and forums, he offers a rewrite oppt for 2 of the papers. Lectures were engaging, he's a great prof

Wong is a super chill professor, and he clearly cares about both the materials that he teaches and the students in his class. I would definitely recommend taking a class of his if you ever get the chance.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Inspirational--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Very intelligent and caring professor. The material we learned about (Chinese Philosophy) was super interesting and a large part of that was because of Professor Wong. Only 3 essays for the grade, and he gives great feedback and opportunities for edits so getting a good grade is quite attainable. The supplementary reading is really cool too.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Class has really interesting material. Professor Wong is also an extremely intelligent and friendly professor. Definitely would recommend any of his classes.
Interesting class. Not a lot of work, but papers are toughly graded.

Second time with Wong as a professor - he's so good I went out of my way to take more of his classes. Very thoughtful and very intelligent. Raises really thought-provoking issues. If you actually care, you'll have a great time. Expects a good amount of effort on papers.

Awesome and super intelligent dude but critical of your work as he would be critical of like... a published philosopher. Helps you grow as a thinker and cares about your writing but, yeah, rigorous. Kind of a role model though.

He's a good professor who makes long, detailed slideshows that cover all the material. He also incorporates your online forum posts into the class discussion. Just one term paper and he is a fair grader if you put in the work. Not the most exciting class or teacher, but definitely a solid one.

Wong gives long lectures with discussion breaks for the most part -  I thought they were cool but some people find them boring. You really should do the readings or the books you read won't make much sense. Grading is fair - spend a good amount of time on the papers and you'll get a good grade.

Professor Wong is generally an extremely intelligent guy; he does a great job of explaining philosophical arguments. His grading is tough but fair. He doesn't sugarcoat criticism, which is good. My only gripe is that he's dull, and spends every class slowly reading through his power-point slides.

EXTREMELY clear lecturer, breaks down complicated philosophical arguments so that they are easy to understand.  Also a really nice guy, always excited to answer questions and meet with students individually.  Very smart but also very respectful of opposing opinions.  Highly recommended!  Only complaint is that class could get a little boring.
Everyone just sits in class on facebook and stuff.  Such a waste of time.  We read really boring books.  Don't take this intro course it suckssss

Wong is a pretty good professor. In this ethics class, most of the readings are interesting/applicable, although there are some ethicists we read who seems to be forced in there. Only other complaint is that Wong has a rigid lecturing style, and sticks very closely to his notes. Wong reads drafts of essays, so, given that, grading is very fair.
great teacher that really knows how to get across the information and connect with the class

Wong is a great teacher and frequently uses contemporary examples to bring ancient concepts to life. He is open to discussing points of view other that his own as well. Overall, I learned a lot in his class.
Best teacher in the philosophy department.  A great class for anyone looking to get better at life.

Helpful and invigorating; encourages a lot of class discussion.  I agree, he may be a bit attached to his own views, but this only showed a couple times over two courses total, and never prevented him from teaching a wide variety of theories.
Prof. Wong is a little harsh when it comes to commenting on pepers, but it doesn't really show in his grading.  He's a nice guy, though maybe a little attached to his own interpretations of things.
No Comments
No Comments

Dude's chill. Gives detailed and concise lectures, problem sets and practice exams are very very very representative of exams. Textbook is completely useless, (just review lectures and watch yt vids/use chatgpt to fill in gaps then do practice questions).
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Inaccessible, no office hours, unclear expectations for covered material, intentionally lowers averages on exams, killed everyones GPA and didn't have a word to say to anyone in the class outside of his incredibly painful lectures. I genuinely think this man is a horrible person and professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's the 2010 MVP season Lebron James of Duke professors.
Hes such a great teacher peak lectures the way hes sounds moves the crowd and hes awesome sauce Hes like like tom brady or the shohei of the professor world.

Dr. Widenhoefer presents organic chemistry extremely sensibly. His lectures focus on the fundamental reasoning for reactivity, so his class requires almost no memorization—just applying basic principles to new molecules. Somewhat intimidating at first, but he is very kind and has a good sense of humor. His knowledge and expertise are great assets.

Took orgo 2 with Ross during the summer. Three midterms, each 33.3% of grade. No extra credits or dropping lowest score. Gives clear lectures on white board. Exams tend to reflect lecture material fairly well, but very difficult. Around 5 ppl withdrew after second midterm. Take very good notes, since anything could be on exam. He is inaccessible.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Widenhoefer is a great lecturer. He is incredibly thorough and expects the same from his students in the exams. There were only 2 midterms and the final to weigh on your grade. His delivery style is not the most inspirational, so if you want to fall in love with Orgo, this is not your instructor.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lecture is super important, so take detailed notes and always do practice exams. Skip textbook reading. Email a week in advance if you want office hours. Tests are difficult but not impossible, though they are 100% of your grade. Do not count on the final to improve your grade - the average was 10 points lower than for midterms.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very challenging course but Widenhoefer lectures extremely well. take good notes and pay close attention in class. Practice tests closely mirror exams and discussions. Reading textbook helps.

Widenhoefer could not care less about his students--doesn't hold office hours and doesn't respond to emails. That being said, his lectures overlap well with the exams, so there's no need to read the textbook. Just do the many practice exams that he gives out. Curve of 1 SD above mean is a little ridiculous, but not impossible.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: take orgo 2 with parise or cox if you can, they seem to actually enjoy teaching. so unapproachable and doesn't really provide resources, just shows up and writes on a whiteboard. tests have no partial credit, which is insane because the entire class is 100% tests. doesn't even hold office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Widenhoefer is an amazing lecturer, and you will learn a lot in this class. He was able to fully answer my questions if I approached him at the end of class. Do end of chapter problems and practice tests. He doesn't agree with everything in the textbook, so you have to pay attention in class. Don't rely on partial credit.

If you consider yourself an average Duke student, do not take this course. Before this course, I was able to get great grades in other chem classes at Duke, however this one ruined me. The exams are graded with no leniency where one extra carbon can lose you all the points, there is no professor support, and lectures are incredibly hard to follow.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
His lectures are organized. Writes neatly on a whiteboard, goes at a slow pace, & pauses for note-takers. 

He's inaccessible. Doesn't respond to emails or hold OH. He clearly wants as little to do with his students as possible. 

"All or nothing" grading approach causes almost no partial credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Put in the bare minimum effort, held no office hours, and took 3+ business days to email back. Doesn't care about learning and made comments about wanting the average on exams to decrease. Expect harsh grading, as 1 mistake can cost you an entire 15 point question. This class is too expensive and important to be taught by someone this incompetent.

Professor Widenhoefer is inaccessible: he does not hold office hours and does not stay after class/come to class early to answer questions. Nevertheless, he teaches very well and his exams are very fair. They test your abilities to recognize patterns and go beyond regurgitating the same easy mechanisms. Read the textbook and do his practice tests!

Solid professor. Class is 3 midterms, each 1/3 of your grade. Scheduling sucks, sometimes we would learn mechanisms and it would be on the test the next day, but Ross is very knowledgeable and gets to the point. He goes fast in lectures but always stops for questions. Honestly just study several hours a day and do practice tests and you'll be fine
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Widenhoefer makes organic chemistry fun to learn. The concepts went over in class were very clear. Tests heavy, so it is necessary to put in some efforts to do well in this class.

Very smart guy. He explains mechanism well and why other mechanisms don't work: makes it easier to understand rather than memorizing. Teaches old school on whiteboard, easy to follow. Exams are mostly applied concepts, so I suggest you let all the info sink in and DO NOT MEMORIZE! He's not good with partial credit and not accessible outside class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Widenhoefer is great. Even though this class is hard, but he always gives good lectures to clear things up. It is true that he might be hard to reach out if you have questions, but you can always go to his office or send him an email to schedule an appointment. Overall, Professor Widenhoefer is a solid choice for this class.

Professor Widenhoefer is a great choice for this class. It is true that organic chemistry is very difficult, but i still think the materials covered by Professor Widenhoefer are super useful. I would recommend his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Widenhoefer is a very knowledgable person. He always explains the concept so well in this class. The exam is tough, but it is reasonable if you put in efforts. I would recommend his class if you are interested in organic chemistry or related fields.

Prof. Widenhoefer's class is really difficult but I learned so much from this class. He doesn't do partial credit on exams, so studying is essential. It is a very rigorous course but that is due to the difficulty of the subject. Widenhoefer teaches the material and you learn so much in this class. Def worth the struggle.

Prof Widenhoefer is a very difficult teacher, but the only drawback is he has no office hours. But with the right TA, the class is totally doable. There is an old saying: "A professor doesn't only hold your hand hand, he also holds you heart"... Dr. Widenhoefer definitely doesn't hold your hand, but truly one of my fav prof ever.

Dr. Widenhoefer is the real MVP! You learn a lot from him. Be prepared to work (and maybe cry) and definitely chase him down to talk to him. But due to Dr. Widenhoefer, I changed to being a Chem Major! He is totally the man, the myth, the LEGEND!

Dr. Widenhoefer is not as bad as everyone says. Is he a tough grader: ABSOLUTELY. Is he hard to track down sometimes: for sure. But when you are able to find him, he is so smart and willing to help out. IF YOU WANT TO ACTUALLY LEARN ORGANIC, TAKE THIS CLASS!

Okay tbh, he isn't nearly as bad as what some ppl say. He can be a bit dry at times but I honestly really enjoyed his lectures & does a good job explaining concepts. Yes, he's a bit inaccessible bc he doesn't hold OH but if you reach out he's really willing to help. Exams are difficult & grading is a bit unclear but he's p generous with grades!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Avoid at all costs. horrible lecturer, does not provide students with any additional help, disrespectful, does not care to speak to students, or answer questions. does not provide materials to help students succeed, lecture is unorganized, and often unclear. tests don't reflect class lecture, his class was one of the worst experiences of my life.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: While organic chemistry is extremely complex and difficult in nature, taking Chem202 with Dr. Widenhoefer online seemed to make the experience even more difficult. Any resources like practice problems and practice tests were often posted late (as well as keys), and there were no office hours; learning from mistakes before exams was difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Ok: here's the objective review you need. I didn't do extremely well or poorly. Im not emotionally swayed like the exaggerators on here. Pros: Lectures clearly with focus on relevant CONCEPTS needed for exam Cons: no office hours, slow/no email response, partial credit: v low pattern recog/synth knowledge on test Its Orgo. Its abt u more than prof
completely unwilling to help, even when asked questions or clarifications. unresponsive, refuses to respond to emails. does not hold office hours. don't know how this guy still works at duke.

Worst teacher I've ever had in my life. Never responded to any emails I sent him, and refuses to have office hours to discuss questions. No partial credit awarded on tests, so if a single part of your answer was wrong, you get no credit. AVOID AT ALL COSTS!!!!!
The exams are essentially a puzzle and they test unnecessarily specific things. They're frequently not an accurate evaluation of a student's understanding of the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Learning orgo with him is like being taught a new alphabet and then being expected to be fluent in the language. His lectures are fuzzy and often out of order and hard to synthesize/correlate information with the book. He gives basically no partial credit on tests. No office hours and extremely unhelpful when asked for advice/clarification.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Amazing class. I love Widenhoefer as a professor, his straightforward demeanor and dry humor make his class genuinely enjoyable. Although he can be a bit dull at times, I have absolutely no complaints. There aren't any surprises on the tests either. Show up to his lecture and you will do well. He rocks!!! Go Ross!!

Prof. Widenhoefer is incredibly intelligent when it comes to orgo, and that certainly comes through in his lectures. Tests are reasonable (with averages around 70%), and previous years' exams are on Sakai. I rarely used the textbook, as lecture provided most of the necessary information. The only time he holds office hours is the week of exams.

Organic chem is never a breeze, but Prof. Widenhofer made it straightforward by giving excellent, clear lectures and then testing fairly on the material he had lectured on. No wonky "figure out how to synthesize penicillin from gasoline" problems here.

Lectures are super clear and his tests are straightforward, fair and basically straight from lecture material. I barely used my book. Dont skip class and use all of the practice tests he releases! Of course org is tough, but Professor Widenhoefer made it surprisingly manageable.
Awesome & clear lecturer
Really amazing lecturer, tests are fair and curved.

Widenhoefer is a fantastic lecturer and managed to make an extremely difficult subject understandable. His tests are tough (not too much partial credit) but he makes it pretty clear what he expects you to know and provides tons of practice tests which help a lot. Plus he's an amusing sort of quirky which made class entertaining.
He's an awesome teacher. The material is hard, but if you go to lecture and studies the problem he gives, you'll do fine.

Very clear lecturer.  Gives you the information you need to do well on the tests and understand Organic 2 in a synthesized way that is continuously building on previous knowledge. Previous tests and solutions as well as attending lecture are very useful for this class (although lecture attendance is not required).
Great lecturer. Explains everything clearly and lectures are easy to follow. He does cover some things that aren't in the book. Tests are all completely doable.
Very clear lecturer, made a supposedly difficult class unexpectedly easy. Relied entirely on notes from class and didn't need the book at all. Overall a great and relaxing class.

Save yourself some time - don't even open the book.  Exam questions come straight from lecture and past exams.  Widenhoefer may not be the most outgoing guy in the world, but lectures are very clear and straightforward, and as long as you study from lecture notes and understand the mechanisms (just knowing them is not enough), you should be fine.

Overall, a very good professor for orgo. His lectures are very, very clear and wonderfully explained, but his tests are hard (but doable if you study A LOT). He is unintentionally very funny, though he does throw a few subtle jokes here and there.  You don't really need the textbook if you take good notes. He provides all of his old exams on Sakai.
Not too difficult if you take notes from lectures and study them. Very clear and very easy to follow lectures.

His tests are very straightforward. The best way to do well in his class is to take really good notes during lecture and refresh your memory on them the day before the exam. You only need to do the suggested problems. Lectures can be boring - find ways to entertain yourself. He has interesting quirks. Keep a list.

Very tough. Tests are hard, and partial credit is hard to come by. Also very boring in lecture, doesn't particularly have any interest in his students, and certainly isn't going to waste his time trying to help you. I loved orgo until this class.

He is not a very accessible man outside of his class, but his lectures are very clear and straighforward. You cannot do the mechanisms enough before each exam. practice practice practice, one wrong arrow can cost you 10/15 points! And do the old exams, as maaaany as you can get your hands on beyond blackboard or sakai

Fair professor. Tough nontheless because it is organic chemistry. very funny and comical. i came to enjoy him a lot more as the semester progressed. his exams are reasonable and he does provide a good amount of exams. he takes a while to respond to emails though.

Widenhoefer is hands down one of the best Orgo professors at Duke. Not only is he clear in lectures and expectations, he also has a great sense of humor-dry, but funny. Doesn't give answer keys to old exams, but is extremely helpful during office hours and will gladly answer your questions. Exams are very fair if you study. Def recommend for orgo
Good professor. funny.

I do not understand why Widenhoefer's ratings are so low. He is a great orgo professor. Very straight forward and very clear. He always answers questions in class and after class. I would recommend taking orgo with him.
He's obviously a very intelligent guy. A little scary maybe, but not after you get to know him. He's a very good teacher with clear and concise explanations.

I don't understand why his ratings are so low. He's honestly is a very clear professor and really great teacher. His exams are difficult, but do-able if you study enough. The class is very difficult by nature, but it's very straightforward.
The class is difficult by nature. However, he has very clear and organized notes, making the lectures very easy to follow. Tests are hard, but definitely doable if enough studying is done.
very difficult grader, barely any partial credit, makes lots of mistakes in class but expects no mistakes on tests. try not to take.
He manages to ignore his students quite well. All throughout class one guy had his hand up and he did not get called on AT ALL. If you can take another prof, do it!
Not helpful. Doesn't teach, just talks. Awful. I loved organic chemistry before his class. Boo.
Confident and clear in his lectures. Emphasizes basic concepts and tests are reasonable.

Very arrogant man. Always late for class. Very unhelpful - you wouldn't find him in his office if there was a tornado outside. His exams are graded harshly and he is unwilling to explain what you did wrong.

Lectures are straightforward, although hard to follow at times.  Tests are tricky... really really tricky... but not hard once you get used to them.  Overall a decent prof, although I wouldn't have him teaching freshmen every year...
Brash, boring and goes completely off topic resulting in really random, useless notes.  Useless!

Widenhoefer is definitely difficult.  However, like the post below states...you will know your organic chemistry after a semester with him.  The tests make you think--a lot.  I never actually went to his office for help, but rate him high because I thought his lectures were helpful.  Don't be scared off as you will learn a lot.

Widenhoefer is...unique.While he didn't do review sessions, practice problem sets or give solutions to the old exams, you will definitely understand the theoretical aspect of organic chemistry if you are able to follow lecture.His tests aren't bad, but require that you know the lecture better than your lover's body.Won't spoonfeed you like Baldwin.
No Comments
His tests were unreasonable. He is very unhelpful. No office hours! Extremely boring lecture! Not a good professor for orgo.

Very unclear, does nothing for the students except lecturing, no review sessions, no solutions for practice exams, takes forever to post anything within period of helpfulness. Lectures are random, unplanned. I always get the sense he's improvising most of the stuff he's teaching. I agree he's intelligent, but as a prof not very good at all.
Ahhh...slick hair man.  He is very intelligent but lecture is a bit dry.  I should have used his office hours earlier in the course.  He'll help you if you ask but you need to be proactive.

Hard teacher to learn from at first, but really good after a while.  Funny guy that made orgo interesting.  Tests are really hard and makes you think... A LOT.  Kind of a rough grader and curves aren't that great.  If you take this class as a freshmen, it gets curved to a B+

Ross lectures quite effectively; much easier to learn from lecture than from the text. Fairly clear, easy to follow, informative, etc. But the tests are quite challenging; many problems are like mind puzzles. One big negative though is that he doesn't seem to take students' performance personally.
dr. widenhoefer is a stud, but he grades on a tough curve.

He's a cool guy, and he really knows his stuff.  I didn't think orgo was that hard at all, he was very clear.  He taught a complicated subject as best as it could be taught, and explained things well.  He posts his old exams online, which is helpful on new ones.
Orgo is hard, and although he's receptive to questions during his office hours, his lectures are somewhat unclear and difficult to follow.
Prof. widenhoefer's lectures were well organized and informative.   he was also helpful outside of class

Good teacher, tough class. Covers lots of information in class and is pretty good at getting it across. The thing is he covers so much information  for an exam that you might think you got it down when you take notes. But there's so much to study before a test. Tests were straight forward but tough.
Go into his office hours, cuz he's a lot of help there.  He knows what he's talking about, so don't be afraid to ask questions.  Also...bring up baseball.
Orgo is tough, Ross is an okay prof. Exams are tricky, lectures usually follow book pretty closely. Not a particularly exciting guy. Explains material pretty well, open to questions.
Ross is a cool dude

She's approachable, kind, and always willing to answer questions or clarify concepts. Be prepared to put in the work, though; her exams are challenging but fair, and they test your understanding, not just memorization. If you take responsibility for your learning, you'll do well.

I am not going to say much, if I do, I cannot really remain anonymous, but I have to agree with what many others have written. I wish her the best at Clemson or wherever, she just was not what was best for me for reasons I do not believe were fair. That is all.

She is not available for help if you need it. She hardly teaches anything-- the class was a bunch of recorded lectures from the medical school. She is unnecessarily strict, unforgiving, and is not willing to meet you half way over anything. Even when things are out of your control, you are penalized.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment:
⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️
The syllabus is clear and thorough, and Dr. Wood is incredibly supportive if you seek help. This course taught me to overcome challenges and pushed me to grow. Every pre-med/pre-dent student needs a class like this, and Dr. Wood delivers it with grace and expertise
Dismissive and unkind. Avoid at all costs.

She is the worst prof I have every had. She has no respect fo her students and always acts like she is better than you and everyone. Her questions on exam are worded to trick you and does not take criticism well.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Latin 308 - I liked the setup of class and prof Woods is a really understanding prof. The translations for class can take a while to prep but the constant practice definitely helps you get better at translating.

Prof. Woods is awesome. She made the graduate level course of Latin Paleography very interesting and engaging as an undergraduate. My graduate student classmates were more than passionate about Latin. I would highly recommend taking a graduate level course by Prof. Woods if you really love classics.

Hardest part about this class is staying awake. Very kind professor and very passionate about the subject matter, however she does not fully engage the students and often goes on confusing tangents. If you can stay awake and contribute to the conversation once a day, you'll get an A.

Woods is a sweetheart with a cute accent. Lectures, however, are very boring unless a project or idea is introduced. Debates and conflict stimulated thoughtful discussion but otherwise half the class was trying to stay awake. She's obviously passionate about Classical Studies and shows it in her work; she just has to get the class involved as well.
HOT!  Her class is cake.  Do the reading and you pass.  She can whinge a bit about her views on things but she's a cool prof.
Took a easy midterm then stopped going to class after that because the final paper had nothing to do with anything she talked about in class. It was great.
She's so cute!  Sexiest prof I've had at Duke.
pretty good. tries really hard to help. do not take  in early morning. lulling british accent. or late afternoon

Easy class.  She's kind of long-winded, but she's got a British accent, so that's ok.  Basically we sat around and discussed myths and occasionally wrote a paper or took a midterm on this.  Easy ALP and fairly interesting.

Dr. Wong is a different breed. He works at an extraordinarily high level, and it's clear in the way he approaches problems and the fast pace of the course. Content volume is intense, problem sets are not long but challenging, and exams can be difficult. He glosses over most algebra, but he provides it in the thorough weekly lecture notes.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Great teacher for PDE. He is very organized and detailed in lectures. He posts notes that correspond line-by-line to what's delivered in class -- which is good bc he lectures FAST. Lots of homework but he's flexible about deadlines. He makes midterm study guides and the exams reflect both hw and study guide. Caring and entertaining, will take again
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Wongs class is the best Math class Ive taken in Duke so far. His lecturers are clear and he really knows in depth about what he is teaching.
