Workloads are heavy (10hr/wk) but it really teaches a lot of useful knowledge. He is also a nice guy in the office hours, definitely go to discuss the final topic with him. Overall hes just great.

Good lectures, but was not helpful at all during office hours. Most math professors either work through problems with you or have you go up to the board to work problems, but he does not give any help whatsoever. Also, most of his HW's and answer keys had typos, so many times I had to redo a problem before it was due because there was a typo.

Wong is nice but really difficult. Much harder than the other professors for the same class. I felt like I knew way more than my other peers from other classes but the final didn't cover a lot of the material Wong taught. Kinda awkward. I went to office hours and they were kind of helpful. Overall, wont be the best or worst class you ever take.

Professor Wong clearly cares about his students and their learning. His lecture notes are organized and he spends time making his own problems for homework. That being said, his lectures themselves are hard to follow. Tests are difficult and conceptual for an engineering math course.

Wong put in a lot of effort making all resources possible to students, including typing up all his notes that are quite detailed. But there were various typos throughout homework and notes. Kind of awkward, but very smart and knows his stuff. Tests are HARD but really prepares you for the final compared to other classes (+curve is very reasonable!)
Amazing professor. You can tell he cares a lot about teaching the materials correctly and clearly which is honestly hard to find at duke math. I felt like I learned a lot.
woojin is the man

Professor Kim does an incredible job of making a difficult subject accessible. Homework and tests were tough: being a math course, that's kind of the deal. He holds office hours and stays way longer than he reasonably has to. And while the exams were tough, he errs on generosity with partial credit. Would 100% recommend! Thank you, professor!

Okay professor, but his tests are insane compared to class examples or homework. We had two NP complete problems on our midterms, all of which were already difficult without that. I built my entire next semester around avoiding his class again. If his midterms/finals accurately reflected what he taught, he’d be average, but now it’s absurd.
A really caring and inspirational professor who truly wants you to succeed in the class. Couldn't ask for a better professor.

I struggled with combinatorics, as it wasn't the most intuitive field of mathematics for me. However, despite the fact that there was some growing pain for Dr. Kim teaching his first official course, I still thoroughly enjoyed it. It was a grind, but mostly worth it. I think he'll only improve from here on, so my review might be obsolete later.

Dr. Kim is the best math professor I have ever had. While he teaches some of the notoriously hard classes such as Multi and Linear, he puts tons of effort into teaching and clearly cares about his students. He makes great slides and is very good at explaining the content. Also just an extremely nice guy who creates a great learning environment.

Prof Kim is one of a kind! I enjoyed math all along but came into Duke not thinking of doing a math major but after taking 212 with him, I decided to become a math major and even consider graduate school! He is extremely caring and takes time even outside of his normal office hours to help us and lessons are very enjoyable and learnable

Although Multi at Duke is infamous for its copious homework and formidable grading, having Dr. Kim as my discussion section professor was such a blessing. Dr. Kim evidently pours his heart into teaching itself, perpetually making adjustments to ensure the most productive lectures possible. He's also approachable and smiley--an excellent professor!!

The course was co-taught by three professors and all of them are down to earth. Prof. Wu replies to emails promptly and welcomes any questions. The essay/report rubrics can be confusing, but you can always ask for clarification. The quiz questions are predictable and moderate.
His lectures are SO interesting. He gives many current examples that help to connect what is going on in the world with the topics you are learning about.
If you do the homework and projects by the deadlines, you will easily get an A or B.

Don't listen to anyone who badmouths this prof. I was upset to hear many students pretending like language barrier was an issue here. It's not. Wu is one of the best MATH profs at Duke. His lectures are clear and engaging, and he is a wizard on the chalkboard. Really takes a visual approach to teaching and honestly the class was easy to understand.

Professor Wu does not mess around. His lectures are fast paced and packed from beginning to end, but he always complements his work with many examples which allows for small breathers in between and they help to clarify the material. On the whole he is a good professor, not too much homework and the exams are fair. I would recommend him for Math212

To be fair, the course as a whole generally sucks, and isn't something that anyone enjoys. However, he wasn't the clearest professor and tended to move very quickly. Many people struggled to learn from him, and I turned to using MIT video lectures rather than relying on him to teach me.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Math 212 gets a bit of an unfounded bad reputation at Duke. Dr. Wu completely obliterates this. He is by far the best multi prof, he really cares about his students, will answer any question regardless of how "basic", and goes out of his way to make sure students know how to solve problems. Tests are fair and based on homework. Nan the Man.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Caring

reviews.comment: Very unclear with his expectations. His grading was super subjective. He would take off points for things that were just his opinions even if our answers were correct. This class didn't really involve a lot of marine science, mostly just social science concepts and a LOT about fisheries. Don't take his class if you don't have to/

most enjoyable class i've taken so far. Prof is rlly knowledgeable and his lectures are interactive & creative, often drawing connections between conservation & philisophical/self-reflecting ideas. Class is clearly designed to show you how you can apply concepts to science career. only thing i'd say is sometimes unclear grading guidelines

Xavier is great. Though the class was conducted on Zoom, he was very responsive and accessible. He does his very best to engage all his students. He is very knowledgeable in his field (duh) and is just a fun and thoughtful professor in general. We also had the opportunity to hear from and converse with guest speakers from all over the globe.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr. Wu is a really, really smart guy. But he doesn't care about teaching as much as he cares about his research, and he makes that evident. For our midterm, he gave us a practice test filled with errors, and an answer key with one sentence answer. Our final was a joke, and he tested 30% of the exam on material from the last lecture.
Class was hard, but that is the nature of 250 in general. Prof. Wu was super accommodating to our needs and showed he really cared outside of the classroom.
Professor managed to cover the content of the course and did not set unreasonable tests. However he can come off as uncaring and he can definitely be milder on his tone and improve his attitude.
He's not especially great, but he's also not bad. He can come off a little harsh, but was a reasonably good teacher, at least for higher level math classes.

Easily the worst professor I've had at Duke and probably the worst professor I will ever have. His lectures are convoluted. The homework was unreasonably difficult and unrelated to what was tested on exams. The average on the second midterm was a 50%, and he blamed the students for not preparing well. Please please don't take this class.

The only thing the professor did during the class was reading his notes and writing them to the board. He wiped out the board when it is full, and repeated reading and writing. What he wrote have consistent notational errors that made students difficult to understand. Worse still, the average grade was about a B, and that was for a graduate course.

The worst professor I've had at Duke. He is bad at lecturing and explaining core statistical concepts, is unresponsive to emails, and the midterm averages of 50 with a standard deviation of over 20 points speaks for itself. You must avoid this professor at all costs.
Literally gave out 3 As out of a class of 50 people. He's easily the worst professor I've had at Duke thus far. Please please don't take his class, you woll regret

Do not take this class with Wu. His lectures are incredibly boring and are not relevant to his tests. The other sections had a much more manageable time with the course material (ie not having a final exam). His expectations are unclear and exams range from easy to impossibly hard. On the 2nd midterm, the mean was a 50 and standard deviation a 20.

He doesn't explain anything, and most of the time won't actually solve problems in class. Homework is worth 20%, and everything else is the exams. When he writes problems, they don't always have answers, and the homework is hard but unrelated to class or tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Please don't take this class with Wu. It is by far the most convoluted and poorly-taught class I've taken in my life. He tests on subject matter that he doesn't even teach, and then is disappointed that the class fails the tests. Unhelpful in office hours, and you often leave more confused after you ask for help than before.

Haven't seen any professors who set each problem 1 point and deduct all of it even if you only made a tiny mistake. But very accesible outside class and really want to help students with their learning. But I will never forgive you for your B.

Prof. Cai is a caring educator with profound knowledge. His lectures are well-designed and pretty inspiring. Generally the course is at a fast pace, it is recommended to preview what you'll learn. There are weekly quizzes with moderate difficulty, but they'll be managable by reviewing your homework. Cai is really a nice professor.

Overwhelming class with weekly 4-question quizzes that cover 60% of your grade. Only options for boosting grades by retaking 3 missed questions. 

Be prepared to study a lot and memorize a lot of formulas/proofs (no cheat-sheets for tests). 

Preparing for the final test, quiz, and retake questions all over a weekend is too stressful. Not worth it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: The grading system is terrible. He gave a lot of fill-in-the-answer type of questions, so either you get a full score or you get nothing, no in between. There are 7 quizzes (you can drop one). Each quiz only has 4 questions, totaling up to 4 points, and losing 1 question meant a C.

Weekly quizzes are manageable, but the final is overwhelming with 3 exams (final, quiz 7, and retake) in 4 hours, with only 5 minute break and no cheatsheet. These exams make up over 45% of your grade, so minor mistakes can drastically lower your score, screwing up all progress made in previous weeks. The grading system feels harsh and frustrating.

The class itself isn't too hard, but it moves pretty fast, and with exams every week. His grading is super unclear, and he only accepts his answers. His jokes are also either super lame or just kinda rude. The worst part is the last week, where you have to study for the final quiz, the final exam, and a retake all at once. It's beyond exhausting.

The course was very fast-paced so it was difficult, but that wasn't because of the professor. Prof. Cai is very fair with marking and tries to give extra credit whenever he can. Just listening to lectures isn't enough, be prepared to self-study the textbook. Exams were similar to homework/textbook problems. Overall a nice professor!

Dr. Dong is sweet and I always found her lectures to be fun and really interesting. The grading is tricky, as it mostly focuses on small buzzwords, but if you really know the lecture material, you'll do fine in the class. Dr. Dong is pretty accessible for questions and clearly really cares about the material. Overall really enjoyed this class!!

This review pertains to the Bio212 (microbiology) lecture component only. Professor Dong is, in and of herself, both knowledgable and kind, and the course material is fascinating in my opinion. But the grading seems to focus on minutia/buzzwords that aren't always obviously relevant to the question, making the course a bit frustrating at times.

Dr. Dong is a smart and caring professor, but her tests are a lot of memorizing trivial details and her lab is a lot of stressful busy work. The course hours are deceptive: on top of the regular hours, you're expected to come in multiple nights a week to complete the lab project, otherwise you won't pass. Lab manager is rude and passive-aggressive.

Her accent was not a problem for me. BUT her class is structured awfully and she does a bad job teaching what's needed for the tests. And her tests are obnoxiously difficult. Her labs are loads of stupid busy work. Fortunately there was a curve that came through. But I did not like her or her course.

Sometimes she was a bit difficult to understand during lecture and there was often a lot of extraneous information that I wasn't sure would be included on exams or not. Exams were pretty difficult and the grading was pretty strict. Beware that she doesn't always curve the class, even if the averages for the exams are below a B.
Very easy class especially if you can get ahold of previous exams, she is a very nice teacher and extremely helpful during office hours.  Get to know her and learn everything she says during lecture

Quite an easy class, especially if you have friends who have taken the class with Dong before and can provide you with old practice exams that aren't posted to Blackboard. Take the lab seriously because it's 31% of the grades and the random unannounced lab quizzes can bring you down. Easiest A in the premed lineup, bar none.

Nice lady who teaches down to students, making the class incredibly easy for any student who has taken upper level Bio classes. Biggest flaw is that she is disorganized resulting in lectures that are disjointed and boring. Overall easy class, little effort needed to get an A.

A nice lady who knows what she's talking about but sometimes gets disorganized - her class lectures often run over, which can get annoying. Her tests aren't bad but there are the occasional obscure question. She speaks with a slight accent but it shouldnt be a problem.

Ever feel like in all of your bio classes no matter how hard you study, you can't get above a B?  Well, this class isn't like that. In this class, your effort is directly proportional to your grade.  The lectures are VERY good and organized - something that most professors at Duke simply lack.  The accent is definitely not impossible to understand.

accent is a little tough,yes, but you get used to it easily after a few lectures. EASY class (103), and the test questions are usually  very simple (I averaged like 90-95 on all the tests and got A-). subjective, but material is easy. labs are fun and no writeups. definitely take if you're bio major
Unclear lectures, her accent makes her difficult to understand. Not recommended.
Easy class, very good professor (if you see her one on one she is quite helpful). Clearly interested in helping her students. I agree that grading is very subjective (both in lab and lecture).
unfair grader, does not teach well

The class seemed very hard at the beginning, but became very chill towards the middle of the semester. The homework got way easier and also way shorter / spaced out. Jason is an amazing lecturer and is very clear with the proofs in class, super nice to talk to as well. Don't drop even if it seems really hard at the beginning.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Sta432 was the highlight of my last semester. Professor Xu has amazing board work and the lectures made me really appreciate being back in person. The material is tough but you get a new appreciation of statistics, and Xu stops for questions often and makes it feel not intimidating. Highly recommend!

Rly difficult class conceptually but you will definitely succeed if you keep up w/ content and review constantly. Jason is such an amazing guy, rly helpful in office hours. He posts recorded lectures from past years so I relied on those a lot. Midterm was rly difficult, everyone got bodied, then he lightened up on the final (take home format)
Very very very difficult class but great guy.

Full honesty, probably the best class I ever took at Duke and almost entirely because of Jason -- if you're not sure if STA is for you, stick it out through this class. The math is beautiful (even if you're not a math nerd), and Jason's one of the best lecturers at Duke bar none. Definitely not an easy class but you won't regret taking it.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Jason was a great professor. His lectures went at a nice pace and were very organized, which was super helpful for learning the material. His homeworks were a bit on the harder side but doable if you went to office hours, and they prepared you well for the midterms and final. Would definitely take a class with him again!!
250 was amazing with Xu and is very fair if you put the work in.

Great professor for STA250! His tests are very fair and if you put in the work and know how to do all the assigned homework, you will do great in the class! Funny guy too! Totally recommend taking 250 with him!
Jason is a great lecturer with very fair tests. You can tell he really cares about students learning and Sta250 gave a lot of context and foundation to understanding statistics

I was a bit nervous about this course coming in, but it wasn't bad at all. Jason's lectures were generally very helpful, and he's always willing to clarify explanations and answer questions. Weekly HW was sometimes challenging but overall pretty fair. Two midterms and final had average scores around 80% with questions based on lectures and HW.
Lectures can feel a bit long but he's the best Stats professor I've had at Duke by far. Definitely Flunch him!

Shiqi made my German experience at Duke and is the reason I will be minoring in the course and studying abroad with the department. She genuinely cares about teaching and making an impact on every student. Class is super engaging and she always makes an effort to include personal touches which truly make her and her teaching remarkable.

Professor Xu is one of the most approachable and compassionate teachers I've had thus far. Her lectures and in-class activities are engaging and informative; you can forgo reviewing the new information the night before & still obtain a good understanding of the material by paying attention in class. She does everything she can to help you succeed.

Shiqi is a real gem. She's a really solid teacher - very detail-oriented in her powerpoints and use of class time, and a super compassionate person on top of that. Do the homeworks and participate and you'll have no problem in the class.
really helpful guy! is a straightforward/clear lecturer. also a pretty funny guy without really meaning to be haha.

Xu was not always the most comprehendible of teachers and sometimes had a hard time relating to the class, however he is a great guy. Math 122L is terrible no matter who you take it with, but Xu makes it manageable. He is the nicest professor I have had, cares about your grades, and will not screw you over. His tests are hard, but could be worse.

Xu was very helpful and would always answer questions outside of class. Although the class was difficult, he was always willing to explain concepts and go over notes again. Nicest professor I've had so far!
Xu is really nice.  This class sucks no matter who you take it with, but Xu is always willing to help. If you have to take math, don't shy away from his class. The other teachers were a lot worse...
The nicest teacher I have ever met in duke. He is extremely helpful and smart. Tests are not easy but reasonable.

Great teacher. He makes sure the class understands everything and gives extremely clear lectures. Tests have a couple curveballs but are relatively straightforward. If you do poorly in the beginning and finish strong, he will just look at your "finishing strong" because you showed improvement. Definitely take a class from Ybarra.

Extremely knowledgeable in his field. Gives very clear lectures, though they can be slow-paced some days (not necessarily bad). Really wants everybody to understand EVERYTHING... if you have a question about some tangential topic he mentioned, he WILL devote the rest of the lecture to discussing it. Which is great. Learned a ton about ECE.

He is a great teacher in that he really cares about his students and whether they understand the material or not.  Really helpful if you ask and he is a crystal clear lecturer.  Can get a little boring at times and his tests can be sorta hard but overall a great teacher

An excellent teacher, perhaps a little hard to get used to initially, he cares a lot about the subject and student's understanding. Definitely very competent. Don't take this class with any other teacher.

One of the best professors I've had at Duke. He speaks and writes somewhat slow, but this is actually more helpful as the material gets harder. He cares about the students. He also understands the material so well that he doesn't even need notes (he can make problems and solve them on the spot).

Great teacher, cares a lot about students.  Explains everything thoroughly and clearly.  Goes out of his way to answer questions and make sure everyone understands.  Does lots of examples in class to prepare students for tests and homeworks.
Really cares about your understanding. Funny at times (don't know if it's intentional) and has detailed notes.
Incredibly helpful professor. Sounds condescending but kind of in a funny way and doesn't turn you off from asking questions. Would recommend a class with him.
Goes slow enough so it is easy to understand all the topics. He tries really hard to make sure everyone understands, not just the few kids who answer. Has ungodly patiences...

Amazing teacher!  Very real about life and assignments.  His tests were VERy straight forward and you knew exactly what he wanted you to know.  It was very difficult and intense though when it came to work and materials.  Amazing guy overall and would take any class he teaches.

Very flexible professor.  For example, gave us extra time on final.  Very fair but is very harsh to people who try to take advantage, such as if you delay in turning in your exam at the end of the period by continuing to write.
Very willing to help and work with you as long as you are willing to put in the time.  Not an easy professor, but clear, gives great notes, and is always willing to walk you through a problem.
Ybarra's class is not easy. He expects you to know a lot, but he will teach you exaclty how to do each problem and make things clear. You just have to do the work.

I dont know what someone above was talking about. Professor Ybarra is one of the MOST flexible teachers that I've had here at school. He's willing to negotiate ALL the time. He's a very good lecturer, and never pulls surprises. VERY GOOD PROFESSOR

Gave good notes which were necessary for homework.  Very inflexible however.  Things had to be done his way or else.  He doesn't take kindly with disagreement.  Really, got the feeling that he was an insincere ass who's upset that his research hasn't rendered him a millionaire.
Great lectures and notes, but demands a lot of work. Put in the time and this will be a very rewarding class.

The concepts in class aren't hard, the workload can seem overbearing at times. However, Ybarra is an excellent teacher and is always avaiable for help.  He is also director of undergrad electrical eng.

I learned the most from this class than almost any class at Duke, but it's a LOT of work!  Dr. Ybarra has VERY clear lectures and is always more than happy to help out his students.  He does not take kindly to dishonesty or missing classes.

easy A, weekly readings summaries can be done w chat, super sweet prof, talks pretty slow though and as someone that watches everything on x2 speed it drove me insane. you need to know a lil chinese before u take this class.
Professor Liu is very sweet and patient. The course is well organized.

Prof. Liu is a very nice and caring professor. She really gives good feedback and provides a lot of help when needed. She is one of the most caring professors I have met at Duke. Definitely would love to take another course with her!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Liu Laoshi is one of the best professors I've had; she clearly genuinely cares about her students. The assignments are reasonable and she's very clear about her expectations.

Professor Liu is a great professor. She tries to make everything taught in class inclusive and lighthearted for all the students. I would highly recommend taking any of her classes! She also offers help out of class time and provides very useful feedback for all assignments (if you ask her for help).
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Liu Laoshi is a great professor. She's very kind, and you can tell that she's really invested in helping students learn to the best of their abilities. She's also very willing to work with you if you're experiencing difficulties, be they personal or academic. Please participate as much as you can in class, because it's a better experience for all.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Liulaoshi is really caring. She's always there to help, not matter in classroom or outside of the class.

Very structured class and pretty specific about grading guidelines. Homework was often but not too hard. The most difficult thing was remembering all the words we'd learned. Liu Laoshi is a really nice person and definitely willing to help students as long as they ask.
Super great teacher, really cares about students' wellbeing. If you're struggling, she will do her best to help you. The chinese department at duke overall is fantastic.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Mandarin tutorial. Students in my class did not seem engaged, despite Liu Laoshi's efforts, which shouldn't reflect on her as a teacher. She could improve in organization, especially sending materials in a more timely fashion. That being said, if you do the work and learn to have fun with with Chinese, you can get a lot out of this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: she's really nice, but class can get boring sometimes. she spends a lot of time trying to engage students, but when kids are tired she seems to have a hard time. but still, shes willing to help outside of class and accommodate to your needs. she's super sweet.

Took CHN333 with Liu Laoshi - she's super nice. Textbook readings are supplemented with videos during class and other short readings. Does a good job teaching vocab and grammar. You have quizzes every chapter and tests every 2 chapters, a final paper. Final exam is basically another chapter test.

Prof.Yamey is a really really nice, respectful, and funny professor. His teaching style is really interesting. And he always welcomes students to share their ideas. No HW, several quizzes(but really easy), one group case study, and one final essay. Also, he is really kind to give credit :) Don't hesitate! Take his class!
Dr.Yamey was such an awesome professor and a sweet guy! Little to no homework and a very easy class. Only three exams and lowest one dropped. No final exam, project instead.

The class was super easy and literally the easiest A I have gotten in my life. Although the lecture and discussion material feels super repetitive, it's a great class if you are looking for something that's stress-free to add to your schedule. The grading is super lenient and the quizzes are also really easy if you pay attention or study for them.

This class is painfully boring. Once a week, Yamey teaches a class, which is intuitive.  You then are required to show up for a second class that week to relearn the EXACT same lesson from the TAs.  However, it is also the easiest class I have taken ever.  There is no homework and the quiz questions are actually so ridiculously stupid.

Really terrible. Huge ego and thinks he is an expert because he has many degrees and has traveled everywhere. But he cant do math to save his life - he makes terrible arguments and doesnt understand statistics. Complete fraud. Turned me away from academia.

Dr. Yamey is an inspiring lecturer with a lot of exciting experiences in global health and policy academia. The course material is similar to that of PUBPOL 301, so it may not be the most interesting option for pubpol/global health comajors. The course grade is mostly based on papers, with one easily-graded but heavy-workload group project.

In my three years at Duke so far, Professor Yamey has struck me as one of the best professors I've had. He engages the class and gives very enthusiastic presentations. He's an expert in the field, and gets ideas across very clearly. The class really improved my writing skills. I felt that I left the class with a lot.

Amazing lecturer and figure in global health policy, learned a ton from him and the guest speakers he had Skype in for us. He's a great guy. Not too many readings and all of them were interesting and useful. Participation is worth a lot of the grade and seems kind of arbitrary and grading for the three papers was a bit hard.

He's an awesome lecturer. He's also done really cool things in the Global Health field, so he knows the topic of this course (Global Health Policy) super well. His lectures are funny and very interactive. Grading is easy except for the three essays.

No tests during virtual semester, so graded by only homeworks and small quizzes. Prof. Yang is very caring and often adjusted the course based on student feedback, like giving out more advice for difficult projects. Her lectures are not always the most clear but she answers student questions and clarifies. Textbook is very helpful.

Virtual semester so no tests. Dr. Yang is a fine lecturer but not always clear and the lectures do get a bit dry at times. There were 5 labs of which the first 3 were fine but the last 2 were exceptionally difficult. Office hours are a must.

Class was absolutely brutal. Professor is very caring but is not the most clear with lectures. We didnt have exams this virtual semester and instead had five labs. The last couple got very difficult if you didnt understand the material well. Office Hours are a must.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The virtual nature of this semester's class caused a lot of logistical challenges. Dr. Yang really tried her best to respond to students' feedback and make changes on time. Not the most clear lecturer but fairly good. Textbook & internet are very helpful. Projects are good but can be difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: Overall a good class. The workload was on the heavy side.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The programming assignments are fairly difficult but doable. This class covers a ton of information. The semester was fine but the final was quite surprising/difficult as it covered topics barely covered in lecture and not even touched on the written homework. She also doesn't curve. Wouldn't take if you only care about grades
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Good class, enjoy

Barry is the most emotionally intelligent human being I have ever met. He is the emblem of why journalism is so powerful. This class was worth every bit of work that was expected. You leave this class a stronger writer, more insightful reader, and a better human being. The class seemed so daunting at first and then became the highlight of my week.
Professor Yeoman cares a lot about journalism and his students. He works with you to do your best and is very understanding. Very accessible outside of class. Would recommend him to anyone!

One of the best journalism professors you could learn from, whether you're new to reporting, a writer, or in any field engaging with media. He goes out of his way to step into others' shoes, making you feel heard and cared for. Assignments seem daunting at first, but he eases you in, and you'll finish with a long-form piece to be proud of.

Barry's longform class is genuinely the most wonderful, insightful class I've ever had, taught by a professor who wants nothing more than to see his students succeed (he spent the last 20 minutes of the final class saying what he appreciated about each person). If you're only going to take one journalism class, it should be this one. Hands down.

Barry was a wonderful addition to my life this semester. He is very organized and clear in his expectations for his students, and that made somewhat hefty projects feel more digestible. He is always willing to talk and give you specific advice or feedback, and his expertise in journalism was engaging. Classes were fun, intimate, and meaningful.

I cannot recommend this professor enough. He is so kind, caring, & respectful to all his students while simultaneously providing thoughtful feedback on our stories. Barry always made our 2.5 hour classes fly by. I'm not studying journalism but if I have any room in my schedule during future semesters, I will absolutely take another class w/ Barry!

Anyone interested in pursuing a career in writing should take a class with Barry. Long-form Journalism was a well-paced and interesting class. Barry offered great feedback and expressed genuine care for us and our projects. An absolute gem within Duke's journalism department!!

Gem of a man and diamond of a teacher. SO SO caring and made an effort to connect with every student. Kept everyone on track for the final long-form article by spreading out due dates between the article sections. He gives amazing and in-depth feedback!!! He genuinely cares about his students and inspires them to improve their writing.
The best teach I had for Chinese class!
Great lecturer
Took the class. It was good.
great course and great professor!
This class is so good lol. You watch a lot of movies and talk about important topics in Chinese culture. Recommend it for anyone who cares about learning Chinese.

Most chill class I've ever taken. Would recommend to anyone who wants to experience an engaging Chinese class filled with interesting content. Professor Ye will help you with anything you don't understand and is super flexible with her time. Definitely try and reach out to her outside of class, because she is someone that you will want to know.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Despite the fact that is a 400 level class and is one of the last requirements for Chinese major, this class is fairly easy to get an A in. Professor Ye makes this class extremely fun and interesting and is very friendly. She really promotes student interaction and student-faculty interaction in various different ways. Professor Ye is amazing!

Professor Yujia Ye is one of the best teachers I have ever had at Duke. She is exceptionally caring, friendly, and helpful all the time. Her classes are easy to understand and are always teaching me new content. She is always accessible outside of class and will help you with your work whenever you need. Overall amazing teacher!! Highly recommend.

One of the best professors I've had at Duke. Great lecturer and is able to tie in experience from his career into the lectures in a really interesting way. Guest speakers were great and the projects were time consuming but I learned a lot by doing them. Highly recommend

This was my favorite class I've ever taken at Duke. Professor Yearley is an incredibly accomplished professional in the restructuring world, but you'd think he was also a full-time professor by the quality of his lectures. A genuine pleasure to get to learn from him and the course is curated so well. Highly recommend!

Best class that I took at Duke, incredibly useful and practical. The speakers were exceptional and the assignments were challenging but felt worthwhile. I loved this class and you should 100% take it.
If you can get in Ye Li's class, do it. He is an unbelievable instructor who simplifies difficult material extremely well. He is also really funny if you pay attention enough.

I had heard mixed reviews about Li before taking this class, but I found that he was quite good. Li is readily available to help. He has a very positive attitude, and is reassuring when students are struggling. His English is fine, just sit near the front because he speaks quietly. Also, he teaches to the final, so that is extremely helpful.

Very good professor!  Was initially nervous about Math 103 because of it's terrible reputation, but Prof. Li explained things very well.  Slight accent, but definitely understandable.  Very helpful, and is always willing to talk outside of class if you need extra help.

Great professor. The content is difficult but that is the nature of the course. Very accesible outside of class and appears genuinly interested in the subject matter. I would definitely recommend him as a professor.
His English isn't great but he knows his material and is very smart.

Professor Li is a fantastic professor, one of the best I've had at Duke. He is genuinely interested in his students' success and is a really funny guy (unintentionally). Knows his stuff, makes it very clear and straightforward. Just do the work outside of class and you'll have a great semester.
His accent is really difficult to understand, and he treats students really bad without any respect. It seems he is not familiar with his slides.
I would suggest all potential PhD students avoid this professor as well as all his graduated students.
Lectures are extremely dense. The homeworks also can take forever if you don't have a good GPU.

I have some background in this area, so this course might a little easy but is still suitable for me. I learnt a lot during the lecture. Professor Chen is kind, he always respond to any questions we raised to him. He is smart and can always quickly respond with logic. I learnt a lot and appreciate the efforts the prof took!

I have some basic knowledge before. And I find this course very interesting and useful since it not only provides me with tons of new knowledge and also refreshes my old knowledge from a different perspective.

A great class to take. It's a pity that due to my busy schedule I do not have enough time to take it. Professors are nice and materials are adequate and interesting for an electrical and engineering graduate.
I havent taken a related course before, so it is a little hard for me. But the professor is patient indeed.
Prof Chen is really nice however I had taken this kind of class in bachelor univerisity I think it is unnecessary to have it again for those who have this kind of background
The most caring teacher I ever met!
Dr. Chen is kind to us. He introduces a lot of interesting things related to the course to us. He also thinks a lot about the students.

My fellow Duke ECE Masters students, be wary of this professor and this course. For the last two years, this course has been a disaster. It is taught so poorly, while the textbook being used shows a great direction, it confuses me. The professor did not care a bit, constantly compared us with the morning class. Double question ECE550, not recommend
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Highly dissatisfied, the content was delivered really poorly overall. This course have been taught for a long time, so I can't understand how the content is butchered so much. Presentations are 150-200 slides long, without any care for whether it is interesting or linear in teaching. If you take the course, INVEST time in reading the book.
It is such an interesting class! Recommend everyone interested in games to take it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Awesome professor ; a lot of readings but very interesting. I recommend taking class with him!!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: A TRUE GEM! The only Professor amidst these online classes that helped me remain calm and motivated. He has been very kind with explanations, feedback, and assignment deadlines. He also is a very knowledgeable person. Highly recommended.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: His lectures are engaging. His feedback and office hours are helpful. Take this class if you wish to understand culture more deeply (what it means, how it relates to ideology, feminism, colonialism and multiculturalism).
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: I like this professor very much, he is very kind and friendly. His speeches are always very interesting and his assignments are challenging but not hard. His feedback is great, and our grade he gave is also very good.

LIT102 This is an intro class of literary theory. His selection of theory reading is well-rounded, abstract, and profound with several crucial movements in literary history. His explaining skill is exceptional; he excellently comprehends the abstract concepts and theories. His assignments are interesting. He also organized the best field task ever!

LIT107: The book excerpts Prof. Lewis assigned for reading are good examples of integrating data into narrative. His analysis and lead of discussion are really compelling, powerful, and helpful in developing the data-employed technique and writing style.

Professor Lewis is an amazing lecturer! Although his classes are lecture heavy, they are so interesting I didnt mind at all. He is accessible, and I always enjoyed talking with him. He does occasionally do card tricks! He is excited to engage with student presentations and ideas, and says he learns new things along with students every class.

LIT107 is a great class to take if you want to improve your writing and understand the interplay between data and narrative. His lectures are thought-provoking and encourage discussion. (Fun fact: He occasionally uses card tricks to make a point.) Prof. Lewis is very approachable. Many students benefit from attending his office hours.

I loved this class and Professor Yin is great! I had very little background in neuroscience but as long as you take really good notes you'll be fine. Lectures were really interesting and he connected a lot of concepts to the real world. Made an extra credit assignment to help boost grades. Great great professor, don't believe the bad reviews!!!

Class was pretty interesting, had a lot of discussion, though be sure to participate and ask questions. He handled questions well, never made you feel dumb for asking something so feel free to. He had reasonable grading and there was a bit of work, but for a class with a writing credit, it really wasn't bad at all. Definitely recommend!
This class was very interesting! Not too much work and participation is a big part of the grade. At times a bit boring but overall a solid class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I was a little scared to take this class from what I had heard about Yin but he adapted well to online learning. There are about 60 pages of intense scientific papers every week for reading and 2 group presentations. There were a lot of details but as long as you can understand the big picture you'll do well
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I almost didn't take the class because of the poor ratings. He is not nearly as bad as they say. He's understanding and willing to help. I would definitely take the class again.

Maybe 7 years ago Dr. Yin was different from how he is now. Honestly the class was good/what it should be. I almost didn't take the class from seeing negative comments here, but the course load was manageable and the lectures were alright. Sometimes he'd ask some philosophical questions, which I enjoyed. Grading was fine. I'd take the class again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: I had heard negative feedback, but he seems to have put a lot more work into the course this semester and cared about how we did. Tests were very fair and indicative of whether or not you went to class. Very nice guy as well. Definitely not a bad professor although it is hard to make any material interesting at 6:15pm

Probably one of the worst professors at Duke. Never seemed happy about teaching the class.  His lectures made little sense and his exams often contained material never mentioned in lecture. Plus, his answers to our questions never made any sense and he is utterly unhelpful outside of class. Avoid taking any of his classes if you can.
Didn't care much about the class. Also, he basically didn't grade our third exam- just gave us whatever would increase our grade by 1/3 of a letter grade. First exam was unreasonably hard.

Did not care how the class turned out, and his TA wrote the majority of the 2 tests. He did not seem to be clear about what was being tested even during the exams. The first test was unreasonably hard. Also, the class is not curved significantly. Grades including the grade for the final paper were never posted on Blackboard. Very monotone lecturer.

He doesn't ever seem to be happy to be teaching. His mundane voice and unclear explanations often make the class difficult to understand. During the first exam, he laughed at us for taking so long to complete the test.

Extremely apathetic at teaching. Sometimes questioned if he even wanted to be there in the first place. Extremely bad to understand his neuro explanations, which is unfortunate because his powerpoint slides are riddled with grammatical errors. Tests were hit or miss. Either do well or poorly, but you always think you did well leaving the exam.
Prof. Solomon provided us with a lot of practical hands-on knowledge, as well as a good theoretical background. Very caring and very fun, 10/10 would take a class with him again.
The greatest Prof I've had at Duke. Challenging, but not overly hard, explains things well, the absolute Goat.
Great lecturer

Lectures were thorough and he made sure to explain textbook examples clearly. Made sure that all student questions were answered to satisfaction. Very responsive to emails and available out of class for extra help. Homework was heavy but not too difficult and overwhelming. Exams were more conceptual and harder than the homework though. Recommend.

Elchanan was one of my favourite professors at Duke. His lectures were really good: He knows how to explain complex concepts in a simple way and he is quite funny. He genuinely cares about students at a personal level. The homework were balanced, each had some easier proofs and one more challenging question. An excellent class overall.

Elchanan is an awesome professor for the MATH 466 Math of ML class. His lectures are pretty clear, giving lots of intuition and background info so that everyone follows his lectures. He's also pretty flexible with homework, and this class is MUCH less work (and easier) than any other math class I've taken at Duke, while actually learning stuff!
I loved this course. Professor Solomon explains well and is very approachable. Tests are a bit tricky.

Dr. Gong is an average professor whose low rating comes from teaching a difficult course. His lectures are less focused than they could be, but do cover all the material, and he is helpful in office hours but will not walk through problems. He does devote time to talking about research and new advances in the field which I appreciated.

Workload/test is unnecessarily demanding, and lecture was a waste of time. Instructor definitely needs to spend time on thinking about how to teach properly because he seems to have no idea. Worst course I have taken.

Lotta people were upset with Gong but he's really not bad. If you go to office hours you can get 100s on all the homeworks. Tests do not require too much studying, they just require actual thought. Waaaaaayyyyyy easier than 244.

Yiyang Gong is young, lauded researcher at Duke University. He likes to make kids think a lot harder than they want to. His lectures are full of fluff that he does not test on his exams, so studying is futile. The material he uses to write exams is not available, because he is testing your intellect than what you have stupidly attempted to learn.

RUN AWAY! Choose a different BME core by all means. Save yourself from death. Imagine Wallace-level exams without the Wallace-level teaching. Did not learn much but spent a lot of time doing all the work. Not useful and super hard.
This entire culture of learning this is not needed skip this curriculum
Not a very interesting lecturer, but helpful if you go to her office hours to talk.  She's a pretty fair grader, but she's not a very engaging professor.
Interesting seminar, professor is a little boring but she knows the material well. Not much work but you have to go to class once a week

Don't take her class unless you know a lot about the subject already.  If you don't, you'll hate it.  If you do, you'll probably do alright, even if the classes are pretty boring.  She is an interesting person if not necessarily an interesting professor.
worst professor EVER. boring, difficult, uninspired, and enough readings to kill a rainforest.
No Comments
Very easy class, meets once a week, but quite boring. One midterm and a take home final.
No Comments
Prof Yoder cares so much about this course!! Take a class with her before you graduate

Professor Yoder is incredibly knowledgeable and accessible out side of class. This course was co-taught by Professor Willis and Professor Yoder, but Professor Yoder definitely had fewer lectures. Regardless, her lectures are interesting and relevant. Problem sets/tests are very fair.

Dr. Yoder did not seem passionate about teaching evolutionary biology. Although a better teacher than Dr. Bejsovec, she still failed to actively engage her students. This class was very dry largely due to the way it was taught.

BIO202***
Yoder was not much better than Dr. B, as it always seemed that she was tired and had other priorities. She wasn't an engaging lecturer, and didn't have a lot of care for the class. I think evolution was easier than genetics, but that had nothing to do with her instruction.

Yoder is really cool. Very no-frills, but a good teacher. The class isn't too hard and the discussions were really interesting, but she won't take any BS. At times it seemed like she was too busy to focus on our class, but that also meant lots of canceled/shortened classes.
some of the readings are difficult, but you're not really expected to understand them completely (just get the gist). class participation is a must. and yes, anne is a fox
just wanted to say anne yoder is the essence of foxy.

His jokes? He's the only one laughing. His lectures? Hard to follow, mostly off-topic, and rarely connected to the actual exams. The homework feels random, the test feels unrelated, and you're mostly left wondering if you missed a secret syllabus. Communication isn't his strong suit either. Be prepared to figure things out on your own — a lot.
His tests are ambiguous. Do not really learn much during the school year. Attempts to build foundation in Economics but learn few intuitions throughout. Do not recommend.
Really nice, deserve higher score for sure.
Great instructor! His notes and lectures are well-organized, providing a solid foundation for learning microeconomics.
Nice person, but excruciatingly difficult midterm with an average slightly above 50.

Definitely does not deserve a low rating, maybe he dramatically changed his teaching style over the past few years. You can do fine if you skip class, because he walks through his pdf notes from Sakai. However, his lectures are fantastic and he connects the content to the real world, which is what you'd ideally learn in an Econ class. 2 tests + HW.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed professor Yildirim this semester. He was a really interesting lecturer and helped break down complex topics beforehand. His review sessions before the exams were incredibly useful and I found him to be very thorough in the lectures and homework. Homeworks were difficult but doable and were great prep for the exams.

Yildirim is a great professor with a knack for bringing economic theory to life. His classes are very lecture heavy, but they feel more like a two-way conversation than just a lecture. He is accessible through Office Hours and though the grades are determined by a few problem sets and the two exams, I felt like all the material was in the notes.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: His teaching seems disorganized and confusing, but what he wrote on the board constitutes all the materials he will test in exams, so take good notes and rely on them. Also need to master every proof technique from the problems done in and after class. He will bump up a grade if someone exhibits improvement over time. Overall not bad but struggling
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof Yildirim is great. He knows the material well and his teaching style is easy to follow. If you are interested in the subject and focus in class you will do well. The grade is heavily based on two tests but they are not that hard if you know the material. He focuses on understanding the underlying mechanics of the topic so make sure to know it.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Nice professor. Short problem sets. Difficult exams.

Horrible lecturer with a terrible accent with an even more awful attitude. If you want to pass, look at previous year's exams and work with other students outside of class. He copied sections out of the book without any explanations, and his TAs couldn't really speak English. Worst professor ever. I had better junior high teachers.

He's the bomb. I can't imagine that you could do well if you don't go to class, but his lectures are always interesting and make you want to go. Problem sets are extremely fair and tests only cover what he lectures on. Wish every Duke Econ class was like this.
Super difficult. Instructor not helpful, condescending, unclear, boring lectures. Tests often include problems that are vastly different from the assignments.

Econ 188 was a more quantitative and difficult elective than I expected. However, Huseyin was a great professor and extremely helpful. If you studied practice tests and problem sets the exams were very similar. Partial credit was generous and most kids got an A-/A. He is also a great guy and relatively funny. Don't take 188 if he's not the teacher.

I Love yildrim! I got a C+ in Leachman and an A in Yildrim's class. He's fair; study the discussion problems, old practice tests, etc. So if you work hard you should be able to do well! Also the TAs are really helpful. Best Econ prof I've had at Duke!
Really good professor.  Just make sure you go to class.  He's extremely fair.
He is a good professor and the tests really are not that bad.  If you go to your TA's section you should do well in the class

I'm typically a good student - kinda lost interest in class because could not understand his accent (especially in a big lecture setting).  Also talked too fast/ erased from board too quickly for me to even write (never a prob for me).  I give him credit for trying hard, however, and the TA's were helpful.

He has an accent, but it does NOT interfere with the clarity of his lectures in any way. I'm inclined to think only bitter students would say it does. His lectures are really organized, and really good--his examples serve a well-defined purpose, and his tests are awesome, in the sense that you think through and learn from them.
the homeworks and lectures were really simple, but the tests were rather irrelevant.  even the practice exams were easy compared to the tests.  be sure to have a good TA in this class.

At first I couldn't stand him, but his lectures steadily got better over the semester. I liked his tests. They don't test your knowledge of the subject, they test understanding. If you understand and can apply the material to new things this class is very easy. My only problem was his accent. It's so irritating I had trouble listening to him.

Tests are off the wall.  He is actually a pretty good lecturer, but his tests are so hard.  You can study for hours and go in and see something on the test that you have never heard of/seen before.  YIKES!

He does take a while to explain things but he is the most helpful professor I ever had. He is very willing to talk to you and really cares about you succeeding in the class. The class is tough but there is about a 20% curve.

Learn how to speak english before giving your students tests that ask never before seen questions.  This guy makes the tests hard with ridic questions and can't explain for****.  I'd also be more entertined picking my nose than listening to this guy.  I also think he explains things really slow just to waste..by the end i'm usually asleep

She is very approachable and lenient. A few deadlines were extended for the entire class. The lectures are BORING and very short. She doesn't introduce you to terminologies. The project is interesting but challenging (4000-word paper). Online classes are way worse than in-person classes. Talk to the TAs about your project and you'd do well!
Her lectures are quite boring and she does not include any student participation during lectures which makes it very boring. She seems nice enough

Very unorganized course, TA showed up without the test and then realize prof wasnt coming after waiting for 10min. No clear grading criteria for the paper and tests, keeps referring us to the TA for questions outside of class. She is very knowledgeable in this field, enjiyed the class but too many logistic issues
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Lee is a great professor! She knows her material very well and teaches the course with great enthusiasm. Will definitely take her again. She is also a fair grader and will reward students who try. Only 2 reading quizzes, film critique, and a project.

Professor Lee is the director of the sociology department. She is a really nice professor and knows her material well. There were no tests in this class but there were 2 reading quizzes to make sure students read. There was also 1 film critique and a presentation with an essay. Participation and attendance matters.
No Comments

Yoonkyung is a great instructor.  She knows a great deal about East Asian politics, highly encourages class discussion, and is open to class feedback.  Readings and assignments are tough at times, but you will come out of the course learning a great deal about East Asia and comparative politics.

Took Econ201 over the summer and YG made it very accessible. He did an excellent job with lectures and was receptive to feedback. English is not his first language, but you can tell he really tries and largely overcomes this. A fair grader and good exam designer. I hope he teaches more classes in the econ department in the future.

I took Econ201 with YG over the summer and he was absolutely great. His lectures are clear and he provides examples to help students out. He's also super available and willing to help outside of class whether by email or during office hours. He really wants his students to succeed. Basically he's a g and I totally recommend taking a class with him.

He always is willing to answer questions after class and make time to help explain topics personally. English isn't his first language, so I feel that the lectures took much longer than they needed for the amount of content, but ultimately I was able to learn from YG. It was very clear what you needed to do to succeed in the class.

I really enjoyed taking ECON201 under YG, who was a pretty funny guy and only assigns work that will be covered on exams. The uncurved exams were graded very harshly but I feel that YG tried to be very equitable on the curves after. I don't think I would have made an A in this class under any other professor, strongly recommend him for 201!!
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Hilarious

reviews.comment: I struggled with the material during the first half of the course, but Professor Young is accessible for weekly HW help and makes himself more accessible before exams. His lectures are clear and he replaces lowest midterm scores with the final. Definitely take MATH230/STA230 with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Super helpful always willing to go over stuff outside class. Explains concepts very well and provides lots of practice material, def take stat230 with him!

Alex is an incredible teacher all-around. He is an interesting, understandable lecturer, and he makes sure to provide lots of help and office hours outside of class. Would highly recommend taking his class!
Great teacher. Explains concepts well and cares about the students.

He explains concepts well and does not assign an excessive amount of homework. The tests are more difficult than the homework, but he gives practice exams. I would recommend taking math/stats 230 (probability) with him.

Go to his lectures/office hours. Do the homework. Make sure you understand the equations and practice. Tests are hard, but the underlying principles behind them are the same as hw. You will learn a lot.  For me it was very interesting. His jokes are pretty funny.  Class curved to a... A- B+?

Very knowledgeablebut not necessarily passionate about this class. If you are a quick learner and "memorize" the hw and practice problems then you will have no troubles getting A in this class. Otherwise,  lack of practice and fundamental understanding can be a real issue. Deriving everything from scratch is not practical during the tests.

I don't know why people complained about him. His lectures clearly derived all the equations that you need to know for the tests and he explains them very clearly. If you had any more problem, he was happy to help during office hour. It feels as if the people who complained are those who never went to class and office hours.
He doesn't help on any questions.

People like to complain about this guy, but I think they're mostly making excuses for themselves. The class is hard. He has an accent, but it's really not that bad (I'm not Asian). His lectures are pretty helpful and he posts slides on blackboard. His tests are hard but not unfair.

This professor is one of the best professors I have ever had. His lectures were very clear and although his test were difficult, you can get an A if you make the effort. This class made me choose BME major. TAKE THIS CLASS
The professor ridiculed students who asked questions and was very reluctant to give outside help during office hours.  Very condescending.  Feedback on tests and homework was little to none.
He is TERRIBLE

worst professor ever, i cant even describe him. can't speak english, makes mistakes constantly, tries to ridicule you if you ask questions, unavailable outside of class, doesn't post solutions and gives tests back ridicously late, awful professor, avoid at all costs, i've never hated a teacher so much, seriously.

very hard class.  exams are returned late with no helpful feedback and no solutions.  no useful feedbacks on labs.  think the class gets curved to a B- or C+.  advice for this class is get the old exams/hw/labs/projects from previous years since he reuses previous material

Dr. You was okay, although his tests were extremely hard and his lectures were difficult to understand at times.  Often he would just "encourage us to look at it on (our) own time" instead of clarifying points students had questions on.  He's not the worst prof I've had, but he's far from the best.

It is easy to see why this class will be loathed by people with very little background in general chemistry; that's why I credit Dr. You for making this class much easier to bear by providing very good and clear lectures. Would recommend him if he teaches this class again in the future.

lowkey after taking two classes with this man I think he might actually be the best professor in DKU overall

---

gives amazing feedback, classes are engaging and interactive and he's such an interesting person it's hard not to be invested in his class. he's very flexible and reasonable with grading and is super motivating with new students. GOAT

I took Professor Yurgel's class was my absolute favorite. He gives such amazing feedback, and as someone who has never learned philosophy before, he did a wonderful job explaining it to me. He is very understanding, likeable, and he allows much freedom of creativity. I would take this class each session if I could.
I really really like his class and the homework!! Missing his feedback

Caio is a charming, encouraging professor. His class was so much fun and the assignments didn't feel like schoolwork at all. He knows his field very well and always has a way to make the boring theories interesting. He gave detailed feedback but some of them could be confusing since they are not very direct.

Professor Yurgel's class was definitely one of my favorites. He gives engaging lectures and always has a joke up his sleeve. I thought his assignments were fun and creative and he gave detailed feedback really pushing me to pay attention to the details of my writing. I would definitely recommend taking one of his classes.
Great professor who is super kind and willing to help. Course has quite a bit of homework, but not a very difficult class, as tests are easy. Really fun and interactive class and 100% worth taking.
Professor Chen (the GOAT) is just a chill guy. He's also really good at guessing your personality and blood type.
Prof. Chen is the best Japanese professor. His class is presentation-heavy but he is a caring professor and will not give a heavy workload.

Dr. Chen is hands down the best professor I've had at Duke. He's incredibly caring and teaches in a way that caters to second language learners. He's always eager to answer any questions and encourages you when you are having a hard time. You can tell he really wants his students to succeed and strives to create a welcoming environment for everyone

Chen Sensei is an amazing, chill teacher who really helps students excel in Japanese. He's all-around a cool, friendly guy who has mastered the language as a learner himself, so he knows what it's like in your shoes. His classes are fun, and you'll learn a lot. However, there will be lots of homework (presentations/worksheets every week) as usual!

she can make her lecture more interesting, maybe if not good for me, good for other students, because i don't want to participate in a class very high , i don't know how to say, very very active, very very action, just want to do homework, and listen to her lecture. if she made her class interesting, maybe not good for me.

reviews.comment: very demanding
