reviews.comment:
Really easy but uninteresting class.....she reads a lot and sometimes it seems she doesn't understand what she is explaining. 

Takes a lot to reply emails
Fantastic lectures and great feedbacks for assignments

Genuinely the most chill professor i've ever had, so merciful with deadlines and partial credit. king. I didn't enjoy the flipped classroom style but he made his own psets so u can't be mad. truly you can't accuse him of anything except being a nic fiend.

Zack is unfathomably chill and approachable. Good lecturer with good insights, albeit slightly monotone. Definitely a tough course with tough exams, given T/F probs involving precise defns and edge cases are 20% of each test. No lecture notes, but provides very useful practice exams. HW is less useful but graded leniently. Solid curve as well.

Super chill guy. Lectures are worthwhile to go to. Posts practice exams for all midterms + final that are very representative of the content. Tough class but grade curves were pretty generous. 30% homework 20% for each midterm and 30% final.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: math 340. absolutely goat. tough class but hes chill and approachable highly recommend, i learned a lot. very lenient on hw

Math 541 stochastic process. One of the coolest math professors you'll find at Duke. Super approachable. Easy course overall, but you will learn and more importantly, apply a lot in your fields if you pay attention and do the codings.

Zack is really nice and approachable, and he explains concepts pretty clearly. He answers Ed questions himself and responds pretty quickly. Duke changed the structure of 230 this year, so if people who took it before fall23 said it was super chill, it's not as easy at it was before, but it's still ok (a lot better than 221/222)

What people are saying here is 100% valid, the grading sucks. That being said, once you figure out the way to succeed, the class is pretty easy. This class is not your average essay class, you need to actually reflect in writing (creating a ton of questions, being vulnerable, etc) You are not there to answer questions, if you try, you won't do well

Unclear grading and we needed to trauma dump to get a good grade. Students participated several times a day and didn't get full points. She encouraged us to use symbolic writing, but marked off points for using symbolism and not getting to the point. Tried to appease her standards, but she changed her expectations for every paper.

I am very frustrated because this was my favorite class at Duke but think the grading is absurd. Professor Zagbayou has an unrealistic standard of her students and even though I wholeheartedly believe I put my absolute best forward, I received an A-. It is sad because I cannot recommend her to others because of the GPA, yet it is such a good class.

Not a bad person, but not a good professor. Holds her students to a higher standard than she holds herself. Grades harshly based on unclear standards but always makes excuses for herself when she's late to class, misses deadlines, etc. She has a good heart, but as a leadership professor, she sets a poor example.

Professor Zagbayou is incredibly articulate and knowledgeable of the topics she teaches. With that being said, this class was incredibly difficult to navigate, as the expectations were incredibly vague and left room for harsh grading. The class content was incredible, but I found the feedback I received and strict deadlines incredibly frustrating.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Prof Zagbayou is a great lecturer and a great person, while I thoroughly enjoyed the class because of my classmates, her grading criteria make no sense. She grades very harshly and will have grading criteria not listed on the rubrics she provides. Everything is reflective, so how are you going to grade us on our feelings?
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: She is a new professor so be prepared for a lack of organization throughout the class at times. While her career is impressive, she doesn't have any teaching experience which is difficult to work with. She also requires attendance and will lower your grade signifigantly if you miss more than a certain amount of classes, even if they are excused.

Prof Zagbayou is a great professor and Women as Leaders with her was really interesting. The readings were pretty doable because of how interesting and accessible they were, and the class had a lot of guest lectures and discussions. Even though her grading is sometimes unclear, she is pretty easy to reach out of class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I would take this class over and over again. Decent amount of readings, but they are chosen carefully. Professor Zagbayou cares about her students, taking their feedback, and picking the best guest lectures. Everything applies to the real world. Grading is tough, ignore previous 5 but difficulty 3-4 to get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: This class is entirely discussion based, which I enjoyed. We also had TONS of engaging guest speakers and readings were pretty interesting. The only reason I give Prof Zagbayou a lower rating is because she is awful when it comes to grading ANYTHING in a timely manner, which is super frustrating/anxiety inducing.

So amazing! I would take this class over and over again if I could. Decent amount of readings, but they are chosen carefully and you will learn a lot. Professor Zagbayou really cares about her students, taking their feedback into account, giving second tries on assignments and picking the best guest lectures. Everything applies to the real world.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Easy class. All homeworks taken right out of the textbook, boring lectures. Usual stuff

The course could have been a lot better. Professor Zavlanos is pretty good: he's smart and speaks clearly, but he hand-waves through a lot of material and leaves a lot of details out that would help greatly with understanding. That becomes evident when working through the completion-graded homework. Labs are tedious with occasional gems.

Very straightforward engineering professor. If you attend the lectures, it is hard to not get at least an 80% on the midterms. Homeworks take a while even though there's not many problems: this is a result of the nature of the course material, not the professor himself. The labs are not hard either. 4.5 hrs (classes +labs)& ave. 5-7 hrs on hw+labs

Mr. Han is the man, maybe the greatest man at Duke to be honest. The guy is absolutely hysterical and at the same time this little genius who can talk about anything... Definitely my favorite class and my favorite teacher. Moo is a stud everyone loves him.
Moo is the man, take physics 49S, you'll have fun and get an A.

Easy class. He gave our entire class an A in the end so none of the work even mattered. You are only expected to write a few short papers and one project. During class you just talk about random cool stuff since he knows everything. The man is a genius and hilarious and highly recommended to anyone who wants an easy A science requirement.
Probably the best class I've taken at Duke so far... interesting, easy and enjoyable lectures.  Plenty of fun tangents.  Ask him about geography!

Moo is the man. This class is by far the best seminar for kids that need some help boosting thier freshmen gpa. The guy is a genius, but he is also a real person that does not expect too much from his students. The kids look forward to going to his class, which is pretty much mandatory. If you want to skip, this might not be the class for you.
Greatest class ever, greatest teacher ever.  Take this class!!
you have to take it, you just sit there and eat and listen to people talk about physics and drinking

The class is a ton of fun.  Everyone goes in talking about plans for the weekend, and the seminar only requires one large project the entire semester.  Small assignments are even given 2 weeks time to do on average.

What can I say about the Great Han? Well, we have a facebook fan club because he is just THAT awesome. The class is awesome, little to no work, easy grades. It was the one class I looked forward to. He is HILARIOUS but if you look up his credentials, you realize he is damn smart. Take this class.
This guy is great! He's funny and gets you interested in what he's teaching. The class is easy and fun. If you have the pre-reqs, take it.
Very easy class and lots of fun. Most amusing professorI've had at Duke
The Great Han teaches one helluva class. He's a riot, tells great stories, and teaches the basics of subatomic physics very well. Easy class, highly enjoyable, best professor at Duke! Yeah riiight.

This was the most enjoyable class that I took this semester. I actually enjoyed going to class. Professor Han is a great man with topnotch expertise in his area. I definately recommend this course to anyone.

Wacky.  A bit hard to understand because of his fairly heavy accent, but made the class very interesting.  Had him for Modern Physics in my senior year, so I wasn't that motivated.  But overall I would recommend the professor.  He studied under Heisenberg, if I recall correctly.  Very cool stories!

Great class.  If you are truly interested in subatomic physics you will learn a lot from one of the pioneers of the subject (as long as you ask questions).  Also great if you just want an easy grade for your seminar class.  Either way, Prof Han is a great guy and you'll enjoy going to class.
Han is the MANNNNNNNN... BEST CLASS EVER NO WORK AT ALL SERIOUSLY
quite possible the greatest class in the history of the world!

Ridiculously easy class that fulfills a science requirement. Moo-Young was absolutely hilarious. Definitely take it if you're looking for an enjoyable, easy class. Maybe not the best class to take if you are trying to learn a lot about physics though...
Sweet class.  Easy A.  Yeeahhh Riiiiiight.
He has been my coolest prof yet! Neato!

This class is rediculously easy.  It consists of one presentation and everyone gets A's.  You do absolutely nothing.  The subject is presented very well and is very interesting, but you don't have to pay attention.  Great class.
This is an easy A  and if you are not a science person it is a very easy way to fulfill your matrix.  You do absolutely no work whatsoever.
This class was the biggest waste of my Duke tuition. I actually wanted to learn about the subject, but he was more interested in talking about where everyone was from.

Not only is the seminar class, "From Quanta to Quarks," really easy, with only one presentation assignment the whole semester, the topics about theoretical physics discussed in class is genuinely interesting. Prof. Han is a leader in the field.

It was difficult getting ahold of him through email for HW questions, which did not align with lecture material and came from textbook.  The class should be renamed theoretical polymer science as applications are scant.  Unless you're really interested in theory, you'd be best served taking another class. Exams were OK in difficulty.

He teaches directly from the textbook, and not in a way that I could learn.  I never left lecture feeling like I'd learned much.  You're better off just reading the book.  I liked when he sent his grad students in to teach because they were better at explaining things.  Tests are hard and few.  Textbook is archaic and poor quality.
Great entertaining professor :) Have the best demos ever!!!

He writes some of the Greek letters a little differently, but aside from that, the handed out notes were very helpful. Excellent professor, showed many real world applications, and brought interesting demonstrations to class to show physically what's being taught. Very nice guy too. Would definitely take another class taught by him.

The notes handed out probably made things harder as opposed to easier, due to his handwriting and partially whited out sections. Sometimes things would be briefly mentioned, and they would end up being large on the test and in other cases a day or two would be spent on a subject, and it would never be seen on an exam.

Frustrating and unclear(and I did well). He gives out illegible handwritten notes which he skips around in during class. There is no logic to the teaching of this class-more like hunt through the textbook and hope for formulas. The lab reports take at least 10hrs a piece with unclear instructions and unfair grading. Nice guy, not good prof though

Professor Zauscher is one of fews professors at Duke that is both knowledgeable about the subject material and good at teaching.  I have great time listening to his lectures.  The professor tries hard to incorporate materials not in the book to provide different perspectives about material science.  I will definitely take his class in the future.
Excellent professor, able to sustain the interest of the class. Very knowledgeable, good-natured guy.

Really good lecturer most of the time. Keeps things interesting and brings in demonstrations occasionally. Always attaches material to real life applications/issues as well. The one test and homeworks were all fair. Good overall.
Nice guy.  Always prepared for lectures, which he makes pretty interesting. Fair homework assignments and exams. All around pretty good.
One of the best teachers at Pratt. Helpful, clear, and interesting. Unlike many other professors at Pratt, he is humble and friendly.

Extremely rude and unlikable personality
Annoying and disrespectful to students
Poor communication skills, making lectures ineffective
Incompetent in teaching, fails to convey concepts clearly
Overall, a highly unpleasant and unprofessional educator
Much better teacher of fluids than of static. He knows his stuff

Dr. Kabala is such a friendly and fun guy. He is awesome in fluid mechanics. Don't be fooled: fluid mechanics is really bland and boring material. It's a lot of work, but Dr. Kabala makes lectures really entertaining. He has a flare for theatrics which is really uplifting in class. I highly recommend this teacher for fluid mechanics.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Lectures are long and rambling. The class has to be attended due to pop quizzes but don't expect to learn anything of value in it. If you can get a different professor for this class do it. The guy is super nice and smart, he just can't teach for his life.
The teacher was hard to understand during lessons. He also graded pretty arbitrarily. He cared more about neatness and final answer than the content and method.

!. No instruction given 2. Impossibly hard/long HW problems that even TA's dont know how to do (15 hours of HW per week) 3. Even if all done, still fair 4. Would rather do anything besides taking his class. 5. Seriously, do not take his courses

Hands down the worst professor I have ever encountered, extremely cluttered lectures of random unconnected problems that he never even fully solves,literally does not teach anything also somewhat hard to understand

His class is pretty straightforward, the material is interesting, and discussions are usually pretty lively. He has three major assignments that build up: a presentation which *theoretically* is related to your individual paper which is *theoretically* related to your term paper. Chill, reduced workload bc of the lockdown, and is very responsive
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Prof Zeng is a great guy + professor. He made this online class come to life, and was exceptionally accomodating towards students in particular difficult circumstances.

I took two courses with Professor Zeng including GCHINA 302 and was able to see how much effort he put into designing and carrying out the course. Even during the middle of the course, he incorporated students' feedback into the course and it was great to see his thoughtful actions. Take his course before it's too late

Prof. Zeng is a great professor who deeply cares about his students' learning. He gives very helpful feedback and is also seeks student feedback on the course which is great. I really enjoyed class with him and look forward to taking another course with him in the future.

I took GCHINA 301 & 302 with Professor Zhaojin Zeng. He has VASTLY improved his class based on Fall 2020 feedback & even scheduled a meeting to understand any concern students have w/ the current class. He is extremely knowledgeable in his research topic, helps students do research, very open to feedback, & is accessible outside the classroom.
He is a knowledge and nice professor. It might be the online class that made his lectures kind of boring.

He is extremely knowledgeable in his area and takes students' opinions into consideration. Though his lectures might be boring sometimes, they are not so bad in the end. He is chill and as long as you do the work, you will most probably get an A.

Zhaojin is a pretty good professor who knows his material, but his lectures are unfortunately put-you-to-sleep dull. To make up for that, he does incorporate group work into the class with breaks things up and promotes discussion out of class (in addition to the usual in-class discussions). Also had to buy additional software to use in class :(

Easy A as long as you do the work. There are forum questions on each reading. Lectures are quite boring. My biggest complaint would be that the professor made us buy Top Hat (an online platform similar to Sakai) simply because he wanted to try it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: As a psych major I wish more people were like him in the department. Genuinely loves psych and teaching. my favorite prof thus far
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Respected

reviews.comment: if you go to lecture and take detailed notes its not that necessary to read the textbook. i would say that rosenthal is an ok lecturer but gets the job done. the guidelines for the research reports and final paper are kinda unclear so just email your ta to clarify anything. abnormal is not that bad as long as you are good at memorizing facts.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Rosenthal is a great professor and really makes class material come alive when he uses memorable anecdotes from real life. Tests are super easy if you read the DSM 5 for fun; otherwise, you might have to study. The course paper is very long, so definitely get started early. This class is still a relatively easy A.

Really awesome professor. Cool guy and he makes the lectures interesting. He tells stories about the fascinating things he's seen in his own clinical experience. Tests really not too hard if you take notes in class, and you don't need the textbook at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Two research reports (5 pages), one course project (10 pages), one midterm, and the final. Don't bother buying the book everything is from lecture. Lectures are mandatory if you want the easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: LOVE Dr. Rosenthal. Keeps class interesting with funny personal stories that will make you remember things. Best Prof I've had for an intro-level lecture course. Take good notes and go to class and an A is doable.

Great lecturer. Rosenthal is a very smart guy who really wants the class to learn and be excited about abnormal psychology. Alongside the wonderful TAs he keeps the course on a clearly outlined path that covers some very interesting topics. Clear grading, not an easy A but if you show up to lecture, take notes/pay attention, you will get an A.

Dr. Rosenthal is a great lecturer. He keeps class interesting. The exams are doable if you read the textbook and take notes in class. He is very knit-picky about language, but he makes sure to clarify his points if people are confused. Dr. Rosenthal also does his best to make sure the whole class is invested and paying attention to his lecture.

Lectures are mandatory unless you have a good friend who is happy with taking great notes and sending them to you. Both TA's my semester were dreadful which definitely doesn't help the cause. Tests are really difficult for an intro psych class, definitely don't expect an easy A. Take 104 with Robinson over this class.

This is a great class! However, getting an A or above isn't as easy as past posters have made it out to be. You need to study A LOT to do well on the exams. Also, you don't even need to read the textbook - everything (or almost everything) on the exams comes from his lectures. Make sure you can wake up for that 8:30. Work hard, and you'll do well.

This class is NOT as easy as people make it out to be.  I took this class expecting an easy A and scraped by with a B+. Work load isn't heavy, but it is an 8:30 AM class and 25% of the final material comes from what was lectured in class.  Averaged a B- on midterm/final, with heavy study. Tests are not curved, essay around 20 pages.

In my opinion, this class is not as easy as some of the post are implying. The class is pretty straightforward, but there is A LOT of information you need to know for the midterm and final (Including specific percentages and ratios). Rosenthal is a great lecturer, he keeps the class interesting.  I wouldn't take it if you're not a psych major.
He is awesome, his lectures are really clear and fun to listen to. definitely my favorite professor at Duke.

Prof. Rosenthal is the best professor I have had at Duke! He gives pop quizzes at the end of some lectures, but they are extremely easy and just there for participation points. The class only has two tests and one final paper. Prof. Rosenthal is really engaging and tells his own personal stories. Take this class!!

Dr. Rosenthal is a really great professor. I enjoyed having him (even at 8:30am). His Abnormal Psychology class is really engaging. I recommend going to all lectures, because there are pop quizzes that are easy points; however, sometimes he rushes at the end of class. Start studying early for exams, because they cover a lot of material.

Loved this course! Dr. Rosenthal is a great professor, he shared so many interesting stories from his own work and made lectures fun to attend. The TAs were also great and extremely helpful! Course is easy and straightforward, would definitely recommend! (:

Dr. Rosenthal is really engaging. He made an 8:30 class interesting, and he offers a lot of interesting stories of real patients he's worked with. His grading is fair and tests aren't too hard. He gives pop quizzes but they're mostly to reward the people who come to lecture.

He is an awesome teacher and so fair in grading it's ridiculous.  Yes, you have to review the lectures slides for a few minutes for a pop quiz, but they're very easy.  The test is extremely fair too.  I started studying the night before and got an A easily.  As an engineer, a professor like Dr. R is a breath of fresh air.  Hilarious & genuine guy!

This class isn't as easy as some posts are implying. His tests aren't easy, and some questions asked for specific percentages of disorders. He talks about a lot in lecture but goes over so much that it's hard to know what's important for the test. I would only suggest this course if you definitely are a psych major.

Great professor - if you need a psychology credit TAKE THIS CLASS. There are tons of extra credit opportunities and he makes class so fun and enjoyable. The one downside: his exams are very nit-picky (some questions were specific percentages for certain mental illnesses).

Professor Rosenthal's lectures are pretty entertaining, and the content is straight from his lectures (don't even bother buying the textbook). The only problem is that he is very vague about what he expects from the essays, but there is a lot of extra credit available. The class overall is very easy, but the final project is a pain.

Lectures are pretty interesting and Rosenthal has really neat stories about patients he's worked with. Sometimes, he spends way to much time on certain subjects so we got pretty behind. Tests were reasonable and papers were graded very easily.

(Don't know the new numbering, but it was Abnormal Psychology). ROSENTHAL IS AMAZING. Best professor I've had at Duke. His class is an 8:30 in the fall because it will get PACKED no matter the time because it's a truly interesting class and Rosenthal is a great lecturer. Not difficult either, he's a fair grader and gives extra credit.
Rosenthal is a great prof--really entertaining and easy going.  Plus, he makes the material completely understandable and interesting (despite the 8:30am class time).
best psy class hands down. don't skip class because there are "pop quizzes" and you'd seriously be missing out

Made an 8:30 as engaging as it could be. Enthusiastic and funny. You have to read the book and go to class, though, because there are pop quizzes. Tests are a bit annoying but not horrible. Lots of opportunities to make up grades with assignments

amazing class and professor. He really knows his stuff and has many stories to draw from since he is a clinical psychologist. Material is very intersting and useful and you don't really need to read the book but it is a good way to reinforce what you learn in lecture. Take this class!

really funny and interesting professor, but he wouldn't finish lecturing from the slides because he would go off on tangents. he also uses slides that are slightly incoherent and don't make sense unless you read the book. also, the pop quizzes are horrible unles you're actually prepared.

Fantastic class. Dr. Rosenthal is a successful clinician and professor with experience and pizzazz. I had him at 8:30 - my only 8:30 class at Duke and it was totally worth it. The class is not difficult and Prof. Rosenthal makes everything fascinating. Definitely one of my favorite professors at Duke!

sooo awesome!! probably the best professor i have had at duke.. he is really brilliant and passionate about what he teaches.  plus he is also a clinical psychologist so he doesn't just teach from the book. highly recommend his abnormal psy class
A really great professor! Really has a passion for the course and is very helpful and accessible outside of class! Definitely take this class!

Really a great professor with a passion for abnormal psychology.  Dr Rosenthal is an incredible researcher and clinician; Duke is truly lucky to have him as a professor as well!  For a man who's been featured repeatedly on national tv (The Today Show, among others), Dr Rosenthal is very personable and accessible to his students.  Highly recommended

Of the best professors at Duke! If you need EI and have any interest at all in psy TAKE THIS CLASS! The simple fact that most of the class was awake and entertained at 8:30 should be enough reason to take it. It is one of the easiest classes at duke but requires you to take notes and attend lectures for pop quizzes, which are VERY EASY.
This class was interesting AND easy. Professor Rosenthal made the material enjoyable. Not much work (you technically don't have to read the book), you just go to class and study his lecture slides.

He is awesome! By far my favorite teacher ever! He is fun, entertaining, and knows his stuff. I didnt mind getting up at 8:30 to go to his Abnormal Psych class because I absolutely love his class. If you like psych and can take a class with him...DO IT
He is very nice. I simply couldn't understand anything he said. Subbed for a few math 230 classes, and I had 0 clue what was happening. Notes were helpful for getting caught up.

Dr. Zhu's lecture notes are well-organized and clear. Tests are reasonable. He's always very willing to help and meet outside of class and wants you to succeed. But a lot of lectures start with repeating the same topics as before and towards the end of the semester, the content was very rushed leaving me unprepared for the final.

The class wasn't bad, I feel like I learned a lot about diffeq. However, I think lectures could use more organization and there were details and applications that were missed that I think would've been helpful for understanding. Make sure to read lecture notes and reference the textbook if needed. Dr. Zhu is available outside of class too.
Overall terrible. Very poor teaching and very difficult to understand. Left every lecture feeling confused
Not very engaging lectures, mostly repeats of Clark Bray's. Not as difficult as some of the other MATH219s though.
Rlly knowledgeable and open to questions but kinda lost sometimes and hard to understand

Just a bad professor. Leeches off of lecture notes from semesters past and does not add any value to the course. Lectures are incomprehensible, and you essentially are forced to teach yourself the material by watching videos online.

This professor has many mistakes in exams, is not communicative with students, and does not implement feedback. The exams are long and have typos. Averages are extremely low for this course. Too in depth and expects students to have it all completely understood and memorized. Often in class the professor can't answer student's questions either.

Engaging and enthusiastic lecturer, but an unacceptably poor proctor and testwriter. Exam errors are corrected at varying times across sections, several errors per exam are the norm, and practice tests are insultingly brief and unrepresentative. In the face of frequent, detailed feedback, Dr. Zhuo takes no corrective action, nor any responsibility.

CS 512 with Prof Zhuo is the hardest CS class I've taken at Duke. Prof Zhuo explains concepts well and I enjoy his lectures, but the exams and labs are soooo hard. Luckily he curved our grades very leniently at the end.

DanYang knows the material well but has an accent (not difficult to understand if you pay attention); sometimes doesn't explain things well (though he's always happy to explain more clearly post-class); I personally found HW really fun and rewarding (all OS programming in C), but I am a 250 TA ;) start HW early b/c debugging and OH is unavoidable!!

Danyang's lectures are average. His accent was difficult to understand at times. The class itself is quite annoying - the homeworks take forever and are impossible to debug. Danyang's TA's were paramount in the class succeeding as he was hard to reach outside of class. Danyang did do and act on polls in the middle of the semester which was nice.

Hardest - & most interesting - CS course I've taken at Duke. Dr. Zhuo is a great lecturer and genuinely seems to care about his students. Best TAs I've ever had in a class. Hard exams, but both exam grades & end-of-semester grade are curved. Start the projects early - they are no joke and I basically lived in 310 office hours this semester lmao
Great professor but courses content is very difficult, don't take if you think this will be any easy systems class.
Great lecturer and he keeps me interested. Presentations articulated well and it makes sense.
Great professor - loved how he asked for feedback along the course. Projects are hard but expected difficulty. Plenty of help available if needed. Good prof for CS310

I think this was his first time teaching OS, but he did a very good job. Asked for feedback through the semester and had good lectures/slides to give us an intuitive understanding of the concepts. Very good at answering questions in class, and funny. A few tough assignments, but if you start early you can get the grade you want.

Operating Systems is a tough topic with a lot of material to cover, so lectures can sometimes be a bit fast-paced. Professor Zhuo does a good job of breaking down topics and he encourages questions. He sent out surveys multiple times during the semester and immediately implemented changes to address the feedback, which is rare for professors to do.

Dr. Zhuo is very intelligent and has notable empathy for students. The lectures are dense and quickly paced, but he is willing to answer questions. Programming assignments are difficult and exams were challenging, although he did grade on a curve. He asked for feedback throughout the semester and acted on it, which is rare for most professors.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Phenomenally curated reading list, nice thematic approach. Saskia deftly provides interesting context, history. Major complaint is in excessive abstraction, lack of disagreement/criticism. In-class discussion can wander without meaningful debates. Seminar-style, but sometimes not vibrant/dynamic. Saskia knows her field, will show you great works.

I really enjoyed Eng 237. I had never taken an English class at Duke before, but Dr. Z was great. Her class does have a lot of work, but she pushes you to engage critically with the content. Every student's opinion is valued, and I felt that she was very considerate and caring. Would definitely take again.

Prof. Ziolkowski is an absolute asset to Duke's English department. I've taken two classes with her, and both have been phenomenal. She's kind and accessible and works extremely hard to make sure her classes are as interesting and engaging as possible. There is a fair amount of reading, but the novels/short stories are enjoyable. Take her class!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: I took America from Abroad with Saskia - an excellent class with an excellent professor. Saskia is caring and reasonable in her grading, and she really makes the extra effort to ensure her students are doing well. There are many assignments in the class, so one bad grade won't hurt you that much, and most of the assignments are fairly light.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Saskia is a great professor! I've taken two English courses with her. Workload is very manageable. She uses a lot of different types of assignments/projects as opposed to the usual English department essays which is refreshing. She goes above and beyond for students and is overall an excellent teacher.
Music isn't pain or emotion.
Really kind person, unfortunately extraordinarily boring. Can't play piano at all. We are required to write music for homework, and he tries to play our work, and constantly fails.

He is very easygoing and laid back. As long as you are making an effort, you are likely to do well. His lectures are a bit monotonous and might be hard to follow if you have no background in music theory (though 55 is technically a prereq, some people in my class had not taken it - and it showed). Fun class!
I love him.

He speaks with a very monotanous tone and he's not very good at explaining things. However, he loves when you ask questions and he's very happy to answer them. If you can read music, play an instrument, and/or have basic music theory knowledge you can easily get an A in this class as long as you do the few homework assignments that he gives.
Great
quirky in a very bad, uninformative, and boring way.  I would imagine that he's an awesome and very talented musician, but he shouldn't be teaching classes.  Sometimes, he was mean.
totally awesome class, totally sweet lecturer. he knows his**** very well, and if you do your work you will love this class
he's a really nice professor; this class was a lot of fun- it helped me gain a greater appreciation for music.
this man can barely complete a sentence, let alone teach a two hour class...i can read music better than he can, which is a little scary.
Don't take Jazz w/him, but 56 was great.

Z-man is awesome. I don't know about his jazz class (74), but songwriting was really fun. Listened to the Beatles, wrote our own stuff, performed in class. Very laid back, as much work as you want to put into it... everyone writes/performs one song final.
No Comments
He does not know how to teach.  No need to even attend his class.
No Comments

Went to every single class and still had to teach myself a lot of the material because the way he tried explaining graphs and concepts was confusing most of the time. Tough grading on homework and tests, definitely have to do a lot of textbook reading and practice questions to feel confident on answers. Lecture slides were online so that was nice
Zelder is a good guy. Tries to make the class interesting and grades pretty leniently. Kind of confusing at points if you dont have a solid understanding of the material.

very nice person and will try to help you as best as he can but has very confusing tests. Hes a little all over the place and its hard to follow his train of thought sometimes. Also goes through the material very quickly.

Terrible lecturer with incredibly tough tests. His test questions don't ask the answers he is looking for. Very frustrating grading style. He tries to be funny but he isn't and there's awkward silence constantly through lecture.  0/10 would not recommend.

He is actually a very good professor. I like his lecture because he makes everything clear, gives interesting examples and asks students if we have any questions that he could answer in class, and he is very willing to help students. The tests are really really difficult!!! But he would curve the grades. Getting a A may not so easy.
His classes are fine but tests are hard and long especially for an introductory course.

Zelder really tries to make lectures interesting and he's incredibly helpful and patient in office hours. Sometimes he gets too caught explaining an easy topic, but he makes a lot of resources available online for self-studying too.
he is trying  to make his lecture more funny

Zelder really wants his students to do well but he isn't the best at explaining things: he belabours the simple points and rushes over the difficult ones. Also, his tests are annoyingly tough. Even if you understand the concepts, it doesn't necessarily mean that you'll do well in the tests because the mark schemes are quite specific.

Decent lecturer who posts the Power Points online for every class. Very nice and entertaining. Approachable as well. First test was harder than I expected but you get used to his odd grading scheme and test style. Have to put all the information you know on his tests to get a good grade.

Literally the best professor I've ever had. He's soooo funny, so you stay engaged and listen, unlike most big lecture classes. He's a great explainer. But best of all he really cares. I mean he REAALLLYYY cares. Almost too much haha. You go to office hours and he wants to help you and will feel so bad if he fails. He is the nicest man on earth.

Zelder is a hilarious, smart dude. But his lectures are just not that helpful. The class is very manageable if you do well on the homeworks and study the textbook. But attending the lectures is simply not necessary or helpful. Zelder is helpful one on one, but don't expect to be prepared for the test just from the lectures.
He's a nice guy but not the greatest lecturer.  Pulled lectures right from the textbook so often didn't know what was going on.
like everyone said, he is a good guy but not the best lecturerer. tests can be real tough, and this is definitely a weed out class to some extent. but a really nice guy.

Zelder is the man and I love him. He sometimes tries too hard to be funny and can interrupt the class dynamic. Te problem with 201 is not that its hard but that it is a lot of material. Stay up to date or the final will kill you
Prof. Zelder is really nice but his lectures are rather dry because he tends to belabor simple points.

We did the flip class system, and Zelder taught the class for a while besides Nechyba. Zelder is very knowledgeable as well, and he often breaks down the hard material into very easy and basic concepts. He is awesome, and really cares about the class and students.
Isn't always the best at explaining things, but Professor Zelder is a very smart guy who is very helpful when approached.

Great professor! I wouldn't be discouraged about taking Econ 201 just because Nechyba isn't taking it. Zelder is extremely knowledgeable as well and helps students to succeed. He isn't quite as clear or funny, but he knows his economics.

He is very invested in making sure his students understand the concepts and tries to relate to his students, but the way he teaches is not always very clear and often doesn't manage to explain things well. He is not the best lecturer, but definitely puts in the effort to be available if you asked for help.
Really really cares about students and teaching. Funny, tries to be engaging but the material can be dry. Really gives his all though and is really willing to help as best he can.

Frau Zimbelius is my favorite teacher at UNC so far and I WANTED to be in class every day. She is very available outside of class (email and office hours) and provides extra resources for language practice. The majority of our class wanted to have her again next sem. UNC German is generally a lot of work, but if you apply yourself you'll do well.

Assigns a lot of homework, roughly 2 hours per night, if not more. The homework is not helpful whatsoever. Yes, it's a language class, but there are more ways to learn a language than just beating it into your head with repeated assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Frau Zimbelius is an extremely hard grader, it seems as though she doesn't understand that most people who take german have never spoken it before. She has high grading standards that are not clear, and she grades the oral exams with the expectation that we speak like native speakers. Assigns a lot of homework, most of which is unhelpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Zibu is a great guy who gives incredibly difficult weekly graded Homeworks. If you're willing to spend easily up to 4-5 hours in the help room where even the TAs will take a while to figure out how to help you in your homework, but also want lectures in which you will actually understand math properly, choose Zibu. Duke math is just hard :(

This class is insanely hard, but a lot of it is at the hands of the math dep't that makes the curriculum. Zibu is one of the better instructors for this class. The work is harder than it should be, problem sets take at a minimum of five hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Amazing.
Boring Lecture. He doesn't seem to have prepared his lessons.

His ENVIR 102, was the most disappointing class I've ever taken at DKU. He is PPT reader, and he doesn't even understand the PPT, and the course is organized in a confusing way. He goes wherever he wants. The entire class was unfocused. And he changed the exam to closed book and it was not easy. Don't come here!!! And also the workload is not easy
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Good grader, homework is not that heavy, but lectures are super boring, and the content is too fast.

Professor Li is knowledgeable and understanding. He is willing to take the time and effort to go over anything that students are confused about. He really pays attention to and cares about student feedback and will adjust lectures and assignments accordingly. His lectures prepare students to excel in his homework and tests, no trickery here.

I was in her ASIA 62 class at UNC. Literally the worst class I have ever taken. We never had a syllabus and she would spring last minute projects on us out of no where. She was rude to many students in the class and blew up if you did not share her same opinion. Please please please never take a class with her, you will regret it.

Can be very nice and passionate, but also has a side that can make any person go insane. Unfortunately, you see more of this side as the semester goes on. I definitely don't blame her for her accent or not understanding english at times, but she is straight up rude. Everyday my intelligence undergoes extreme suffering from her insulting words.
She is really nice.  Very emotional.  I spent a lot of time wondering exactly what my assignments were, but if you do the readings, she will like you.
She is very nice teacher.

She definitely means well, but Prof. Zulfikar is really a pretty terrible teacher. I don't think she got through a lecture once all semester, was very emotional about the topic, and relied too heavily on guest lecturers. The class had no cohesion whatsoever. Assignments were simple but never graded and rarely clear. Avoid this class!
by far the worst teacher i have ever had in my academic career. she continually scheduled guest lectures as a way to avoid teaching us because she doesnt know how to teach. unreasonably opinionated.

She means well but can be evil if you dont participate or agree with her views. She keeps personal grudges and will fail you if you do not participate in class. Assignments are simple but she never grades them or gets them back. If she likes you, then you'll get an A and if she doesn't, don't expect above a C-.
No Comments

While she is a very nice lady, she'll teach you extremely little.  Should be an incredibly interesting topic, but you have to agree with her views. Never returns an assignment all year so who knows how your grade is determined.  Again, nice, but no instructing ability or concept of an academic study.  Grade based on the 'validity' of your opinions.

Dr. Zucker is an absolute queen. Her lectures are so engaging, and the only 8:30am class ever worth taking at Duke. Writing assignments are long but fun to do; for example, writing about a habit that you engage in.
She is super knowledgeable, highly recommend scheduling a one on one meeting with her.

I took Professor Zucker for Psych105. The class was an easy A and I liked the final research project. However, I found lectures to be pretty dry and hard to follow and mainly used the textbook to study for tests. Dr. Zucker's lectures on eating disorders were incredible, just not so much for everything else.

Dr. Zucker is super nice and it is clear that she really loves what she does but lectures could be boring at times and she brought in so many guest lecturers which were interesting but it kind of got annoying. It's not hard to get a good grade just make sure you read the textbook and actually study and don't procrastinate on the long paper.

Prof Zucker is awesome. She's just very real, and she's funny. She's down-to-earth and tells it like it is. Her abnormal class changed the way I understood some psychological disorders completely. There are many guest lectures, which isn't terrible, but I wish I could've heard from her more cause she's cool. She brings her little pup Thor to class.

I'd say 66-75% of lectures are guest speakers, who are interesting and experts in their field. Zucker rarely lectures, but when she does it's boring as hell, so I'm not complaining. You can probably get 80-90 range by skimming the lecture slides but to get a solid A you need to go to class & read the book to get the nit-picky questions on the test

Good professor, just wish she would lecture more. Most of the semester is guest lectures that are interesting but can be a lot of material. Also, you have to read the textbook to do well on the tests. 4 tests, lowest dropped, 1 paper, discussion
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: easiest class ive ever taken, sad its over:(
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I love Dr. Zucker! She is super sweet and approachable for office hours and makes the content interesting through her lectures. Procrastinating for the term paper (20 pages or so) is definitely going to hurt you, so I suggest starting early. Tests are manageable, but sometimes she pulls out nitty-gritty questions from the textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Zucker is amazing! Brings her cute puppy to class and has super interesting lectures. The long 20 pg paper wasn't bad because they spread out the due dates and the tests weren't bad if you went to class and read the textbook. The topics are super interesting and Dr. Z makes it a really good class, even if it is at 8:30 am. Not hard to do well!

Prof Zucker is so sweet. She gives you so many chances to get an A: extra credit essays, dropping the lowest exam, takes exam questions directly from the slides, etc. Plus, she knows so many amazing psychologists that come in to help speak that no class is dull. Highly recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Zucker is a great lecturer. She works hard to keep students engaged and has a very extensive syllabus outlining the progress of the class. There are 4 exams, she drops the lowest one. There's also a term paper which is pretty extensive, but it is interesting to write. Overall, Dr. Zucker's course is interesting and easy to do work for.

Zucker's a great professor, gives great insight into the material (esp. eating disorders). The structure of the class is pretty solid. If you want a pretty woke class with less stigmatized insight into mental health issues, this is the class to take.

Great experience in class so far; a couple of lectures can be a little dry, though that could have been because it was an early 8:30am class. Guest lectures are usually interesting, and the subject matter is always deep. The TA discussions were always engaging and pretty fun. Highly recommend for any student; it's an eye-opening class
I love Thor! Good teacher, fair tests.

Zucker is an awesome professor. We had 4 exams (the lowest of which she dropped) and a final paper. The final paper is quite long, so don't procrastinate! The exams are multiple choice and straight-forward -- make sure you go to lecture! Added plus: she brings her dog to class :)

Zucker's lectures were not as interesting as I hoped, but the TAs were kind and helpful. A few of the guest lectures are more compelling. Her office hours are hard to reach, but you don't really need them. The class isn't rocket science, put it's important to pace your readings and not procrastinate for tests or the final paper.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Barely taught a class, instead just brought in guest lecturers.

I had Zucker for Abnormal Psych and I think she did a phenomenal job. She always brings in guest lecturers (hint: go to the lectures or at least read their powerpoint bc questions about them are usually on the exam) who are pretty interesting. TAs were really good. She had 4 exams and dropped the lowest grade. Gives a big final paper, not too bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Great Professor!

Professor Zucker is an extremely nice teacher who is knowledgeable about the topic. However, the organization of the class was frustrating since deadlines were constantly shifted and papers were not graded in a reasonable amount of time. On the plus side, there are many good guest lectures, easy papers, and interesting topics to discuss.

Professor Zucker was pretty disorganized in terms of reading/responding to emails, grading papers, etc., but overall, I enjoyed her class.  She was incredibly knowledgeable on the subject matter, she brought in really interesting guest speakers for each disorder we learned about, and she was an easy grader with clear guidelines and example papers.

Dr. Zucker is really nice and means well but takes her/the TAs FOREVER to give back assignments meaning you'll be handing in your next paper before you get the last one back (and we didn't get some papers back at all) which can be annoying but she provides incredibly clear guidelines for papers. Lectures are really interesting! Final is easy!

Ok so basically she is the most disorganized professor I've had at Duke. Don't take this class if you are trying to take an easy/interesting psych class because the lectures are incredibly dry and boring and the textbook reading is more interesting and engaging than Dr. Zucker. The TA system is awful and they provide no guidance on our assignments.

The course on eating disorders was the most interesting one I've ever taken at Duke. It's a small seminar so you really need to read the articles she assigns every week or it'll be awkward. Professor Zucker is busy but still manages to take time to talk with students, especially about the final paper (20 pages). Take it!

Professor Zucker is great at making students feel comfortable breaching topics that are often hard to bring up. Sex, eating disorders, depression - she isn't afraid to be up front with us, a blunt attitude that usually makes lectures more interesting! Only complaint I could give would be that guidelines on essays were sometimes unclear.

Prof. Zucker is great, specializes in eating disorders and know a lot about anorexia etc. Brushes over a lot of the specifics about mental illnesses but you get a good sense of the info. Very willing to meet outside of class even though she's super busy. Very sweet, and only assigns papers.

Very interesting topic and an easy class. No tests, only papers to write.  She is very nice, but lectures tend to be a little boring. She spices it up by bringing in lots of guest speakers throughout the semester. I highly recommend!
